prs.title: fix(core): keep atomic-write temp file name within NAME_MAX
prs.body:
## Summary

Writing a file whose name is 215-255 bytes fails with `ENAMETOOLONG`, even though the name itself is valid. The atomic-write temp file name is the destination name plus a 41-byte `.<uuid>.tmp` suffix, which goes over NAME_MAX (255 bytes). This PR keeps the temp file name within the limit so any name the filesystem accepts can be written or overwritten. Non-Latin names are hit sooner because the limit is in bytes (a CJK character is 3 bytes in UTF-8).

## Details

- `packages/core/src/services/fileSystemService.ts`: added `MAX_NAME_BYTES = 255` and `buildTempPath(realPath)`, which `writeTextFile` now uses for `tmpPath`.
- Names that already fit keep the existing `<dest>.<uuid>.tmp` format. The existing tests pin that regex, so I did not switch to a fixed name.
- For longer names, only the base name in the temp path is truncated, by whole characters measured in UTF-8 bytes, so a multi-byte character is never split.
- The temp file stays in the same directory, so the rename remains atomic. The `catch` cleanup reuses `tmpPath`, so nothing else changed.
- Out of scope: other temp-name sites (`oauth2.ts`, `policy/config.ts`) use fixed config names and are not affected.
- Tests: new `long file names` block in `fileSystemService.atomic.test.ts` (skipped on Windows): 214-byte ASCII (control), 215, 254 and 255-byte ASCII, a 244-byte CJK name, and overwriting an existing 254-byte name. Each checks the content and that no `.tmp` file is left behind.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29702

## How to Validate

1. Run `npx vitest run packages/core/src/services/fileSystemService`. Expected: 2 files, 19 tests pass.
2. To see the bug: `git checkout upstream/main -- packages/core/src/services/fileSystemService.ts`, rerun step 1. The 5 failing-case tests fail with `ENAMETOOLONG` and the 214-byte control passes. Restore with `git checkout HEAD -- packages/core/src/services/fileSystemService.ts`.

What I ran locally (Fedora Linux, Node 20.19):

- Typecheck passed for every package. Tests passed for core (8325), a2a-server, sdk and vscode-ide-companion.
- `packages/cli/src/gemini.test.tsx` had 9 failures. 8 were `FatalUntrustedWorkspaceError` (my clone is not a trusted directory) and pass with `GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true`. The 9th, `should handle session selector error`, is order-dependent: it passes alone, failed 2 of 3 full-file runs on this branch, and also failed in one run on clean `upstream/main`.

prs.title: fix(vscode-ide-companion): track all activate() disposables in context.subscriptions
prs.body:
Fixes #27790.

## What
In `packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/extension.ts`, `activate()` wrapped two pairs of registrations in extra parentheses, turning them into comma expressions:

```ts
context.subscriptions.push(
  (vscode.commands.registerCommand('gemini.diff.accept', ...),   // <- evaluated, then discarded
   vscode.commands.registerCommand('gemini.diff.cancel', ...)),  // <- only this reaches push()
);
```

Only the last Disposable of each pair (`gemini.diff.cancel`, `onDidGrantWorkspaceTrust`) reached `context.subscriptions.push()`. The `gemini.diff.accept` command and the `onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders` listener were registered but never tracked, so they leak on extension deactivation.

This PR removes the extra parens so each Disposable is its own `push()` argument, and adds a regression test asserting all four disposables land in `context.subscriptions`.

## Verification
- New test `should push every disposable to context.subscriptions (no comma-expression leaks)` **fails on unfixed code** and **passes with the fix**.
- `npx vitest run src/extension.test.ts`: 13/13 green.
- `npx eslint` on both changed files: clean.
- Checked for duplicates: no open PR currently addresses #27790.

## Note for maintainers
I saw several previous PRs for this issue were auto-closed by the stale bot because #27790 lacks the `help wanted` label. If a maintainer could add the label, it would keep this PR from meeting the same fate. Happy to adjust the approach if you'd prefer a different shape for the fix.

prs.title: fix(core): fall back across model tiers only when Auto quota is exhausted
prs.body:
### Summary

Auto quota routing currently dead-ends a session after a hard quota exhaustion, and capacity-shaped failures are recorded as permanent unavailability. This PR rebuilds the terminal-quota handling so that **Auto mode** immediately routes across model tiers (Pro ↔ Flash) on true quota exhaustion, while **manual selections** always stay on the user's chosen model.

The behavior this restores was last healthy around 0.53. The regression chain, in upstream history:

- #28599 (Jul 30) — capacity messages introduced a delay-less `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` path that classified terminal.
- #28716 (Aug 6) — capacity reason codes classify as `terminal` even with `RetryInfo`; the prompt-on-attempt-1 behavior and the a2a `retry_always → stop` wiring landed here.
- #28730 (Aug 11) — added the false "usage limit" wording plus quota-bucket `modelId` normalization.
- #28790 (Aug 13) — added three silent capacity retries and the 30s TTL, but only for reason `'capacity'`.
- #28761 — maintainer/user-confirmed fallout thread: *"MODEL_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED is definitely not terminal"*, *"0.53.1 seems to be the last version with retries"*; closes "in #28790" but the terminal-marking mismatch survived.

The concrete interlock today:

1. `DEFAULT_STATE` maps every failure kind → `'terminal'` (`policyCatalog.ts`), and `applyAvailabilityTransition` derives the terminal reason from the failure kind instead of the error: `failureKind === 'terminal' ? 'quota' : 'capacity'` (`policyHelpers.ts`). Capacity-shaped `TerminalQuotaError`s therefore get a **permanent `'quota'`** mark, while the `'capacity'` TTL from #28790 only applies to errors already classified as capacity — the TTL and the error's permanence are inverted.
2. Marking only happens after a fallback intent is accepted (`handleFallback`), never during silent retries.
3. After one exhausted-quota outcome, both chain models can be marked in a single turn (`failedModel` + the alternate it is about to silently try). `selectFirstAvailable` then has no candidates, `lastResort === failedModel`, and `handleFallback` returns `null` — the request fails with no retry, no dialog, and no reset-until-session-restart path that a user can influence.

### What this changes

- **Classification split (`googleQuotaErrors.ts`)** — new `isQuotaExhaustedError()` returns `true` only for errors driven by an exhausted usage entitlement. It excludes `MODEL_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED`/`MODEL_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED` (reason or message), `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (`ErrorInfo` reason), per-minute `QuotaFailure` violations, insufficient-credit errors, and 5xx statuses. Transient conditions keep their existing retry rules.
- **Reason-aware terminal marking (`policyHelpers.ts`, `handler.ts`)** — `applyAvailabilityTransition` takes an optional terminal reason computed from the error. Capacity failures land in the #28790 TTL bucket; true exhaustion is a permanent `'quota'` mark, recorded through `markQuotaExhausted()` for every alias/backend ID that maps to the exhausted model so the same backend is never retried under another name.
- **Quota-aware selection (`policyHelpers.ts`)** — `resolveQuotaFallbackModel()` picks the other tier for Auto selections. It skips models whose quota is advertised as zero (`remainingFraction`/`remainingAmount`, including the legacy Code Assist Flash bucket), honors no-Pro-access and preview/Gemini 3.1 access flags when resolving the tier candidates, keeps distinct API-key backend IDs separate from Code Assist aliases, skips candidates whose runtime override resolves back to an exhausted model, and consults availability health. Zero-quota knowledge is applied *before* a request is sent (`selectModelForAvailability`), so a known-exhausted model is not even attempted.
- **Immediate cross-tier switch (`retry.ts`, `baseLlmClient.ts`)** — new `onQuotaExhausted` retry hook. When a hard-quota error arrives and the current model is an Auto selection, `handleFallback` marks exhaustion, rotates the session ID, sets the active model to the selected alternate, and the retry loop continues with the attempt counter reset. This is silent (no dialog) in both interactive and unattended Auto use, and stops with an enriched error when no eligible model remains, instead of waiting for a reset.
- **Manual selections stay manual** — a manual selection whose own quota is exhausted keeps the selected model (availability never substitutes another model for it), and the existing same-model retry / stop / upgrade affordances are unchanged. Temporary model activation during fallback preserves exhaustion marks; an explicit model selection still clears availability state except for exhaustion marks.
- Preserved by design: the three-objective behavior from #28716 (fail-fast prompts, silent capacity retries from #28790, launch-flag chain behavior) and `isOriginallyGemini3` manual wrap-around semantics are unchanged.

### Behavior

| Scenario | Auto | Manual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hard quota exhausted (e.g. daily limit) | Immediately switches to the other tier, no prompt; marks the exhausted model and all its aliases/IDs | Stays on the selected model; same-model retry / stop / upgrade dialog unchanged |
| Both tiers exhausted | Stops with an enriched quota error instead of waiting for a reset | Stays on the selected model |
| Known zero quota on the requested model | Skips to the alternate before sending a request | Stays on the selected model |
| Capacity exhaustion (`MODEL_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED`) | 3 silent in-turn retries (interactive) / bounded retries (unattended); TTL-bucketed availability per #28790 | Unchanged behavior |
| Per-minute rate limits, credits, 5xx | Unchanged (existing retry/backoff) | Unchanged |

### a2a-server

The a2a-server intentionally returns `stop` from its in-request fallback handler (per #28716); future requests still fall back through `activateFallbackMode`. This PR's scope is core Auto quota routing, so that behavior is unchanged — noting it here because the terminal-marking change touches the shared `handleFallback` path.

### Tests

All tests live in the existing upstream test files (no new test files), extending:
- `googleQuotaErrors.test.ts` — exhaustion vs capacity / rate-limit / credits / per-minute violations / 5xx classification.
- `policyHelpers.test.ts` — cross-tier selection, zero-quota skip (including legacy Code Assist buckets), alias/backend mapping, no-Pro-access + runtime override resolution, access-flag refinement, manual fixedness under exhaustion.
- `modelAvailabilityService.test.ts` — `reset({ preserveQuota })` keeps exhaustion marks only.
- `config.test.ts` — `activateFallbackMode` in Auto keeps the user's Auto selection while routing the active model; manual activations preserve exhaustion marks.
- `retry.test.ts` — `onQuotaExhausted` hook fires only for true exhaustion, resets attempts, falls back to the enriched error otherwise.
- `handler.test.ts` + `baseLlmClient.test.ts` — Auto silently switches with no handler invocation; manual keeps the dialog; the hook is only wired for eligible Auto selections; already-exhausted alternates route to `null` rather than switching.
- `geminiChat.test.ts` / `geminiChat_network_retry.test.ts` — resolved-config refresh during the persistent-429 path and real-retry coverage, including a renamed manual Gemini-3 case (upstream previously re-routed manual Gemini-3 models on quota; this PR intentionally fixes those fixtures to the new no-switch behavior).

### Pre-submission checklist

- [x] Core `typecheck` (tsc) clean; CLI and a2a-server `typecheck` clean.
- [x] Core `npm run build` and CLI build succeed.
- [x] Full core vitest suite green (420 files) plus all touched focused suites, run serially (`--maxWorkers=1`).
- [x] `eslint` on every changed file; `prettier --check` on every changed file; `git diff --check` clean.
- [x] Behavior documented in `docs/cli/model.md`.
- [x] Linux: Docker offline-intercept fixture (`node:20-slim`, mock Code Assist backend via `CODE_ASSIST_ENDPOINT`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_ACCESS_TOKEN` auth) — real HTTP flow: router classifies → `gemini-2.5-pro` turn returns `429` + `ErrorInfo(QUOTA_EXHAUSTED)` + `RetryInfo(3600s)` → classified `TerminalQuotaError` → silent Auto switch ("Usage limit reached on gemini-2.5-pro. Switching to gemini-3.5-flash." in debug output) → second `:streamGenerateContent` request on flash returns SSE and the user turn completes with the flash answer, exit 0, no dialog, no forced wait.
- [ ] Linux: Podman + the same fixture. *Blocked on host sudo — pending install.*
- [x] Linux: `npx` smoke via `npm pack` of the fixed workspace (CLI + core tarballs installed into a scratch project, `npx --no-install gemini --version` → `0.66.0-nightly.g204db94ae`).
- [x] Windows (native `node.exe` v24.14.1 on an NTFS checkout of this head): `npm ci` clean; core + CLI `typecheck` clean (exit 0); CLI package `npm run build` clean (exit 0, `dist/index.js` produced); root `npm run bundle` clean; version probes: `node bundle\gemini.js --version` and `node packages\cli\dist\index.js --version` → `0.66.0-nightly.g204db94ae`. Focused vitest across the same 12-suite set as Linux (quota classification, retry, handler, policy helpers, config, availability service, baseLlmClient, both integration files, network-retry, useQuotaAndFallback, ProQuotaDialog): 300 tests ran, 267 pass; the only failures are 33 `config.test.ts` cases in Windows-specific areas (path normalization, ripgrep discovery, GitService/initialize) that reproduce **byte-identically on unmodified upstream `main`** (baseline checkout of `main` on the same NTFS volume: same 33 failures, verified with a name-by-name diff; this PR adds 50 tests to that file and all 50 pass on Windows). Known upstream-environment quirk, also baseline-reproduced: core's `npm run build` under the npm lifecycle aborts with a native `0xC0000409` (STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN, npm exit 3221226505) after the browser-mcp bundling step — identical crash point and code on unmodified `main`; every individual step (`tsc --build`, browser-mcp bundle, `copy_files.js`, docs `cpSync`) passes standalone on both checkouts, `tsc` output completes before the crash on both, and the CLI workspace build is unaffected. Note: `npx --no-install gemini --version` is not usable as a workspace probe on this host because it resolves to a pre-existing global install (0.63.0), so that specific sub-check is intentionally left unchecked; the built artifacts were invoked directly instead.
- [ ] macOS (Seatbelt sandbox). *Not available in this environment — leaving unchecked.*

### Review notes

- The protected-1-4 conflict surface is `handler.ts` + `policyHelpers.ts` — both files' changes are additive; existing shapes (chain resolution, policy catalog, `SILENT_ACTIONS`) are untouched.
- `applyModelSelection` now throws a `TerminalQuotaError` when the selection finds no eligible model (Auto behavior: stop instead of waiting for a reset). It only throws for Auto selections; manual selections return the backup model exactly as before.

- `modelAvailabilityService.reset()` gained an optional `{ preserveQuota }` argument (default behavior unchanged: clear everything).
- The retry hook (unlike `onPersistent429`) is not gated behind `isInteractive`: interactive gating stays only where a user prompt can be shown; exhaustion routing works in unattended contexts.

prs.body:
Fixes #25369.

Terminals (wcwidth) render U+0E33/U+0EB3 (SARA AM) as a spacing column, but Ink folds it into the preceding cluster and measures it with `string-width`, which returns 1 for "กำ" (terminal: 2). The resulting cursor desync causes duplicated lines / jumping input in tmux.

Fix: add one column per SARA AM in `getCachedStringWidth`, and register it with Ink via `setStringWidthFunction` before render.

Tests: unit cases for กำ, ทำ, น้ำ, กำลัง, แนะนำ, Lao ຫຳ, mixed ASCII, plus no-regression for Thai without SARA AM. `textUtils.test.ts` passes (85/85); prettier, eslint and cli typecheck pass.

Not verified in a live tmux session.

prs.title: fix(skills): handle single-line descriptions in SKILL.md frontmatter
prs.body:
## Summary

Fix skill discovery silently failing when the `description` field in `SKILL.md` frontmatter is written on a single line (i.e., the closing `---` marker immediately follows the description with no blank line). Affected skills were completely invisible in `/skills list`.

## Details

The root cause was two-fold:

1. **`FRONTMATTER_REGEX`** did not account for UTF-8 BOMs (`\uFEFF`) at the start of files, or trailing whitespace on `---` delimiter lines, causing the regex to fail to match valid frontmatter blocks.

2. **`parseSimpleFrontmatter`** (the fallback YAML parser) incorrectly split single-line descriptions when subsequent lines contained `name:` or `description:`. It also was not case-insensitive and required exact colon formatting.

**Changes to `skillLoader.ts`:**
- Updated `FRONTMATTER_REGEX` to strip UTF-8 BOMs and tolerate trailing spaces/tabs on `---` lines.
- Refactored `parseSimpleFrontmatter` to be case-insensitive, support optional spaces before colons, and use a negative lookahead to prevent misidentifying value lines as new keys.
- Replaced an unsafe `as Record<string, unknown>` type assertion with a proper `isRecord()` type guard to satisfy `@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-type-assertion`.

**Changes to `skillLoader.test.ts`:**
- Added 7 new regression tests covering: single-line descriptions, UTF-8 BOM presence, trailing spaces after delimiters, case-insensitive keys, optional spaces before colons, robust non-string value casting, and indented description edge cases.

## Related Issues

Fixes #25693

## How to Validate

1. Create a skill with a single-line description:
   ```markdown
   ---
   name: my-test-skill
   description: A single-line description
   ---
   Skill body here.
   ```
2. Place it in `~/.gemini/skills/my-test-skill/SKILL.md`
3. Run `npm run build && npm run start`
4. Inside the CLI, run `/skills list`
5. **Expected:** `my-test-skill` appears with its description
6. **Before fix:** The skill would be missing from the list entirely

Alternatively, run the unit tests:
```bash
npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/skills/skillLoader.test.ts
```
All 21 tests should pass.

issues.title: --agent code-review fails before inference with "Selected custom agent system prompt callback is unavailable"
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

Selecting the built-in `code-review` profile with `copilot --agent code-review` fails with an internal system-prompt callback error before inference. A normal CLI coordinator can successfully invoke `code-review` as a synchronous task in the same environment.

It is unclear whether direct selection of this built-in is supported. If it is intentionally subagent-only, the CLI should reject this selection with actionable guidance rather than an internal callback failure.

## Affected version

```text
GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.98.
```

## Steps to reproduce the behavior

Run a code-free prompt with the built-in selected:

```bash
env -u GH_TOKEN -u GITHUB_TOKEN copilot \
  --agent code-review \
  --model gpt-6.1-sol \
  --reasoning-effort xhigh \
  --silent --stream off --log-level error \
  --no-ask-user \
  -p 'Reply with exactly OK. Do not read files or call tools.'
```

The reproduction uses the existing Copilot login and does not require a pull request, source files, or an actual code review.

Observed result:

- Exit status: `1`.
- Stdout: empty.
- Stderr:

```text
Error executing prompt: Error: GenericFailure, host interaction call failed: Error: Selected custom agent system prompt callback is unavailable
```

Separately captured usage output reported:

```json
{
  "totalUserRequests": 0,
  "totalApiDurationMs": 0,
  "modelMetrics": {},
  "agentMetrics": {},
  "lastCallInputTokens": 0,
  "lastCallOutputTokens": 0
}
```

These are selected fields, not the complete usage document.

## Expected behavior

Either:

1. If direct built-in selection is supported, execute the selected profile with the supplied prompt.
2. If `code-review` is intentionally subagent-only, fail early with a clear message explaining the restriction and the supported invocation route.

Please clarify the intended support for built-in agents with `--agent`.

## Additional context

- Operating system: macOS 26.6.2.
- Architecture: arm64.
- Requested model and reasoning effort: `gpt-6.1-sol`, `xhigh`.
- Successful comparison: a normal CLI coordinator invoked exactly one synchronous task with `agent_type: code-review`. The reviewer completed and its final response was returned to the coordinator.
- Direct selection and task delegation are distinct routes. The successful delegated run does not establish the cause of the direct-selection failure.
- The root cause is unknown. This report does not assume that a missing custom agent file is responsible.
- The failure also occurred in a separate review invocation; the code-free reproduction above removes the need to disclose that repository or its contents.
- No private source code, repository identifiers, credentials, session identifiers, or raw execution logs are included.

issues.title: Regression: Manual Approval no longer prompts for repository-mutating Git commands after Copilot harness migration
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

## Critical Facts

1. **Regression introduced with the October 2026 Copilot agent harness migration.**
   - Before the migration, VS Code Copilot Chat consistently requested explicit approval before executing repository-mutating Git commands.
   - This included `git add`, `git commit`, `git push`, `git checkout -b`, `git branch -D`, merges, rebases, and similar operations.
   - After the migration to the new Copilot agent harness, some of these commands execute without approval.
   - The developer did not request or authorize a change to this approval behavior.

2. **Reproduced in both Copilot CLI and VS Code Copilot Chat.**
   - Both environments exhibit inconsistent approval behavior.
   - This suggests the problem may originate in the shared Copilot CLI agent harness or its permission-handling implementation.

3. **Manual Approval mode is explicitly enabled.**
   - Both Copilot CLI and VS Code Copilot Chat are running in Manual Approval mode.
   - Neither environment was intentionally configured to allow unrestricted tool execution.
   - The observed behavior is inconsistent with the developer's expectation that repository-mutating Git commands require approval.

4. **Controlled reproduction demonstrates inconsistent authorization.**
   - Executed `git branch -D nope` through Copilot CLI.
   - The command executed without requesting approval.
   - Git reported `error: branch 'nope' not found`, confirming the command was actually executed.
   - In the same Copilot CLI session, deleting `PR_DESCRIPTION.md` through PowerShell triggered an explicit approval request.
   - Therefore, the approval mechanism is operational but is not consistently applied to potentially destructive Git commands.

5. **VS Code terminal auto-approval is explicitly disabled.**
   - `chat.tools.terminal.enableAutoApprove` is set to `false`.
   - `chat.agent.sandbox.allowAutoApprove` is set to `false`.
   - `chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowNetwork` is set to `false`.
   - File-edit auto-approval is also explicitly disabled.
   - Investigation suggests that the new harness may execute commands through a `powershell` tool rather than VS Code's traditional terminal tool, potentially bypassing the VS Code terminal approval configuration.
   - This execution-path explanation remains a hypothesis, not a confirmed root cause.

6. **No evidence of a persisted blanket approval.**
   - `%USERPROFILE%\.copilot\permissions-config.json` does not exist in the inspected configuration directory.
   - Extensive configuration analysis has not identified an intentional authorization for automatic execution of destructive Git commands.
   - The absence of this file does not conclusively exclude other permission sources.

7. **Related existing issue.**
   - GitHub Copilot CLI issue #4156 describes `git branch -D` executing without approval.
   - https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/4156
   - However, this report concerns the broader regression in Git operation approvals observed after the October 2026 harness migration.

## Expected Behavior

In Manual Approval mode, repository-mutating Git operations should require explicit authorization before execution, consistent with the behavior of VS Code Copilot Chat before the October 2026 agent harness migration.

This includes commands such as `git add`, `git commit`, `git push`, branch creation/deletion, merges, and rebases.

## Actual Behavior

Some repository-mutating Git commands execute without requesting authorization, despite Manual Approval mode being active.

Other destructive operations, such as deleting files through PowerShell, correctly request approval.

The resulting permission behavior is inconsistent and difficult for developers to predict.

## Impact

This regression undermines human-supervised, non-autonomous coding workflows.

Previously, developers could depend on the IDE to mediate repository-mutating Git operations. After the harness migration, that authorization boundary is no longer consistently enforced.

This is particularly concerning for operations such as `git push`, forced branch deletion, resets, merges, and rebases, where an unintended operation can have significant consequences.

**This is not a request for a new feature. It is a report of an established authorization behavior that regressed during the Copilot agent harness migration.**

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- VS Code: 1.140.0
- Copilot CLI: Manual Approval mode
- Copilot CLI version: 1.0.98
- VS Code Copilot Chat: New Copilot agent harness (October 2026 migration)
- Chat : Agent: Sandbox Enabled: off

## Requested Resolution

Restore reliable, explicit approval for repository-mutating Git operations in Manual Approval mode.

Ideally, approval enforcement should be deterministic and independent of the agent model's judgment about whether a command is safe.

At minimum, developers need a supported configuration that guarantees approval before executing Git commands that modify repository state.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.98

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Manual Permissions mode is on. 
2. No auto approval settings for repo-mutating git commands
3. ask GH CLI or VS Code copilot chat to execute `git branch -D nope` and it executes it without prompting for approval. 
4. `git push` commands and many other repo-mutating commands also execute without first requesting approval via the built-in terminal approval mechanism. 

### Expected behavior

Repo-mutating `git` commands should prompt for approval via the built-in terminal approval mechanism as it did before the October 2026 update. 

### Additional context

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- VS Code: 1.140.0
- Copilot CLI: Manual Approval mode
- Copilot CLI version: 1.0.98
- VS Code Copilot Chat: New Copilot agent harness (October 2026 migration)
- Chat : Agent: Sandbox Enabled: off

issues.title: Linux sandbox: shell commands are killed after ~10 s (bwrap parent-death signal bound to an exited thread)
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

On Linux with the sandbox enabled, a shell command that runs longer than ~10 s is killed
with SIGKILL. The tool reports `exit code -1`. There is no error message. The same command
passes without the sandbox, and it also passes with plain `bwrap` outside the CLI.

### Affected version

1.0.98 (Linux x64). Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.8, bubblewrap 0.9.0.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Enable the sandbox (`/sandbox`, or `"sandbox": {"enabled": true}` in settings).
2. Run:
   ```
   copilot -p 'Run this exact shell command once: date +%T; sleep 30; date +%T' --allow-all-tools
   ```
3. Result: only the first `date` prints, then `Failed with exit code -1` after ~10 s.

In `-p` mode it fails every time. In interactive sessions it fails only on some runs.

### Expected behavior

The command runs to the end (exit 0 after ~30 s).

### Additional context

Cause, from `strace -f` of the CLI:

```
<bwrap>   11:58:37.324667 prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGKILL) = 0
<thread>  11:58:47.432660 exit(0)
<bwrap>   11:58:47.433353 +++ killed by SIGKILL +++
```

The CLI starts `bwrap --die-with-parent` from a worker (pool) thread. On Linux,
`PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` fires when the thread that forked the child exits, not when the
process exits. The runtime stops that thread after ~10 s idle, so the kernel kills bwrap
and the command. There is no `kill()` syscall and no OOM event.

Possible fixes: spawn bwrap from a long-lived thread, or watch the CLI process (for
example with a pidfd) instead of using `--die-with-parent`.

Workaround: put a small `bwrap` wrapper first in `PATH`. The wrapper starts the real bwrap
from its own process and kills it when the CLI process exits.

issues.title: HydraFusion (policy max): router returns models outside the policy universe, then silently falls back to gpt-5.6-luna

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

With **HydraFusion** selected (policy `max`), most turns fail at the routing step and silently continue on a lower-tier model. The UI only shows:

> HydraFusion routing failed; continuing with gpt-5.6-luna

The session log records the reason:

```json
{
  "type": "session.fusion_route_failed",
  "syntheticModel": "hydrafusion",
  "policy": "max",
  "reason": "invalid_response",
  "errorMessage": "fusion routing returned an invalid response: fusion route references a model outside the selected policy universe: gpt-6.1-sol",
  "fallbackModel": "gpt-5.6-luna"
}
```

In one session over two days there were **10 routing failures against 3 successful routes**:

| Model returned by the router | Failures |
|---|---:|
| `gpt-6.1-sol` | 9 |
| `claude-sonnet-5.5` | 1 |

Both rejected models are **enabled for the account**. The model list the runtime publishes to VS Code in the same session lists `gpt-6.1-sol` (and `claude-sonnet-5.5`) with `"policyState": "enabled"`. The server-side router (`routeSource: "capi_plan"`) therefore seems to work with a different model set than the runtime's "policy universe" for `max`. I couldn't find out how the runtime builds that set.

There are two problems here:

1. **Router and runtime disagree on the allowed models.** The router keeps choosing models the runtime then rejects, so most turns never run as HydraFusion.
2. **The fallback is a silent capability downgrade.** When the route is rejected, the turn runs on `gpt-5.6-luna` instead. A user who picked HydraFusion with the `max` policy for a demanding task (planning, in my case) ends up on a much cheaper model, with only a transient warning.

A related observation: the routes that *did* succeed under `max` also only used `gpt-5.6-luna` (primary/fallback/follow-up) and `gpt-5.6-terra` (secondary) with the Critique pattern. Higher-tier models such as `claude-opus-5.5`, which is enabled for the account, were never chosen. Those resolved routes also report `"policyVersion": null` and `"modelUniverseVersion": null`, which may be relevant to the mismatch.

### Affected version

Copilot runtime `1.0.92-4.unstable.r37397886721.gad270aa` (bundled `@github/copilot-sdk-linux-x64` `1.0.17-unstable.37397886721.gad270aa`)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. In VS Code agent mode (Copilot SDK agent host), select **HydraFusion** as the model. The routing policy is `max`.
2. Send a normal multi-step coding/planning request.
3. The warning "HydraFusion routing failed; continuing with gpt-5.6-luna" appears for most turns.
4. The session's `events.jsonl` contains `session.fusion_route_failed` events with `reason: "invalid_response"` and "fusion route references a model outside the selected policy universe: <model>".

This happened consistently over two days. I haven't tested other policies.

### Expected behavior

- The router only returns models that are inside the runtime's policy universe for the selected policy. Models the account has enabled (such as `gpt-6.1-sol`) should either be in the `max` universe or not be routed to.
- If a route is invalid anyway, the fallback should not silently downgrade capability. Either fall back to a model of comparable tier for the selected policy, or fail the turn with a clear, retryable error so the user can pick a model.
- Ideally, the UI makes it obvious that the turn did not run as HydraFusion.

### Additional context

- VS Code 1.141.0, Windows client with a WSL (Ubuntu) remote; the agent host runs in WSL (Linux x86_64).
- GitHub Enterprise Cloud account with data residency (`*.ghe.com` host). I don't know whether the router's model set differs for those tenants.
- Possibly related: microsoft/vscode#339959 (HydraFusion offered although the runtime rejects it: a different symptom, but the same client/runtime model-policy mismatch) and github/app#4569 (preference for higher-capability routing).
- I can share more `session.fusion_*` event fields if that helps.

issues.title: HydraFusion: after a 400 on the routed model, the session is re-routed to a small-context model that cannot load the static prompt; tool set changes mid-session

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
## Summary

With HydraFusion selected, a session that had run for 37 minutes on the routed model (gpt-5.6-sol) got a `400 The requested model is not supported`. On the next user turn the router re-resolved and switched the **same session** to `mai-code-1.1-flash`, whose context window cannot hold Copilot's own static system prompt and tool definitions. Every turn after that failed with `compaction_static_context_blocked` and `No response was returned`, so the session was unrecoverable without abandoning 372 AI credits of context. The fallback also replaced the tool set mid-task.

## Environment

- Copilot CLI 1.0.91, Windows 11, PowerShell 7
- Enterprise endpoint (`api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`)
- Model: HydraFusion (picked in `/model`; `policy: max`, `routeSource: capi_plan`, `pattern: single`)
- Session id `a1200a27-25bf-4981-b556-788df9b3e211`
- Request ID of the 400: `D852:1368A9:1B5D885:1D72AED:6ABFFD3A` (serviceRequestId `21db88d8-c245-4158-b37f-4124608cdc35`)

## Timeline (from `session-state/<id>/events.jsonl`)

| time (UTC) | event |
|---|---|
| 18:13:52 | `session.model_change` source `model_picker`: `auto` → `hydrafusion` |
| 18:13:57 | `session.fusion_resolved` policy `max`, routeSource `capi_plan`, pattern `single`; the solver is gpt-5.6-sol (`session.usage_checkpoint.modelCacheState`) |
| 18:14 to 18:51 | 76 assistant turns, 114 tool calls, all on gpt-5.6-sol; `totalNanoAiu` reaches 372,060,920,000 |
| 18:51:38 | `session.error`: `Execution failed: 400 The requested model is not supported.` |
| 18:58:58 | user sends `continue`. The transformed message carries `<tools_changed_notice>The model has been switched from gpt-5.6-sol to mai-code-1.1-flash. New tools available: create, edit, grep. Tools no longer available: apply_patch, rg</tools_changed_notice>` |
| 18:58:58 | `session.warning` `compaction_static_context_blocked`: "Static system messages and tool definitions exceed the model's usable context budget. Reduce static context or switch to a larger-context model." then `session.error` "No response was returned. Send your message again to retry." |
| 18:59:12 | second `continue`: identical warning and error |

## What went wrong

1. **Fallback ignores the session's context requirements.** A session carrying 372 credits of conversation on a 1M-window model was re-routed to a model that cannot even load the static prompt. The router treats "which solver" as a per-turn choice while the session carries state that constrains it. Whether a candidate fits the static context is knowable before the call.
2. **The 400 itself.** The model the router had been calling successfully for 37 minutes became "not supported" mid-session. The router should retry within the same capability class rather than surface the 400 and then fall to the smallest model.
3. **Tool set swapped mid-task.** The fallback changed the available editing tools (`apply_patch`/`rg` removed, `create`/`edit`/`grep` added) while the agent was in the middle of editing files. Even when a fallback fits, this is a correctness hazard for long autonomous runs.

## Expected

- A re-route never selects a model whose usable context is smaller than the static prompt plus the live conversation; if none fits, say so and keep the previous model selected so the user can `/compact` or continue.
- After a 400 on the routed model, retry with an equivalent-class model (same or larger context) before anything else.
- No tool-set change inside a session without the user choosing it.

## Workaround

Pin a large-context model for long autonomous sessions instead of HydraFusion.

I can share the full `events.jsonl` privately if useful.

issues.title: Reduce latency and review-loop overhead in subagent workflows
issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Subagent-driven implementation and review workflows can feel extremely slow. Agent startup, task handoffs, and repeated review/fix/re-review cycles often take minutes per round trip, making modest repository changes take much longer than expected.

### Proposed solution

Reduce subagent startup and handoff latency, reuse context more efficiently between fix and review rounds, and collapse redundant review passes when prior findings have been addressed. Show clearer elapsed-time and current-work indicators so users can distinguish useful background work from a stalled workflow.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. Implement a small configuration option plus regression coverage.
2. Run an implementer followed by a code-review agent.
3. Apply one review fix and re-review only the changed portion.
4. Complete a documentation-only task without another expensive full-context handoff.

### Additional context

Observed with Copilot CLI 1.0.83 on Linux. The main concern is end-to-end latency and the number of sequential agent round trips, not model answer quality.

issues.title: HydraFusion: emit per-phase model, verdict and credit attributes to OpenTelemetry
issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

A HydraFusion turn can run several models, but from the outside I only get one answer and one credit figure. The CLI already writes every routing decision down in `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl`. None of it reaches OpenTelemetry or the UI, so the only way to see which model did what is to read session state, which carries no compatibility promise.

### Proposed solution

#### What the CLI emits today

I measured this on 1.0.84-2 with `COPILOT_OTEL_FILE_EXPORTER_PATH`, no collector involved. Every turn arrives as one `invoke_agent` span, several `chat hydrafusion` spans, and `execute_tool` spans. Every one of those chat spans carries `gen_ai.request.model=hydrafusion`.

That is correct. The [GenAI semantic conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) define `gen_ai.request.model` as the model the client asked for, and the client did ask for `hydrafusion`. The conventions have no notion of a router that expands one request into several model calls, so there is nowhere for the per-phase detail to sit. This is a spec that has not caught up with the architecture, not a defect.

The metric side has the same shape. Six instruments, no token metric, no credit metric, and `gen_ai.request.model` is always `hydrafusion`. A turn that spent 51 credits across two models from two vendors is indistinguishable from a cheap single-model turn except by duration.

#### Where the data already lives

All of it is in the session log, fully structured. One event per phase:

```json
{"phaseKind":"judge","role":"judge","model":"gpt-5.6-sol","status":"succeeded",
 "verdict":"reject","durationMs":4522,
 "usage":{"requestCount":1,"inputTokens":12500,"outputTokens":7,
          "cachedTokens":7680,"cacheWriteTokens":0,"totalNanoAiu":2249200000}}
```

Plus `session.fusion_resolved` for the routing decision (pattern, policy, `routeSource`, `routingLatencyMs`, the phase plan), `session.fusion_handoff` for escalations, and `session.fusion_completed` for the turn rollup. Per-phase credits sum to the turn total exactly, to the nanounit, across every turn I checked.

So the instrumentation work is basically done. The values are computed, named and written to disk. They just never leave the process through a supported channel.

#### 1. One span per fusion phase

Emit a child span per phase under the turn root, carrying the model that actually served it:

```
invoke_agent                        github.copilot.fusion.pattern = cascade
└─ chat hydrafusion                 gen_ai.request.model  = hydrafusion
   ├─ phase 1                       gen_ai.response.model = mai-code-1.1-flash
   │                                github.copilot.fusion.phase.kind = primary
   │                                github.copilot.nano_aiu = 575436000
   ├─ phase 2                       gen_ai.response.model = gpt-5.6-sol
   │                                github.copilot.fusion.phase.kind = judge
   │                                github.copilot.fusion.phase.verdict = reject
   │                                github.copilot.nano_aiu = 2457200000
   └─ phase 3                       gen_ai.response.model = gpt-5.6-sol
                                    github.copilot.fusion.phase.kind = repair
                                    github.copilot.fusion.phase.committed = true
                                    github.copilot.nano_aiu = 11686960000
```

`gen_ai.response.model` needs no spec change. The conventions already define it as the model that generated the response, and per phase that is unambiguous. Everything router-specific goes under a `github.copilot.fusion.*` namespace, which keeps it out of the way if the WG later standardises orchestration attributes. If GitHub wanted to take that shape to the semconv group as a routing extension, there is now a working implementation and 24 turns of data behind it.

Suggested attributes:

| Attribute | Source field |
|---|---|
| `gen_ai.response.model` | `model` on the phase event |
| `github.copilot.fusion.pattern` | `pattern` |
| `github.copilot.fusion.phase.kind` | `phaseKind` |
| `github.copilot.fusion.phase.role` | `role` |
| `github.copilot.fusion.phase.verdict` | `verdict` |
| `github.copilot.fusion.phase.committed` | derived from `finalSourceModel` |
| `github.copilot.fusion.route_source` | `routeSource` |
| `github.copilot.fusion.routing_latency_ms` | `routingLatencyMs` |
| `github.copilot.nano_aiu` | `usage.totalNanoAiu` |

Metadata only. No prompt or response content needs to cross this boundary.

#### 2. Token and credit metrics dimensioned by serving model

`gen_ai.client.token.usage` is already a standard semconv histogram and the numbers are all in the phase events. A credit metric with the same dimensions would let people answer cost questions without running a trace backend at all.

#### 3. Something in the CLI itself

Not everyone will stand up a collector. A `/usage` view, or an expandable breakdown on the turn that just finished, showing the phases, who drafted, what the reviewer said and where the credits went. The [announcement](https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/github-copilot/project-hydrafusion-frontier-quality-via-multi-model-orchestration/) explains that intermediate drafts are held back so unfinished work does not read as final, which is the right call while the turn is running. After it finishes, I would like to be able to ask.

#### 4. An official reference dashboard

Once the attributes exist, ship a Grafana dashboard JSON and a collector config alongside the docs. Right now anyone who wants this reverse-engineers their own, and they will all diverge. One maintained dashboard in-repo settles the question of what the panels are supposed to mean.

#### Why I think this is worth doing

Three of these were surprises I could only get at by reading the log, and they are the kind of thing I would expect an org paying for credits to ask about:

- Across 24 turns, the phases that did not supply the answer came to 2.5% of spend. I would not have guessed that low, and I could not have found it from the CLI output.
- One model took 42% of total credits from three phases, all of them heavy refactors. Per-model attribution is invisible today because every span says `hydrafusion`.
- `routeSource` was `capi_plan` on all 24 turns, meaning routing policy is served remotely and can change without a CLI release. Without per-phase telemetry, a policy change lands as an unexplained shift in the credit line, with nothing to diff against.

I built a working version to prove the data supports it: [samueltauil/hydrafusion-traces](https://github.com/samueltauil/hydrafusion-traces). It tails the session log and rebuilds each turn as a trace. It is roughly 400 lines of stdlib Python, and it will break the first time the log format moves, which is exactly the argument for doing this properly upstream.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. "Why did this turn cost 51 credits?" Today the answer is one number. With per-phase spans it is a draft phase at 51.11 and a critic phase at 0.69, and you can see immediately that the review was cheap and the draft was not.
2. Finance asks which models an org's credits went to this month. Currently unanswerable from telemetry, because every span reports `hydrafusion`.
3. A routing policy changes server-side and credit spend jumps 30%. With `github.copilot.fusion.pattern` and `route_source` on spans, you can see the mix shift. Without them you can only see the bill.
4. "Is the quality gate paying for itself?" Judge rejection rate needs `phase.kind=judge` and a verdict. My sample had 2 rejections out of 3, which is far too small to mean anything, and that is the point: nobody can gather this at scale right now.
5. A turn returns a weak answer and you want to know which model committed it. `phase.committed` answers it in one click.

### Additional context

The dashboard I ended up with, for reference on what the data supports:

![HydraFusion routing dashboard in Grafana](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samueltauil/hydrafusion-traces/main/docs/screenshots/dashboard.png)

One cascade turn as three phases. `mai-code-1.1-flash` drafted for 22 seconds and 0.58 credits, `gpt-5.6-sol` reviewed it, returned `reject`, then redid the work itself in 42 seconds and 11.69 credits. The CLI showed one answer and the figure 14.72:

![Tempo waterfall for a cascade turn showing draft, judge and repair phases](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samueltauil/hydrafusion-traces/main/docs/screenshots/cascade-waterfall.png)

The whole ask sits on two attribute rows. `gen_ai.request.model` is `hydrafusion`, per the conventions. `gen_ai.response.model` is `gpt-5.6-sol`, which my tailer added from the session log. Both are true, and only the first one is available today:

![Span attributes showing request model hydrafusion and response model gpt-5.6-sol](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samueltauil/hydrafusion-traces/main/docs/screenshots/span-attributes.png)

Credits split by phase kind, which is the question I actually cared about and could not answer any other way:

![Credits by phase kind: primary, draft, repair, judge, critic](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samueltauil/hydrafusion-traces/main/docs/screenshots/where-credits-went.png)

Caveats on my end. This is one machine, one operator, 24 turns, one small Python project. It describes what the telemetry contains and shows the dashboard works. It is not a benchmark and says nothing about model quality. HydraFusion is a research preview and is expected to change. Model identifiers above are routing labels I observed, not product names.

Measurements and method: [docs/SPIKE.md](https://github.com/samueltauil/hydrafusion-traces/blob/main/docs/SPIKE.md) for what the CLI actually emits, [docs/FINDINGS.md](https://github.com/samueltauil/hydrafusion-traces/blob/main/docs/FINDINGS.md) for the 24-turn breakdown, and a [write-up](https://samueltauil.github.io/github-copilot/devops/2026/09/10/hydrafusion-model-routing-grafana-traces.html) of how I got there.

Possibly related:

- #4782, desktop app spans omitting GitHub context attributes. Different surface, same general theme of telemetry not carrying enough to attribute work.
- #4726, `invoke_agent` roots missing input on resumed turns.

Happy to split this into separate issues for the span work, the metrics, the in-product view and the dashboard if that suits triage better. I kept them together because the last three depend on the first.

issues.title: Copilot CLI remote SSH session reports “Copied” but clipboard remains empty on macOS

# Summary

When using Copilot CLI on a remote Linux machine over SSH from macOS Terminal, copy actions report success ("Copied to clipboard") but the selected text is not actually placed into the macOS clipboard.

    Local OS: macOS (Apple Terminal)
    Terminal: Terminal.app Version 2.15 (470.2)

        ssh -p <port> <host>

    Generate output in the CLI and select part of the text in the terminal.
    Try to copy the selected text (right-click copy or Ctrl+C in the terminal context).

Selected text should be copied to the macOS system clipboard and be available for paste in other local apps.

Copilot CLI shows a "Copied" confirmation, but the text is not present in the macOS clipboard.

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.80

_No response_

_No response_

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Since 1.0.99-0, the agent's `bash` tool denies, without showing a prompt, any command that `cd`s into a directory created earlier in the same command and then does something that needs a permission check (a write redirect, `git status`, `git log`, …). It returns:

```
Permission denied and could not request permission from user. Copilot needed the user's approval and no one could answer. This is not an OS or sandbox error.
```

This happens in an interactive session with `/allow-all` on, with the user at the terminal. The process log attributes it to the permissions engine:

```
[WARNING] [rust:permissions_engine::orchestrator] permission request denied: unusable session working directory
```

The denial happens before execution: none of the command runs, not even the leading `mkdir`.

It breaks common agent flows such as `git worktree add <dir> <ref> && cd <dir> && git log` (e.g. creating a worktree to review a PR) and `gh repo clone owner/repo <dir> && cd <dir> && …`. The agent then abandons the approach (for example, reviewing from `gh pr diff` instead of a worktree) because the error says approval was impossible.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.100-1 (also 1.0.99-0, 1.0.99-1, 1.0.99-3, 1.0.100-0)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

In an interactive session with `/allow-all` on, ask the agent to run each command as a single `bash` tool call:

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `mkdir -p /tmp/A && cd /tmp/A && echo hi > f.txt` | **Denied** |
| `cd /tmp && git init -q C && cd /tmp/C && git status --short` | **Denied** |
| `mkdir -p ~/tmp-B && cd ~/tmp-B && echo hi > f.txt` | **Denied** |
| `cd /tmp/existing-dir && echo hi > f.txt` (dir already exists) | OK |
| `mkdir -p /tmp/D && cd /tmp/D && pwd` | OK |
| `mkdir -p /tmp/E && cd /tmp/E && touch x && pwd` | OK |
| `d=$(mktemp -d); cd "$d"; touch f.txt` | OK |
| `git init -q /tmp/F && git -C /tmp/F status --short && echo hi > /tmp/F/f.txt` | OK |

Workaround: create the directory in one tool call and `cd` into it in the next, or avoid `cd` by using absolute paths and `git -C <dir>`.

### Expected behavior

With allow-all on, the command should run. If the CLI can't evaluate the command's paths before execution (because the `cd` target doesn't exist yet), it should ask the user rather than hard-deny. The error shouldn't say no one could answer when an interactive user is present.

### Additional context

- **Regression boundary**, from my local session history, counting `bash` calls shaped like `<mkdir -p | git init | git clone | gh repo clone | git worktree add> … && cd …`:

  | Versions | Such calls | Denied |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | 1.0.95 – 1.0.98-2 | ~64 | 0 |
  | 1.0.99-0 – 1.0.100-0 | ~57 | 24 |

- **Not caused by hooks:** my configured hooks return no permission decision for these commands, and the log line above comes from `permissions_engine::orchestrator`.
- **Likely cause:** pre-execution shell path analysis appears to resolve the `cd` target before the command runs. It can't resolve a directory that doesn't exist yet, and it hard-denies instead of falling back to a prompt.
- **Environment:** macOS 26.7.1, arm64. Terminal: iTerm2. User shell: zsh; the agent's bash tool uses `/bin/bash`.

issues.title: Rewind file tracking backs up gitignored secret files; add an exclude or an off switch

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
**Version**: Copilot CLI 1.0.91, Linux x64, interactive mode.

**What happens**

Since `/rewind` became git-free (1.0.78), the CLI saves the earlier content of every file that a turn changes under the session's working directory into `session-state/<session-id>/rewind-file-snapshots/backups/`. Gitignored files are included. When the agent edits a `.env` file in a turn (for example to rotate an API token), the old file, with every secret in it, stays in session state as a plain file at mode 644. It stays there after the session ends.

A session with one long autonomous turn has one snapshot, so every file that turn changes is held in that snapshot.

**What I checked**

- `copilot help config`, `copilot help environment` and `copilot --help` name no setting, flag or variable for rewind file tracking. `respectGitignore` covers only the `@` file picker.
- The interactive CLI starts each session with `enableFileChangeTracking` set to `true` as a constant. Only SDK clients can pass the option.
- The tracker skips a file only for its size, a non-regular file or an unverifiable identity. It does not skip files that `.gitignore` excludes or files that hold secrets.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. In a git repository, put `.env.local` in `.gitignore` and give it a line such as `EXAMPLE_TOKEN=old-value`.
2. Start `copilot` in that repository and ask it to change the value to `new-value` with a shell command.
3. List `session-state/<session-id>/rewind-file-snapshots/backups/`. One file holds `EXAMPLE_TOKEN=old-value`, and `index.json` maps it to `.env.local`.

**Expected**

A secret file that Copilot edits does not stay copied in session state. Any one of these would do:

1. Skip files that `.gitignore` excludes, or files that match `.env*`, when the tracker saves earlier content. `/rewind` then lists them as not restorable.
2. A setting, for example `rewind.excludePatterns`, that takes path patterns the tracker skips.
3. A setting or flag that turns off file tracking, leaving conversation-only rewind.

Also: write the backups at mode 600, the same as the other session files.

issues.body:
Title: CLI 1.0.97 starts a model outside the exact repository allowlist during a prompt-mode turn

Environment
GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.97, macOS arm64, official standalone binary.
Provider: GitHub Copilot; selected model claude-opus-5.5; reasoning effort high.

Observed behavior, 16 October 2026
A fresh prompt-mode session was launched in an isolated directory with --model claude-opus-5.5 --reasoning-effort high --output-format json --stream off. The directory contained .github/allowed_models.txt with:

fallback: claude-opus-5.5
claude-opus-5.5

The wrapper also disabled configured MCP servers and excluded tools. Actual telemetry reported zero tool definitions/requests and no changed files. It used a finite timeout and credit limit. No Auto model selection was requested; continueOnAutoMode is unset (documented default false).

Sanitized event sequence (UTC):
08:02:04.161 model.call_start model=claude-opus-5.5
08:02:10.566 model.call_start model=claude-opus-4.8
08:02:10.571 model.call_finished outcome=cancelled

Our external guard sent SIGINT when the second model appeared. agent.interrupted identified claude-opus-4.8, high effort, /v1/messages, cancelPhase=pre_first_token, elapsedMs=4. No final answer was returned. The CLI exited 0 despite the guard cancellation. Our wrapper has since been corrected to preserve a nonzero failure result and permanently invalidate a mismatched attempt.

The usage file attributed 3.07754 AI credits to claude-opus-5.5 and still listed currentModel=claude-opus-5.5. This does not establish that the alternate model completed inference or was charged. No refusal or rate-limit event in the retained evidence establishes why the alternate-model path started.

An earlier fresh invocation that day using the same model, effort and relevant controls completed on claude-opus-5.5. Therefore the failure is not a claim that this model never works. There is no known deterministic public reproduction prompt. The original private task prompt, raw logs, credentials, account identity, session identifiers and project data are intentionally omitted.

Expected behavior
With an exact model allowlist and explicit model selection, either use only that model or return an explicit failure before dispatching another model. A selected/currentModel field should not obscure an alternate internal call.

Questions for maintainers
1. Does this event sequence represent a real internal alternate-model dispatch, or incorrect event attribution?
2. Does .github/allowed_models.txt govern every internal fallback call? If not, what supported setting enforces that boundary?
3. Does the official SDK allowedModels restriction cover this same internal path, rather than only session selection?
4. Is there a corrected CLI version or supported configuration? The 1.0.98 release notes do not identify a matching correction.

No further paid reproduction has been run. Please provide a supported correction or clarify event/enforcement semantics before another test.

Official references
https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-config-dir-reference#repository-level-models-allowlist-githuballowed_modelstxt
https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/blob/main/changelog.md
https://github.com/github/copilot-sdk/blob/main/nodejs/src/generated/rpc.ts

issues.title: 1.0.98: Copilot Enterprise account routed to api.business.githubcopilot.com — 401 on model catalog, 'Authentication failed' despite valid token

labels.name: area:authentication
labels.description: Login, OAuth, device auth, token management, and keychain integration

labels.name: area:enterprise
labels.description: GitHub Enterprise (GHE/GHES) support, org policies, and enterprise settings

issues.body:
## Environment

- Copilot CLI 1.0.98 (installed via official `gh.io/copilot-install` script, Linux x64, headless — no system keychain, token stored in plaintext `~/.copilot/config.json`)
- Auth via `copilot login --device-code` on github.com (not a GHEC data-residency tenant, `GH_HOST` unset)
- Account shape: personal account whose GitHub Copilot access is provided by a **GitHub Enterprise Cloud organization with a Copilot Enterprise seat** (org Copilot management page shows "GitHub Copilot Enterprise", seat assigned and listed under "members with access to Copilot")

## Symptom

Every `copilot -p "<prompt>"` invocation fails immediately:

```
Error: Authentication failed (Request ID: ...)

Your GitHub token may be invalid, expired, or lacking the required permissions.
```

CLI log (same run):

```
[ERROR] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed, when Client(OAuthChallenge { status_code: 401 ... })
[WARNING] MCP OAuth authorization failed; reporting the server as needing auth {"server":"github-mcp-server","error":"Browser-based OAuth required for https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/mcp/readonly"}
[ERROR] Error loading models: Error: 401 "Unauthorized"
```

The model-catalog fetch and the built-in `github-mcp-server` both target **`api.business.githubcopilot.com`** for this account.

## The token is valid

The stored token returns `200` on `GET https://api.github.com/user` with the correct account, so "invalid/expired token" is not the cause.

## Host matrix (same token, `GET <host>/models`)

| Host | Result |
|---|---|
| `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` | **401** `Unauthorized` (x-copilot-service-request-id: 717f9174-81b4-4f3d-a2bb-816f5b9e0d0b) |
| `https://api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com/models` | **200** — full model catalog returned |
| `https://api.githubcopilot.com/models` | **200** — full model catalog returned |

So the account is authorized on the enterprise (and generic) Copilot API hosts, but the CLI routes this Copilot **Enterprise**-seat account to the **business** host, where it is rejected with 401. The CLI appears to classify the account as Copilot *Business* rather than *Enterprise* when resolving the Copilot API base (`authGetCopilotApiUrl`).

## Impact

CLI is completely unusable for Copilot Enterprise accounts with a valid seat: the first authenticated call (model catalog) 401s, before any prompt can run. The error message is misleading — it suggests a token problem, but the token is fine; only the target host is wrong.

## Reproduction

1. Have a personal account whose Copilot is provided by a GitHub Enterprise Cloud org with a Copilot Enterprise seat.
2. `copilot login` (device code flow).
3. `copilot -p "hi"` → `Error: Authentication failed`.
4. `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <stored token>" https://api.githubcopilot.com/models` → 200, while the CLI's business host → 401.

## Related

- #4527 — prompt-mode model-catalog fetch hit the wrong host (fixed for GHEC data-residency tenants); same defect class for enterprise-routed accounts.
- #4408 — enterprise-routed accounts resolve the Copilot API base to `api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`; for this account the CLI resolves it to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` instead, and that host 401s.

issues.title: Switching sessions in the Sessions sidebar leaks plugin MCP servers and extension hosts (OOM)

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
## Summary

Switching to sessions not previously opened in the current CLI process through the Sessions sidebar starts additional sets of plugin-provided stdio MCP servers and extension hosts (`extension_bootstrap.mjs`). Earlier sets remain alive under the same CLI process during the observation window. With the installed plugins, each additional set used approximately 500 MB.

This appears related to #4049 (stdio MCP duplication on `/new` and `/resume`) and #4468 (extension-host accumulation in `--server --stdio` mode). This report adds observations from the interactive Sessions sidebar on Linux with CLI 1.0.98, involving both plugin MCP servers and extension hosts.

The findings below are inferred from process lists and CLI logs, not a review of the CLI source. They have not been independently reproduced on a newer version. In particular, retaining background sessions may be intentional; the concern is the observed resource growth and lack of cleanup during ordinary sidebar use.

## Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.98.

Linux 6.12, Cloud Workstation, 7.8 GB RAM, 2 vCPU.

## Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Install a plugin that provides a stdio MCP server, for example `awesome-copilot@awesome-copilot` (`docker run -i --rm ghcr.io/microsoft/mcp-dotnet-samples/awesome-copilot:latest`), and one that provides an extension.
2. Start `copilot`. Open 3-4 new sessions from the Sessions sidebar.
3. Inspect child processes of that CLI process, for example `ps --ppid <copilot-pid> -o pid,lstart,rss,args`, and inspect `docker ps`.
4. Switch back to a session already opened during this CLI run and compare process counts.

**Actual:** additional instances accumulate for each newly opened session. Switching back to an already-opened session reuses its existing extension service instead of starting another set.

## Expected behavior

Session navigation should not cause unbounded accumulation of plugin MCP servers and extension hosts. Share instances where safe, or provide lifecycle cleanup when their owning sessions are disposed of, while preserving intentionally running background work.

## Evidence

Logs from CLI PID 4941. Each `reloading extensions` event correlated with a new process set. Switching back to a previously opened session logged `adopting existing extension service` and did not start a new set:

```text
20:11:50.153Z Session changed (0177f3b9… → b5b66840…), reloading extensions
20:11:51.954Z Installed 2 native extension(s) for session b5b66840…
20:12:01.713Z Session changed (b5b66840… → 0177f3b9…), adopting existing extension service …
20:12:11.488Z Session changed (b5b66840… → db281308…), reloading extensions
20:12:21.374Z Session changed (db281308… → a7090f05…), reloading extensions
20:13:16.781Z Session changed (db281308… → 47311be8…), reloading extensions
```

Children of PID 4941 after 9 session registrations, including 4 newly opened sessions:

| Signature | Instances | Start times |
|---|---|---|
| `npm exec @playwright/mcp@latest --browser msedge` (+ node) | 4 | 20:11:47, 20:12:08, 20:12:18, 20:13:13 |
| `docker run -i --rm …/awesome-copilot:latest` | 4 (4 containers in `docker ps`) | same |
| `extension_bootstrap.mjs` (transcript-workbench, signals-dashboard) | 8 | same |

Stopping the 3 older process sets freed approximately 1.5 GB (used RAM decreased from 5.6 GB to 4.1 GB).

The previous CLI process logged 20 session registrations before the workstation went down under memory exhaustion. These observations suggest that accumulated child-process memory contributed to the failure, but do not establish the CLI's internal ownership or disposal logic.

## Related observations

These may be separate lifecycle/configuration issues:

1. Editing a plugin's `.mcp.json` while the CLI was running started two new server instances while the old instance remained alive.
2. After `copilot plugin uninstall X` was run from another terminal, the running CLI rewrote `~/.copilot/settings.json` at a subsequent session switch and the plugin was reinstalled. This appeared consistent with stale in-memory `enabledPlugins` overriding the on-disk change; the internal cause has not been verified.

## Impact and workaround

On this small development VM, normal sidebar use accumulated enough memory to make the workstation slow and eventually unusable. Fully restarting the CLI clears the accumulated processes.

## Related reports

- #4049: Docker stdio MCP servers duplicated on `/new` and `/resume` (v1.0.68).
- #4468: extension-host accumulation across sessions in `--server --stdio` mode.
- #4892: hourly extension reload/MCP re-enumeration, a different trigger; that report explicitly states that old process generations are reaped.

issues.title: Regression: default-context Sol models rejected before first prompt after tool definitions grow from 15K to ~260K tokens

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Beginning around 2026-10-14, `gpt-5.6-sol` and `gpt-6.1-sol` at the default context tier fail before accepting a prompt:

```
compaction_static_context_blocked: Static system messages and tool definitions exceed the model's usable context budget. Reduce static context or switch to a larger-context model.
```

Selecting `long_context` immediately makes the same model, session, MCP configuration, and prompt work. Usage telemetry then reports `maxPromptTokens: 922000` and approximately 258K-260K tool-definition tokens.

This did not occur previously with the same broad tool configuration. A successful October 9 session on CLI 1.0.92 used `gpt-5.6-sol` with the default tier and reported 615 tools / 15,457 tool-definition tokens. The current configuration reports 676 tools / approximately 260,000 tool-definition tokens: roughly 10% more tools but a 17x increase in tool tokens.

The local standalone MCP configuration was unchanged during this period. A historical default-tier session that worked before the rollout also failed with the same warning when resumed on October 14.

### Affected versions

- GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.93, 1.0.97, and 1.0.98
- macOS 26.7.1, Apple Silicon
- Models: `gpt-5.6-sol` and `gpt-6.1-sol`
- Agency versions observed during the rollout window: 2026.10.13.x and 2026.10.14.3

Because 1.0.93 also began failing after the rollout window, this may involve remotely supplied tool catalogs, Agency integration, or context-budget metadata rather than only a 1.0.97 client change.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start Copilot CLI with a broad enterprise MCP/tool configuration.
2. Select `gpt-6.1-sol` with the default context tier.
3. Submit a short prompt.
4. Observe `compaction_static_context_blocked`, followed by `No response was returned`.
5. Switch only the context tier to `long_context`.
6. Resubmit the prompt; it succeeds.
7. Repeat with `gpt-5.6-sol`; default context fails and `long_context` succeeds.

### Expected behavior

The default tier should continue working with a tool configuration that worked previously. At minimum, the CLI should:

- avoid offering a model/tier combination that cannot fit its own static context;
- lazy-load or defer tool schemas instead of eagerly injecting hundreds of definitions;
- identify the largest static-context contributors;
- clearly report the effective default-tier prompt budget.

### Additional evidence

- October 9, CLI 1.0.92: 615 tools, 15,457 tool tokens, default-tier `gpt-5.6-sol` worked.
- October 14-15: approximately 258K-260K tool tokens; default-tier Sol models fail before a model request.
- `long_context` reports a 922K prompt allowance and succeeds without changing the tool setup.
- Related issues: #5042 and #3542.

Please investigate whether tool schemas or descriptions changed around October 13-14, whether more definitions are now eagerly materialized, or whether static-context token accounting/default-tier reserves changed. I can provide redacted event excerpts or confidential debug logs privately.

issues.title: Skill discovery crashes with ENAMETOOLONG on symlink cycles
issues.body:
## Problem

When a skill discovery directory (e.g. `~/.agents/skills`) resolves to a path inside a source skill collection, `ln -s` creates a self-referential symlink. OpenCode's skill scanner follows it recursively and crashes with `ENAMETOOLONG`.

This happens because `scan()` in `packages/opencode/src/skill/index.ts` passes `symlink: true` to glob (which maps to `follow: true`), and there is no cycle detection or depth limit.

## Reproduction

```bash
# clone a skills repo
git clone git@github.com:example/skills.git && cd skills

# make the discovery dir point into the source collection
ln -s "$PWD/skills" ~/.agents/skills

# create a skill link -- ln follows the directory symlink and
# creates skills/foo/foo pointing at itself
ln -s "$PWD/skills/foo" ~/.agents/skills/foo

# start opencode -- glob follows the cycle until ENAMETOOLONG
opencode
```

## Suggested fix

Any of these would work (in order of simplicity):

1. **Add `maxDepth` to the glob call.** Skill bundles are shallow (`skills/<name>/SKILL.md`), so a depth of 3-4 prevents infinite traversal without changing behavior.
2. **Catch `ENAMETOOLONG` and `ELOOP`** in the `scan` function and skip the path with a warning.
3. **Track visited realpaths** before descending into each directory.

issues.title: server (NixOS): watcher subscribes /nix/store as parent-directory watch for home-manager skill derivations, consuming ~523k inotify watches and causing system-wide ENOSPC
issues.body:
**Related:** #53416 (file watcher restart loop). I'm not certain this is the same bug — it may be a variant that only shows up on NixOS — but it's the same subsystem, and my symptoms are more severe than the restart-loop churn described there. Splitting it off if maintainers agree it has a distinct root cause.

*Correction 2026-10-14: the original root-cause section attributed this to the watcher following `.direnv` symlinks. Further investigation showed the watcher never follows symlinks — it subscribes `/nix/store` directly as a parent-directory watch for home-manager-managed skill derivations. See the comment below for the evidence. The symptoms, numbers and reproduction are unchanged.*

## Summary

On NixOS, a freshly started `opencode serve --service` consumes ~523,000 of my 524,288 inotify watches (`fs.inotify.max_user_watches`) within seconds of starting. With the system-wide per-user budget exhausted, every other file-watching application on the machine fails with `ENOSPC` — which is inotify exhaustion, not disk space.

## Environment

```
Linux framework-13 7.2.9 #1-NixOS SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sat Oct  3 10:43:16 UTC 2026 x86_64 GNU/Linux
NixOS 26.11.20261010.6510408 (Zokor)
opencode v2.0.27 (opencode2 from numtide/llm-agents.nix)
fs.inotify.max_user_watches = 524288
```

My `~/.config/opencode` is managed by home-manager (config in [modules/home/ai/ai-agents.nix](https://github.com/britter/nix-configuration/blob/main/modules/home/ai/ai-agents.nix) of my dotfiles). This matters because of how home-manager deploys config files: it materializes everything under `~/.config` as symlinks into the nix store, e.g.

```
~/.config/opencode/opencode.json -> /nix/store/vk3h8583hi3vd6qfm7m28gyslw17raxg-home-manager-files/.config/opencode/opencode.json
~/.config/opencode/themes/stylix.json -> /nix/store/f948xrwrc111fvkygc8dwbv8hhrgk9xs-opencode-stylix.json
```

## What happens

A freshly started `opencode serve --service` accumulates ~523,226 inotify watches on a single inotify fd within seconds of starting (measured via `/proc/<pid>/fdinfo/<fd>`). Effects:

- `nh switch` (nixos-rebuild wrapper) fails with `nom: addWatch: resource exhausted (No space left on device)`
- new opencode TUI instances crash at startup: `Error: ENOSPC: no space left on device, watch '~/.config/opencode'`
- opencode's own log records the starvation:

```
level=ERROR message="location watcher subscription failed" path=/home/bene/github/britter/nix-configuration/.git/HEAD
cause="... Error: ENOSPC: no space left on device, watch '/home/bene/github/britter/nix-configuration/.git'"
```

Killing the service fixes everything; the next instance consumes the budget again immediately. Fully reproducible. Note the effect is system-wide: unrelated applications (`nom`, other TUIs) are the visible victims.

## Root cause

The skill directories resolve to their real locations, which on home-manager-managed NixOS are **top-level store entries**: `/nix/store/<hash>-hm_expert`, `/nix/store/<hash>-hm_tutor`, etc. The service log shows the watcher subscribes each resolved skill directory, then immediately subscribes `/nix/store` itself:

```
watcher subscribe path=/nix/store/0dj3vjkvs055qlfibpi4x416hghp7g1g-hm_expert type=directory
watcher subscribe path=/nix/store/zda04fwpaa5kk36dykj6cl9qfaf3kx24-hm_expert type=directory
... (7 skill directories total)
watcher subscribe path=/nix/store type=directory
```

The `/nix/store` subscription looks like a parent-directory watch — watching the parent of a resolved directory so that its replacement or deletion is noticed, which is exactly what happens on `home-manager switch`. On NixOS, the parent of a top-level derivation is the store root itself, so this parent watch becomes a recursive watch over 1,416,513 directories (`find /nix/store -type d | wc -l`). That exceeds the 524,288 watch budget, so the watcher stops only when the kernel refuses.

On a normal filesystem the same logic resolves to `~/.config/opencode/skills/` — a few dozen entries — which is why this doesn't reproduce elsewhere.

## Reproduction

1. NixOS with home-manager managing `~/.config/opencode` (skills resolving to top-level store derivations)
2. `opencode serve --service`
3. `grep -c '^inotify wd' /proc/$(pgrep -f 'serve --service')/fdinfo/*` reaches ~523k within seconds
4. Other applications' file watchers fail with ENOSPC

## Workaround

`OPENCODE_DISABLE_FILEWATCHER=true` in the service environment stops it (see also #53417 for the confusion around this variable). Cost: no config hot-reload, which is acceptable under home-manager since config changes arrive via `home-manager switch` and sessions get restarted anyway.

## Expected behavior

The watcher should not recursively expand parent-directory watches over trees with enormous entry counts, and should degrade gracefully on ENOSPC instead of starving every other file-watching process on the system. Candidates: skip the parent watch when the resolved path is already a top-level entry of a huge tree, refuse roots above some size threshold, or cap recursive expansion.
