prs.title: fix(console): redirect /en URLs to the unprefixed English pages
prs.body:
### Why

`opencode.ai/en`, `/en/zen`, `/en/go` and every other `/en/...` URL return 200 with the English page, so the whole English site exists twice. The pages declare the unprefixed URL as canonical and as `hreflang="en"`, so `/en/...` is a duplicate that only collects stray links and crawl budget.

### What Changes

| Request | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /en` | 200, English homepage | 301 → `/` |
| `GET /en/zen` | 200 | 301 → `/zen` |
| `GET /en/go?x=1` | 200 | 301 → `/go?x=1` |
| `/de/zen`, `/zen` | 200 | 200 (unchanged) |
| `/en/data/...` | English stats | unchanged |

Only `GET` and `HEAD` redirect. Other methods keep the existing locale rewrite. `/data` keeps `/en` because unprefixed `/data` redirects by cookie and `Accept-Language`, so `/en/data` is the only way to pin English there. Leading slashes are collapsed, so `/en//example.com` redirects to `/example.com` rather than off-site.

### Verification

```sh
cd packages/console/app && bun run typecheck
bunx vite dev --port 5199
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{redirect_url}\n" http://[::1]:5199/en/zen
```

On the local dev server, the `/en` paths above return 301 to their unprefixed URLs with the query string kept, and `/de/zen` and `/zen` still return 200. `/en//evil.com` returns 301 → `/evil.com`. With `Accept-Language: de`, `/en/data` reaches the stats proxy instead of redirecting.

prs.title: fix(console): make the mobile menu and copy buttons keyboard accessible
prs.body:
### Why

Keyboard and screen-reader users hit several dead ends on the marketing pages:

- The mobile menu button always reports `aria-expanded="false"`, and Escape doesn't close the menu.
- The install command buttons on `/`, the newsletter button, the mobile menu button and the download rows on `/download` set `outline: none` with no replacement, so focus is invisible.
- On `/brand` (desktop), the PNG/SVG download buttons only appear on mouse hover, so tabbing focuses invisible buttons.
- On `/download`, the copy icon only appears on hover.

### What Changes

| Control | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mobile menu button | `aria-expanded="false"` always | follows the menu state |
| Open mobile menu | Escape does nothing | Escape closes it and focuses the menu button |
| Install commands, newsletter button, menu button, `/download` rows, `/brand` buttons | no focus indicator | 2px focus ring on `:focus-visible` |
| `/brand` asset actions | visible on hover only | also visible while a button inside has focus |
| `/download` copy icon | visible on hover only | also visible on keyboard focus |

The focus rings live in a shared `style/component/focus.css`. They use `!important` because each page resets `outline` with more specific selectors.

### Scope

Mouse and touch behavior is unchanged. Long install commands are still truncated with an ellipsis on narrow screens. Clicking copies the full command, and making them scroll inside a button is a separate design call.

### Verification

```sh
cd packages/console/app && bun run typecheck
bunx vite dev --port 5199
```

In a browser on the local dev server: the menu button reports `aria-expanded` `false` → `true` after a click → `false` after Escape, which also removes the menu, with no console errors. With focus on a menu link, Escape moves focus back to the menu button.

prs.title: perf(console): load only the IBM Plex Mono faces the site uses
prs.body:
### Why

Every marketing page loads `@ibm/plex/css/ibm-plex.css`, the stylesheet for the whole Plex family: Sans, Serif, Condensed, Arabic, Thai, Hebrew, Devanagari, JP, KR and Mono. That is 424 `@font-face` rules in a 181 KB render-blocking stylesheet. The site uses only IBM Plex Mono (`--font-sans` is `var(--font-mono)`, and no other Plex family is referenced).

### What Changes

`app.tsx` imports the split IBM Plex Mono stylesheets for the weights the CSS actually uses, instead of the full family file:

| CSS weight used | Face loaded |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | Regular |
| 440 | Text (450) |
| 500 | Medium |
| 530, 600 | SemiBold |
| 650, 700, `bold` | Bold |
| `italic` (black fine print) | Italic |

| Build output | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entry-client-*.css` | 181 KB, 424 `@font-face` | 22 KB, 30 `@font-face` |

The split files cover Latin 1–3, Cyrillic and Pi. Compared with the complete font they lack 36 rarely used code points (combining diacritics, a few modifier letters, and the dashes ‐ ‑ ‒ ―), which now render in the fallback monospace font. Scripts that Plex Mono never covered (Arabic, Thai, CJK) still fall back to system fonts.

### Verification

```sh
cd packages/console/app && bun run typecheck && bunx vite build
grep -o "@font-face" .output/public/_build/assets/entry-client-*.css | wc -l
```

The build passes, and the client CSS has 30 faces whose `url()`s point to emitted `IBMPlexMono-*.woff2` assets.

prs.title: fix(app): focus the composer when switching session tabs
prs.body:
## Why

Switching to another session tab leaves the destination session's composer unfocused. While typing plain characters still routes to the composer through the document keydown fallback, there is no caret and `⌘V` (`Ctrl+V`) does nothing until you click into the composer first. This happens when clicking a vertical sidebar tab, clicking a horizontal titlebar tab, or cycling session tabs with the keyboard.

## What Changes

**Before:** switch to another session tab (vertical sidebar tab, horizontal titlebar tab, or keyboard shortcut) -> the clicked `[data-titlebar-tab-link]` or `document.body` holds focus -> pressing `⌘V` does not paste into the destination composer.

**After:** switch to another session tab -> once the active session composer's draft state is ready, the editor is focused on the next animation frame with its saved caret position restored -> pressing `⌘V` immediately pastes into the destination composer.

- `createSessionComposerController` runs a one-shot effect when `adapter.ready` becomes true, focusing the connected composer editor and restoring `adapter.state.cursor()` (or the end of the draft) on the next animation frame.
- Focus is only claimed when `document.activeElement` is `document.body`, the editor itself, or a `[data-titlebar-tab-link]` (used by both horizontal titlebar tabs and vertical sidebar tabs). It does not steal focus when the composer is hidden, a child session view is shown, a dialog (including the `⌘K` command palette) is open, an inline tab title rename (`[data-slot="tab-title"][contenteditable="true"]`) is active, or another control (such as a terminal, browser, or review pane) already owns focus.

## Demo

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01d7cc2d-73e3-466b-9317-d8ab482d3dc1

Left: `beta` (`BEFORE`). Right: this branch (`AFTER`). Recorded against the e2e mock server with vertical sidebar tabs (`tabLayout: "vertical"`):
1. Click `Session Beta` in the vertical sidebar, then press `⌘V` (`"bun run test:e2e"`): on `beta`, focus stays on the sidebar tab link with no caret and `⌘V` does nothing; on this branch, the composer immediately receives focus with a caret and pastes `"bun run test:e2e"`.
2. Switch back to `Session Alpha` (`⌥↑`), then press `⌘V` (`" ready to ship"`): on `beta`, `"Notes for Alpha:"` has no caret and `⌘V` does nothing; on this branch, the caret is restored at the end of `"Notes for Alpha:"` and `⌘V` appends `" ready to ship"`.

<details>
<summary>Side-by-side stills after clicking the sidebar tab and pressing ⌘V</summary>

**After clicking `Session Beta` in the vertical sidebar:**

![After clicking Session Beta in sidebar](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/462e17c1-9152-4437-8e19-cbafbd8ee300)

**After pressing `⌘V` (`"bun run test:e2e"`) in `Session Beta`:**

![After pressing ⌘V in Session Beta](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1db846ef-886e-4f77-bce0-837c4d7d087d)

</details>

## Scope

This PR only restores composer focus and caret position when an active session composer becomes ready after session activation. New-session draft tabs already call `restoreFocus()` on `composer.ready` in `NewSessionPage`.

## Verification

```sh
cd packages/app
bun typecheck
PLAYWRIGHT_PORT=4319 bun run test:e2e:built -- e2e/regression/tabs.spec.ts -g "switching session tabs restores the caret|a tab does not reopen its title editor"
PLAYWRIGHT_PORT=4319 bun run test:e2e:built -- e2e/regression/tabs.spec.ts -g "switching session tabs restores the caret" --repeat-each=5 --workers=3 --retries=0
PLAYWRIGHT_PORT=3217 bun run test:e2e -- e2e/regression/session-summary.spec.ts -g "summary toggle" --workers=1
cd ../.. && bun run lint:changed origin/beta
```

- `switching session tabs restores the caret and pastes into the destination draft` covers `horizontal` titlebar tab clicks, `vertical` sidebar tab clicks, and `keyboard` tab switching, verifying both immediate paste into an empty destination session and caret-position restoration when pasting into an existing draft. All 3 cases fail on `origin/beta` (`expect(editor).toBeFocused()` times out with `inactive`) and pass 15/15 across 5x repeat runs on this branch.
- `a tab does not reopen its title editor while a rename is saving` double-clicks an inactive tab to both switch sessions and open the inline title editor, confirming the composer focus effect does not steal focus from tab renaming.
- `summary toggle custom shortcut follows the active session` in `session-summary.spec.ts` uses `alt+f8` (a modified keybind, since `details.toggle` does not set `Command.editable` and switching tabs now focuses the composer text field rather than leaving focus on the tab link).
- `bun typecheck` and `bun run lint:changed origin/beta` pass with 0 problems.

prs.title: docs(plugin): fix Session interrupt field in example (continue -> resume)
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #56574

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [x] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The Sessions example in the V2 plugin docs calls `ctx.session.interrupt` with `continue`, but the field is `resume`. `continue` is not part of `SessionInterruptInput` and is silently ignored at runtime, so copying the example and writing `continue: true` gives no error and a no-op.

This changes one line in `services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/index.mdx`:

```diff
-await ctx.session.interrupt({ sessionID, continue: false })
+await ctx.session.interrupt({ sessionID, resume: false })
```

`SessionInterruptInput` in `@opencode/client` is `{ sessionID; resume?: boolean }`, and the OpenAPI spec for `POST /api/session/{sessionID}/interrupt` defines a `resume` query parameter. There is no `continue` field in the contract.

### How did you verify your code works?

Applied the patch to a fresh clone of `dev` and confirmed `git apply --check` passes. Compared the corrected line with `SessionInterruptInput` in `packages/client/src/effect/api/api.ts`, the generated client's `query: { resume: input["resume"] }`, and the `resume` query parameter in `packages/protocol/openapi.json`. I did not run the docs site build.

Not a UI change.

prs.title: fix(console): take the page language from the URL only
prs.body:
### Why

opencode.ai picks the language of an unprefixed page from the `oc_locale` cookie or the browser's `Accept-Language`. A German browser asking for `https://opencode.ai/` gets the German homepage, with `<html lang="de">` and `<link rel="canonical" href="https://opencode.ai/de">`, and the response has no `Vary` header. One URL serves different languages to different visitors, so shared links, link unfurlers and caches can show the wrong language, and the page tells search engines it's a copy of `/de`. The v1 `/docs/*` proxy does the same and sets a one-year `oc_locale` cookie on every docs visit.

### What Changes

Pages take their language from the URL alone.

| Request (German browser, `oc_locale=de`) | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/` | German, canonical `/de` | English, canonical `/` |
| `/zen` | German, canonical `/de/zen` | English, canonical `/zen` |
| `/de`, `/de/zen` | German | German (unchanged) |
| `/docs/agents/` | German v1 docs, sets `oc_locale` | English v1 docs, no cookie |
| `/docs/de/agents/` | German v1 docs | German v1 docs (unchanged) |

The language picker still works: it links to the localized URL (`/de/...`).

### Scope

Only page rendering and the v1 docs proxy change, through a new `pageLocale()` helper. Requests without a locale in the URL keep the cookie and `Accept-Language` fallback (`localeFromRequest`): the enterprise form API's messages, share pages and `/t`. `/data` keeps its separate 308 redirect to the visitor's locale. That's a redirect rather than different content at one URL, so it's less of a problem.

### Verification

```sh
cd packages/console/app && bun run typecheck && bun test test/language.test.ts
bunx vite dev --port 5199
curl -s -H 'accept-language: de-DE,de;q=0.9' -H 'cookie: oc_locale=de' http://[::1]:5199/ | grep -o '<html lang="[^"]*"\|rel="canonical" href="[^"]*"'
```

With a German `Accept-Language` and `oc_locale=de` on the local dev server, `/` and `/zen` render `lang="en"` with their own canonical URLs, and `/de` and `/de/zen` render `lang="de"`.

`opencode.ai/sitemap.xml` lists 594 v1 docs URLs and no v2 docs, even though the header now links to the v2 docs. ### What Changes

**Console sitemap** (`packages/console/app`)

- Adds `/download` and both legal pages for each locale, plus `/changelog` once.
- v1 docs URLs end with `/` to match their canonicals, and duplicate URLs are dropped.
- `uk` now maps to the English v1 docs, so Ukrainian visitors following a docs link no longer hit `/docs/uk/…` 404s, and the sitemap stops listing those URLs.
- `robots.txt` advertises `https://opencode.ai/v2/sitemap.xml`.

**v2 docs** (`services/www`)

prs.title: test(app): fix races in the mobile timeline scroll e2e tests
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No issue. Follow-up to #55866: the remaining flaky e2e tests, in `mobile-timeline-scroll.spec.ts`, from a census of recent `test` runs.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Fixes the remaining flaky tests in `packages/app/e2e/regression/mobile-timeline-scroll.spec.ts`. Each was a test-side race; none is a product bug. No timeout, retry or assertion changed.

| Test | Where it flaked | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| :79 keeps the reading anchor when 2 earlier images load (both devices) | Linux, ~5-6% of jobs | Release fling | Stamp the drag 100 ms early |
| :639 returns Home after scrolling the touch target out of view (touchEnd) | Linux, 3 in the census | Release fling | Stamp the drag 100 ms early |
| :227 nested output owns the gesture or chains at its boundary (500) | Linux, ~35% of sharded jobs; Windows rarely | Control+Home dropped at the end of Control+End's animation | Wait for `scrollend` at the end |
| :153 reaches the start without a gap or release jump | Windows, 7-17% | Screencast frames arrive out of order | Sort frames by capture timestamp |

#### Root causes

**Release fling (:79, :639 touchEnd).**
- The drags sent unstamped `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` calls, so CDP stamped each event when it arrived.
- Chromium's velocity tracker (ui/events/velocity_tracker) flings when two things hold:
  - the last two moves are less than 40 ms apart;
  - the touchEnd comes less than 80 ms after the last move.
- When the check before the release passed on its first try, both held, and the drag carried momentum:
  - **:79:** the anchor ended 108-717 px past 704.
  - **:639:** without a fling, the delayed image's row ends 5 px above the viewport. A fling moves the viewport ~158 px further toward the start, which brings that row into view. Its 300 px growth then correctly pushes the anchor down, by exactly the +300 px seen in CI. Every census failure of this test was a touchEnd variant; touchCancel never flings.
- Both drags now stamp touchStart and touchMoves 100 ms early (`restingTimestamp()`) and stamp the release from the same clock, so the release always lands at least 100 ms after the last move, and no fling starts.

**Dropped Control+Home (:227 (500)).**
- Control+End on the nested output is a native 150 ms compositor keyboard scroll. It reaches its end offset about one frame before it finishes.
- Chromium drops a keyboard scroll that arrives in that gap: the retargeted animation is reset when the old one's finish notice arrives.
- The old poll checked only the offset, so it could press Control+Home inside the gap, and `scrollTop` stayed at 2229.
- The test now registers a `scrollend` listener that marks the scroller once a scroll ends at its bottom. It waits for that mark before pressing Control+Home.

**Out-of-order screencast frames (:153).**
- Chromium stamps each screencast frame at capture. It then JPEG-encodes up to three frames at once on unsequenced thread-pool tasks and emits each frame when its encode finishes.
- On Windows runners, a slow encode arrived after newer frames. In the painted-motion check that read as `reversed` or `missing`.
- `capturePromptMotion` now orders frames by `metadata.timestamp` before reading motion.

### How did you verify your code works?

All runs were on macOS in built mode, chromium-touch-scroll project, `--workers=5 --retries=0` unless noted. The before/after probes add `--disable-blink-features=MacDisableCtrlHomeEnd`, because macOS ignores Ctrl+Home/End.

**Forced CI timing, before vs after the fix:**

| Test | Forced timing | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| :79 | Back-to-back release | 10/10 failed (Received 687-1558) | 0/10 |
| :639 touchEnd | Immediate release | 4/16 failed; all 4 natural flings in 32 runs landed here and failed | 0/16, no flings |
| :227 (500) | Control+Home in the frame Control+End reaches its end | 19/20 failed with Received 2229 | 0/20 |
| :153 | Every 5th frame delivered 2 frames late | 10/10 failed | 0/10 |

**Whole file, with the fix:**
- 222/222 passed with `--repeat-each=6`.
- The changed tests passed 140/140 at `--workers=10 --repeat-each=10`, load ~19.

**Checks:**
- `bun run lint:changed`: clean.
- `bun typecheck` in packages/app: passes.
- `typecheck:e2e`: only the 4 known errors.

## Notes

- **:153 cannot be reproduced on macOS.** The frame reorder only shows on Windows CI, so it was validated by injecting late frames.
- **macOS-only overscroll on :153.** Under heavy local load, :153 can fail from elastic-overscroll spring-back (116 → 110). Windows CI frames never go past 110.
- **:431 (held) is not touched.** Its Windows flakes were navigation and mount stalls from before the Bun static server.

### Screenshots / recordings

N/A

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix: preserve WebSocket bursts while consumers are paused
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #49523

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A paused consumer receiving a burst of small WebSocket deltas fails at the 129th frame. A localhost regression reproduces this in the socket adapter; fixing that layer alone still overflows the session queue.

The socket adapter now admits bursts within a 64 MiB ingress accounting budget and a 4,096-frame ceiling, preserving the 16 MiB individual-frame guard. The async session reader waits for its consumer instead of failing a second queue. Both streams take one frame at a time: Effect's batched queue drain would otherwise release byte accounting early and hide frames after a terminal event.

Actual overload remains a typed error and closes the connection. Cancellation and post-terminal data still poison it; no silent drops or automatic retries. The ingress budget is not a total process-memory bound.

### How did you verify your code works?

On macOS arm64 with the repository's Bun 1.4.2:

- Full AI suite: 1,404 passed, 28 skipped.
- Core transport, real WebSocket, checkpoint and session-runner suites: 254 passed.
- Both affected package typechecks, repository-wide lint, changed-file formatting and diff checks passed.
- New tests cover a paused 1,024-frame localhost burst and connection reuse, byte/count overload, budget reclamation, exact/oversized frame limits, cancellation and trailing data after completion.

Full `bun run check` reaches unrelated workspace typechecks but cannot finish with this filtered dependency installation (`@tsconfig/node22` missing in console-core). No manifest or lockfile changes. CI is still needed for the full workspace/platform matrix.

AI-assisted implementation and independent review.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not applicable; transport behavior only.

issues.title: Stale lock dirs from crashed processes break all future startups with EEXIST (auth/settings/models-store), surfacing as invalid_state for every provider

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Summary

When a `pi` process dies without releasing its locks (crash, SIGKILL, sandboxed fs interference), the `proper-lockfile` lock directories it leaves behind (`settings.json.lock`, `auth.json.lock`, `models-store.json.lock` in the agent dir) break **every subsequent pi startup** with `EEXIST`, until they are removed by hand.

The failure is unusually confusing because:

- `pi auth check --provider X` reports `{"status": "invalid", "reason": "invalid_state"}` for **all** providers — including ones with valid env API keys that never touch `auth.json`.
- A real `pi --print` run prints `Credential store read failed for kimi-coding: EEXIST: file already exists, mkdir '.../auth.json.lock'` and fails.
- One failed startup leaks the other lock dirs too, so the fault spreads: cleaning only the dir named in the error is not enough.

## Root cause

`getRetryableLockErrorCode()` in both `dist/core/auth-storage.js` and `dist/core/settings-manager.js` (1.3.0) only retries `ELOCKED`:

```js
function getRetryableLockErrorCode(error) {
    const code = error instanceof Error && "code" in error ? error.code : undefined;
    if (code === "ELOCKED")
        return code;
    if (code === "EPERM" && process.platform === "win32")
        return code;
    return undefined;
}
```

`lockfile.lockSync(path, { realpath: false })` throws `EEXIST` when the lock dir already exists. A stale dir left by a dead process is indistinguishable from a live lock at `mkdir` time, so the error propagates, settings/credential loading fails, and `modelRuntime.getError()` being non-empty turns any later auth check into `invalid_state`.

Related but different: #8928 (long OAuth refresh while holding the lock — parallel startup), #9448 (auth check cannot see extension providers — also surfaces as `invalid_state`, different cause). This one is about **stale lock dirs after unclean exit never being recoverable without manual rmdir**.

## Minimal reproduction

Deterministic, no crash needed — just create the lock dir a dead process would leave:

```sh
export PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=/tmp/pi-issue-repro/agent
mkdir -p /tmp/pi-issue-repro/agent
export KIMI_API_KEY=sk-...   # any api-key provider works

# A. baseline
$ pi auth check --provider kimi-coding --json
{"status":"ready","provider":"kimi-coding","authType":"api_key"}

# B. simulate a stale lock dir
$ mkdir -p $PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/auth.json.lock
$ pi auth check --provider kimi-coding --json
{"status":"invalid","provider":"kimi-coding","reason":"invalid_state"}

$ pi -p --provider kimi-coding --model k3 "hi" 2>&1 | head -1
Credential store read failed for kimi-coding: EEXIST: file already exists, mkdir '/tmp/pi-issue-repro/agent/auth.json.lock'

# note: this failed run ALSO leaves settings.json.lock / models-store.json.lock behind

# C. full manual cleanup restores everything
$ rm -rf $PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/*.json.lock
$ pi auth check --provider kimi-coding --json
{"status":"ready","provider":"kimi-coding","authType":"api_key"}
```

Verified with pi 1.3.0 (npm `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`), macOS 27.0.1 arm64.

## Impact for fleet use

Anything that spawns pi programmatically (Orca-style orchestrators, CI, wrappers) hits this regularly: a killed/slow-shutdown pi bricks the next runs, and the misleading `invalid_state` points investigation at providers instead of locks. This makes pi hard to use as a subprocess fleet.

## Suggested fixes (any of)

1. On `EEXIST`, verify liveness of the existing lock instead of failing: `proper-lockfile` lock dirs contain a `owner.<pid>` concept on some platforms; treat a lock whose owner process is gone as stale, remove and retry.
2. At startup, sweep `*.json.lock` dirs older than some threshold (e.g. mtime > 1h) before acquiring.
3. At minimum, retry/treat `EEXIST` as retryable in `getRetryableLockErrorCode` — after the standard lock timeout a stale dir would be reclaimed.
4. Improve the error surface: when settings/credential loading fails, `pi auth check` should report the underlying EEXIST rather than a generic `invalid_state` for every provider.

Happy to turn the repro into a PR with a regression test if the maintainers prefer option 1 or 3.

## Environment

- pi 1.3.0 (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`)
- macOS 27.0.1, arm64
- installed via pi's own installer (`~/.local/bin/pi` -> `~/.pi/agent/bin/pi`)

issues.title: Scale unset compaction token defaults with the model's context window

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Compaction's built-in defaults are fixed token values: `reserveTokens: 16384`, `keepRecentTokens: 20000` (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/settings-defaults.ts`). I'd like unset defaults to scale with the model's context window: reserve becomes `max(16384, min(floor(window × 0.10), 100000))`, keepRecent becomes `max(20000, floor(window × 0.10))`. Explicitly configured values (including `modelOverrides`) are used verbatim, per field, at any window size.

### Why?

Since #11036, `reserveTokens` only decides when compaction starts, so the fixed value is now purely a trigger headroom — and on large windows it's badly undersized:

- 1M window: compaction triggers at 98.4%, leaving 16K of headroom. One large tool result or an estimate error hits the provider overflow first, costing a failed request plus compact-and-retry.
- After compaction, only 2% of the window is kept as raw recent messages (20K of 1M). File paths, error messages, and intermediate decisions all depend on summary quality.

For comparison, DeepAgents keeps 10% of the window and triggers at 85%; Hermes keeps 20% of its threshold. The 10% ratio I'm proposing is not a new number — it's exactly what the current defaults already mean on a 200K model (20000/200000), so nothing changes on today's common windows (trigger unchanged up to 163,840; tail unchanged up to 200,000).

### How? (optional)

A small pure `resolveCompactionSettings(settings, contextWindow)` in `compaction.ts`, called at the settings-manager getter exit so all consumers (including virtual-model routing, where the routed physical model's window must drive the scaling) see resolved values. **I'd like to implement this myself** — I have it done with tests on a local branch and will open a PR once approved.

---

This issue text was drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code) and reviewed by me.

issues.title: Tool preview text inherits terminal foreground and becomes unreadable on light cards

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

Tool previews become almost unreadable when Pi's theme differs from the terminal's default foreground. With `light` on a dark terminal, the card is pale green but ordinary body text stays pale. The `write` title, path and collapse hint remain readable; the content is what disappears. This affected a Markdown plan in my screenshot, not just a custom subagent renderer.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a dark terminal with a light default foreground; start `pi -ne --use-theme light`.
2. Ask it to write `/tmp/contrast.ts` containing `plainIdentifier` and `const answer = 42;` on separate lines. Inspect the preview. A resumed display-only tool-call fixture reproduces it too, without executing a tool or calling a provider.
3. `plainIdentifier` has no foreground SGR, while the card has `48;2;222;233;225m`. The keyword/number have explicit syntax colors. The uncolored identifier therefore inherits the terminal's foreground.

Verified in an isolated PTY with `-ne`. Also traced the shared highlighter: `buildCliHighlightTheme()` has no `default` formatter, and `renderHighlightedHtml()` emits uncolored text unchanged. `write` and `read` use those highlighted lines without a base foreground.

### Expected behavior

Uncolored preview text should use Pi's current theme foreground, while retaining syntax colors, including after SGR resets. It should not depend on the terminal default foreground matching the card background. I'm implementing a local renderer extension workaround; an upstream fix should cover the shared highlighter.

### Version

Pi 1.0.4, macOS. Screenshot paths and private document content omitted; the minimal text above replaces them.

issues.title: High CPU usage on Mac OS with long session

issues.body:
### What happened?

On Mac OS, when running Pi, I can experience very high cpu usage, 100% and more; it appears to swing between 50-110%, while memory usage is at 600-800MB.

Anecdotally this appears linked to the context size (or perhaps rather the length of the session; I haven't tested with a large context but only a few turns). When I run multiple sessions, it is clearly the larger one that hits 100% cpu and not the others; cpu usage does seem to grow with the size of the session. 

But the weird thing is that the cpu usage is in the hot rendering path, so not in the actual processing of requests or responses from the llm (where I assume a longer context would take more time to process). So the problem is that the tui appears to use more cpu as the session gets longer, and I would expect this to be stable since at any time only a given portion of the session is on screen. 

An overview of sampling findings from the AI is available [here](https://gist.github.com/gterzian/3473a87df286d9c22c0872e61a2d1255)

I had the AI itself try to patch it, with some limited success, overview of what was tried and what the results were is [here](https://gist.github.com/gterzian/dbead50582b6f3bab546a23ef4bb76da )

### Steps to reproduce

Run Pi on Mac OS, and notice how the longer the session gets, the more CPU and memory is used. I get 100% on a long session with a 700k context. 

Here is the breakdown of the session in which the problem was noticed:

Stable CPU usage on the rendering path.

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Preserve provider/model identity with auxiliary usage in native Pi sessions: model-tool calls, compaction and branch summaries. A small per-call usage record would let extensions export accurate per-model totals.

### Why?

We export recorded token usage from Kintsugi to Graphite. In `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.2.0, assistant messages and `UsageEntry` identify the model, but `CompactionEntry` and `BranchSummaryEntry` can store usage without that identity.

Code mode also combines classifier/image usage into one tool result. Its call rows retain model names and costs, but not per-call token counts. If a script uses two models, we cannot split those counts accurately or assign them to the parent model. These shapes are also present on current main.

### How? (optional)

Expose or persist model-attributed usage for each physical call, with a stable invocation ID so an exporter can avoid counting both the call and its roll-up. The exporter can remain an extension; no Graphite support is needed in core.

Related: #9773 concerns missing compaction request hooks; this request is about recorded usage attribution.

labels.name: last-read
labels.description: A marker label for triaging

issues.body:
Compaction file lists grow without bound, and split-turn compaction copies them again each time.

Checked on main 898ab80:

1. `extractFileOperations()` (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/compaction.ts:59-87`) seeds every compaction with the previous compaction's full `details.readFiles`/`modifiedFiles`. Nothing is ever removed. `compact()` (line 1079) appends the merged lists to the summary. Each compaction therefore carries the lists of every earlier one.
2. With a split turn and no earlier user-message span, `compact()` uses `previousSummary` verbatim as the history text (line 1017). That previous summary already ends with the `<read-files>`/`<modified-files>` blocks, and the new merged blocks are appended again. Otherwise the old blocks are also sent to the summarizer inside `<previous-summary>`.

Effect in real long-running sessions: one compaction summary was 528K chars, of which 510K were file paths and 18K were prose. With a 150K-token threshold, the session compacted 13 times in 15 minutes because the summary itself nearly filled the budget.

Repro: compact repeatedly, reading or editing different files between compactions. The summary grows by the full list each time. Split-turn compactions duplicate the list blocks.

Suggested fix: strip the generated file-list blocks from `previousSummary` (they are carried in `details`) and cap each merged list at the N most recently touched paths. Existing oversized sessions then shrink on their next compaction. I have a small patch with a repeated-compaction regression test and can open a PR if you want it.

This issue is AI-generated by `pi-ordinary-supplier` for Smarty Pants.

issues.title: Provider request errors drop error.cause: the session log says only "Connection error."

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Summary

When a request fails at the connection layer, the `AssistantMessage` written to the session file carries `errorMessage: "Connection error."` — the `openai` SDK's generic `APIConnectionError.message`. The actual reason (`error.cause`: `ECONNREFUSED`, `ECONNRESET`, `ENOTFOUND`, socket hang up) is nowhere in the log, so a session log cannot be used to diagnose a dead or unreachable provider after the fact.

pi already states the fix for this exact problem in another place. `ModelsError` wraps its message with `withCauseDetail()`, whose comment reads: *"Callers surface `error.message` only, so keep the underlying reason in it"* (`utils/models-error.ts`, using `formatThrownValue` from `utils/diagnostics.ts`). The provider request path never applies it.

## Where

`normalizeProviderError` (`utils/error-body.ts`) returns `{ status, body, message }`, and each adapter composes a display string with `formatProviderError`. For a connection-level failure there is **no status and no body**, so the composed string is just `error.message` — `"Connection error."` — and `error.cause` is never read.

In the 1.3.0 build, `api/openai-completions.ts`:

```ts
output.stopReason = options?.signal?.aborted ? "aborted" : "error";
output.errorMessage = formatProviderError(normalizeProviderError(error));
```

## What it looked like

A local llama.cpp endpoint (`http://192.168.1.68:8080/v1`) was restarted while a long-lived pi session was idle. Twelve consecutive requests in that session recorded this:

```json
{
  "role": "assistant",
  "usage": { "input": 0, "output": 0, "cacheRead": 0, "cacheWrite": 0, "totalTokens": 0 },
  "stopReason": "error",
  "errorMessage": "Connection error.",
  "durationMs": 4
}
```

`durationMs: 4` is shorter than one LAN round trip (RTT 12–14 ms; a trivial completion against that endpoint takes ~600 ms), so the requests never reached the network. Nothing in the log says whether that was `ECONNREFUSED`, `ECONNRESET`, a poisoned keep-alive socket in the 13-hour-old process, or the endpoint being down — and a second session started at the same moment on the same provider and model worked fine, which is only explainable with the errno in hand. Switching models mid-session did not help, and the log gives no way to tell "the server is down" from "this process's HTTP client is broken".

## Ask

Small: when `normalizeProviderError` finds no status and no body, carry the cause the way `withCauseDetail` already does — `formatThrownValue(error.cause)` — so the session log reads:

```
Connection error.: connect ECONNREFUSED 192.168.1.68:8080
```

Doing it inside `normalizeProviderError`/`formatProviderError` fixes every adapter that goes through them at once, rather than one per provider.

Related but distinct: #7234 (keep HTTP status / error kind on the errored `AssistantMessage`) and #10941 (Node errno forms in retry classification). This is the third gap: for a connection failure there is no status at all, and the errno only exists on `error.cause`.

issues.title: Startup crashes with a raw stack trace when a configured npm package fails to install

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

If a package in `settings.json` fails to install at startup, pi dies with an uncaught rejection and a raw Node stack. No `crashes.json` is written. It happens with `pi -p`, `pi --list-models`, `pi --help` and `pi -ne`. `pi install <bad pkg>` prints one error line and exits, so only the startup path is affected.

Output:

```
npm error code E404
Error: npm install @example/definitely-not-a-real-pkg-xyz --prefix /tmp/p/agent/npm --legacy-peer-deps failed with code 1
Node.js v25.8.2
```

Exit code 1. A real case is an `npm:owner/repo` entry. npm reads it as a GitHub dependency, so with no network (or a failing prepare step) pi won't start until the entry is removed by hand. `pi list` and `pi remove` still work.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `mkdir -p /tmp/p/agent`
2. `echo '{"packages":["npm:@example/definitely-not-a-real-pkg-xyz"]}' > /tmp/p/agent/settings.json`
3. `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=/tmp/p/agent pi -p hello` (`PI_OFFLINE` must be unset)

### Expected behavior

Warn about the package that failed and start without it. At minimum print one clean error line that points to `pi remove`.

Cause: `resolvePackageSources` awaits `installMissing()` with no try/catch, and `runCommand` rejects on a non-zero exit. The `uncaughtException` handler that writes `crashes.json` is only registered in `InteractiveMode.init()`, after the runtime is built. I can send a PR if you want one.

### Version

1.1.0 and 1.3.0. Same code on main (c268154c).

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
## What do you want to change?

Add a `supportsContentArray` compat flag to `openai-completions`. When it is `false`, text-only user messages are sent as a plain string instead of a content-parts array.

## Why?

I'm using pi against IFM (`https://api.ifm.ai/v1`), which validates `messages[].content` more strictly than the OpenAI Chat Completions API. It rejects the parts array the adapter emits for text-only messages:

```
400 {"message":"Invalid value for 'messages.content'."}
```

Both request forms are valid under the spec, so I read this as an interoperability gap rather than a bug in pi. A few other OpenAI-compatible endpoints behave the same way, and `supportsStore` already exists for the sibling `store` problem, so this fits the existing compat-flag pattern.

## How?

Add `supportsContentArray` to `OpenAICompletionsCompatSchema`, default it to `true` in `detectCompat`, merge it in `getCompat`, and in `convertMessages` join the already-built text parts into a string when it is `false`. Messages carrying non-text parts keep the array form, since a string cannot represent them.

The flag is optional on `ResolvedOpenAICompletionsCompat`, matching `cacheControlFormat` and `supportsThinkingTokenBudget`, so callers that spell out a compat object do not need to change.

Tests assert on the actual outgoing request body, covering the flag on, off, and the image case. `npm run check` passes at parity with `main`.

I'd like to work on this — `lgtm` if the approach looks right to you.

## Version

pi 1.3.0, Arch Linux, Bun.

issues.title: Extensions cannot reuse the host ModelRuntime for createAgentSession

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
# Extensions cannot reuse the host ModelRuntime for `createAgentSession`

## Environment

- `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.3.0 (bundled CLI)
- Scenario: a plugin creates a pi sub-session inside its own background process (not the TUI main session).

## Background

Two plugins are loaded in the same pi process:

1. **custom-providers** registers a native provider via `pi.registerProvider(provider)` (`commandcode-goat`); its models come from the provider's `getModels()`.
2. **feishu** (a Feishu/Lark bridge) creates sessions with `createAgentSession()` in a separate daemon process to handle Feishu messages.

Expected: the Feishu session can pick a model from `commandcode-goat`.

## Observed

1. The Feishu `/model` card only lists built-in providers (deepseek / local-gpt).
2. Switching the list to `ctx.modelRegistry.getAvailable()` does list the extension provider's models (the host registry is correct), but the selected model is not what the session runs: `createSession`'s own `ModelRuntime.getModel(provider, id)` returns `undefined`, so it silently falls back to the default model — the user believes the switch happened when it did not.

## Root cause

Extensions cannot obtain the **host** `ModelRuntime`:

- `CreateAgentSessionOptions.modelRuntime?: ModelRuntime` (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/sdk.ts:54-55`).
- `createAgentSessionServices` does `options.modelRuntime ?? await ModelRuntime.create({...})` (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session-services.ts:140-146`) — when omitted it **creates a new** runtime that only loads built-in providers.
- The extension context only exposes `modelRegistry: ModelRegistry` (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/types.ts:337`), and `ModelRegistry.runtime` is `private` (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-registry.ts:44`) with no `getRuntime()` or similar accessor.

So an extension can only hand `createAgentSession` a runtime with built-in providers; native providers registered by extensions live only in the host runtime.

## Why there is no workaround

- Extensions do not hold a reusable provider registry: `pi.registerProvider(provider)` hands the object to the host, and there is no entry point to register it into a new runtime.
- Even if a `Model` object (with `baseUrl`) is taken from the host registry and passed to a self-created runtime, `ModelRuntime.stream()` still needs that provider's `stream` implementation and auth; the self-created runtime does not have it, so the request fails or falls back.

## Suggested fix (any one)

1. Expose `getRuntime(): ModelRuntime` on `ModelRegistry` (or make `runtime` a read-only getter).
2. Accept `modelRegistry?: ModelRegistry` in `CreateAgentSessionOptions` and use its runtime internally.
3. Provide `ExtensionContext.createAgentSession(options)` that reuses the parent runtime by default.

## References

- `packages/coding-agent/src/core/sdk.ts:54-55`
- `packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session-services.ts:140-146`
- `packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-registry.ts:44`
- `packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/types.ts:337`

issues.title: pi-durable: permanently delete a conversation from storage
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add a way to permanently delete a conversation from pi-durable storage, e.g. `harness.deleteConversation(id, ctx)`: it refuses (or aborts first) while a run is active, then removes the conversation's entries, docs, inbox items and scheduler state from the store.

### Why?

We host pi-durable for end users (SQLite storage, one harness per process). When a user deletes a conversation we can drop our own index row and files, but the message history stays in the durable store forever: in 1.2.0 the store is append-only and the only removal I could find is for inbox items (`removeInboxItem`). So "delete" only means "nobody can look it up any more", which is a weaker privacy guarantee than users expect, and the store only ever grows.

Deleting rows from the SQLite file ourselves would depend on the internal schema and break on upgrades.

### How? (optional)

A storage-level `deleteConversation` implemented by each backend, plus a harness method that checks the live run state, evicts the conversation from memory (rooms/subscriptions get a terminal "deleted" signal), and calls it. Tombstoning the id so a later `submit`/`entries` fails with a clear "not found" error would keep callers honest.

issues.title: Don't send another model's thinking as plain text after a model switch

labels.name: pkg:ai
labels.description: LLM API package

issues.body:
When you switch models mid-session, `transformMessages()` turns the earlier model's thinking blocks into plain assistant text. The new model copies that pattern and writes its own reasoning into the visible reply.

Example: a user ran several turns with GLM-5.3, then switched to Kimi K3. Kimi received GLM's reasoning as part of earlier replies and started putting its own thinking in the output. Kimi K3 asks callers not to do this.

**Proposal:** Drop thinking blocks that came from a different model instead of turning them into text. Frontier models only give summaries or encrypted thinking, so little is lost. Full reasoning from DeepSeek, GLM, and similar models is long and makes the output worse.

**Maybe later:** add a compat flag so related models can keep each other's thinking as real thinking blocks, for example Sonnet to Opus.

issues.title: powershell tool falls back to Windows PowerShell 5.1 when pwsh 7 is the Microsoft Store build
issues.body:
### What happened?

With PowerShell 7 installed from the Microsoft Store (7.6.7, no MSI), the built-in `powershell` tool runs Windows PowerShell 5.1.

`getPowerShellConfig` in `utils/shell.js` finds pwsh with `where pwsh.exe` and checks the first hit with `fs.existsSync`. The Store build puts an app-execution alias on PATH (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps\pwsh.exe`, a zero-length reparse point). On that alias `existsSync` is false and `statSync` throws EACCES, while `lstatSync`, `accessSync`, and spawning it all work. So the check rejects a working pwsh and silently falls back to `powershell.exe`.

Windows 11 Pro 26300, Node 26.8.1, managed install. The resolver is identical in 1.0.0 and 1.2.0.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Only the Store PowerShell 7 installed (`Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.PowerShell`), no `C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7`.
2. `pi -ne -p -t +powershell,-bash "Use the powershell tool to run: $PSVersionTable.PSEdition"` → `Desktop`.
3. Resolver directly:
   ```
   node -e "import('@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/utils/shell.js').then(m=>console.log(m.getPowerShellConfig().shell))"
   ```
   → `C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe`
4. `where pwsh.exe` → the WindowsApps alias. On that path: `fs.existsSync` → `false`, `fs.statSync` → EACCES, `fs.lstatSync` → 85-byte reparse point, `spawnSync` → prints `Core`.

### Expected behavior

pwsh 7 is used, as `docs/windows.md` says ("runs commands through pwsh.exe when available"). Microsoft is steering users to the Store/MSIX build and retiring the MSI, so more Windows users will hit this.

Fix is small: in the Windows branch of `findExecutableOnPath`, verify the `where` hit with `fs.lstatSync` or `fs.accessSync` instead of `existsSync`, or trust `where` the way the Unix branch trusts `which`. Workaround I use today: `$env:Path = "$PSHOME;$env:Path"` before starting pi, so the real package folder comes first (a user-PATH entry alone is not enough from pwsh, because the Store build prepends its alias folder to PATH at startup). Happy to send a PR if you want one.

Related: #8582 has the same symptom from a different cause (a `where` timeout under load); this one is deterministic on an idle machine.

### Version

1.2.0

issues.title: `pi -p` silently uses another model when an extension provider's catalog is stale; `pi update --models` skips extension catalogs
issues.body:
### What happened?

My settings have `defaultProvider: "pengepul"` and `defaultModel: "opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash"`. pengepul is an extension provider (@pwguler/pi-pengepul-provider 0.5.3) whose `refreshModels` fetches `GET /v1/models` from my relay and persists the list. Its `models-store.json` entry was from Oct 4, before the relay served any `opencode/*` ids.

`pi -p --no-tools "Reply with exactly: ok"` printed `ok`, but the session file says `anthropic/claude-fable-5`, and nothing mentioned the default. Print mode only refreshes with `allowNetwork: false` (`core/agent-session-services.ts:142,194`). So pengepul restored its old list, and `findInitialModel` fell through to the first available model with `fallbackMessage: undefined` (`core/model-resolver.ts:690-704`), which print mode wouldn't show anyway (`main.ts:986`).

`pi update --models` printed "Model catalogs refreshed" and left the pengepul entry alone, because `refreshModelCatalogs` never loads extensions (`package-manager-cli.ts:583-609`). `docs/models.md` names that command as the way to force a refresh.

Starting `pi --mode rpc` once with stdin held open fixed it: `main.ts:938-946` runs a network refresh for RPC, and print mode has nothing like it. The entry went from 500 to 535 models and `-p` ran on `pengepul/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash`. I had to do that on all three hosts.

Paths are under `packages/coding-agent/src/` at v1.0.4. main at f10993bc7 has the same code.

### Steps to reproduce

The bug needs an extension provider, so `-ne -e` loads just this one. Its "relay" is a file:

```ts
// /tmp/stale.ts
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { createProvider, openAICompletionsApi } from "@earendil-works/pi-ai";

const model = (id) => ({ id, name: id, provider: "stale", api: "openai-completions",
  baseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:9/v1", reasoning: false, input: ["text"], contextWindow: 128000, maxTokens: 8192,
  cost: { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0 } });

export default (pi) => pi.registerProvider(createProvider({
  id: "stale", api: openAICompletionsApi(), models: [],
  auth: { apiKey: { name: "key", check: async () => ({ type: "api_key", source: "test" }),
    resolve: async () => ({ auth: { apiKey: "x" }, source: "test" }) } },
  fetchModels: async () => readFileSync("/tmp/stale-ids", "utf8").split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean).map(model),
}));
```

I ran this with `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` set to an empty dir and no provider keys in the environment. Node's fetch refuses port 9, so requests end in `Connection error.` and nothing is sent.

1. `echo model-a > /tmp/stale-ids`, put `{"stale": {"type": "api_key", "key": "x"}}` in `auth.json`, then `sleep 10 | pi -ne -e /tmp/stale.ts --mode rpc`. `models-store.json` now has `model-a` under `stale`. Without the stored key, startup sometimes misses the provider entirely, like #8810.
2. `echo "model-a model-b" > /tmp/stale-ids` and set `"defaultProvider": "stale", "defaultModel": "model-b"` in `settings.json`.
3. `pi -ne -e /tmp/stale.ts -p hi`. The new session's `model_change` is `stale/model-a`, and stderr says only `Connection error.`
4. `pi update --models` prints "Model catalogs refreshed", `models-store.json` stays byte-identical, and step 3 still lands on `model-a`.
5. Repeat the RPC command from step 1, then step 3. Now it's `stale/model-b`.

### Expected behavior

`pi -p` runs the configured default, or says on stderr which model it used instead. `pi update --models` refreshes extension catalogs too, or says it skipped them.

When the default isn't in the restored catalog, print mode could refresh just that provider before falling back, e.g. `modelRuntime.refresh({ providers: [defaultProvider], signal })` with the usual 15 s timeout. That costs nothing when the default resolves. A stderr warning whenever a configured default gets replaced would have pointed straight at this; #8810 asks for it too. `pi update --models` could load extensions the way `createAgentSessionServices` does.

### Version

1.0.4, repro run on it (Linux, Node 24.20.0). First seen on 1.0.1 and 1.0.2 on three hosts, Linux and macOS.

issues.title: Anthropic tool calls: corrupted non-ASCII edit arguments are silently accepted (dropped `u` in `\uXXXX` → `\b`/`\f` control chars)
issues.body:
### What happened?

With Claude models, `edit` calls on files containing Korean text fail very often, and occasionally corrupt a file. I have been tracking this for about three weeks. It keeps coming back and costs a lot of retries.

There are two symptoms, usually in the same sessions:

1. **Control characters instead of Korean.** The arguments contain C0 control characters where Korean characters were intended.
2. **Garbage calls.** An `edit` whose `oldText` is a few meaningless characters that exist nowhere in the file. Several in a row can occur.

Both usually fail safely as "Could not find ... oldText". Once, a corrupted `newText` was written to a file and had to be repaired by hand.

### The pattern behind symptom 1

It points to a `\uXXXX` escape whose `u` is missing in the tool-input JSON. When the next hex digit happens to be `b` or `f`, the result is still **valid JSON**: `\b` / `\f` followed by the remaining three hex digits. `JSON.parse` accepts it, so the tool runs with wrong strings instead of returning an error.

Illustration (synthetic): intended `\ub0b4` → emitted `\b0b4` → parsed as U+0008 + `0b4`.

### Evidence

Automated scan of my local session logs (edit arguments only, no file contents):

| Model | edit calls | errors | error rate | args with C0 control chars |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| openai-codex/gpt-6-astra | 398 | 9 | 2.3% | 0 |
| openai-codex/gpt-6-sol | 82 | 5 | 6.1% | 0 |
| xai/grok-4.7 | 27 | 3 | 11% | 0 |
| anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 | 212 | 86 | 40.6% | 15 |
| anthropic/claude-opus-5 | 34 | 20 | 58.8% | 8 |
| anthropic/claude-fable-5-1 | 20 | 8 | 40% | 2 |

- All control characters found in Claude edit arguments are U+0008 (`\b`) or U+000C (`\f`). 848 of 873 are followed by exactly three hex digits.
- An earlier manual classification over 20 days: 52 of 68 failed Opus 5.5 edits had lost their Korean text. GPT, Grok and DeepSeek had none.
- I found no case where `repairJson` turned an invalid escape into a literal backslash, so I don't think the repair path causes this. The corrupted cases are already valid JSON before any repair.

### What I ruled out

- **`eager_input_streaming`:** on vs off, 21 attempts each. One corrupted call in each group.
- **Session length:** I forked an affected session and ran four edits each with the default `edit`, a hash-anchored edit extension, and all extensions loaded. All 12 succeeded. On the same day, the original window failed 3 of 4.
- **Edit tool format:** the hash-anchored edit tool made no difference.
- **Encoding in general:** in the same failing window, shell edits, `write`, and a Node script inside the shell all wrote Korean correctly.

### A context effect

The failures cluster after corrupted strings have been visible in the context. In the original window, the broken calls closely resembled an example string that had just been displayed during analysis. Later, a fresh session reproduced it twice in a row right after reading notes that contained such an example. I also hit the garbage-call symptom about six times today in a long session, after the raw examples had already been removed from those notes, so removing them does not prevent it.

So this looks like a model-side tendency that feeds on its own output. I can't prove where the `u` goes missing from the client side.

### Why report it here

Even if the root cause is the model, the pi-side problem is that corruption is silent. A cheap guard would make it a normal retryable validation error:

- For `edit` / `write` (or any string tool args), reject C0 control characters other than `\t`, `\n`, `\r`, with a message like "argument contains control character U+0008; possible malformed \u escape".
- Or, in the Anthropic provider, flag `\b`/`\f` followed by hex digits in the raw `partialJson` before parsing.

If the context effect is real, the error should not echo the corrupted string back to the model. Naming the code point is probably enough.

I can write this guard as a local extension (a `tool_call` handler returning `{ block, reason }`). It seems worth handling in core, though, because every non-ASCII user on Claude is exposed to silent file corruption.

Related: #6278 (Claude tool-call schema errors, closed as model behavior). This case is narrower: non-ASCII content only, and it can corrupt files without any validation error.

### Steps to reproduce

Not deterministic. Using a Claude model, ask for several `edit` calls that replace Korean text in a UTF-8 file. It is much more likely once a corrupted string has appeared in the conversation. Failures show up as oldText mismatches whose arguments contain U+0008/U+000C, or as very short oldText values.

I can share the log-scanning script (counts only) if helpful.

### Version / environment

- pi 0.87.1 (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`), Windows, PowerShell 7
- Provider `anthropic`, Claude subscription login through the third-party `@gotgenes/pi-anthropic-auth` 3.3.2 extension. It only handles authentication, but I have not tested with an API key.

issues.title: detectInstallMethod mislabels non-pnpm installs under PNPM_HOME
issues.body:
### What happened?

`detectInstallMethod()` treats any path containing `/pnpm/` as `pnpm`. Installs that only *share* `PNPM_HOME` for bins (e.g. under `$PNPM_HOME/global-nub/...`) are labeled `pnpm`, then `isManagedByGlobalPackageManager` correctly rejects them.

Result:

- Error text: “not managed by a global **pnpm** install” (implies method is pnpm)
- `getUpdateInstruction` / banner still suggest `pnpm install -g …` (wrong tool)

`pi -ne update` reproduces. 0.84.1.

This is a **detection/messaging** bug, not a request to first-class every package manager.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install so the package realpath is under `$PNPM_HOME/…` but **not** under `pnpm root -g` (e.g. `$PNPM_HOME/global-nub/…`)
2. `pi -ne update`
3. Observe pnpm-specific wording and `pnpm install -g` suggestion

### Expected behavior

When the install is not actually managed by that PM:

1. Do not claim install method `pnpm` / do not suggest `pnpm install -g`
2. Prefer: unknown/wrapper wording, or fall through after managed-check fails
3. **Optional generic escape hatch** (preferred over hardcoding each PM): settings/env self-update command, e.g. `selfUpdateCommand` / `PI_SELF_UPDATE_COMMAND` with `{installSpec}` — so wrappers can declare how to upgrade without growing `case "nub" | "foo" | …` in core

Out of scope for this issue: adding first-class support for any specific third-party package manager.

### Version

0.84.1

issues.title: Default system prompt doesn't tell the model what `@path` mentions mean

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

One sentence in the default system prompt explaining that a `@path` token in a user message is a file or directory mention. e.g.
> A `@path` token in a user message is a file or directory mention, resolved from the current working directory: inspect the target as the request warrants — read, list, or search it.

### Why?

The `@` convention is wired into the UI but never explained to the model. As far as I can tell, exactly three places understand it, none of them the prompt:

- CLI startup: `@file` args are expanded into the first prompt 
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/381a2d8eb62b9f7e4c710cf66aa516f8a92cb9bd/packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts#L223
- Interactive editor: `@` opens file autocomplete
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/381a2d8eb62b9f7e4c710cf66aa516f8a92cb9bd/packages/tui/src/autocomplete.ts#L119
- Tools: path resolution strips a leading `@` 
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/381a2d8eb62b9f7e4c710cf66aa516f8a92cb9bd/packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/path-utils.ts#L41

[The default prompt](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/381a2d8eb62b9f7e4c710cf66aa516f8a92cb9bd/packages/coding-agent/src/core/system-prompt.ts#L155-L170) says nothing about it.

So mid-session a mention reaches the model as plain prose, and the model has to infer both the intent and the resolution rules. In practice this is unstable rather than broken: paths that look unambiguous (`@data/`, `@src/index.ts`) usually work, but a bare filename like `@my-conf.toml` gets guessed at — I've seen a frontier model search the whole repo for the name and read a file from the wrong directory instead of resolving the mention from the working directory. The model usually understands the token refers to a file; the point is that the whole convention needs stating — where a mention resolves is only the part that fails most visibly.

To be clear, I think the pass-through itself is the right design and worth keeping. Mentions are often targeted rather than whole-file reads — pointing at a log file to look for errors, or a directory to search for something — so always auto-expanding them into the context would bloat it. Send-time rewriting (as Codex does, turning `@data/` into `data/`) depends on visual affordances — highlighting or similar hints so users can tell a path was rewritten — while pi's plain-text pass-through needs none of it; only the model-side contract is missing.



### How? (optional)

Append a line to the default preamble in `system-prompt.ts` to explain the syntax.

I'm willing to submit this one-liner as a PR once approved.

#### Disclosure

GLM 5.3 Flash in Pi help me explore how Codex and Pi work about `@path` mentions syntax now(2026 10 17)

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Provide a shared typed contract for HTTP status, provider error code and optional explicit retryability on terminal error events / `AssistantMessage`, using the existing diagnostics mechanism if appropriate.

### Why?

Cherry Studio Mobile needs these facts for retries, credential fallback and error presentation. Provider adapters already see structured SDK errors, but the [Responses catch path](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/8efd314fa3d3232ce197d8d7a6a5660530b9d83e/packages/ai/src/api/openai-responses.ts#L250) reduces them to display text, and generic retry classification uses `errorMessage` patterns.

For example, an opaque/localized message with status 503 should remain distinguishable from status 401. A provider error inside an HTTP 200 stream also needs its provider code preserved. Temporary rate limits and exhausted subscription quotas must remain distinguishable.

### How? (optional)

Our 1.3.0 patch carries these fields in `provider_response_failure` diagnostics across adapters and lets consumers prefer structured facts over text matching. Could this become a consistent public contract?

Related: #10697 (lost cause), #10600 (Retry-After transport), and declined #5617 (retry-classification hooks). This proposal focuses on preserving existing provider facts through the message boundary for all consumers.

Checked against main `8efd314` by source inspection. Downstream regression sources exist; no tests or builds were run for this proposal.

issues.title: Pi Durable support for client-side tool execution and tool approval
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Submitting this as a contribution proposal because there's no feature option and this isn't a bug. I initially submitted a [discussion](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/discussions/10632) but not sure if that's the right area.

Some tools require human approval before they run, or require client-side information before they run. Here's an example for each scenario.

Destructive tool that requires human approval:
1. The model calls a tool
2. The run stops before the tool executes. The pending call is persisted, and nothing is held in memory
3. The user approves, denies it, maybe hours or days later 
4. The run continues from that same tool call and the tool executes (or a denial result is written), and the agent loop continues.

For requiring client-side information for a tool result (a good example of this is WebMCP, or a `askUserQuestion` style tool):
1. The model calls a tool
2. The run stops before the tool executes (because it has no execute function in its definition). The pending call is persisted, and nothing is held in memory
3. The client receives the tool call, executes what's necessary, and sends back the tool output result
4. The run continues from that same tool call: the agent loop receives the tool result, and the agent loop continues.

It seems like something like this doesn't exist for Pi durable. There's some similar examples but they seem to wait in memory or return a terminated tool result.

Questions:
- Is there an existing solution I missed?
- Is support for something like this planned or in consideration?

If you only plan on supporting one of these, I would kindly ask for it to be the second: client-side tool execution (it doesn't have to be client side, but basically "paused" or "deferred" tool execution). I think this pattern can support the human-approval feature if need-be, it just might be a bit awkward in its implementation depending on the design.

Related:
- https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5901 but that was for pi, not pi durable
- This could also tie-in with support of the MCP spec with tools that return with an [input required] request(https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#input-required-tool-results), 
- Examples of how this is designed elsewhere:
  - Vercel's AI sdk has approval states for tool execution: https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/agents/tool-approvals. And for client-side tool output, if you don't define an `execute` for a tool, when that tool is called it stops the agent run, and the client can start the run again by providing the tool result (see `getLocation` tool here https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-ui/chatbot-tool-usage)
  - Cloudflare think similarly has a [tool approval](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/harnesses/think/tools/#tool-approval), as well as [client side tools](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/harnesses/think/client-tools/) 

### Why?

The UX for many agent interfaces need humans to approve certain actions. There's also many situations where a tool's execution is done on the client.

### How? (optional)

_No response_

issues.title: Support Anthropic's native advisor tool in anthropic-messages

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## What do you want to change?

Add opt-in support for Anthropic's native advisor tool (`advisor_20260301`, beta `advisor-tool-2026-03-01`) to the `anthropic-messages` provider: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool

This is Anthropic's hosted executor/advisor pair. It is not a client-side second-model loop (#7845) and not a generic cross-provider server-tool abstraction (#1740).

## Why?

Pi cannot currently send the advisor tool, parse `server_tool_use` / `advisor_tool_result`, replay that pair on later turns, resume an advisor `pause_turn`, or report `advisor_message` usage. An extension cannot do this reliably: it cannot add the beta/tool at the provider layer, preserve encrypted advisor blocks in content order, or resume a paused response within one assistant turn.

With a supported pair (for example a Sonnet executor consulting an Opus advisor), this avoids running the strong model as the full executor while still getting its input at key points.

## How? (optional)

Keep it Anthropic-only and opt-in; no built-in model would enable it by default:

- Configure per executor model via Anthropic compat, with a provider-option override/disable.
- Preserve `server_tool_use` + `advisor_tool_result` (including encrypted results) as content blocks, replay paired blocks verbatim, drop orphans, and keep the beta when history contains them.
- Resume advisor `pause_turn` inside the provider response; keep the current stop mapping for non-advisor pauses.
- Report advisor sub-inference tokens separately under `usage.advisor`; executor token totals stay unchanged.
- Cover tool injection, streaming, replay/pending across client tool results, pause resume, and usage with fake-SSE tests.

I am willing to implement this. I already have a tested local branch based on current `main` (`npm run check` and `./test.sh` pass), and I am opening this proposal first per CONTRIBUTING before any PR. Happy to adjust naming or scope.

Disclosure: this proposal and the local branch were prepared with AI assistance, from the Anthropic docs and the linked issues above.

issues.title: Throwing from preflightResult("started") leaves the session busy forever (regression in 1.2.0)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
> AI disclosure: drafted with an AI coding assistant. I reproduced the bug myself on 1.1.0, 1.2.0 and 1.3.0 and checked every detail below.

### What happened?

Since #10739 (1.2.0), `_startRun` sets `_isAgentRunActive = true`, runs `_prepareRun` in a try/catch that resets it, then calls `onStarted?.()` outside any try. `onStarted` is `preflightResult?.("started")`. If that callback throws, `prompt()` rejects but the session stays busy for good: `isStreaming` is `true`, `waitForIdle()` and `abort()` never resolve, and every later `prompt()` fails with `Agent is already processing`.

In 1.1.0 `preflightResult("started")` ran before the flag was set, so a throw just refused the prompt.

My app embeds `AgentSession` and throws there to refuse a prompt the user stopped while `before_agent_start` handlers were still running. Handler errors are swallowed, so there's no later point to refuse it. My integration tests caught this when I upgraded: after Stop in that window the chat never recovers. RPC mode's callback doesn't throw, so `pi -ne` can't hit this; it's SDK-only. I saw #11044 was declined, so if throwing from `preflightResult` isn't supported, what's the supported way to refuse a prompt at that point?

### Steps to reproduce

```js
// createAgentSession with the faux provider, no extensions besides registerProvider
await session.prompt("x", {
  preflightResult: (d) => { if (d === "started") throw new Error("refused"); },
}).catch(() => {});
session.isStreaming;                           // 1.3.0: true, 1.1.0: false
await session.prompt("next").catch((e) => e); // 1.3.0: "Agent is already processing", 1.1.0: runs
await session.abort();                         // 1.3.0: never resolves, 1.1.0: resolves
```

Same on 1.2.0. Nothing is written to the session.

### Expected behavior

A throw from `onStarted` cleans up the way the `_prepareRun` catch does: reset `_isAgentRunActive`, flush pending messages, call `_resolveIdleWaitIfIdle()`, and rethrow. Moving `onStarted?.()` into that try would do it. I'd like to send the PR with a test.

### Version

1.3.0 (regressed in 1.2.0, still on main)

issues.title: Add a /cd command to start a new session in another directory

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add a `/cd <directory>` command that starts a new session in another working directory. Right now the only way to switch projects is to quit pi and launch it again.

### Why?

I work across several repos and switch between them constantly. Quitting and relaunching throws away the session and reloads everything just to change directory. The working directory is what decides which project files, context, and trust rules load, so a fresh session in the target directory is the right behavior rather than moving the existing one.

### How?

`newSession()` already replaces the session, but it always reuses the current directory, and nothing in the extension API can change that, so this cannot be an extension. Add a `cwd` option to `newSession()`, give the new session its own session directory so `pi -c` finds it in the right place, and re-run the project trust check for the new directory. `/cd` is the interactive command on top, with directory name completion. A missing path should error and leave the current session alone.

I have implemented this and tested it locally, including the RPC `new_session` command taking the same option. I would like to open the PR myself, so a reply with `lgtm` would let it through the auto-close gate.

prs.title: feat(durable): inject a timer for task sleeps
prs.body:
## Summary

Pi Durable already takes an injected clock (`HarnessOptions.now`), but `TaskRuntime.sleep()` always waited with an in-process `setTimeout`. A long retry backoff or deferred-response poll therefore kept a timer and its task invocation in memory, and a host such as a Cloudflare Durable Object could not wait on an alarm or delayed queue message instead.

This adds `HarnessOptions.timer: (until, context) => Promise<void>` next to `now`:

- `until` is an absolute time on the Harness clock. `sleep()` rechecks the clock after every wake and calls the timer again while the deadline is ahead, so early or duplicate wakes only rearm it.
- A cancelled sleep rejects at once with the cancellation reason, even when the timer ignores `context`, so a late wake cannot resume an ended invocation.
- A timer rejection rejects the sleep (and faults the task unless handled); there is no fallback to `setTimeout`.
- The Harness resolves the default (`setTimeout`, chunked at 2^31 - 1 ms) like its other options; the scheduler receives a required timer.
- Other `setTimeout` uses (progress throttles, cache expiry, environment timeouts) are unchanged: they pace active work or free memory and must not cause durable wakeups.

An alarm cannot restore a lost process: the host reopens the storage and calls `resume()`, the task reruns its phase from the committed deadline, and arms the new Harness's timer. The README and spec state the host's remaining duties: keep an alarm armed while tasks are live, and keep a single storage owner.

## Testing

- `npm run check`
- `vitest --run test/harness-tasks.test.ts test/harness-generation-recovery.test.ts test/harness-generation.test.ts test/harness-compaction.test.ts test/harness-tasks-recovery.test.ts test/harness-lifecycle.test.ts test/harness-scheduler-retention.test.ts` (231 tests)
- New tests fail without the change: host timer use and rearming, abort with a timer that ignores cancellation, timer failure, retry backoff resumed after reopen through a fresh timer, and a non-Error cancellation reason.

prs.title: fix(powershell): accept Microsoft Store app-execution aliases in PATH resolution
prs.body:
## Summary

With PowerShell 7 installed from the Microsoft Store, the built-in `powershell` tool was running Windows PowerShell 5.1. Store installs put an app-execution alias on PATH (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps\pwsh.exe`, a zero-length reparse point). On that path `fs.existsSync` returns false and `statSync` throws EACCES, so `findExecutableOnPath` rejected a working pwsh and silently fell back to `powershell.exe`. Reported in #10976.

## Fix

Verify the `where` hit with `fs.lstatSync` instead of `existsSync`. lstat does not follow the reparse point, so it still rejects paths that do not exist, but it accepts the Store alias. This also brings the Windows branch closer to the Unix branch, which already trusts `which`.

## Testing

- Added a Windows-only regression test: whatever `getPowerShellConfig()` returns must pass `lstatSync` (a real file and a Store alias both satisfy this; a phantom path does not).
- `vitest --run test/powershell-tool.test.ts`: 3 passed (2 pre-existing + 1 new).
- On this machine (no pwsh 7 installed) the resolver still returns 5.1, which is correct behavior when pwsh is absent.

Fixes #10976

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): defer sendMessage triggerTurn until compaction ends
prs.body:
Fixes #10982.

## Problem

`pi.sendMessage(msg, { triggerTurn: true })` started a run immediately while a manual compaction was in progress. The run executed concurrently with compaction — using uncompacted context — and its messages landed before the compaction entry, corrupting message order.

`sendCustomMessage` only checked `isStreaming` before calling `_startRun`; it did not check `isCompacting` (`isIdle` already accounts for both, so the two disagreed).

## Fix

Queue `triggerTurn` submissions made during compaction in a new `_deferredCompactionActions` queue (mirroring the existing `_deferredSettledActions` pattern) and flush it once compaction state is cleared. Flush points cover all three compaction paths: manual compaction, auto-compaction, and branch summarization.

- Deferred run failures are reported through the extension error channel (`send_message` event) instead of becoming compaction failures.
- Finishing compaction does not wait for the newly triggered runs (fire-and-forget).
- `deliverAs: "nextTurn"` and non-triggerTurn direct-append paths are untouched (already queue semantics / out of scope).

## Tests

- New `test/suite/regressions/10982-send-message-during-compaction.test.ts` (13 tests): 3 compaction triggers (manual/threshold/overflow) x 3 outcomes (success/failure/abort) — triggerTurn waits for `compaction_end` before starting the run, `agent_start` lands after `compaction_end`, message lands after the compaction entry; steer/followUp `deliverAs` ordering; deferred failure goes to the `send_message` error channel; branch summarization also releases the queue. 13/13 pass.
- Neighbors: `agent-session-compaction` 29/29, `agent-session-auto-compaction-queue` + `custom-message` 7/7.

Closes #10982

prs.title: fix(env): include stderr in pi-env startup errors
prs.body:
When the daemon exits before `hello`, the error has only the exit code. For example, with `loginShell: true` and a profile that aborts on a missing file:

```
pi-env exited with code 3 before it was ready
```

`sshConnection`'s probe and deploy steps already report ssh's stderr, so this is about the launch itself: a login profile, a daemon that can't execute, or a `Connection` created with its own command, which has no probe or deploy step, so auth and network errors also end up here.

This keeps a short stderr tail until `hello` and adds it to startup errors:

```
pi-env exited with code 3 before it was ready
remote stderr:
profile: /opt/toolchain/env.sh: No such file or directory
```

The tail is capped at 20 lines / 2000 chars, with terminal escapes and control characters stripped. Ready sessions are unchanged.

I hit it while testing `loginShell` against an sshd in Docker. Tests are in `test/connection.test.ts`, and `npm run check` and `./test.sh` pass.
