issues.title: NoNewPrivs child-matrix tests fail deterministically in NNP-pinned containers

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
### Summary

The NoNewPrivs child-matrix tests in `crates/tui/src/sandbox/process_hardening.rs` fail deterministically when the test process itself already runs under a pinned `NoNewPrivs` (e.g. inside a container whose runtime sets `no-new-privileges` tree-wide, such as Docker with `--security-opt no-new-privileges` or a hardened Kubernetes pod). The matrices assert that a child spawned with the `NoNewPrivs` flag reports `PR_GET_NO_NEW_PRIVS == 0` rows:

- `no_new_privs_flag_tracks_startup_posture_in_child_processes` (~line 435) — the danger-full-access row expects `NNP=0`
- `no_new_privs_env_override_beats_posture_in_child_processes` (~line 456) — the falsey-override row expects `NNP=0`

`NoNewPrivs` is a one-way kernel ratchet: once the parent process has it, no child can clear it, so those assertions are environment-impossible rather than product bugs — the suite reads as red on hardened CI hosts even though the sandbox behavior is correct.

### Proposed fix

Probe the parent flag first (`prctl(PR_GET_NO_NEW_PRIVS)`) and, where pinned, substitute the ratchet assertion for the affected rows: assert the flag **stays 1** in the child (the actual kernel contract) and print a one-line disclosure per substituted row. Unpinned environments keep the full matrix unchanged. Test-module-only change; no production code.

### Context

We run this suite inside NNP-pinned containers and hit exactly this. A working ratchet-aware variant exists in a private fork and can be submitted as a PR here if the approach sounds right — happy to send it.

Happy to adjust the substitution/disclosure shape if maintainers prefer a different convention (skip vs. flipped assertion vs. `#[ignore]` with a reason).

issues.title: sandbox(linux): every command aborts with "bwrap: Can't mount on symlink destination" when a mounted $HOME path is a symlink

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What happened? 发生了什么？

With the OS sandbox enabled on Linux, **no shell command runs at all**: every tool call aborts before executing anything — including read-only ones like `pwd` or `ls` — with:

```
bwrap: Can't mount on symlink destination $HOME/.kube
```

I expected the command to run inside the sandbox with writes confined to the workspace. Instead nothing was executed, and the only way to get any work done was to escalate each call to `danger-full-access` by hand.

The trigger is a **symlink** under `$HOME` that the sandbox's bind plan mounts. On this machine:

```
$ ls -ld ~/.kube
lrwxrwxrwx 1 caligari caligari 28 Jan 14 2026 /home/<user>/.kube -> /home/<user>/Sync/etc/kube
```

My dotfiles live in a synced directory, so `~/.kube` has been a symlink for a long time, and I want to keep it that way.

I have no extra roots configured — `config.toml` only sets `sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"` — so the failing bind comes from the built-in plan.

bubblewrap itself refuses a bind whose destination is a symlink. Reproduced standalone, bwrap 0.12.0, payload `/bin/true`:

```
$ bwrap --ro-bind / / /bin/true
exit=0

$ bwrap --ro-bind / / --bind /tmp /home/<user>/Sync/etc/kube /bin/true   # resolved target
exit=0

$ bwrap --ro-bind / / --bind /tmp /home/<user>/.kube /bin/true           # the symlink
bwrap: Can't mount on symlink destination /home/<user>/.kube
exit=1
```

Mounting the resolved path works; mounting the symlink cannot work.



### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

1. Linux, a codewhale build that applies the bwrap sandbox, with `sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"`.
2. Make a path that the sandbox mounts under `$HOME` a symlink instead of a real directory: `ln -s ~/Sync/etc/kube ~/.kube`.
3. Ask for any shell command, even `pwd`.

The call fails with the bwrap error above and nothing is executed.

### Codewhale version 版本

0.10.1 (fead51eeea0f)

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

TUI (terminal interface) in a local workspace.

### Operating system 操作系统

Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie); kernel `6.17.13+deb13-amd64`; bubblewrap `0.12.0` (`/usr/bin/bwrap`).

### How did you get Codewhale? 获取方式

Official script (codewhale.net/install.sh)

### Provider and model 提供商和模型

Not relevant — the command fails before it runs.

### Terminal and shell 终端

Not relevant to the failure; `bash` on the same machine.

### codewhale doctor (optional)

```text
The two lines that matter:


· runtime posture: ... sandbox=workspace-write (config), ...
! sandbox not available (commands run best-effort)
```

### Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

Same machine, same config, same symlink, different version:

- **0.10.1**: the sandbox is applied, the mount plan fails to build, and *every* command aborts with the bwrap error above. The session is unusable unless each call is escalated by hand.
- **0.10.0**: `codewhale doctor` reports `! sandbox not available (commands run best-effort)`. Commands run, but **unsandboxed**: writes outside the workspace (in `$HOME`) succeed and the network is reachable. That is a silent loss of isolation, not a fix.

I report both because they are the same failure from two sides: when the mount plan cannot be built, the session either cannot run anything (0.10.1) or runs everything without isolation (0.10.0).

What would help:
1. When a bind destination is a symlink, mount the resolved path (or its parent directory) instead of failing the whole plan.
2. When the plan cannot be built, fail loudly with a clear message and a way forward, instead of making every tool call abort.
3. Treat symlinked dotfile directories as normal: they should not be able to break or silently disable the sandbox.

issues.title: Turn snapshots fail with "git commit-tree failed: fatal: <sha> is not a valid object" since 2026-10-12 (0.10.0 after rollback from 0.10.1); old user turns are re-delivered
issues.body:
Hello,

I would like to report a defect in CodeWhale 0.10.0. We run it on Windows 11 in daily work, and the instance
in question holds a long-running session (about 99 MB) that we would very much like to keep. The problem has
been with us since 12 October 2026.

**Environment**

- CodeWhale **0.10.0** (npm package installed globally). Binary: `%APPDATA%\npm\node_modules\codewhale\bin\downloads\codewhale.exe`,
  100 331 520 bytes, last written **2026-10-12 15:48**.
- Current version in npm: **0.10.1**.
- Windows 11 IoT Enterprise LTSC 10.0.26100, git 2.55.0.windows.5.
- Data dir `%USERPROFILE%\.codewhale`; workspace `C:\Users\Public\CodeWhale`.
- Session journal `sessions\fd452c83-….json`: **98 989 231 bytes** (it was ~72 MB on 2026-10-12 and grows).

**Symptom 1 — every turn snapshot fails**

```
WARN snapshot: snapshot 'pre-turn:2: <first words of a user message>' failed:
     git commit-tree failed: fatal: 6a55c90c6ada7206170f178fd20032f813a3b3d9 is not a valid object
```

**Symptom 2 — old user turns are re-delivered as new input**

Because snapshots never complete, past turns are never marked done and are fed back. The order is stable and
reproducible: in the most recent run the app re-delivered turns 2, 3 and 4 — the same three messages, in the
same order, as in every previous run (logs `tui-2026-10-14-20628`, `-14004`, `-23528`). The user sees his own
old messages answered again.

**Symptom 3 — shell operations frequently fail**

```
WARN codewhale_tui::tools::shell: shell work-graph registration skipped;
     running without a bound operation shell_id=shell_<hex>
     error=To-do state is busy; operation was not registered

WARN codewhale_tui::tools::shell: failed to reconcile shell lifecycle shell_id=shell_<hex>
     error=operation binding shell:shell_<hex> is not registered
```

273 such lines in the logs; on the user's side roughly every 3rd–4th shell call fails. Possibly the same root
cause as the snapshot failure.

**Symptom 4 — at startup the store looks empty**

```
WARN snapshot: boot prune failed: git log failed: fatal: bad object HEAD
```

**When it started**

- first occurrence: **2026-10-12T16:00:16Z** — `snapshot prune failed: commit-tree failed: fatal: c6d19349dd4298bf49945c1e64e4e7b35c4b334c is not a valid object`;
- 458 lines containing “is not a valid object” in total, over four runs;
- only two lost objects in total: `6a55c90c6ada7206170f178fd20032f813a3b3d9` and `c6d19349dd4298bf49945c1e64e4e7b35c4b334c`.

**What correlates with the date**

On the same day the user updated to **0.10.1** and then **rolled back to 0.10.0**. The package directory is
stamped **2026-10-12 15:48** (the rollback), and the first snapshot failure is at **19:00** local time.
Hypothesis: a snapshot store was begun by 0.10.1, and after the rollback 0.10.0 cannot complete that chain.

**What we tried**

- Reinstalled the same version (`npm install -g codewhale@0.10.0`) — **no effect**. The store is not part of
  the program files; `boot prune failed: bad object HEAD` still appears and snapshots still fail with the same SHA.

**Where we looked for the store (found nothing)**

Workspace `C:\Users\Public\CodeWhale` (not a git repo; only `.codewhale\state` with subagent state);
`%USERPROFILE%\.codewhale` (no `work-graph`, `objects`, `refs`, `.git` — only `sessions\.work-graph-import-archive`);
`%LOCALAPPDATA%` and `%APPDATA%` (depth 4); `%TEMP%`; the app package dir (only `bin`, `scripts`, `test`,
`package.json`, `README.md`); the app's `state.db` is empty and stale (2026-10-04).

**Questions**

1. Where are the snapshot store and the work-graph kept, and how can a corrupted chain be repaired on the
   user's side?
2. How can the **turn queue / parent-commit pointer** be reset so that snapshots work again and old turns stop
   being re-delivered **without discarding the session**? The session is 99 MB and losing it would be costly.
3. Is the `To-do state is busy` shell failure the same root cause as the snapshot failure? Both began in the
   same period.

**Related: cannot move to 0.10.1 with a long session**

On 2026-10-12 we also tried 0.10.1: it installs cleanly, but resuming our session fails:

```
error: selected saved history could not be captured
caused by: session exceeds full-history transport bound; source retained
```

The session file was ~72 MB then and is **98 989 231 bytes** now, so this bound will trigger even more readily.
We cannot test 0.10.1 — and therefore cannot check whether it fixes the snapshot store — while it stands.
Is there a way to raise or bypass it?

**Materials available on request**

Full log excerpts (458 snapshot lines, 273 work-graph lines), the environment dump, and our extended Russian
report. Happy to attach or translate anything you need.

Thank you for the tool, and for taking the time to look at this. I will gladly provide any further logs,
dumps or reproductions you need.

Best regards,
Sergej Malevich

issues.title: 号召：成立汉化组（Call to Action: Form a Chinese Localization Group）

labels.name: localization
labels.description: Localization, i18n, and non-English language support

milestone.title: Backlog
milestone.description: Kept ideas without a release commitment: platform requests, integrations and speculative features. Say why when you pick one up or close it; nothing here blocks a release.

issues.body:
CodeWhale 是个大项目，有海量的文档。虽然后期借助了 LLM 来翻译，但翻译那些文档进中文已经耗费了我太多的心神。后期英文文档更新，中文文档应当一起同步。然而，AI翻译的技术文档质量，大家懂得都懂——只停留在“能读”，至于看着费不费劲，那是另一码事。

不只是我们 CodeWhale，其他许多开源项目也面临着这样的困境。我希望能够牵头成立一个小型的汉化组，用爱发电，去汉化、跟进开源的英文项目或日文项目，让更多的简中网友能了解到这些它们。不仅让这些优秀的项目免于雪藏，也降低了许多项目的使用门槛。

如果有意愿加入此组的，请在此 Issue 下留言。如果人齐，到时候我会建立一个 QQ 群，把大家都拉进去。到时候我们一起合作，打通语言壁垒。

肯定会有人觉得这没必要。但我觉得千里之行始于足下，或者说不积小流无以成江海。

现在，大部分文本都是AIGC——我这不是在怪罪 Hmbown 兄弟，他已经很尽力了，换作我，我肯定连i18n都没想到，但他竟然同时维护这么多语言。我觉得我们这样做，也是为 Hmbown 和像他一样的人减轻一部分负担。

语言的壁垒是真实存在的，我听说很多外国人看中国汉字都看得头昏，可能 Hmbown 老兄也觉得我们汉语的方块字有点难懂。既然如此，我们就成立一个志愿的汉化组吧！就让我们来帮他点忙，也相当于是分工协作了；同时也帮 CodeWhale 这条大鲸鱼游得更远！

欢迎所有想要给 Codewhale 贡献、但是却觉得无从下手的人——路就在这里！

开源万岁，协作万岁，共享万岁，知识万岁！

> 如有意愿，请添加我的QQ号：2163018547（彁）并注明来意。

---

CodeWhale is a large project with a huge amount of documentation. Although we later used LLMs to help translate it, translating those documents into Chinese still cost me far too much time and energy. Going forward, when the English docs are updated, the Chinese docs should be synced as well. However, everyone knows the quality of AI-translated technical documentation—it only reaches the level of “readable.” Whether it’s actually easy to read is another matter entirely.

It’s not just CodeWhale. Many other open-source projects face the same predicament. I hope to take the lead in forming a small Chinese localization group, powered by love rather than money, to translate and keep up with open-source English or Japanese projects, so that more Simplified Chinese-speaking users can learn about them. This would not only keep these excellent projects from being buried and forgotten, but also lower the barrier to entry for many of them.

If you’re interested in joining this group, please leave a comment under this issue. I’ll then create a QQ group and invite everyone in. Together, we can work to break down language barriers.

Some people will definitely think this is unnecessary. But I believe that a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step—or, as the saying goes, without accumulating small streams, one cannot form rivers and seas.

Right now, most of the text is AIGC—I’m not blaming our friend Hmbown for this. He’s already trying his best. If it were me, I definitely wouldn’t have even thought of i18n, yet he’s actually maintaining so many languages at the same time. I think by doing this, we’re also easing some of the burden for Hmbown and people like him.

Language barriers are real. I've heard that many foreigners get dizzy just looking at Chinese characters, and maybe our friend Hmbown also finds our Chinese square characters a bit hard to understand. In that case, let's form a volunteer Chinese localization group! Let's give him a hand—it would essentially be division of labor and collaboration—and at the same time help CodeWhale the big whale swim even further!

Everyone who wants to contribute to CodeWhale but feels at a loss about where to start is welcome—the path is right here!

Long live open-source! Long live collaboration! Long live sharing! Long live knowledge!

> If you're interested, please add my QQ: 2163018547 (彁) and mention your purpose.

`web/`'s public tool-surface contract fails against the current working tree:

```
$ cd web && npm test
FAIL  lib/public-surface-contract.test.ts > public surface contracts > keeps public tool facts aligned with the native core and discovery boundaries
AssertionError: expected [ 'read', 'write', 'edit', …(8) ] to deeply equal [ 'read', 'write', 'edit', …(9) ]
- "file_search"      ← in DEFAULT_ACTIVE_NATIVE_TOOLS, missing from docs/public-surface-facts.json
Test Files  1 failed | 73 passed (74)
Tests       1 failed | 771 passed (772)
```

`web/lib/public-surface-contract.test.ts:432` pins `docs/public-surface-facts.json` → `toolSurface.defaultActive` to the names parsed from `DEFAULT_ACTIVE_NATIVE_TOOLS` in `crates/tui/src/core/engine/tool_catalog.rs`. The guard is behaving exactly as designed.

## Cause

The in-flight promotion of `file_search` to default-active (`crates/tui/src/core/engine/tool_catalog.rs:54`, between `edit` and `bash`) has not moved the public rows with it. Committed `main` (643b724d9; Web Frontend green at that SHA) is consistent at eleven names on both sides, so this is not a broken main: it is the landing checklist for that promotion.

## Rows that must move in the same slice

- `crates/tui/src/core/engine/tests/test_cases_10.rs:3` — `EXPECTED_NATIVE: [&str; 11]` is still the eleven-name literal; the Rust guard fails by construction against the same change
- `docs/public-surface-facts.json` — `toolSurface.defaultActive` (compared exactly, order included)
- `docs/TOOL_SURFACE.md` — "eleven eager native names" (lines 22, 37), the numbered list, and the receipt line (353)

`.github/workflows/web.yml` runs `npm test` and `npm run check` on every push. Landing the native-side promotion without the rows above turns the Web Frontend gate red.

**What happened (2026-10-08, 0.10.2 CI).** The version bump to 0.10.2 left two artifacts stamped 0.10.1, and the Ubuntu test job failed on both:

- `route::export::tests::golden_providers_export_matches_registry` — `providers-export.golden.json is stamped 0.10.1; regenerate with: WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p codewhale-config --lib -- --ignored write_golden_providers_export_when_requested` (`crates/config/src/route/providers-export.golden.json`)
- `commands::contract::config_policy_baseline::status_public_output_and_read_only_state_match_baseline` — `public command baseline status`: left `codewhale 0.10.2` vs right `codewhale 0.10.1` (`crates/tui/src/commands/contract/fixtures/config_policy/status.json`)

**Why the local gate missed it.** The pre-push gate's nextest filters do not cover either test — `nextest-small` covers `codewhale-localization` + `codewhale-command-contract`, and `nextest-tui` runs a per-area filter that excludes `route::export::` and `commands::contract::config_policy_baseline` — while `check-versions.sh` reports `Version state OK` with both fixtures stale. The cost lands as a full CI round (macOS suite ≈ 2h40m).

**Proposal.**
- Extend `scripts/release/check-versions.sh` (runs in the CI `versions` job on every push/PR) with cheap checks that each version-stamped fixture matches the workspace version: `providers-export.golden.json` → `runtimeVersion`, `config_policy/status.json` → the `codewhale X.Y.Z` first line.
- And/or have `prepare-release.sh` rewrite both during the bump.
- Broaden the local pre-push gate so it exercises both tests before a push.

0.10.2 carries the corrected files; this is the guard that keeps the next bump from rediscovering the same failure in CI.

issues.title: Workflow: a verify gate whose blocks_role names its own role deadlocks the run instead of failing at plan admission

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: workflow-runtime
labels.description: Workflow IR, executor, control flow, and replay runtime

issues.body:
## What happened

A phased Workflow run died before its most expensive phase could start:

```
Error: script error: Error: spawn rejected: workflow gate blocks role `implement`: waiting for required gate outcome
```

The plan declared one verify gate to grade the implement phase:

```js
gates: [{
  id: "v1",
  gate: "verify",
  on: "role_complete",
  role: "implement",
  blocks_role: "implement",   // <-- the deadlock
  on_fail: "escalate",
  max_retries: 1,
  require_explicit_verdict: true,
}]
```

`blocks_role` means "this role may not start until the gate passes". Naming the
gated role itself means the phase waits for an outcome that can only exist
after the phase it is holding back. The run ended `Failed` with
`dispatch_failure_count: 1`, and the implement phase produced nothing.

The plan also routed `verify` as a later phase, so the intent was obviously
"gate implement, then run verify" — the mistake is easy to make because
`role` and `blocks_role` sit next to each other in the schema and, for a
single-gate plan, read as near-synonyms. `require_explicit_verdict: true`
makes it likelier, since the author is thinking about the verdict rather than
the dependency edge.

## Why it is worth fixing rather than documenting

- The error names a **role**, not the cause. Nothing in it says the gate's
  own `role` equals its `blocks_role`; the reader has to know the semantics to
  decode it.
- It is **deterministic**: re-launching the identical plan reproduces it, so a
  retry spends the same tokens to fail the same way.
- The **cost lands on the phase that never ran**. Earlier phases return their
  results and are salvageable; the blocked phase silently contributes nothing,
  and a harness that reports "3 of 4 agents finished" can read as partial
  success.
- The gate cannot ever pass, so this is a *static* contradiction — exactly the
  class of thing that should be rejected at compile/admission time rather than
  discovered after the earlier phases have burned their budget.

## Suggested direction

1. **Reject it at admission.** When compiling or admitting the plan, if a gate
   has `on: role_complete` with `role: X` and `blocks_role: X`, fail with a
   message that states the contradiction ("a gate cannot block the role whose
   completion triggers it; block a later role"). This turns a mid-run `Failed`
   into a pre-dispatch plan error.
2. **Say it in the rejection.** Name both fields and the phase order the plan
   actually declares, so the fix is mechanical.
3. **Cross-check against the phase schedule.** If the plan declares ordered
   phases, a `blocks_role` that names a role in an *earlier or equal* phase is
   suspicious even when it is not literally the same role.

## Acceptance

- A plan with `role == blocks_role` fails before any child is dispatched, with
  a message naming the contradiction.
- The existing valid shape (gate an early role, block a later one) still
  compiles and runs.
- A regression fixture covers both, using the plan JSON above as the failing
  case.

## Evidence

Run report: `.codewhale/reports/workflow_d8a733a6.md` — `status: Failed`,
`dispatch_failure_count: 1`, phases `localize` (completed, results returned),
`implement` (dispatch failed), `verify` (never reached). The localize phase had
already proven that no implementation work was needed, so this particular run
lost nothing material; the same defect on a plan whose blocked phase *did* have
work would silently drop it.

The broader consolidation issue retains its follow-up scope; private billing migrations and invoice reconciliation are not prerequisites for this repair.

The read-only audit at Engine `c54be26ec8ddcacb0d054831209025b531e605f9` confirmed four remaining defects: sparse provider rows shadow rich metadata; live [models.dev](<http://models.dev>) rates are explicitly rejected; the parser misses current identity/pricing fields; and different consumers use competing readers. Remote fetching, bounded caching and generated offline seed support already exist. Recheck drift and continue rather than restarting that investigation. Preserve the active implementer's claimed paths and progress below. This checklist is requested work, not evidence of implementation or acceptance.

### Implementation checklist

- [ ] Establish a reproducible baseline and claim the existing work.

  Work in canonical main. Coordinate dirty files before editing. Compare relevant stranded changes by content against main before recovering anything; preserve backups and inventory, and never use an old checkout as a new development lane. Use the Core execution plan and codewhale-hq/Codewhale#6396 for ownership/evidence. Capture one fetched catalog with timestamp/hash and the matching Codewhale raw JSON/list/picker/runtime outputs. Record the actual provider/endpoint/auth mode and active config overrides without secrets. This gives an exact before/after comparison without depending on a changing upstream website.
- [ ] Define which facts each source owns.

  [Models.dev](<http://Models.dev>) supplies public model facts and provider-offering specifications/prices. The selected provider/account supplies actual access, route identity and any account-specific metadata. Explicit Codewhale configuration supplies user overrides and effective operating settings. Preserve these distinctions within one resolver: a catalog listing is not proof the account can call the model, and a published price is not an invoice. Keep supported, configured, available, deprecated and unknown states distinct. Do not automatically switch the selected model, account or billing route when a catalog refreshes.
- [ ] Parse the generated upstream schema completely for the features Codewhale uses.

  Read the combined catalog, including canonical models and provider offerings. Consume `canonical_model_id` from generated JSON, retaining legacy `base_model` compatibility where needed and rejecting conflicting identity claims rather than guessing. Preserve display names/families, distinct context/input/output limits, capability booleans, modalities, reasoning controls, interleaving, lifecycle status, provider/model transport hints and pricing structure. Preserve descriptive metadata needed by existing views; unknown optional fields must not break all ingestion. The generated provider row already incorporates upstream inheritance and overrides: do not reconstruct a different result or refill intentionally removed fields. Invalid required values must produce a bounded visible diagnostic rather than silently erasing the entire previous good catalog.

  Owner: `crates/config/src/models_dev.rs` and its projection in `crates/config/src/catalog.rs`. Several fields parse today but are lost in downstream projection, so follow each required field to the final consumer. References: [current upstream schema](<https://github.com/anomalyco/models.dev/blob/dev/packages/core/src/schema.ts>) and [API/identity/inheritance documentation](<https://github.com/anomalyco/models.dev#api>).
- [ ] Correct model identity and availability joins.

  Keep canonical model ID separate from the exact provider wire ID sent on a request. Normalize provider aliases consistently and preserve distinct endpoint/account/auth scopes. Use explicit upstream canonical relationships instead of name prefixes, family guesses or flattening gateway IDs. Same-named models on direct Anthropic, a gateway and a custom endpoint can have different limits and rates. Metadata-only entries may be shown in discovery without inventing a callable route. Check pagination and completeness of provider discovery before absence in a response is treated as removal; preserve configured custom models through existing explicit policy.
- [ ] Replace whole-row shadowing with field-aware resolution.

  An ID-only provider response states that a model exists; it does not state that context, capabilities and prices became unknown. Enrich that row from the exact compatible [models.dev](<http://models.dev>) provider offering. Preserve explicit provider values, false, zero and empty values with meaningful upstream semantics; fill only genuine absence. Scope signed corrections and user overrides to the facts/routes they actually name. Track where each resolved fact came from so a provider roster cannot relabel a [models.dev](<http://models.dev>) price as provider-confirmed.

  Repair both merged-list and exact-route paths in `crates/tui/src/provider_lake.rs`, plus any used `CatalogCompiler::compile` path in `crates/config/src/catalog.rs`. Both currently insert whole rows. Keep the source of ID-only offerings in `crates/tui/src/client.rs` honest; do not replace missing provider facts with invented defaults there. A single resolver should own this merge rule wherever consumed.
- [ ] Accept live [models.dev](<http://models.dev>) rates as published-price estimates.

  Remove the blanket capabilities-only rejection in `crates/tui/src/pricing.rs`. Its current `verified_catalog_offering` path replaces live [models.dev](<http://models.dev>) pricing with bundled rates or strips it. Update existing assertions that demand that obsolete behavior. Live catalog rates should refresh displayed estimates; Codewhale-managed billable rates, provider-reported charge receipts, enterprise terms and subscription quotas retain their own explicitly identified basis. Missing price is unknown, not free. An unpriced portion must not disappear from a total presented as complete.
- [ ] Preserve and evaluate the actual price structure.

  Support input/output, cache read/write, context tiers and relevant separately priced reasoning/audio token classes. Normalize the legacy `context_over_200k` representation with `tiers` when encountered, without counting both. Apply the tier threshold and usage definitions for the actual serving route. Do not silently flatten an unsupported tier/mode into the cheapest base rate; make the unsupported estimate explicit. Preserve provider-specific schedules and pricing modes already supported, instead of losing them in the merge. Avoid double-counting cached input or reasoning tokens that are subsets of total output.

  Reuse `crates/config/src/pricing.rs` for a shared quote calculation, with precise amounts/rounding and explicit currency/units; retire duplicate TUI calculations as their last consumers migrate. Four optional f64 fields in `ModelsDevCost` cannot express the upstream pricing structure. Do not introduce another parallel quote engine. Preserve sufficiently small rates without rounding them to zero.
- [ ] Make price freshness and history truthful.

  Distinguish source fetch time, upstream update metadata, any actual rate effective time and cache expiry. A fresh download alone is not an invoice verification or a provider's declared effective date. Show whether a current estimate is live, cached, stale or unavailable. Keep offline facts available under an explicit fallback policy; do not silently advertise an expired fallback price as current. Persist the quote used for each dispatch in the existing receipt path. Never apply today's refreshed rate retroactively to old usage or discard authoritative historical amounts.
- [ ] Fix context/output budgeting through the entire runtime.

  Use resolved limits for the picker, request validation, output ceiling, compaction and context percentage. Preserve advertised context, separate max input/output, configured output budget and effective usable context as distinct values. Respect explicit user/route overrides and any applicable endpoint constraint. When effective capacity is smaller than the catalog maximum, show the reason. Remove stale hardcoded fallbacks where an actual fact exists. For genuinely unknown limits, preserve a labeled conservative policy rather than presenting a guess as a published maximum. Do not set every Claude model to 1M: the dated snapshot includes both 1M models and Haiku 4.5 at 200K.

  Trace `crates/tui/src/config.rs`, `crates/models/src/lib.rs`, `crates/config/src/catalog/reviewed.rs`, route-budget/compaction consumers and the picker/footer. A correct picker number with an old runtime denominator does not complete the repair.
- [ ] Fix capability labels and request settings together.

  Distinguish reasoning supported, unsupported and unknown from the current reasoning selection. Preserve supported toggle/effort/token-budget options and their actual values; do not collapse every provider into one low/medium/high set. Display unknown as unknown, not “off”. Make supported tools, image/file/audio/video input, structured output and temperature controls agree with the resolved offering and Codewhale's implemented transport. Only send parameters the selected route supports. Preserve prior user settings when valid, explaining a now-invalid setting rather than silently changing route or account.
- [ ] Make every relevant consumer use the same resolved facts.

  Cover both `codewhale models` and `codewhale model list`, model resolve/set, the TUI picker/detail views, defaults/fallback selection, runtime planning/compaction, parent and delegated model selection, status/usage/cost views, and Engine API/client projections. The singular CLI command still constructs `ModelRegistry::default()`, while other paths consume the provider lake. Remove separate live-ignorant decisions in agent ModelInfo, bundled intrinsic helpers, constants and generated web facts as their consumers migrate. Keep exact user-selected model IDs and existing persisted config/session compatibility. Do not build a resolver with one caller and leave the rest on the old system.
- [ ] Complete refresh, persistence and offline behavior without adding another fetcher.

  Reuse `crates/tui/src/models_dev_live.rs`: it already supplies background fetching, TTL, bounded responses, disk caching and atomic writes. Ensure all catalog entry points initialize/use it consistently; successful refresh invalidates every derived snapshot and visible projection. Provide a working explicit refresh/retry action through existing controls. Keep input responsive, avoid per-card network requests and repeated parsing, and preserve the last good snapshot on timeout/parse failure. Handle old cache formats through the existing migration/invalidating path; do not tell the user to delete all configuration or credentials. Check source override isolation, empty/partial responses and restart persistence. Pin each active request to coherent facts while allowing later requests to see new metadata.
- [ ] Regenerate the fallback and remove catalog drift.

  Use the existing generated offline seed pipeline from [models.dev](<http://models.dev>); do not paste new model values into Rust match arms. Ensure its documented coverage meets supported cold-start behavior and does not accidentally freeze an obsolete six-model list. Keep any seed-size subset intentional and visible. Shrink `catalog_corrections.json` and other local overrides to current, sourced exceptions. Data-only corrections belong upstream when practical; transport/account policy belongs in Codewhale. Unknown new providers may be discoverable without claiming an unimplemented transport is callable. Existing supported providers should gain new model facts through data refresh, without another binary release.
- [ ] Make mismatches explainable and verify the finished behavior.

  Through existing model detail/diagnostic output, expose the selected provider and exact wire ID, canonical ID, relevant source/fetch time, config override, effective limit and price basis. Keep the ordinary picker compact. Produce a bounded comparison of one upstream snapshot against resolved Codewhale output; every difference must be an explicit route/config/policy difference or an identified defect. This is a direct verification artifact, not a new permanent audit service.

  Required checks: Anthropic ID-only refresh retaining its metadata; current 1M rows and a 200K control; reasoning unknown versus disabled; cache/tier-edge estimates; a gateway override and custom endpoint with the same model spelling; a subscription route with no fabricated per-token bill; refresh during use; offline first start; stale/corrupt cache; historical cost stability; consistent values across both CLIs, picker, context usage and Engine API. Verify that model changes reach the installed candidate and that responsiveness/idle CPU do not regress. Run existing focused checks, update obsolete expectations and run required repository gates. Add no new unit/integration tests or code comments without an explicit task request. Report real nonzero counts; direct execution, tests, provider acceptance and installed behavior are separate evidence.

### 0.10.2 acceptance and handoff

- [ ] Capture one catalog snapshot with timestamp/hash and compare the same provider/endpoint/model against Codewhale before and after. Explain every remaining mismatch.
- [ ] Demonstrate that an Anthropic ID-only refresh retains prices, context, output limits and capabilities; both CLI model commands, picker, runtime context usage and Engine API agree.
- [ ] Demonstrate tier/cache pricing, supported versus enabled reasoning, route/account isolation, offline/stale/corrupt-cache behavior and frozen historical costs.
- [ ] Qualify the installed candidate with exact source identity, installed version/hash, actual nonzero existing-check counts and responsiveness evidence. Do not infer provider/invoice/physical-terminal acceptance from unit checks.
- [ ] Update existing help/feature/release documentation and this issue's evidence; clearly identify the completed 0.10.2 slice and broader consolidation work still open.

Use canonical `codewhale` on `main` under the current workspace instructions; preserve peer changes and reconcile older checkout work before editing. Do not add new unit/integration tests or code comments without explicit task authorization; run existing checks and update obsolete expectations. Config pricing is currently floating-point: reuse its provenance/quote ownership while correcting precision, rather than assuming an exact-money implementation already exists.

The related [ChatGPT authorization repair #6925](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6925>), [xAI authentication inspection #6926](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6926>), responsiveness and every-shell inspection work remain separate active requirements; this checklist does not replace them. Release visibility: [0.10.2 planning tracker #6094](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6094>).

---

## Earlier scope, implementation history and active ownership

> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): partly done. Filed against 0.10.0 (filed 2026-09-22, the day v0.10.0 was tagged; body cites 0.10.0 commit 2dca7fcdda).
>
> **What remains**
>
> * Pricing: fold crates/tui/src/pricing.rs (5,888 lines, f64) into the provenance model in crates/config/src/pricing.rs - integer micros, sourceRef/checkedAt/expiresAt per rate, one quote function, golden vectors for DeepSeek time-of-day and tier edges
> * Catalog: move aliases and supports_tools out of crates/agent/src/lib.rs ModelInfo into the catalog; retire the remaining match tables in crates/models/src/lib.rs and the consts in crates/config/src/provider_defaults.rs
> * Reconcile the three price authorities (TUI [pricing.rs](<http://pricing.rs>), platform rate cards, cwc_usage_rate_cards) and diff rates against real provider invoices
> * Upstream thin vendors (AICraft, MiMo, SenseNova, StepFun, DashScope, command-code) to [models.dev](<http://models.dev>) and shrink crates/config/assets/catalog_corrections.json accordingly
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
>
> * Slice A done: crates/config/src/catalog.rs:448-487 at v0.10.1 enumerates namespaced top-level `catalog.models` keys as offerings after provider rows (comment cites #6396)
> * Slice B done: commits cbfbcb699c 'upstream-keyed canonical entries join offline (#6396 slice B)', 6227825dd7 'generate the offline seed from a reviewed spec and a lock', cd5e643512 'regenerate the offline seed from [Models.dev](<http://Models.dev>)'; CHANGELOG.md:834-841 'The offline model list is now generated from [Models.dev](<http://Models.dev>) instead of edited by hand'
> * Bundled seed now carries upstream-shaped keys: crates/config/assets/models_dev.bundled.json at v0.10.1 has models keys xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro and xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-flash plus `_meta`/`_reviewed`
> * Slice C partly done: `git grep -w ApiProvider v0.10.1 -- crates` matches only a test-local enum (crates/tui/src/config/tests.rs:16519) and `git grep KIND_LOOKUP v0.10.1` is empty; crates/models/assets/model_catalog.bundled.json no longer exists; crates/tui/src/config/models.rs is down to 34 lines / 6 consts
> * Slice C still open: crates/agent/src/lib.rs:29-35 still owns ModelInfo aliases (21 supports_tools hits); crates/tui/src/pricing.rs is still 5,888 lines; crates/config/src/provider_defaults.rs and web/lib/facts.generated.ts still exist
> * Pricing partly done: unknown-is-a-value exists as UnpricedReason (crates/tui/src/pricing.rs:1197) and provenance-carrying rows in crates/config/src/pricing.rs:1-19, but [pricing.rs](<http://pricing.rs>) still has 56 f64 lines and there are two Rust pricing modules; CHANGELOG.md:823-833 and :842-845 record the 0.10.1 price corrections

---

Supersedes #4173, which was opened from a 2026-07 architecture doc with counts that have since drifted (it says 81 models / 31 providers; both are now far larger). Its acceptance criterion was "there is an inventory of which registries are product contracts vs generated/catalog data vs internal implementation." That inventory now exists and is below, so the old issue is closed in favour of this scoped one.

## Root cause, verified

`offerings_from_models_dev` (`crates/config/src/catalog.rs:344`) enumerates catalog offerings from `catalog.providers[*].models` **only**.

[models.dev](<http://models.dev>) deliberately splits facts *about a model* from facts *about a provider serving it*. We implemented one half. A model that exists only in the top-level `models` map therefore produces no offering and can never be listed — so we are structurally late for **every** vendor, not just the one that surfaced it.

Two precisions worth recording, because they change the fix:

1. The top-level map is not entirely unread — `crates/config/src/models_dev.rs:86` reads it for reasoning-support enrichment. The defect is in *enumeration*, not deserialization. The fix is "enumerate from the union", not "read a field nobody reads".
2. `ModelsDevModel` (`models_dev.rs:199`) carries **no provider field** — `id`, `name`, `family`, capabilities, `limit`, `modalities`, and nothing naming who serves it. The join must therefore come from the map key (`xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro`). That works against live upstream data, but our bundled snapshot keys models bare (its only two entries are `deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek-v4-flash`). So the ingestion fix alone does **not** repair offline/first-boot until `crates/config/assets/models_dev.bundled.json` is regenerated in upstream shape.

Consequence for 0.10.0: commit `2dca7fcdda` (hand-seeded MiMo 2.6 rows) is a human doing the join the code refuses to do, and it stays load-bearing for cold offline start. Retire it when the seed is regenerated, not when the ingestion fix lands.

## Inventory: seven independent declarations of the same model facts

<!-- linear:table-colwidths:266,266,266 -->
| \# | Source | Size |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | `crates/models/src/lib.rs` match tables | \~150 ids |
| 2 | `crates/models/assets/model_catalog.bundled.json` | 56 entries |
| 3 | `crates/config/assets/models_dev.bundled.json` | 99 rows / 21 providers |
| 4 | `crates/agent/src/lib.rs` `ModelInfo` | 155 entries — the only home for aliases + `supports_tools` |
| 5 | `crates/config/src/provider_defaults.rs` | 169 consts, duplicated verbatim in `crates/tui/src/config/models.rs` |
| 6 | `crates/tui/src/pricing.rs` | 5,920 lines, 287 price match arms |
| 7 | `web/lib/facts.generated.ts` | 50 providers / 77 models |

Plus two parallel provider enums — `ProviderKind` (52) and `ApiProvider` (53) — bridged by a fixed-size `KIND_LOOKUP: [_; 53]` in `crates/tui/src/config.rs`.

Adding one provider today costs \~14 hand edits across `provider_kind.rs`, `provider.rs`, `lib.rs`, the TUI enum and that fixed-size array. That cost is why vendors go missing: adding one is a code change, so it competes with feature work and loses.

## Slices

**A — model-only ingestion.** Enumerate offerings from the union of `providers[*].models` and namespaced top-level `models` keys. \~30 lines plus a test. Stops every vendor being late. Land first, independent of everything else.

**B — regenerate the offline seed in upstream key shape**, so A also fixes cold start, then retire the hand-seeded rows.

**C — collapse to one authority.** Migrate the last consumer of each of the seven, deleting as you go; move aliases + `supports_tools` out of `crates/agent` into the catalog (their only home today); collapse `ApiProvider` into `ProviderKind` so `KIND_LOOKUP` dies. Large blast radius — exhaustive matches across two crates — so it is deliberately not a release-window change.

**D — upstream the thin vendors to [models.dev](<http://models.dev>)** (AICraft, MiMo, SenseNova, StepFun, DashScope, command-code). It is a public repo; the live refresh then picks them up with no infrastructure, and every other tool benefits. Keep a local overlay only for what [models.dev](<http://models.dev>) structurally cannot carry: transport facts and prices we bill against.

## Pricing: hold it to billing standard before billing exists

Display-only today, but `PRODUCT_PRD.md:220` commits to "an evidence-backed model catalog". A wrong cost number is a false product claim regardless of whether money moves.

There are currently **three** pricing authorities: `pricing.rs` (display), the platform rate cards (`CWC_MANAGED_MODEL_RATE_CARDS_JSON`), and `cwc_usage_rate_cards` (Postgres). When they disagree we show one number and would charge another. Managed inference is gated off today, so fixing the divergence now costs nothing; after it is enabled it means migrating historical charges.

The rate-card shape in `wrangler.jsonc` is already the professional one — `revision`, `sourceRef`, `pricingPolicy`, `checkedAt`, `expiresAt`, integer micros, customer vs provider rates, `CWC_RATE_CARD_MAX_AGE_DAYS`. The work is propagating it, not inventing it:

1. Integer micros end to end, never `f64`.
2. `sourceRef` / `checkedAt` / `expiresAt` on every rate; past expiry reads unpriced, never stale-priced.
3. Unknown is a value, not zero — `Quote::Unpriced { reason }` as a type, so no surface can render a guess as `$0.00`. The MiMo seed already gets this right in data; make it unrepresentable to get wrong.
4. Separate rate data (catalog rows) from billing-surface detection (credential logic, stays local) from rate rules (time-of-day, context tiers) as a few typed variants over data rather than 287 arms.
5. Freeze the quote at dispatch and persist it in the receipt; a later refresh must never reprice history. Already correct on the cloud-facts path — generalize it.
6. One quote function, one stated rounding rule, an audit trail per number.
7. Golden vectors: `(route, usage, timestamp)` → exact amount, covering the DeepSeek time-of-day windows and the 512k/272k/200k tier edges.
8. **Reconcile against real invoices.** The evidence file records invoice reconciliation as "unqualified". 287 arms nobody has diffed against a bill are 287 guesses, however tidy. This is the only item that needs something we do not already have, and it is the one that separates professional from merely organized.

Items 1–7 are engineering. Item 8 is ground truth, and no amount of 1–7 substitutes for it.

2026-10-08 Codex /root takeover (local 0.10.2 candidate, no push): claimed crates/config/src/{models_dev.rs,[catalog.rs](<http://catalog.rs>),[pricing.rs](<http://pricing.rs>)}, existing related tests/literals, crates/tui/src/{provider_lake.rs,provider_catalog_live.rs,[pricing.rs](<http://pricing.rs>),tui/model_picker.rs}, and crates/cli/src/lib.rs for current [models.dev](<http://models.dev>) schema, sparse-roster completion, scoped/frozen estimates, and CLI agreement. Source confirms config pricing is currently floating-point; the earlier handoff's claim of an existing exact-money implementation was inaccurate. Broader invoice and managed-billing consolidation remains open. No new test cases or code comments under current operator instructions; existing cases will be adapted where behavior changes.

issues.title: codewhale resume refuses any session whose saved history still holds a raw sub-agent handoff — the canonical acknowledgement compares the Engine-restored messages with the saved document
issues.body:
# Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

Searched open and closed in this repository: `"mailbox acknowledgement"` → 0,
`"selected saved history"` → 0, `"exceeds full-history"` → 0, `"retained outcome"`
→ 6 unrelated results (release and PR titles). Closest reports, each a different
mechanism: #6102 (closed — resume failed with ENOENT while resolving the runtime
store dir), #6225 (closed) and #6418 (closed) — older "cannot restore/resume"
reports. None of them mention this comparison.

# What happened?

`codewhale resume <id>` fails deterministically for a saved session, and no
retry or recovery route works:

```
$ codewhale resume f5ba9347-…
error: canonical history operation mounted-history:48204ec8-…; retained outcome must be recovered using this exact key
  caused by: canonical history mailbox acknowledgement changed
```

Expected: the session resumes. The suggested recovery ("retained outcome must be
recovered using this exact key") cannot succeed, because the recovery path runs
the same acknowledgement: `settle_prepared_history_operation` also calls
`synchronize_history_operation` (`crates/tui/src/runtime_api/thread_history.rs:1032`;
the fresh path is `:1663`).

# Steps to reproduce

1. In a project, run `codewhale` and have the session spawn a sub-agent (the
   `agent` tool) so a `subagent_completion` handoff is appended to the live
   history. Let the turn end and quit.
2. Confirm the saved document still holds the RAW envelope: the message has
   exactly two text blocks, block 2 is exactly
   `<turn_meta>\nInput provenance: subagent_handoff (non-authoritative)\n</turn_meta>`
   and block 1 starts with `<codewhale:runtime_event kind="subagent_completion"
   visibility="internal">` (`crates/tui/src/runtime_handoff.rs:15`).
3. `codewhale resume <id>` → the error above.

Observed on a 351-message, 3.97 MB session with 5 such envelopes: every attempt
failed. After neutralising the recognition of those 5 messages in the saved data
(renaming the transport tag so the restore projection becomes a no-op), the same
command resumed normally and printed `Resumed session: …`.

# Codewhale version

`codewhale 0.10.1 (dev)`, built from a git checkout. Still present on `main`
(today): `synchronize_history_operation` is unchanged at
`crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs`.

# Where did it happen?

- TUI (terminal interface)
- CLI command (`codewhale resume`, `codewhale fork`)

# Operating system

Linux

# How did you get Codewhale?

Built from a git checkout

# Provider and model

custom openai-compatible route (does not matter — the failure is before any provider call)

# Terminal and shell

tmux + fish

# codewhale doctor (optional)

Not run for this report; the refusal happens in the resume preflight, before the
TUI starts, and leaves no log line in `~/.codewhale/logs/`.

# Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

Written from reading `main` (not a guess at the cause):

- `RuntimeThreadManager::synchronize_history_operation`
  (`crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs:11684`) sends `Op::SyncSession` and then
  requires `observed.messages == session.messages` (`:11708`-`:11713`), i.e. the
  Engine's post-restore messages must equal the saved document byte for byte.
- The Engine's restore first replaces every live sub-agent handoff with a
  restored checkpoint: `Engine::restore_session_history`
  (`crates/tui/src/core/engine.rs:2931`) calls
  `runtime_handoff::project_owned_messages_for_restore`
  (`:2959` → `crates/tui/src/runtime_handoff.rs:918`,
  rewrite decision in `rewrite_message_for_restore`, `:927`, recognition in
  `raw_runtime_handoff_text`, `:1042`).
- So the two sides are structurally different objects whenever the saved
  document still holds a raw envelope, and the equality can never hold. The
  document only becomes "projected" after a *successful* restore persists it,
  which is exactly the step this check forbids — the first canonical resume of a
  session that used sub-agents is the failing case.

Suggested fix directions (maintainer's call):

- **A. Make the acknowledgement projection-aware.** Compare against
  `project_owned_messages_for_restore(session.messages.clone())` (plus the
  compaction checkpoint step `compaction::restore_compaction_checkpoint`, to
  mirror `restore_session_history` exactly). The same codebase already does this
  for the sibling rollback check: `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/apply.rs:1406` projects
  `.messages` before demanding that the Engine acknowledged them.
- **B. Persist the projected form** so a saved document is always in the form a
  restore produces (bigger change; it would drop raw envelopes from saved
  sessions earlier than today).

Related, found while recovering this session: a refused canonical attempt still
publishes a holder thread plus an uncommitted turn operation in the Runtime
store. Once the document is repaired, the next attempt then stalls on the holder
checkpoint (`saved holder checkpoint differs from the saved history; refresh
history`, `crates/tui/src/runtime_api/thread_history.rs:1255`) and, with the
checkpoint refreshed, on `saved holder has a successor outside the selected
document` (`:1281`) — the holder fingerprints the pre-repair bytes. A refused
attempt could avoid publishing a holder, or the repair path could refresh it.

Done when:

- [ ] a saved session whose history still contains a raw `subagent_completion`
      (or `subagent_failed` / `waiting_for_subagents` / `agent_topology`)
      envelope resumes through the canonical path;
- [ ] `codewhale fork` works for the same session;
- [ ] the acknowledgement still refuses a genuinely changed history (an Engine
      that did not install the document), i.e. the check is not simply removed;
- [ ] a regression test in `crates/tui/src/lib.rs` (`mod mounted_history_tests`)
      saves a fixture session containing one raw handoff envelope and asserts the
      mounted resume succeeds.

Verification:

```sh
scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-tui --lib
scripts/dev-test.sh crates/tui/src/lib.rs mounted_history_tests::
```

Out of scope:

- The sub-agent handoff wire format and the restore rendering itself.
- The size bound on the saved document (separate report).

issues.title: A saved session document larger than 8 MiB can no longer be resumed or forked, and the refusal names no remedy — the journal is what pushes it over
issues.body:
# Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

Searched open and closed for: `"transport bound"`, `"exceeds full-history"`,
session document size limit, resume + size, journal + resume. Closest matches:

- **#6842** (open) — the session journal has no bound and grows without limit.
  That is the growth side of the same structure; this report is the *access*
  side: once the file crosses a hard 8 MiB transport bound, the session can no
  longer be opened at all.
- **#6688** (closed) — same class (an oversized input is refused before anything
  runs), different path (`exec` argv vs the session document).
- #6161, #6175, #6361 — unrelated changes that only matched the search terms.

# What happened?

```
$ codewhale resume 481c2659-…
error: selected saved history could not be captured; no mutation attempted
  caused by: session exceeds full-history transport bound; source retained
```

The source is retained (good), but there is no way forward. `codewhale fork`
refuses the same way, and I could not find any CLI path that reduces a saved
document: `codewhale --help` lists no prune/compact command, and `codewhale thread`
offers only list/read/resume/fork/archive/set-name/clear-name. The message does
not name the size, the field that dominates it, or any remedy.

Measured on the affected session (the file is 13 982 336 bytes against an 8 MiB
bound, i.e. 8 388 608 bytes):

| part of the document | size (approx, as serialized in the file) |
|---|---|
| whole file | 13.98 MB |
| `journal.entries` (3870 entries) | 8.96 MB |
| `messages` (1361 messages) | 2.96 MB |
| `work_state` / `metadata` | 0.38 MB / 0.13 MB |

The conversation itself is well inside the bound. Only the 1361 journal entries
on the active leaf path are projected into messages
(`crates/runtime/src/session_tree.rs:262`, `:329`); the remaining 2509 entries
are abandoned branches — yet the whole document has to fit.

# Steps to reproduce

The check is a plain file-size comparison, so any saved document over the bound
reproduces it deterministically; I did not build a synthetic one, my numbers are
from a real session (a long session with heavy sub-agent use, which is what grows
the journal — see #6842).

1. `stat -c%s ~/.codewhale/sessions/<id>.json` — compare against 8 388 608.
2. `codewhale resume <id>` (and `codewhale fork <id>`) → the error above.

Code path, read from `main`:

- `prepare_mounted_session` reads the source with
  `load_session_snapshot_bounded(&id, MAX_CANONICAL_HISTORY_BYTES)`
  (`crates/tui/src/lib.rs:9943`). Every `codewhale resume` goes through this
  (`run_interactive_with_notice`).
- The read refuses before parsing when the *file* is larger than the limit:
  `crates/tui/src/session_manager.rs:3406`
  ("session exceeds full-history transport bound; source retained").
- `MAX_CANONICAL_HISTORY_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024`
  (`crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:79`; the entry-count sibling is at `:78`).
- The same constant bounds the serialized mutation request, which embeds the
  whole document as JSON: `crates/tui/src/runtime_api/thread_history.rs:221` —
  so raising only the read would not be enough; the transport itself is bounded.

Recovery that worked by hand (and is what a supported path would need to do):
keeping only the active leaf path in `journal.entries` took the file from
13.98 MB to 7.61 MB and the session resumed. It costs the abandoned branches'
structure (`/branch` history), which is why it should be an explicit,
maintainer-designed operation rather than a user's manual surgery. The same
operation is not the only lever — any bound change has to keep the request under
the same limit, because the document travels inside it.

# Codewhale version

`codewhale 0.10.1 (dev)`, built from a git checkout. Still present on `main`
today (`MAX_CANONICAL_HISTORY_BYTES` is unchanged).

# Where did it happen?

- CLI command (`codewhale resume`, `codewhale fork`)

# Operating system

Linux

# How did you get Codewhale?

Built from a git checkout

# Provider and model

custom openai-compatible route (does not matter — the failure is before any provider call)

# Terminal and shell

tmux + fish

# codewhale doctor (optional)

Not run for this report; the refusal happens in the resume preflight, before the
TUI starts, and leaves no log line in `~/.codewhale/logs/`.

# Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

Impact: the session is readable in files but unreachable from the product; the
only routes left are manual surgery on the JSON or discarding the session.

Options as I see them (maintainer's call):

- **A. Transport only what the operation needs.** The canonical handoff needs
  the messages, the journal witness (leaf + entry count) and the metadata; the
  journal body is copied only because the target document is the source document.
  A host-side rebuild of the target document would remove the journal from the
  payload entirely.
- **B. Make the bound count the projected history, not the file**, or expose it
  as a bounded, documented knob. `messages` here was 2.96 MB of a 13.98 MB file.
- **C. Keep the bound and make the failure actionable**: name the size and the
  dominant field, and provide a supported prune/compact command that drops
  journal entries outside the active path (with a dry run and a backup), so an
  oversized session is recoverable. Also worth a pointer to #6842.

Open questions: is 8 MiB a memory/allocation guard or an API payload guard? Should
a journal that is not projected into messages count against it at all? What is a
user expected to do today when a session crosses it — is discarding the session
the intended outcome?

Verification (for A/B/C, once the direction is chosen):

```sh
scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-tui --lib
scripts/dev-test.sh crates/tui/src/session_manager.rs
```

Out of scope:

- Bounding the journal itself (#6842).
- Changing the conversation, or auto-truncating history on resume.

issues.title: Windows runtime floor blocks read-only piped commands under Full Access, on a native (non-npm) install

labels.name: windows
labels.description: Windows-specific behaviour

issues.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What happened? 发生了什么？

## Summary

Follow-up to #6827. The Windows runtime floor (`SessionRuntimeRisk`, `crates/tui/src/core/authority/auto_review.rs`) refuses ordinary read-only commands that pipe test output, with `UnclassifiedWindowsInvocation`. It does this while the session shows **Full Access**, although the floor's own test says Full Access skips it.

Refused:

```
cd C:\Users\me\repo; .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests\runner -q --tb=line 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 6
cd C:\Users\me\repo\apps\extension; node .\node_modules\vitest\vitest.mjs run 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 30
cd C:\Users\me\repo; .\.venv\Scripts\ruff.exe format .; Write-Output "fmt=$LASTEXITCODE"; .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests\e2e --collect-only -q 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 3
```

Every refusal reads:

> Built-in safety gate requires approval: Windows command input cannot be classified safely enough to exclude termination of Codewhale npm launchers; use a direct PID- or port-specific command.

The same commands without `2>&1 | Select-Object ...` run fine. None of them stops a process.

## Two problems

1. **Full Access does not skip the floor.** `windows_runtime_floor_holds_across_reviewing_postures_but_skips_full_access` (around line 2104) asserts that under `ApprovalMode::Bypass` "Full Access skips the platform hold with the rest of the floor". The TUI status bar shows `Full Access` and `operate`, and the operator and its Fleet sub-agents are still blocked. Either the operate/Fleet posture does not carry `Bypass` into tool review, or sub-agents get a different `ApprovalMode`.
2. **Unparseable means blocked, even for read-only pipelines.** When `command_invocations(command)` returns `None`, `windows_session_runtime_risk_scoped` returns `UnclassifiedWindowsInvocation` (around line 1371). A pipeline into a read-only cmdlet (`Select-Object`, `Select-String`, `Where-Object`, `Format-*`, `Out-String`, `Measure-Object`) with `2>&1` cannot terminate anything, but it is held. Agents use this pattern constantly to trim test output.

3. **The npm-launcher hold fires on a non-npm install.** This machine uses the native installer, so there is no `node.exe` launcher in Codewhale's process tree. Yet the hold's reason is "termination of Codewhale npm launchers". `windows_tool_runtime_risk` does not check the install method, so the floor applies to every Windows install. #6906 already detects npm installs with `codewhale_release::current_install_method()`, and the same check could scope this hold. (A broad `node.exe` kill could still hit *another* npm-launched session on the same machine. That is a narrower risk, and it does not apply to read-only pipelines either way.)

## Impact

In one Fleet run of about 70 minutes (DeepSeek V4 Flash, about 8 workers), one implement sub-agent had 12 refused or failed tool calls out of about 60. 4 were this gate; each refusal costs a model turn while the agent re-plans. The operator hit it repeatedly as well. It is avoidable: the agent can drop the pipe. But every model reaches for this pattern first, so it fails again and again.

## Expected

- Under Full Access, the floor does not apply, as the existing test asserts. Or, if the floor is meant to apply under Full Access in operate/Fleet mode, the test and the docs should say so.
- A pipeline whose stages are all known read-only cmdlets, with stream redirection like `2>&1`, is classified as non-terminating rather than unclassified.

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

1. Windows 11, Codewhale from the native Windows installer (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\CodeWhale\bin\codewhale.exe`, launched through `codewhale.bat`; **not** npm), started from PowerShell in Windows Terminal.
2. Select Full Access and run in operate mode, with Fleet sub-agents.
3. Have the agent run: `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 5` (any command, piped into `Select-Object`).
4. It is refused with the message above. Without `2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 5`, it runs.

### Codewhale version 版本

codewhale 0.10.1 (fead51eeea0f)

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

TUI (terminal interface)

### Operating system 操作系统

Windows

### How did you get Codewhale? 获取方式

GitHub Releases download (native Windows installer)

### Provider and model 提供商和模型

deepseek / deepseek-v4-flash

### Terminal and shell 终端

Windows Terminal + PowerShell 5.1

### codewhale doctor (optional)

_No response_

### Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

- Evidence: `.codewhale/state/subagents.v1.json`, worker events marked `refused or failed`, and checkpoint tool results carrying the safety-gate text.
- Related: #6827 (the original gate), #6906 (agent environment line for the npm launcher), #6011 (tool-call error diagnostics).
- I am happy to send a PR for part 2 (read-only pipeline classification) once the intended Full Access behaviour in part 1 is confirmed.

issues.title: Deferred-toolbox eviction is economically net-negative under provider prompt caching: full-prefix re-prefill + write premiums, permanent stale recovery notes, wire-byte-blind budget
issues.body:
### What happened? 发生了什么？

The bounded deferred-tool toolbox (`ToolActivationCache`, 8 names / 16 KiB, `crates/tui/src/core/session.rs:17-19` at HEAD `008d21d69`) is **cost-blind**, and under current provider prompt-cache pricing its eviction path is economically net-negative. Concretely:

**1. Eviction invalidates the entire downstream prefix — the one toolbox operation with no offsetting benefit.**
The prefix fingerprint is `SHA256(system) + SHA256(tools wire array)` with order load-bearing (`crates/tui/src/prefix_cache.rs`), and tools sit at the front of the rendered prompt on every provider. Any admission/eviction mutates the tools array, so system + tools + the **entire conversation history** re-prefills at miss price. `docs/CACHE.md` calls this "an expected, one-request miss" (lines 39-40) — wording written when cache writes were free:

| Provider/API | Cached-input read | Write premium | Tool-change invalidation |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenAI Chat/Responses | 0.1x | 1.25x (GPT-5.6+) | prefix from that point (tools are first) |
| Anthropic Messages | 0.1x | 1.25x (5m) / 2x (1h) | **any tool change invalidates the entire cache** (tools are block 1) |
| DeepSeek | 1/30 – 1/50 | none | prefix-based |
| Moonshot Kimi k3 | 0.1x | 1x (5m) / 2x (1h) | prefix from that point |

Break-even for evicting one ~400-token schema from a session with H tokens of history: pay ≈ 0.9–2.25 × H once, save ≈ 0.9 × 400 per later request → needs ~75 further tool-free requests at H = 30K. Real conversations run 6–40 requests. Admission at least unlocks a needed capability; **eviction only pays when the session is about to end anyway**. LRU position alone is the eviction trigger today — no hysteresis, no cost term, and two alternating overflowing searches would re-prefill the full prefix every round.

**2. The eviction→recovery cycle multiplies the loss (relevant to the in-flight reporting work).**
Reporting evictions (as the Pinvou fork's open PR #101 does) is necessary for correctness — silent eviction caused a live incident where a model fabricated tool results for tools that had vanished from its `<functions>`. But the recovery contract ("re-search to re-activate") completes a cycle whose full cost stack, for one eviction of 4 browser tools (~460 tokens of schema) in a 30K-token history with 20 requests remaining (0.1x reads, 1.25x writes):

| # | Cost item | Tok-eq |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Eviction invalidation (re-prefill + write premium) | ~34,500 |
| 2 | Eviction note in history (≈72–147 tokens/event; rides the result forever; 1 + 19×0.1x) | ~427 |
| 3 | Recovery re-search round trip | ~3,050 |
| 4 | Search-result payload becomes history | ~1,160 |
| 5 | Re-activation invalidation (tools array changes again — second re-prefill + write) | ~34,500 |
| | **Total vs never evicting** | **≈ 73,600 (~2.5× the entire history)** |

Two structural gaps in the reporting design: (a) **notes are never retracted** — ride-time netting (`render_toolbox_eviction_notes`) only trims the note at the moment it attaches to a result; once in history it is permanent, and the only "compaction" that removes it is generic conversation compaction; (b) **re-activation carries no supersession marker** — the re-admitting search result is byte-identical to a first-time hit (`tool_references` list only), so after recovery the model's history permanently contains "these tools are no longer callable" next to a tools array that has them again. (Compare: the direct-call hydration path does emit an explicit "was deferred and has now been loaded" receipt.)

**3. The headline saving is first-turn-only, and the budget does not measure wire bytes.**
The historical justification ("reduce catalog tokens 73%") measures a first-request, native-tools-only, `bytes/4`-estimated ratio — no provider, no tokenizer, no MCP, caching never modeled. Under caching, both an eager stable header and the deferred header are hit-priced after request 1; the durable steady-state saving is ~0.1x-scale. Separately, the 16 KiB toolbox budget is measured in engine-side serde bytes (`ToolActivationCache::serialized_bytes`), while the same tool serializes differently per wire family (Chat Completions wrapper ~69 B/tool, Anthropic ~40 B, Responses ~71 B) and per-provider sanitizers (Moonshot MFJS, root-level `oneOf/anyOf` flattening) change schemas further — so the budget is a proxy that matches no provider's actual token accounting.

**4. In practice the mechanism survives by accident.**
Across five real sessions on k3/DeepSeek (93–94% hit ratios with heavy `tool_search` churn vs 92.5% baseline without), activation happened at request 1 (short history) and the surface then stayed stable within turns. The measured re-prefill drivers were skill loading and engine restarts — not tool_search. The one live failure (mid-task silent eviction) is exactly the case with no offsetting saving.

### Expected 期望

Surface-change decisions — especially LRU eviction — should be cost-aware or at least cost-attributed, and the eviction-recovery loop should not leave permanent stale statements in history:

1. **Hysteresis / eviction economics**: a minimum activation lifetime, or an eviction cost term once current re-prefill size exceeds a few multiples of the evicted schema. Pure LRU position makes mid-task eviction the default worst case.
2. **Update `docs/CACHE.md`**'s "expected, one-request miss" for the write-premium era, and reconcile observed `cache_hit_tokens`/`cache_miss_tokens` against declared `change:<what>` re-pins — today telemetry and decisions never meet (`calculate_cache_savings` is `#[cfg(test)]`-only).
3. **Supersession semantics for recovery**: when a reported-evicted tool is re-activated, emit an explicit restored/re-admitted marker (hydration-receipt style) so the history's "no longer callable" note is not left as the last word; consider bounding note persistence (e.g. drop after the next successful activation of the named tools, or fold into compaction).
4. **Evaluate append-in-context injection** for dynamic tools (Moonshot's documented pattern: keep the top-level `tools` array stable, append dynamic declarations as a trailing system message inside `messages`) — zero prefix invalidation by construction, which sidesteps items 1 and 5 of the cost stack entirely.
5. **Measure the toolbox budget in wire-shaped bytes** (or tokenizer tokens) per active wire format rather than engine serde bytes.

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

Economic issue rather than a crash; the observable sequence:

1. Start a conversation that activates ≥8 deferred tools (e.g. a browser task: `tool_search` for browser tools, then a second search for page-management tools).
2. Observe the second search silently evicting earlier activations from the request tools array (no model-visible signal at HEAD `008d21d69` — `delta.evicted` is consumed by `remove_evicted_cache_activations` in `execute_tool_search_inner`, `tool_catalog.rs:1546-1551`).
3. Watch `/cache stats` + provider usage: the next request reports a miss covering the full history; on Anthropic routes the write premium applies; re-searching to recover triggers a second full miss + write.
4. Cross-check the arithmetic against `calculate_turn_cost_from_usage_with_prision`-billed totals for the session.

### Codewhale version 版本

`008d21d69` (workspace 0.10.2; latest tag v0.10.1) — verified at this HEAD on 2026-10-13; the mechanism is unchanged from v0.9.12 through HEAD. Observed live via the Pinvou downstream (fork pinned at v0.9.12 + maintenance), engine-level, platform-independent.

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

Engine — affects all surfaces (TUI / CLI / Desktop / Web) and all providers with prefix caching, which in 2026 is all of them.

### Before you start 前置确认

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。（recent 100 issues swept for tool/cache/deferred/eviction — no overlap）

issues.title: Вставка текста отправляется как сообщение без нажатия Enter
issues.body:
Приветствую.

Пишу о дефекте CodeWhale 0.10.0 (сборка 1be1a703b975, Windows, запуск в Windows Terminal). Воспроизводится устойчиво. Разбор — со стороны пользователя: наблюдения и содержимое файлов, внутрь кода я не заглядывал.

ДЕФЕКТ: ВСТАВЛЕННЫЙ ТЕКСТ УХОДИТ КАК СООБЩЕНИЕ БЕЗ ENTER

Что происходит. При вставке многострочного текста в окно CodeWhale текст отправляется как сообщение, хотя Enter не нажат и текст ещё нужно править. Правка до отправки невозможна — сообщение уже ушло.

Обстановка, в которой это наблюдается: Windows Terminal, Windows, CodeWhale 0.10.0, сборка 1be1a703b975.

Что проверено. В двоичном файле приложения (bin/downloads/codewhale.exe, около 100 МБ, установка через npm) механизм вставки блоком присутствует: двенадцать упоминаний bracketed paste, пять упоминаний соответствующего модуля и управляющая последовательность ?2004. То есть приложение этот режим знает и, судя по наличию последовательности, у терминала его запрашивает.

Significantly reduce context overhead

### What should Codewhale do? 希望 Codewhale 怎么做？

https://github.com/yc-duan/fastctx

A significant reduction in token consumption through FastCtx, rather than through model compression or conversation summarization. The actual amount of token savings depends on how the Agent is used and the type of tasks.

Core principles:

**1. Batch reading:** Read multiple files or code ranges in a single call, reducing the number of tool invocations and repeated reads.
**2. Limit output length:** Set output budgets for file reading, searching, and command execution to avoid irrelevant content consuming context.
**3. Reduce redundant operations:** Simplify command execution through structured tools, minimizing syntax errors, failed retries, and redundant work.
**4. Optimize truncation handling:** Clearly indicate omitted content and allow on-demand log retrieval, avoiding repeated execution of already completed commands.
**5. Simplify tool descriptions:** Shorten MCP tool descriptions to reduce token consumption from the tool definition itself.
**6. Background task execution:** Run time-consuming tasks such as building and testing in the background, and retrieve results only when needed, reducing repeated polling and output.

issues.title: ACP regression in 0.10.1: config sandbox_mode/ask ignored — Paseo ACP sessions run sandboxed and approval-gated

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
# ACP regression in 0.10.1: `sandbox_mode` / `ask` from config ignored again — Paseo ACP sessions run sandboxed and approval-gated

## Summary

The ACP posture bug from #6310 (fixed in the 0.10.0 nightlies and verified in Paseo) is back in stable **0.10.1**: sessions launched via `codewhale serve --acp` ignore `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` and `ask = "never"` from `~/.codewhale/config.toml`, and run with the OS sandbox on, network off, and approval gates firing on every shell call.

## Environment

- codewhale **0.10.1** (build `fead51eeea0f`), macOS (Apple Silicon)
- Launched as an ACP provider for the Paseo app (verified: multiple `codewhale serve --acp` processes owned by Paseo)
- `~/.codewhale/config.toml`:
  ```toml
  approval_policy = "suggest"
  sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"
  ask = "never"
  ```

## Observed (live session, 2026-10-15)

- `CODEWHALE_SANDBOX=seatbelt` is set in the session environment → the OS sandbox is applied despite `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"`.
- `python3 -c 'import socket; s=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX); s.bind("/tmp/x.sock")'` → `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted` — the exact #6310 signature; this breaks Node test runners and Playwright webServer.
- `ps` → `operation not permitted` (can't even list processes).
- Network is blocked: `curl -sI https://example.com` returns nothing (`000`).
- Every shell call still hits the typed-ask gate and requires a manual approval in the client UI, even though `ask = "never"`. (`gh` could not even read its own config at `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml` — EPERM — until the shell was escalated.)
- The policy engine itself agrees these should be skipped: `codewhale sandbox check --ask never 'ls -la /tmp'` → `{"allow": true, "requires_approval": false}`. So the disconnect is between the policy engine and the posture actually applied to live ACP sessions.

## Difference vs the original #6310 report

- Writes to `/tmp` now succeed (in 0.9.13 they were EPERM), but AF_UNIX socket creation is still blocked — the one thing Playwright/Node runners need.
- Approval prompts now reach the Paseo UI and can be approved manually (in 0.9.13 they were auto-denied). Still: `ask = "never"` should not gate at all.

## Suspected relation

#6473 (Full Access now requires per-session confirmation) combined with #6310's fix ("makes Full Access discoverable **without letting a client select it**") leaves the ACP path with no way to enter Full Access at all. `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` is effectively dead config for Paseo users, and every real workflow — network, sockets, process listing, CLI tools like `gh` — breaks. If per-session confirmation is the intended mechanism, the ACP client needs a way to request/confirm it. Until then this is a regression from the verified-working 0.10.0 nightly.

## Ask

1. Restore config-derived posture for ACP sessions when the client does not pin one, or
2. Expose a Full Access selection/confirmation path to ACP clients (Paseo), or
3. At minimum, honor `ask = "never"` so gated commands skip instead of prompting.

Happy to provide full transcripts or run a nightly/repro build. Greetings from Colombia 🇨🇴

> Template: agent-task (agent-ready, `docs/ISSUE_TRIAGE.md`). Labels: `bug`, `agent-ready`.

## Goal / Why
Filesystem, subprocess, git, secret-store, and tempfile work is executed synchronously inside `async` call chains (engine tasks, tool handlers, UI event loop, runtime API). > Template: agent-task (agent-ready, `docs/ISSUE_TRIAGE.md`). Labels: `bug`, `agent-ready`.

State, session, ledger, goal, and job records are written with non-unique temp names, without fsync, or as multi-step commits.
