prs.title: fix(route): honor a custom table's wire on runtime routes
prs.body:
## What

A named `[providers.<name>]` table with `wire = "responses"` (or `"anthropic"`) minted a Chat Completions candidate: `RouteRequest` had no wire channel, so `candidate.protocol()` came from Custom's backward-compatible static policy, and every per-turn client built by `CodewhaleClient::from_candidate` bound Chat regardless of the table's dialect. The ambient spawn-time client (`provider_wire_format_for_config`) and the capability reporter *did* honor the override — so a host that resolves routes per turn silently POSTed `{base}/chat/completions` while its config said Responses, and a cross-model rebind rebuilt the client around the static protocol, downgrading the transport mid-session.

- `RouteRequest` gains `wire_override`, honored **only** for `ProviderKind::Custom` (built-ins keep their descriptor policy; a Chat override cannot demote a fixed-Responses builtin either). The resolver binds the Custom gate once so the protocol stamp cannot desync from it.
- The tui route layer populates the override from the resolved identity's **scoped** config — the same table `provider_wire_format_for_config` reads — so receipts, preflight, readiness, and the per-turn client all see one protocol. The app-server `/v1/chat/completions` pass-through threads the same override, so a Responses-bound table fails closed at its Chat-only guard instead of silently receiving a chat body.
- The client-internal model re-resolution pins the transport's own wire for Custom clients, so an engine-internal model switch cannot downgrade it. Same-table per-request switches that bypass rebind still fail closed at the protocol-mismatch guard (unchanged behavior, no silent downgrade).
- The per-config dialect parse moves into the config crate next to the field it reads (`wire_dialect_override` plus the two alias predicates), replacing the byte-identical private copies in the client and capability readers so one alias list cannot drift. A misspelled dialect keeps degrading to the static Chat policy, now with a warning naming the table.

## Tests

- Resolver: the override mints the wire-true candidate (Responses and Anthropic) even on a relay base URL with no first-party catalog facts resurrected; builtins ignore it; absent/`chat` dialects keep the static policy.
- Route layer: a `wire = "responses"` custom table mints a Responses runtime route; a typo'd dialect degrades to Chat.
- Shared parse: canonical alias sets, case/separator normalization, explicit-chat arm, unknown degrade.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-config --locked` 177 passed; app-server suite 15 passed; targeted tui filters green; clippy `-D warnings` clean (config, app-server, tui lib).

Ported from the Pinvou/CodeWhale fork (#79), rescoped: the fork's encrypted-reasoning capture widening already landed upstream (all Responses routes that send `include` capture now).

prs.title: fix(client): capture and replay Anthropic redacted thinking blocks
prs.body:
## What

Anthropic sometimes returns a `redacted_thinking` content block instead of a decodable thinking block (safety/policy on extended-thinking models). The stream decoder had no variant for it: the block was dropped with a warning, the turn survived — but the assistant tool_use then replayed without its thinking block, and Anthropic rejects that with an **unretryable 400** on every retry of the turn. The non-stream decode path dropped it wholesale, and the block was never persisted or replayed.

This PR captures `redacted_thinking` byte-exact on both paths, persists it, replays it byte-exact on native Anthropic request building, and withholds the payload from non-native-Anthropic routes (a conservative call — a forwarding proxy might handle the block, but withholding is fail-safe). Redacted payloads never reach the visible transcript; display treats them like any elided thinking.

Alongside the capture plumbing, finished thinking blocks now persist in wire order (an ordered buffer instead of last-block-wins) — strictly necessary for correct redacted placement in multi-block turns, and a no-op for histories that only ever carried one block.

## Scope

Deliberately excluded from the same-titled fork work: Responses pairing integrity, final-tool-turn strip rules, Gemini signature-gate scoping, encrypted-reasoning capture widening (upstream already captures on all Responses routes that send `include`), signature-only-block persistence, and token-estimator accounting for redacted bytes (disclosed here as a known approximation).

## Tests

- Stream decode (including the missing-key and `"data": null` gateway shapes), non-stream decode shim, native byte-exact replay, non-native strip, redacted-only assistant message drop, serde round-trip with field-absent session compat, and an engine-level pin that the block persists into the follow-up request in wire order.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-models --locked` 44 passed; `-p codewhale-tui --lib redacted` 34 passed; targeted `anthropic`/`thinking`/`flush` filters green; clippy `-D warnings` clean (models, protocol, tui lib); `check --workspace` green.

Ported from the Pinvou/CodeWhale fork (#91), redacted-thinking slice only.

prs.title: fix(compaction): scope legacy checkpoint recognition by era
prs.body:
## What

The restore lane already prefers the provenance-stamped compaction carrier, but the recompaction family still ran the loose predicate, which matches any user turn whose text merely starts with a legacy summary header. In a history that carries the stamped carrier, that misread silently drops the turn: last-round anchoring walks past it, old-turn retention skips it, and the coverage floor classifies user prompts through the same loose predicate, so it cannot catch the loss. The survival contract meanwhile counts the retained turn as a duplicated summary, so a replacement that *does* keep the turn fails closed — fixing the drop alone would have made every such rewrite refuse.

Checkpoint recognition in the recompaction family is now era-scoped through `history_is_post_provenance`:

- A history that contains a stamped carrier recognizes only stamped carriers as checkpoints. A pasted bare-header turn anchors the round, is retained verbatim, and does not count as a duplicated summary.
- A history without a stamped carrier predates the stamp — there the pasted header is indistinguishable from the saved bare carrier, so the loose form keeps applying, now pinned explicitly.
- The receipt count reads the replacement in its own era, except that a post-provenance **original** raises the bar to a stamped carrier: the engine stamps every replacement it builds, and the stamp is the only form request rewriting relocates, so a stampless replacement of a modern history is a dropped receipt even where a retained pasted turn would loosely count as one.
- Retention derives the era from the history the slice belongs to, not the slice: the pre-round prefix's carrier may sit inside the round.
- The `/context` inspector's last-round heuristic reads the same era-aware anchoring.

`validate_survival_contract.mjs` mirrors the era rule and the fixture matrix gains the pasted-header pass/fail pair; `SURVIVAL_CONTRACT.md` documents the raised receipt bar and the era signal (the history's content, not the session's age — one-way and destructible: `/edit` or a host rewind can truncate away the only stamped carrier).

## Tests

- `pasted_legacy_header_turn_is_content_in_a_post_provenance_history` — the pasted turn anchors the round, is retained verbatim, a replacement keeping it validates with exactly one receipt, and dropping it fails the coverage floor.
- `legacy_history_still_recognizes_a_bare_header_checkpoint` — the legacy-era boundary both ways.
- Two fixture-matrix cases (`pasted-legacy-header-survives-post-provenance` pass / `-dropped-` fail) run through both the Rust enforcement and the mjs validator (16 fixtures green).
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib compaction` 186 passed / 0 failed; clippy `-D warnings` clean (lib).

Ported from the Pinvou/CodeWhale fork (#103), rescoped to the recompaction family: upstream's wire-only edit targeting and restore preference are already stricter than the era result there, so those lanes are untouched.

prs.title: ci(sync): skip the CNB mirror when its token secret is absent
prs.body:
## What

`sync` fails on every push to a mirrored branch when the `CNB_GIT_TOKEN` repository secret is absent: "CNB_GIT_TOKEN secret is not set; cannot push to CNB." That is a repository-secret state, not a property of the commit — forks can never inherit the secret, so they report a red check no contributor can fix.

A `credentials` gate job probes the secret and skips the push when it is absent, emitting a notice that names the missing secret. Configured repositories keep the previous behavior, including the existing hard failure inside the push step, which still covers a caller pinned to an older revision of this workflow plus the window where the secret is deleted between the gate's probe and the push step.

`docs/CNB_MIRROR.md` documents the skip path and distinguishes "skipped because absent or misspelled" from "failed because expired" in the rotation section.

## Tests

- Workflow-parse level: jobs `credentials` + `sync`, `sync.if = needs.credentials.outputs.configured == 'true'` (verified locally; CI exercises the rest).
- The skip path is exercised by forks of the repository, where the secret cannot exist.

Co-authored with @zhuowp (original patch in the Pinvou/CodeWhale fork, #64); adapted to this workflow's retry/concurrency/`workflow_call` plumbing.

prs.title: fix(kimi): repair empty items schemas instead of dropping the tool
prs.body:
## What

Moonshot's MFJS schema validation fails any empty schema node with `MissingType`, and `sanitize_moonshot_chat_tools` answers by silently excluding the whole tool from the request. A tool that ships `"items": {}` — legal JSON Schema for "items are unconstrained", and the exact shape a browser-automation MCP server in the wild advertised for its `args` array — therefore never reached Kimi: the model only saw a `tool_search` reference it could never call and kept emitting the nearest advertised tool instead.

The Kimi parameters sanitizer now removes the empty `items` keyword instead of the tool: an absent `items` keyword already means unconstrained items, so the repair is semantics-preserving. Untyped nodes without a semantics-preserving MFJS equivalent (e.g. `{"items": {"description": "..."}}`) still fail closed with `MissingType`.

The walker visits children before the node's own `items` check, so a nested repair can empty the parent (`"items": {"items": {}}` is vacuously true once the inner keyword is gone, making the outer drop still semantics-preserving), and it visits every schema-value position the validator recurses into: property values, `items`, object-form `additionalProperties`, `anyOf` branches, and `$defs` entries — including a root `items` keyword beside `$defs`.

## Tests

- `kimi_parameters_repairs_empty_items_as_unconstrained` — the wild-found shape, nested occurrences, and the still-fail-closed described-only node.
- `kimi_parameters_repairs_nested_and_sibling_empty_items` — items-in-items, root-items-beside-`$defs`, `additionalProperties` and `anyOf` positions.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib schema_sanitize` 63 passed / 0 failed; clippy `-D warnings` clean (lib).

Found in the wild on a browser-automation MCP catalog; ported from the Pinvou/CodeWhale fork (#101). The fork commit's tool-search eviction-reporting half already landed upstream (#6969) and is not included.

prs.title: fix(client): drop sampling params for the Claude 5 generation and Haiku 5.5
prs.body:
## What

`anthropic_model_rejects_sampling` gates `temperature`/`top_p` out of Anthropic Messages bodies. The gate only knew `opus-4-7`, `opus-4-8`, `fable`, and `mythos`. Every model released after Opus 4.6 carries the same restriction — the Messages API reference states those models "do not support" setting `temperature`/`top_p` beyond their backwards-compatible defaults (`temperature: 1.0`, `top_p >= 0.99`), and the migration guides restate it per family: "Setting `temperature`, `top_p`, or `top_k` to any non-default value on Claude Opus 4.7 and later models, including Claude Opus 5.5, returns a 400 error". So user-configured sampling params reached the Claude 5 generation and Haiku 5.5 and returned a 400.

The gate extends its own family list with `opus-5`, `sonnet-5`, and `haiku-5` substring arms. Dropping the params entirely is always safe; sending a forbidden one bricks the request. The gate deliberately stays independent of `model_supports_reasoning`'s exact-id list, which answers a different question (thinking capability, not sampling rejection).

Pinned across opus-5(-5) plus a datestamped spelling, sonnet-5(-5), haiku-5-5, fable-5, and mythos-5, with the older opus-4-6 / sonnet-4-6 / haiku-4-5 passthrough asserted so a future over-broad arm like `contains("opus-4-")` cannot slip through. Docs re-checked 2026-10-08.

## Tests

- Extended `body_drops_sampling_params_for_models_that_reject_them`: the eight Claude-5/Haiku-5.5/Fable/Mythos spellings must omit both params; older models keep temperature (or top_p when alone).
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib body_drops_sampling` green; clippy `-D warnings` clean (lib).

Ported from the Pinvou/CodeWhale fork (#93, commit 3118c36b8); the Gemini and DeepSeek hunks of that fork commit are already covered upstream and are not included.

prs.title: fix(catalog): discover a custom relay model list
prs.body:
## What and why

A custom OpenAI-compatible relay's model list never reached `/model`. Five
separate defects were in the way, and each one alone was enough to keep the
list empty, so they are fixed together here — the commits are split so each
stands on its own, but no single one makes the feature work.

1. **The roster envelope rejected its own payload.** `ModelsPage` declared its
   row array as `#[serde(borrow, alias = "models")] data`. A serde alias is a
   second name for the *same* key, so a body carrying both `data` and `models`
   failed with `duplicate field data` and the probe reported
   `invalid_response` — while `data` held a complete roster. A relay that
   echoes the wider spelling as a stub (one entry, empty `id`) is common.
2. **Only the active route was probed.** The provider panel lists every
   configured route, but startup probed just the one the session was on, and
   opening `/model` triggers no probe at all.
3. **The probe gate could not see the endpoint.** `provider_owns_live_catalog`
   took only a `ProviderKind`, so a builtin name pointed at a private relay
   (`[providers.openai]` against an Aliyun MaaS endpoint) read as official
   OpenAI and was never probed.
4. **`/v1/models` inherited the Messages auth convention.** `x-api-key` is
   Anthropic's own service convention, not a property of the Messages wire
   format. A custom table declaring `wire = "anthropic"` is still reached
   through the OpenAI-compatible surface, and such a relay can accept
   `/v1/messages` on either header while rejecting `x-api-key` on `/v1/models`
   with `401 missing_api_key`.
5. **The picker's default view hid the roster.** `/model` opens on
   `Configured`, which shows only rows placed in a current / pinned / recent /
   provider-default section. A relay's rows exist only in the listing that
   route answered, and none of them carried a section.

## Changes

- `crates/tui/src/client.rs`: `ModelsPage` enumerates `data` and `models` as two
  separate optional `RawValue` fields, with a `rows()` accessor resolving
  `data` first.
- `crates/tui/src/client.rs`: `build_default_headers` and
  `http_client_builder_with_auth_mode` take an `AuthHeaderSurface`. Inference
  keeps the wire-derived choice, so the Messages `x-api-key` default stays for
  Anthropic and the dual-wire vendors; Listing — the provider's own `/models`
  endpoint — uses Bearer for a custom host.
- `crates/tui/src/provider_catalog_live.rs`: `provider_owns_live_catalog` takes
  the route's `base_url` and consults
  `provider_preserves_custom_base_url_model`.
- `crates/tui/src/client.rs`: `spawn_configured_provider_catalog_refresh` sweeps
  the remaining configured routes at startup, each through the same
  `update_provider_catalog` the explicit `models --update` uses — so the TTL,
  typed receipt, credential-change guard and superseded-refresh ticket are
  shared, not reimplemented. A route already fresh is skipped.
- `crates/tui/src/tui/provider_picker.rs`: the panel row's catalog status
  weighs the provider-level snapshot *and* the route's roster, so
  "catalog snapshot missing" appears only when neither has anything beyond the
  configured default.
- `crates/tui/src/tui/model_picker.rs`: a custom route's live rows reach the
  default view, bounded per route
  (`CUSTOM_ROSTER_ROWS_IN_DEFAULT_VIEW`) so a gateway fronting a thousand
  models cannot take the view over.
- `crates/tui/CHANGELOG.md`: one entry for the whole fix.

`models` is not an alias — that was the bug — but it is load-bearing as a
fallback: the ChatGPT/Codex roster serves `models` as its **only** key and is
parsed downstream by `parse_models_response_for_provider`. Removing the
fallback breaks that route, which
`chatgpt_models_http_uses_visible_roster_and_rejects_secret_labels` catches.

Errors stay typed: with neither key present, or `"data": null` beside a
populated `models`, the probe still ends in `InvalidResponse` rather than a
silently empty roster. `Vec<T>` rejects a present `null` with or without
`#[serde(default)]`, verified directly.

## Issue

No-Issue: a custom gateway's rosters were unusable from a local session; no
upstream issue was filed for these defects.

## How I tested it

- **End to end, in a fresh isolated home** (`CODEWHALE_HOME` pointed at an
  empty directory, `provider = "deepseek"` active). One startup probed every
  configured relay — no `models --update`, no provider switch:

  | scope | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | `custom:intern` | failed / 0 | fresh / 11 |
  | `custom:agnes` | fresh / 10 | fresh / 10 |
  | `custom:opendesign` | failed: unauthorized / 0 | **fresh / 12** |
  | `openai:openai` (a relay endpoint) | *never probed* | **fresh / 176** |

  `deepseek` itself is an official endpoint, so it correctly owns no roster.
  One configured host, `custom:weixin`, still fails: `GET /openai/v1/models`
  answers `400 missing required parameter: model` on every path while
  `POST /openai/v1/chat/completions` answers 200, so that server publishes no
  listing at all.
- **The auth fix measured against the failing relay.** `GET /v1/models`: 200
  with `Authorization: Bearer`, `401 missing_api_key` with `x-api-key`.
  `POST /v1/messages`: accepts either.
- **Regressions fail without their fix.** The two envelope tests report
  `InvalidResponse` against the unmodified `ModelsPage`
  (`test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 2 failed`) and pass with it. The default-view
  test leaves an empty visible-row list when the per-route bound is zero.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib -- catalog model_picker provider_picker`
  → **469 passed; 3 failed; 3 ignored**. The three are pre-existing on this
  Windows host and none of them touches a file in this PR:
  `fleet::scout::tests::unpinned_…` passes when run alone (it flakes only in the
  parallel run), and the two `plugins::install::dsh::tests::raw_…` fail inside
  the Windows Native isolation probe (`extension_host/windows.rs`).
- `cargo check --profile test -p codewhale-tui --lib` after rebasing onto
  `72c1327be` — clean.
- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on every touched file — clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, rebased on current `main` (on `72c1327be`)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] `docs/features.toml` — unchanged: this repairs the existing `providers`
      feature rather than adding a command, `[features]` flag or provider

## Attribution

🤖 Generated by SpikeBot 000(CodeWhale-LOCAL)

## What and why

`/statusline` describes the Mode item as `plan · act · operate`, but the chip it turns on reads `work` in the footer. At 80×24, before:

```
        │  ▸ [✓] Mode  (plan · act · operate)                          │
```

and the footer under it:

```
 ● ask   work (Tab)   Work bar (Ctrl+])            Model set to: deepseek-flash
```

After:

```
        │  ▸ [✓] Mode  (plan · work · operate)                         │
```

#6466 sets the rule that user-facing text says Work while the stored value stays `agent`. This hint isn't in that issue's list of places, so I'm noting it here. It's the only change; the rest of #6466 (the `AppMode` labels, toasts and the hook `DEEPSEEK_MODE` contract) is untouched.

prs.title: refactor(commands): adopt portable core navigation Shapes (FEAT-031)
prs.body:
## Summary

Completes the **13-command core navigation slice** behind portable command Shapes, in preparation for later crate extraction. No intended user-visible behavior change.

Commands: `/anchor`, `/help`, `/hotbar`, `/links`, `/transcript`, `/turn`, `/home`, `/overview`, `/workspace`, `/translate`, `/voice`, `/voicesend`, `/voicecontrol` (all existing aliases retained).

- Commands own parsing, branching, formatting and rendering; host adapters supply typed facts and narrow effects. Shared metadata/results/actions/payloads have no App/TUI dependency.
- Keep the existing `u32` capability identities; use bits 30/31 for navigation/voice input. Unrelated commands do not gain these new facet slots. The existing WORKSPACE facet does now expose confined anchor operations to its consumers; per-operation authority narrowing remains an acknowledged design follow-up.
- Remove the obsolete App-bound implementations, retain confined anchor I/O and workspace semantics, and move the unchanged voice capture runtime outside the movable command closure. Builtin voice shortcuts cannot be hijacked by a shadowing user command.
- Compile the actual complete production root independently through unpublished `tests/portable-core-navigation`. Check all 13 registrations exactly once in relative order, complete source closure, all-target normal dependency graph and rejection controls. Integrate CI/developer routing and release-order validation.

This is intentionally one coherent slice: the diff includes moved host tests/runtime and shared-contract consumer updates, rather than shipping parallel implementations. **The other 27 core registrations remain out of scope, the `core` frontier remains pending, and no physical crate movement is claimed.**

## Current review follow-up — 6e73d36cb

Preserved the maintainer's `fc5ac7d904` merge, then addressed the two merge blockers and the developer-routing/proof-maintenance findings in [6e73d36cb](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/6e73d36cb). [Point-by-point response](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/7009#issuecomment-6236636441).

- Blocking-call allowance relocated, total unchanged at 540; both localization guides corrected.
- Native command paths run host tests again; proof tolerates unrelated registrations while rejecting omissions, duplicates and reordering. Heavy main/PR lint now checks source and normal dependency closure.
- Fresh focused checks: **1,215 native command tests (all 34 relocated host tests), 9 portable tests, 7 proof controls, 34 blocking-call controls**, workflow regression, formatting and web facts/docs passed.
- Workspace/anchor per-operation authority remains an explicitly documented **unresolved design follow-up**. No silent widening or renumbering of `u32`.
- This new commit is signed off; existing published history was not rewritten. New-head hosted CI/review and maintainer merge remain pending.

## Original preservation and verification (historical inputs below)

- Captured 1,125 native observations across 15 locales before migration; subsequent replays were byte-identical for messages, actions, state and persisted bytes. Preserved all 44 original scoped test identities and strengthened existing behavior assertions.
- Fresh Linux full workspace: **19,075 passed, 0 failed, 34 configured skips**. Instrumented full workspace: the same counts. Doctests: 3 passed, 8 ignored.
- Native/PTY selection: 58 passed. Actual portable navigation: 9 passed plus 7 rejection controls. Config portability: 35 passed. Architectural boundary/migration controls: 30/63 passed.
- Debug CLI, optimized CLI/TUI release build, formatting and all-target/all-feature Clippy passed.
- Root npm groups 101/101, 19/19, 418/419 (1 skip), 7/7; web 772/772 across 74 files. Web facts/docs/tokens/lint/types/build passed.
- Changed executable production Rust lines: **856/978 = 87.53%**, minimum 80%; advisory 95% not reached. Relocated production code, including the unchanged capture body, is included. This is not a claim of full microphone/provider runtime coverage.

All 27 declared local final checks passed at the original recorded input. Native checks ran at `a0a9f2541`; final `d22dfbba9` only refreshes stale generated documentation inherited from current main. All executable sources/manifests/test inputs are identical; affected web checks ran on the final generated bytes. The initial stale-doc failure was retained and repaired, not waived. Hosted CI and maintainer review remain separate evidence.

Base: `5fe4df9c24c61ae4b4bd582bdda52fdbdeab8594`.
Head: `d22dfbba91863bedd85e4489b7f3369e4e3f9a7b`.

Portable proof:
```sh
python3 -B scripts/test_check_command_core_navigation_proof.py
sh scripts/check-portable-core-navigation.sh
```

## Original hosted observation — 2026-10-17 (historical, not current head)

At head `d22dfbba9`, CI run [39005160298](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/39005160298) has passed Ubuntu tests (**19,075 passed, 34 skipped**), Rust lint, safety, MSRV and extension-host checks. Windows concluded success with **18,331 passed, 27 skipped**, but nextest reported one leaky browser-launcher test (`external_url_launcher_does_not_wait_for_browser_process`); this is **not a leak-free qualification**. macOS native tests had not finished at that observation, so that receipt did not claim full hosted CI. Synthetic CI merge `19c618de33162d1ac567a9ba7796610bb25f99df` is not an upstream delivery merge.

prs.title: fix(tui): give the /mcp panel's detail pane the rows its text wraps to
prs.body:
## What and why

The Extensions panel (/mcp) shows the selected row's name, description and detail in a pane fixed at three rows. Each part wraps, so as soon as one takes two lines the rest is cut off, with no ellipsis. At 80×24 that hits four of the five tabs. MCP, before:

```
  Browse server suggestions · available
  Suggested MCP servers (nothing installs automatically)
  Looking adds nothing. Adding writes config only — review it before /mcp
```

After:

```
  Browse server suggestions · available
  Suggested MCP servers (nothing installs automatically)
  Looking adds nothing. Adding writes config only — review it before /mcp
  restart connects anything.
```

Plugins, before:

```
  computer-use · off · needs review
  Control apps with Codewhale. macOS beta; unsigned Windows preview and
  experimental Linux/Docker support.
```

After:

```
  computer-use · off · needs review
  Control apps with Codewhale. macOS beta; unsigned Windows preview and
  experimental Linux/Docker support.
  Codewhale runs a plugin's skills, MCP servers and hooks only after you
  review exactly what it can do. Enter opens that review. · Skills: 1, MCP: 1,
  Commands: 1
```

Marketplace loses its publisher/components/source line the same way, and the Skills `research` row stops at "synthesis, and unresolved" without its path. It still happens at 100×32, and on the longer rows at 140×40.

The pane is now sized from the wrapped text: at least the three rows it has today, at most a third of the panel, and the list keeps the rest. Anything that fits in three lines renders as before, and the one-row layout under 16 rows doesn't change. I didn't make the pane scroll, because that would need keys of its own, and the list already scrolls to keep the selection in view when it gives up a few rows.

## Issue

No-Issue: detail text clipped in the Extensions panel, no issue filed for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME, opened /mcp and pressed Tab through all five tabs at 60×16, 80×24, 100×32 and 140×40, with this change and with a build from before it. The rows above are copied from the 80×24 screens. Every tab whose text already fit (Hooks at every size, MCP and Marketplace at 140×40) is byte-identical before and after, and so is every tab at 60×16.
- At 80×24 on Skills, pressed Down 14 times: the list scrolls and the selected row stays the last visible one above the taller pane.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags, and `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets`: clean. Clippy also on 1.99, plus `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15326 passed, none failed.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on 15f1804fe; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: fix(tui): don't call an empty terminal dock "reset or lost"
prs.body:
## What and why

With no terminal started, the Terminal view in the Ctrl+] dock says "No live terminals. Start one with Ctrl+N." Typing or pasting into it then adds a line that says the opposite. At 100×32, after typing `ls`, before:

```
Ctrl+N new · ⌥Down next session · Esc composer
No live terminals. Start one with Ctrl+N.
Terminal: The selected terminal was reset or lost. Select a session explicitly.
```

After:

```
Ctrl+N new · ⌥Down next session · Esc composer
No live terminals. Start one with Ctrl+N.
```

`input()` sets the lost error whenever no session matches the selection, and with no sessions at all that is every keystroke. It now only does that when sessions exist and none of them is the selected one. Keys and paste both go through `input()`, so both are covered.

The case where the selected terminal is gone but others are still live is unchanged; I couldn't reproduce it without a model-driven reset.

## Issue

Refs #6912

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build in a 100×32 pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME, pressed Ctrl+] three times to reach the Terminal view, typed `ls`, then sent `echo hi` as a bracketed paste. Did the same with a build from before this change. The lines above come from those screens; the composer stays empty in both.
- Then Ctrl+N, typed `exit`, and pressed another key: the dock still shows "Terminal: selected terminal has exited; start a fresh terminal", so a real error still comes through.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags, and `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets`: clean. Clippy also on 1.99, plus `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15326 passed, none failed.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on 3f0bcb416; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.body:
Bumps [aws-lc-rs](https://github.com/aws/aws-lc-rs) from 1.18.1 to 1.18.2.
Release notes

Sourced from aws-lc-rs's releases.

aws-lc-rs v1.18.2

What's Changed

  • Implement Eq and PartialEq for RSA and EdDSA parameters by @​dsykes16 in aws/aws-lc-rs#1228
    • RsaParameters can now be compared directly against RSA verification constants. Algorithms with different digests, padding schemes, or modulus-size ranges compare unequal. EdDSAParameters also gains equality support.
  • Add wasm32-wasip2 and wasm32-wasip3 support by @​ricochet in aws/aws-lc-rs#1239
    • Adds non-FIPS builds using universal bindings, with CI coverage under Wasmtime and wasi-sdk 34. WASIp3 requires nightly Rust.
    • Direct aws-lc-sys consumers must disable the default all-bindings feature for these targets.
  • Publish the intended RandomizedNonceKey::open_in_place documentation by @​Serophots in aws/aws-lc-rs#1227
    • Makes the existing nonce, ciphertext/tag layout, and buffer-on-error contract visible in rustdoc. No runtime behavior changes.

Upstream AWS-LC

  • aws-lc-sys v0.46.0 aligns with AWS-LC v5.11.0 (previously v5.7.0). See also the release notes for v5.8.0, v5.9.0, and v5.10.0.
    • The Ed25519 C-implementation decoder now rejects non-canonical public keys, matching the assembly-optimized implementations: aws/aws-lc#3457
    • Includes ChaCha20-Poly1305 key-material zeroization and fixes ML-KEM CPU feature detection to avoid illegal-instruction failures on x86-64 CPUs with AVX2 but no BMI2: aws/aws-lc#3552 and aws/aws-lc#3596
  • aws-lc-fips-sys v0.14.3 updates its bundled AWS-LC FIPS 4.2.0 snapshot and regenerates bindings. It remains on the FIPS 4.x release line.

Build Improvements

  • Raise the minimum system AWS-LC version to 5.7.0 by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1243
    • Non-FIPS system-library installations must now provide AWS-LC 5.7.0 or newer, previously 1.68.0. Bundled-source builds and FIPS version requirements are unchanged.
  • Fix static FIPS system-library linking by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1236
    • Fixes unresolved FIPS_mode references with GNU ld.bfd when linking a prebuilt static FIPS library, including binaries that do not call crypto and builds where LTO removes those calls.
    • Uses whole-archive linking to retain libcrypto, including in downstream Rust staticlib outputs. This can increase binary size; dynamic FIPS and non-FIPS linking are unchanged.
  • Fix Cranelift linking by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1234
    • Normalizes binding link names to avoid undefined-symbol failures, including when Cranelift is selected through Cargo profiles rather than RUSTFLAGS. The AWS_LC_SYS_NO_U1_BINDINGS workaround is no longer needed.
  • Fix jitterentropy builds with optimizing CFLAGS and newer cc versions by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1254
    • Keeps filtered flags in effect throughout the jitterentropy builder's lifetime, preventing cached environment reads from allowing flags such as -O2 to override its required -O0.
  • Honor AWS_LC_SYS_CC in the main library build by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1255
    • Applies crate-specific compiler overrides before compiler lookup in both CC and CMake build paths, keeping compiler selection and capability probes consistent when cc caches environment reads.
  • Improve archive reproducibility through symlinked build paths by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1238
    • Prevents the non-Windows CC builder from incorporating symlink-resolved absolute build paths into archive member names, avoiding unnecessary downstream compile-cache misses. Windows short-path handling is unchanged.
  • Upgrade bindgen to 0.73 by @​xtqqczze in aws/aws-lc-rs#1244
  • Document the system-library trust model by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1218
    • Clarifies that supplied paths and pkg-config results are trusted build inputs, and that FIPS validation can execute candidate library code before accepting or rejecting it. Documents runner requirements and how to disable automatic system-library detection.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

For a custom (non-built-in) ACP harness spawned through `sessions_spawn({ runtime: "acp" })`, OpenClaw pushes a `thinking` level it *derived itself* (`resolveThinkingDefault` → `"off"` when a `model` was given) as a hard requirement over `session/set_config_option`. If the harness advertises a `configOptions` list that does not contain `thinking` (or the `effort` alias), the whole turn aborts with `ACP_BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED_CONTROL` — even though the harness never claimed to support thinking, the value is the default, and the user asked for nothing.

The same happens for `model`: the brain passes its own resolved `provider/model` ref (e.g. `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`) as `sessions_spawn`'s `model` argument, and it is pushed at a harness whose advertised model list cannot contain it.

Net effect: a spec-conformant custom harness that honestly advertises the one option it has (a fixed `model` select) cannot be used from the gateway at all. The only way to make it work today is for the harness to advertise **no** config options (reply to `set_config_option` without a `configOptions` list), which is what we ended up doing.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Register a custom ACP harness in the acpx plugin (`plugins.entries.acpx.config.agents.myharness = { command, args }`) and an OpenClaw agent `{ id: "myharness", runtime: { type: "acp", acp: { agent: "myharness", backend: "acpx" } } }`. The harness (any minimal ACP agent over stdio) returns from `session/new` and from `session/set_config_option`:
   ```json
   {"configOptions":[{"id":"model","name":"Model","type":"select","category":"model","currentValue":"fixed","options":[{"value":"fixed","name":"fixed"}]}]}
   ```
   and accepts `set_config_option` for `model`.
2. `openclaw agent --agent myharness -m 'Use sessions_spawn with runtime "acp" and agentId "myharness" to delegate: reply with only the token OK.'` — the brain calls `sessions_spawn({runtime:"acp", agentId:"myharness", model:"anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001", …})` (it adds `model` on its own on most calls).
3. Observe the turn abort before `session/prompt`.

Also reproducible when the harness advertises **no** `configOptions` in `session/new` but echoes any list from `set_config_option`: acpx narrows its advertised set to that list and the next control (`thinking`) fails with `Supported config options: model` (or `none` if the list is empty).

### Expected behavior

- A `thinking` value OpenClaw derived by default (not user-requested) should be best-effort: skipped, or downgraded to a warning, when the harness advertises neither `thinking` nor `effort` — the way `timeout`/`timeout_seconds` are already tolerated (`isUnsupportedOptionalTimeoutConfigRejection`).
- Pushing OpenClaw's own `provider/model` ref at a custom harness whose advertised `availableModels` does not include it should not be fatal either (the harness's model is its own; the acpx CLI path already validates `--model` against the advertised list and refuses client-side, but the runtime path just sends it).

### Actual behavior

```
AcpRuntimeError: ACP session agent:myharness:acp:…:oneshot:… does not advertise config option 'thinking'. Supported config options: model.: code=ACP_BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED_CONTROL
```
and, when the harness advertises only `thinking`/`fast` and leaves `model` to the legacy `models` field:
```
AcpRuntimeError: ACP backend "acpx" does not accept config key "model". code=ACP_BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED_CONTROL
```
The brain then reports "The ACP harness session failed and produced no output to relay."

Where it happens (2026.7.1 dist): `applyManagerRuntimeControls` in `src/acp/control-plane/…` builds the pairs via `buildRuntimeConfigOptionPairs(options)` — `model` and `thinking` come from `resolveAcpSpawnRuntimeOptions` (`src/acp/spawn`), which sets `thinking = resolveThinkingDefault(...)` whenever a `model` is present — and throws `ACP_BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED_CONTROL` when `advertisedKeys.size > 0 && !advertisedKeys.has(key)`. acpx's side is `resolveSupportedConfigOptionId` in `src/runtime/engine/manager.ts`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.1-2 (0790d9f), `@openclaw/acpx` 2026.7.1 bundling acpx 0.11.2

### Operating system

macOS 15 (Darwin 24.5), Node 24.19.0

### Install method

npm (global), dev profile (`--dev`)

### Model

anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 (the OpenClaw brain); the harness's own model is fixed server-side and not selectable

### Provider / routing chain

`openclaw agent --agent <acp-agent>` → OpenClaw brain (anthropic) → `sessions_spawn(runtime:"acp")` → acpx (embedded) → custom harness command over stdio

### Additional information

Context: the harness is `fountain acp` (https://github.com/BinaryBourbon/fountain, ADR 0015) — a remote-conversation ACP agent whose model is a property of the server-side agent, so per-session `model`/`thinking` genuinely do not exist. Full investigation with the acpx code paths: https://github.com/BinaryBourbon/fountain/issues/760 and PR https://github.com/BinaryBourbon/fountain/pull/767. Happy to test a fix against a live gateway.

A related but separate acpx report (one-shot `ensureSession` creating a second backend session per spawn) is filed on openclaw/acpx.

issues.body:
## Summary

A session lane can wedge such that the queued user message is never dispatched, while the built-in stuck-session recovery repeatedly **detects** the condition and deliberately **declines to act** — logging `action=observe_only reason=active_embedded_run` in a loop for as long as the wedge lasts. Only a gateway restart recovers it.

The core problem is that recovery trusts an `activeSessionId` handle as proof of liveness. When an embedded run leaks that handle without making progress, recovery treats "a run is registered" as "work is happening" and permanently defers, even though no model call, tool call, or reply has occurred for many minutes.

## Observed incident

Production gateway, healthy process (uptime 1h18m, `NRestarts=0`), no OOM, ~17% CPU, RSS 1.2 GiB. Signal session `agent:main:signal:direct:+13093634600` (`sessionId=e20100a2-9922-47d7-8577-3fbb89456372`) showed `status=running` with a queued inbound message that was never answered.

**Last provider activity gateway-wide was 22:57:56.** Nothing followed for ~14 minutes until a manual restart:

```
22:57:55.850 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] start  provider=openai model=gpt-5.6-sol
22:57:56.293 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response status=200 elapsedMs=444
   ... no model-fetch, no tool call, no reply for ~14 min ...
23:11:33 (manual `systemctl restart openclaw`)
```

Throughout that window recovery fired continuously and skipped every time:

```
23:01:45 [diagnostic] stuck session recovery skipped: sessionId=e20100a2-… sessionKey=agent:main:signal:direct:+1… age=360s queueDepth=1 activeSessionId=e20100a2-…
23:01:45 [diagnostic] stuck session recovery outcome: status=skipped action=observe_only … activeWorkKind=embedded_run reason=active_embedded_run
23:03:43 [diagnostic] long-running session: … state=processing age=578s queueDepth=1 reason=queued_behind_active_work classification=long_running activeWorkKind=embedded_run
23:06:06 [diagnostic] stuck session recovery skipped: … age=360s queueDepth=1 …
23:07:45 [diagnostic] stuck session recovery skipped: … age=360s queueDepth=1 …
```

Two things stand out:

1. `queueDepth=1` the entire time — a real user message was waiting.
2. **`age=360s` never advances** across ~6 minutes of repeated attempts, while the separate `long-running session` line shows `age` growing correctly (128s → 278s → 578s). The recovery path appears to observe a frozen/rebased age, so any age-based escalation cannot trigger.

## Code analysis

`src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts:150-173` — if an active run handle exists, recovery bails out unless `allowActiveAbort === true` or the run is judged progress-stale:

```ts
if (activeSessionId) {
  const reclaimStaleActiveRun =
    params.allowActiveAbort !== true &&
    isActiveRunProgressStale({ sessionId: activeSessionId, sessionKey: params.sessionKey,
                               queueDepth: params.queueDepth, staleAbortMs: staleActiveProgressAbortMs });
  if (params.allowActiveAbort !== true && !reclaimStaleActiveRun) {
    const outcome = { status: "skipped", action: "observe_only",
                      reason: "active_embedded_run", /* … */ };
    diag.warn(`stuck session recovery skipped: …`);
    return outcome;
  }
```

So the *only* escape hatches are `allowActiveAbort` and `isActiveRunProgressStale`. In this incident neither engaged.

`allowActiveAbort` is supplied from `src/logging/diagnostic.ts` only when the abort ladder deems the session eligible, which requires a `stalled_agent_run` classification (`:504-512`):

```ts
return (
  params.classification?.eventType === "session.stalled" &&
  params.classification.classification === "stalled_agent_run" &&
  params.classification.activeWorkKind === "embedded_run" &&
  params.ageMs >= params.stuckSessionAbortMs
);
```

But the wedged session was **never** classified `stalled` — it stayed `long_running` for the entire wedge. Log counts over the incident window:

```
8 classification=long_running
0 session.stalled          (grep -c "session.stalled" over the full hour: 0)
```

Because classification never reached `session.stalled`/`stalled_agent_run`, `allowActiveAbort` was never set, so the `observe_only` early-return was unconditional in practice.

`isActiveRunProgressStale` (`:46-61`) depends on `lastProgressAgeMs` from `getDiagnosticSessionActivitySnapshot`, and `lastProgressAt` is refreshed by `touchSessionActivity` (`src/logging/diagnostic-run-activity.ts:185-188`). This is the crux: whatever the leaked run was doing still counted as "progress" (or the handle kept the activity record warm) even though no model call, tool call, or reply occurred for 14 minutes — so the run never looked stale and the second escape hatch also never opened.

Net effect: **liveness is inferred from handle existence plus a progress signal that a wedged run can keep alive, rather than from externally observable forward progress** (model calls, tool results, emitted replies). A leaked-but-idle run therefore blocks its lane indefinitely and suppresses its own recovery.

## Why this looks distinct from existing issues

- #103690 (open) reports the same *user-visible* symptom (inbound starves, restart recovers) but is scoped to WhatsApp/Baileys + claude-cli with heartbeats dispatching normally. This report is Signal + embedded/codex runtime and focuses specifically on recovery self-suppressing via `observe_only`/`active_embedded_run` with a frozen `age`.
- #112479 (closed) covered looping tool calls being *counted as progress*. Related in spirit, but here there were **no tool calls at all** during the wedge — the run was completely idle.
- #86056 / #91802 / #114058 ("reclaim wedged session lanes with a stale leaked active run", "release wedged session lane…", "make stuck recovery truthful") clearly target this family. `#114058` is merged on `main` (2026-07-26), yet `main` still contains the same unconditional `observe_only` early-return shown above, and the two escape hatches remain the only bypass — so the leaked-idle-handle case still appears reachable.

Happy to fold this into #103690 if maintainers consider it the same root cause.

## Reproduction sketch

1. Run an agent with `agents.defaults.subagents.delegationMode: "prefer"`, `agents.defaults.maxConcurrent: 8`, `subagents.maxConcurrent: 12` so several embedded runs are in flight.
2. Restart/interrupt the gateway mid-run so an embedded run handle is registered for a session but its driving work is gone (observed after gateway restarts during compaction work; several subagent sessions were left `status=running` with transcripts containing only the spawn prompt and no output).
3. Send a new inbound message to the affected session key.
4. Observe `queueDepth=1`, repeated `action=observe_only reason=active_embedded_run`, no provider traffic, and no dispatch until restart.

## Suggested fix

1. **Ground staleness in externally observable progress.** Judge liveness by last model call / tool result / emitted reply for the *active run*, not by handle presence or a progress timestamp the wedged run can keep warm.
2. **Add a hard ceiling.** If `queueDepth > 0` and there has been no observable progress for `stuckSessionAbortMs`, abort-drain regardless of classification — do not require reaching `stalled_agent_run` first.
3. **Fix the frozen `age`.** `age=360s` was constant across repeated recovery attempts while the sibling `long-running session` line advanced correctly; recovery appears to compute age from a rebased/dedup-suppressed origin, which defeats age-based escalation.
4. **Escalate on repetition.** Emit a distinct, louder diagnostic (and escalate to abort) after N consecutive `observe_only` outcomes for the same `sessionId`, instead of logging the identical warning indefinitely.
5. **Make it operator-recoverable without a restart.** During the wedge, `sessions.abort` over the gateway RPC was not usable as a targeted remedy, leaving full-process restart as the only lever — which also kills healthy concurrent subagent runs.

## Suggested regression tests

- Given an active embedded run handle whose last observable progress (model/tool/reply) exceeds `stuckSessionAbortMs`, with `queueDepth > 0` and classification still `long_running`, assert recovery abort-drains the lane instead of returning `observe_only`.
- Assert the `age` reported by consecutive recovery attempts is monotonically non-decreasing for an unchanged wedge.
- Assert a queued inbound message is eventually dispatched (or the lane released) without a process restart.

## Environment

- OpenClaw `2026.7.1-2 (0790d9f)`
- Line references from checkout `4475c3a0844`; `origin/main` verified to still contain the same early-return
- Linux (KVM), gateway under systemd, Signal channel, `gpt-5.6-sol` primary
- `diagnostics` block unset in config, so `stuckSessionWarnMs` / `stuckSessionAbortMs` were at defaults

issues.body:
## Environment

- iOS app on iPhone, iOS 26.5.2 (App Store build)
- OpenClaw gateway v2026.7.1-2 on Windows, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` backend
- Remote gateway via `wss://` (Cloudflare Tunnel)

## Summary

After enabling the "show reasoning and tool activity" display option in the iOS app, the app becomes noticeably laggy: scrolling stutters, the UI responds slowly, and long replies with many tool calls make it worse. Disabling the option restores smooth performance.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the iOS app, connect to a remote gateway.
2. Enable the option that displays reasoning steps and tool activity inline (per-message).
3. Run a conversation with a multi-tool, long-turn task.
4. Observe scroll stutter and slow UI response during and after the turn.

## Expected behavior

Showing reasoning/tool activity should not noticeably degrade scrolling or UI responsiveness, even for long turns with many tool calls.

## Notes

- Suspected cause: per-block rendering cost for reasoning/tool cards without list virtualization, or frequent re-layout during streaming.
- This is a display-performance issue; the same session in the Control UI (webchat) is smooth.

_Reported by Jiyao, the user's OpenClaw agent._

issues.body:
### Summary

Headless Logbook screen capture is macOS-only. `logbook.snapshot` hard-fails on every other platform, so a Windows node host can enable the Logbook plugin but never contributes a single frame to the timeline.

### Problem to solve

`handleLogbookSnapshot` guards on the platform and bails before doing any work:

```ts
// extensions/logbook/src/node-host.ts:33
if (process.platform !== "darwin") {
  return { error: `logbook.snapshot is not supported on ${process.platform}` };
}
```

The capture itself then shells out to the macOS-only `screencapture` binary, and the command's node-invoke-policy ships macOS as the only default platform:

```ts
// extensions/logbook/index.ts:112
defaultPlatforms: ["macos"],
```

Everything else in Logbook is already cross-platform — storage, the Control UI timeline tab, retention, and the vision-analysis pass. Capture is the single platform-bound piece, and it is the one that produces the data the rest of the feature exists to display.

The practical result is a silent-ish dead end: on Windows the plugin installs, enables, and renders its timeline tab, but the failure only surfaces per-tick as a platform error string, and the journal stays permanently empty.

### Proposed solution

Add a Windows branch to `handleLogbookSnapshot` that:

- lazily `import()`s a win32-only runtime module, so the native binding is never loaded during node-host startup on macOS or Linux
- captures via `node-screenshots` and normalizes through Rastermill to JPEG quality 60 / max side 1440 — the same output contract the macOS path already produces, so downstream storage and analysis are unchanged
- enumerates monitors in a deterministic order (primary first, then desktop x/y, then native id), since native enumeration order is not a stable `screenIndex` contract
- returns actionable errors for enumeration failure, no displays, out-of-range `screenIndex`, capture failure, and encode failure
- adds `windows` alongside `macos` in the `logbook.snapshot` node-invoke-policy defaults

The existing macOS `screencapture` implementation stays untouched.

### Alternatives considered

**Ship it as a third-party plugin instead.** Not possible without forking. The platform guard, the capture handler, and the node-invoke-policy platform list all live inside the bundled `logbook` extension. The plugin SDK has no seam for an external plugin to add a platform to an existing bundled command — the guard would still reject the call before any external code ran.

**Replace `screencapture` with one cross-platform library for all platforms.** A production-equivalent macOS benchmark showed the native path is materially faster and preserves cursor and profile behavior better than the candidate library. Swapping it out would regress working macOS behavior to buy consistency, so the macOS path is deliberately left alone.

**Bridge a WSL node host to the Windows host desktop.** A different surface with its own transport problem; it does not help a native Windows node host, which is the common case.

**Cover Linux in the same change.** X11 and Wayland have materially different headless and session stories, and bundling them would make one PR that is hard to validate and hard to review. Better as separate follow-ups.

### Impact

- **Affected:** any operator running a Windows node host who wants Logbook. The rest of the plugin already works there.
- **Severity:** blocks the workflow — the feature is installable but functionally inert on Windows.
- **Frequency:** always, on every capture tick, for the lifetime of the install.
- **Consequence:** Windows operators either keep a macOS machine in the loop purely to generate frames, or go without the feature entirely. There is no configuration that works around it.

### Evidence/examples

Current upstream behavior is the platform guard and policy defaults quoted above, plus `docs/plugins/logbook.md`, which documents only the headless macOS path.

Prior art: Logbook landed in #99867 / #99930 as a general work-journal feature; capture is the one piece that never got a second platform.

Feasibility is validated, not theoretical. Running the exact capture-and-normalize logic against a real Windows desktop (single 1440x900 display):

```
monitors found: 1
  [0] id=65537 primary=true x=0 y=0 w=1440 h=900
captureImage+toPng: 39ms, png bytes=525760
rastermill encode: 163ms, jpeg bytes=113723, width=1440, height=900
total elapsed: 202ms
```

The resulting JPEG was fetched back and visually confirmed to be a correct capture of the live desktop, not a black or garbage frame.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself — implementation and tests are ready, and I will open the PR against this issue immediately.

### Additional information

Limits I would document rather than claim support for:

- The native capture path does not composite the mouse pointer.
- One snapshot captures one monitor; there is no multi-display stitching.
- Capture requires an interactive signed-in desktop session. Locked-session and RDP-disconnected behavior is **unverified** — I would not claim either works.

New dependency disclosure:

issues.body:
### What happened

`openclaw doctor` reports Telegram as unconfigured on a multi-account setup where every
account already defines `groups`, and group routing demonstrably works:

```
- channels.telegram: Telegram is in first-time setup mode. DMs use pairing mode, so new
  senders must start a chat and be approved before regular messages are accepted. Group
  messages stay blocked until you add allowed chats under channels.telegram.groups (and
  optional sender IDs under channels.telegram.groupAllowFrom), or set
  channels.telegram.groupPolicy to "open" if you want broad group access.
```

The bots in those groups reply normally, so the warning is a false positive.

### Reproduction

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "telegram": {
      "enabled": true,
      "dmPolicy": "pairing",
      "groupPolicy": "allowlist",
      "groupAllowFrom": ["11111111"],
      "defaultAccount": "default",
      "accounts": {
        "default": { "groups": { "-1001111111111": { "requireMention": true } } },
        "second": { "groups": { "-1002222222222": { "requireMention": true } } }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Run `openclaw doctor`. The `channels.telegram` line appears even though both account
scopes are fully configured and neither of them warns.

### Root cause

Two layers, and the first one is the more consequential.

**1. `resolveDoctorChannelAccountIds` returns `undefined` for every channel during a real
doctor run.** It resolves the channel through `normalizeAnyChannelId`, which only knows
channels present in the plugin *registry*. Doctor inspects config without starting
channels, so that registry is empty. Measured on a real run with temporary instrumentation:

```
TMPDIAG2 channelId=null
TMPDIAG  telegram accountIds=undefined implicit=true active=6
```

Because `accountIds` is `undefined`, `hasImplicitActiveAccount` is unconditionally `true`
in `empty-allowlist-scan.ts`. That means **`suppressParentGroupAllowlistWarning` — added in
#93434 to avoid exactly this class of parent-scope false positive — is always `false` in
production.** Its tests pass because they run in a context where the registry is populated.

Note the inconsistency inside doctor itself: `channel-doctor.ts` finds the Telegram adapter
fine via `resolveReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfig` (config-driven), so the *warning* is
produced, while `channel-capabilities.ts` needs the registry, so the data that would
*suppress* it is missing. `getDoctorChannelCapabilities` already dodges this by consulting
the bundled catalog first; `resolveDoctorChannelAccountIds` has no such fallback.

**2. The parent container scope is checked as if it were an account.**
`scanEmptyAllowlistPolicyWarnings` calls `checkAccount(channelConfig, "channels.telegram",
…, parent: undefined)`. With `accounts` in use that scope holds no `groups` of its own, so
Telegram's first-time guidance fires there while both account scopes stay silent. The
scanner's suppression signal is forwarded to `collectEmptyAllowlistPolicyWarningsForAccount`
but not to the channel-supplied `extraWarningsForAccount` hook, which is where that
guidance comes from.

Fixing only layer 1 leaves the warning in place; fixing only layer 2 is dead code, because
the suppression data never arrives. Verified by building the repo and running the real CLI:

| Applied | `first-time setup` warnings |
|---|---|
| neither | 1 |
| layer 1 only | 1 |
| both | 0 |

### Expected

No first-time setup warning on the parent scope when every active account configures
`groups`. Accounts that are genuinely unconfigured keep warning at their own scope, setups
with no `accounts` block are unaffected, and a container-level `botToken`/`tokenFile`/
`$TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` (which synthesizes an implicit `default` account inheriting the
container) must keep its guidance.

### Environment

- Reproduced against `main` (`3e0634f7ed9`); originally seen on 2026.7.1-2
- Linux, Node 26.5.1

*Filed with AI assistance (Claude Code).*

issues.body:
## Problem or Use Case

The MCP specification release candidate **2026-07-28** (now past its scheduled date) is the largest revision of the protocol since launch and makes MCP **stateless** ([RC announcement](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28-release-candidate/)):

- The `initialize`/`initialized` **handshake is removed**.
- The **`Mcp-Session-Id` header is removed** — any request can be routed to any server, so MCP works behind a plain load balancer. Protocol/client version info moves into per-request `_meta` fields.
- The TypeScript v2 SDK has **shipped stable (2026-07-27)** — but as **new split packages**, not a 2.x bump of the current monolith ([SDK announcement](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/sdk-betas-2026-07-28/)):
  - `@modelcontextprotocol/client@2.0.0`
  - `@modelcontextprotocol/server@2.0.0`
  - `@modelcontextprotocol/core@2.0.0`
  - The legacy monolith `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` currently tops out at **1.30.0** (published 2026-07-27) and does not implement the stateless protocol.

OpenClaw currently pins **`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk": "1.30.0"`** (root `package.json`, also in `ui/package.json` alongside `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps`). To speak the new spec, OpenClaw needs to migrate onto the split v2 packages — there is no issue currently tracking this.

### OpenClaw's MCP surface area (from a repo-wide grep)

**72 files** import from `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`; the main touch points:

**Client side:**
- `src/agents/mcp-transport.ts` — transport factory importing `SSEClientTransport` (`client/sse.js`), `StreamableHTTPClientTransport` (`client/streamableHttp.js`), and `FetchLike`/`Transport` types (`shared/transport.js`).
- `src/agents/mcp-stdio-transport.ts` — custom stdio client transport.
- `src/agents/mcp-oauth.ts`, `mcp-oauth-fetch.ts`, `mcp-oauth-provider.ts`, `mcp-oauth-store.ts` — the OAuth stack (v2 also reworks the auth story; `jose`/PKCE now live in the new packages).
- `src/agents/mcp-http-fetch.ts`, `mcp-auth-profile.ts` — header/auth plumbing around the transports.

**Server side (16 files import `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/*`):**
- `src/mcp/tools-stdio-server.ts` — low-level `Server` + `StdioServerTransport` with `CallToolRequestSchema`/`ListToolsRequestSchema`.
- `src/mcp/channel-server.ts`, `channel-server-runtime.ts`, `channel-bridge.ts`, `channel-tools.ts` — channel MCP runtime.
- `src/mcp/openclaw-tools-serve.ts`, `plugin-tools-serve.ts`, `codex-supervision-tools-serve.ts` — tool-serving surfaces.

**Hand-rolled HTTP server:**
- `src/gateway/mcp-http.ts` + `src/gateway/mcp-http.handlers.ts` — the gateway loopback MCP server is a bespoke JSON-RPC implementation, so its handshake/session semantics must be audited directly against the stateless spec (no SDK upgrade will fix it automatically).

**Existing `Mcp-Session-Id` references** (4 files, incl. `extensions/parallel/src/parallel-mcp-search.runtime.ts` and tests) — these encode the session model the new spec removes.

## Proposed Solution

A staged migration, one PR per step:

### Step 1 — Inventory & spike
- Catalog all `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` import sites and classify them client / server / shared-types.
- Spike one client path (e.g. streamable-HTTP connect + `tools/list` + `tools/call`) against `@modelcontextprotocol/client@2.0.0` to surface the transport/API delta.

### Step 2 — Migrate the MCP client paths
- Move `src/agents/mcp-transport.ts` and the OAuth stack onto `@modelcontextprotocol/client@2.0.0`.
- Remove session-bound assumptions (handshake ordering, `Mcp-Session-Id` handling) from `extensions/parallel` runtime and any client code.
- Keep the legacy `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.x` path available behind config/feature flag if needed, so users on older MCP servers are not broken.

### Step 3 — Migrate the MCP server surfaces
- Move stdio tool servers (`src/mcp/*-serve.ts`, channel server) onto `@modelcontextprotocol/server@2.0.0`.
- Audit the hand-rolled gateway loopback server (`src/gateway/mcp-http*.ts`) against the stateless spec: drop any `initialize` gating / session-id coupling, accept per-request `_meta`.

### Step 4 — Tests & compatibility matrix
- Add a CI leg exercising OpenClaw as client against an `@modelcontextprotocol/server@2.0.0` reference server, and vice versa.
- Keep a 1.x test leg for at least one minor release so existing user-configured MCP servers keep working.

### Step 5 — Docs
- Update `docs/tools/mcp.md` and `docs/cli/mcp.md` with the new transport/config behavior and any migration notes for users running custom MCP servers.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] OpenClaw can connect, list tools, and call tools against a stateless (2026-07-28 spec) MCP server over HTTP without `initialize`/`Mcp-Session-Id`.
- [ ] Server surfaces (stdio + gateway loopback) accept stateless clients.
- [ ] CI green against both a 1.x server/client leg and a 2.0 leg.
- [ ] `Mcp-Session-Id` references removed or explicitly gated for legacy compat.
- [ ] Release/migration note added in `docs/`.

## Alternatives Considered

1. **Stay on `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.30.x` indefinitely.** Rejected: 1.x will not speak the stateless protocol, so OpenClaw will stop interoperating with servers that upgrade once the spec goes final — and the v2 stable already shipped.
2. **Fork the monolith SDK and patch in stateless support.** Rejected: upstream v2 is stable in the new split packages; forking creates a permanent maintenance burden.
3. **Wait for the monolith `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` to reach 2.x.** Risky: the v2 line was deliberately split into `client`/`server`/`core` packages; there is no indication the monolith gets a 2.0.

## Related

- [NousResearch/hermes-agent#69931](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/69931) — sibling issue tracking the same migration for the Python `mcp` SDK (`mcp==2.0.0b2`), incl. discussion of a governance wrapper for stateless MCP security (rug pulls, tool-description drift)
- OpenClaw #91556 — `notifications/tools/list_changed` support (behavior may shift under the stateless model)

## References

- [The 2026-07-28 MCP Specification Release Candidate](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28-release-candidate/)
- [Beta SDKs for the 2026-07-28 MCP Spec Release](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/sdk-betas-2026-07-28/)
- [`@modelcontextprotocol/client` on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@modelcontextprotocol/client) (2.0.0 stable, published 2026-07-27)
- [Developer migration guide for the 2026-07-28 breaking changes](https://www.developersdigest.tech/blog/mcp-2026-07-28-breaking-changes)

## Contribution
- [x] I'd like to help with this migration

issues.body:
### Summary

Set `AI_AGENT=openclaw` for OpenClaw-managed subprocesses when the caller has not already supplied a nonblank `AI_AGENT` value.

### Problem to solve

OpenClaw already marks child execution consistently with `OPENCLAW_CLI=1`, but that product-specific marker requires every downstream tool to maintain an OpenClaw-specific heuristic. Tools that want to choose machine-readable output, suppress pagers or interactive prompts, or reduce noisy progress need one stable way to recognize agent-driven execution across products.

### Proposed solution

Extend the existing `markOpenClawExecEnv` / `ensureOpenClawExecMarkerOnProcess` owner boundary so it also defaults `AI_AGENT` to the lowercase slug `openclaw`. Preserve any explicit nonblank `AI_AGENT` value so wrappers and nested agents retain the more specific caller identity.

Keep `OPENCLAW_CLI=1` unchanged for existing OpenClaw-specific consumers. `AI_AGENT` is additional universal, advisory metadata; it must not be treated as telemetry, authorization, sandbox policy, or a trust boundary.

### Alternatives considered

- Use only `OPENCLAW_CLI=1`: preserves current behavior but requires downstream tools to add a separate detector for every agent.
- Replace `OPENCLAW_CLI`: unnecessarily risks existing integrations; the universal marker can coexist with the product-specific one.
- Set `AI_AGENT` unconditionally: would erase useful identity when OpenClaw is launched from another agent or wrapper.
- Add marker logic independently at each spawn call: duplicates policy and risks missing host, node, sandbox, cron, or future execution surfaces. The existing shared execution-environment helper is the canonical boundary.

### Impact

- Affected: developers and CLI/tool authors whose commands run under OpenClaw.
- Severity: interoperability improvement; current execution still works.
- Frequency: every OpenClaw-managed subprocess can benefit automatically.
- Consequence: downstream tools can use one cross-agent signal instead of product-specific heuristics, while existing OpenClaw detection remains intact.

### Evidence/examples

Vercel documents `AI_AGENT` as a universal environment-variable convention for AI development tools and recommends lowercase, hyphenated slugs: https://github.com/vercel/vercel/tree/main/packages/detect-agent#the-ai_agent-standard

OpenClaw already centralized subprocess identification in #41411 using `OPENCLAW_CLI=1` across CLI startup, host execution, generic command spawning, node-host execution, and Docker sandboxes. Extending that helper covers those same surfaces without creating a parallel path.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

### Additional information

The proposed change is intentionally small: no new configuration, permissions, network calls, telemetry, or output behavior. Focused tests should cover the default marker, preservation of an explicit nonblank value, replacement of a blank value, cloning behavior, and process-environment mutation.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (live UI state is missing; persisted history is intact)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On the current `main` branch, Control UI / WebChat does not reliably show tool activity such as `exec` in real time. The tool call and its result become visible only after refreshing the page.

This makes an active tool-running turn look idle or incomplete even though the Gateway has recorded the events correctly.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw from a current `main` checkout.
2. Open Control UI / WebChat.
3. Send a prompt that triggers one or more tools, for example a multi-step request using `exec`.
4. Observe the chat while the tools are running and after they complete.
5. Refresh the page.

### Expected behavior

Tool-call activity and results should appear in the chat as the corresponding live `agent` / `session.tool` events arrive, without requiring a page refresh.

### Actual behavior

Some tool calls or results do not appear in the live UI. After refreshing, history hydration loads and displays them, showing that the events were persisted and that the failure is in the live Control UI rendering/reconciliation path rather than tool execution or transcript storage.

### OpenClaw version

Current `main` checkout (exact downstream checkout SHA was not captured).

### Surface

Control UI / WebChat

### Additional information

This appears related to, but distinct from:

- #92122, which concerned incorrect live ordering and was closed by #93184. In this report the activity is missing until refresh, rather than merely displayed out of order.
- #98540, where the composer appears idle while the Activity panel still shows running tools. In this report the live tool activity itself is not reliably rendered and only appears after refresh.
- #98461, which was closed as already implemented because current releases expose live tool activity over the Gateway WebSocket. The present behavior may therefore be a regression in consuming or reconciling those live events on `main`.

Likely investigation area: the Control UI live tool stream and history reconciliation/hydration path.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Several `macos-swift` suites assert wall-clock deadlines that a hosted GitHub runner cannot meet, so the job fails nondeterministically. The clearest is `BoundedProcessTests.swift:32`, which asserts an operation completes in under 2 seconds and measured `2.357511334` on CI.

This is visible without any external repro loop, because the `Swift test` step already retries 3× inside one job — and **the set of failing suites changes between those retries on identical code**. That divergence is the evidence: a code defect reproduces, a deadline race does not.

Fork PRs make it much more likely. `ci.yml` routes same-repo branches to `blacksmith-12vcpu-macos-26` but sends fork PRs to the hosted `macos-26` runner (`ci.yml:3007`), and these deadlines appear to be tuned for the faster machine.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a PR from a fork that touches a path selecting `macos-swift` in `preflight`.
2. Let the `macos-swift` job run. The `Swift test` step retries up to 3× on its own.
3. Compare the failing suite set across those three attempts within the single job.

Measured on run [30863402064](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/30863402064), job `91850136345`, head `4d09189fcc8` — same commit, same runner, same job:

| `swift test` attempt | failing suites | issues |
|---|---|---|
| 1/3 | 7 — `AppStateVoiceEarsTests`, `BoundedCommandTests`, `BoundedProcessTests`, `DashboardWindowSmokeTests`, `MacNodeModeCoordinatorTests`, `QuickChatPowerFeaturesTests`, `RemoteGatewayProbeTests` | 11 |
| 2/3 | 4 — `BoundedCommandTests`, `BoundedProcessTests`, `DashboardWindowSmokeTests`, `RemoteGatewayProbeTests` | 6 |
| 3/3 | 5 — the four above plus `MacNodeModeCoordinatorTests` | 6 |

`AppStateVoiceEarsTests`, `QuickChatPowerFeaturesTests` and `MacNodeModeCoordinatorTests` drift in and out; four suites fail in all three.

Second observation on an unrelated diff — run [30863288585](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/30863288585), job `91849747565`, head `1271bfbd00a` — same `ContinuousClock` overruns with a partly different set of 11 suites, adding `PortGuardianRecordStoreTests`, `RemotePortTunnelTests`, `GatewayChannelConnectTests` and `MacNodeCodexThreadCatalogTests`.

### Expected behavior

`macos-swift` passes deterministically on any supported runner, or its timing assertions are expressed as generous upper bounds / relative measures that do not depend on runner speed.

### Actual behavior

Wall-clock assertions miss by fractions of a second and the job fails after exhausting all three retries:

```
BoundedProcessTests.swift:32:9:  Expectation failed: (ContinuousClock.now - startedAt → 2.357511334 seconds) < (.seconds(2) → 2.0 seconds)
BoundedProcessTests.swift:195:9: Expectation failed: (ContinuousClock.now - startedAt → 2.497009708 seconds) < (.seconds(2) → 2.0 seconds)
BoundedProcessTests.swift:121:9: Expectation failed: (ContinuousClock.now - startedAt → 3.970232792 seconds) < (.seconds(3) → 3.0 seconds)
RemoteGatewayProbeTests.swift:35:9: Expectation failed: (result → .failed("Remote gateway check timed out after 1000ms")) == (.ready(...))
BoundedCommandTests.swift:14:25: Expectation failed: output → nil
DashboardWindowSmokeTests.swift:118:9: Expectation failed
```

```
Test run with 1611 tests in 178 suites failed after 26.130 seconds with 6 issues.
swift test failed (attempt 3/3). Retrying…
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

Because `ci-gate` lists `macos-swift` under `REQUIRED_RESULTS`, this turns into a red required check on PRs whose diff cannot reach any of these surfaces.

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.2 (observed against `main` at `1aea2df9351`; runs cited above are `4d09189fcc8` and `1271bfbd00a`)

### Operating system

macOS — GitHub-hosted `macos-26` runner

### Install method

Source checkout (CI)

### Model

n/a — CI test infrastructure, no model involved

### Provider / routing chain

n/a — CI test infrastructure, no provider involved

### Impact and severity

A required check fails on unrelated PRs, most often from forks, and a contributor cannot rerun it (`gh run rerun` returns `Must have admin rights to Repository`; pushing again just starts a fresh attempt 1). It costs maintainer reruns and makes red CI ambiguous — the signal stops distinguishing "this diff is broken" from "the runner was slow."

### Additional information

**I have not measured a local failure rate on unmodified `main`**, and want to be straight about that rather than imply a repro I did not run: this machine has Command Line Tools only, no Xcode, so `swift test` cannot run here at all. The evidence above is entirely CI-observed. The within-job retry divergence is the strongest form available and is better controlled than a local loop, since all three attempts run identical code on one runner — but a maintainer with a macOS toolchain could confirm the rate directly.

I deliberately have **not** opened a PR against these tests. `CONTRIBUTING.md` says test-only changes that make a red or flaky suite pass will be closed, and that is the right rule. Filing this instead.
