issues.body:
### Summary

At the spawn-depth ceiling the sub-agent tool policy strips every tool that can produce a
completion event, but keeps the tool whose only purpose is to wait for one. A leaf that calls
`sessions_yield` ends its turn waiting for an event that nothing in its toolset can cause. The
run is then closed as `succeeded` with an empty result, and whatever it had already produced is
reported to the requester as nothing.

### Why the leaf has the tool at all

From the installed bundle's sub-agent tool policy:

- `SUBAGENT_TOOL_DENY_ALWAYS` = `gateway`, `agents_list`, `session_status`, `cron`, `sessions_send`
  (plus `message`, disabled at spawn time)
- `SUBAGENT_TOOL_DENY_LEAF` = `subagents`, `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, `sessions_spawn`

`sessions_yield` appears in neither list, so it survives into the leaf's effective toolset. But
the depth table is explicit that a depth-2 leaf can never spawn, and the docs describe yield as
the primitive to use "after spawning required child work". For a leaf, that precondition is
unsatisfiable by construction: there is no legal way for it to have a pending child.

### What it cost us

Chain: `main` (depth 0) → coordinator (depth 1) → worker (depth 2, leaf), `maxSpawnDepth: 2`.

1. The leaf did its job correctly and wrote three artifacts to disk (verified afterwards).
2. It then called `sessions_yield` with the message "waiting for the terminal result of the
   headless screenshot" — the screenshot was a synchronous `exec` that had already returned.
   There was no child, so no event would ever arrive.
3. The task closed. `openclaw tasks show` reports `status: succeeded`, `result: n/a`.
4. The orchestrator saw an empty return, treated it as "nothing was produced", and reissued the
   step. The second run rebuilt everything from scratch, producing a worse artifact than the one
   already sitting on disk.

Roughly 30 minutes of a 53-minute pipeline was spent recovering from a return that was empty
only because the wait primitive had no possible producer. Nothing in the logs surfaced the
cause: there is no error, no refusal, and no warning — the yield is accepted normally.

### Suggested fix

Either would close it:

1. Add `sessions_yield` to `SUBAGENT_TOOL_DENY_LEAF`. A leaf has no legal use for it, and the
   sub-agent system prompt already tells the model `canSpawn=false` at that depth.
2. Or make `sessions_yield` fail fast when the calling session has zero pending children or
   tasks — returning "nothing to wait for" instead of ending the turn. This is the safer of the
   two if some deployment does have a legitimate leaf-side wait we are not aware of.

Option 2 also helps non-leaf callers, where the same mistake is possible whenever a yield is
issued before (or without) the spawn it was meant to wait on.

### Environment

OpenClaw 2026.7.1-2, `maxSpawnDepth: 2`, native (pi) runtime, Linux.

issues.body:
## Summary

Prompt cache hit-rate dropped to ~0% after upgrading to OpenClaw 2026.7.1 on proxy-like endpoints (starport / group3 / deepseek / bailian / grok). Root cause: the 7/25 release silently changed the default cache-key pass-through behavior for proxy-like endpoints, and the subsequent 7/29 fix only covered one model (`sol`), leaving ~17 other models broken.

## Environment

- OpenClaw `2026.7.1 (2d2ddc4)`
- macOS 26.3.1 (arm64)
- Node v24.x
- Config: `models.providers.*.models[].supportsPromptCacheKey` per-model flag

## Observed behavior

1. Before the 7/25 upgrade: prompt cache hit-rate ~90% on proxy endpoints (cache key forwarded).
2. After the 7/25 upgrade (silent): hit-rate dropped to ~0% — proxy-like endpoints started stripping the cache key from upstream requests.
3. The 7/29 fix added the flag back for **one** model (`sol`) only; the other ~17 models using proxy-like endpoints remained broken. No migration notice, no schema change surfaced in changelog.

## Root cause hypothesis

- The cache-key pass-through is enforced per-model via `supportsPromptCacheKey` with **no provider-level default and no wildcard**.
- Proxy-like endpoints (endpoints that forward to an upstream aggregator) now require the flag explicitly, but the upgrade changed the default behavior without a migration path or startup warning.
- Consequence: silent regression that is only detectable by monitoring hit-rate (no error logs).

## Reproduction steps

1. Configure a proxy-like provider (e.g. `starport`, `group3`) with multiple models.
2. Do NOT set `supportsPromptCacheKey` on each model (as was valid pre-upgrade).
3. Upgrade to 2026.7.1, run traffic, observe prompt cache hit-rate ~0%.

## Suggested fixes (any of)

1. **Provider-level default / wildcard**: allow `supportsPromptCacheKey: true` at provider scope (or `*`) instead of per-model only.
2. **Proxy-like endpoints default to pass-through**: if the endpoint type is an upstream proxy, keep forwarding cache keys by default unless explicitly disabled.
3. **Migration guard**: on upgrade, if existing models lack the flag and the previous default was pass-through, either preserve the old behavior or emit a startup warning listing affected models.

## Impact

Silent cost regression (prompt cache miss → full context re-encoding per request) with no visible error; only detectable by comparing hit-rate before/after upgrade. Affected our setup with ~18 models on 5 proxy-like providers.

## Related context

- Fix workaround applied on our side: scripted batch config patch adding `supportsPromptCacheKey: true` to all affected models, hot-applied via `config patch` (no restart). This is a workaround, not a fix.

issues.body:
## Bug Report

**Version:** 2026.7.1-2
**Platform:** WSL2 (Ubuntu), Node v26.5.0

## Summary

When multiple subagents complete around the same time and all attempt to announce their results back to the parent (main) session simultaneously, they race to write to the same session JSONL file. OpenClaw detects the conflict via `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError`, retries 4 times with exponential backoff (5s → 10s → 20s), exhausts all retries, and then delivers a generic "Something went wrong" error to the user's channel (Telegram) instead of the actual completion content.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Spawn 6 subagents in parallel using `sessions_spawn` in a single turn
2. Each subagent also spawns its own child subagent internally (e.g. an editor agent)
3. Multiple subagents complete within a short window (~30–60 seconds of each other)
4. All attempt to announce completion back to the same main session simultaneously

## Expected Behaviour

Completion announcements queue and are processed in turn without stomping on the session file. The user sees each result delivered successfully.

## Actual Behaviour

From `/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-2026-08-03.log`:

```
lane task error: lane=main durationMs=59996 error="EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError: session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released: /home/frank/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/02a98ca1-4801-4753-9353-38f9a5996ef9.jsonl"

[warn] Subagent announce completion direct announce agent call transient failure, retrying 2/4 in 5s: EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError: session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released...
[warn] Subagent announce completion direct announce agent call transient failure, retrying 3/4 in 10s: EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError: ...
[warn] Subagent announce completion direct announce agent call transient failure, retrying 4/4 in 20s: EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError: ...
```

After exhausting all 4 retries, the user receives the generic error on Telegram:

> ⚠️ Something went wrong while processing your request. Please try again, or use /new to start a fresh session.

This happened multiple times across a single session with high subagent concurrency. Importantly, the underlying work had often **completed successfully** — the error was only in the delivery of the completion announcement back to the parent session.

## Impact

- User sees misleading error messages implying failure when the work may have succeeded
- Subagent completion events are silently dropped after retry exhaustion
- Makes it difficult to trust whether parallel subagent work actually reported back
- The error message suggests `/new` which would lose all session context unnecessarily

## Suggested Fix

A serial completion announcement queue for subagents reporting back to the same parent session — rather than all attempting concurrent writes to the session JSONL file. Alternatively, a proper blocking file lock (rather than retry-with-backoff against a race) would prevent the collision entirely.

## Workaround

Limit concurrent subagents to 2–3 max to reduce collision probability. Not viable for workloads that genuinely benefit from higher parallelism.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add a default-off Feishu option that natively mentions the current human sender on every group reply.

### Problem to solve

In busy Feishu group chats, an agent reply can be visually separated from the triggering message. Without a native mention, the person who asked may miss the answer or cannot tell which participant the bot is addressing. Prompting the model to type a name is not reliable and does not produce a native Feishu notification.

### Proposed solution

Add `channels.feishu.mentionSenderOnReply: true`, with the same option available per account. When enabled, automatic group replies include the inbound human sender as a required native mention recipient. Direct messages and proactive sends remain unchanged. Reuse the existing required-mention delivery path already used by Feishu bot-to-bot replies, including text chunking and static cards. Because Feishu streaming cards cannot carry native mention recipients, use normal text/static-card delivery for these replies.

The option remains off by default for backward compatibility.

### Alternatives considered

- Prompt-only name prefix: not deterministic and not a native mention.
- A plugin hook: `message_sending` can rewrite text but does not own Feishu mention recipients, so this would duplicate channel transport behavior.
- A new gate or approval layer: unrelated to delivery addressing and unnecessarily complex.

### Impact

- Affected: operators using OpenClaw in shared Feishu/Lark group chats.
- Severity: moderate usability issue.
- Frequency: every group reply when the operator wants explicit addressee notification.
- Consequence: missed or ambiguous replies in active groups.

### Evidence/examples

The Feishu channel already has a `requiredMentionTargets` path for bot-authored ingress replies. It attaches native mentions to text chunks and static cards and disables streaming cards when required mentions are present. The proposed change extends that existing path to human senders behind one default-off config flag.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

### Additional information

The implementation is intentionally channel-local and minimal: one config field and one condition at inbound reply-dispatch setup, plus tests, docs, and required generated config metadata.

issues.body:
## Summary

The Kimi Coding provider (`kimi/...`, subscription-backed Kimi Code API at `https://api.kimi.com/coding/`) does not expose usage or quota information on any OpenClaw surface: the Control UI usage views, the `/quota` command, or `openclaw status`. Kimi Code is a paid subscription product (Moderato/Allegretto/Allegro tiers) with hard quota limits, so users have no in-app visibility into how much of their subscription quota remains.

This is a revival of #67593, which was auto-closed as stale (not resolved) and is now locked. The problem still exists on the latest stable release.

## Current behavior (verified on OpenClaw 2026.7.1)

- The provider-usage modules (`dist/provider-usage.*.js`) contain zero references to `kimi`, `kimi-coding`, or `moonshot` — usage display is still limited to providers like `anthropic`, `openai-codex`, `zai`, `minimax`, `github-copilot`, `google-gemini-cli`, `xiaomi`.
- Usage display appears to key off OAuth auth profiles; Kimi Code authenticates via an `api_key` auth profile (`kimi:default`), which is not picked up by any usage surface.
- Users running subscription models `kimi/k3`, `kimi/k3-256k`, `kimi/kimi-for-coding` (and `kimi/kimi-for-coding-highspeed`) get no quota feedback.

## Expected behavior

- Kimi Coding provider participates in provider usage collection alongside zai/anthropic/openai-codex.
- `/quota`, the Control UI Usage page/composer indicator, and `openclaw status` report remaining Kimi Code quota when a Kimi Code credential is configured.
- api_key auth profiles are eligible for usage display, not only OAuth profiles (or the Kimi provider implements its own usage fetch regardless of credential mode).

## Kimi Code quota model (relevant for implementation)

Per Kimi's official docs (<https://www.kimi.com/code/docs/en/kimi-code/membership.html>):

- Weekly quota that refreshes every 7 days from subscription date (no rollover).
- A rolling 5-hour rate-limit window in addition to weekly quota.
- Quota is shared across all devices and API keys, and shared with the broader Kimi membership monthly cap.
- Plan tiers gate capabilities: `k3` requires Moderato+, 1M context on `k3` requires Allegretto+, `kimi-for-coding-highspeed` requires Allegretto+.
- Remaining quota and rate-limit status are visible in the Kimi Code Console (<https://www.kimi.com/code/console>), so the data exists server-side.

## Context

- #67593 — original feature request; auto-closed as stale and locked; problem unchanged.
- PR #20343 — previously implemented this (Kimi BillingService `GetUsages` parsing, Moonshot balance endpoint fallback, `KIMI_BALANCE_API_KEY` / `KIMI_BILLING_BEARER_TOKEN` / `KIMI_WEB_AUTH_TOKEN` support) but was closed without merging. The approach there still looks like the right starting point.

## Why it matters

Kimi Code subscriptions are paid plans with hard weekly + 5-hour quota windows. Users choosing between `k3` (1M context, ~2x quota cost) and `k3-256k` are making quota-consumption tradeoffs on every session switch — exactly the decision that in-app quota visibility would inform. Without it, the only option is manually checking the Kimi Code Console web UI.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.7.1 (stable, npm install)
- Provider: `kimi` via `@openclaw/kimi-provider` 2026.7.1
- Auth: `api_key` auth profile (`kimi:default`)
- Models in use: `kimi/k3`, `kimi/k3-256k`, `kimi/kimi-for-coding`
- Plan: Kimi Allegro

issues.body:
## Summary

The `@openclaw/feishu` channel plugin (2026.7.2-beta.5) fails to process inbound `im.message.receive_v1` events. The message content is decoded as a single `?`, the ingress spool throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'catch')`, and the agent turn finishes with `replies=0` — so the bot never replies to any DM.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.7.2-beta.6 (gateway local, macOS 26.5.1, x64)
- Plugin: `@openclaw/feishu` 2026.7.2-beta.5 (community maintained, installed from npm)
- Connection mode: websocket
- config: `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`, `allowFrom: [user open_id]`, `groupPolicy: "open"`, `requireMention: true`

## Reproduction

1. Configure the Feishu channel with a valid appId/appSecret and websocket mode.
2. Send a plain text DM to the bot from an allowlisted account.
3. Observe gateway logs.

Gateway log on every inbound DM:

```
info channels/feishu feishu[default]: received message from ou_<id> in oc_<p2p> (p2p)
info channels/feishu feishu[default]: Feishu[default] DM from ou_<id>: ？
info channels/feishu feishu[default]: dispatching to agent (session=agent:main:feishu:direct:ou_<id>)
warn channels/turn/execution visible channel turn dispatched with no queued reply payloads: ... sessionKey=agent:main:feishu:direct:ou_<id>
info channels/feishu feishu[default]: dispatch complete (queuedFinal=false, replies=0)
```

Concurrently, the same event id repeatedly fails on the durable spool:

```
error channels/feishu feishu ingress: spooled update 67be56cc64779b2ec4c41a9d4b05d851 failed; keeping for retry: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'catch')
```

## Expected behavior

- The inbound text should be decoded to its real content (not `?`).
- The agent turn should produce a reply and deliver it back to the DM.

## Actual behavior

- Inbound text is decoded as a single `?` regardless of what was sent.
- The turn completes with `replies=0`; no reply is ever delivered back to the DM.
- The ingress spool keeps retrying the same event and throwing `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'catch')`.

## Notes

- Outbound works: sending from the gateway to the DM succeeds (message is received in the Feishu app).
- A gateway restart clears the stuck event briefly, but any new inbound DM reproduces the decode failure and `replies=0` immediately.
- `openclaw plugins update feishu` reports the plugin is already up to date (2026.7.2-beta.5), so there is no newer version to fix this.
- Suspected area: event payload decoding in the ingress path (the `?` decode + `undefined.catch` suggest a missing/renamed field on the inbound event or reply-encoding object).

This makes the Feishu channel effectively unusable for two-way chat (inbound is received, but no reply is ever returned).

issues.body:
### Summary

Follow-up to #175951, closed as "already implemented" because #159697 removed the voice-only confirmation gate (10.10-beta.1). The closing review noted that the transcription part was not addressed: "browser transcription still lacks the proposed language hint … treat browser transcription-language control as a separate improvement." This request is that improvement: give the realtime input transcriber a language, derived from `talk.speechLocale` or a new `talk.realtime.transcriptionLanguage`, instead of letting it guess per utterance.

### Problem to solve

Realtime Talk (OpenAI provider) starts the client session with `audio.input.transcription: { model: "gpt-4o-mini-transcribe" }` and no `language` (`extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider-factory.ts` ~line 162; the GA session policy in `realtime-voice-session-policy.ts` already accepts `language`, the Talk client path just doesn't pass one). With no hint the transcriber guesses the language for each utterance, and short utterances come out wrong: a clear "Yes" transcribed as "Ja.", "Ies.", "Les."; "make the change" as "Make a deal."; "Set the real-time talk silence timeout" as "Real-time Talk, silent, timeout, setting". The transcript is not only a caption: user turns reach the agent as that text, and the agent-consult prompt includes the recent voice transcript as context, so mis-transcribed words change what the agent is asked to do. Removing the confirmation gate (#159697) doesn't change that.

### Proposed solution

1. In the Talk client-session builder, set `audio.input.transcription.language` from `talk.speechLocale` (BCP-47 → ISO-639-1, e.g. `en-US` → `en`) when it is configured.
2. Optionally add `talk.realtime.transcriptionLanguage` (and `transcriptionModel`) to override it, which would also cover #166773 (Azure needs a configurable transcription deployment).
3. Apply the same to the Gateway-controlled GA branch, which the closing review notes also omits `language`.

### Alternatives considered

- Longer confirmation phrases in `talk.realtime.instructions` (what we do now): helps, doesn't fix mis-transcribed requests.
- Switching the transcriber model: no config exists for it either.
- Leaving it: works for long sentences, fails on short ones; non-English users have the same problem in reverse.

### Impact

All realtime Talk users whose short utterances get auto-detected as another language; English users saying one or two words are the common case. Low risk: the OpenAI Realtime API already accepts `language` on input transcription; this is a one-field change plus config plumbing.

### Evidence/examples

From #175951 (Gateway 2026.10.3): Control UI user-turn transcripts "Ja.", "Ies.", "Les." for a clear "Yes"; "Make a deal." for "make the change" while the realtime model's own spoken reply said it heard "make the change". Request text reaching the agent: "Real-time Talk, silent, timeout, setting, and tell me what it is." Code: realtime-voice-provider-factory.ts sends `transcription: { model: OPENAI_REALTIME_INPUT_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL }` with no language; realtime-voice-session-policy.ts `buildOpenAIRealtimeGaSessionPolicy` has an optional `language` parameter.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Related: #175951 (closed), #166773 (Azure transcription deployment), #159697 (gate removal).

labels.description: Crash, hang, restart loop, or process-level availability failure.

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦐 gold shrimp

issues.body:
## Summary
Gateway event-loop stalls of ~33 s (internal DEF-61) are caused by SQLite lock contention on the main state database, not disk I/O or a plugin leak.

## Evidence
- **3 concurrent write-mode handles** are open on `state/openclaw.sqlite` from the same process.
- WAL is sitting at the 4 MB autocheckpoint threshold and is **not draining**.
- In 35 minutes after a gateway restart, there were **32 slow SQLite transaction lock waits**.
- Each wait blocks the Node.js event loop for up to **5,000 ms**; clusters of 4–5 back-to-back waits produce ~25 s of blocking, matching the observed ~33 s stalls.
- **I/O pressure is zero** (`%iowait = 0`). Contention is entirely inside SQLite's in-process locking layer.
- Workboard plugin was investigated and ruled out: it is disabled and has no `workboard.sqlite` on disk; earlier 19-connection reading was a misread.

## Root cause
`state/openclaw.sqlite` write access is not serialized. Multiple write connections from the same process compete on every write, preventing the WAL from checkpointing and stalling the event loop.

## Suggested fix
Serialize all writes to `state/openclaw.sqlite` through a single connection with an explicit write queue, rather than opening multiple concurrent write handles.

## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.7.2-beta.4
- Gateway runtime on Linux (WSL)
- Local model provider: Ollama

## Cross-reference
Internal tracker: DEF-61 (REBAR operating notes).

issues.body:
## Problem

Outbound channel plugin adapters cannot correlate a send with the canonical agent session, even though the delivery pipeline already carries `OutboundSessionContext`. Hook contexts expose a session key, but `ChannelOutboundContext` does not, so adapters must omit that relationship or infer it from unrelated fields.

## Proposed solution

Add an optional `sessionKey` to `ChannelOutboundContext` and forward `OutboundSessionContext.key` through the existing channel-handler boundary. Omit the field when no session is available so existing adapters and callers remain compatible.

## Why this shape

- It reuses the canonical session context already owned by the delivery pipeline.
- It is additive and requires no adapter changes.
- It avoids plugin-specific side channels or identity reconstruction.

## Prepared implementation

A focused implementation and regression test are available for review on the contributor fork:

https://github.com/usedhonda/openclaw/tree/contrib/plugin-outbound-session-key

AI-assisted: Yes. The contributor reviewed the problem statement, implementation shape, test evidence, and final diff.

issues.body:
## Summary

In a Docker-sandboxed session (`agents.defaults.sandbox.mode: "non-main"`), the native `apply_patch` tool consistently fails on paths **inside the rw-mounted workspace** and returns a failure payload with **no error detail at all**. In the same session, `bash` `git apply` on identical content succeeds, and the `write` tool works. The empty tool failure then becomes the cron job's `lastError` ("⚠️ 🩹 Apply Patch failed"), masking the run's actual first failure in the failure alert.

Distinct from #93140: that report is about paths *outside* the workspace (e.g. `/tmp`) without Docker sandboxing. Here the target paths are ordinary workspace paths on the rw bind mount, and the shell can write them fine.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.7.2-beta.4 (5e63b36), Linux 6.17 x86_64 (Ubuntu)
- Agent runtime: codex (`@openclaw/codex`), model `gpt-5.6-sol` via `openai` provider
- Sandbox: `mode: "non-main"`, custom image `openclaw-sandbox:grayden` (Debian bookworm based); also observed on the predecessor container before the image swap, so not image-specific
- Workspace bind: `/home/<user>/.openclaw/workspace -> /workspace` (rw)
- Container user: uid 1001 == host workspace owner uid 1001
- Trigger context: cron job with `sessionTarget: isolated` (runs sandboxed under non-main mode)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Sandboxed session (isolated cron session under `sandbox.mode: "non-main"` with an rw workspace bind).
2. Agent calls `apply_patch` with an `add` of a new file under `/workspace/raw/...` and/or an `update` to an existing file under `/workspace/research/...`.

## Actual behaviour

Every `apply_patch` call fails with a payload that carries no reason:

```json
{
  "status": "failed",
  "changes": [
    { "path": "/workspace/raw/cre-data/2026-07-31_....json", "kind": { "type": "add" } },
    { "path": "/workspace/research/cre/2026-03-29_....md", "kind": { "type": "update", "move_path": null } }
  ]
}
```

No `error`, no `reason`, no stderr — nothing to diagnose from.

In the **same session**, on the **same paths**:

- `bash` `chmod o+w <dirs>` succeeds (and does not fix `apply_patch`)
- `bash` heredoc `git apply --whitespace=nowarn` with the same diff content: **succeeds** (`exitCode: 0`)
- Directory listing shows the mount is writable for the container user (uid 1001, same as host owner; dirs 775, files 644)

Observed daily across five consecutive scheduled runs (2026-07-27 → 2026-07-31), spanning two sandbox container generations.

## Expected behaviour

- `apply_patch` should succeed on writable paths inside the mounted workspace (parity with `write` and shell writes), or
- at minimum, the failure payload should carry the underlying error so the agent/operator can react to the real cause.

## Impact

1. Sandboxed agents cannot use the native patch tool against their own workspace; they burn turns on retries/chmod attempts and eventually shell workarounds.
2. The empty failure is undiagnosable from transcripts.
3. Worst part operationally: the tool-level diagnostic (`⚠️ 🩹 Apply Patch failed`) is promoted to the cron job's `lastError`/failure alert, displacing the run's actual first failure. In our case the real defect was network egress (sandbox `network: "none"`), but five days of Telegram failure alerts reported only "Apply Patch failed" — the alert pointed at the wrong defect the entire time.

## Secondary (unconfirmed)

One report on the same host of a native patch-writer failure on a writable workspace path in an *unsandboxed* session the same day (fallback path succeeded). Not yet reproduced with receipts; noted in case the fault is not sandbox-specific.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (previous MiniMax VL routing fix no longer covers the newly image-capable M3 catalog entry)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

OpenClaw 2026.7.2-beta.5 (`ee929db`) marks `minimax/MiniMax-M3` as accepting `input: ["text", "image"]` while the provider uses MiniMax's Anthropic-compatible endpoint. OpenClaw therefore treats the active model as natively vision-capable and the `image` tool returns the image to M3 as `Loaded 1 image for direct visual inspection` instead of invoking the plugin-owned `MiniMax-VL-01` image-understanding provider.

MiniMax's compatible Anthropic API documentation says image/document input is not supported on that route: https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/text-anthropic-api

This silently loses image understanding rather than producing a provider error. It is the M3 version of the routing regression previously tracked in #64244.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install OpenClaw `2026.7.2-beta.5` (`ee929db`) and enable the bundled `minimax` plugin.
2. Configure MiniMax with `api: "anthropic-messages"` and `baseUrl: "https://api.minimax.io/anthropic"`.
3. Use `minimax/MiniMax-M3` as the active chat model with the bundled/catalog capability `input: ["text", "image"]`.
4. Send an image and ask the agent to inspect it, or call the `image` tool on a local image.

### Expected behavior

OpenClaw should route image understanding through the plugin-owned `minimax/MiniMax-VL-01` provider and return a textual image analysis, as documented for MiniMax and as intended by the fix cited when #64244 was closed.

### Actual behavior

The transcript records:

```text
assistant stopReason=toolUse: image(...)
toolResult: Loaded 1 image for direct visual inspection.
```

The following M3 response says the tool returned no description and repeatedly plans to retry/analyze, but never obtains visual content. In the observed Telegram turn it emitted 22,755 characters of planning text and stopped at `Let me finalize.` without an actual answer.

There was no 4xx response, so normal model fallback did not activate.

### Root cause evidence

- The beta.5 MiniMax catalog and provider docs declare M3 with `input: ["text", "image"]`.
- The image tool prioritizes the `modelHasVision` native path before configured image-model fallback selection.
- The native path returns the image block to the active M3 Anthropic-compatible request rather than calling `MiniMax-VL-01`.
- MiniMax documents that the compatible Anthropic API does not accept image/document input.

### Verified workaround

Override M3 as text-only and explicitly select the plugin-owned vision provider:

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "imageModel": {
        "primary": "minimax/MiniMax-VL-01"
      }
    }
  },
  "models": {
    "providers": {
      "minimax": {
        "models": [
          {
            "id": "MiniMax-M3",
            "input": ["text"]
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

After restarting, a no-delivery test with M3 produced this image-tool result:

```text
Text: "VISION TEST 731"
Blue Shape: Square, left side
Orange Shape: Circle, right side
```

The final assistant answer was one concise sentence with the correct text and shapes.

### Suggested fix

Make image capability route-aware for MiniMax M3, or special-case MiniMax chat models on the Anthropic-compatible route so image-tool resolution prefers the plugin-owned `MiniMax-VL-01` media provider instead of the native active-model path. Add a regression test equivalent to the M2.7 coverage referenced in #64244, but with M3's new catalog entry.

### Environment

- OpenClaw: `2026.7.2-beta.5` (`ee929db`)
- Install: npm global
- OS: Linux
- Provider: `minimax`
- Chat model: `MiniMax-M3`
- Chat API: `anthropic-messages`
- Image provider: bundled MiniMax plugin / `MiniMax-VL-01`

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug

### Is this a beta blocker?

No

### Summary

In Telegram `streaming.mode: "progress"` with commentary enabled, the first user-visible commentary/preamble can appear twice in the same progress bubble even though the model emitted the commentary only once.

The duplicate occurs when a provider bridge forwards the same normalized commentary as a streaming snapshot and then as a completed snapshot with different `itemId` values. `pushCommentaryProgress()` currently deduplicates by line ID, so both snapshots are appended.

### Reproduction steps

1. Configure Telegram progress commentary:

```json
{
  "streaming": {
    "mode": "progress",
    "progress": {
      "commentary": true,
      "label": false,
      "toolProgress": false
    }
  }
}
```

2. At the progress compositor boundary, send two adjacent preamble events containing the same normalized text but different item IDs:

```ts
await progress.pushCommentaryProgress("Checking the workspace", {
  itemId: "streaming-preamble",
});
await progress.pushCommentaryProgress("Checking   the workspace", {
  itemId: "completed-preamble",
});
```

3. Inspect the Telegram progress preview.

A provider-level instance presents the same shape: a streaming preamble snapshot followed by its completed snapshot under a different ID.

### Expected behavior

The adjacent snapshots represent one logical commentary message, so the progress bubble should contain:

```text
Checking the workspace
```

once.

### Actual behavior

The progress bubble contains the same first commentary twice. Later commentary messages are not duplicated unless they arrive in the same two-snapshot shape.

### Root cause

`pushCommentaryProgress()` creates a compositor line keyed by `itemId`. Existing `seenLineIds` and merge behavior correctly handle repeated updates under the same ID, but cannot recognize equivalent adjacent commentary when the provider changes IDs between streaming and completion snapshots.

The text has already been normalized, so the compositor sees equal `line.text` values but distinct `line.id` values and appends both.

### Proposed fix

Coalesce only an immediately adjacent `Commentary` line whose normalized text is identical. Replace the previous line with the newest line object so a later retraction using the completed item ID still works:

```ts
const previousLine = lines.at(-1);
if (
  typeof previousLine === "object" &&
  previousLine.label === "Commentary" &&
  previousLine.text === line.text
) {
  lines = [...lines.slice(0, -1), line];
  return false;
}
```

This is deliberately narrower than global text deduplication. Repeating the same commentary after an intervening tool or progress event remains valid and visible.

### Regression tests

A local source patch at `ee929dbb857c717a60f3b2b502db5a6dd31b5c11` adds:

- a core compositor test with identical normalized commentary and different IDs;
- a Telegram dispatch integration test using `streaming-preamble` and `completed-preamble` IDs.

Before the fix:

```text
pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/progress-draft-compositor.test.ts --config vitest.config.ts --pool forks --testTimeout 10000

FAIL 1 / 36: expected one occurrence, received two
```

After the fix:

```text
PASS src/channels/progress-draft-compositor.test.ts: 36 / 36
PASS extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.progress-updates.test.ts: 25 / 25
```

A direct smoke against the generated runtime bundle produced `occurrences: 1` after the patch.

### OpenClaw version

`2026.7.2-beta.5 (ee929db)`

### Operating system

macOS 26.5.2 arm64, Node.js 26.0.0

### Installation method

Global npm installation under Homebrew Node

### Additional evidence

For the observed production occurrence:

- the native model transcript contained exactly one commentary item with the duplicated text;
- the channel ingress log contained one inbound Telegram update;
- the duplication was therefore introduced during progress rendering rather than by the model or duplicate inbound delivery.

Related but not duplicate: #111944 concerns commentary not being delivered at all. This report concerns delivered commentary being rendered twice when snapshot IDs change.

issues.body:
**Bug type:** Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

**Beta release blocker:** No

### Summary

A positive `timeoutSeconds` below 1 on `POST /hooks/agent` is floored to `0`, and `0` is the "no timeout" sentinel downstream, so the agent turn runs with an effectively unlimited timeout (~24.8 days) — longer than if the field were omitted (48 h default). The docs say invalid/nonpositive values are ignored; 0.5 is positive, yet it is neither honored nor ignored.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable hooks and send `POST /hooks/agent` with `{"message": "ping", "timeoutSeconds": 0.5}`.
2. `normalizeAgentPayload` (`src/gateway/hooks.ts`) accepts it because `0.5 > 0`, then stores `Math.floor(0.5) = 0` as `payload.timeoutSeconds`.
3. The isolated cron run passes it to `resolveAgentTimeoutMs({ overrideSeconds: 0 })` (`src/agents/timeout.ts`), where `override === 0` returns `NO_TIMEOUT_MS`.

Running that path from current main (`6facd0d02d`):

```
timeoutSeconds=0.5  -> payload.timeoutSeconds=0         -> agent timeout = 2147000000 ms (24.85 days) | cron run override = undefined
timeoutSeconds=1.9  -> payload.timeoutSeconds=1         -> agent timeout = 1000 ms (0.00 days) | cron run override = 1000
timeoutSeconds=2    -> payload.timeoutSeconds=2         -> agent timeout = 2000 ms (0.00 days) | cron run override = 2000
timeoutSeconds=0    -> payload.timeoutSeconds=undefined -> agent timeout = 172800000 ms (2.00 days) | cron run override = undefined
```

### Expected behavior

Per `docs/gateway/config-hooks.md` ("Positive numeric turn-timeout override; direct payload values are floored to whole seconds. Invalid/nonpositive values are ignored."), a value that floors to 0 should be treated like an ignored value (fall back to the configured/default timeout), never as "no timeout".

### Actual behavior

`timeoutSeconds: 0.5` disables the turn timeout entirely (2147000000 ms), while `timeoutSeconds: 0` correctly falls back to the 48 h default.

### OpenClaw version

main @ 6facd0d02d (package version 2026.10.4)

### Operating system

macOS 26.7.1 (arm64)

### Install method

From source (main)

### Model

N/A — the timeout is resolved before any model call; independent of model.

### Provider / routing chain

N/A

### Impact and severity

A caller asking for a very short timeout gets the opposite: a hook-triggered run that can hang for weeks, holding a run slot. Narrow trigger (sub-second values), but silent.

---

Suggested fix: in `normalizeAgentPayload`, keep the documented flooring but drop the result when it floors to 0 (`floored >= 1 ? floored : undefined`), so sub-second values behave like other ignored values. I'd like to send a PR with a regression test.

This issue was generated with AI (Claude Code) following my direction; I reviewed it.

issues.title: server_is_overloaded on ChatGPT-subscription OAuth: fallback fails when fallback model missing from agent catalog + session overrides silently bypass fallback chain

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Normal backlog priority with limited blast radius.

labels.name: clawsweeper:needs-info
labels.description: ClawSweeper needs more reporter information before it can verify this issue.

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦪 silver shellfish

issues.body:
### Environment
- OpenClaw: 2026.7.1-2 (Windows 11, node 24)
- Primary model: `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` via ChatGPT-subscription OAuth (`openai-chatgpt-responses` API)
- Fallback: `openrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k3`
- ~20 agents on one gateway

### Observed behaviour
1. Since ~23 July (and through 30 July), primary-model calls fail with `errorCode: server_is_overloaded`, `errorType: service_unavailable_error`, zero tokens processed. Failures are intermittent and do not appear on status.openai.com.
2. On most agents the overload classification works and the run falls back correctly (observed on the main agent: overload → profile rotation → model fallback to OpenRouter — success).
3. On agents where the configured fallback model was **not present in that agent's `models.json` catalog**, the run ended `non_deliverable_terminal_turn` with no fallback attempt — the user got a raw "service temporarily overloaded" message.
4. Separately, sessions carrying a user-sourced `modelOverride`/`authProfileOverride` (set during an earlier incident) silently bypassed the fallback chain entirely and failed hard on 401/403s.
5. Fleet-wide, the global `auth.order.openai` put one subscription profile first, so every agent auto-resolved to a single ChatGPT subscription — concentrating the unpublished 5-hour/weekly subscription caps across ~20 agents and producing 429s that look like "no heavy usage" per agent.

### Expected behaviour
- Fallback should fire on `server_is_overloaded` even when the fallback model is missing from the agent catalog (skip gracefully to the next fallback, or warn loudly in config audit), never end terminal on first failure with an unresolvable fallback.
- Session-level model overrides should be visible/expiring, or at least surfaced in `/status`, so stale overrides from past incidents don't silently pin agents to dead providers.
- Docs should call out that ChatGPT-subscription OAuth has unpublished usage windows, and that N agents sharing one subscription profile share its caps.

### Workarounds we applied
- Added the fallback model entry to every agent's `models.json`.
- Cleared stale session-level model/auth overrides across the fleet.
- Reordered `auth.order.openai` to spread agents across subscription profiles.

### Happy to provide
Redacted trajectory excerpts, catalog diffs, and repro steps on request.

issues.body:
## Summary

OpenClaw plugin daemons (e.g. `kaka-coord-daemon.py`, `5why_daemon.py` for LALA / kaka) use **PID-only liveness check**: if the PID is alive in `ps`, launchd + framework think it's healthy. But the daemon can be **stuck** (process alive, no work done) for many hours with **no detection**.

## Reproduction

```
2026-07-29 13:41  LALA 5why_daemon health log last write
... 21 hours no health log entries ...
2026-07-30 14:41  LALA still writes to vault via separate path (vault ok, daemon dead)
```

- daemon process: PID 72038, alive (0% CPU, 0.1% MEM, just sits)
- daemon stderr/stdout: 0 bytes written in 21 hours
- daemon health log: last entry from 7/29 13:41
- BUT vault still receives daemon-written entries (via separate FSEvents path that bypasses the stuck main loop)

→ **Process alive ≠ process working**. launchd doesn't know to restart it.

## Diagnosis (5 Why)

1. Why daemon stuck? → main loop is blocked / deadlocked somewhere (no log emitted)
2. Why no detection? → launchd liveness = PID exists. Framework health check = same PID check. **Both fail to probe actual work being done.**
3. Why liveness is PID-only? → Framework / launchd never had a "real liveness" concept. Stale health log was never flagged.
4. Why never added real liveness? → Initial daemon design prioritized startup simplicity over fault tolerance. **Not in vendor's first-pass scope.**
5. Root cause: **OpenClaw daemon architecture assumes daemons that "die cleanly"** — but real-world daemons silently hang on blocking IO / unhandled exceptions / dependency death. PID-only liveness can't catch this.

## Suggested Fix (vendor-side, 3 options)

### Option A: Watchdog with mtime check (smallest change)
- Add `daemonWatchdog.checkLastHealthLog()` that compares `mtime(daemon_health_log)` to `now()`
- If `now - mtime > 30 minutes`, daemon is considered stuck → log warning + trigger `launchctl kickstart`
- ~30 lines in framework / daemon side

### Option B: Real liveness probe (medium)
- Daemon exposes a `/healthz` endpoint that **actually does work** (e.g. reads 1 vault entry + writes 1 timestamp)
- Framework polls this endpoint (not PID)
- If endpoint times out or returns stale timestamp → kill + restart
- ~50 lines daemon + ~30 lines framework

### Option C: Per-component daemon split (large)
- Currently 1 daemon = multiple components (coord + FSEvents + cron + state)
- Split into N small daemons, each with own health check
- Stuck one doesn't affect others
- ~weeks of refactor

## Impact

- **P1**: Production users (LALA / kaka) experience silent failures where daemon "looks alive" but isn't doing work
- Workaround: users have to manually `kill -9 <pid>` then `launchctl kickstart` — fragile
- Vault data path **bypasses stuck daemon** (FSEvents separate) so it doesn't lose data, but coordination / heartbeat / state sync breaks silently

## Related

- `#116258`: Plugin runtime surface missing `dispatchReplyWithBufferedBlockDispatcher` (separate issue, opened earlier today for LALA / kaka)
- Both stem from same root: daemon framework assumes "die cleanly, restart cleanly" — doesn't handle "silent hang"

## Diagnostic commands for maintainers

```
# Stuck daemon detection (any platform)
ps -p <pid> -o pid,etime,%cpu,command
ls -la <health_log_path>
stat -f "%Sm" <health_log_path>

# If ps says alive BUT health log mtime > 1h → daemon stuck
```

## Author

- Logged in as `xiaov1024` (v's GitHub account, authorized for OpenClaw issue creation)
- Diagnosed from LALA 5why_daemon PID 72038 (22:51+ uptime, 21 hours of stale health log on 2026-07-30)

issues.body:
### What happened

The Signal plugin in OpenClaw `2026.7.2-beta.5` repeatedly failed with Node's internal module-state assertion:

```text
Unexpected status of a module that is imported again after being required
```

There were 149 occurrences during the incident date. The Signal channel repeatedly failed and could not provide reliable messaging.

Rolling the OpenClaw core and Signal plugin back to compatible `2026.7.1` versions removed the assertion. The stable Signal plugin then loaded successfully.

### Why this appears Signal-specific

The assertion text matches open issue #114176, but that report reproduces through `openclaw agent` with a custom `openai-completions` provider. This reproduction occurs during Signal plugin/channel initialization. The entry path and affected product surface are different, so this report is cross-linked rather than assuming an identical root cause.

### Expected behavior

The Signal plugin loads once and starts or connects to its managed `signal-cli` daemon without an ESM/CommonJS module-state assertion.

### Actual behavior

The beta plugin repeatedly entered the assertion/failure path, adding restart work and making the channel unavailable. A controlled rollback eliminated the assertion.

### Reproduction evidence

- Affected core: `2026.7.2-beta.5` (`ee929db`)
- Affected Signal plugin: beta-compatible version installed with that core
- Node: failures occurred before and after the host runtime update from `v24.18.0` to `v24.18.1`
- Occurrences: 149 on the incident date
- Recovery: rollback to core `2026.7.1-2` and Signal plugin `2026.7.1`

The failure predated the Node runtime update, so a resident mixed-runtime process did not initiate it.

### Suggested investigation

- Trace Signal plugin initialization across native import and fallback `require` paths.
- Compare that loader boundary with the custom-provider path in #114176 and the previously fixed loader reports referenced there.
- Add a regression test that initializes the Signal plugin repeatedly in the same process and across plugin reload/restart paths.
- Preserve the original stack/cause when reporting the Node assertion.

Redacted logs and preserved beta package artifacts can be supplied if needed.

issues.body:
## Problem

There is no single CLI surface to enumerate the tools an agent can actually
call through the OpenClaw gateway: built-in tools, plugin-contributed tools,
and MCP-server-exposed tools live in three different inspection paths today.

For users auditing "what tools does my agent have", this means scanning
`openclaw --help` for subcommands, reading each `~/.openclaw/plugins/<id>/`
manifest, and talking to MCP servers separately.

## Proposal

Add a top-level `openclaw tools` subcommand with three actions:

- `openclaw tools list [--source plugin|mcp|builtin]` — flat list of tool names
- `openclaw tools describe <name>` — schema, source, version, plugin/server id
- `openclaw tools call <name> --args-json '{...}'` — invoke directly
  (subject to the same exec approvals as an agent-driven call; no new bypass)

Output JSON or table via `--json`.

## Why now

- `#64671` (closed) established the pattern with `openclaw skills list` for one category.
- `#53215` (closed) acknowledged MCP tool exposure conceptually, but no CLI aggregation.
- `#70533` (closed) surfaced plugin-discovery pathology, suggesting users want to *see* what plugins contributed.

This is a discoverability layer over tools that are already wired — no behavior
change, no new approval path, no allowlist relaxation.

## Reproduction

```
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.7.2-beta.3 (d111bef)
$ openclaw tools --help
(unknown command — falls back to generic --help output)
```

## Notes

- Reuse existing `tools.allow` and exec approvals — do not bypass.
- Read-only by default; `call` mirrors what an agent would do under current security policy.
- Suggest labels: `enhancement`, `area: cli`, `area: tools`.

Reported by: OpenClaw end-user (琬弦) on behalf of an operator who needs
to audit tool availability across plugin/MCP/builtin categories.

issues.body:
### What problem does this solve?

Workboard cards can currently appear complete without strong execution evidence. Examples include:

- Cards marked `done` without structured proof.
- Parent cards completed while required children or dependencies remain active.
- Planning/decomposition treated as implementation completion.
- Cards linked to open pull requests marked complete before review or merge.

This can make automation report work as finished when it is not.

### Proposed scope

Introduce fail-closed completion gates that:

- Require passed proof containing an exact command, URL, or artifact path plus a result note.
- Reject completion when required children, dependencies, or blockers remain unresolved.
- Keep planning/decomposition states distinct from execution completion.
- Require appropriate review/merge evidence for pull-request-linked work.
- Record explicit, reviewable waivers when follow-up child work intentionally remains open.
- Add diagnostics for legacy inconsistent cards without deleting or overwriting history.
- Preserve the existing authority split: Workboard records execution evidence; higher-level GitHub/Speculoos workflows remain authoritative for review and integration.

### Compatibility questions

- Should this enforcement live in core Workboard or remain a plugin-level policy?
- What legacy/import path should exist for cards created without proof?
- Should decomposition leave the parent open by default?
- What exact evidence is required for pull-request-linked cards?
- Should proof URLs, paths, or notes receive additional redaction or validation?

### Scope exclusions

This proposal intentionally excludes canonical task identity, source-reference metadata, tenant redesign, production configuration, credentials, and scheduler changes.

### Validation evidence

A local implementation prototype passes:

- Workboard extension tests: 185
- Contract tests: 1,428
- TypeScript extension check
- Oxlint with zero warnings/errors

No repository code, configuration, or credentials were changed; this issue is a proposal for maintainer discussion.

## Summary

Move Nostr channel status and profile editing into its packaged plugin Settings presentation.

## Problem to solve

The Nostr plugin owns the channel backend, but the Control UI still owns its custom status card, profile form, request controller, and translations. This leaves channel-specific behavior in the shared Settings implementation during the maintainer-requested plugin ownership cutover.

## Proposed solution

Use the existing packaged Settings loader for an owned channel-detail placement. Keep the editor instance page-scoped so drafts survive closing the detail and reconnecting the same client. The host retains schema configuration and supplies account-scoped authenticated HTTP operations with cancellation and credential retry fences.

A modal-scoped mount would lose existing drafts and pending-operation behavior. Keeping the old renderer beside a plugin implementation would leave competing owners.

No intended visual or backend behavior change. Preserve profile import/publication, account routing, saved-credential fallback, timeouts, translations, and host configuration controls. No new RPC, runtime plugin activation, or publishing workflow.

## Evidence/examples

The existing Nostr profile backend and channel Settings tests define the preserved behavior. The implementation will include plugin-owned view tests, real host lifetime/configuration tests, and a packaged browser integration case.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The exported terminal-outcome merge produces different canonical results for equivalent provider-failure and queue-timeout evidence depending on which observation is processed last.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Check out OpenClaw 2026.7.2 and run the focused reproduction against the source tree.
2. Build a provider-failure observation and a queue/gateway wait-timeout observation, then call the exported terminal-outcome merge with the two observations in both possible orders.
3. Compare the canonical `reason` returned for each order.

Focused reproduction result:
- `queueTimeout -> providerFailure`: `reason=failed`
- `providerFailure -> queueTimeout`: `reason=timed_out`

### Expected behavior

Queue-layer or gateway-draining wait timeouts are wait-layer uncertainty and must not overwrite a provider failure when there is no hard-timeout attribution. Equivalent evidence should produce the same canonical terminal outcome regardless of observation order; in this case both orders should remain `failed` (or otherwise preserve the provider failure), not become `timed_out` solely because the queue timeout was observed last.

### Actual behavior

The result depends on observation order. The focused pure merge reproduction reports `timeoutThenFailure.reason=failed`, but `failureThenTimeout.reason=timed_out`. A later non-sticky queue timeout overwrites the earlier provider failure. Relevant merge logic is in `src/agents/agent-run-terminal-outcome.ts` (around lines 517, 524, 681, and 724), with the snapshot preservation call sites in `src/gateway/server-methods/agent-job.ts` (around lines 104 and 115).

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.2

### Operating system

Windows 11 with WSL2 Ubuntu 22.04.5

### Install method

Source checkout / pnpm test

### Model

N/A - pure runtime terminal outcome reproduction

### Provider / routing chain

N/A - no model/provider request is required

### Additional provider/model setup details

This is a deterministic merge-logic reproduction and does not depend on model inference, credentials, or provider routing.

### Logs

```shell
Observed output from the focused reproduction:

timeoutThenFailure.reason=failed
failureThenTimeout.reason=timed_out


The existing focused `agent-run-terminal-outcome` baseline tests pass; the additional order-permutation reproduction fails the expected order-invariance contract.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected systems: agent-run terminal outcome classification and gateway job status reporting.
Severity: Moderate; this can misclassify a provider failure as a timeout and distort diagnostics or retry decisions.
Frequency: Deterministic for the two observation orders in the focused reproduction; a full live runtime path emitting both orders has not yet been demonstrated.
Consequence: callers can receive different terminal status/reason fields for equivalent evidence, with a provider failure reported as `timed_out` when the queue timeout arrives last.

### Additional information

This is distinct from closed issues #106652 and #122045: those concerned successful completion being discarded or reply-run queue rejection, not order-dependent merging of provider failure with a non-sticky queue timeout.

Evidence strength is currently a pure terminal-merge reproduction plus source/call-site mapping. The focused reproduction does not yet prove that the same live runtime run can emit the two observations in both orders.

### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Running `openclaw channels login --channel whatsapp` on OpenClaw 2026.7.1-2 (macOS) consistently produces "WhatsApp Web connection ended before fully opening. Non-Error rejection" error. The machine has working internet (browser can access web.whatsapp.com and display QR code fine), WhatsApp plugin dependency baileys@7.0.0-rc13 is installed, and no proxy/env overrides are active.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `openclaw channels login --channel whatsapp`
2. Observe output: "Waiting for WhatsApp connection..."
3. After a few seconds, observe: "WhatsApp Web connection ended before fully opening. Non-Error rejection"
4. The error persists across:
   - Multiple `openclaw channels remove --channel whatsapp` + re-add cycles
   - `openclaw gateway restart` ×2
   - `npm install` of WhatsApp plugin dependencies
   - Adding account with `--use-env` flag
   - No proxy env vars set

### Expected behavior

Running `openclaw channels login --channel whatsapp` should display a QR code in the terminal for the user to scan with WhatsApp mobile app, then pair successfully and save credentials to disk. This was working on a previous session that was linked and running before the error occurred. The browser on the same machine can access web.whatsapp.com and display a QR code for manual pairing.

### Actual behavior

Running `openclaw channels login --channel whatsapp` produces:

```
Waiting for WhatsApp connection...
WhatsApp Web connection ended before fully opening. Non-Error rejection
Channel login failed: Error: Non-Error rejection
```

The WebSocket connection from the Baileys library (7.0.0-rc13) to WhatsApp servers closes before the QR code can be generated. The `lastDisconnect` update from Baileys has no detailed error (undefined), causing the OpenClaw WhatsApp plugin to fall back to "Non-Error rejection".

Network diagnostics confirmed:
- DNS resolution OK (web.whatsapp.com → 31.13.87.51)
- HTTP connectivity OK (curl https://web.whatsapp.com returns 200)
- Ping OK (g.whatsapp.net responds in ~25ms)
- No proxy environment variables set
- Browser on same machine successfully loads web.whatsapp.com and displays QR code

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.1-2 (0790d9f)

### Operating system

macOS 26.5.2 (arm64) - running on UTM virtual machine

### Install method

npm global (via Homebrew: brew install openclaw)

### Model

N/A - WhatsApp channel login, not model-related

### Provider / routing chain

N/A - Channel login, no model routing

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
Running from terminal:


$ openclaw channels login --channel whatsapp
✅ Added WhatsApp account "default".
Waiting for WhatsApp connection...
WhatsApp Web connection ended before fully opening. Non-Error rejection
Channel login failed: Error: Non-Error rejection


From cron run context (via tool api):
- OutboundDeliveryError: No active WhatsApp Web listener
- Both stock-portfolio and daily-fortune cron jobs completed analysis but failed to deliver due to WhatsApp being disconnected

Source code analysis:
- session-DriaHt7V.js: `reject(toLintErrorObject(update.lastDisconnect ?? new Error("Connection closed"), "Non-Error rejection"));`
  - This fires when Baileys emits connection.update with connection="close" before emitting connection="open"
  - lastDisconnect is undefined/null, indicating the WebSocket closed without a specific error from WhatsApp's side

- login-C48y0jlx.js shows the normal flow: createWaSocket → waitForLoginResult → onQr callback for QR rendering
  - The onQr callback never fires because the connection closes before QR generation

- socket-timing: connectTimeoutMs defaults to 60000ms (60s), so timeout is not the issue

Resolved with browser.test:
- web.whatsapp.com loads in Chrome and displays QR code for scanning ← confirms network is not blocked
- DNS resolves, PING ~25ms latency
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: All WhatsApp channel users on OpenClaw 2026.7.1 (baileys@7.0.0-rc13)
Severity: High - blocks WhatsApp channel setup and reconnection entirely
Frequency: 100% - reproduced on every attempt across multiple reinstall/restart cycles
Consequence: 
- Cannot link WhatsApp Web account
- Existing sessions that get disconnected cannot reconnect
- All scheduled cron jobs targeting WhatsApp (stock reports, daily fortunes) fail to deliver
- No fallback channel for WhatsApp users

### Additional information

Key finding: The Baileys WebSocket connection closes with no error from WhatsApp's side (lastDisconnect is undefined). This differs from a similar reported issue (#64296) where the error was "408 Request Time-out WebSocket Error" with a clear timeout. Our case shows "Non-Error rejection" which means the connection is being terminated by the server without sending an error frame.

Hypothesis: baileys@7.0.0-rc13 might use an outdated protocol handshake or WebSocket subprotocol that WhatsApp servers no longer accept, while the browser-based web.whatsapp.com uses the latest protocol version.

Workaround attempted:
- Gateway restart (multiple times) ❌
- WhatsApp account removal and re-add ❌
- npm install / dependency rebuild ❌
- --use-env flag for account setup ❌
- No proxy env vars to clear ❌

Browsers on same machine work fine with web.whatsapp.com ✅

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On 2026.7.2-beta.5 and 2026.7.2-beta.7, the gateway main thread burns a sustained 100–110% of one core under normal multi-agent load (~65 agents, ~50 Slack socket accounts), with perf showing 75.97% of main-thread CPU in zlib CompressionStream::AfterThreadPoolWork callbacks and strace showing ~17,900 failing readlink/s cycling agent SQLite state paths, while instance CPU sits at ~10%.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a gateway with a large fleet (~65 agents, ~50 Slack socket-mode accounts, Anthropic provider) on 2026.7.2-beta.5 or beta.7 (npm global install, Ubuntu 24.04, Node v24.18.0, systemd unit).
2. Let normal weekday agent traffic flow (streaming model calls across multiple agents).
3. Within hours, observe the gateway PID at 100–110% CPU (state R) and [diagnostic] liveness warnings with eventLoopUtilization=1, cpuCoreRatio≈1.0.
4. During the burn: `strace -c -p <pid>` for 10s → 178,725 readlink calls, 178,725 errors (~17.9k/s failing), 25,662 statx. `perf record -F 99 -g` for 15s → 75.97% of samples in node::CompressionStream<ZlibContext>::AfterThreadPoolWork under uv__work_done.
5. Restart the gateway: CPU settles, then climbs back with load (we run a nightly restart as mitigation).
Control: a second gateway on the same host, same binary, carrying 9 accounts, shows 0% CPU and zero liveness warnings — the cost scales with fleet size × streaming activity.

### Expected behavior

Per the gateway docs' liveness diagnostics, the event loop should remain unsaturated during ordinary operation: a near-idle gateway when agents are not actively processing, and streaming turns that do not pin the loop. Compression completion work should not consume ~76% of the main thread, and stable agent state paths should not be re-resolved ~18k times/second (100% failing) — the small-fleet gateway on the same host demonstrates the expected profile on the identical binary.

### Actual behavior

Main thread pinned at 100–110% for hours whenever the fleet is under business load, on both beta.5 and beta.7. Liveness warnings every 30–90s (eventLoopUtilization=1, P99 loop delay 3–6s steady-state, worst 160s during startup grind). perf: 75.97% of main-thread samples in CompressionStream<ZlibContext>::AfterThreadPoolWork. strace: ~17,900 failing readlink/s + 25k statx cycling per-agent SQLite paths. Ruled out: instance resources (10% instance CPU), client polling, subagent orphans (the #91517 snapshot-cache fix IS present in our beta.7 dist), oversized bootstrap files, session-store bloat, poisoned sessions. Related: #75707, #75688, #76188, #13758, #75297.

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.2-beta.7 (dabe191); same symptom on 2026.7.2-beta.5

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04 (kernel 6.8), AWS EC2 ap-southeast-2, 32 vCPU / 123 GiB

### Install method

npm global, run as a systemd system unit

### Model

anthropic/claude-fable-5 (primary on the orchestrator); anthropic/claude-opus-4-7 and anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 across the fleet

### Provider / routing chain

Direct Anthropic API (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY via systemd EnvironmentFile) — no proxy or model router. Channels: Slack socket mode (~50 accounts) + Telegram. Gateway binds loopback :18789 behind tailscale serve; second gateway (same binary, 9 accounts) on :19789 same host.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Single-host, two-gateway setup: HQ gateway (~65 agents, state dir ~/.openclaw, loopback :18789) and a second gateway (9 agents, ~/.openclaw-biz, :19789) running the same npm-global binary — the second gateway is the control: 0% CPU, zero liveness warnings. Per-agent model overrides in agents.entries (fable-5 orchestrator, opus-4-7 / sonnet-4-6 fleet). active-memory plugin disabled (its qmd backend hung; unrelated to this issue, disabled before these captures). No proxy or router; direct api.anthropic.com. ~57 plugins enabled including many credential-less providers (pruning experiment planned; will report before/after).

### Logs

```shell
strace -c over 10 s of a burn window (beta.7):


% time     seconds  usecs/call     calls    errors syscall
------ ----------- ----------- --------- --------- ----------------
 85.29    1.184728           6    178725    178725 readlink
 14.62    0.203123           7     25662       131 statx
  0.07    0.000912           7       124           access
  0.02    0.000283          21        13         2 futex


perf record -F 99 -g, 15 s, same burn:


99.46% _start → node::Start → SpinEventLoopInternal → uv_run
  └─ 98.32% uv__io_poll
       └─ 91.34% uv__async_io
            └─ 77.25% uv__work_done
                 └─ 75.97% node::CompressionStream<ZlibContext>::AfterThreadPoolWork(int)
                              → AsyncWrap::MakeCallback → InternalMakeCallback ...


Representative liveness lines (steady-state burn):


[diagnostic] liveness warning: reasons=event_loop_delay,event_loop_utilization,cpu interval=31s eventLoopDelayP99Ms=3783.3 eventLoopUtilization=1 cpuCoreRatio=1.037 active=4 waiting=0 queued=1
[diagnostic] liveness warning: reasons=event_loop_delay,event_loop_utilization,cpu interval=33s eventLoopDelayP99Ms=3821 eventLoopUtilization=1 cpuCoreRatio=1.01 active=4 waiting=0 queued=1


Earlier capture on 2026.7.2-beta.5 (28 Jul): same readlink storm at ~60k/s; zlib CompressionStream already the top perf frame (~40% then). Raw strace, full perf report, V8 .cpuprofile, and CloudWatch instance-CPU graph (≈10% instance during 110% process burn) available on request.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: all agents on any large-fleet gateway (~65 agents / ~50 Slack accounts in our case); every user messaging those agents feels the loop delays.
Severity: degrades the whole gateway — P99 event-loop delays of 3–6 s steady-state (worst 160 s), sluggish replies, CLI/RPC calls queueing; also burns one core continuously (cost + thermal on 24/7 hosts).
Frequency: always under business load, on both 2026.7.2-beta.5 and beta.7, across ~3 weeks of operation; recurs within hours of every restart.
Consequence: nightly forced restart required as mitigation; a small fleet (9 accounts) on the identical binary shows none of this, so the cost scales with fleet size and effectively caps how many agents one gateway can serve.

### Additional information

Not filing as a regression — no certified-clean prior version on this fleet; the burn spans every version we've run at this scale. The #91517 fix (subagent snapshot cache) is present in our beta.7 dist and this persists, so it's a distinct main-thread hot path in the same family. We can capture a V8 .cpuprofile of a burn window, provide raw (redacted) strace/perf output, and run controlled experiments on request — a credential-less provider-plugin prune (per #76188) is already planned and we'll post before/after CPU numbers as a comment.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Since 2026.9.1, every attempted macOS Desktop update has failed to complete; the verified 2026.9.7 to 2026.9.8 run published the new package but remained indefinitely in activating/post-core settlement.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw Desktop 2026.9.7 on macOS with the Gateway managed by the Desktop app.
2. Click the official update button for 2026.9.8.
3. The app launches `openclaw update --tag 2026.9.8 --json --timeout 900`.
4. Wait after package publication completes.
5. Observe that the UI remains on the Gateway updating screen beyond the configured timeout and the old updater process remains alive.
6. Inspect the update ledger: candidate checks pass, package activation reaches `publication-complete`, and the run remains at `activating` until recovery marks it abandoned.

### Expected behavior

After the candidate package is published, the post-core worker and parent updater should settle within the configured timeout. The Desktop app should then verify the new Gateway and report success, or automatically run recovery with the newly installed binary if the old updater cannot settle.

### Actual behavior

The package advanced to 2026.9.8 and candidate admission checks passed, but the old updater did not finish. The Desktop UI stayed on the updating screen. The original run later showed `activating: failed` and `reason: abandoned`. Running the new 2026.9.8 binary with `openclaw update repair --yes --json` completed recovery successfully.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.7 -> 2026.9.8; Desktop App 2026.9.8 build 2609000890

### Operating system

macOS 15.7, x86_64

### Install method

Official macOS Desktop App; OpenClaw core installed as an npm global package managed by the app

### Model

N/A (update lifecycle bug; no model request involved)

### Provider / routing chain

N/A (update lifecycle bug; no provider or routing involved)

### Additional provider/model setup details

Not applicable. No model, provider, API key, token, or routing configuration is involved in the reproduction.

### Logs

```shell
Sanitized evidence:


package activation phase: publication-complete
previous version: 2026.9.7
candidate version: 2026.9.8
candidate admission: admit
config check: ok
database-schema check: ok
node-runtime check: ok
plugin-availability check: ok
failed run step: activating
final recovery status: succeeded
active recovery sets after repair: 0


A normalized diff of the 2026.9.7 and 2026.9.8 `update-command-post-update` module bodies is empty after removing generated chunk hashes. Both versions use `killProcessTree: true`, `requireProcessTreeExtinction: true`, and wait on `activationTimeoutMs` in the delegated post-core path.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Direct local evidence was collected from the package activation journal and the update run ledger. No private logs, credentials, usernames, hostnames, or absolute paths are included in this report.

### Impact and severity

Affected system: macOS Desktop with an app-managed npm-global OpenClaw installation.

Severity: blocks the normal non-technical update workflow and requires manual recovery.

Frequency: every attempted release upgrade from 2026.9.1 through 2026.9.8 failed to complete through the official Desktop update button on this host.

Consequence: the user cannot rely on the official update button and repeatedly needs terminal-level assistance to finish an otherwise successfully published update.

### Additional information

First observed bad version: 2026.9.1. Every attempted release upgrade since 2026.9.1 through 2026.9.8 has failed to complete through the official Desktop update button on this host. Last known good version: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

Recovery boundary: the installation is now healthy on 2026.9.8 after running the new binary's official `update repair` command. This confirms recovery, but does not prove the next cross-version Desktop update is fixed.

Suggested fix:
1. Give post-core process-tree settlement a reliable hard deadline.
2. If package publication and version advancement are confirmed but the old updater exceeds the deadline, have Desktop terminate only its owned updater tree and invoke `update repair --yes --json` with the new binary.
3. Treat ledger `finished`, no active run, and a healthy Gateway as the success condition.
4. Add a macOS cross-version integration test where the new worker commits but the old parent does not exit.

issues.body:
## Bug type

Behavior bug (downgrade compatibility failure without database corruption)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

After a newer OpenClaw build adds the nullable `secret_store_entries.allowed_hosts` column, the previous OpenClaw CLI rejects the otherwise healthy state database as noncanonical instead of accepting the compatible additive column.

## Steps to reproduce

The following was reproduced against two independent SQLite backups of the same state database:

1. Use OpenClaw commit `928942d48d68ee6d083678d871f0bd94612e5a39` to create/use a secret store so `secret_store_entries` contains nullable column `allowed_hosts TEXT`.
2. Stop OpenClaw and make a consistent copy of the state database.
3. Point the previous OpenClaw build `6ec62315e42f5d7a67982b321eb8be36f72a58c3` at the copied state directory.
4. Run `openclaw tasks list --json`.
5. As a control, run the `928942d` CLI against a separate copy of the same database.

Observed A/B result:

```text
previous CLI: exit 1
current CLI:  exit 0
```

## Expected behavior

The previous CLI should accept a bare nullable additive `TEXT` column under its existing `allowCompatibleAdditiveColumns: true` contract, or a downgrade preflight should identify the incompatibility before activation without making unrelated CLI commands unusable.

## Actual behavior

The previous CLI exits 1 before listing tasks:

```text
[tasks/registry] Failed to restore task registry: SQLite schema is incomplete or noncanonical for <temp-state>/state/openclaw.sqlite: column definitions differ for secret_store_entries
[openclaw] Could not start the CLI.
[openclaw] Reason: Task registry restore failed: SQLite schema is incomplete or noncanonical for <temp-state>/state/openclaw.sqlite: column definitions differ for secret_store_entries | SQLite schema is incomplete or noncanonical for <temp-state>/state/openclaw.sqlite: column definitions differ for secret_store_entries
```

The current CLI reads the separate copy successfully. SQLite integrity and foreign-key checks pass; no corruption was observed.

## OpenClaw version

- Database-producing/current build: `OpenClaw 2026.8.1 (928942d)`
- Previous/rejecting build: `OpenClaw 2026.8.1 (6ec6231)`

Exact commits:

- `928942d48d68ee6d083678d871f0bd94612e5a39`
- `6ec62315e42f5d7a67982b321eb8be36f72a58c3`

## Operating system

macOS 26.5.1 (25F80)

## Install method

Packed npm runtimes built from the exact commits. The reproduction runs the OpenClaw binaries directly against isolated database copies; no supervisor-specific migration logic is involved.

## Model

Not applicable. The CLI fails during shared-state/task-registry restoration before model execution.

## Provider / routing chain

Not applicable.

## Additional provider/model setup details

Not applicable.

## Logs

```text
previous CLI exit: 1
current CLI exit: 0

[tasks/registry] Failed to restore task registry: SQLite schema is incomplete or noncanonical for <temp-state>/state/openclaw.sqlite: column definitions differ for secret_store_entries
[openclaw] Could not start the CLI.
```

## Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

PR #123216 describes `allowed_hosts` as a same-version additive nullable column:

- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/123216
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/928942d48d68ee6d083678d871f0bd94612e5a39/src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql#L2434-L2449

The previous runtime enables compatible additive-column handling:

- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6ec62315e42f5d7a67982b321eb8be36f72a58c3/src/state/openclaw-state-schema-compatibility.ts#L84-L86
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6ec62315e42f5d7a67982b321eb8be36f72a58c3/src/infra/sqlite-schema-contract.ts#L447-L496

The stock CLI supports confirmed downgrades, while warning that older versions may break configuration:

- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8885be47563f2648fb618da08b9ec0a4387226e2/docs/cli/update.md#L64-L69

No exact issue or PR was found by searching `secret_store_entries`, `allowed_hosts`, and the complete noncanonical-schema error.

## Impact and severity

- **Affected:** Users tracking development builds, or future released builds containing this column, who downgrade while retaining the newer state database.
- **Severity:** Medium edge case; the database remains healthy, but the previous CLI cannot restore the task registry and refuses to start the command.
- **Frequency:** One deterministic A/B reproduction against independent copies of the same database.
- **Consequence:** A binary-only downgrade can leave the older CLI unable to run task-management commands. Restoring a pre-upgrade state backup avoids the failure.

## Additional information

This report is about OpenClaw schema compatibility, not an external supervisor. The direct-binary A/B removes supervisor behavior from the reproduction.

Regression status is not claimed because arbitrary cross-build downgrade compatibility may be intentionally limited. The narrower observed inconsistency is that this bare nullable additive column is rejected even though the previous validator enables compatible additive columns.
