### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.9.6, an idle gateway main-process heap snapshot contained at least 48,032 plugin-source records across 13 maps and 11,434 ModuleWrap objects.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start OpenClaw 2026.9.6 from the global npm package with WhatsApp linked.
2. After a fresh restart and 28 minutes with no agent task running, capture a V8 heap snapshot of the gateway main process.
3. Group PluginSourceInput records by their inputs maps and ModuleWrap objects by capture-directory-normalized URL.

Observed on one installation. I have not established a deterministic reproduction across machines.

### Expected behavior

The loader documents why core-shipped code keeps process identity: recapturing it leaves native ESM jobs retained after an inventory retires. I would expect unchanged package-plugin code to be reused where plugin-instance isolation permits it. I do not have a known-good version or a specified memory budget for this path.

### Actual behavior

The snapshot had at least 48,032 PluginSourceInput records across 13 inputs maps. Map sizes were 7,175 (four maps), 3,752 (three), 2,678 (three), and 14 (three). It also had 11,434 ModuleWrap objects; normalizing capture-directory URLs yielded about 6,398 logical paths. The main isolate held about 457 MiB of V8 node self-size, including about 185 MiB of strings and 81 MiB of compiled code. Gateway RSS was about 722 MiB after 28 minutes. These are aggregate observations, not a measurement of reclaimable memory.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.6

### Operating system

macOS 27.0.1, arm64

### Install method

Global npm package, supervised gateway LaunchAgent; Node.js 26.8.2

### Model

Not involved: gateway idle, no model call

### Provider / routing chain

Not involved: no model request in the measured idle period

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The relevant source path appears to be capturePluginGenerationArtifact -> createPluginSourceCapture -> loadPluginModule:
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.6/src/plugins/plugin-generation-artifact.ts
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.6/src/plugins/plugin-package-metadata-capture.ts
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.6/src/plugins/plugin-instance-module-loader.ts

The loader notes that recapturing core-shipped code creates native ESM jobs retained after inventory retirement. The raw heap snapshot is private and not attached because it may contain messages and credentials. I can provide redacted aggregate counts or a synthetic reproduction.

### Impact and severity

Affected: one observed macOS gateway installation with WhatsApp connected. Severity: memory footprint, no crash observed. Frequency: one post-restart snapshot, so unbounded growth is not established. Consequence: about 722 MiB RSS for a mostly idle gateway.

### Additional information

This is separate from prepared-model-catalog worker growth in #159514 and its fix in #160055; these counts are from the main gateway isolate. The snapshot alone does not show which captures must stay distinct for plugin isolation or quantify a safe saving. Could maintainers point to the intended ownership boundary? I am happy to build a repeatable before/after case and submit a focused PR that preserves instance isolation, config reload, dependency changes and hot reload.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With channels.imessage.groupPolicy set to "allowlist" and both channels.imessage.allowFrom and groupAllowFrom empty ([]), the agent still processed inbound group messages and sent live responses in multiple group chats, including a group unrelated to any business context and a private family group.

Expected: per docs and the gateway's own startup warning ("Every inbound group message will be dropped"), messages should have been dropped with no session created.

Actual: the agent created a live session in group chat "imessage:group:1870" and, when an NVIDIA API call failed with a 503, sent the raw error text ("The AI service is temporarily overloaded. Please try again in a moment.") into that group as if it were a normal reply. Separately, in an unrelated private family group, the agent responded to an unrelated question with a generic AI disclaimer.

Reproduction evidence:
- Log: lane=session:agent:main:imessage:group:1870 error="FailoverError: The AI service is temporarily overloaded..."
- openclaw config get channels.imessage.allowFrom → []
- openclaw config get channels.imessage.groupPolicy → allowlist
- openclaw config get channels.imessage.groupAllowFrom → Config path not found

Impact: raw internal error strings are surfaced as message content to real external contacts with no indication it's automated. Group allowlist protection is not enforced consistently. Affects any group the account's iMessage number is in, not just business-context groups.

Suggested fix: (1) enforce the group allowlist check consistently for all inbound group triggers; (2) never surface raw provider error strings as deliverable message content to any external channel — log/route those to a private admin channel only.

Environment: OpenClaw 2026.7.1-2 (build 0790d9f), macOS, iMessage channel plugin, nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set channels.imessage.groupPolicy to "allowlist" and leave channels.imessage.allowFrom and groupAllowFrom empty ([]).
2. Start the gateway and let it run with an iMessage number that is a participant in one or more group chats.
3. Wait for API errors or unrelated messages to occur in a group chat.
4. Observe the agent creates a session and sends a reply into the group (either a normal reply or, on API failure, the raw error text), despite no allowlist entries existing for that group or sender.

### Expected behavior

Per documentation and the gateway's own startup log warning ("groupPolicy=allowlist ... no group sender allowlist is configured ... Every inbound group message will be dropped"), no session should be created and no message should be sent for any group when allowFrom and groupAllowFrom are both empty.

### Actual behavior

The agent created a live session in group chat "imessage:group:1870" despite empty allowFrom/groupAllowFrom, and when an NVIDIA API call failed with a 503, it sent the raw error text ("The AI service is temporarily overloaded. Please try again in a moment.") into that group as a normal-looking reply. Separately, in an unrelated private family group chat, the agent responded to an unrelated question with a generic AI-assistant disclaimer.

Evidence:
- Log: lane=session:agent:main:imessage:group:1870 error="FailoverError: The AI service is temporarily overloaded. Please try again in a moment."
- openclaw config get channels.imessage.allowFrom -> []
- openclaw config get channels.imessage.groupPolicy -> allowlist
- openclaw config get channels.imessage.groupAllowFrom -> Config path not found

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.1-2 (build 0790d9f)

### Operating system

macOS (host: MacBookPro / Coens-MacBook-Pro)

### Install method

npm install -g openclaw@latest

### Model

nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b

### Provider / routing chain

nvidia provider, openai-completions API, direct to https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/chat/completions, no proxy, no fallback model configured (fallbackConfigured: false)

### Additional provider/model setup details

Single NVIDIA API key/profile configured (profileId sha256:354ea9687bc3). No per-agent model overrides for the affected sessions. iMessage channel plugin (imsg) reading from local Messages database. Gateway run as a macOS LaunchAgent with KeepAlive: true.

### Logs

```shell
{"subsystem":"gateway/channels/imessage"}: embedded_run_agent_end, isError:true, error:"The AI service is temporarily overloaded. Please try again in a moment.", failoverReason:"overloaded", model:"nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b", providerRuntimeFailureKind:"timeout"

lane task error: lane=session:agent:main:imessage:group:1870 durationMs=1310 error="FailoverError: The AI service is temporarily overloaded. Please try again in a moment."

model_fallback_decision: decision:"candidate_failed", reason:"overloaded", status:503, fallbackConfigured:false, fallbackStepFinalOutcome:"chain_exhausted"

Config check at time of incident:
openclaw config get channels.imessage.allowFrom -> []
openclaw config get channels.imessage.groupPolicy -> allowlist
openclaw config get channels.imessage.groupAllowFrom -> Config path not found

Earlier startup log (same install, prior to incident) explicitly warned:
"imessage: groupPolicy=\"allowlist\" for account \"default\" but no group sender allowlist is configured (channels.imessage.groupAllowFrom, or its allowFrom fallback). Every inbound group message will be dropped."
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: any iMessage group chat the account's number participates in, including business-context groups and unrelated private/personal groups.
Severity: data/safety risk — raw internal error strings and unintended AI responses are delivered to real external contacts without disclosure that the message is automated, in contexts (private family group) with no relation to bot usage at all.
Frequency: observed at least twice across two separate group chats on the same day; underlying condition (empty allowlist not being enforced) is persistent, not a one-off, so recurrence should be expected whenever a group receives any inbound activity or an API call fails mid-session.
Consequence: unintended/confusing messages reaching real contacts and family members; reputational risk for business use; account owner had to manually leave affected group chats as the only reliable mitigation since config settings did not prevent the behavior.

### Additional information

(we don't have a last-known-good version to compare against — this is the only version tested)

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In containerized deployments without systemd, tools.exec.security=ask issues a Telegram approval card but executes the pending command ~3.5s later regardless of the approval outcome, instead of blocking until approved or denied.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the gateway (ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.7.1-2) in a Docker container without
   systemd/launchd, with tools.exec.security=allowlist, ask=on-miss,
   approvals.exec.mode=targets (Telegram DM routing).
2. Trigger an exec command that misses the allowlist, e.g. `mkdir -p /tmp/inline-button-test`.
3. An approval card is issued via Telegram (observed: card `eeff8125-df93-4fe4-85d7-41671515a74b`
   at 2026-08-17T12:39:10Z), with Allow Once/Allow Always/Deny options and a 30m expiry.
4. Do not respond to the card. Check the filesystem for the command's side effect immediately.

### Expected behavior

In the same deployment (same image, same config) with tools.exec.security=deny instead of
ask, an equivalent unmatched command (`mkdir -p /tmp/deny-canary-test`) is blocked
synchronously and never executes ("Exec denied (user-denied)", directory never created,
confirmed via stat/ls). This confirms blocking is achievable in this deployment. ask mode
should likewise block execution pending the approval decision or TTL expiry, consistent with
the card's own presented semantics (expiry countdown, pending response options).

### Actual behavior

The command executed 3.5 seconds after the approval card was issued — directory birth time
(via `stat`) was 2026-08-17T12:39:13.524Z, vs. card issued at 12:39:10Z. No approval or
denial record for this card exists in the session log or openclaw.sqlite-wal at the time of
execution (grep confirmed). The command ran regardless of the pending/unresolved approval
state.

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.1-2

### Operating system

Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm), arm64, kernel 6.12.76-linuxkit (Docker on macOS host)

### Install method

docker

### Model

zai/glm-5.2 (agents.defaults.model.primary — likely irrelevant to this bug, which reproduces at the exec-approval gateway layer independent of model)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> zai (Z.ai) GLM-5.2 (no separate provider field in config; provider is embedded in the model spec)

### Additional provider/model setup details

Model: zai/glm-5.2 via agents.defaults.model.primary (no per-agent override for main).
Provider is embedded in the model spec (zai = Z.ai); no separate provider field exists in
config. Not relevant to root cause — the reported bug is at the exec-approval gateway layer,
independent of model/provider.

### Logs

```shell
Approval card raw text (issued 2026-08-17T12:39:10Z, id eeff8125-df93-4fe4-85d7-41671515a74b):
"Approval required. Run: /approve eeff8125-df93-4fe4-85d7-41671515a74b allow-once
Pending command: mkdir -p /tmp/inline-button-test
Other options: /approve eeff8125-df93-4fe4-85d7-41671515a74b allow-always /
/approve eeff8125-df93-4fe4-85d7-41671515a74b deny
Host: gateway / CWD: ~/.openclaw/workspace / Expires in: 30m"

grep -A2 -B2 "eeff8125" openclaw.sqlite-wal: no approval/denial record found at time of
execution (12:39:13.524Z).

Workaround confirmed (deny mode canary test, same command shape):
"Exec denied (user-denied)" — directory never created (verified via stat/ls).

openclaw gateway restart failure (separate finding, same environment):
"Gateway service disabled. / Start with: openclaw gateway install /
systemctl --user start openclaw-gateway.service / systemd user services are unavailable;
install/enable systemd or run the gateway under your supervisor. / If you're in a container,
run the gateway in the foreground instead of `openclaw gateway`."
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: Any OpenClaw deployment using tools.exec.security=ask as an approval-gated
security control — verified in a Docker container without systemd/launchd
(ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.7.1-2). Not tested on systemd/launchd-supervised hosts, so
scope beyond this environment is unconfirmed.
Severity: Critical — the approval gate provides no actual access control. A command executes
regardless of whether it is approved, denied, or left unresolved, so ask mode grants no
protection beyond the allowlist itself.
Frequency: Deterministic in the tested case (1/1) — reproduced with exact timestamps (card
issued 12:39:10Z, exec completed 12:39:13.524Z, no approval record at execution time). Not
yet tested across repeated trials.
Consequence: Any exec command missing the allowlist executes immediately regardless of the
human approval decision, defeating the purpose of approval-gated exec as a safety control.
Confirmed workaround: tools.exec.security=deny blocks correctly and synchronously, but
sacrifices ask mode's per-request approval flexibility for an allow/deny-only model.

### Additional information

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO regarding last-known-good version — no evidence was collected that ask mode
ever correctly blocked exec in any prior release; this may not be a regression.

Grounded additional context: switching tools.exec.security from ask to deny in the same
deployment (same version, same config) blocks an equivalent command synchronously and
correctly (canary-tested: "Exec denied (user-denied)", directory never created). This confirms
the underlying blocking mechanism works for deny but not for ask.

issues.title: [Bug]: 2026.10.4 Windows - 10-min boot from sequential plugin loads with silent network handshakes (discord ~86s, whatsapp ~50s, tavily ~20s) x3 passes

labels.name: clawsweeper:intake:bug
labels.description: Preliminary submission classification; full source review pending.

labels.name: clawsweeper:intake:needs-repro
labels.description: Preliminary submission classification; full source review pending.

issues.body:
## Environment
- OS: Windows 10 (10.0.19045, x64)
- Node: v24.18.0
- OpenClaw: 2026.10.4 (383c124), npm global install
- Launcher: scheduled-task `OpenClaw Gateway` -> gateway.vbs (hidden) -> gateway.cmd -> node (matches #140161 chain verbatim)
- Date observed: 2026-10-18, ~06:00-10:30 MYT (5 gateway restarts in ~4h)

## Summary
Cold boot takes ~10 min. Co-investigation found the bulk is sequential plugin-registry loads where three chat/search plugins (discord, whatsapp, tavily) stall on silent network handshakes, repeated across 3 back-to-back passes. A separate SQLite freeze-trap on a 286 MB main agent DB can then get the gateway killed by the watchdog past boot-grace, forcing a 10-min reboot loop.

## Proven links (verified by reporter unless marked [R] = reported by co-investigator, not independently re-measured)

1. **Sequential plugin loader (verified).** `dist/loader-runtime-load-BrZtlYge.mjs` line ~1477 is `for (const candidate of orderedCandidates)` with per-candidate load inside; line 1034 logs `[plugins] loading X` BEFORE each load, so stagger between those lines is an exact per-plugin timer. (Line numbers off-by-one vs co-investigator's 1476; same loop, file hash matches this build.)

2. **Per-plugin cost, 10:29 boot batch #1 [R].** 10 plugins (browser, google, memory-core, memory-wiki, ollama, openai, telegram, tts-local-cli, brave + others) load in ~1s TOTAL. discord ~86s (10:31:21 -> 10:32:47, only ~5 log lines in that window), tavily ~20s silent, whatsapp ~50s silent. 86+20+50 = 156s vs batch total 158s. I could not re-derive these timings (no plugin-timing log in `logs/`, cache-trace.jsonl is 2.4 GB); reporting co-investigator's numbers.

3. **Import is cheap [R].** Direct node import timing: discord 600ms, whatsapp 3ms, tavily 1956ms. So the 86/20/50s is register()/init = network handshakes, not module load. Not re-measured by me.

4. **Timeout constants [R, with caveat].** Co-investigator reads: discord DEFAULT_DISCORD_GATEWAY_INFO_TIMEOUT_MS=30s / MAX=120s / fallback-log 60s (explains silence); whatsapp connectTimeoutMs=60s; tavily search 30s. Caveat: I grepped my `dist/*.mjs` for `GATEWAY_INFO_TIMEOUT` and whatsapp `connectTimeoutMs=60` and found NO matches (only unrelated realtime/websocket hits) — likely different build hashes (their `socket-close-DU7eerAa.mjs` does not exist in my dist). Constants unverified on this build.

5. **Everything runs 3x back-to-back [R].** Batch totals ~151s + ~146s + ~145s (~7.7 min of a ~10 min boot), identical plugin sets, sequential. Scope of each pass unconfirmed (no per-agent markers in logs; guess: workspace + agent scopes). Not verified by me.

## The paradox (network fine when idle) [R]
Direct fetch from the same box, outside boot windows: `discord.com/api/v10/gateway/bot` = 416ms, api.tavily.com = 1s, DNS 30ms, no proxy, discord.com has no AAAA (no IPv6 issue). Stalls happen during boot windows only. **Hypothesis (unproven):** service-side throttling after repeated login bursts (6+ restarts that day), or transient contention. Same shape as #119861 (in-process timeout while curl answers 0.27s).

## Compounding factor: SQLite freeze-trap (partially verified)
- Main agent DB is **286 MB** (299,933,696 bytes, verified by me 10:43 MYT today).
- Co-investigator reports log shows main-thread SQLite holds: session.canonical-validation.certify 1705ms, artifacts-prepare 2538ms (isMainThread:true), transaction holds, reclamation worker retired after 9889ms. Gateway alive + port listening but unresponsive for seconds -> watchdog kills past boot-grace -> 10-min reboot. I did not re-derive these timings.
- Related hard evidence I DID verify: `logs/stability/openclaw-stability-2026-10-17T22-06-56-804Z-286900-gateway.restart_close_failed.json` (06:06 MYT today) shows `Gateway shutdown did not complete cleanly` with plugin-runtime close retained, agent DB drainage failed, and stale state-owner locks on `agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`.
- Mitigation applied by operator: boot-grace raised 12 -> 18 min in gateway-watchdog.ps1 (reported done, not verified by me).

## Restart evidence (verified)
`logs/gateway-restart.log` shows `[Sun 10/18/2026 10:14:32] restart attempt source=windows-task-handoff previousPid=197572` finishing 10:16:00, with NO preceding CLI or safe-rpc trigger line — consistent with supervisor recovery during instability. Session uptimes confirm ~5 restarts 06:25-10:29 MYT. The 06:25 restart interrupted cron jobs mid-run (Bullshit Filter: "interrupted by gateway restart").

## Upstream corroboration (all verified OPEN today via `gh issue view`)
- #140161 (scheduled-task boot hangs 5-7+ min, foreground 7-12s) — our launcher chain matches verbatim.
- #159499 (two sequential plugin-registry phases are 175s) — same mechanism.
- #119861 (in-process timeout while curl answers 0.27s) — same paradox shape.
- #168955 (10.1 ready ~1030s vs ~410s on 9.9) — same regression family.
- #164854 ("prepared model runtime publication (workspace plugins; agent main) timed out") — exact error seen on our 10:14 restart.

## Suggested fix directions (opinion, not proven)
1. Parallelize plugin registry loads (or at least overlap the three network handshakes) instead of a strict sequential for-loop.
2. Add progress logging during long handshakes (discord's 60s silent window is what makes this invisible).
3. Single plugin-registry pass instead of 3x back-to-back, or cache registry across scopes.
4. Move main-thread SQLite certify/prepare off-thread or add boot-grace awareness so the watchdog doesn't kill a healthy-but-busy boot.

## Notes
- `[R]` items above are co-investigator measurements I am relaying in good faith but did not independently reproduce. Happy to run any specific repro the maintainers need.
- Fallback-chain note: this box's main agent had `openrouter/free` as first fallback; operator has since replaced it with `ms12`. Defaults/utility/cabal agents still list free. Unrelated to boot time, mentioning for completeness.

issues.body:
### Summary

`openclaw cron list --json` is a read-only command served by an already-running
gateway, but each invocation costs **3.9 s of CPU** and peaks at **273 MB RSS**,
issuing **9,281 `openat` calls** — to print a list of cron jobs.

On a 2 vCPU host this is enough to starve the machine. It also affects OpenClaw
itself: **the gateway shells out to this same command 73 times per hour** to read
state it already owns (measured, see below).

**Version**: OpenClaw 2026.7.1-2 · gateway v2026.7.1-beta.2
**Host**: 2 vCPU Linux VM, gateway running as a systemd user service (uid 1000)

### Measurements

Median of repeated runs on the same host and session:

| command | wall | CPU | peak RSS |
|---|---|---|---|
| `su - openclaw -c true` | 0.015 s | 0.010 s | — |
| `su - openclaw -c 'node -e 0'` | 0.065 s | 0.060 s | — |
| `su - openclaw -c 'openclaw --version'` | 0.070 s | 0.060 s | — |
| `su - openclaw -c 'openclaw cron list --json'` | **5.540 s** | **3.900 s** | **273 MB** |

The `--version` row is the control that matters: **Node.js startup plus CLI entry
costs 0.06 s**. The remaining ~3.84 s of CPU is work done *after* startup, around
what should be a single RPC to a service that is already up. The output is 334 KB
of JSON describing 100 jobs.

For scale, reading the same 100 jobs from a pre-rendered JSON file on the same
host takes **15 ms** — about 260× cheaper for identical data.

### The gateway calls it too

We ran an eBPF `sched_process_exec` tracer for 36 hours and attributed every
`openclaw` invocation by cgroup:

```
all openclaw invocations           31,761   (883/hour)
  of which `cron list`             19,037   (529/hour)

`cron list` by origin:
  external automation / SSH        13,405   (70.4%)
  openclaw-gateway.service          2,619   (13.8%)   <-- the gateway itself
  other local units                 3,013   (15.8%)
```

The 2,619 figure is the one we would flag first: the gateway process, which owns
the cron state, spawns a full Node process costing 3.9 s CPU and 273 MB **73 times
an hour** to read that state back. That looks like an internal call path that
could go direct.

### Impact

At peak this host saw ~2,500 `openclaw` invocations in one hour. 2,500 × 3.9 s ≈
2.7 hours of CPU demanded inside a 1-hour window on a 2-core box — i.e. ~271 %
of available CPU, purely for status reads.

The machine became unreachable: load average reached 276, and `tailscaled` could
not emit a keepalive, so the host appeared offline while it was in fact still
running and slowly serving work.

### Expected

A read-only command backed by a running gateway should cost roughly one RPC —
tens of milliseconds and tens of MB, in the same order as `--version`, not 65× it.

### Not measured

We did **not** capture the split between "application preparation" and "the RPC
itself" (planned: timestamp `execve` → first `connect()` to the gateway, versus
`connect()` → response). So this report establishes **that** the cost exists and
how large it is, but **not** which internal phase owns it.

### Possibly related, untested

`openclaw gateway call cron.list` exists and looks like a thinner path to the same
data. We did not benchmark it. If it is materially cheaper, that would localize
the cost to the `cron list` command wrapper rather than to the CLI or RPC layer.

### Smaller observation

`cron list` reports only enabled jobs, while other surfaces count all jobs (we saw
100 vs 105 with exactly 5 disabled crons). Worth documenting, or adding an
`--include-disabled` flag; `gateway call cron.list` accepts an `includeDisabled`
parameter.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When a plugin approval originates in a Telegram forum topic, the approval request can contain the originating group but omit its thread metadata. The Telegram native approval resolver then rejects the origin as inconsistent with the persisted topic session and the delivery planner falls back to the configured approver DM.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable Telegram native approvals with execApprovals.target: "channel" and a configured approver.
2. Enable plugin approvals with the following redacted configuration:

   ~~~json
   {
     "approvals": {
       "plugin": {
         "enabled": true,
         "mode": "session",
         "agentFilter": ["main", "todo"]
       }
     }
   }
   ~~~

3. Start a plugin tool from a Telegram forum topic through before_tool_call -> requireApproval.
4. Use an approval request whose live source contains turnSourceChannel: "telegram" and the group target, but no turnSourceThreadId; keep the topic in the session key and persisted session delivery target.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add a config option to place the message-envelope timestamp at the END of the envelope body (after the message text) instead of in the header prefix, so DeepSeek/Anthropic prefix caches can hit on stable prefixes.

### Problem to solve

OpenClaw wraps every inbound message with an envelope that includes a second-precision timestamp in the header prefix:
```
[Clawling Chat group:cnv_xxx Mon 2026-08-03 15:30:56 GMT+8] ClawChat group messages:...
```

Because DeepSeek's context hard-disk cache requires **EXACT prefix matching** ([DeepSeek KV Cache docs](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/kv_cache/)), the volatile timestamp in the header invalidates the entire prefix on every message. Measured impact on our setup (ClawChat group channel, DeepSeek v4-flash/pro):

- clawchat channel cache hit rate: **~67%** (146 calls, 19.3M miss tokens)
- wecom channel hit rate: ~93%
- main/CLI agent hit rate: ~91%

The difference is caused by the **timestamp position**, not the channel itself. The system prompt already follows this principle: the [date-time docs](https://docs.openclaw.ai/date-time) note the *Current Date & Time* section shows only the time zone (no dynamic clock) **explicitly to keep the prompt cache-stable**.


### Proposed solution

Add a config option to control where the envelope timestamp appears. Proposed schema under `agents.defaults`:

```json5
agents: {
  defaults: {
    envelopeTimestamp: "on", // "on" | "off" | "suffix"
  },
}
```

- `"on"` (default, backward-compatible): timestamp in header prefix (current behavior)
- `"off"`: no timestamp at all (existing behavior)
- `"suffix"`: timestamp appended at the **END** of the message body, e.g.:

```
[Clawling Chat group:cnv_xxx] ClawChat group messages:... [at Mon 2026-08-03 15:30:56 GMT+8]
```

**Implementation sketch**: in `formatAgentEnvelope` (`src/auto-reply/envelope.ts`), when the option is `"suffix"`, don't push the formatted timestamp into the header `parts` array; instead append `[at <ts>]` after `params.body`. The elapsed-time suffix (`+2m`) could stay in the header or follow the same rule.

Optionally also allow per-channel override (`channels.<id>.envelopeTimestamp`) for finer control.


### Alternatives considered

1. **Remove the timestamp entirely** (`envelopeTimestamp: "off"`): loses time context the model may need.
2. **Drop seconds precision** (minute-level): reduces but does not eliminate churn; still changes the prefix every minute.
3. **Patch node_modules at install time** (what we currently do): works but is overwritten by every OpenClaw update and can't be shared.

The suffix approach keeps **full timestamp fidelity AND cache stability**.



### Impact

- **Affected**: All users on prefix-cache providers (DeepSeek context caching, Anthropic prompt caching) using channel auto-reply (ClawChat, WhatsApp, Telegram, WeCom, etc.) with long system prompts / tool schemas.
- **Severity**: Medium-High for cache-cost-sensitive users.
- **Frequency**: Every message in group/direct auto-reply channels.
- **Consequence**: Cache miss on ~30%+ of input tokens costs up to **20x more** (DeepSeek: 2 yuan/M vs 0.1 yuan/M). On high-volume channels this is a meaningful cost and latency penalty.



### Evidence/examples

Measured from OpenClaw trajectory data, DeepSeek `usage.cacheRead` vs `usage.input`:

| Channel | Calls | Hit tokens | Miss tokens | Hit rate |
|---------|-------|-----------|-------------|----------|
| clawchat | 146 | 39.9M | 19.3M | **67.4%** |
| wecom | 104 | 21.8M | 1.7M | **92.8%** |

Same account, same models, same period — the only structural difference is the volatile timestamp in the ClawChat envelope prefix (each group message carries a second-precision GMT+8 timestamp at the start of the message body).

- Official DeepSeek caching doc: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/kv_cache/ (exact prefix unit matching)
- OpenClaw date-time doc: https://docs.openclaw.ai/date-time (system prompt time section is deliberately cache-stable: time zone only)
## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance




### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance

### Additional information

Backward compatible: default `'on'` preserves current behavior; only the new `'suffix'` value adds the new mode. We also have a **working local patch** that implements this for the clawchat channel; happy to turn it into a PR with maintainer guidance.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

sessions_send between agent sessions replays the same logical message multiple times (byte-identical content, and/or duplicated under two sourceChannel markers) during HTTP 429 rate limiting or receiver-lane congestion; every duplicate enqueue triggers a full model turn on the receiver.

### Steps to reproduce

Observation-based (a deterministic minimal repro was not constructed; findings are from production observation):

Run a multi-agent OpenClaw deployment (single gateway, tools.sessions.visibility=all, tools.agentToAgent.enabled=true) with frequent inter-session sessions_send.
Push a provider into rate limiting (HTTP 429) or saturate the receiver session lane (long-running turns, lane wait exceeded).
Observe the target session transcript: identical content re-delivered (short replays at 12s/15s/24s intervals; delayed replays 4–16h later), and single logical sends arriving twice within 2–5s tagged sourceChannel=webchat then sourceChannel=unknown.
Correlate with gateway log chain: provider 429 → embedded run FailoverError → [agents/sessions-send] announce flow failed → sender retry → duplicate enqueue.

### Expected behavior

A single logical sessions_send is delivered exactly once to the target session. Other paths already guarantee this: subagent completion handoff uses a stable idempotency key; cron/webhook payloads expose idempotencyKey.

### Actual behavior

The same content is enqueued multiple times. Each duplicate triggers a full model turn on the receiver, multiplying token consumption and causing agents to re-process already-handled messages. Observed 83 md5-identical duplicate-delivery groups over 2026-07-24 → 08-16.

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.1-2 (0790d9f)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04

### Install method

npm global (systemd-managed single gateway)

### Model

multi-agent deployment across a Token Plan endpoint (openai-completions API)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> token-plan (openai-completions) direct; deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash as fallback

### Additional provider/model setup details

None beyond the above. No API keys, tokens, or passwords included.

### Logs

```shell
<gateway> [agent/embedded] embedded run agent end: ... isError=true error=API rate limit reached ... rawError=429 status code (no body)
<gateway> [agent/embedded] embedded run failover decision: ... decision=surface_error reason=rate_limit ...
<gateway> [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=session:<redacted> ... error="FailoverError: API rate limit reached."
<gateway> [agents/sessions-send] announce flow failed
<gateway> [diagnostic] lane wait exceeded: lane=session:<redacted> waitedMs=15343 queueAhead=0 activeAhead=1
(Four announce flow failed occurrences over the observation window; session keys redacted.)
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: any multi-agent deployment using sessions_send under provider rate limiting or lane congestion. Severity: high token amplification — in one incident, replay × echo-loop produced on the order of 10^8 tokens within a 4-hour window; protocol-level zero-response rules mitigate cost but do not fix the transport. Frequency: reproducible under rate limiting / congestion; intermittent otherwise.

### Additional information

Root cause is the transport, not agent behavior. Suggested directions (maintainer discretion): (1) idempotency key on inter-session delivery; (2) receiver-side content-hash window dedup (~60s, with allowlist); (3) single-path delivery resolving the webchat/unknown dual-marker pair. Do you plan to open a PR for this? — No, proposing the idea only.

issues.body:
## Summary

`openclaw agent exec` cannot run ephemerally against a normal multi-agent installation that uses the stock Codex OAuth route.

The command has no `--agent` selector. With three configured agents it fails before the run, even when `--cwd` points at the default agent workspace and the config explicitly assigns `systemAgent`, `authInheritance`, and `sessionStore` ownership to that agent. Narrowing a pinned config to one agent gets past selection but the isolated temporary run then loses the working Codex OAuth credential route and receives a 401.

## Environment

- OpenClaw `2026.8.1-beta.2` (`8f382a2`)
- Linux arm64 (Raspberry Pi)
- npm global install
- Three explicit agents: `default`, `family`, `dabbot`
- Primary model: `openai/gpt-5.6-terra`
- Resolved Gateway runtime: `codex` (implicit)
- Gateway-backed turns authenticate and complete successfully

## Reproduction 1: agent selection

```sh
openclaw agent exec \
  'Reply with exactly E2E_OK and nothing else.' \
  --cwd /home/user/.openclaw/workspace \
  --timeout 120 \
  --json
```

Result:

```text
Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner. Select an agent explicitly...
```

`openclaw agent exec --help` exposes no `--agent` option.

The active config already contains:

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "systemAgent": { "agentId": "default" },
      "authInheritance": { "agentId": "default" },
      "sessionStore": { "agentId": "default" }
    }
  }
}
```

## Reproduction 2: ephemeral OAuth inheritance

Create a private temporary pinned config containing only the `default` agent and its original workspace/agentDir, then run:

```sh
openclaw agent exec \
  'Reply with exactly E2E_OK and nothing else.' \
  --config /tmp/private-config/openclaw.json \
  --cwd /home/user/.openclaw/workspace \
  --timeout 120 \
  --json
```

Result:

```text
unexpected status 401 Unauthorized: Missing bearer or basic authentication in header
```

Using `--isolated --model openai/gpt-5.6-terra` instead fails earlier because the prepared run lacks the plugin registration for the `codex` runtime.

The equivalent Gateway-backed command succeeds immediately:

```sh
openclaw agent --agent default --message 'Reply with exactly GATEWAY_E2E_OK and nothing else.' --json
```

The resulting session reports `modelProvider=openai`, `model=gpt-5.6-terra`, `agentRuntime.id=codex`, `status=done`.

## Expected behavior

One of:

1. `agent exec` accepts `--agent <id>` and resolves that agent's workspace, runtime and credentials while keeping run state temporary; or
2. it deterministically infers the explicit default owner/workspace and inherits the selected agent's configured OAuth route.

Omitting `--state-dir` should remain fully ephemeral as documented, without requiring an API key when the selected agent already has a working stock OAuth login.

## Impact

The documented native CI/test path cannot be used for production-faithful ephemeral validation in a multi-agent OAuth installation. Operators are pushed toward persistent Gateway test sessions or bespoke temporary-config/credential copying, both of which undermine the purpose of `agent exec`.

issues.body:
## Summary

The `openclaw` delegation tool (used for system setup/config changes) consistently fails with:

> OpenClaw requires working inference: Inference setup probe cleanup did not finish safely.

The failure survives Gateway restarts and a full Windows reboot. CLI commands (`openclaw config set/get`, `openclaw models list`, etc.) work normally, so this appears isolated to the setup-inference probe lifecycle.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.10.4 (383c124)
- OS: Windows 10.0.26200 (x64)
- Node: v24.19.0
- Gateway: loopback, port 18789, token auth, Tailscale serve (private)
- Main agent model: `deepseek/deepseek-flash`
- `agents.defaults.model.primary`: unset
- Plugins enabled: `tokenjuice`, `memory-lancedb`, `@openclaw/llama-cpp-provider`
- Memory: `memory.search.provider = "local"` (managed llama.cpp / EmbeddingGemma)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install the official plugins `tokenjuice`, `memory-lancedb`, and `@openclaw/llama-cpp-provider`.
2. Trigger a plugin runtime generation change (plugin install/reload).
3. Observe a failed Gateway close in the stability log (see Evidence).
4. Call the `openclaw` tool with any request (even a read-only health check).
5. Restart the Gateway, then reboot Windows, and retry.

## Expected

The delegator returns a normal reply.

## Actual

Every call fails with:

```
OpenClaw requires working inference: Inference setup probe cleanup did not finish safely.
```

One call also returned:

```
OpenClaw could not reach working inference. Run `openclaw onboard` on the machine running OpenClaw to reconnect — it live-tests the route before saving it. Then try again.
```

## Evidence

Stability report (path redacted):

```
~/.openclaw/logs/stability/openclaw-stability-2026-10-17T03-56-39-549Z-36512-gateway.restart_close_failed.json
```

Message:

```
shutdown step failed (gateway close): Plugin runtime still owns resources; inspect cleanup failures before retrying Gateway close.
| Prepared model runtime failed to close
| Prepared plugin generations failed to close
| Prepared plugin generation cleanup failed
| Prepared plugin resources failed to close
| Plugin inspection resources could not all be disposed
```

Stack frames referenced in the report:

```
prepared-model-runtime.plugin-generation-DSCwgM5-.mjs:1724
prepared-model-runtime.lifecycle-ADHVLWEn.mjs:48
```

## Troubleshooting already tried

- `openclaw doctor --fix` from an independent elevated shell with the Gateway stopped
- Multiple Gateway restarts, including a clean stop -> start cycle
- Full Windows reboot
- `openclaw models list --refresh --provider deepseek` (model is present and configured)
- Unset `agents.defaults.model.primary`
- Killed an orphaned `llama-server.exe` (left by a setup command)
- Confirmed no pending session inputs (`pendingInputs.total = 0`)

None of the above restored the delegator.

## Impact

The `openclaw` tool is unusable, so config/plugin/system changes must be performed via CLI. Normal chat, web search, memory, and file operations are unaffected.

## Workaround

Use the CLI for configuration changes:

```bash
openclaw config set <path> <value>
openclaw config get <path>
```

## Possibly related

The failure first appeared immediately after installing/reloading the three plugins above and coincided with a Gateway close failure reporting retained plugin/model runtime ownership. It is not clear whether the plugin set is causal or whether the failed close merely left persistent state that the setup probe now refuses to work with.

issues.body:
## Current status and preferred contract — October 13, 2026

Source-only follow-up on [`605065ce7461`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/605065ce7461177e9b438c8d8917641a8e8380e0). The ordinary [dynamic-tool timeout resolver](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/605065ce7461177e9b438c8d8917641a8e8380e0/extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.ts#L393) still chooses explicit call arguments, selected built-in configuration, or the 90-second watchdog default, with a 600-second ordinary cap. Its owner-supplied execution-budget lookup is currently restricted to `node_exec`; dynamic MCP tools cannot supply their server budget there.

[PR #155490](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155490) is merged and projects `requestTimeoutMs` to native Codex `tool_timeout_sec`. That improves the **native MCP route**, while requester-scoped servers still use dynamic tools and remain outside that projection.

Preferred direction: carry the effective owning MCP server's existing request budget into dynamic execution, without a second configuration knob or an `mfs_*` name-specific rule. Explicit call precedence, the bounded cap, abort propagation, and completion grace for a structured timeout result must remain explicit. The [current timeout reference](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/codex-harness-reference/timeouts) defines separate inner/outer budgets, so inheritance needs an intentional maintainer contract decision before implementation.

No slow MCP operation was dispatched for this update; no new production timing is claimed.

---

### Summary

The Codex dynamic-tool watchdog uses one default timeout for every tool call. An MCP server that is legitimately slower than that default has its calls aborted even when the operator has already configured a longer `requestTimeoutMs` for that server — the two numbers never meet.

### Problem to solve

An operator configures an MCP server with a multi-minute request timeout because some of its operations genuinely take that long (one tool call fronting a bulk business operation). The MCP client honours it. The dynamic-tool watchdog does not, and kills the call at its own default.

The result is the failure class this repo ranks worst: the call ends with no useful outcome, and the model receives a timeout that says nothing about the server's real behaviour.

Before proposing new surface I checked whether existing behaviour can already express this, per the config-surface bar in AGENTS.md. In the current beta the watchdog resolves a configured value for exactly three tools — image generation, image, and message — through dedicated config paths. There is no generic per-tool or per-server path and no environment variable. The MCP client's `requestTimeoutMs` lives in the MCP runtime and is never read by the dynamic-tool module.

### Proposed solution

Preferred, because it adds **no** config surface: let the dynamic-tool watchdog derive its default from the owning MCP server's already-configured `requestTimeoutMs`. The operator has already stated the intended bound; the watchdog just needs to see it.

If that coupling is unwanted, a server-scoped or tool-scoped configurable default would also solve it.

Either way, explicit per-call timeouts should keep winning, and the existing hard cap should still bound whatever is resolved.

### Alternatives considered

Raising the global default — rejected, it weakens the watchdog for every fast tool to accommodate one slow server.

Patching the built watchdog — this is what we do today, and it is precisely what we would like to stop doing.

### Impact

Any deployment fronting a slow backend through MCP hits this. The workaround is a dist patch that must be re-derived on every upgrade.

### Evidence/examples

Reproduced on a six-agent fleet whose bundled MCP server routinely exceeds the watchdog default on bulk operations.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, if maintainers indicate which of the two directions is acceptable — I did not open one first because this touches config/default surface and reads as a product decision.

### Additional information

Filed with AI assistance; investigated and validated by me.

issues.body:
## Current status and proposed scope — October 13, 2026

Source-only follow-up on [`605065ce7461`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/605065ce7461177e9b438c8d8917641a8e8380e0). The [sandbox process owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/605065ce7461177e9b438c8d8917641a8e8380e0/extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/processes.ts) still has no elapsed-process lifetime deadline. Closed-record eviction, cancellation, and [process-tree cleanup](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/605065ce7461177e9b438c8d8917641a8e8380e0/extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/sandbox-child.ts) are distinct bounds.

[PR #154188](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154188) is merged and intentionally preserves independent background work while a consumer retains its sandbox lease. Therefore our downstream fixed 300-second command wrapper is an operator policy, not a suitable unconditional upstream default. This proposal should become a Codex-plugin-owned **opt-in process lifetime bound**, with visible timeout results and the existing termination owner; keep normal background continuation unless maintainers choose a different default and exemption policy.

OpenClaw's process adapter owns this execution path. The pinned Codex 0.160.0 `process/start` protocol has no lifetime parameter; this is distinct from native Codex MCP request budgets. The stronger historical claim that a long-lived process permanently exhausts shared slots is not established by this source review and is not a reason to remove legitimate background behavior.

No process was started or terminated for this update. Maintainer direction on the configuration/default contract remains the next step.

---

### Summary

Processes started through the Codex sandbox exec-server have no maximum lifetime. A command that keeps producing output but never finishes — a tail, a watch, a stuck build, a hung network client — holds its execution slot indefinitely. Nothing terminates it.

### Problem to solve

The existing timers do not cover this case. The closed-process eviction timer only reaps records for processes that already exited, and the `SIGTERM`-on-abort path with its bounded finalize wait only fires once something else has decided to abort. Neither bounds a process that is alive and producing.

In the current beta there is no `maxProcess*` symbol anywhere in the built package, no exec/process/command timeout key in the config schema, and no environment variable for it.

An agent that starts such a command loses that slot for the rest of the session and the operator gets no signal explaining why — again the silent-failure class. On a multi-agent host the slots are shared, so one stuck process degrades unrelated agents.

### Proposed solution

A bounded maximum process duration for the sandbox exec-server, with a sane default and an operator override, terminating the same way an abort does today (`SIGTERM`, then the existing bounded finalize wait) so the outcome is visible and typed rather than silent.

### Alternatives considered

Wrapping every admitted argv in a hard `timeout` invocation — this is our current workaround. It hardcodes an absolute path to a coreutils binary inside whatever sandbox image is selected, which is fragile now that the container backend has been reworked, and it has to be re-derived on every upgrade.

Relying on the agent to not start such commands — not a control, and it fails exactly when the agent is least able to recover.

### Impact

Any deployment running sandboxed Codex agents that can execute long-lived commands. Degrades shared capacity and produces no operator-visible reason.

### Evidence/examples

Six-agent fleet running sandboxed Codex agents through the app-server exec-server; observed slots held by producing-but-endless processes until the session ended.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, if the direction is acceptable — filed as an issue first because it adds a default/config surface and changes failure behaviour.

### Additional information

Filed with AI assistance; investigated and validated by me.

issues.body:
## Problem

A Feishu app can have only one reliable long-connection consumer for a given event stream. Feishu documents multiple long-connection clients for the same app as a cluster: a given event is delivered to one client, not broadcast to every client.

Today the bundled Feishu channel plugin owns the Gateway long connection but does not register `contact.user.*_v3` or `contact.department.*_v3` handlers. When a tenant enables those events, the Gateway can receive them and log that no handler exists. Starting a second listener for the same app is not reliable because either connection can receive the event.

This blocks a legitimate integration pattern: an in-process workflow plugin needs to react to organization changes while the Feishu channel plugin remains the only long-connection consumer.

## Evidence

- OpenClaw source: `extensions/feishu/src/monitor.account.ts` registers message, chat, drive, VC, reaction, menu and card handlers, but no contact user/department handlers.
- The bundled Webhooks plugin is external -> Gateway ingress, so it cannot receive a Feishu event already consumed by the Feishu channel.
- The public agent-events API is explicitly for sanitized agent workflow/UI events, not provider-native event delivery.
- Feishu cluster behavior is documented here: https://open.feishu.cn/document/server-docs/event-subscription-guide/event-subscription-configure-/request-url-configuration-case?lang=zh-CN

## Proposed capability (discussion requested before code)

Add a provider-owned, opt-in Feishu organization-event bridge. The Feishu channel remains the sole Lark SDK `EventDispatcher` owner and can register these six events when at least one in-process consumer subscribes:

- `contact.user.created_v3`
- `contact.user.updated_v3`
- `contact.user.deleted_v3`
- `contact.department.created_v3`
- `contact.department.updated_v3`
- `contact.department.deleted_v3`

The bridge should expose a narrowly scoped, typed in-process subscription surface owned by the Feishu plugin (not a core raw-event hook), with a minimal normalized envelope such as:

```ts
{ accountId, eventId, eventType, data }
```

A separate installed workflow plugin can then decide how to enqueue/forward the event. OpenClaw must not contain product-specific endpoint URLs, bearer tokens, or tenant logic.

## Constraints

- No second Feishu long connection for the same app.
- No new public inbound port.
- No product-specific FabricOS integration in the bundled Feishu plugin.
- Do not expose raw app credentials through the plugin API.
- Consumer failure must be isolated and logged; it must not break normal Feishu message handling.
- No configured/subscribed consumer means no additional contact event registration.

## Alternatives considered

1. **Second listener process** — rejected: Feishu cluster delivery means it races the Gateway and loses events.
2. **Use the bundled Webhooks plugin** — rejected: it is inbound HTTP to Gateway, the opposite direction.
3. **Add a global core raw-channel-event hook** — possible, but much broader than this requirement and would enlarge the core SDK contract for every channel.
4. **Add an arbitrary outbound URL to `channels.feishu` config** — possible, but introduces SSRF, secret, retry, and operational policy concerns; an installed in-process consumer is safer if the use case is accepted.

## Acceptance matrix

| Requirement | Evidence required |
| --- | --- |
| One Gateway connection owns Feishu delivery | Integration test proves one dispatcher registers all required handlers |
| Opt-in only | Test proves no contact handler is registered without a consumer |
| All six event types reach a typed subscriber | Unit test table for each type |
| Stable delivery key | Test validates `eventId` and `eventType` are preserved |
| Failure isolation | Throwing subscriber does not affect message handler or another subscriber |
| No competing listener / public port | Deployment instructions require neither |
| Real Feishu E2E | Tenant event -> one bridge delivery -> downstream sync run -> directory update, plus duplicate-event and failure proof |

## Request

Please confirm whether a Feishu-plugin-owned in-process subscription bridge is an acceptable extensibility boundary, and if so whether it should be exported from `@openclaw/feishu` or exposed through another supported plugin mechanism. I will not open an implementation PR until that boundary is agreed.

_This issue was prepared with Codex after reproducing the integration boundary; no tenant secrets, endpoints, or identities are included._

issues.body:
## Summary

Add an opt-in `openclaw memory duplicates` diagnostic that locates repeated Markdown blocks without modifying memory.

## Problem to solve

Operators who manually consolidate copied memory notes need to know which source files and line ranges repeat the same content. Search diversity can reduce repeated search hits, but it does not identify source locations for this maintenance workflow. Reindexing does not remove repeated source content.

## Proposed solution

A small Memory Core CLI command using the existing Markdown discovery, authorized reader, and chunker. It scans the selected agent's configured Markdown sources and reports only counts and file/line references. It does not emit block text or content hashes, open an index, call an embedding provider, or edit/delete files.

The first version compares exact non-overlapping chunks, normalizing CRLF and empty boundary lines. It supports within-file and cross-file repeats, a minimum character threshold, and capped output with explicit omitted counts. It intentionally does not detect semantic similarity or arbitrary common substrings across different chunk boundaries.

## Alternatives considered

- Existing MMR reranking (#121224) handles result diversity, not a source-content diagnostic.
- Index rebuild and memory reset repair derived state, not source duplication.
- An independent plugin could provide a related workflow. This proposal reuses Memory Core's existing source discovery/reader and CLI namespace without adding a core tool, SDK seam, schema, configuration setting, or background job. Maintainers still need to decide whether this diagnostic belongs in the bundled CLI.

## Impact and example

Synthetic example: the same refund-policy bullet appears twice in `MEMORY.md` and once in `memory/shop.md`. The report lists one group with three source locations; a changed policy is not grouped with it. The operator decides whether repetition is intentional and performs any consolidation separately.

Reports still contain file names and can be sensitive; users should inspect them before sharing. Scans are observations of current files, not a transactional snapshot or a report on persisted index contents.

## Implementation and evidence

Implementation PR: #176037. It includes synthetic-only tests and real official-CLI proof. No private notes, configuration, credentials, or real-user logs are included.

Product acceptance is not assumed. The PR makes the implementation and tradeoffs reviewable alongside this feature request.

issues.body:
**Bug type:** Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

**Beta release blocker:** No

**Summary:**
While a blocked `ask_user` tool call was pending, the user's plain-text answer was appended to the session's SQLite transcript; the blocked-tool resume path then attempted a transcript rewrite whose optimistic `expectedMutationAt` snapshot check threw `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError`; the resume caller does not re-base and retry (unlike the append and metadata-mutation paths, which already do), so the run ends `isError=true` — the turn dies and the answer is lost to the model.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Start an agent turn that calls `ask_user`; the run blocks awaiting the answer. Diagnostics show repeated `stalled session … reason=blocked_tool_call lastProgress=tool:ask_user:started` (observed 6×, age 142s→292s).
2. While blocked, send a plain-text reply in the same chat. The inbound path appends it to the session's SQLite transcript, bumping the transcript's `updatedAt` (observed `Inbound message … (direct, 253 chars)` at `20:46:00.285-04:00`).
3. ~123 ms later the blocked-tool resume path performs the rewrite that injects the tool result and continues the turn.
4. That write goes through `runTranscriptWriteSnapshotSync` (`src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write-snapshot.ts:45`); its `expectedMutationAt` guard (lines 71–74) throws `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError` — message `SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for <sessionId>` (class defined at lines 26–31) — because `before.updatedAt` no longer matches.
5. The error propagates unhandled to the tool layer: `[tools] tool_call failed: SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite …` at `20:46:00.408-04:00`.
6. The run ends `isError=true` at `20:46:00.432-04:00`; the user sees "OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply" and the turn never continues.

**Expected behavior:**
The append path (`src/agents/sessions/session-manager-append.ts:237`) and the metadata-mutation path (`src/agents/sessions/session-manager-persistence.ts:352`) already classify this exact error via `isSqliteTranscriptMutationConflict` (`src/agents/sessions/session-manager-persistence-error.ts:32`) and re-base `expectedMutationAt` from fresh state before retrying the write. The blocked-tool resume/rewrite path should behave the same: re-base and retry, so the answer is processed and the turn completes.

**Actual behavior:**
The resume/rewrite path treats the conflict as fatal — no re-base, no retry. Observed 2026-10-16 (EDT), full log excerpt below.

**OpenClaw version:** 2026.10.3 (1ecf113) — `git describe`: `v2026.10.3-27-g1ecf113bef6`
**Operating system:** macOS 26.5.1 (arm64)
**Install method:** local source checkout; gateway launched as a launchd service (`node <checkout>/dist/index.js`)
**Model:** gpufarm/qwen3.8-27b (self-hosted)
**Provider / routing chain:** openclaw → gpufarm.lan (self-hosted OpenAI-compatible API)
**Additional provider/model setup details:** Not relevant to the failure — the error is thrown in the transcript-write fence before any model fetch on the resume path.

**Logs:**
```
20:43:23.643 [diagnostic] stalled session: sessionId=aebb89e7-… state=processing age=142s queueDepth=0 reason=blocked_tool_call classification=blocked_tool_call activeWorkKind=tool_call lastProgress=tool:ask_user:started activeToolCallId=chatcmpl-tool-ab458a2c005bcd5e
20:43:53.644 [diagnostic] stalled session: … age=172s … (same shape; repeats at 20:44:23, 20:44:53, 20:45:23, 20:45:53; age 202s→292s)
20:45:57.716 [telegram] [diag] isolated polling worker update received updateId=735980841 queued=1
20:45:57.728 [telegram] [diag] isolated polling update spooled updateId=735980841
20:45:57.729 [telegram] [diag] isolated polling offset queued updateId=735980841
20:46:00.285 [telegram] Inbound message telegram:<chat> -> @<bot> (direct, 253 chars)
20:46:00.408 [tools] tool_call failed: SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for aebb89e7-… raw_params={"id":"openclaw:core:ask_user","args":{…REDACTED…}}
20:46:00.432 [telegram] embedded run agent end: runId=a7354fd9-… isError=true model=qwen3.8-27b provider=gpufarm error=⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply. … rawError=SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for aebb89e7-…
20:46:03.711 [diagnostic] message processed: … messageId=<inbound-id> sessionId=aebb89e7-… sessionKey=agent:main:direct:<chat> outcome=error duration=588007ms
```
(redacted: `raw_params` contained private conversation content; session/run/tool-call UUIDs truncated for privacy. Full unredacted lines exist in `gateway.log` of the reporter's host.)

**Screenshots, recordings, and evidence:**
- Source trace (verified against the installed 1ecf113 tree):
  - Error class + message: `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write-snapshot.ts:26-31`
  - Throw sites: `session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write-snapshot.ts:74` (`expectedMutationAt` guard inside `runTranscriptWriteSnapshotSync`); `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write.ts:569` (`replaceEvents` stale-snapshot guard under `withTranscriptWriteLock`); `session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write.ts:713` (`assertSqliteTranscriptSnapshotUnchanged`)
  - Retry siblings that already handle this error: `src/agents/sessions/session-manager-append.ts:237` and `src/agents/sessions/session-manager-persistence.ts:352`, both via `isSqliteTranscriptMutationConflict` at `src/agents/sessions/session-manager-persistence-error.ts:32` (walks the `cause` chain, depth 3)
- Related open issues — checked, NOT duplicates (different failure modes; no SQLite rewrite conflict involved):
  - #162241 — per-chat 300s cap evicts an `ask_user`-pending turn; the answer then fails pre-transport with a bare "LLM request failed"
  - #150795 — `ask_user` after `sessions_yield`; answers refused with "question answer caller policy does not match its creator"
- Related merged PRs — checked, none covers this path:
  - #169306 (fix: carry question answer custody into async writes, merged 2026-10-11) — its marker `resolveSessionTranscriptQuestionAnswer` IS present in the installed 1ecf113 build (`dist/session-transcript-read-fence-*.mjs`), and the failure still occurred on 2026-10-16. Custody handling, not conflict retry.
  - #169061 (recover actor appends after steering receipt rewrites) — steering receipt path
  - #168155 (pin ask_user timeout settlement against stale transcript fence) — timeout/no-answer settlement path
  - #164372 (keep native Talk consults running during transcript updates) — Talk/voice path

**Impact and severity:**
- Affected: any channel where a plain-text reply arrives while a blocking tool (`ask_user` observed) is pending; observed on a Telegram DM
- Severity: High — the turn dies mid-conversation, the user's answer is lost to the model's context, and the user must re-send; the whole blocked turn counts as `outcome=error` (duration 588007 ms)
- Frequency: intermittent — race between the resume path's snapshot read and write and the concurrent inbound append (observed window: 123 ms)
- Consequence: failed run + lost user message + error notice instead of a reply

**Additional information:**
- The guard itself is intentional for cross-process safety (`session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write.ts` ~line 577 comment: "The writer queue is process-local. Revalidate after BEGIN IMMEDIATE so a committed cross-process append cannot be deleted by the rewrite."). The gap is that the resume/rewrite caller treats a tripped guard as fatal instead of re-basing and retrying, while the two sibling callers already retry.
- Workaround observed: re-send the answer (starts a new turn; the lost turn's `ask_user` state is superseded).

issues.body:
## Problem

On paired-node turns, the skill-resource transfer owner can deliver verified instructions while prompt/catalog consumers discard that snapshot. Installed skill search/read then tries the sandbox filesystem bridge, which the paired node may not provide. Eligible discovery-only skills are also omitted from transfer selection, so they cannot be read or searched through the delivered catalog.

## Reproduction

On main at `30184f85d02ec9d34918c39c1017b9026bc36522`, transfer an eligible skill through the existing node worker workspace carrier, then bind the installed-skill catalog under the admitted resource context with its exact read-only mounts and no filesystem bridge. Exercise prompt instruction reading, body search, and skills_read. Repeat with an eligible discovery-only skill. The accompanying production-path regression fails before the fix for the discarded prompt snapshot and missing discovery-only delivery.

## Expected behavior

Prompt references, search, and whole instruction reads must consume the same verified delivered bytes for that admitted turn. Retired turns and different mount identities must not reuse them, and changed Gateway content must not substitute for delivered bytes. Discovery delivery should retain the existing resource budget and lifecycle/transport owners.

issues.body:
## Problem

When an OpenClaw Codex turn disables the native tool surface, allowed dynamic tools can remain deferred even though native JavaScript discovery is unavailable. Fallback metadata for an unlisted model also disables native tool search. The model can therefore receive guidance to discover tools through a runner it does not have, while session tools remain unlisted.

## Reproduction

On upstream main at `30184f85d02ec9d34918c39c1017b9026bc36522`, prepare a dynamic-tool bridge with default searchable loading for a turn whose native surface is disabled. Project an allowed session tool and build its thread configuration with `nativeCodeModeEnabled: false`. The schema stays deferred while the thread disables native code mode. The focused regression in the accompanying fix exercises this projection, thread configuration, and actual bridge invocation without credentials or a live Gateway.

## Expected behavior

The existing dynamic-loading owner should publish allowed direct schemas whenever the native surface is disabled. Prompt producers should describe the actual capability and exact qualified tool names. Native-enabled searchable/direct/code-mode-only behavior, tool policies, session authority, pairing, and native-versus-managed delegation guidance should remain intact.

`ALL_TOOLS` and `tools` belong to the native JavaScript runtime; they are not shell environment variables. Shell execution is not a substitute for that discovery runtime.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In `steer` mode, on turns whose visible reply must go through the `message` tool (`sourceReplyDeliveryMode: "message_tool_only"`, where the final assistant text is private), steering can skip the `message(action=send)` call that carries the finished answer. The call gets the synthetic result `Skipped to process an incoming message.`, the answer is never delivered, and the model moves on to the newer message. A user who sends follow-ups while the agent works can go minutes without seeing any reply, because each completed answer is dropped at the send step.

### Steps to reproduce

Current `main`:

1. Use the built-in runtime with `messages.queue.mode: "steer"` (the default) on a turn that resolves to `message_tool_only`, for example a direct chat with `messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`.
2. Give the agent a tool that runs sequentially. Bundled MCP server tools are sequential unless the server supports parallel tool calls.
3. Ask for something that makes the model answer in one assistant message: `[<sequential tool call>, message(action=send, <answer>)]`.
4. While the sequential tool is running, send a second message.

Minimal in-repo reproduction (scripted model, no live provider): a real `Agent` with the real `message` tool (WebChat internal source sink), `installMessageToolTerminalHook` in `message_tool_only` mode, a `lookup` tool with `executionMode: "sequential"` that receives a steer while it runs, and a model that answers input A with `[lookup, message(send, "Answer for input A.")]`, then input B with `[message(send, "Answer for input B.")]`.

On 2026.9.5 step 2 is not needed: before #163852 every launch was steering-checked, so even a lone `message(send)` was skipped whenever a steer was waiting.

### Expected behavior

The answer to the first message is delivered, then the steer is applied after the tool results and the model answers the second message. That is the documented contract in `docs/concepts/queue-steering.md`: "In the built-in runtime, each steered user input gets its own delivered answer in order. A later answer does not replace a completed answer to an earlier input, even when steering skipped its pending tools."

### Actual behavior

The `message(action=send)` call for the first answer is never executed. Its tool result is `Skipped to process an incoming message.` (`details: { status: "skipped", deniedReason: "steering" }`). Only the answer to the second message is sent.

From the in-repo reproduction on current `main`:

```
expected { sent: ["Answer for input A.", "Answer for input B."], requests: 2, deliveries: 2 }
received { sent: ["Answer for input B."], requests: 2, deliveries: 1 }
```

### OpenClaw version

Observed on 2026.9.5. Reproduced on `main` at 9b707074b5f (2026-10-17), in the narrower form described under Additional information.

### Operating system

Reproduction: macOS (Darwin 25.6.0), Node 26.12.0. The host OS of the original observation was not recorded.

### Install method

Reproduction: source checkout (`pnpm test`).

### Model

Model-independent. Reproduced with a scripted model stream; the original observation's model was not recorded.

### Provider / routing chain

Not involved: the reproduction uses a scripted stream. Original observation: built-in OpenClaw runtime, Telegram direct chat.

### Logs

```shell
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (no sanitized gateway log from the original observation; the reproduction output is above)
```

### Impact and severity

Affected: users of `message_tool_only` turns (direct chats configured with `messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`, room events, and other turns whose final text is private) in the default `steer` queue mode.
Severity: High for those surfaces. The user sees no reply to a message the agent already answered, and there is no error or notice.
Frequency: every time a steer is waiting when the answer's send is reached in a sequential batch after another call has started. On 2026.9.5, every time a steer was waiting at any send launch.
Consequence: replies to earlier messages are silently lost while the user keeps typing; the conversation looks stalled.

### Additional information

Root cause, read from `main` at 9b707074b5f:

- On `message_tool_only` turns the final assistant text is private and the visible answer must be `message(action=send)` ([`src/agents/system-prompt-messaging.ts:41`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9b707074b5f231f6976456ea7431567893fe7d1c/src/agents/system-prompt-messaging.ts#L41), mode chosen in [`src/auto-reply/reply/source-reply-delivery-mode.ts:58-93`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9b707074b5f231f6976456ea7431567893fe7d1c/src/auto-reply/reply/source-reply-delivery-mode.ts#L58-L93)). So the answer is a tool call, not assistant text.
- Since #163852, an assistant message's tool calls are a committed plan until one starts executing. In a sequential batch, once any call has started, the steering checkpoint runs before every later call and a waiting steer skips the whole unstarted tail ([`packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.ts:600-607`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9b707074b5f231f6976456ea7431567893fe7d1c/packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.ts#L600-L607) and [`:629-632`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9b707074b5f231f6976456ea7431567893fe7d1c/packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.ts#L629-L632), tail completed at [`:769-778`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9b707074b5f231f6976456ea7431567893fe7d1c/packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.ts#L769-L778) with the message at [`:80`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9b707074b5f231f6976456ea7431567893fe7d1c/packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.ts#L80)).
- The whole batch becomes sequential when any of its tools is sequential ([`agent-loop.ts:534-547`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9b707074b5f231f6976456ea7431567893fe7d1c/packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.ts#L534-L547)), and bundled MCP tools are sequential unless their server supports parallel tool calls ([`src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.ts:217-218`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9b707074b5f231f6976456ea7431567893fe7d1c/src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.ts#L217-L218)). The `message` tool is parallel-capable, so whether the answer can be dropped depends on its sibling calls.
- Skipping makes sense for work the model may want to replan after a steer. It does not make sense for the answer itself: the text was already composed for the earlier input, and on these turns nothing else will deliver it.

Suggested direction: let the steering checkpoint leave a call that delivers the turn's visible reply (a `message` send to the current conversation on a `message_tool_only` turn) unskipped. The reply goes out and the steer follows its result. Running tools are unaffected, parallel batches are unchanged, and later calls in the same batch stay skippable.

Related: #163852 (narrowed this from every launch to the sequential tail), #153522 (the skip note leaking as visible text, a different symptom of the same boundary).
