issues.body:
## Summary

OAuth authorization for the official Todoist HTTP MCP server fails during the authorization-code → token exchange with `InvalidGrantError`.

The browser authorization step succeeds, but `openclaw mcp login todoist --code '<code>'` consistently fails.

## Environment

Initially reproduced on:

- OpenClaw: `2026.7.1-2 (0790d9f)`
- Install: npm global
- Channel: stable
- OS: Ubuntu headless VPS

Also reproduced after upgrading to:

- OpenClaw: `2026.8.1-beta.1`
- Channel: beta

## MCP configuration

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "url": "https://ai.todoist.net/mcp",
  "transport": "streamable-http",
  "auth": "oauth",
  "codex": {
    "agents": ["main"],
    "defaultToolsApprovalMode": "prompt"
  }
}
```

`openclaw mcp status` reports:

```text
todoist: streamable-http oauth
launch: https://ai.todoist.net/mcp
timeouts: connect=30000ms request=60000ms
oauth: tokens=no client=yes
```

So OAuth client registration appears to succeed, but user tokens are never obtained.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run:

```bash
openclaw mcp logout todoist
openclaw mcp login todoist
```

2. Open the generated authorization URL in a browser.

The URL contains PKCE parameters and a loopback redirect similar to:

```text
response_type=code
code_challenge=<challenge>
code_challenge_method=S256
redirect_uri=http://127.0.0.1:8989/oauth/callback
scope=data:read_write
resource=https://ai.todoist.net/mcp
```

3. Approve access in Todoist.
4. Copy the fresh authorization code from the redirect URL.
5. Immediately run, without starting another login flow:

```bash
openclaw mcp login todoist --code '<fresh-code>'
```

## Actual result

```text
[openclaw] Could not start the CLI.
[openclaw] Reason: InvalidGrantError
```

With `OPENCLAW_DEBUG=1`:

```text
InvalidGrantError
    at parseErrorResponse (.../@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/esm/client/auth.js:132:16)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:104:5)
    at async executeTokenRequest (.../@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/esm/client/auth.js:776:15)
    at async authInternal (.../@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/esm/client/auth.js:263:24)
    at async auth (.../@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/esm/client/auth.js:158:20)
    at async runMcpOAuthLoginAttempt (...agent-bundle-mcp-runtime...js:452:9)
    at async runMcpOAuthLogin (...agent-bundle-mcp-runtime...js:474:10)
```

The failure appears to occur during the token request rather than during discovery/client registration.

## Expected behavior

The second command should exchange the authorization code using the PKCE verifier associated with the original login attempt and store the resulting OAuth tokens.

`openclaw mcp status` should then report OAuth tokens as available.

## Additional observations

The issue persists after:

- generating a completely new OAuth flow/code
- ensuring the authorization code is only used once
- `openclaw mcp logout todoist`
- killing stale/suspended OpenClaw CLI processes
- starting a fresh login flow
- upgrading from stable `2026.7.1-2` to beta `2026.8.1-beta.1`

The generated redirect URI is:

```text
http://127.0.0.1:8989/oauth/callback
```

After `openclaw mcp login todoist` returns, no process is listening on port 8989:

```bash
ss -ltnp | grep 8989
```

returns no output.

This may be expected for the documented manual/headless `--code` flow, but I mention it in case it is relevant.

The OpenClaw state DB exists at:

```text
~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite
```

The database contains tables such as:

```text
auth_profile_state
auth_profile_stores
schema_meta
migration_runs
```

but no table named `mcp_oauth_stores` on this installation. I have not manually modified the database.

## Possible cause

Could the temporary PKCE verifier / OAuth transaction state be lost or retrieved incorrectly between:

```bash
openclaw mcp login todoist
```

and:

```bash
openclaw mcp login todoist --code ...
```

Alternatively, could the token request be using a different `redirect_uri`, client registration, or PKCE verifier from the authorization request?

## Related issues

There are some related MCP OAuth lifecycle/interoperability issues (e.g. #122947 and #119914), but I did not find an existing Todoist-specific issue reproducing `InvalidGrantError` with this flow.

## Security

Authorization codes, OAuth client IDs, PKCE challenges/verifiers, state values, and tokens are intentionally omitted/redacted.

issues.body:
## Summary

In Talk mode with `realtime.brain: "agent-consult"` and `realtime.transport: "gateway-relay"` against the OpenAI provider, if the sub-agent behind `openclaw_agent_consult` takes more than a few seconds to reply (e.g. a sub-agent session with a heavy startup routine, running on a slower/larger model), the realtime voice turn dies with a `session.error` **before** the real answer arrives. The underlying `chat.send` to the sub-agent session is never aborted and completes normally — the reply shows up correctly in the text transcript — but the voice side never speaks it and the user hears/sees nothing, or an apparent "no reply" state.

## Environment

- OpenClaw version: 2026.7.1
- Talk config: `realtime.provider: "openai"`, `realtime.transport: "gateway-relay"`, `realtime.brain: "agent-consult"`
- Reproduced talking to a sub-agent session (Opus-backed) whose consult replies routinely take 12–25s due to session-start context loading.

## Repro sequence (from Gateway logs, `talk` subsystem events for one `sessionId`)

```
tool.call                                    (openclaw_agent_consult invoked)
tool.result  final:false                     (~10ms later — "working…" placeholder submitted via submitRealtimeAgentConsultWorkingResponse)
session.error final:true                     (~150ms later — realtime turn is killed)
...
tool.result  final:true                      (12–25s later — the REAL answer, delivered too late to reach the closed turn)
```

This pattern repeats on essentially every turn where the consult takes more than a couple seconds.

## Root cause (best guess from source, v2026.7.1)

- `talk-CBDoMLuy.js`: `submitRealtimeAgentConsultWorkingResponse` submits a placeholder tool result with `willContinue: true` to keep the realtime turn open while the real `chat.send` result is pending (gated on `bridge.supportsToolResultContinuation`, which is `true` for the OpenAI provider per `realtime-voice-provider-nQwhq8dv.js`).
- When the real result is later ready, delivery apparently races against OpenAI's realtime response lifecycle. `realtime-voice-provider-nQwhq8dv.js` `handleEvent()`'s `case "error"` only recovers from two specific, narrowly-matched error shapes:
  - `OPENAI_REALTIME_ACTIVE_RESPONSE_ERROR_PREFIX = "Conversation already has an active response in progress:"` — but only when `rejectsManualResponseCreate` is true, i.e. the error's `event_id` matches a tracked `manualResponseCreateEventId`.
  - `OPENAI_REALTIME_NO_ACTIVE_RESPONSE_CANCEL_ERROR`.
  - Any other error shape (including, seemingly, the same "active response in progress" condition arising from the deferred tool-result delivery path rather than a manual response create) falls through to the generic `this.config.onError?.(new Error(detail))`, which bubbles up to `onError` in `talk-CBDoMLuy.js` and fires a terminal `session.error`, ending the turn.
- Net effect: the turn is killed by an unrecovered protocol error at almost exactly the moment the real answer would otherwise have been deliverable, and there's no retry/reopen path once that happens.

## Expected behavior

- A consult that finishes after the "working" placeholder was accepted should still be deliverable back into the realtime session (or, if the turn genuinely can no longer accept it, this should be handled gracefully — e.g. speak the answer as a fresh assistant turn — rather than surfacing as a dead-end `session.error` with no spoken output).
- At minimum, `session.error` in this specific consult-delivery race should not be indistinguishable from a hard connection failure, so clients/users aren't left thinking the consult produced nothing when it actually succeeded moments later.

## Impact

Realtime Talk against any sub-agent whose reply latency exceeds OpenAI's realtime response-lifecycle patience becomes unreliable: the user hears nothing (or a stall), while the correct answer is silently sitting in the text session log, confusing about whether the request even landed.

issues.body:
**Version:** `2026.8.1-beta.1` (ff8a3fe)
**Runtime:** `claude-cli` backend, `anthropic/claude-opus-5`
**Surfaces affected:** Control UI (webchat) and the Android app. Telegram is **not** affected.

## Summary

With the `claude-cli` backend, every assistant turn is persisted twice through two independent writers, and clients that render the transcript show both. The user sees the full turn, then immediately a second copy of the same turn as one plain block.

The two copies are not byte-identical, so the Control UI's "consecutive duplicate text-only messages collapse into one bubble with a count badge" rule (documented in `web/control-ui.md`) never fires.

## Expected vs actual

**Expected:** one assistant turn appears once.

**Actual:** the turn appears twice:

1. **Live/canonical view** — each assistant text block as its own bubble, interleaved with tool-call cards, imported from the Claude Code transcript (`importedFrom: "claude-cli"`, `api: "anthropic-messages"`, `stopReason: "end_turn"`).
2. **Aggregate record** — a single message whose `content` holds **one text block** with every intermediate narration line *and* the final answer concatenated (`api: "cli"`, `stopReason: "stop"`, `idempotencyKey: "cli-assistant:<runId>"`), written ~650 ms later.

The more intermediate text a turn emits, the larger the visible duplicate.

## Evidence

Session store: `~/.openclaw/agents/<agentId>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`, table `transcript_events`.

```sql
select seq, event_json, created_at
from transcript_events
where session_id like '<session>%'
order by seq;
```

A turn that emitted two narration lines plus a final answer produced this aggregate:

```
seq 44  api=cli  len=1835  text blocks in content: 1
"Son 18 (16 "New chat", una sin etiqueta y la del móvil). Voy con la del móvil primero…
 \n\nLa herramienta está limitada a mi propio árbol de sesiones. Voy por la CLI.
 \n\nHecho. Las 18 archivadas, verificado contra la base de datos. …"
```

That single record reproduces, verbatim and in order, the three separate bubbles the client had already rendered for the same turn.

Across the whole store: **84 duplicated turns out of 307 assistant messages carrying text.** The pattern is constant — a `cli` record paired with a twin whose `api` differs (`anthropic-messages`, `openclaw-transcript` or `openai-responses`) and whose byte length is identical.

## Where it comes from

`persistCliAssistantTranscript()` in `dist/cli-runner-*.js` writes the aggregate via `appendExactAssistantMessageToSessionTranscript` with `idempotencyKey: cli-assistant:${runParams.runId}`.

It is gated by `runParams.persistAssistantTranscript`, computed in `dist/agent-runner.runtime-*.js` as:

```js
persistAssistantTranscript:
  turn.followupRun.currentInboundEventKind !== "room_event" &&
  turn.followupRun.run.suppressTranscriptOnlyAssistantPersistence !== true
```

and `suppressTranscriptOnlyAssistantPersistence` is only set for room events (`get-reply-*.js`: `suppressTranscriptOnlyAssistantPersistence: isRoomEvent`). So for ordinary DM turns the aggregate is always written, in addition to the per-block import from the CLI transcript. There is no user-facing setting to disable it.

## Possibly related condition

`openclaw doctor` reports on the same install:

```
- Main session transcript missing (~/.openclaw/agents/<agentId>/sessions/<sessionId>.jsonl).
```

That directory holds **138 `*.trajectory-path.json` pointers and zero `.jsonl` transcripts**. With no native transcript to reconcile against, the two writers never converge.

## Why Telegram is unaffected

Channel delivery sends the final text once — the gateway log shows a single `outbound send ok` per message. Telegram renders what was delivered, not the transcript, so the aggregate is never shown there.

## Related

PR #98117 (`fix(ios): avoid transient duplicate final replies`) addresses a neighbouring symptom in the shared chat view model, where a live `chat.final` row is adopted by the canonical `session.message` instead of being appended twice. This report is one layer lower: two rows are genuinely persisted, so adopting at render time would hide the duplicate rather than prevent it.

issues.body:
## Summary

Slack starts its typing indicator as soon as a model turn begins. For ambient channel turns that intentionally finish with `NO_REPLY`, this can add and remove a reaction even though no response is ultimately sent. In busy channels, those transient reactions make a silent observer look indecisive or noisy.

Current main avoids that flash for ambient room events by suppressing typing indicators entirely. That also removes useful feedback from long-running turns that perform tool work before producing visible output.

## Desired behavior

Allow Slack accounts to configure an initial typing-indicator delay. A turn that finishes before the delay should never start the indicator. A turn that remains active past the delay should start the existing indicator lifecycle and clean it up normally.

The default behavior should remain unchanged.

## Reproduction

1. Configure a Slack account with `typingReaction` and ambient channel participation.
2. Send a channel message that the agent should observe but not answer.
3. Let the turn finish with `NO_REPLY`.

## Current behavior

On a deployed Slack observer, the reaction appeared immediately and was removed when an 11.5-second `NO_REPLY` turn completed. A sample of 27 recent `NO_REPLY` turns completed in 11.4 seconds on average; none exceeded 16 seconds.

## Proposed behavior

Add an optional non-negative delay for Slack typing indicators. When configured, ambient turns should retain typing feedback, but only after the delay has elapsed.

## Environment

- Channel: Slack
- OpenClaw: 2026.7.2 beta-series deployment; behavior confirmed against current main's typing lifecycle

issues.body:
### Summary

Outbound Signal attachments are handed to signal-cli as a **filesystem path**, which silently assumes the gateway and the signal-cli daemon run as the same uid. When they don't — a hardened deployment where signal-cli has its own service user — every generated image or video fails at the last hop, after appearing to work.

`extensions/signal/src/send.ts` (still current on `main`):

```ts
const resolved = await resolveOutboundAttachmentFromUrl(opts.mediaUrl.trim(), maxBytes, { … });
attachments = [resolved.path];
```

The path lives under `~/.openclaw/media/outbound`, which is `0700` and owned by the gateway user, so a signal-cli running as anyone else cannot traverse it:

```
Signal RPC -32603: Failed to send message: …/media/outbound/image-….jpg
  (Permission denied) (AttachmentInvalidException)
```

### Why the obvious workaround doesn't hold

Granting the signal-cli user traverse-only access to the chain does not survive: **OpenClaw re-asserts `0700` on `media` on every generation.** Measured directly — `0710` before a run, `0700` after — so any `chmod` is undone before the send, and a watcher would be racing it. The file itself is world-readable; the path is not.

### Suggested fix, which needs no signal-cli change

signal-cli's `send` already accepts a data URI in place of a path. From its own `--help`:

```
-a, --attachment       Add an attachment. Can be either a file path or a
                       data URI. Data URI encoded attachments must follow
                       RFC 2397. Additionally a file name can be added, e.g.
                       data:<MIME-TYPE>;filename=<FILENAME>;base64,<BASE64 ENCODED DATA>
```

So passing `data:<contentType>;filename=<name>;base64,<…>` instead of `resolved.path` removes the shared-filesystem assumption entirely — the bytes travel over the JSON-RPC connection that is already open. The `filename=` parameter also preserves the original name, which the path form does not always manage.

Base64 inflates the payload by about a third, so this may be better as opt-in (a `channels.signal.attachmentTransport: "path" | "inline"` style switch) rather than an unconditional change, especially for video against `mediaMaxMb`.

A narrower alternative would be a configurable outbound media directory, so an operator can point it somewhere both uids reach. That works but keeps the assumption; the data URI removes it.

### Why a deployment would separate the uids

Not an unusual setup: signal-cli's state directory *is* the Signal account — anything that can read it can send as that identity and deregister the number — so it is worth confining to its own service user with `StateDirectoryMode=0700`, separate from the process that runs model output and tools. Path-based delivery makes that split cost media support, which is a surprising trade to discover at the last hop rather than at config time.

The workaround available today is to run signal-cli at the gateway's uid, which is what we ended up doing, and it means the gateway can read the account key material.

### Environment

- OpenClaw `2026.7.1-2`, `@openclaw/signal@2026.7.1`, npm global
- signal-cli 0.14.7 under its own systemd unit, `--http 127.0.0.1:8081`, `apiMode: "native"`, `autoStart: false`
- Debian Bookworm (Raspberry Pi OS), arm64
- Verified against `main` at the time of writing: `send.ts` still passes `resolved.path`

issues.body:
A focused update regression run hit an intermittent native crash in the repository's pinned Bun on macOS arm64. The SQLite read-only worker exited with `SIGTRAP` before it reached the test's injected Doctor error. This needs runtime-owner investigation; passing a replay is not a fix.

Observed with the unchanged pinned runtime `openclaw-v1.4.3-20261017-b76e4b4e67-webkit-01f208ae7a` (`1.4.3-canary.1+b76e4b4e6`), macOS 27.0.1 / arm64. The executable SHA-256 is `09905676b154ec3953042f720341907bdc9f76a4c42a34ba033ab0298e37dfd1`, matching `scripts/lib/openclaw-bun.json`.

The failing entry point was:

```sh
HOME="$PWD/.artifacts/bun-repro/home" \
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$PWD/.artifacts/bun-repro/state" \
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/update-command-finalize-refusal.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The first failure occurred while this file was selected as part of a larger importer sweep, in `preserves the repair failure and recovery policy at doctor (inherited=false)`. Instead of `Synthetic half-applied schema write`, the assertion received:

```text
SQLite read-only worker exited with signal SIGTRAP
Bun Canary v1.4.3-canary.1 (b76e4b4e6) macOS Silicon
Elapsed: 1ms | User: 2ms | Sys: 1ms
RSS: 2.54 MB | Peak: 2.54 MB | Commit: 16.71 MB | Faults: 11
panic(main thread): Trap instruction at address 0x1847CEC58
```

The native crash report records `EXC_BREAKPOINT` / `SIGTRAP`, about 70 ms after process launch. Bun was launched by Bun. Its main-thread native trace contains `std::__1::__call_once` and Bun image offsets, with no symbolized application frame. The binary is stripped, so the precise native mechanism is still unknown; the low startup memory and 1 ms runtime localize this to early runtime initialization, rather than a slow SQLite operation.

The failure is pre-existing relative to #175928: the failing test, `src/infra/sqlite-readonly-worker.ts`, `src/infra/sqlite-readonly-worker-session.ts`, `src/infra/runtime-worker-url.ts`, and the Bun manifest have identical Git blob IDs on the PR base `104dc5af5625e3995531624f03fe6b50e8448c06` and PR head `9785a1e9764acfcdfe434cba04abdbc6713eafda`. The service diagnostic patch does not alter the worker launch or Bun artifact.

Bounded follow-up:

- The same test passed on targeted replay, including the original error-identity assertion; no code or assertion was weakened.
- 100 minimal `bun --no-install -e 'console.log("startup-ok")'` launches from Node passed in 808 ms total.
- 500 identical minimal launches from the same pinned Bun parent passed in 4005 ms total.
- These results establish intermittence, not a repair or complete reproduction. No retry, timeout increase, runtime fallback, or dependency change was added.

Please investigate the pinned Bun/macOS native startup path using its matching symbols. A targeted test result cannot close this issue until the native cause or an upstream fix is identified.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On 2026.10.10-beta.1 (Windows), a Discord channel session of agent `main` was left wedged after a subagent's completion announce stalled. Every later inbound Discord message to that channel was dropped:

1. **Before the restart:** messages were rejected at pre-dispatch with `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED`, retried 7 times, then dead-lettered (`session-start-conflict-retry-limit`).
2. **After a gateway restart:** main-session restart recovery failed on every pass with `Requester settle recovery lacks its original cohort or operator authority`. Each new message then failed with `Restart recovery failed: <sessionKey>` and was dead-lettered (`retry-limit-exceeded`).

`/health` and `/readyz` stayed green throughout, and `channels status` showed the account connected. The only outward signal was `deliveryQueues.ingressFailed` growing.

`sessions.abort` did not clear it. `sessions.reset` (with `expectedSessionId`) did, and a message still in its retry window then processed normally.

### Steps to reproduce

This was observed once; I don't have a deterministic repro.

1. Agent `main` (claude-cli runtime, Opus) is bound to a Discord guild channel. In that channel session it spawns a visible subagent.
2. The subagent finishes. Its announce to the requester keeps failing with `GatewayProtocolRequestTimeoutError: gateway request timeout for chat.history` while the gateway is slow: the main thread was stalling 1-9 s at a time, and a WAL checkpoint was blocked by a reader.
3. The requester's embedded run shows no progress. Stuck-session recovery aborts it after 365 s: `action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=false forceCleared=true released=1`. About 25 minutes later the subagent announce gives up: `Subagent announce give up (expiry) ... retries=11 deliveryError="gateway request timeout for chat.history"`.
4. Send a normal user message in the same Discord channel.

### Expected behavior

The next user message starts a turn, and the abandoned announce is settled or dropped. At worst, the wedged session reports itself as degraded in health instead of silently dead-lettering user input.

### Actual behavior

Log excerpts (times ET; channel ids redacted):

```
17:01:00 diagnostic: stalled session: sessionKey=agent:main:discord:channel:<ch> state=processing age=125s reason=active_work_without_progress classification=stalled_agent_run activeWorkKind=embedded_run lastProgress=embedded_run:started
17:05:15 diagnostic: stuck session recovery outcome: status=aborted action=abort_embedded_run ... aborted=true drained=false forceCleared=true released=1
17:32:48 [warn] Subagent announce give up (expiry) run=<run> child=agent:main:subagent:<id> requester=agent:main:discord:channel:<ch> retries=11 endedAgo=2085s deliveryError="gateway request timeout for chat.history"

18:33:01 channels/discord: discord message run failed: DispatchSessionRefreshRequiredError: Session "agent:main:discord:channel:<ch>" changed while starting work. Retry.
   (x7 over about 2.5 minutes)
18:35:24 channels/discord: discord ingress: spooled update <msg> failed with non-retryable session-start-conflict-retry-limit: ... | SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED; dead-lettered
19:31-19:33  same sequence for the next message, dead-lettered

-- gateway restart at 20:15 (trigger-file restart; healthy at 20:19) --

20:25:18 main-session-restart-recovery: requester settle recovery source unavailable for agent:main:discord:channel:<ch>: Error: Requester settle recovery lacks its original cohort or operator authority
20:25:18 main-session-restart-recovery: main-session restart recovery startup complete: started=0 settled=0 failed=1 skipped=0
   (repeats every recovery pass)
20:33:14 diagnostic: message processed: channel=discord ... sessionKey=agent:main:discord:channel:<ch> outcome=error error="Error: Restart recovery failed: agent:main:discord:channel:<ch>
20:35:32 channels/discord: discord ingress: spooled update <msg> on lane channel:<ch> reached retry limit after 8 attempts; dead-lettered
```

Recovery attempts:

- **Gateway restart:** did not help. It moved the failure from `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED` to `Restart recovery failed`.
- **`gateway call sessions.abort {"key": ...}`:** returned `{"ok":true,"abortedRunId":null,"status":"aborted"}`. A resubmitted message still failed with `Restart recovery failed`.
- **`gateway call sessions.reset {"key": ..., "expectedSessionId": ...}`:** succeeded. The message then in its retry window started a normal claude-cli turn about 90 s later and replied.
- **`openclaw channels dead-letters resubmit <id> --channel discord --account default`:** worked once the session was reset.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.10-beta.1

### Operating system

Windows 11 Pro 26200. The gateway runs as an elevated background process; Node 24.18.0.

### Install method

npm global

### Model

claude-cli runtime (claude-opus-5-5) for agent `main`

### Provider / routing chain

claude-cli (Anthropic subscription OAuth) primary, with OpenAI fallback configured.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Disclosure: this install carries small local patches for unrelated Windows issues:

- a model runtime timeout;
- the plugin lease;
- a computer-use preempt;
- an `lstat` fix in `linkDependency`;
- skipping the fd-3 Claude token hand-off on win32;
- claude-cli native auth for cron turns.

None of them touch channel dispatch, session admission or restart recovery.

### Logs, screenshots, and evidence

See above. `health` showed `deliveryQueues.ingressFailed[discord/default].count` growing while every other surface was green. Twelve dead letters were retained across about 16 days; three came from this incident.

### Impact and severity

- **Affected:** every user message in the main Discord channel for about 3.5 hours (17:05 to 20:44).
- **Severity:** high. Messages are lost silently; the user sees no reply and no error.
- **Frequency:** once so far. Several earlier `retry-limit-exceeded` dead letters on 10-14 and 10-15 may be related.
- **Consequence:** dropped user input, and an operator has to intervene (`sessions.reset` plus `dead-letters resubmit`).

### Additional information

These look like the same family:

- #143334: lost subagent completion delivery parks the requester and starves queued user messages. Same trigger class, but here a restart did not recover the session.
- #166203 (closed): leftover `mainRestartRecovery` aggregate makes requester-settle wakes fail `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED`.
- #173412: restart recovery leaves the main session unrecoverable. Here `sessions.reset` did work.
- #127195: the undifferentiated "changed while starting work" message.

Two suggestions:

1. When a session is wedged in restart recovery, mark it degraded in `health`/`readyz`, or reply in-channel, instead of dead-lettering silently.
2. Let a requester-settle recovery that "lacks its original cohort" drop itself instead of blocking every new inbound turn.

issues.body: ### Bug type Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash) ### Beta release blocker No ### Summary When creating an ACP session with `session/new` and specifying `cwd`, the returned `session.cwd` correctly reflects the requested value, but subsequent prompt requests execute in the agent's default workspace (`~/.openclaw/workspace`) instead of the requested directory. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Call ACP `session/new` with `cwd` set to a non-default directory (e.g., `/tmp/my-project`). 2. Verify the response: `session.cwd === "/tmp/my-project"` ✓ 3. Call `prompt` with the returned `sessionKey` and a message like "print the current working directory". 4. Observe the agent reports the default workspace, not `/tmp/my-project`. ### Expected behavior The agent turn initiated via ACP `prompt` should execute in the `cwd` specified at `session/new` time. ### Actual behavior ACP `session/new` with a custom `cwd` correctly stores and returns that `cwd` in the session metadata, but when a subsequent `prompt` is sent with the returned `sessionKey`, the agent turn executes in the default workspace (`~/.openclaw/workspace`) rather than the requested directory. The agent's responses and actions reflect the default workspace path, not the `cwd` specified at session creation. ### OpenClaw version 2026.7.1-2 ### Operating system Windows11 ### Install method npm -g ### Model ornith:35b ### Provider / routing chain openclaw -> local ollama -> ornith:35b ### Additional provider/model setup details The `cwd` is stored in the ACP bridge session store but dropped when forwarding the prompt to Gateway's `chat.send`: - `session/new` correctly saves `cwd` to the ACP session store: `src/acp/translator.session-lifecycle.ts:54` - `prompt` forwarding to Gateway omits `cwd` from the payload — only `sessionKey`, `message`, etc. are sent: `src/acp/translator.prompt-stream.ts:190` - Gateway `chat.send` protocol schema has no `cwd` field: `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/logs-chat.ts:116` - Gateway lazily creates the actual agent session from the session key, falling back to the default workspace. The upstream `acpx@0.13.0` manager correctly handles `cwd` as the ACP client spawn directory and passes it to `createSession(cwd)`. The bug is in OpenClaw's ACP bridge, not in `acpx` or the caller. ### Logs ```shell ``` ### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence ### Impact and severity **Affected users/systems/channels** Affected users: - Any client or integration that uses the ACP (`session/new` → `prompt`) flow and specifies a non-default `cwd` to control the agent's working directory. This includes IDE extensions, CLI wrappers, or automation scripts that rely on ACP sessions to scope agent work to a project directory. Affected systems: - The OpenClaw ACP bridge → Gateway `chat.send` path. The ACP session store itself is not faulty; the break occurs at the bridge-to-Gateway boundary. Affected channels: - ACP protocol channel only. Direct Gateway `chat.send` callers are unaffected because that protocol has no `cwd` field to begin with. **Severity** Blocks workflow for ACP callers who rely on `cwd` to scope the agent to a specific project or repository. It is not a data-loss or security issue — the agent runs in the default workspace, so files may be read from or written to an unintended directory. If a caller assumes the agent is operating in the requested `cwd` (which the `session.cwd` metadata falsely confirms), this can lead to **unintended file creation or modification in the wrong directory**, which has a secondary data-integrity risk. ### Additional information _No response_

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After a normal Element client Megolm session rotation, OpenClaw stops decrypting inbound Matrix E2EE messages from that device while other devices in the same encrypted room continue to work.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw 2026.7.1-2 with Matrix E2EE against a self-hosted Synapse server.
2. Use a verified OpenClaw Matrix device in a private encrypted room.
3. Send messages from an Element client and confirm OpenClaw decrypts and processes them successfully.
4. Let the same Element client rotate to a new outbound Megolm session during normal operation.
5. Send another message from that same Element device.
6. Observe that Synapse accepts and delivers the encrypted event to OpenClaw, but OpenClaw fails to decrypt it with:
   "The sender's device has not sent us the keys for this message."
7. Observe that another Element device using a different Megolm session can still send messages successfully in the same room.

### Expected behavior

When an Element client rotates its outbound Megolm session during normal Matrix E2EE operation, OpenClaw should receive and persist the new session key and continue decrypting inbound messages from that device without manual intervention.

### Actual behavior

After the Element Android client rotated from a previously working Megolm session to a new Megolm session, OpenClaw received the encrypted event via /sync but failed to decrypt it with:

DecryptionError: The sender's device has not sent us the keys for this message.

OpenClaw then queried the room-key backup for the new Megolm session and Synapse returned:

404 - No room_keys found

At the same time, Element Desktop messages in the same encrypted room continued to decrypt and receive OpenClaw replies normally.

The same class of failure had previously occurred with an Element Desktop Megolm session. Logging that Desktop client out and back in created a new Matrix device/Megolm session and restored communication, but Android later independently rotated its Megolm session and reproduced the failure.

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.1-2

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04

### Install method

Docker

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Additional provider/model setup details

Not relevant to this issue. The failure occurs in the Matrix E2EE decryption path before agent/model processing.

### Logs

```shell
OpenClaw gateway:

Error decrypting event (... type=m.room.encrypted sender=<redacted> room=<redacted> ...):
DecryptionError[msg: The sender's device has not sent us the keys for this message.,
sender_key: <android-device-key>,
session_id: <new-megolm-session>]

Synapse immediately around the same event:

PUT /_matrix/client/r0/rooms/<redacted>/send/m.room.encrypted/<redacted> -> 200

GET /_matrix/client/v3/sync?... {@openclaw-bot:<redacted>} -> 200

GET /_matrix/client/v3/room_keys/keys/<redacted-room>/<new-megolm-session>?version=3
-> 404 "No room_keys found"

Observed session transition for the same Android device:

sender/device key: unchanged
previous Megolm session: <session-A>  -> OpenClaw decrypted successfully
new Megolm session:      <session-B>  -> OpenClaw failed to decrypt

A separate Element Desktop device in the same encrypted room continued working normally.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

No additional screenshots. Sanitized OpenClaw and Synapse logs are included above.

### Impact and severity

Affected: Users running OpenClaw with Matrix E2EE, observed with Element Desktop and Element Android clients.

Severity: High for production Matrix E2EE usage.

Frequency: Intermittent and tied to Megolm session changes. The failure was observed with separate Desktop and Android Megolm sessions during the same incident.

Consequence: Messages from one Matrix device stop being processed by OpenClaw while the room and other devices continue working normally. Outgoing OpenClaw messages can still work, so the failure can be silent and device-specific. Manual client logout/login temporarily restored one affected device but did not prevent recurrence on another device.

### Additional information

The issue was first suspected to be caused by a single corrupted Desktop client, but this was disproved when Android later rotated to a new Megolm session and reproduced the same decryption failure.

The OpenClaw bot device had previously shown an inconsistent signed_curve25519 one-time-key pool on Synapse. After backing up and repairing that pool, /keys/upload succeeded again with HTTP 200. However, normal later Megolm rotation on Android still produced a new undecryptable session.

This suggests the remaining issue is related to handling or persistence of newly shared inbound Megolm session keys rather than a single corrupted Element client.

Possibly related:
- #66171
- #76611

All user IDs, room IDs, domains, IP addresses, recovery keys, access tokens and full crypto identifiers have been redacted.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Realtime Talk (OpenAI provider, agent-consult) creates the client session with input transcription `{ model: "gpt-4o-mini-transcribe" }` and no `language`, even when `talk.speechLocale` is set (`en-US`). The voice-confirmation gate checks that transcript, so short confirmations are frequently transcribed in the wrong language or garbled, and high-impact actions are refused even when the user clearly said an accepted phrase. A clear spoken "Yes" was transcribed as "Ja.", "Ies." and "Les."; "make the change" was transcribed as "Make a deal." The realtime voice model itself heard the audio correctly. Its spoken reply said it heard "make the change", but the gate saw the transcriber's text.

The GA session policy on main already supports a language hint (`buildOpenAIRealtimeGaSessionPolicy({ language })` in `extensions/openai/realtime-voice-session-policy.ts`), but the Talk client-session path in `extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider-factory.ts` (around line 162 at 406772b) still sends `transcription: { model: OPENAI_REALTIME_INPUT_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL }` without it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure Talk: `talk.realtime.provider = "openai"`, `talk.realtime.model = "gpt-realtime-2.1"`, `talk.realtime.brain = "agent-consult"`, `talk.speechLocale = "en-US"`.
2. Start Talk from the Control UI (browser) and ask for an action that needs voice confirmation, e.g. "Set the realtime Talk silence duration to 1100 milliseconds."
3. When asked to confirm, say a single accepted phrase clearly, e.g. "yes" or "make the change".
4. Repeat a few times and compare the user-turn transcript with what was said.

### Expected behavior

With `talk.speechLocale = "en-US"`, the realtime session's input transcription is pinned to English (`language: "en"`), so a clearly spoken accepted phrase is transcribed correctly and the confirmation succeeds on the first try. The gate stays exactly as strict.

### Actual behavior

Short confirmations are often transcribed as another language or as different words, and the gate refuses them:
- "Yes" → "Ja." / "Ies." / "Les." (two consecutive confirmations failed; the user was told to type the change instead)
- "make the change" → "Make a deal." (refused; the second attempt succeeded)
Longer sentences in the same session were transcribed correctly, which fits language auto-detection struggling on one or two words. Moving the microphone closer didn't help.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.3 (59cb447); the code path is unchanged on main at 406772b

### Operating system

Gateway: Ubuntu on WSL2 (Windows 11), systemd user service. Talk client: Control UI in a desktop browser on the same Windows 11 PC, USB speakerphone microphone.

### Install method

npm global

### Model

Talk: gpt-realtime-2.1 (input transcription gpt-4o-mini-transcribe, hard-coded); agent behind agent-consult: gpt-6.1-sol

### Provider / routing chain

Control UI Talk → talk.client.create → OpenAI Realtime (provider "openai", mode "realtime", brain "agent-consult") → openclaw_agent_consult → main agent

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
[ws] ⇄ res ✗ talk.client.toolCall 5ms errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=Error: explicit spoken confirmation was not found after the action request
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

User-turn transcripts from the Control UI for clearly spoken confirmations: "Ja.", "Ies.", "Les.", "Make a deal." In the "Make a deal." case the assistant's spoken reply was "I heard 'make the change', but … explicit spoken confirmation was not detected", which suggests the realtime model understood the audio while the separate transcriber did not.

### Impact and severity

Voice-confirmed actions become unreliable: users repeat confirmations several times or fall back to typing, which defeats hands-free use (e.g. while driving). It fails safe (nothing runs without a matched phrase), but it pushes users toward weakening confirmation rules.

### Additional information

Suggested fix: in the Talk client-session builder, pass a language derived from `talk.speechLocale` (BCP-47 → ISO-639-1, e.g. `en-US` → `en`) as `audio.input.transcription.language`, as the GA session policy already allows. Optionally make the input transcription model configurable (see also #166773, which needs a configurable transcription deployment for Azure).

## Problem

OpenClaw currently accepts named GPT-Live voices, but cannot preserve the object-shaped reference returned for a saved prompt-created voice. This prevents operators from selecting an existing custom voice with `gpt-live-1`.

## Proposed behavior

- Accept OpenClaw's existing `speakerVoiceId: "voice_..."` setting for `gpt-live-1` and translate it to OpenAI's `{ "id": "voice_..." }` reference inside the provider.
- Preserve named string voices and their existing defaults.
- Reject malformed references and reject custom references on incompatible models without echoing the supplied value.
- Keep the saved voice reference server-side rather than returning it in the browser reservation.

## Validation

Direct provider validation confirmed that a saved prompt-created voice reference is accepted by `gpt-live-1`, produces PCM16 audio, supports interruption, and fails closed for an invalid reference. Focused OpenClaw session-shaping tests cover preservation, malformed input, compatible-model enforcement, and existing named-voice behavior.

Implementation: [PR #175940](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175940).

## References and documentation

- [OpenAI custom voices guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/custom-voices): creating prompt-generated voices and using saved IDs with GPT-Live, including `session.audio.output.voice.id`.
- [OpenAI Live session API reference](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/live/methods/create): built-in voice names and custom voice objects.
- [OpenClaw OpenAI voice and speech documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/providers/openai/voice-and-speech.md).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When a subagent's requester resolves to `message_tool_only` reply mode (a group, channel, or thread requester), and the completion agent does not call the `message` tool, the child's completed result is discarded with no user-visible output and no fallback — and the existing direct-text salvage is deliberately forbidden from covering that case, so there is currently no mechanism that can deliver it.

This is filed as a **design question** rather than a patch, because the obvious fix conflicts with an explicit upstream invariant. Two PRs (#123546, #123547) cover the parts of the surrounding defect that do not need a policy decision; this issue is the part that does.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a group/channel requester with `messages.groupChat.visibleReplies = "message_tool"`, so announce delivery resolves to `message_tool_only`.
2. From a session in that conversation, run a subagent task that completes successfully and returns result text.
3. Have the completion agent finish its turn without calling the `message` tool (in practice: any turn that ends with reasoning or an empty visible reply — no special provocation needed).
4. Observe that nothing is posted to the conversation, the announce retries up to `maxAnnounceRetryCount` (3), and then gives up.

### Expected behavior

The user who asked for the work either receives the result or receives an explicit, user-visible failure. Silent discard of a completed subagent result should not be a reachable outcome.

### Actual behavior

The result is discarded silently.

The relevant code path, on `main` (2026.8.1):

- `src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-direct-delivery.ts` — the message-tool-only site returns `reason: "message_tool_delivery_missing"` without attempting any salvage, and the incomplete-result throw path likewise has no fallback. Both are reached only when `requiresMessageToolDelivery` is true.
- `src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-completion-delivery.ts` — `deliverCompletionDirect()` is gated on `isDirectMessageDeliveryTarget(...)`, so it declines for exactly the requesters that hit the case above.
- `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-helpers.ts` — `logAnnounceGiveUp()` then emits one `[warn]` line. Before #123547 that line did not say whether any result text was lost, which is why this went unnoticed for weeks in the deployment where it was found (20 occurrences over five weeks).

### The design question

The mechanical fix is to let `deliverCompletionDirect()` salvage the raw child text for non-direct requesters too. That is **not** acceptable as a drive-by change: it breaks eight named invariants in `src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts`, including

- `does not raw-send channel completions just because the requester key is direct`
- `does not raw-send grouped child results when requester-agent output is empty`
- `fails configured channel subagent completions when parent skips required message tool`
- `does not fail stale channel subagent completions only because the parent stayed private`

Those tests encode a deliberate policy: raw child text must never enter a group, channel, or thread — the completion agent relays it in its own voice or it does not go out. #90041 proposed a blunter version of the same widening and was closed unmerged, with the review noting that a direct bypass conflicts with the message-tool delivery contract. So the policy has already been defended once, and re-proposing it as a patch would be litigating it a third time in a PR body.

That leaves a genuine gap. Some candidate directions, in rough order of how much they respect the existing contract:

1. **Retry the completion agent with an explicit corrective instruction** ("you must call the `message` tool"), rather than retrying the same prompt three times and giving up.
2. **A synthesized relay message from the completion agent's own voice** as the terminal fallback — e.g. a short system-authored "the subagent finished; here is its result" wrapper — so the group never sees raw child output, but the user still gets the content.
3. **A user-visible failure notice in the conversation** ("a background task finished but its result could not be delivered"), so the loss is at least observable to the person who asked, even if the content is not recovered.
4. **DM the requesting user the raw text out-of-band** while the group gets nothing, if the requester identity is resolvable to a direct target.
5. **Accept the loss as intended** and treat option 3 as sufficient — in which case the current `[error]` log added in #123547 plus a conversation-visible notice closes it.

Options 2 and 3 look most consistent with the existing contract, but the choice is a maintainer call about what a group is allowed to see, not something a contributor should pick unilaterally.

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.1-2 (observed); code path confirmed unchanged on main at 2026.8.1

### Operating system

Linux (Ubuntu-class, kernel 6.17)

### Install method

npm global

### Model

Not model-dependent — the defect is in announce delivery routing, downstream of model output

### Provider / routing chain

Not provider-dependent; reproduced with the completion agent simply not emitting a `message` tool call

### Additional provider/model setup details

No provider-specific configuration is involved. The trigger is `messages.groupChat.visibleReplies = "message_tool"` on the requesting conversation, which is what makes announce delivery resolve to `message_tool_only`.

### Logs

```shell
[warn] Subagent announce give up (permanent_failure) run=<id> child=<key> requester=<key> retries=3 endedAgo=<n>s
```

That single line was the entire trace before #123547 added `discardedResultChars`, which is why the loss was not attributable to a cause.

### Impact and severity

Affected: any deployment using `visibleReplies: "message_tool"` on group/channel/thread conversations that also dispatches subagents from those conversations.
Severity: data loss — completed work is destroyed, and before #123547 it was destroyed invisibly.
Frequency: intermittent, driven by whether the completion agent happens to call the `message` tool; 20 occurrences over five weeks in the deployment where it was found.
Consequence: the user who requested the work receives nothing at all, with no error, and no indication that a task ever ran.

### Additional information

Related PRs, both open and both intentionally narrower than this issue:

- #123546 — `length`-stop turns discarding visible text (separate defect, same "result silently replaced by nothing" family).
- #123547 — the announce-path fixes that need no policy decision: duplicate-send prevention via `hasAnnounceSendEvidence`, and escalating the give-up log to `[error]` with `discardedResultChars` so this failure is alertable. #123547's PR body names this issue's scope as an explicit non-goal.

Happy to implement whichever direction maintainers pick.

_AI-assisted: written with Claude, from a production incident report. The code references were verified by hand against `main`._

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression / data corruption

### Summary

The stock OpenClaw shared state database was corrupted twice on a Raspberry Pi 5 with local NVMe/ext4. In both incidents, a valid internal SQLite index leaf page was copied byte-for-byte over database page 1, replacing the SQLite header. This wedges Telegram delivery, task/subagent persistence, plugin state, device-pair, memory-core, and gateway RPC with `file is not a database`.

This is not NFS/SMB/SSHFS. The state file is on `/dev/nvme0n1p2`, ext4, `rw,noatime`. Kernel logs show no NVMe, ext4, or I/O faults. It is therefore not covered by #90491 / #91247.

### Environment

- OpenClaw: `2026.8.1` (`c3e3a09fe6`), clean `main`
- Original runtime: Node `24.18.0`, embedded SQLite `3.53.1`
- OS: Raspberry Pi OS / Linux `6.12.96+rpt-rpi-2712`, aarch64
- Storage: local NVMe, ext4
- Shared DB: stock `~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite`
- Configured concurrency at time of incidents: `agents.defaults.maxConcurrent=2`, `agents.defaults.subagents.maxConcurrent=3`

### Incident evidence

Incident 1:

- Corruption time/mtime: `2026-08-13 18:25:25 BST`
- First failure occurred while a Telegram reply was being delivered.
- Corrupt page 1 SHA-256 exactly matches healthy database page **1631**.
- `dbstat` identifies page 1631 as a leaf of `idx_channel_ingress_lane`.

Incident 2:

- Corruption time/mtime: `2026-08-13 22:06:43 BST`
- Immediately preceded by a Telegram turn plus delegated/task-registry activity.
- Corrupt page 1 SHA-256 exactly matches page **1040** elsewhere in the same corrupt database.
- After restoring the prior header for forensic inspection, `dbstat` identifies page 1040 as a leaf of `sqlite_autoindex_plugin_state_entries_1`.

Both corrupt files begin with `0x0a`, the SQLite index-leaf b-tree page type, instead of `SQLite format 3\0`. This is not random damage: an internal database page is being written to file offset zero.

Representative errors after page 1 is overwritten:

```text
[telegram] isolated polling spool drain failed: file is not a database
[gateway] Delivery recovery failed: Error: file is not a database
[agents/subagent-registry] failed to complete subagent run
[tasks/registry] Failed to persist task registry upsert
[plugins] device-pair: ... ERR_SQLITE_ERROR
[skills/workshop] skill experience review failed: Error: file is not a database
[ws] parse-error ... code=ERR_SQLITE_ERROR
```

### Recovery and current containment

- Stopped the gateway immediately on each incident.
- Preserved both corrupt files and sidecars.
- Restored a verified clean database with SQLite `.backup` while the gateway was stopped.
- All shared and per-agent databases pass offline `PRAGMA quick_check`.
- Temporarily serialized stock execution with:
  - `agents.defaults.maxConcurrent=1`
  - `agents.defaults.subagents.maxConcurrent=1`
- Upgraded only the gateway runtime using the native service installer to official Node `24.19.0`, which embeds SQLite `3.53.3`.
- OpenClaw config validates; all Telegram accounts connect; real Telegram turns complete; no recurrence observed yet.

The runtime upgrade is a containment step, not proof of root cause. SQLite 3.53.3 includes fixes for problems in 3.53.0–3.53.2, but I have not identified a release-note item that explicitly describes this page-to-offset-zero failure.

### Expected behavior

Concurrent stock gateway activity must never overwrite page 1. If SQLite reports terminal corruption, the gateway should also stop the write/retry storm and quarantine/fail closed rather than repeatedly hammering the corrupt store.

### Available evidence

I can provide redacted stability bundles, logs around both exact corruption timestamps, page hashes/comparison output, schema/dbstat mapping, and the two corrupt databases if maintainers specify a safe upload route. The databases may contain private state, so they are not attached publicly.

issues.body:
### Summary

Since the June state migration (JSON files under `workspace/memory/.dreams/` renamed to `*.migrated`, state moved into the `plugin_state_entries` keyed store), the memory-core short-term recall working set on this host has been frozen at 17 entries whose newest member is a memory from 2026-07-24. The ingestion namespaces update nightly, but the recall and phase-signal namespaces hold a small, static incumbent set, so the dreaming phases replay the same fragments for weeks. REM phase output is literally byte-identical across long runs: one md5 appears on 21 consecutive artifacts (2026-06-14 through 2026-07-15), another on 7 (2026-08-03 through 2026-08-09).

The dreams look alive from the outside (files dated nightly), but they have been dreaming about the same June and July material on repeat.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.7.1-2 (0790d9f), macOS 26.5.2 (arm64), node 24.18.0
- memory-core bundled 2026.7.1, `dreaming.enabled: true`, all other dreaming config at defaults
- Migration artifacts present: `short-term-recall.json.migrated` (2.9 MB), `phase-signals.json.migrated` (564 KB), `session-ingestion.json.migrated` (271 KB), all dated at the migration; no successor JSON files

### Observed state (plugin_state_entries, plugin_id = memory-core)

| namespace | rows | notes |
|---|---|---|
| dreaming-session-ingestion-seen | 1,270 | updates nightly, healthy |
| dreaming-session-ingestion-files | 701 | updates nightly, healthy |
| short-term-recall | **17** | pre-migration JSON was 2.9 MB |
| short-term-phase-signals | **17** | pre-migration JSON was 564 KB |
| short-term-meta | 2 | |

The 17 recall entries reference memories from March through 2026-07-24 (recallCount 1 to 18). Nothing recalled in the three weeks since, despite new memory files landing in the corpus daily (the ingestion-seen namespace confirms they are being seen).

### Why the set cannot grow

`writeMemoryCoreWorkspaceEntries` (extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-state.ts) registers the replacement entries and then **deletes every existing key not in the replacement set**:

```js
for (const entry of await store.entries())
  if (entry.key.startsWith(prefix) && !replacementKeys.has(entry.key)) await store.delete(entry.key);
```

Whole-namespace replace-write semantics mean the recall state is capped at whatever one sweep produces, and incumbents with accumulated recallCount crowd out newcomers in the ranker (frequency-weighted scoring), so the working set entrenches. Combined with whatever the migration carried over (17 rows out of a 2.9 MB corpus), the effect is a frozen input set and byte-identical REM output for weeks at a time.

### Impact

- REM and light phases surface the same themes and snippets nightly (byte-identical REM markdown for up to 21 consecutive days).
- Deep promotion ranked exactly 1 candidate and promoted 0 on every recent night here.
- Diary narratives, when they survive at all (see the concurrent-phase discard issue I filed separately), recycle June and July fragments while months of newer memories never enter the pool.

### Questions / suggested direction

1. Was the migration expected to carry the full recall history? 2.9 MB to 17 rows looks like a truncation rather than a compaction.
2. Should namespace writes merge (read-modify-write with decay or size-based eviction) instead of replace-set semantics? Replace-set makes the working set structurally unable to admit new memories unless they out-signal an incumbent within a single sweep.
3. A recency or novelty floor in `rankShortTermPromotionCandidates` (some slots reserved for never-before-recalled memories) would break the rich-get-richer lock-in regardless of storage semantics.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add a read-only CLI command that follows one durable background task from its current state through execution and completion delivery.

### Problem to solve

Operators can inspect a task with `openclaw tasks show`, but following a long-running task from a terminal requires repeated polling. Gateway-wide logs are noisy and not task-scoped, while the Control UI is not always available in headless, remote, or shell-first workflows. This makes it easy to miss useful progress transitions or confuse execution completion with completion delivery.

### Proposed solution

Support `openclaw tasks follow <lookup>` and `openclaw tasks follow <lookup> --json`, using the same task ID, run ID, or session-key lookup accepted by `tasks show`.

The command should print a bounded current snapshot, follow visible task progress in order, report execution and delivery as separate states, reconnect and replay durable state after transient Gateway interruptions, and exit when both execution and delivery are terminal. Human-readable output should work interactively, while JSON Lines output should give each record a stable identifier for duplicate handling. Ctrl-C should stop only the viewer and must never cancel or otherwise mutate the task.

The stream should honor the same authorization, visibility, redaction, and payload limits as existing task and session reads.

### Alternatives considered

Repeated `tasks show` polling can miss intermediate transitions and requires callers to invent their own interval, terminal-state, and duplicate logic. `openclaw logs --follow` is useful for Gateway diagnostics but mixes unrelated activity and exposes a different operational surface. The Control UI is a good visual inspector but does not cover terminal-only workflows. Forwarding every child update into the parent chat would add channel noise and change notification semantics.

### Impact

Affected users are operators who run subagents, ACP sessions, cron work, or other durable background tasks from remote shells and automation. The current limitation is a recurring workflow interruption rather than data loss, but it adds manual polling, delays awareness of failures or delivery problems, and makes scripting less reliable. The impact is highest for long-running or concurrent tasks and for installations without continuous Control UI access.

### Evidence/examples

The current CLI provides point-in-time task inspection with `openclaw tasks show`, and Gateway-wide observation with `openclaw logs --follow`, but no task-scoped follow command. A useful JSON Lines sequence would include an initial task snapshot, bounded progress records, any reconnect/resume markers, an execution outcome, and the final completion-delivery state.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself

### Additional information

This request is intentionally read-only. It should not introduce a second transcript or persistence owner, forward every child message into a parent channel, or change execution, cancellation, notification, delivery, or restart-recovery behavior beyond what a reconnecting viewer needs.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

`resolveAgentRuntimeMetadataPluginIds` adds every installed plugin that declares `startup.agentHarnesses` to every agent-runtime load plan, whether or not any agent selects that harness runtime. With the official `codex` plugin installed and enabled but no agent using the codex runtime, each embedded agent turn spawned a short-lived compute worker that captured the codex plugin's npm project (including `node_modules`, about 0.9 GB / about 14k files). Gateway CPU sat at 125-170% of one core. Disabling only the unused `codex` plugin brought it down to 28-71%.

The capture cost itself (no content-keyed reuse) is tracked in #157989 and #160959. This report covers the separate selection defect: a plugin that the selected runtime does not need should not be loaded or captured at all. The same function is unchanged on `main` today (`src/agents/harness/runtime-plugin-load-plan.ts`, lines 116-121).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install openclaw 2026.9.9 (npm global) on Windows and install the official `codex` plugin (`plugins.entries.codex.enabled: true`, `codex` in `plugins.allow`).
2. Do not configure any agent to use the codex harness. Every agent runs on the default runtime with a plain provider model.
3. Start the Gateway and let a few ordinary agent turns run from a chat channel.
4. Watch `<stateDir>/tmp/plugin-captures/` and per-thread file activity of the Gateway process.
5. Set `plugins.entries.codex.enabled: false`, remove `codex` from `plugins.allow`, restart, and repeat step 3.

### Expected behavior

An installed harness plugin is added to an agent-runtime load plan only when a selection or the configured harness policy resolves to that harness runtime. An agent turn on the default runtime does not load, capture, or hash the codex plugin.

### Actual behavior

- Each embedded agent turn reached the `runtime_plugins` milestone and spawned a compute worker. Worker spawn times matched new entries under `<stateDir>/tmp/plugin-captures/` one for one. Startup and config reload produce the same pattern.
- A thread-level file trace of one worker (3.0 s window, 4 MiB cap reached) recorded **9,161 file opens**. All of them were under `<stateDir>/npm/projects/<codex plugin project>/...` (about 5.1k directories, 1.4k `.js`, 0.9k `.mts`, 0.9k `.mjs`, plus `.md`/`.json`) or `<stateDir>/tmp/plugin-captures/`.
- The codex plugin npm project is at least 0.9 GB and about 14k files per generation. No agent used it.
- Gateway CPU, sampled in 30 s windows 17-19 min after boot: **125-170% of one core**, 6.5k-13.5k read ops/s, 24-51 MB/s read.
- With only the codex plugin disabled (otherwise the same config), a trace of a worker after restart showed **0** opens under the codex project. CPU fell to **28-71% of one core** (4 x 30 s samples). An agent turn then completed normally on the default runtime.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.9 (npm global). Source on `main` checked 2026-10-17: the same unconditional loop is still present.

### Operating system

Windows 11 Pro (x64), 8 cores / 16 logical CPUs

### Install method

npm global; Node v24.18.0; Gateway run as a background service

### Model

Not specific to a model. The turns ran on ordinary provider models via the default (non-harness) runtime.

### Provider / routing chain

Default embedded runtime -> ordinary provider plugins. No agent selects the codex harness runtime.

### Additional provider/model setup details

`plugins.allow` includes `codex` plus the provider and channel plugins. No `agents.*.runtime` / harness setting is configured anywhere.

### Logs

```text
(per-turn sequence, timestamps relative)
+0.0 s   embedded run milestone runtime_plugins
+0.0 s   compute worker thread created
+0.1 s   new <stateDir>/tmp/plugin-captures/<instance>/captures/... directory
+0-3 s   worker: 9,161 file opens under <stateDir>/npm/projects/<codex plugin project>/node_modules/...
+0.5 s   embedded run milestone attempt_dispatch
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Source pointers (installed 2026.9.9 dist; same logic on `main`):

- `<openclaw-dist>/runtime-plugin-load-plan-*.mjs`, `resolveAgentRuntimeMetadataPluginIds` (lines 43-61):
  ```js
  const pluginIds = new Set();
  for (const plugin of params.index.plugins) if (plugin.startup.agentHarnesses.length) pluginIds.add(plugin.pluginId);
  ```
  This runs before, and independently of, the per-selection harness resolution further down (`resolveSelectedAgentHarnessRuntime` -> `lookup.addAgentHarnessOwners(pluginIds, runtimeIds)`). That later step already adds the right harness owner when a runtime is actually selected.
- `<openclaw-dist>/plugin-generation-artifact-*.mjs`, `createPluginSourceCapture` (lines 595-660) and `inspectDirectory(..., sourceDependencies)` (lines 708-758): every load in a new worker creates a fresh capture directory and walks/stats the package plus its dependency tree. Nothing is reused by source fingerprint across workers. (Capture cost: see #157989.)
- On `main`, #166310 already scopes the `isolated-completion` purpose to the selected runtime owners. The ordinary `agent` purpose still takes the unconditional loop above.

### Impact and severity

Affected: any installation with a harness plugin (`codex`, `acpx`, ...) installed but unused, on every agent turn.
Severity: high CPU/IO tax on the Gateway host. On a busy Windows host it starved other services, and an external health watchdog had to recycle the Gateway.
Frequency: every agent turn, plus startup and config reload.
Consequence: a harness plugin that a user installed but does not use adds about 1 core of continuous load. The only workaround is to disable or uninstall it.

### Additional information

Suggested fixes, in order of leverage:

1. **Include harness plugins only when needed.** Drop the unconditional `agentHarnesses` loop from the `agent` purpose. Rely on the existing `resolveSelectedAgentHarnessRuntime` / `addAgentHarnessOwners` path, plus configured harness runtimes (`collectConfiguredAgentHarnessRuntimes`), to add only the owners of runtimes that are actually selected or configured. #166310 already does this for `isolated-completion`.
2. **Cache captures by source fingerprint.** Key a capture on the plugin package and dependency-tree identity, which `inspectDirectory` already computes for `pluginNativeNamespaceIsCurrent`. Then a new worker for an unchanged plugin reuses the existing capture instead of re-walking and re-copying it (overlaps #157989).

Workaround: disable unused harness plugins (`plugins.entries.<id>.enabled: false` and remove them from `plugins.allow`).

issues.body:
## Problem

A deployment may use native hosted search for ordinary interactive conversations, but require a specific managed search provider for an isolated scheduled workflow. For example, a daily news job needs the date controls of its managed provider without forcing all interactive conversations to use that provider.

The current isolated `agentTurn` payload can override the model, thinking level and tool allowlist, but not the web-search provider. Temporarily changing the global provider around a scheduled execution is unsafe when other conversations or jobs run concurrently.

## Proposed solution

Add an optional `payload.webSearchProvider` to isolated agent-turn jobs, with CLI set/clear support. An omitted field retains existing behavior. An explicit value pins only that invocation's managed search provider, including its credentials and the actual tool-execution path; it must not silently fall back to another provider.

The implementation should preserve global configuration and other conversations, respect disabled tools/plugins and sandbox/domain restrictions, and leave the job's prompt, schedule, model and delivery unchanged. Unsupported session targets should fail explicitly rather than ignoring the setting.

## Alternatives considered

- Changing the global provider before/after the job: cross-run races and failure recovery make this inappropriate.
- Asking the model to choose a provider in its prompt: the current tool surface does not provide that choice.
- A separate Gateway instance: operationally expensive for one per-job setting.

This is distinct from per-agent tool configuration (#37584): the same agent may own interactive conversations and isolated jobs with different search requirements.

A focused implementation is being validated against current main, with tests for set/clear/persistence, scoped execution, late binding, credentials and preservation of the global configuration. No live search calls or external deliveries are needed for those tests.

### Summary
In the Android app, an assistant reply that had already been delivered and was being read disappeared from the chat view. It was replaced by assistant messages that arrived from a different run a few seconds later. The gateway transcript still has every message in the right order (checked with `sessions_history`), so this looks like a client-side display problem, not message loss.

### Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.10.3 (59cb447), gateway on Linux
- Client: OpenClaw Android app (`openclaw-android`, mode `ui`) on a Pixel 9
- Single main session (`agent:main:main`, `session.dmScope=main`), runtime `claude-cli`

### What happened (timestamps 2026-10-17, America/Toronto)
1. 20:31:15 The user sends a question from the Android app.
2. 20:31:32 The main run replies (transcript seq 184, normal `cli-assistant:<runId>` idempotency key). The user starts reading it.
3. 20:32:32 A subagent spawned earlier by the same session (`sessions_spawn`, `completionTarget: "parent"`) finishes. It also calls the `message` tool, which records a `delivery-mirror` assistant message (seq 186, idempotency key `announce:v1:agent:main:subagent:<id>:<runId>:message-tool:...`).
4. 20:32:37 The parent's private completion turn produces its own assistant reply (seq 187, key `cli-assistant:announce:v1:...`).
5. In the app, the message from step 2 was no longer visible. The user saw it replaced by the newer message(s) while reading it.

### Expected
Messages from different runs append in order; an already rendered reply is never replaced or removed.

### Possibly related (separate issue?)
- The subagent had `completionTarget: "parent"`, but its `message` tool call still delivered to the user's current source. I expected results to go only to the parent.
- The parent's completion-turn reply (step 4) also reached the client, although it was internal reconciliation text.

### Repro idea
Spawn a hidden subagent with `completionTarget: "parent"` that calls `message(action=send)` near the end. Send a new user message and let the main run reply. Have the subagent finish within a few seconds of that reply, while the app is open on the conversation.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior / design flaw

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A spawned subagent that calls `sessions_yield` on its **first turn, with no children spawned and no pending wake source**, has its run finalized immediately with `status: "ok"` — the yield message becomes the entire "result" that is auto-announced to the requester. There is no guard, no warning, and nothing in the outcome marks the run as degenerate.

The tool description actively invites this misuse:

- `sessions_yield`: *"End current turn. Use after spawning subagents; results arrive as next message."*
- `subagents` tool: *"If sessions_yield exists, use it for completion; do not busy-poll wait loops."*
- Subagent context preamble: *"Results auto-announce to your requester; do not busy-poll for status."*

A model that wants to acknowledge a long-running task ("I'll start researching now") pattern-matches `sessions_yield` as a status/ack tool, calls it as its first action — and the run is over.

Related but distinct from #101862 (required-completion runs finalize as *blocked* on first-turn yield) and #100065 (direct session parks with no wake source). Here the run is a plain spawned subagent run, and the failure is *silent success with an empty deliverable*.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an orchestrator agent that can spawn a researcher-style subagent (`maxSpawnDepth: 2`, so the child is spawned as an orchestrator-capable role and keeps `sessions_yield`).
2. From a channel session, have the parent call `sessions_spawn` with a substantial research task.
3. The child model (observed with a Kimi K2-class model, but any model can fall into this) opens its turn with:
   ```
   sessions_yield({ "message": "Starting comprehensive research on <topic>. Will use multiple search strategies and synthesis." })
   ```
4. Observe the run.

Observed transcript of the child session (complete — this is everything that happened):

```
user       [Subagent Context] You are running as a subagent (depth 1/2). Results auto-announce
           to your requester; do not busy-poll for status. [Subagent Task] <large research task>
assistant  TOOL: sessions_yield {"message": "Starting comprehensive research on ..."}
toolResult {"status": "yielded", "message": "Starting comprehensive research on ..."}
```

`subagent_runs` outcome: `{"status":"ok","elapsedMs":7118}` — 7 seconds, ~32 output tokens.

### Expected behavior

One or more of:

- `sessions_yield` errors (or no-ops with a corrective message to the model) when the calling subagent run has **no pending children / no fresh wake source** — yielding with nothing to wait for can never be what the task intended;
- the run outcome is marked degenerate (e.g. `status: "yielded-empty"`) instead of `ok`, so the requester-side announce can say so;
- the tool descriptions distinguish "end turn to wait for spawned children" from "send a progress note" (and point to the correct mechanism for the latter), so models stop reaching for `yield` as an ack.

### Actual behavior

The run ends immediately with `status: "ok"`. The auto-announce delivers essentially nothing to the requester. The requester model has to detect the empty result heuristically (in our case it noticed "32 output tokens" and redid the research itself), and in a group-chat context this cost a full spawn round-trip plus a duplicated final answer when the late completion event triggered a second turn.

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.1-beta.6

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux 6.8.0-111-generic)

### Install method

npm (global), gateway managed via systemd user unit

### Model

kimi-for-coding (K2-class); failure mode is model-agnostic

### Provider / routing chain

n/a

### Additional provider/model setup details

n/a

### Logs

```
19:51:47 subagent run created  task_name=<research task>  spawn_mode=run
19:51:50 tool policy removed 3 tool(s) via subagent tools.deny: agents_list, session_status, sessions_send
19:51:55 subagent run ended    outcome={"status":"ok","elapsedMs":7118}
19:56:31 [agent] run announce:v1:agent:<child>:subagent:<id> ended with stopReason=stop
```

**Workaround:** add `sessions_yield` to `tools.subagents.tools.deny` — acceptable for leaf-style workers, but it also takes the tool away from legitimate orchestrator subagents, so it is a blunt instrument.
