issues.body:
## Summary

The nightly memory-core **"Memory Dreaming Promotion"** job runs heavy synchronous work (`node:sqlite` `DatabaseSync` + `writeFileSyncAtomic` + scoring) on the gateway's main thread. On our install this parks the event loop hard: healthz stops answering, log flushes stop, and every in-process protection (liveness monitor, lane timeouts, rescue crons) is starved along with it — they all share the loop they're supposed to protect.

Two eras, same mechanism:

- **State on FUSE-backed storage** (Unraid `/mnt/user` shfs bind): the park lasted **89–95 minutes** nightly.
- **State moved to native btrfs**: the same job still parks the loop **~3–6 minutes**, now purely CPU-bound + fsync. The filesystem only amplified; the synchronous work itself scales with store size.

Related open reports (different reproducers, same family): #78805 (sync I/O blocking), #85366 (startup sidecars saturate loop), #112698 (notification path starves main thread). This report adds a nightly in-product reproducer (memory-core dreaming), `/proc`-level evidence, and four concrete asks.

## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.7.1** (docker, `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw`, tini init)
- Host: Unraid 7.x; gateway state initially bind-mounted from `/mnt/user` (shfs/FUSE), later remounted to native btrfs — both reproduce, FUSE amplifies ~15-30×
- memory-core dreaming enabled (`0 3 * * *`), memory index ~1.9 GB sqlite

## Observed — era 1 (FUSE-backed state)

- The dreaming promotion cron failed to complete for 6+ consecutive nights (killed/interrupted every run). Worst case: event loop dark **03:05:38→04:34:54 (89 min, zero log lines)**.
- A custom heartbeat cron scheduled mid-window fired 25 minutes late into the stall and died to its own starved timers (its lane error reported 288883 ms = a 210 s timeout + 79 s of timer starvation).
- Liveness fingerprint while parked in syscalls: `eventLoopUtilization=1.0` with `cpuCoreRatio≈0.09`; boot phases `bootstrap-context` 60 s / `session-resource-loader` 56 s vs ~5 s / 2.5 s healthy.
- Recovery only ever came from an **external** `docker restart`. The container healthcheck went unhealthy but nothing acts on it (`unless-stopped` ignores health).

## Observed — era 2 (native btrfs, current)

Live `/proc` sampling during the park (5s cadence):

- main thread: state **R**, `wchan 0`, `/proc/<pid>/syscall` = `running` (one sample caught mid-`fsync` — consistent with synchronous sqlite commits); all worker threads idle in `epoll_wait`/`futex`.
- healthz: curl exit `000` (no HTTP response) for the entire window.
- The single liveness warning that ran *after* recovery reported `eventLoopDelayMaxMs=141733` while `eventLoopDelayP99Ms=1589` — the histogram percentile hides a solid park, so p99-based alerting misses it.
- Measured park lengths at ~2.7k-chunk store size: 2m54s+ (run killed externally), **5m50s** (allowed to finish; the run then completed successfully in 360 s total).

## Why in-process guards can't help (as shipped)

1. The liveness monitor (`emitDiagnosticLivenessWarning`) computes delay/ELU/cpuCoreRatio and **logs** — there is no action hook (self-exit, abort, callback).
2. Lane timeouts are `Promise.race` **abandonment** — the losing task/socket keeps running; nothing is aborted.
3. Model streams: callers pass no fetch timeout and `DEFAULT_UNDICI_STREAM_TIMEOUT_MS=1800000` is applied as a `Math.max` floor → streams are bounded at ≥30 min unless `model.requestTimeoutMs` is set — and the 2026.7.1 strict config schema **rejects** `requestTimeoutMs` inside `models[]` entries (attempting it crash-loops the gateway on boot).
4. After any restart, cron catch-up bursts (default `cron.maxConcurrentRuns=8`) pile more synchronous work onto a freshly booted loop, amplifying recurrence.

## Asks

1. **Liveness escalation option**: a configurable action when pathological thresholds hold (e.g. `eventLoopDelayP99 ≥ N` in M-of-K samples → self-exit with a marker file, or a user hook). The monitor already computes everything needed.
2. **Abort propagation** for lane timeouts — abort the underlying task/socket instead of abandoning the promise.
3. **Move memory-core dreaming/promotion sync work off the main thread** (`worker_threads`), or make state I/O async. At minimum, document a hard requirement that gateway state must live on local/native filesystems — FUSE/network state dirs turn this class from minutes into hours.
4. **Post-restart cron catch-up throttle/jitter.**

## Workarounds we run today (happy to share)

- External host watchdog: healthz + deep-RPC probes, forensics-first, budgeted `docker restart`, plus an evidence-gated defer while a dreaming run is active (so the bounded ~3–6 min park isn't treated as a terminal wedge).
- Local dist patches: default 300 s deadline on cloud model fetches (local inference exempt); an observe-mode liveness-escalation scaffold with a pre-spawned kill helper; preflight probe single-flight + 60 s negative TTL.
- State moved off FUSE to native btrfs.

All numbers above are from live `/proc` sampling and container logs on a production install; full traces/thread dumps available on request.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add a durable, per-session way for an external orchestrator to declare that it owns retry/recovery, so OpenClaw does not independently restart-recover the same session.

### Problem to solve

Main-session restart recovery is deliberately automatic. OpenClaw already skips subagent, cron, and ACP sessions because another subsystem owns their lifecycle. An external orchestrator using the gateway `agent` / `agent.wait` APIs has the same ownership relationship, but cannot declare it.

This can create duplicate execution:

1. An orchestrator starts a gateway run and waits for it.
2. Its wait budget expires, so it marks the orchestration run terminal and may schedule a replacement.
3. The gateway restarts while the corresponding OpenClaw session is still recorded as running or interrupted.
4. OpenClaw automatically resumes that session while the orchestrator independently runs its replacement.

The resumed request is invisible in the orchestrator's live-run dashboard. It still consumes model capacity and can repeat tools or external effects.

In one observed Docker/Kubernetes deployment, the orchestrator reported 4 live agents while the model server had 10 requests (4 running, 6 waiting). Four of those requests belonged to orchestration runs already recorded as timed out; they had been resumed outside the orchestrator's retry policy. The remaining two were legitimate non-orchestrator work. This request amplification caused queueing and further timeouts.

### Proposed solution

Add a persisted recovery-ownership field accepted by the gateway `agent` RPC, for example:

```json
{
  "restartRecoveryOwner": "external"
}
```

or equivalently:

```json
{
  "recoverOnGatewayRestart": false
}
```

Desired semantics:

- Persist the setting in the session entry; it must survive the gateway process.
- Default to existing OpenClaw-owned recovery behavior for backward compatibility.
- Skip externally owned sessions in startup-orphan marking, stale-lock marking, and recovery dispatch.
- Report the skip reason in restart-recovery telemetry/logging.
- Do not infer ownership only from a session-key naming convention.

Suggested regression coverage:

1. A normal interrupted Telegram/main session is still recovered.
2. An otherwise identical externally owned session is not marked or resumed.
3. Restarting twice remains idempotent and never creates a recovery task for the externally owned session.
4. Changing unrelated session metadata does not erase the ownership marker.

### Alternatives considered

- **Hard-coded session-key prefix:** resolves one integration but is brittle and not a general ownership contract.
- **Disable restart recovery globally:** prevents legitimate channel recovery.
- **Require the external orchestrator to abort first:** still races with forced restarts and process loss.
- **Dedupe after recovery:** the duplicate has already consumed model capacity and may have executed tools.

### Impact

- **Affected:** external schedulers and agent control planes using OpenClaw gateway sessions while maintaining their own timeout/retry state.
- **Severity:** high for sustained workloads; duplicate calls can saturate model concurrency and create a timeout feedback loop.
- **Frequency:** occurs whenever a still-running externally owned session overlaps a gateway restart and the external owner retries.
- **Consequence:** hidden inference load, delayed legitimate work, duplicate tool execution, and disagreement between control-plane and gateway status.

### Evidence/examples

- OpenClaw restart-recovery documentation says recovery is automatic and identifies subagents, cron, and ACP-managed sessions as excluded because another owner handles them: https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/restart-recovery
- Related cross-owner lifecycle discussion: #117052.
- Related explicit-abort/recovery confusion: #120315.
- The complementary Paperclip client-side timeout/abort problem is tracked in paperclipai/paperclip#3305; closed PR paperclipai/paperclip#4681 attempted remote cancellation. Client-side cancellation does not replace an OpenClaw-side ownership contract because restart/process-loss races remain.

As a bounded operational workaround, we added `sessionKey.includes(":paperclip:run:")` to `shouldSkipMainRecovery`. After one restart and stale-task reconciliation, OpenClaw running tasks matched orchestrator live run IDs 3:3, and model-server load settled to 2 running / 0 waiting (the third agent was doing tool work). The requested upstream solution is the general persisted ownership field, not that product-specific prefix.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance on the preferred gateway API and persisted session-field shape.

### Additional information

Observed on OpenClaw 2026.6.34, Docker on Linux arm64. The current behavior is documented, so this is framed as a missing integration contract rather than a regression.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug / upgrade-safety defect

### Summary

`openclaw update status` reports that a core update is available without evaluating whether the **plugins actually configured or active on the local installation** can be resolved compatibly for the candidate core version. It also does not disclose whether applying the candidate will perform forward-only configuration or database migrations.

This means an operator can be encouraged to update a healthy installation even when:

- required official/externalized plugin artifacts do not exist for the target release or channel;
- the only resolvable plugin artifact belongs to an older release cohort;
- the target changes plugin-owned configuration schemas;
- the target performs migrations that make a straightforward binary downgrade impossible.

The `2026.7.2-beta.7` → `2026.8.1-beta.1` incident demonstrated the consequence: core replacement and Doctor ran, the updater printed `Update Result: OK`, and only the post-core plugin phase exposed an incompatible/incomplete release cohort. The managed Gateway had already been stopped and the installation had crossed configuration/database migration boundaries.

Issue #121675 addresses the immediate beta.1 publication/convergence failure on current `main`, but not this missing **read-only, installation-specific preflight**.

### Current-main source evidence

Current `main` still implements `openclaw update status` as a core update check only:

- it reads the local config for `update.channel`;
- it calls `checkUpdateStatus(...)` for core/source/registry availability;
- its human-readable rows are only `Install`, `Channel`, optional `Git`, and `Update`;
- it does not load the active plugin inventory, resolve configured official plugin specs for the candidate, or inspect migration risk.

Source:

- [`src/cli/update-cli/status.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/cli/update-cli/status.ts)

### Environment from the incident

- Previous core: `2026.7.2-beta.7`
- Candidate/applied core: `2026.8.1-beta.1` (`ff8a3fe`)
- OS: Debian/Linux, systemd user service
- Node: `24.18.0`
- Install: global npm under the user prefix
- Configured/active plugin paths included Codex, WhatsApp, and `diffs`

### Observed update sequence

The updater stopped the working service before mutating the installation:

```console
Stopping managed gateway service before package update...
Stopped systemd service: openclaw-gateway.service
```

It then reported the core transition as successful:

```console
Update Result: OK
  Root: ~/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw
  Before: 2026.7.2-beta.7
  After: 2026.8.1-beta.1
```

Only in the subsequent plugin phase did the release-cohort mismatch become visible. For example, ClawHub still resolved `diffs` to the previous beta cohort:

```console
Resolving clawhub:@openclaw/diffs@beta…
  Package   @openclaw/diffs@2026.7.2-beta.7
  Requires  pluginApi >=2026.7.2-beta.7 · minGateway >=2026.4.30
```

The plugin/config convergence then failed:

```console
Installing @openclaw/whatsapp@beta ...
Error: Config validation failed: channels.whatsapp: invalid config for plugin whatsapp:
must not have additional properties: "debounceMs"
```

Afterwards, status showed an unreachable Gateway while claiming no plugin compatibility problem:

```console
Gateway              ... unreachable (connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:18789)
Gateway service      systemd user installed · enabled · running
Plugin compatibility none
```

The broader missing-companion-package condition for this release is documented in #121675. That report also documents the forward-only config/database changes that complicated rollback.

I did not retain the literal pre-update `openclaw update status` output for this host. The current-main implementation above establishes directly that this command has no configured-plugin or migration-risk preflight to report.

### Reproduction shape

1. Start with a working OpenClaw installation on release cohort A.
2. Enable/configure one or more externalized official plugins, for example `codex`, `whatsapp`, or another `@openclaw/*` package.
3. Publish or select core release B while at least one locally required plugin:
   - has no artifact for B;
   - resolves through the selected channel to A;
   - or has a config schema incompatible with the current authored config.
4. Make release B include a forward-only config or SQLite migration.
5. Run:

   ```console
   openclaw update status --json
   ```

6. Observe that it reports core update availability but no local plugin-cohort incompatibility and no migration/rollback warning.
7. Run `openclaw update`; the service and state may be mutated before plugin convergence fails.

### Expected behavior

`openclaw update status`, preferably through the same preflight used by `openclaw update`, should resolve an **installation-specific candidate plan** before the Gateway is stopped or state is mutated.

For each configured, enabled, slotted, or otherwise required official/version-bound plugin, report at least:

- plugin ID and package/source;
- currently installed version/spec;
- version/spec selected for the candidate core/channel;
- artifact availability;
- declared `pluginApi` and `minGateway` compatibility;
- result: `exact`, `compatible`, `fallback`, `unavailable`, `incompatible`, or `unknown`;
- an actionable repair or exclusion path where possible.

It should also report candidate migration risk, for example:

- no state migration;
- additive/backward-compatible migration;
- forward-only config migration;
- forward-only database migration;
- rollback support available/unavailable/unknown.

A possible human-readable result:

```text
Target core: 2026.8.1-beta.1

Configured plugin compatibility:
  codex       unavailable for target
  whatsapp    unavailable for target
  diffs       channel resolves to 2026.7.2-beta.7

Migration risk:
  config: forward-only
  agent database: downgrade unsupported

Assessment: unsafe to update
```

The JSON form should expose a stable machine-readable equivalent, including an overall result such as:

```json
{
  "safeToUpdate": false,
  "blockingReasons": [
    "required_plugin_unavailable",
    "forward_only_migration_without_rollback"
  ]
}
```

### Update behavior

When a required plugin cannot be resolved and the transition is irreversible or rollback-unsafe, `openclaw update` should abort **before stopping the Gateway or writing state**, unless the operator supplies an explicit risk-acceptance option.

This is separate from whether startup later quarantines an unavailable plugin. Quarantine limits the outage after an unsafe update; it does not make the pre-update decision truthful.

### Related issues

- #121675 — exact beta.1 missing-companion-package and convergence incident; release/startup behavior fixed on `main`, but no `update status` preflight requirement.
- #83337 — canonical open issue for post-upgrade core/plugin drift and pin policy; diagnostics occur after drift exists.
- #17215 — broad proposal for a pre/post-update compatibility scanner, without the concrete candidate-plugin resolution contract.
- #121002 — notes that current CLI update status exposes channel/config/source/update availability, while effective target/version provenance needs a defined contract.
- #14526 — safer update proposal with backup, health checks, and rollback.

This report is narrower: **before mutation, tell the operator whether this specific candidate can support the plugins this installation actually uses, and whether retreat remains possible.**

_AI-assisted investigation and drafting; reviewed by the human reporter._

issues.body:
## Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

Feishu inbound `mentionTargets` are automatically attached to ordinary and error replies again after #93522, reintroducing the multi-bot mention cascade previously fixed by #71396.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use a Feishu group with the OpenClaw bot and at least one other mentioned user or bot.
2. Send a message that mentions both OpenClaw and the other participant.
3. Let OpenClaw send an ordinary final reply or an error/fallback reply whose generated text contains no mention of that participant.
4. Observe that the outbound Feishu message still contains a native `at` element for the other participant.

A deterministic unit-level reproduction is to create the Feishu reply dispatcher with inbound `mentionTargets`, deliver a plain `final` error payload, and inspect the first `sendMessageFeishu` call: it receives `mentions` even though the outbound body did not request them.

## Expected behavior

Inbound mentions should remain contextual metadata only. Ordinary, final, error, fallback, block, card, and streaming replies should not automatically mention other inbound targets.

Explicit outbound mentions, including caller-provided `mentions` and `<at user_id="...">...</at>` rendering, should continue to produce native Feishu `at` elements.

This was the behavior restored by #71396 / commit `43ea5c3e6fe8fe7a25a4ea8fc2ae256fd97f5289` for #70065.

## Actual behavior

PR #93522 / commit `e46bcb834faa94aac4f038c5f69cf0ab26533874` passed inbound `ctx.mentionTargets` back into `createFeishuReplyDispatcher`. The dispatcher then adds those targets to the first final reply or first independently sent block.

As a result, normal replies and terminal error messages can unexpectedly notify every user or bot mentioned in the inbound message. In multi-agent groups this can trigger an unintended reply cascade.

## OpenClaw version

2026.7.1 and current `main` as checked on August 11, 2026

## Operating system

Linux 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2

## Install method

Source checkout, built with pnpm, Gateway launched through a systemd user service

## Model

Model-independent; observed with `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`

## Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw direct model route; the bug is in the Feishu outbound dispatcher and does not depend on the model provider

## Additional provider/model setup details

No provider-specific setup is required to reproduce the dispatcher behavior.

## Logs

```shell
# Regression-introducing data flow
bot.ts:                         mentionTargets: ctx.mentionTargets
reply-dispatcher.ts (final):    mentions: mentionTargets
reply-dispatcher.ts (block):    mentions: mentionTargets
```

## Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- Original report: #70065
- Original fix: #71396 / `43ea5c3e6fe8fe7a25a4ea8fc2ae256fd97f5289`
- Regression: #93522 / `e46bcb834faa94aac4f038c5f69cf0ab26533874`
- The regression commit also replaced the earlier "does not attach automatic mentions" test expectation with an expectation that forwards inbound mentions.

## Impact and severity

- Affected: Feishu group chats, especially multi-bot or multi-agent groups where one inbound message mentions several participants.
- Severity: High in multi-agent groups; terminal error or fallback replies can wake multiple agents and create a cascade.
- Frequency: Deterministic whenever the dispatcher receives non-empty inbound `mentionTargets` and sends the affected first final/block reply path.
- Consequence: Unrequested notifications, unnecessary agent runs, extra model usage, and noisy multi-agent reply chains.

## Additional information

Last known good behavior: #71396, merged May 9, 2026.

Regression introduced: #93522, merged June 16, 2026.

The rendering improvement from #93522 should be preserved. The fix only needs to stop feeding inbound `ctx.mentionTargets` into the reply dispatcher; explicit outbound/native mention rendering remains available through the existing send path.

issues.body:
## Summary

`sessions.patch` silently drops `toolOverrides.webSearch: true` during normalize, so a session-level **enable** override cannot persist. `webSearch: false` already persists, and sibling boolean maps (`skills`, `mcpServers`) already keep `true`.

## Actual

Patching:

```json
{ "key": "agent:main:main", "toolOverrides": { "webSearch": true, "skills": { "docs": true } } }
```

succeeds, but the stored entry keeps `skills.docs: true` and **omits** `webSearch`. A lone `{ "webSearch": true }` normalizes to an empty overlay (`undefined`).

## Expected

`typeof webSearch === "boolean"` values persist (both `true` and `false`), matching `skills` / `mcpServers` boolean-map behavior. Control UI already emits `webSearch: true` when the global base is off (`nextWebSearchToolOverrides(..., true, false)`).

## Anchors (pre-fix)

- `src/gateway/sessions-patch.ts` `normalizeSessionToolOverrides`: previously `raw.webSearch === false ? { webSearch: false } : {}`
- Schema allows boolean: `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/sessions-row.ts` (`SessionToolOverridesSchema.webSearch`)
- UI intent: `ui/src/lib/sessions/tool-overrides.ts` (`nextWebSearchToolOverrides`)

## Impact

When `tools.web.search.enabled` is false (or the composer base is off), toggling web search **on** for one session appears to succeed over RPC but does not stick on read-back. Deny (`false`) works; enable (`true`) is a silent no-op.

## Repro

1. Call `sessions.patch` with `toolOverrides: { webSearch: true }`.
2. Read the session entry / list row.
3. Observe `toolOverrides.webSearch` missing (or entire overlay absent).

## Notes

Out of scope for this issue: whether the agent runtime honors a persisted `webSearch: true` against a global config disable (separate follow-up). This tracks **persistence/normalize** only.

issues.body:
**Title:** Session archival state is unrepresentable in the CLI and indistinguishable from a default filter in the tool
**Reported by:** Chief (fleet coordination), with reproduction by Nexus
**Date:** 2026-10-17
**Severity:** Medium (misdiagnosis risk, no data loss)
**Status:** Ready-to-File
**External URL:**

## Summary

Three surfaces expose session state, and none of them can tell a consumer whether a session is
archived:

1. `openclaw sessions --json` emits **no archival field at all**, and recognises **no
   `--archived` option**.
2. `sessions_list` **does** carry a correct boolean `archived`, but only when the caller already
   knows to ask for `archived: true` — and that mode returns archived rows **only**, never both.
   Its own description promises `archived=all`, which the schema cannot express.
3. The `/new` remedy for an archived key is refused with `INVALID_REQUEST`, i.e. the error text
   names an action that cannot succeed.

The practical effect: a consumer filtering `archived === false` cannot distinguish "this session
is live" from "this session was archived and removed before serialisation".

## Environment

- OS: Linux 6.18.54.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2, host `XPS15-9520`
- OpenClaw 2026.10.10-beta.1 (87175a8)
- Affected components: `sessions` CLI serializer, `sessions_list` tool, session archive handling

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Establish what the CLI emits:

```bash
openclaw sessions --all-agents --json > /tmp/s.json
grep -c '"archived"'       /tmp/s.json   # 0
grep -c 'archivedAt'       /tmp/s.json   # 0
grep -c 'archived_at'      /tmp/s.json   # 0
grep -ci 'archiv'          /tmp/s.json   # 0
python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('/tmp/s.json'));print(len(d['sessions']))"  # 71
```

2. Ask the CLI for archived rows:

```bash
openclaw sessions --agent hal --json --archived true
# OpenClaw does not recognize option "--archived".
```

3. Compare the two `sessions_list` modes for an agent with one archived main:

```
sessions_list(agentId="nexus")                 -> count 4, agent:nexus:main ABSENT,
                                                  archived:false on every row
sessions_list(agentId="nexus", archived=true)  -> count 1, agent:nexus:main PRESENT,
                                                  archived:true
```

4. Ask for the documented union:

```
sessions_list(agentId="hal", archived="all")
# rejected: schema types `archived` as boolean, but description says
# "archived=all includes active and archived rows"
```

5. Attempt the advertised recovery on an archived key:

```
/new  -> INVALID_REQUEST ... "ended during restart recovery"
```

## Expected Result

- Every emitted row carries a boolean archival state, in every mode, in both surfaces.
- The population is stated: active-only, archived-only, or all.
- A documented union mode exists and is expressible in the schema.
- A remedy offered in an error message is actionable, or the message does not offer one.

## Actual Result

- CLI: field absent entirely (0 hits across 71 rows / ~86 KB). Absence is indistinguishable from
  `null` to any consumer using `.get()` / optional chaining — a JSON-key-existence check is
  required to tell them apart, and no consumer does that.
- CLI: no flag exists to request archived rows.
- Tool: correct boolean, but the default silently excludes archived rows and the payload reports
  only `count`, never which population produced it. `archived=true` is a partition rather than a
  union, so "all" is unreachable.
- Tool: `archived:"all"` fails schema validation while the description advertises it.
- Remedy string advises `/new` or `/reset` for a condition neither can clear.

## Root Cause (if known)

Two independent serializers (CLI and tool) over the same store, with different field sets: the
tool has the concept, the CLI does not. Because the tool's default is a filter, its `false` is
the filter's complement restated, not a measurement of the row.

## Impact

Fleet monitoring produced four mutually inconsistent answers within one hour — "0 dead lanes",
"4 rolled over", "6 rolled over", and "one archived key visible, one vanished" — each defensible
from the surface used. Any operator or agent reasoning about lane health from these projections
will misdiagnose. No data loss.

## Proposed Fix (if known)

1. Emit `archived: <boolean>` on every row in **both** serializers; make `null`/absence invalid.
2. Add an explicit population selector: `active | archived | all`, defaulting to `active`, and
   echo the resolved population in the payload alongside `count`.
3. Add `--archived`/`--all` to the CLI (currently unrecognised).
4. One serializer shared by CLI and tool.
5. Stop offering `/new` or `/reset` as a remedy for an archived key, or make one of them work.

Acceptance test (falsifiable, per-line):

```
1. agent:hal:main has archived_at set        -> CLI emits archived:true
2. same row in sessions_list(archived=all)   -> PRESENT with archived:true
3. an active row                             -> archived:false in both
4. payloads declare population and count
5. sessions_list(archived=all) returns union, not partition
```

Note on test design: an assertion of the shape `(.archived|type)=="boolean"` **passes** a
serializer that emits `false` only on surviving rows. It must be `has("archived") and type ==
"boolean"`, and line 5 is what prevents the partition/union confusion.

## Workaround (if any)

Read the session store directly for archival state (`archived_at`), and treat any projection as
advisory. Never infer "not archived" from a missing or false field.

## Related Issues

Internal: T-NEXUS-016 (requirement, `c04fd90d`), T-CHIEF-008 (ruling).

## Attachments

Reproduction script and acceptance test held with Nexus; durable copy at
`life/team-comms/requests/to-chief-2026-10-17-r6-and-archived-at-column.md`.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After a parent yields for required subagents, an explicit parent `NO_REPLY` is retried as missing output while the child Task can be credited before requester settlement finishes.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start OpenClaw 2026.8.1 from commit `d60a5f7dd41e7ffcc5bebc8b9361a12a8c0172fe` with an ephemeral QA Gateway and deterministic OpenAI-compatible mock provider.
2. Have a parent call `sessions_spawn` for a required child and then `sessions_yield`.
3. Let the child finish, resume the parent through the requester-settle wake, and return the exact token `NO_REPLY` from that resumed parent turn.
4. Observe that the requester settlement reports `visible_reply_missing` and retries even though the parent made an explicit intentional-quiet decision.
5. Exhaust requester settlement and observe that child delivery can already be credited before the requester result is resolved.

### Expected behavior

The yielded requester owns completion. One parent-authored visible final or the exact parent token `NO_REPLY` should settle the existing requester wake exactly once. Missing or empty output should remain failure. Requester settlement failure should project through the existing Task delivery failure/blocked state, and requester-owned completion should never raw-send child output.

### Actual behavior

The yielded requester wake forces a visible reply, so exact parent `NO_REPLY` becomes `visible_reply_missing`. The redundant child announcement can also credit delivery before requester settlement has produced either a visible final or explicit intentional silence. Exhausted requester settlement can therefore lose truthful blocked state.

### OpenClaw version

2026.8.1 (`d60a5f7dd41e7ffcc5bebc8b9361a12a8c0172fe`)

### Operating system

macOS 26.2 (arm64)

### Install method

Full source checkout; `pnpm` development build; ephemeral QA Gateway

### Model

Deterministic OpenAI-compatible mock provider

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw ephemeral QA Gateway -> local mock OpenAI-compatible provider

### Additional provider/model setup details

No external model or user channel is required for the deterministic reproduction.

### Logs

```shell
requester settlement: visible_reply_missing
child delivery: credited before requester settlement resolves
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Current source documents that the parent decides whether an update is needed, but requester settlement passes `requireVisibleReply: true`. Existing requester-settle tests reproduce the retry behavior. A focused fix adds deterministic unit, lifecycle, restart/race, and ephemeral Gateway QA coverage for quiet, worthy, missing-output, and failed-handoff paths.

### Impact and severity

Affected: users of required subagent work that yields back to a parent requester.

Severity: high for background work, because intentional quiet can retry or leak an unwanted completion; high for failure handling, because a failed parent handoff can be credited prematurely.

Frequency: deterministic whenever the yielded parent explicitly returns `NO_REPLY` under the current requester-settle contract.

Consequence: unwanted user-facing output, misleading Task delivery state, or a completion failure that is not truthfully blocked.

### Additional information

Related work: #118584, #118703, #119463, #119696, #120453, #120538, #90944, #111647, #117823, and #118631. This report does not add a parallel lifecycle; it narrows the existing requester-settle outbox and native Task delivery projection.

issues.body:
### Summary

In `memory-core` dreaming, the deep-sleep ranker and the promotion applier disagree about candidate eligibility, and nothing surfaces the disagreement. The ranker nominates candidates the applier is structurally guaranteed to refuse, so the nightly report reads `Ranked N candidate(s) ... Promoted 0` indefinitely while appearing to be working.

On my workspace this ran for weeks: 9–10 candidates ranked every night, 0 promoted, no warning anywhere.

### Root cause

**The ranker performs no provenance check; the applier does.**

`extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion-apply.ts:295` rejects any candidate whose `provenance.originClass` is `untrusted` or `system`:

```ts
if (isPromotionOriginBlocked(candidate)) {
```

`extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion.ts` — `rankShortTermPromotionCandidates` — never references `isPromotionOriginBlocked` or `originClass` at all. So untrusted-origin entries are ranked, counted, and reported as candidates, then silently dropped at apply time.

**Secondary, same area:** the two functions call the same contamination helper with different arguments.

- ranker, `short-term-promotion.ts:130` — passes the flag, deliberately admitting raw transcript turns from session-corpus paths:
  ```ts
  isContaminatedDreamingSnippet(entry.snippet, {
    allowTranscriptTurnSnippet: isShortTermSessionCorpusPath(entry.path),
  })
  ```
- applier, `short-term-promotion-apply.ts:301` — omits it, so those same snippets are contaminated:
  ```ts
  if (isContaminatedDreamingSnippet(candidate.snippet)) {
  ```

The ranker is written to *include* exactly the class of snippet the applier unconditionally *excludes*.

### Why it becomes self-sustaining

`signalCount = recallCount + dailyCount + groundedCount`. In my main workspace the totals across 512 entries were `recallCount=21`, `dailyCount=656`, `groundedCount=0` — about 97% of all signal is `dailyCount`, which increments merely because the daily sweep re-read the file a line sits in.

The text that benefits most is `memory/.dreams/session-corpus/*.txt`. Those held 328 of 512 slots (64%) at `dailyCount=11`, while genuine memories sat at 1. Because the store is capped at 512 and high-count entries survive eviction, the unpromotable content crowded out everything promotable. The store sealed itself: the only entries able to persist were entries that could never be promoted.

All ten candidates from one night, with the gate each died at:

```
1-8. memory/.dreams/session-corpus/2026-07-28.txt, 2026-07-29.txt
     sig=11 (all dailyCount) recalls=0
     rejected: originClass=untrusted + transcript-turn
9.   memory/2026-07-24.md   rejected: already promoted
10.  memory/2026-08-04.md   rejected: already promoted
```

### Suggested fix

1. Apply the same origin check in the ranker that the applier uses, so ineligible entries are never nominated.
2. Make the contamination call consistent between ranker and applier — whichever way is intended.
3. Report the gap. When `ranked > 0 && applied === 0`, the deep report should say why rather than printing two numbers that silently contradict each other. A per-gate rejection count in the report would have made this obvious on night one instead of after several weeks.

Separately, and possibly worth its own issue: `groundedCount` was `0` for all 3,154 entries across all eight workspaces on this machine. If that channel is expected to fire, it does not appear to.

### Environment

- OpenClaw `2026.7.2-beta.7`
- macOS 27.0 arm64, node v26.7.0
- `plugins.entries.memory-core.config.dreaming` enabled, no `phases` block, so deep-phase defaults apply (`minScore` 0.75, `minRecallCount` 3, `minUniqueQueries` 3)

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

OpenClaw sets the memory-flush threshold from a 1.05M-token context window, while Codex natively compacts at approximately 205k tokens, causing compaction before that threshold is reached.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run an OpenClaw agent using Codex with memory flush enabled and no agents.defaults.contextTokens override.
2. Continue the same session until Codex reaches its native compaction point (observed at ~205k tokens).
3. Inspect the logs: OpenClaw resolves contextWindow=1050000 and a ~1.026M-token flush threshold, while Codex compacts first.

### Expected behavior

OpenClaw should use an effective context window no larger than Codex’s runtime native compaction budget, so its memory flush is triggered before Codex performs context compaction.

### Actual behavior

In the observed session, Codex performed three native compactions while OpenClaw recorded only two memory-flush compactions. OpenClaw logged contextWindow=1050000 and threshold=1026000; after compaction, it logged tokenCount=60888 with forceFlushByTranscriptSize=true.

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.1-2 (0790d9f)

### Operating system

Kali GNU/Linux 2026.1, running under WSL2 (6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2)

### Install method

npm global

### Model

gpt-5.6-terra

### Provider / routing chain

OpenAI

### Additional provider/model setup details

The agent uses the default model routing: openai/gpt-5.6-terra as primary, with OpenAI-hosted fallbacks. Authentication is through an OpenAI OAuth profile.

The original observation occurred with no agents.defaults.contextTokens override, so OpenClaw resolved contextWindow=1050000. A current temporary mitigation sets agents.defaults.contextTokens to 210000, yielding an approximate flush threshold of 186000 tokens; this is a workaround, not a fix for native pre-compaction coordination.

### Logs

```shell
OpenClaw 2026.7.1-2 (0790d9f)
Model: openai/gpt-5.6-terra
Provider: OpenAI

contextWindow=1050000
threshold=1026000
tokenCount=60888
forceFlushByTranscriptSize=true
compactionCount=3
memoryFlushCompactionCount=2

The session metadata/logs indicate native Codex compaction at approximately 205k tokens, well below OpenClaw’s resolved 1.026M-token flush threshold.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

• Affected: The observed OpenClaw agent using openai/gpt-5.6-terra with memory flush enabled; potentially other Codex-backed agents where the catalog window exceeds the runtime compaction budget.
• Severity: Data/continuity risk. A native compaction can happen before OpenClaw persists a memory-flush summary.
• Frequency: Reproduced three times within the observed long-running session (compactionCount=3); broader frequency is not established.
• Consequence: Context that exists only in the raw transcript may not be captured by the memory-flush mechanism before native compaction, degrading continuity in long sessions.

### Additional information

This is not yet established as a regression: no last known-good or first known-bad version was observed. The correlation with the GPT-5.6 upgrade is plausible but confounded by the OpenClaw upgrade and managed app-server changes.

The contextTokens: 210000 override is a reversible mitigation only; it moves OpenClaw’s turn-start threshold to approximately 186k tokens but cannot guarantee a final flush if Codex compacts later in the same turn.

Requested fixes: runtime-aware context-window resolution, explicit logging of the resolved window/threshold sources, and supported pre-contextCompaction coordination so OpenClaw can flush durable memory before native compaction.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Gateway idle cleanup treats an existing retained npm marker as cleanup-eligible when the marker cannot be read or parsed, so it can delete package files that an explicit `plugins uninstall --keep-files` intended to preserve.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On current main, create a managed npm generation with a package under `node_modules`.
2. Leave its OpenClaw-owned `.openclaw-retained-npm-installs/*.json` marker truncated, malformed, or otherwise unreadable.
3. Run `cleanupRetainedManagedNpmInstallGenerations`, as Gateway idle cleanup does.
4. Observe that `markerPreservesPackageFiles` catches the read/parse error and returns `false`, after which cleanup removes the package/project root.

Source: `src/plugins/managed-npm-retention.ts:12-18`, legacy cleanup at `:161-175`, and generated-root cleanup at `:205-233` on `8fdf7570a17ffbbafe825bd379bab858f263b8ca`.

### Expected behavior

An existing marker whose intent cannot be classified must preserve its package files and report the read/parse failure through the existing cleanup `onError` callback. Only a valid marker with a known non-keep reason should make the package eligible for deletion.

### Actual behavior

Every marker read or JSON parse failure is converted to `false`. Both legacy and generated managed npm cleanup therefore proceed with deletion, while recovery treats marker existence as sufficient to suppress loading.

### OpenClaw version

Current main at `8fdf7570a17ffbbafe825bd379bab858f263b8ca` (source regression from merged PR #113902).

### Operating system

All supported platforms; the failure is in platform-independent filesystem cleanup logic.

### Install method

Source checkout / managed npm plugin install.

### Model

N/A

### Provider / routing chain

N/A

### Additional provider/model setup details

N/A

### Logs

```shell
Current classifier:
try { read + JSON.parse } catch { return false }
false -> cleanup removes the retained package/project root
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The durable ClawSweeper review on merged PR #113902 identifies this exact P2 and recommends preserving unreadable markers for both legacy and generated roots while retaining deletion for valid known non-keep reasons. Live duplicate searches for `managed npm marker cleanup unreadable`, `retained npm`, and `keep-files cleanup plugin` found no same-root open issue or PR.

### Impact and severity

Affected: users who explicitly retain managed npm plugin files and encounter a truncated/corrupt marker or marker read error.
Severity: medium data-loss risk for retained plugin package files.
Frequency: limited to marker corruption or filesystem read failures.
Consequence: Gateway cleanup can permanently remove files that the operator asked OpenClaw to keep.

### Additional information

Best fix is a tri-state marker classifier at the cleanup owner: valid keep marker -> preserve; valid known non-keep marker -> cleanup eligible; unreadable/malformed marker -> preserve and call `onError`. This is a narrow follow-up to #113902 and requires no config, protocol, SDK, or migration change.

issues.body:
### Summary
On 2026.10.3/2026.10.4 (npm-global, Linux systemd, macOS launchd, Windows Scheduled Task), `openclaw node install` writes a service that runs the **gateway entrypoint** `dist/index.js node run ...` instead of the package bin `openclaw.mjs`. Only `openclaw.mjs` / `dist/entry.js` call `runNodeHostLauncher`, and `startNodeHostAutoUpdate` only starts when `isNodeHostLauncherChild()` is true (runner: `announceLauncherReady`). So installed headless nodes **never self-update**, contradicting docs/install/updating/automatic-updates.md ("installed node services update automatically by default").

### Evidence
- `resolveNodeProgramArguments` → `resolveCliProgramArguments` → `buildDistCandidates`/`findFirstAccessibleGatewayEntrypoint` picks `dist/index.js` (schtasks-*.mjs in 10.4).
- 4 nodes (jetson, pi, mac-studio, windows) stayed on 2026.10.3 for ~10 h after 10.4 was latest; `nodeHost.autoUpdate.enabled=true`, no opt-out env.
- Reinstalling with the documented `OPENCLAW_WRAPPER=<path to openclaw bin>` makes the unit run `openclaw.mjs`; the launcher parent + child appear, and on the Pi the node self-activated 2026.10.4 within ~1 min (global CLI still 10.3).

### Second bug (Windows)
With `OPENCLAW_WRAPPER=%APPDATA%\npm\openclaw.cmd`, `openclaw node install --force` writes node.cmd correctly but then fails `Node install failed: AggregateError: spawn EINVAL` (Node refuses to spawn .cmd without shell) and "The previous service definition could not be restored"; the old node process keeps running until killed.

### Expected
`node install` should target the launcher entry (`openclaw.mjs`) by default so auto-update works out of the box; Windows install should not spawn .cmd without a shell.

Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164516

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes approved plugin tools refusing execution when runtime preparation captures a separate environment object.

## User Impact

Allow-once approval and tool execution retain the same plugin registration. Registration-local consent stays private and single-use; denied calls remain rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The prepared runtime owns its captured environment and plugin generation. Defaulting tool resolution to `process.env` discarded that generation through an identity mismatch. Resolve an omitted environment from the prepared load context first. Explicit caller overrides still take precedence.

No Agent System changes, shared consent store, or approval bypass. No live deployment yet.

## Evidence

Local validation below ran on `v2026.9.7` plus the fix. The branch was then aligned to `main` (`28a6f71449a`) with a history-preserving merge; its net diff is exactly the two reviewed files. Post-merge checks have not been rerun.

- Reproduced on `v2026.9.7`: the new approval-ownership regression fails with `Approval missing from this registration`; the same regression passes with the fix.
- Five focused resolver/hook/inspection suites: **162 tests passed**. Coverage includes allow-once consumption, denied calls, and explicit environment overrides.
- Single-worker regression cost: **3 cases passed in 12.30 s wall** using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/tools.prepared.test.ts --reporter=dot --maxWorkers=1`; most time was compiler/harness preparation. CI timing is not yet available.

prs.body:
Closes #175917

## What Problem This Solves

Supported Codex cloud-worker chats cannot start or resume core OpenClaw Goals, native tool filtering hides core Goal controls, and automatic Goal turns omit continuation accounting.

## User Impact

Operators can start and resume Goals on supported idle Codex cloud-worker sessions and use core Goal controls with native execution enabled. Normal deny/custom policies still apply. The continuation count includes the automatic turn that completes the objective; human Start/Resume do not increment it. No configuration or schema migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use existing placement, chat admission, transcript receipt, and follow-up completion owners. Keep input pending until worker setup admits it, commit the Goal/input/receipt together before success acknowledgment, and account each automatic turn against its original Goal identity. Codex’s separate autonomous Goal engine stays disabled. No provider-specific forwarding, private worker-auth dependency, alternate scheduler, persistent cache, or new authority owner is introduced.

Main already contains definitive busy-Resume classification before retry/reconciliation, intent retirement, and distinct later Resume; this PR preserves and freshly verifies that behavior.

## Evidence

The original port's 167-test/build evidence predates the review repairs. Current follow-up proof on the corrected source includes:

- 36 ordinary-chat pending-input tests, including the unchanged same-generation CI regression.
- 31 Goal cases and 30 pending-input owner cases: only typed Goal mutations opt into interrupted recovery; ordinary chat keeps its original default rejection.
- Production placement launcher and actual SQLite claims for allowed execution and claim revocation/reassignment at native COMMIT, proving no forbidden Goal activation, user-transcript write, or model execution.
- Four production-host sandbox Goal-control cases also preserve an existing paused Goal and configured custom allow/deny restrictions after a denied update.
- Owning core/Codex type graphs, six-file lint/format, diff checks, and fresh independent Auto Review of the complete corrected candidate pass.

External node/model I/O is simulated; no live worker provisioning is claimed. The persisted Goal contract remains schema version 1 and this PR introduces no Goal migration. Stored-state/custom-policy compatibility is tested, but an actual latest-stable old-binary-to-new-binary upgrade run has not been performed.

### Remaining before merge

Fresh hosted CI and review must complete on ccacd9fb053ad69630207e76a10af1160a655ca6. The earlier same-generation recovery regression and dispatch mock type error are repaired; previous failing runs are historical, not green evidence for this head. The reviewer's old-binary upgrade request remains distinct from the stored-state/policy compatibility proof above. No merge is requested while these items are unresolved.

prs.title: refactor(infra): share admission finish observation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Worker publication callers duplicate the same finish-callback chaining across approval, binding, and registry owners. Exact-head CI also exposed a concurrent same-owner worktree creation failure; the repair closes its pending-to-live observation gap without adding another contention mechanism.

## User Impact

Concurrent inferred-name creation for the same owner continues to reuse one managed worktree instead of intermittently rejecting a duplicate owner during publication. No operator action is required. Authorization, committed data, rollback, unknown-outcome handling, and public contracts remain unchanged; no schema or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Put the existing bound synchronous finish/`finally` decoration in the settlement owner and reuse it from six publication consumers. Their callback bodies, receiver binding, repeated invocation, nested order, later-error precedence, and consumer-specific once/authority/settlement guards stay intact. Unconditional per-database pending-receipt accounting remains unchanged.

This is an owner-plus-first-area split to keep CI attribution narrow: **7 net production lines removed** (+71/-78 across eight production files), with 57 net test lines added across the admission regression and strengthened existing worktree case. The original finish cleanup removed nine production lines; the bounded concurrency repair adds two.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None: this consolidates identical callback decoration. No guard, write settlement, failure fencing, or recovery behavior is removed.

## Evidence

### Current reviewed repair

Current signed head is `47a5200384abffbeaa422095e5b4b2d5c29b344d`, parent `84e97fbc22894696e501d3c86f200638d996ff82`, tree `19b1e1ebbaf02796df27eefa9af9ecdbe76f473f`. Root verified signature G, Peter as author and committer, clean task worktree, and exact identity with the fresh full-composition review. Normal guarded signing and hooks completed; hook formatting passed in 13ms on two files with one thread, without edits or bypass. The stable full-index patch SHA256 against base `7aab596ad005c15824143c482e9d6da732c6f102` is `911c0510e8abf4ed1cfd0cdfaafbbb0d416d2b645903b87be7bbc71a0b9cf7f9`. Abbreviated-index diff output has a different hash only because its ten index lines shorten blob IDs; all source bytes match.

The exact reviewed two-file repair was replayed in the qualified full checkout. Canonical type-aware lint passed with no diagnostics in 69.35s; formatting passed unchanged in 238ms, and diff checking passed. Changed-check dry run completed in 60.08s and selected the actual two changed files; its listed broad checks were not executed. Mandatory suppression policy ran once and passed all 14 cases (8524ms test time, 104.29s Vitest, 133.16s wall), including production inventory in 8414ms and the allowlist in 101ms. All proof processes completed naturally and drained. Logs: `/private/tmp/r01-b9-allocation-scoped-proof.ArS3RV/`. No retry, timeout/assertion/allowance/skip change, cold worker compiler, broad semantic graph, build, install, or new lease was used.

The repair was published with a lease pinned to prior head84; both the remote branch and PR were independently verified at exact `47a5200384abffbeaa422095e5b4b2d5c29b344d`, open and mergeable, with no retained auto-merge request or merge outcome. New exact-head hosted CI and native admission remain pending. The prior failure below remains a failure with unknown attribution; source review and policy/lint passes do not prove the new barrier regression executes or establish Node/Bun parity. Local baseline/fixed runtime proof remains unavailable for the specific worker-cache reason recorded below.

### Prior conflict-repaired head and CI failure

Prior signed head `84e97fbc22894696e501d3c86f200638d996ff82` has parent `7aab596ad005c15824143c482e9d6da732c6f102` and tree `48f16a86c2f364e8e23a5d37d8fdd22fac17d0e7`. Root verified signature G, Peter as author and committer, and its then-clean task worktree. This conflict-only rebase incorporates main's admission-fixture cleanup rather than restoring the superseded test helper. All seven original production outputs are byte-identical to original reviewed head `36d36477629080cc961c449be00416cbe218d1ee`; the conflict adaptation is confined to the admission regression's imports/context, raw `createAdmission`, four assertions and `finally` cleanup, preserving main's current fixtures. That head removed nine production lines with 26 test lines added; its results below are prior-head evidence, not proof for the new repair.

- Fresh scoped proof91964 completed naturally with exit 0 and full child/output drain at current head: changed-check dry-run, one-test-file formatting (133ms), `git diff --check`, and canonical type-aware lint of `src/infra/sqlite-worker-operation-admission.test.ts` passed. The dry-run only lists selected commands; it does not mean those listed checks, semantic types or runtime suites executed. Current-head one-file lint is distinct from the reusable original seven-production-file lint evidence below.
- The normal Node suppression-policy invocation ran once and passed all 14 cases: 2387ms test time, 42.01s Vitest and 70.38s wrapper. Its production inventory case passed in 2363ms; repeated reporter summaries count once. No retries, timeout/assertion/allowance/skip change or source/configuration edit. Original results below remain historical proof, not a substitute for this current failure. The only non-aggregate failure was job `117562319543`, `checks-node-changed-compact-large-12`: the existing worktree service case “reuses concurrent inferred names for the same owner” received “Managed worktree name or owner already has a live or pending checkout” (603ms). The repair captures pending slots before the live-owner lookup under the existing allocation lease, then carries the snapshot into the unchanged later collision decision. The existing service-level case now gates real publication and lookup to exercise that transition, preserving its three assertions. No worker protocol, schema, additional retry, fence or production test seam is added. This adds a pending read on the already-live reuse path but no additional read on new creation. The complete candidate removes seven net production lines, including the bounded CI repair rather than claiming the original nine-line cleanup unchanged.

Fresh full-composition review8494 completed scoped-clean at P0–P2 with no findings, confidence 0.94, one complete attempt, final source verification and full process drain. Root inspected actual structured status/report and human report. Exact two-file formatting passed in 17ms without edits; diff checking passed. The reviewed base-to-dirty patch SHA256 is `911c0510e8abf4ed1cfd0cdfaafbbb0d416d2b645903b87be7bbc71a0b9cf7f9`. These are source/static results, not regression execution.

Local baseline/fixed runtime reproduction remains unavailable under the no-cold-compiler budget: all six retained compiled-worker manifests include a different worktree-service input hash from both prior84 and the repair. The supported infra runner would therefore build the broad worker graph before running this case; no source-mode, setup bypass, cache mutation or new lease was used. The original failure's precise attribution remains unresolved. New repair lint and suppression policy have passed as recorded above; exact-head hosted runtime proof remains pending.

Actual current-head hosted proof and native admission remain pending. No current-head runtime owner-suite pass, full semantic compiler run, global graph/build pass, live Gateway result, deployment or new lease is claimed. Full build-artifacts was skipped in the historical run, not passed; future conditional build selection also requires an actual receipt rather than an envelope inference. The retained partial local install was not reconciled or used for a broad cold compiler/build run.

### Historical original-head evidence

The following evidence belongs to original signed `36d36477629080cc961c449be00416cbe218d1ee` and its recorded CI merge context. It is retained for attribution and unchanged-production proof reuse, not as fresh CI for `84e97fbc22894696e501d3c86f200638d996ff82`.

- Fresh independent P0–P2 full-owner review60424 of the actual eight-path reconstruction completed scoped-clean, no findings, confidence0.99. Root inspected the actual terminal status/report; one complete attempt, with complete changed owners, real admission/state publication/SQL context and six consumer suites. The earlier incomplete-context attempt was stopped without verdict, not counted as clean.
- Canonical formatting passed for the exact eight files (28ms, one thread), without source edits.

- Normal guarded hooks and signing completed at `36d36477629080cc961c449be00416cbe218d1ee`, with Peter as author and committer and verified G signature. Initial default-tooling-owner formatter mismatch refused before signing; the supported explicit qualified tooling-owner selector then passed the normal hook (72ms/eight files/one thread), without hook/signing bypass, dependency installation or source edits. The committed patch still exactly matches the reviewed source and the task worktree is clean.
- A bounded isolated Node26.12/normal repository TSX probe imported the ACTUAL production admission and settlement owners from the exact signed full checkout, and passed nested/repeated callback order, later-error identity, and actual admission closure. It used the real MessageChannel admission, no fake finish object, copied module, stub, setup bypass or database fixture. prs.title: fix(update): wait for state maintenance before git checkout
prs.body:
Closes #175913

## What Problem This Solves

A managed Git update could pass candidate validation, stop the serving Gateway, and then abort before `git-checkout` because the recovery-state guard met a transient `sqlite-maintenance` owner. The guard's synchronous state read raised the native offline-maintenance refusal, so an otherwise admitted update failed and the previous build had to be recovered.

`executeMutableUpdate` now performs the inspected-target guard read through the existing bounded state-read wrapper. A temporary maintenance owner is retried within the update deadline instead of aborting the update immediately. Live ownership, requester revocation, data-at-risk refusals, cancellation, and an expired deadline remain authoritative.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuse `withUpdateStateRead` around `recordInspectedGitTarget` and its execution-authority assertion, so only retryable state-read contention is retried.
- Bound the wait by the remaining update deadline, falling back to the existing update step timeout when no deadline is supplied.
- Keep the change inside the mutable Git execution path; do not bypass the guard, remove a live maintenance lease, or read through its exclusion.
- Preserve the existing behavior for real maintenance ownership, revocation, data-at-risk findings, and deadline exhaustion.

## User Impact

Managed Git updates no longer fail between admitted imports and checkout merely because state maintenance briefly holds the database. If the maintenance owner persists or the operation reaches its deadline, the update still fails safely under the existing policy and the prior build remains recoverable.

## Evidence

- Added a real-checkout regression through the production `executeMutableUpdate` and `updateGitInstall` path. A child process takes a real `acquireGatewayLock` lease with role `sqlite-maintenance`; the native recovery-state read is refused, the bounded wait observes the lease release, and the production Git updater imports the candidate and completes `git-checkout` against a real local repository and bare remote. The worktree HEAD is asserted to equal the candidate SHA.
- Non-Git build/install/Doctor commands are stubbed for the isolated fixture; all Git commands, the maintenance lease, the native state guard, the updater, and checkout are real. The fixture intentionally stops at `doctor-entry-missing` after checkout because it is not a complete installed runtime; no success beyond the asserted checkout boundary is claimed.
- Reverse control: removing only the production wrapper while keeping the regression makes the test fail because HEAD remains at the base commit and checkout is not reached; restoring the fix passes.

Actual focused-test trace from `2d88f210`:

```text
maintenance-checkout-proof {
  "result": {
    "status": "error",
    "reason": "doctor-entry-missing"
  },
  "refusal": {
    "isMaintenance": true,
    "name": "StateDatabaseAccessError"
  },
  "releaseRequested": true,
  "head": "5d98503edb1c537081571d4fd9ec9be904b78f82",
  "checkout": {
    "name": "git-checkout",
    "command": "git -C ... checkout --detach 5d98503edb1c537081571d4fd9ec9be904b78f82",
    "durationMs": 13,
    "exitCode": 0,
    "stderrTail": "HEAD is now at 5d98503 candidate"
  }
}
✓ waits for a real transient maintenance owner before Git checkout 32040ms
```

- `pnpm test src/cli/update-cli/update-command-execution.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/update-command-post-update.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/update-command-recovery-cost.test.ts` - 140 tests passed across 3 files.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` - passed.
- CLI update test TypeScript project (`test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.cli-update.json`) - passed.
- Type-aware oxlint on both changed files - passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on both changed files - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.

No live macOS managed-update replay was run in this environment. The proof above is the production execution path with a real foreign maintenance lease, native recovery-state refusal, release, candidate import, and real Git checkout.

## AI Assistance

AI assistance was used for source analysis, implementation, test design, and validation. The change was checked against the issue's acceptance criteria and the existing update state-read and recovery-safety contracts.

prs.title: feat(naming): opt-in one-time refinement of automatic session and topic names
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The first automatic session or Telegram DM topic name is based on the opening message, so it can become misleading as the conversation develops. This adds an **opt-in, one-time** refinement after a configurable number of later task messages (1–100, default 6). It remains off by default, never renames a manual title, and consumes at most one additional naming attempt per session or topic. This deliberately avoids the continuous renaming proposed in #99583 and #81781.

## Resulting Behavior

For dashboard sessions, generated-name provenance and bounded recent task context are tied to the session ID. The ordinary title-producing turn is excluded by the chat-send scheduler; a title prepared before an opening turn (including worktree and public `sessions.create` titles) carries an explicit skip marker. Later concurrent turns count toward refinement without losing the first follow-up. Private `titleRefinement` state, which can contain task excerpts, is removed from public and plugin session-entry projections.

For Telegram DM topics, refinement is armed only after the bot creates the initial label. The one-shot edit rechecks the current topic name after inference so a manual rename wins, then revalidates the owning account immediately before the Bot API edit. Per-DM `autoTopicLabel: true` overrides account-level `false`; an absent direct setting still inherits the account policy and prompt. Existing boolean/object configurations remain valid.

## Evidence

On current head `d1d5290e3835`, 36 dashboard-title tests, 1 public/plugin projection test, 7 Telegram config tests, 15 Telegram topic-refinement tests, and the focused created-title scheduler test passed locally. Scoped `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed. Hosted CI for this head is running; no current-head full typecheck result is claimed.

prs.title: refactor(gateway): simplify startup plugin publication ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway plugin startup and reload maintain a second claim/reservation protocol
and an artificial startup service handle around owners that already serialize
reloads and settle real service work.

## User Impact

Normal startup, plugin reload, readiness reporting, and shutdown retain their
existing paths. A config-file edit overlapping deferred startup can now receive
late startup facts; another reload or restart repairs that recoverable overlap.
Security checks, admitted writes, and actual service cleanup are not relaxed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the private claim/reservation/wait/publication protocol and publish the
existing actual service handle directly. Keep the existing reload queue, closing
and effect checks, startup producer joins, physical service settlement, bounded
recovery, discovery FIFO and acquired-handle cleanup, and failure diagnostics.
There is no replacement epoch, barrier, mutex, cache, or startup-readiness wait.

This is one startup/publication AREA recovered from a previously parked wide
cleanup, not the wider family's proof. It changes 21 files, including the
orphaned model helper predicate and its claim-only tests: production +150/-381,
231 net lines removed; tests/support +62/-580, 518 net lines removed. The
independent final-drain and startup-metric cuts are excluded. Existing internal
module/factory/kernel names stay to avoid an unrelated migration.

No public config, schema, protocol, SDK, dependency, permission, retention or
durability change. Installed update formats and migration paths are unchanged;
startup still lazily loads the same service owner and retains cleanup failures.
Phase E standalone session memory, its factory/registry/expiry/federation, and
its tests remain untouched. The shared resumeMemory path changes only its
generic handle-publication invocation, not memory behavior.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Startup reservation/winner gating originated in #126627's deterministic
  internal fixture, not a cited human actual-use incident. Today's file watcher
  can really overlap deferred startup: already-admitted startup may publish old
  registry/model/service/transcript-selection facts after reload. A later reload
  or restart repairs it. Closing, live credentials, invoker/source/config and
  capability checks remain; startup readiness is not delayed by a new barrier.
- Discovery no longer waits outside its FIFO for claim settlement. The same
  synthetic reservation provenance does not justify that replay protocol. A
  mode-only update may briefly advertise the prior registry before the following
  registry update retires it through normal FIFO and acquired-handle cleanup.
- The artificial startup service handle and its pending-owner/timeout forwarding
  originated in #124309 and #145816's scanner/reentrant/import and controlled
  contention probes, not a cited human import-custody incident. There is now one
  actual service handle, published synchronously before service startup yields.
  Close during lazy import refuses start at the existing final closing check;
  ordinary shutdown still joins the startup producer and actual cleanup.
- A second unsupported direct internal reload no longer gets a reservation's
  special rejection/status fence. Normal callers remain serialized by their
  existing owner. We do not add another scheduler for that unsupported call.

Peter's actual production cleanup/readiness incident in #150953 is distinct:
paused-channel release, admitted-write settlement, unavailable/sibling failure
diagnostics, captured-code rollback and bounded recovery all remain.

## Evidence

Fresh independent P0-P2 review completed scoped-clean across two passes, with
27 intact selected owner/test contexts. The complete 21-file diff and all 236
captured source/context files verified unchanged before and after review.
After the mixed serial replay, a fresh independent P0-P2 review reassessed the
complete unchanged diff with the exact failure results and 16 intact critical
fixture, observer, prewarm, root-admission and service contexts. It completed
scoped-clean in one pass while explicitly leaving causality unresolved; this
static review is not runtime acceptance or an inherited-CI exception.
Formatting and whitespace checks pass. No new production import edge is added;
the lazy services import only moves within its existing owner.

Focused isolated proof covered all seven selected roots. The tooling benchmark
root passed all 12 cases (12ms test time, 247.18 seconds configuration wall time).
Discovery passed 27 cases, startup-early 15, model startup five, and reload-status
one; recovery passed 102 cases with the two original indexing failures below.
The initial Gateway run was interrupted after four failures. One serial replay
then ran those same four cases, candidate followed by exact authored base
7aab596ad005c15824143c482e9d6da732c6f102, with original deadlines and one worker:

| Retained case | Candidate | Exact base |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Indexing checkpoint recovery | FAIL: expected reloading, observed recovering; 34,851ms | PASS; 27,437ms |
| Indexing restart recovery | PASS; 10,228ms | PASS; 15,089ms |
| Startup-gated methods | FAIL: original 120,000ms deadline; 120,914ms | PASS; 18,085ms |
| Main-session restoration, failure false | FAIL: original 120,000ms deadline; 122,147ms | PASS; 20ms |

Candidate configuration wall time was 1,458.34 seconds; exact base was 994.80
seconds. This pair does not establish inherited failures or a load-only cause.
The passing restart replay does not repair its original failure. The indexing
helper and complete startup-gated-method case remain byte-identical to base;
no deadline, retry, skip declaration or assertion was changed.

Earlier #175706 recorded these indexing phase failures on its exact 7836689
base. That helper, reload owner and generation owner are byte-identical between
that historical base and this authored base. This is historical intermittent
baseline evidence, not attribution of the current candidate or a CI waiver.
The candidate's contribution to the checkpoint mismatch and startup timeouts
remains unresolved. Remaining interrupted keeper coverage completed with 65

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the optional Decision tool prefilter retaining every tool when a V2 provider returns valid result metadata or usage such as cost and native billing units.

## User Impact

Agents with Decision assistance enabled can apply a confident conversational decision from V2 providers. Explicit yes/abstention, question errors, missing probabilities, and either probability at or above 0.35 retain tools. Probability-only V1 providers remain supported.

## Why This Change Was Made

The prefilter called the V1 runtime, so a valid V2 result reached the strict, lossless V1 codec and became `unsupported-input`. The consumer now calls V2 with tagged JSON evidence. The strict codec, evidence budget, 500ms deadline, optional priority, opt-out and admission callbacks remain intact.

The simplify pass removes this internal V1 consumer path and shares the strong-no predicate between the two questions. Production: +23/-10 (net +13 for the V2 evidence shape and explicit-answer policy); tests: +86/-23; generated mock baseline: -1 obsolete allowance. No configuration or SDK surface changes.

## Evidence

- Baseline reproduction: the registered V1 control passed; the registered V2 provider ran once and then returned `unavailable/unsupported-input`.
- Fixed source: **83 tests passed across seven focused files** on the same [Testbox allocation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39091380795). Covers registered V1/V2 results with metadata, explicit zero cost, native units and raw usage; uncertainty policy; optional admission and physical settlement; preparation deadlines; prompt/tool application; prefix stability; strict compatibility.
- Behavioral/static proof tree: `132dc530db24c1c5c61d1b85ea3b138026d286fe`, based on `df60ac04eddbc96d7bfa76c783f93f4eb5c847a5`. Final signed head `82c07203be8d4c256f238fc4499e390053408563` adds only a mock-isolation comment and one canonical generated baseline removal; executable behavior is unchanged.
- Independent source review and fresh external autoreview: no actionable findings. Formatting and whitespace checks passed. Targeted lint and both canonical test type graphs (`agents-other`, `other`) passed.
- Initial [CI attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39092154100) passed runtime, build, UI, lint and all type graphs, but its mock-export ratchet required an explicit isolation rationale for the changed policy mock. The correction adds that annotation and regenerates the obsolete allowance with canonical `--prune`. The exact guard now passes against the failed attempt's base; [Fresh exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39093099808) completed successfully: 37 passed, 26 intentionally skipped, no failed or pending jobs. Both required CI-gate contexts passed, including the repaired [ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39093099808/job/117574090412).
- Exact-head [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176022#issuecomment-6245158911): no findings, no before-merge actions, and no rank-up moves. Its noted absence of a shipped Gateway turn is an explicit proof limit below; this internal consumer repair is covered by the registered-host regression and existing prompt-application tests.
- This is registered host/consumer integration proof. The existing host test isolates credential/catalog preparation; it does not claim live vendor inference.

Release note: Decision assistance now accepts rich V2 results without losing the optional tool-prefilter decision. Accepted-call usage accounting remains a separate owner-boundary follow-up.
