prs.title: [AI-assisted] fix(config): include overridden plugin path in duplicate-id warning
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When two copies of the same plugin id are discovered during registry resolution, the `duplicate plugin id detected` config warning names only the winning copy and omits the overridden (losing) copy path. When both origins are `global`, the warning reads `global plugin will be overridden by global plugin (/path/to/winner)` — the only actionable path is the winner itself, which must be kept.

The `PluginDiagnostic.source` field already carries the overridden copy path (`overriddenCandidate.source`), but `pushRegistryDiagnostics` in `src/config/validation.ts` discards it when rendering the config warning, using only `diag.message`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Append the overridden copy path to the warning message when `diag.source` is present and the diagnostic is a duplicate plugin id warning. The registry producer stamps those diagnostics with the closed `code: "duplicate-plugin-id"`, and **both** validation consumers classify duplicates by that typed code instead of parsing the mutable message text.

Upgrade path (head `4debace07f3` after the 2026-08-26 rebase onto main `54db7d4f99`; code unchanged by the test-only follow-ups): released v1 installed-plugin indexes still persist duplicate diagnostics *without* that code. `parseInstalledPluginIndex` now backfills `code: "duplicate-plugin-id"` on uncoded diagnostics whose message starts with `duplicate plugin id`, so a valid persisted index is not left hiding the overridden path or misclassifying config-selected duplicates after upgrade. Seeded legacy-index regressions cover the store parse and both validation consumers.

## User Impact

Operators will now see which file to remove directly in the config warning:
```
plugin ekho-adapter: duplicate plugin id detected; global plugin will be overridden by global plugin (/path/to/winner) — overridden copy at /path/to/loser
```

## Terminal proof (real CLI, before/after)

Reproduced on real binaries with a temp `HOME` containing a duplicate plugin `demo-dup-7f3a`: one config-selected copy registered via `plugins.entries` under `~/config-copy/`, and a discarded global copy under `~/.openclaw/extensions/demo-dup-7f3a/`. Command: `node --import tsx src/entry.ts config validate`.

**BEFORE — current `main` `248966d3`:**
```
Config valid: ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json
1 warning(s):
  ! plugins.entries.demo-dup-7f3a: plugin demo-dup-7f3a: duplicate plugin id resolved by explicit config-selected plugin; global plugin will be overridden by config plugin (~/.config-copy/demo-dup-7f3a/index.js)
```

**AFTER — this PR branch (`03d2322cf745`):**
```
Config valid: ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json
1 warning(s):
  ! plugins.entries.demo-dup-7f3a: plugin demo-dup-7f3a: duplicate plugin id resolved by explicit config-selected plugin; global plugin will be overridden by config plugin (~/.config-copy/demo-dup-7f3a/index.js) — overridden copy at ~/.openclaw/extensions/demo-dup-7f3a/index.js
```

Difference: `— overridden copy at <discarded copy path>` is appended, naming the file an operator can actually delete.


## Terminal proof (persisted-index upgrade, end-to-end CLI)

Upgrade-path proof observed through the real CLI, not just the parser. A temp `HOME` was seeded by running the **pre-fix base** `5e438e9d0b` (merge-base with main) with two copies of plugin id `demo-dup-7f3a`: a config-selected copy under `~/config-copy/demo-dup-7f3a/` and a discarded global copy under `~/.openclaw/extensions/demo-dup-7f3a/`. `openclaw plugins registry --refresh` on the pre-fix build persisted the installed-plugin index to `~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite` with the **released v1 diagnostic shape** (raw `diagnostics_json` row, no `code` field):

```json
[{"level":"warn","pluginId":"demo-dup-7f3a","source":"~/.openclaw/extensions/demo-dup-7f3a/index.js","message":"duplicate plugin id resolved by explicit config-selected plugin; global plugin will be overridden by config plugin (~/config-copy/demo-dup-7f3a/index.js)"}]
```

**BEFORE — `config validate` on pre-fix base `5e438e9d0b`, same seeded state:**

```
Config valid: ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json
2 warning(s):
  ! plugins.entries.demo-dup-7f3a: plugin demo-dup-7f3a: duplicate plugin id resolved by explicit config-selected plugin; global plugin will be overridden by config plugin (~/config-copy/demo-dup-7f3a/index.js)
  ! agents.entries: Moved agents.list to keyed agents.entries.
```

**AFTER — `config validate` on head `8fa2bfb79b` / unchanged tree at `4debace07f3` (rebase did not touch these files' code), same seeded state (no re-refresh, files untouched):**

```
Config valid: ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json
2 warning(s):
  ! plugins.entries.demo-dup-7f3a: plugin demo-dup-7f3a: duplicate plugin id resolved by explicit config-selected plugin; global plugin will be overridden by config plugin (~/config-copy/demo-dup-7f3a/index.js) — overridden copy at ~/.openclaw/extensions/demo-dup-7f3a/index.js
  ! agents.entries: Moved agents.list to keyed agents.entries.
```

The persisted-index read path is confirmed, not assumed:

- `openclaw plugins registry --json` on the head reports `state: "fresh"`, `refreshReasons: []` (persisted read, no re-derivation), and its read-time `diagnostics` entry shows the closed code backfilled from the legacy row: `"code": "duplicate-plugin-id"` with `source` naming the discarded copy.
- Re-dumping the raw SQLite `diagnostics_json` after the head-side runs shows the row is byte-identical (still no `code`) — the upgrade happens at read time via `parseInstalledPluginIndex`; nothing is rewritten behind the user's back.
- Negative control: after deleting the discarded copy from disk, `config validate` on the head drops the duplicate warning entirely (staleness re-derivation works; the persisted diagnostic is not blindly trusted) and the store row is again unchanged.

Commands (paths redacted; `~` was a scratch `HOME` for the run): `node --import tsx src/entry.ts plugins registry --refresh` (seed, pre-fix base), `node --import tsx src/entry.ts config validate` (both builds), `node --import tsx src/entry.ts plugins registry --json` (head), plus a read-only `node:sqlite` dump of `installed_plugin_index.diagnostics_json` before/after.

## Evidence

- **Root cause**: `pushRegistryDiagnostics` constructs the warning via `${pluginLabel}: ${diag.message}` without using `diag.source` (line 216 of `validation.ts`).
- **Fix verification**: The diagnostic object at `manifest-registry.ts:1283` already stores `source: overriddenCandidate.source`. The change in `pushRegistryDiagnostics` reads it and appends it.
- **Closed-code migration**: both validation consumers in `src/config/validation.ts` (compat set ~line 260, overridden-ID set ~line 302) now filter on `diag.code === "duplicate-plugin-id"` instead of `diag.message.includes(...)`. Regression test: "counts config-selected duplicate diagnostics as overridden in validation consumers" in `src/config/config.plugin-validation.test.ts`.
- **Regression gate**: No non-duplicate diagnostics carry `source` with a "duplicate plugin id" message, so the `message.includes` guard is safe. The `diag.source` guard prevents appending to diagnostics that lack a source.
- **Focused regression test**: Two new test cases added:
  - Verifies the overridden copy path appears in the warning message for duplicate-id diagnostics with a source.
  - Verifies non-duplicate diagnostics with a source (e.g. blocked plugin) do not get the "overridden copy at" hint.
- **After-fix behavior**: see the fenced before/after CLI traces under "Terminal proof" above.
- **Tests** (head `4debace07f3`, re-run after the rebase): `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-store.test.ts src/config/config.plugin-validation.test.ts` — 90 + 32 passing (main's #130031 added store tests; all green), including `migrates duplicate-id diagnostics persisted before the closed code existed`, `appends overridden copy path after migrating a legacy persisted duplicate diagnostic`, and `counts a legacy persisted config-selected duplicate as overridden after index parse`.

**Note**: This PR addresses warning rendering plus the persisted-index upgrade classification. The broader registry recovery behavior described in #124468 (stale index state preventing recovery) is a separate concern not covered by this diff.

Related: #124468 (warning rendering only; does not close the broader report)

[AI-assisted] Evidence and diff produced with AI assistance. Change rationale and terminal verification verified by author.
- **Test types** (head `4debace07f3`, re-run after the rebase): `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.config-cli.json --builders 1` — exit 0. Reproduced the CI `check-test-types-core-3` TS4104 failures (readonly `parsed!.diagnostics` assigned into the mutable `PluginManifestRegistry.diagnostics`) on `8fa2bfb79b`, fixed by spreading into a fresh array at both seeded-test sites; production types untouched.

- **Lint (max-lines) (head `5fdad32876f`)**: `check-lint-core-4` failed on the merge ref because main grew `installed-plugin-index-store.test.ts` by +63 lines in #130031; combined with this branch's migration test the merged file hit 1004 counted lines (test-file limit 1000, `skipBlankLines`/`skipComments`). Reproduced locally on the exact merge-tree file with the pinned oxlint 1.78.0 (`1094:4 File has too many lines (1004)`), compacted the seeded fixtures (single-line messages kept to the matcher-relevant `duplicate plugin id` prefix, dropped the unused `source` field, collapsed the unrelated fixture; 7 counted lines saved, merged file now 997), and re-verified the compacted merge tree passes oxlint exit 0. Re-ran `vitest run src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-store.test.ts` — 26/26 passed; `oxfmt --check` clean. Migration semantics unchanged: the backfill only keys on `code === undefined && message.startsWith("duplicate plugin id")`. Re-verified on the rebased head `4debace07f3`: `installed-plugin-index-store.test.ts` counts 997 non-blank/non-comment lines (limit 1000), pinned `oxlint@1.78.0` exit 0 on all 7 changed files, `oxfmt@0.60.0 --check` clean.

- **Rebase (2026-08-26, per review P1/P2)**: branch rebased onto main `54db7d4f99` (was 1132 commits ahead of the merge-base); replay was conflict-free and the tree diff vs the pre-rebase head `5fdad32876f` is empty for all 7 changed files. All 7 commits are authored by Santhi Prakash and SSH-signed (GitHub **Verified** on the new head). Required checks re-running on `4debace07f3`.

prs.title: feat(memory): report duplicate Markdown blocks
prs.body:
Related: #176036

## What Problem This Solves

Operators consolidating copied Markdown memory need source locations for repeated content, rather than only more diverse search results.

## User Impact

`openclaw memory duplicates` reports identical blocks and their file/line references without changing files or printing memory text. Both same-file and cross-file repeats are included. `--agent`, `--min-chars`, `--max-groups`, and `--json` support focused local inspection.

This is a proposed optional CLI feature, not an accepted product direction. It follows existing offline CLI ownership rules and refuses another plugin's memory slot. File paths can still be sensitive and should be reviewed before sharing reports. Maintainer edits are disabled because the author has not authorized fork workflow/secrets access.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse Memory Core's existing Markdown discovery, authorized file reader, and chunker. Group exact, non-overlapping chunks locally, normalizing CRLF and empty boundary lines. Return bounded location lists with explicit total and omitted counts. No new model-facing tool, SDK contract, database, configuration setting, background task, deletion, or search-ranking change.

The command inspects live files, not persisted index contents. It does not find paraphrases or arbitrary matching substrings across chunk boundaries. Repeated content can be intentional; consolidation remains a separate manual decision.

## Evidence

- Focused CLI and ownership tests: 25 passing (final wrapper wall time 24.85s, including cold compiler preparation; the new diagnostic test file itself used approximately 0.75s). Synthetic fixtures exercise within/across-file repeats, CRLF, changed text, configured extra paths, excluded unrelated/session files and symlinks, agent selection, thresholds, output limits, no text disclosure, unchanged source bytes, disabled memory, another slot owner, and invalid options. CI timing is not available yet.
- Production Memory Core package typecheck, targeted two-file test typecheck with the repository's ambient declarations, targeted lint, and formatting passed.
- Real official source CLI, using an isolated credential-free child environment and synthetic config/state: JSON and human output both reported one duplicate group with three occurrences at `MEMORY.md:3-4`, `MEMORY.md:5-5`, and `memory/shop.md:1-1`. The unrelated `private.md` was not scanned, all fixture bytes stayed unchanged, and no `openclaw-agent.sqlite` index database was created. An unset synthetic embedding SecretRef was not needed.
- Line-cap, assertion-safety, and mock-export ratchets passed. The full max-lines suppression check reports three existing `main` UI paths outside this diff: `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts`, and `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts`. Their suppressions are already present in the base; no baseline or unrelated UI files are changed.
- Independent Codex autoreview completed: no actionable P0–P2 findings (`scoped-clean`, confidence 0.90). The reviewer assessed supplied source and evidence without executing project code. Broad repository CI has not run locally. This is CLI boundary proof, not an installed release or model-generated conversational workflow claim.

Only generic code and synthetic fixtures are included. No private workspace content, personal configuration, credentials, raw real-user logs, screenshots, or build artifacts are part of the change.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw sessions --json` drops the session's persisted sidebar category, so offline scripts cannot group the same sessions shown by the Gateway. The canonical store and Gateway already retain that value.

## User Impact

JSON rows include the existing optional `category` value, such as `Research`. Unset and cleared categories remain omitted. Human tables, cleanup behavior, sorting, limits, store selection and authorization are preserved. No new flag, configuration/default, schema, migration, protocol or dependency.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add the field to the existing shared session display-row owner. The actual sessions command already serializes those rows from canonical SQLite; no parallel query, storage reader or formatting policy is introduced. Existing-solutions preflight: Gateway/tool APIs cannot replace offline CLI JSON, and asking operators to query private SQLite tables is not an adequate supported alternative.

October 18 maintenance normally merges `9b707074b5f231f6976456ea7431567893fe7d1c`, preserves main's consolidated session fixture, and retains the one-field production change. This fixes the real test conflict and brings in the current CI entry scripts missing from the old event baseline; no force push, unrelated CI patch or guard bypass. Main's shared mapper/command/cleanup sibling and canonical store contract were read.

## Evidence

Current contributor head: **`df85498352116add97f16eac7414b033b034a40d`**. Clean checkout. Linux, Node 24.16.0; source Gateway and actual command-owner proof, with no packaged CLI, model conversation or UI claim.

Acceptance control baseline: current main **`9b707074b5f231f6976456ea7431567893fe7d1c`**. prs.title: fix(agents): agents claim no shell or hand off when Code Mode and terminal text say so
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agents wrongly conclude they have no shell or must hand work to a human. This happens when the Code Mode tool summary says "never shell", or when a terminal tool call finds no shared terminal.

## User Impact

User impact: in Code Mode, agents keep using the nested shell `exec` tool instead of claiming shell access is unavailable. A missing shared terminal no longer makes them ask the operator to open one; unattended runs (for example, scheduled cleanup jobs) continue with their own commands.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Code Mode tool summary:** the startup tool list described `exec` as "…call exact catalog tools from code, never shell/Python/imports". The same prompt also says "Use the shell tool `exec` for heavier computation". Models read the first line as "no shell". The clause is removed. The `exec` schema still says "`code` is JavaScript, never a shell command", so the warning about what goes in `code` is kept. Net startup prompt change: −3 words.
- **Terminal tool error:** the recovery text "ask the operator to open one in this chat" made the agent stop and hand off. It now says the tool cannot open a terminal and to run your own commands with `exec`.

## Evidence

- Source: a review of 84 real agent self-knowledge failures in team sessions, plus a random sample of 80 sessions. The baseline is 1.8 failures per 100 assistant turns, and these two strings were implicated in several of the failures.
- `pnpm vitest run` passed on `terminal-tool.test.ts` (updated assertion), `system-prompt*.test.ts` and `code-mode*`: 36 files, 503 tests. oxfmt and `git diff --check` are clean.
- Gap: no model-level before/after result. In cut-at-failure replays on `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, the historical failures reproduced in only 2/50 trials, so a paired eval could not show a difference. Follow-up metric: the failure rate per 100 assistant turns on randomly sampled sessions after release, compared with the frozen baseline.

prs.title: fix: surface mandatory config schema failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The shared runtime configuration owner silently skips its mandatory schema read when a replacement Gateway omits config.schema from its method list. UI and Gateway ship as one install/version; current coupling policy forbids this older-Gateway fallback.

## User Impact

Unsupported version skew reaches the existing visible schema-error state instead of silently retaining an old schema. Normal replacement still refreshes config and schema. Connected-client admission, read scopes (including scope-less access policy), current-request checks, config drafts and all write/settlement behavior stay unchanged. No rendering, style or visible-copy change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the mandatory-method advertisement skip and its import, and replace the obsolete compatibility comment. The existing loadConfigSchema owner records request failures; reconnect schema refresh now follows config refresh so the config success cannot erase that schema failure. This is a narrow shared-owner area in the mandatory-method fallback family, split under the campaign's area rule: four net production lines removed, eleven net test lines added. No parallel error owner or new state.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- An unsupported mismatched Gateway lacking config.schema now receives the request and reports its missing-method error through existing lastError; the previous schema is retained. The gate originated in f8ba65636c23/#125492, whose scope-access and scope-less policy are preserved. Its method-list fallback was compatibility rationale/test evidence, not a cited human incident; current UI/Gateway coupling explicitly retires that fallback.
- Reconnect's schema refresh follows that reconnect's config read, not an arbitrarily superseding read. An unsupported mismatched Gateway combined with another overlapping refresh may still overwrite its old error or delay this refresh; reload/explicit schema refresh recovers. We accept that edge instead of introducing latest-read arbitration or another error-state owner. A second review's P2 proposed that additional coordination; declined under the best-effort doctrine, not claimed fixed or clean.
- No security guard, permission, connection/request lifetime, mutation authority or write settlement is removed. No config/schema/protocol/persistence/dependency/SDK change. Phase E standalone memory backend/factory/registry/expiry/federation/tests remain untouched.

## Evidence

- Current owner, full companion suite, state model and harness, determining schema operation and direct caller frames inspected. Canonical core descriptor unconditionally registers config.schema with operator.read; actual handler returns the runtime schema. No optional plugin/config registration is involved.
- Migrated owner-level reconnect regression fails pre-cut because lastError stays null (one intended failure, 37.15s Vitest/52.43s wrapper). Independent review found that a later config success could erase an earlier schema failure; the deferred-config regression reproduced it in the gate-only proposal (25.65s Vitest/35.13s wrapper). Sequencing the existing reads fixes that loss without new state. Final owner and state-model suites:37/37 passed in37.50s Vitest/56.26s wrapper; changed case52ms. Retains normal replacement, scope denial, scope-less access, stale-result exclusion, dirty-draft and write settlement proof. No new seam, sleep, retry, timeout, skip or suppression.
- Final full two-file/five-dataset independent review completed, final source verification successful. Its remaining P2 for overlapping superseding reads is explicitly declined above; the first ordering finding was reproduced and fixed. A subsequent mechanical default type-argument removal fixes the owned lint diagnostic without behavior change. Targeted graph reports36 existing parse5/MCP dependency diagnostics, none in changed paths: NOT a local type pass. A proof-config ambient root omission was corrected using the existing modal-dialog owner. Corrected canonical type-aware lint, formatting54ms and whitespace passed. Mandatory suppression guard14/14 passed in94.92s Vitest/126.68s wrapper; no suppression/baseline/budget changes. Exact-head hosted ci:full is the broad/UI-browser gate; no local build/E2E/live/performance claim. Only an import edge is removed, so no new runtime cycle/component can arise. Plain TypeScript owner remains plain TypeScript; no reactive/render lifecycle machinery added.

Release-note context: surface missing mandatory config schema methods instead of silently skipping their reads on reconnect.

prs.title: fix(update): never publish over a live Gateway when service probes fail
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Package updates could replace an installation underneath a live Gateway when native service probes failed. The Gateway's rewritten process title hid its installation from the fallback consumer check, and native exceptions bypassed retained service admission. The replacement could restart the Gateway while update history remained in `activating`.

Refs #175869. This addresses the additional failure exposed by the live proof in #175928; it does not establish the original reporter's Pi root cause.

## User Impact

A live or unverified Gateway owner blocks package replacement when native inspection is unavailable. Losing native inspection after service admission refuses before stop/publication. Confirmed-dead update drivers no longer leave a run active for the 30-minute inactivity grace period: status records a failed terminal outcome and a repair next action. Live/unknown drivers, unrecorded adopters, and retained recovery remain protected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Gateway lock reader owns PID/start-time verification, including legacy lock locations. Publication now uses that reader and permits a live owner only when its argv positively identifies a disjoint installation. The same guard runs during admission and immediately before publication. The native exception path uses the existing retained-admission comparison instead of returning an unchecked `unavailable` result.

Existing run reconciliation owns terminalization; no new timer, schema, option, dependency, or identity store was introduced. Production **+81/-41 (net +40)**; tests **+118/-45 (net +73)**; docs **+19/-6**. The old caller-side raw-PID/argv check is removed. The fix applies when the installed updater contains it; an older installed driver keeps its shipped behavior.

## Evidence

- Original-source controls failed for the retitled/unreadable live owner, native exception after admission, and immediate dead-driver settlement. The Linux package entry-point control reached the later schema guard instead of the required Gateway refusal. Fixed focused run: **87 tests passed in four files**.
- The required **113-file direct/one-barrel importer sweep** completed eight shards in **29m 27.1s**: **2,065 tests passed**, one test failed, and 57 existing test skips. The failure was the unchanged `update-command-service.integration.test.ts` case “refreshes a verified installed root with retained source launcher”: a one-second real-clock readiness budget expired under host I/O load. A controlled 1.1-second healthy response reproduced the same `restart-health-failed`/readiness-timeout result. Transition tests now control the monotonic clock; production deadlines and assertions remain unchanged. The delayed control then passed with the same assertions; after removing the injected delay, the complete file passed **79/79 tests** (39.90s aggregate test time; 47.95s Vitest duration). The rest of the importer sweep passed; only this affected file was rerun after the fixture fix.
- Unchanged slow fixture files on the final head: `update-command-database-rollback.test.ts` **135.53s** aggregate test time (max case 18.32s), `update-cli.windows-lifecycle.test.ts` **133.59s** (max 14.57s), `update-command-original-service.test.ts` **155.60s** (max 8.59s), and `update-command-lease.test.ts` **186.38s** (max 7.70s). These repeatedly prepare real package/state/Doctor subprocess fixtures per case; no timeouts, retries, assertions, or skips were changed to mask them.
- CLI-update and infra targeted `run-tsgo.mjs` checks passed. Touched-file oxlint/oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and Madge passed (**0 cycles**). Full package build passed in **3m 15s**; tarball integrity and built import-graph checks passed. The initial runtime-only package lacked declaration exports; a full build corrected that preparation error. SQLite inventory was skipped under the campaign's local gate budget; PR CI remains the broad gate.
- Independent Codex reviews of the rebased production change and the final test-clock fix completed with no accepted/actionable P0/P1 findings. The first review attempt rejected the default temporary-directory isolation; selecting the OS-provided private temporary directory resolved that setup issue. Unchanged helper implementations were also inspected manually.

### Live proof

Both runs used fresh local Linux ARM64 containers, the real packed build, an isolated OS-account HOME/state, port 19879, the canonical fake systemd from `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/update-restart-auth.sh`, and a synthetic 2026.10.5 candidate generated with `packNodeUpdateFixture`. The updater omitted XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS.

```sh
# Host packaging and tests used this isolated environment:
export HOME="$PWD/.artifacts/l1681/home"
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$PWD/.artifacts/l1681/state"

node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mts \
  --skip-build --output-dir "$PWD/.artifacts/l1681/pack-rebased" \
  --output-name openclaw-base.tgz

# Inside the container: HOME=/proof/home3, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/proof/home3/.openclaw
# Probes unavailable from the beginning:
env -u XDG_RUNTIME_DIR -u DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS \
  timeout 180 openclaw update --yes --tag file:/proof/openclaw-candidate.tgz

# Native admission succeeds; probes fail after candidate-state cleanup:
env -u XDG_RUNTIME_DIR -u DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS \
  timeout 180 openclaw update --yes --tag file:/proof/openclaw-candidate.tgz

openclaw update status --json
openclaw gateway call health --json
openclaw gateway call themes.list --params '{}' --json
```

On the combined production changes, initial unavailability refused in **65s**, exit **1**, with `gateway-stop-unverified`. The default-command delayed replay refused in **173s**, exit **1**, with `managed-service-preflight`. Both completed within the 180-second harness bound, recorded **failed/finished**, had no active run, and supplied a next action.

All **38,990 installed file hashes**, the original Gateway PID/start time, and package version remained unchanged in each run. Health and a cold `themes.list` RPC passed. There were **zero update stop/start/restart effects**. Both owned containers were removed. The final follow-up only controls a test fixture's clock; these runs use identical production code.

```text
initial: failed/finished; gateway-stop-unverified; exit 1; 65s
 delayed: failed/finished; managed-service-preflight; exit 1; 173s
both: 38,990 file hashes unchanged; Gateway identity unchanged; health/RPC OK
```

Earlier trials on the prior base also refused both scenarios with unchanged package/process evidence. One trial with an extra 150-second command deadline reached a terminal `update-activation-timeout` before refusal cleanup completed; the default command is used for the final proof above. Those earlier trials are not counted as current-head proof.

The branch incorporates #175928's inspection diagnostics and untouched-recovery guidance. It preserves that landed fix while closing the remaining consumer-detection and native-exception gaps.

prs.title: fix: preserve valid automatic Codex model selections
prs.body:
Closes #174053

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes configured or inherited automatic OpenAI model selections being cleared during ordinary reply preparation when the matching primary uses Codex.

## User Impact

Valid automatic selections keep their stored model and origin metadata. Legacy fallback cleanup and heartbeat cleanup retain their existing behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The subagent selection owner deliberately writes self-origin metadata, but the legacy Codex predicate still treats those selections as stale. Exempt only complete, explicit stored provider/model pairs equal to their trimmed origin fields; incomplete and cross-origin entries remain eligible for cleanup. Equality is a stored-selection contract, not evidence of freshness.

Thanks @flyto168 for the report and proposed solution in #174053. Related #157391 changes a separate cleanup operand and leaves this legacy predicate unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before the production repair, the new owner-boundary regression failed for the two valid self-origin selections (2 failed / 22 passed). Afterward, all 24 cases pass.
- Tests call the real reply model-selection owner and verify the returned selection and session snapshot. They cover complete and trimmed origins, legacy/mismatched/incomplete origins, literal model identity, missing/blank stored providers, and stale heartbeats.
- Focused regression: `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.resolved-pin.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 24 passed, 475.43s launcher wall time (441.87s Vitest duration, dominated by shared worker compilation; test execution about 11%).
- Adjacent provenance and stored-override suites: 23 passed across two files; 376.25s launcher wall time, including cache verification. Formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Full `pnpm tsgo:core` was stopped after over 13 minutes without a result (exit143); it is not a passing typecheck. The targeted messaging test type graph passes (167.9s, exit0), and targeted type-aware lint passes (exit0).
- Independent read-only review found no P0–P2 issues. The required shared autoreview helper was attempted, but its Codex process timed out refreshing available models; no valid autoreview report was produced.
### Cross-process behavior proof (2026-10-17)

Validated on head `bbec1b7aab74b5ef343e570e8a18028623d3cd2d` using the source-built CLI and real Gateway processes in an isolated temporary HOME/state directory. Only the external Codex app-server JSON-RPC transport was simulated, using a fixture adapted from the existing QA auth fixture; no paid/live model inference is claimed.

1. CLI `doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive` imports synthetic OAuth credentials.
2. Public Gateway `tools.invoke` calls `sessions_spawn` with a configured/inherited `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` model. The real producer writes the automatic self-origin selection to SQLite.
3. Restart Gateway and send an ordinary `chat.send` reply through `getReplyFromConfig` / `createModelSelectionState`. Wait for the exact run's `chat.final`, verify a fresh unique request marker in the latest assistant message, stop Gateway, and read the actual persisted session.
4. With Gateway stopped, use the session owner to change only the origin model to `gpt-old`; restart and repeat the same ordinary reply and persistence checks as a stale-origin control.

| Check | Persisted result |
| --- | --- |
| Real `sessions_spawn` producer | `provider=openai`, `model=gpt-5.6-luna`, `source=auto`, `originProvider=openai`, `originModel=gpt-5.6-luna` |
| Ordinary Gateway reply | All five fields remain identical; run status `ok`, matching `chat.final`, fresh assistant marker verified |
| Stale-origin control before reply | Same selection, with only `originModel=gpt-old` |
| Stale-origin control after reply | All five override/origin fields absent; run status `ok`, matching `chat.final`, fresh assistant marker verified |

The proof command exited 0, including test-instance cleanup. The baseline-before-fix failure is established by the focused regression tests above; a cross-process baseline replay is not claimed.

The transport fixture uses unique native turn/message IDs across process restarts, avoiding transcript deduplication. Reads and the control edit occur with Gateway stopped; production selection/persistence code is not mocked. No full build or full suite is claimed.

### CI attribution still open

Production/test type checks and lint passed in PR CI. The remaining failed job is [checks-node-changed-4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38883348888/job/116915801611): the X publication production-owner E2E times out after 120 seconds waiting for `childWritten.promise`, rather than failing a model-selection assertion. That test file is unchanged between this PR's base and head, and its `x-proof/proof-model` provider does not meet the changed OpenAI predicate's preconditions.

This is causal evidence, not a proven inherited failure: `pnpm test:ci-failed 174077` classified it **unknown** because no matching job was found on main. An exact-base replay installed dependencies successfully but was stopped after more than 13 minutes in the declaration build, before the test started (exit 143). There is no baseline test verdict. The CI gate remains unresolved pending owner attribution; no gate bypass or unrelated test change is requested.

Simplification: no new helper, owner, state field, or compatibility path; production +10 lines, tests +71 lines.


## Main integration (2026-10-18)

Merged main `2a628fcba` into head `747a3568452c5d94083750c15223a59c6abf37f9` to resolve actual merge conflicts. The original self-origin comparison and ten regression cases are unchanged; main's canonical OpenAI provider constant, authentication cleanup and test refactors are retained. An independent read-only review found no actionable conflict-resolution issues.

Fresh merged-tree proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.resolved-pin.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed **24/24**, exit 0 (408.80s wrapper wall time). The project wrapper fell back from an unavailable pinned Bun download to Node. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Targeted lint did not run to completion: its shared plugin SDK declaration preparation timed out at 300 seconds; this is a validation gap, not a passing lint result. The targeted messaging typecheck was stopped after more than five minutes of actual compiler work (in addition to waiting for the shared artifact lock), exit 143; no typecheck result is claimed. New-head PR CI owns the remaining broad/static proof.

The cross-process behavior proof above belongs to the original `bbec1b7` head; it has not been rerun after main integration. Earlier CI failures likewise belong to that original head. New-head PR CI must establish current broad-check results; no claim of a green gate is made.

prs.title: fix(ci): skip discarded Linux fixture package builds
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Linux native fixture CI builds and installs the full desktop npm package, then immediately deletes it to install a synthetic CLI.

## User Impact

CI avoids that discarded package build, archive validation, npm install, and resource traversal. Desktop application behavior is unchanged. The synthetic fixture no longer provides incidental per-PR Linux npm-package coverage: Linux-only package or dependency failures can instead surface in full package validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use an explicit runtime-only staging invocation at the synthetic Linux fixture boundary. It retains verified pinned Bun resources; the existing fixture supplies its CLI before Cargo compiles it. Ordinary Tauri build/dev hooks and Windows retain full package staging, with no cache or artifact-sharing path.

Production/config delta: net -2 lines (+5/-7). Test delta: net +61 lines. The small runtime option expresses the fixture/package ownership boundary; the unused Linux package timeout is removed.

## Evidence

- The new actual-CLI regression fails on the original source because runtime-only still invokes the real package builder. It passes after the change; default staging still reaches the package builder and retains the previous destination on failure. Bun envelope, hash, manifest, staged file inventory, and scratch cleanup are checked.
- Native staging/package/runtime-boundary tests: 19/19 pass. Existing Linux and Windows package, release, cache-isolation, and runtime contracts remain covered. Python first-run tests: 13/13 pass, including package-present and Bun-only fixture inputs plus stale copied-resource removal.
- Targeted actionlint, formatting, and diff checks pass. The workflow contract test retains Windows packaging budgets and verifies the fixture invocation versus unchanged Tauri hooks; exact-head CI will execute it.
- Exact-head native Linux fixture CI and a separate canonical full Linux package staging proof are pending. No measured wall-time savings claim.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `mcp add` silently changes quoted executable and working-directory paths containing surrounding whitespace.

## User Impact

User impact: the configured MCP server starts with the exact executable path and working directory supplied by the operator. Blank commands remain rejected and HTTP options keep their existing normalization.

## Why This Change Was Made

The flag adapter used a trimming string normalizer for filesystem paths. Use the existing nonblank-string reader for `--command` and `--cwd`, consistently with the runtime's existing literal-path behavior and the JSON configuration entry.

## Evidence

The complete 32-test suite passed in an isolated container before the final equivalent inline predicate adjustment. prs.title: fix(update): report unavailable systemd inspection without a false recovery failure
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An update refused before changing its managed Gateway could report a false recovery failure, while unavailable systemd inspection discarded the native cause needed to diagnose it.

Refs #175869. The reporter's Pi root cause remains unknown until its native diagnostic is collected.

## User Impact

An untouched managed-service refusal records `No recovery needed; still serving <before>` (or honestly reports the unchanged installation when no running observation exists), without a `restart-unhealthy` verdict. Existing refusal messages and failure facts retain the failed probe, exit/termination, and a sanitized first stderr line, together with the unchanged-installation and inspection guidance.

This does not make every unavailable-inspection path refuse safely: the live proof below exposed an existing admission gap, which remains outside this explicitly narrowed patch.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native execution owner keeps the bounded diagnostic in the existing inspection error; the existing runtime detail and managed-service failure facts carry it. The recovery owner skips restart verification when nothing was stopped, started, or changed. The failure-fact formatter is consolidated rather than duplicated.

No added retry, process-owner fallback, diagnostic propagation object, option, schema, or dependency. Existing inspection deadlines and user-bus derivation remain unchanged. Production **+115/-76 = net +39**; tests **+126/-27 = net +99**, relative to `bbd73bc442f4`. The remaining production growth is native diagnostic capture/formatting and the untouched-recovery condition.

## Evidence

- Native `show`/`cat`/`is-active` diagnostic regressions, untouched recovery, and lost-inspection guidance failed on the untouched base. The deadline regression also failed because the native probe cause was lost.
- Final focused run: **187 tests across six owner suites passed**, three Vitest shards in **55.46 s**. Both refusal codes, native causes, preserved public refusal facts, existing absence/ownership classification, and lost-inspection guidance passed.
- The required **168-file importer sweep** completed in **31 m 22 s**: 2,905 tests passed, 30 existing skips, five assertion failures. It caught an obsolete signal-message expectation and four cases where diagnostic facts replaced the public refusal fact. The public fact is now preserved and diagnostics appended; the five cases passed in the final owner-suite replay. The other passing results were reused because their behavior was unchanged.
- Targeted CLI/services `run-tsgo.mjs` checks, touched-file oxlint/oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and Madge passed (**0 cycles**). Final runtime build passed in **80.6 s**; packed-package integrity passed. SQLite inventory was skipped under the campaign's local gate budget; PR CI owns broad checks.
- Independent Codex review found no actionable P0/P1 issues.
- Pre-existing slow fixtures: `update-command-original-service.test.ts` spent 180.6 s across 48 cases (maximum 10.7 s); `update-command-database-rollback.test.ts` spent 177.6 s across 13 cases (maximum 24.5 s). Their retained-service and package/Git/database rollback fixtures repeat real setup per case; `update-command-lease.test.ts` also spent 144.1 s across 54 cases (maximum 6.7 s), repeatedly launching its fresh-process lease/Doctor fixture. These suites and their timeouts/assertions were not changed.

### Live proof and limitation

The isolated package was built with `pnpm build:runtime` and packed with:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mts \
  --skip-build --output-dir "$PWD/.artifacts/l1679-final/live" \
  --output-name openclaw-base.tgz
```

Inside each isolated container, the principal commands were:

```sh
env -u XDG_RUNTIME_DIR -u DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS timeout 180 \
  openclaw update --yes --tag file:/proof/openclaw-candidate.tgz
openclaw update status --json
openclaw gateway call health --json
openclaw gateway call themes.list --params '{}' --json
```

Both runs used a real built Gateway, isolated HOME/state, port 19879, a canonical fake systemd surface, and a locally packed 2026.10.5 candidate. The update command omitted XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS. One run made native probes unavailable initially; the other retained successful initial inspection and failed probes after candidate cleanup.

**Neither run proved safe refusal.** Both replaced 2026.10.4 with 2026.10.5 without a native stop/start/restart call. The installation observer requested a supervisor restart (`gateway.installation_replaced`), replacing the original process. The bounded commands ended at about 182 s with exit 137 while status still showed `running` / `activating`; a SIGTERM recovery message was observed, but there was no terminal refusal or recovery result. The precise cause of exit 137 was not established. HTTP health, health RPC, and a first `themes.list` call (11 themes) passed on the replacement processes, not on a retained old process. Both owned containers were removed.

Source diagnosis: the existing package guard requires an installation path from argv, but the Gateway rewrites its process title to `openclaw-gateway`; the native-exception path can also return unavailable before checking the retained service admission. Those decisions are unchanged by this patch. Matching PID/start-time/port/systemd-owner evidence was captured before the delayed run. This patch adds no new authority path and makes no claim to fix that separate gap.

The initial Bun worker SIGTRAP is a pre-existing intermittent native startup defect, tracked in #175961. Worker/launch/pinned-runtime blobs were unchanged; 600 minimal launches passed, establishing intermittence rather than a repair. No retry, timeout increase, or weaker assertion was added.

prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves

Let an agent recall sibling threads in one verified channel without exposing every session owned by that agent.

## User Impact

Opt-in `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` enables same-channel retrieval while excluding other agents, channels, accounts and workspaces. Existing defaults and other visibility modes are unchanged. Sibling send, status/model changes and session mutations remain denied.

Cross-session list, history, search and transcript-backed recall require a Gateway-hosted owner and fail closed when that owner, route, incarnation, or policy is withdrawn. Ordinary memory/wiki results remain available.

## Implementation

- Require matching stored provider, explicit account, opaque channel destination, chat kind and workspace/space under the same agent.
- Recheck route, incarnation, aliases, physical owner, and policy at final disclosure.
- Carry query-local transcript-owner bindings through memory and direct Wiki consumers; filter final snippets, citations, and recall side effects synchronously.
- Preserve self-only reads, ordinary memory/wiki retrieval, and archived metadata-only inventory behavior.

## Verification

Exact head: `2955558891cbfd9cb7c21b2a9a1efcf4531c9d3c`. Ordinary merge of upstream main `90127436fa45e539616c7b123a549cbd3919c725`; no force push.

- Focused authority validation passed: **3 files / 46 tests**. The direct Wiki production adapter now runs under the real Gateway row owner with controlled synthetic search input and proves:
  - allowed sibling snippet/citation output;
  - the nearest, highest-ranked forbidden transcript cannot enter or displace final results;
  - missing transcript owners and a requester with no Gateway owner fail closed;
  - route and policy withdrawal after capability preparation remove buffered transcript output;
  - ordinary durable memory remains available.
- Official extension test typecheck, touched-file type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and the full candidate build passed. The build included public plugin-SDK export verification.
- Focused autoreview found that the original fixture did not make the forbidden result nearest; the fixture now ranks it first with a limiting result cap, and the focused tests/typecheck/lint pass after that correction.

## Real behavior proof

prs.title: fix(memory): Active Memory's recall prompts show up in memory search results
prs.body:
Closes #176024

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: memory search returns Active Memory's own recall prompts instead of real conversation excerpts when Active Memory runs with session sources.

## User Impact

User impact: recall and `memory_search` stop surfacing Active Memory's internal prompt; recall runs already indexed by earlier versions are pruned on the next sync, with no reindex needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each blocking recall is a sub-agent session whose transcript is the recall prompt, not a conversation. The indexer now skips these runs the way it skips cron, heartbeat and dreaming transcripts. A run is recognized by its session key (`<parent>:active-memory:<12 hex>`), or by its session id (`active-memory-<base36>-<8 hex>`) for transcript artifacts that reach the indexer with no session store entry and so no key. The key check is shared with `isPrivateConversation`, which already treated these keys as not a conversation.

## Evidence

- New tests in `manager-sync-ops.startup-catchup.test.ts`: a recall run is not indexed by a targeted sync; a recall transcript with no store entry stays out while an ordinary archived transcript is indexed; a recall run indexed earlier is pruned at startup catch-up. All three fail without the change; the no-store-entry test also fails with a key-only check.
- `manager-session-sync-state.test.ts`: recall runs are not indexable by id or by key; ordinary conversations, including ones that mention active memory, are.
- Local (Node 24.22): the touched test files pass; `tsgo` on the extensions and extensions-test projects clean; oxlint and oxfmt clean. `pnpm test:extension memory-core`: running, result to follow here.
- Live: in a deployment where 4 of the top 6 `memory_search` hits for a personal question had been recall prompts, a build carrying this change as a patch on 2026.10.3 ran 6 recall runs; afterwards a search worded like the recall prompt itself returned 0 recall-run transcripts among its top 30 hits.

Investigated and written with Claude Code; the canonical `autoreview` skill was not run (not installed here).

prs.title: fix(claude-cli): stop cache-prefix churn after child completion
prs.body:
Related: #146902

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Claude CLI prompt-cache rebuilds on managed local `claude-cli` sessions. Ordinary turns and verified child completions used different tool surfaces and system prompts, so a completion started a new cache prefix.

## User Impact

Managed local `claude-cli` turns now use one OpenClaw-mediated tool surface for ordinary turns and completions. A completion no longer switches the session between Claude's native tools and the restricted MCP surface.

**Behavior change:** on `main`, ordinary managed turns ran with `--setting-sources user` and Claude's native tools; only completion/restricted turns were isolated. All managed local turns now use the isolated path: OpenClaw's policy-filtered MCP tools, and no Claude user settings, `CLAUDE.md`/rules, auto-memory, user hooks/plugins, Chrome or extra native MCP servers. OpenClaw supplies instructions, selected skills and tools. Explicit native-tool selections, node execution, side questions and isolated utility completions are unchanged. Existing sessions take one cache miss on the first turn after upgrade.

**Configured MCP servers stay available.** Because managed turns no longer hand MCP servers to Claude natively, OpenClaw now serves `mcp.servers` (and enabled bundle-MCP servers) through its own loopback bridge as `<server>__<tool>` tools. Claude never connects to them directly; `tools.allow`/`tools.deny` and each turn's cap decide what is listed and callable, and ordinary and completion turns list the same catalog. Requester-scoped servers need a verified sender and are not offered on these turns. Thanks @holgergruenhagen and @cassthebandit for the reports.

Tool authority does not change. The `transcripts` gap noted in earlier revisions is closed on `main` by #175309 (one definition per tool; a turn without a caller gets a refusal). This branch is rebased on it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary local bundled Claude turns now reuse the existing exact mediated projection that verified completions already required (`prepare-tool-policy.ts`). Bootstrap routing runs after the final tool projection, so mediated read/write count as file access, and the native skill plugin is skipped on exact runs so selected skills stay in the prompt (`prepare.ts`). For exclusive runs, `loopback-bundle-mcp.ts` leases the session's configured MCP runtime for the run and hands its tools to the loopback grant; `resolveGatewayScopedTools` puts them through the same policy pipeline and exact grant allowlist as Gateway tools (core names win collisions). The lease is released after the grant is revoked. Docs updated.

Maintainer direction (@VACInc): keep native isolation on the managed path, with OpenClaw-owned instructions, skills and memory.

## Evidence

- Focused tests pass on `b166c1cacaf` (8 suites, 211 tests), including new `prepare.completion-tools` cases with a real MCP server: allowed (listed and callable on ordinary and completion turns, same catalog), denied by `tools.deny` (not listed), and a completion whose requester cap excludes it (not listed or callable on that turn). `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src`, type-aware lint and format pass. Local `bundle-mcp*` stdio suites fail identically on the untouched base on this host (stdio child cleanup), so they are environmental.
- **Live Anthropic, built Gateway plus real Claude Code 2.1.302** (Blacksmith Testbox, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` via `claude-cli`, WebChat `chat.send`, logging proxy in front of `api.anthropic.com`, a stdio `mcp.servers.probe` server). Flow: ordinary → `sessions_spawn` → completion → call `probe__echo` → ordinary ×2 → spawn → completion → ordinary. Base is `7badd73ed35` (includes #175309). Cache hit = cacheRead / (input + cacheRead + cacheWrite):

| turn | `main` 7badd73 | this PR b166c1c |
|---|---|---|
| first child completion | **0.0%** (35.2k written, new Claude session) | **97.7%** (0.9k written) |
| second child completion | 94.5% | **97.9%** |
| configured MCP tool call | works (Claude spawns the server) | works (`probe:KIWI`; only the Gateway spawns the server) |
| ordinary turns | 99.3–99.5% | 98.8–99.2% |
| user `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` sentinel | loaded | **excluded** |

- Request capture, parent session: `main` sends 73 tools / 42.5k-char system prompt on ordinary turns and starts a new Claude session with 49 tools / 29.3k on completions. This PR sends the same 50 tools (including `mcp__openclaw__probe__echo`) and identical system blocks on all 12 parent requests; every Claude launch, ordinary and completion, lists the probe tool.
- Correction to an earlier revision: the "0% on the ordinary turn after a completion" WebChat result came from a faulty test driver. With the fixed driver, ordinary turns after a completion hit cache on both `main` and this PR.
- The `gateway-cli-backend.live` cache probe also asserts cache reuse on the completion turn and the following ordinary turn.

AI-assisted implementation by @Marvinthebored, with follow-up work co-authored by @VACInc.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @VACInc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/13bde8a4-8871-483d-810e-9f67f6fd8bfc)
- [Scope reduction, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/d0a61139-e2e3-46b9-ba68-6536a886cb28)

prs.title: fix: browser inspect validation leaves JSON output empty
prs.body:
Related: #167252, #167294

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `browser screenshot --json` and `browser snapshot --json` return empty stdout for invalid format, mode, or numeric options, so callers cannot parse the promised JSON error.

## User Impact

Invalid inspection options now produce the CLI's standard `{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "..." } }` document and exit 1 before connecting to a Gateway. Human mode still reports the invalid option on stderr and exits nonzero, using the common CLI error renderer.

## Why This Change Was Made

Let the existing root CLI error owner render validation failures instead of exiting inside the inspection parsers. The choice parser either returns a valid choice or throws, allowing its callers to drop unreachable rejection branches. Optional numeric values remain optional.

This covers screenshot type and snapshot format, mode, limit, and depth. The two command handlers share these parsers. It does not change browser settings/resize validators, legacy inline RPC-error policy, browser execution, config, or protocol. Commander already propagates rejected action promises to the CLI; no new error renderer or dependency is needed.

## Evidence

Native built CLI on Linux / Node 24.16.0. Parent: `90127436fa45e539616c7b123a549cbd3919c725`. Clean exact head: `e449b0cd26532f6f51ab1b9f82678e95cb91d772`, matching `dist/build-info.json`. Each invocation uses isolated synthetic HOME/state/config and an independent loopback WebSocket receiver.

| Scenario | Parent | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Invalid screenshot type | Exit 1; stdout empty | Exit 1; one standard JSON error |
| Invalid snapshot format or mode | Exit 1; stdout empty | Exit 1; one standard JSON error per case |
| Invalid snapshot limit or depth | Exit 1; stdout empty | Exit 1; one standard JSON error per case |
| Invalid type in human mode | Diagnostic on stderr, exit 1 | Diagnostic on stderr, exit 1 |
| Valid ARIA snapshot and JPEG screenshot options | One correctly formed request each; response printed as JSON | Same requests and response JSON |

The independent receiver records zero connections and zero requests for all six rejected-input invocations on both versions. The two valid controls each authenticate, send the expected `browser.request`, and expose the receiver's response through CLI stdout. This proves CLI validation/output and RPC construction, not Chrome rendering or a screenshot capture.

<details>
<summary>Exact-head receipt, commands, and limits</summary>

- Claims: C1=Emit parseable JSON for all five inspection-validation failures; C2=Reject before Gateway dispatch while retaining valid request behavior and human diagnostics.
- Entry / identical command on parent and head: `node openclaw.mjs browser --url "$LOOPBACK_WS" --token "$SYNTHETIC_TOKEN" --json screenshot --type invalid`, plus snapshot `--format invalid`, `--mode full`, `--limit 0`, and `--depth -1`; positive controls use `snapshot --format aria --limit 1` and `screenshot --type jpeg`. Human control omits `--json`.
- Owner: `extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-inspect.ts` parsers and registered actions, through actual built CLI registration and the existing root error renderer. Product code and transport run unmocked.
- Before: RED, 5/5 invalid JSON invocations exit 1 with empty stdout; human/valid controls work.
- After: GREEN, 8/8 native invocations pass; 5/5 invalid JSON invocations yield the standard envelope, human failure remains stderr/nonzero, both valid controls preserve their wire requests and JSON responses.
- Readback: child stdout/stderr and exits; receiver connection count and actual WebSocket request frames. Control: 0/6 rejected invocations connect or dispatch; 2/2 valid controls connect and dispatch exactly once.
- Harness: same independent subprocess/WebSocket recorder on parent/head, SHA-256 `e4759a48a0c4db441b2fef338f120c1992d0374af9900d80a2d84adaf354b40a`.
- Tests: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-inspect.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 12 passed. Both JSON and human parser paths cover all five option families; existing config defaults, explicit timeouts, signed numeric values, request fields, and atomic output-file failure tests also pass.
- Other checks: source-scoped tsgo and typed Oxlint exited 0; oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed. Exact-head build `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts sourcePerformance` exited 0. The temporary type/lint config extends the repository extension-test config and selects changed files plus their actual source dependency closure; packaged declaration preparation was omitted for lint.

prs.title: refactor(config): trust owned preparation inputs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Config loading and writes repeat preparation checks and deep copies after their values already have an authoritative owner.

## User Impact

No intended feature, config-key, persisted-format, durability, retention, permission, Gateway protocol, dependency, or Plugin SDK change. Managed source/path/hash/secret authority, write serialization, environment rollback, canonical reread, and both real write validations remain. The standalone session-memory backend and its factory, registry, expiry, federation machinery and tests are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Config preparation repeats deep copies and reconstructs publication identity with generations and hashes even though its actual caller already owns publication authority. This area recovery uses the existing publication object as the managed environment identity, keeps the caller's current-authority checks, and removes independent preparation generations, candidate/environment rehashing and one-shot/reentrant-consumption bookkeeping.

This is a rule-11 config-area split of the wide closed z05 storage cleanup, kept separate from native resource, session-input, and reader-resource ownership changes for exact-head CI attribution.

Internal write projection uses copy-on-write ancestors and borrowed immutable leaves, then detaches the public result once. Include metadata is transferred from its exclusive producer; journal fingerprints read the input without first copying it. Session-store ownership clearing uses the existing unset owner and preserves the outward empty-agents shape. Schema model cloning happens once rather than independently for the model and its properties.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Global snapshot/preparer generations: introducing #148305/6718352a63d describes synthetic architectural supersession controls, not a cited human actual-use incident. Unsupported config/preparer reset during off-path preparation may leave the captured candidate until the next reload/restart; the actual caller still checks publication authority.
- Candidate/environment preparation fingerprints and repeated contribution checks: internal preparation receives caller-owned values; mutation of those private inputs while pending is unsupported best effort. Current caller authority is checked before and after contributions; managed environment identity still rejects a changed publication at its effect boundary.
- One-shot/reentrant preparation consumption: real callers invoke their private publication closure once. A synthetic repeated/reentrant invocation is no longer independently tracked by another state machine.
- Repeated internal deep copies: exclusive producers and copy-on-write operations already own these graphs. Unsupported private mutation of borrowed leaves is an owner bug; public source/projection results still detach once, and untrusted/persisted input parsers remain.

The numeric environment generation is not an authority removal: publication identity replaces it, including fresh identities on reset/rollback and refusal to overwrite a newer publication. The second write validation stays because stamping, native preferences and include deltas materially transform the candidate. No source-basis outward clone is removed.

The copy consolidation preserves the original [journal privacy](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111147), [completed include ownership](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/114251), [authored-parent](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/131413), [authored-value/SDK](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140579), [provider-model schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/129434), and [fixed-store ownership](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/114388) contracts. These features and fixes are not waived: public projection detachment, all keyed fingerprints, schema output isolation, include precedence, and ownership/security predicates remain.

## Evidence

Against fresh remote-main base `5b64c3d0ff539ab44a9bec2b769509e3a135c030`, this changes 15 paths: 12 production files, +86/-153 = **67 net production lines removed**. Two tests (+78/-159) include a new 37-line ownership-boundary test. One assertion allowance shrinks from two to one, with no production credit. The whole candidate is +165/-313, or 148 lines removed. Main's newer database-access handling and schema/redaction hints remain. The final-residue config packet is deliberately excluded.

Published head: `5c4ab08e8bd78dd0ee4dd76dea02f66e1c12ec4c`. Exact-head hosted CI run39090753189 completed successfully, including CI gate117568512474 and security-fast117567021764. Complete ALL/filter-all paginated census:241 completed checks,115 success/123 intentional skips/one neutral CodeQL/two superseded context cancellations; zero failed or pending. Canceled117566716791 and117566636510 are replaced by same-head successful context117566795856. Neutral CodeQL117567146001 reports17 unavailable baseline configurations and zero annotations, not a successful introduced-alert comparison. Current completed connector review6244799943 has no findings; formal and inline reviews are empty. ClawSweeper advisory review is still pending. No CI rerun, source re-push, or dispatch.

Targeted types (14 roots), type-aware lint, formatting (14 files), whitespace, official scoped assertion counts, runtime cycles (zero), and static Madge cycles (zero) pass. Only session-store ownership's count decreases, matching the exact baseline shrink. The fresh complete independent review is scoped-clean through P2, confidence 0.91, with final-source verification complete and no accepted/actionable finding. Focused proof covers 16 owner/consumer files: **262 cases pass and one local consent-preparation timeout remains unresolved**. All worker-generation verification completed. Wrapper inventory (one selected case, 18 filtered), source closure (three cases), mandatory suppression (14 cases), and final whitespace pass. No new suppression is added. Public SDK exports are unchanged; its five existing plugin-config boundary cases pass, with the broad API artifact gate left to exact-head CI.

The first seven-file group passed 137 cases (686.63s wrapper); the next four-file group passed 80 (279.90s wrapper). The final five-file selection passed 45 and failed one across four Vitest configurations (1132.29s completed wrapper): provider-model boundary five, Claw legacy fail-closed one, journal/schema 34, and public SDK five. The unchanged Claw late-registration case expired at 127505ms against its unchanged 120000ms deadline. Complete fixture, consent owner, provenance publisher, and actual config preparation were inspected: the case awaits a dynamic import and then a held mocked worker result that it explicitly resolves; current path/admission checks remain in the real synchronous publisher. No concrete cause, assertion mismatch, or baseline inheritance was established. The failure is retained, not attributed to load or relabeled green. No deadline, retry, skip, or kept assertion was changed. Tooling wrappers completed in 129.26s (inventory), 61.66s (source closure), and 178.39s (suppression); duplicate reporters are not extra coverage. The driver intentionally exits one to preserve the local timeout. Successful exact-head hosted CI does not erase that investigated local failure; no aggregate local-green or merge claim.

QA evidence records outcomes, but does not clearly separate catalog mappings from execution, missing declared proof, and evidence that cannot establish coverage.

Qualification also exposed a pre-existing ownership defect: a completed no-op binding operation could leave a prepared conversation selection invalidated.

The coverage command has one runtime implementation, exposed through the canonical report command owner. Main's CLI extraction and parity path are preserved. prs.title: fix(doctor): avoid repeated database copies in selected reports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw doctor --lint --only ...` repeatedly copied shared state between ordinary reads, adding unnecessary I/O and delay on large databases.

## User Impact

Selected reports reuse one private shared-state image for ordinary reads. Each new report sees fresh committed data, and inspection preserves the source database, WAL, and shared-memory files.

## Why This Change Was Made

Selected reports now enter the same report-owned snapshot scope as full reports, with preparation deferred until the first shared-state read. Synchronous and asynchronous readers join one retained preparation and reuse a stable source identity. The source owner retains private bytes until accepted readers drain, while preserving cancellation, fresh/current reads, and cleanup.

## Evidence

- Regression against the frozen pre-fix implementation: the selected-report case fails because its report snapshot is missing; full-report and absent-database controls pass.
- Fixed implementation: 95 tests pass across nine Doctor, shared-state lifecycle, and subagent-reader files. Coverage includes mixed sync/async acquisition, cancellation, admission, drainage, cleanup, fresh subsequent reports, and source-file preservation.
- Type-aware lint, both affected TypeScript test graphs, and the full package build pass. After the final getter-binding correction, the three report regression cases pass again.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39091559861) passes at `5555cccdfe6`, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards and the repaired wrapper inventory/provisioning paths.
- Independent review and ClawSweeper's exact-head review found no actionable issues.

Behavior proof uses real database/report harnesses; no packaged-CLI trace or production rollout is claimed.

Production changes are +185 lines, tests +325, docs +1, wrapper inventory +1. The added production logic owns lazy materialization shared by sync/async readers; extracting acquisition and cleanup keeps that ownership separate from reader transport. No config or schema version changes.

Cross-worker auth snapshots and writable plugin inspection copies require their own ownership changes and remain separate follow-ups.

Fixes: agent turns read the wrong prompt when `--message-file` names a file with leading or trailing whitespace and a trimmed-name neighbor exists.

prs.title: fix(skills): keep paired-node skill reads on delivered instructions
prs.body:
Closes #175905

## What Problem This Solves

Paired-node turns can lose access to verified skill instructions through skills_search and skills_read, including eligible skills omitted from the prompt directory.

## User Impact

Prompt references, instruction search, and whole-skill reads consume the same verified delivery for the admitted turn, even without a node filesystem bridge. Retired turns and different mounts cannot reuse it. Eligible discovery skills share the existing 8 MiB transfer budget; no configuration or schema migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing session skill-resource context and exact mount identity to bind the delivered catalog. Transfer preparation includes eligible discovery candidates, publishes delivered locations and verified instruction bytes, and removes stale host provenance. Consumers retain the delivery owner’s lifecycle checks. No authority owner or persistent cache is added.

## Evidence

The original transfer/catalog regression proves delivered prompt/search/read byte equality, changed-host/cache rejection, mismatched-mount exclusion, and retirement. Review added red-to-green regressions for prompt-omitted native node discovery and catalogs above the existing 256-item wire limit. Prompted, explicit, and pinned resources retain priority; the 8 MiB limit is unchanged.

All 62 focused transfer, resource-preparation, and workspace-resource tests pass after repair. Targeted source/test typechecks, lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. Independent Auto Review of the corrected candidate has no actionable P0–P2 findings. The original 118-test/build evidence is historical; no fresh full build or live paired-node/provider proof is claimed for the repair. Fresh hosted CI is pending.

Thanks @galiniliev for the original implementation.

prs.title: fix: preserve settled failures during relay startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: service-command readiness can report success when secret-data preparation rejects with an undefined reason.

## User Impact

Failed secret-data preparation now rejects readiness and follows the existing stop/cleanup path. Ordinary startup errors still take precedence over consequent secret-pipe errors and retain their acknowledgment and cleanup waits. No credentials, permissions, native process authority or public interface changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing Promise.allSettled status directly instead of converting rejected reasons into undefined sentinels. Inline a naming-only abort-listener removal wrapper at its two unchanged cleanup points and express the Windows terminal condition positively, bringing the touched owner within its existing700-code-line budget. Six net production lines removed; no test changes.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- No safety guard removed and no new rare-race machinery added. Both operations still settle together; startup rejection still waits for acknowledgment and confirmed cleanup before propagation, and the same catch drains output and stops the existing process owner.
- The sentinel came from ffc94d0ff056/#124081 and was moved by6caadadb/#147903. The current3ab06f/#171397 cleanup ordering is preserved. Human issue120386 supports keeping real child/tree settlement; it does not report this undefined-callback bug. No human incident is claimed for that value.
- No schema, persistence, retention, protocol, configuration, dependency or SDK contract change. Phase E standalone memory backend and its factory/registry/expiry/federation/tests remain untouched.

## Evidence

Focused baseline stopped before assertions when the actual broad cold-worker compiler appeared; no equivalent retry, baseline failure, runtime pass or candidate timing is claimed. The proposed undefined-throw regression was withdrawn because canonical lint disallows deliberately throwing a non-Error; no suppression, cast, helper/seam or delivery-owner mock was added to evade that policy. Formatting/whitespace and corrected canonical type-aware lint passed. No live native process extinction claim. Exact-head hosted CI remains the execution and broad gate.

The unchanged delivery implementation was excluded after the review helper refused its sensitive filename; no renamed copy or path-policy bypass. prs.title: fix(ui): recheck camera consent before sending frames
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A pending Chat camera capture can transmit after camera consent or source changes while awaiting preview readiness. Google Live also sends the pending frame if its track becomes muted or disabled during that wait.

## User Impact

An in-flight OpenAI frame is not transmitted after the camera is disabled, switched, muted, ended or the call stops. Google Live suppresses frames while the current track is muted or disabled and resumes its existing polling after the track recovers.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain the exact preview being captured, then check the current camera/usable-track owner immediately before sending the image. A stopped OpenAI call stays silent. Google Live keeps its polling tail when a pending frame loses track authority, so unmute recovery remains intact. No new generation manager, cancellation state machine, protocol or config change.

Net production LOC: 14 added.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None: this is camera privacy authority at the transmission boundary.

## Evidence

The test-only OpenAI disabled-camera baseline failed because actual outbound conversation.item.create contained input_image after camera disable during loadeddata wait. The existing capture-readiness fixture covers unchanged/disabled/switched/muted/ended/stopped; the earlier OpenAI-only media run passed 12/12.

The Google production baseline passed the unchanged control and failed both muted and track-disabled cases at the actual outbound-video assertion (2 failed / 1 passed, 35.72s Vitest / 59.58s wrapper). The table retains existing frame-size, tool, polling and cleanup assertions and now also proves unmute recovery.

Fresh combined focused proof passed 19/19 across both files (16.70s Vitest / 40.01s wrapper); exact-file format, runtime cycles (zero), diff checks and mandatory suppressions (14/14; 88.77s Vitest / 142.17s wrapper) passed. These are transport-boundary synthetic media tests, not real-device or live-provider claims.

Conflict integration against main `53b3334d626532f6b8c83297879cdb9546f1bac8` preserves main's consolidated Google WebSocket/session fixture and every existing frame-size, tool, polling and cleanup assertion. Both production transport patches are unchanged. Fresh focused proof passed 19/19 (19.50s Vitest / 38.92s wrapper); the official targeted UI test typecheck, four-file type-aware lint, zero runtime cycles, 14/14 suppression tests (82.83s Vitest / 106.10s wrapper) and diff checks passed. The Google test needed only formatter line wrapping, corrected and rechecked after the frozen review finished. Fresh independent integration review completed scoped-clean through P2 with no findings. Hosted CI must qualify the new exact head; prior-head evidence is not substituted.

### Hosted failure and test synchronization repair

Run `39084433565` at head `67f38a17a37b6b7bac19380dcc19fbfbe7b755fb` completed red: browser shard 6/9 failed the app-hosted link-routing case in `config-controls-visual.e2e.test.ts`, and the aggregate gate failed downstream.
