prs.title: fix(agents): retry ready context-engine turns behind old admissions
prs.body:
Refs #135628 — repairs cross-session retry starvation; historical admission retirement remains outside this PR.

## What Problem This Solves

Sixteen older unresolved session heads consume the bounded context-engine retry list. A later `ready` turn is not selected even when an independent session finishes successfully. Protecting the current accepted turn and disposing new admissions does not make the existing retry slots available to other ready sessions.

## User Impact

Ready context-engine commits can progress despite unresolved admissions in other sessions. Same-session FIFO, blocked audit evidence, engine/plugin isolation, idempotent commit, and current admissions remain intact. No historical cleanup, TTL, new queue, config/default, schema, protocol, dependency, provider-authentication, or permission change. This is a bounded part of #135628, not a claim to resolve its broader recovery request.

## Why This Change Was Made

Identify each session's oldest non-blocked row **before** filtering for readiness and limiting the retry list. Keep ownership filters on both queries and apply the same invariant to the memory-store sibling. An unresolved head still blocks later work in its own session, without consuming another session's retry slot.

The canonical owners are the existing outbox kernel and memory session store; the finalizer/drainer continues to own commit, retry accounting and acknowledgment. Existing-solutions preflight: this is a missing invariant in the current queue owner; neither an external queue nor a new plugin/library is needed. Installed Kysely aggregate/subquery types and source, database schema and executor, callers and memory sibling were inspected.

October 18 maintenance normally merges `9b707074b5f231f6976456ea7431567893fe7d1c`. The query now uses main's canonical explicit `enqueue_sequence` and typed `fn.min`; it does not restore deleted rowid helpers or alter schema. The accepted-turn regression uses main's consolidated fixture and places 16 unresolved rows ahead of the ready retry. The other stale type-check failure was in unrelated `memory-core` Worker/MessagePort test code; no contributor workaround was added there.

## Evidence

Current contributor head **`1c4293e5c87f389f7e1e634859c414465da67968`**, tree `0d1f835de572ef70426d49346ea3228277c57085`; clean checkout. Built OpenClaw **2026.10.4**, Linux, Node **24.16.0**. Build metadata records this exact head and `2026-10-18T03:08:46.938Z`.

The original acceptance RED was captured before production edits on `d4256984ac0435d8f5225e0d1706235b798f1e9e`: an independent successful CLI turn left the ready backlog behind 16 unresolved admissions. The October 18 exact-head GREEN replays the same immutable native harness after integrating main:

```text
node context-outbox-live-proof.mjs <checkout> <new output directory> green
```

Three real `openclaw.mjs agent --local --agent main --session-key ... --message ... --thinking off --timeout 60 --json` processes use isolated state, a normally registered context-engine fixture and a loopback HTTP/SSE model endpoint. Every invocation returns the expected current answer and exits 0.

| Native scenario | Authoritative SQLite/engine-ledger readback |
| --- | --- |
| Warm control | 1 real engine commit; 0 outbox rows |
| A new turn's genuine engine commit fails once | 16 historical admitted rows + 1 ready row; recorded attempt count 1 |
| Independent successful turn triggers normal drain | 3 engine commits; ready row acknowledged; 16 historical rows retained byte-for-byte |

The recovered ledger contains the exact closed-turn user/assistant payload. **1/1 ready backlogs drain**, compared with **0/1** on historical RED. **16/16 historical admission hashes remain identical**. Fixture initialization represents reported persisted state; it does not claim to recreate the original crash. No external model account, channel recipient, production state or Mac environment is used.

GREEN completed `2026-10-18T03:16:14.687Z`; three CLI invocations took 30.60 / 31.45 / 29.58 seconds. Harness SHA-256 `c217e70233acdfc99d10341774048fc4c549f91ac5b5e62459673376dc261a3b`; current receipt SHA-256 `d5f2e9e303906f3fe41cbd2635a7a9f1e108542959c3c6f872b836f68cd04ac0`. Local logs/databases/receipts retained; the table supplies sanitized observations, without claiming a hosted artifact.

Against merged main: **5 files**; production **+25/-9, net +16**; tests **+83/-9, net +74**. No contributor generated/lock/release-changelog changes. Added production lines implement the shared session-head invariant. No speculative index/schema expansion.

prs.title: refactor(sessions)!: give each session one controller for turns, queues, and Stop
prs.body:
Current head: `a13051580be07f42a0e1d1112fff14785f878343`, integrating main `aa11c6c05c5c0ee276db2bcd516932495632f300`. The one maintenance-fixture conflict is resolved; main’s Gateway reload and UI cleanup changes are retained. The integration passes 133 maintenance/Gateway cases, 72 UI cases, core/UI and affected test typechecks, targeted lint, and committed Codex review (three partitions, scoped-clean P2). Fresh extension/SDK consumer typechecks, surface, and public-subpath checks pass. The final API comparison, build, and native/restart refresh are running. The detailed measurements below are explicitly the preceding `67d955408a0ad` checkpoint until these complete.

Replaces #165957. Rebuilt from Josh Lehman’s controller cutover and the Team controller review and repair findings. Josh retains co-author credit.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes queued input, Stop, and restart recovery choosing different owners for the same session, leaving work stuck or interrupting its replacement.

## User Impact

Each physical session has one controller for admission, queued input, steering, Stop, and settlement. Cancellation captures the intended source and invocation. A successor cannot take over while the original producer or preparation still owns execution; required terminal persistence remains joined.

**Three immediate breaking changes for third-party harness and plugin authors:**

1. **Session-keyed `setActiveEmbeddedRun(...)` requires host admission.** Register inside the host-provided `runAttempt` callback and retain its exact cleanup function. A session key, agent ID, or plugin-created operation does not grant admission. Unadmitted registration throws `AgentHarnessPreflightError` with code `SESSION_CONTROLLER_ADMISSION_REQUIRED` and migration guidance. The five public arguments remain. Sessionless registration and queueing remain supported.
2. **Plugin RPC context removes mutable `chatAbortControllers` and `chatQueuedTurns`.** Keep `api.registerGatewayMethod(...)`. To compose session operations, declare `contracts: { gatewayMethodDispatch: ["authenticated-request"] }` and use `dispatchGatewayMethod` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/gateway-method-runtime` for the existing session RPCs. Dispatch retains caller authority; this declaration adds no scopes. Removed-property access throws `PluginCapabilityRemovedError` with code `PLUGIN_CAPABILITY_REMOVED`, the capability name, and migration guidance. No replacement mutable map is exposed.
3. **`AgentTurnStartOwner.observe()` renames `expiresAtMs` to `startDeadlineAtMs`, without an alias.** Update `onStartOwner` consumers. A finite value is the execution-start deadline; `null` means a live wait without a finite deadline; an absent field means no deadline is available. An undefined observation means the captured owner is no longer current. Stop watching once `executionStarted` is true. The observation grants no authority and is not a runtime timeout. Old-property access throws `PLUGIN_CAPABILITY_REMOVED`; unrelated `expiresAtMs` fields are unchanged.

All bundled consumers migrate together. See the [harness migration](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-agent-harness/attempt-runtime) and [SDK migration guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-migration#session-keyed-harness-registration). External usage is unknown: ClawHub queries were incomplete or returned HTTP 404; the bundled inventory does not establish zero third-party consumers.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main’s [reply operation registry](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5b64c3d0ff539ab44a9bec2b769509e3a135c030/src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.operation.ts#L61) and [queued RPC cancellation map](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5b64c3d0ff539ab44a9bec2b769509e3a135c030/src/gateway/chat-queued-turns.ts#L195) select ownership separately. Lifecycle admission and native registration add further state that can disagree. The cutover removes the old reply-run registry family, Gateway queued-turn map, and lifecycle admission/lock owners. Transports use the controller’s operations; transcript writers, durable recovery registries, worker placement, and global capacity keep their existing responsibilities.

The controller is keyed by physical session ownership. It retains producer, input, delivery, and cancellation custody through settlement, including per-invocation ACP cancellation. Gateway shutdown and terminal-event lookup follow the canonical Gateway owner through nested resolver wrappers without invoking retired execution resolvers. This fixes the reproduced extra recovery turn after a private child completion: the unchanged restart/prompt test now observes exactly five provider requests and preserves every prefix assertion.

Channel Stop and native `sessions.abort` acknowledge accepted cancellation after required cleanup and terminal persistence, while the controller fences successors until raw producer cleanup settles. Standalone effects retain the existing requester and side-run selection rules. Queued delivery and asynchronous native injection retain exact source custody through settlement.

**Preserved public contracts:** ACP `cancelSession` retains run/instance/owner filters and exact nested-invocation cancellation. Completion delivery retains `phases`, both reason values, `requireDirectDelivery`, and phase-aware durability: a delivered direct result with `phases: []` remains non-durable. `retainFailureUntilComplete()` remains a documented no-op because the controller retains failure unconditionally until completion. Sessionless native queueing, opaque generation identity, exact registration cleanup, and recovery-result fields remain. Queued-delivery cancellation notifications and lifecycle diagnostics are retained. Asynchronous legacy steering failures produce operator warnings without automatically replaying an uncertain effect.

Native requester liveness keeps the physical database observation through nested same-store admission, preventing an extra private completion from being queued after a child finishes. Worker transcript preparation preserves the logical admission target while the captured physical source continues to own database access and authority. Independent queued follow-ups leave their predecessor’s async placement scope and obtain fresh admission; nested calls within the same turn still reuse the live scope. Both corrections have independent failing-before/passing-after boundary regressions (9 worker transcript/memory cases and 51 follow-up/placement cases).

Current restart semantics are preserved: capture the original source, revalidate live authority before effects, keep explicit cancellation cancelled, and let recovery inspect unknown side effects. The mailbox in this PR is process-local. Durable queued-input recovery and further subagent/cron continuation remain follow-on work. The independent worker-abandonment repair is excluded.

Recovery predecessor insertion advances the mailbox sequence counter so later input cannot bypass a preparing tail. A real reserve/join/injection regression fails before this owner correction and passes afterward.

Private completion retries retain the original raw prompt with their dispatch identity in the existing durable wake record. A descendant finishing between attempts cannot change the bytes under an accepted request key. The field is optional in the existing JSON payload; there is no new table, column, schema version, or scheduler. It is removed with the wake or when its identity resets. Older already-dispatched wakes without the saved bytes retain strict mismatch refusal; rollback may discard the new field. Queued Stop separately joins cancellation notification and accepted terminal persistence while raw preparation continues to hold source, registration, and authority custody until it drains.

This remains one atomic controller/caller/SDK cutover: splitting ownership migration would leave competing schedulers. The composition audit distinguishes production, tests, moves, and generated outputs; no unclassified changes remain, and no full-file reversions remain among the 626 newly audited incoming-main paths. 

| Scope | Paths | Added | Deleted | Net |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Production | 671 | 40,381 | 28,333 | +12,048 |
| Tests/helpers | 1,151 | 78,167 | 37,852 | +40,315 |
| Documentation | 26 | 783 | 125 | +658 |
| Tooling | 7 | 27 | 84 | −57 |
| Total | 1,855 | 119,358 | 66,394 | +52,964 |

These are physical line counts against the pinned main base, including moves, formatting, and fixture migrations—not a count of new logic. Git detects nine moves at 30% similarity and four at 50%; net totals are unchanged. The controller family contains 55 production files. The final incoming-main audit accounts for 626 paths: 591 match main exactly and 35 have reviewed integrations. All 24 incoming additions and 28 deletions match main; all 27 retired production owners remain absent. The earlier correction hashes remain verified. No unrelated category or unclassified path remains; the main-equivalent session-row-scope change was dropped.

## Evidence

Final source: `67d955408a0adffbd4fd85076fd4176a56694c2c`. Main base: `5b64c3d0ff539ab44a9bec2b769509e3a135c030`.

Sanitized Team journal evidence: line 976005 recorded `queueSize=62 pendingReplies=17 embeddedRuns=31`; line 976200 still recorded `56/15/28`. Lines 976326–976375 contain five terminal-write owner refusals. These motivated the ownership repair; they are not a claim that every queue entry had the same cause.

The final integration passes 531 cases across 19 focused files in 324.19s, production typecheck, affected test type graphs, targeted lint, and formatting. All 12 original regression controls pass on the final tree (48.36s). The queued-Stop repair passes 140 owner and Gateway cases. Seven corrected replay cases pass, including SQLite reload, private input-byte stability, revoked authority, and bounded public retry exhaustion; ten earlier passing replay cases remain applicable. The preceding integration passed 18 Gateway cases and 15 maintenance protection cases. These are recorded-source results, with unchanged-input proof reused rather than presented as a fresh full-tree sweep.

The refreshed SDK API comparison on `67d955408a0ad` against the exact main base passes (326.12s): 201 affected export signatures or reachable types, no added/removed exports or entrypoints, and no additional unapproved public break. SDK exports, public subpaths, surface checks, extension types, and SDK consumer types pass. Fresh extension lint passes after preparing 14,009 declaration files (127.02 seconds); no limits were raised. Extension and SDK-consumer typechecks pass on the final commit (14.67s and 10.22s).

The final canonical build completed runtime output, declarations, plugin output, runtime postbuild, and UI in 240.44s, with its only failed phase at the private-QA public-entry declaration size check: 5,503,156 bytes against a 5,340,536-byte cap. The exact main control fails the same unchanged check at 5,478,498 bytes. No cap was raised. The native freshness owner confirms the produced runtime is current without rebuilding; this qualifies runtime proof but does not make the full build pass.

Committed-source Codex review is scoped-clean at P2: the complete cutover through `3d3301c9653a` completed 43 passes; incremental reviews of `3d3301..b46337` and `b46337..e52af5` each completed one pass with full relevant owner context and no accepted/actionable findings. The committed main integration then completed 13 further partitions, all scoped-clean at P2. Together these incremental reviews cover all subsequent source changes; they are not presented as another 43-pass whole-branch run.

Both restart E2E files pass all six cases with zero skips (251.79 seconds): managed restart, raw SIGTERM/SIGKILL, second restart during recovery, multi-session recovery, explicit cancellation, and revoked authority. Source and the full runtime artifact manifest remain unchanged.

Final native process proof passes on `67d955408a0ad`: requester completion under both placements (68.85s), paired-node approved execution/file reconciliation/disconnect handling (180.10s), and required-native same-session queued input through public RPC (112.51s). Original assertions and budgets are unchanged, and the full runtime manifest remained identical after each run. The two earlier passing QA scenarios—completion direct fallback and empty-result recovery—remain source-qualified: their configuration does not enable the required-worker scope changed by the final correction. Exact-head PR CI is pending.

The existing 403-file focused selection is retained where its inputs remain source-qualified. Subsequent integration and CI failures were reproduced and repaired at their owners, with clean-main controls used for attribution. Filtered tests do not count as executed. Earlier qualified checks passed the 12 regression controls, 12 context/compaction/progress cases, 10 native cancellation/cleanup cases, five selected test-type graphs, production typecheck, and targeted lint. The original prompt/restart test passed unchanged (135.25 seconds), including exactly five provider requests and every prefix assertion. The four review corrections passed 113 registry cases, 116 Stop cases, six selected authority cases, core typecheck, and seven qualified type graphs (six in a mixed run, followed by the corrected seventh). The correction checkpoint also passed 79 Stop cases, 29 mailbox cases, two prepared-media queue controls, and all three eager-import controls after adding the omitted extraction dependency. These are recorded-source results, retained where their inputs remain unchanged.

**Accepted evidence limits:** Responses fixture observer is corrected, but the unchanged producer five-second timeout remains unresolved locally; no equivalent main fixture exists and no inherited-failure claim is made. Historical HTTP/auth-removal and Codex private-launcher failures retain their recorded prior-main attribution. Current main contains a later Codex fixture repair; those historical results are not presented as fresh failures of current main. A prior native same-session run reported an unavailable pending-input database/schema; a later diagnostic passed that assertion and exposed the independently repaired placement-scope bug. The earlier unavailable-store result remains unexplained; a passing rerun alone is not attributed to that repair. CI results will be updated after the exact-head run completes.

Representative commands:

```sh
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --ci-graphs-json '["core-test-messaging","core-test-gateway-server","core-test-gateway-methods"]' --concurrency 1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/gateway.prompt-cache.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json <changed-files>
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts
OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/gateway-process-shutdown-recovery.e2e.test.ts test/gateway-subagent-restart.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

prs.title: feat(providers): add Bifrost provider and allow anonymous self-hosted gateways
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

[Bifrost](https://getbifrost.ai) is an OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway that unifies 20+ providers with failover, load balancing, and virtual-key governance. OpenClaw ships bundled providers for LiteLLM, SGLang, and vLLM, but not Bifrost — so operators had to configure it by hand in `models.providers`.

## What This Changes

**New bundled provider** (`extensions/bifrost`), built on the LiteLLM provider shape:

- Interactive setup asks for the gateway base URL, then whether a virtual key is needed, then lists the models the gateway advertises via `/openai/v1/models` and defaults to the first.
- Discovery failures name the reason (`HTTP 404`, `empty model list`, `unreachable`) before falling back to manual entry, and a config change during discovery aborts before credentials are sent to a stale endpoint.
- Non-interactive setup accepts `--custom-base-url`.

**Provider artwork**, which every other user-facing bundled provider ships and Bifrost initially did not:

- `extensions/bifrost/assets/icon.png` — 512×512, the official Apache-2.0 mark inverted to dark-on-white so it matches the other bundled provider icons, which are all light-background (verified: LiteLLM, SGLang, vLLM and OpenRouter icons are 0% transparent with a dominant white background). Geometry unchanged.
- `extensions/bifrost/assets/activity.svg` and `ui/public/provider-icons/ProviderIcon-bifrost.svg` — OpenClaw-authored gateway glyph (many upstreams converging on one routed endpoint), `currentColor` so it renders on light and dark. Neither Simple Icons nor LobeHub ships a Bifrost glyph, so these are drawn in-repo and labelled in-file as *not* a Bifrost trademark, matching the precedent where SGLang's activity icon is an unbranded server box.
- Registering `bifrost` in `PROVIDER_ICON_NAMES` also fixes a visible defect: `resolveProviderIconName("bifrost")` returned `null`, so the model picker was rendering a **letter "B"** avatar for this provider.

Provenance is pinned to upstream commit `a30e57dd` in `ATTRIBUTION.md`, following the format of the existing third-party entries.

**Two design decisions worth review:**

1. **Base URL is `http://localhost:8080/openai`**, Bifrost's OpenAI-compatible surface, not the core `/v1` API. Both serve chat completions, but only the `/openai` surface makes discovery and inference share one base URL. Bifrost's own OpenAI SDK and OpenCode guides use this path.

2. **Keyless gateways use `auth: "none"`.** A fresh Bifrost has no authentication — that's the documented zero-config default — so setup records the provider as explicitly anonymous rather than storing a key that resolves to nothing. This reuses the existing explicit-no-auth owner (`resolveExplicitProviderNoAuth`) instead of adding a second mechanism. Re-running setup for a URL change keeps an already-configured key.

**Shared-helper change:** `promptAndConfigureOpenAICompatibleSelfHostedProviderAuth` forced a non-empty API key, which pushed SGLang and vLLM users toward a placeholder value for servers that accept anonymous requests. It now accepts an empty key and records `auth: "none"`, matching what the config schema already models. The Bifrost provider does not use that helper — it uses the LiteLLM path, which already prompted for a URL and a key.

**Config-surface budget, raised deliberately:** the Bifrost plugin schema grows the plugin config surface from 4693 to 4714 keys (+21), which trips the `config-docs` baseline ratchet. I regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` and raised the budget in `config-baseline.counts.json` rather than leaving it failing. The +21 is the provider's own declared schema — a base URL, an optional virtual-key auth profile, and the provider's setup metadata — not a new core config surface. Core stays at 2565 and channel at 4043, both unchanged. If a maintainer would rather the provider ship without declaring those keys, say so and I will trim the schema rather than hold the budget increase.

## Evidence

Verified against a running Bifrost gateway at `http://bifrost` (port 80), with isolated state via `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

**Discovery through the production code path** (`discoverOpenAICompatibleLocalModels`, the real function the plugin calls):

```
base url passed to discovery: http://bifrost/openai/v1
discovery kind: success | rows: 12
first row: {"id":"Nvidia/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b","object":"model","owned_by":"nvidia","created":735790403}
rows reporting context_window: 6/12
```

**End-to-end agent turn** through the shipped CLI, provider configured with `auth: "none"`:

```
winnerProvider: "bifrost"
winnerModel: "Vercel/poolside/laguna-s-2.1-free"
result: "success",  fallbackUsed: false,  runner: "embedded"
finalAssistantMessageRawText: "LOCAL_BIFROST_OK"
```

`openclaw models list --provider bifrost --refresh --json` returns the nested-slash key `bifrost/Vercel/poolside/laguna-s-2.1-free` with `available: true`.

### Two findings the live gateway surfaced that mocks did not

**1. Model IDs are multi-segment.** Bifrost returns IDs like `Nvidia/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b` and `Vercel/alibaba/qwen3.7-flash`, so refs become `bifrost/<vendor>/<provider>/<model>`. Verified this round-trips exactly: `parseProviderModelRef` splits on the **first** slash (`packages/model-catalog-core/src/model-catalog-refs.ts:54`), and `normalizeAgentModelRefForConfig("bifrost/Nvidia/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b")` returns the input unchanged. The committed tests cover the single-slash case, so I noted this rather than claiming the nested case is regression-guarded.

**2. The gateway echoes a different model string than requested.** Requesting `Vercel/poolside/laguna-s-2.1-free` returns `"model": "poolside/laguna-s-2.1-free"` — the `Vercel/` prefix is a routing selector the gateway drops when reporting the resolved upstream model. OpenClaw surfaces this as `modelRouteChange: "Model route changed: bifrost/Vercel/… → bifrost/poolside/…"`. **This is expected behavior, not a defect**: `agent-run-terminal-receipt.ts:66` reports `effective.responseModel || effective.model`, so it is faithfully relaying the gateway's echo. Worth documenting so operators don't read the notice as a misroute.

### Parity control

The `--refresh` path prints `Model discovery could not refresh all providers`. I checked whether Bifrost caused it by pointing the **proven LiteLLM provider** at the same gateway: identical warning, identical single-authored-model result. It's pre-existing behavior in an isolated state where credential-less bundled providers can't refresh, not a Bifrost defect.

### Live authority-chain proof on an enforcing gateway

The earlier anonymous proof ran against a keyless gateway, which cannot demonstrate the authentication defects. I repeated it against the same Bifrost deployment after enabling **Enforce Virtual Keys on Inference**, so it now rejects unauthenticated inference with `401 virtual_key_required`. That makes the defect observable rather than merely arguable.

Non-interactive onboarding with the key supplied **only through `BIFROST_VIRTUAL_KEY`** — no `--bifrost-api-key`, no inline `apiKey` — which is precisely the case the old `hasKey` check missed:

```jsonc
// config written by onboarding
"models": { "providers": { "bifrost": {
  "baseUrl": "http://bifrost/openai",
  "api": "openai-completions",
  "models": []            // non-interactive preset: discovery-backed
} } },
"auth": { "profiles": { "bifrost:default": { "provider": "bifrost", "mode": "api_key" } } }
```

No `auth` field is written, and the credential lands in the profile. Agent turn through the shipped CLI:

```
winnerProvider: "bifrost"
winnerModel: "Vercel/poolside/laguna-s-2.1-free"
result: "success"        fallbackUsed: false      runner: "embedded"
authMode: "auth-profile"
finalAssistantMessageRawText: "KEYED_OK"
```

`authMode: "auth-profile"` is the load-bearing line: it shows the credential was resolved and sent, not silently stripped.

Now inject `auth: "none"` into that same row — which is exactly what the pre-fix code wrote — and re-run:

```jsonc
"bifrost": { "baseUrl": "http://bifrost/openai", "api": "openai-completions", "auth": "none" }
```

```
virtual key is required. Provide a virtual key via the x-bf-vk header.   (x8)
401
no winnerProvider, no fallbackUsed
```

Remove the field again and the same turn returns `RECOVERED_OK` with `authMode: "auth-profile"`. So the single `auth` field is the whole difference between a working and a failing credential: **live failure with the marker, live success without it.** This is the authority-chain evidence the review asked for, and it only became obtainable once the gateway stopped accepting anonymous requests.

The third instance has the same live shape. Starting from a row carrying `auth: "none"` alongside an active
`bifrost:default` profile, re-authenticating with the key and **no** `--custom-base-url` clears the marker and the turn
succeeds:

```
before:  models.providers.bifrost.auth = "none"   (profile bifrost:default present)
action:  onboard --non-interactive --auth-choice bifrost-api-key      (no --custom-base-url)
after:   auth = <unset>
turn:    winnerProvider: "bifrost"   authMode: "auth-profile"   fallbackUsed: false
         finalAssistantMessageRawText: "REAUTH_OK"
```

### Authentication defects found in review, and their regression proof

ClawSweeper's review found that Bifrost onboarding could discard a supplied credential. I confirmed both against source before changing anything, and traced the runtime consequence to `resolveExplicitProviderNoAuth`, which is terminal on `auth: "none"` and strips the `Authorization` header via `applyLocalNoAuthHeaders`.

1. **`applyBifrostConnection` merged `...existing` and only ever *added* the marker.** Re-running interactive setup against a gateway that now has a virtual key inherited `auth: "none"` through the merge and through `applyBifrostModelConfig` (`applyProviderConfigWithMergedModels` spreads `existingProviderRest`). The keyed branch now clears the marker, which is how the `omlx` and `llama-cpp` gateway providers already drop anonymous state once a credential exists.
2. **`runNonInteractive` inferred anonymity from `--bifrost-api-key` and the inline provider `apiKey` only**, while the delegated method also resolves `BIFROST_VIRTUAL_KEY` and existing profiles. A key in either of those made the wrapper write `auth: "none"`, which the delegate then preserved while saving the key it had just resolved. The ad-hoc check is removed: the delegated method owns the decision and returns `null` when no credential resolves, so this path always applies one.
3. **`runNonInteractive` still skipped the fix when `--custom-base-url` was absent.** My own refactor added an early return that handed the delegate the original config, so `applyBifrostConnection` never ran and an earlier `auth: "none"` survived — the delegate saved the key, the preset spread `existingProviderRest` through, and the marker stayed terminal. Caught in the Revision 2 re-review. This path always applies a credential, so a gateway already on file counts as configured: the base URL now resolves from the flag *or* the existing row, and either way the credentialed update runs.

Base-fail/head-pass evidence — both new tests fail against `4d2478c4a6` and pass against `838b5e17cc`:

```
pre-fix  (4d2478c4a6):  Tests  2 failed | 16 passed (18)
post-fix (838b5e17cc):  Tests  18 passed (18)

pre-fix failures:
  × clears a previous anonymous marker once the operator supplies a virtual key
  × stays credentialed when the key resolves from a profile rather than a flag
```

`resolveExplicitProviderNoAuth` is core-internal with no Plugin SDK subpath, so the tests assert its precondition — that `auth` is not `"none"` whenever a credential is available — rather than importing across the extension boundary.

### Gates on this head

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, and the `tsconfig.core.test.plugins-platform.json` lane — pass
- `oxlint` on all changed files — clean
- `oxfmt --check` — clean; `format-docs --check` clean (1365 files)
- `docs:check-links` — 15646 links, 0 broken; `docs:check-config-examples` — pass
- `generate-config-doc-baseline.ts --check` — pass after the budget raise above
- `pnpm plugins:inventory:gen` — no diff (artwork is not part of the generated inventory)
- Tests: **106 across the 9 Bifrost/SGLang/vLLM/shared-setup test files** (Bifrost 19 on this head), 561 package-manifest + extension-runtime-dependency contracts, 65 boundary invariants, 126 manifest-registry + bundled-manifest contracts, 31 provider-icon/public-asset — all pass

### Known Gaps

- **The UI browser-test project could not run locally.** Its Playwright Chromium binary is absent from this machine's cache (`chrome-headless-shell` not installed), so that project reports `no tests` with a launch error. This is environmental and unrelated to the change; every other project in the same run passed (3217 UI tests + 166 + 65). Worth a CI confirmation rather than trusting the local run for that project.

- **Full `pnpm lint` fails on three inherited `max-lines` violations** in files this branch does not touch: `extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-warm-image-store.ts` (718/700), `extensions/oc-path/src/cli.test.ts` (1125/1000), `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-coalescing.e2e.test.ts` (1028/1000). None are in `config/max-lines-baseline.txt`. Every file changed here lints clean.
- **Discovery contributed no additional models under `--refresh`.** The live catalog/discovery refresh path did not merge the gateway's 12 models into the model list; only the authored model appeared. LiteLLM against the same gateway behaves identically, so this is existing merge-mode semantics rather than something introduced here. The onboarding path *does* call discovery directly and receives all 12. This is the `models.mode=replace` half of #121584 ("Auto-discover all models when configuring a provider"): this PR delivers the interactive-configuration half, and does not attempt to close that issue — it carries `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr` and `needs-product-decision`, so the refresh-merge semantics are a product decision, not a side effect of adding a provider.
- **Related pre-existing bug, not fixed here, and no issue tracks it:** the same helper still passes `initialValue: params.defaultBaseUrl` for its base-URL prompt, so a typed URL appends to the prefilled default under the shipped wizard. This is the defect #173164 fixed for LiteLLM, still live for SGLang and vLLM. Fixing it changes their behavior, so it is left as a follow-up rather than bundled here. I can file it as a separate issue if that is wanted.
- Interactive onboarding was not driven interactively over a pty; the base-URL and model prompts are covered by tests through the registered plugin.
- **Proof the review asked for that this head still does not carry.** I want to be explicit rather than let the checklist imply otherwise:
  - ~~*Authenticated onboarding against a real gateway.*~~ **Now closed** — see the authority-chain proof above: the credential reaches the gateway (`authMode: "auth-profile"`) and the anonymous marker alone flips the same turn from `KEYED_OK` to `401`.
  - *Revocation at egress.* The narrower half is still open: showing that a revoked or replaced setup authority blocks a credential-bearing request **before** any network effect. Deactivating the virtual key mid-flow would show Bifrost refusing it, which proves Bifrost's enforcement, not OpenClaw's. The OpenClaw-side proof needs a stale credential held locally while authority changes underneath it.
  - *The key is sent as `Authorization: Bearer`, not Bifrost's native `x-bf-vk`, and this must not be "fixed" with a static header.* **Now documented for users**, not just in this body: `docs/providers/bifrost.md` carries a support matrix stating plainly that a legacy key (no `sk-bf-` prefix) or a gateway with `auth_config.is_enabled` will not work, plus the `x-bf-vk` provider-row configuration to use in that case. Verified against a local listener that the configuration sends both headers, and that an unset env reference sends the literal `${BIFROST_VIRTUAL_KEY}` — which Bifrost rejects with `401` while ignoring the valid `Authorization` on the same request.

    **`x-bf-vk` takes absolute precedence over `Authorization` for virtual keys.** Bifrost does not fall back once `x-bf-vk` is present:

    | Request | Result |
    |---|---|
    | valid `Authorization` + empty `x-bf-vk` | `401 virtual_key_required` |
    | valid `Authorization` + literal `${BIFROST_VIRTUAL_KEY}` | `401 access_not_found` |
    | valid `Authorization` alone | `200` |

    So sending both is not a hedge — it is "`x-bf-vk` decides, `Authorization` ignored." Declaring `request.auth` or `headers` with a `${BIFROST_VIRTUAL_KEY}` reference would therefore send an empty or unresolved `x-bf-vk` whenever that variable is unset — which is every interactively-entered key — converting a provider that works today into one that returns `401` by default.

    **`x-bf-vk` must carry the resolved credential or be absent**, and no current seam can place a profile credential there: `SecretInput` accepts only `env`/`file`/`exec`/`store` refs with no auth-profile source; `apiKeyHeader` is hardcoded to the `api-key` header and only participates in Model Setup resume; `wrapStreamFn` explicitly excludes credential material; and `prepareRuntimeAuth` receives `apiKey` but can only return a replacement credential and base URL.

    Fixing this properly needs a narrow provider capability — declare a credential-header name, host places the resolved credential there — which is a Plugin SDK boundary expansion rather than a config change. Filed as #175583 rather than bundled here, so the shared-SDK decision can be made on its own merits and Bifrost's bundling question stays separate. The shipped path stays on `Authorization`, which is correct for `sk-bf-` keys with HTTP auth off; a legacy key without that prefix, or a deployment that later enables `auth_config.is_enabled`, would still fail.
  - *Shared SGLang/vLLM anonymous inference.* The shared helper's optional-key change is covered by `provider-self-hosted-setup.interactive.test.ts`; I have not run a live anonymous turn through SGLang or vLLM.
  - *Before/after model-picker screenshots.* The artwork is a visual change and the repo's gate wants inspected captures in the PR; none are attached yet. I rendered the assets at 16/28/64/96px locally to verify legibility, but a picker capture needs the UI browser-test project, which cannot run on this host — Playwright's `chrome-headless-shell` is absent from `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/`. CI's `checks-ui-e2e` is the available path.

### Data-model compatibility

No stored data changes shape. The provider adds a new `models.providers.bifrost` row and reuses the existing `auth: "none"` field that `ModelProviderConfig` already declares, so there is no migration and no change to how an existing config is read. The one behavior change to existing consumers is the shared helper's optional key, and that is the documented intent: a gateway that was previously forced to store a placeholder key can now record `auth: "none"` instead.

prs.title: fix: preserve refreshed context windows after stale model discovery
prs.body:
Closes #175739

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: refreshed model context-window metadata disappears when an older model-discovery request finishes after a configuration reload.

## User Impact

User impact: completed context-window refreshes survive older discovery successes and failures. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the currently tracked discovery promise may publish its staged cache. Superseded loads still settle normally, without new state, generation counters, cancellation, or retries.

PR #172669 deliberately accepted stale discovery metadata as a simplification. This narrowly changes that tradeoff with one existing-promise comparison; broader optional-prewarm overlap behavior remains unchanged.

## Evidence

- Both new regression cases fail before the fix: an older success or failure erases the refreshed 222,000-token entry.
- All 14 context-lookup lifecycle/provider tests pass. Targeted agent-root types, typed lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass.
- Rechecked the unchanged two-file patch against refreshed main fdd81a25; full-context independent P0–P2 review found no issues.
- Proof exercises the production cache owner with deferred catalog I/O, not a live Gateway reload. Required PR CI remains the broad pre-merge gate.

## Worked on by

- @gideonpraise

prs.title: fix(projects): preserve clone targets after inspection errors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Project cloning treats every failed target lstat as proof that the target is absent. On a non-missing filesystem error, Git can subsequently refuse an existing checkout and the clone-failure path can recursively remove it. A canonical URL lease and registry miss do not prove physical absence.

## User Impact

Only ENOENT permits cloning into the target. Other inspection failures stop before parent creation, Git execution or cleanup with the existing clone_failed classification and filesystem-access/retry guidance. Existing target_exists behavior, credentials, live admission, network retry, registration and process settlement remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a narrow silent-failure bug repair, not removal of a speculative guard. The original feature #121818/8876528f introduced the all-errors-to-absence callback. Its full body describes Gateway-managed cloning and same-URL serialization, not a human target-probe incident; no actual user data-loss report is claimed. Nine net production lines added (+10/-1), plus two boundary tests; no new helper, error kind, option, schema or protocol shape.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- No security or data-preservation guard is removed. Failure to inspect the destination is no longer silently treated as absence: operators receive an actionable retryable clone_failed result instead of risking cleanup of a preexisting checkout. The error message does not expose raw Git output, credentials or filesystem details.
- Separate failed-clone cleanup swallowing and uncertain-process artifact retention remain unchanged, explicit follow-ups. This patch does not add a blanket ignore comment, new retry or finally deletion.

## Evidence

- Complete runtime, materialization-before-checkout-lease ownership, determining Gateway failure mapping and spawn/temp-helper contracts inspected. The existing ProjectCloneError Gateway shape is retained; state/schema/durability/retention/permission behavior is unchanged.
- Fresh complete two-file/10-dataset independent review scoped-clean P0-P2/0.98 with final source verification at02bc89cc. Exact candidate source/test blobs9bc0d399/7674192b; formatting241ms and whitespace passed. Simplification/test-audit pass keeps one real sentinel preservation regression and one genuine-absence positive control, using fixed command-boundary fixtures rather than a mocked clone owner or duplicated Gateway/registry replay.
- Root at53b3334d after named main type-gate repair; all13 determining source/test/dependency/instruction paths are unchanged from the reviewed02bc candidate. Exact reviewed production blob matches; the only post-review test change mechanically renames a catch parameter to fix no-shadow, with no assertion/type/behavior change. Current format checks passed17ms/52ms and whitespace passed. Targeted two-root types completed with36 unchanged parse5/MCP dependency diagnostics, byte-identical to the prior Git area; NOT type PASS. Canonical type-aware lint passed after that owned test-only shadow fix; current suppression guard passed14/14 (67.13s Vitest/93.56s wrapper). Exact-head hosted CI pending. Existing errno owner imports only the fs-safe path leaf, so the one added import cannot introduce a runtime cycle; no public SDK surface changes.
- Actual isolated baseline owner attempt stopped130 BEFORE assertions when prohibited broad worker compilation started; only the verified owned wrapper was signaled and all seven tracked processes drained. No baseline reproduction, red/green, head runtime PASS or real data-loss reproduction claimed, and no equivalent cold retry. No live network clone, credentials or native platform proof claimed. Hosted exact-head CI is the runtime/broad gate under this host's local proof budget; no local broad suite/build/E2E.
- Phase E standalone session-memory backend/factory/registry/expiry/federation and tests untouched. No new suppression, timeout, retry, skip or baseline expansion.

Release-note context: preserve existing managed project data when a clone destination cannot be inspected.

prs.title: refactor(infra): stop replaying native Git failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Low-level Git error handling repeats the same synchronous HEAD lookup after all baked fallbacks failed, and treats native ref-lock/CAS errors as transient transport failures. Neither needs a second recovery owner.

## User Impact

Cache the existing unknown commit result after the first Git probe and baked metadata fallbacks. Return settled native ref contention immediately. Keep bounded DNS/socket/eligible HTTP/object-transport retry, the original deadline, native ref mutation queue, beforeRun/startRun credential and authority admission, cancellation, uncertain-process refusal, explicit partial-clone hydration and leased publication effects.

## Why This Change Was Made

Existing low-level Git area of the wide preservation family:13 net production lines removed (+4/-17), tests9 net added (+15/-6). No new helper, state, public signature or import edge. Simplification pass retained only the duplicate synchronous probe and the private ref-replay classifier; the changed tests retain cache/fallback contracts and move lock/CAS cases into the no-replay table.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Git becoming readable between two synchronous probes in one invocation may now leave the cached commit unknown until LRU eviction or restart. The #39712/ca5e introduction and later dd747 isolation retained a baked-first fallback tail; no separate human incident requiring the duplicate same-call probe was found in that provenance. Environment overrides, first Git probe, baked build/package metadata and loaded-artifact stamp semantics remain.
- An external/manual ref writer or existing native lock may cause a settled fetch failure that requires the caller/user to retry. #167691/4ad94b56 fixes the real config.lock registration defect through the retained mutation queue; its external-ref replay coverage is synthetic, not a separate human actual-use report. No lock deletion, second queue or new retry is added. A cannot-lock-ref diagnostic stays nonretryable even when accompanied by the generic missing-object message.

## Evidence

- Complete changed owners and suites, Git execution/native queue, publication transport and determining clone/worktree/authority frames inspected. Actual publication mock commandResult omits termination, so those fixtures are not claimed as transient-classifier proof. The dedicated Git network suite is primary; publication authority/content/settlement tests protect separate contracts.
- Fresh complete four-file/16-dataset independent review scoped-clean P0-P2/0.98 with final source verification. All23 determining source/test/instruction paths unchanged from mirror f84d to current02bc. Root's four source blobs exactly match reviewed909f32cd/f575277a/87939b88/c593a37a. Formatting28ms and whitespace passed. No new import edge or cycle introduced.
- Focused two-owner runtime attempt stopped130 when the actual broad worker compiler started; only verified owned wrapper39172 was signalled and all nine known descendants drained. All14 commit-resolution assertions were observed passing, but there is no complete two-file/suite PASS or network assertion result. No equivalent cold retry, causal red/green, load-cause or performance claim. Changed-file cost/completed runtime proof remains for hosted CI. Targeted four-root types retain36 unchanged parse5/MCP dependency diagnostics, byte-identical to the preceding area; NOT type PASS. Canonical four-file type-aware lint and current14-case suppression guard passed. Exact-head hosted CI pending. No live-provider or platform pass claimed.
- Mandatory current suppression guard passed14/14 (77.35s Vitest/99.11s wrapper). Phase E standalone session-memory backend/factory/registry/expiry/federation and tests untouched. No config, schema, protocol, dependency, durability, retention or permission change. No new suppression, timeout increase, retry, skip or baseline expansion.

Release-note context: simplify redundant low-level Git failure handling while retaining real transport recovery and write settlement.

prs.title: fix(gateway): render Claude CLI history turns once
prs.body:
Closes #123792

## What Problem This Solves

Claude CLI history could render one assistant turn twice in the Control UI and Android app. The rich imported turn appeared first with native tool cards. A flat persisted copy appeared below it.

Telegram delivery is not affected because it does not render merged history.

## Root Cause

The CLI runner persists one synthetic assistant aggregate with `api: "cli"` and `idempotencyKey: "cli-assistant:<runId>"`. The Gateway also imports the bound Claude transcript as native text and tool-call blocks.

The old merge compared one message at a time. It could not match one aggregate such as `text one\n\ntext two` to several imported blocks from the same turn.

Underneath that, nothing linked the two shapes at all. Only the producer sees both the flattened aggregate and the native records it came from, and it recorded no relation, which left every reader inferring one from text, provider and timing.

## Fix

The producer records the relation, and the merge resolves it instead of inferring one.

- Run settlement already resolves the native record id of a run's terminal assistant message, for resume. It now records that id, with the native session that owns it, on the aggregate it persists: `cliNativeTurn: { cliSessionId, terminalRecordId }`, a declared field on the transcript message contract.
- The Gateway history owner groups imported assistant messages into turns and indexes them by the native record their last message came from.
- An aggregate is only ever replaced by the turn it names, in the native session it names.
- The remaining text comparison is a completeness check on that identified pair, not an identity test: a trimmed or partially imported turn no longer covers the aggregate's text, so the aggregate is kept as the durable copy.
- Imported native blocks are unchanged, including `toolcall` IDs, names, and arguments.

This removes the five-minute window for aggregates, the text-and-provider keyed index, the ordered pairing and the nearest-turn selection. The resolver uses result identity so a one-for-one replacement still counts as an import.

**Fail-open by construction.** An aggregate that names no native turn is never replaced. That covers every record persisted before this field existed, every backend that writes no native transcript, and every run whose terminal record was not reported. The consequence is deliberate: the duplicate stays visible for history already on disk until those sessions produce new turns. Removing those would require exactly the text-and-time inference this design rejects, because no rule built from text, provider and time can tell a true duplicate from a distinct same-text turn when either history is partial.

The async snapshot reader projects any JSONL line past 1 MiB through a bounded worker. That projection rebuilds the entry from a fixed field list, so the turn-boundary facts the grouping reads have to survive it; an importer/resolver parity regression covers both readers over the same oversized transcript.

The rebase onto current `main` integrates #130463 and #133316, the commits that have touched `cli-session-history.merge.ts` since this PR's original base. #133316's prepared-facts refactor is the base — its injected identity key, its `localImageMediaCounts` map — and the aggregate/turn matching is layered on top, so its tests and this PR's regressions both hold. Preparing the whole import ahead of the merge loop is gated on the session actually holding a persisted aggregate, so a session without one keeps #133316's lazy, skip-on-identity path unchanged.

## Evidence

Head: `8a7447409ff9c3ae3118a029116e1ab7a83fa2c6`, rebased onto `43e9a3d817` (current `main`). The evidence below was measured on `b538e9752c`, the same four commits before that rebase; the rebase carried them across 409 upstream commits with no conflicts and no diff change.

Current-main reproduction, re-run on that exact base: applying this PR's regression file to `86b6ec0afa` and leaving main's merge owner in place fails 11 tests.

```text
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  11 failed | 77 passed (88)
```

Four of them:

- `replaces a persisted aggregate with the imported native turn blocks` — expected a length of 4, got 5. The persisted aggregate remains beside the imported native blocks.
- `keeps a skill instruction row inside the turn it belongs to` — expected 0 aggregates, got 1. #130269 already hides the skill instruction row on that base, and the turn still renders twice.
- `projects an oversized skill instruction row exactly as the sync reader does` — expected 0 aggregates, got 1. The same defect through the async snapshot's bounded worker projection.
- `keeps the only local aggregate when the import holds a different turn with the same text` — the aggregate is deleted. This is the crossed partial-history loss path, and it is the reason this PR resolves aggregates by recorded identity rather than by text and time.

Focused proof on the head:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts
88 passed

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-pages.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server.chat-history-cursor.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/embedded-gateway-stub.test.ts \
  src/agents/cli-runner/cli-run-transcript.test.ts
273 passed (3 shards)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/lib/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts \
  -t 'detects tool messages by toolcall content blocks'
1 passed | 85 skipped
```

One of those, `carries the recorded native turn from the CLI producer through to the merge`, drives the real producer, the real SQLite store, the real display projection, the real JSONL importer and the real resolver, so a field lost at any of those seams fails the suite instead of silently disabling the fix.

Repo checks on the head: `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` clean, `run-oxlint src/gateway src/agents` 0 warnings and 0 errors, the assertion-safety and max-lines ratchets OK, `oxfmt --check` clean. The `cli-session-history.merge.ts` assertion-safety baseline entry shrinks `6 → 1`.

The resolver test reads a real Claude JSONL fixture. It asserts the retained imported content is exactly the text block plus `{ type: "toolcall", id: "toolu_1", name: "Bash", arguments: { command: "pwd" } }`. The UI normalization test confirms that shape remains a native tool card.

Repeated-text benchmark with 24,000 imported turns and 24,000 aggregates. Measured on `6e25b0ae`, an earlier head, and not re-run since:

| Matcher | Three samples | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Previous claim forests | 95–112 ms | 72,000 native messages, 0 aggregates |
| Ordered turn pairing | 80–95 ms | 72,000 native messages, 0 aggregates |

The Telegram fallback run, also on `6e25b0ae`, recorded one deterministic direct-message turn because this history-only change is not Telegram-visible. The bot typed and returned `OPENCLAW_E2E_OK`; the mock provider received one `POST /v1/responses`.

## Control UI Proof

Measured on two live Gateways, each built from source and serving its own `chat.history` from **the same store**: a copy of a production OpenClaw agent store holding 878 persisted `cli-assistant:<runId>` aggregates. Only the commit differs, and the Control UI is byte-identical on both sides because this PR changes 0 files under `ui/`.

| | commit |
| --- | --- |
| base | `86b6ec0afa` |
| head | `b538e9752c` |

The turn was produced by **running a real agent turn through the head build**, not by editing a store: Claude CLI 2.1.250 on the `claude-cli` backend, prompted for a line of text, then `pwd` through Bash, then a closing sentence — the two-text-blocks-around-a-tool-call shape this bug needs. The producer recorded the relation on that run:

```json
"idempotencyKey": "cli-assistant:be40a3bc-c230-4e59-bb83-c5fa6e8846c9",
"cliNativeTurn": {
  "cliSessionId": "881503c4-fa93-4da4-b514-b94ba6afd637",
  "terminalRecordId": "5d666065-18d8-4a2c-8651-d2dfa6e330c9"
}
```

`terminalRecordId` is the turn's terminal native assistant record.

| rendered rows | `86b6ec0afa` | `b538e9752c` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| imported native blocks | 3, incl. the `Bash` card | 3, unchanged |
| persisted aggregate `msg:id:687e4295-…` | present — the turn renders twice | absent |
| total | 6 | 5 |

The durable fallback holds on that same head: a session whose aggregate predates `cliNativeTurn` keeps its 6,781-character aggregate, because it names no native turn. In that store 1 aggregate carries the relation and 877 do not, and none of the 877 can be replaced.

Screenshots and the full measurement are in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/124543#issuecomment-5477930396), including what the capture does not cover: that store holds no `Skill` turn, so the skill case stays covered by the regressions rather than by a capture.

prs.title: refactor: simplify state lease heartbeat liveness protocol
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The state-lease heartbeat maintains synchronous ACKs, an odd/even native-occupancy counter and a shared completed-request witness alongside its actual durable lease and typed request/reply transport. They add blocking work and duplicate ownership reads.

This is a fresh-main heartbeat-only area recovery from closed storage cleanup donors #174230/#173527. The earlier PR175408 is closed and unmerged; its historical proof is not current-head proof. Its PostgreSQL Git-backup timeout now has an exact matching scheduled-main failure, recorded below, so that historical failure no longer justifies dropping this family.

## User Impact

Healthy maintenance, independent renewal and ordinary delayed replies keep working. Synchronous protected effects check the local lifetime and exact current durable lease owner once. A worker exit before its queued parent callback is delivered is observed best-effort through ordinary delivery or expiry.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one finite operation deadline bounded by the observed lease expiry, ordinary request-ID correlation and the existing independent renewal/native-cleanup owners. Remove the sibling admission pump used only by the blocking ACK loop. Preserve startup handoff, slow-storage contention, current durable authority and accepted-write/native settlement.

Explicitly preserve #175588's long native-COMMIT lease fix: ownerFence slot/buffer size, holdOwnerFence/holdWriteFence, unchanged owner/grant renewal inside managed transactions, PostgreSQL distinction, commit/rollback settlement, wakeup and warnings. The real-worker commit/owner-replacement/grant-replacement/rollback regression remains unchanged. No schema, columns, stored shape, durability, retention, permissions, public configuration/protocol/SDK, dependency or Phase E change.

Pinned base8cf4ec4d8aa0d1096a9987a898f53b79e22c1e60. **113 net production lines removed**, five production paths +69/-182. Five test/support paths +44/-160; total10paths+113/-342. Rule11 area split, overlapping donors counted once.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Synchronous ACK (#157696/#164615): it detects worker exit before ordinary queued callback delivery. Those PRs provide mechanism/synthetic reproduction provenance, not a cited human incident requiring this extra protocol. Current durable ownership remains the effect boundary; delayed exit notification waits for delivery or expiry. Independent renewal and final current-row checks remain.
- Native-occupancy witness (#157696): the one-second watchdog needs odd/even progress to avoid false loss on slow storage. Replace the short watchdog and witness together with the finite operation/lease bound. No unbounded operation or changed lease duration; unusually late replies fail visibly.
- Completed-request witness (#168214): it makes a reply survive delayed delivery under that short watchdog. Ordinary replies now have the same finite operation bound without a second completion channel. Matching requests, current expiry/lost refusal and a fixed ceiling still apply.
- Sibling admission pump: only serviced the removed synchronous ACK wait. Ordinary asynchronous admission and actual last-member native settlement retain their owners. A hypothetical future synchronous wait must not rely on an undocumented sibling pump.

## Evidence

Fresh complete-area independent review is scoped-clean through P2, confidence0.94, with successful final source verification; the full report/status were personally read. Review included current durable-effect owners, the unchanged long-COMMIT owner/grant/rollback regression and current consolidated tests. No accepted/actionable finding remains. Source review is not runtime proof.

Focused 11-root types, ten-file type-aware lint and formatting passed. Runtime proof passed47 selected cases:23 lifetime/async-maintenance,16 real heartbeat, all4 unchanged long-COMMIT regressions,1 Gateway startup/cleanup-custody case and3 project cancellation/outcome cases. Gateway38 and project12 filtered cases are not coverage. The four-file invocation completed in1364.74s, Gateway selected wrapper369.60s and project selected wrapper563.67s, each with successful final worker-generation verification. Much of this loaded-host wall time was compiler/import preparation, not test execution. No timeout, retry or skip change. Runtime and static/Madge cycles both passed0.

Final wrapper inventory passed1 case (18 filtered;143.58s wrapper), source closure passed3 (76.23s wrapper), mandatory lint suppressions passed14 (215.67s wrapper), and whitespace passed. The complete serial proof script exited0. Duplicate tooling reporters are counted once. Changed-path classification was inspected with check-changed --dry-run; printed broad commands were not executed. No broad local suite, whole-graph typecheck, build or E2E was run. Hosted CI on the exact published head remains the broad gate.

Historical attribution, not a new-head gate waiver: scheduled main39036754999@f9d61d37da210dea4671b5a725021e65259fdcee, PostgreSQL infra117408256358, failed the exact same src/infra/database-engine/git-backup.postgres.test.ts217 case, "keeps distinct scopes, preserves degraded agents, and prunes removed Matrix stores without losing extras or history", at120000ms as old PR175408/run39023411673/job117369878191. prs.title: feat(logs): filter tailed records by minimum severity
prs.body:
Closes #146978

## What Problem This Solves

Operators using the root `openclaw logs` command cannot select a minimum severity for the bounded gateway log tail without an external filter.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an optional `--level` presentation filter at the existing emission owner, reusing the canonical log parser and severity ordering. The source request, byte/line bounds, cursor, source selection, follow/reconnect behavior, metadata, notices, and errors remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators can use `openclaw logs --level warn` to display warning, error, and fatal records in plain or JSON output. Unclassified records are omitted only when filtering is requested; omitting the option preserves existing output.

## Evidence

### October 18 integration and fresh product-head validation

- Product head: `37ffa851ddccde13036fef2d14293acb7d6ae184`; real merge parents: `86706b13f5ee96a4397121589a2d95023ed96cfa` and `0e19fca34b53db04b0adcc719976763a6900087c`. Contributor commits are preserved; normal push, no force-push.
- Normal Node 26.1.0 build completed; the clean build stamp matches this SHA. Focused tests and changed-file type-aware lint passed. Independent adversarial source review passed. Hosted CI is tracked separately.
- The original acceptance-red scenario and SHA remain below. This integration reruns GREEN and legal / must-not-fire controls through the same existing collector; prior-head results are not relabeled as a new baseline.

Full owned logs/receipt are retained at `/media/vdc/0668001470/cache/user-tmp/alix-logs-integration-1bCnZL/receipt.json` (SHA-256 above). prs.title: fix(database): refuse FIFO recovery manifests without blocking startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A FIFO without a writer at `recovery/database-port/manifest.json` blocks the synchronous recovery guard before it can reject invalid content. `openclaw gateway run` never reaches readiness or the existing recovery guidance. This concerns malformed local state; normal port operations do not create FIFOs, and no remote attacker capability is claimed.

## User Impact

The invalid artifact now refuses promptly and remains intact for recovery. Missing manifests still allow startup; malformed regular JSON retains the same refusal. No config/default, protocol, schema, migration, dependency, authorization, or supported valid-manifest behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add the existing native `O_NONBLOCK` flag to the canonical manifest reader's no-follow open. The existing JSON/schema refusal handles the resulting invalid input. Startup, recovery intent validation, publication, and archival share this owner; no pre-stat race, alternate storage, helper, or production timeout is added.

Existing-solutions preflight: the current filesystem API already provides this flag; a plugin or new dependency is unnecessary. Read the Node filesystem flag/types contract and the startup/Gateway/recovery callers. The Linux reproduction does not establish a macOS/Windows result.

October 18 maintenance merges `9b707074b5f231f6976456ea7431567893fe7d1c` normally, preserves the upstream test-fixture cleanup, and retains the bounded FIFO regression. It removes the obsolete exact-filesystem-call assertion that main removed; it does not restore that test. No history rewrite.

## Evidence

Current contributor head: **`878d93b06c0058575feffcbce1c3a63c2daeb5ec`**; tree `f167650e4c733479b1433a9fbdd4ca324db8bfa0`. Clean checkout. Built OpenClaw **2026.10.4**, Linux, Node **24.16.0**; `dist/build-info.json` records this exact commit, built `2026-10-18T03:05:02.032Z`.

The original acceptance RED was captured before production edits on `3d9637ef6301e6823f621cf7ed419dd2a75e8c61`: a native FIFO hung for 15.08 seconds until the harness killed its own child. Missing-manifest startup and regular malformed-JSON controls worked. That historical RED is separate from the October 18 exact-head GREEN, completed `2026-10-18T03:11:14.718Z`:

| Real built CLI scenario | Current head readback |

| Malformed regular JSON `{` | Exit 1 in 2.21 s; existing recovery/Doctor guidance; bytes unchanged |

Three isolated native `openclaw.mjs gateway run` processes use synthetic homes/configurations/state and loopback ports. No filesystem mocks, helper-only startup, external provider, channel recipient, or production environment. **0/1 FIFO startups hang; 2/2 malformed artifacts remain intact.**

prs.title: fix(skills): fail skill upload installs that lose their install lease
prs.body:
Fixes #173076

## What Problem This Solves

An operator could be told a skill upload installed successfully even though the install had already lost the lease that authorized it. Confirmed lease loss now fails the install instead of being folded into success.
- Problem: `withCommittedUpload` renews its install lease on a heartbeat, but the heartbeat collapsed every renewal outcome to `undefined` in `src/skills/lifecycle/upload-store.ts`. `skillUploads.renew` resolves `false` when the lease was expired or re-owned, so the process no longer owned the upload it was installing — yet the install kept running and resolved successfully.
- Solution: read the renewal result. A confirmation that the lease is gone is latched and fails the operation once the install callback and its accepted renewal have settled; a rejected renewal stays retryable.
- What changed: `src/skills/lifecycle/upload-store.ts` (heartbeat result handling plus the post-install settlement check) and two regressions in `src/skills/lifecycle/upload-store.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: the install callback and its `remove()` control, the lease `claim`/`renew`/`consume`/`release` operations, transient-renewal tolerance, the SQLite schema, and the consume-path `not-owner` check.

## Why This Change Was Made

The heartbeat discarded a value-returning operation's result, so one module disagreed with itself: `remove()` already throws `SkillUploadRequestError("upload install lease is no longer active")` for the same lost lease. The confirmed-loss case now reports it the same way.
- Best fix: latch the boolean, stop renewing once ownership is gone, and decide after joining the accepted renewal so a heartbeat landing as the install finishes cannot be missed.
- Alternative: treating every renewal rejection as terminal was rejected — it would delete the intentional retry tolerance for transient database failures, and a rejection does not prove the lease was lost.
- Risk / non-goals: the install callback cannot be interrupted mid-flight, so a confirmed loss is reported when the install settles rather than pre-empted, and a long run of rejected renewals is still tolerated. No live Gateway run was performed.

## User Impact

A skill install that loses its upload lease now fails with `upload install lease is no longer active` instead of reporting `Installed <slug>`, so callers and operators can retry instead of trusting a lease-less install. Healthy installs and transient renewal errors behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

Confirmed lease loss now rejects instead of resolving (real SQLite lease expiry, real heartbeat, real `skillUploads.renew`); the same test fails on unpatched source:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/skills/lifecycle/upload-store.test.ts -t "renewal"
 ✓ |infra| src/skills/lifecycle/upload-store.test.ts > skill upload store > fails an install whose renewal confirms the lease was lost 3625ms
 ✓ |infra| src/skills/lifecycle/upload-store.test.ts > skill upload store > keeps a rejected renewal retryable instead of failing the install 3196ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed | 15 skipped (17)
```

The same regression on unpatched source reproduces the reported defect (install resolves while ownership is gone):

```text
 FAIL  |infra| src/skills/lifecycle/upload-store.test.ts > skill upload store > fails an install whose renewal confirms the lease was lost
Error: expected upload request error
 ❯ expectUploadError src/skills/lifecycle/upload-store.test.ts:200:9
 ❯ src/skills/lifecycle/upload-store.test.ts:728:5

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 16 skipped (17)
```

Behavior matrix:

| Renewal outcome | Lease state | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| resolves `true` | owned | install resolves | install resolves (unchanged) |
| resolves `false` | expired or re-owned | **install resolves** | install rejects `upload install lease is no longer active` |
| rejects | unknown | retried next heartbeat | retried next heartbeat (unchanged) |

Surrounding coverage and static checks:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/skills/lifecycle
 Test Files  3 passed (3)      Tests  87 passed (87)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-methods/skills-upload.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/skills.install-upload-policy.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)      Tests  24 passed (24)

$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services.json   # no diagnostics, exit 0
$ node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/skills/lifecycle/upload-store.ts src/skills/lifecycle/upload-store.test.ts   # clean
```

What was not tested: no live Gateway install was run, and the install callback is not interrupted when loss is confirmed — the failure is reported when the install settles.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted (agent-authored on behalf of @xiaopan-xydt). The reporter's static audit and the ClawSweeper review were the starting point; the renewal/heartbeat, consume, and cleanup paths in `upload-store.ts`, `upload-store.kernel.ts`, and `upload-store.sqlite.ts` were read directly, and the regression above was written to fail on unpatched `main` before the fix was applied. I understand the code: the heartbeat only runs while the install is active, and the `false` result of `skillUploads.renew` is the same lease-loss signal the consume path already treats as fatal.

prs.title: fix(models): retain plugin generation during catalog projection
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Deferred model-catalog refresh rebuilds configured facts outside the prepared plugin generation, allowing registry normalization to resolve a different runtime owner.

## User Impact

Catalog refresh keeps the metadata and executable registry captured for that prepared runtime. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bind every synchronous projection invocation to the captured-generation scope, covering configured normalization, both materializations, and final identity deduplication. Existing inventory, native-model, route, and context-capacity owners remain unchanged; no new cache, state, or public contract is introduced.

## Evidence

The extended deferred-refresh regression fails on the incoming PR head: a differing ambient generation leaves equivalent aliases as duplicate catalog rows. The complete-projection scope repair passes all 60 focused projection, configured-catalog, publication, and scoped-refresh tests, including both catalog collections and caller-scope restoration. Targeted lint/format, core and owning-test typechecks, and diff checks pass. A broader test-typecheck command timed out on a later unrelated shard; no fresh full broad-gate result is claimed.

Independent Auto Review of the corrected candidate has no actionable P0–P2 findings. Fresh hosted CI is pending; no new live provider proof is claimed.

Thanks @galiniliev for the original implementation.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/5d7025af-d81f-4e71-b504-2cf18e52b736)

These links cover review fixes and preparation; the original implementation predates this review.

prs.title: fix(plugins): preserve credential scope during static model discovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Static manifest model discovery drops a provider’s declared credential scope when creating its discovery descriptor.

## User Impact

Providers declaring plugin-owned credentials retain that scope during configured static catalog discovery. Agent-scoped providers keep their normal scope. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the canonical provider owner index to populate static descriptors and retain its existing conflict handling. Credential resolution remains with the existing owner; no runtime provider execution or new state is introduced. The fix adds eight production lines and a 49-line regression fixture.

## Evidence

The original port reports red-to-green scope regressions, 32 passing focused discovery/credential-owner tests, targeted checks, and a full build. Exact-head hosted CI is green. Native preparation completed without changing the source head; no additional live provider-auth proof is claimed.

prs.title: feat(agent): read piped messages in ordinary agent turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary agent turns cannot consume a piped prompt through the existing message-file option; exact `-` is treated as a filename. Closes #167076.

## User Impact

Scripts can pipe multiline prompts into ordinary agent turns without managing a temporary file. Exact `-` now means stdin; use `./-` or an absolute path to address a literal dash file. The existing 4 MiB byte budget, strict UTF-8 and empty-input checks remain in force.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the stdin convention already used by `agent exec` to ordinary turns, through their shared message-input admission. Extract the existing descriptor-compatible file reader intact, add bounded byte-stream input only for exact `-`, and update option help and both agent guides. No new flag, default, config, protocol, permission or dependency.

## Evidence

- Normal Node 26.1.0 build completed; the clean build stamp matches this SHA. Focused tests and changed-file type-aware lint passed. Independent adversarial source review passed. Hosted CI is tracked separately.
