```js
    const file = path.join(root,'scratch.txt');fs.writeFileSync(file,Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('before '),Buffer.from([0xff]),Buffer.from(' after')]));
    const a = await run('invalid-file',['cron','scratch','proof-job','--file',file,'--expected-revision','0','--json']);
    const writes = a.records.filter(r=>r.method==='cron.scratch.set');
    if (phase === 'red') {assert.equal(a.terminal.code,0);assert.equal(writes.length,1);assert.equal(writes[0].params.content,'before \ufffd after');}
    else {assert.equal(a.terminal.code,1);assert.match(a.stderr,/valid UTF-8/);assert.equal(writes.length,0);}
    const good = ' Exact 中文 😀\r\n';fs.writeFileSync(file,good);
    const control = await run('valid-file-control',['cron','scratch','proof-job','--file',file,'--expected-revision','0','--json']);assert.equal(control.terminal.code,0);assert.equal(control.records.find(r=>r.method==='cron.scratch.set')?.params.content,good);
    receipt.readback = {invalidWrites:writes.length,validWrites:control.records.filter(r=>r.method==='cron.scratch.set').length,validContent:control.records.find(r=>r.method==='cron.scratch.set')?.params.content};
    for (const kind of ['scratch','payload','trigger']) {
      const prefix=kind==='scratch'?'before ':'return {text:"before ';
      const suffix=kind==='scratch'?' after':' after"}';
      const bytes=Buffer.concat([Buffer.from(prefix),Buffer.from([0xff]),Buffer.from(suffix)]);
      for(const source of ['file','stdin']) {
        fs.writeFileSync(file,bytes);
        const location=source==='file'?file:'-';
        const args=kind==='scratch' ? ['cron','scratch','proof-job','--file',location,'--expected-revision','0','--json'] : kind==='payload' ? ['cron','add','--name','proof','--every','30m','--script',location,'--session','isolated','--json'] : ['cron','add','--name','proof','--every','30m','--trigger-script',location,'--system-event','changed','--session','main','--json'];
        const bad=await run(`invalid-${kind}-${source}`,args,source==='stdin'?bytes:undefined);
        const mutations=bad.records.filter(r=>r.method==='cron.scratch.set'||r.method==='cron.add');
        if(phase==='red') {assert.equal(bad.terminal.code,0);assert.equal(mutations.length,1);const text=kind==='scratch'?mutations[0].params.content:kind==='payload'?mutations[0].params.payload.script:mutations[0].params.trigger.script;assert.equal(text,prefix+'\ufffd'+suffix);}
        else {assert.equal(bad.terminal.code,1);assert.match(bad.stderr+bad.stdout,/valid UTF-8/);assert.equal(mutations.length,0);}
        const valid=kind==='scratch'?'\uFEFF Exact 中文 😀 \ufffd\r\n':' return {text:"中文 😀 \ufffd"}\r\n';
        fs.writeFileSync(file,valid);
        const legal=await run(`valid-${kind}-${source}`,args,source==='stdin'?Buffer.from(valid):undefined);
        assert.equal(legal.terminal.code,0);const observed=legal.records.find(r=>r.method==='cron.scratch.set'||r.method==='cron.add');assert.ok(observed);
        const text=kind==='scratch'?observed.params.content:kind==='payload'?observed.params.payload.script:observed.params.trigger.script;assert.equal(text,kind==='scratch'?valid:valid.trim());
      }
    }
  }
  receipt.result='PASS';
} finally {
  for (const client of wss.clients) client.terminate();
  await new Promise(resolve=>wss.close(resolve));await new Promise(resolve=>server.close(resolve));
  receipt.cleanup='All owned CLI processes joined and both loopback listeners closed; only isolated synthetic HOME/config/state/input files were used. No production Mac, channel, provider or session was accessed.';
  assert.deepEqual(fingerprint(),receipt.ownerSha256,'Product source changed during proof');
  for(const [file,sha]of Object.entries(receipt.builtArtifacts))assert.equal(digest(fs.readFileSync(path.join(checkout,file))),sha,'Build metadata changed during proof');
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(root,'receipt.json'),JSON.stringify(receipt,null,2),{mode:0o600});
  console.log(JSON.stringify({result:receipt.result ?? 'FAILED',receipt:path.join(root,'receipt.json')}));
}

```

All recorded inputs and credentials are synthetic. The collector closes its listeners and joins every CLI child. It retains only the isolated fixture directory/receipt for inspection; no existing config, channels, processes or Mac environment are accessed.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Scope, alternatives, test cost and compatibility</summary>

- 7 changed files. Production LOC +64/-57; test LOC +55/-0; docs/ratchet LOC +4/-3.
- Existing-solutions/competition preflight: Existing agent-exec stdin and accepted #93351/#101442 file-input owners were read. Earlier #103028/#94423 proposals are closed; this preserves existing descriptor semantics instead of reintroducing their file restrictions. No viable ordinary-turn stdin competitor was found in all-state semantic/path searches.
- Sibling coverage: Ordinary Gateway and embedded routes share input admission; agent exec already has its separate stdin convention. Existing descriptor-reader symlink/procfs/FIFO, file-size and file-error regressions remain in the ordinary owner suite.
- Config/protocol/schema/security/upgrade impact: no config shape, protocol/schema, permission, dependency, migration or upgrade-lifecycle change. Only the described CLI input behavior changes.
- Tests and static checks passed on byte-identical candidate source. The final proof was actually rerun on the clean product commit above. Earlier RED receipts used the same base, CLI scenarios and input bytes. The collector's later portability/fingerprint-only change did not alter acceptance logic.

</details>

</details>

prs.title: feat(code-mode): send current replies without an extra turn
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Enables one host-authorized reply to the current conversation from an OpenClaw Code Mode cell without an extra model turn, while preventing retained or substituted tools from borrowing later authority.

## Why This Change Was Made

The host owns the exact private tool instance, source invocation, writer lifetime, and cancellation. Same-cell terminal delivery is available only to a runtime advertising per-result terminal handling. Acknowledged or ambiguous delivery suppresses duplicate ordinary final delivery.

Permission refresh shares one atomic admission at the private completion record while rebuilding tool instances. Reservation precedes awaited preparation. Producer-recorded non-dispatch permits a retry only after preparation settles before adapter handoff; post-handoff ambiguity retains the one-shot fence. Original errors and late acknowledgements retain their meaning.

The follow-up composes real outer-loop completion with delivery and persistence. It addresses prepared custom activity whose captured parent was not passed to append, and outer-completion leaf drift after a legitimate delivery mirror. Shared repairs live in PR1; this layer supplies real-loop regression coverage and integration wiring. A newer user, writer, or lifecycle must not be adopted by the old invocation.

## User Impact

The model receives explicit **OpenClaw Code Mode** framing, positive **JavaScript/TypeScript** guidance, and deterministic **one-cell composition**. Observation is reserved for genuine ambiguity or authority conflicts. Retained tools cannot reuse closed or replacement authority.

## Stack And Scope

All five PRs remain draft. Frozen integration base: `fe1c715de7eccc5ce1ec9f7de6b2eb64c6248ad1`, observed on September 11, 2026. This exact target is fixed for the proof; it is not a claim to track later moving main.

| Layer | Current Frozen-Main Candidate Head |
| --- | --- |
| [PR1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/119055) | `2ad458b0cbfdcd4c327d11ceb5169464b53b7f54` |
| [PR2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/135969) | `6db9a7156affee1c9ee182bcf41d61e93f40d195` |
| [PR3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/119056) | `a64afa8675245ff71ab3d954fecb625ae9b5ec56` |
| [Slack](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/142151) | `7e7df513bddb6ee15f342e3fe1cd4cb94afe9d6b` |
| [PR4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/119057) | `708809cdc2cdbb09c1184ce74838fbf283b71419` |

Base branch: `fix/code-mode-slack-transport-stack-20260908`; candidate layer base: `7e7df513bddb6ee15f342e3fe1cd4cb94afe9d6b`. Final composed candidate tree: `ad32f67773244e30f12d07d8d634d1584a17630f`. The stack has 43 signed commits and spans 359 changed paths against frozen main `fe1c715de7eccc5ce1ec9f7de6b2eb64c6248ad1`. The inherited full-runtime wake repair and completion-order regression are placed in PR3; downstream layers are replayed in their existing ownership order. All 41 prior author/message/date records and reviewed replay patches are preserved after the test insertion. Reviewed main-composition adaptations are described below. Temporary diagnostic-helper commits are excluded. Focused exact-tree proof is recorded below; this is not full-stack, type, release or moving-main qualification.

PR1 owns shared repairs, fixture/setup/lint and filesystem-race corrections, and stack-local npm/Workshop prerequisites; these prerequisites are not already supplied by main. PR3 owns R's released-ownership fixture; Slack owns B's Enterprise physical-transport tests.

Frozen main already contains the canonical native locale repair from [PR 143928](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143928), commit [`89a1abd12ff92d78e0a5d2cf22641968dce828ea`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/89a1abd12ff92d78e0a5d2cf22641968dce828ea). The duplicate stack commit was omitted only after ancestry and all 44 generated postimages matched; canonical contributor credit remains in main.

This layer owns A, real foreign-session construction rejection with zero effects and unchanged state; C, native HTTP upload allow/revoke/lost-completion cases; and real embedded outer-loop tests for persisted activity, permission refresh, once-only mutation/reply, and next-turn isolation. The shared helper uses the bundled plugin public surface, without a new boundary allowlist or production export.

TaskFlow, streaming, and loader/models-set diagnostics remain separate from causal fixes. Self-yield passed 2/2 on `64fa`; the OTel caller-context fixture repair still needs new-head execution. The predispatch diagnostic captures bounded request digests and one best-effort history summary only after the unchanged two-request assertion fails, then rethrows the original failure. No request filter, assertion, deadline, or production behavior is relaxed; the extra request's cause remains unclassified.

`createToolSurface` and `commitProviderTranscriptPrefix` stay independent. Requester-yield filtering precedes final wrapping; plugin namesakes and public inventory cannot supply private terminal authority. The per-instance one-shot latch remains intentional.

## Evidence

### Full Runtime Wake Retirement And Frozen-Main Integration (2026-09-11)

Release note: full runtime close/restart now retires stale heartbeat wake work with its discarded runtime payloads. Ordinary handler replacement still preserves pending work. The repair adds lifecycle fencing, terminal waiter settlement and cancellation checks before resumed preparation, session mutation, typing and dispatch; it adds no empty-wake skip, timeout, retry or public API.

The inherited owner mismatch was reproduced on signed `59d7b211646336d042e4a5275cdcdf1d54278f00`: both deterministic close/restart cases failed at the intended stale successor-call assertion ([before run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34583859669)). On diagnostic-backed `5789c87d38da11dac66c907ec350f5b19e52bbc0`, all 24 lifecycle cases and the unchanged allowed/cancelled/retained Gateway prefix passed ([repair run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34584891169)); retained notice and durable-state assertions were reached. That diagnostic tree recorded 2/0/0 physical POSTs with complete bounded correlation and cleanup. Those physical-count facts apply only to that diagnostic tree.

The diagnostics-free composed tree `615c58eb2676faa936ef121fed674be0c3b59e88` separately passed the same 24 lifecycle cases and original Gateway prefix ([clean run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34586174932)). All selected cases ran with zero automatic retries; the canonical E2E private-QA build and all test/report exits passed. This proof does not transfer to the later rebase.

The frozen-main integration run on `6b9bb1514c196d217af2d718d9778575b4beda7a` executed all 207 selected cases with zero automatic retries: 206 passed and one main-added subscription assertion failed because it still expected one argument. Infra 34/34, agent support 68/68, reply lifecycle 33/33, packaging 16/16 and the original Gateway prefix 3/3 passed; embedded tests were 52/53. The SDK gate measured 4457 public exports/153 entrypoints with zero forbidden subpaths, and the canonical E2E build passed ([integration run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34588303421)). The nonzero outcome is retained.

The test-only correction on `708809cdc2cdbb09c1184ce74838fbf283b71419` keeps the original media-trust matcher, explicitly requires the absent second completion-owner argument, and adds one-call and Set-reference assertions. The affected file then passed 29/29 with zero automatic retries on the corrected SHA ([focused follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34589733727)). Test, native-report and process exits were zero; its owned lease stopped. All other source bytes match the integration tree; their evidence remains bound to `6b9bb1514c196d217af2d718d9778575b4beda7a`, not described as a second 207-case run.

The final stack is rebased onto frozen main `fe1c715de7eccc5ce1ec9f7de6b2eb64c6248ad1`. Reviewed composition preserves both Windows test-list additions, combines the SDK surface at 4457 exports/153 entrypoints, retains main's migration recovery/refusal and lane-controller behavior, and ports the stack's activity/observer fencing into main's pure task publication owner. Completion performs explicit managed-cancellation reconciliation before deferred observers. A new direct completion regression checks committed task/subagent/flow visibility, exact observer count and reopened durable generation. Both cancellation tests and both subscription capability sets remain.

The wake repair contributes net +95 production lines and +410 test lines, justified by full-lifecycle ownership. Its clean PR3 placement and downstream replay exclude all temporary diagnostic-helper commits. The final 43-commit signed stack preserves the prior 41 author/message/date records and reviewed replay patches, with two additional test-only integration commits. Gateway helper bytes match the prior public source.

This is focused correctness and frozen-main integration proof, not a new 48-case run, frontier comparison, Beta recommendation, supported-release/upgrade proof, typecheck or moving-main guarantee. The original 47/48 failure and subsequent diagnostic failures below remain historical evidence; the exact historical event46-to-wake31 lineage was never established. Exact-head CI/type/lint, remaining owner/upgrade review gates and landing approval remain outstanding.

### Admission Trace; Original Failure Preserved (2026-09-11)

The [native diagnostic run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34581153464) used unpublished source `6fb2b529ae05e9e68712782878f60b11a78d9a08`, tree `d56fdd6aee6025edb35b06899acbf74873db5f78`, and exact-tree carrier `9f63430ec7fbf8eadf459cab268db1b48ea31005`. Two planned invocations ran once each, with zero automatic test retries: isolated retained **1/1 passed**, then the original allowed/cancelled/retained prefix **2/3 passed**. Prefix physical POSTs were **2/0/1**, three total. The original **47/48** result and its retained failure are not replaced by the isolated pass.

The failing POST uniquely joins a background-task heartbeat requester and precedes the held recovery dispatch by **4,595 ms**. Its requester claim was validated, but originating task authority remains unproven: the earlier cancelled-task event cannot be uniquely joined to the wake, whose pending and selected event lists were empty. Admission capture correctly remains incomplete despite no capture drops and completed cleanup. The original zero-call assertion remains red; later durable-state assertions were not reached. This does not establish a stale held-recovery dispatch or a legitimate originating-task request.

Source review separately establishes a full-close lifecycle mismatch: [Gateway close stops the heartbeat runner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8d7c8caba1d1bbdc06dff641d4b71fcd7b318261/src/gateway/server-close.ts#L504), then [drains global lifecycle state](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8d7c8caba1d1bbdc06dff641d4b71fcd7b318261/src/gateway/server-close.ts#L658). System-event queues are cleared, but pending wake state survives. These eight relevant production files are byte-identical to frozen base `8d7c8caba1d1bbdc06dff641d4b71fcd7b318261`; this is neither latest-main nor shipped-behavior proof. The repair owner is full runtime drain, preserving [intentional handler-replacement retention](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8d7c8caba1d1bbdc06dff641d4b71fcd7b318261/src/infra/session-event-wake.preemption.test.ts#L101), not an empty-wake consumer guard. No repair is published here.

**12 review moves remain**, not 12 proven bugs; overlapping Before-merge owner/upgrade risks remain unresolved or only partially evidenced. Earlier dated evidence below remains historical. No Beta, performance, or current-main qualification is claimed. Next evidence is a deterministic full-close/wake-owner lifecycle regression, then the original prefix after an approved owner fix, not another broad or model campaign.

### Focused Verification; Unresolved Failure (2026-09-10)

- The published composed stack at `076c0f6da337bec075322e5c85b6b0de9cc4008b` / tree `270fa87b134f9cbc1bfbbef36a0a47e7e4d0a319` executed all **48 selected mock/loopback cases: 47 passed, 1 failed, 0 selected skips, zero framework retries**; the wrapper's no-output retry was also disabled. QA cleanup 11/11, session mutation 22/22, observer cases 6/6, Gateway ownership 4/5, transport rejection recovery 1/1, and Slack Enterprise 3/3. The original retained-owner zero-POST assertion remains red; its later durable assertions were not reached. [Initial execution](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34523487264) and [nine-case continuation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34525146081) are separate attempts, not one successful run.
- **Unpublished, test-only diagnostics are not part of these PR heads.** At `b84bb7b28d7843b4bf81daab5e240e92b098de11`, retained alone passed 1/1. At `e46789e3ebfce51300f5b7676b079d4549adced0` / tree `f5abfd72151421e86a1ec081cde9281e916bbfee`, the [paired diagnostic](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34529507765) passed retained-alone 1/1, then passed only 2/3 in the original allowed, cancelled, retained order. Separate invocations, reports and exits are preserved; no failed-case retry or assertion weakening occurred.
- Unique trusted model-start/physical-POST correlation attributes the failing request to a requester run, **not the held recovery run**. It precedes the held dispatch by **4,566 ms**. Requester producer and authority remain unresolved; repeated fixture session identity does not prove carry-over. No production repair, legitimate-traffic exemption, or green reclassification is claimed. Next required fact: a pre-start canonical producer admission joining run/generation to provenance, source owner/revision and admission/idempotency identity, covering announcement Gateway and heartbeat inbound dispatch. No further experiment is authorized by this update.
- The original consumer/dependency startup error, multi-config reporter error, retained-capsule transport failure, and portal metadata timeout warnings remain recorded. All owned leases are stopped. ShellBench was untouched. These results provide **partial focused proof only**; all 12 rank-up proof/owner requirements remain pending. This stack is **not requalified against current main; compatibility remains unknown**. No type-test or matched frontier benchmark result is added. Frontier Beta remains **NO-GO**, with efficacy **INCONCLUSIVE**: no accuracy, underlying-call, token, or latency improvement is established.

### Frozen-Main Integration; Historical Source Review

- The semantic integration retains main's metadata-only task observers without losing the stack's atomic registration, cache-before-observer publication, full backing/generation checks, or successor activity ownership. It also retains main's removed pending-message state, one-deadline process cleanup, QA Lab workspace dependency, and assertion-ratchet reductions. SDK limits compose the existing increments exactly; canonical runtime count collection remains unrun.
- The additional registry follow-up is **three test files, +29/-0; production delta zero**, at [PR3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/119056), inherited by Slack and PR4. Four non-vacuous no-detail checks run outside caught observer callbacks and retain expected event counts/order plus durable backing/generation assertions. The earlier PR1 +13/-0 state-owner fixture repair remains inherited by all five layers.
- Fresh native review completed on tree `270fa87b134f9cbc1bfbbef36a0a47e7e4d0a319`: **three passes, no P0-P2 findings, minimum confidence 0.64**. It covered the 13-path integration delta with complete supplied owner/caller context, not all 352 stack paths. The first pass explicitly limited its conclusion to its first evidence batch; all three helper passes subsequently completed. Actual report/status bytes and exact-source Git receipts are retained. Independent registry, subscription, and identity audits also passed. This is source review, not runtime qualification.
- Codex contracts were personally inspected at commit `414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6`: [task replacement, exact active-owner cleanup, and cancellation](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6/codex-rs/core/src/tasks/mod.rs#L320), lines 320, 784, and 825; [model follow-up and retry accounting](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L305), lines 305 and 1204. This is dependency-source evidence, not a new live-model trace.
- Published-head [CI 34511914820](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34511914820) and [CI 34511914495](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34511914495), attempt 1, were **skipped** on `8fc45edc048aa7ac67d2237fd5a857408d37ce87`; relevant shard/Gateway jobs executed zero steps, and no separate E2E run matched that complete head response. These are not passes. At integration publication, no runtime tests, type tests, or matched benchmark had run on the new candidate heads; the focused results above are subsequent evidence.
- At integration publication, one focused **48-case** mock/loopback Testbox proposal, including remote dependency/build preparation, awaited explicit execution approval; its approved execution is recorded above. It adds six observer cases to the earlier 42-case proposal. It does not replace supported-host, owner-acceptance, authenticated Enterprise, retained-history-cost, or supported-frontier benchmark gates. ShellBench remains untouched.

### Earlier c2d7 Integration; Historical

- The integration preserves main's explicit session-cleanup ordering, selected-model source marker, Copilot input-provenance hook assertions, Gateway send-test consolidation, and shrink-only assertion baseline changes.
- The additional repair is one test file, **+13/-0; production delta zero**, inserted at PR1 and inherited by all five layers. Seven fixture scopes establish the temporary state owner before the first database open; three direct database opens reuse that environment and assert the retained owner. No production behavior, schema, deadline, or mutation assertion was changed by this repair.
- Native integration review was reported clean in four passes with no P0-P2 findings, confidence 0.87, for the five-file integration diff on exact final tree `439d46bc20d1d85a3bf4e2acec787425c7e3157b`. Its temporary report files are now unavailable; current report-byte verification is not claimed. Retained Git freeze/assembly receipts and independent exact-source verification remain available. This was not a holistic review of all 352 paths or runtime qualification.
- No runtime tests, type tests, or matched benchmark ran on those earlier candidate heads. The then-proposed 42-case Testbox scope was unrun; the current 48-case proposal above supersedes it without granting execution approval. ShellBench remained untouched.

### Earlier Follow-up; Historical Source Review

- Earlier follow-up against the prior `64fa` candidate: three test files, +391/-53; production delta zero. It remains in the stack, but its review and earlier CI/E2E results are historical, not execution proof for these heads.
- The earlier test-only follow-up repairs OTel caller context and R5 successor visibility, terminal settlement, and Vitest `it.for` context. Failure-only R5 and predispatch diagnostics retain the existing request filters, exact assertions, and deadlines. The retained-successor POST origin and unexpected third HTTP request remain **UNCLASSIFIED**; diagnostics are not causal fixes.
- Results on terminal `64fa593ec6e8cc0e329f9c3d3b85ed27e81609be`: P4 21/21 passed; Gateway 1,915 passed, 8 failed, 20 skipped; UI 1,995 passed; self-yield 2/2 passed. These do not qualify the new head. At that historical head, inherited static defects, including Control UI locale parity, were separate from unresolved execution causes; not every failure was classified as baseline.
- A/C use the real host, session store, Slack SDK/public barrel, and native upload guard. The native cases inspect exact bytes, bearer separation, completion payloads, post-settlement effects after revocation during held preparation, and one-shot behavior after a lost completion.
- **Transport proof:** the three C core-host cases are included in P4's 21/21 passes on historical `64fa593ec6e8cc0e329f9c3d3b85ed27e81609be`; new-head execution remains pending. The three Enterprise B cases remain unexecuted and outside the approved manual CI/non-live Repo E2E inventory. A focused Testbox route awaits user approval; the broader Plugin Prerelease route remains out of scope.
- Real outer-loop cases persist the outer call, delivery mirror, nested activity, and result; reject old activity after the same manager accepts a new user; and continue ordinary work after permission refresh without replaying the earlier mutation or reply.
- The optional `preparedTurnParentId` SDK draft is accepted only for the scoped repair. It is not a released-host capability claim or a landing/upgrade acceptance waiver.
- **Earlier scoped native source review: reported PASS**, zero findings, confidence 0.5, across the two-file R5/predispatch diff in three context partitions. The separate OTel caller fix also passed scoped source review. These historical reviews are not holistic stack review, current artifact verification, runtime proof, or type qualification; execution remains pending.

### Historical Evidence Only

[CI 34483907441](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34483907441) and [Repo E2E 34483936399](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34483936399) ended red on `64fa593ec6e8cc0e329f9c3d3b85ed27e81609be`: CI 184 passed, 8 failed, 2 skipped in 40m40s (seven causal failures plus the aggregate); E2E 11 passed, 3 failed, 14 skipped in 39m46s. prs.title: fix(config): redact authored credential fallbacks in public snapshots
prs.body:
Closes #168147
Related: #168109 (closed by its author, unmerged).

## What Problem This Solves

Credential fields containing `${VAR:-fallback}` were treated as secret-free environment references. Even when `VAR` supplied a different active credential, authenticated `config.get` could expose the authored fallback through its parsed and raw views. The shared redaction owner also serves `/config show` and configuration response previews.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing environment-template parser to distinguish a bare or empty-fallback reference from a literal credential. Redact nonempty fallbacks using the existing sentinel. Withhold the raw view when an authored sensitive fallback is present: resolved-value replacement cannot safely redact a different, possibly JSON5-escaped fallback. This uses the existing `raw: null` contract; the UI already reconstructs its editable view from the structured snapshot.

Existing-solutions preflight: SecretRefs avoid embedding credentials and remain the recommended authoring option, but they do not repair redaction of existing supported fallback templates. This repair belongs in `src/config/redact-snapshot.ts`; no plugin, library, or additional redaction system is needed. The unmerged previous proposal is closed; a fresh issue/timeline and semantic PR search found no active implementation or human rejection.

## User Impact

Fallback credential material stays hidden in public configuration projections. Bare `${VAR}`, empty `${VAR:-}`, blank strings, and nonsensitive fallbacks stay editable. Actual sentinel-based configuration writes continue to preserve the authored template and its environment binding. Configurations with sensitive fallbacks receive the existing structured-editor representation instead of raw text; comments/formatting are not exposed through that raw view.

No configuration/default, protocol, schema, dependency, migration, authorization, or provider-routing change. This is redaction hardening within the existing authenticated operator surface, not a claim of unauthenticated access. Security-owner review before merge remains appropriate.

## Evidence

### CI attribution check — October 18, 2026

The contributor head remains `a1176b96f21666576d2fdd7f02bf48bdde63c530`; no code or head update was made. Hosted job [115748918633](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38532765415/job/115748918633) failed because the existing owner-reload scenario exceeded its 20-second `config.patch` RPC deadline. Replaying that exact named scenario on the unchanged head with Node 24.16.0 succeeds: **1 passed, 66 skipped**, native wrapper **168.55 s**, Vitest **129.93 s**. The other cases were deliberately not replayed by this diagnostic. Log SHA-256: `0ebc2ef80943caa832dc9bd59b0a529a1d30f528b4e4a86c637f1ae82b21c44e`.

```text
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/gateway/server.config-patch.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 \
  -t 'reloads owners independently and reports a changed unresolved owner as cold'
```

This passing local replay does not resolve or prove the cause of the old hosted timeout. Required hosted CI remains failed. The separate `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` explicitly requires a maintainer to approve this revision; contributor proof cannot replace that approval. Leon has upstream read permission and cannot rerun its Actions jobs. No guard, timeout, permission, or security policy has been weakened.

Real Linux proof uses Node 24.16.0 and the normal built OpenClaw 2026.10.3 `openclaw.mjs gateway run` entry point, isolated homes/state/configs, loopback-only authentication, and synthetic credentials. No existing configuration, model account, channel, or external recipient is used.

| Scenario | Parent `502a942ca53e` | This head |
|---|---|---|
| Environment supplies a different active key | Full authenticated snapshot exposes authored provider/header fallbacks | No fallback in any returned projection; unsafe raw view withheld |
| Environment variable absent | Parsed/source projections expose fallback; raw may already be withheld | No fallback in any returned projection; unsafe raw view withheld |
| Bare and empty-fallback header controls | References preserved | References preserved |
| Real `config.patch`, redacted provider key plus unrelated response-prefix edit | Not run on parent | Both cases return success; disk readback preserves the exact original fallback template, updates the prefix, and retains bare references |

The provider fallback includes an escaped newline in raw JSON, exercising a case that literal resolved-string replacement cannot protect. Both gateways reach readiness, execute authenticated WebSocket calls, and are stopped after proof. Providers use a closed loopback endpoint and are never invoked.

Acceptance-red was captured before production edits: 4 new regression cases failed, 5 controls passed. After the repair the complete focused file passes **37/37**. Tests cover schema/heuristic behavior, all snapshot projections, empty/bare controls, non-sensitive fallbacks, restoration, and nonmutation; existing SecretRef, raw-ambiguity, array-identity, and independent-projection regressions also pass.

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/redact-snapshot.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  37 passed, exit 0; single-worker lane 83.09 s
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --type-aware --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/config/redact-snapshot.ts src/config/redact-snapshot.test.ts
  passed, exit 0
oxfmt --check src/config/redact-snapshot.ts src/config/redact-snapshot.test.ts
  passed
git diff --check
  passed
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts runtime
  passed on the committed head
node 168147-config-live-proof.mjs <checkout> <new-output-directory> green
  2/2 real Gateway read/write scenarios passed
```

Exact proof head: `a1176b96f21666576d2fdd7f02bf48bdde63c530`; tree: `6f4c27301ab45a8d790c70d5468b2cafc786faea`; working diff empty. Build metadata reports the same commit, built `2026-10-14T07:57:39.493Z`; proof completed `2026-10-14T08:02:04.624Z`. Harness SHA-256: `1ecf04a727a486e7e1b82fd7cbafff9232c96457a7866876ccc052434e699497`. Parent receipt: `58a882cbd6d2caa4e281111d63dd6958a48235afae3f686f2a7847261c575697`; head receipt: `9f1aa4f408f2920992bb89d56004415f579eed75a5bf2de79c8b52ca51700151`. Local receipts/logs are retained; the table above supplies sanitized readback, not a publicly hosted artifact claim.

Production: 1 file **+30/-11, net +19**. Tests: 1 file **+68/-0**. Generated/lock files: none. Production growth removes a separate permissive placeholder grammar and enforces the existing raw-withholding contract for authored fallbacks.

Not tested: a browser GUI session, `/config show` through a real messaging channel, external model calls, non-Linux hosts, or the complete project suite. The shared owner/callers and UI raw-null handling were inspected; real behavior proof is the normal authenticated Gateway plus on-disk writeback. CI supplies broader checks.

<details>
<summary>AI disclosure and redacted agent transcript</summary>

Implemented with AI assistance for Leon-SK668. The agent read the configuration redaction owner, environment parser, Gateway read/write callers, chat sibling, UI structured fallback, existing tests, and JSON5 parser contract. It reproduced the leak against the unmodified main build and failing regressions, then implemented the bounded repair, ran checks, rebuilt the committed head, and repeated the real Gateway scenario with writeback controls. A fresh competition scan preceded publication. No maintainer confirmation or review outcome is claimed. Credentials, authentication tokens, private endpoints, local account details, and production data are omitted. This is a concise sanitized transcript, not a raw session-log attachment.

</details>

prs.title: fix: path JSON refusals leave redirected output empty
prs.body:
Related: #167294

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw path ... --json` leaves redirected stdout empty for handled path/file refusals, while sending the JSON result to stderr.

## User Impact

Scripts can read handled refusals from the same JSON stdout stream as successful results. Errors include `ok: false` and `error.type: "cli_error"`, retaining the existing domain `error.code`, message, redaction, and exit status. Explicit `--human` diagnostics stay on stderr. Scripts consuming these JSON refusals from stderr should read stdout instead, as documented for CLI JSON output.

## Why This Change Was Made

Correct the plugin's existing error writer, which already owns path parse errors, unsupported patterns, oversized/nonregular files, invalid editing bytes, and sentinel refusals. This follows the JSON stdout contract in `docs/cli/index.md` without changing filesystem parsing, editing, configuration, dependencies, or permission decisions.

The existing `validate` and edit-result payloads have their own command-specific fields; this change concerns the shared handled-error writer. No new renderer, SDK API, or fallback is introduced.

## Evidence

Native built CLI on Linux / Node 24.16.0 with isolated synthetic HOME/state/config/workspace. Parent `90127436fa45e539616c7b123a549cbd3919c725`; exact clean head `b5a379de5b1fc0ee008477bb3318d9b28db05e7c`, matching `dist/build-info.json`.

| Scenario | Parent | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Invalid `oc://` path | Exit 2; stdout empty; JSON only on stderr | Exit 2; one JSON stdout error with retained domain code/message |
| Unsupported file wildcard | Same missing stdout result | Same corrected JSON stdout stream |
| Malformed UTF-8 editing input | Safe refusal, but JSON only on stderr | Same safe refusal; standard JSON stdout metadata; input byte-identical |
| Explicit human-mode invalid path | Text on stderr, exit 2 | Same text/error status |
| Valid Unicode write followed by a separate CLI read | Disk value and readback match | Same disk value/readback; unrelated field retained |

The three JSON refusals and human control preserve the input file's original bytes. The positive control writes `中文 🦞 literal �`, checks the actual JSON file, then calls `path resolve` in a new process and checks the reported leaf value.

<details>
<summary>Exact-head proof receipt, checks, and limits</summary>

- Claims: C1=Put handled path/file JSON refusals on stdout with common failure metadata and preserved domain diagnostics; C2=Keep refusal safety, human output, and valid file editing/readback.
- Same command on parent/head: `node openclaw.mjs path find 'oc://*.json/key' --json`; also actual CLI invalid-path and malformed-edit cases, a `--human` control, and `path set` followed by `path resolve` for the Unicode control.
- Owner: `extensions/oc-path/src/cli.ts` `emitError`, reached unmocked through built plugin registration and actual path/file command handlers.
- Before: RED, 3/3 handled JSON refusals leave stdout empty; human control and valid write/readback work.
- After: GREEN, all 5 scenarios / 6 native CLI invocations pass; three JSON results are on stdout, the human error remains stderr, and a successful write is independently read back. Control: 0/4 refused operations change input bytes; 1/1 valid write preserves the unrelated field and returns exact Unicode through a second CLI process.
- Readback: subprocess stdout/stderr and exit, raw on-disk input bytes or post-write JSON, separate CLI leaf readback. Harness SHA-256 `cbe23d3045a3d5031772ed313d4c5071584974a837637b12aaa5ee13d05f8620`, identical subprocess/file-readback driver on parent/head.
- Tests: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/oc-path/src/cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 68 passed, wrapper wall 8.84s / Vitest duration 5.28s. Existing oversized-input, FIFO, UTF-8, sentinel, valid editing and output checks remain covered. Tests are updated in place with zero net line growth.
- Static/build checks: source-scoped tsgo, typed production-file Oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` pass; exact-head `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts sourcePerformance` succeeds. Temporary type config selects both changed files and their real dependency closure; packaged declaration preparation was omitted for lint.
- Inherited local lint limitation: the existing test file violates `max-lines` on both parent and head: 1,125 counted lines against a 1,000-line limit. Both versions produce the same diagnostic. Full typed lint's only diagnostic was this file-length rule; it is not represented as a clean full lint pass. `scripts/lib/check-limits.mts` makes size limits advisory in GitHub Actions. No limit, baseline, configuration, or suppression was changed.
- Test cost: focused wrapper wall 8.84s / Vitest duration 5.28s; hosted CI seconds unavailable before creation.
- Scope: 2 files; production +3/−1 lines, tests +12/−12; no generated files or lockfiles.
- Not tested: Windows/macOS, the full repository suite, all possible domain diagnostics through native subprocesses, or unrelated plugins. Existing CLI tests cover the sibling error callers; explicit common-envelope changes for other command-specific payloads are outside this fix.

AI-assisted implementation and verification with Codex.

</details>

prs.title: refactor(plugins): call existing operation owners directly
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Bundled plugin paths carry private test selectors, constant policy plumbing and forwarding layers around their only production operation owners.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Browser upload retention/quota and security checks, Copilot sandbox/tool authority and shutdown settlement, Matrix startup, Nextcloud guarded downloads and OpenShell filesystem behavior remain. Public SDK, config, CLI, protocol, dependencies and persisted shapes are unchanged. The Phase E standalone session-memory backend and its factory, registry, expiry, federation and tests are untouched; the small ordinary Memory Core index queue change is unrelated to that backend.

## Why This Change Was Made

Call the existing operation owners directly. Browser recovery uses its existing fixed policy; tests exercise the actual limits. Copilot and Matrix fixtures intercept actual module boundaries instead of production operation selectors. Nextcloud calls the same guarded transport directly, and OpenShell constructs its sole filesystem bridge directly. Ordinary Memory Core index admission keeps the same local FIFO reader/writer queue without forwarding or repeated synchronous native-signal observations.

This is the extension-area slice of an86-path accumulation under the campaign's area-split rule, not a final residue or claim of exhaustion. Current delta:25 paths, **104 net production lines removed**, **181 test/support lines added**, **77 lines added overall**. Moved or test code is not credited as production reduction.

Fresh main had substantially reorganized Copilot's test fixture. The migration preserves its current helper functions, tables and assertions rather than replaying the older fixture. Module registration order, shared override identity, synchronous resolver results and owned teardown remain explicit.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Private test policy, clock and operation overrides disappear; production already used the same default operations. Browser still uses24-hour retention,256MiB and64-directory bounds. No security, credential, cancellation, persistence or shutdown guard is removed from those paths.
- Memory Core no longer defends fabricated or monkey-patched AbortSignal getters/listener methods that synchronously mutate cancellation during listener registration/removal. Native admission contains no await or user callback; native pre-abort, queued abort, active-reader ownership and FIFO publication remain covered. The original guards came from #112214; the inline-release pre-counting accommodation came from #158172, whose refactor explicitly established no independent product bug. The real closed-database report #112196 still protects serving/publication/drain behavior. Unsupported exotic signal objects may fail rather than receive special handling.

## Evidence

Fresh25-root owning-graph semantic types passed27.326s; formatting passed0.433s and whitespace/index checks passed. Independent full25-path review completed scoped-clean through P2 (correctness0.89). Mandatory suppression policy passed14/14 in62.500s. Exact-path check-changed dry-run passed60.401s; this classified the required routes, not execution of its broad recommendations.

All existing production source preimages matched fresh main before composition. Copilot's evolved test was adapted from its exact current-main bytes with27 unique forward/reverse hunks; before formatting all467 assertion call expressions,18 tables and30 existing functions remained byte-identical. Its three related support/integration modules preserve leading registration imports and retrieve the same cached fixture exports without duplicate static value imports. These are source-transfer checks, not runtime proof.

The ordinary extension lint route requires package-wide declaration preparation, prohibited by the campaign's local build budget. Focused runtime has the same known cold-worker compiler prerequisite. Neither is claimed passing, no preparation/cache bypass was used, and no timeout/retry/skip/suppression was added. Current runtime, lint, architecture/SDK and build proof must come from exact-head hosted CI. No live provider/device or full build result is claimed.

## Exact-head CI repairs

Run39089902105 at0f00a7ff6f8b049506eb507f53d64d9d9b4a9567 completed with four owned failures and its downstream gate. No inherited exception is requested:

| Job | Failure | Repair |
| --- | --- | --- |
| checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1 (117564485961) | Copilot integration collection rejects exported vi.hoisted declaration | Keep private hoisted binding and export an ordinary alias to the identical object. |
| checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-2-2 (117564486151) | Same Copilot attempt collection failure | Same single fixture correction. |

| check-lint-extensions-3 (117565014854) | Shadowed mock binding, redundant conditional spread and unused mock-result local | Rename only the local alias, pass the same conditional object directly and retain the identical mock chain without the unused local. |

The actual installed Vitest transform rejects the exact original fixture and accepts its repair; that compiler-boundary control passed0.956s, not a runtime-case pass. prs.title: fix(sessions): long transcripts pin a database read snapshot while being decoded
prs.body:
Closes #171467
Related: #160386

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on a gateway with a long-running session, a memory session-index pass over a large transcript holds a SQLite read transaction on the agent database open for the whole time it takes to decompress, parse and project the transcript (the fenced transcript read used by hydration and SessionManager open shares the same in-transaction decode; it is not changed here, see Gaps), which logs `slow SQLite transaction hold ... operation="session transcript export snapshot"` (on current main also `operation="session transcript export batch"`, the memory batch) and keeps agent-database WAL checkpoints from completing.

#171467 is scoped to exactly this defect: the agent-database export snapshot is held across decode and parse of a whole transcript (and, in the memory batch, of every transcript in the group). Its expected behavior, quoted: "Exports of one large transcript should not stop passive checkpoints on the agent database from completing." That is what this PR delivers for the export snapshot reader and for the memory export batch; the readers it leaves alone are listed under Gaps. #157092 reported the same hold earlier and was closed by #157278, which bounded the retained projection memory and added the reset-boundary path; on main the export still decodes, parses and projects inside the read transaction, and three of the #160386 reports below post-date #157278.

Four commenters on #160386 report exactly this line (1.0 to 6 s per hold on stores from about 260 MB to 2.6 GB, hundreds of times a day), and a fifth reports testing this approach on a 115 KB transcript. The `openclaw-state WAL checkpoint TRUNCATE remained busy` reports in the thread concern the shared-state database, which this reader never opens; they are a separate holder and are not addressed here.

#160386 is a P0 umbrella with several independent contributors. This PR is the repair for one of them, the agent-database export snapshot hold. The others stay with their own open issues: the shared-state read-admission seal (`STATE_DATABASE_READ_ADMISSION_INVALIDATED`, #162085 and #160521), shared-state release stalls and session-write latency (#161439, #163748), and Gateway native-memory growth with session SQLite stalls (#170179). That is why #160386 stays `Related:` and the closing keyword is on #171467, which covers this contributor alone.

## User Impact

User impact: for transcripts above 4 MiB in the memory batch, and above 2 MiB in the export snapshot reader, a reader snapshot stays open only for the export head and one slice of at most 2 MiB of payload text at a time, instead of for the whole transcript, so passive WAL checkpoints on the agent database can finish while exports run. The memory session-index batch transaction still reads the transcripts the worker's retained-snapshot cache admits (at most 4 MiB) as it does on main; larger transcripts, which that cache never retains, are read after it, in slices.

No transcript content, ordering, fence, byte budget, incremental export rule, cold-transcript handling or export result changes. Each slice holds at most 2 MiB of decoded payload text (plus the row that crosses that budget), produced by the same SQL decode function the old path uses, and parsed and released before the next slice is read. No memory improvement is claimed. Through the shipped plugin-SDK entry with and without an enforced total-process cap, the before and after lifetime footprints overlap (12 interleaved runs per side at three settings, tables under Memory). This does not claim to resolve `STATE_DATABASE_READ_ADMISSION_INVALIDATED` (see Gaps).

Cost: warm exports of the large session take longer after the change. Mean of the three warm exports (rounds 1 to 3) over all 12 runs per side: 4.0% longer without a cap (1375.2 against 1322.7 ms), 8.9% longer at the 768 MiB cap and 8.6% longer at the 896 MiB cap (tables under Memory). In exchange the reader snapshot is released between slices, and with exports running passive checkpoints backfilled every frame in 230 of 242 attempts after the change against 11 of 249 before it (Evidence).

## Why This Change Was Made

`docs/reference/database-schemas/integrity-and-recovery.md` says periodic agent maintenance "keeps the shared WAL backfilled" with passive checkpoints, and that a reader-blocked checkpoint is recorded as blocked rather than complete. A reader that holds its snapshot across seconds of work defeats that. Nothing in the history says the parse had to sit inside the transaction: `9d5615cee1c` moved preparation to a worker and left the decode where it was.

Each slice is one read transaction; the slices of one read are tied together by the transcript context version, not by one SQLite snapshot (see Gaps). The first read transaction resolves the fence, the export statistics and rewrite generation, the incremental-export decision (`previous`, `throughSeq`, unchanged), the session key and the transcript context version (`readTranscriptContextVersionInTransaction`: rewrite generation, highest raw seq, `transcript_updated_at`) together with the first slice. Each slice selects its rows' payload text through `transcriptEventJsonSql`, the same SQL decode the whole-transcript read uses, so per-row decode work and memory are unchanged; `JSON.parse` and the projection run after the slice's transaction closed, and each captured string is released as it is parsed. The slice budget counts each row's payload bytes with the existing `transcriptEventReadBytesSql` (`coalesce(event_utf8_bytes, octet_length(event_json))`): the decoded size for compressed rows, not their stored size, because the slice holds decoded text. Every later transaction first re-reads the context version and continues after the last captured seq only while it is unchanged; that version is the token `SessionManager` writes already validate their loaded bytes against, and the in-place rewrite and suffix paths change it (`rotateTranscriptGenerationInTransaction`, `touchTranscriptMutationInTransaction`). If it changed, the slices read so far are dropped and the transcript is read inside one transaction, exactly as on the base. A transcript under the budget is read in one transaction, as before.

The memory session-index batch (`prepareSessionMemoryEntries`) reads a group of transcripts of one agent database inside one read snapshot through the batch export owner `readTranscriptExportSnapshotsFromDatabase` (#175174), which reads the group's statistics in one query and the requested rows in set-based queries. It keeps that snapshot for every transcript the worker's retained-snapshot cache admits: at most `MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES` (4 MiB) of recorded size. Those transcripts are read, parsed and projected inside the batch exactly as on main. For a transcript above that limit the batch owner, given `deferAboveBytes: MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES`, still computes the head (fence, statistics, generation, cold check, incremental decision, byte admission check) and leaves its rows out of the row query, and the worker records the transcript context version in the same snapshot. After the batch transaction closed, each marked transcript is read through the sliced reader above, under the same current-turn fence admission (`runWithSessionTranscriptReadFence`), with the same retained incremental projection (`previous`) and the same cold handling (`SessionTranscriptColdError` becomes `{ cold: true }`, which sends the caller through archive restoration). No slice runs inside the batch transaction, and no new threshold is introduced into the batch: the only boundary is the one the cache already draws; the export snapshot reader uses the new 2 MiB slice budget.

That boundary is the owner's recorded retention limit. The batch was introduced on main in `8e02d1ae9694393d84ea51bb573a93bb7212a0f1` (PR #170404, "Reduce per-source worker transactions and preparation overhead by reading bounded source groups together"), on top of the retained-snapshot cache from `a00f58286fa` (PR #170302). #170302 records: "The cache retains at most 16 transcripts of at most 4 MiB each; larger/evicted transcripts use the full read path." #170404 records that groups are "bounded to eight sources, 128 publication rows, and the existing transfer budget; an oversized single source retains its atomic streamed replacement", and that "all sources use their pass snapshot and later transcript notifications catch subsequent writes." This change keeps the group bound and the retention limit and departs from one statement: a transcript above the retention limit no longer uses the pass snapshot. It is read after the batch in version-checked slices, and a later write is caught by the next transcript notification, which #170404 already relies on. In #170302 "full read path" means a non-incremental read, which #170404 placed inside the batch; only those transcripts move out of it. The batch transaction's decoded payload is bounded by the group bound times the retention limit (eight sources of at most 4 MiB), where on main it was unbounded. #175174 (merged 2026-10-17) moved the batch onto one export owner and records: "One export owner reads metadata for the group and fetches requested transcript ranges in set-based queries. Payload queries are bounded by session count and the existing source-size estimate; oversized individual sessions run alone." This change keeps that owner as the only place the head is computed, for both the batch and the sliced read, and uses the same source-size estimate as its boundary; it departs in that a session above the retention limit is read after the batch snapshot in version-checked slices rather than alone inside it. #175174 also records: "An archive transition after the pinned read snapshot is observed by the next read; the current export remains snapshot-consistent." Each transcript read after the batch remains internally consistent through the version check; it is not consistent with the batch snapshot of the other sources, which is the tradeoff this PR asks the owner to accept.

The head the batch already read is reused. The sliced reader reads the transcript context version before the head in its first slice's transaction; when that version equals the one the batch recorded, the snapshot head the batch owner returned (statistics, generation, cold check, incremental decision, session key) is used as it is and no statistics are read a second time. When the version differs, the head is read again in that transaction through the same batch owner for that one transcript, under the same fence. Both cases are pinned by tests.


Callers of the export snapshot reader: the memory session entry and entries (`buildSessionEntry`, `buildSessionEntries` through `prepareSessionMemoryEntries`, and the worker's single-entry snapshot request), explicit Memory Core source inspection (which goes through the same worker batch since #175174), the in-process `buildSessionEntry` fallback, and reset recall (`projection: "reset-boundary"`, still one transaction). Each read above the slice budget now adds one context-version read per slice. The fenced reader `loadTranscriptReadSnapshotSync` (hydration, `SessionManager` open and reload, the incognito history worker, the bundled session-memory hook capture, `loadTranscriptEventsSync` callers, `prepareTranscriptCommit`) is unchanged; its hold was not measured and is listed under Gaps.

### The change in one sentence

Read the payload text of a whole transcript in slices of at most 2 MiB of payload bytes, one read transaction each, through the existing SQL decode, parse every slice after its transaction closes, and continue only while the transcript context version is unchanged, in the export snapshot reader; and have the batch export owner leave the rows of transcripts above the memory worker's existing 4 MiB retention limit to that reader after the batch's read snapshot instead of inside it, reusing the export head the batch already read while the transcript context version is unchanged.

<summary>Cap supervisor (Python 3.9, full source)</summary>

```python
# Enforced total-process memory cap for one child process on macOS.
# Polls proc_pid_rusage(RUSAGE_INFO_V4) every 2 ms. The kernel tracks the
# lifetime maximum physical footprint itself, so the verdict does not depend
# on catching the peak in a sample: once that high-water mark exceeds the cap,
# the child is SIGKILLed, the way a cgroup memory.max OOM kill ends it.
import ctypes, os, signal, subprocess, sys, time
cap_mib = float(sys.argv[1])
cmd = sys.argv[2:]
libproc = ctypes.CDLL("/usr/lib/libproc.dylib")
buf = (ctypes.c_uint64 * 64)()
RESIDENT, FOOTPRINT, LIFETIME_MAX = 6 + 2, 7 + 2, 28 + 2  # +2: the 16-byte ri_uuid prefix
def usage(pid):
    if libproc.proc_pid_rusage(pid, 4, ctypes.byref(buf)) != 0:
        return None
    return buf[RESIDENT], buf[FOOTPRINT], buf[LIFETIME_MAX]
mib = lambda n: round(n / 2**20, 1)
child = subprocess.Popen(cmd)
peak_rss = peak_fp = life = 0
killed = False
while child.poll() is None:
    u = usage(child.pid)
    if u:
        peak_rss, peak_fp, life = max(peak_rss, u[0]), max(peak_fp, u[1]), max(life, u[2])
        if not killed and life > cap_mib * 2**20:
            os.kill(child.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
            killed = True
    time.sleep(0.002)
rc = child.wait()
print(f"CAP capMiB={cap_mib:g} exit={rc} killedByCap={killed} lifetimeMaxFootprintMiB={mib(life)} sampledPeakFootprintMiB={mib(peak_fp)} sampledPeakRssMiB={mib(peak_rss)}", flush=True)
```

### Regression proof (red / green)

The export test charges each parse and each projection to a virtual `Date.now` clock (2,000 ms per step) and asserts that the transaction diagnostics log no `slow SQLite transaction hold`; it also asserts `projectEvent` receives every event once, in sequence order. The slice test sets the budget to 1 byte and records each transcript read transaction and each projection: transaction, parse, transaction, parse, and so on, one row per transaction. The compressed-row test sets the budget to the smallest decoded size of the two zstd rows, asserts both rows' stored size is below it, and asserts each of them ends its own slice. The two Unicode tests (UTF-8 store and UTF-16le store, checked with `PRAGMA encoding`) append three plain rows of 250 CJK characters, set the budget to the smallest stored size of those rows, assert each row's string length stays below it, and assert that every one of those rows ends its own slice. The incremental test reads the transcript once with `previous: null`, then passes the first three events as `previous` and asserts that only the remaining rows are read and projected, one per transaction, that the result equals the whole transcript, and that an unchanged `previous` reads no row in a single transaction. The reread test rewrites the already parsed first row in place between slices (and bumps `transcript_updated_at`, as the writers do) and asserts that the reader returns the rewritten transcript whole, after exactly three transactions. The corrupt-row test pins that the length error still reaches the caller unchanged, also from a later slice, and passes on the base too, by design. The 3 MiB in-batch test also passes on the base, where every transcript is read in the batch; red 4 is its discriminator.

The memory batch tests call `prepareSessionMemoryEntries` directly (the head test calls `readTranscriptExportSnapshotsFromDatabase` and the read-only reader). The head test asks the batch export owner `readTranscriptExportSnapshotsFromDatabase` for the two-row transcript with `deferAboveBytes: 0` and records its context version, reads with that head while nothing changed and asserts zero statistics reads (counted by a mock around `readTranscriptStatsFromDatabase` and `readTranscriptStatsBatchFromDatabase`) and equal statistics; then it takes a second batch head, appends a message, reads with the stale head and asserts one statistics read, an event count one higher, and the appended event in the result. The fence test anchors the admission at `entry-2`, appends the two large rows after it so the transcript passes 4 MiB, and asserts the entry stops before the fence, once with the transcript untouched after the batch transaction (one statistics read) and once with its update time bumped right after the batch transaction closed (two statistics reads). The order test seeds three transcripts in one store (small, two 2.5 MiB rows, small), sets the slice budget to twice the large transcript's size, and asserts one batch transaction and then one transaction for the large one, with each result in its entry's position. The in-batch test seeds one 3 MiB transcript (above the 2 MiB slice budget, within 4 MiB) and asserts the batch transaction is the only one. The incremental test seeds a 3 MiB transcript, prepares it (retained), appends a message of about 2 MiB so the transcript passes 4 MiB, prepares it again and asserts the batch transaction plus two (one slice, one end check), exactly one parsed payload, the appended text, and the earlier content kept, both untouched and with the update time bumped after the batch transaction (one and two statistics reads). The cold test inserts a cold archive row right after the batch transaction closed, before the transcript's own read, and asserts `{ cold: true }`; then, with the archive row present, asserts `{ cold: true }` from the batch transaction alone. The transactions these tests count include the engine-neutral read snapshot (`runSqliteReadSnapshotSync`) the batch runs in.

### Other checks

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `git diff --check` against the base | exit 0 |
| `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on the five changed source and test files | exit 0 (`All matched files use the correct format.`) |
| `pnpm exec oxlint --type-aware` on the five changed source and test files | exit 0 (`Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.`) |
| `pnpm tsgo:core` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm test test/scripts/pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts test/scripts/pr-wrappers.test.ts test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts --maxWorkers=4` | `Test Files  3 passed (3)`, `Tests  102 passed (102)`, `[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 270.98s` |
| `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 288dd0a8a62` | exit 1 after 1282 s, on four steps that fail identically on a clean checkout of the base: the max-lines suppression ratchet (three `ui/` files), the core test shard root budget, the core test typecheck (two type errors in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-placement.test.ts`) and the dead export scan (30 unused exports outside this diff). Every other step passes, including `Line-cap ratchet OK: 6 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth.`, the SQLite worker and dialect ratchets, mock exports, wrapper shadowing, `Import cycle check: 0 runtime value cycle(s).` and `lint core changed files` `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.` |

`pnpm test src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-read-hold.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 24.17 s vitest duration, 27.73 s for the shard, on a host with load averages of 23.29, 39.67 and 49.30 when the gates started; the sixteen tests take 1.03 s, 0.81 s and 0.77 s, and 0.07 to 0.43 s each for the other thirteen. CI seconds not measured.

## Gaps

- `STATE_DATABASE_READ_ADMISSION_INVALIDATED` is not reproduced and not fixed here. On this base the harness's close no longer overlapped an export on either side, so this run does not exercise a close during an export; no read was refused as invalidated on either side (`invalidated=0`). The seal lifecycle is #162085 territory and is untouched.
- Shared-state WAL checkpoint starvation and shared-state write stalls (#161439, #163748) are a different database and are not addressed.
- Decompression stays inside each slice's transaction (the same SQL decode function as before), so only parsing and projection leave it. Readers are still open for most of a back-to-back export, which is why the `TRUNCATE` probe improves much less than passive checkpoint completion.
- The batch transaction still reads the export statistics over the whole session (`readTranscriptStatsBatchFromDatabase`, which walks every row) for every transcript it reads the head of, including the ones it leaves to the sliced read. The after side logged one `slow SQLite transaction hold` line for the batch transaction in the pair run (1669 ms, before the round 0 line, so the first export) and one in the worker-memory run (1465 ms); the PASSIVE arms logged none.
- Transcripts above the 4 MiB retention limit are no longer read from the batch's SQLite snapshot: each is read after the batch transaction from its own, later snapshot (internally consistent through the version check). Transcripts within the limit, the only ones the cache retains, still share the batch snapshot as on main. Main's batch already returned each transcript as its own entry, and #170404 states that later transcript notifications catch writes after the pass snapshot; I found no consumer that compares entries of one batch with each other, but I did not audit every caller of `buildSessionEntries`.
- Transcripts within the 4 MiB limit are still decoded, parsed and projected inside the batch transaction, as on main, for a group of up to eight sources (the group bound #170404 records); this change does not shorten that hold and I did not measure it.
- The slices are tied together by the transcript context version (rewrite generation, highest raw seq, `transcript_updated_at`), not by one SQLite snapshot, and the same token also decides whether the batch's head is reused. A writer that changed stored rows below the fence without changing any of those three could let one read combine rows from two states, or reuse a head that no longer describes them. Every rewrite path I read changes one of them (`rotateTranscriptGenerationInTransaction` or `touchTranscriptMutationInTransaction` in the transcript store and suffix paths), and `SessionManager` writes already rely on the same token; payload re-encoding (`createTranscriptPayloadUpdater`) changes the stored form, not the decoded event. I did not audit every writer.
- Any append to the same session between two slices changes the raw seq, so that read falls back to the whole-transcript read in one transaction, with the base path's hold. How often that happens for an actively written session under real traffic is not measured; the harness writer appends to a different session.
- The 2 MiB budget is a fixed constant. A slice holds at most 2 MiB of payload text plus the one row that crosses the budget (a compressed row decodes to at most 4 MiB by the table's `CHECK`; a plain `event_json` row has no size check). A large transcript takes about 300 short transactions per export on this fixture instead of one.
- Warm exports of the large session through the memory batch are slower after the change: 4.0%, 8.9% and 8.6% in the three memory sets; in the pair, 8.1% slower (rounds 1 to 3, 1351.3 against 1250.0 ms) and 12.1% slower over the exports of the 20 s probe (1570 against 1401 ms); in the worker-memory run, 8.4% slower (1362.0 against 1256.0 ms). The sliced side runs about 300 short transactions per export, each with a read-only borrow and a context-version read; I did not profile which part costs the difference.
- With exports running, the writer's p99 append latency is higher after the change in all three PASSIVE repetitions (13.2 to 25.2 ms against 6.7 to 8.5 ms), and its mean append count is 4.9% lower (see Evidence). I did not profile this either.
- Under the TRUNCATE probe the writer completed 38% fewer appends after the change (364 against 586) while 1.9 times as many TRUNCATE checkpoints completed; not measured separately.
- The cap was enforced by a footprint supervisor on macOS, not by a Linux cgroup, so page-cache accounting and reclaim under a cgroup are not exercised. The test host has 512 GiB, so only the process was capped, not the host.

<details>
<summary>Further gaps</summary>

- Per-sync work is still proportional to the whole transcript for large sessions: the memory session entry keeps an incremental projection only for transcripts up to 4 MiB (`MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES` in `session-memory-entry.worker.ts`), so this fixture's session is decoded whole on every export, and one session-entry worker serializes behind it.
- The fenced reader (`loadTranscriptReadSnapshotSync`, used by hydration, `SessionManager` open and reload, the incognito history worker, the bundled session-memory hook capture, `loadTranscriptEventsSync` and `prepareTranscriptCommit`) still decodes and parses a whole transcript inside one read transaction, as on main. #171467 is about the memory session index, its hold was never measured, and `prepareTranscriptCommit` calls it inside an outer transaction where slicing releases nothing; it belongs in a follow-up with its own measurement.
- Readers that decode inside a writer or other outer transaction (`loadTranscriptEventsFromDatabase` callers in message cut, parent session, recovery, transcript mirror and incognito lifecycle; `prepareTranscriptCommit`) and `inspectTranscriptEventsSync` (Doctor one-shot) keep their in-transaction decode. Their writers need the decode and the rows to share one authoritative snapshot, and moving it is a write-path change that this PR does not need.
- The checkpoint probes use their own connection with `busy_timeout = 0` (`TRUNCATE`) or every 250 ms (`PASSIVE`); they measure whether a reader snapshot is open, not how the production checkpoint owner schedules work.
- The fixture is synthetic (random-word text, one large session). Compression ratio and decode cost on real transcripts differ; absolute milliseconds and MiB will differ on other hosts.
- #160386 also proposes delta ingestion in Memory Core (index only the events after the last indexed seq). This PR does not do that and does not reduce the total decode work of an export; it only bounds how long a read snapshot is held.

</details>

prs.title: feat(memory): read sections by heading
prs.body:
Related: #173706

## What Problem This Solves

Agents that know a Markdown memory section by name currently need to discover its source line range before reading it, which can leave nearby conditions or exceptions out of a bounded excerpt.

## User Impact

Users can ask for a named section such as "Refunds" and receive its child "Exceptions" section too, within existing excerpt budgets and with accurate source line numbers. No configuration or migration is required, and reads without `heading` are unchanged.

First version: unique, exact ATX heading text (`#` through `######`); memory corpus only. Missing/duplicate headings fail explicitly instead of guessing. Other heading styles and wiki/all reads remain available through the existing line-based interface.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds optional `heading` to the existing memory-core tool and selects the section in the existing authorized memory reader. Child sections are preserved, fenced examples and complete leading frontmatter are ignored, and the next same-or-higher-level heading ends the section. Keep `heading` with an absolute `from: nextFrom` for bounded continuation; offsets outside the section are rejected.

No new tool, index, database schema, permission, dependency, or configuration switch. The heading-aware retrieval idea is adapted from Orca, not a transfer of its application data or runtime.

### October 18 review repairs

- Container-prefixed fences now retain list indentation and quote prefixes through their closing fence or enclosing-container boundary. Coverage includes bullet/numbered lists, quotes, nested list/quote fences, and container exits.
- A first-line BOM is ignored only during heading recognition; original excerpt bytes and source line numbers remain intact.
- A leading `---` is excluded as frontmatter only when a closing delimiter exists. A horizontal rule without a close no longer hides the rest of the file.

## Evidence

### Regression, checks, and independent review

- On the original `5daa50b` implementation, the three reported examples each failed with `MEMORY_HEADING_NOT_FOUND` (3 failed / 22 passed in the initial augmented result-shaping suite).
- After repair: **59 focused tests passed across 3 files**: result shaping, authorized file reader, and real `memory_get`/manager integration. Wrapper wall time 93.04s, including fresh worker compilation; the existing manager suite took 79.65s (new heading feature case 41ms). Prior-head evidence also includes 28 passing tool-contract tests; those are not counted as fresh repair-head runs.
- Targeted lint, formatting, core production typecheck, assertion-safety and line-cap ratchets passed. The official source CLI completed its runtime build successfully before the live Gateway check below. Broad suites and full test-typecheck matrices remain PR CI's responsibility.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview of this repair: **scoped-clean at P0-P2**, with the complete result-shaping source supplied as context. No accepted/actionable findings. The review itself did not execute project code; the test and Gateway evidence are separate.
- Simplification: retain the existing reader, authorization, and truncation owners. This repair changes two existing files: production +37/-19, tests +45/-0. No new state or exports.

### Real built Gateway evidence (not an in-process mock)

Launched the official `pnpm openclaw gateway run --bind loopback --auth none --port <claimed-test-port>` with a fresh task-only state directory, configuration, workspace, and a credential-free environment. Only `memory-core` was enabled and only `memory_get` was allowlisted. No existing Gateway was changed or restarted. The task-owned Gateway was stopped and its port claim released afterward.

The built Gateway's actual `POST /tools/invoke` endpoint received:

```json
{"tool":"memory_get","agentId":"main","args":{"path":"memory/store-policy.md","heading":"Refunds"}}
```

The synthetic source includes a list-prefixed fenced example before Refunds, an Exceptions child, and a following Shipping section. Selected terminal output (JSON-escaped):

```json
{"case":"section-and-child","http":200,"status":"ok","text":"## Refunds\nRefunds are available within 30 days.\n### Exceptions\nCustom items are excluded.","path":"memory/store-policy.md","from":6,"lines":4}
{"case":"bounded-first-page","http":200,"status":"ok","text":"## Refunds\nRefunds are available within 30 days.\n\n[More content available. Use from=8 to continue.]","path":"memory/store-policy.md","from":6,"lines":2,"truncated":true,"nextFrom":8}
{"case":"bounded-continuation","http":200,"status":"ok","text":"### Exceptions\nCustom items are excluded.","path":"memory/store-policy.md","from":8,"lines":2}
{"case":"leading-BOM-preserved","http":200,"status":"ok","text":"\uFEFF## Refunds\n30 days","path":"memory/bom.md","from":1,"lines":2}
{"case":"horizontal-rule-not-frontmatter","http":200,"status":"ok","text":"## Refunds\n30 days","path":"memory/rule.md","from":3,"lines":2}
{"case":"authorization-unchanged","http":200,"path":"private.md","text":"","status":"error","code":"MEMORY_PATH_NOT_ALLOWED","error":"path is not an allowed Markdown memory file"}
```

All six calls passed independent assertions. Shipping never appeared in the selected section or its continuation. The denied `private.md` file is also a synthetic fixture inside the temporary workspace, not a personal file.

Runtime reader SHA-256: `02e270cc0efa2545ae083e02063cf10154d7f85016265d2dc8159eea94fc7553`. This binds the compiled working-tree proof to the source bytes committed in this repair. The capture does not claim a released version or an authenticated model-generated agent response: it proves the real public Gateway tool-invocation boundary without tool/provider mocks or external model calls.

### Privacy and remaining decision

All documents and state used above are synthetic. No personal notes, existing configuration, OAuth profiles, credentials, IP addresses, non-public endpoints, or raw operator logs are included in this PR or proof. Maintainer edits remain disabled because workflow/secrets access on the fork has not been authorized.

This remains a new optional capability. Maintainer product acceptance is still required; the repair and runtime proof do not substitute for that decision. The previous CI pass belongs to `5daa50b`; the new repair head requires its own CI and hosted re-review.

The core message-action vocabulary is repeated in dispatch read policies, scheduled-write policies, delivery classification, target mapping, and cross-context policy. Adding an action requires keeping several independent inventories synchronized.
