Consumers use those facts; the duplicate tables and sets are removed. The public ordered 57-name readonly tuple and action union remain unchanged. Plugin-specific aliases, runtime dispatch, live authority, and security effects stay at their existing owners.

This is an area slice of a widely imported vocabulary owner, not a new generic registry. It deliberately preserves differences between retrieval, conversation-read authority, delivery, and visible-content markers.

An adjacent boundary defect is also fixed: unknown action names such as `constructor`, `toString`, and `__proto__` no longer inherit properties from the target-mode object. They now produce the existing unknown-action error without mutating parameters. A regression exercises the actual target-mapping entry point.

## User Impact

Declared actions, ordering, user-visible text, target behavior, and authorization behavior are unchanged. Invalid prototype-property action names are consistently rejected.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None. Only duplicate static classifications are removed. Security/authorization checks, effect-boundary revalidation, supported failure handling, and public contracts are retained. No config, schema, protocol, dependency, persisted-data, or permission change.

## Evidence

Pinned-baseline comparison passes all 57 ordered actions across eight independent facts and 360 target cases. prs.title: fix(ui): keep Delete unavailable for model-selection-locked sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Web chat header still offers **Delete** for an adopted Codex harness session, and confirming the dialog only fails with `This session cannot be deleted while model selection is locked.`, when the session is model-selection-locked.

Related: #169184

## User Impact

A model-selection-locked session no longer advertises a Delete that cannot succeed. The chat header menu, the Sessions menu, and the sidebar menus now hide/disable **Delete** for those rows instead of navigating to the chat home page and displaying a lock error.

No behavior change for ordinary sessions, main/global protection, or the active-run rule.

## Why This Change Was Made

`canDeleteSessionRows` (`ui/src/lib/sessions/session-key.ts`) is the single UI delete-capability owner consumed by all three Delete entry points:

- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-header.ts` — the chat header actions menu
- `ui/src/pages/sessions/session-menu.tsx` — the Sessions menu
- `ui/src/components/sidebar-menus-render.tsx` — the sidebar menus

It mirrored the main/global protection and all-idle-or-all-archived rules, but not the Gateway's model-selection lock. The Gateway's delete owner (`src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-delete.ts`) rejects `isModelSelectionLocked(entry)` before the archive-state check, for every non-plugin-owned session. So the three surfaces rendered a destructive confirmation whose request is always refused.

The fix treats a locked row as undeletable in both the idle and archived branches, matching the Gateway's ordering. Rows already carry `modelSelectionLocked` (the sidebar projection normalizes it to a boolean, the other two surfaces pass `GatewaySessionRow`), so no new plumbing is needed and the capability stays in its existing owner rather than being spread across the three call sites.

This deliberately does not remove the model-selection lock or bypass active-session safety — it only stops advertising an action the lock forbids.

## Evidence

Root cause confirmed by reading both sides of the contract: `canDeleteSessionRows` returned `true` for a locked, idle, non-main session, while `sessions-delete.ts` returns `INVALID_REQUEST` for the same row.

Standalone repro of the real exported owner (before → after this change):

```text
$ node --import tsx .agents/GOAL-R2-REPRO-169184.mts

# before the fix
gateway would REFUSE delete for locked row: true
canDeleteSessionRows(locked)   = true <-- BUG: UI offers Delete
canDeleteSessionRows(unlocked) = true ok
RESULT: FAIL (UI offers a Delete the Gateway always rejects)

# after the fix
gateway would REFUSE delete for locked row: true
canDeleteSessionRows(locked)   = false ok
canDeleteSessionRows(unlocked) = true ok
RESULT: PASS (UI mirrors Gateway capability)
```

Regression tests added to the colocated `ui/src/lib/sessions/session-key.test.ts`, covering idle unlocked (still deletable), idle locked, a locked adopted harness key, and locked-but-archived (the branch the Gateway also rejects):

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/lib/sessions/session-key.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  49 passed (49)
```

Sibling callers of the same owner (no regression in the surfaces that consume it):

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-session-controls.test.tsx ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-projection.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  28 passed (28)
```

Cost: the touched test file runs in ~12.6 s (1 shard, 30.2 s wall with startup); the two sibling files in ~90 s together.

Format, lint, and types for the changed project:

```text
$ node node_modules/oxfmt/bin/oxfmt --check -- ui/src/lib/sessions/session-key.ts ui/src/lib/sessions/session-key.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ node node_modules/oxlint/bin/oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json ui/src/lib/sessions/session-key.ts ui/src/lib/sessions/session-key.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.

$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.ui.json --noEmit
(no output — clean)
```

Gap, stated plainly: the reported reproduction needs a paired Linux node with native Codex and an adopted harness session, which this Windows-only environment cannot provide. The evidence above is the shared capability owner's before/after behavior plus the Gateway contract it must mirror, not a live paired-node screenshot of the header menu.

<details>
<summary>🤖 AI-assisted PR</summary>

Implemented with an AI coding agent under maintainer direction: the agent read both sides of the delete contract, wrote the repro script and regression tests, and ran the local gates above. A human reviewed the diff, the PR body, and the proof before submission.

</details>

prs.title: fix: finish accepted ACP replay writes during shutdown
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: ordinary ACP shutdown can silently discard already-admitted replay updates and leave truncated replay marked complete.

## User Impact

Updates accepted before shutdown now finish recording in order before shutdown completes. If an admitted write fails during the drain, replay is marked incomplete so a later session load can use its existing transcript fallback. New work remains blocked after shutdown starts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Check stopped state once when a ledger mutation is admitted, not again after it has waited behind earlier storage I/O. The existing stop owner already joins those accepted writes before database/transport teardown. Its private incomplete-marker is only called by an admitted mutation's failure handler, so it must also finish during that drain.

Two net production lines removed (+4/-6),54 test lines added. One existing owner-boundary table holds external ledger I/O to cover successful and failed first writes while a second accepted update waits. No new helper, exported seam, scheduler or custody state. No persisted schema, SQLite durability setting, retention, permission, protocol, config or dependency change.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Remove inside-queue stop revalidation: ordinary storage I/O can delay an already-accepted update until shutdown, so the guard incorrectly dropped real work. One admission check remains; accepted work drains under the existing stop owner instead of being silently cancelled.
- Remove stop refusal in the private incomplete marker: its only caller is the retained failure handler of accepted ledger work, and storage is still alive until that handler settles. Actual marker failures remain logged. No speculative after-close write or new cleanup protocol is introduced.
- Introducing queue1eda44ee3627/#108827 and shutdown-drain98813c23905e/#168587 were inspected. Their per-session ordering and accepted-work settlement remain; neither provides a contract to discard accepted updates. This queue-loss bug is source-established, not claimed as an independently reported human incident. Actual disconnect/grace/accepted-turn recovery is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Complete update owner and existing focused suite inspected, plus actual agent/server shutdown ordering, session-load complete-replay selection, existing ledger facade/types and determining worker complete-flag operations. This is ACP transport replay, NOT the standalone Phase E session-memory backend.
- Original production with the two new regressions:2 intended assertion failures,3 existing tests passed (11.49s Vitest/58.87s wrapper). Both failures show only the first update recorded instead of both; not fixture/startup failure.
- Fixed focused owner proof5/5 passed (59.90s Vitest/87.60s wrapper); new regressions9ms/8ms, retained first case6.593s, transformation65% of file duration under load. No timeout/retry/skip change or performance claim. Final formatting25ms/whitespace passed. Full two-file/seven-dataset independent review scoped-clean P0-P2/0.98 with final source verification successful. Only a mechanical test callback binding rename followed, fixing the owned no-shadow lint finding without changing behavior/assertions; source is unchanged and root/mirror final blobs match. Targeted types retain36 known parse5/MCP dependency diagnostics, none in touched paths: NOT a local type pass. Corrected lint and mandatory suppression result will be recorded before publication. No SQLite persistence/reopen, live ACP client, native process, broad local build or E2E proof is claimed by this held-I/O owner regression; hosted exact-head CI is the broad gate.
- Corrected canonical two-file type-aware lint passed. Mandatory suppression guard passed 14/14 (54.15s Vitest/63.81s wrapper); no suppression or budget change.
- No imports/edges change, so no new cycle/component or plugin startup fanout. Existing read drain, post-stop refusal, delivery ordering and independent session queues remain tested and unchanged.
- Phase E standalone session-memory backend/factory/registry/expiry/federation/tests untouched.

Release-note context: finish already-accepted ACP replay writes and their failure markers during normal shutdown instead of retaining incomplete history as complete.

prs.title: fix: Hermes migration silently corrupts malformed YAML configuration
prs.body:
Related: #172742

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: importing a Hermes `config.yaml` containing malformed UTF-8 silently changes imported configuration values and still reports success.

## User Impact

Operators receive a configuration-file error with UTF-8 repair/re-encoding guidance before migration writes imported settings. After repairing the source, the same command succeeds. Valid Unicode, including a literal replacement character, remains intact. Previously corrupted imports are not repaired automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read and validate the YAML bytes at the existing configuration-planning boundary before decoding. The YAML parser otherwise accepts replacement-decoded strings, so syntax validation does not detect the data loss.

The check belongs to Hermes configuration planning. It intentionally does not change the shared text reader: skill files can be copied verbatim for later loader diagnostics, and memory imports already have their own byte check. Node's existing `isUtf8` handles validation without a new dependency, option, config schema, or protocol.

## Evidence

Real built CLI on Linux / Node 24.16.0 with synthetic isolated HOME, state, source, config, and workspace. Parent `90127436fa45e539616c7b123a549cbd3919c725`; exact clean head `3ffbe8c3f88bd09ec2b53858ecf5fd34a12d7e98`, matching `dist/build-info.json`.

| Scenario | Parent | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bytes `c3 28` inside a YAML skill-config string | Exit 0, migrated, persisted value `�(` | Exit 1, UTF-8 error with recovery guidance; destination config byte-identical |
| Same source re-encoded as valid UTF-8 | — | Exit 0, migrated; exact Unicode read back from destination config |
| Valid `中文 🦞 literal �` input | Exact Unicode imported | Same exact Unicode imported |

All source bytes remain unchanged after each CLI invocation. Successful imports are checked against the destination config on disk, the actual migration `report.json`, and the pre-migration backup archive. This exercises migration, not model/MCP execution.

<details>
<summary>Proof receipt, commands, and limits</summary>

- Claims: C1=Reject malformed Hermes YAML bytes before importing configuration; C2=Preserve valid Unicode and support a re-encoded retry.
- Same native entry on parent and head: `node openclaw.mjs migrate apply hermes --from "$SOURCE" --item config:skill-entry:proof --no-auth-credentials --yes --json --backup-output "$PROOF_ROOT/backups/"`.
- Owner: `extensions/migrate-hermes/plan.ts` `buildHermesPlan`, reached unmocked from the built CLI/provider/apply path and existing config writer. Memory-only planning still exits before YAML parsing.
- Before: RED, damaged YAML exited 0 and persisted replacement text; valid Unicode control succeeded.
- After: GREEN, 3 head invocations: damaged source rejected without changing destination bytes, repaired retry succeeded, independent valid input succeeded. Control: 0/1 damaged input changed destination on head versus 1/1 on parent; 2/2 successful head imports retained exact Unicode; 3/3 inputs unchanged.
- Readback: subprocess exit/stdout; destination config bytes and imported label; source bytes; actual report and backup archive on successful imports.
- Harness: same migration subprocess/readback driver on parent/head, SHA-256 `519b5e160d33fec7a9eee04008ba7c9fb8b5c0e4b9e81b74dcc08462a769cccc`.
- Tests: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/migrate-hermes/config-encoding.test.ts extensions/migrate-hermes/config.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 18 passed; wrapper wall 84.30s, Vitest duration 72.50s. The new regression failed on the parent because migration resolved with the corrupted setting. Its first cold-worker run timed out during preparation; the warmed parent run exposed the intended failure, and the unchanged test passed after the fix.
- Checks: source-scoped `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs --project <temporary-extension-test-config>` exited 0; typed `OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig <temporary-extension-test-config> extensions/migrate-hermes/plan.ts extensions/migrate-hermes/config-encoding.test.ts` exited 0; oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed. Native exact-head build `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts sourcePerformance` exited 0. Source-scoped config selects changed files and their real dependency closure; packaged declaration preparation was omitted for lint.
- Test cost: 84.30s focused wrapper wall / 72.50s Vitest duration; upstream CI seconds unavailable before creation.
- Not tested: Windows/macOS, full repository suites, actual model/MCP execution, or repair of older corrupted imports. No OpenClaw state-shape/updater/Doctor change is claimed.
- Scope: 2 files; production +12/−1 lines, tests +33/−0. Added production code prevents irreversible replacement decoding and supplies recovery guidance; no generated files or lockfiles.

AI-assisted implementation and verification with Codex.

</details>

prs.title: fix: Claude migration silently corrupts malformed MCP configuration
prs.body:
Related: #172953

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Claude migration reports success after silently changing malformed UTF-8 inside MCP arguments, paths, or other imported JSON settings into replacement characters.

## User Impact

Migration now identifies the damaged configuration file and asks the operator to re-save or re-encode it as UTF-8 before retrying. It stops before writing imported configuration. Valid Unicode, including a literal U+FFFD character, still migrates unchanged. This does not repair values altered by an earlier migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Validate the original bytes in the existing Claude JSON reader before decoding. A damaged quoted JSON string can remain syntactically valid after replacement decoding, so `JSON.parse` alone cannot protect imported settings. Missing/unreadable files and JSON syntax errors retain their existing handling.

The same reader owns project MCP configuration, user Claude configuration, Desktop MCP configuration, and settings used during discovery/manual review. Instruction appends and command-to-skill imports have separate byte checks already. Node's built-in `isUtf8` supplies the check; no dependency, configuration option, protocol, state format, or migration framework is added.

## Evidence

Native Linux / Node 24.16.0 CLI proof, using fresh synthetic HOME, source, state, config, and workspace directories. Base: `90127436fa45e539616c7b123a549cbd3919c725`. Exact committed head: `e176db77ac8bb74ed85e9d55e6a4b7c49f833d76`; the clean head's `dist/build-info.json` reports the same commit.

| Source | Base with malformed bytes | Head with the same bytes | Re-encoded retry |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Project `.mcp.json` | Exit 0; reports migrated; persisted argument becomes `�(` | Exit 1; actionable UTF-8 error; destination config byte-identical | Migrated; exact Unicode read back |
| User `.claude.json` | Same silent alteration | Same safe refusal | Migrated; exact Unicode read back |
| Claude Desktop JSON | Same silent alteration | Same safe refusal | Migrated; exact Unicode read back |

The malformed value contains bytes `c3 28` inside a JSON string. Positive controls use `中文 🦞 literal �`. All source files remain byte-identical after every invocation. Successful migrations are checked against the actual destination config, on-disk `report.json`, and pre-migration backup archive; rejection is checked against the original destination-config bytes. No MCP server or model is executed.

<details>
<summary>Proof receipt, commands, and limits</summary>

- Claims: C1=Reject malformed Claude configuration bytes before a config write; C2=Preserve valid Unicode and support an operator's re-encoded retry.
- Entry / same command on base and head: `node openclaw.mjs migrate apply claude --from "$SOURCE" --item "$ITEM" --no-auth-credentials --yes --json --backup-output "$PROOF_ROOT/backups/"`.
- Owner: `extensions/migrate-claude/helpers.ts` `readJsonObject`, reached through the built CLI, source discovery, configuration planning, and the existing migration apply/config writer. Product code ran unmocked.
- Before: RED, 3/3 malformed inputs exited 0 and persisted replacement text; 3/3 valid controls imported exact text.
- After: GREEN, 9 native CLI invocations; 3/3 damaged inputs refused with unchanged config bytes, 3/3 repaired retries imported successfully, 3/3 valid controls retained exact Unicode.
- Readback boundary: subprocess exit/stdout, destination config on disk, unchanged source bytes, actual migration reports and backup archives for successful imports.
- Control: 0/3 malformed inputs changed the destination on head versus 3/3 on base; all 6 successful head imports retained the expected Unicode.
- Harness: same subprocess/readback driver on base and head, SHA-256 `519b5e160d33fec7a9eee04008ba7c9fb8b5c0e4b9e81b74dcc08462a769cccc`.
- Tests: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/migrate-claude/config-encoding.test.ts extensions/migrate-claude/provider.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 35 passed; wrapper wall 9.88s, Vitest duration 5.52s. The three new cases failed on the parent because `apply` resolved after writing corrupted values.
- Other checks: source-scoped `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs --project <temporary-extension-test-config>` exited 0; typed `OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/migrate-claude/helpers.ts extensions/migrate-claude/config-encoding.test.ts` exited 0; oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed. Exact-head native build: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts sourcePerformance` exited 0. Source-scoped types include the changed files and their real dependency closure; packaged declaration preparation was not rerun for lint.
- Not tested: Windows/macOS, the full repository suite, actual MCP server execution, or recovery of previously corrupted settings. This is an external-input admission fix; no OpenClaw state-shape/updater/Doctor change is claimed.
- Test cost: 9.88s focused wrapper wall / 5.52s Vitest duration; upstream CI seconds unavailable before creation.
- Scope: 2 files; production +11/−1 lines, tests +71/−0. The production growth checks bytes before an irreversible decode and provides recovery guidance. No generated or lockfile changes.

AI-assisted implementation and verification with Codex.

</details>

The released tsc-ts 0.0.2 candidate predates three upstream compiler fixes found during qualification. This follow-up reruns the existing comparison against one immutable upstream CI build.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/175541
Stack base: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175567

## User Impact

No product or default compiler change. This remains a draft qualification experiment; adoption and landing require separate approval. The upstream artifact expires on 2026-10-20, so this branch is a time-bounded experiment and fails closed after expiry.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the upstream native artifact from successful [run 39064305206](https://github.com/vercel-labs/tsc-ts/actions/runs/39064305206), attempt 1, source `f43cb6bc130db3e451a28a0a49f3c7e2ed7a26f5`. Stage it outside the checkout, verify the tar and compiler hashes, and extract only the compiler to a fixed path. This is an unreleased CI distribution, still reporting TypeScript 7.0.2.

The repository compiler, 7.0.2 reference, declaration libraries, canaries, auditor, flags, sandbox and resource policy are unchanged. No custom compiler build or fork is involved.

## Evidence

**Negative qualification: keep the repository-pinned compiler.** Exact head `41b2ac4e5d799989e5acfc96e7d33ef661f863be`, [run 39088243171](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39088243171), attempt 1, completed. Tooling tests in both files, both typechecks, lint, formatting and workflow validation passed. All five collection steps succeeded; their qualification audits failed.

279 planned and attempted trials: **273 valid, 6 rejected, 0 unattempted**. All five artifact SHA-256 digests were verified and independent local auditor replays exactly matched the hosted verdicts.

| Scope | Attempted | Valid | Rejected | Verdict |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| [Core + canaries](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39088243171/artifacts/12122661028) | 216 | 216 | 0 | divergent |

| [Root E2E typecheck](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39088243171/artifacts/12122577156) | 9 | 9 | 0 | divergent |

The candidate starts in the pinned Linux x64 sandbox and reports TypeScript 7.0.2. The pinned compiler reports 7.1.0-dev.20260928.1. The existing 4-CPU, 12-GiB, zero-swap limits and isolation/deadline smoke proofs passed.

**The three targeted port defects are resolved in the covered fixtures.** All 180 canary trials completed, across both modes and three repeats: [indexed compound writes](https://github.com/vercel-labs/tsc-ts/pull/155) now report TS2532; [variadic inference](https://github.com/vercel-labs/tsc-ts/pull/167) accepts the valid tuple and reports the correct invalid-tuple diagnostic; [CommonJS runtime syntax](https://github.com/vercel-labs/tsc-ts/pull/156) reports TS1287 and both TS1286 diagnostics while type-only syntax passes. The narrowed-status canary reproduces the first version difference. The generic-union reduction still does not reproduce the actual repository diagnostic difference. Six supplementary nonincremental trials record process exit 137 versus GNU-time exit 0: UI reference 1; plugins reference 1–3 and pinned 1; scripts reference 3. prs.title: fix: updates roll back when an idle CLI process recently used an agent database
prs.body:
Related: #172772

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an update still rolls back (or `openclaw update repair` exits 2) with "An agent database is in use" when another OpenClaw CLI process, such as a plugin command, used an agent database in the last 30 minutes and is now sitting idle.

## User Impact

Updates no longer wait out an idle CLI process. A CLI process now closes an unused agent database about 30 seconds after its last use, so Doctor's existing lease wait from #172772 ends shortly after that process goes idle. The Gateway keeps its 30-minute reuse window. Work that is still running (a borrowed handle or an open transaction) keeps its lease, and Doctor waits for it as before.

**Update behavior:** the change lives in the process holding the database, not in Doctor. It helps updates *away from* a release that contains it. A process started from an older release, including every 2026.10.3 process during the 2026.10.3 → next update, keeps the 30-minute window and can still outlast Doctor's ~20-minute wait. Operators should stop such processes before updating; the docs now say so. No config, schema, lease rows, or stored data change.

## Why This Change Was Made

An idle agent database handle keeps its lease row until its idle timer fires, and Doctor maintenance needs every lease gone. #172772 makes Doctor wait, but the idle timer was 30 minutes in every process, longer than the wait.

**Mechanism choice.** I first looked for a way to tell an idle holder in another process that maintenance was requested (the `core:agent-database-maintenance` lease idea). There isn't one without new infrastructure: Doctor deliberately releases its locks while it waits, the holder is idle so it never rereads state, SQLite has no cross-process notification other than polling (`data_version`, or watching the WAL), and signalling the holder PID is unsafe (an old release or a non-OpenClaw handler would treat `SIGUSR2` as fatal) and unavailable on Windows. Every option is either freshness polling, which AGENTS.md forbids, or a new IPC/sidecar owner. So I took the simpler alternative: CLI processes don't keep the 30-minute idle cache.

**Why the 30 minutes exists.** #153601 (`perf(state): retain SQLite handles for 30 minutes of inactivity`) added it to stop reopening on every operation. Its measurements are Gateway-style workloads (paced reads, many warm agent stores, reclamation every 61 s), and the PR records a maintainer decision to accept the descriptor/memory cost for a 30-minute idle-only window. Nothing relies on it for correctness: callers that need the exact connection across awaits borrow it. A 30-second window still covers a command's bursts (100 reads over 60 s still reuse one handle).

**Where the policy lives.** `resolveAgentDatabaseIdleHandleTtlMs()` sits next to `SQLITE_IDLE_HANDLE_TTL_MS` and keys on the database process role that entry points already install (`cli-oneshot` from `src/entry.ts`/`src/index.ts`, `gateway` from `gateway run` and `startGatewayServer`). It returns 30 s for `cli-oneshot` and 30 min otherwise. The three owners that keep an agent lease while idle use it: the handle cache (`refreshAgentDatabaseIdleTimer`), the idle executor pool (`openclaw-agent-execution-owner`), and the session reclamation Worker. The existing close paths are reused unchanged. Worker threads install no role and keep the shared window; their handle is pinned by the executor generation and retired by the parent thread's owner, which follows the role. Embedders that install no role keep today's behavior.

Busy work is unchanged: borrowers and open transactions still postpone the idle close, and FIFO admission, live-authority and integrity checks, and write settlement are untouched. This is lifecycle mechanics, not data retention, so it stays inside the repair-and-land scope of the storage checkpoint.

**Known tradeoffs.**
- A CLI process that went idle for more than 30 s reopens the database, claims a new lease, and re-registers. That's a cost, not a correctness change.
- The deprecated `sqlite-runtime.openOpenClawAgentDatabase` hands out an unborrowed handle. A plugin CLI command that keeps that raw handle across awaits for more than 30 s now finds it closed, where before it had 30 minutes. That API is deprecated with removal planned, and borrowing (`borrowOpenClawAgentDatabase`, `withOpenClawAgentDatabaseAsync`) keeps the handle open.
- The bare `openclaw` entry (local TUI/onboarding) is classified `gateway` by `resolveCliDatabaseProcessRole`, so it keeps the 30-minute window. It already holds the embedded state lock for its whole life, so an update contends with it either way.

## Evidence

All times are PT on 2026-10-17. The holder in every run is a real OpenClaw CLI process: a synthetic local plugin whose `leaseholder` command reads the `main` agent database once through `plugin-sdk/sqlite-runtime` (`withOpenClawAgentDatabaseAsync`), then stays alive doing nothing (a ref'd no-op timer). Doctor runs from the candidate in every run, so only the holder's version differs. State is isolated and synthetic. No operator Gateway was touched.

**`openclaw update repair`** (candidate package installed in an isolated npm prefix):

| Holder version | Holder idle | Doctor | Lease | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main `e39ce04` | 18:11:14 | `Waiting up to 1197 s for OpenClaw process 28476…`, then `Doctor could not enter maintenance. Waited 1199 s; OpenClaw process 28476 still has an agent database open.` | still held at 18:31:18 | **exit 2**, Doctor and plugin maintenance pending |
| this head `7027486` | 19:11:48 | `Waiting up to 1197 s for OpenClaw process 42014…`, then `Agent databases closed after 28 s; continuing Doctor maintenance.` | gone by 19:12:19, holder still alive | **exit 0** at 19:13:32 |
| candidate `44a340b` (earlier revision) | 18:07:52 | same wait, `Agent databases closed after 28 s` | gone by 18:08:23 | **exit 0** at 18:10:16 |

**Update-time Doctor from source** (`OPENCLAW_UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS=1 pnpm openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`):
- main holder idle from 16:22:09: Doctor waited 1199 s and refused at 16:45:02 (`maintenance deferred`). The lease was still held at 16:46:39.
- candidate holder idle at 17:02:59: its lease was gone by the next 1 s observation after 30 s (17:03:30), with the process still alive. Doctor then completed (`Doctor complete.`) with the holder alive and printed no wait.

**Published driver 2026.10.3 × candidate** (`scripts/e2e/published-driver-update-docker.sh`, driver `2026.10.3`, candidate packed from `44a340b`; the only difference from this head is the reclamation-Worker timer and test reshaping). The holder runs the **driver's own 2026.10.3 binary**, because during a real 10.3 → candidate update every pre-existing process is 10.3. I first tried a candidate-version holder. It can't open state there: the 10.3 Gateway owns it and the candidate schema migration is pending ("refused shared state schema mutation…"). So this cell shows the documented gap, not the fix:
- 18:11:26: the holder is idle. 18:13:44: the Gateway's leases are gone and only the holder's remains.
- Activation `openclaw doctor` ran 18:16:51–18:36:55: `Doctor could not enter maintenance. Waited 1199 s; OpenClaw process 1082 still has an agent database open.` The update **rolled back** to 2026.10.3 and the run recorded `finished` / `rolled-back`.
- This is the expected old-holder behavior. The fix takes effect for updates away from a release that contains it.

**Published driver 2026.10.3 × this head `7027486`, no holder** (same script, unmodified): `PASS published 2026.10.3 → candidate 2026.10.4 (7027486d01b3…): finished, readyz=200, running version verified`, exit 0 at 19:10:52. The update path is not regressed.

**Tests** (each new test fails with the production change reverted and passes with it):
- `openclaw-agent-db.lease-owner.test.ts`: a CLI process's idle handle releases its `agent_database_leases` row at 30 s (read through `readActiveOpenClawAgentDatabaseLeasesReadOnly`, the reader Doctor's wait uses). A borrowed handle in the same process keeps its row until release, and a Gateway keeps its row for 30 min.
- `openclaw-agent-execution.idle.test.ts`: a CLI process's warm executor retires at 30 s.
- `session-accessor.sqlite-reclamation-reuse.test.ts`: a real reclamation Worker retires at 30 s for `cli-oneshot` and at 30 min for `gateway`.
- `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall times (Node; Vitest duration in parentheses): lease-owner 12 s (4.7 s), execution idle 7 s (5.0 s), reclamation reuse 26 s (23.4 s; the existing file uses real Workers, and the new case adds one more Worker cycle). Fake timers only, no sleeps.
- Node pass: 150 tests across the touched suites plus `doctor-maintenance.agent-lease-wait`, `contention-wait`, `settlement`, both migration-refusal suites (`src/commands/doctor-maintenance.migration-refusal.test.ts`, `src/flows/doctor-health.migration-refusal.test.ts`), `openclaw-agent-worker-store.test.ts`, and `session-accessor.sqlite-reclamation-worker.test.ts`. All passed.
- Bun pass (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun`, also this host's default) on the new and changed tests: all passed. One earlier Bun run of the full set failed `session-accessor.sqlite-reclamation-worker.test.ts › retains a late lease receipt… (established)` once. It passed on 3 later runs with this change and on main, and that file's behavior is unchanged in the final head (role undefined keeps 30 min).
- Wider sweeps under heavy host load: `src/state`, `src/config/sessions`, and then `src/commands src/flows src/gateway src/infra src/plugins src/proxy-capture src/cli extensions/memory-core`. The second sweep's 32 failing files were rerun alone: 29 passed. The remaining 3 (`node-workspace-upload-reader`, `sessions-create-worktree-base`, `server.startup-websocket-race`) fail identically on main `e39ce04` on this host.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` passed. Type-aware oxlint on the changed source and test files, oxfmt, `pnpm format:docs:check`, and `git diff --check` are clean. No new source file, so `wrapper-components.txt` needs no line (`sqlite-handle-lifecycle.ts` is already listed).

**Gaps**
- Processes started from a release without this change keep the 30-minute window (the 10.3 cell above), so the next update from 2026.10.3 still needs the operator to stop such processes. The docs now say so.
- The positive published-driver cell (a fixed-version holder during a published update) can't run until a published release contains this change. The candidate × candidate `update repair` run is the closest proof today.
- The mechanism is keyed on `cli-oneshot`. Embedders that install no role keep 30 minutes, and so does the bare `openclaw` TUI entry, which is classified `gateway`.

Private registration, preparation, and rendering helpers make several internal workflows depend on one-use interfaces instead of the operations that own them.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior, supported interface, migration, or required action changes. Channel admission and cleanup, command options, output, provider requests, cancellation, security checks, and lifecycle settlement remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep these implementations inside their existing owners and move their tests to the real registration or execution boundary. This coherent residue combines the already-reviewed channel/QA, node, browser, message, Gateway output, and Comfy portions of the single-consumer family. Against pinned main `81a4ac385dd665c31d55aaa56d1152b66de85538`, the integrated candidate removes **426 net production lines** (+1459/-1885 across 32 production paths; 59 paths total). This uses the campaign's 300-line residue waiver and stays below its wide-change limit.

Current main's condensed QA fixtures and Discord voice-listener imports are preserved. The QA conflict removes only the retired projection tests and their orphaned fixture; the isolated launch-boundary cases remain. Matrix reuses its existing content view instead of moving three assertions into the handler, retaining the handler's allowance of two and deleting the obsolete prefix-file row. Mock and assertion baselines only shrink by exact obsolete entries.

Comfy registers the same three provider objects directly. All six synchronous/asynchronous configuration callbacks, the December 31 SDK compatibility comments, input-image helpers, workflow runtime, history, redaction, and live setup remain. Tests use the existing typed SDK registration capture once per file and preserve all 94 assertions; no test-only production interface is added.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None. No guard or supported feature is removed. Public SDK/package entry points, lazy imports, configuration, protocol and storage contracts, security authority, and write-capable settlement stay with their existing owners. The complete standalone Phase E session-memory backend, factory branch, registry, expiry/federation machinery, and tests are untouched.

prs.title: fix(ui): resolve a bare filename link to its nested workspace file
prs.body:
Fixes #173975

## What Problem This Solves

Control UI turns an inline-code filename in an assistant message into a file link.
The link asked the Gateway for that bare name, which resolves against the workspace
root, so a file that lives in a nested workspace directory answered
`session file not found` while an explicit full-path link to the same file opened
fine. The preview then showed the generic missing-file message even though the file
was present and readable.

## User Impact

A basename link now opens the file it names when the session workspace holds exactly
one file with that name. The reported case - `ORGANIZATION_REPORT.md` inside
`labs/file-organizer/output/sorted-copy-001/` - opens instead of failing.

References that cannot be resolved honestly keep the existing failure and never open
a different file: several files share the name, the workspace search was truncated,
the only match sits outside the workspace root, the match is a directory, or the
reference already carries a path (`labs/output/REPORT.md`). Absolute and
`../`-bearing references are never searched.

Nothing else changes: authorization still runs on `sessions.files.get`, the
`session_file_too_large` metadata fallback and the existing `resolveError` copy are
untouched, and no configuration or migration is involved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The chat reference carries only the displayed name, so the client is the only layer
that knows a basename was intended and can offer a second look before reporting it
missing. The lookup reuses the existing workspace search the Files browser already
uses (`sessions.files.list` with `search`), and retries the normal read with the
resolved path, so every existing path check and admission step still applies.

A single exact match is required. Ambiguity or a truncated listing keeps the original
failure rather than silently picking whichever entry the search returned first -
the same guard the reporter validated in their local workaround.

## Evidence

New owner test `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-session-workspace-reference.test.ts`
(6 cases) drives the shipped entry point `openSessionWorkspaceFile` with the existing
session-capability fixture: one nested match resolves and re-reads by the resolved
path; four negative cases (ambiguous, truncated, escaping, directory) keep the
missing-file failure; a path-bearing reference never searches.

- Red before the source change: `5 failed | 1 passed (6)` - the resolution case and
  all four guards fail with `session file not found`.
- Green after: `6 passed (6)`.
- The pre-existing owner suite `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-session-workspace.test.ts`
  still passes, as do the sibling `chat-session-workspace-{artifacts,loading,rail}`
  suites (27 passed).
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` pass on both changed files.

The first red/green pair ran on the `2026-10-15` main tree; after rebasing onto
`main@32748bce75c` (which merged the Files download work in `#172042`) the red/green
pair was re-run on the same source and reproduced exactly: `5 failed | 1 passed`
before, `6 passed` after.

## Not verified

- No live browser click-through: the evidence is the shipped `openSessionWorkspaceFile`
  entry point under the repository test harness, not a captured UI session.
- `tsgo` was not run over the full UI graph locally; the day-old worktree used for the
  local runs predates the Files download merge, so the later rebase is verified by the
  focused suites above rather than a whole-graph type check.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-session-workspace.ts` is also touched by the open
  `#162552` (binary/PDF file links); this change is additive to the loader wrapper and
  the bare-name guard, so it should rebase, but the overlap is worth a reviewer's eye.

## AI Assistance

AI (Codex) drafted the analysis, the code change, and the tests, and ran the local
verification above. A human reviewed the diff before submission.

prs.title: fix(qianfan): DeepSeek replies arrive all at once instead of streaming
prs.body:
Closes #163657

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: replies from Qianfan-served DeepSeek models are held until the full response is generated and then delivered as one block, even with block streaming on. Two-platform reproduction in the issue (2026.9.5 on Windows, 2026.9.7 on Linux), with a cURL control showing the raw API emits proper SSE deltas, so the loss is client-side.

## User Impact

User impact: Qianfan users on DeepSeek models (deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v3.2) see replies stream incrementally again, matching the same models through the volcengine provider. No config or migration needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The qianfan manifest had no `providerRequest` block at all, so capability resolution treated the endpoint as not supporting streaming usage and every qianfan request went out without `stream_options.include_usage`. The volcengine provider, which serves the same DeepSeek family through the same openai-completions adapter, already declares `supportsStreamingUsage` for both of its providers. Qianfan's v2 chat completions API documents `stream_options.include_usage` on the exact base URL in the manifest (`https://qianfan.baidubce.com/v2`), so the declaration is safe for the whole catalog, ERNIE models included.

The declaration is provider-level (the manifest schema has no per-model flag), which matches how volcengine declares it.

## Evidence

Request-shaping path traced end to end on current main (`ccab514b100`): manifest `providerRequest.providers.qianfan.openAICompletions.supportsStreamingUsage` → plugin metadata snapshot → `resolveProviderRequestCapabilities` (`supportsOpenAICompletionsStreamingUsageCompat`, src/agents/provider-attribution.ts) → `resolveOpenAICompletionsCompat` (`supportsUsageInStreaming`, packages/ai) → `params.stream_options = { include_usage: true }` in packages/ai/src/transports/openai-completions-params.ts. Without the manifest entry, the defaults resolver cannot turn this on for qianfan: it is a configured non-OpenAI endpoint, so the `!usesConfiguredNonOpenAIEndpoint` fallback never fires.

- New manifest contract test in `extensions/qianfan/index.test.ts`, mirroring the volcengine one: `pnpm test extensions/qianfan/index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 4 passed, 22.9s wall.
- `pnpm test src/plugins/bundled-manifest-contract-plugins.test.ts src/plugins/manifest-registry.provider-metadata.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → passed.
- `pnpm test test/plugins/bundled-provider-auth-literal-parity.test-support.ts --maxWorkers=1` → passed.
- autoreview (codex, branch vs origin/main): scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings, patch assessed correct.

Gap I want to be explicit about: I don't have a Qianfan API key, so the live end-to-end streaming check rides on the issue's two-platform reproduction and the reporter's cURL control. The request-side half of the fix is fully traced in source; the exact spot where a missing usage chunk turns into held-back delivery is the one link I could not pin from source alone (the same flag is the only difference from the working volcengine path for this model family). A maintainer with a key can confirm in one run by watching a qianfan DeepSeek reply stream.


## Runtime proof (added 2026-10-04)

The gap note above is now closed. Ran the gateway against an isolated mock that emulates the reported Qianfan DeepSeek quirk (usage-only final chunk only when asked, otherwise one held block), at head 358cb449:

- PR state: request carries `"stream_options":{"include_usage":true}` (verbatim body logged by the mock), channel delivers 12 incremental deltas over ~3.3 s.
- Control with the manifest boolean flipped off on the same head: request has no `stream_options` at all, channel sits silent 4.8 s then delivers the whole reply as one delta, the reported behavior.

Full timelines and setup details: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163698#issuecomment-5971723272

prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175824

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: update workers stopped for excessive output can be reported as unexplained signal failures, with misleading process-supervisor advice and no public cause.

## User Impact

User impact: inspection, inventory, and snapshot failures now identify the capture limit, including when warnings precede the failure. The closed `output-limit` code survives public report redaction.

## Why This Change Was Made

The process runner already records why it stopped the worker separately from its resulting signal. The inspection callers now preserve that fact through the shared diagnostic owner; the snapshot wrapper carries its code across the existing redaction boundary. Warning-derived codes cannot replace the known stop reason, and incomplete stdout JSON stays out of cap errors.

This removes duplicated cap-message fallbacks. Production changes are +34/-19 lines (net +15) to preserve the causal fact and public code; tests are +165/-10 (net +155). Capture budgets, deadlines, cleanup, and free-text redaction are unchanged. This is distinct from the retained-runtime reply-size repair linked above.

## Evidence

- Independent owner/caller/sibling review and fresh autoreview: no actionable findings through P2.
- Native formatter qualification and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Regression coverage: real child output cap and signal, empty stderr, deterministic warning/code precedence, exact public failure-fact projection, inventory cap, snapshot stdout/stderr caps, and ordinary signal/timeout behavior.
- Exact-head [CI run 39089812720](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39089812720) at `4f93d598b7504a8b801a548f53b87a5f6609b5cb`: all 16 budget cases passed in [job 117564379511](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39089812720/job/117564379511), and all 14 diagnostics cases passed in [job 117564379575](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39089812720/job/117564379575). Actual per-case results were verified, including both real inspection/public-report warning variants. The complete CI run passed: 46 successful jobs, 27 skipped, and no failures, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards.
- The first CI run caught an incorrect `it.each` test-context argument in the new cases. The follow-up uses Vitest's `it.for`; production code is unchanged. Fresh correction review and commit hooks passed.
- Execution limits: the local worktree has no qualified test install; the focused Testbox allocation queued and was stopped before tests ran. PR CI supplied runtime proof. Before-fix negative controls remain **unexecuted**. No live-host changes or attribution of a particular observed signal failure.

prs.title: chore(gateway): cover accepted replies with lost QA acknowledgements
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The existing tests do not compose a real QA message commit and lost HTTP acknowledgement with the Gateway's authoritative pending source-reply receipt.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. This regression test checks that an uncertain acknowledgement does not permit a duplicate reply for the same admitted source.

## Why This Change Was Made

The test uses the real Gateway handler, capability and approval validation, ordinary SQLite source admission, and QA bus. A test-local proxy fully consumes the upstream response and verifies the committed business message before dropping the downstream acknowledgement. A distinct second call and idempotency key must preserve the original pending receipt and return `delivery_ambiguous` with `delivered: false`, without another HTTP request or message.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/119057. This covers one remaining native transport composition, not the entire older PR. It complements https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175535 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175616 without replaying their separate experiments.

## Evidence

- Independent source review and formal autoreview accepted the two-file test and worker registration with no actionable findings; the subsequent static-contract correction received exact-byte independent review and a clean incremental autoreview. Formatting and whitespace checks passed. Production LOC: 0; test/registration LOC: +327.
- The original case passed in [CI run 39089306311](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39089306311/job/117562674005), with generation cleanup and exit 0: PR head `cad451f3c60e78d347236496411f46ae106573d3`, tested merge `afe4e0c1defab616e21c597946295af8dcc159f3`, main parent `5588de47ba5cbec1cbd5bd997b446b8f2b27014e`.
- That run failed static gates on this test's extension type imports, noncanonical bus facade, missing invariant context arguments, catch typing and explicit cleanup throw. The correction uses public facade contracts and preserves the receipt/effect assertions and joined cleanup; no failed gate was waived.
- Corrected head `281c993f0a8a33851d7f6adce8538cc54ee4affa` passed [CI run 39090070936](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39090070936): 34 successful jobs, 28 skipped. The [exact case](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39090070936/job/117564990573) passed 1/1 with exit 0 and generation cleanup on merge `9ab64aa61afc4fdc9c3cb97da8abbcbd4ae7265a`, main parent `90e30d0c40d85e6c09479759d72fb4e893a8f33a`. Production/test types, lint and boundary gates passed. Build was skipped, not claimed. Determining Gateway/receipt/QA owners are unchanged between the frozen source and this tested main parent.
- The local source checkout is code-only; no test pass is claimed from tooling qualification. Exact-head review and native landing gates remain separate from this proof.
- Scope: direct Gateway handler/API invocation, real Node HTTP, QA business-message storage and SQLite receipts. This does not prove a live Gateway connection, default-local tool routing, real external channel behavior, refresh/restart recovery or performance.

prs.title: fix: keep refreshed upstream changes out of managed task diffs
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves After a local managed workspace accepts a refreshed upstream base, Review can include upstream-only changes when the checkout's shared default-branch refs still point to an older commit. That makes a small task look larger and exposes upstream commits in the task's Review history. ## User Impact Review now compares all changes against the managed workspace's accepted source base and uses the same base for branch history and individual-commit admission. Uncommitted content remains relative to HEAD, and an admitted individual commit still shows its real first-parent diff. Authorized archived reads and the existing fallback for workspaces without a stored projection remain available. The change requires no configuration, migration, ref fetch, or worktree reconciliation. Remote repository and stored-artifact reads keep their existing behavior. ## Why This Change Was Made The workspace owner already records the accepted base, and the Git diff implementation already accepts it. The local route was omitting that input and inferring a base from shared refs instead. A narrow state-worker read now returns only the accepted base and session binding facts. The local consumer checks the agent, session identity, and managed registry identity/path, retains the current session lifecycle and source guards across Git reads, and passes the selected base to the existing diff owner. It does not load the projection's manifests or recovery payloads. A normal session reset can advance the current lifecycle while preserving the same workspace and accepted base; Review remains available immediately, without reconciling the projection. ## Evidence The regression runs the actual local diff route against real Git and existing workspace/registry writers. With a deliberately stale `origin/HEAD`, the unchanged implementation returned `task.txt` plus `upstream.txt`; only `task.txt` belongs to the accepted-base comparison. The same scenario covers working edits before committing, the committed task afterward, exact totals and history, empty HEAD-relative uncommitted output, upstream-commit rejection, preserved individual-commit content, archived reads, ownership mismatches, and absent-projection fallback. It also observes that projection reads perform no data SQL on the caller thread. Changed-file formatting/lint and the selected production/test consumer type checks pass. `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-diff.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes all 24 tests in 25.02 seconds wall time; the new regression takes 0.998 seconds. The three adjacent repository/incognito/workspace-store files pass another 24 tests in 44.10 seconds. Hosted CI passes on the corrected head; workflow wall time is 658 seconds. prs.title: fix: restore Bun-only global installs with Bun 1.4.4
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Bun-only global installation without Node when Bun places inherited PATH between package-local and ancestor binary directories.

## User Impact

Bun-only installations work with both the pinned Bun 1.4.3 fork and Bun 1.4.4. Persistent Node selection and the explicit Bun launcher requirement remain intact, including when inherited PATH contains ancestor binary directories.

## Why This Change Was Made

[Upstream Bun commit 9510e741520](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/commit/9510e74152073d850a18758ca41114d8f214ffa6) deliberately checks inherited tools before shared ancestor package binaries in dependency scripts. OpenClaw assumed all lifecycle directories formed one prefix and rejected the new layout.

PATH alone is ambiguous when inherited entries also name ancestor directories. The preinstall now uses Bun's runtime version and package-root metadata to distinguish prefix-only root/older lifecycles from reordered dependency lifecycles, then removes only the complete generated chain. Temporary shim classification remains unchanged.

Release-note context: fixes Node-hidden Bun-only global installation with Bun 1.4.4 while preserving the pinned Bun 1.4.3 install path and persistent Node validation.

## Evidence

The original failure was reproduced through both a minimal package and the real OpenClaw preinstall. Diagnostics isolated PATH ordering; the launcher, executable identity, and temporary Bun shim were intact.

prs.title: fix(gateway): distinguish queued chats from completed empty replies
prs.body:
Closes #124447

Related: #50298, #116649, #31346, #33016

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Gateway clients submitting a chat turn while a session is busy under `collect` would receive an empty successful `final` indistinguishable from an ordinary completed empty reply, even though the prompt had instead been accepted for a later queue drain.

This is the independently fixable classification part of #50298. It does not claim to correlate the initiating run with a later aggregate run.

## Why This Change Was Made

Queued client runs keep their existing terminal `final`, preventing older request clients from waiting forever, but now carry the backward-compatible literal `queued: true`. The marker is emitted only after successful queue admission, including the post-admission dispatch-error path; ordinary successful finals retain their exact existing payload.

The change adds no queue owner, worker, retry, or lifecycle behavior. It extends the shared protocol schema and regenerated Swift model, then marks the two existing queue-admission terminal producers.

## User Impact

Gateway clients can now distinguish “your requested run completed” from “your prompt was retained for later processing.” Existing clients can continue treating the event as a terminal final, while clients that understand the optional marker can avoid reporting the queued turn as a completed empty reply.

Clients still need a future resolution of #50298 if they must correlate the initiating run with the later aggregate response.

## Evidence

- Red before the production change: the focused direct Gateway regression expected `queued: true` on the accepted follow-up final and failed on the unchanged payload; the other 101 tests in that file passed.
- Protocol schema tests: 6 passed, including acceptance of literal `true`, rejection of `false`, and unchanged ordinary finals.
- Direct Gateway server chat tests: 102 passed, covering normal queue admission and the post-admission dispatch-error path.
- Chat terminal broadcast tests: 6 passed, including exact ordinary-final payload compatibility.
- Real authenticated Gateway WebSocket regression over loopback with an isolated session store and mock OpenAI Responses SSE: 1 selected collect/FIFO test passed (4 skipped); it observed `queued: true` before the retained prompt drained in FIFO order.
- `tsgo:core`, changed core-test/root-test TypeScript checks, targeted Oxlint/Oxfmt, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Protocol registry, JSON generation, Swift generation check, Kotlin generation, protocol-since guard, and generated-file cleanliness: passed.
- Tested under the repository-supported Node.js 22.23.1 toolchain. The optional `$crabbox` wrapper was not available in this environment, so these were repository-native local lanes; GitHub CI remains the independent containerized check.
- Exact-head GitHub CI on `ca61005f2bff82a647d39e75ac9b1736c53bc1d1` passed the protocol, Gateway boundary, security, lint/type, Node matrix, iOS debug/release build, and focused iOS lifecycle lanes. One unrelated shard is red: [`checks-node-compact-large-9`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31930838182/job/95125328789) observed `776` instead of an exact `777` ms in `workspace-sync.test.ts`; this PR does not touch worker workspaces or timeout budgeting. That test passed once in its full 7-test file and 10/10 additional focused repetitions locally. Contributor permissions cannot rerun the upstream job.

AI-assisted: Codex helped investigate prior art, implement the focused patch, and run the validation above. I reviewed the diff and evidence. Maintainer edits are enabled.

prs.title: feat(openrouter): discovery-driven per-model image generation controls
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Follow-up to #101367. On the dedicated `POST /api/v1/images` path, `buildDedicatedImageBody()` only forwards `aspect_ratio` / `resolution` when the model id starts with `google/gemini-`. That predicate is a carryover from the older `/chat/completions` + `image_config` shape, not a capability decision: on the dedicated endpoint both fields are normalized cross-provider axes.

Two user-visible defects:

1. **Wrong for non-Gemini models.** `openai/gpt-5.4-image-2` honors `aspect_ratio` (measured: `16:9` → 1536x864 PNG, exact 16:9), but OpenClaw silently drops it today.
2. **It fails silently.** The provider advertises `supportsAspectRatio`/`supportsResolution: true` unconditionally, so the override sanitizer passes the value through as supported and the provider then discards it — no error, no `ignoredOverrides` entry. This is on the default path (`google/gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview` is the default model, and most users never pick one explicitly).

A static per-model table would rot — the OpenRouter image model list changes continuously. So per-model support is **discovered live** from `GET /api/v1/images/models` (`supported_parameters`), the same way this extension already discovers video capabilities from `videos/models`.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Core seam (mirrors the existing video one):**
- `src/image-generation/types.ts`: `ImageGenerationModelCapabilitiesContext` + optional `resolveModelCapabilities` hook on `ImageGenerationProvider` — the image twin of `VideoGenerationProvider.resolveModelCapabilities`.
- New `src/image-generation/capability-overlays.ts`: merge + `resolveProviderWithModelCapabilities()`, modeled on `src/video-generation/capability-overlays.ts`. Same invariants: request-local provider copy (per-model caps never leak across candidates), and any hook failure degrades to static caps with a `log.debug` — discovery can never fail a generation.
- `src/image-generation/runtime.ts`: the overlay is applied right after the candidate's provider resolves and **before** the `maxInputImages` gate, so both the reference-image check and the geometry sanitizer see discovered caps. Everything downstream is unchanged; `ignoredOverrides` now reports axes the selected model does not support.
- Re-exported from `src/plugin-sdk/image-generation.ts`; SDK docs updated.

**Extension:**
- New `extensions/openrouter/image-model-catalog.ts`: fetches `${canonicalBaseUrl}/images/models` (canonical bases only — custom proxies keep the legacy path and skip discovery), cached via `getCachedLiveCatalogValue` with a 10s discovery timeout. Descriptors are parsed **per parameter**: `enum`/`range` are read, while `boolean`, unknown future types, and malformed values (non-string enum entries, negative or fractional range maxima) drop only their own parameter — never the model, never the catalog. Mapping: `aspect_ratio` → `geometry.aspectRatios`, `resolution` → `geometry.resolutions` (filtered to `1K|2K|4K`; a set entirely outside the union counts as unsupported so raw values can't bypass sanitization), `quality` → `output.qualities`, `background` → `output.backgrounds`, `input_references.max` → `edit.maxInputImages` (absence means edits unsupported — reference images then skip visibly instead of being sent to a model that never advertised them; every current catalog model advertises the parameter). `n` is deliberately **not** mapped to `maxCount`: `n` is the per-request batch size and this provider fans out `count` parallel requests with `n: 1`, so Gemini's `n: {min:1,max:1}` must not declare it a one-image model.
- `buildDedicatedImageBody()` no longer gates by model family and now also forwards `quality`/`background` (previously dropped by the provider even when requested; the runtime already reported them ignored because the static caps declare no `output` block — mapping the enums without forwarding the fields would have turned a reported drop into a silent one).
- The legacy custom-base `/chat/completions` path is byte-identical to before: Google-shaped `image_config` with the Gemini predicate, no discovery request — pinned by test.
- Static caps stay as the documented fallback: discovery outage, custom base, or a model missing from the catalog degrades to today's behavior — `aspect_ratio`/`resolution` forwarded (API remains the authority), `quality`/`background` reported ignored as they are today (the static caps declare no `output` block, so those two only flow when discovery vouches for them).

## User Impact

- Aspect ratio now works on `openai/gpt-5.4-image-2` (and any non-Gemini model that advertises it) instead of being silently dropped.
- Unsupported axes are reported back as `ignoredOverrides` instead of vanishing — e.g. `resolution=2K` on `gpt-5.4-image-2` now tells the user it was ignored.
- `quality` and `background` now reach models that advertise them (previously never sent).
- Gemini gains the aspect ratios the static list was missing (`1:4`, `1:8`, `4:1`, `8:1`), and edit-mode reference-image limits rise from the static 5 to the advertised 14 (Gemini) / 16 (gpt-5.4-image-2) on the runtime path.
- A newly launched OpenRouter image model gets correct controls with no OpenClaw code change.
- Custom-base proxy users see no change.

Known follow-ups (out of scope here):
- The `image_generate` tool pre-validates reference-image count against static registry caps before the runtime overlay runs, so the discovered 14/16 limits are not yet reachable through that tool (the static 5 still applies there, as today). Discovery-aware tool pre-validation is a separate change.
- `resolveProviderWithModelCapabilities` intentionally mirrors its video sibling near-verbatim (the spec for this change was "core seam minimal and symmetric with video"); folding both into one generic helper is a natural sibling-dedup refactor once a third media type needs the hook.

## Evidence

- Focused suites: `pnpm vitest run extensions/openrouter/image-generation-provider.test.ts extensions/openrouter/image-model-catalog.test.ts src/image-generation/` → 15 files, **151 tests passing** (baseline before this change: 12 + 94). `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`, `pnpm format:docs:check`, `pnpm docs:check-mdx` all green.
- **Regression test proven against pre-fix code**: "forwards aspect_ratio for non-Gemini models on the dedicated endpoint" fails on the pre-change provider (body arrives without `aspect_ratio`) and passes after.
- Catalog fixtures are trimmed from the live payload (captured 2026-08-15) and cover: `512` filtered from resolutions, `boolean`/unknown descriptor types dropping only their own parameter, no `maxCount` derived from `n`, request-local overlay isolation across models, exactly one catalog fetch across repeated lookups (cache), no discovery on custom bases, discovery failure degrading to static caps without failing the generation.
- **Live matrix** (raw `POST /api/v1/images`, one axis at a time, 2026-08-15; status / media type / decoded pixels):

| model | aspect_ratio=16:9 only | resolution=2K only | neither |
|---|---|---|---|
| `google/gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview` | 200 · jpeg · 1376x768 (honored) | 200 · jpeg · 2816x1536 (honored) | 200 · jpeg · 1408x768 |
| `google/gemini-3-pro-image-preview` | 200 · jpeg · 1376x768 (honored) | 200 · jpeg · 2816x1536 (honored) | 200 · jpeg · 1408x768 |
| `openai/gpt-5.4-image-2` | 200 · png · 1536x864 (honored, exact 16:9) | 200 · png · 1122x1402 (ignored upstream — matches metadata: no `resolution` advertised) | 200 · png · 1122x1402 |

  Discovered metadata agrees with measured behavior on every cell; no disagreements to report. (`supported_parameters` for the OpenAI wrapper slugs was corrected upstream on 2026-08-15 — all 43 catalog models now advertise `aspect_ratio`.)
- **Live end-to-end through the runtime** (real API, requests recorded at the provider-http seam): Gemini → one `GET /api/v1/images/models` discovery hit, `POST https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/images` body carries `aspect_ratio: "16:9"` + `resolution: "2K"`, empty `ignoredOverrides`, image returned. `openai/gpt-5.4-image-2` → body carries `aspect_ratio: "16:9"` + `quality: "high"` and omits `resolution`, `ignoredOverrides` = `[{key: "resolution", value: "2K"}]`, returned PNG is 16:9.
- Production LOC: +404/−17 (extension catalog 271; core seam 105 across types/overlays/runtime/SDK re-export, symmetric with the video seam; provider body builder +31/−9). Tests +769, docs +18/−5. The growth is the discovery capability itself; no per-model literals anywhere in the diff.

prs.title: fix(context-engine): wrap JSON.parse in try/catch in context-engine-turn-outbox.ts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In `src/agents/harness/context-engine-turn-outbox.ts`, two `JSON.parse()` calls are not wrapped in try/catch:
1. `writeContextEngineTurnOutboxPayload` parses `existing.payload_json` without error handling
2. `recoverContextEngineTurnOutbox` parses `row.payload_json` without error handling

If the stored JSON is corrupted, this throws an unhandled `SyntaxError` with no context about which row or advancement key caused the failure.

Worse, a corrupted row left in the table also breaks every pending-work query: `outboxPayloadRequiresAdvancement()` projects `json_extract(payload_json, '$.state')`, and SQLite raises `malformed JSON` on the invalid row before the query can reach later valid rows. The agent-run attempt path recovers the outbox and immediately drains it, so one corrupted durable row degrades the lease and blocks valid session turns from advancing.

## Fix

1. **writeContextEngineTurnOutboxPayload**: Wrap `JSON.parse` in try/catch, re-throwing with a descriptive error including the `advancementKey`.
2. **recoverContextEngineTurnOutbox**: Wrap `JSON.parse` in try/catch, logging a warning with the `advancement_key` and skipping the malformed row (`continue`). The row stays durable as audit evidence, matching how blocked rows are retained.
3. **outboxPayloadRequiresAdvancement**: Guard the JSON projection with `json_valid(payload_json)` before `json_extract(...)`, so malformed rows are excluded from every pending-work selection path (pending-session grouping, the per-session row pick, and `hasPendingContextEngineTurn`) instead of faulting the query. This follows the existing containment pattern used by the subagent SQLite registry (`json_valid(payload_json) AND ...`).

## Evidence

Regression tests in `src/agents/harness/context-engine-turn-outbox.test.ts` (the whole file — 11 tests — passes in CI):
- `throws a descriptive error when existing outbox payload JSON is malformed` — the write path re-throws with the `advancementKey` instead of a bare `SyntaxError`.
- `skips outbox rows with malformed payload JSON during recovery` — recovery logs a warning naming the `advancement_key` and keeps the row as inspectable audit evidence.

### After-fix production-path proof (real context plugin persisting messages + database reopen + context reassembly)

`persists real turn messages through a durable plugin and reassembles them after a reopen past a malformed row` drives the **production entry point** `drainPendingContextEngineTurnsBeforeRun` against a **real durable context plugin** — there is no mocked `commitTurn` and no pass-through `assemble`. The plugin's `commitTurn` persists each accepted turn's **actual messages** (`{ role, content }` records, shaped exactly like the entries the transcript hands to `commitTurn` in production) to its own on-disk JSONL context store, and honours the `atomic-idempotent-v1` contract so a host retry of an already-committed key returns `{ status: "duplicate" }` instead of storing the same messages twice. Its `assemble` reconstitutes a session's persisted turns from that store and appends the incoming run's messages — the same contract a real retrieval-oriented engine implements.

The test:
1. Enqueues a turn, corrupts its stored `payload_json` to `{not-valid-json`, then enqueues a later valid turn **carrying real user/assistant messages** in the same session.
2. Runs the pre-run owner (`drainPendingContextEngineTurnsBeforeRun`) — **corruption recovery + message persistence**: the malformed row is skipped with a warning, the later valid turn commits through the real plugin and its **messages are written to the plugin's durable store**, and the lease is **not** degraded. (Before the `json_valid` guard the pending-work projection faulted on the corrupted row, so the owner reported a retry failure and degraded the lease.)
3. **Closes and reopens the existing database**, then continues — **persistence across reopen**: a later accepted turn (`session-a:after-reopen`) advances and its messages are appended to the same on-disk store, while a host retry of the already-committed `session-a:later-valid` turn stays idempotent (`duplicate`, never stored twice).
4. Calls `assemble` for a **subsequent run** — **context reassembly**: the plugin returns the messages persisted before and after the reopen, followed by the next run's prompt, proving committed turn content is reused rather than dropped.
5. Asserts the reopened database reports `pending: false`, the corrupted row is the only retained outbox row (kept as audit evidence, excluded from pending work), and neither run degraded the lease.

Trace emitted by the test's terminal `console.log` and captured in CI output (reformatted below for readability; values are exact) — shard `agentic-agents-support-hosted-1`, job [`checks-node-compact-large-10`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34037447490/job/101498164469), where the full `context-engine-turn-outbox.test.ts` file passes 11/11:

```json
{
  "scenario": "durable-plugin-message-persistence-and-reassembly",
  "database": "openclaw-agent.sqlite",
  "persistedTurns": [
    { "advancementKey": "session-a:later-valid", "messages": [
      { "role": "user", "content": "later valid user turn" },
      { "role": "assistant", "content": "later valid assistant turn" } ] },
    { "advancementKey": "session-a:after-reopen", "messages": [
      { "role": "user", "content": "after reopen user turn" },
      { "role": "assistant", "content": "after reopen assistant turn" } ] }
  ],
  "assembledContext": [
    { "role": "user", "content": "later valid user turn" },
    { "role": "assistant", "content": "later valid assistant turn" },
    { "role": "user", "content": "after reopen user turn" },
    { "role": "assistant", "content": "after reopen assistant turn" },
    { "role": "user", "content": "next run user prompt" },
    { "role": "assistant", "content": "next run assistant reply" }
  ],
  "assembledTokenEstimate": 6,
  "retainedOutboxRows": ["session-a:malformed"],
  "leaseDegradations": 0
}
```

Read against the fix, the trace shows — through a real context plugin that persists message content, on a **reopened** database:
- **later-turn message persistence**: `persistedTurns` records the **actual `{ role, content }` messages** the plugin's `commitTurn` received and wrote to its durable store, not merely keys, session IDs, or a status;
- **database reopen**: `session-a:after-reopen` messages are persisted **after** the database is closed and reopened, and the retried `session-a:later-valid` turn is **not** duplicated (idempotent across the reopen);
- **subsequent context assembly**: `assembledContext` is the plugin's `assemble` output for a later run — the persisted turns reconstituted from the on-disk store, followed by the next run's prompt (`assembledTokenEstimate: 6`);
- **corruption containment**: `retainedOutboxRows: ["session-a:malformed"]` — the corrupted row survives as audit evidence but is excluded from pending work, and `leaseDegradations: 0` — no run degraded its context path.

Before the `json_valid` guard, step 2 fails: SQLite raises `malformed JSON` inside the pending-work query, the pre-run owner reports a retry failure and degrades the lease, so the later valid turn's messages are never persisted.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: shared Git fetch repair can hide an unsettled command outcome and let worktree preparation continue using an older, settled fetch failure.

## User Impact

An uncertain repair command now surfaces the existing canonical cleanup error with its original cause instead of being treated as ordinary repair unavailability. Settled unavailable repairs still warn and return the original failure; successful missing-tip recovery and local branch/worktree preservation stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared repair catch already preserves canonical cleanup errors but misses errors carrying the process runner's private recorded outcome. Recognize that existing metadata before the ordinary warning/fallback return. Both repair-command and retry rejections use this catch; no new helper, export or Result transport is introduced.

The existing real Git-fetch boundary table adds one privately recorded uncertain variant, retaining canonical exact identity, settled unavailability and actual local branch/detached HEAD assertions. Four production and17 net test lines added for a real propagation repair, not cleanup savings. No public API, protocol, configuration, dependency, schema or authority change.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- No safety guard is removed. The repair owner stops discarding an existing uncertain-process fact; it does not claim native process extinction or invent a new custody protocol.
- Ordinary settled repair failure still logs and returns the original fetch result. Real missing-tip recovery, protected refs, output budgets, caller authority and command settlement are retained.
- Original repair290266a77959/#167473 intentionally preserved uncertain native outcomes. Its complete PR description and determining introduction were inspected; this fixes an omitted encoding path, not an alleged human incident or removal of that recovery feature.
- The separately landed project-command adapter remains intact. This shared catch closes nonproject worktree consumption, where the previous settled result could otherwise reach cached-default fallback.

## Evidence

- Complete shared repair, actual worktree Git owner, process metadata/canonical owner and existing Git-fetch suite inspected; actual default-base fetch/fallback and recorded-throw normalization traced. Whole-src repair callers are projects and worktree Git only. No dependency edge is added: the imported metadata reader comes from an already imported module, so no new cycle/component can arise.
- Simplification/test-audit retains one shared error catch and extends one actual owner-boundary table; no test-only production seam, duplicate helper suite, sleep, retry, timeout, skip or suppression added.
- Canonical two-file type-aware lint passed; formatting1702ms/whitespace passed. Targeted touched graph reported36 known parse5/MCP dependency declaration diagnostics, none in changed paths: NOT a local type pass.

The prior same-owner cold route entered prohibited broad worker compilation before assertions; no equivalent retry or local broad build/E2E run was attempted. Exact-head hosted CI is the runtime and broad gate. The historical #167473 timing is not current candidate proof.
- Fresh complete two-file/six-dataset independent review completed scoped-clean P0-P2/0.99 with final source verification successful. Root and isolated mirror source/test blobs match exactly. Current mandatory suppression guard14/14 passed (46.53s Vitest/77.83s wrapper).
