prs.title: fix(cli): restore archived sessions
prs.body:
Closes #124491

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the CLI, Gateway lifecycle contract, focused tests, public docs, and a real isolated Gateway run.

## What Problem This Solves

Headless users could archive a session with the stock CLI but could not restore it. Once archived, a fixed routing key rejected new work and told the operator to restore it, while the CLI offered only destructive deletion.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `openclaw sessions restore <keys...>` to the existing lifecycle command family. It calls the same `sessions.patch` operation used by the Control UI with the caller-observed session identity and `archived: false`; no new Gateway protocol, persistence, compatibility path, or configuration is introduced.

Restore supports the existing agent, Gateway credential, timeout, JSON, multi-key, and dry-run options. Active sessions return `already_active`, and an archived row without durable identity is refused before mutation. The Sessions CLI reference now documents the non-destructive restore flow alongside archive and delete.

## User Impact

CLI and SSH operators can resume archived sessions safely under the same routing key without deleting transcripts or invoking raw Gateway RPC.

## Evidence

Focused validation after rebasing onto current main:

```text
Test Files: 2 passed (2)
Tests: 52 passed (52)
```

Documentation validation:

```text
Docs formatting clean (758 files)

Docs MDX check passed
checked_internal_links=6496
broken_links=0
```

Real behavior proof used an isolated temporary state directory and a foreground stock Gateway built from this branch. The session identity stayed constant across both lifecycle transitions:

```json

{"gatewayAfterArchive":{"key":"agent:main:restore-proof","archived":true,"sessionId":"d7ebae9c-a647-49da-90c7-c53d07935b74"}}
{"ok":true,"operation":"restore","results":[{"key":"agent:main:restore-proof","ok":true,"status":"restored"}]}
```

The temporary Gateway shut down cleanly and its temporary state directory was removed.

Production LOC remains the missing public CLI capability plus user-facing help/examples; it reuses the existing lifecycle owner and adds no duplicate runtime path.

## What Problem This Solves

Windows desktop packaging rewrites every retained runtime file immediately after copying the same bytes, adding avoidable disk I/O to installer builds.

## User Impact

The Windows staging step keeps the copied payload directly. Installed file contents and manifest hashes remain unchanged; Linux still receives its required resource envelope. No measured Windows wall-time improvement is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`stageInstalledPackage` owns the copy, pruning, hashing, and resource wrapping. Only Linux needs the final payload write. Keep the existing validation and size accounting, and skip the byte-identical write on Windows.

The regression extends the existing real filesystem fixture with a delegated write spy: it observes payload writes without replacing their behavior. Production: +4/-1 lines (net +3 for the platform boundary/comment); tests: +11 lines. No new helper, dependency, cache, or runtime setting.

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep panels and terminals through reconnects
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: terminals, embedded apps and canvas previews are torn down and rebuilt on every brief Gateway disconnect.

On a blip the Terminal panel disposed every emulator (scrollback, tabs, selection) and aborted upload batches; a failed restore could prune saved session ids, and input/resize failures were swallowed as success. MCP app iframes and raw canvas previews were keyed on the handshake or connection generation, so they remounted and lost in-app state. The link reader reset fetched documents and cached transport failures as missing previews, read-aloud stopped already-downloaded audio, and an aborted Talk `chat.abort` produced an unhandled rejection.

## User Impact

User impact: terminals, embedded apps and previews stay as they were through a short disconnect. Terminal input is disabled while offline and the session reattaches with its output when the Gateway returns; nothing typed is replayed later.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Terminal: the connection suspends instead of disposing (old-transport requests are retired by generation), tabs go read-only, and resume reattaches each session with a replay. Unknown restore/attach results keep saved session ids; input/resize rejections surface a delivery error and are never queued.
- MCP apps and canvas frames keep their iframe while content identity is unchanged, suspend bridge calls offline, and re-initialize only on real identity or resource change; MCP init timeouts get a Retry.
- Link reader keeps fetched documents and previews and no longer caches transport failures; downloaded read-aloud audio keeps playing; Talk abort rejection is handled.
- Identity changes (different client, recovery scope, or retired offline access) still reset everything.

Part of the offline-first series.

## Evidence

- Focused suites (terminal reconnect/restore/connection, MCP view/bridge/catalog, canvas frame retention, link reader and preview, read-aloud reconnect, Talk) passed on a remote Testbox (265 tests); typecheck/lint findings from that run are fixed in this branch.

Landing repair at `7830e8fcb30` merges main `33b5bee3901`, retaining the newer chat projections and MCP transport fixtures alongside the offline availability and subscription-reconnect contracts. The branch-caused dictation E2E failure selected the hidden desktop button at a mobile viewport; its selector now targets the visible mobile control, with every geometry and visibility assertion unchanged.

Focused validation: three unit files (MCP bridge, chat pane, warm boot), 52 tests passed in 192.48s; the dictation E2E file passed all 13 tests in one rerun (159.47s total, 60.94s test time). The browser suite proves actual dictation controls and layout through the production UI. Scoped formatting, lint, and diff checks passed. Independent selector review and merge-resolution review found no actionable issues. These are focused local results; current-head GitHub CI remains the broad landing gate.

prs.title: refactor(agents): trust admitted runner facts and retain accepted receipts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Runner internals repeatedly inspect values already admitted by their parser, normalizer, or private worker producer. Some receipt consumers also check authority after a successful transcript append, potentially losing the receipt for a write that already happened.

## User Impact

Accepted transcript writes retain their actual receipts instead of being reported as failures after authority closes. Existing authorization, cancellation, deadlines, and recovery behavior remain protected; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Trust those existing admission owners, type private worker task unions directly, share the display-action constructor, and capture the compaction-transition snapshot once. Keep authorization at effects, real concurrency, cancellation, deadlines, pending-answer capture, and durable transcript settlement. There are no public API, config, schema, protocol, retention, or dependency changes; the standalone memory backend is untouched.

Production: +66/-129, **63 net lines removed**. Tests: +33/-25, eight net lines added. Whole repaired candidate: 34 files, +99/-155, including one removed zero-count baseline row. Main already removed the prompt-context freeze; that hunk is omitted and receives no additional credit.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Duplicate finite/type checks on internal numeric projections disappear after their boundary normalizers have admitted them. Raw model limits, context-window admission, bootstrap limits, usage clamping, timestamps, and unknown/unavailable measurements retain validation. These cuts remove downstream duplication, not the boundary or a human-reported failure.
- Private Code Mode and provider-prompt workers trust their host-owned typed task union rather than revalidating the same input shape. Host admission, configuration/budget validation, continuation checks, guest bridge validation, and effect checks remain. A hypothetical malformed private host task is not supported as an alternate public ingress.
- Persisted OAuth strings and diagnostic string output trust their existing parser/redaction owners. Raw credential parsing and all actual redaction remain; no credential or authorization gate is removed.
- Shallow freezes on fresh private prompt/permission containers disappear; adapters still create their separate contexts and the immutable execution override remains. No production caller mutates these private containers; arbitrary mutation by an internal caller is not a new supported contract.
- Recovery no longer guards against arbitrary synchronous registry replacement inside question/liveness callbacks. The additional checks came from #132122 and #134755; their human-reported secret-answer and native-deadline failures remain protected by current delegated authority, exact run identity, pending-answer tracking, and real native liveness. The callback-reentrancy scenario is distinct from those human reports.
- Private attempt controls no longer carry a competing active-owner generation. #134755 introduced it alongside the real deadline repair, but actual dispatch/finalizer callers close each control before constructing its successor. Closed, revoked, aborted, rotated-lifecycle and placement checks remain; overlapping unclosed private controls are not supported.
- Steering drops only the immediate synchronous lease recheck following acquisition and cleanup-ownership transfer. Complete answer capture from #149223 / human report #138555 stays; authority is revalidated after awaited persistence/observation and immediately before provider dispatch. There is no external effect between acquisition and the removed check.
- Transcript adapters stop discarding real accepted append receipts after the write succeeds. The awaited adapter originated in #163264; before-effect SessionManager/transcript assertions remain. Authority closure after an accepted write does not turn the completed write into a fictitious failure.
- Compaction settlement reads its frozen transition snapshot once, only in the durable branch. It does not change compaction facts, target authority, native fallback, or persisted fields.

prs.title: fix: keep sidebar group on /reset, clear it on /new
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`/reset` is commonly used to clear a session context, similar to `/compact`, but it should not remove the session from its user-organized left-sidebar group. Starting a fresh ungrouped session stays the job of `/new`.

Two writers rotate a session entry, and both dropped the group:

- `performGatewaySessionReset()` (Control UI reset, `sessions.reset` RPC, bare `/reset` and `/new`)
- the auto-reply session writers (`initSessionState()` and the fast reply bootstrap), which own resets that arrive as chat messages, including `/reset <prompt>` and implicit idle/daily rollovers

Fixing only the Gateway writer left chat `/reset` still falling out of its group, so this PR now covers both paths behind one shared rule.

## Behavior After This Change

| Trigger | Sidebar group |
| --- | --- |
| `/reset`, `/reset <prompt>` | kept |
| `/new`, `/new <prompt>` | cleared (ungrouped) |
| `sessions.reset` with `reason: "reset"` (or omitted) | kept |
| `sessions.reset` with `reason: "new"` | cleared |
| implicit idle/daily rollover | kept |

## Summary

- `session-reset-service.ts`: preserve `category` only when the lifecycle reason is `reset`
- `session-reset-command.ts`: add `explicitResetPreservesSessionCategory()` as the single source of truth for the trigger rule
- `session.ts`: carry `category` through `resolveReplySessionRolloverState()` according to that rule
- `get-reply-fast-path.ts`: apply the same rule when the fast bootstrap mints a reset entry
- channel/group routing metadata (`groupId`, `groupChannel`, `subject`, `space`) is untouched
- regression tests on all three writers

## Evidence

Local test runs (`corepack pnpm` / repo runners):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-server.config.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` → **95 passed**, including `sessions.reset preserves the session sidebar category` (reset keeps it, `reason: "new"` clears it)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply-reply.config.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.fast-path.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.fast-path.reset-category.test.ts` → **passed**, including the new `keeps the sidebar category on /reset and clears it on /new` cases on both auto-reply writers
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/auto-reply` → 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` → clean

Real behavior on a running gateway (2026.7.1-2, session seeded into the custom group `回归测试分组`, group read back from the session store after each command):

| Path | Command | Stored `category` after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sessions.reset` RPC | `reason: "reset"` | `回归测试分组` |
| `sessions.reset` RPC | `reason: "new"` | `null` |
| bare chat command | `/reset` | `回归测试分组` |
| bare chat command | `/new` | `null` |
| auto-reply with payload | `/reset 只回复 OK` | `回归测试分组` |
| auto-reply with payload | `/new 只回复 OK` | `null` |

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep plugin reload admitted-work drain deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

During a plugin reload, the gateway drains the previous generation's admitted work with a 60-second budget. If the wall clock jumps while that drain is in flight (NTP correction, suspend/resume, manual time change), the drain either hangs well past its 60-second budget or is declared timed out prematurely even though the work is healthy.

- Problem: The drain budget was seeded and re-read with the wall clock (`Date.now()`), but the consuming timer (`setTimeout` via `raceWithTimeout`) runs on the monotonic clock. A wall-clock rewind between seed and read inflates the budget (drain hangs past 60s); a forward jump collapses it (healthy drain prematurely times out).
- Solution: Seed and re-read the admitted-work drain budget on the monotonic clock (`performance.now()`), the same clock the consuming `setTimeout` uses.
- What changed: `src/gateway/server-plugin-reload-cleanup.ts` — three `Date.now()` calls in the admitted-work drain deadline path (`admittedWorkDeadline`, `observeDrain`, and the `drainWithDeadline` recovering branch) now use `performance.now()`.
- What did NOT change: the `PLUGIN_SERVICE_REPLACEMENT_STOP_TIMEOUT_MS` (services.stop) deadline family is a separate cross-clock-domain case covered by other fixes and is left untouched here.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the same clock-domain alignment already shipped for 20+ sibling deadlines (e.g. #171838 node lifecycle drain, #169151 update operation, #173142 cloud attachment transfer): seed and remaining-budget reads must share the monotonic clock that `setTimeout` runs on. Replacing `Date.now()` with `performance.now()` for the seed and the remaining computation is the minimal, behavior-preserving alignment.

- Best fix: yes — identical pattern to the merged monotonic-clock family; no dual-clock bookkeeping is needed because `deadlineAtMs` is passed to the readiness API as a raw diagnostic number with no `Date` conversion anywhere.
- Alternative: converting `deadlineAtMs` to a wall-clock value before display was considered and rejected — there is no such consumer today.
- Risk: the live verification below simulates a wall-clock jump with independent `Date.now()`/`performance.now()` spies rather than an actual host clock change; the services.stop deadline family (a separate bug family) is intentionally out of scope for this change. Production delta is net-zero (4 lines replaced, 4 removed).

## User Impact

Operators reloading plugins (via config change or `openclaw plugins reload`) will no longer see the gateway drain hang past its 60-second admitted-work budget after a wall-clock jump, and healthy drains will not be prematurely aborted by a forward clock jump. No configuration or API change; behavior is otherwise identical.

## Evidence

Live verification of the clock-domain distortion (real `node` run):

```console
$ node -e '...'
wall clock rewind: 300000ms, monotonic advance: 1000ms
OLD (Date.now)  setTimeout budget: 360000ms  -> drain hangs past 60s
NEW (perf.now)  setTimeout budget: 59000ms  -> stays within budget
PROOF: new monotonic budget unaffected by wall-clock rewind; old inflated.
```

Regression test (`src/gateway/config-reload.plugin-drain.test.ts`, added in this PR): constructs `createPluginReloadCleanup` directly, holds a never-settling retained-work token, and drives an independent `Date.now()` rewind of 300000ms between the budget seed and the remaining read while advancing `performance.now()` by only 1000ms. It asserts the armed `setTimeout` budget stays on the monotonic clock.

Pre-fix (source reverted, test kept) — fails, proving the bug:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/config-reload.plugin-drain.test.ts --run
 FAIL  ... > plugin drain recovery > keeps the admitted-work drain budget on the monotonic clock
AssertionError: expected 360000 to be less than or equal to 60000
```

Post-fix — passes:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/config-reload.plugin-drain.test.ts --run
 ✓ ... > plugin drain recovery > keeps the admitted-work drain budget on the monotonic clock
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```

- What was not tested: an actual host wall-clock jump on a running gateway (simulated with independent clock spies instead); the services.stop deadline family (a separate bug family).
- Open PR collision check: searched open PR topics and scanned changed-file lists for `src/gateway/server-plugin-reload-cleanup.ts` and `src/gateway/config-reload.plugin-drain.test.ts`; no open PR touched either file. The same clock-domain pattern is already canonical in merged monotonic-clock PRs (#171838 et al.) and this change applies it to the admitted-work drain deadline specifically.


## Follow-up: adapt existing drain tests to the monotonic deadline

CI flagged `server-plugin-reload.installed-package.test.ts` with `TypeError: Negative ticks are not supported`. Cause: existing drain tests computed the remaining fake-timer budget as `deadlineAtMs - Date.now()`, which goes hugely negative now that `deadlineAtMs` is seeded with `performance.now()`. Adapted the three isomorphic sites (the installed-package active-call block and the two active-call test-support helpers) to read the budget with `performance.now()` and to fake `performance` where it was not already faked.

- `src/gateway/server-plugin-reload.installed-package.test.ts`: fake `performance` and use `performance.now()` for the remaining budget.
- `src/gateway/server-plugin-reload.active-call.test-support.ts`: use `performance.now()` in both drain helpers.

prs.title: fix: retain project Git artifacts when cleanup is uncertain
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: pinned project hydration and repository refresh can remove their working artifacts even when Git command cleanup cannot confirm that owned work stopped.

## User Impact

Unsettled Git work now reports the canonical cleanup error and retains its checkout or refresh staging for recovery. Settled success, authentication failures, ordinary rollback and normal refresh cleanup retain their existing behavior. No public API, configuration, protocol or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

One private project-Git adapter applies the existing process cleanup classification at both command entry points: initial clone and prepared checkout Git. It replaces the initial-clone-only result check and also recognizes privately recorded uncertain thrown outcomes before hydration, repair, remote observation or artifact cleanup. Required-commit rollback and refresh cleanup consume that canonical classification rather than deleting potentially live artifacts.

This real error-propagation repair adds33 production and261 test lines; it is not cleanup savings. Fifteen new owner-boundary cases cover direct recorded failure, pinned probe/fetch/repair, refresh staging and remote-head observation, with settled success/authentication/removal-error controls. They use fixed external command I/O and real task-owned temporary sentinels, not new production test seams or process-extinction claims.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- No safety guard is removed. The older initial-clone-only uncertainty check is superseded by one adapter serving both actual Git entry points; command admission, credential authority, FIFO ordering, retry policy, output validation and ref publication remain unchanged.
- Refresh retains its temporary staging after any canonical uncertain command, including repair against the managed checkout. A recoverable extra temporary artifact is preferable to deleting it while work may still write; no speculative custody classifier or automatic reclamation protocol is added.
- Ordinary settled cleanup rejection remains visible and may replace an ordinary primary failure, as before. This patch does not invent a new secondary-error policy.
- Provenance inspected: staging introduction #135917/d4edc4134d09, requiredCommit #138900/140d9e705ea3 and presence probe #170970/e86f92805ea. These are source-established propagation/cleanup defects, not claims of an independently verified human incident and not removal of those features.

## Evidence

- Complete changed runtime and suite, project clone owner, Git command/result/retry/repair owners and determining Gateway materialization/transport ordering inspected. One private adapter covers both command invocation sites; no shared transport or SDK interface changed. Imports target an already imported module, so no new dependency edge or cycle/component is possible.
- Simplification and test-audit pass retained distinct artifact-retention and settled-cleanup controls, removed the superseded initial check and added no public helper, test-only seam, formatter, suppression or baseline expansion.
- Full two-file/eleven-dataset independent review: scoped-clean P0-P2/0.91, final source verification succeeded. Both final blobs match the reviewed inputs after normal signed commit.
- Canonical two-file type-aware lint passed; formatting46ms and whitespace checks passed. Mandatory suppression guard14/14 passed (61.29s Vitest,104.61s wrapper). Targeted types reported36 known dependency declaration diagnostics, none in changed paths: NOT a local type pass.
- Local runtime and red/green timing remain unproved: the earlier same-owner cold route entered prohibited broad compiler preparation before assertions, and no equivalent retry was run on this loaded shared host. Exact-head hosted CI is required for runtime/broad proof; no native process-extinction, live-network, build or E2E claim.
- Phase E standalone session-memory backend, factory, registry, expiry, federation and tests remain untouched.

Release-note context: retain project Git checkout/staging artifacts and surface cleanup uncertainty instead of treating unsettled work as successful or deleting its artifacts.

prs.title: fix(hooks): stop executing escape sequences from hook manifest metadata
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A workspace hook's `HOOK.md` frontmatter is user-authored content, but `openclaw hooks list`, `openclaw hooks info`, and the human `openclaw hooks check` report printed it straight into the terminal. A hook declared as:

```yaml
name: "Evil \x1b[31mRED\x1b[0m\aHook"
description: "Desc \x1b[2Jwiped\a tail"
homepage: "https://example.com/\x1b[2Jdocs"
metadata:
  {
    "openclaw":
      {
        "emoji": "\x1b[2K",
        "events": ["command:new", "command:\x1b[31mbogus"],
        "requires": { "env": ["DEMO_\x1b[2JHOOK_TOKEN"] },
      },
  }
```

moved the cursor, repainted the screen, and rang the bell of the terminal that rendered the report: the table column that should show a hook name instead clears the screen. The same bytes reached the detail heading, the description paragraph, the homepage line, the `Events:` and unknown-event lines, the `Requirements:` values, the verbose `Missing` column, and the `Hooks not ready:` rows. The hook directory name reaches `Path`/`Handler` the same way.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/cli/hooks-cli.ts` was the last status surface in the CLI that rendered hook-owned strings without the shared sanitizer. `skills list` (its sibling through `formatCliStatusTable`) already routes description, source, and missing-requirements cells through `packages/terminal-core/src/safe-text.ts`, and the plugins list/inspect surfaces do the same. This change applies that existing helper at every place the hooks commands print manifest-derived text, and changes nothing else: no new helper, option, config, or output shape.

Two owners receive the guard rather than each call site: `formatHookMissingRequirements` builds the missing-requirement strings once for both the verbose `Missing` column and the `check` reasons, and `formatCliRequirements` (shared with `skills info`) formats manifest requirement values. JSON output (`--json`) is untouched — it is data, not a rendered surface.

Fix classification: `behavior-preserving` (rendering only; no hook loads, matches, or mutates differently).

## User Impact

A hostile or accidental `HOOK.md` can no longer drive the terminal that lists or inspects it. Normal hooks render exactly as before; control-free names, descriptions, emoji, homepages, events, and requirement names are byte-identical. `\n` inside a description is escaped rather than executed, consistent with the table cells it sits in.

## Evidence

- Base `3d61650b022`, head `41cb4c158785730467ab6c49b752f74bf29a112f`; secretless Linux container, Node 24.18.0, isolated `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`.
- Fixture: two workspace hooks under `<state>/workspace/hooks/` — `evil` (hostile description, emoji, homepage, event name, and required env name) and `evilname` (hostile name). Seeded by `python3 mkhook.py`, read by the real CLI.
- Real entry, identical commands on both revisions:

| command | base | this head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hooks list --verbose` | 2213 bytes, `esc=5 bel=2 csi=5`; rows render `^[[2Kevil`, `Desc ^[[2Jwiped^G tail`, `Evil ^[[31mRED^[[0m^GHook`, missing column `DEMO_^[[2JHOOK_TOKEN` | 2190 bytes, `esc=0 bel=0`; rows render `evil`, `Desc wiped tail`, `Evil REDHook`, `DEMO_HOOK_TOKEN` |
| `hooks info evil` | 573 bytes, `esc=6 bel=1 csi=6`; heading, description, homepage, `Events: command:^[[31mbogus`, unknown-event line, and `Environment: ✗ DEMO_^[[2JHOOK_TOKEN` all carry controls | 545 bytes, `esc=0 bel=0`; same lines render `evil`, `Desc wiped tail`, `https://example.com/docs`, `command:bogus`, `DEMO_HOOK_TOKEN` |
| `hooks check` | 323 bytes, `esc=4 bel=1 csi=4`; rows `^[[2K evil - workspace hook (disabled by default); env: DEMO_^[[2JHOOK_TOKEN` and `Evil ^[[31mRED^[[0m^GHook - ...` | 304 bytes, `esc=0 bel=0`; rows `evil - ...; env: DEMO_HOOK_TOKEN` and `Evil REDHook - ...` |

Byte census command: `python3 count.py out/list.out out/info.out out/check.out` counts raw `0x1b`, `0x07`, and `ESC[` occurrences.

Focused regression: `node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/cli/hooks-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

```text
Tests  12 passed (12)   (the new case now covers list, info, and check through one hostile fixture)
```

Shared-formatter sibling: `node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/cli/skills-cli.formatting.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → `Tests  2 passed (2)`.

Changed-file Oxfmt clean, Oxlint clean (`0 warnings and 0 errors`). Whole diff: production `+27/-12` across 2 files, test `+40`; no new files, options, or protocol changes.

Not tested: `hook.blockedReason` strings are core-generated phrasings (`workspace hook (disabled by default)`, `missing requirements`), not manifest bytes, and are left as-is.

prs.title: fix(decisions): stop stale V1 requests before dispatch
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an explicit decision evaluation can send a V1 provider request after prepared credentials or model selection change while transport preparation is suspended.

## User Impact

Stale evaluations stop before external I/O and return the existing unavailable outcome. Valid evaluations and caller cancellation keep their current behavior. No new configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Always pass the existing composed host admission callback to V1 providers, including callers that supply no separate predicate. The host already owns secret/config generations, selection, deadline and lifecycle checks; withholding its callback let adapters send the request before the host rejected the eventual result. The V2 route already supplies this guard.

Production executable LOC is unchanged; the production delta adds two invariant-comment lines. Three portable explicit-tool cases cover unchanged admission, secret-generation invalidation and model-selection publication; existing caller-guard and physical-drain tests remain intact.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171965

## Evidence

- Real public SubQ registration, the actual explicit decision tool, real prepared SecretRef publication, the original guarded-fetch callback and an owned loopback server reproduced both credential replacement and removal: each sent one POST before the fix. With the host patch, both reject before HTTP (zero POSTs). Allowed, model-denied and consumer-revoked controls also pass: five cases total, physical request counts 1/0/0/0/0.
- That behavioral proof uses the SubQ `5d7676e` source tree plus this host patch and two added proof cases. It proves host authority at the physical-effect boundary, not authenticated vendor inference, vendor TLS or native provider qualification.
- The portable main-based admission suite passed all 8 tests on [Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39088755054). Its verified source tree `7b4e24ae` exactly matches signed head `d902d461`. The wrapper reported a cleanup timeout after the tests passed; native stop and authoritative lease status subsequently confirmed completion. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39088918918) completed successfully at `d902d461`, including typecheck and lint. Landed as [71692ce01a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/71692ce01aae1e50ab16e83b2649005db82da4f1).
- Targeted oxfmt and `git diff --check` pass. Independent source review and fresh Astra/high autoreview (P0–P2) are clean.

Connected follow-ups, outside this repair: migrate the internal tool prefilter to V2 so valid metadata/cost does not trigger lossy V1 rejection; unify Decision usage attribution for core-tool, prefilter and plugin calls without duplicate events.

prs.title: refactor(storage): simplify native resource close ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Startup certification reconstructs cleanup from a second close acknowledgement and several mirrored flags, even though the task already closes its native handles and leases. Resource retirement also projects a second completion promise for passive readiness observers. These duplicate lifetimes make the real native-close and failure-custody boundaries harder to follow.

## User Impact

No intended feature, storage-format, migration or durability change. Startup still uses at most two certification workers and hands each database to runtime only after its task cleanup. Actual close callers and test teardown still join native cleanup and receive its failure. A readiness probe during retirement now returns false immediately; an already-aborted probe retains its AbortError and original reason.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry one cleanup result from the native certification task through successful pool completion. Keep parent writer admission until that completion, without a second release handshake or reconstructed close flags. Keep explicit native termination before orphan-lease cleanup, with failed cleanup retaining custody and retry. Store the real generic close operation for teardown instead of a deferred mirror, and use a Boolean close observation for readiness. Snapshot pending opens once under the existing synchronous close-admission exclusion.

This is a small area split of the closed/parked storage recovery family under campaign rule11. Against fresh main d508bbe3c96a73fe97117afe29a17e98ac92c813, nine production files remove **55 net production lines** (+62/-117). Current whole diff:16 files +137/-216. This includes the now-unused task-failure custody projection and private getter; actual pool-local input-consumed custody and termination policy stay. Main's newer consolidated resource tests and multi-symbol publication teardown inventory remain; donor overlap is counted once. The constructor-input clone and final residue are not part of this slice.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

| Removed mechanism | Provenance and accepted scenario | What happens now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pooled close/release acknowledgement and mirrored flags | [#152378](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/152378), original f9d9f3dffeda: synthetic fleet/startup proof, not a cited human need for another acknowledgement after native cleanup. | Successful task completion carries actual cleanup and releases its slot; the parent still holds writer admission until completion. A late checkpoint hint can be lost after channel close, but native checkpoint/lease cleanup has already settled. |
| Passive full-close completion projection | [#154069](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154069), original e0d80000067d: synthetic finalizer proof alongside retained projection responsiveness, not a human passive-observer settlement incident. | Readiness returns false during close rather than waiting or receiving the close error. Actual close caller and teardown retain the real operation, native failure, ordering and retry. |
| Repeated pending-open snapshots | [#140897](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140897), original7ab507770f3; later extraction is not its birth. Existing producer synchronously rejects matching opens while close selection is installed. | Join one complete pending-owner snapshot. A future producer bypassing admission must be fixed at that producer rather than accommodated by an unbounded rescan. |

COMMIT-service [#139469](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/139469), whose inspected description records an actual Team Gateway lock/deadlock, and blocked-WAL/archive [#154302](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154302) contracts remain. The latter is retained for data correctness; this PR does not newly classify its underlying report as human evidence. Measured staged-grant performance, current authority, FIFO, accepted-write/COMMIT settlement, native-last cleanup, warnings, exact lease receipts and failed-stop retry remain. No schema, column, durability, retention, permission, dependency, public config, Gateway protocol or Plugin SDK change. No standalone session-memory backend, factory, registry, expiry, federation machinery or tests are removed or shrunk.

## Evidence

Initial15-root targeted types and15-file type-aware lint pass. After removing the newly orphaned projection, fresh four-root types, changed-source lint, correctly scoped root-helper lint, formatting, one-page MDX and canonical docs formatting pass. Runtime cycles zero, static Madge cycles zero and whitespace pass. The initial independent composed-area review was scoped-clean P0-P2 (source-only confidence0.87). After the failure-path receipt repair, fresh four-root types, lifetime-only lint/format and whitespace pass; a fresh full composed review also completed scoped-clean P0-P2, no accepted/actionable findings, confidence0.82, with final-source verification. Its verdict is source-only, not runtime proof.

The resources owner suite passed27/27, with completed worker-generation verification (1042.72s wrapper;803.59s shard,96percent transform). Startup concurrency completed3pass/3fail plus a custody-teardown error (764.93s wrapper): successful sibling drainage, idle cleanup retry and pending-lease drainage; failures were first handoff's unchanged120000ms deadline, refusal close observed2calls instead of1, and overlapping-drain retryEntered false. Teardown reported uncertain reclamation cleanup. These are recorded failures, not baseline/load attribution or a passing aggregate. No timeout, retry, skip or assertion was changed.

Source investigation found pooled failed tasks report actual native cleanup over their private closed message before rejecting, but the candidate ignored that receipt. The one-line repair restores receipt consumption for both transports without restoring the ACK/deferred/four flags. The original driver was retired only after the startup wrapper completed. A serial successor replayed startup after that substantive fix: five cases passed, including the original handoff/one-close refusal assertions, with no custody-teardown error; overlapping-drain retryEntered false remains unresolved (10476ms). The wrapper completed generation verification and failed984.14s; a passing replay is not proof of every earlier cause.

Previously unrun siblings then passed the real clean-sibling receipt and committed-finalization-before-successor cases. Readiness during-close expired its unchanged30000ms deadline at30036ms, without an assertion mismatch or established cause. Both configs completed generation verification; their invocation failed904.42s. The owning readiness fixture/flow was inspected; no timeout/retry/skip/assertion change or failed-case rerun.

The native/admission group subsequently passed all nine selected cases: real readonly native join and selected-root pending admissions; blocked WAL/resource/shared-state close; crashed reused Worker exact lease and restored-receipt retry; accepted COMMIT writer admission; idle collection. The complete group took731.84s including generation verification. These bring distinct passing runtime proof to43 cases, not an aggregate green run. The non-isolated SQLite lifecycle harness then expired its unchanged120000ms deadline (120220ms) and aborted its managed child before final report assertions. Wrapper inventory1 and source-closure3 cases passed. Mandatory suppression reported13pass/1fail: Git-tracked enumeration fell back to filesystem enumeration1103calls; the intentional suppression allowlist passed and no suppression is added. An exact standalone isolated Git enumeration later completed in639ms/status0; this does not establish the failed invocation's cause or a fix.

The overlapping-retirement fixture's Boolean/default short polling was replaced with the existing deferred helper, resolved in its already-controlled second native-termination callback. It races the existing startup-settlement rejection, preserving the outer deadline and every subsequent pending/native/shared-close/exact2calls/lease assertion. This tests causal ordering, not a one-second public latency contract; the original fixture explicitly injects synthetic dispatch and retirement failures. Fresh targeted test types/lint/format and whitespace passed. The fresh full candidate review completed scoped-clean P0-P2, confidence0.88, no actionable findings, with final source verification. The selected repaired case passed79846ms; the other five startup cases were filtered, not replayed. Its shard took345.52s (67percent transform/23tests); the wrapper completed artifact verification and passed423.38s. The mandatory suppression suite passed14/14 (60.98s shard/144.45s wrapper), including Git enumeration and the unchanged explicit allowlist. No new suppression is added; the earlier fallback failure's cause remains unestablished. Current distinct runtime proof is44passing cases; earlier failures remain historical evidence, not a claimed aggregate green suite. The readiness and harness failures remain investigated but unresolved; no blanket baseline/load attribution. Whitespace passed. Exact-head hosted CI remains mandatory; no landing claim.

The current-main resource test integration preserves its existing custody/retry tables and helpers. Success/native-failure cases additionally call real teardown while native close is held, yield one event turn and assert teardown remains pending, then release and join it. Startup tests remove only obsolete release interception and cross-port closed markers; certification waves, row/readiness/lease checks, failed native retirement, shared drainage and pending-lease settlement stay. No timeout, retry, skip, assertion relaxation or suppression is added. English reference wording changes only one existing paragraph; headings, links, anchors, current Doctor/NOCOW guidance and generated translations remain unchanged.

## Exact-head hosted CI

[CI run 39085877827](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39085877827) passed on `0564cbbffa57c587b5b639671332378daa3a273d`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. prs.title: fix(telegram): route model-confirmation edit through rich funnel
prs.body:
Closes #123886

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with `richMessages: true` on their Telegram account and who complete the `/models` picker would see the final "✅ Model changed to…" confirmation rendered on top of / mixed with the stale rich-text markup from the picker's prior provider/model-list step, instead of a clean confirmation message. The picker's intermediate steps (provider list, model list, pagination) already fully replace the rich body correctly; only the terminal confirmation edit was affected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `/models` picker sends its initial body as a rich message when `richMessages` is enabled, and every lifecycle edit to that message (provider list, model list, pagination) already routes through the rich funnel in `createTelegramCallbackMessageActions`. The final selection confirmation was the one exception: it always fell back to the legacy HTML `editMessageText` path. Editing a rich-sent message through that legacy text path does not fully replace the prior rich body — Telegram renders the new plain/HTML text mixed with the stale rich markup underneath it.

The fix converts the model-confirmation call site to author rich content via hand-built `RichText`/`InputRichBlock[]` when `richMessages` is enabled, following the existing `progress-draft-preview.ts` precedent for opting a `parse_mode: "HTML"` edit back onto the rich funnel:

- `TelegramCallbackRichTextOverride` lets `editCallbackMessage`/`editCallbackMessageWithButtons` accept an optional `richTextOverride`; when supplied, the edit routes through `getTelegramRichRawApi(bot.api).editMessageText(...)` with hand-built `rich_message` blocks instead of the legacy text funnel.
- `buildModelSelectionConfirmation` (new file) builds both the HTML and rich-block confirmation bodies from one shared text-building function, so the two representations can't drift apart — only model-id HTML-escaping and the runtime placeholder spelling differ per funnel.
- Non-rich accounts (`richMessages` disabled or unset) are unaffected; the legacy HTML path is unchanged for that funnel.

As a side effect of this fix, `bot-handlers.callback-router.ts` grew past the repo's 700-line oxlint `max-lines` cap, so the pre-existing ~290-line `handleTelegramModelCallback` function was extracted verbatim into a new file, `bot-handlers.model-callback.ts`, with no logic changes — pure file-split, kept in this PR so CI stays green (`AGENTS.md`: "Split files around ~700 LOC... never add a `max-lines` suppression").

This PR supersedes closed PR #124173, which introduced rich-block sending but left the confirmation edit on the legacy HTML path — ClawSweeper's own review of that PR classified it as `partial_overlap`, i.e. it fixed the picker's rich-block plumbing but not the actual reported bug (the confirmation still overlapped stale rich text). This change closes that exact gap.

## User Impact

Telegram operators with `richMessages: true` now see a single clean confirmation message when they finish the `/models` picker — no more stale/mixed rich-text markup left behind. Operators without `richMessages` enabled see no behavior change.

## Evidence

- Targeted tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.model-callback.ts extensions/telegram/src/model-confirmation-message.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts` (and related callback-router/harness specs) — 151/151 passing, including a new regression test asserting `richTextOverride` routes through the rich funnel and 3 new `buildModelSelectionConfirmation` tests asserting HTML vs rich-block parity/escaping.
- Full extension suite: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram` — 3593/3594 passing; the 1 failure (`setup-surface.test.ts > accepts numeric sender ids only`) is a pre-existing, unrelated sandbox-locale artifact (`zh`-locale string vs expected English string), reproducible on `main` before this change.
- Typecheck: `pnpm tsgo:extensions` clean.
- Lint: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on all touched/added files — exit 0, confirms the `max-lines` violation from the file-split is resolved (`bot-handlers.callback-router.ts` now 395 lines, down from 706).
- Format: `pnpm format` — no diff.
- Pre-land `$autoreview` (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning): `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported`, `overall: patch is correct (0.96)`.
- Live Telegram bot-to-bot proof was not feasible in this environment (no bot token configured); the mock-harness/unit proof above exercises the exact changed rich-funnel edit path per the ClawSweeper Review Policy real-behavior-proof gate for channel-visible changes.

## Update (commit 6973bab29b9)

Two fixes on top of the original commit:

- **ClawSweeper P1 finding addressed** — `editCallbackMessage`'s rich-routing branch previously fell back to `buildTelegramRichMarkdown(text)` for *any* rich-account callback edit that wasn't `parse_mode: "HTML"`, not just the model-picker confirmation. That silently ran markdown parsing over arbitrary un-authored text from approval receipts (`terminalizeApprovalMessage`), the plugin SDK's `respond.editMessage`, and the model picker's own intermediate pagination/provider-list/model-list/error edits — none of which are markdown-authored, so incidental `*`/`_`/backtick/`[` characters (e.g. in provider/model ids or user-controlled error text) could be reinterpreted as formatting instead of sent literally. Fixed by making rich routing strictly opt-in per call: it now only fires when the caller explicitly supplies `richTextOverride`'s hand-built blocks (as the model-picker confirmation does); every other caller — regardless of `richMessages`/`parse_mode` — stays on the legacy literal-text funnel, exactly as before this PR. `buildTelegramRichMarkdown` is no longer imported by this file (still used correctly elsewhere: streaming draft previews and the general outbound-delivery pipeline, where callers genuinely author markdown).
- **CI fixes**: `check-test-types` (two `bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts` blocks needed explicit `vi.fn<T>()` typing plus a null-check helper for `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`-safe `.mock.calls.at(0)` access) and `check-dependencies`/knip (`ModelSelectionConfirmationParams`/`ModelSelectionConfirmation` had no external importer and shouldn't have been exported).

**Correction to my earlier claiming comment on #123886**: I stated "clean typecheck" there; at that point `check-test-types` and `check-dependencies` were actually failing on CI (fixed now, in this commit). Apologies for the inaccurate evidence claim — flagging it here so the record is accurate.

### Updated evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts` — 7/7 passing, including a rewritten test asserting plain-text edits with no `richTextOverride` stay on the legacy funnel even when `richMessages` is enabled (inverts the prior test, which asserted the now-fixed over-broad behavior), and updated fallback/error-path tests that now supply an explicit override to exercise the rich funnel.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram` (full extension suite) — 3593/3594 passing; same single pre-existing unrelated `setup-surface.test.ts` locale failure noted above, reproduced identically on this branch's pre-fix HEAD via `git stash`.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — both clean.
- `knip` production + all-exports check — clean, no new dead exports.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt` — no diff. `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on touched files — exit 0.
- Pre-land `$autoreview` (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning) rerun on this commit: `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported`, `overall: patch is correct (0.98)`.
- Live Telegram bot-to-bot proof remains not feasible in this environment (no bot token configured), unchanged from the original PR evidence.

## Update (commit a0dec118a21): delete-and-reply instead of legacy-edit on rich-edit failure

ClawSweeper's follow-up P2 finding on the prior commit: `editCallbackMessage`'s
catch block fell back to `legacyEditCallbackMessage(text, editParams)` whenever
the rich raw-API edit failed for a non-terminal reason. `richTextOverride` is
only ever supplied for a message that was itself sent as rich (the model
picker's final confirmation edit), so a legacy-text retry there reproduces the
exact stale-rich-markup symptom #123886 reported — the new text lands mixed
with the prior rich body instead of replacing it.

Fixed by extracting a shared `deleteAndReplyCallbackMessage` helper (delete
the rich-sent message, then send a plain reply) and using it both for this
new failure path and for `editCallbackMessageWithButtons`'s existing "no text
in the message" recovery, which had the same delete-then-reply logic inlined
already — a small dedup alongside the fix, not just a symptom patch.

### Updated evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts`
  — 8/8 passing, including a new test ("deletes and replies instead of
  legacy-editing when the rich edit fails for a non-terminal reason") and the
  `editCallbackMessageWithButtons` describe block's "deletes and replies,
  through the real /model-picker-confirmation call shape, when the rich edit
  fails" case, now reusing the shared helper.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram` (full extension suite) —
  3594/3595 passing; same single pre-existing unrelated `setup-surface.test.ts`
  locale failure noted above (reproduces identically on `origin/main`, not
  touched by this branch).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — clean.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on both touched files — exit 0.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt` on both touched files — no diff.
- `knip` (production + dependencies) — clean, no new unused exports.
- Pre-land `$autoreview` (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning) rerun on this
  commit: `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported`,
  `overall: patch is correct (0.97)`.
- Live Telegram bot-to-bot proof remains not feasible in this environment (no
  bot token configured), unchanged from the original PR evidence.


## Update (commit f082965e64c): correct inline comment on rich-funnel invariant

ClawSweeper's re-review on `a0dec118a21` surfaced one actionable finding:

- **[P3] Correct the callback-funnel explanation** — `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.model-callback.ts:294-298`. The inline comment claimed the picker's provider/model-list edit steps "already edit through the rich funnel when richMessages is enabled." That's inaccurate: `editCallbackMessageWithButtons` only takes the rich path when the caller explicitly supplies `richTextOverride`, and none of the list/pagination/error edit calls in this file pass one — only the terminal confirmation does.

Verified the finding against real code before fixing:
- `bot-handlers.callback-actions.ts` gates rich routing on `if (!richMessages || !richTextOverride)` falling back to legacy — both conditions are required, not just `richMessages`.
- Grepped all 10 `editMessageWithButtons`/`editCallbackMessageWithButtons` call sites in `bot-handlers.model-callback.ts`: only the final confirmation call supplies rich blocks; every provider-list/model-list/pagination/error edit omits `richTextOverride` and stays on the legacy funnel.

Fix: reworded the comment to state the true invariant — those list/pagination/error steps stay on the legacy HTML funnel, and this terminal confirmation is the one call that explicitly opts into the rich funnel via `richTextOverride`. Comment-only change, no behavior difference.

Validation:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts` — 149/149 passing.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.model-callback.ts` — clean.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.model-callback.ts` — applied.
- `git diff --check` — clean.

Note: ClawSweeper's proof-confidence score on this PR is driven by the disclosed, unresolved "no bot token configured in this sandbox" limitation — real Telegram behavior proof for the rich-edit/delete-and-reply path is still outstanding and I can't produce it here. That gap remains honestly disclosed rather than worked around.



## Update (commit 952e6f88239): correct remaining rich-funnel comment (late finding)

ClawSweeper's re-review on `f082965e64c` surfaced one actionable finding:

- **[P3] Correct the remaining rich-funnel explanations** — `extensions/telegram/src/model-confirmation-message.ts:4-7`. Flagged as a late finding: the same inaccurate claim fixed at `bot-handlers.model-callback.ts:294-298` in the prior commit was still present in this file's JSDoc header ("the picker's provider/model-list edits already went through the rich funnel"), and duplicated in a regression-test comment at `bot.test.ts:2881`.

Verified before fixing: grepped every `richBlocks` usage in `extensions/telegram/src/**` — `model-confirmation-message.ts` is the sole producer, and the terminal confirmation edit in `bot-handlers.model-callback.ts` is the sole consumer. Provider/list/pagination/error edits never supply `richTextOverride` and stay legacy-only, confirming the same corrected invariant already landed in the previous commit.

Fix: reworded both comments to state that legacy HTML is used by every other picker step (and as this confirmation's fallback), while rich blocks are used only by this terminal confirmation, which explicitly opts into the rich funnel via `richTextOverride`. Comment-only change, no behavior difference.

Validation:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts` — 149/149 passing.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt` on both touched files — clean, no reformatting needed.
- `git diff --check` — clean.

Note: the disclosed "no bot token configured in this sandbox" real-Telegram-proof gap remains unresolved and unchanged from prior updates.



## Update (commit d55b43e32ef): send fallback before deleting the picker

ClawSweeper's re-review on `952e6f88239` (reviewed_at `2026-08-16T01:39:38.304Z`) surfaced one actionable finding:

- **[P2] Send the fallback before deleting the picker** — `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.ts:115-118`. `deleteAndReplyCallbackMessage` deleted the rich picker before awaiting `sendMessage`. If that send failed, the model selection had already been applied but the user lost both the picker and its confirmation — a silent-failure outcome per this repo's own severity doctrine (silent failure ranks above crash or missing feature).

Verified before fixing:
- Read `deleteAndReplyCallbackMessage` in full: it awaited `deleteCallbackMessage()` (swallowing its own errors) and only then called `replyToCallbackChat(text, replyParams)`. Exactly as described.
- Confirmed via `git log --oneline -- extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.ts` that this helper (and its ordering) was introduced by this PR's own commit `a0dec118a21`, not a pre-existing unrelated defect — squarely in-scope to fix here.
- Confirmed via grep that no existing test covered this ordering (only that both calls occurred, not their order or the rejection path).

Fix: reordered `deleteAndReplyCallbackMessage` to call `replyToCallbackChat` (send) first, then make `deleteCallbackMessage` best-effort only after a successful send. A send failure now propagates untouched and never triggers a delete, so the picker is never destroyed without a working replacement.

Added two regression tests in `bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts`:
- asserts `sendMessage`'s invocation order is before `deleteMessage`'s (fails pre-fix: order was reversed);
- asserts a `sendMessage` rejection propagates and `deleteMessage` is never called (fails pre-fix: delete already happened unconditionally before the send was even attempted).

Both new tests were confirmed to fail against the pre-fix code (via `git stash` of the production change alone) for the intended reason, then pass after the fix.

Validation:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts` — 151/151 passing.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt` on both touched files — applied, clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- `.claude/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` (Codex, gpt-5.6-sol, high reasoning) — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

Note: the disclosed "no bot token configured in this sandbox" real-Telegram-proof gap remains unresolved and unchanged from prior updates.


## Update (commit 4ebf2f18165): forward business context to the fallback picker's deletion

ClawSweeper's re-review on `d55b43e32ef` (reviewed_at `2026-08-16T03:37:58.723Z`) surfaced one actionable finding:

- **[P2] Forward business context when deleting the fallback picker** — `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.ts:119-121`. `deleteAndReplyCallbackMessage` sends the replacement with the callback's business context but then calls `deleteCallbackMessage`, whose delete omitted it. On a Business callback whose rich edit fails, the replacement could be sent while deletion silently failed and was swallowed, leaving the stale interactive picker behind.

Verified before fixing:
- Re-read `deleteCallbackMessage`: it called `bot.api.deleteMessage(chat_id, message_id)` unconditionally, while its siblings `legacyEditCallbackMessage` and `replyToCallbackChat` both forward `business_connection_id`.
- Checked grammY's typed API surface (`node_modules/grammy/out/core/api.d.ts`): `deleteMessage(chat_id, message_id, signal?)` has **no** `business_connection_id` parameter at all — unlike `editMessageText`/`sendMessage`/`editMessageReplyMarkup`, which all accept one.
- Cross-checked against the Telegram Bot API's own method list (`@grammyjs/types/methods.d.ts`): `deleteMessage` genuinely has no such field. Telegram instead exposes a dedicated method for this exact case, `deleteBusinessMessages(business_connection_id, message_ids)`, which grammY surfaces as `bot.api.deleteBusinessMessages(...)`. Deleting a business-sent message is a different Bot API call, not `deleteMessage` plus an extra field.

Fix: `deleteCallbackMessage` now calls `bot.api.deleteBusinessMessages(business_connection_id, [message_id])` when the callback carries business context, and falls back to the existing `bot.api.deleteMessage(chat_id, message_id)` otherwise.

Added a regression test in `bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts` asserting that a Business callback's rich-edit-failure recovery deletes via `deleteBusinessMessages` with the right connection id and message id, and never calls `deleteMessage`. Confirmed it fails against the pre-fix code (via `git stash` of the production change alone — `deleteBusinessMessages` is never called pre-fix) for the intended reason, then passes after the fix.

Validation:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.callback-actions.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts` — 152/152 passing.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — clean.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt` on both touched files — applied, clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- `.claude/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` (Codex, gpt-5.6-sol, high reasoning) — clean, no accepted/actionable findings ("patch is correct (0.99)").

Note: the disclosed "no bot token configured in this sandbox" real-Telegram-proof gap remains unresolved and unchanged from prior updates.


## Update (head 6328eb54392): mock-gateway harness — executed transcript + verdict JSON (real-behavior proof)

ClawSweeper's `needs real behavior proof` gate asks for the added Gateway harness to be *executed* against this head, with its terminal output **and** verdict JSON supplied together. This section supersedes and consolidates my two earlier (separately-posted, and confusingly-worded) proof updates into one honest, co-located block.

Per `AGENTS.md`'s real-behavior-proof gate — "a mock-gateway harness run (mock channel API + mock provider + ephemeral gateway, verdict JSON in the PR body) satisfies it for channel-visible changes covering the changed path; live-channel proof is stronger evidence."

prs.title: fix(agents): surface tool loop warnings to models
prs.body:
Closes #120449

## What Problem This Solves

Warning-tier tool-loop detections were emitted through server-side diagnostics but were not included in the normal tool result returned to the model. This left the model without the existing recovery guidance until the loop reached the critical blocking tier.

## Changes

- attach each emitted warning to its admitted tool call
- carry the warning through successful and failed tool execution without consuming it early
- finalize and consume the warning once after result-replacing outcome hooks have settled
- restore the warning when `afterToolCall` or `afterToolOutcome` replaces tool-result content
- cover server-executed and client-executed tools
- preserve the warning when a tool throws and the failure becomes an error result
- clear pending warning state when an aborted call produces no result
- cover calls without a run ID and atomic batch rejection cleanup
- preserve existing diagnostics and critical-tier blocking behavior

Warning-tier calls continue to execute normally.

## Evidence

### Exact-head CI

- Head: `0a08a336377631bee153430c8b261a1c892fe708`
- CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/32574281911
- Result: 210 checks passed, 0 failed, and 38 non-applicable checks were skipped

### Focused Regression Validation

The current-head focused suites passed across agent-core, embedded-agent-run, and transcript paths:

```text
Test Files  13 passed
Tests       492 passed
```

The regression coverage includes:

- an actual `runAgentLoop` transcript regression where `afterToolCall` replaces the result content
- an actual `runAgentLoop` transcript regression where `afterToolOutcome` replaces the result content
- final warning restoration after either replacement hook
- one-time consumption without duplicate warning text when the original tool result retains the warning
- warning delivery for successful server and client tool results
- warning preservation when a tool failure becomes an error transcript result
- pending-warning cleanup when an aborted call produces no result

Also verified locally on the changed files:

- formatter check passed
- Oxlint passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors
- `git diff --check` passed

### Exact-head Live Runtime Proof

The exact PR head was built as an isolated Docker image:

```text
Image:    openclaw-pr120572:0a08a336377
Image ID: sha256:36630ffcd11ab280f7ed7065a569418b1f2dd1a265b47934fe642cd13e0243ec
Commit:   0a08a336377631bee153430c8b261a1c892fe708
```

Runtime conditions:

- model: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`
- read-only container root and proof workspace mount
- no host home directory or Docker socket mounted
- tool surface restricted to `read`
- one assistant batch containing exactly 11 parallel `read` calls
- every call used the same arguments: `{"path":"/work/proof.txt"}`

Observed transcript result:

```text
read calls:                   11
successful read results:     11
results containing payload:  11
results containing warning:  1
warning result ordinal:      11
tool failures:               0
final assistant response:    proof complete
```

The eleventh tool result retained the normal result and appended the guidance:

```text
proof payload

Tool loop warning: WARNING: You have called read 10 times with identical arguments. If this is not making progress, stop retrying and report the task as failed.
```

This confirms that warning-tier calls still execute, the model receives the warning through the committed tool-result transcript, and the warning is emitted and consumed exactly once.

The PR container received only a relay placeholder. A temporary relay held the provider credential, forwarded only `/v1/messages`, capped the proof at four requests, and was deleted afterward. Exact-key scans found 0 matches across 33,482 tracked files and 3 temporary proof files.
