prs.title: fix(anthropic): partial agent exec block drops restrictive global security
prs.body:
Related: #121678 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where an operator who set a restrictive global exec policy would still have a Claude CLI agent launched with permissions bypassed, as soon as that agent had any per-agent exec settings of its own. Concretely: the operator sets `tools.exec.security: "deny"`, then gives one agent a small per-agent block such as `tools: { exec: { ask: "off" } }` — a block that says nothing about `security`. The expectation is that the agent inherits `deny`. What actually happens is that the global block is discarded entirely, the missing `security` falls back to the permissive default, and the run is launched with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`, so Claude Code's own Bash/Write/Edit tools run without prompting. ## Why This Change Was Made The Claude CLI backend resolved exec policy with its own private logic that replaced the global block with the per-agent block wholesale: ```ts const exec = agentExec ?? context?.config?.tools?.exec; ``` Two independent failures, both in the permissive direction: the global block is never consulted once a per-agent block exists, and any field the per-agent block omits falls back to the most permissive default rather than to the global setting. The repository already owns this layering. `applyExecPolicyLayer` merges field by field, and keeps the "an explicit `mode` wins" rule intact; it is used by `resolveExecToolConfig` (`src/agents/lazy-exec-tool.ts:77`), `resolveExecDefaults` (`src/agents/exec-defaults.ts:190`), `agent-tools.ts:555`, and `node-host/invoke-system-run.ts:214`. This change makes the Claude CLI backend the fifth consumer of that seam instead of a fifth implementation of it. `applyExecPolicyLayer` is re-exported from the existing `plugin-sdk/exec-approvals-runtime` module, next to `resolveExecModePolicy`, which this file already imports. This is the non-live counterpart of #121678, which repaired the same defect on the live-session lane. That PR's description named this exact case — *"a partial per-agent exec block inherited a restrictive global security setting"* — and its regression suite covers it for live sessions. **Which lane this flag actually reaches.** On the default `claude-stdio` live transport the value computed here is not final: `prepareClaudeCliTransportArgs` treats `--permission-mode` as a protocol-owned flag, drops whatever arrived (`extensions/anthropic/cli-runtime-args.ts:15`, `:53`) and appends its own `--permission-mode default` (`:99`). So on that lane Claude is never launched with `bypassPermissions` either way, and this change is a no-op there. The flag is final on the lanes that run per-turn processes instead, where the runner strips `liveSession` before execution: ```ts // src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts:1809 (side question) and :1816 (disableCliLiveSession) const { liveSession: _liveSession, ...backend } = preparedBackend.backend; ``` There is a second gate after that one, and adding the runner's `resolveExecutionArgs` hook to the trace surfaced it. When a run carries per-run tool availability, the backend takes the restricted-execution path, and `--permission-mode` is on its strip list: ```ts // extensions/anthropic/cli-shared.ts:309-311 const CLAUDE_RESTRICTED_VALUE_ARGS = new Set([ CLAUDE_PERMISSION_MODE_ARG, ... ``` So the flag computed here survives to the process only when the run is **both** off the live transport **and** without per-run tool availability. Measured against the five `disableCliLiveSession: true` call sites: | call site | `cliToolAvailability` | flag survives? | |---|---|---| | `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.ts:156` | not set | **yes** | | `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts:722` | `{ native: [], openClaw }` | no - stripped | | `src/agents/isolated-completion.ts:224` | `{ native: [], openClaw: [] }` | no - stripped | | `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/cli-backend-dispatch.ts:258` | built at `:117`, always set | no - stripped | | `src/system-agent/agent-turn.ts:386` | `resolveSystemAgentCliToolAvailability` returns a value for this backend (`selectable` + `execution-args` + `resolveExecutionArgs`) | no - stripped | Compaction runs are the confirmed surviving lane, and they are the case worth repairing: they are unattended and long-running, which is exactly where an accidental `bypassPermissions` matters. The node-bound lane (`sessionEntry.execHost === "node"`, `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts:1046`) and side-question entry points that do not set availability behave the same way, but I have not enumerated them individually and am not claiming them. Scope, stated plainly: this fixes the global → per-agent layering only. `CliBackendNormalizeConfigContext` carries just `config`, `backendId`, and `agentId`, so session-level `execSecurity` and approvals-file floors never reach this lane at all. Extending the context to carry those is a larger change and is deliberately not attempted here. ## User Impact An agent with a partial per-agent exec block now inherits the global `security` setting instead of silently escalating to bypassed permissions. Operators who set a restrictive global policy get the policy they configured. Behavior narrows for one configuration shape on a narrow set of runs: a partial per-agent block that previously produced `bypassPermissions` will no longer do so on per-turn process runs that carry no per-run tool availability. Compaction runs (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.ts:156`) are the measured case; they are unattended and long-running, which is where an accidental bypass matters most. Those runs now fall back to Claude's own default permission behavior instead of bypassing it. Runs on the default `claude-stdio` live transport are unaffected in either direction because that transport pins `--permission-mode default`, and runs with per-run tool availability are unaffected because the restricted-execution path strips the flag for both code states. An explicit per-agent `mode` still overrides the global policy wherever the flag survives at all; the argv table below shows both override rows byte-identical before and after. That is the intended direction and matches #121678. ## Evidence AI-assisted change. Re-measured on head `57ecf19007e`, Node 22.23.2, Windows. The real-binary arms below use Claude Code 2.1.268. **Real behavior — the argv a spawned process actually receives on the affected lane.** Rather than reading the normalized config, this drives the production chain to a real process and records the argv from inside it: the shipped `claude-cli` backend registration -> the real `normalizeClaudeBackendConfig` hook -> the `liveSession` strip the runner performs at `prepare.ts:1809`/`:1816` -> the `{sessionId}` substitution at `execute.ts:238-245` -> **the runner's `resolveExecutionArgs` hook** (`execute.ts:246`, i.e. the backend's own `resolveClaudeCliExecutionArgs`, which the earlier trace skipped) -> the real `buildCliArgs` (`execute.ts:275`) -> `spawnSync`. The only substitution is the executable itself: a stub script stands in for the `claude` binary and writes its own `process.argv.slice(2)` to a file. Nothing inside OpenClaw is mocked, and the hook ran in every row below. Operator config in every row: `tools.exec.security: "deny"`, `tools.exec.ask: "off"` globally, and one agent with the per-agent block shown. | per-agent `tools.exec` | run | per-run tool availability | `main` | this branch | |---|---|---|---|---| | `{ ask: "off" }` (partial, omits `security`) | fresh | none | `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` | flag **absent** | | `{ ask: "off" }` (partial, omits `security`) | resumed (`--resume`) | none | `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` | flag **absent** | | `{ mode: "full" }` (explicit override) | fresh | none | `bypassPermissions` | `bypassPermissions` | | `{ mode: "full" }` (explicit override) | resumed (`--resume`) | none | `bypassPermissions` | `bypassPermissions` | | `{ ask: "off" }` (partial) | fresh | `{ native: ["Bash","Read"], openClaw: ["memory_search"] }` | flag absent | flag absent | | `{ mode: "full" }` (explicit) | fresh | same as above | flag absent | flag absent | The last two rows are the restricted-execution path described above: the hook strips `--permission-mode` for both code states, which is what makes the availability column part of the scope statement rather than a footnote. Full argv recorded by the stub for the partial-block fresh run: ``` main ["-p","--output-format","stream-json","--include-partial-messages","--verbose", "--setting-sources","user","--allowedTools","mcp__openclaw__*", "--disallowedTools","ScheduleWakeup,CronCreate,Bash(run_in_background:true),Monitor", "--permission-mode","bypassPermissions", "--model","claude-sonnet-4-6","--session-id","00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"] branch ["-p","--output-format","stream-json","--include-partial-messages","--verbose", "--setting-sources","user","--allowedTools","mcp__openclaw__*", "--disallowedTools","ScheduleWakeup,CronCreate,Bash(run_in_background:true),Monitor", "--model","claude-sonnet-4-6","--session-id","00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"] ``` With the flag absent, Claude Code falls back to its own default permission behavior and prompts, which is the restrictive global policy the operator configured. The explicit-override rows are the control: they are byte-identical on both sides, so the narrowing is confined to the defect. The two code states differ by one file. **Real Claude behavior once the flag is absent.** The previous revision stopped at the argv. This one carries it into the real `claude` binary - Claude Code 2.1.268, authenticated, no stub anywhere. The two argv rows are produced by the production normalizers themselves: `main`'s `normalizeClaudeBackendConfig` and this branch's, imported side by side in one probe, given the same operator config (`tools.exec.security: "deny"` globally, agent block `{ ask: "off" }`). Each resulting argv is handed to `spawnSync("claude", [...args, prompt])` in a fresh empty working directory, with one permissioned request as the prompt: > Create a file named proof.txt containing OK in the current directory, then reply DONE. The observable is the filesystem, not the transcript. Each arm gets a throwaway `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` holding nothing but a `settings.json` written for that arm (plus the credential file, so the CLI can authenticate), so no operator CLAUDE.md, plugin or hook reaches the run, and every `CLAUDE*` variable is stripped from the child environment. | arm | argv produced by | user `settings.json` | `proof.txt` | Claude's own reply | |---|---|---|---|---| | A | `main` | `{}` | **created** | `DONE` | | B | this branch | `{}` | **absent** | "If you grant write permission for this directory (or run in an interactive session and approve the prompt), I'll create `proof.txt` with `OK` immediately." | | C | this branch | `{"permissions":{"defaultMode":"bypassPermissions"}}` | **created** | `DONE` | A against B is the change, measured rather than quoted from documentation: with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` the write happens unattended; with the flag gone the same request is refused by the permission system and nothing is written. Two consecutive runs of the probe produced identical results. C answers the open decision. The narrowing binds only where the operator's own Claude settings do not already bypass, because this branch stops passing a flag rather than starting to pass a restrictive one. A host whose Claude `settings.json` pins `permissions.defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"` keeps bypassing after this change. So affected compaction runs stop receiving an automatic bypass *from OpenClaw*, and an operator who wants the old behavior keeps two explicit ways to ask for it: a per-agent `mode: "full"` (rows 3 and 4 of the argv table, byte-identical before and after) or their own Claude settings (row C).

Harness (temporary probe, run with node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs probe.mts; not committed) ```ts const plugin = buildAnthropicCliBackend(); // shipped claude-cli registration const normalized = normalizeClaudeBackendConfig(plugin.config, { backendId: "claude-cli", agentId: "agent", config: { tools: { exec: { security: "deny", ask: "off" } }, agents: { list: [{ id: "agent", tools: { exec: agentExec } }] }, }, }); // exactly what prepare.ts:1809 / :1816 do before a non-live run const { liveSession: _liveSession, ...backend } = normalized; const sessionId = "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"; const baseArgsWithSkills = useResume // execute.ts:238-245 ? (backend.resumeArgs ?? []).map((a) => a.replaceAll("{sessionId}", sessionId)) : (backend.args ?? []); const resolvedExecutionArgs = plugin.resolveExecutionArgs?.({ // execute.ts:246 config, workspaceDir: process.cwd(), provider: "anthropic", modelId: "claude-sonnet-4-6", executionMode: "agent", toolAvailability, // undefined, or the availability object useResume, baseArgs: baseArgsWithSkills, }); const args = buildCliArgs({ // execute.ts:275 backend, baseArgs: Array.from(resolvedExecutionArgs ?? baseArgsWithSkills), modelId: "claude-sonnet-4-6", sessionId, useResume, }); spawnSync(process.execPath, [STUB, ...args], { env: { ...process.env, STUB_ARGV_OUT: out } }); // STUB: writeFileSync(process.env.STUB_ARGV_OUT, JSON.stringify(process.argv.slice(2))); ```
**Tests:** ``` vitest --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts extensions/anthropic/cli-shared.exec-policy.test.ts Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 2 passed (2) ``` **Control arm — the same two tests with `isOpenClawRequestedYolo` reverted to main's expression** (`const exec = agentExec ?? context?.config?.tools?.exec;`): ``` Tests 1 failed | 1 passed (2) × keeps restrictive global exec security when the agent block omits it AssertionError: expected [ …(11) ] to not include 'bypassPermissions' ``` Exactly one test falls, and it is the partial-block case. ## What Problem This Solves

MCP Events mirrors its sole service owner through an eleven-callback ingress abstraction, splitting one lifecycle across two private owners.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Signed callbacks retain current authority checks, bounded-body and schema validation, durable-before-ack admission, FIFO/capacity/deduplication, cursor revision ordering, secret overlap, retries and ordinary shutdown settlement. No SDK, protocol, config, dependency or persisted-data shape changes. The Phase E session-memory backend is untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Delete the private ingress class and owner interface. Existing service state owns the account queues and drain; the existing HTTP handler owns callback admission; the existing status handler owns diagnostics. There is no reverse service-to-HTTP/index import or replacement owner abstraction.

Serialized updates still draft one shallow copy and publish facts only after guarded persistence succeeds. Each producer explicitly clears its own optional fields instead of writing undefined for a second owner to scan away. Timestamping remains at the same serialized write point. Tests keep all existing behavioral assertions and use the actual diagnostics projection called by the registered status handler.

Current formatted delta: five paths, **82 net production lines removed**, **5 test-layout lines added**, **77 lines removed overall**. Relocated bodies are not counted as removal. This is the MCP Events area slice of a wider 86-file cleanup accumulation; the campaign's area-split rule allows this coherent slice below its usual size floor.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- No security, authority, durability, concurrency or shutdown guard is removed. The generic owner mirror had one real implementation, introduced with the active MCP Events feature in #165399; that feature and its external contracts remain.
- The redundant optional-field cleanup scan disappears because existing typed producers now delete cleared properties directly. Subscription response fields remain validated at the remote trust boundary; failed writes still leave published facts unchanged. No additional unrealistic edge case is intentionally accepted.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor --fix` deletes an explicitly configured `agents.defaults.compaction.model` when the agent uses Codex. After #175256, a fresh Codex thread can need an OpenClaw host history summary, and that path reads this setting. Doctor should not erase a configuration the host still consumes.

## User Impact

Doctor retains the host summary model during manual repair and the same repair invoked by updates. Native Codex compaction and `/compact` remain Codex-owned; locked model selection remains unchanged. No new setting, runtime routing change, or database migration is introduced. Previously deleted values are not reconstructed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Limit unsupported-override detection/removal to `compaction.provider`, and canonicalize retained legacy model references without adding runtime-policy pins. Keep Lossless migration, conflict handling, and shared non-Codex consumers intact. Update the warning and Codex configuration guide to distinguish host summaries from native compaction.

The existing consumer is `src/agents/harness/host-seed.ts` → `compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirect` → `resolveEmbeddedCompactionTarget` in `compaction-runtime-context.ts`. This PR changes only Doctor, its regression tests, and documentation.

prs.title: fix(trajectory): session.ended timestamp matches model.completed before cleanup
prs.body:
Closes #102014

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where trajectory exports showed `session.ended` with the same timestamp as `model.completed`, so cleanup duration looked like zero even when teardown took real wall-clock time.

## Why This Change Was Made

`session.ended` was recorded at finalize time, right after model completion, so its timestamp preceded session teardown. This PR captures the terminal payload at finalize and records `session.ended` only after attempt cleanup completes, on both the embedded runner and the Codex app-server. No new event types or exporter knobs; payload fields are unchanged, only emit timing moves from finalize into post-cleanup.

Rebased note (2026-08-26): the original branch predated the embedded-attempt lifecycle rewrite, so this was re-implemented onto current `main` (`attempt-finalize.ts` / `attempt-session-settle.ts` / `attempt-settle.ts` on the embedded side, `run-attempt-finalize.ts` / `run-attempt-cleanup.ts` / `run-attempt-turn-start.ts` for Codex). Review findings from the previous round are addressed:

- P1 "Guarantee terminal recording when Codex cleanup throws": `cleanupCodexAttempt` now records `session.ended` (captured payload, or the derived fallback) inside its `finally` block as the `codex-trajectory-terminal` step, followed by a terminal flush, so a teardown failure can no longer skip terminal recording.
- P2 "Finish startup-failure teardown before ending the session": the Codex turn-start failure path now captures the payload and records it only after binding clear, thread unsubscribe, route release, sandbox release, and shared-client lease release all finish.

## User Impact

Operators reading trajectory traces can measure real session end time versus model compute time, including cleanup latency.

## Evidence

Verified at head `0d46a743604` (current `origin/main` `636e21b1985` plus these two commits), Windows 11, Node v24.15.0.

Embedded runner tests:

```
npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-cleanup.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-execution-settle.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-execution-phase.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-stream-finalize.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-result.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-finalize.media.test.ts

Test Files  16 passed (16)
     Tests  141 passed (141)
```

Codex app-server tests (new ordering coverage: `session.ended` recorded after `thread/unsubscribe` and after the one-shot client `closeAndWait`, on both the success path and the startup-failure path):

```
npx vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts -t "session.ended"

Tests  2 passed | 146 skipped (148)
```

Full `run-attempt.test.ts` A/B on this machine: 13 failures are `EBUSY: resource busy or locked, unlink *.sqlite` temp-dir cleanup flakes that reproduce identically on unmodified `origin/main` (13 failed / 133 passed baseline vs 13 failed / 172 passed with this PR's files in the same run); the failure set is identical test-for-test, so they are pre-existing Windows-only flakes, not regressions.

Revert-red check: with only the production hunks stashed, the new Codex ordering tests fail (2 failed) and the new/updated embedded cleanup tests fail (12 failed); all pass with the hunks restored.

Repo checks: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` all clean. `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files. `pnpm check` guards pass, including the assertion SAFETY comment ratchet (the one new field uses a typed spread instead of an `as` assertion).

### Live embedded trajectory artifact (2026-08-26, this head)

Ran on this PR head (`0d46a743604`), Windows 11, Node v24.15.0, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, embedded `openclaw agent --local --json`, model `mistral/mistral-small-latest` (no Telegram / Vertex / gateway secrets).

Runtime event order from `trajectory_runtime_events`:

```
seq=0 session.started      2026-08-26T10:52:02.672Z
seq=1 trace.metadata       2026-08-26T10:52:02.680Z
seq=2 context.compiled     2026-08-26T10:52:02.741Z
seq=3 prompt.submitted     2026-08-26T10:52:02.746Z
seq=4 model.completed      2026-08-26T10:52:05.364Z
seq=5 trace.artifacts      2026-08-26T10:52:05.364Z
seq=6 session.ended        2026-08-26T10:52:05.371Z
```

`session.ended` is recorded after `model.completed` and after `trace.artifacts` (7ms delta on this short no-tool turn), matching the fixed ordering: the terminal event now carries the post-cleanup wall-clock time instead of sharing the `model.completed` timestamp.

### What was not tested

- `pnpm test` full suite and `pnpm build` artifacts beyond the local build used for the live run above (targeted suites only, per above).
- Codex app-server live run (its ordering is covered by the new harness tests instead).

## AI-assisted

Yes. Authored with Cursor/Grok assistance. Human: Stan Shih (stantheman0128). Rebase onto current main, review-finding follow-up, and live proof also Cursor.

prs.title: fix(gateway): let delegated OpenClaw changes work from CLI-backend agents
prs.body:
Related: #136036, #137017

## What Problem This Solves

Delegated `openclaw.chat` calls from CLI/subprocess and worker harnesses failed with `delegated OpenClaw approval requires an active run authority`. Fully in-process agents retained the ambient caller identity, but harness tool calls crossed the Gateway WebSocket boundary, where that process-local identity is intentionally unavailable.

## User Impact

CLI and worker-harness delegated calls retain their signed source ownership and approval guard, including when optional wire delegation metadata is absent. Existing run, tool-abort and worker-lifetime fencing remains fail-closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Root cause

The approval gate only consulted the process-local Gateway tool caller identity. OpenClaw already has a host-minted, HMAC-signed `agentRuntimeIdentityToken` for trusted cross-process calls, including the exact admitted run authority and worker turn claim, but `openclaw.chat` was not included in that transport.

The first revision attempted to mint replacement authority from the delegated session id. Review identified that as unsafe. The signed-identity revision then exposed two narrower defects:

- Distinct calls in one source run receive distinct tool-bound lease claim ids. Approval reconciliation compared those claim ids, so a later call retired the original pending decision even though its exact lease was still live.
- The wire fallback retained the generic 30-second request timeout although delegated human interaction is budgeted for 900 seconds and the approval owner can wait 600 seconds before staging/application completes.

## Design

This revision carries the existing source-run authority instead of synthesizing or transferring it:

- `openclaw.chat` is eligible for the signed agent-runtime identity token.
- The host binds the exact tool abort signal into the delegated run authority before signing it.
- Explicit host-prepared Full Access is transported only for `openclaw.chat`; model-authored parameters cannot create it.
- On Gateway arrival, signed agent/runtime/session/routing facts establish delegation even when the optional wire field is omitted; model-supplied metadata cannot override or opt out of that binding.
- Ambient in-process identity remains authoritative when present. Wire calls use the verified signed runtime identity.
- Pending-approval reconciliation first validates the original exact application lease, then compares both callers' active canonical source owner plus local/worker kind and exact worker turn claim. It never replaces the authority stored on the pending record.
- The delegated wire call uses the existing 900-second human-interaction budget. The generic Gateway default remains 30 seconds, and the Codex owner retains its separate 30-second completion grace.
- Run release/replacement, original tool abort, Gateway replacement, worker-claim loss, and delegated-session replacement still fail closed.

No new configuration keys, SQLite surfaces, dependencies or retries are introduced. The existing transient signed-identity token carries an optional host-prepared Full Access fact. Existing canonical owner and human-wait helpers were sufficient.

## Security properties

- No authority is derived from a session id or model-authored delegation fields.
- The signed identity can only be minted by the host holding the local runtime-token secret.
- Full Access is a host-prepared restrict-only fact; omission never bypasses approval.
- Reuse grants observation of an existing pending decision only after its original exact application lease is revalidated.
- The original record retains its exact lease, signals, and application predicate. Closing a later sibling lease cannot transfer or cancel that authority; closing the original lease still blocks application.
- Worker authority remains bound to the canonical placement/turn claim.

## Evidence

- Published head `cea0acc7028934a9609bb656a14cb21a3496db94` integrates GitHub-confirmed current-main conflicts against pinned upstream `3260d7b41a8c2404b8b3dc800240573dfb1cc7e1`. Preserves upstream compact delegate-test layout and PR timeout/permission/session-continuation contracts. Production authority changes merged without manual conflict; removed a now-unused moved import and compacted a local parameter name to satisfy changed-file lint. Validation passed: 91 focused authority/identity/delegate tests across five suites (55.731s wrapper), production core types and all three affected test-type shards, changed-file type-aware lint, formatting, pinned-main diff check, line-cap and assertion-safety ratchets. The newly integrated cron fixture needed a true-or-undefined permission normalization in its test transport only; its affected integration suite and Gateway-method types pass after that correction. Fresh independent scoped review of the frozen production tree found no actionable P0/P1; retained for the final one-line test-adapter correction. No fresh real delayed-human transport proof, replacement-head hosted verdict, or maintainer signed-carrier acceptance is claimed.

- Prior published head `fad89b4b638381fbb5e964c5d0cade97d01b0afc` reconciles a GitHub-confirmed approval-test conflict onto pinned upstream `d1618ccd0b276f985711ff297b1b87a77bdad35d`. Upstream removed a redundant ambient-only parameter case; the later maintained cross-lease wire/ambient approval coverage remains intact. Seventeen patches replay identically; the first differs only in its upstream conflict context. Prior independent review is retained for this mechanical delta, not claimed as fresh review. All 10 local gates passed: 99 tests across five focused suites (56.058s wrapper), production core types, all three affected test-type shards (agents-root, agents-other and Gateway-methods), changed-source type-aware lint, formatting, diff, line-cap and assertion-safety checks. The initial lint attempt could not load the newly required eslint-plugin-solid; refreshing the isolated installation from the unchanged frozen lockfile resolved it without source or lockfile workarounds. No replacement-head hosted verdict or fresh live-runtime result is claimed. Real delayed-human-decision proof and area-owner signed-carrier acceptance remain outstanding.

- Prior published head `db8ec1bb286e5b9bd9a77a7fcaea911869673b9a` addresses revision 24’s test-quality feedback: removed the synthetic delayed-decision mock test and unused fake-timer cleanup. The retained relay test verifies the requested 900-second budget and returned approval outcome. All 15 delegate-tool tests passed (`pnpm test src/agents/tools/openclaw-delegate-tool.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 8.655s wrapper / 6.67s Vitest); affected agents-other test types, type-aware changed-file lint, formatting, diff check, line-cap and assertion-safety gates passed. Production sources are byte-unchanged from the prior validated head, whose exact-head hosted CI was observed SUCCESS at 07:13 UTC and durable revision 24 found no production defect. Those prior-head results are historical. That prior head’s hosted CI was observed SUCCESS at 2026-10-08 17:53 UTC; durable ClawSweeper revision 25 reviewed that head and reports no actionable findings, with area-owner acceptance still outstanding. No fresh independent production review or live run is claimed for this test-only deletion.
- A real human decision after 30 seconds remains unverified by the historical CLI evidence. The removed synthetic timeout test did not establish that transport behavior; the historical timeout RED/GREEN results below are synthetic test evidence only.

- Prior published `4cde0ad5c4cd3cbe31b96320f8a7e01954e2d74b` reconciled a confirmed import conflict onto pinned upstream `2f1f73ccb2224bbe7d961b4c0d3b29cfdd51e7f8`. prs.title: fix(config): keep deep config loading stack-safe past include resolution
prs.body:
Closes #153430

Related: #152847 (include resolution itself, already stack-safe in #152889) — this PR extends the same stack-safe contract to the loading stages that run after the resolver.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: loading a config whose deeply nested value passes `$include` resolution still crashes with an opaque `RangeError` when the resolved value reaches value merging, env substitution, or the legacy migration probes. The first iteration of this PR also reversed object key order on every substituted config (leaves were resolved in a reverse loop, and object slots record first-write order); that regression is fixed here, with a unit test pinning document key order.

## User Impact

User impact: a machine-generated config that nests deeply now fails with the normal actionable schema error instead of a stack-overflow crash from a stage after the one that already promises stack safety; nothing that was previously accepted is rejected, and persisted config key order matches the authored document.

## Why This Change Was Made

The include resolver walks documents on an explicit work stack, but every later stage still recursed. Each remaining walk now runs on an explicit work stack so document depth costs heap instead of call frames:

- `src/infra/deep-merge.ts`: `mergeDeep` and its plain-object sanitizer clone walk iteratively; prototype-key filtering is preserved.
- `src/config/env-substitution.ts`: `substituteAny` allocates object slots in source order (key order follows the document) and schedules child tasks depth-first, so `onMissing` warnings keep their original order.
- Legacy migration probes: the load-time `structuredClone(root)` calls (Node's built-in clone recurses too) are replaced by a shared iterative `deepCloneForMigrationProbe` in `legacy-config-record-shared.ts` across the models/providers/retired/config-tranche probes.

Net production growth is the shared clone helper plus the iterative walkers; no new configuration surface is added.

Competition/fix-surface note: #129403 overlaps on the env-substitution walk but does not touch the deep-merge or migration-probe clone crash points; this PR covers all three stages with tests.

## Evidence

All commands run from the PR checkout (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs` over the real CLI sources — the installed CLI runs dist and predates any local change).

**1. Full CLI chain, normal config through `$include` to merge, env substitution, migration probes, and schema (fresh config behavior).** `settings.json` is a minimal gateway block; `main.json` includes it and defines a provider whose `baseUrl` is `${PROOF_BASE_URL}/v1`:

```
$ PROOF_BASE_URL=https://proof.example.local OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/proof-153431/main.json \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts config get models.providers.proof-provider.baseUrl
https://proof.example.local/v1
(exit 0)
```

**2. Full CLI chain, 600-level nested value.** `nested600.json` nests a scalar 600 levels deep under a top-level key. The chain runs to completion and the value is rejected by schema validation with the actionable error, not by a RangeError:

```
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/proof-153431/nested600.json \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts config get agents.defaults.timeout
OpenClaw config is invalid: /tmp/proof-153431/nested600.json
- nested600.json:1 — agents.defaults: Unrecognized key: "timeout"
- <root>: Unrecognized key: "deep"
(exit 0; the CLI reports the schema error and the next step instead of crashing)
```

**3. Depth matrix over the changed walkers** (module-level probe: build an n-level nested object, call `mergeDeep(v, v)` and `resolveConfigEnvVars(v, {})`):

| depth | recursive implementation (base 8ebc8cd021e) | this PR (iterative) |
|---|---|---|
| 4000 | mergeDeep RangeError; envSub RangeError | both OK |
| 8000 | both RangeError | both OK |
| 20000 | both RangeError | both OK |

The same matrix over the legacy migration probe clone (`findLegacyConfigIssues` -> `LEGACY_CONFIG_MIGRATION_RULES[].match` -> `deepCloneForMigrationProbe`, the load-time doctor detection path): recursive baseline RangeError at 5,000 levels; this PR completes the probe at 100,000 levels.

**4. Boundary note on depth.** At 4,000+ levels the still-recursive include resolver aborts the load before the stages this PR owns (Include resolution failed: RangeError); stack-safe include resolution is #152847's contract, delivered by #152889. See items 6-7 for the full real-loader crash-point chain and the 2,000-level end-to-end window measured after the include-resolver fix.

**5. Tests.** `src/config/env-substitution.test.ts` (19 cases: the 4,000-level no-overflow case, plus a key-order case that fails on the reversed-write implementation) and `src/infra/deep-merge.test.ts` (6 cases incl. the 4,000-level merge) are green on this head.

**6. Real-loader crash-point chain (post-Rev3 update).** Walking the real CLI load chain depth-by-depth with an isolated config (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, synthetic values) maps every recursive crash point between the loader and the stages this PR owns, observed through a load-path probe on the real sources:

| Load stage | Observed crash depth | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| `$include` resolution (`resolveConfigIncludes`) | ~600 (2,000+ RangeError) | #152889 (stack-safe) |
| Read-path `$include` pre-scan (`containsConfigIncludeDirective`, `io.read-helpers.ts`) | 2,000 OK / 2,300+ RangeError | newly located; fixed by #153711 |
| Deep merge / env substitution / legacy migration probes | >2,300 — masked upstream on recursive baselines; isolated matrix in item 3 | **this PR** |
| `stableConfigStringify` (`runtime-snapshot.ts`) | 2,200 OK / 2,400+ RangeError | not yet fixed (family follow-up) |

**7. Full-chain proof at the new window.** On a checkout combining #152889 (include resolution) with this PR's three stages, a 2,000-level document under `agents.defaults.params` loads **end-to-end through the real CLI**:

```
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/proof-153431/state OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/proof-153431/config/openclaw.json \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/index.ts config get agents.defaults.model
test-model
(exit 0)
```

With this PR's three-stage fix removed from the same tree (recursive merge/env restored), the identical document also loads — because on a real load the recursive merge crash point sits deeper than the two masked stages above, the merge stages can only be observed through the isolated matrix in item 3. The depth-4,000 end-to-end claim therefore remains blocked by `stableConfigStringify` (item 6, last row), a recursive walker outside this PR's surface; recording it here so the family follow-up (#153708's chain) has the measured map.

**8. Doctor CLI chain over a legal deep config (real `openclaw doctor` on both baselines).** A config with an 800-level value under the schema-legal `tts.providers` catchall, run through the real CLI sources against the recursive base (origin/main `e63393bddc3a`) and this PR head, with isolated state dirs (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`): both runs complete the full doctor flow (health checks, legacy-state detection, migration preview) with no RangeError, and the probe/merge/env stages this PR changes process the same config. At 1,300+ levels both runs abort with `Maximum call stack size exceeded` before the doctor flow completes. On the recursive baseline that abort is consistent with the merge/env/probe crash points this PR owns (item 3 matrix); on this PR head those stages are iterative, so the remaining abort sits in the still-recursive post-probe clones (the candidate `structuredClone` in `doctor-config-flow.ts`, `cloneConfigWithResolutionFacts` in `resolution-facts.ts`). The full-chain before/after delta is therefore masked by those family stages; the measured window is recorded here for the follow-up.

`tsgo` core (`tsconfig.core.json`) and the core-test shards exit 0; `oxlint` and `oxfmt` are clean on the touched files; the line-cap and assertion-safety ratchets report no violations for the touched files.

prs.title: fix(talk): voice consults end with no reply when the primary model cannot run
prs.body:
Related: #161885

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: realtime Talk ends every turn with no reply when the agent's primary model can't run on the consult path (for example `anthropic/*` routed through `claude-cli` with no direct Anthropic API key), even though a working fallback model is configured.

## User Impact

User impact: voice consults now fall back through the agent's configured `model.fallbacks` the same way normal turns do, so Talk answers instead of going silent. Setups whose primary model works are unchanged.

This does not route consults through the CLI runtime itself; that half of #161885 is a separate change and stays open.

## Why This Change Was Made

`consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` called `runEmbeddedAgent` with a single model, so an auth `FailoverError` from the primary was never acted on. The consult now runs inside `runWithModelFallback`:

- The primary attempt passes the caller's original `provider`/`model` (often unset), so how the primary resolves is unchanged.
- Fallback candidates are tried only while no tool has run in the consult (`onAgentToolResult` sets a flag checked by `canFallbackAfterError`), so a consult that may already have acted is never replayed on another model. Aborts never fall back.
- Consults skip candidates that can only run through a subscription CLI runtime. The consult path is embedded and never dispatches to a CLI backend, so those candidates failed auth on every voice question. If no candidate can run, the configured chain is kept so the real error still surfaces.
- Each attempt defers its terminal lifecycle and the consult emits one terminal event, as chat replies already do, so a failed candidate no longer records "This turn ended before a reply".
- `createTalkClientAgentRuntime` reuses one operational run instance per `runId`. The fallback attempt re-enters the Talk runtime under the same `runId`; without this the completion claim rejects it with "The active Talk consult admission is no longer current".
- **Voice run binding across attempts (review P1).** Each attempt emits its own `run.completed`. For runs without a gateway root-work owner, the voice-session subscriber retired the run binding on the first one, before the fallback model ran. The consult now holds the run's voice completion (`client-voice-run-hold.ts`) for the whole fallback chain and releases it when the consult settles; a `run.completed` seen during the hold is deferred until then. Root-backed runs keep main's behaviour (they already ignore diagnostic completion). Since #159697, voice requests use ordinary permissions rather than a voice-specific confirmation gate, so the risk is now losing the binding that run ownership and effect capture use, not a confirmation bypass. The hold covers both.
- **Fallback attempt options (review P2).** The `run` callback now forwards `allowTransientCooldownProbe` to each embedded attempt. `isFinalFallbackAttempt` and `modelRoutingProvenance` are not part of `RunEmbeddedAgentParams` (the public runtime runs its own candidate loop and derives them there), so there is nothing to forward for those.

Rebased onto current `main` as a single commit; the earlier four commits conflicted with the move of the Talk client runtime into `client-agent-runtime.ts` and with the voice-session settlement rework.

## Evidence

- Regression tests that fail on `main` and pass here:
  - `walks the agent model fallback chain when the primary cannot run (#161885)` (consult runtime).
  - `keeps one owned run instance when a consult retries on a fallback model` (gateway Talk). On `main` it fails with "The active Talk consult admission is no longer current", the same error seen live.
  - `keeps the voice run binding when a failed attempt completes before the fallback` (consult runtime). Fails with the hold removed. The hold is not yet proven on a live call.
  - Companion tests: no replay after a tool ran; one terminal lifecycle event when a fallback answers; a subscription-CLI-only primary is skipped.
- `pnpm test src/talk src/gateway/talk src/meeting-bot extensions/voice-call extensions/facetime`: all pass except `extensions/voice-call/src/manager.test-harness.test.ts` (`PLUGIN_STATE_OPEN_FAILED`), which fails identically on unmodified `main`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean.
- Live, on a macOS gateway with the fallback, admission, notice and skip changes as local patches (iOS Talk on iPhone and iPad, plus the macOS app; primary `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` via `claude-cli`, fallback `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`): voice consults fall back and answer, with no admission refusals, no "ended before a reply" notice, and no anthropic auth attempt per question:

  ```
  model_fallback_decision decision=candidate_failed    lane=talk requestedProvider=anthropic ...
  model_fallback_decision decision=candidate_succeeded lane=talk requestedProvider=anthropic ...
  ```

- Original failure, from a 2026.9.7 gateway:

  ```
  lane task error: lane=talk durationMs=39 error="Couldn't sign in to anthropic. ... (No API key found for provider "anthropic". ...)" errorName=FailoverError runId=talk-realtime-consult-<uuid>
  OpenAI GPT-Live delegation consult failed: Couldn't sign in to anthropic ...
  ```

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: refactor(ui): retire legacy session-group downgrades
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

New Session still carries an older-Gateway downgrade that silently drops a resolved folder group from creation, while the catalog treats an explicitly missing core method as an empty successful catalog. UI and Gateway now ship together; their documented contract forbids those version fallbacks.

## User Impact

Resolved groups flow directly from the canonical route owner into session creation, including groups without saved folder defaults. Catalog failures use the existing unavailable/retry state. Permissions, write-scoped path disclosure, reconnect handling, migration and creation authorization are unchanged. No rendering, styling or visible copy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the private category downgrade, migrate its sole caller, and delete the catalog's missing-method successful-empty branch and duplicate defaults-advertisement check already performed by the access owner. Use the existing resolved-group owner directly in the unchanged expression-bodied builder; its synchronous snapshot reads have no intervening await or mutation. This five-file UI area completes an existing wide preservation-family slice:18 net production lines removed,10 net test lines removed. It is not a new large-family or duplicate savings claim.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- An unsupported mismatched Gateway lacking the mandatory group-list method now reaches the existing unavailable/null path instead of pretending the catalog is successfully empty. #106169/#106141 documented transient retry recovery and quiet older-version behavior; current UI/Gateway coupling supersedes only the latter. Real retry and connection settlement remain.
- An older Gateway lacking the newer group-category contract no longer gets a silently ungrouped create. #123276 introduced the explicit downgrade and legacy E2E together; current same-install/version policy retires that compatibility. Unsupported skew may fail visibly. Supported creation and all scope/participation/containment checks remain.
- The duplicate defaults advertisement check disappears because readSessionMethodAccess already checks the connected client, advertised method and permission. Read-only clients still do not request path-bearing defaults. No security or persisted-data contract is removed.

## Evidence

- Complete affected production owners, determining route/create/access owners and current core descriptor/advertisement/defaults authorization inspected. All five preimages matched the qualified preservation base; four final blobs match its UI slice, with the independently reviewed expression-body correction in the submission builder. Phase E backend/factory/registry/expiry/federation/tests untouched.
- Focused supported UI owner proof:4 files,48 tests passed in84.34s Vitest. Retains migration read/write authority, invalidated import refusal, reconnect exclusion, catalog retry/mutation outcomes and grouped create assembly. The obsolete no-probe test is removed; the existing real-page legacy test becomes supported grouped creation without saved defaults. No test-only seam, sleep, retry, timeout increase, skip, suppression or expanded baseline.
- Actual submission-flow owner:33/33 passed in142.92s Vitest (individual cases0–65ms; cold transformation dominates). Covers accepted draft cleanup, reconnect resumption, authority loss and failed materialization without additional Gateway/CLI boots. Exact final five-file independent review scoped-clean P0-P2/0.99; five-file formatting17ms, whitespace and canonical type-aware lint passed. The initial added snapshot block hit max-lines702vs700; restoring the existing expression body fixed it without a baseline/suppression change, and the exact corrected delta was independently reviewed. Only import edges are removed, so no new runtime cycle/component can arise.
- Targeted touched UI graph reports36 existing parse5/MCP dependency declaration diagnostics, none in changed files; NOT a local type pass. Broad types/runtime and selected page E2E belong to exact-head hosted ci:full under the campaign budget. No local broad suite/build/E2E or live/performance claim.
- Fresh mandatory suppression guard14/14 passed (29.96s Vitest/40.85s wrapper). No new suppressions or baseline expansion.

Release-note context: keep resolved folder groups on New Session creation and report unsupported catalog methods through the existing unavailable flow.

prs.title: fix(codex): preserve whitespace in /codex bind --cwd paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `/codex bind --cwd` CLI argument had its leading/trailing whitespace silently trimmed at two points: `normalizeOptionalString` in `parseBindArgs` (entry) and `requestedCwd?.trim()` in `resolveCodexSessionPermissionCwd` (permission owner). A quoted path like `--cwd "/repo/job "` loses its trailing space, causing the bound thread to use `/repo/job` instead of `/repo/job `.

## Why This Change Was Made

Unix paths may legally contain leading/trailing whitespace. The fix replaces `normalizeOptionalString` with `readNonBlankString` at both points. Both preserve significant whitespace while rejecting blank-only input. Containment (`isPathInside`) is unaffected.

## User Impact

Users who pass workspace paths with significant whitespace via `/codex bind --cwd` will now have the correct directory bound. All other users are unaffected.

## Evidence

**End-to-end proof (standalone terminal script, shipped production code + real Codex app-server)** — a `proof-202-e2e.mts` script directly imports the shipped production functions (`parseBindArgs`, `createCodexConversationBindingData`, `readCodexConversationBindingData`, `resolveCodexSessionPermissionCwd`) and connects them to the real installed Codex app-server (v0.162.1, stdio transport, isolated `CODEX_HOME`, no credentials). `thread/start` does NOT call OpenAI API — only `turn/start` would.

Pre-fix (both fix points reverted to `normalizeOptionalString` / `.trim()`):

```console
$ PROOF_MODE=pre-fix node --import tsx proof-202-e2e.mts

=== Layer 1: parseBindArgs ===
  input: --cwd "/tmp/oc-174871-work/job " (len=24)
  parsed.cwd: "/tmp/oc-174871-work/job" (len=23) preserved=false

=== Layer 2: binding data ===
  workspaceDir: "/tmp/oc-174871-work/job" (len=23) preserved=false

=== Layer 3: deserialization ===
  workspaceDir: "/tmp/oc-174871-work/job" (len=23) preserved=false

=== Layer 4: resolveCodexSessionPermissionCwd (permission owner) ===
  permission-resolved cwd: "/tmp/oc-174871-work/job" (len=23) preserved=false

=== Layer 5: Real Codex app-server thread/start ===
  thread/start cwd="/tmp/oc-174871-work/job" → ACCEPTED
  MARKER.txt content: "MARKER_NO_SPACE"     ← wrong directory!

RESULT: WHITESPACE BROKEN (pre-fix)
```

Post-fix (head `cc956be3e35`, `readNonBlankString`):

```console
$ PROOF_MODE=post-fix node --import tsx proof-202-e2e.mts

=== Layer 1: parseBindArgs ===
  parsed.cwd: "/tmp/oc-174871-work/job " (len=24) preserved=true

=== Layer 2: binding data ===
  workspaceDir: "/tmp/oc-174871-work/job " (len=24) preserved=true

=== Layer 3: deserialization ===
  workspaceDir: "/tmp/oc-174871-work/job " (len=24) preserved=true

=== Layer 4: resolveCodexSessionPermissionCwd (permission owner) ===
  permission-resolved cwd: "/tmp/oc-174871-work/job " (len=24) preserved=true
  containment: isPathInside(parent, cwd)=true

=== Layer 5: Real Codex app-server thread/start ===
  thread/start cwd="/tmp/oc-174871-work/job " → ACCEPTED
  MARKER.txt content: "MARKER_TRAILING_SPACE"  ← correct directory!

RESULT: ALL LAYERS PRESERVED WHITESPACE (post-fix)
```

**Before/after comparison matrix** for input `--cwd "/tmp/oc-174871-work/job "`:

| Layer | Before (pre-fix) | After (post-fix) |
|---|---|---|
| `parseBindArgs` cwd | `/tmp/job` (trimmed, len=23) | `/tmp/job ` (preserved, len=24) |
| binding data `workspaceDir` | `/tmp/job` (trimmed) | `/tmp/job ` (preserved) |
| deserialized binding data | `/tmp/job` (trimmed) | `/tmp/job ` (preserved) |
| permission-resolved cwd | `/tmp/job` (trimmed) | `/tmp/job ` (preserved + containment) |
| native `thread/start` cwd | `/tmp/job` (wrong dir) | `/tmp/job ` (correct dir) |
| MARKER.txt read | `MARKER_NO_SPACE` (wrong) | `MARKER_TRAILING_SPACE` (correct) |

**Sibling directories** with distinct markers:

```console
$ cat /tmp/oc-174871-work/job/MARKER.txt
MARKER_NO_SPACE
$ cat "/tmp/oc-174871-work/job /MARKER.txt"
MARKER_TRAILING_SPACE
```

**Downstream consumer** — `conversation-binding-preparation.ts:353` passes `resolved.workspaceDir` directly as `cwd` in `CodexThreadStartParams`, which Layer 5 above sends to the real Codex app-server.

**Environment note:** `thread/start` creates a thread without invoking the model. A revoked maintenance caller can retire the native database generation still retained by another admitted reply. That reader then rejects with `Agent database execution lost its native owner`.

Physical replacement remains a hard refusal: on an exceptional exit, the execution owner checks its captured canonical file and joins native retirement if that file was replaced or disappeared. This check runs only on failure and uses the owner's file, not a caller alias. Authority checks and assertions are unchanged. There are no new retries, timeout changes, schema changes, or public configuration changes.

## Evidence

- Extending the existing maintenance refusal cases with a retained session reader reproduced the lost-native-owner error before the fix; caller revocation failed while the lost-preparation-reply control passed.

## What Problem This Solves

Backup scratch allocation retries speculative maintenance interleavings before any backup payload exists, adding a second recovery policy around the existing lifetime owner.

## User Impact

Normal backups, interrupted-backup cleanup and abandoned-payload reclamation remain unchanged. If allocation or lifetime admission fails, the original error surfaces and the operator can rerun the backup command; the CLI guide now states that best-effort policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the three-attempt pre-payload loop and missing/native-open/path-mismatch retry classifier with straight-line allocation. Keep native busy/retired-owner refusal, non-owner failure cleanup, exact error identity, private directory/Root identity checks and the admitted lifetime unchanged. Payload copying begins only after this operation returns in the actual archive/offsite/download callers.

Fifteen net production lines removed (+21/-36),44net test lines removed, one net documentation line added. This is the backup area of the existing wide preservation family, not a new large-family or duplicate credit. Remove only synthetic retry-success variants; retain read-only pending-creator inspection, replacement/symlink preservation, native failure identity and cleanup, retired-token refusal/maintenance recovery, active transactions, real abandoned payload and failed-retirement cleanup contracts.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- If maintenance wins the brief empty-allocation window, allocation now reports its original failure rather than making up to two new directories. Introducing #154199/#151917/#155947 provenance documents synthetic creator/reclaimer interleavings and CI proof, not an independently verified human pre-payload incident. Rerunning backup is the recovery; no payload exists before successful return.
- Physical-absence/native-open/path-mismatch retry classification and its extra reread disappear. Ordinary non-owner failure still invokes the same identity-bound cleanup; busy/retired tokens remain untouched because another native owner may hold them. Changed directory identity remains rejected, never adopted or deleted as ours.
- Human issue #154114 reports approximately2.5GB of abandoned payload after failed updates. Its payload reclamation, warning, lifetime transaction, retirement and ordinary restart behavior remain entirely unchanged. No SQL, schema, durability, retention or permission policy changes.

## Evidence

- Complete current owner, old483-line suite, complete439-line candidate suite and affected CLI guide frame inspected; previous complete consumer/token/private-directory/published fs-safe0.26.7 Root/context/native admission/move/remove closure retained. Exactly eight tracked determining preimages remain unchanged from the previously qualified parent to fresh3260d7b; dependency pin remains0.26.7. prs.title: fix(nodes): sanitize terminal controls in camera list report
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Running `openclaw nodes camera list --node <id>` prints the remote node's reported device `name`, `position`, and `id` fields verbatim into the human-readable camera table. A compromised or malicious paired node (or a driver that injects junk into a device name) can place C0/C1 terminal control sequences — `ESC`, `BEL`, `OSC` like `\x1b]0;...\x07` — into those fields, and the terminal interprets them (retitle the window, clear the screen, render fake output), letting the node drive the operator's terminal instead of just reporting cameras. Render the list through `renderTerminalSafeTable` so every cell passes through `sanitizeTerminalText`.

- Problem: remote node's `device.name` / `device.position` / `device.id` were rendered verbatim into a human-readable `renderTable`, so terminal control sequences reached the operator's terminal.
- Solution: switch the camera list table to the canonical safe wrapper `renderTerminalSafeTable`, which runs every cell value (and header) through `sanitizeTerminalText` (strip ANSI + remove C0/C1 controls). The sibling `nodes status` report (`register.status.ts`) already sanitizes every remote field; this file was the remaining gap in the same module.
- What changed: `src/cli/nodes-cli/register.camera.ts` swaps `renderTable` → `renderTerminalSafeTable` (import updated) for the `camera list` report; `register.camera.test.ts` adds a regression test feeding control-sequence-laden device fields and asserting the rendered log output is clean.
- What did NOT change: the `--json` branch still writes the original raw payload to stdout for scripts; only the human-readable table rendering is sanitized.

## Why This Change Was Made

`renderTerminalSafeTable` (in `packages/terminal-core/src/table.ts`) is the canonical single point that renders untrusted single-line values for terminal tables without changing `renderTable`'s trusted-ANSI contract. Reusing it keeps the fix at the canonical boundary (no new parser or policy branch, no per-field repetition), matching how the pairing table was fixed in #175179 and how `register.status.ts` already sanitizes remote node fields. `sanitizeTerminalText` strips ANSI first so removed bytes cannot form a new escape sequence, and removes C0/C1 controls while preserving readable text.

- Best fix: yes — reuse the existing canonical safe table renderer; the fix is a one-line swap at the render boundary.
- Alternative: wrapping each of the three device fields individually in `sanitizeTerminalText` — rejected because it repeats the guard per field and would diverge from the table-level canonical wrapper already used for pairing.
- Risk: none beyond the intended sanitization; the `--json` output path is untouched, and readable device names are preserved (only control bytes are removed).

## User Impact

Operators running `nodes camera list` no longer risk having a compromised or malicious paired node inject terminal control sequences (window retitle, clear screen, fake output) through the camera device fields. The human-readable report is now safe; `--json` consumers still get the exact raw values they need.

## Evidence

**Real end-to-end proof — shipped `nodes camera list` command** — drives a real Gateway server with a real paired node that replies to `camera.list` with injected `BEL` (`\u0007`) and `OSC` (`\u001b]0;title-pwned\u0007`) control characters, then spawns the **shipped CLI** `src/entry.ts nodes camera list` as a real subprocess and captures its terminal output:

| | Base (pre-fix, `b2144b385e`) | Head (post-fix, `657bc5ab`) |
|---|---|---|
| Renderer | `renderTable` (passes control chars through) | `renderTerminalSafeTable` (strips them) |
| Device name 1 | `front\u0007bell` rendered as `front^Gbell` (BEL visible) | `frontbell` (BEL removed) |
| Device name 2 | `\u001b]0;title-pwned\u0007` rendered as `^[]0;title-pwned^G` (full OSC visible) | (empty — OSC stripped) |
| `dev-1` / `dev-2` | present | present |
| Exit status | 0 | 0 |

Pre-fix raw output (`cat -v` to reveal control bytes — `^G` = BEL, `^[` = ESC):
```
│ front^Gbell                                  │ front    │ dev-1  │
│ ^[]0;title-pwned^G                           │ back     │ dev-2  │
```

Post-fix output (clean — no ESC/BEL anywhere):
```
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬──────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Name                                                  │ Position │ ID                                                │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ frontbell                                             │ front    │ dev-1                                             │
│                                                       │ back     │ dev-2                                             │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴──────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The proof runs under the real `gateway-server` vitest shard (not committed). The node goes through real device-pairing approval + durable node-pairing approval, intercepts the forwarded `node.invoke.request`, and replies with the injected devices. The CLI subprocess connects via real WebSocket and invokes `node.invoke` — the `camera.list` command genuinely reaches the node and is answered.

**Live command verification** — the sanitization primitive invoked by the fix, run against real injected control sequences:

```console
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module -e '
import { sanitizeTerminalText } from "./packages/terminal-core/src/safe-text.ts";
console.log("BEL:", JSON.stringify(sanitizeTerminalText("front\^Gbell")));
console.log("OSC:", JSON.stringify(sanitizeTerminalText("\^[]0;title-pwned\^G")));
'
BEL: "frontbell"
OSC: ""
```

A standalone `BEL` (`\x07`) inside a device name is removed while the surrounding text (`frontbell`) survives; an `OSC` window-title sequence (`\x1b]0;...\x07`) is stripped entirely so neither the control bytes nor the injected payload reach the terminal.

**Regression test (pre-fix RED / post-fix GREEN)** — the new test feeds `{ name: "front\^Gbell", ... }` and `{ name: "\^[]0;title-pwned\^G", ... }` through the mocked `camera list` RPC and asserts the rendered log contains no `ESC`/`BEL` and no `title-pwned`:

```console
# pre-fix (renderTable restored, test kept)
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/nodes-cli/register.camera.test.ts --run -t "strips terminal controls"
 FAIL  > nodes camera snap CLI option forwarding > strips terminal controls from device fields in the camera list report
       expect(raw).not.toContain("\^[")  // failed: control bytes present in output

# post-fix
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/nodes-cli/register.camera.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
```

**Full test file** passes 11/11, `oxlint` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean.

**What was not tested**: the `snap`/`clip` subcommands (their output paths were already hardened and are unchanged here); the `--json` output is intentionally not sanitized.

**Open PR collision check**: searched open PRs for `register.camera.ts` and its neighbors; no open PR touches this file (the only recent history is a UI media-ownership refactor #174721 that moved pre-existing code). The related canonical pairing-table fix #175179 uses the same `renderTerminalSafeTable` and does not overlap with the camera list path.

prs.title: fix(cli): attach crashes when the gateway sends an out-of-range grant expiry
prs.body:
Closes #174524

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw attach` crashes with `RangeError: Invalid time value` when the gateway answers `attach.grant` with an `expiresAtMs` outside the representable Date range, instead of reporting a bad gateway response and exiting. The throw happens inside the `try` whose `finally` owns grant revocation, so the operator also never gets the CLI's own exit path — they see a bare failure with no diagnostic.

## Why This Change Was Made

The grant admission check near the top of the `attach` action only proves `expiresAtMs` is a finite number (`src/cli/attach-cli.ts:119`). `Number.isFinite` accepts `1e16`, but `new Date(1e16).toISOString()` throws (`src/cli/attach-cli.ts:139`).

The fix reuses the existing owners instead of adding new machinery. The expiry is formatted with the shared `timestampMsToIsoString` helper (the `number-coercion` owner that already wraps `asDateTimestampMs`). When it returns `undefined` the action emits the existing malformed-grant diagnostic and calls `defaultRuntime.exit(1)`, which throws `ExitError` and unwinds through the existing `finally`, so the minted grant is still revoked before the process exits.

Extending the early-admission guard alone was rejected: returning there would skip revocation of a grant the CLI already owns.

## User Impact

Attaching now fails cleanly. An out-of-range grant expiry prints `attach.grant returned an unexpected response from the gateway.`, the minted grant is still revoked, and the command exits 1. No stack trace, no leaked live grant. In-range grants behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

### Shipped CLI + real Gateway client against a protocol-speaking fault server

Nothing in the CLI is stubbed: the run executes the shipped `openclaw.mjs` entry (loading the built `dist/`), the real `callGateway` WebSocket client, the real session-target resolution, the real `attach` action, the real grant custody and `finally` revocation, and reports the real process exit code.

A protocol-speaking fault server runs on `127.0.0.1` using a real `ws` `WebSocketServer`. It speaks the actual Gateway wire protocol — sends `connect.challenge`, answers `connect` with `hello-ok`, then answers `attach.grant` with `expiresAtMs: 8640000000000001` (`MAX_DATE_TIMESTAMP_MS + 1`) — and records the `attach.revoke` exchange so revocation is observable at the wire.

**Before (current `main` at `c1fcdfaeb9e`):**

```
=== fault server: expiresAtMs = 8640000000000001 ===
  exit code            : 1
  diagnostic           : (none)
  wire methods         : connect -> attach.grant -> connect -> attach.revoke -> attach.revoke
FAIL  fault server: prints the malformed-response diagnostic
RESULT: 6/7 -> FAIL
```

**After (this PR, head `40094527cc1`):**

```
=== fault server: expiresAtMs = 8640000000000001 ===
  exit code            : 1
  diagnostic           : attach.grant returned an unexpected response from the gateway.
  wire methods         : connect -> attach.grant -> connect -> attach.revoke -> attach.revoke
PASS  healthy gateway still attaches (exit 0)
PASS  healthy gateway does not report a malformed grant
PASS  fault server: shipped CLI exits 1
PASS  fault server: no RangeError escapes
PASS  fault server: prints the malformed-response diagnostic
PASS  fault server: attach.revoke reached the wire
PASS  fault server: grant was minted before revoke
RESULT: 7/7 -> PASS
```

The same run also covers a healthy gateway as a control (`connect -> attach.grant`, exit 0, no diagnostic, no revoke), so the valid path is unchanged.

Both runs used the identical harness; only the built `dist/` differed. The distinction the fix produces is the malformed-response diagnostic replacing an uninformative failure, with the `attach.grant -> attach.revoke` exchange present on the wire in both cases.

### Focused test

`src/cli/attach-cli.action.test.ts` covers `MAX_DATE_TIMESTAMP_MS + 1` and `-1e16`, asserting exit 1, the diagnostic, and a following `attach.revoke`.

```
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/cli/attach-cli.action.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
   Duration  53.90s
```

### Static checks

`oxfmt --check` passes on both touched files.

### Defect still present on main

`src/cli/attach-cli.ts:139` on `c1fcdfaeb9e` is still the unguarded `new Date(grant.expiresAtMs).toISOString()`, and line 119 still admits any finite number, so this is not a duplicate-already-fixed case.

<details>
<summary>🤖 AI-assisted PR</summary>

Prepared with AI assistance; the fault-server harness and commands above are reproducible on a standard checkout (Node >= 24.16) and I understand and stand behind the change.
</details>

prs.title: fix(workers): reclaim idle buffers and reduce catalog decoder memory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Catalog decoder workers retain unrelated runtime modules, and completed large buffers can remain uncollected when JavaScript heap growth stays below the idle-GC threshold.

## User Impact

Lower decoder overhead and reclamation of dead external buffers while keeping workers warm. No configuration, schema or supported public SDK change. This is a bounded improvement, not a demonstrated fix for the separate multi-GiB Gateway report or a guarantee that RSS returns to the OS.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep catalog routing, terminal text helpers and admission transport on lightweight imports. Heap and external-memory growth have independent anchors in the existing idle collector, preserving its threshold, burst debounce, cancellation and warm-worker reuse. The terminal facade remains official-plugin-private.

Shared transport state and task scopes use one lightweight context; native clean-close seals remain at the native owner. Current decoded-fact envelopes, process-lived physical facts, loader custody, revocation, reader scope and worker publications are preserved.

## Evidence

Signed head `08605da665f1cf76a8c43c3498a5135f2faef411`, integrating canonical main repair `5b64c3d0ff539ab44a9bec2b769509e3a135c030` from [#175964](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175964). That repair landed after [its exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39084888904): 52 jobs passed, 26 skipped. It fixes the inherited deferred-message ordering defect and five fixture failures independently of this worker feature.

This conflict-free integration leaves the feature at **27 paths (+380/-263)**. Every authored added/removed line is identical to reviewed head `127f76b2`; no new feature behavior or public SDK surface was added. The existing whole-delta P0–P2 independent review is reused for this mechanical integration, not represented as a new review. The canonical repair had its own fresh P0–P2 review with no actionable findings.

Fresh integrated-tree qualification on macOS arm64, Node24.16 and the repository-pinned Bun fork:

- **123 cases / 10 files passed:** admission retention and worker publication, task lifecycle, idle GC, real warm-worker heap/external payload finalization and reuse, catalog worker/preview behavior, SDK metadata generation, and the repaired ingress-lane contracts.
- Core production types, infra and state/logging test-type graphs, owner typed lint, SDK export/surface contracts, formatting and whitespace passed.
- Qualification tree: `4ab870def1f95e1611beed5b3ef854705d10a01d`; the dependency lock and Bun pin are unchanged.

Fresh exact-head [CI39087723703](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39087723703) is attached and still pending. It was naturally triggered by the integration push; current-head CI success is not yet claimed.

The original [CI39077683748](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39077683748) failed and remains failure history; it was not rerun. Prior passing [CI38985267299](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38985267299), on `023bc2c1`, and the earlier 90-case qualification on `127f76b2` remain historical evidence only. No unchanged push or hosted rerun was requested. **Feature merge and auto-merge remain off.**

Earlier full SDK producer/consumer and broader focused proof remain qualified historical evidence, not current-head reruns. No new cold-decoder benchmark, production-Gateway memory measurement or multi-GiB/RSS result is claimed.

Original validated commit `e71df5c160e02fcae56ffa3de6db5eef72896c6b`: decoder settled heap18.66→6.46MiB; prepared-model worker65.99→66.04MiB (no material improvement). prs.title: refactor(gateway): simplify config restart ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Simplifies Gateway config-restart ownership while preserving truthful pending
status, security preflight, active-work draining, and ordinary shutdown settlement.

## User Impact

Normal config reloads and explicit restarts keep their existing behavior. If an
accepted restart is canceled by a later config edit, that unrelated edit no longer
automatically retries it. Pending status remains visible; reapply the accepted
config or restart the Gateway manually when the warning requests it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The managed reloader already records accepted restart requirements. Keep that
fact for pending/applied-hash reporting and explicit same-source reapplication,
instead of transferring paused/conservative debt and accepted-target custody
between successive config candidates. Hot-recovery requirements report through
the same owner. One selected operation guards emission; one lifecycle AbortSignal
replaces duplicate numeric lifecycle/current/shutdown-cutoff checks.

This is the maintainer-requested restart-owner AREA of a previously parked wider cleanup: eleven
paths, six production files, +111/-420 = 309 net production lines removed. The
separate config/plugin-drain cut is not included. Public protocol/config/SDK,
persisted shapes, dependencies, permissions and durability are unchanged.
Phase E standalone session memory and its factory/registry/expiry/federation/tests
remain wholly untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- An unrelated accepted edit does not rearm an earlier accepted-but-canceled
  restart. The debt/target machinery originated in #105289; linked #103736 uses
  a stubbed-channel synthetic handler reproduction, not a human actual-use debt
  transfer incident. The accepted requirement stays pending and warns; explicitly
  reapply its source or restart manually.
- A superseded detached tail does not borrow a newer config target or deposit
  debt for its acceptance window. The same synthetic provenance supplies no human
  incident for that handoff. It logs reapply/restart guidance; current-owner
  recovery, admitted-work settlement and actual security checks remain.
- A superseded request can finish read-only preparation. The selected-operation
  and lifecycle checks prevent emission at the effect; source/credential/database
  preflight remains. A request-generation counter and its intermediate bookkeeping
  checks add no independent authority.
- Constructing replacement handlers aborts the previous handler lifecycle.
  Actual channel cancellation remains: human #79487 describes late old startup
  after restart, and human actual-use report #71637 requires draining long-running
  work. The signal replaces numeric bookkeeping, not their effect or settlement
  protections.

## Evidence

Fresh independent P0–P2 review completed scoped-clean (confidence .87), including
verification of all eleven changed files and the complete captured diff. Twenty-five
intact permitted owner/caller contexts were supplied; unchanged token/secrets contexts
were explicitly excluded after preflight filename refusals, with no guard changes.
The reviewer retained the runtime uncertainty below without claiming a causal fix.
Targeted nine-root types passed in 185.43 seconds. Targeted formatting and diff whitespace checks pass.
Changed-edge comparison across all six production owners adds only node:util,
with zero new nonbuiltin dependency edges; no new cycle component can be formed
by this change. Broad runtime/static cycle gates remain hosted CI proof.

The initial isolated invocation has no verified suite result. Its retained log
contains the unchanged supervised-child case's 205545-millisecond
timeout and construction-abort cleanup failure; that result was not passing proof.

One subsequent serial candidate/base replay used the same selected case,
original 120000-millisecond deadline and maxWorkers=1. Candidate failed at
261711 milliseconds with construction-abort identity loss and an unreleased
nested-resource receipt (child exit 2). Exact base passed the case in 95172
milliseconds and completed normally (child exit 0). The complete pair took
2010.11 seconds. All eleven candidate files, five prerequisites and the full
candidate diff hash were verified after restoration; no baseline files remain.

The failure remains unresolved, not proven inherited, load-caused or repaired.
The retained candidate fixture has its watcher script and cleanup release marker
but no child-run marker; this bounds the observation without certifying the
underlying cause. Its retained temporary namespace is not represented as cleanly
settled. Subsequent focused keeper proof passed: all eight restart-coordinator
cases (704.58 seconds runner, 834.97 seconds shard, 862.68 seconds isolated
wrapper), then 28 selected handler/security/service/contention cases across two
files (1129.33 seconds runner, 1290.31 seconds shard, 1320.15 seconds isolated
wrapper; 93 unrelated cases name-filtered). Both completed compiler generations
were verified. The two real contention cases prove refusal before writes,
owning-reload completion and successful retry. These passes do not resolve or
erase the separate supervised-child failure. Eleven-file official-core type-aware
lint passed in 231.46 seconds with one thread.

The mandatory suppression audit ran and finished 13/14 passing (79.67 seconds
runner, 116.13 seconds shard, 137.14 seconds isolated wrapper). Its only failure
is an old-base expected 95/actual 97 mismatch: two existing suppressions in the
unchanged MCP lifecycle fixture. Both that fixture and the old audit are identical
to the pinned base; this cut changes neither and adds no suppressions. Current
main already accounts for those exact Node-worker false positives in
[7ed47ac06405](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7ed47ac06405cc12baecb15b888df2d0fa023a4b).
No baseline, fixture, ignore or allowance was changed here, and no passing rerun

nor static review waives exact-head CI.
