prs.title: fix(telegram): route private topic reactions to topic sessions
prs.body:
Closes #175665

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram reaction updates omit topic fields. The reaction handler recovered the originating topic from OpenClaw's message cache for forum and channel Direct Messages, but not for private-chat topics. Those reactions were routed to the base DM session, and accounts with `requireTopic: true` dropped them entirely.

This change recovers the provider-observed `dm` topic for private-chat reactions, authorizes against that topic's config, and finalizes the route with the existing DM topic session-key owner. A reaction whose cached topic is unavailable still keeps the previous flat-DM fallback unless `requireTopic` requires one.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Private-chat reactions now use the same bounded message cache as forum and channel Direct Messages, accepting only a cached `dm` scope with a concrete topic ID.
- The handler applies `resolveTelegramTargetSession` and recomputes `lastRoutePolicy` after route resolution, matching normal inbound DM message handling instead of duplicating suffix logic.
- The `requireTopic` guard now checks for a recovered `dmThreadId`, so a valid cached topic is allowed while an unresolved topic is still rejected.
- The Telegram events documentation now describes private-chat topic recovery and its flat-DM fallback.
- No routine info-level logging was added, and forum/channel Direct Messages retain their existing strict cache-miss behavior.

## User Impact

Users reacting to bot messages inside a private-chat topic now wake the agent in that topic session, including topic-specific agents and bindings. The system event produces the expected `thread:<chat>:<topic>` session key. Reactions in ordinary private chats continue to use the base DM session, and unresolved topics are still dropped when `requireTopic` is enabled.

## Evidence

- Added a regression through the production reaction handler that recovers `{ scope: "dm", id: 77 }`, passes `requireTopic: true`, and asserts the exact `agent:topicbot:telegram:direct:5678:thread:5678:77` session key.
- The same test uses the real system-event queue: the notified topic session contains the reaction event and the base DM session remains empty.
- `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.reaction.runtime.test.ts` - 15 tests passed.
- `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.message-context.runtime.test.ts` - 8 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` - passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` - passed.
- `pnpm exec oxlint --type-aware` on changed source/test files - passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on all changed files - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.

No live Telegram probe was run in this environment. The regression exercises the production reaction handler and real system-event queue, with the Telegram transport and message-cache boundaries mocked.

## AI Assistance

AI assistance was used for source analysis, implementation, documentation, and validation. The change was checked against the issue's acceptance criteria, the Telegram plugin invariants, and adjacent reaction/session tests.

prs.title: fix(feishu): release per-chat queue lane at turn adoption (#54409)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #54409. Feishu users who send rapid follow-up messages (supplements, corrections) get one independent reply per message instead of human-like merging. The per-chat sequential queue serialized the **full agent turn**: message 2's turn was never submitted to core's reply queue while message 1's run was active, so the queue policy (`resolveActiveRunQueueAction` in `src/auto-reply/reply/queue-policy.ts`) always observed `isActive=false` and every rapid message ran as its own full run. The only relief was the queue's 5-minute eviction (`sequential-queue.ts`), which could start a second concurrent run — the visible symptom.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Feishu plugin was the last full-turn serialization point for inbound messages:

- Core's inbound debouncer already releases its queue lane at admission (`src/auto-reply/inbound-debounce.ts`).
- The durable drain completes its row at run adoption, i.e. run start (`agent-runner-execute.ts:297` calls `onAdopted`).
- Telegram, the sibling channel, already releases its lane at adoption (`extensions/telegram/src/bot-message.ts`).

Feishu's queue released its lane only when `handleMessage` resolved — after the whole turn. This change releases the lane at **turn adoption (run start)** instead, so during-run messages reach the queue policy while the first turn keeps running under core's reply-run registry. All changes live in `extensions/feishu/` plus one docs paragraph — no core, SDK, or config surface changes.

## User Impact

- Rapid follow-up messages during a run now reach the queue policy: default `steer` merges them into the active run (one reply), `collect` batches compatible messages, `followup` queues FIFO. Per-chat ordering is preserved (admission serialization, single-flight drain, `maxConcurrent 1` lane).
- `/stop` is unaffected — it still routes through the independent `:control` queue. Steering never interrupts running tool calls.
- Withdrawn-message (`recalled_v1`) handling stays out of scope: the repo has no event support for it (independent feature, PR #102165 unmerged).
- Documented: `docs/concepts/messages.md` now states channel plugins should release the inbound queue lane at adoption; Telegram and Feishu both do.
- **Shutdown safety is unchanged from current main**: a monitor shutdown while a message is dispatched but not yet adopted abandons the durable claim for restart retry — it never marks the row adopted (the gate's abort path runs the durable abandonment before freeing the lane; see the shutdown section below).

## Evidence

**Design** — new `extensions/feishu/src/turn-adoption-gate.ts`:

- `createTurnAdoptionGate(lifecycle)` wraps the ingress lifecycle and returns a one-shot gate promise. Release happens: after the original `onAdopted` settles (so replay claims are committed and the drain tombstone is durable before the lane frees), on `onDeferred` (preserving the returned accepted flag — `queue/types.ts:264` checks `=== false`), on `onFailed`/`onAbandoned` (try/finally), and on abort (listener detached at release, once-only).
- `enqueueAdoptionGatedTurn(...)` returns `{ lane, turn }`: the task settles a turn-capture first (a synchronous `runTurn` throw becomes a rejection without wrapping the value), then races the gate against the turn's catch leg. The lane never rejects; the sequential queue's 5-minute eviction remains the final bound for a never-adopting turn.

**Flush dispatch** (`monitor.message-handler.ts`, both sites) — `await Promise.race([turn, lane])` **before** `await settle()`:

- A pre-adoption failure deterministically rejects via the turn leg → existing catch → `onAbandoned` → rethrow → debounce `onError`, preserving abandon retry accounting (settling first would tombstone a failed turn via `transportLifecycle.onAdopted()`).
- A never-adopting turn is bounded by the queue's eviction through the lane leg, so the flush cannot hang.

**Error-path repair (ClawSweeper rounds: P1 adoption-failure propagation → P2a tagged outcome → P2b queued-abort abandonment → P1 shutdown tombstone → P1 pre-adoption dispatch cancellation → P1 same-document comment lane)**:

- P1 root cause (adoption failure): the gate's `finally` released the lane on adoption failure too, and `turn.catch(() => undefined)` turned the rejected turn into a successful queue task. The real dispatcher runs adoption several promise hops deep, so the caller's `Promise.race([turn, lane])` settles on the lane **before** the adoption rejection propagates to `turn`; `settle()` is then a no-op (`handedOff=true`), and the flush completed "successfully" — the debounce `onError` abandon/retry accounting (claim release + ingress abandon) never ran for a failed durable adoption.
- P1 fix (adoption failure): the gate carries the adoption failure and the task rethrows the carried value — the lane rejects, so the flush's existing `catch → onAbandoned → rethrow → onError` path runs and the failure contract of `feishu-ingress.test.ts:430` (adoption persistence failure abandons logical claims, never commits) survives the gate.
- P2a root cause (falsy failure lost): the gate carried the raw rejection value and the task only threw when truthy, so a falsy durable-adoption rejection (`throw undefined`) released the lane as success and skipped the same abandon path.
- P2a fix: the gate resolves a **tagged outcome** — `{ kind: "released" }` for every non-failure release, `{ kind: "failed", failure }` when the durable adoption rejected — so a falsy rejection can never be conflated with a success release. The task throws `toErrorObject(outcome.failure, …)` (SDK `error-runtime`, preserving Error identity and mapping strings to same-message Errors; the exact CI `typescript(only-throw-error)` + `no-base-to-string` lane caught the raw-value variant first).
- P2b root cause (queued-abort abandon swallowed): the gate task's pre-start-abort branch settled the turn capture with a resolved promise before awaiting the durable abandon — when the abandon rejected, the flush's race resolved on the (settled-success) turn leg and the failure died in the lane, unobserved.
- P2b fix: the turn now captures the abandon promise itself, so an abandonment persistence failure rejects the turn; the flush's race rejects via the turn leg → `catch → onAbandoned` retry (guarded by the flush lifecycle's `terminal` single-flight) → rethrow → `onError`, and abandon retry accounting survives.
- **P1 root cause (shutdown tombstone): the abort listener released the lane as success.** On normal monitor shutdown — which aborts active drain lifecycles (`src/channels/message/ingress-monitor.ts:734`, `shutdown.abort(...)`), while the non-guillotined drain lifecycle still accepts `onAdopted` and completes the durable claim — a message dispatched but not yet reply-lane-adopted resolved the flush on the lane leg; `settle()` then adopted the transport row (`feishu-ingress.ts:329-343`). The message was **tombstoned**: marked delivered/adopted without ever running, never retried after restart. The earlier rounds covered adoption failure but not the cancellation path.
- P1 fix (shutdown tombstone): the abort listener now runs the durable abandonment through the original lifecycle's `onAbandoned` **before** releasing the gate. On success, the flush's `settle()` no-ops (`onAbandoned` sets `handedOff` synchronously), so the row stays abandoned — the drain re-delivers it after restart, matching current-main shutdown semantics. On abandonment persistence failure, the gate carries the `failed` outcome so the flush's catch retries the abandonment and surfaces the error. The lane still frees, so the per-chat queue never blocks on a shutdown; the abort listener still never forwards its `Event` argument — only failed terminal transitions carry the `failed` outcome.
- **P1 root cause (pre-adoption dispatch not cancelled): the abort path abandoned the durable claim and released the lane but never cancelled `runTurn`.** Feishu supplied the lifecycle only as nested turn-adoption options, while core initial-dispatch cancellation reads `replyOptions.abortSignal` (`dispatch-from-config.lifecycle.ts` pre-dispatch/dispatch abort checks, `reply-turn-admission.ts` first-line admission check) — so after a shutdown abort the original pipeline could still advance to run start and agent/tool work while the reopened claim waited for replay, letting replay overlap an orphaned execution after restart.
- **P1 fix (pre-adoption dispatch cancellation)**: the plugin binds the drain's own signal at `replyOptions.abortSignal` through a feishu-local helper (`extensions/feishu/src/reply-options.ts`). The shared `bindIngressLifecycleToReplyOptions` keeps its return shape unchanged — irc and nextcloud-talk spread its whole return value into their replyOptions, so a top-level signal there would silently change their pre-adoption shutdown behavior (ClawSweeper P1 shared-path finding; scoped to the plugin on the current head). Admission and pre-dispatch abort checks therefore cancel the dispatch (the real `DispatchReplyOperationAbortedError` path) before any agent or tool work; the flush race rejects via the turn leg → catch → `onAbandoned` (joins the gate's in-flight abandonment through the flush lifecycle's single `abandoning` slot) → rethrow → `onError`. The drain aborts the signal only while the claim is dispatching/deferred (`ingress-drain.ts` `abortActiveClaims`/`dispose` skip adopted claims), so an adopted run is never cancelled through this surface — the binding is pre-adoption-only by the drain's own contract. All three Feishu lifecycle-bound dispatch surfaces — single-agent (`bot.ts:1909-1913`), broadcast (`bot.ts:1631-1638`), and comment notifications (`comment-handler.ts:312-313`) — use the local helper.
- Regression coverage (each fails on the pre-fix gate, verified by stashing the gate source; 5 failed | 28 passed → 33/33 on the repaired head; this round's two cancellation regressions additionally fail on pre-fix code, stash-verified — 1 core + 1 integration):
  - `turn-adoption-gate.test.ts` — the lane **rejects** when adoption fails (Error and falsy values) while the turn is still pending; the turn **and** the lane reject when a pre-start abandon fails; an in-flight abort runs the durable abandonment **before** releasing the lane; the lane **rejects** when that abort-path abandonment fails; the gate resolves `{ kind: "released" }` on an already-aborted signal.
  - `monitor.message-handler.ingress.test.ts` — the flush **rejects** on durable adoption persistence failure with an Error **and** with a falsy rejection (parametrized; the logical claim is released twice by contract — replay guard + admission-time abandon handler — and never committed; the transport abandons exactly once); the flush **rejects** when a queued pre-start abandon fails to persist; a queued pre-start abandonment whose gate-attempt fails is retried by the task and the flush **completes** with the claim abandoned; a **pre-adoption abort abandons the durable ingress instead of settling it as adopted** (transport `onAdopted` never called, transport abandons once, claim released-not-committed, flush completes silently — the shutdown path); a persistently-failing abandonment still **rejects** the flush (retry accounting survives: 3 abandon runs, 6 releases).
  - This round (pre-adoption dispatch cancellation): the core binding test keeps asserting the shared binding's **unchanged** shape (keys `[turnAdoptionLifecycle]`, no top-level signal); the integration test drives the **real feishu binding** — the mock binds the gated lifecycle through `bindFeishuLifecycleToReplyOptions` exactly like `resolveTurn`, observes the drain signal by identity, and **rejects on abort** like the real dispatch-abort path — the flush **rejects** with the cancellation error, the row stays abandoned (transport `onAdopted` never called, transport abandons once, claim released-not-committed — 2 releases by contract), and only replay executes after shutdown (pre-fix: the mock never sees an abort signal, the flush completes silently, and the pipeline was free to reach agent/tool work).
- **P1 root cause (same-document comment lane not gated): the document-keyed comment queue still awaited the full handler.** `handleFeishuCommentEvent` runs `core.channel.inbound.run` to turn completion, and the durable comment handler's enqueue task awaited it — so a rapid second notice on the same document could not reach the shared queue policy while the first run was active: the exact #54409 defect the message lane fix removed, still present on the comment sibling (its held-first-turn test at `monitor.comment.test.ts:737` proved it). The docs' adoption-release claim covered "Feishu" as a whole, which the comment path contradicted.
- **P1 fix (same-document comment lane)**: the durable comment-notice handler now routes through the same `enqueueAdoptionGatedTurn` as the message lane — the document lane frees at turn adoption (run start), so a same-document notice during the first run reaches the queue policy; the gated lifecycle is passed through to `handleFeishuCommentEvent`, which binds it to reply-options (`comment-handler.ts:312-314`), inheriting the pre-adoption dispatch cancellation from the shared core seam. Non-durable (no-lifecycle) comments keep today's full-turn serialization — there is no claim to release. The gate's pre-start abort still abandons without running, and pre-adoption failure or a failed durable adoption rejects the flush so the caller's `settle()` cannot tombstone the row. New regression: a held first comment turn (adopted, still running) must let the second same-document notice start — fails pre-fix (stash-verified 1 failed | 19 passed), green post-fix.

**Tests** — `turn-adoption-gate.test.ts` (17 unit tests: release timing relative to original callbacks, deferral flag preservation, once-only across repeated terminal signals, pre-aborted signal, no-lifecycle full-turn wait, lane-at-adoption/deferral/abandon while turn pending, failed-adoption lane rejection for Error and falsy values, pre-start-abandon turn+lane rejection, abort-path abandonment + abort-path abandonment-failure lane rejection, same-key ordering — all driven through the production entry `enqueueAdoptionGatedTurn`, the gate helper itself is private per ClawSweeper P3), integration regression tests in `monitor.message-handler.ingress.test.ts` (17, including the new pre-adoption dispatch-cancellation test) using the real inbound debouncer + real sequential queue + real flush lifecycle (`buildFeishuFlushIngressLifecycle`) + gated lifecycle: message B's `handleMessage` is called while A's turn is still running, order A→B, one adoption each, and the same-document comment-lane regression in `monitor.comment.test.ts` (20, including the new held-first-turn test: the first comment turn is adopted but still running when the second same-document notice arrives and must start anyway). **Every error-path regression fails on pre-fix code and passes with the fix** (verified by stashing the gate source: `5 failed | 28 passed` pre-fix, 33/33 post-fix; the two cancellation regressions additionally fail pre-fix, stash-verified; the comment-lane regression fails pre-fix, stash-verified `1 failed | 19 passed`). 64/64 focused tests green on the current head (`turn-adoption-gate` 17 + `monitor.message-handler.ingress` + `monitor.comment` + `comment-handler` + the core binding test); full Feishu shard 1599/1600 on the new head — the single failure is `setup-surface.test.ts`'s English status-line expectation on this zh-locale machine (plugin emits "已连接为 Feishu Main"), a pre-existing environment artifact in a file this PR does not touch (`git diff origin/main HEAD -- extensions/feishu/src/setup-surface.test.ts` is empty). The restart half of the shutdown contract is the existing real-drain recovery test (`feishu-ingress.test.ts:243`, "recovers an uncompleted envelope with a fresh drain and dispatches exactly once") — abandoned rows are re-dispatched by a fresh drain, so the integration regression above (claim abandoned, never adopted) is a retry, not a tombstone.

**Local gates** — `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `check:test-types`, `oxfmt`, `git diff --check`, oxlint on the changed files, and `deadcode:knip` (the gate's knip exemption is removed) all green on the current head (`e4da58cf7de`). A full-extensions-lane oxlint additionally surfaces three `typescript(no-redundant-type-constituents)` type-resolution errors in `extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/...`; those files are byte-identical to `origin/main` (`git diff origin/main HEAD -- extensions/qa-lab/` is empty) and the repo's own CI `check-lint` lane is green on `main` (run 31938502373) and on sibling PRs — so that local noise is a local type-resolution artifact, not a lane failure. The changed-surface lint gate for this PR is the focused run above.

**LOC** — the pre-adoption cancellation round added +6 production lines on the shared core binding seam; the current head removes that shared surface again (the top-level signal is feishu-local now, because irc/nextcloud-talk spread the shared return value — ClawSweeper P1), netting **~0 production delta for the round**: −6 core binding, −3 knip exemption, +17 feishu-local binding helper (`reply-options.ts`), gate privatization neutral, plus the earlier +36 lines in the durable comment-notice handler (`monitor.comment-notice-handler.ts`) — the gated branch replaces the old enqueue block, non-durable handling is unchanged. The gate module's lines carry the failure semantics the earlier rounds' findings required (tagged outcomes, retry accounting), and both per-session Feishu ingress lanes (message + comment) now share the one gate helper; docs unchanged (the adoption-release claim now holds for the comment lane too).

**Mock-gateway harness verdict (changed-path real-behavior proof)** — `test/feishu-turn-adoption-gateway.e2e.test.ts` (landed at `31c5797193b`; this round adds the same-document comment-lane block, +162 test lines), rerun locally against the rebuilt dist (**6/6 tests, ~87s — 3 message modes + 3 comment modes**; the message-path tests are unchanged):

```json
{
  "harness": "mock-gateway e2e — test/feishu-turn-adoption-gateway.e2e.test.ts",
  "changedPath": "feishu webhook channel -> core reply queue policy, both per-session ingress lanes (per-chat messages + same-document drive comment notices), all three queue modes",
  "topology": "ephemeral gateway (createOpenClawTestInstance, own port + state dir) + mock OpenAI-responses provider (first /v1/responses held) + real signed feishu webhook transport (sha256(timestamp+nonce+encryptKey+body), x-openclaw-delivery-accepted: durable). The comment block points the account domain at a dead local https port so drive comment-context resolution (document meta / thread text) fails instantly and degrades to an empty context — requestFeishuOpenApi never throws — keeping the harness local and deterministic; the changed path under test is the document queue lane, not the drive fetch.",
  "steps": [
    { "step": 1, "action": "POST signed im.message.receive_v1 (MESSAGE_ONE)", "observed": "200 + durable ack; run 1 reaches mock provider and is held" },
    { "step": 2, "action": "POST signed im.message.receive_v1 (MESSAGE_TWO) while run 1 is still active", "observed": "a message.queued event appears while mock provider requests == 1 (steer: source=followup-queue-steer park; collect/followup: source=dispatch, queueDepth=2); 200 + durable ack", "proves": "second same-chat message reached resolveActiveRunQueueAction with isActive=true — the per-chat lane was released at turn adoption, not at turn completion" },
    { "step": 3, "action": "release run 1", "observed": "request #2 carries MESSAGE_TWO in every mode; no third model request — message 2 never starts a second concurrent run" },
    { "step": 4, "action": "wait for run terminal", "observed": "session.state with outcome=idle and queueDepth=0" },
    { "step": 5, "action": "POST signed drive.notice.comment_add_v1 (comment_harness_1, document docx_harness_token) via the same webhook + durable drain", "observed": "200 + durable ack; the comment turn reaches mock provider and is held" },
    { "step": 6, "action": "POST a second same-document drive.notice.comment_add_v1 (comment_harness_2) while run 1 is still active", "observed": "a message.queued event appears while mock provider requests == 1 (steer: source=followup-queue-steer park; collect/followup: source=dispatch); 200 + durable ack", "proves": "second same-document comment notice reached the active-run queue decision with isActive=true — the comment-doc lane was released at turn adoption, not at turn completion (pre-fix the notice is not even dispatched until run 1 completes)" },
    { "step": 7, "action": "release run 1", "observed": "request #2 carries the second notice's event identity (drive-comment:evt_comment_2) in every mode; no third model request — comment 2 never starts a second concurrent run" },
    { "step": 8, "action": "wait for run terminal", "observed": "session.state with outcome=idle and queueDepth=0" }
  ],
  "verdict": "PASS (6/6 tests, steer + collect + followup x message + comment lanes) — changed path proven on a real gateway for every queue mode on both Feishu ingress lanes: adoption-gated lane release lets a same-chat message and a same-document comment notice reach the active-run queue decision while run 1 is still held"
}
```

**Shutdown-path proof boundary** — the e2e harness cannot deterministically hold the pre-adoption window: reply-lane adoption happens at run start, which precedes the first provider interaction that the harness holds, and the drain offers no pause hook between dispatch and adoption. The shutdown path is therefore proven at its owner boundary (flush dispatch + gate) by the integration regressions above, using the real inbound debouncer, real sequential queue, real flush lifecycle, and real gate — the deterministic equivalent of "stop the monitor before reply-lane adoption". The cancellation half ("only replay executes after shutdown") is the new dispatch-cancellation regression: the dispatch pipeline observes the drain's own signal through the feishu-local binding and cancels (rejects) exactly as the real dispatch-abort path would, so no agent/tool work can start after the claim reopens; the mock-gateway harness still proves the changed-path queue behavior on the rebuilt dist (6/6 rerun on the current head after the binding was scoped to the plugin, including the comment lane). The same adoption gate covers both lanes, so the gate's shutdown/abort/failure semantics apply identically to the comment lane; the comment-lane unit regression additionally covers its pre-start abort branch.

**Known gaps** — live Feishu-channel verification is still pending (no test bot on my side); the harness verdict above is the mock-gateway evidence ClawSweeper requested (now covering both the message and the same-document comment lane), and the integration tests remain the per-dispatch and shutdown regression proofs. Both earlier `openclaw/ci-gate` reds were infrastructure events, not code failures: (1) run 375217 on head `097c1e400d2` was externally cancelled at 23:42:07Z (no push, no PR event, every completed job green); (2) run 31938245620 on head `a3e2fb092aa` — ~90/90 completed jobs green, but the `check-lint` job was killed mid-lint by a **hosted-runner shutdown signal** (`##[error]The runner has received a shutdown signal…`, `[oxlint] FAILED (exit 143)`, annotation "The operation was canceled.") with no lint output at all. Repo-wide CI was healthy at the same moment (`main` 09:14 ✅, PR #124509 09:18 ✅, PR #124372 09:12 ✅), and the pr-ci-sweeper's revive lane only reruns runs whose conclusion is `cancelled` (that one is `failure`), so no repo automation would have recovered it. Head `4e605ae5999` — an empty, tree-identical CI-kick commit — started fresh run 31939348553 that superseded it (the same hosted-runner shutdown flake already hit this PR once before; see commit `9a6176c144b`). **Run 31939348553 completed green (09:44:17Z), as did run 31941202610 on head `3ccbfd6bd39` (the same-document comment-lane fix) and run 31998082032 on head `a9bd3ced34c` (gate privatization + scoped abort forwarding): `openclaw/ci-gate` success each time.** Head `34a1097c694` rebased the branch onto current `main` (493 commits, per the Aug 17 05:40 UTC ClawSweeper review's Rank-up move) with no conflicts; exact-head proof rerun: 64/64 focused tests, `tsgo:extensions`, `check:test-types`, `deadcode:knip`, `oxfmt`, `git diff --check`, and the mock-gateway harness **6/6 (~76s)** against the dist rebuilt on that head; CI green (run 31999494771). Head `e4da58cf7de` (current) is the follow-up rebase after the Aug 17 20:21 UTC ClawSweeper issue review flagged the branch again: `main` had advanced 326 commits, of which one (`eb38d5e4863`, "report settled delivery outcomes once", #124773) touched the Feishu comment handler — resolved with one conflict (the binding import), absorbing main's `resolveInboundReplyDispatchCounts` into the comment dispatch log while keeping the feishu-local binding; `extensions/feishu/` is otherwise untouched by the new main range (only the knip ratchet-consolidation touched `config/knip.config.ts`). Exact-head proof rerun on `e4da58cf7de`: 64/64 focused tests, `tsgo:extensions`, `check:test-types`, `deadcode:knip`, `oxfmt`, `git diff --check`, and the mock-gateway harness **6/6 (~94s) against the dist rebuilt on the new head**. The fresh CI run for `e4da58cf7de` follows. Fork-CI reds on the user's fork `main` are fork-environment artifacts (missing fork secrets; control-ui i18n baseline drift pre-existing on upstream `main`, proven by a clean-tree local run; bundled-protocol origin fetch) and do not involve this branch. The `extension-codex-app-server-attempt-extra` config's five local-operator MCP tests time out at 120s on this machine, alone and under load; `git diff origin/main HEAD -- extensions/codex/` is empty — the failure is current-main code on this environment, untouched by this PR.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reduces repeated setup and assertion boilerplate in the test suite (campaign batch d248).

## User Impact

No production behavior or API changes. This batch consolidates test fixtures and equivalent cases; runtime proof is delegated to PR CI under the operator's CI-only policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replayed 28 of 30 supplied commits onto pinned main `cb38ef7074e56112b4ae866643a40f9a830ae88f`. Changed paths are tests/test support plus eight shrink-only mock-baseline rows: +7,970 / -12,450 lines, net -4,480. Production LOC: +0 / -0.

### Replay decisions

- Skipped `3460c9afdc8` (x7989): sessions-tool tests have already been rewritten on main, including shared sessions-list fixtures in `63beded0ddd` (#173031). Preserve main rather than reinstate obsolete fixtures.
- Skipped `49fd61a21de`: its event-publication follow-up applies only to the discarded event-refresh rewrite.
- x7981: kept the initial bootstrap consolidation and clean changes; dropped later conflicting edits to `bootstrap.test.ts` and `browser-bootstrap.test.ts`, retaining main's additional route/auth cases.
- x7995: dropped conflicting picker/event-refresh edits; preserved main's keyboard, filter, event and lifecycle cases. Kept other component consolidation.
- x8000: dropped changes to `dead-config-keys`, `defaults`, `doc-baseline.integration` and `env-preserve` tests to retain expanded main contracts.
- x7998: retained SDK imports and new main cloud/QA cases; dropped second-pass SDK rewrite, kept the other changes.
- x7997: preserved main's CLI help/invalid-argument test and runCli helper alongside the new fixture helpers.
- x7992: dropped the entire batch change to `device-pairing-node.test.ts` and `device-pairing-prune.test.ts`; their newer reconnect/provenance tests overlap the fixture migration. Other infrastructure changes retained.
- x8003: retained main's `plugin-prerelease-test-plan.test.ts` including hourly coverage/runtime policy assertions; kept remaining release-fixture consolidation.

## Evidence

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline`: passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --write <72 changed paths>`: passed (exit 0).
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json <71 changed TS/TSX paths>`: passed (exit 0).
- `git diff --check cb38ef7074e56112b4ae866643a40f9a830ae88f`: passed.
- No local Vitest, typecheck, check-changed, coverage, or Testbox run: explicitly prohibited by the CI-only work order. No Testbox leases created.
- Required `openclaw/ci-gate` is the merge gate. Independent autoreview runs concurrently with hosted CI.
- No CODEOWNERS-listed path is changed. No screenshots: test-only changes, no intended visual behavior change.

### CI correction

Initial run [39084781751](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39084781751) found batch-caused failures. The correction removes the later x7991 shared-hoisted-mock migration (Bun cannot export the hoisted variable), all x7996 model-provider E2E edits (fixture failures), and later x8001 custody migration (invalid delivery-completion variant and mock-export ratchets). Earlier independent x7991 and x8001 consolidation remains. Fixed a floating stream call by awaiting it, removed single-use fixture generics, retained named pointer-capture mocks, made WAL cleanup an arrow function, and documented intentional transcript mock isolation. No retries, skipped tests, relaxed assertions, or production changes.

The interrupted first autoreview had no verdict. The restarted independent review completed all three passes on `c84d9de6a76`: two passes reported no actionable findings; the third reported one P1 selector concern. Rejected after source verification: old `tabViewport()` delegates to `.tabstrip`, current `tabStrip()` selects the same `.tabstrip`, and production attaches the observer/listener to that element. Reviewed-head UI jobs passed. No selector change was needed.

Second CI run [39085427110](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39085427110) passed the runtime shards and surfaced the remaining precise static issues. Final correction removes exactly the eight obsolete mock-baseline rows named by CI, binds the temp-directory method, converts subprocess diagnostics to strings, preserves required SQLite worker environment typing, and uses literal candidate discriminants. The `system-agent-session-ownership.test.ts` cleanup is dropped entirely to retain main's legacy-reply fixture contract. No new baseline allowances or weakened assertions. Final correction commit: `1dc5b6ae8b3`.

prs.title: fix: disconnection watchdog in provider lifecycle owner
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the Discord gateway disconnects and an event-loop stall prevents the reconnect timer from firing, the gateway stays in 'reconnect scheduled' state indefinitely and goes deaf to Discord. The existing lifecycle owner (provider.lifecycle.ts) already handles startup stalls (gateway opens but READY never arrives) via startReadyWatch, but does NOT cover runtime stalls after steady-state — when the gateway was already connected, disconnects, and the reconnect stalls.

## The Fix: Disconnection Watchdog in the Lifecycle Owner

Extended createGatewayStatusObserver in provider.lifecycle.ts to start a disconnection watchdog when the gateway closes (after initial readiness). The watchdog polls isConnected and, if the gateway stays disconnected longer than runtimeReadyTimeoutMs (30s default), calls triggerForceStop — which goes through the existing lifecycle cleanup path (waitForDiscordGatewayStop -> finishReject -> proper disconnect and listener cleanup).

Key design:
- Only arms after `markRuntimeReady()` (after initial `waitForGatewayReady` completes)
- Arms on both "Gateway websocket closed" AND "Gateway reconnect scheduled" (covers Invalid Session, server RECONNECT, heartbeat timeout, failed IDENTIFY)
- Deadline preserved across reconnect cycles (startDisconnectWatchdog is no-op if already running)
- Grace period: if a reconnect is in progress (socket CONNECTING/OPEN) when the watchdog fires, it defers and grants another runtimeReadyTimeoutMs
- Stopped on READY/RESUMED dispatch, on dispose, and when lifecycle is stopping

## Evidence

**Live transport proof, CONNECTING-at-cap branch (head `3acb82dec3b`, 2026-09-03):**
```
[+      0ms] graceful ws.close(1000), reconnectAttempts preset → backoff 16000ms
[+    ~100ms] reconnect-scheduled: 16000ms → watchdog rearmed to min(21000, cap−elapsed)
[+  16108ms] RESUME dial stranded on a stuck TCP server — socket readyState=0 (CONNECTING)
[+  21105ms] watchdog fires → grace 1/2, rearm capped to remaining budget 3895ms (< T)
[+  25105ms] watchdog fires → grace 2/2, remaining budget 0
[+  25107ms] force-stop at cumulative cap: elapsed 25005ms vs cap 25000ms, socket still CONNECTING
[+  ~25200ms] supervisor recovery → fresh READY → inbound MESSAGE_CREATE delivered
```
Full redacted log: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/124162#issuecomment-5525733609

**Live transport proof (runDiscordGatewayLifecycle public entry point, prior head `9cb5b13ebd2`):**
```
[+     9ms] proof: connecting to Discord gateway
[+   317ms] gateway.debug: Gateway websocket opened
[+   820ms] proof: gateway READY (isConnected=true)
[+  2821ms] proof: terminating gateway websocket; reconnect disabled
[+  2823ms] gateway.debug: Gateway websocket closed: 1006
[+ 32828ms] runtime.error: discord gateway: disconnection watchdog fired after 30004ms — force-stopping lifecycle
[+ 32830ms] proof: PASS — disconnection watchdog force-stopped the real lifecycle
```

Exercised the REAL `runDiscordGatewayLifecycle` — the public exported entry point — with a live Discord gateway connection. Watchdog fired after 30004ms, lifecycle rejected with proper cleanup (threadBindings.stop called).

**Unit tests (provider.lifecycle.test.ts):**
- "force-stops the lifecycle when the gateway stays disconnected past the ready timeout"
- "does not force-stop when the gateway reconnects before the watchdog threshold"
- "defers force-stop when a reconnect is in progress at the watchdog threshold"

**ClawSweeper review:** Zero code findings, proof: sufficient, patch quality: platinum hermit (4/6), status: ready for maintainer look.

## Changes

- **provider.lifecycle.ts** (+76): startDisconnectWatchdog, clearDisconnectWatchdog, wired into onGatewayDebug (close + reconnect-scheduled), dispose, markRuntimeReady, grace-period deferral for in-progress reconnects
- **provider.lifecycle.test.ts** (+73): three tests covering force-stop, quick-reconnect, and grace-period deferral
- **gateway.ts** (-35): removed old gateway-level watchdog (shouldReconnect=false in maxAttempts kept)
- **gateway-lifecycle.ts** (-39): removed GatewayConnectionWatchdog class
- **gateway.test.ts** (-149): removed old watchdog tests

Net: +149 -224 = -75 lines

Closes #122950

prs.title: feat(continuation): context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work / continue_delegate / request_compaction)
prs.body: ## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Persistent OpenClaw agents today are externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation delegate store** (TaskFlow-backed) persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts. The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **TaskFlow backing**: durable delegate queue via the platform's managed-task infrastructure - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → TaskFlow record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, TaskFlow delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. Spans emitted (all in `openclaw.*` or `continuation.delegate.dispatch` namespace — no platform/OTel-semconv emissions): | Span | Emitted when | |---|---| | `openclaw.run` | Each agent turn (root + every continuation/delegate-spawned child run) | | `continuation.delegate.dispatch` | Each `continue_delegate` consumption from TaskFlow (one per delegate hop) | | `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.context.assembled`, `openclaw.model.call`, `openclaw.model.usage`, `openclaw.tool.execution` | Existing per-turn observability surfaces, parented under their `openclaw.run` | --- ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** Sessions can elect future work with `continue_work`, dispatch bounded background work with `continue_delegate`, and request guarded compaction with `request_compaction`. The runtime preserves budgets, restart recovery, finalization ownership, and trace lineage across those boundaries. **Presented candidate:** `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` (tree `d5e701bcce20bb3c972ddf1451b02d88cc04808e`) — the exact upstream-visible head of `codeagent/85651-upstream-1ba243c8-gates`. The branch was advanced to this head by fast-forward from the previously presented `e76395810becd0ad0f2997cae8b4f777e6439d81`, which remains an ancestor (`git merge-base --is-ancestor e7639581 3821eaef` holds). No presented history was rewritten. **Presented and current candidate are now the same commit.** There is no undisclosed descendant: `3821eaef72` is content-frozen and every receipt below is bound to it. **Current candidate validation:** Mode-B run [`35364768803`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw-bootstrap/actions/runs/35364768803) (`openclaw-local-ci`, `workflow_dispatch`) is bound to product `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and routing/workflow head `fcf0478fd1c8cbec0489d022a7e4eac6188de153`. It ran 2026-09-18T15:49:35Z to 2026-09-18T17:47:43Z and finished **68 jobs succeeded, 3 failed, 3 cancelled, 3 skipped**. The run is terminally **non-green and release-ineligible**, and every residual is classified: - `agentic-gateway-methods` (job `105667082763`) was **cancelled at the workflow's exact 90-minute job limit** on the `ronan` seat while still heartbeating and emitting new log lines. The same shard completes on the `elliott` and `emeric` seats. This is seat throughput against a 5,231-test shard, not a product verdict — and that same cancelled log carries **111 `sessions.send-followup-status` lines, all 111 passing**, against the real stale `/tmp/openclaw-agent.sqlite` on the host that originally produced the `uses schema version 17` failure. - `hosted(agentic-agents-tools,auto-reply-reply-dispatch,…)` (job `105667083998`) received `The runner has received a shutdown signal` and exited 143. 778 passing test lines were captured and **no test failure precedes the signal**. Two further hosted jobs (`105667084144`, `105667084159`) are the same reclamation class. - `hosted(core-runtime-media-ui-3,core-runtime-infra-repo-tooling,…)` (job `105667084127`) is red only because `subagent-announce.live-tree-chain-proof` hit `sessions_spawn model "openai/gpt-6-astra" is not usable: The selected account ... unavailable`. That is an account provisioning gap, observed identically in six prior runs. - `aggregate + status` (job `105701732269`) is the expected fail-closed policy consequence of the residuals above, not an additional product-test failure. **No product-owned test failure and no routing failure occurred in this run.** Newly green on this exact head: the four re-laned toolchain shards `core-tooling-5`, `core-tooling-7`, `core-tooling-12` and `core-tooling-14` all succeeded on hosted runners after per-seat tooling failures, and `agentic-commands-doctor-config-state` succeeded on two different seats. The Mode-B planner identity digest `sha256:42dffd23ec447c6e4b726d0e6345f1dc2417801048aee49b96f3332233ef1f34` is preserved across those lane moves, so no shard identity changed. These residuals are runner, seat-throughput, and account-provisioning properties of the execution environment. They are not addressable inside this branch and are recorded here rather than presented as green. **Real environment tested:** An OpenClaw instance exercised live Discord ingress/egress and OTel/Tempo with content capture disabled. The full evidence chain, execution identity, ancestry, and materiality record are contained in the linked corpus rather than repeated here. **Observed behavior:** - A real retained ambient Discord event aged to 1,069,503 ms and was suppressed as `stale-ambient-backlog`; attempts remained zero. - A fresh addressed request completed with attempts zero and produced a visible response after 45.565 seconds. - Typed `continue_work` and bracket `CONTINUE_WORK` each armed and fired one five-second wake with granted provenance and completed Tempo model-call spans. - Cost-cap rejection passed an exact-source disposable fixture. - Max-chain matrix, scheduler, durable recovery, typed tool, and product delegate regression surfaces passed; the row remains partial because a docs-owned generated wrapper is stale. ### Evidence The canonical matrix contains 38 rows: **31 pass, three partial, one fail, and three missing** (`PROOFS/INDEX.json` -> corpus `7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567`). `R-CD-2` is the single fail. The partial rows are `R-CD-COLLECTION-ON-COLLAPSE`, `R-CD-TOKEN` and `R-RC-2`. The three missing rows are `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY`, `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2`. This is not acceptance-complete. The two return rows and `R-OBS-2` are missing for different reasons, and all three are producer gaps rather than absent behavior: - `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY` records zero of its 24 observations (12 authority cases against both the typed-tool and bracket-token surfaces). Its pending receipt requires allowed delivery to show exact effects, revoked and reassigned recipients to show zero prompt, wake and channel effect, schema v18/v19, restart replay, a signed authority, and full cleanup. The row's own `manifest` and harness `supporting_docs` pointers are currently **dangling on the docs default branch**: the harness exists but was never merged there. - `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2` each have a present manifest and failed only because the current-corpus input they read (overlap evidence file, exported trace tree) is absent. **Limits:** Historical live and Mode-B evidence for earlier heads is ancestry/materiality evidence, not exact-target execution. Run `35364768803` above *is* exact-target for `3821eaef72`. All seven non-pass rows remain gated on producer execution against this frozen head; no acceptance receipt from an older deployment composite is reused as final evidence. ## Proof links and ClawSweeper🦞 guidance Proof artifacts live in `karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs` on `main`. `PROOFS/INDEX.json` points at the corpus for the SHA this PR presents, `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`. Reviewed docs checkpoint: `c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c`. - [Corpus directory](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393) - [README — identity, what is proven, honest limits](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/README.md) - [RESOLVED-SHA.md — SHA identity and gate verdicts](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/RESOLVED-SHA.md) - [METHOD.md — reproducer commands](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) - [TRANSPOSED-FROM.md — why nothing was transposed](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/TRANSPOSED-FROM.md) - [Manifest](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/proofs-manifest.json) - [INDEX.json](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/INDEX.json) - [Prior published board (not superseded)](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567) ### What this corpus claims, and what it does not **Status: `STATIC_GATES_ONLY_NO_LIVE_ROWS_AT_THIS_SHA`.** Rollup `38 total / 0 pass / 0 partial / 0 fail / 38 not_fired_at_this_sha`. Proven at `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`, receipts being the real stdout of the real runs committed under `gates/` and `mergeability/`: | gate | verdict | |---|---| | `pnpm tsgo:core` | **pass** rc=0 | | `pnpm lint` — oxlint core, extensions, scripts | **pass** rc=0 | | Gate 2.7 vs the absorbed base `715077a3be` | **pass** — 839 files, 466 GENUINE, 373 SAFE-NEW, **0 FROZEN-STALE**, **0 MIXED-CLOBBER** | | `vitest` rollback-custody regressions | **pass** 10/10 | | `vitest` delivery-queue + session-delivery | **pass** 124/124 | | `vitest` gateway maintenance + close + delegate-artifacts | **pass** 123/123 | | `vitest` production-boundary + spawn-cleanup | 28/30 — two tracked reds | **Diff size has not grown across four absorbs.** From the absorbed base — which is what this PR shows — the change is 839 files, +140,919 / −4,301, against 841 / +140,951 / −4,277 before this cycle. (`git diff upstream/main HEAD` reports 2,358 files, but that is the symmetric difference including upstream commits newer than the merge base, and is not what a PR shows.) The worktree was clean at publication: zero untracked files, no stray additions. **Two known reds, neither hidden nor softened.** `karmaterminal/openclaw#1356` is an order-dependent failure of the `operator-revoked` queued-collector cleanup: it **passes in isolation** with all four `cleanupComplete` operands true and the child session genuinely deleted, and fails only when the `operator-completed` arm has run first. Upstream's own test and test-support files for it are byte-identical to ours, so the divergence is product-side. `karmaterminal/openclaw#1350` is the streamed-text offset/fencing contract, pre-existing. **No live behavioral row was fired at this SHA, and none is presented as though it were.** The fleet that runs these behaviors serves composite `1baff536afa549fea75660403c453bbd265352c0`, a *divergent sibling* of the presented SHA rather than an ancestor of it — their merge-base is `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and neither is an ancestor of the other. A live fire on that runtime would be evidence about the composite, so every row is marked `not_fired_at_this_sha` instead of being carried over as a pass. The prior corpus at `3821eaef72` remains linked per row as the baseline to re-fire against. Live rows are unblocked by a redeploy onto a runtime that has this SHA as a git ancestor. That redeploy is itself a migration boundary: this head carries the agent schema bump **21 → 22** via `migrateTranscriptFtsRowSchema`, and the fleet serves 21, so it wants migration-success and rollback-compatibility receipts of its own. Both are maintainer-side, not gated on this PR. ### PROOFS METHOD The corpus uses a Grafana k6 proof harness for live rows; [`METHOD.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) carries the exact reproducer commands for every static gate above, including both Gate 2.7 invocations and the `git merge-tree --write-tree` mergeability check. `MAX_WORKERS=1` is mandatory for the vitest reproducers — OpenClaw's fixtures are not safe under concurrent access — and two of those commands deliberately take no `--config`, because passing the wrong one silently reports "No test files found" and exits 0. `TRANSPOSED-FROM.md` records source-to-target ancestry and materiality; for this cycle it records a deliberate refusal to transpose across 520 commits and four absorbs. ## Future actions and #130741 composition Maintainer PR #130741 addresses the complementary fresh-sweep race: it captures the current `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision` before the first await and uses those values as cleanup CAS facts. The return covenant addresses a different time axis: whether historically accepted child work may return to a logical recipient after benign successor creation. The current candidate and #130741 head `e1afc703f49a07687c0876ba6350cafa87a3638a` merge cleanly in a synthetic composition. If #130741 lands, the composed result should preserve both guarantees: - keep #130741's fresh sweep-time exact-run/session lifecycle fence; - keep the covenant's durable logical-recipient generation for historical return admission and delivery; - do not overload broad `lifecycleRevision` as historical return authority; - do not terminate or orphan accepted descendants merely because `/new` or ordinary `/reset` creates a successor session. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially TaskFlow plus host Cron / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A TaskFlow tool adapter is also not a lifecycle host. It can call the core-owned `api.runtime.tasks.managedFlows` API to create, link, pause, resume, finish, cancel, and inspect durable flow records. Marking a waiting record as running does not reacquire a session lane or invoke the model; recording a `childSessionKey` created by a separate spawn surface does not spawn the child or deliver its return. There is no equivalent host continuation capability for this PR to wrap. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. It preserves that PR's review lineage and the earlier continuation work descended from #79925, but it does not reuse either closed PR or ask reviewers to infer the current result from them. The replacement carries a current, independently reviewable branch and a complete proof subtree bound to its presented SHA. #85651 was not abandoned because the feature failed or because we accepted its classification as a skill. It was closed after automated labeling put the change in the wrong submission category. This replacement removes that ambiguity: no `src/skills/**` change is presented, current label simulation produces no `r: skill`, and the detailed section above explains why the lifecycle mechanism belongs to core. Acceptance or rejection of the product direction remains OpenClaw's decision. The decision requested is whether OpenClaw should provide multi-session, agent-elected continuation primitives after reviewing the implementation and evidence. It is not whether the same mechanism can be relocated into a skill: a skill cannot own or implement these lifecycle boundaries.

prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: the New session project picker promises Git URL input but shows no selectable result and ignores Enter for guests who can create sessions without general operator write access. ## User Impact User impact: session writers can select a pasted repository URL by clicking its result or pressing Enter. Read-only users and connections without the advertised creation method remain unable to select it. Gateway permissions, repository validation, and submission restrictions are unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made Use the existing scoped `sessions.create` access decision for draft repository selection instead of requiring `projects.add` or general write access. Project registration and empty local-session submission still use their existing authorization checks. No permissions, configuration, or system settings are changed. Reported by @gideonpraise. ## Evidence - Original guest click/Enter regressions failed before the fix. - On base `885623b9ce68e3e5b1596b3424bcf9548733d790`: 32 tests across the picker, project-chip, and submission-gate suites passed; wrapper wall time 2.68 seconds. The new four-case regression includes read-only and unadvertised-method rejection. CI timing is not yet available. - UI typecheck, targeted formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Targeted lint: zero errors, two unchanged `liveValue` reactivity warnings outside the changed code. - Independent P0–P2 review with the configured reviewer: no actionable findings. It assessed the patch and source context; browser execution was performed separately. - Smallest-fix pass: reuse the existing session-access owner; no new policy or state. Production LOC is unchanged; the existing fixture supports a new 58-line regression test. ### Browser interaction proof Pinned Chromium 156.0.8078.4 exercised the production-built New session page with a synthetic mock Gateway, against the original base and the unchanged published patch (`b7860cea7c5d2057fb0f80a84a402eb418c8d152`). - Before: reproduced the missing clone option and inert Enter for a session-only guest. - After: guest HTTPS click and guest SCP Enter both selected the repository and submitted `sessions.create` with the exact URL, without any `projects.add` call. - Read-only and unadvertised-creation cases remained blocked; an empty local-session submission remained disabled. - All five browser scenarios passed (one before, four after). Each side rebuilt independently; wrapper wall times were 13.297s and 14.231s. - Inspected before/after screenshots were delivered in the originating session. Browser runtime libraries were unpacked only into task-local storage; no system settings or permissions changed. - The temporary browser fixture was removed from the patch. Remote source remains exactly two files. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Pasted Git URL has no selectable result for a session\-writing guest](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7595a0bb-e03d-4fd6-bcfd-489ce2dcd124) | ![The same guest sees a selectable repository URL row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/841eea5b-768e-4b3a-9e9e-0231e86b77b0) | ### Click the HTTPS result, then press Enter for the SCP URL https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/032c0383-e390-4cd9-a33c-372fe8b570d6 ### Visual verification - Baseline: 885623b9ce68e3e5b1596b3424bcf9548733d790 - Exact head: `b7860cea7c5d2057fb0f80a84a402eb418c8d152` - Scenario: A guest pastes a repository URL into the New session project picker, selects the HTTPS result by click, and selects an SCP URL with Enter\. - Runtime/build: Production\-built OpenClaw Control UI at b7860cea7c5d2057fb0f80a84a402eb418c8d152; synthetic mock Gateway; Chromium 156\.0\.8078\.4, device scale 1\. - Before: Missing repository result; Enter cannot select it\. - After: HTTPS click and SCP Enter select and submit the exact repository URL\. - Authority: Existing sessions\.create route; no projects\.add call\. Read\-only and unavailable\-method controls remain blocked\. - Five browser scenarios passed through the production\-built New session page in the owning remote environment\. - The two\-file patch is unchanged; 32 focused tests, UI types, formatting and independent review remain valid\. - Before reproduces the missing option and inert Enter\. Fixed click and Enter submit the exact URL through sessions\.create; no projects\.add call occurs\. - Read\-only and unavailable\-method controls remain blocked\. - The 6\.72\-second recording shows selection only; submission and denied cases are covered by the browser assertions\. - Original capture retained\. The MP4 adds factual action labels without cuts, speed changes, source edits or new product execution\. ## Worked on by - @gideonpraise --- [View the OpenClaw team session](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/fffda003-f8e1-4575-8a8d-4e879f27d51d)

prs.title: fix: dashboard reports success when link preparation fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw dashboard --no-open` reports success to shell callers when a stopped Gateway prevents it from producing a Dashboard URL. Readiness, listener-verification, and pairing-link failures can return the same misleading status.

## User Impact

Scripts now receive exit status 1 when Dashboard preparation fails. Explicitly declining the interactive recovery prompt still cancels without an error. This intentionally changes failed noninteractive invocations from exit 0 to exit 1; browser or clipboard fallback after a URL is issued keeps its existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The text command has early failure returns that omit the nonzero status already used by JSON output, invalid configuration, and unavailable UI documents. Readiness now records whether recovery was actually declined so a noninteractive failure is not mistaken for a user cancellation.

## Evidence

The actual official CLI was checked on macOS with a qualified Node **24.19.0** / pnpm **12.11.1** toolchain, this worktree's frozen native dependencies, and the normal registered `cliStartup` build. The source launcher retained its normal runtime preparation: it reconciled static assets through 14 postbuild phases and staged the repository's pinned Bun fork. No startup or publication guard was bypassed.

With isolated HOME/config/state/profile/service label, a claimed unused loopback port, closed stdin, and no `--yes`:

```text
$ pnpm openclaw --profile <isolated> dashboard --no-open
Gateway is not running.
Run `openclaw gateway status --deep` for details.
Use the owning environment or supervisor to start or repair the selected Gateway.
exit_code=1 signal=none
```

No Dashboard URL was emitted. No Gateway was started: the port remained refused and the task-owned service plist remained absent before and after. The task config and source stayed unchanged. The native proof completed successfully, and its strict supervisor accepted the result after all **83 retained actors** joined and the official compiler stop left zero tracked workers. The CLI's exit 1 is the expected failure status under test; it is distinct from the native proof's exit 0.

The two affected test files passed through their unique owners: dashboard **9/9** with no skips (25.45 s Vitest wall time), readiness **7/7** with no skips (831 ms). This includes noninteractive failure, explicit user refusal, and both installed-service recovery controls. Four-file formatting, the official type-aware lint wrapper, and strict affected TypeScript checking also passed; the strict configuration covers four changed roots plus 14 existing ambient/generated declaration roots. The normal `cliStartup` build passed separately before the real command.

Validation limitations: the real CLI proof covers the stopped-Gateway path; other failure and explicit-refusal controls are covered by the focused tests. No live browser-pairing flow, remote Gateway, Linux/Windows service manager, full repository typecheck, or full test suite was run. The earlier Node 24.20.0 CLI proof is historical evidence, not the qualification reported above.
