prs.title: fix(agents): describe sessions_spawn agentId allowed targets in the tool description
prs.body:
Fixes #149550

## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_spawn` never said which `agentId` targets are allowed, so models only learned by being rejected.

## User Impact

User impact: the tool description lists the targets the spawn path accepts, for native subagents and ACP. Text only. Lists are capped at 20 ids, so a large roster cannot bloat every turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

The text is built from the real admission rules: ACP ids go through the ACP resolver and `acp.allowedAgents`, and `requireAgentId` is honored. Callers pass the requester's already-resolved subagent status, so building the tool reads no session store. One helper resolves `allowAgents` and `requireAgentId` for all four callers.

Native and ACP lists share one renderer (`describeTargetIdList`, built on `summarizeStringEntries`). It lists the first 20 sorted ids, then `(+N). Only the first 20 ids are listed.` Agent ids are at most 64 chars, so the count cap also bounds bytes (about 1.4 KB per list). The overflow text does not assume `agents_list` exists.

It lives in the tool description, not the `agentId` schema property. Codex drops every schema description once a tool schema passes 5,000 bytes (first pass of `compact_large_tool_schema`), and `sessions_spawn` is already at 5,045 on `main`. The schema is unchanged; the tool description is kept.

Tests: the metadata-only suite that imported the full spawn runtime is deleted. Policy and cap cases live in the target-policy and ACP target tests. One registration assertion and the prepared-requester regression (never a store read) sit in the existing `sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts`.

## Evidence

Shipped entry point: `pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent main --message hi` against an isolated state dir and a local OpenAI-compatible mock that records the model request. Agents `main` and `planner`, `tools.toolSearch: false`. `sessions_spawn.description` in the captured request:

| Config | `main` (base) | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No allowlist | no `agentId` text | `` `agentId` targets: Only the requester agent is allowed as a target; no other agentId is configured. Omit to keep the requester agent ("main"). `` |
| `agents.entries.main.subagents.allowAgents: ["planner"]` | no `agentId` text | `` `agentId` targets: Configured agent to target: planner. Omit to keep the requester agent ("main"). `` |

The schema `agentId` stays `{"type":"string"}` in both.

ACP, through the Gateway with a backend enabled: an isolated `pnpm openclaw gateway run` (own state dir, loopback port) with `acp.enabled`, `acp.backend: "acpx"`, `acp.defaultAgent: "codex"`, `acp.allowedAgents: ["codex","claude"]`, agents `main` and `planner`, and `main.subagents.allowAgents: ["planner"]`. The Gateway logs `embedded acpx runtime backend registered lazily`. `pnpm openclaw agent --agent main --message hi` then sent this `sessions_spawn.description` fragment (head `02c4032`) to the local OpenAI-compatible mock (full text, nothing truncated, no secrets):

```
`agentId` targets: With runtime="subagent" (default): Configured agent to target: planner. Omit to keep the requester agent ("main"). With runtime="acp": ACP harness id from: claude, codex. Omit to use the configured ACP default ("codex").
```

The captured `agentId` schema is still `{"type":"string"}`.

Real output, config with `main`, `planner`, `acp.defaultAgent: codex`:

```
description: `agentId` targets a configured agent; ... `sandbox` inherit|require. `agentId` targets: With runtime="subagent" (default): Only the requester agent is allowed as a target; no other agentId is configured. Omit to keep the requester agent ("main"). With runtime="acp": ACP harness id, for exam...
schema agentId: {"type":"string"}
acp agentId=codex:     accepted
acp agentId=main:      rejected: agentId "main" is an OpenClaw config agent, not an ACP harness
acp agentId=(omitted): accepted
requireAgentId=true:   ... agentId is required; the requester agent is "main".
```

Codex fixture, `sessions_spawn`: schema 5,045 bytes on both `main` and this branch (byte-identical); tool description 2,805 to 2,884. Checked against `openai/codex` at `064c6b8c`, `codex-rs/tools/src/json_schema/compaction.rs`. A local Codex checkout was not available, and Codex's own normalized byte count was not measured.

The existing `agents_list` rewrite of `configured agent;` still applies (`agent-tools.deferred-followup-guidance.test.ts`).

Cap regressions: exactly 20 ids has no overflow text, 21 ids does, and 5,000 allowed ids render under 1,000 chars (native); 25 ACP ids are capped for both the allowlist and example forms.

Main merged; prompt snapshots regenerated with `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen`. Focused tests, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, `tsgo:core`, changed `tsgo:core:test` graphs and `prompt:snapshots:check` pass.

prs.body:
Related: [#171524](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171524). This is its canonical shared CI repair; the worker feature remains unmerged.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes message reordering when a deferred message's retry is still being persisted, and repairs the CI fixtures that failed alongside it.

## User Impact

Retried messages stay ahead of later messages in the same lane. No configuration, migration, or user action is needed; the remaining changes affect test fixtures only.

## Why This Change Was Made

A failed deferral retains its lane while its release is settling or has failed without giving up custody. Ordinary released album/forward deferrals still admit later members. The fixtures now respect async retirement, the Node-only launcher contract, explicit catalog invalidation, real HTTP sockets under fake time, and byte-exact comparison of oversized pages.

## Evidence

- Original failed CI: [run 39077683748](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39077683748). Untouched controls reproduce the launcher, OpenAI reservation, and Telegram ordering failures. The new core regression also fails before the fix, including the unknown-outcome custody control.
- **109/109 focused cases in 8 files passed**, covering the real ingress queue, both affected source E2Es, and all repaired fixtures. Core, all 29 core-test graphs, extension-test types, targeted typed lint, and formatting pass. Fresh independent Codex **P0–P2 review is clean**.
- The original six-file Linux memory envelope reproduced 94 passing events followed by the unchanged 300s watchdog. A persisted discriminator proves pruning/read/native byte comparison complete before deep Buffer matching spins. The one-line byte-exact fix passes **104/104 cases in 6 files**; the former stalled 17 MiB case takes 307 ms. No input-size or timeout reduction.
- Signed head `161a313d0c12` is a patch-identical replay of the reviewed seven-file tree onto main `885623b9ce68`; all changed-file bytes and reviewed owning context are unchanged. Exact-head [CI39084888904](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39084888904) **passed** (52 jobs passed,26 skipped). The reviewed head landed as [`5b64c3d0`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5b64c3d0ff539ab44a9bec2b769509e3a135c030).

<details>
<summary>Qualification limits and local-check exceptions</summary>

The source E2Es own their fixtures and use the maintained skip-build path; this is not packaged-runtime or live-Gateway proof. Linux reproduction used Node 24.19 and the repository-pinned Bun on a 2 CPU/8 GiB amd64 container under Rosetta, not native x64; the initial Node compile cache was cold. The preceding Codex procfs plan had three extra assertion failures absent from original CI, so the entire three-plan replay is not claimed green.

The full local staged-check run is **not passing**: unchanged global UI max-lines suppressions, 729/741-root shard limits, and unrelated whole-tree unused-export findings remain on main. Size limits are intentionally strict locally and warning-only in genuine GitHub Actions. No limits, baselines, or checks were weakened. Exact-head CI remains required.

GitHub rejected the emergency direct-main push with GH013 (changes must use a PR), so this PR is the canonical repair path. Native merge verification also reported mainline drift in `scripts/lib/ci-proof-test-inventory.mts`; repository policy treated it as a warning and verified landing of the exact reviewed head. The worker PR receives a fresh integrated CI run.

</details>

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Voice-call polling carries a redundant internal Result envelope, and webhook processing logs the same rejected event at two nested owners.

## User Impact

No user-facing feature or protocol change. Pending/completed/failed polling payloads, consumed-ID errors, signed callback/replay behavior, and visible webhook HTTP500 failures remain.

## Why This Change Was Made

Return the private stored operation or undefined directly; its sole consumer already owns the exact INVALID_REQUEST/operation not found response. The store replaces entries instead of mutating returned objects, so its shallow copy is unnecessary. Let event rejection reach the existing HTTP error/log owner instead of logging and rethrowing internally.

Twelve net production lines removed (+7/-19), 23 net test lines added. This is the voice-call area of the existing wide family, not a new large-family or duplicate credit. Extend existing registered polling and signed Plivo failure tests rather than adding another fixture or test seam. Public manager Results, partial call receipts, shared operation identities and ordinary shutdown settlement remain untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Remove only the private shallow copy: pending entries are replaced on completion, terminal entries are removed before return, and the sole adapter only encodes the returned value. Nested results were already shared. No public copy/identity guarantee changes. Polling was introduced by #75459 to retain long-running results and proper protocol error frames; that real behavior is kept, not treated as slop.
- Duplicate event-specific logging disappears; processing failures still reach the existing HTTP logger and return500 so the carrier can retry. Original #118754 established signed callback/durable replay behavior and disclosed synthetic cryptographic/SQLite proof, not a human incident requiring two logs. All its security, persistence, replay ownership and retry contracts remain.

## Evidence

- Complete private operation owner/test and determining adapter, command error, HTTP server/logger, signed Plivo failure/replay and realtime callback closure inspected. Eight determining files unchanged from branch base through fresh fetched main after the two preceding landings. No new imports/cycles, helper, SDK export, config/schema/protocol/dependency or state changes. Simplification/test-audit keeps existing strong boundaries: consumed IDs retain exact protocol framing; signed processing failure remains visible through HTTP500 and the outer logger.
- Five-file formatting and whitespace passed; supported syntax-only lint using the actual root configuration passed. Targeted five-root types completed with36 dependency diagnostics byte-identical to the prior recorded baseline, none in changed files; NOT local type PASS. Full extension type-aware lint requires generated package preparation outside this host budget and is left to exact-head hosted CI.
- Mandatory suppression guard passed14/14 (55.98s Vitest/79.40s wrapper). Full independent five-file/eight-dataset review completed scoped-clean P0-P2/0.99, including final source verification; no subsequent source change.

Prior supported focused cold startup hit prohibited broad worker compilation before assertions; no equivalent retry, bootstrap bypass, added skip/retry, timeout increase or suppression. Exact-head hosted CI is the runtime/broad gate.
- Phase E standalone session-memory backend/factory/registry/expiry/federation/tests untouched.

Release-note context: consolidate internal voice-call error handling without changing asynchronous polling or carrier callback outcomes.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Client private identities, token caches and native socket credentials move to `<resolved-client-root>/client/credentials.sqlite`, independently versioned at **local schema 1**. Swift and TypeScript cut over together, including Gateway startup's pre-readiness CLI pairing. Native credential bootstrap no longer opens the selected Gateway database. Approval policy remains shared with unchanged semantics and effect-time authority.

This implements Peter's **R0 approval of 2026-10-14**, following #174294 (PR1a) and #174360 (R14b). It replaces #174485, which ClawSweeper closed after roughly 49,000 frozen predecessor lines pushed the diff over 50,000 changed lines. Those copies are removed; this diff has **28,736 changed lines**, using delta SQL, compact predecessor metadata and regenerated current artifacts.

**Published READY and mergeable at `1cd5e4629c46f455b86f2656365ce146abf1a9e9`, auto-merge off.** [Exact-head CI run 39083829461](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39083829461) is terminal: **184 success / 5 failure / 16 skipped**. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards, all seven typecheck jobs, all six TypeScript lint jobs and all Periphery scans passed. **GitHub CI remains red**: three test failures have qualified manual inherited classifications, one screenshot job lacks a Watch runtime, and the aggregate gate fails. Automated main comparison remains unknown. No merge was performed.

The final correction removes two UI-test imports made obsolete by main's helper refactor; the file now matches main exactly and leaves the PR diff. All eight affected local commands pass, including the full 27-case file and owning type graph; its scoped review is clean. Actual local proof used 333d source plus the exact committed patch, with no product-dist use or restamp. Earlier runtime/PG/native proof retains its execution heads and bounded applicability. **signed real-Mac proof pending (landing gate)**.

## Ownership and recovery

The running app serves bounded authenticated operations; app-absent clients acquire exclusive local custody. A definite pre-send connection refusal or authenticated response that the app does not own the root permits offline custody. Uncertain or post-dispatch failures are never replayed offline. There is one store, without timestamp reconciliation or permanent dual ownership.

Canonical migration runs under updater/Doctor custody: capture → copy exact rows → verify → publish copied receipt → retire shared credentials → complete after shared commit. `destinationVersion` means **local schema 1**, independently of **shared cutover 28**. Receipts bind source identity/generation and content hash. Stale contents rebuild from authoritative shared state, never merge; exact identity/key/token bytes and socket material survive.

Independent native sources stay byte-identical and read-only: no chmod, checkpoint, marker, private backup, retirement or JSON unlink. Unchanged sources preserve local tokens and consumed-import claims; changed/restored sources trigger a bounded rebuild. Revoked credentials cannot reimport from retained JSON. Old native clients refuse retired canonical layouts and accept untouched independent sources.

| R14b need | Resolution |
| --- | --- |
| Captured SQLite authorization | Reuse updater custody. Standalone Doctor takes a fresh same-custody backup and verifies row hashes. Exact scope: `[device_identities, device_auth_tokens, gateway_origin_device_tokens, exec_approvals_config]`, plus `sqlite_stat1`/`sqlite_stat4` for retired indexes. Older backups never authorize retirement. |
| Local-companion attribution | Narrow extension through R14b's existing capture coordinator; generations stay in backup owners. No parallel journal/borrow registry. |
| Native-v0→PG publication | Removed. Refuse with recovery: start Gateway once on SQLite, run `openclaw doctor --fix`, then port. Normal PG extraction verifies before retiring server rows. |

Ordinary archives retain capture-time canonical source identity separately from lexical extraction paths. Restoring an aliased source works after the original paths disappear, without weakening receipt matching or changing the archive format version.

## Update behavior

PR1a enables no production local reader/writer, so the store does not exist before first cutover. Published SQLite drivers capture the shared database while it still contains credentials. Rollback restores shared tables/socket policy; old versions ignore the orphaned local store. **Credentials issued between upgrade and rollback are lost; affected clients re-pair.** Restored identity/generation/hash triggers rebuilding credential rows while preserving consumed-import claims; credentials are never merged.

PG-state installations begin with PR1a/R14b-capable drivers supporting shared families/local companions. Independent native sources remain usable by old readers. Orphaned WAL/SHM/journal files without their shared database cause recovery refusal instead of fresh-store initialization.

prs.title: fix(setup): keep first-run model metadata from restricting the picker
prs.body:
Fixes #175533.

## What Problem This Solves

First-run provider setup can restrict the model picker to the selected model when the provider adds an alias before setup saves its runtime choice.

## User Impact

Fresh setup keeps other available models selectable. Existing legacy restrictions still allow the approved model without admitting unrelated provider metadata. Previously saved explicit policies remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Setup now migrates legacy restrictions from the configuration that existed before provider setup, extending that prior model map only with the approved selection. This prevents newly added aliases from becoming an allowlist.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the first-run restriction through the production setup selection and model visibility owners: the new regression failed before the fix.
- After rebasing onto main `7f6a90441a21da9d68edcf672b1cc271e79f01f7`: focused model selection suite 16 passed; config metadata suite 10 passed.
- Regression coverage preserves legacy restrictions and source immutability, retains the selected model and alias, and rejects unrelated provider metadata.
- Scoped oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and the canonical services and UI-chat test TypeScript projects passed. These are focused checks; the full repository suite was not run locally.
- Independent P0–P3 review: no actionable findings. The canonical autoreview helper was unavailable under the workspace's chat-launch governance; this was a narrative review without helper isolation or machine-status guarantees.
- AI-assisted implementation and tests; the source path and resulting policy behavior were reviewed.
- Native macOS DMG onboarding was not exercised. Hosted CI passed all 36 selected jobs on the rebased head: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39083660258. This change prevents new accidental restrictions; it does not rewrite existing explicit policies.

## Shipped behavior and upgrade evidence

Follow-up on the behavior/upgrade proof requested above, using candidate `a656307519ac918edae6a008bc4bbacd9dc85c95`. These runs were performed by the coding agent assisting this PR.

**Scope and provider disclosure.** This is Linux integration evidence through the built `openclaw.mjs` CLI and shipped Gateway RPCs. It uses the built-in `openai` provider, its supported `OPENAI_BASE_URL` setting, a loopback OpenAI Responses HTTP fixture, and a dummy key. The actual provider activation performed and parsed a streamed `/v1/responses` request; production code was not patched, mocked, or told to skip verification. The fixture supplies simulated responses, so this does not establish real-account credentials, model entitlement, or external inference. All state/workspace/cache paths were isolated, the real OS home was masked, and the process network namespace had no outbound network. IPs, endpoints, dummy keys, and local paths are redacted below.

**Fresh setup: stable fails, candidate passes after restart.** The published `openclaw@2026.10.4` npm artifact identifies commit `383c124cc32ffee3f8e56f549b88da94d269a4af`; its archive matched the registry SHA-512 integrity. The candidate was built with the canonical `pnpm build` command, which passed. Both versions were exercised through:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs gateway run --allow-unconfigured --bind loopback \
  --port "$TEST_PORT" --token "$TEST_GATEWAY_TOKEN"
node openclaw.mjs gateway call openclaw.setup.activate \
  --url "$GATEWAY_URL" --token "$TEST_GATEWAY_TOKEN" --json \
  --params '{"kind":"api-key","authChoice":"openai-api-key","apiKey":"<dummy key>","modelRef":"openai/gpt-6-astra","workspace":"<isolated workspace>","nativeSessionCatalogsEnabled":false}'
```

The response on both was `{"ok":true,"modelRef":"openai/gpt-6-astra",...}` with `Inference verified: openai/gpt-6-astra`. The fixture recorded `POST /v1/responses`, model `gpt-6-astra`, `stream:true`.

| Observation | Published 2026.10.4 | Candidate, after clean Gateway restart |
|---|---|---|
| Saved `models["openai/gpt-6-astra"]` | GPT alias + OpenClaw runtime | Same metadata |
| Saved `modelPolicy.allow` | `["openai/gpt-6-astra"]` | No `modelPolicy` created |
| `models.list` visibility | Astra only | Astra and Mini both `available:true` |
| `sessions.create` with Astra | Success | Success |
| `sessions.create` with Mini | `INVALID_REQUEST: model not allowed: openai/gpt-5.4-mini` | Success, resolved `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` |

The candidate was stopped cleanly after activation and restarted from the saved config before these selection checks. The saved migration marker remained set, and startup did not materialize a restriction from the GPT alias. `models.list` exposed 15 entries from the configured OpenAI catalog; this is the application's availability classification, not verified external account entitlement. The two selection calls used distinct session keys and returned `runStarted:false`.

Commands for those observations:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs gateway call models.list --url "$GATEWAY_URL" \
  --token "$TEST_GATEWAY_TOKEN" --json \
  --params '{"provider":"openai","includeDetails":true}'
node openclaw.mjs gateway call sessions.create --url "$GATEWAY_URL" \
  --token "$TEST_GATEWAY_TOKEN" --json \
  --params '{"key":"agent:main:proof-gpt-5.4-mini","label":"Proof gpt-5.4-mini","model":"openai/gpt-5.4-mini","agentRuntime":"openclaw"}'
```

**Stable-to-candidate saved-state check.** Using the published stable CLI, I authored `modelPolicy.allow=["openai/gpt-6-astra","openai/gpt-6-luna"]`, `userTimezone=UTC`, and `ui.seamColor=#336699`. Stable Gateway RPCs created a session, wrote a synthetic `MEMORY.md` through `agents.files.set`, and saved a synthetic conversation entry through `chat.inject`. After stopping stable and freezing the checkpoint, I switched to the candidate executable against the same state/workspace and ran:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs doctor --fix --non-interactive --full-integrity-check
# exit 0; reported agent database migration v24 -> v31
node openclaw.mjs gateway run --allow-unconfigured --bind loopback \
  --port "$TEST_PORT" --token "$TEST_GATEWAY_TOKEN"
# Then gateway call: agents.files.get, chat.history, sessions.list, models.list
# And CLI: config get agents.defaults --json; config get ui --json
```

Observed results:

- The original session ID, label, saved message ID, and message content loaded through the candidate's normal RPCs.
- `MEMORY.md` was identical, SHA-256 before and after: `0818fae5078e490ed9405c8b002b08d1d5f6899f41110a67d88feed2fabe9582`.
- Default model/auth-profile reference, GPT alias/runtime, workspace, timezone, UI color, and the explicit two-model allowlist were unchanged. The full config bytes changed because doctor added current agent/skills/wizard metadata; this is not a claim of an unchanged config hash.
- Selecting Mini still returned `INVALID_REQUEST: model not allowed: openai/gpt-5.4-mini`, so upgrade did not silently broaden the authored restriction.

Limitations: this was a manual stable-to-candidate executable transition, not the `openclaw update` package-install transaction or macOS DMG/UI interaction. It is a focused synthetic-data compatibility sample. Doctor exited 0 but emitted diagnostics about unavailable original-state capture, an open-store NOCOW repair, and model-specific tool-schema inspection of the auth-qualified default; I am not claiming a warning-free doctor run. Actual session/history/workspace reads and the policy checks above passed.

An initial upgrade attempt migrated the DB but failed when an overly long test TMPDIR caused the socket owner to fall back to read-only temporary storage. Its explicit Astra/gpt-4.1 policy remained unchanged at that point; gpt-4.1 was not available in the observed current catalog, and successful use of that model was not proven. The final control used a shorter isolated TMPDIR and a common stable/current model pair. An exploratory rerun with overlapping harness setup was discarded; the final stable-write/checkpoint/candidate sequence was serialized. No source changes were needed for these proof runs.

prs.title: fix(backup): older archives with hardlinks cannot be verified or restored
prs.body:
Related: #89257

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: verification and restore reject older backups whose hardlinks retain a working-directory-relative target.

## User Impact

Users can recover complete legacy backups containing hardlinked files. Ambiguous or missing recovery targets remain rejected. This addresses the verification/restore compatibility failure reported in #89257; the historical writer exit-code-13 failure and truncated archives are outside this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Older archives can name a member under the archive payload while its hardlink target remains `.openclaw/state/a.bin`. If the existing qualified/root-relative lookup misses, resolve an exact regular-file match along that member's ancestors and reject multiple matches. Restore consumes the same verified target map.

Thanks to @hoobnn for the earlier reproduction and proposed verifier repair in #89345.

## Evidence

Verified the synchronized candidate `ed44748b799a` on macOS with Node 24.19.0, pnpm 12.11.1 and Python 3.14.6. A real `os.link` source pair was archived in schema-v1 USTAR format, explicitly retaining the reported historical hardlink target `.openclaw/state/a.bin`. The official CLI verified and restored the same unchanged archive into a fresh isolated target:

```sh
pnpm --silent openclaw --profile <isolated> backup verify <legacy-archive> --json
pnpm --silent openclaw --profile <isolated> backup restore <legacy-archive> --target <fresh-target> --json
```

Both commands exited naturally with status 0 and each complete stdout response parsed as standalone JSON with `ok: true`, one asset, three archive entries and no symlinks. After restore, both files contained the exact original 84 bytes (SHA-256 `dc3b91bbf7f6150bcae9bacdb42a1ba7e5085b2afbcaf59579e110cc4e059a8b`):

| Restored member | Bytes | Device | Inode | Link count |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `a.bin` | 84 | 16777231 | 201046552 | 2 |
| `b.bin` | 84 | 16777231 | 201046552 | 2 |

The archive stayed byte-identical. All CLI children, retained descendants and compiler processes exited before success was recorded; source, manifests and proof inputs were unchanged. No Gateway was started: this is the offline backup verification/extraction path.

The three affected command test files passed **57 tests**, with **one Windows-only test skipped** on macOS: “verifies a canonical global SQLite backup beyond MAX_PATH” (`process.platform === "win32"`). This includes all six legacy-hardlink regressions and the existing verification/restore suites. Scoped format, type-aware lint and strict type checking passed, and the normal registered `cliStartup` build completed. The reported Vitest duration was 30.94 seconds; process supervision and metadata collection took additional time.

Limitations: the original reporter archive and Linux host were unavailable. This proof recreates its archive encoding on macOS; it does not claim Linux/Windows execution or a repair of the historical writer exit-code-13 failure or truncated archives. The live fixture contains ordinary files, so its JSON reports `sqliteInventoryVerified: false`. No full repository test or type-check suite was run. Prior-head proof remains historical; the results above were captured for this synchronized candidate.

prs.title: fix: keep Code Mode work resumable after observer completion
prs.body:
Fixes #175937

## What Problem This Solves

A Code Mode cell can return `waiting` while a nested operation is still pending. Successful cleanup of the observing model response or dynamic tool call then cancels that cell, leaving its returned `runId` unavailable to the next `wait`. This interrupts ordinary sequential work even though the parent agent run remains live and earlier actions may already have completed.

## User Impact

Pending work remains resumable after the observer finishes successfully, so the next `wait` continues the same cell without replaying completed actions. Parent cancellation, cancellation during an active call, catalog disposal, snapshot expiry, and Gateway shutdown retain their existing cancellation behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared cell owner retained the completed observer's abort listener until the next call bound a replacement. Both the built-in streamed response and the Codex adapter normally abort their observer scopes during successful cleanup, exposing the same gap. Release that listener after the shared owner records a resumable result. The cell's parent signal and existing resource owners continue to govern its lifetime, so neither harness needs a new exception or API.

The existing repeated-resume regression now closes each observer immediately after its `waiting` result, before the next wait starts. Previously it closed the old observer only after a replacement had already been bound, missing the failing interval. The lifecycle documentation describes this ownership boundary.

## Evidence

Isolated source-level reproductions before the correction reached a pending file read after one completed write. The built-in streamed path cancelled it with `Model response closed`; the Codex dynamic path cancelled it with `OpenClaw dynamic tool call finished.` Their direct and non-streamed controls completed. The original tested revision was 69eefd48c800ed575b43949c451c004cc942373c; the affected contracts are unchanged at this PR's base f84d2ca6726ccab0ac72c7898bc09f358b62fa63.

Remote formatting and source lint passed. All nine related lifecycle test files passed 131 tests through `run_recipe openclaw-tests.sh` in 83.22 seconds; the agents-core shard containing the changed regression took 13.47 seconds. Production, plugin, script, and root-test compilation passed, as did 28 of 29 core test type groups. The remaining group reports two missing imports in an unchanged placement test; both errors were independently reproduced on baseline 195f85848cdf1d540e49df14f06b136a672bb87e, and #175942 owns their repair.

The focused batch covers repeated resumes, active cancellation, expiry, catalog disposal, Gateway shutdown, Node/QuickJS worker cleanup, and required work. Both original harness compositions now pass: four scenarios completed in 49.52 seconds, with a live read across observer cleanup, exact returned file contents, and exactly one write per scenario. These use synthetic model/backend inputs through the actual adapters, not a live provider or deployed service. Independent engineering review is clean. Hosted CI completed successfully on this head (6,388 aggregate executed-job seconds). ClawSweeper completed its exact-head review with Gold readiness, Platinum patch quality, and no findings. Its proof limit is the synthetic actual-adapter scenarios described above; no deployed-service verification is claimed.

## What Problem This Solves

Decision failure accounting repeats identity, secret-revision and retirement checks after the request owner has already classified interruptions. This private function updates only the captured advisory Health object, not effect authority.

Remove only the second fence around advisory failure counts. No security, credential, dispatch or lifecycle owner is removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Eight net production lines removed in one owner, no tests changed. This is the Decisions area of the prior wide cleanup family, split for bounded attribution; historic residue savings are not counted again. Both fail callsites follow the retained interrupted() classifier synchronously, without another await. A replaced Health remains separate; success accounting already writes its captured object without this fence.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Supported provider envelope getters can synchronously reenter lifecycle code between interruption classification and advisory failure accounting. If such a getter pauses the host, a returned failure or existing bounded cooldown can carry across reload rollback. This requires effectful returned-envelope access, not ordinary async replacement. It does not authorize dispatch or mutate a newer Health; half-open success or config/secret revision replacement recovers. Keep the executable-envelope single-read/privacy contract, every live authority check and actual work settlement.

prs.title: feat(openai): support saved GPT-Live voices
prs.body:
Closes #175909

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw cannot currently select an existing prompt-created GPT-Live voice because the provider does not translate OpenClaw's `speakerVoiceId` setting into the object-shaped reference required by OpenAI.

## User Impact

Operators can select a saved prompt-created voice with `speakerVoiceId: "voice_..."` and `gpt-live-1`. Named `speakerVoice` values keep their existing behavior, precedence, and defaults.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenAI realtime provider now validates `speakerVoiceId` and converts it to the provider-native `{ id: "voice_..." }` value only at the OpenAI session boundary. Malformed or model-incompatible references fail closed without echoing the supplied value, and browser reservation responses do not expose saved voice references.

## Evidence

- Direct provider validation: a saved prompt-created voice produced PCM16 audio, supported interruption, and an invalid reference failed closed.
- Focused OpenClaw session-shaping test: 7/7 passed under Node 24.16.0 and Vitest 5.0.3.
- Added routing coverage for `speakerVoiceId` normalization and config-to-broker propagation, plus broker coverage that browser responses omit custom references.
- `oxfmt` completed on all changed files; `git diff --check` passed before publication.
- Added a mocked HTTP integration test through real config normalization, broker reservation, offer handling, and public API serialization. It checks the saved voice reaches the API request and remains absent from the browser response.
- Independent review of the request-union repair and HTTP integration test found no actionable P1/P2 findings.
- Local rerun under Node 24.21.0 stopped before test collection because the shared dependency install lacks `@openclaw/proc-safe/windows-job`; the local assertion guard also lacks the pinned TypeScript AST module. Formatting passed. These startup failures are not test passes.
- PR CI owns production/test type checks, repository guards, and extension integration proof on the current head. Earlier red checks exposed an unsafe assertion, an overly narrow voice input type, and a non-distributive `Omit` that erased native-control request variants; the repair removes the assertion and preserves the request union at validation ingress.
- On `3a66dc68`, [CI run 39084389813](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39084389813) passed production/test type checks and repository guards. The config lane passed 652 tests, including the new HTTP integration test, and failed the existing `realtime-quicksilver-peer-worker.test.ts` RTP startup assertion (expected at least five packets, received zero); the routing lane passed 21/21. Those media implementation/test files are unchanged by this PR, but inherited failure or flakiness is not yet proven.
- An isolated Linux/Node 24.21.0 focused replay was stopped before test collection after more than eight minutes without test output, near its assigned memory cap. It provides no passing test evidence; the RTP failure still needs a bounded reproduction and, if reproducible, a matched-base comparison.
- Live proof limitation: the earlier direct-provider result does not establish an end-to-end OpenClaw audio session with the final `speakerVoiceId` configuration. That live journey remains unproven; no live provider calls were made during this repair.

## References and documentation

- [OpenAI custom voices guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/custom-voices): prompt-generated voices and the GPT-Live `session.audio.output.voice.id` contract.
- [OpenAI Live session API reference](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/live/methods/create): voice names and custom voice objects.
- [OpenClaw OpenAI voice and speech documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/providers/openai/voice-and-speech.md).
- [OpenClaw Talk documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/nodes/talk.md).
- [Existing OpenClaw `speakerVoiceId` schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/channels.ts): reuse the existing string ID setting at the configuration boundary.
- Related, complementary work: [PR #174084](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174084) expands named voices for `gpt-live-1-codex`; this PR supports saved voice IDs for public `gpt-live-1`.

prs.title: feat(tui): report run lifecycle through OSC 7501 program status
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Supporting terminals cannot show whether an OpenClaw TUI run is working or has finished.

## User Impact

Terminals supporting OSC 7501 receive working, done, error, and idle status, with the status cleared on exit. Switching sessions, interrupted recovery, or a still-pending submission does not falsely signal successful completion. Unsupported terminals receive only the existing support query.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use pi-tui’s existing program-status API and support detection. Successful completion comes from the existing run lifecycle owner rather than a display transition to idle; concurrent or pending work keeps the terminal working. The PTY evidence parser accepts only the exact new protocol records and continues rejecting unknown controls.

No new configuration, persistence, dependencies, blocked state, or message payload. No changes outside the TUI and its tests.

## Evidence

Current head: `ed791a025e86489ed97e0391cc15923577ef01e8`, rebased onto `b2299356fb9` from main. The rebase preserves the feature and both lifecycle repairs and incorporates the upstream SQLite lint fix ([#175796](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175796)).

- **Exact-head CI is green:** [run 39083734786](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39083734786) completed successfully, with no failed jobs. Both aggregate CI gates, dependency review, and security-sensitive review passed.
- **Real Gateway/model smoke passed on this exact head in AWS:** built OpenClaw Gateway and TUI, a real PTY, and three successful upstream model requests. Verified normal completion, switching sessions while the model is running without false completion, ignoring the retired session’s eventual completion, a successful new-session turn, and clean exit/status clearing.
- **Rebased focused checks:** 267 owner tests and all 3 program-status PTY tests passed.

Earlier repair validation (before this mechanical rebase):

- Red/green real-PTY regression: switching away during deterministically gated streaming failed on the original candidate (unexpected done), then passed after the repair. The retired session’s final is ignored, and a new-session turn completes normally.
- Red/green owner regressions: a terminal acknowledgment with other active/pending work, and completion while another submission awaits acknowledgment, fail before their guards and pass after them.
- Full non-PTY TUI suite: **1040 passed**. Final command/event/session-action checks: **261 passed**. Full real-PTY fixture lane: **106 passed, 1 intentionally skipped** (the opt-in live local-backend scenario); all 10 files passed. Added strict protocol allowlist tests passed separately.
- Composed final-before-ACK regression fails before the follow-up and passes afterward; successful, errored, and aborted accepted runs preserve their outcomes.
- Changed-file formatting and lint, core TypeScript, and the affected command/TUI test typecheck graph passed during repair validation. Current-head CI now also passes the previously failing SQLite lint job; no gate was waived.
- Independent P0–P3 autoreview of the repaired candidate completed with no actionable findings. [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175692#issuecomment-6237070124) of the pre-rebase repaired head (`62d0374`) also found no issues and confirmed the prior findings were repaired. Earlier findings were reproduced and repaired, not waived; the rebase did not add a new behavioral change.

The earlier regression suites use deterministic fixture backends; the new live smoke above does not. The live smoke uses a loopback auth-forwarding adapter to reach the protected real model endpoint without exposing its credential to the VM. It forwards unchanged request bodies and upstream response bytes; no model responses or Gateway behavior are mocked.

**Remaining validation limits:** the new live smoke enables OSC status with `PI_PROGRAM_STATUS=1` and checks the actual PTY byte stream. It does not test terminal support negotiation, a visible terminal indicator, or desktop notifications. The author-supplied Rex negotiation evidence below is historical evidence from the original candidate, not a fresh visual run of this repair.

<details>
<summary>Current-head live smoke observations</summary>

```text
normal real-model turn: idle → working → done
switch while real model runs: working → idle (no done)
retired real-model turn finishes: no extra status
new-session real-model turn: working → done
/exit: clear; process exit 0
upstream Responses requests: 3; HTTP 200: 3
```

The built Gateway’s conversation history independently confirmed real assistant replies. Smoke-owned processes were stopped and synthetic Gateway state removed after verification.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Author-supplied original terminal proof and limitations</summary>

Real PTY, TUI against the PTY fixture gateway, one full chat run, then `/exit`. The new e2e test's evidence lines:

```
[behavior-evidence] {"label":"a terminal with OSC 7501 support","sequences":["state=idle:app=openclaw","state=working:app=openclaw","state=done:app=openclaw","state=clear"],"terminal":"real PTY"}
[behavior-evidence] {"label":"a terminal that never answers the support query","sequences":["?"],"terminal":"real PTY"}
```

With reporting on, the run goes idle, working, done, and exit clears it. A terminal that never answers the query only ever sees the query.

**Live in a real OSC 7501 terminal (Rex beta, macOS):** a fresh clone of this branch on a Mac, running the same TUI PTY fixture script the e2e tests generate (real `runTui`, fake gateway backend), launched as a Rex terminal block **without** `PI_PROGRAM_STATUS`, so pi-tui's support query had to be answered by Rex itself. Input was sent with `rex send` (`program status probe`, then `/exit`) and the block's events were read with `rex events -s <session> --json`:

```
program_status_changed "idle"
program_status_changed "working"
program_status_changed "done"
program_status_removed {"ids": [""], "reason": "clear"}
child_exited {"exit_code": 0}
```

So Rex detected support, showed the run as working, marked it done when the reply landed, and dropped the record on exit. Before this change, a raw capture of the OpenClaw TUI during a full chat run contained no `7501;state=` records at all, so Rex had nothing to show.

### Limits of the original author-supplied proof

- No run against a real gateway and model: the Rex proof used the e2e fixture backend. A current-main build wants a newer state schema than the locally deployed gateway, so it was not pointed at live state.
- Rex's on-screen indicator and desktop notification were not visually checked (the Mac was locked); the proof is Rex's own block event stream.
- Other OSC 7501 terminals were not tried.

</details>

Fixes #165045 ## What Problem This Solves `ui/src/e2e/session-suggestions.e2e.test.ts` checked the typing-row avatar with `.chat-message-avatar-anchor > :is(.chat-avatar, .chat-avatar-slot)`. The `:is()` alternative also accepts the layout wrapper, so the assertion passes whenever a placeholder slot is present, even when no avatar is rendered for the sender. ## Why This Change Was Made The assertion now scopes to `.chat-message-avatar-anchor` and asks for the rendered sender avatar through its accessible name (`getByRole("img", { name: "Owner" })`), which a wrapper-only DOM cannot satisfy. The existing companion checks (`toBeVisible`, `toHaveCSS("position", "absolute")`) are unchanged, so this only tightens which element they apply to. No production code is touched; other `:is(.chat-avatar, .chat-avatar-slot)` uses in the suite are layout-measurement queries that intentionally accept either grid item. ## User Impact No user-visible change. Control UI coverage now fails when the typing avatar disappears while its wrapper stays behind, instead of passing silently. ## Evidence Local runs on this branch (Node 24.22.0) using the repository's own Playwright/Chromium Control UI harness. | Proof | Command | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | E2E spec, this branch | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/session-suggestions.e2e.test.ts` | 8/8 passed | | Mutation, current assertion | in `chat-typing-indicator.tsx`, `` replaced by `` | 2/2 **passed** — the current selector accepts the placeholder wrapper | | Mutation, this branch | same mutation, with this branch's assertion | 2/2 **failed** — `getByRole('img', { name: 'Owner' })` resolved to 0 elements | | Type check | `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-e2e.json` | passed | | Lint / format | `oxlint`, `oxfmt` on the changed file | clean | The mutated case renders this anchor — visible, but with no avatar for the sender: ```html
``` The passing case renders the sender avatar the assertion now addresses: ```html
…
O
``` The mutation was reverted before committing; the branch contains only the assertion change. ## AI Assistance This change was produced by an AI coding agent (Codex CLI) and reviewed by the human author. The model was asked to verify the reported weak assertion, reproduce it in the repository's own Chromium harness, and tighten it. The human author reviewed every line, ran the commands in the Evidence table, and confirms understanding of the selector semantics: `:is(.chat-avatar, .chat-avatar-slot)` accepts either the avatar or its wrapper, while `getByRole("img", { name })` only resolves a rendered avatar.

prs.title: feat(tasks): follow background task progress from the CLI
prs.body:
Closes #123488

## What Problem This Solves

Operators can inspect durable background tasks from the CLI, but they cannot stay attached to one task without repeatedly polling `tasks show`. Gateway logs are too broad for this job, and the Control UI does not cover every remote, headless, or shell-first workflow. As a result, operators can miss progress transitions and may not know whether execution finished while completion delivery is still pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds `openclaw tasks follow <lookup>` with human-readable and JSON Lines output. The viewer reuses the `tasks show` lookup contract, connects with `operator.read`, projects existing bounded task summaries and visible session history, filters the existing task event stream to one task, and replays durable state after event gaps or Gateway reconnects. Stable record identifiers suppress replay duplicates, execution and delivery remain separate, and Ctrl-C closes only the viewer.

The change is read-only. It adds no task or session persistence, protocol schema, cancellation, notification, delivery, or restart-recovery owner.

## User Impact

Operators can follow one subagent, ACP, cron, or CLI task from a terminal until both execution and completion delivery reach a terminal state. `--json` supports line-oriented consumers with bounded, redacted records and duplicate-safe identifiers. Existing `tasks show`, Control UI, task execution, and delivery behavior remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `e5c7ebd3143c014fdb0412043c71b10bf66737f5`, based on `6bd21a11222af41e7c758739c0e0cd2994dee445`.
- Focused CLI, command, and Gateway callsite-guard tests: 44/44 passed, covering human output, JSONL, bounded and redacted visible history, hidden reasoning and tool-result exclusion, `operator.read`, ordered updates, event gaps, duplicate suppression, reconnect, separate execution and delivery terminal behavior, Ctrl-C viewer-only behavior, lookup failure, and the production `GatewayClient` allowlist.
- `pnpm check:changed` passed all selected core, core-test, and docs lanes. Crabbox 0.41.6 matched the current stable release but had no ready remote provider, so the repository used its documented local fallback.
- `pnpm build` passed through the rebased CLI invocation, including CLI bootstrap imports, runtime post-build module loading, bundled plugin assets, and the Control UI build.
- Built CLI help exposes `openclaw tasks follow [options] <lookup>` and `--json` as JSON Lines.
- AutoReview loop 3 reviewed the exact rebased 37,028-byte bundle with `gpt-5.6-luna` at maximum thinking. TruffleHog passed and the review reported no accepted or actionable findings.
- The original `check-lint` failure had no lint finding. Every core shard completed, then the GitHub-hosted runner received a shutdown signal while linting extensions and exited 143. The new head retriggers that infrastructure-cancelled job.

### Live Gateway transcript

This proof used a loopback-only development Gateway and a dedicated temporary state root. It did not read or operate the normal Gateway. The controlled task had finished execution while delivery was still queued, so the viewer stayed attached. I stopped the isolated Gateway, completed delivery in the same SQLite-owned task row while it was down, and restarted it. The existing viewer emitted one disconnect marker, reconnected, replayed the durable terminal state, and exited 0. The task identifier below is redacted; the event order, timestamps, state, and exit status are unchanged.

```console
$ openclaw tasks follow proof-task --json

prs.title: refactor(browser): keep termination failures at one owner
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Best-effort browser cancellation suppresses the same termination failure at four nested layers. The private helper has one awaited caller, which already owns suppression before retiring its captured Playwright adapter.

## User Impact

Keep the existing termination recovery and disconnect behavior. Remove three inner discovery/command/socket catch shells; retain the one documented best-effort caller, detached detach observation, socket cleanup, budgets, endpoint policy, discovered-address pinning and current-connection checks immediately before effects. No browser feature, user-visible text or public signature changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Four net production lines removed (+15/-19), thirteen test lines added. This is the browser area of the existing wide preservation family, not a new large-family claim or duplicate credit. Add one existing-owner boundary case: failed discovery still resolves the exported disconnect operation, closes only its cached adapter and opens no socket. Existing authority-loss, SSRF and pinned-socket cases stay unchanged.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- No new failure tradeoff: discovery, handshake and termination-command failure still reach the same documented best-effort cancellation owner. The original #13498/424d2dddf580 contains a first-person actual-use slow-device failure report, so the actual termination/reconnect feature stays. Its same diff introduced the redundant inner catches alongside the outer owner; no separate incident requiring duplicate suppression was identified.
- Detached detach failure remains locally observed because it is deliberately not awaited and cannot reach the outer catch. Every security and connection-ownership check remains; no relaxed endpoint or execution policy.

## Evidence

- Complete changed actions owner and termination suite personally inspected, plus determining caller, socket, discovery, cache retirement and navigation frames. All eleven determining owners/callers/tests are unchanged between prior reviewed51128567 and freshfd3a2122. Exact production/test candidate blobs baaad07e/f5277374 match the completed full two-file independent review scoped-clean P0-P2/0.97 with final source verification; patch-identical input proof reused, no substantive post-review change. Simplification/test-audit pass keeps one cancellation outcome owner and independent real failure coverage. No new imports/cycles, helper, public SDK export, config/schema/protocol/dependency or state change.
- Current two-file formatting passed136ms, whitespace and supported syntax-only lint using the actual root rule configuration passed. Targeted two-root types completed with38 known missing parse5/split MCP declarations and associated diagnostics, none in the changed paths; NOT type PASS. Current suppression guard passed14/14 (161.59s Vitest/195.46s wrapper). Full extension type-aware lint requires generated package-boundary preparation; broad local compilation/build is outside this host's proof budget and is deferred to exact-head hosted CI, not claimed passing locally. The explicit focused syntax mode is documented by the canonical wrapper; no artifact-preparation skip environment or test/build bootstrap bypass was used.
- Prior actual baseline attempt stopped130 BEFORE assertions when the supported focused wrapper spawned prohibited cold worker compilation; only its verified owned wrapper was signaled and all tracked descendants drained. No baseline/head runtime PASS, red/green, live Chrome/device proof or performance claim; no equivalent cold retry, bootstrap bypass, suppression, timeout increase, added retry or skip. Exact-head hosted CI remains the runtime/broad gate.
- Phase E standalone session-memory backend/factory/registry/expiry/federation and tests untouched.

Release-note context: consolidate duplicate browser termination failure handling without changing best-effort cancellation recovery.

prs.title: fix(agents): refuse recovery-instruction echoes in settled-turn finalization
prs.body:
Closes #137915

## What Problem This Solves

When a turn ends with tool calls and no answer, OpenClaw re-asks the model for the final reply. Three defects followed:

- The re-ask never said the reply would be published, so a model could read it as internal state and have its planning script, or the re-ask text itself, delivered as the user's answer.
- The refusal that covers the re-ask text ran after the reply had already been written, so refused runner-authored text stayed in saved history and in the next model call's context.
- Two further owners had the same ordering defect: the Copilot journal published the reply before validation, and the worker retried on a session that still held the refused turn.

- Solution: every injected nudge carries a delivery contract; validation refuses a reply reproducing two distinct runs of the injected wording; each owner drops it at its own write edge.
- What changed: `recovery-nudge-text.ts` (new dependency-free leaf: contract, 7 nudge bodies, matcher), `run/incomplete-turn-recovery.ts` and `run/terminal-resolution.ts` (compose prompts through it), `harness/settled-turn-finalization-result.ts` (refuse an echo), `embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-prepare.ts` with `session-tool-result-guard.ts`/`-wrapper.ts` (drop it at the transcript write edge; re-pointed when a guarded session is reused), `extensions/copilot/src/attempt-transcript-journal.ts` (refuse it before the journal append/publish), `extensions/codex/src/app-server/settled-turn-finalizer.ts` (refuse it before the settled-finalizer mirror, so the retry keeps its identity), `src/worker/embedded-agent.runtime.ts` (restore the settled messages before a re-ask).
- Not changed: no new retry channel, budget, config flag, public API, or schema; empty and silent finalization, the bounded retry, and the worker's empty-finalizer failure path behave as before; a reply carrying tool calls is never dropped.

## Why This Change Was Made

The invariant is "delivered text must be the model's answer; runner-injected instruction text must never be delivered, nor remembered." Each owner is fixed at its own write edge instead of filtering downstream, which is also why #141206 was not reused: it filtered after publication.

- Best fix: yes — the existing validation point, bounded tool-free retry, and each owner's own write edge are reused.
- Alternative: filtering at delivery time (rejected: #141206), or duplicating the nudge strings in the validator (rejected: drifting copies; the shared predicate is hosted on the private harness attempt facade).
- Risk / non-goals: the matcher needs two distinct 8-word runs, so a reply quoting one short fragment is not an echo. Each drop is scoped to the restricted finalization attempt whose prompt *is* the injection, and never fires without an injection or when the reply carries tool calls.

## User Impact

Users no longer receive the agent's planning notes, or OpenClaw's own recovery text, as the answer, and refused text never reaches saved history, the published transcript, or the next model call. Such a turn is re-asked once, then falls back to the existing failure path.

## Evidence

Real worker process + real Gateway (`native-worker.integration.test.ts`, loopback provider; scratch scenario):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/worker/native-worker.integration.test.ts -t "zz-proof"
[zz-proof] provider requests: 4          # tool call, empty settled stop, echo, answer
[zz-proof] persisted echo count: 0
[zz-proof] persisted accepted answers: 1
[zz-proof] retry-context echo count: 0   # 1 with the worker fix removed
[zz-proof] preview echo count: 0
```

Shipped CLI (`openclaw agent --local`, loopback mock provider, real session store, no stubs):

```
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs echo-then-answer-cli-trace.with-history.mjs <repo-root>
AssertionError: rejected recovery-instruction echo reached saved local history  1 !== 0
# AFTER (fix applied)
model calls: 4; calls carrying the injected recovery instruction: 2 (requests 3, 4)
persisted messages containing the injected instruction: 0     # was 1
persisted messages equal to the genuine answer: 1
PASS: rejected bytes absent from saved local history; accepted answer persisted once.
```

Copilot extension (`runCopilotAttempt`, `settled-tool-finalization`: production journal, event bridge and session store; the SDK client is a scripted in-process double, as in `attempt-session.integration.test.ts`):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/copilot/src/zz-echo-trace.integration.test.ts
[zz-copilot] persisted echo rows: 0        # 1 with the journal fix removed
[zz-copilot] persisted accepted answers: 1
[zz-copilot] roles: [user, assistant, toolResult, assistant]
```

Validator matrix (`verify-recovery-echo.mjs`, no stubs): restating the nudge or the contract is refused after the fix, delivered before it; genuine answers, planning prose quoting one nudge run, and empty/silent input are unchanged.

Each write edge has a regression test captured red without its fix: the session-tool-result guard (a reused manager re-points the instruction; an ordinary attempt clears it), the Copilot journal (echo never reaches the transcript; the answer persists once), the codex settled finalizer (`mirror` is never called for an echo), the worker retry context, and both harness finalization suites. `run-vitest.mjs` on 7 files → 222 pass; `run-tsgo.mjs` core + extensions exit 0.

What was not tested: no live third-party model provider (no credentials here); `worker.runtime.test.ts` keeps four pre-existing `stops registered background execs after …` failures identical on the base commit.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used `rg`, `git log`, `git diff` and `node --import tsx` against production modules to trace issue #137915 and implement the fix. The implementer understands the code: the runner injects a re-ask whose reply is published verbatim, so the contract lives in the wording, validation refuses a reply reproducing two distinct runs of the injected text, and each persistence owner drops that reply at its own write edge.

prs.title: feat(subagents): carry a machine-readable reason on a registry-settled yielded collector
prs.body:
Related #165685

#164445, which this PR was stacked on, has merged (squash `e02ae3ecb66`). This branch merges `origin/main` at `bda0e040fec`, so `git diff origin/main...HEAD` is this PR's change only: 8 files, 49 insertions, 10 deletions (production 4 files +15/-3, tests 1 file +25/-5, docs 3 files +9/-2).

Simplified before review (the repo's `pr-simplify` pass, after the merge): the earlier revision also had an `agents.run` bridge assertion (that bridge reads the same `completionResult` projection as `agents_wait`), an `outputSchema` plus `reason` case (two independent spreads on one path), a standalone ordinary-failure test (now one assertion in the existing ordinary collector test), a settle-yielded unit test for a frozen completion the sweeper never settles, and an `agents_wait` unit test (its schema half is now one `Value.Check` on every real wait result in the integration test). Those are gone, as are restatements in the three docs. Reduction against the previous revision's own change (merged onto the same main): 10 files +211/-14 to 8 files +49/-10. Production behavior is unchanged.

Scope: part 1 of #165685 only (the machine-readable reason on a registry-settled yielded collector). Part 2 (leaf diagnostics) is not in this PR. ClawSweeper's comment on the issue says `agents_wait` stays collector-only and leaf diagnostics belong to `subagents list`, so this PR makes no leaf change and claims none.

## What Problem This Solves

A caller of `agents_wait` cannot tell a collector the registry sweeper settled as failed, because it was parked in a legacy yield with no recorded outcome, from a collector that failed for an ordinary reason: both come back as `status: "failed"` and only the free-text `error` differs.

Since #164445, the registry sweeper settles a collector that an earlier version persisted as yielded without a collector completion. A row with a recorded `ok` outcome keeps it and settles as `done`. A row with no recorded outcome settles as `{ status: "failed", error: "Collector yielded under a build that predates the admission gate, ..." }`. Recovery code that wants to rerun only that case has to match the English sentence in `error`, which is a message and not a contract.

## User Impact

`agents_wait` gains one optional field, `reason`. The `agents.run` host bridge returns the same completion object, but the Code Mode guest helper turns any non-`done` completion into a `SwarmAgentError` carrying only `runId`, `status` and a detail string, so guest code does not see `reason`; this PR does not change that helper. It is `"yielded_without_result"` only on a collector the sweeper settled as failed from a legacy parked yield with no recorded outcome. Every other completion has no `reason` key: a legacy `ok` collector settled as `done`, a legacy collector settled with its own recorded `error`, ordinary failures, killed, timeout, done, and schema errors are unchanged.

No config, schema, or migration changes. `status` keeps its four values. Nothing settles earlier, later, or differently, and no stored outcome changes; only the recorded fact is new. A collector settled by a build without this change has no `reason` and keeps returning exactly what it returned before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The settle path already knows why it is completing the run: `settleYielded: true` on the completion request, and the outcome it settles with. The reason is recorded where the collector completion is frozen (`updateSwarmCollectorCompletion`), as one optional member of the existing `collectorCompletion` payload, then projected by `completionResult()` in `agents-wait-tool.ts`.

- `subagent-registry-lifecycle-completion.ts`: passes `"yielded_without_result"` to `updateSwarmCollectorCompletion` only when `completeParams.settleYielded === true` and the row being settled has no recorded `execution.outcome`, which is exactly the case where the sweeper substituted the diagnostic error. `settleYielded` has one producer, the sweeper's `settleUnreachableYieldedSubagentRun`, which settles with the row's recorded outcome when there is one and with the diagnostic error otherwise. A settled row with a recorded `ok` or `error` outcome keeps that outcome and is not marked. A row cannot acquire a recorded outcome while yielded (`pauseSubagentRun` in `subagent-registry-run-pause.ts` deletes any recorded outcome when it parks the row), so a recorded outcome on a yielded row is a legacy shape. `planTerminalCompletion` returns before any mutation when a settle request meets a run that is no longer yielded.
- `swarm-collector.ts`: records the reason on the completion it creates. A collector whose completion is already frozen returns before the write, so a frozen completion is never rewritten and never gains a reason.
- `subagent-registry.types.ts`: `reason?: "yielded_without_result"` on the persisted collector completion.
- `agents-wait-tool.ts`: `reason` added to `CollectorCompletionSchema` (`additionalProperties: false`) and to `completionResult()`.
- Docs: `docs/tools/swarm.md` (result shape, and a sentence telling callers to branch on `reason` rather than `error` text), `docs/tools/subagents/tool-reference.md`, `docs/concepts/subagent-yield-handoff.md`.

Why this is not a persisted-schema change: the collector completion lives inside `subagent_runs.payload_json`; an optional key is absent on every existing row and read as undefined. No column, index, or migration changes, and `docs/reference/database-schemas` is untouched. Existing rows are never rewritten to add it: a frozen completion returns before the write, and only a completion created by the failed settlement carries it. The `$.collectorCompletion.*` retained-payload and session-list path lists in `subagent-registry.store.sqlite.ts` do not name `reason`, and `projectSubagentRunForSessionList` copies only `status`, so the field does not enter any trimmed projection. `CHANGELOG.md` is release-owned and is not edited.

The one other consumer of the schema, the `agents.run` host bridge, reuses `waitForCollectorCompletion`, which reads the same `completionResult()` projection, so its result carries the field with no further change and the `agents_wait` assertions cover it. The Code Mode guest helper (`code-mode-swarm-controller-source.ts`) reads `error`, `schemaError`, and `result` only, throws `SwarmAgentError` for a non-`done` status, and is unaffected.

## Contract choices

- Shape: a one-member literal `reason: "yielded_without_result"` on the collector completion, not a new `status`. #165685 asks for a field `agents_wait` callers can branch on without parsing `error`; keeping `status` at its four values leaves every existing consumer of the union untouched. The schema is a single `Type.Literal`; a later cause would widen it to a union of literals without touching `status`.
- Surface: `agents_wait` (and the `agents.run` host bridge result, which is the same object), which is what #165685 asks for. The Code Mode guest error, session list and board projections are unchanged.

## Contract table

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Collector parked in a legacy yield with no recorded outcome, settled by the registry sweeper | `status: "failed"`, `error` unchanged, `reason: "yielded_without_result"` |
| Same collector with an `outputSchema` and no captured structured output | `status: "failed"`, `schemaError: "structured_output was not called"` and `reason: "yielded_without_result"` together |
| Collector parked in a legacy yield with a recorded `ok` outcome, settled by the registry sweeper | `status: "done"` with the reply its yielded turn ended on, no `reason` |
| Collector parked in a legacy yield with a recorded `error` outcome, settled by the registry sweeper | `status: "failed"`, `error` is the recorded error, no `reason` |
| Collector failed or interrupted for any other cause (run ended with outcome `error`, completion frozen as `failed` by the normal terminal path) | no `reason` |
| Collector `done`, `killed`, or `timeout` | no `reason` |
| Collector whose completion is already frozen when a settle request arrives | no `reason`, completion unchanged |
| Collector settled by a build without this change | no `reason` |
| Unknown `reason` value in a result | not declared: `CollectorCompletionSchema` has `additionalProperties: false` and declares `reason` as the single literal |
| `status` values | unchanged: `done`, `failed`, `killed`, `timeout` |

`reason` is independent of `schemaError`: it is present exactly when the registry settled the collector as failed, whether or not a schema error is also recorded.

## Evidence

All of the following ran on one machine (Mac Studio, macOS, Node v24.21.0) at `892a6cddce7` (built and run as the unsigned tree-identical commit `ceeb8c90984`) and its base `bda0e040fec` (current `origin/main` when merged). Isolated HOME and state directories, loopback ports, no real Gateway touched.

Build summaries, verbatim:

```
base bda0e040fec: [build-all] phase timings: total 9m 4.7s; slowest write-unified-entry-dts 2m 38s; tsdown 1m 41.1s; tsdown-packages 1m 10s; tsdown-ai 38.6s; external-plugins:local-dist 32.4s; plugins:assets:build 20.9s; ui:build 19.4s; runtime-postbuild 18.9s; check-cli-bootstrap-imports 13.1s; write-cli-startup-metadata 5.85s; plugins:assets:copy 5.57s; check-plugin-sdk-exports 1.43s; native-protocol 772ms; build-stamp 353ms; runtime-postbuild-stamp 124ms; write-build-info 119ms
head ceeb8c90984: [build-all] phase timings: total 11m 49.5s; slowest tsdown 3m 12.9s; write-unified-entry-dts 3m 3.2s; external-plugins:local-dist 2m 7.9s; tsdown-packages 1m 43.7s; runtime-postbuild 27.6s; ui:build 18.7s; check-cli-bootstrap-imports 13s; tsdown-ai 12.7s; plugins:assets:build 9.03s; write-cli-startup-metadata 5.95s; plugins:assets:copy 5.32s; check-plugin-sdk-exports 1.76s; build-stamp 768ms; native-protocol 205ms; runtime-postbuild-stamp 200ms; write-build-info 150ms

Each arm copies that state, starts its own built Gateway (`node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port <port> --bind loopback`; HEAD built at `892a6cddce7`, BASE built at `bda0e040fec`) with its own HOME, state dir, and config and a stub model, waits until the first registry sweep has settled both parked collectors, then calls `agents_wait` over `POST /tools/invoke` with `{"tool":"agents_wait","sessionKey":"agent:main:main","args":{"ids":["<runId>"],"timeoutSeconds":0}}`. The seed is now written through current main's persistence path (`bda0e040fec`), same six rows.

One state directory, upgraded in place. The legacy rows are written by the v2026.10.4 source tree (`383c124cc32`) through that release's own registry persistence (`addSubagentRunForTests`): `run-collector-absent` (yielded, no outcome, no collector completion), `run-collector-ok` (yielded, outcome `ok`, no collector completion), `run-collector-frozen` (yielded with a frozen `{"status":"done"}` completion), `run-collector-failed` (ordinary failed collector, frozen `{"status":"failed"}`, never paused), and controls: `run-parked-leaf` (declared message wait, paused 50 hours), `run-awaiting-orchestrator` with its `run-awaited-child`, and `run-finished-worker` (ordinary finished run). The released Gateway from npm `openclaw@2026.10.4` then runs on that directory twice (the second run is a plain restart), then `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` from the candidate (the candidate refuses the schema 24 agent database v2026.10.4 writes until doctor migrates it, `v24 -> v31` in the doctor log; this is main's migration, not this PR), then the candidate Gateway built at `892a6cddce7`.
