prs.title: fix(session-binding): /codex detach and rebind fail with "Telegram runtime not initialized"
prs.body:
Closes #175372
Related: #171013 #171029 #173667

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `/codex detach` and re-running `/codex bind` fail with `Codex command failed: Telegram runtime not initialized` when run in a Telegram conversation bound to Codex, and the conversation stays bound.

## User Impact

User impact: in Telegram conversations bound to Codex, `/codex detach` and re-running `/codex bind` succeed instead of failing, so `/session unbind` is no longer needed as a workaround.

The change is in core, so it applies to every channel's session binding adapter, not only Telegram's:

- **Behavior change:** a channel session binding adapter that was registered inside a plugin instance now runs in that instance whenever core calls its methods, including calls that start in another plugin (for example a `/codex` command). This is the fix.
- **Risk:** every call into such an adapter now enters the owning instance first, including sync reads (`resolveByConversation`, `getCapabilities`), unscoped listings (`listBySession` / `listBySessionAsync`), and unscoped fan-out operations (`touch` or `unbind` without a scope), which visit every registered adapter.
  - **Reload interval:** in plugin reloads that replace or remove a channel plugin (config changes or `openclaw plugins reload <id>`), the Gateway closes ordinary admission to that plugin's instance (`quiesceInstances()`), drains admitted work, and only then stops its channels (`channels.stopPrevious()`), per `src/gateway/server-plugin-reload.ts` and `docs/plugins/architecture.md`; the replacement summary in `docs/plugins/sdk-runtime.md` lists the channel stop before the drain and omits the admission close. The adapter stays registered until the channel's binding manager stops. Admitted-work drains share a 60-second deadline (none with `--wait`); other awaited teardown can extend the interval. If the drain times out, the reload fails and admission resumes.
  - **Observable consequences:** in that interval, a call not already admitted in the retiring instance fails with `Plugin <id> was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools.` This applies to scoped calls for the reloading channel and to unscoped listings and fan-out, even when the reloading channel has no matching binding. Fan-out runs adapter by adapter: earlier successful adapter calls may already have committed and are not rolled back, and later adapters, including the generic current-conversation store, are skipped. From source reading: `sessions.delete` deletes the session, then fails at its unbind step, skips its remaining cleanup and `sessions.changed`, and can leave persisted bindings that point to the deleted session; subagent completion routing through bound delivery is returned/recorded as retryable (actual replay was not traced). Before this change these calls skipped admission; Telegram's adapter answered them from the retiring manager's in-memory state and reaches runtime-dependent persistence only when a matching binding must be persisted (other channels not checked). The fencing follows the documented lifecycle ("Retiring the instance stops new calls through its managed handles", `docs/plugins/sdk-runtime.md`). I did not add a skip for retiring adapters, since a skipped unbind would leave that channel's binding behind without an error.
- **Unchanged:** unregistering still matches the original adapter object, and adapters registered outside any plugin instance still run in the caller's context (both covered by guard tests).

## Why This Change Was Made

Core registered session binding adapters without their owning plugin instance. `/codex` handlers run in the Codex plugin instance, so when they changed a Telegram binding through the core service, Telegram's adapter ran in the Codex instance and its runtime lookup hit the Codex instance's empty slot. `/session unbind` is a core command that stays in Telegram's inbound scope, which is why it worked.

This change wraps the normalized adapter with `wrapCurrentPluginInstance` at registration, the same way core already registers plugin command handlers and channel plugin objects, and the same shape as #171029 for the Discord voice registry. It brings adapters in line with the documented plugin value boundary, where registered callables retain their instance scope and lifecycle fencing (`docs/plugins/sdk-runtime.md`). The registry already keeps the original adapter for unregistration and identity checks, so only the call view changes. Fixing the caller (Codex) or Telegram's persistence instead would each cover a single plugin.

#147609 (open when checked on 2026-10-17; it does not touch session binding) adds `bindCurrentPluginInstanceCallbacks`; if it lands first, this registration can switch to it. #173667 fixed the same class of error for the X channel by wrapping a retained child-session publication callback at message ingress resolution.

<details>
<summary>Call path (source reading on cd3eb90)</summary>

- `/codex detach` runs the Codex handler, which core registered with `wrapCurrentPluginInstance` (`src/plugins/command-registration.ts`), so it runs in the Codex instance. It calls `ctx.detachConversationBinding()`, then `getSessionBindingService().unbind()`, then Telegram's adapter `unbind` (`extensions/telegram/src/thread-bindings.ts`).
- Re-running `/codex bind` takes the auto-refresh branch in `src/plugins/conversation-binding.ts` and calls the adapter's `bind` from the same Codex instance.
- Telegram queues the persistence write, and the queue keeps the caller's async context (`AsyncLocalStorage.snapshot()` in `src/shared/store-writer-queue.ts`), so the write still runs in the Codex instance.
- Persistence calls `getTelegramRuntime()` (`extensions/telegram/src/thread-bindings-persistence.ts`). The runtime store reads the current plugin instance's slot (`getPluginInstanceRuntimeSlot`) and only falls back to the default slot outside any instance. The Codex instance's `plugin-runtime:telegram` slot is empty, so it throws `Telegram runtime not initialized`.
- Telegram registers its adapter during channel account startup, which runs inside the Telegram plugin instance (`src/gateway/server-channel-startup.ts`), so the wrap binds the adapter to the Telegram instance.
- `/session unbind` and the first `/codex bind` (written from Telegram's approval-button callback) already run in the Telegram instance, so they were never affected.

</details>

Authority after this change: a different plugin root is refused before any adapter mutation or persistence, and the remaining checks still run at Telegram's store write. The wrap adds an instance admission check at the adapter entry and removes none of the existing checks. Details:

<details>
<summary>Checks on a cross-plugin bind or detach</summary>

- The plugin binding owner (`src/plugins/conversation-binding.ts`) first reads the current binding through the adapter, which now enters the channel's plugin instance and passes its admission check. It then refuses a different plugin root (bind returns an ownership error, detach is a no-op); this comparison does not depend on the calling instance.
- Telegram's manager rejects mutations once `stop()` has started, and rechecks its generation and the captured record when the queued write runs.
- For bind, the caller's assertion and the adapter selection, including registration identity, are passed into the store write ([`extensions/telegram/src/thread-bindings.ts:379` at `5b38bf2`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5b38bf2fe3a73ebeadec4224ce37d6c22fcbaf52/extensions/telegram/src/thread-bindings.ts#L379)).
- In production, the plugin runtime's keyed store also checks the plugin runtime (`assertRuntimeCurrent`) at each write. One of its admission branches is an active call in the plugin's instance; a revoked owner is still refused.

</details>

## Evidence

- **Regression test** (`src/infra/outbound/session-binding-service.test.ts`, `runs unbind|bind in the registering plugin instance`): registers a fake channel adapter inside one `PluginInstance` and calls the core service from another.
  - Without the production change: `2 failed | 19 passed (21)`. Both new cases fail with `Fake channel runtime not initialized`, the same mechanism as the Telegram error.
  - With the change: `21 passed (21)`.
- **Guard tests** (pass with and without the change): an instance-bound adapter still unregisters by its original object; an adapter registered outside any instance still runs in the caller's instance.
- **Cross-instance authority test** (`src/plugins/conversation-binding.cross-instance.test.ts`, new): Telegram's real thread-binding manager with persistence, its adapter registered inside a Telegram `PluginInstance`; bindings are changed through `requestPluginConversationBinding` / `detachPluginConversationBinding` from two other plugin instances. Assertions read the stored entry for the target conversation. It lives in core because it needs several `PluginInstance`s, which the plugin SDK does not export; Telegram is loaded at runtime through its public `runtime-api` entry, the only public entry that exports the thread-binding manager factory (it also re-exports the runtime setter).
  - `lets the owning plugin root refresh|detach a Telegram binding across plugin instances`: the owning plugin root refreshes (one case) or detaches (another case), and the stored entry is updated or removed. Without the production change, each case fails with `Telegram runtime not initialized`.
  - `rejects a different plugin root without touching stored Telegram routing`: bind returns `This conversation is already bound by plugin "Codex".`, detach returns `{ removed: false }`, and the stored entry is unchanged. Passes with and without the production change; the refusal happens before any adapter mutation.
  - `rejects detaching after the Telegram plugin instance is quiesced`: detach from the owning root fails at the binding read with `Plugin telegram was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools.`, and the stored entry is unchanged. Without the production change, it gets `Telegram runtime not initialized` instead.
  - `rejects a queued Telegram write when its session binding adapter is replaced`: the owning root's bind is queued and paused at the store write while another registration is stacked for the same account (the shape of Telegram's disabled-bindings adapter, which registers outside the queue). The write is refused with `Session binding owner changed for telegram:default`, and the stored entry is unchanged. The test injects that registration directly; Telegram's manager replacement and stop are queued after the paused write.
  - `rejects a queued Telegram write when its registry owner is retired`: with a real plugin registry runtime, the owning root's bind is paused at the store write, then the plugin registry that holds the Telegram record is retired (`markPluginRegistryRetired`). The production store refuses the write with `Plugin "telegram" runtime is no longer active.`, and the stored entry is unchanged.
  - Existing Telegram proof is not repeated: in `extensions/telegram/src/thread-bindings.test.ts`, "drains accepted mutations in order before restart and rejects retired writes" covers manager-level retirement, and "does not publish a revoked binding (persist=%s)" covers a caller revoked while its persisted write is paused.
  - Results: `6 passed (6)`. Without the production change, `5 failed | 1 passed (6)`: both owning-root cases and both queued-write cases fail with `Telegram runtime not initialized`, and the quiesced case fails because it gets that error instead of the admission error; the only case that passes is `rejects a different plugin root without touching stored Telegram routing`. Timings are under Test cost.
- **Channel contract tests:** `pnpm test:contracts:channels`, run on `5b38bf2`; the follow-up commit changes only `session-binding-service.test.ts` (one guard test renamed, along with its runtime-store key, and its owner check simplified) and adds the cross-instance test file. Exit 0; 4 shards, 49 test files, 235 tests, all passed. Their harness creates binding managers outside any plugin instance, so those adapters stay unwrapped: this run guards against regressions and does not prove the fix.
- **Test cost:** `src/infra/outbound/session-binding-service.test.ts`, run back to back on the same host with Vitest on Node, separately from the runs below: 3.45s / 17 tests on `19c5e58` vs. 3.61s / 21 tests with this change (Vitest `Duration`). In CI on `5b38bf2` (`checks-node-changed-4`, [job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39020657515/job/117361856514)), `session-binding-service.test.ts` ran 21 tests with a file Duration of 3.56s (shard 5.59s); the four cases this PR added to that file took 85, 49, 27 and 28 ms.
  - New `src/plugins/conversation-binding.cross-instance.test.ts`: locally (same host, Vitest on Node), the six cases take about 3.4s together (per-case times in the output below), and the file Duration is 12.82s with a warm local compile cache (a separate run on the same tree; about 3s of that is the cache prepare step). The runs below show 27.98s and 28.12s because the local compile cache was cold: in this Vitest config, the `vitest-workers` prepare step (`prepared … in 17902ms`) falls inside Duration. In CI ([job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39053507285/job/117456978809)): `checks-node-changed-4`, 6 tests, file Duration 18.81s (summed test time 2.71s), shard 20.43s. No cheaper layer proves this: the fake-adapter cases (27–85 ms) prove the wrap itself, but not that Telegram's queued store write still runs in the Telegram instance, or that the adapter recheck at the write and the production store's runtime check still refuse on this new path.
- **pr-simplify:** no change to the production diff. What disappears is the implicit requirement that callers already be inside the adapter's plugin instance: an adapter registered in an instance now re-enters that instance on every call. Unregistering by the original object and adapters registered outside any instance running in the caller's context stay as before; the guard tests cover both. On the follow-up test file, pr-simplify's cuts were applied (one shared registration gate, one load of Telegram's runtime entry, a single detach in the quiesced-instance case), and teardown is registered with `onTestFinished` as each resource is created. Every refusal still asserts its exact result or error and the unchanged stored Telegram row. Relative to `19c5e58`: +3/-2 production lines (`session-binding-service.ts`) with no new production machinery; tests +110 in `session-binding-service.test.ts` (the follow-up commit renames one guard test there and simplifies its owner check) and +445 in the new `conversation-binding.cross-instance.test.ts`.
- **Local checks** (Linux x86_64, Node 24.21.0, `5b38bf2` plus the follow-up test changes (the same tree as `8607d6d`); Vitest ran on Node):
  - `git diff --check` is clean.
  - `pnpm check:changed`: the lanes covering this diff pass (typecheck core and core tests, lint, format, plugin boundaries, core tsgo graph boundary, import cycles, SQLite worker ratchet with "no T1 call-count growth", 182 -> 182). Two lanes fail on files this diff does not touch: the max-lines suppression ratchet (new suppressions in three `ui/` files) and the dead-export scan (unused exports in untouched files such as `extensions/tavily/` and `src/plugins/install-record-commit.ts`).
  - On a tree identical to `19c5e58`, both lanes fail the same way (the same three `ui/` files; unused exports in the same untouched files), so they were already red there. The env-var budget check also fails on that tree (`OPENCLAW_* count 456 exceeds budget 452`); this diff adds no `OPENCLAW_*` names.
- **Real Telegram (dedicated test bot, paired private chat):** a local dev Gateway built from this branch on the earlier base `cd3eb90`; the production hunk is byte-identical after the rebase. The codex plugin was enabled. The dev Gateway is intentionally run without model credentials. Before and after used the same build environment, bot, and chat; the only difference was `src/infra/outbound/session-binding-service.ts` (reverted to `cd3eb90` for the before run, then rebuilt; 0 vs. 2 `wrapCurrentPluginInstance` references in that source file and its built output).

  - After: re-running `/codex bind` replied `Bound this conversation to a new thread in <tmp-dir>. The next message will initialize it.` (path redacted); `/codex detach` replied `Detached this conversation from Codex.`; `/codex binding` replied `No Codex conversation binding is attached.`
  - No message was sent before detach, so both runs exercised the detach branch without an initialized native thread (`/codex binding` showed `Thread: unknown`).
  - The re-bind step goes through the real Telegram adapter's `bind`, including the owner check callback (`input.assertCurrent`) that the account-scoped binding adapter calls before persisting, and the real persistence write; it succeeded end to end after the change. The regression test in `session-binding-service.test.ts` uses a fake adapter that neither calls this callback nor persists.
  - Inferred, not directly observed: the after run implies that the real loader registers Telegram's adapter inside the Telegram plugin instance. If it did not, the wrap would return the adapter unchanged and the after run would fail like the before run.
  - The error is sent only as the command reply; it did not appear in the Gateway console log of either run.
  - My 2026.9.9 deployment showed the same before behavior (repeated, including after a Gateway restart).
- **QA lanes not used:** Crabline 0.1.29 (the version this repo pins) lists `callback_query` as an unsupported update type, and the live Telegram QA transport (`pnpm openclaw qa telegram`, which also needs Convex-leased credentials) has no button-press action, so neither lane can press the bind approval button. The live run above covers the entry point instead.

Not covered:

- Other channels: Discord and Matrix thread-binding persistence also open their state store through the runtime on demand (source reading at `9c54108`, three days before `cd3eb90`; not re-checked on `cd3eb90`). No other channel was tested live.
- The detach branch with an initialized native Codex thread was not run live: no message was sent before detach, so the bound Codex thread was never initialized (`/codex binding` showed `Thread: unknown`). Both branches end in the same `ctx.detachConversationBinding()` call (source reading).
- Not run live: a Gateway restart after the successful detach (whether the unbind stays persisted), the "Always allow" bind path, and groups and forum topics.
- Unscoped listings and fan-out during the reload interval (see User Impact) are not exercised; the cross-instance test covers one scoped detach in that interval, not fan-out or `sessions.delete`.
- Sender authorization runs at command entry and does not depend on the plugin instance; it is not re-tested here.
- Rejections in the cross-instance test come from the plugin ownership check, instance admission, the core adapter-selection check that Telegram runs inside its store write, and the production store runtime check (the last only in the real-registry case; the other cases use a test store whose authority is a no-op).
- This fix was not tested on 2026.9.9, and I did not check whether that release also registers channel adapters inside managed plugin instances.
- The call overhead of the instance view was not measured (it is the same view mechanism core already uses for channel plugin objects).
- Possible follow-ups, not in this PR: let unscoped `unbind` / `touch` continue past a failing adapter and report the errors at the end; let `sessions.delete` finish its post-commit cleanup and events when unbinding fails; list only the requester's channel and account in bound delivery. The fan-out stop and the skipped post-delete cleanup already happen on any adapter failure; this PR adds the reload interval as one more trigger.
- No Telegram Test Server (userbot) run: that lane needs maintainer-held Convex credentials. The live run above used a dedicated bot against a local dev Gateway and covers the owning plugin's path only (no different-root or retirement case). Telegram's shared draft-stream fixture still carries configuration paths that no remaining test uses.

- Baseline at `09cf9282b8fc8d17f3b90ffcc91c574bbdd6026b`: 85 passing tests across seven files.

- Scoped type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent preservation review is clean through P2, with complete caller and keeper source.
- CI run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39081024652 at `d514f96cb685a58a638dfd1fca7d680b21443f37` failed on missing imports in the unrelated placement authority tests introduced by newer main context. This attempt remains failed.
- Main now repairs that setup through the existing placement fixture in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8dc9734028569ef2319973cd7bf81971c8738ee1, superseding the alternative import repair at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175942.
- Native baseline correction `61108b1f3fab88537f544ec6c2bf3bac3cb820ab` incorporates that landed repair while preserving the exact Telegram cleanup and incoming review history. All 13 Telegram source/caller/keeper files and relevant dependency/test configuration inputs are unchanged from the tested candidate.
- Fresh independent correction review is clean through P2, covering the complete Telegram candidate and the landed placement fixture repair.
- Exact corrected-head CI passed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39083380609 at `61108b1f3fab88537f544ec6c2bf3bac3cb820ab`. The native watcher completed GREEN with no pending checks. The prior failed CI attempt remains historical failure, not reused passing proof.

prs.title: improve(memory): faster vector memory_search on the sqlite-vec store
prs.body:
Related: #112758, #140681, #164773

## What Problem This Solves

`memory_search` on the builtin SQLite store with sqlite-vec spends most of its vector-query time reading candidate embeddings back out of vec0 chunk blobs, not on the KNN scan. The KNN child opens a read-only connection per request with SQLite's default 2 MiB page cache. The cosine rerank selects `v.embedding` for each of the k candidates (the default `maxResults` 6 and `candidateMultiplier` 4 give a limit of 24, which the child widens eightfold to k = 192), and each embedding lives in a 16 MiB vec0 chunk blob (1,024 vectors of 4096 float32).

Diagnosis, measured at the previous base `b0ab44081ef` (the child, the cache helper, and the plan builder are unchanged on current `main`): on a 6,012-vector store with `memory` and `sessions` searched, one query through the real child took about 257 ms on a quiet host. On a reused connection the KNN scan alone takes about 16 ms and point lookups of the 192 candidate embeddings alone take about 225 ms. Lookups of 64 ids near the start of a chunk blob cost 0.6 ms and near the end 111 ms, and the cost disappears once the connection's page cache covers the blob, so deep reads are being repeated rather than served from cache. The exact sqlite-vec read path was not read in its source; the page-cache explanation is the one the measurements support.

## User Impact

User impact: vector `memory_search` returns faster on the builtin SQLite store with sqlite-vec, with byte-identical rows, order, and distances. The gain depends on how many of the k candidates survive the source filter and on store size. Measured at the current head against its merge base, on a shared host under load (load average 40 to 60), so absolute times are higher than on an idle machine:

| Store | Sources searched | Before (2 rounds) | After (2 rounds) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6,012 vectors (224 memory, 5,788 sessions), 4096 dims, 430 MB | memory, sessions | 295 to 300 ms | 119 to 123 ms |
| same store | memory only | 110 ms | 83 to 87 ms |

On the 43,490-vector, 4.86 GB store the difference under the same load is not separable from the run-to-run spread: memory only, AFTER was lower in all 5 interleaved pairs, by under 2 ms in one (median of pair medians 603 to 521 ms); memory and sessions, AFTER was lower in 3 of 5 pairs and higher in 2. No speedup is claimed for that store from these runs.

Cost: the KNN child's resident size after a query rises from about 118 MiB to 165 to 197 MiB on these stores (+46 to +79 MiB). The SQLite page cache is capped at 64 MiB per connection and the connection closes after every request, but the allocator keeps the freed pages, so the child stays at the higher size until it exits. Up to two KNN children run at once (`MAX_CONCURRENT_VECTOR_KNN_CHILDREN = 2`) and an idle child exits after `SQLITE_IDLE_HANDLE_TTL_MS` (30 minutes). Worst case on a host that has used both children is roughly +160 MiB resident for up to 30 minutes after the last query. The in-query peak was not sampled.

No config keys, defaults, schema, stored bytes, retention, durability, permissions, or child protocol change, so the storage-changes review checkpoint is not triggered. This PR is scoped to the disposable read-only KNN child connection; it does not decide what retained runtime handles get, which is the open question in #112758.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repo already has one owner for a connection-local page-cache budget on disposable handles: `configureSqliteMaintenanceCache` (`src/infra/sqlite-maintenance-cache.ts`, 64 MiB), used by the integrity worker, migrations, schema inspection, and repair. The KNN child's connection is the same kind of handle: opened for one request, read-only, closed before the next request. Applying that policy keeps the engine-specific pragma at its existing owner (the SQLite dialect ratchet in `check:changed` rejects a new pragma site in the child) and does not create a second budget.

The helper is reused rather than split into a second vector-specific budget because both callers want the same thing, headroom for a disposable handle that revisits pages, and a second constant would be a naming-only duplicate. The trade is that retuning the maintenance budget also retunes the KNN child; the helper's doc comment now names vector-read handles so that is visible at the retune site. A separate budget is a reasonable alternative if the owner prefers the two to move independently.

Alternatives:
- `PRAGMA mmap_size` on the same connection (measured at the previous base) helps only when the mapping covers the pages holding the blobs: on the 430 MB store, 64 MiB and 128 MiB mappings gave 239 and 207 ms against 223 ms default, and 1 GiB gave 28 ms; on the 4.86 GB store 1 GiB gave 272 ms against 351 ms. The mapping size would have to track the file, and whether to use mmap at all is open in #112758.
- Ordering by vec0's own L2 distance, reranking from the float64 copy in `memory_index_chunks.embedding`, or rebuilding the vec0 table with a smaller `chunk_size` each change scores, tie order, or the derived index. With the raw query vector, `l2^2 / 2` differs from the cosine distance by up to 1.742e+2; with a unit query by up to 1.383e-7. Those need owner direction and are not in this PR.
- Reusing one connection per database inside the child does not beat a fresh connection with a budget (the reopen cycle, open plus pragmas plus extension load plus close, costs about 1.9 ms) and would keep a handle on an agent database that deletion may remove.

## The change in one sentence

After the KNN child's existing `query_only` and `busy_timeout` pragmas, call `configureSqliteMaintenanceCache(db)` on that per-request connection; the helper's doc comment names vector-read handles as a third disposable-handle user.

Diff against current `main`: 2 production files (+6/-1: 5 added lines in the child, a one-line doc comment edit in the helper) and 1 test file (+39).

Simplified before review: an earlier revision also reflowed the helper's inline comment and edited its `sqlite-allow-raw` reason, and the test seeded a vec table it never reads. Both are gone; the helper body is byte-identical to `main` except the doc comment, and the test opens an empty database file. The branch has since merged current `main` because it conflicted with it; the only conflict was the test file's imports, where `main` added a test that already imports `node:fs/promises`, `node:os`, and `node:path`, so the new test uses the promise API and adds no imports beyond `matchesVectorRow`.

| Input case | Expected outcome |
|---|---|
| Vector query on a file-backed store (the subprocess path) | Same rows, order, and distances as before; faster when candidates sit deep in a chunk blob |
| Query on an in-memory store (`db && !admitted.databasePath`, no child) | Unchanged; that connection is not touched |
| Candidate underfill and widening (`rows.length < plan.limit`) | Unchanged decision; the widened rerun shares the same connection and benefits the same way |
| sqlite-vec extension fails to load | Unchanged: `{ rows: [], fallbackScanRequired: true }`; the pragma runs before the load and has no effect on the failure path |
| Node runtime replaced under a running Gateway | Unchanged: the parent refuses before spawning the child (`NODE_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE`), so the child and its pragma never run |
| PostgreSQL vector capability | Not on this path |
| Memory: child RSS | Measured +46 to +79 MiB after a query, retained until the child exits (up to 30 min idle); the page cache itself is capped at 64 MiB per connection |
| Deliberately unhandled: stores on page sizes other than 4 KiB, other dims | Not measured; the budget is in KiB, so the mechanism is the same, the gain may differ |

## Evidence

All of the following ran on one machine (Mac Studio, macOS, Node v24.21.0, sqlite-vec 0.1.9, SQLite from node:sqlite) at the current head (tree `3e0483cbd19`), whose merge base with `main` is `09cf9282b8f`.

### Method

BEFORE is a clean build of `09cf9282b8f`; AFTER is a clean build of this branch. The two builds differ only by this diff. `main` has not changed the child, the cache helper, or the SQLite plan builder (`sqlite-vector.ts`) since the previous measurement; it did change the parent launcher (runtime-viability check before spawn) and search orchestration, so both arms were rebuilt and re-measured rather than reused. The production child (`dist/infra/database-engine/sqlite-vector.child.js`) is driven through its stdin/stdout protocol with the production `memory_search` statement (limit 24, k 192, snippet 700, model and source filters as `buildMemorySourceFilter` produces them), one child reused across requests and reopening per request as the child does. Each figure is the median of 5 runs after 2 warmups (large store: 3 warmups, 5 and then 9 runs), BEFORE and AFTER interleaved. `sha256(rows)` over every returned field is equal for BEFORE and AFTER in every pair. Stores are `sqlite3 .backup` snapshots of two real agent databases opened read-only (430,518,272 and 4,855,853,056 bytes). The host was shared with other builds and test runs during measurement; load average is printed in each output. Script and raw outputs: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/tree/assets/knn-child-cache-evidence/pr-knn-cache/merge (script `measure-child.mjs`; outputs `measure-child-dev-merge.out`, `measure-child-main-merge.out`, `measure-child-main-merge-r9.out`).

### Build

`pnpm build` succeeded for both arms:

```
BEFORE [build-all] phase timings: total 10m 20.6s; slowest write-unified-entry-dts 3m 50.3s; runtime-postbuild 2m 28.4s; ui:build 53.2s; ...
AFTER  [build-all] phase timings: total 10m 16.8s; slowest write-unified-entry-dts 3m 41.4s; runtime-postbuild 2m 27.1s; ui:build 53.1s; ...
```

The AFTER child contains the `configureSqliteMaintenanceCache` call; the BEFORE child does not.

### Behaviour, case by case

6,012 vectors, 430 MB (load average 50 to 60):

```
BEFORE  sources=[memory]           rows=24 sha256(rows)=6174f733f3090583 median=109.532 ms runs=[110.8, 105.3, 115.7, 109.5, 107.5] child rss=118.1 MiB
AFTER   sources=[memory]           rows=24 sha256(rows)=6174f733f3090583 median=83.323 ms  runs=[86.2, 78.8, 83.3, 88.1, 78.0]  child rss=165.5 MiB
BEFORE  sources=[memory]           rows=24 sha256(rows)=6174f733f3090583 median=109.592 ms runs=[115.5, 109.6, 114.9, 108.3, 105.7] child rss=118.8 MiB
AFTER   sources=[memory]           rows=24 sha256(rows)=6174f733f3090583 median=87.245 ms  runs=[90.6, 81.9, 86.6, 92.9, 87.2]  child rss=165.2 MiB
BEFORE  sources=[memory,sessions]  rows=24 sha256(rows)=e279c239e982e2c4 median=295.181 ms runs=[295.2, 352.5, 311.7, 293.9, 290.8] child rss=118.4 MiB
AFTER   sources=[memory,sessions]  rows=24 sha256(rows)=e279c239e982e2c4 median=122.591 ms runs=[122.6, 120.6, 124.6, 125.3, 114.2] child rss=195.8 MiB
BEFORE  sources=[memory,sessions]  rows=24 sha256(rows)=e279c239e982e2c4 median=300.224 ms runs=[296.5, 300.2, 317.5, 296.5, 310.0] child rss=118.2 MiB
AFTER   sources=[memory,sessions]  rows=24 sha256(rows)=e279c239e982e2c4 median=118.526 ms runs=[132.2, 118.4, 118.5, 125.1, 116.4] child rss=195.9 MiB
```

43,490 vectors, 4.86 GB (load average 40 to 56), medians per interleaved pair; the first two pairs are 5 runs after 3 warmups (`measure-child-main-merge.out`), the last three are 9 runs after 3 warmups (`measure-child-main-merge-r9.out`):

```
sources=[memory]           sha256(rows)=25a343a9e7e542fe  BEFORE 602.2 566.7 646.5 603.8 602.7 ms  AFTER 507.0 520.6 547.8 601.9 507.0 ms
sources=[memory,sessions]  sha256(rows)=25d77cb9e0f70967  BEFORE 667.2 570.9 723.0 602.4 619.8 ms  AFTER 633.1 699.9 533.5 760.1 507.4 ms
child rss after last request: BEFORE 118.2 to 120.9 MiB, AFTER 195.7 to 196.8 MiB
```

Where the time goes, measured at the previous base `b0ab44081ef` on a quiet host (raw outputs in the parent directory of the evidence link, `evidence/research-*.out`), on a single reused connection with default pragmas against the 6,012-vector store at k 192: full query 240 ms; vec0 KNN alone (id, distance, no join) 16 ms; point lookups of the 192 candidate embeddings alone 225 ms; the same join ordered by vec0's own distance without reading `v.embedding` 16 ms. A 64-id lookup set costs 0.6 ms at the start of a chunk blob and 111 ms at the end of it. A fresh-connection sweep on the same store at the same query: default 223 ms, `cache_size` 16 MiB 191 ms, 64 MiB 67 ms, 128 MiB 60 ms. These diagnose the mechanism and do not depend on the code in this PR. The three default-pragma figures for the same store (257 ms through the child, 240 ms on a reused connection, 223 ms on a fresh connection) differ by method: the child adds the JSON and stdio round trip.

### Tests

`pnpm test src/infra/database-engine/sqlite-vector-subprocess.test.ts`:

```
 ✓  infra  src/infra/database-engine/sqlite-vector-subprocess.test.ts > classifies a replaced runtime that cannot be executed before vector worker startup 74ms
 ✓  infra  src/infra/database-engine/sqlite-vector-subprocess.test.ts > forwards a discovered SQLite library through stdin without inheriting its environment 26ms
 ✓  infra  src/infra/database-engine/sqlite-vector-subprocess.test.ts > budgets the page cache on the child's per-request read-only connection 151ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
   Duration  28.43s (transform 97%, setup 2%, tests 1%)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 32.52s
```

Owning directory and the production consumer of the child:

```
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=8 pnpm test src/infra/database-engine
 Test Files  9 passed | 1 skipped (10)
      Tests  59 passed | 1 skipped (60)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
 Test Files  18 passed | 41 skipped (59)
      Tests  80 passed | 241 skipped (321)
[test] passed 3 Vitest shards in 142.66s

pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-knn-subprocess.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  19 passed (19)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 14.46s
```

### Regression proof (red/green)

The new test spawns the real child through `runVectorKnnInSubprocess` against a file-backed database. Its plan statement is `SELECT cache_size FROM pragma_cache_size WHERE ? > 0`, which the child runs verbatim on the connection it configured, so the returned row is the budget that connection actually has. This guards the configuration (the child must apply the disposable-handle cache budget); it does not by itself prove the speedup, which the benchmark above shows. It requires sqlite-vec to load in the child, the same precondition the existing memory-core subprocess test has.

On unchanged `09cf9282b8f` with only this branch's test file copied in, it fails on the original behaviour:

```
 FAIL   infra  src/infra/database-engine/sqlite-vector-subprocess.test.ts > budgets the page cache on the child's per-request read-only connection
- Expected
+ Received
-       "cache_size": -65536,
+       "cache_size": -2000,
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 2 passed (3)
```

On this branch it passes (output above).

### Other checks

`pnpm check:changed --base 09cf9282b8f` on the current head:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| typecheck core / core tests | ok |
| lint core changed files | ok |
| format changed files, `oxfmt --check` on the 3 files | ok |
| SQLite dialect ratchet | ok (engine-maintenance constructs in changed files 3 -> 3) |
| SQLite worker ratchet | ok (T1 live calls 181 -> 181) |
| database-first legacy-store guard, runtime import cycles, line-cap growth ratchet | ok |
| `git diff --check` | clean |
| max-lines suppression ratchet | failed on `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts`, `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts`; none are in this diff, and the same check fails on the same three files in a clean checkout of `09cf9282b8f` |
| core tsgo graph boundary | failed: `gateway-root` 728 and `infra` 741 test roots exceed the advisory 720; this diff adds no test file, and the same check fails with the same counts on a clean checkout of `09cf9282b8f` |
| dead export scan | failed on 30 exports, none in this diff; a clean checkout of `09cf9282b8f` reports the identical 30 |

### Measured test cost

| Suite | Wall (shard) | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| `src/infra/database-engine/sqlite-vector-subprocess.test.ts` | 32.52 s (test file 28.43 s, mostly transform; the new case 151 ms) | 3 |
| `src/infra/database-engine` | 142.66 s | 145 passed, 242 skipped |
| `extensions/memory-core/.../manager-search-knn-subprocess.test.ts` | 14.46 s | 19 |

The new case adds one real child spawn and one empty database file, 151 ms on a loaded host. Measured without `--maxWorkers=1`.

## Gaps, stated plainly

- `pnpm changed:lanes --json` for this diff returns `core: true, coreTests: true` and every other lane false, with `extensionImpactFromCore: false`. The memory-core consumer test above ran anyway because it is the production caller of this child. Unrelated suites were not run.
- The three `check:changed` failures above are in files outside this diff and reproduce on a clean checkout of the merge base; they are not addressed here.
- The benchmark ran on a shared host under load. The 430 MB store shows a clear gain; the 4.86 GB store does not show one outside the run-to-run spread in these runs.
- Measurements are from one host, two stores, both at 4096 dims and 4 KiB pages. 1536- and 3072-dim stores, other page sizes, Linux, and Windows were not measured. The mechanism does not depend on those, but the size of the gain does.
- The vec0 blob read path was not read in the sqlite-vec source; the page-cache explanation is inferred from the start-of-blob versus end-of-blob lookup cost and from the cache-size sweep.
- Child RSS is measured after the last request, once the connection has closed. The in-query peak was not sampled.
- The helper keeps its `maintenance` name; whether the vector reader should have its own budget constant is the owner's call.

prs.title: refactor(agents): trust workspace and sandbox prepared facts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workspace, sandbox, and outbox internals repeat copies and checks on facts their existing owners already prepared.

## User Impact

User impact: no intended user-visible change, schema migration, or required action; durable writes, current authority, FIFO ordering, and ordinary shutdown settlement stay with their existing owners.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use private outbox payload state directly, carry the validated workspace receipt envelope, and retire expired cache state from the committed native receipt instead of comparing two results from the same write. Borrow already-prepared internal command inputs until the existing worker serializer captures them. Keep the generation snapshot across the mutable external backend callback. Migration fixtures retain independent explicit SQL expectations.

Production delta: +38/-63, net 25 lines removed. Test delta: +14/-17, net 3 lines removed. No new schema, option, dependency, compatibility layer, or test-only production seam.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Private outbox state is read directly from the admitted typed union, whose constructors set the literal state after payload spread. The removed generic decoder came from #169315 / 84a834e2334. Historical raw JSON migration validation is unchanged; unsupported mutation of an internal typed payload is not an input contract.
- Internal caller mutation before asynchronous dispatch no longer receives extra registry, recovery-predicate, or deletion-plan snapshots. Audited callers prepare local values and await writes; the synchronous worker serializer still captures actual wire input. Provenance: #165558 / 7f4cf3466b3, #163496 / 6c1e1667bd6, and #167547 / 24d599636ab. Two synthetic immediate-mutation assignments are removed; ordinary immutable-field, custody, target, FIFO, authority, and settlement assertions remain. The generation snapshot across the mutable external backend callback remains.
- Expiry retirement trusts the operation's canonical committed receipt instead of separately matching its own grant result (#163496 / 6c1e1667bd6). There is one write and one retained native receipt, not competing result owners. Lost ordinary replies still retire the cache within awaited FIFO settlement.
- The workspace receipt boundary checks the raw record/domain once and carries that narrowed envelope instead of testing it again (#168094 / 73039895153). Native receipt source/coverage and publication validation remain mandatory; malformed external receipts are not accepted.
- Native Date.now is trusted after explicit caller nowMs validation (#158797 / 2442c302693). A monkeypatched noninteger native clock is an unsupported synthetic edge; stored-row/hash/filename validation and current write authority remain.

## Evidence

Source inspection covered the complete changed owners, relevant callers, worker serialization and admission boundaries, migration SQL, and introducing commits. Author simplification and test audit completed. git diff HEAD --check passed. Independent canonical isolated P2 review completed scoped-clean with no findings on the frozen nine-file candidate.

Fresh functional and targeted-type proof is not claimed: the once-installed shared task dependencies do not match current main's fs-safe version. No shared install is reconciled or retried. Exact-head PR CI is the broad gate; any failure will receive its own attribution before landing. No measured performance gain is claimed.

Publication base: dca14adbd8704bc61eb63fa16a99030417e9a3d6. All nine targets remain unchanged from the reviewed packet's base; the full patch matches SHA256 a0f836a83105513ee306a1ba5b78100acc40a20283bfbb58e5ca3d982a68c733. Root personally inspected the complete affected owners, synchronous wire serialization, canonical native-receipt retirement, changed tests, and the scoped-clean P2 report. Newer state-domain publication uses a synchronous capture stack; this packet retains its synchronous capture and native receipt contract unchanged. Formatting passes all eight existing TypeScript files, diff-check passes, retired references are absent, and no import edge is added. Fresh functional/type proof is not dependency-qualified by the once-installed task dependencies; exact-head CI owns broad proof.

The serial isolated suppression audit completed naturally within its fixed 180-second budget: four cases passed and the inventory case failed (41.271 seconds test time, 82.06 seconds Vitest, 112.02 seconds shard). It reports 95 production entries versus 94 expected: backup-restore preserve-caught-error is 2 rather than 1, and the native-bridge target-origin suppression is unlisted. None of the eight surviving changed files contains suppression directives, and the audit plus both implicated source blobs are identical between base and head. No suppression or allowance was added or changed. This is input/source attribution, not an executed baseline or passing audit; the failure remains disclosed. All known owned processes and groups exited.

Pre-publication source freshness through materialized main `a34f1be0bc1e6a0557122f497f89aab6b86b4911`: eight of nine packet paths remain unchanged. The JSON-predicate test now exercises real compressed transcript payloads, denies transcript updates during migration, reads lazy predicates, preserves stored bytes, and covers stable-v24 admission/rollback as well as v26 version/table markers. Root inspected the full main delta and this packet's separate literal outbox expectations. Preserve all main coverage and apply only the helper-import removal and the five explicit payload/state cases contextually; no production migration or Phase E change belongs to this packet. This is static drift evidence, not fresh runtime proof or permission to overwrite the test.

The same eight-of-nine source comparison was refreshed against materialized main `fd4bc6556220881f758b361891fd2121afd0c0bb`, then all nine targets were unchanged through freshly fetched main `1595951a2274857f39f1cd80f945ea6530bb0308`. GitHub reported the original draft head CONFLICTING, so it received a conflict-only rebase. The sole conflict was the JSON-predicate test: main's real compressed-payload loop and every expanded migration/rollback assertion remain; only our five explicit outbox expectations and retired-helper import removal transfer. Signed repair head is `8661dd3062b8177c2f7fa0975adf7d4bb25eb6fd`. Its full nine-file patch is identical to the reviewed original after excluding only blob-ID and hunk-offset headers. Original scoped-clean P2 review is reused for that unchanged cleanup, not claimed as a new execution. The conflicted file passes formatting; diff-check passes. The stated 25-line production reduction remains candidate credit, not landed credit.

One post-conflict repository-wrapper attempt selected only the conflicted migration test and mandatory suppression audit, serially with one worker and fresh isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG state. It reached its fixed 180-second budget during managed-worker preparation, with no assertions (exit 124; 181.67 seconds; all tracked children drained). This is an unfinished proof gap, not a test failure, passing audit, baseline result, or typecheck pass. There was no retry, install reconciliation, timeout increase, skip, or suppression change. The private checkout has the pinned fs-safe0.26.7/Vitest5.0.3/oxfmt0.72.0; its earlier install timeout remains disclosed, not a global setup-success claim. Exact-head CI must supply the missing runtime/type/broad proof before landing.

## Completed exact-head CI

Ready [CI run39075392029, attempt1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39075392029) completed successfully on exact `8661dd3062b8177c2f7fa0975adf7d4bb25eb6fd`. All14selected lanes succeeded,26were unselected, with zero selected execution gaps. Its70actual jobs are43success/27skipped, with no non-skipped zero-step job. The complete200same-head CheckRun census matches the live rollup:73success,124skipped,1neutral and2historical startup cancellations, each with a later same-head successful replacement. All three latest status contexts succeeded. PostgreSQL conformance was selected and passed; build artifacts were unselected, not passed. No CI rerun, dispatch or green-only push was used.

Root independently verified all24artifact hashes and retained the actual tested merge `3d0c80bd45f0c78e6156e673e690ad3b3d3457b8`, ordered parents `dedba2075aa177347e7c3925cf8f510d137aaab6` and exact PR head, tree `536fce57889e1c3a673f3d4c34b5b2730744a945`. Its complete nine-file delta is identical to the reviewed cleanup apart from blob-ID/hunk-offset headers; diff-check passes. Actual tested production+38/-63 is25net removed; tests+14/-17 is3net removed, still candidate rather than landed credit. Main's compressed-payload, lazy-predicate, transcript-denial, byte-preservation, v24 rollback, v26, FIFO and Phase E coverage remains intact. Normal native landing is pending. Hosted success does not retroactively pass the original four-pass/one-failure local audit or the later no-assertion local attempt.

prs.title: fix(wizard): honor session cancellation during hosted setup
prs.body:
## Update 2026-10-16 — rebased onto current `main`

Recreated as a single commit on `main` (`73bb9054970`); the branch previously carried a divergent fork history, which is why GitHub reported it as conflicting. `src/gateway/server-methods/wizard.ts` was the only hand-resolved hunk — `main` restructured `wizard.start` (`wizardRequestScopes.set(...)`, block-bodied arrow) — and the resolution keeps that structure while threading the session `signal` into the setup runner call. Re-verified on this head on the test host: base (`main` plus these tests) `Tests 2 failed | 50 passed (52)`, candidate `Tests 52 passed (52)`.

---

## What Problem This Solves

Closes #127374.

Classic hosted setup (`wizard.start` with flow `setup`) never hands the wizard session's `AbortSignal` to the setup runner.

`WizardSession` owns the controller and passes the signal to its runner (`src/wizard/session.ts`), but the gateway built the setup session as `new WizardSession((prompter) => …)` and `SetupWizardRunner` had no signal parameter, so the signal was dropped at that hop. Downstream, `runSetupWizard` → `runSetupModelAuthStep` → `prepareAuthChoice` could not receive one either, even though the provider-auth owner already accepts `signal` and forwards it to device-code polling and token exchange.

Effect: `wizard.cancel` during provider authentication does not abort that provider work. The cancelled session keeps setup admission until the provider eventually settles (device-code expiry can be 15 minutes), so an immediate replacement setup attempt is rejected as busy.

## Fix

Carry the session signal that already exists down the setup path:

- `SetupWizardRunner` gains an optional `signal`, and `wizard.start` passes the session's signal to it. `GatewayKernelContext.wizardRunner` now reuses that contract instead of restating it.
- `runSetupWizard` / `runSetupWizardOnce` accept and forward it.
- `runSetupModelAuthStep` forwards it, and `ApplyAuthChoiceParams` accepts `signal`.
- `prepareAuthChoice` and the provider-auth owner (`provider-auth-choice.ts`) already forward the signal end to end, so no new cancellation mechanism is added.

Scope correction (thanks @clawsweeper): the earlier body overstated durable-write protection. `beforePersistentEffect` is supplied only to the channels runner (`channelWizardRunner`); classic setup never receives that hook, before or after this change. This patch changes no durable-write behavior on either flow.

## Evidence

### Rebase note (2026-10-11)

This revision's head is `1f7bb369d31e1e508cbe87806257a4344ea603f6`, rebased onto `main` @ `b6fa7b58004` because the previous base (`e62f5f37442f152d238d5e838b52a48b2102f682`) predated a material amount of merged work. The rebase replayed the same commits with no conflicts and the patch is unchanged: `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD` still reports +69/-3 across 6 files. The proof receipts below were captured on the pre-rebase head and were not re-run on this base; CI re-runs on this head.


**Real behavior proof — full production chain, no mocks, no injected runner.**

- Real gateway process: `node dist/index.js gateway run --port 19777 --auth token` (production bundle built from the tested commit), fresh state dir.
- Real WS client driving `wizard.start` → `wizard.next` → `wizard.cancel` over the gateway protocol (token auth, signed device identity).
- Real provider authentication: the bundled github-copilot plugin's device flow, redirected through the provider's supported `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN` seam to a live local HTTPS stub: `proof-x.ghe.com` resolves via /etc/hosts to a public IP bound to loopback (so the SSRF guard's hostname allowlist + resolved-address checks pass), TLS via a local CA in `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`. The stub issues a real device code (interval 1s), answers `authorization_pending`, and withholds poll #3's response for 5s so cancellation lands mid-request.

Environment: Linux x86_64 (kernel 4.19), Node v24.18.0, 2026-10-02 (UTC).

**After fix (head `0e7a28c6c2f8`):** cancellation aborts the in-flight poll and frees setup admission.

```

+ 62890ms stub: token poll #1 received
+ 63905ms stub: token poll #2 received
+ 64920ms stub: token poll #3 received        <- response withheld 5s
+ 65003ms stub: poll #3 connection CLOSED BEFORE RESPONSE (in-flight abort)

+ 65012ms replacement wizard.start attempt 1: REJECTED (setup already in progress)
+ 65525ms replacement wizard.start attempt 2: ACCEPTED sessionId=0d61e25e-... status=running
```

prs.title: fix(cli): reject reserved __proto__ keys in provider-env and mcp env/header
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw config set ... --provider-env` and `openclaw mcp add --env/--header` accept `KEY=VALUE` entries and build them into a plain object with `entries[key] = value`. When the key is `__proto__`, that assignment hits `Object.prototype`'s legacy setter instead of creating an own property, so the entry is silently dropped — the command still exits 0 and writes the config, just without the requested key. No warning, no error, nothing in the written file.

This is the same failure mode the repository already guards against at the MCP server-name boundary (`src/config/zod-schema.root-support.ts`):

```ts
// Plain assignment treats "__proto__" as a setter, so one unhardened map builder
// can silently drop the server. Reject the name at the config boundary instead.
```

This change applies that same principle to the two CLI `KEY=VALUE` boundaries: instead of dropping a reserved key silently, reject it with a message that names the flag and the key.

## User Impact

- An operator who passes `--provider-env __proto__=…` (or `mcp add --env/--header __proto__=…`) now gets an actionable error instead of a silently incomplete config.
- No change for any other key: normal entries are parsed and written exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The silent drop happens at the point the CLI parses each entry, so the guard is added there — that is also where the message can name the offending flag (`--provider-env`, `--env`, `--header`), which a schema-level error cannot.

- `src/cli/config-cli-input.ts` — `parseProviderEnvEntries` rejects a `__proto__` key.
- `src/cli/mcp-cli.ts` — `parseKeyValueEntries` (used by both `--env` and `--header`) rejects a `__proto__` key.

Scope follows the existing precedent exactly: only `__proto__` is rejected (the key that is silently dropped). `constructor`/`prototype` are not touched — plain assignment to those keys creates ordinary own properties, so they are not affected by this bug.

## Evidence

### Control-red: same commands, base vs this change

Run through the real CLI entry (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts …`) with an isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`.

| Scenario | Base (`main`) | This change |
|---|---|---|
| `config set secrets.providers.runner --provider-source exec --provider-command <cmd> --provider-env __proto__=injected --provider-env NORMAL_KEY=control` | exit `0`, no error, written `env` keys = `["NORMAL_KEY"]` (`__proto__` dropped) | exit `1`, `--provider-env key "__proto__" is reserved; use a different key name.`, nothing written |
| `mcp add probe --command <cmd> --no-probe --env __proto__=injected --env NORMAL_KEY=control` | exit `0`, no error, written `env` keys = `["NORMAL_KEY"]` (`__proto__` dropped) | exit `1`, `--env key "__proto__" is reserved; use a different key name.`, nothing written |
| `mcp add probe --url https://mcp.example.test/mcp --no-probe --header __proto__=injected --header X-Normal=control` | exit `0`, no error, written `headers` keys = `["X-Normal"]` (`__proto__` dropped) | exit `1`, `--header key "__proto__" is reserved; use a different key name.`, nothing written |

Raw JSON from the proof (base):

```json
{
  "providerEnv": { "exitCode": 0, "stderrHasError": false, "writtenEnvKeys": ["NORMAL_KEY"] },
  "mcpEnv":     { "exitCode": 0, "stderrHasError": false, "writtenMsKeys": ["NORMAL_KEY"] },
  "mcpHeader":  { "exitCode": 0, "stderrHasError": false, "writtenHeaderKeys": ["X-Normal"] }
}
```

Raw JSON after the change:

```json
{
  "providerEnv": { "exitCode": 1, "stderrFirstLine": "--provider-env key \"__proto__\" is reserved; use a different key name.", "writtenEnvKeys": [] },
  "mcpEnv":     { "exitCode": 1, "stderrFirstLine": "--env key \"__proto__\" is reserved; use a different key name.", "writtenMsKeys": [] },
  "mcpHeader":  { "exitCode": 1, "stderrFirstLine": "--header key \"__proto__\" is reserved; use a different key name.", "writtenHeaderKeys": [] }
}
```

### Regression tests

Added cases assert the rejection and that no config is written, for both boundaries:

- `src/cli/config-cli.test.ts` — `rejects a reserved __proto__ provider env key before writing`
- `src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts` — `rejects a reserved __proto__ key in --env and --header before writing`

```
$ node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  72 passed (72)
```

```
$ node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.mcpcheck.config.ts
 Tests  33 passed | 1 failed (34)
```

(`src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts` is excluded from the default CLI project and needs the host-owned SQLite broker, so it was run through an isolated scoped config.)

The single failure is a pre-existing environment failure on this host — `requires initialize to finish within the configured probe timeout before saving` — which spawns a probe child process; it fails identically on the unmodified base and is unrelated to this change (the new test passes in isolation).

### Lint

```
$ oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json src/cli/config-cli-input.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
```

### Types

Scoped `tsgo` over the changed files reports no errors in `src/cli/config-cli-input.ts` or `src/cli/mcp-cli.ts`. The remaining errors in the run are pre-existing dependency gaps in unrelated files (`pg`, `@resvg/resvg-js`, `@openclaw/proc-safe`) and are identical on the base.

### Sibling check

`gh search prs` for `__proto__ env`, `reserved prototype`, and `parseKeyValueEntries` returns no open or closed PR touching these two sites. This is distinct from #171770, which preserves `__proto__` keys in plain runtime maps (`cron` command env / process-env merge); the sites here flow into config that is validated through `z.record`, where the key is dropped regardless, so rejection — not preservation — is the correct fix and matches the existing boundary precedent.

prs.title: fix(ui): reset the provisioning elapsed timer when a placement is retried
prs.body:
Closes #132473

## What Problem This Solves

After a failed cloud provisioning attempt, clicking **Retry** starts a new
attempt, but the working indicator's elapsed timer keeps counting from the
**failed attempt's** start time. The new attempt immediately appears to have
been running for the whole duration of the earlier failure.

The placement-startup runtime stamped each entry with a single `createdAt`
that was exposed as `startedAt` on the status surface and rendered by
`openclaw-elapsed-time` in the chat working indicator. `retry()` passed the
entry's original `createdAt` into the new `start`, and `start()` also forced
the existing `createdAt` through when the message id was unchanged — so the
retried attempt never got its own timer start.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime owner (`ui/src/app/session-placement-startup.runtime.ts`) now
separates the **message creation time** from the **attempt start time**:

- A new `entry.attemptStartedAt` drives the working-indicator elapsed timer
  and resets to `Date.now()` on Retry.
- `entry.createdAt` stays the original message creation time and continues to
  feed `initialTurn.createdAt` and accepted-message retention, so a retried
  prompt keeps its original transcript timestamp.
- `start()` honors `input.createdAt` for `mode === "retry"` when building
  `attemptStartedAt`, while the `createdAt` branch keeps the existing message
  time across retries.

The renderer owner (`ui/src/pages/chat/chat-progress.ts`,
`resolveWorkingProgress`) receives the placement initial turn's id from the
thread build (the existing `initialTurnId` prop) and lets the live attempt
start (`streamStartedAt`) override the queued message time for that turn
only; an ordinary in-flight send keeps counting its acknowledgment wait from
its own `createdAt`. Durable inline states
(`failed`/`unconfirmed`/`waiting-reconnect`) still retain their reconnect
timing, matching existing tests.

No new option, validator, or configuration surface is added.

Production LOC is `+25/-4` net `+21`.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

A user who retries a failed cloud startup now sees the new attempt's elapsed
timer start near zero, instead of inheriting the failed attempt's elapsed
time — while the queued prompt keeps its original message timestamp in the
transcript. Existing recover/reconnect paths and non-retry behavior are
unchanged.

## Evidence

### Unit tests (RED -> GREEN)

`ui/src/app/session-placement-startup.retry.test.ts` restores a paused entry
at `10_000`, then retries at `20_000`, and asserts:

- the retried `startedAt` advances to `20_000` (the attempt clock resets), and
- the retried `initialTurn.createdAt` stays `10_000` (the message timestamp is
  preserved).

A rejected `sessions.send` rotates the message id on Retry. The delivery
suite's rejected-send cases (`rpc`/`error`/`timeout`) now assert the
accepted-message timestamp stays at `input.createdAt` (`1_000`) through the
rotated-id handoff — red with `Date.now()` (`1789779743055` vs `1000`),
green on this head. This is why `retry()` passes `entry.createdAt` and
`start()` resets `attemptStartedAt` to `Date.now()` itself, independent of
the message id.

The placement-startup unit suite stays **122 passed / 122**.

`ui/src/pages/chat/chat-progress.test.ts` adds a case where a live
`streamStartedAt` (`20_000`) must win over an in-flight submitted send's
message time (`10_000`): **122 + 27 = 149 passed** across the placement and
chat-progress suites.

### Placement E2E with before/after capture

`ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.cloud-startup-retry-timer.e2e.test.ts` drives a
real mocked-Gateway flow: a cloud startup stays in provisioning (first
attempt), fails, then Retry starts a second provisioning attempt. The browser
clock is driven instead of slept through — the system time is set five seconds
past the first attempt's start, then the retried attempt's label is read with
time frozen — so both readings are exact: `first === 5`, `retried === 1`, plus
the invariant that the retried attempt started its own clock at least five
seconds after the first (`retryStartedAt - firstStartedAt >= 5_000`).

- **RED** with the runtime-only split (no renderer change): fails at
  `expect(retried).toBe(1)` — `AssertionError: expected 6 to be 1` — the
  retried indicator keeps the first attempt's elapsed because
  `resolveWorkingProgress` selects the older queued message time.
- **GREEN** with this head: passes; the retried indicator starts over while the
  message timestamp is preserved.

Before/after captures from the green run (mock Gateway, no real credentials):

| State | Capture |
| --- | --- |
| First attempt, 5s in — elapsed counts from the original start | `01-retry-timer-before-first-attempt.png` |
| Retried attempt, 1s in — elapsed restarts near zero | `02-retry-timer-after-retry.png` |

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/evidence/provisioning-retry-timer/01-retry-timer-before-first-attempt.png)

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/evidence/provisioning-retry-timer/02-retry-timer-after-retry.png)

### Review follow-up: deterministic retry-timer regression

The P2 finding was that the browser regression slept 5.2s + 1.1s of real time
and asserted the retried attempt stayed under three seconds, so a slow runner
could fail a timer reset that actually happened. Both sleeps are gone and both
readings are now pinned with `page.clock.setFixedTime(...)`: `install()` alone
keeps ticking and `setSystemTime()` only shifts the clock, so either could let
a slow runner read `2s` from a correctly reset timer. Fixed time holds
`Date.now()` for each reading while timers keep running, so the startup path
still schedules its own work.

| | Before (sleeps) | After (fixed time) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Test duration | 9,887 ms | 4,050 / 4,611 ms (two consecutive runs) |
| Whole e2e invocation | 52.2 s | 45.9 / 46.1 s |
| Displayed readings | `retried < 3` (wall-clock dependent) | `first === 5`, `retried === 1` |
| Independent RED check | none | `retryStartedAt - firstStartedAt >= 5_000` |

RED/GREEN was re-measured with only the two production files reverted to
`main`: `AssertionError: expected 0 to be greater than or equal to 5000` — the
retried attempt inherits the failed attempt's start time (RED) — and the exact
head passes (GREEN).

### Review follow-up: attempt-start override scoped to placement retries (2026-09-28)

The previously reviewed filter dropped the queued message time for **every**
in-flight send whenever `streamStartedAt` existed, so an ordinary chat send
whose first render follows the stream start would lose its acknowledgment
wait from the elapsed timer. The override is now scoped to the placement
initial turn: `buildChatItems` passes the existing `initialTurnId` prop into
`resolveWorkingProgress`, and only that turn's `createdAt` is excluded when a
live attempt start is present.

- `chat-progress.test.ts` covers both directions at the unit level: the
  retried placement turn renders from the attempt start (`20_000`), while an
  ordinary send with the same timestamps keeps its message time (`10_000`).
- `session-placement-startup.retry.test.ts` adds a thread-build wiring test:
  a real retried placement entry renders its working indicator from the
  retried attempt start, and an ordinary in-flight send through the same
  renderer keeps counting from its message time.
- RED/GREEN: with the renderer reverted to the previously reviewed head, both
  ordinary-send assertions fail (`expected 10_000`, got `20_000`); the
  placement direction stays green in every variant. On this head all pass.
- The branch is merged up to current `main` (the Control UI deslop moved
  `resolveProgress` next to the queue selection; the override param rides
  along). 69/69 green across `chat-progress`, placement retry, and placement
  delivery suites on the merged tree.

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/app/session-placement-startup.{test,delivery,disconnect,reload,retry,stop}.test.ts` — **127 passed** (retry suite gained the wiring test)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/pages/chat/chat-progress.test.ts` — **26 passed** (gained the ordinary-send regression)
- Merged-tree run (2026-09-28, this head): placement retry + placement delivery + chat-progress suites — **69 passed / 69**
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.cloud-startup-retry-timer.e2e.test.ts` — **1 passed** (green) at `d6556788112`, two consecutive runs, 4.1-4.6 s per test; RED reproducibly on base production (`expected 0 to be greater than or equal to 5000`) and with the earlier rejected-send `Date.now()` variant
- `tsc -p tsconfig.ui.json --noEmit` on the touched files: no new errors (pre-existing `TS4094`/`TS2883` elsewhere are baseline)
- `oxlint` on all touched files: clean
- `git diff --check`: clean

Not tested: no real cloud provider / live Gateway was used; the E2E harness
exercises the mocked-Gateway placement flow only. The visual capture runs in
the same harness with `OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1`.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+25/-4` across `session-placement-startup.runtime.ts`
  (`+13/-1`), `chat-progress.ts` (`+11/-3`), and `chat-thread-build.ts` (`+1`)
- Test LOC: `+39` unit + `+114` E2E
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the runtime's existing `createdAt`
  plumbing and the `Date.now()` convention already used by persisted recovery;
  the renderer change narrows an existing candidate filter, preserving all
  prior `resolveWorkingProgress` behaviors verified by its suite.
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade
  impact: none.

prs.title: fix(matrix): show reasoning when explicitly enabled
prs.body:
Related: #81892

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Matrix users enabling `/reasoning on` receive only the answer even when the model supplies explicit reasoning.

## User Impact

Authorized reasoning appears as separate quiet `m.notice` messages without replacing the answer preview or consuming its first-reply target. Authorized inline `/reasoning on` and `/reasoning off` affect only that turn. Turning reasoning off stops unsent chunks; notices already accepted by Matrix remain visible. Matrix still does not display `/reasoning stream` updates.

## Why This Change Was Made

Matrix opts into the existing reasoning payload lane and consumes a new optional `onReasoningVisibility` callback. Core binds each payload to its producing turn's authorized policy, including inline overrides, session identity, cancellation and delivery lifetime. Matrix checks that exact payload before each HTTP send, after asynchronous preparation and DNS resolution, and on redirects/retries. It no longer reconstructs permission from stored settings or defaults.

The callback is additive; no configuration or storage schema changes are required. Same-value `/reasoning off` writes revoke an earlier inline `on`. Queued turns retain their own policy; mixed-participant batches cannot inherit another sender's reasoning authority. Reasoning-send failures preserve existing answer drafts and original partial-delivery evidence.

## Evidence

Seven current checks passed at `39b6c22bbd99`: the selected core presentation cases (3 passed, 51 skipped), Matrix transport cases (4 passed, 12 skipped), formatting for eight affected files, strict types over 43 affected roots, both scoped typed-lint groups, and the registered Gateway build.

Actual Gateway runs exercised authenticated Matrix SDK sync/ingress, canonical session policy and guarded Matrix HTTP delivery against task-owned loopback Matrix/model endpoints. Both observed runtimes produced one authorized quiet reasoning notice, zero reasoning sends after persistent same-session `off`, and two ordinary answers; both sessions finished `done`, inactive and `off`.

```text
Gateway runtime  authorized reasoning  revoked reasoning  answers  overall native result
Bun 1.4.3       1                     0                  2        FAIL (exit 1)
Node 24.19.0    1                     0                  2        FAIL (exit 1)
```

**Runtime shutdown qualification failed.** Both runs logged native server shutdown but did not close the Gateway/CLI naturally within 30 seconds and required forced cleanup. A separate Node startup/initial-sync/shutdown run, with no business turns or model requests, reproduced the failure: every logged native cleanup phase finished in about 858 ms, yet the actual Gateway remained alive at 25 seconds. The final referenced handle/process owner is unresolved. Neither Bun alone nor this PR's reasoning worker is established as the cause. Supervision ultimately joined all retained actors and the client worker count reached zero; this does not make the failed end-to-end runs pass. All original failed records remain preserved.

Encrypted rooms, an external Matrix/Element deployment, a live model provider and the reporter's deployment were not verified; reporter credentials were unavailable. The Gateway cases use persistent `sessions.patch` policy; inline producer behavior has separate owner-test coverage. Already accepted Matrix notices cannot be retracted. The additive public SDK callback remains a maintainer compatibility consideration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replay the requested 30 commits onto pinned main `5dfd7197827e3edb7513edf3377a768066110f8f`. Applied 29 commits; skipped `54049c82aba` (x7914 chat) because all eight files conflicted with newer main lifecycle/fixture ownership. Existing owners and current main behavior win.

Final diff: **+10,316/−14,179 test/support LOC (−3,863)** plus **eight obsolete mock-baseline lines removed**, across **66 files** (overall net −3,871). Production: **+0/−0**. Declaration counts below are static source declarations (including parameterized declarations), not expanded test counts. Fixture extraction/table consolidation can reduce declarations without deleting expanded scenarios.

## Evidence

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline`: passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --write <72 changed files>`: passed; no additional changes.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json <72 changed files>`: exit 0.
- `git diff --check 5dfd7197827e3edb7513edf3377a768066110f8f`: passed.
- Per operator CI-only instruction: **no local Vitest, check-changed, tsgo, coverage, or Testbox**. Local test wall time/CI seconds: not measured locally; hosted CI is the runtime proof.
- Required `openclaw/ci-gate` is the merge gate. Independent review runs during CI.
- No CODEOWNERS paths in this diff. No production UI changes or screenshots needed.

### CI repair

prs.title: docs(macos): explain the Bun local-network and Git prompts on first launch
prs.body:
Closes #175540

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: new macOS users get two unexplained prompts on first launch of the DMG install, a local-network request that names Bun and a request to install Git or the Command Line Tools.

## User Impact

User impact: the macOS onboarding page now says why each prompt appears, when it is safe to deny or cancel it, and how to enable it later. A short pointer is added to the macOS platform page.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway runs on the bundled Bun runtime (`apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/NodeMode/BundledRuntime.swift`) and advertises itself over Bonjour by default (`src/gateway/server-discovery-runtime.ts`, mdns mode `minimal`), so macOS attributes that local-network request to Bun. The Gateway still binds to loopback by default (`defaultGatewayBindMode` in `src/gateway/net.ts`), so a local-only setup keeps working if it is denied.

The Git prompt comes from the `git --version` probe in `ensureGitRepo` (`src/agents/workspace-git.ts`), which only runs for a brand-new workspace and silently skips `git init` when Git is unavailable. Per the triage note, Git is described as optional rather than adding a mandatory `xcode-select --install` step.

## Evidence

- `markdownlint-cli2` with `config/markdownlint-cli2.jsonc` on both files: 0 issues.
- `oxfmt --check` with `.oxfmtrc.jsonc` on both files: clean.
- `<Step>` open and close tags in `docs/start/onboarding.md` still balance (7/7).
- Not run: the docs link audit and MDX check, which need Node 22 locally. The only link added (`/start/onboarding`) already exists on the macOS page.
