prs.title: refactor: fold private single-consumer operations into owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Several internal modules exist only to turn one owner's facts into a one-use argument/result bag or re-export a private operation. This separates decisions from their actual callers and leaves tests coupled to those private seams.

## User Impact

No supported behavior, public interface or migration changes. Prompt bytes, link processing, channel authentication discovery, Slack/IRC behavior, hook discovery, TLS startup defaults, catalog normalization, systemd parsing, subprocess transport and Talk diagnostics remain with their existing owners.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep private implementations with their existing production operations and remove superseded modules, DTOs and exports. Reply preparation now builds its prompt envelope through lexical closures over the same current facts; link context application owns the existing guarded processor loop and final projection. Generic channel package-state probes replace three literal-key adapters. Slack's event registration and IRC's plugin adapters remain in their existing registration/plugin owners; the separately owned Slack assistant lifecycle remains unchanged. Existing tests enter the real preparation, context-application, generic probe and plugin boundaries rather than replacement test-only exports.

This is the lane's one coherent residue branch, eligible under the campaign's 300-line residue waiver. At signed head 53df8d709863b9e68b6df8bd5d47e0e7ad9f9c59 against bda0e040feccbb5d8da2660a9bd144cdad78e4fb, production changes are +1,433/-1,819 across 42 paths: **386 net production lines removed**. The complete change touches 77 paths. Moved implementations count as additions. Metadata changes remove exact orphaned assertion/mock/wrapper entries; no allowance grows.

The approval production fold was dropped after CI correctly rejected moving its three grandfathered casts to a new filename. Both approval production modules and their original allowance are now byte-identical to the base; the migrated 15-case safety suite still enters the real registration boundary. Sanitization, Unicode and wire bounds, external verification, decision normalization, and rejection before row/waiter creation remain intact. The unrelated public SDK presentation export remains unchanged. This intentionally gives back 25 net production lines rather than broaden the type contract for a small fold.

Doctor preflight keeps its rehearsal latch, repair planner and post-migration convergence sequence as closures in the existing operation. Shared recovery, measurement, admission, file-only recovery and integrity-check forwarding retain their existing owners. Degraded-plugin publication, deferred bookkeeping, refreshed snapshot reads, warnings and metadata invalidation retain their order.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None. No guard or supported behavior is removed. Preserve lazy runtime boundaries, live authorization and effect receipts, SSRF validation, content-free diagnostics, subprocess cancellation/backpressure/cleanup, read-only discovery, immutable catalog metadata generations, transport/body distinctions, prompt ordering, reset/provenance semantics and fresh admission-time context reads. No schema, retention, durability, configuration, protocol, dependency, public SDK or protected standalone session-memory backend change. Phase E, its factory, registry, expiry, federation and tests are untouched.

## Evidence

Current exact-head hosted CI is green: run39078236210 on53df8d709863b9e68b6df8bd5d47e0e7ad9f9c59 completed successfully, including all selected PostgreSQL, UI, prompt/media, typing, lint, ratchet and architecture lanes. The CI gate117533878264 and security-fast117529995986 pass. The170-check census contains no failed or pending check; two cancelled administrative context/auto-response jobs each have a successful counterpart on the same head, not a missing test suite. No CI rerun or synthetic push was used. Earlier-head failures and local proof gaps below remain historical evidence, not a claim that this PR repaired unrelated tests. Native preparation/merge admission must still verify the live head, security and review gates.

Each source slice received independent P0-P2 review. A fresh review of the seven-commit candidate is scoped-clean (0.92); the former approval append separately received scoped-clean review (0.98). The repair review correctly accepted the finalized-context fixture change but raised one ratchet finding based on comparing with the failing PR head rather than its base. That finding is rejected: the base already owns the restored presentation-file allowance, both production modules have zero diff against it, and the exact-base ratchet passes. No accepted/actionable finding remains. The simplification pass retains actual implementation/resource boundaries and removes only redundant internal surfaces; no compatibility shim, test-only production hook or new owner is introduced. Formatting and diff checks pass through normal signed commits.

The Doctor append received independent scoped-clean review (0.98); range comparison confirms its patch is unchanged by integration. Conflict repair preserves main's shared catalog coercion and vocabulary, consolidated Talk/IRC/Slack tests, removed duplicate empty-body logging, and source-captured cron-authority callback. The prompt-fold resolution received independent scoped-clean review (0.98). Its consolidated tests enter real reply preparation; the completed-audio fixture explicitly supplies the same transcript as session text, preserving all assertions. All nine replayed commits have verified signatures.

Whole-tree caller closure found two shared prompt fixtures still importing the retired envelope module. They now await the real reply-preparation owner through one standalone-compatible fixture, with real command, directive, conversation and typing factories. It preserves scenario metadata and canonical text without initializing unused model/auth/catalog state. The callers select the same prefixed and queued prompt bodies as before; no assertion or snapshot changes. Fresh independent P0-P2 review is scoped-clean (0.96), with final source verification complete.

Focused integrated-head proof initially stopped before tests on a misspelled suppression-test path. The corrected selection failed before collecting composition cases because this sparse checkout lacked QuickJS's package-local quickjs-wasi dependency (269.28 seconds Vitest, 320.76 seconds shard, 353.5 seconds wrapper; exit2). No selected case ran. The extension manifest is unchanged from the installed source and pins3.6.2; an absent-only link to the matching existing package dependency corrected that setup without an install or shared mutation. The qualified replay still stopped before cases because the sparse checkout omitted five preserved compiled script entries (448.21 seconds Vitest, 508.94 seconds shard, 530.3 seconds wrapper; exit2). These remain local setup gaps, not product-failure attribution or passing replays; hosted CI owns broad proof.

The repair's exact-base assertion-safety ratchet passes (2,592 files, 5,938 grandfathered assertions; 243.0 seconds wrapper). The required isolated one-worker suppression suite passes all 14 cases (123.16 seconds Vitest, 170.54 seconds shard, 227.6 seconds wrapper). The audio fixture now supplies `BodyStripped` on the actual finalized session context, not the raw transport-message field bag; assertions are unchanged.

### CI attribution for the superseded head

Run 39068575576 on 97a1bd50d50c507a6d29157f7346adf026641c03 completed with seven failed leaf jobs and the downstream aggregate. Two are PR-caused and repaired here: test-types-core-2 job117501793966 rejected the raw-message `BodyStripped` property; baseline-ratchets job117501532546 rejected the relocated cast allowance. The relevant UI tests are unchanged against their main baseline. The PostgreSQL test and owning storage sources are unchanged; shared catalog/subprocess dependencies were considered, so separation alone was not used as attribution. This records pre-existing failures, not a root-cause, flakiness, or repair claim. Aggregate117505584665 reflects those seven leaves.

### Prior repaired-head CI (historical after conflict replay)

Run39070446059 on0cba4d5fd0c9739397f4433e6a27c9ccf929f133 is complete. The two PR-caused checks now pass: test-types-core-2/117507407564 and baseline-ratchets/117507135878. This is a comparison of the real merge checkout, not the raw older branch against later main. Failed CI remains failed; no rerun, synthetic push, or optional gate waiver is claimed.

### Current conflict replay

The required suppression-only guard passes on current53df:14cases/onefile,129.27seconds Vitest/169.39seconds shard/190.4seconds wrapper, exit0. The duplicate summary is counted once. This is current-head suppression proof only; composition and the qualified lint/type/cycle graph remain for exact-head hosted CI as described below.

prs.title: fix: keep committed skills visible during reader startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Newly committed skills can appear unavailable when a reader opens during their first schema publication, preventing the reply from reaching inference.

## User Impact

Readers observe the committed skill library through the existing schema invalidation path. No schema migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Warm reader startup read retained schema facts before sampling their generation. A sibling commit between those reads could attach the new generation to old facts, retaining an absent-table result even while a native query returned the committed row. Sample the existing generation before adopting facts, preserving cold-open behavior and historical snapshot ownership.

The ordering originated in #167739 (`bb7d32e55d48`), whose body explicitly promises that stale adoption cannot overwrite the committed catalog. This preserves its shared admission design. The schema-generation lookup now lives with the other admission readers so the owner stays within its line budget.

## Evidence

The deterministic regression commits real sibling DDL at the admission-read boundary. Before the fix, the same reader returns the inserted row but incorrectly reports that its table does not exist. It passes after the fix. No assertions, retries, or timeouts were weakened.

Final validation: 121 focused tests pass across six schema, snapshot, worker, and native-observer files on Bun; three existing runtime-specific skips remain. Core and state-test type graphs, touched-file lint/format, line-cap and diff checks pass. Independent P2 autoreview reports no actionable findings.

The original Gateway E2E passed on the baseline, confirming the natural failure is intermittent. The final native Bun Gateway E2E passes (43.954s test body), and all 52 native schema tests pass on Node. The full runtime build passes. The deterministic owner regression, rather than a passing replay, establishes the fix.

prs.title: fix(workboard): finalize running execution on terminal status transitions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workboard dispatch slots could be permanently starved by stale execution state and uncleared dispatch claims, blocking follow-up work for the same owner agent.

Two related bugs caused this:

1. **Stale running execution on terminal transitions**: When a card left `running` status via `releaseClaim`, generic `updateCard`, `move`, or `reassign` (paths that don't pass an explicit execution patch), the execution record stayed `running`. The dispatcher's capacity predicate then counted the card as occupying the owner's slot indefinitely.

2. **Dispatch claim not released on lifecycle success**: `syncLifecycle` mapped the card to `review` and execution to `review` on lifecycle success, but did not clear `card.metadata.claim`. `workboardCardConsumesOwnerSlot` still counted the active (non-expired) claim against the owner's capacity, so the next ready card for that owner was blocked until the claim's TTL expired (30 minutes by default).

Closes #122911.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Fix 1: Finalize running execution on terminal status transitions only

`updateCard` (`store-core.ts`) is the shared owner for execution lifecycle. It already had logic to sync session keys, but lacked the symmetric finalization for execution status. The fix adds a finalization step: when a card transitions from `running` to a **terminal** status (`done`/`review`/`blocked`) without an explicit execution patch, the execution status is closed to match the card's terminal state. `done`/`review` are successful outcomes (attempt succeeds, `failureCount` resets); `blocked` is an explicit failure or abandonment path.

Non-terminal statuses (`todo`, `backlog`, `triage`, `scheduled`, `ready`) preserve execution occupancy so a worker moved aside can still complete successfully. The original broad condition (`status !== "running"`) incorrectly finalized executions for non-terminal moves, causing `completeDirect` to retain `blocked` on later successful completions (ClawSweeper P1 re-review).

The dispatcher's unguarded `card.execution?.status === "running"` capacity arm was removed — with execution now finalized at the owner, legacy stale rows no longer need a downstream guard.

### Fix 2: Release terminal review claims before capacity counting (ClawSweeper P1)

`syncLifecycle` (`store.ts`) is the lifecycle owner that transitions the card to terminal-for-dispatch status (`review`/`blocked`). The claim must be released at this boundary so the owner's slot is freed immediately, not after claim TTL expiry. Without this, `normalizeMetadata`'s fallback preserved the stale claim, and `workboardCardConsumesOwnerSlot` counted it against capacity.

The fix clears `card.metadata.claim` in `syncLifecycle` when the card transitions to any non-running, non-done status. `workboardCardConsumesOwnerSlot` (`store-constants.ts`) additionally excludes `review`/`blocked` claims as defense-in-depth, covering legacy rows where `syncLifecycle` did not clear the claim before this fix shipped.

### Production LOC delta

- `store-core.ts`: +19/-1 (execution finalization at the shared owner, terminal-only)
- `store.ts`: +15/-0 (claim release at the lifecycle owner)
- `store-constants.ts`: +7/-4 (defense-in-depth capacity exclusion)
- `dispatcher.test.ts`: +12/-4 (updated review-slot test)
- `dispatcher-ownership.test.ts`: +5/-2 (use non-terminal status for claim-expiry test)

Production: +41/-5 net +36 across 3 lifecycle owners. Tests: +703/-6 net +697.

Each change lives at its architectural owner — `updateCard` owns execution lifecycle, `syncLifecycle` owns claim lifecycle, `workboardCardConsumesOwnerSlot` owns capacity semantics. The terminal-only narrowing absorbs the ClawSweeper P1 finding without expanding the production surface: the broad `status !== "running"` condition and `finalizedExecutionStatus` ternary were replaced by a direct terminal-status check, keeping net production LOC proportional to the three owners repaired.

## User Impact

Workboard dispatch recovers immediately when a worker finishes or fails — no 30-minute starvation window. Follow-up cards for the same owner agent dispatch as soon as the lifecycle transition completes. Legacy cards with stale claims (from before this fix) also no longer hold slots. Moving a running card aside to a non-terminal status (e.g., `todo`) no longer corrupts the execution record — the worker can still complete successfully and the attempt is recorded as `succeeded`. This is a default-path fix: every operator using workboard dispatch was affected.

No config, API, default, protocol, or schema change; existing operator behavior is unchanged except that stale executions are now finalized and stale slots are released.

## Evidence

Linux, Node 22 (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` wrapper).

Rebased onto current main. The dispatcher's unguarded `card.execution?.status === "running"` capacity arm is removed at its canonical helper location in `store-constants.ts`, so both `dispatcher.ts` and `sqlite-store.ts` call sites are repaired in one change.

### Focused proof (two files, 46 tests)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher-ownership.test.ts \
    extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher-ownership-stale-execution.test.ts

 ✓ |extensions| extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher-ownership.test.ts (30 tests) 166ms
 ✓ |extensions| extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher-ownership-stale-execution.test.ts (16 tests) 180ms

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  46 passed (46)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 48.40s
```

### Full workboard suite — no regression

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/workboard/

 Test Files  19 passed (19)
      Tests  360 passed (360)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 53.70s
```

### Pre-fix failure proof (12 of the new tests fail on main)

```
$ git checkout origin/main -- extensions/workboard/src/store-core.ts \
    extensions/workboard/src/store.ts extensions/workboard/src/store-constants.ts
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher-ownership.test.ts \
    extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher-ownership-stale-execution.test.ts

Tests  12 failed | 34 passed (46)
[vitest] FAILED (exit 1)
```

Failures (grouped by invariant):

- `releaseClaim(status=done)` → execution stays `running` (expected `done`)
- `releaseClaim(status=review)` → execution stays `running` (expected `review`)
- `generic update(status=done)` → execution stays `running` (expected `done`)
- `move(status=done)` → execution stays `running` (expected `done`)
- Legacy `done` + running execution → ready card NOT started (persisted, SQLite boundary)
- Legacy `review` + running execution → ready card NOT started (persisted)

prs.title: fix(minimax): match CN host on a dot boundary for region detection
prs.body:
## Summary

fix(minimax): bind CN region detection to the `minimaxi.com` host on a dot boundary, so look-alike hosts such as `notminimaxi.com` no longer route web search to the CN endpoint

## What Problem This Solves

The MiniMax web search provider infers the region (`cn` vs `global`) from `MINIMAX_API_HOST` or the configured provider base URL, and picks the search endpoint accordingly (`https://api.minimaxi.com/v1/coding_plan/search` for CN, `https://api.minimax.io/v1/coding_plan/search` for global).

**代码证据**: in `extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.runtime.ts`, `isMiniMaxCnHost` used:

- `new URL(trimmed).hostname.endsWith("minimaxi.com")` — matches any host that merely *ends* with the string, e.g. `notminimaxi.com` or `evilnotminimaxi.com`.
- `trimmed.includes("minimaxi.com")` as the fallback for scheme-less values — a pure substring check that also matches look-alike hosts.

So a misspelled or maliciously crafted host like `MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://notminimaxi.com` was classified as CN, and search traffic (including the query and the `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header) would be sent to the CN search endpoint derived from that wrong classification.

Trigger condition: any host value that ends with the literal string `minimaxi.com` without being `minimaxi.com` or a subdomain of it.

## Root Cause

- Violated invariant: region inference is a security-relevant routing decision (it selects which endpoint receives queries and credentials), but the host check was a suffix/substring match instead of a dot-boundary host match.
- `endsWith("minimaxi.com")` has no label boundary: `notminimaxi.com`.endsWith(`minimaxi.com`) is `true`. The scheme-less fallback `includes(...)` is weaker still.

## Why This Fix

- Option A: keep `endsWith` but prepend a dot (`endsWith(".minimaxi.com")`). Handles the URL-parseable path but leaves the scheme-less substring fallback untouched.
- Option B (chosen): extract a single `isCnHostname` predicate — `hostname === "minimaxi.com" || hostname.endsWith(".minimaxi.com")` — and use it for both paths; for scheme-less values, prepend `https://` so only the host is inspected (never the path or query), and return `false` if the value still cannot be parsed.
- Not chosen: a regex over the raw string — duplicates URL parsing logic and still mixes host and non-host content.

## User Impact

- Affected scenarios: users setting `MINIMAX_API_HOST` or a provider `baseUrl` to a host that shares the `minimaxi.com` suffix (typo'd or look-alike domains).
- Before: such hosts were classified as CN and search requests were routed to the CN endpoint.
- After: only `minimaxi.com` and its subdomains classify as CN; everything else falls back to global.
- Behavior change: legitimate CN endpoints (`https://api.minimaxi.com`, `https://minimaxi.com`, `https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic`) are unaffected — still classified as CN.

## Real Behavior Proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** look-alike hosts sharing the `minimaxi.com` suffix were classified as CN, routing MiniMax web search to the wrong (CN) endpoint.
- **Real environment tested:** worktree `wt-minimax-cn-host-boundary` on latest `origin/main`, Node v24.19.0, importing the real `extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` via tsx and calling the exported `testing.resolveMiniMaxRegion` / `testing.resolveMiniMaxEndpoint` with `MINIMAX_API_HOST` set per case. No mocks of the functions under test.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  $ node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs minimax-cn-host-boundary.proof.mjs
  $ npx vitest run extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix (8/8 PASS):**
  ```bash
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://api.minimaxi.com -> region=cn
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic -> region=cn
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://minimaxi.com -> region=cn
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://api.minimax.io -> region=global
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://notminimaxi.com -> region=global
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://evilnotminimaxi.com/v1 -> region=global
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=notminimaxi.com -> region=global
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://example.com/redir?u=minimaxi.com -> region=global
  RESULT: ALL PASS
  ```

**Before (on main, same script, exit code 1):**

```bash
FAIL MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://notminimaxi.com -> region=cn (expected global), endpoint=https://api.minimaxi.com/v1/coding_plan/search
FAIL MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://evilnotminimaxi.com/v1 -> region=cn (expected global)
FAIL MINIMAX_API_HOST=notminimaxi.com -> region=cn (expected global)
RESULT: 3 case(s) show WRONG region/endpoint
```

- **What was not tested:** a live search request against the real MiniMax endpoints (requires valid credentials); the proof exercises the real region/endpoint resolution code paths end to end.

## Tests and Validation

- `npx vitest run extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.test.ts` — 23/23 passed, including new regression cases: apex CN domain still classifies as CN; `https://notminimaxi.com`, `https://evilnotminimaxi.com/v1`, scheme-less `notminimaxi.com`, `https://minimaxi.com.evil.com`, and a query-string-only mention all classify as global.
- `npx oxlint --deny=warn` on both changed files — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Before/after real-behavior proof logs are embedded above.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: unit tests on the real exported `resolveMiniMaxRegion` / `resolveMiniMaxEndpoint` (via the module's `testing` surface), with `MINIMAX_API_HOST` as the input vector.
- Target test file: `extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.test.ts`
- Scenario locked in: suffix-sharing look-alike hosts (`notminimaxi.com`, with scheme, with path, scheme-less) and non-host mentions (query string) never classify as CN, while the real CN hosts (`api.minimaxi.com`, apex `minimaxi.com`) still do.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: it pins the exact predicate that makes the routing decision, using the exact inputs that previously misclassified.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Node status/location work retains a separate queue for every retired pairing,
then sweeps those inaccessible queues on each current request.

## User Impact

Keep one status/location queue for the node's admitted pairing. Ordinary
same-pairing reconnects retain work; another pairing's read cannot consume it.
Existing TTL, deduplication, ordering, paging and baseline-status behavior remain.
Pairing removal still clears pending work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace nested pairing buckets and their retirement sweeper with one tagged
bucket. A different-pairing enqueue replaces the predecessor's advisory work;
reads, exact rollback and tagged clearing still require matching ownership.
The separate executable-action queue, authenticated connection checks, current
pairing checks and APNs/wake authority are unchanged.

This is the two-file node-pending AREA of the previously parked wider worker
bookkeeping family, not fresh discovery or a new residue branch. The qualified
production delta is +26/-67, 41 net lines removed; implementation and focused
local proof are complete. Exact-head CI is green. No protocol, config, SDK, schema, persisted shape, retention,
dependency, permission or durability change. Phase E session memory and its
factory, registry, expiry, federation and tests are untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- A different-pairing enqueue discards its predecessor's status/location work
  instead of retaining it for hypothetical later resumption. The original
  #109647 lifecycle matrix and visible comments do not cite a human actual-use
  need for inaccessible retired buckets. A valid current caller can request
  status/location again; pairing authority remains enforced.
- A retired enqueue that resumes just after the existing awaited authority
  check can replace newly queued advisory work. Existing post-wake rejection
  and exact rollback remain. The current pairing may need another request;
  this never grants executable-command, approval or APNs authority. No new
  fence or admission protocol is added for that recoverable timing edge.

## Evidence

The focused owner, RPC and real pairing-store removal invocation passed all
21 tests in three files: 498.46 seconds runner, 619.59 seconds shard and
628.86 seconds isolated wrapper, including completed-generation verification.
The TTL case remains and the existing replacement-pairing case is extended.
RPC mocks do not constitute live-device or APNs proof. Historical parked-family
results are not credited as current runtime, types, lint, review or CI proof.

intact owner/caller context files completed scoped-clean (confidence .98).

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Core tool names have separate catalog, factory-routing, and replay-safety inventories that can drift when tools change.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Tool descriptions, profile and group membership, factory selection, mutation classification, and replay permissions remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing pure, UI-safe tool catalog now owns factory and replay facts. Factory callers consume its derived descriptor list; the separate factory roster and duplicate replay-name sets disappear. Recorded-call replay and blind attempt retries remain distinct, including the existing PDF and skill-tool differences. Action-dependent mutation and replay decisions share one normalization and classification pass, while plugin owner declarations still take precedence.

This is the first area-sized slice of a widely imported descriptor owner. Activity presentation and subagent-policy projections remain separate follow-ups rather than widening this change's CI attribution.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None. This cut removes duplicate static facts and dispatch, not guards, authorization checks, features, or supported failure handling. No config, schema, protocol, dependency, or persisted-data changes.

## Evidence

Pinned-baseline parity passes for 82 tool names and 2,542 argument combinations, plus exact factory membership and all profile/group/launch-tool and capability-filtered catalog output.

Focused tests: 58 passed across tool catalog, tool mutation, replay safety, and embedded tool construction; all 14 lint-suppression checks passed. Targeted typecheck, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Runtime value cycles: zero; static import cycles: zero. Independent review found no actionable P0-P2 findings.

Two additional registration/Gateway catalog suites were attempted serially with one worker and isolated state. After ten minutes the loaded host was still compiling the Gateway worker, without a test result; the task-owned run was stopped (SIGTERM/143). This is incomplete local proof, not a passing result or evidence of a product regression. Exact-head PR CI must cover these boundaries; no timeouts, retries, skips, assertions, or baselines were changed.

Production delta: 191 added, 260 removed, 69 net lines removed. Tests: zero net lines. Broad proof belongs to PR CI on the exact submitted head.

prs.title: fix(ui): recheck placement stop authority after confirmation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Confirming a Chat cloud-placement stop can use permission and target facts captured before the dialog opened.

## User Impact

Confirmation cannot stop a replaced, busy, unavailable or newly unauthorized target.

## Why This Change Was Made

Immediately after confirmation and before placement pause/reclaim, sample current Gateway/session facts and reuse the existing placement policy. Keep this check at the effect boundary without a new lifecycle manager. No protocol, config or persisted-state change.

Net production LOC: 30 added.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None: this is a live-authority check, not speculative bookkeeping.

## Evidence

The test-only read-only-confirmation baseline failed because placement pause still occurred after permission revocation. The repaired eight-case table covers unchanged, read-only, method removed, replaced session, busy, offline device, new placement and removed row. Original operation assertions remain; no timeout, skip or retry added.

Fresh-main focused proof passed 27/27 in the complete placement file (172.69s Vitest / 220.78s wrapper; transform/import work dominates). Its official targeted UI test graph, exact-file lint/format, runtime cycles (zero) and diff checks passed.

The mandatory suppression file returned 13/14: the actual suppression allowlist passed, but its separate Git-list/no-directory-walk assertion observed a filesystem fallback. The helper falls back on a nonzero Git result; that original result was not retained, so its cause is unresolved. An isolated Node subprocess probe succeeded in 541 ms. The exact unchanged failed case then passed through the test wrapper (116.97s Vitest / 166.15s wrapper; 13 other cases unselected). This is not a repair or a load-only attribution. No helper, assertion, timeout, retry, skip or baseline was changed; the original local failure remains recorded for native review and exact-head CI remains required.

The fresh-main application is patch-identical to the independently reviewed retained fix. Its placement policy, runtime, stop-request and access-owner base blobs are unchanged; the current caller was personally rechecked. No visual markup, protocol, config, dependency or persisted-state change.

## CI fixture repair

The initial exact-head run 39070060614 found seven failures in the sibling worker-stop tests. Those fixtures called the header action without installing the selected session row that the production header supplies. The stop-local fixture now seeds that row through the existing pane state before invoking the same action. Every consent, request, ordering, failure and progress assertion is preserved; no production fallback, timeout, skip or retry was added. Focused serial replays pass: worker-stop 14/14 (45.79s Vitest / 72.11s wrapper) and placement 27/27 (97.17s / 129.94s).

The repair's targeted official two-test UI types, exact-file lint, runtime cycles (zero), mandatory suppressions (14/14; 66.35s Vitest / 94.32s wrapper), and diff check passed. The formatter initially rejected the helper signature layout; its mechanical correction and exact-file recheck passed. Fresh independent fixture-only review completed scoped-clean through P2, with no actionable findings. This does not resolve or relabel the earlier Git-list/no-walk failure recorded above.

The same initial run also failed Models E2E shards 1, 3 and 7. Each exactly matches scheduled main run 39066988478: the reconnect draft remains openai/failed-draft rather than openai/reconnected-model; replacement config retains fixture/previous rather than empty; both defaults-recovery variants show GPT-4.1 mini rather than GPT-4.1. These are historical inherited signatures, not a passing result or an exception for the repaired head.

## Repaired-head hosted result

Exact head b2706aaf8774d1c983bbd13c5952051b0b363b5b completed run 39073035700. The exact-head watcher returned GREEN/exit0, pending0. Full check-run enumeration has106 terminal records, no failed checks and no pending checks. The only cancelled records are superseded auto-response and PR metadata, not missing test suites. No inherited-failure exception, CI rerun or rebase was used. The historical local Git-list/no-walk uncertainty above remains recorded; native admission is still required.

## Post-merge integration repair

This PR merged as `195f85848cdf1d540e49df14f06b136a672bb87e`. Meanwhile, main's fixture consolidation in #175856 removed setup imports still referenced by the newly appended eight-case authority table. The conflict-free merge therefore left those tests failing before their assertions; production behavior was unaffected. The landed baseline reproduced all eight failures as `createSessionCapabilityFixture is not defined` (127.49s Vitest / 145.21s wrapper).

Direct main repair [`8dc9734028569ef2319973cd7bf81971c8738ee1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8dc9734028569ef2319973cd7bf81971c8738ee1) reuses the current shared `createPlacementPane` fixture with identical scope, method, client, selected row and assertions. It removes six net test lines and changes no production code. Placement and stop tests passed 41/41 (74.61s Vitest / 123.10s wrapper); targeted official UI-test types, lint/format, zero runtime cycles, suppression 14/14 (68.15s / 95.29s), diff checks and fresh independent P0–P2 review passed. Relevant owner/caller, guide and dependency blobs were unchanged on the fresh main base. The signed fix was pushed directly under the red-main policy and its remote ancestry verified. prs.title: fix(webchat): make voice transcript echo visible in WebChat/Control UI history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing recognized speech in saved user-message history when transcript echo is enabled for a voice note sent from WebChat/Control UI or a native chat client.

## User Impact

The approved transcript stays with the original user message after reopening history. The existing `tools.media.audio.echoTranscript` setting remains opt-in, with no new configuration or default change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway prepares the transcript through the existing selected-agent media runner, then passes the display text through the ordinary approval and canonical user-turn writer. The agent-facing speech remains machine-generated/untrusted, and synthesized speech is not promoted to slash-command input. Completed audio selections, including empty/failed/dropped outcomes, are reused by later enrichment without repeating that selection. Telegram's first-note mention preflight and outbound echo remain separate.

Transcription can precede the durable input acknowledgment. Declared `audio/*` client requests therefore wait on the captured connection by default; cancellation, disconnect, and explicit native deadlines remain available. This is not an unlimited agent-run timeout or a promise to terminate an already-running provider request/process immediately.

## Durable State

- Successful, approved speech becomes ordinary content on the existing canonical user message. Existing pending-input custody can hold the same enriched message while it waits for transcript commit.
- Embedded dispatch may capture the separate model-facing rendering in the existing optional `__openclaw.modelPromptProjection` metadata. This adds no new field contract, table, column, schema version, or persistence owner.
- Audio files and `media://inbound/…` references keep their existing format and lifecycle. Selection decisions and already-transcribed flags are request-local reuse state, not a new durable STT cache or job queue.
- No historical backfill or re-transcription is performed. Disabling the setting or rolling back does not erase already saved speech. Incognito retains its existing memory-actor behavior; attachment/CLI file lifecycles remain separate.

## Current Main Integration

Prepared head `5eeb132797fc2b8ed1ad8bb6da0736597a8b3a6d` incorporates main `1ae7b3c3590082865cc1bd6ba2bff20711c5eb33` through a signed merge, preserving incoming head `547532bde15cddd274c0b13f8be9a5480b695af1` and all contributor ancestry without a rebase or squash.

- Resolve three media-understanding conflicts while retaining main's removal of routine success diagnostics, guarded image-request handling, command-name simplifications, and compacted CLI-audio suite.
- Keep the PR's existing input-authority checks before provider upload, ffmpeg conversion, and CLI execution. Preserve the existing deferred admission-revocation regression in main's flattened test layout. The extracted conversion helper also retains main's removal of a redundant directory creation; no duplicate inline conversion owner is restored.
- Feature scope remains 26 files. Added/removed feature lines are unchanged in 22 paths; four paths are mechanically adapted to the current owners. There is no new configuration, default, schema, or public contract.

## Evidence

- Current prepared head: `5eeb132797fc2b8ed1ad8bb6da0736597a8b3a6d`; tree: `d44256349cbaeb239327c128e33cb2dad57876f9`. Signature, ordered parents, contributor ancestry, source scope, whitespace, and absence of unresolved entries were verified. The committed tree exactly matches the isolated tested and independently reviewed source.
- Secretless offline Linux Docker proof used the frozen lockfile with Node 24.21.0 and pnpm 12.11.1. `pnpm test src/media-understanding/runner.cli-audio.test.ts src/media-understanding/audio-preflight.attachments.test.ts src/media-understanding/runner.entries.guards.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 49 tests in three files; combined wall time was 267.96 seconds, including cold worker preparation and x86-64 emulation on the ARM host. No contributor runtime or tests executed on the operator host.
- Changed-file cost measurement: `pnpm test src/media-understanding/runner.cli-audio.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 26 tests in 176.42 seconds wall time, including 87.21 seconds of cold worker preparation plus transform/verification and emulation overhead. Current-head hosted CI seconds are not yet available; they are not inferred from this container run.
- Targeted formatting and lint passed for the four adapted files; the core TypeScript production check also passed. Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the complete 26-file feature delta reported no actionable findings. That review is patch-scoped; runtime proof is the separate isolated test execution.
- Fresh current-head [CI run 39082771267](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39082771267) was naturally triggered and is running. Current-head CI/security/bot results are not yet complete. This update does not claim all-green CI or merge readiness; the PR stays open and auto-merge is off.
- Incoming head `547532bde15cddd274c0b13f8be9a5480b695af1` had failed `ios-screenshots` and downstream `openclaw/ci-gate` in [CI run 38971050535](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38971050535). Those failures remain historical, are not attributed to main here, and are not represented as results for this refreshed head.

- [Operator-reported mobile/macOS/WebGUI acceptance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163557#issuecomment-6022733558) is separate from those transport receipts.

![Android voice transcript in the user message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw/669a7dfd1ec8576cc97f4e35fe579cccf7d73c72/proofs/voice-user-transcript-20261005/android-user-transcript.png)

prs.title: test(gateway): prevent cron placement live-test deadlock
prs.body:
Closes #174956

## What Problem This Solves

The `gateway-cron-placement` live test deadlocks after #165310 made a session-bound cron run wait for an in-flight session writer. The `HOOK_ROTATED` case paused an agent reply inside the hook, then forced the same cron job on the same root session to rotate its generation. The forced cron now correctly waits for that paused writer, while the writer only resumes after the cron run finishes, so the test times out instead of testing revocation.

This change keeps the production waiting contract and repairs the test:

- `HOOK_ROTATED` now rotates the root generation through a test-only Gateway RPC that writes from inside the Gateway process without entering the lifecycle fence.
- The stale reply hook still resumes against the old generation, so the test continues to prove that its delivery is rejected, its outbound effect is never sent, and the rotated root is retained.
- A new `HOOK_WAITS` phase explicitly proves the #165310 contract: with a real writer paused in the hook, a forced cron run is still pending after one second; after the writer is released, the cron run succeeds and rotates the root generation.

No production code or runtime behavior changes. The added RPC lives only in the existing live-test hook probe plugin.

## Why This Change Was Made

#165310 fixed a real corruption path by making a session-bound cron claim wait for another admitted writer. The old test encoded the pre-#165310 assumption that forcing cron could rotate the session while that writer was paused. Reverting or bypassing the wait would reintroduce the production bug, so the test needs to separate two concerns:

- Writer settlement: a forced cron run must wait for the in-flight writer and then complete normally.
- Generation revocation: a reply that resumes with an older session generation must be rejected before it can publish an effect.

Rotating the generation directly from the test process is insufficient because the Gateway does not observe that external store write as a generation change. The test probe therefore exposes `cronHookProof.rotateGeneration`, which uses the Gateway plugin runtime's session API to replace the entry in-process. That mutation is visible to the same generation checks used by the live run but does not exercise the lifecycle fence whose waiting behavior is now intentional.

The new helper also requires the expected previous session ID, so a concurrent generation change fails the test instead of silently rotating the wrong generation.

## User Impact

None at runtime. This restores a deterministic live regression test for cron session placement and hook-delivery revocation while preserving the safety behavior that prevents a cron claim from racing an active writer. Maintainers get one test that now covers both sides of the contract instead of timing out on the old assumption.

## Evidence

Local end-to-end proof used the production Gateway, cron scheduler, hook plugin, and a real OpenAI-compatible provider (`zte/Qwen3-235B-A22B`) with an isolated state directory. The local harness launched the built Gateway directly because this host's managed service-child test wrapper fails independently in the repository's own `test/test-live-service-child.live.test.ts` with `service child cleanup identity lost: native owner closed without kernel descendant extinction`; the committed live test itself is unchanged in how it launches the Gateway.

Successful run output:

```text
[proof] initial cron root=88fc3005-2d86-42a5-b87e-278ba0cbe09c
[proof] writer settlement: forced cron waited while HOOK_WAITS held the session writer
[proof] writer settlement: released hook completed; cron rotated root=28a8e4e1-6eda-4867-b6cf-0abd4c7f17d9
[proof] hook revocation: stale writer rejected; outbound effects=0; rotated root retained
```

The run verified:

- The forced cron run did not complete while the `HOOK_WAITS` writer was held.
- Releasing the hook produced exactly one allowed reply, and the cron run then completed with a new root session ID.
- Rotating the generation while `HOOK_ROTATED` was held caused the resumed reply to fail with `original session generation no longer accepts this delivery`.
- The revoked hook produced zero outbound effects, and the session row retained the rotated generation.

Static validation completed successfully:

```text
oxfmt --check 2 files: passed
oxlint 2 files: passed
pnpm tsgo:core: exit 0
git diff --check: passed
```

The live test continues to use the repository's normal OpenAI provider path in CI. The local proof substituted a reachable OpenAI-compatible provider and model only in a temporary copy of the harness.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Codex traced the deadlock through the #165310 writer admission change, inspected the cron placement and hook-delivery generation paths, implemented the in-process test rotation probe, and ran the real-provider proof plus oxfmt, oxlint, tsgo, and diff checks. The implementer understands the change: production must continue waiting for in-flight writers, while the test must rotate generation through an observable Gateway-side path and independently assert both writer settlement and stale-delivery revocation.

prs.title: feat(android): photo + voice note keep one message shape through send and transcription
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on Android, one message with a photo and a voice note looks different in each state. After sending, it shows a photo bubble plus a separate "See attached." bubble with a raw `voice-note-<uuid>.m4a` row. After transcription, the photo disappears and the text shows a literal `**[Transcription]**` marker with a quote block.

## User Impact

User impact: a photo + voice-note message keeps one shape after sending and after transcription. The photo stays when the history row carries loadable image data. The voice note is a compact "Voice note · 1:16" row. The transcript is a light quote under that row and is included in Copy / Select / Share / Reply. "See attached." no longer appears when it is the whole caption of an attachment message.

## Why This Change Was Made

- User bubbles that carry attachments drop the `See attached.` send placeholder only when it is the entire caption body (the sender synthesizes it only for an empty caption). A caption that merely starts with that text is the author's text and is kept. The wire format is unchanged.
- A `[Transcription]` / `**[Transcription]**` marker and the transcript after it are split out of the user text and rendered under the voice row, but only when the payload is the quoted (`>`) block or the turn carries a voice note. An authored `[Transcription]` heading over plain text, or a bare marker, stays ordinary text.
- The gateway's default echo format (`tools.media.audio.echoTranscript`, default `📝 "{transcript}"`), which is what a WebChat user turn carries after transcription (`See attached.\n📝 "..."`), is recognized too: a trailing `📝 "..."` block is split out as the transcript only when the turn carries a voice/audio attachment and the quote is terminated. Echo-shaped text without audio, or an unterminated echo, stays ordinary text.
- History rows: images are restored from canonical `__openclaw.media` facts when they carry inline base64 or a managed artifact; voice notes are restored from `__openclaw.media` audio facts (label, size, duration), since canonical rows omit `MediaPaths`/`MediaTypes`. Legacy `MediaPaths`/`MediaTypes` audio is still read and de-duplicated. `media://inbound/...` loading is left to #169470 and is not guessed at here.
- **Dependency:** with a gateway that offloads chat attachments, the history row for the photo is a `media://inbound/<file>` fact with no inline data. Rendering that photo after transcription / after a history reload depends on #169470 (Android loading of `media://inbound` images). Without #169470 this PR still renders the voice row and the transcript quote, but the photo is only kept when the history row carries inline data or a managed artifact.
- Only recorder-generated `voice-note-<uuid>.m4a` names show as "Voice note"; other file names are shown as before.
- Queued (offline) sends: the outbox bubble now uses the same shape as the sent bubble, instead of `item.text` plus raw `📎 <file name>` rows. The exact placeholder is dropped. The photo comes first, as a thumbnail decoded from that attachment's stored `outbox_attachment_chunks` (images only, up to 6 MB, through `ChatCommandOutbox.loadAttachmentBytes`), or a "Photo" row if the bytes aren't available. Then come the author's text and the "Voice note 0:05" row. This holds after an app restart, and recovery rows render the same way.
- Out of scope (split out of this PR): the adaptive collapse threshold (the shared 12-line / 700-char rule is unchanged) and the composer file-name chip change.

## Evidence

**Installed-app run (2026-10-17):** Android emulator (Pixel 7 Pro, API 35), Android app build of this PR's head with #169470 merged in, connected to a live test gateway built from current main plus open PRs, with a local Whisper speech-to-text model and the default `echoTranscript` format. The model behind the gateway is a local test mock, so the assistant replies are placeholders.

Voice input: the emulator has no working microphone, so the audio is a **pre-recorded spoken-English clip** (`spoken-clip-github-url.m4a`, text-to-speech, 7 s) attached through the app's real Files picker together with a gallery photo. It is not a live recording, so the row shows the file name rather than "Voice note".

| Composer | After transcription | After app restart |
|---|---|---|
| ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw/pr-assets-unified-msg/emulator-run-2026-10-17/01-composer-photo-and-clip.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw/pr-assets-unified-msg/emulator-run-2026-10-17/02-after-transcription.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw/pr-assets-unified-msg/emulator-run-2026-10-17/03-after-app-restart.png) |

| Message actions | Reply quotes the transcript | Link preview from the transcript URL |
|---|---|---|
| ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw/pr-assets-unified-msg/emulator-run-2026-10-17/04-message-actions.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw/pr-assets-unified-msg/emulator-run-2026-10-17/05-reply-quotes-transcript.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw/pr-assets-unified-msg/emulator-run-2026-10-17/06-link-preview-from-transcript.png) |

Checked on the device:
- After transcription the stored user turn is `See attached.\n📝 "Here is the photo from today. More details are at www.github.com"` with `__openclaw.media` facts for the `media://inbound/...jpg` photo and the `.m4a` audio. It renders as one message: photo, audio row, transcript quote, with no "See attached." and no raw `📝` marker.
- The photo is still there after transcription and after a force-stop and relaunch (history reload).
- Copy (pasted back into the composer), Select text, Share (the share sheet previews the transcript), and Reply (`> transcript`) all use the transcript text.
- `www.github.com` in the transcript is linkified and gets a link preview.

**Queued while the gateway is unreachable (2026-10-17):** same emulator setup. The app's network was cut with airplane mode; the shared gateway kept running. I attached a gallery photo, recorded a 5 s voice note with the in-app recorder, and sent it. prs.title: fix(zalo): handle unsupported inbound messages
prs.body:
Closes #175421

## What Problem This Solves

Zalo delivers direct messages with a link-preview card as `message.unsupported.received`. The monitor logged that event and returned without dispatching it or replying, so a schema-valid, authenticated DM could be silently lost even when Zalo included recoverable message text.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Unsupported events with non-empty `message.text` now use the same authorization, session, dispatch, and reply pipeline as ordinary text messages.
- When no text is recoverable, the event still passes through the existing Zalo authorization policy. Authorized senders receive one short notice asking them to resend the content as text or an image; blocked senders receive no fallback.
- The fallback reuses the existing durable webhook ingress, so transport replays with the same message ID do not send duplicate guidance.
- The change intentionally does not guess at attachment fields or claim recovery of a URL that the upstream payload may omit.

## User Impact

URL-bearing Zalo DMs are no longer silently dropped. If Zalo supplies text, the agent receives it. Otherwise the sender gets actionable resend guidance instead of no response, while existing DM policy and pairing behavior remain intact.

## Evidence

- Added a production-boundary webhook regression that first failed with zero dispatches/no fallback, then passed after the fix.
- Covered recoverable text, authorized no-text guidance across duplicate webhook replay, and blocked-sender fallback suppression.
- `pnpm test extensions/zalo/src` — 26 test files, 147 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — passed.
- `pnpm exec oxlint --type-aware` on changed files — passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on changed files — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

## AI Assistance

AI assistance was used for source analysis, implementation, and validation. The changes were checked against the issue's acceptance criteria and the complete Zalo test suite.

prs.title: fix: recover chat after a transient session subscription change
prs.body: Fixes #175915. ## What Problem This Solves A newly opened chat can remain on “session changed before sessions.messages.subscribe; retry the request” after its task has completed. The answer is saved, but history waits for a successful message subscription and never loads it automatically. Pressing **Retry** recovers the conversation without resending the task. ## User Impact Chat now recovers this specific transient subscription failure through its existing bounded retry. Once fresh subscription admission succeeds, the saved conversation becomes visible. Unsent input remains intact, and recovery does not submit another message. Access checks remain authoritative on every attempt. Permission denials, replaced connections, and obsolete chat selections still stop recovery. A persistent transient failure stops at the existing one-minute deadline and leaves manual Retry available. No configuration, permission, dependency, or protocol change is required. ## Why This Change Was Made The Gateway correctly rejects subscription admission when the selected session identity changes while access is being checked. Its structured response uses `INVALID_REQUEST` with the `SESSION_MUTATION_AUTHORIZATION_CHANGED` detail code. The chat reader previously recognized only request timeouts and retryable `UNAVAILABLE` responses, so it treated this recoverable read as terminal. The correction accepts that exact structured error only for the matching `sessions.messages.subscribe` method. It reuses the subscription owner's existing retry, cancellation, and history-admission behavior. Other invalid requests and mutations retain their existing handling. ## Evidence The current-main regression failed at the actual subscription/history boundary: subscription resolved false and the saved history read did not begin. The equivalent synthetic browser scenario showed the Retry banner and no completed answer. The corrected candidate passed 61 focused tests across six files, including successful history admission after the structured error, unchanged timeout recovery, the one-minute deadline, disposal/selection invalidation, and rejection of denied or unqualified errors. All selected compiler groups, changed-file lint/format, and the UI localization check passed. The synthetic browser scenario passed: the completed answer becomes visible automatically, the error disappears, and `chat.send` remains unused. The browser case took 14.44 seconds in Vitest (16.17 seconds through the test command); the six-file test batch took 5.94 seconds. Before/after captures are retained and inspected. The complete recording is inspected and attached below; the virtual retry clock is disclosed. Independent engineering review is clean. Exact-head ClawSweeper reports Gold readiness/proof, Platinum patch quality, and no findings. Live Team deployment is outside this PR’s verified result. The first CI run identified the assertion allowance made obsolete by removing the cast; this PR shrinks that entry. Its separate pane-visibility render-count failure remained unreproduced in isolated pinned-Bun runs: 20 cases pass on both the candidate and original base. That check passes on the corrected head. [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39080779958) retains two inherited failures, plus their aggregate: the placement tests added by #175843 omit imports for `SessionCapability` and `createSessionCapabilityFixture`. The exact upstream revision 195f85848cdf1d540e49df14f06b136a672bb87e reproduces both compiler diagnostics and all eight runtime failures, with 19 controls passing. This PR leaves those files unchanged; their separate repair is #175942. Other selected checks, including this change’s recovery coverage, pass. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![A session change error and Retry button hide the completed conversation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c19d454-78e6-424d-a4bf-d75b557c41b5) | ![The saved answer appears automatically and the read\-only composer remains unchanged](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d8647f08-8f34-4695-914f-7f547697fa28) | ### Open conversation and recover automatically \(virtual retry clock\) https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a1b26e19-dcc8-456f-a393-57779e052689 ### Visual verification - Baseline: 32820c2618f75b51383f34678b28a5332c5c8ac4 - Exact head: `3a6c3d0e8c503a4d5654d4099f8d3823d1fb6962` - Scenario: Open the Task estimates conversation after a transient subscription identity change\. The same saved answer loads without pressing Retry or resending the task\. - Runtime/build: Production UI built from carrier 4d4bb877026da9c7a6716117ca9f76dbb354d0ac, source tree 54a94bd07232d10333ba4cd17aef9f80669a9316 \(6918beb7\)\. Current head changes only the assertion\-baseline entry; all runtime, fixture and dependency inputs are identical\. Synthetic Gateway and virtual retry clock\. - Saved answer visible: Before: 0; after: 1 - Error banner after recovery: 0 - Messages resent by recovery: 0 chat\.send calls - Real production chat UI with the existing synthetic Gateway wire harness - Original base fails at history admission; corrected scenario passes - Matched 1280 by 900 screenshots inspected - All 45 recording frames inspected across two complete contact sheets; original 1\.8\-second recording preserved - The retry clock is virtual; no live latency or Team deployment claim

prs.body:
Closes #173396 Related: #171106 ## What Problem This Solves - Problem: with `channels.telegram.richMessages: true`, the Telegram formatting contract ended with `structured bullets=
  • (not literal bullets)`. The model writes that HTML into the reply, Telegram renders it natively, and every other client shows the tags: Control UI deliberately escapes authored HTML (#13937 / #13952), so one stored reply is readable in Telegram and littered with `
      `, `
    • `, ``, ``, and `` in Control UI. - Solution: the contract now asks for Markdown for ordinary lists, bold, italic, inline code, and links, and reserves HTML islands for what Markdown cannot express (checkbox tasks, `
      `, tables with caption/span attributes, `tg-*` islands, block media). New replies only; stored transcripts are untouched. - What changed: `extensions/telegram/src/agent-prompt.ts` (the rules), `docs/channels/telegram/rich-messages.md` (authoring contract), plus regressions in `extensions/telegram/src/channel-actions.contract.test.ts`, `extensions/telegram/src/rich-blocks.test.ts`, and `ui/src/components/markdown.test.ts`. - What did NOT change: HTML island support in Telegram, Control UI's HTML escaping, caption handling, and the rich-block renderer. ## Why This Change Was Made - Best fix: change only the authoring contract. Both renderers already accept Markdown lists — `markdownToTelegramRichBlocks` maps `- item` to a native list block, and Control UI renders `- item` as a list — so no renderer change is needed and Telegram output stays native. - Alternative: teach Control UI to render Telegram-authored `
        `; rejected, because the issue explicitly keeps the deliberate HTML escaping of #13937 and the escaping is the security boundary for authored text. - Risk / non-goals: the contract applies to every turn delivered to the account, so rich media captions also stop asking for HTML bullets (that is #171106's symptom). Checkbox tasks, `
        `, span tables, and `tg-*` islands keep their HTML form, so no Telegram-only feature is lost. ## User Impact A reply written for Telegram now reads the same in Telegram and in Control UI, and new transcripts stop carrying HTML list markup that another client shows as literal tags. Existing transcripts are unchanged. ## Evidence Before/after through the shipped renderers, same reply text (bold + inline code + link): ```text Control UI (ui/src/components/markdown.ts, toSanitizedMarkdownHtml) before, model-authored HTML: "
          \n
        • Option A: Run example --check.
          • …" -> "

          Here are two options:

            element after, Markdown: "- **Option A:** Run `example --check`.\n- **Option B:** See [the docs](https://example.com/docs)." -> "
              \n
            • Option A: Run example --check.
              • \n
            • … the documentation
              • \n
            " Telegram rich blocks (extensions/telegram/src/rich-blocks.ts, markdownToTelegramRichBlocks) after, Markdown reply -> [{type:"paragraph",text:"Here are two options:"}, {type:"list",items:[{blocks:[{type:"paragraph",text:[{type:"bold",text:"Option A:"}," Run ", {type:"code",text:"example --check"},"."]}]},{blocks:[{type:"paragraph",text:[{type:"bold",text:"Option B:"}, " See ",{type:"url",text:"the documentation",url:"https://example.com/docs"},"."]}]}]}] plain text: "Here are two options:\n• Option A: Run example --check.\n• Option B: See the documentation." ``` The contract itself, through the exported plugin (`telegramPlugin.agentPrompt.inboundFormattingHints`): ```text before: "…Collapse=`
            ` (not expandable blockquote); structured bullets=`
            • ` (not literal bullets)." after: "Ordinary lists, bold, italic, inline code and links = Markdown (`- item`, `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `` `code` ``, `[label](url)`): Telegram rich blocks and Control UI both render it, while authored HTML shows up as literal tags in Control UI." "Collapse=`
              ` (not expandable blockquote); HTML `
                `/`
                  ` only for checkbox tasks." ``` ```text vitest extensions/telegram channel-actions.contract + rich-blocks -> 45 passed (45) vitest ui/src/components/markdown.test.ts -> 29 passed (29) negative control: new contract test against the pre-fix rules -> 1 failed (old "structured bullets" rule) oxfmt --check / oxlint / git diff --check -> clean ``` What was not tested: no live Telegram account in this environment, so no real send or caption capture; the Telegram path is exercised through the shipped renderer and the exported contract, and the CLI/Control-UI side through the shipped markdown renderer. The fix changes only the authoring contract — no stored transcript is migrated or re-rendered. ## AI Assistance 🤖 This PR is AI-assisted.
