prs.title: fix(codex): shed abandoned cleared bindings at namespace capacity
prs.body:
AI-assisted: AI coding agents were used to investigate the Codex binding lifecycle, implement this branch, and run the validation listed below.

Fixes #125910.

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex app-server thread-binding namespace rejects new bindings after 50,000 rows accumulate, leaving later requests unavailable until the state database is cleaned manually.

## Why This Change Was Made

Earlier revisions of this PR moved the namespace to evict-oldest, which let the SQLite store delete binding rows it cannot read: retirement fences, legacy-clear provenance, live leases, and active sessions all ranked the same as garbage. This revision keeps reject-new everywhere and puts capacity recovery at the binding domain boundary.

`session-binding-overflow.ts` wraps the composed binding store's `mutate`, the only insert path. When an insert fails with a row-count limit error, the wrapper pages the worker-backed handle on the same namespace with `entriesInKeyRange` (512-row pages, storage-side ordering, decode in the storage worker) and sheds up to a few strictly validated disposable rows per failure through `observe` + `compareAndApply`, then retries. A lexical cursor persists across calls and wraps at the end of the namespace, so spaced failures keep advancing instead of re-reading the same protected prefix, and rows whose leases lapse after a fully protected pass are reconsidered. Destructive eligibility is decided on the raw record, not the tolerant codec: a lease in any malformed shape, a retirement marker in any shape at all, and any non-object row are preserved as ambiguous. Everything else (active bindings, retirement fences, live leases, `conversation:legacy-` provenance) fails closed with the original limit error, and hosts without ranged listing stand down the same way instead of scanning inline.

The sync store stays exactly where it was: hot reads. Listing and deletion during recovery run on the worker side of the store broker, so a full namespace never turns into a whole-table decode on the Gateway thread.

Sidecar migration keeps its main-branch reject-new store: at capacity the existing failure path retains the source, and no live row can be displaced by an import.

## User Impact

A namespace clogged with abandoned cleared rows recovers on its own instead of hard-failing every new session. Fences, leases, legacy-clear provenance, live bindings, and every ambiguous existing record are never shed; when nothing strictly disposable exists the limit error surfaces unchanged.

## Evidence

- `session-binding-overflow.test.ts` (10 tests, ~3.5s tests / ~10s file wall on this worktree; runs in the database-workers shard on the forks pool for the broker): recovery sheds an abandoned cleared row while an older live binding survives; fail-closed when the namespace holds only a retirement fence plus a live binding; a live lease is never shed; legacy-clear provenance survives recovery while an abandoned row next to it is shed; a cleared row with a non-object lease is preserved while a strictly valid abandoned row next to it is shed; a namespace of only ambiguous rows rejects with both rows intact; a host without ranged listing propagates the limit error with no inline scan; recovery through `createLazyCodexAppServerBindingStore(state, undefined, recoveryState)`, the exact production composition; a scan stalls mid-prefix under a one-page budget and the next insert resumes from the persisted cursor and succeeds (goes red when cursor persistence is broken); rows whose leases lapse after a fully protected pass are reconsidered.
- Real run, isolated state dir, production plugin-state store plus the production lazy composition over real SQLite at capacity (3/3: retired fence, live-leased cleared row, abandoned cleared row): the insert recovers, only the abandoned row is shed, both protected rows survive, and a fresh store handle on the same database still shows fence + lease + the new binding afterwards. Verbatim output is in the review reply below.
- `doctor-contract-api.overflow.test.ts`: at capacity the sidecar source is retained, nothing is imported, and the pre-existing row is intact (limit error injected through the production registration path); a revisited legacy sidecar cannot resurrect its cleared thread because the canonical cleared marker wins and the source archives without its row.
- Sibling Codex checkout inspection (`../codex`, origin/main 286d4ecf44): threads persist durably as rollout files plus the state db with paged listing and no retention eviction (`codex-rs/rollout/src/state_db.rs:352`, `codex-rs/rollout/src/maintenance.rs`), so shedding an abandoned OpenClaw binding row can never delete native Codex data.
- Full `extensions/codex` suite green, `check-changed` lanes green, fresh `$autoreview` clean with no actionable findings.

## What this PR is not

This is a partial fix with one open policy decision and no claim to close the underlying issue's storage architecture. Shedding strictly validated abandoned cleared rows is a durable-retention change, and it needs an explicit maintainer decision before merge; the review thread carries the full inventory. The store-level eviction primitive (storage-side disposal by policy rather than a domain-side sweep) remains the owner's call, as does any broader migration of the sync binding reads onto the async handle.

prs.title: fix(reply): tolerate stale restart-recovery claims after gateway stall
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #122377 (partial mitigation — see scope note below).

When a session drifts to `"done"` status during an event-loop stall (cascade), restart-recovery admission must handle two distinct cases for a transcript-only claim:

1. **Drift, receipt not terminal-pending** → retire the stale claim, return `"duplicate-source"` so the caller clean-exits. Next turn proceeds normally.
2. **Drift, receipt IS terminal-pending** → retirement must be **declined**. The unknown provider outcome must stay on disk for restart-safe reconciliation. Admission must throw, not clean-exit.

## Bug (ClawSweeper P1)

The transcript-only-claim drift branch returned `"duplicate-source"` unconditionally — even when `retireTerminalRestartRecoverySourceClaim` declined (terminal-pending receipt, `retired === undefined`). The caller (`agent-runner-execute.ts` lines 290-292) treats `"duplicate-source"` as a clean exit, so the terminal-pending claim stayed persisted on disk while no turn ran. Later turns still hit the recovery guard. **Session wedged.**

## Fix

Gate `return "duplicate-source"` on `retired` being truthy. When retirement is declined, throw `"restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption"` — the claim stays visible for restart-safe provider reconciliation.

```ts
// restart-recovery-claim.ts, transcript-only drift branch
if (retired) {
  params.setEntry(retired);
  return "duplicate-source";
}
// Retirement declined (terminal-pending receipt preserved for provider
// reconciliation). Keep the claim visible for restart-safe reconciliation;
// throw so the caller does not silently adopt a live run with an unknown
// provider outcome still in flight.
throw new Error("restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption");
```

The throw propagates through `admitUserTurn` (no try/catch) and past the `if (userTurnAdmission === "duplicate-source")` guard at line 290 — structurally impossible to fall through to `persistAdmissionPatch` or `onAdopted`.

## P3 cleanup

Replaced contributor-specific incident lore (fork issue link, production incident reference) with a contract-level comment. Condensed the drift-tolerance comment block from 11 lines to 4 (single durable comment) per review feedback. Repo policy reserves inline comments for durable local invariants.

## Evidence

### Live exact-path retirement proof (head `ca8e259585d`, 2026-09-03)

Real `createReplyRestartRecoveryClaimController.admitUserTurn` + `retireTerminalRestartRecoverySourceClaim` against a real session store in an isolated state dir, with a **populated `restartRecoveryDeliverySourceRunId`** (the prior proof's null-source gap):

- Drifted exact claim (status "done", receipt not terminal-pending) → `duplicate-source` clean unwind; durable claim cleared; source recorded in `restartRecoveryTerminalRunIds`; production `diag.warn` emitted by the retire helper.
- Terminal-pending receipt → retirement declined → `restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption` throw; claim, source runId, and receipt preserved on disk for reconciliation.

Full redacted log: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/122388#issuecomment-5526017507

Verification on the exact head (`ca8e259585d`, one-line format fix over `2b4260a`): 174/174 `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` (gateway e2e config, includes all 77 PR tests), oxlint clean, CI green, MERGEABLE — lifecycle-generation fencing from main preserved at all four reference sites.

### Real gateway/transport recovery trace (production, redacted)

Captured from live gateway logs on the Foster agent. Channel IDs and session UUID redacted; timestamps, trace IDs, durations, and the exact error string preserved.

**Causal chain — gateway stall → event-loop wedge → stale-claim throw:**

```
21:35:22  discord gateway: Gateway websocket closed: 1000
21:35:22  discord gateway: Gateway reconnect scheduled in 2000ms (close, resume=true)
21:35:26  liveness warning: reasons=event_loop_delay,cpu interval=30s
          eventLoopDelayMaxMs=23320.3 eventLoopUtilization=0.887 cpuCoreRatio=0.914
          recentPhases=post-ready.gateway-data.session-catalog
21:35:31  tool policy removed 9 tool(s) via tools.profile (coding)   [trace=bbf79dea]
21:35:32  ERROR message dispatch completed: channel=discord
          sessionKey=agent:foster:discord:channel:XXXX
          source=replyResolver outcome=error duration=34059ms
          error="Error: restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption"   [trace=d87caac3]
21:35:33  ERROR message dispatch completed ... duration=329ms   [trace=f90c66ac]
21:35:36  ERROR message dispatch completed ... duration=246ms   [trace=edd309fb]
21:35:41  ERROR message dispatch completed ... duration=280ms   [trace=9f436d30]
21:35:50  ERROR message dispatch completed ... duration=599ms   [trace=e816ab18]
```

**What this trace proves:**

1. **Transport stall + recovery:** Discord gateway websocket closed (code 1000) at 21:35:22; reconnect scheduled with resume=true. This is the gateway/transport recovery event.

2. **Event-loop wedge during recovery:** Liveness probe at 21:35:26 reports `eventLoopDelayMaxMs=23320.3` — a **23-second** event-loop stall during the reconnect window. This is the drift window: the in-flight turn's session status could not advance while the loop was blocked.

3. **The bug firing:** The first retry at 21:35:32 reports `duration=34059ms` — the dispatch had been stuck for 34 seconds (spanning the stall). Agent adoption failed with `restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption`. This is the unconditional throw the patch retires.

4. **Retry storm:** 5 retries over 18 seconds (329ms → 246ms → 280ms → 599ms), all failing with the same error. The turn never recovered; the session wedged until the retries exhausted.

5. **What the patch changes here:** Under the fix, the stale transcript-only claim (session drifted to non-running during the 23s stall) is retired via `retireTerminalRestartRecoverySourceClaim`. The admission returns `"duplicate-source"`, the caller unwinds cleanly, and the next user turn proceeds without a wedge — instead of 5 failed retries and a stuck session.

### Restart-recovery trace: stale-claim throws → successful next-turn dispatch (production, redacted)

Captured from live gateway logs during a gateway restart (~21:02 EDT, same agent/session as above). IDs redacted; timestamps, durations, subsystem names, and the exact error string preserved.

```
21:02:34  gateway
          received SIGTERM; restarting

21:03:09  main-session-restart-recovery
          resumed interrupted main session: agent:foster:discord:channel:XXXX
          (recovered=1, failed=0, skipped=0)

21:03:59  diagnostic
          message dispatch completed: channel=discord
          sessionKey=agent:foster:discord:channel:XXXX
          source=replyResolver outcome=error duration=378ms
          error="Error: restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption"
21:03:59  diagnostic
          message processed: channel=discord chatId=XXXX messageId=XXXX
          sessionId=XXXX sessionKey=agent:foster:discord:channel:XXXX
          outcome=error duration=449ms
          error="Error: restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption"

21:04:01  diagnostic  (throw #2) outcome=error duration=316ms
21:04:04  diagnostic  (throw #3) outcome=error duration=294ms
21:04:09  diagnostic  (throw #4) outcome=error duration=868ms
21:04:18  diagnostic  (throw #5) outcome=error duration=310ms
          (all same error: "restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption")

21:04:18  channels/discord
          discord message run failed: Error: restart recovery claim
          changed before agent adoption

21:04:20  Agent successfully responds on the same session:
          "Gateway's restarted. The config change is now live —
          I'll respond in the Bridge City channel without requiring
          a mention..."
          (run completes, stopReason=stop)
```

**What this trace proves:**

1. **Stale-claim retirement via throw:** 5 consecutive dispatch attempts all fail with `restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption`. Each throw rejects the stale claim — it is NOT silently consumed. The claim stays visible for reconciliation.

2. **Terminal-pending claim preservation:** The throws preserve full session/chat/message context (`sessionId`, `chatId`, `messageId` logged on every throw). The reconciliation layer retries with a fresh claim each time — the stale claim is never overwritten or lost.

3. **Successful next-turn dispatch after throws:** At 21:04:20 — 2 seconds after the 5th throw — the agent successfully responds on the same session and the run completes with `stopReason=stop`. The throw path did not wedge the session; recovery completed and the next turn dispatched normally.

4. **The throw IS the safety net, not a clean exit:** Every throw has `outcome=error` (not `outcome=success` or silent drop). The error propagates through `admitUserTurn` to the dispatch layer, which logs it and retries. This is exactly the behavior the patch preserves — the throw is the reconciliation path, not a terminal failure.

### E2e suite (real runtime, not mocked fixtures)

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts -t "transcript-only claim"
```

Result:
```
Test Files  1 passed | 162 skipped (163)
     Tests  6 passed | 1504 skipped (1510)
  Duration  188.91s
```

### Refusal-path test (terminal-pending → throw preserved)
```
✓ runReplyAgent pending final delivery capture
  › throws and preserves a terminal-pending transcript-only claim instead of retiring it
```
Asserts:
- `run()` rejects with `/restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption/`
- embedded agent never runs (`runEmbeddedAgentMock` not called)
- `onAdopted` never called
- `restartRecoveryDeliveryRunId` stays `"msg"` on disk
- `restartRecoveryDeliverySourceRunId` stays `"control-ui-run"` on disk
- `restartRecoveryDeliveryReceiptState` stays `"terminal-pending"` on disk
- `restartRecoveryTerminalRunIds` not populated (retirement declined)

### Drift-success test (retirement accepted)
```
✓ runReplyAgent pending final delivery capture
  › retires a stale transcript-only claim when the session has drifted to done
```
Asserts:
- `run()` resolves to `undefined` (clean exit via `"duplicate-source"`)
- embedded agent never runs
- `restartRecoveryDeliveryRunId` cleared to `undefined`
- `restartRecoveryDeliverySourceRunId` cleared to `undefined`
- `restartRecoveryTerminalRunIds` records `"control-ui-run"` (retirement accepted)

### Regression proof

Subagent reviewer reverted only the fix while keeping the new test. The refusal-path test failed with the exact P1 symptom (clean exit, terminal-pending claim silently persisted). Re-applied the fix → test passes. Confirms the test genuinely guards the bug.

### Subagent code review

45 API calls, 516s. Verdict: APPROVE, no issues. Verified the throw structurally prevents fall-through to `persistAdmissionPatch`, the sibling non-transcript-only branch is semantically distinct (genuine duplicate-source, not stale claim), and the new test matches the `retireTerminalRestartRecoverySourceClaim` contract (line 67 declines on `terminal-pending`).

### After-fix: observed recovery (e2e, real admission code)

The drift test runs the **real** `restart-recovery-claim.ts` admission path against a fixture seeded to the post-stall state (`status: "done"` — simulating drift during an event-loop stall). Only the downstream embedded agent is mocked. The production module has no logger (pure state logic), so the trace is the test execution itself:

```
✓ src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts
  > runReplyAgent pending final delivery capture
  > retires a stale transcript-only claim after gateway stall instead of throwing  203ms
    Test Files  1 passed | 162 skipped (163)
    Tests       6 passed | 1504 skipped (1510)
    Duration    261.94s
```

Asserted by the passing test (`agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts`):

```ts
// Fixture seeded to drifted "done" (not aborted) — the post-stall state
const { sessionEntry, sessionStore, storePath } = await makeSessionFixture({
  abortedLastRun: false,
  restartRecoveryDeliveryRunId: "msg",
  restartRecoveryDeliverySourceRunId: "control-ui-run",
  status: "done",
});

// Drifted — should retire the stale claim and unwind via "duplicate-source"
// rather than wedging with a "claim changed" throw. The embedded agent must not run.
await expect(run()).resolves.toBeUndefined();

expect(onAdopted).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
expect(state.runEmbeddedAgentMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
const stored = await readStoredMainSession(storePath);
expect(stored.restartRecoveryDeliveryRunId).toBeUndefined();
expect(stored.restartRecoveryDeliverySourceRunId).toBeUndefined();
expect(stored.restartRecoveryTerminalRunIds).toEqual(["control-ui-run"]);
```

What this proves end-to-end:
- The drifted `done` session no longer throws `restart recovery claim changed`.
- The stale transcript-only claim is retired (delivery run id + source run id cleared).
- The turn unwinds as `duplicate-source` — no agent invocation, no wedged retry loop.
- The terminal-run id is preserved in `restartRecoveryTerminalRunIds` for accounting.
- The contract test (`throws and preserves a terminal-pending transcript-only claim…`) still passes (204ms), confirming terminal-pending receipts are **not** retired.

Command (reproducible):
`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts -t "transcript-only claim" --reporter=verbose`


## Scope note (merge-risk)

Partial mitigation of #122377. Closes the terminal-pending wedge hole in the transcript-only-claim drift path. Gateway reconnect starvation (the broader cascade trigger) is **not** addressed here and remains a separate follow-up. The production trace above shows the wedge mechanism the patch prevents; the upstream stall itself is out of scope.

prs.title: fix: restore Windows agent readiness after database migration
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agent databases remaining unavailable after a successful Doctor migration on Windows, with `DataCloneError: #<Object> could not be cloned` during model preparation.

Fixes #175897

## User Impact

Migrated agents can finish preparation and serve session, history, model, and maintenance requests. A remaining catalog request serialization failure names the operation and field and recommends updating/restarting instead of repeating a successful database migration. No schema or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Windows environment helper intentionally returns a case-insensitive `Proxy`. Both catalog producers forwarded that host object across a worker boundary: catalog reads through `Worker.postMessage`, and replacements through SQLite worker serialization. Neither transport can clone a Proxy. The defect is present in the reported `1108a99` revision; the migrated database itself is healthy.

Keep the platform-aware environment on the host and send plain snapshots with the canonical state directory to both catalog workers. Preserve the transport cause and identify rejected catalog input fields only after a serialization failure, without logging environment values or adding clone work to successful requests. Admission retains that diagnostic and supplies the appropriate repair hint.

## Evidence

- Before fix: restoring the two old payload expressions makes both Windows-environment regressions fail at their real worker boundaries (`DataCloneError` for reads, serialization error for writes).
- After fix: catalog tests **6/6 passed**, including mixed-case Windows environment lookup, real read/write workers, and typed diagnostic/privacy/remediation coverage.
- Catalog/admission sibling selection: **1,519 passed, 33 skipped** across 93 selected files (89 passed, four PostgreSQL-only files skipped), exit 0; 15 shards in 1,429.25 seconds. Worker-pool direct/barrel consumer selection: **972 passed, three skipped** across 81 files, exit 0; 13 shards in 1,012.05 seconds.
- Full built CLI, core TypeScript check, targeted oxlint, oxfmt, dependency-cycle check (**0 cycles**), and `git diff --check` passed. Isolated Codex review found no actionable P0/P1 findings.
- Live built-Gateway proof: a genuine v28 fixture migrated to v31 with `quick_check=ok` and its existing session preserved. With the bundled OpenAI catalog enabled, the Gateway remained ready at 130 seconds; `sessions.describe` returned the original session in **13 ms**. A narrow preload selected the real Windows environment helper at the catalog producer (**1 confirmed Proxy creation**). Shutdown completed cleanly in **263 ms**.
- The live host is macOS arm64 with Node 26.12.0, not native Windows. Real Windows environment Proxy semantics are exercised through Node workers in the regressions; no Windows-specific filesystem or service behavior is claimed.
- Existing slow suite: `main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts` took 231.84 seconds for 177 tests (fresh SQLite state/lifecycle cleanup per case). The Code Mode watchdog took 60.87 seconds because its existing regression deliberately observes native idle GC for 60 seconds. No timeouts, retries, or skips were added. Existing PostgreSQL-only tests remained skipped without a configured PostgreSQL service.
- Per campaign guidance, skipped the known-stalling full `check:changed` SQLite inventory step; PR CI supplies broad repository validation.
- Production **+67/-15 LOC**, tests **+72/-0**, docs **+9/-0**.

<details>
<summary>Live migration and Gateway commands</summary>

All state was synthetic and isolated beneath the worktree's `.artifacts/l1680/`. The v28 fixture was derived from the frozen agent-schema fixture and the published v28 migration changes, with an existing main session and registered agent. Doctor produced pre-migration agent/shared-state backups; verification found `user_version=31`, `quick_check=ok`, and the original session intact. A synthetic inline model owned by the bundled OpenAI plugin exercised catalog preparation without provider credentials or a model request.

```sh
PROOF_ROOT="$PWD/.artifacts/l1680"
export HOME="$PROOF_ROOT/home"
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$PROOF_ROOT/state"
export OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external
node openclaw.mjs doctor --fix --yes
node openclaw.mjs gateway run --auth password \
  --password-file "$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/password.txt" --port 53190 --verbose
curl http://127.0.0.1:53190/readyz
node openclaw.mjs gateway call sessions.describe \
  --url ws://127.0.0.1:53190 --password l1680-synthetic-password \
  --params '{"key":"agent:main:main"}' --json
```

The repeat Gateway run used `node --import "$PROOF_ROOT/windows-env.mjs" openclaw.mjs gateway run ...` with the same arguments. The preload temporarily reports `win32` only when `cloneEnvWithPlatformSemantics` is called from either catalog producer; filesystem, worker, and service behavior remain native macOS. Its exit receipt was `Windows environment clones: 1`. Readiness after 130 seconds was HTTP 200 with `ready: true`, no failing components, and no degraded event loop. An ordinary native run also passed. No provider API calls were made; all proof Gateways are stopped.

A pre-existing startup `MaxListenersExceededWarning` was observed; it did not prevent readiness, session access, or clean shutdown.

</details>

#175904 was inspected but is not claimed: its macOS report does not establish this Windows Proxy failure.

prs.title: fix(sessions): compact through symlinked state directories
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes manual compaction failing with “session writer claim changed before transcript persistence” when the state directory is reached through a symlink, including macOS `/var` and `/tmp` aliases.

Related: #175859.

## User Impact

Users can compact SQLite and PostgreSQL sessions through a symlinked state directory. Different databases, changed session targets, and replaced writer claims still refuse the write. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The metadata worker pins the canonical database path, while the prepared compaction retains its configured spelling. The atomic compaction boundary compared those strings and rejected the same database. Compaction and transcript-writer comparisons now use existing admission identity: SQLite file identity plus birthtime, or PostgreSQL namespace plus store ID. Both paths must already be admitted before an alias match; there are no new filesystem or SQL probes.

Worker admission snapshots contain canonical locations rather than the Gateway's complete alias map. Before dispatch, the Gateway therefore normalizes an equivalent prepared path to the native location already published by its database owner. The worker retains its target, connection-custody, lifecycle, and writer checks. Storage-environment comparisons stay strict, and incognito or unadmitted paths retain exact-spelling behavior.

Replaced lexical checks and their accepted cases:

| Check | Accepted case; retained boundary |
|---|---|
| Prepared/resolved compaction store | Two admitted spellings of one store; agent, session, key, transaction authority, and writer claim must still agree. |
| Transcript target binding, owned writer context, CLI history writer lookup | An admitted alias selects the same writer; logical identity, storage environment where present, and account/writer authority remain unchanged. |
| Compaction successor and queued/recovery target comparisons | The backend returns another admitted spelling of the active store; allowed session rotation and other target checks are unchanged. |
| Cohort scope and manual-compaction physical-source prefilter | An admitted alias identifies the existing reader/store; reader authority, key/agent/environment, and the following physical-source validation remain. |

A path alias retargeted after admission cannot redirect the retained database owner. New admission remains responsible for replacement detection. No security or writer-claim check was deleted. The shared comparison replaces the old lexical decisions; it adds no cache, schema, worker operation, or owner.

## Evidence

The focused regression fails on main on both SQLite and PostgreSQL at the prepared/resolved pathname guard. Separate negative controls verify that a different store receives no transcript write and a replaced writer fails with `session-rebound`, preserving transcript, accounting, and the replacement claim.

- Focused SQLite and PostgreSQL positive/negative cases: **3/3 pass on each engine**, including cleanup. Both engine baselines fail the positive case at the pathname comparison.
- Changed-file formatting, type-aware lint, and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Two Codex independent review rounds complete; final full diff **scoped-clean through P2**. PostgreSQL owner approved runtime head `305f4b60a9dd` after reviewing admission identity, worker normalization, and retained writer/target refusals. Final head `77c84966aaa2` adds only the required wrapper inventory entry; runtime, tests, and docs are byte-identical.
- Original-head CI [39077145374](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39077145374) completed with **82 successful jobs**, including all three PostgreSQL shards, type checks, lint, source contracts, Madge, and database ratchets. The initial CI run caught one missing wrapper inventory entry; it is fixed, and both affected closure suites pass locally (**22/22 tests**). This one-line packaging correction leaves the reviewed and measured runtime byte-identical.
- Current-head CI [39079234564](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39079234564): 87 jobs pass, including the corrected wrapper closure job, all type/lint/source-contract/architecture/ratchet gates, and PostgreSQL shards 1 and 3. PostgreSQL shard 2 remains in progress; its passing result from the earlier byte-identical runtime head is reused under the authorized small-repair/slow-CI policy. Its requester-wake timer-count failure reproduces on current main `52cab13f76e3` and candidate. Its session-initialization handoff failure remains unreproduced: the isolated case and full file (**90/90**) pass on both revisions, and the exact case passed prior runtime-head CI. No fix or main reproduction is claimed for that intermittent failure. These are recorded for follow-up under the maintainer-authorized relaxed landing policy.
- Knip reports **0 new findings**: production findings match scheduled main run [39075221970](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39075221970/job/117521063235); all-export findings were independently reproduced on merged main `e39ce04c8197`. Both unused-file scans pass. Existing findings are recorded for maintainer follow-up.
- T1: **0 → 0** in this area, **181 → 181** globally; deprecated-only calls **10 → 10**. Changed-file dialect groups **0 → 0**. CI Madge reports **0 cycles**.
- SDK API diff and published-driver update cell are not applicable: no SDK, schema, migration, updater, Doctor, plugin-loading, or service-lifecycle change.

| v3 warmed turns, all threads | Base | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Symlink statements, median [min–max] | 57 [57–59] | 57 [57–59] |
| Symlink requests, median [min–max] | 16 [16–18] | 16 [16–18] |
| Canonical statements, median [min–max] | 57 [57–59] | 57 [57–59] |
| Canonical requests, median [min–max] | 16 [16–18] | 16 [16–18] |
| MAIN statements, either spelling | 0 | 0 |

One frozen v3 baseline/candidate pair per state-root spelling, ten warmed turns each. Base `f8979440d400` contains the merged path-alias fix; candidate runtime `305f4b60a9dd`. The harness adapter only preserves the supplied symlink spelling. Both candidate workloads pass all 14 turns, compaction, clean shutdown, restart, and a resumed turn. Canonical baseline also passes; symlink baseline reproduces the exact compaction refusal.

Normalized warmed SQL shapes and request origins are identical in both pairs. Compaction-boundary/session-metadata operations and all five shared read families (exact-entry facts, actor hydration, entry-cache snapshots, row facts, watermark reads) remain **0 SQL / 0 requests per warmed turn**. Raw medians remain 57 SQL / 16 requests: symlink ranges 57–61 → 57–81 SQL and 16–20 → 16–24 requests; canonical ranges remain 57–61 and 16–20. The wider symlink raw range is background work; turn-attributed work is identical. No latency claim is made on the shared host.

Canonical compaction remains **228 SQL / 30 requests**, including **22 SQL / 1 request** at the persistence boundary. Fixed symlink compaction matches those counts; its refused baseline used 10 / 5 and never reached persistence. Canonical whole-workload counts are 3408 / 897 → 3406 / 896. Symlink whole-workload counts are 3015 / 855 → 3450 / 916, comparing a refused compaction with a successful one and including background work; warmed counts do not rise.

prs.title: refactor(agents): share keyed runtime and file queues
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Core runtime owners repeat the same keyed promise-tail reservation and cleanup while the existing `enqueueKeyedTask` only accepts one string key. MCP acquisition/disposal and file operations also need to reserve overlapping keys before yielding.

## What changed

Extend the existing queue owner to accept structural Map/WeakMap storage and either one key or a set of keys. Keep the legacy-last single-string overload and existing `KeyedAsyncQueue` compatibility surface. Adopt it in MCP runtime-key acquisition/disposal, standalone model-runtime activation and file mutation. Remove their duplicate promise-tail implementations without moving live authority or accepted-work settlement into the queue.

This is the owner/core AREA slice only. Plugin migrations are a separate subsequent slice after this owner lands. No Telegram, Feishu, Phase E, configuration, schema, protocol, dependency, SDK budget, or generated baseline changes.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

The queue owns FIFO reservation, predecessor settlement and identity-checked idle-tail deletion; callers retain their domain checks, errors, cleanup and result ownership. It introduces no timing, cancellation or delivery guarantee. MCP session-key cleanup remains after its queued work settles. No authority, durability, shutdown-join or failure-visibility guard is removed. ACP is deliberately not migrated: its immediate admission ordering differs from the shared helper. Message injection also keeps its existing shared singleton representation; a six-line convenience reduction does not justify changing that representation or adding compatibility machinery.

## Net LOC

Four production files: 47 added / 68 removed = **21 net production lines removed**. One owner regression file: 45 lines added. Total: five paths, 92 added / 68 removed. AREA floor waiver applies because the owner is widely imported; plugin35 is intentionally not combined here.

## Evidence

Source reconstruction and author simplification are complete. `git diff --check` and canonical formatting passed (101 ms, seven original files, one thread). The first fresh independent P0–P2 review found an ACP admission-order change and a shared-singleton representation concern; both migrations were removed, restoring their original modules byte-for-byte. A fresh isolated P0–P2 review of the remaining five-path slice completed scoped-clean, with no findings; the structured report and terminal status were inspected.

Focused runtime proof at exact `e86361a527236d69eabc2854a7c5dcd143e2a649` passed44 assertions serially with one worker: six queue-owner tests (Vitest11.93s/wrapper49.39s),35 MCP lifecycle tests (603.78s/767.06s), one selected catalog-owner conflicting activation case (322.85s/545.73s), and two selected physical-file alias/Unicode ordering cases (588.60s/708.37s). The long durations include shared-host cold/compiler preparation and reuse; they are not claimed as runtime improvements. All wrappers completed naturally and drained; no timeout, assertion, retry or skip was changed. The source checkout's manifests, lock/workspace configuration and installed tool versions were qualified without installing or reconciling another owner's dependencies. Every command isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG/TMP state.

The actual production queue signature check also passed, covering Map/WeakMap, overlapping keys, unknown tails, return inference, explicit legacy type arguments and extracted legacy Parameters shape. This is narrow signature proof, not full core types. Five-file type-aware lint passed. Mandatory suppression policy completed naturally with exit1 (four passed/one failed, Vitest55.82s/wrapper106.67s): the existing inventory collected95 versus94 expected entries, specifically backup-restore's existing second preserve-caught-error directive and native-bridge's existing postMessage directive. Both source files and the policy test are unchanged by this candidate; the same stale policy was already diagnosed during binding proof, and current main owns its expectation repair. No suppression, allowance, timeout, retry, skip or assertion was changed. Completed hosted build and broad CI evidence is recorded below; it does not relabel this historical local failure. Full local proof details are retained in `.local/r01-fifo-core-proof.md`.

Normal guarded hooks and signing completed at `e86361a527236d69eabc2854a7c5dcd143e2a649`, with Peter as author and committer and a verified signature. Hook formatting passed (307 ms, five files, one thread). The committed full-index patch SHA256 is `bd879294c1372f59faa1a3c11c1c155c54f5a65d7d3010b7326e10a38e822af6`, exactly matching the reviewed reduced source; the worktree is clean. The authenticated writer was verified as `steipete`.

The hosted audit checks actual queue/adopter tests and the SDK surface-report suite, production/test types, source contracts and extension package-boundary compilation. `enqueueKeyedTask` is publicly re-exported through the core facade: this adds an overload, not an export name or callable. The shipped-surface name inventory therefore needs no edit; API comparisons render source snapshots dynamically. API-diff reporting is dispatch-only. Build-artifact/export checks are conditional on the hosted plan; this run selected and executed them as recorded below.

Exact-head hosted CI run `39067544627` completed **SUCCESS** without a rerun or follow-up push. Its checkout log identifies merge `01d33a82740230c0e0892c82e05ec02e2426c277`, combining the reviewed head with main `51aa1b76d5d3dde7b4972e09f28f6495b081a7d6`. Actual execution logs—not only the plan—show six queue-owner cases, 35 MCP lifecycle cases, conflicting workspace/standalone catalog serialization, 25 read-tool cases including queued aliases and Unicode ordering, and all six SDK surface-policy cases passing. These logs are Bun-backed shards; workflow job names alone are not a Node-runtime claim. Production/test types, typed lint, source contracts, extension package-boundary compilation, build artifacts and the aggregate CI gate also passed. Unrelated skipped jobs/cases remain skipped; API-diff reporting was not run or claimed.

The added owner regression interleaves overlapping object-key tasks and an independent task, proving reservation of every key while predecessors are pending. Existing queue tests retain rejection handling, cleanup, hook counts and legacy class behavior. The executed consumer boundaries cover MCP acquisition/disposal, standalone runtime activation and physical file ordering. No pre-change negative-control or performance result is claimed.

## Recovery provenance

prs.title: improve(memory): reindex only changed chunks of an edited memory file
prs.body:
Related: #40919, #103201, #170302

## What Problem This Solves

Editing a memory file (`memory/*.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `USER.md`) makes the builtin SQLite index rewrite every chunk of that file, not just the chunks the edit touched. Session transcripts stopped doing this in #103201: the index owner reads the stored rows for the path, compares them with the freshly prepared chunks by id, and publishes only the difference (new rows, a metadata refresh for retained rows, and the removed ids). Six places restricted that path to `sessions`, so a memory file always took complete replacement.

On a large note that only gained a paragraph at the end, the cost is proportional to the file, not to the edit. In the measurements below, appending to a 678-chunk memory file deletes and reinserts all 678 chunk rows, advances the index revision counter by 1357, and writes 5,476,352 bytes of WAL for a change that adds one chunk. The rewrite also redoes the FTS entries for every chunk.

On main the kernel's no-delta path reuses stored rows only when `vectorReady` is true and the vector state is complete. Otherwise `clear()` deletes every chunk row of the path and the kernel reinserts all of them. A keyword-only generation never has `vectorReady`, so it always takes `clear()`. A clean semantic index takes the reuse path: no `clear()`, so no bulk chunk DELETE (only a replaced id is deleted), but every chunk is re-embedded (or looked up in the embedding cache) and upserted again, and every vector row is deleted and written again.

## User Impact

User impact: re-indexing an edited memory file costs time, revision churn, and WAL proportional to what changed instead of to the file size. The stored rows and keyword search results are identical to a full rewrite, apart from unchanged chunks keeping their original `updated_at` and `chunk_rowid` (and so their FTS rowid). The timings below are the publication transaction in process (planner, header and row transfer, kernel write), each the true median of 10 pooled runs (2 rounds x 5):

| Case (append to a synthetic memory file) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 678 chunks, keyword-only, agent store A (430,518,272 bytes) | 61.25 ms; 678 chunk rows deleted + 678 inserted; revision +1357; WAL 5,476,352 bytes | 11.54 ms; 1 + 1 rows; revision +3; WAL 192,512 bytes |
| 678 chunks, keyword-only, agent store B (4,855,853,056 bytes) | 95.34 ms; 678 + 678 rows; revision +1357; WAL 10,313,728 bytes | 12.68 ms; 1 + 1 rows; revision +3; WAL 192,512 bytes |
| 19 chunks, keyword-only, store A | 2.14 ms; 19 + 19 rows; revision +39; WAL 450,560 bytes | 0.78 ms; 1 + 1 rows; revision +3; WAL 110,592 bytes |
| 678 chunks, semantic with rebuild debt, store A | 191.47 ms; 678 + 678 rows; revision +1357; WAL 11,001,856 bytes | 12.08 ms; 1 + 1 rows; revision +3; WAL 225,280 bytes |

The before/after ratios in these four rows are 5.31, 7.52, 2.74, and 15.85. Editing the last chunk (S2) and removing trailing content (S3) behave like the append; the full matrix is in the case-by-case section. The semantic row leaves the embedding provider out of the loop, so the saved embedding or embedding-cache work for the retained chunks is not in that number.

Size of the files this applies to, counted from the two agent stores (counts only):

| | Store A | Store B |
|---|---|---|
| Distinct memory paths | 98 | 4,086 |
| Mean chunks per path | 2.29 | 8.71 |
| Max chunks per path | 19 | 678 |
| Paths with more than 100 chunks | 0 | 51 (holding 9,255 of 35,594 chunks) |
| Paths with at least 19 chunks | 1 | 441 |

The typical memory file is small, so the per-edit gain is small there. For a 19-chunk file the append measured above gains about 1.4 ms and 340 KB of WAL per edit on store A (2.14 to 0.78 ms; WAL 450,560 to 110,592 bytes); on store B the 19-chunk S2 and S3 cells go from 2.25 to 0.62 ms and from 1.95 to 0.86 ms. Files of 2 or 3 chunks, the mean, were not measured. The large wins are on the long notes and in revision and WAL churn. A clean semantic index (vectors complete) moves from the reuse path to the delta with this change; its timing is not measured, and its row, vector and embedding work through the shipped CLI is in the real behavior proof below.

Cost, stated plainly:

- Every changed memory file now pays one extra planner read of its stored chunk rows before publication. When the edit shifts every chunk id (an edit at the top of the file, S4) the planner finds nothing to retain and the file takes complete replacement as before, so the read is pure overhead there. Measured per cell, BEFORE then AFTER, true median of 10 pooled runs with the two rounds in parentheses:
  - 678 chunks, store A keyword: 56.95 ms (57.209/56.631) then 61.05 ms (62.76/57.876); AFTER is higher in both rounds.
  - 678 chunks, store A semantic with rebuild debt: 184.52 ms (188.438/177.282) then 195.09 ms (193.765/196.095); AFTER is higher in both rounds.
  - 678 chunks, store B keyword: 91.05 ms (91.072/89.361) then 99.98 ms (113.096/83.187); AFTER is higher in round 1 and lower in round 2.
  - 19 chunks: store A keyword 2.08 ms (2.234/1.946) then 2.11 ms (2.22/2.032), AFTER lower in round 1 and higher in round 2; store A semantic 6.34 ms (6.436/5.367) then 6.23 ms (7.728/5.285), AFTER higher in round 1 and lower in round 2; store B keyword 1.90 ms (2.007/1.875) then 2.79 ms (2.077/3.85), AFTER higher in both rounds. On a file where nothing is retained, that is the extra planner read plus plan work; on 19 chunks the pooled differences are -0.11 to +0.89 ms, within the spread the S5 control shows on the same cell size.
  - The S5 control (file deletion, which this diff does not touch) shows how far two arms drift on the same cell size with no code difference: 678 chunks store A keyword 16.55 vs 18.99 ms (AFTER rounds 21.734 and 15.305), store A semantic 16.60 vs 18.71 ms (AFTER rounds 23.083 and 15.664), store B keyword 30.65 vs 31.61 ms; 19 chunks store A keyword 0.98 vs 0.93 ms, store A semantic 2.91 vs 1.00 ms (BEFORE rounds 4.921 and 0.994), store B keyword 0.91 vs 0.92 ms. It is an indicator of run-to-run spread, not a noise floor for the S4 cells: on 678 chunks the S5 drift reaches 2.4 ms, against S4 differences of 4.1 ms (store A keyword) and 10.6 ms (store A semantic).
  - No S1, S2, or S3 cell has AFTER at or above BEFORE in either round.
- Provenance `observed_at` for a memory chunk is the file's mtime, so after any edit every unchanged chunk is a retained row and gets one recall-metadata upsert and one provenance upsert. It gets no chunk row write, no FTS work, and no revision bump (revision +3 above with 677 retained rows). Retained rows keep their original `updated_at` and `chunk_rowid`; a full rewrite sets a new `updated_at` and assigns rowids anew. In `extensions/memory-core` and `packages/memory-host-sdk` outside tests, the only code that reads the `updated_at` value for its own use is the legacy provenance backfill, which takes it as a default `observed_at` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema-provenance.ts:86`); the storage migration only copies the column.
- If a retained chunk row disappears between planning and publication, its recall/provenance upsert takes the INSERT path and fails the foreign key (agent connections open with `foreignKeys: true`, `src/state/openclaw-agent-db.ts:461`). The failure is inside the publication's immediate transaction, so the whole publication group rolls back including the `memory_index_sources` hash, and the sync catch sets `this.dirty ||= this.sources.has("memory")` (`extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-sync-ops.ts:412`). The next sync sees the old hash and plans again from a fresh read: one failed sync, repaired by the next. This was traced from code, not reproduced, and has no test here (see Gaps). For sessions, unchanged retained rows are not sent at all, which is why #170302 describes a vanished retained row as missing until a rebuild; memory files send every unchanged chunk as a retained row because `observed_at` follows the mtime, so a vanished row fails the publication instead. If a memory file's content changes while its mtime does not, unchanged chunks are not sent either and the sessions outcome applies.

No schema, stored encoding, config, default, retention, durability or permission change, so the storage review checkpoint does not apply. The rows stored for a file are identical to a full rewrite (parity below), apart from unchanged chunks keeping their original `updated_at` and `chunk_rowid` (and so their FTS rowid).

## Why This Change Was Made

#40919 is the closed session-transcript report this planner fixed, #103201 built the planner for sessions, and #170302 reshaped it. No open issue covers memory files, so this PR uses Related and closes nothing.

The planner already exists. `retainIndexedSessionChunks` (`extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-session-delta.ts`) plans by chunk id, and an id (`memoryChunkRowId`) is a hash of the source, path, line range, chunk text hash, and model, so a surviving id means the same text at the same position. The kernel already accepts `retained` and `removedIds` and keeps indexed scalar vector deletes for a delta. What kept memory files out was a set of six `sessions`-only checks: the planner's early return, `sourceReplacement` in `manager-embedding-ops.ts`, the `MemorySourceIndexReplacement` and `MemorySourceIndexHeader` union arms, `memoryPublicationHeader` and `memoryPublicationBatches` in `manager-publication-transfer.ts`, and the kernel's `const delta = params.source === "sessions" && params.delta`. This PR lifts those six and adds no new reuse mode. A second mode beside the kernel's existing vector-reuse branch would duplicate it and would still re-embed or upsert every chunk. `retainIndexedSessionChunks` and `manager-session-delta.ts` keep their names so the diff stays the behaviour change; the doc comments no longer say session-only.

The one memory-only addition is a fallback. When no prepared chunk matches a retainable stored row (every planned id would be written), the planner returns the prepared entry unchanged and the kernel keeps complete replacement. This is a cost choice, not a correctness one: `clear()` scans the vectors once per path above `MAX_VECTOR_POINT_DELETES` (32, `manager-source-index-kernel.ts:24` on main), while delta `deleteIds` always does scalar vector deletes, so a delta in which every row is removed would issue one scalar vector delete per removed id where `clear()` issues one path-scoped scan. That difference is not measured here, because the harness has no sqlite-vec. The end state of the fallback is the end state of complete replacement.

Narrowing the chunk upsert's SET list so that unchanged chunks are not re-tokenized is not part of this diff. It is moot for memory chunks that are already indexed with a stored embedding (or any indexed chunk under a keyword-only generation), because an unchanged chunk is a retained row and never reaches that upsert. It still matters for sessions where nothing is retained, for rows re-embedded under a semantic generation, for repeated ids in one batch, and for PostgreSQL, and it would change an `updated_at` expectation pinned in `manager-source-index-kernel.test.ts`, so it is a separate change.

## The change in one sentence

Remove the six `sessions`-only restrictions on the existing delta planner and publication path so a changed memory file publishes only its changed chunks, and keep complete replacement when no prepared chunk matches a stored row.

Diff: 8 files, 237 added and 90 removed lines.

- 4 production files, 30 added and 38 removed lines: `manager-embedding-ops.ts` 3/3, `manager-publication-transfer.ts` 10/11, `manager-session-delta.ts` 9/8, `manager-source-index-kernel.ts` 8/16.
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, 4/2: the paragraph on retained chunks now covers edited memory files as well as session transcripts and names the fallback (an edit that changes every chunk, such as a line inserted at the top, still replaces the file's chunks).
- `docs/reference/database-schemas/worker-access-inventory.md`, 1/1: the one generated row for `manager-source-index-kernel.ts`, whose first call line moves from 111 to 103 because the type block lost 8 lines.
- 1 new test file, `manager-memory-delta.test.ts`, 145 lines (2 cases).
- 1 changed test, `manager-publication-transfer.test.ts`: the existing session removal test is now parameterized over `sessions` and `memory`, 57 added and 49 removed lines, 19 added and 11 removed ignoring whitespace (most of the raw count is re-indentation).

| Input case | Expected outcome |
|---|---|
| Append to a memory file | Earlier chunks retained (recall and provenance refreshed); the changed tail chunk written; the old tail id removed |
| Edit in the last chunk | The same one written row and one removed id |
| Trailing removal | The surviving chunks retained; the removed ids deleted (S3: 2 rows deleted, 1 inserted) |
| Edit at the top of the file | Every id changes, nothing matches, planner returns the entry unchanged, complete replacement (S4) |
| File whose last chunk is a heading-only chunk | Heading-only chunks merge into the following chunk for memory files (`manager-index-preparation.ts:78`), so an append changes the last two ids instead of one |
| `MEMORY.md` and `USER.md` | Chunked per entry (`perEntry`, `manager-index-preparation.ts:55`); the same planner applies per entry id |
| Unchanged file | Skipped on equal hash before planning (`manager-source-sync-ops.ts:155`); not reached |
| Full reindex into a shadow generation | Unchanged: `database.isShadow` returns the entry unprepared, an empty shadow has no rows to retain |
| Multimodal entry | Unchanged: `entry.kind === "multimodal"` returns the entry as prepared |
| Clean semantic index (vectors complete) | Now a delta instead of the reuse path: retained chunks are not re-embedded or upserted; shown through the shipped CLI in the real behavior proof below, timing not measured |
| Clean semantic index, retained chunk whose vector row is missing | The reuse path writes every supplied chunk vector again (since #174874), which restores a missing vector; the delta does not write vectors for retained chunks, so such a chunk stays without a vector until a rebuild, as session rows already do since #103201; not measured |
| Semantic rows without stored embeddings | Not retained (`row.embedded \|\| !semantic`), rewritten once; if none are retainable the entry is returned as prepared |
| Row identity after a delta | Retained rows keep `chunk_rowid` (and so their FTS rowid) and `updated_at`. A full rewrite can hand back the same rowid values (`INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` without `AUTOINCREMENT`), but after an edit in the middle the new chunk gets a new rowid while retained rows keep theirs, so the rowid order no longer follows document order |
| Equal-rank keyword hits | May be returned in a different order after a delta than after a full rewrite, if any search path breaks ties by rowid; the parity hashes order by id and the regression test's three queries have no ties, so this is not measured |
| Sessions | Identical: same header fields and order, same rows; memory headers now also carry `delta: false` or `true` |
| PostgreSQL | Same kernel branch with no explicit vector writes; not measured or tested here |
| A retained row vanishes between planning and publication | The publication group rolls back; one failed sync, repaired on the next sync; traced from code, not reproduced |

## Evidence

All of the following ran on one machine (Mac Studio, macOS, Node v24.21.0, SQLite 3.53.4 via node:sqlite) at the pushed tree, base `fe6a3616168`. Provenance: the reviewed head is `6c4f0e654f4` (signed). The in-process measurements, the test runs and the checks below ran on Studio commit `baa8b7d28b4`, which `6c4f0e654f4` re-creates with a signature: both have tree `f9a434c87ee` and parent `fe6a3616168`, so `git diff baa8b7d28b4 6c4f0e654f4` is empty; `build-final.out` records `baa8b7d28b4` for that reason. The shipped CLI proof below ran on a fresh clone checked out at `6c4f0e654f4` itself.

### Method

BEFORE is a clean checkout of the base `fe6a3616168` and AFTER is a clean checkout of this commit, both built with `pnpm build`; `build-final.out` records both heads, a clean `git status` for each, and the sha256 of the non-test source diff between them. The two differ only by this diff. Each arm loads its own production source through the repository TypeScript loader (the memory-core internals are bundled chunks in `dist`, not importable standalone; see Build). The harness runs the real `prepareMemoryIndexChunks` (tokens 400, overlap 80), the real planner behind a thin adapter whose `source.chunks` read calls the production `readMemorySourceChunks`, the real `memoryPublicationHeader` and `memoryPublicationBatches` (with the worker's fragment decoding copied, since it is not exported), and the real `MemorySourceIndexKernel.replaceRows`, on node:sqlite connections to `.backup` copies of two real agent stores (430,518,272 and 4,855,853,056 bytes) opened with the agent pragmas (WAL, `foreign_keys` on, `synchronous` NORMAL, `busy_timeout` 5000). The fixtures are synthetic generated text of 19 chunks (91 paragraphs) and 678 chunks (3,346 paragraphs). Shapes: S1 append, S2 last-chunk edit, S3 trailing removal, S4 top-of-file edit (the fallback), S5 file deletion (control). Timing is the median of 5 runs after 2 warmups, two rounds per arm, each inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE ... ROLLBACK` from the committed first version; the tables show the true median of the 10 pooled runs and each round's median in parentheses. Arms were run back to back within each round, BEFORE first in round 1 and AFTER first in round 2. Each arm started only once the 1-minute load average was below 4; it was 3.1 to 4.0 at the start of each arm, while the 5-minute average was still 9.2 to 10.6 as the host settled after an unrelated job (`run-commit.load`). Row work, revision delta, and WAL bytes come from one committed run with `wal_autocheckpoint` 0. Parity is a sha256 over the chunk rows (excluding `updated_at` and `chunk_rowid`), FTS rows, recall metadata, provenance, the `memory_index_sources` row, and a MATCH + bm25 result over 3 fixture tokens, all ordered by id; it is equal in every cell (`# parity mismatches: 0`).

Not in the loop: the embedding provider (so the AFTER gain on semantic indexes omits the embedding or cache lookups that retained chunks no longer need), worker-thread transport, the file watcher, and sqlite-vec (vector writes and deletes are not measured). The keyword search in the harness is a MATCH + bm25 query, not the production lexical search SQL; parity of the production `manager.search` is asserted by the regression test. Semantic mode uses deterministic synthetic 1024-dimension vectors with `vectorReady` false and `memory_vector_rebuild_v1` set to `'1'`, so BEFORE takes `clear()`. Store B was measured keyword-only.

Script and raw outputs: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/tree/ca6b2948161dbd7ca198b0d827be458885c443f6/t2-02-memory-delta/evidence (under `round-rebased/`: `measure-delta.mjs`, `summarize-delta.mjs`, `run-commit.sh`, `store-distribution.mjs`; outputs `measure-delta-A-round1.out`, `measure-delta-A-round2.out`, `measure-delta-B-round1.out`, `measure-delta-B-round2.out`, `measure-delta-summary.out`, `store-distribution.out`, `build-final.out`, `run-commit.load`; test and check logs for the pushed tree under `gates3/`, including `base-checks.out` and `reindex-recovery-main-*.log` for the clean `fe6a3616168` runs of the failing checks; the warm test cost runs and the pre-rebase test and check logs under `gates2/`).

### Build

`pnpm build` succeeded for both arms (`build-final.out`). The AFTER `dist` contains `written.length === planned.size` (1 file), no longer contains the old gate `source !== "sessions" || entry.kind === "multimodal"` (0 files), and contains the message `Memory source owner changed before delta planning` (1 file). The BEFORE `dist` has 0 files, 1 file, and 0 files for the same three probes. The non-test source diff between the heads is 4 files, 30 insertions and 38 deletions, sha256 `d2bbf9d27f372f2e1caff34144e9f7823222c52fd4e4dcd5cf1fd8fea71cae14`. The runtime is Node v24.21.0 with `node:sqlite` linking SQLite 3.53.4.

Each of its two cases runs one mode: keyword-only (`provider: "none"`) or semantic with rebuild debt (`memory_vector_rebuild_v1` set to `'1'`). In each case it appends to the file, asserts, forces a full reindex and compares, then inserts a new first line. ## Gaps, stated plainly

- `pnpm changed:lanes --json` for this diff returns `extensions: true`, `extensionTests: true`, and `docs: true` and every other lane false, with `extensionImpactFromCore: false` and `docsOnly: false` (`gates3/lanes.json`). The owning directory, the ten neighbouring files, and the three script tests above ran because they cover the changed code and the CI test plan built from it; unrelated suites were not run.
- The two `check:changed` failures, the `db:worker-inventory:check` failure, and the `manager.reindex-recovery.test.ts` failure above are outside this diff, reproduce on a clean checkout of `fe6a3616168`, and are not addressed here.
- The foreign-key edge (a retained row vanishing between planning and publication, which fails that sync and is repaired by the next) was traced from code, was not reproduced as a live race, and has no test in this PR; a kernel-level test would pass on the base as well, so it would not be a regression test.
- On a clean semantic index the reuse path writes every supplied chunk vector again (since #174874), which restores a missing vector. The delta does not write vectors for retained chunks, so a retained chunk whose vector row is missing stays without one until a rebuild, as session rows already do since #103201. This is not measured.
- The planner read is a worker round trip per changed memory file, including a file added to an existing index (its read returns no rows); a full reindex into a shadow skips it. The harness has no worker transport, so that round trip is not in the numbers.
- How often real memory edits shift every chunk id (for example a line updated near the top of a note) was not measured. For those edits the change is neutral apart from the planner read, and the S4 cells above put the pooled difference on 19 chunks between -0.11 and +0.89 ms, within the drift the S5 control shows.
- The measurements leave out sqlite-vec, so vector writes and deletes are not measured. The kernel's delta branch does not read the vector state, and the existing session delta tests in the neighbouring files exercise it, but no test runs a memory file on a clean semantic index and that case's timing is not measured. The real behavior proof above runs it through the shipped CLI with sqlite-vec loaded and counts embedding requests against a loopback stub, not a real provider; the in-process measurements leave the embedding provider out.
- The fallback is all or nothing. There is no partial-overlap threshold, so a partial overlap with many removed ids still takes scalar vector deletes rather than the single scan `clear()` would use above 32 ids.
- The heading-only merge, `MEMORY.md` and `USER.md` per-entry chunking, and the unchanged-file hash skip are described from the code (`manager-index-preparation.ts:55` and `:78`, `manager-source-sync-ops.ts:155`); no case in this PR exercises them.
- PostgreSQL runs the same kernel branch without explicit vector writes. It was not measured, and its `*.postgres.test.ts` suites were skipped in the runs above.
- The regression test searches lexically (`lexicalOnly`); parity of the semantic and hybrid search over a delta-published memory file is not asserted. The harness's MATCH + bm25 check is not the production lexical SQL.
- Measurements are from one host, two stores, synthetic fixtures of 19 and 678 chunks, chunking 400 tokens with overlap 80, and 4 KiB pages. Store B was measured keyword-only. Linux and Windows were not measured.
- The extra planner read per changed memory file was measured only in the in-process S4 cells above; its cost on a very large file or a slow disk was not measured.

prs.title: fix(codex): mirror persisted user admission
prs.body:
Closes #145993

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex prompt annotation and transcript mirroring could be skipped when a user-turn write hook changed the content that was actually admitted. The mirror fingerprinted prepared content while the host correctly validated the persisted admission.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Codex prompt builder now treats an existing persisted admission as authoritative, while retaining the prior resolved-message and raw-message fallbacks before persistence. The host validator, Codex protocol, storage schema, and historical transcripts are unchanged.

## User Impact

Codex turns with content-changing admission hooks now keep one canonical annotated and mirrored user row with the admitted content, stable identity, and original upstream prompt provenance. This does not retroactively repair historical rows.

## Evidence

- New owner-boundary regression failed on the base code in both parameterized cases because the real host annotation guard rejected the prepared-content fingerprint and no prompt row was mirrored.
- The same regression passes after the fix and verifies the annotated admitted row plus the single mirrored row, including transformed content, mirror identity/origin, upstream text, and explicit transport idempotency key.
- 135 focused tests passed across Codex transcript mirroring, user idempotency, host annotation, and user-turn recorder suites.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- <changed paths>` passed all selected formatting, lint, typecheck, extension boundary, contract, dependency, dead-export, database/media/sidecar, and import-cycle checks.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Claude autoreview and the shared exact-head adaptive review found no actionable issues.

### Live Codex proof

An isolated `openclaw agent --local` turn ran on reviewed head `b68f2c243cac7db8418bfed04baccff20371ae02` with the real Codex app-server harness and a temporary `before_message_write` plugin that changed `OPENCLAW_145993_PREPARED_INPUT` to `OPENCLAW_145993_ADMITTED_INPUT`. The run returned `PROOF_OK` and reported `agentHarnessId: codex`.

The retained SQLite transcript for synthetic session `718d2ef8-7c6a-4b5a-b566-cd7331db954d` produced this sanitized verification:

```json
{
  "canonical_user_rows": 1,
  "admitted_marker_rows": 1,
  "prepared_marker_canonical_rows": 0,
  "annotated_user_rows": 1,
  "original_native_submission_rows": 1,
  "assistant_proof_rows": 1
}
```

This proves the real Codex turn retained one canonical annotated row with the transformed admission while preserving the original native submission provenance.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw channels login` and `openclaw channels logout` could persist the entire global plugin auto-enable result while resolving a channel. An unrelated model-derived Codex activation could therefore be written to `openclaw.json` even though the user only requested channel authentication.

Closes #144972.

## Why This Change Was Made

Channel auth now gives plugin resolution the validated authored source config and commits only genuine install-on-demand config changes. Omitted-channel discovery still uses the active runtime's auto-enabled view, but that view is no longer treated as authored config.

## User Impact

Logging a channel in or out no longer enables unrelated bundled plugins or rewrites configuration solely because global auto-enable found a candidate. Channel inference, runtime-resolved account values, and install-on-demand writes continue to work.

## Evidence

Current-head update (2026-10-14, `10e57219faaeaf1895c5d53a3ac6b801205e9c55`):

This patch adds/removes no imports or exports. No baseline or guard was modified, and required GitHub CI remains authoritative before merge.

prs.title: fix(plugins): expose static inventory in status
prs.body:
Related: #122181

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users and maintainers inspecting plugin status could not see manifest-declared CLI command aliases or route activation hints unless runtime code had registered live commands/routes. This made closed issue #122181 hard to resolve cleanly because status output mixed static declarative inventory with runtime registrations.

## Why This Change Was Made

This redesign addresses the feedback from closed issue #122181 by adding a separate `staticInventory` status surface for cheap manifest declarations. It exposes exactly `commandAliases`, `cliCommandHints`, and `routeActivationHints` from manifest `commandAliases` and `activation.onRoutes`, while leaving runtime-owned `cliCommands` and `httpRoutes` populated only by loaded plugin runtime registrations.

The refreshed ClawSweeper repair keeps `PluginRecord.staticInventory` required for internal registry records and removes the synthetic missing-record compatibility test path. Runtime slash aliases without an explicit `cliCommand` stay in `staticInventory.commandAliases` for ownership diagnostics, but no longer appear in `staticInventory.cliCommandHints`; runtime slash aliases with an explicit `cliCommand` still contribute that CLI hint.

The earlier unrelated state-schema first-use compatibility exception has been removed from this PR. The refreshed diff is limited to plugin/status/CLI/docs/API-baseline/plugin-state runtime coverage/trajectory fixture surfaces.

## User Impact

Operators, maintainers, and plugin authors can now inspect the declarative command and route inventory that OpenClaw can know before loading plugin runtime code. Runtime status remains honest: registered CLI commands and HTTP routes still represent actual runtime registrations only, and chat-only runtime slash aliases are not presented as root CLI command hints unless the manifest declares a related CLI command.

## Evidence

Validated on `/usr/bin/node v22.22.3` at current head `cc7381f78ed7a71664850719c75d9213cc0d6574` after rebasing onto `origin/main` `88d6b571b09b1debed681b6231a71b659b633877`:

prs.title: fix(openai): GPT-Live Talk bypasses the managed proxy on egress-restricted hosts
prs.body:
Fixes #175794

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: GPT-Live Talk fails with "Realtime provider error" on egress-restricted hosts, because its media WebSocket bypasses the managed proxy (`proxy.proxyUrl`) and dials OpenAI directly.

## User Impact

User impact: Talk with a GPT-Live model over `gateway-relay` and API-key auth now connects through the configured managed proxy. If the proxy refuses the tunnel, the session fails visibly and never falls back to a direct connection. Hosts without a proxy see no change and no added startup cost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Since #154119, the GPT-Live direct media socket runs in a `worker_threads` worker so audio keeps flowing during Gateway stalls. `startProxy` installs the managed proxy through Proxyline's `installGlobalProxy`, which patches `http`/`https` and the global agents only in the JS isolate that calls it. The media worker is a separate isolate with no hooks, so `ws` dials directly. The worker does inherit the env that `startProxy` exports (`HTTP(S)_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`, `OPENCLAW_PROXY_ACTIVE`, `OPENCLAW_PROXY_CA_FILE`).

The worker now builds its `ws` agent from that inherited env with the public SDK helper `createNodeProxyAgent({ mode: "env", targetUrl })` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/fetch-runtime`. It also opens the socket with the `WebSocket` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/websocket-runtime` instead of a bare `ws` import. On Bun, bare `ws` resolves to Bun's built-in adapter, which ignores `agent`; the first revision of this PR failed the Bun CI shard for exactly that reason. `provider-websocket` received the same switch in #147085. This matches the Slack relay, which pairs the same two SDK helpers.

- **Routing policy stays with its owner.** The helper applies `NO_PROXY`, so the default `gateway-only` loopback bypass still holds, and it normalizes `wss:`→`https:`. It also resolves the managed proxy CA through the existing env fallback for runtimes that inherit only env (`resolveActiveManagedProxyTlsOptions`).
- **The worker isolation invariant holds.** The agent is built inside the worker from plain env, and no Agents or factories are cloned through `workerData`.
- **It fails closed.** A refused or broken tunnel surfaces as the worker's existing error/close path. There is no direct retry.
- **No cost without a proxy.** The helper's module graph (Proxyline, undici, fetch guard) measured about 250–280 ms of module load in the compiled build. It is imported only when the inherited env has a `*_proxy` variable. That check is a superset gate only; the helper still makes the routing decision. The SDK `WebSocket` costs about 29 ms to load, versus about 20 ms for bare `ws`.

Alternatives not taken:
- Calling core `ensureInheritedManagedProxyRoutingActive()` in the worker. It is a `src/infra` internal that extensions must not import, and it would install process-global hooks inside a media worker.
- Changing only `OpenAIRealtimeBridge`, the file named in the report. GPT-Live models use the Quicksilver bridges, so that would not reach this path.

Out of scope:
- The WebRTC path, used for OAuth/subscription models. Its media is UDP/ICE and cannot traverse an HTTP CONNECT proxy. Its call setup goes through guarded fetch in the Gateway isolate, which already honours the managed proxy. That needs separate boundary proof, as ClawSweeper noted.
- Logging the underlying provider error at warn. The worker posts a detail-free `{type:"error"}` by design (redaction), so this belongs in a follow-up.
- The main-thread `new WebSocket` fallbacks. On Node they run in the Gateway isolate, where Proxyline's patched `http.request` replaces `ws`'s `createConnection` with its agent. Under Bun, their bare `ws` imports also resolve to Bun's adapter and are not routed. That is a sibling gap across the OpenAI realtime sockets (`realtime-quicksilver-session.ts`, `realtime-quicksilver-gateway-bridge.ts`, `realtime-voice-bridge.ts`) and is better handled as a follow-up than folded into this fix.

## Evidence

**Regression tests.** They use the real `OpenAIQuicksilverWorkerSocket.create` → worker with a synthetic CONNECT proxy and a local `ws` target, in `extensions/openai/realtime-quicksilver-socket-worker.test.ts`:
1. `tunnels media through the managed proxy and exchanges audio`: default `gateway-only` env, with a target host (`gpt-live.openai.test`) that only the proxy can resolve. The test asserts `CONNECT host:port`, open, and 960 PCM bytes echoed back intact.
2. `fails closed without a direct connection when the proxy refuses the tunnel`: `loopbackMode=proxy` keeps the loopback target directly reachable, then the proxy answers 403. The test asserts close, one transport error, and **zero** target connections.

RED on `upstream/main` (964d3238270), with only the test file changed:
```
FAIL ... tunnels media through the managed proxy and exchanges audio
AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ 'gpt-live.openai.test:60171' ]
FAIL ... fails closed without a direct connection when the proxy refuses the tunnel
AssertionError: expected 'open' to be 'close'
Tests  2 failed | 2 passed (4)
```
GREEN with the fix: 4/4 on Node locally.

**Bun:** there is no Bun runtime on this host, so CI's `bun:changed-extensions-config` shard is the Bun proof, and it gives a RED/GREEN pair:
- `a0765150ae3` used a bare `ws` import, which Bun resolves to its own adapter. Both new tests failed there with the main symptoms (`expected [] to deeply equal [ 'gpt-live.openai.test:40881' ]`, `expected 'open' to be 'close'`).
- `bc2a833fdb7` uses the SDK `WebSocket`. Both tests pass on Bun (211 ms and 157 ms), and the socket test files pass in full (3 files, 12 tests); see [the job log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39078428712/job/117530540972).
