prs.title: fix: queued messages show no typing indicator while they wait behind a live run
prs.body:
Closes #162547

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a direct message that queues behind a live run shows no typing indicator for the whole wait, even though `docs/concepts/queue.md` says typing still fires on enqueue.

## User Impact

User impact: on Telegram and other channels whose turns carry an adoption lifecycle, a message queued behind a busy session keeps showing "typing…" until its own run starts and replies. Typing stops when the queued item finishes, is cancelled, or is dropped from the queue. Messages that do not queue are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The enqueue path already signals typing when a follow-up queues behind a live run, and the follow-up runner keeps the same typing controller. But the buffered dispatcher that handled the inbound message then returns. Its dispatcher idle callback and its `finally` (`markRunComplete` and `markDispatchIdle` in `src/auto-reply/dispatch.ts`) seal that controller and call the channel's `onIdle`, which closes the channel typing loop for good. So typing starts and stops within the same ~360 ms dispatch the issue's log shows (`message dispatch completed ... duration=363ms`).

Related: #92287 starts typing when a queued turn begins to execute (#92267). This change covers the wait before that, and keeps the controller that run would use from being sealed when the inbound dispatch returns.

This follows the direction in the ClawSweeper review: the queued item owns typing from enqueue to settlement.

- `createReplyDispatcherWithTyping` returns a new internal `onTypingHandoff` reply option. It lives in `InternalReplySessionOptions` next to `onReplyOperationOwned`, not in the public `GetReplyOptions`, and `publicReplyOptions` strips it from plugin-supplied options. Core builds these reply options itself in `dispatchReplyWithBufferedBlockDispatcher`, so Telegram still gets the handoff. After it is called, the dispatcher no longer completes the typing controller. When typing comes only from `typingCallbacks`, their `onIdle` (typing teardown) is deferred, and the queued item's typing cleanup runs `onCleanup` and then that `onIdle` once. The handoff state lives in `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher-typing-handoff.ts`.
- A channel that passes its own `onIdle` gets no `onTypingHandoff`, so its whole typing lifecycle is unchanged. That `onIdle` can do more than stop typing: Feishu's (`extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts:1232`, `queueIdleSideEffects`) finalizes streaming delivery and closes the card preview. Deferring it made finalization wait on itself (ClawSweeper revision 3). Running it while the handed-off controller kept ticking let the next tick's `onReplyStart` reopen the closed preview (revision 5). So Feishu does not get typing through the queued wait. Channels that pass only `typingCallbacks`, such as Telegram, do.
- `runReplyAgent`, on the enqueue-behind-a-live-run path, closes typing from the queued item's `turnAdoptionLifecycle.onSettled`. Queue completion calls that for a run that finished, a cancelled item, a cleared queue, and the sources of a collected batch.
- The handoff happens only when the follow-up has an adoption lifecycle and queued typing actually started (`typing.isActive()` after `signalToolStart`). Without a lifecycle nothing would settle the typing. In `message` typing mode typing does not start before text, so the controller's `cleanup` never calls `onCleanup` and a deferred `onIdle` would never run. Both cases keep today's behavior. That keeps a dropped item from leaving a typing loop running forever.
- The dispatcher exposes `onTypingHandoff` only when the channel supplied a cleanup callback, because the deferred `onIdle` runs from that callback.
- Each queued `FollowupRun` now carries the typing controller of the dispatch that queued it (`typing`), and the follow-up runner completes that one (`queued.typing ?? defaults.typing`). The queue keeps only the latest runner per key, so before this an earlier queued message, when it finished, completed the later message's controller and sealed it before that message's own turn (ClawSweeper revision 6).

`waitForReplyDispatcherIdle` moved to `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher-idle.ts` with main's current body (including its `abortSignal` handling), the queued item's `onSettled` wrap lives in `bindQueuedFollowupTyping` in `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-typing.ts`, and the two queued-typing cases moved to `agent-runner.runreplyagent.queued-typing.cases.ts`, so the line-cap ratchet holds for `reply-dispatcher.ts`, `agent-runner-run.ts`, and the runner e2e file.

## Evidence

- New `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts` case drives a real `createReplyDispatcherWithTyping`, `createTypingController`, and `createTypingCallbacks` (channel TTL off, as on Telegram) through handoff, dispatcher idle, `markRunComplete`, and `markDispatchIdle`. On the test commit the channel `start` runs 0 times in the next 60 s. On the fix it runs 30 times, `stop` is not called during the wait, and `stop` runs once after the queued run settles.
- New `agent-runner.runreplyagent.queued-typing.cases.ts` case: a follow-up with a lifecycle queued behind a live run calls `onTypingHandoff` once and keeps typing open, and `completeFollowupRunLifecycle` on the queued item cleans typing up once. On the test commit `onTypingHandoff` is called 0 times.
- Channel with its own idle (ClawSweeper revisions 3 and 5, fixed in 0f720c428ae). The `reply-utils.test.ts` case with distinct `onReplyStart`, `onIdle`, and `onCleanup` callbacks uses fake timers: it calls the handoff option if offered, completes the run and the dispatcher, then advances 5 s. On 4f0fc716970 it fails: the controller never cleans up (`["idle"]` instead of `["cleanup", "idle"]`) and keeps calling `onReplyStart`, which is the call that reopens a Feishu preview. On 0f720c428ae it passes: cleanup and `onIdle` run once at dispatcher idle, and `onReplyStart` is not called again. It replaces the case that raced finalization against a real 50 ms timer.
- Message typing mode. New `queued-typing.cases.ts` case: a follow-up queued behind a live run in `message` mode never starts typing, so it must not take over idle. On 10d05599818 `onTypingHandoff` is called once. On a0ebdb83961 it is called 0 times. The existing handoff case now marks the mock controller active when its typing loop starts, as the real controller does.
- Two messages queued behind one live run (ClawSweeper revision 6, fixed in 2c7c47c9acd). New `followup-runner.test.ts` case runs a queued item that carries its own controller through a runner whose default controller belongs to a later message. On 0f720c428ae it fails: the item's own `markRunComplete` runs 0 times and the later message's controller is completed instead. On 2c7c47c9acd it passes: the item's own controller is completed once and the later one is untouched. The queued-typing handoff case now also checks that the enqueued run carries the dispatch's controller.
- On 2c7c47c9acd: `followup-runner` 30/30, `src/auto-reply/reply/queue` 75/75, `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` 226/226 with the e2e config, `dispatch-from-config.delivery.test.ts` 294/294, `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts` 79/79, `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass.
- On 0f720c428ae: `reply-utils` and `reply-flow` 74/74, `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts` 79/79, `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` exit 0, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files clean. `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` (226/226 on 4f0fc716970) was not rerun: this commit does not touch the runner, and its queued-typing cases pass a mock `onTypingHandoff`.
- CI on 0f720c428ae: `checks-node-changed-1` failed in `src/agents/model-fallback.reply-entry.e2e.test.ts` and `checks-node-changed-5` in `dispatch-from-config.delivery.test.ts` ("delivers deferred Telegram text when generation fails after a block"). Both assert the old error copy ("API rate limit reached", "Authentication failed", "Something went wrong") that main changed in d0b48d63efb (#163381) after this branch's base. CI's merge ref picked up the new copy. Main updated the delivery test in 08eb496e2c6. The model-fallback e2e on main still expects the old strings. On this branch's base the delivery file passes locally (294/294) and the model-fallback e2e passed 10/10 in an earlier pass. This PR does not touch the error copy.
- Earlier, on a0ebdb83961: rebased onto upstream/main 836087a89a4 (green CI); `src/agents/model-fallback.reply-entry.e2e.test.ts`, red in an earlier CI run and on main at that time, passed 10/10 locally.
- 2026-10-05: rebased onto upstream/main e7edee1790d to clear a conflict (main added an import next to this PR's import in `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts`; both kept, no code change). On 8afd852ac2d: `followup-runner`, `reply-flow`, and `reply-utils` 103/103, `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` 226/226 with the e2e config, `pnpm tsgo:core` exit 0. The other suites listed above were not rerun after the rebase.
- 2026-10-06: rebased onto upstream/main d8a62a83f37 after main's #166085 deleted `reply-dispatcher-observers.ts` and made `invokeReplyDispatcherObserver` local to `reply-dispatcher.ts`. 242a714b8d8 resolves it: `createReplyDispatcherWithTyping` wraps the channel idle in that observer guard once and passes it to `createTypingHandoff`, which no longer imports anything. Commit ids in the bullets above name the head they were measured on; the 2026-10-09 line below gives the current ones. On 242a714b8d8: `followup-runner`, `reply-flow`, `reply-utils`, and `src/auto-reply/reply/queue` 179/179, `dispatch-from-config.delivery.test.ts` and `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts` 373/373, `pnpm tsgo:core` exit 0, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean. `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` was not usable locally: most cases fail with "Session database target changed outside captured discovery custody", and three of them fail the same way on d8a62a83f37 with no PR changes.
- 2026-10-09: rebased onto upstream/main 6725e574130 to clear a conflict with main's dispatcher changes; no behavior change. Commits then: test 643347e6c5d, fixes 493bf7ddf41 through 6c5cf6c679e. On 6c5cf6c679e: `followup-runner`, `reply-flow`, and `reply-utils` 103/103, `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` 229/229 with the e2e config, `pnpm tsgo:core` exit 0, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean on the touched files. In the intermediate rebase the three new queued-typing tests failed on main's source and passed on the branch. prs.title: fix(mcp): surface failed session cleanup in CLI checks
prs.body:
Related: #147701

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes false-success MCP checks when catalog discovery succeeds but session cleanup cannot be confirmed.

## User Impact

`mcp probe` keeps the discovered catalog and reports cleanup failure in JSON/text with a nonzero exit. `mcp doctor --probe` reports an error in its complete report, and connection verification before `mcp add` or `mcp configure --probe` saves configuration rejects uncertain cleanup.

Cleanup failures tell operators to check the MCP server's session termination support and rerun the command. Rejected checks before add/configure save explicitly state that configuration was not saved.

This addresses the reporting gap in the linked issue. Robinhood's original DELETE rejection remains unexplained; the [latest metadata-only investigation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/147701#issuecomment-6208865486) observes sessionless discovery without exercising the historical DELETE path.

## Why This Change Was Made

One CLI probe owner now disposes the runtime and joins its recorded cleanup outcome before returning. The optional top-level `cleanupError` describes aggregate cleanup uncertainty without assigning it to the wrong server; catalog diagnostics and successful discovery stay available. Existing discovery errors retain priority when cleanup also fails.

The catalog projection moves intact into the probe owner to keep the command module within its existing line budget. MCP production changes total +15 lines; the regression suite and its existing host-broker lane assignment add 260 lines. HTTP transport and OAuth behavior are unchanged. This affects the explicit MCP CLI checks; it does not change the updater, top-level Doctor, schemas, or migrations.

## Evidence

Current head `3549e30baab6244503dc7b7da5335a751bbdecda` integrates main `ec90dc1ef23dd9c9dd731479b4431d9b082b78d5` to resolve GitHub's merge conflict. The only conflict was in a UI import from the earlier CI repair; that file now exactly matches main and has no PR delta. MCP source, tests and docs are unchanged from reviewed head `27d89042af66d96e06a97dbe24415a9affb0fd55`; upstream test-routing additions and this suite's fork-lane entry are retained. Two independent resolution/requirements reviews found no actionable findings.

[Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38932924284) passed on current head `3549e30baab6244503dc7b7da5335a751bbdecda`: 48 jobs succeeded, 28 were skipped, and none failed. Applicable security review also passed on this exact head. Prior head `27d89042af66d96e06a97dbe24415a9affb0fd55` passed [hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38859037422), security and PR-context/evidence gates; that is prior-head evidence. Original head `cb73071aabb19088860a7980ff2f39ac35268767` also passed [hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38853631247).

After conflict repair, all 53 focused MCP tests pass (69.39s command wall time), along with core and affected config/CLI test typechecks, scoped typed lint, formatting, assertion-safety ratchet and `git diff --check`. A fresh CLI startup build passes in 45.3s, including bootstrap/postbuild checks. The built CLI again passes the synthetic fixture: DELETE 204 exits 0; DELETE 400 exits 1 with catalog retained and recovery guidance in JSON/stderr, with the issued session/protocol/synthetic auth received and no business tool calls.

Original reporting proof compared built upstream `9e96763562abd5bb49a812b14daa3adc81f77307` and this candidate through `openclaw.mjs mcp probe fixture --json`, using the same credential-free loopback MCP server and isolated state:

| Cleanup response | Upstream | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DELETE 204 | exit 0; one tool; no cleanup error | exit 0; one tool; no cleanup error |
| DELETE 400 after successful discovery | exit 0; empty diagnostics; no warning | exit 1; one tool retained; `cleanupError` and stderr explain unconfirmed closure |

The fixture received the issued session ID, negotiated protocol header and synthetic authorization on DELETE. It received no `tools/call`. Both original CLI startup builds and bootstrap/postbuild checks passed (45.1s upstream, 44.0s candidate). ## What Problem This Solves
When a user sends several Discord messages while an earlier turn is still running, the next follow-up turn should be able to see the whole compatible queued intent instead of only the last message. At the same time, Discord transport must keep every inbound event flowing into core admission so active-run steering and `/stop`-style control inputs are not delayed behind a local plugin queue.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes group slash commands corrupting arguments when a configured mention pattern also appears inside a path, URL, label, or identifier.

prs.title: perf(memory): evict superseded embedding cache rows first at the cap
prs.body:
Refs #114612

## What Problem This Solves

`memory_embedding_cache` is capped at 50,000 rows. When new vectors would take it past the cap (insertion-time reservation from #164083) or it is already over the cap (the post-publication prune), the cache deletes the rows with the oldest `updated_at`. It does not look at whether a published chunk still uses a row.

Editing a memory file changes its chunk hashes, so the vectors for the old text are never read again, but they keep their place in the cap. A cache that sits at the cap is mostly such rows, and plain oldest-first order deletes a vector that a live, unchanged chunk still needs whenever that vector is older than the superseded ones. The next full reindex then pays the provider to embed unchanged text again.

## User Impact

At the cap, the vectors of unchanged indexed text survive eviction while superseded vectors are available to take their place, so a forced reindex of unchanged content makes no provider request. In the real CLI run below, on a store seeded to the 50,000-row cap with superseded vectors and three new files added, the base build deleted the vector of an unchanged file and re-embedded it on the next reindex (1 request); the head build made 0 requests.

Nothing changes below the cap, and the number of rows deleted at the cap is the same as before. The database file size, schema, and row cap do not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

`docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md` describes the cache as bounded by the existing row cap. The bound stays exactly as it is; this change only decides which rows fill the deletions the cap already makes.

The eviction preference is narrow on purpose:

- Only rows of the active provider identities are preferred. Rows of any other provider, model, or provider key keep plain oldest-first order, so a fallback or previously configured provider is not singled out.
- A preferred row has no published chunk carrying its hash, and was written before the oldest published chunk. A full reindex rewrites every chunk, so after one such a row predates the index that dropped it.
- A row written at or after the oldest published chunk keeps plain oldest-first order even when nothing references it yet. It may be a vector a failed rebuild cached for its retry, or one another sync cached and has not published.
- The fence is read from `memory_index_chunks` in SQL, so it holds across processes and restarts. No new state is kept in memory.
- The deletion count is computed exactly as before. Preferred rows fill it first; if there are fewer, the remainder is taken oldest-first, as today. At or below the cap nothing is deleted.

For the review checkpoint in `docs/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes.md`, the persisted effect is this: when the cap deletes, it picks superseded vectors of the active identities before other rows. The cap, the number of rows deleted, the schema, durability, and rollback do not change. `memory-builtin.md` documented the old order ("removes the oldest entries"), and that sentence is updated. The cache is derived data. Any deleted vector can be recomputed by the provider, and the run below shows a base build reading a head-written store with no provider request. #114612 is the linked discussion for cache retention.

## The change in one sentence

Capacity eviction of `memory_embedding_cache` first takes, oldest first, active-identity rows that no published chunk references and that were written before the oldest published chunk, then falls back to plain oldest-first for the rest of the same, unchanged count.

Diff shape: 2 commits, 8 files, 488 insertions and 15 deletions. Production is 108 insertions and 12 deletions, docs 12 and 3, tests 368 and 0. The second commit removes only tests (27 insertions, 98 deletions): three manager cases that repeat existing coverage, and redundant assertions in two others.

- `manager-embedding-cache.ts`: `evictMemoryEmbeddingCacheRows` and `deleteOldestUnreferencedMemoryEmbeddingCacheRows`, used by both `pruneMemoryEmbeddingCache` and `upsertMemoryEmbeddingCache`.
- `cache.prune` and the cache upsert header carry `unreferencedFirst: { identities }` to the existing publication worker (`manager-publication-task.ts`, `manager-publication.worker.ts`, `manager-database-context.ts`, `manager-embedding-cache-ops.ts`).
- In `pruneEmbeddingCache`, the return expression is now a `const` followed by `return pruned ?? false`. The behavior is the same; the change keeps `manager-database-context.ts` within its 700-line cap.
- Docs: `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`.

Tests: three unit cases in `manager-embedding-cache.test.ts` and one manager file `manager.cache-unreferenced-eviction.test.ts` with four cases.

The identity comparison casts the TEXT key columns (`CAST(provider AS text)` and so on). This is a no-op on values. It stops SQLite from answering the identity filter through the primary key and then sorting every matching row by `updated_at`, which reads each vector. With it, SQLite walks the `updated_at` index and stops at the limit. In the benchmark below, removing only the three casts makes the median batch cost 126.04 ms with 1,000 chunks and 123.07 ms with 10,000 chunks, against 3.93 ms and 31.78 ms with them (output quoted there).

## Contract

| Case | Outcome | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Cache at or below the cap | nothing deleted | unchanged |
| Insertion or prune past the cap | same number of rows deleted as before | unchanged cap |
| Active-identity row, no published chunk carries its hash, written before the oldest published chunk | deleted first, oldest first | superseded text |
| Row a published chunk carries | deleted only when no preferred row is left, oldest first | live content |
| Active-identity unreferenced row written at or after the oldest published chunk | plain oldest-first | a retry's or another sync's unpublished vector |
| Rows of another provider, model, or provider key | plain oldest-first | a fallback or previous provider may be switched back to |
| Empty published index, or no active identities | plain oldest-first | no fence |
| Full rebuild fails before publication, including a source that fails partway | no extra deletion; the retry reuses cached vectors | unchanged failure semantics; covered by `manager.reindex-recovery.test.ts` and CLI step C |
| Incremental sync | same rule; unchanged chunks keep their `updated_at`, so the fence is older and fewer rows qualify | the fence never moves past a live chunk |
| Schema, config keys, public API | unchanged | none added |

## Upgrade and rollback compatibility

No `.sql` file, migration, table, column, or index changes, and `PRAGMA user_version` is 26 before and after (transcript below). The only persisted effect is which rows remain after a deletion the cap already makes.

- Upgrade: the head build runs `memory index --force` on a store the base build created and filled to the cap, exit 0. The vector of the unchanged `delta.md` keeps its row and its original `updated_at`, and rows of another identity are untouched.
- Rollback: the base build runs `memory index --force` on the store the head build last wrote, with 0 provider requests and no change to rows or checksums, then answers `memory search`.

### Measured eviction cost

The benchmark uses one file-backed SQLite database and the real schema from `ensureMemoryIndexSchema`. It calls the real `pruneMemoryEmbeddingCache` with 1536-dimension vectors. The cache is at 50,000 rows. Live rows are the oldest, and the unreferenced rows predate the published chunks. Each round adds 100 rows and then times one prune, which is one 100-row eviction batch inside a transaction. There are 15 rounds per mode. It ran in the build directory of tree `445ba525b57`, whose production files are identical to the pushed tree. The benchmark file is not part of the diff.

```
chunks=1000 mode=oldest-first batch=100 rounds=15 median_ms=1.10 max_ms=2.33 cache_rows_after=50000 live_rows_after=0/1000
chunks=1000 mode=unreferenced-first batch=100 rounds=15 median_ms=3.93 max_ms=4.62 cache_rows_after=50000 live_rows_after=1000/1000
chunks=10000 mode=oldest-first batch=100 rounds=15 median_ms=1.02 max_ms=2.15 cache_rows_after=50000 live_rows_after=8500/10000
chunks=10000 mode=unreferenced-first batch=100 rounds=15 median_ms=31.78 max_ms=42.15 cache_rows_after=50000 live_rows_after=10000/10000
```

Load average (1, 5, 15 minutes) at the start was 5.16, 11.07, 12.64.

The same benchmark with only the three `eb.cast(...)` calls in `deleteOldestUnreferencedMemoryEmbeddingCacheRows` replaced by plain column references (reverted afterwards, `git checkout`), load average 6.86, 8.71, 10.86:

```
chunks=1000 mode=unreferenced-first batch=100 rounds=15 median_ms=126.04 max_ms=132.96 cache_rows_after=50000 live_rows_after=1000/1000
chunks=10000 mode=unreferenced-first batch=100 rounds=15 median_ms=123.07 max_ms=132.23 cache_rows_after=50000 live_rows_after=10000/10000
``` The added cost is two scans of `memory_index_chunks`, one for the minimum `updated_at` and one for the hash set. SQLite evaluates each scan once per statement. The cost grows with the number of chunks and is paid only when the cache is over the cap. In the same runs, oldest-first deleted every live row (1,000 of 1,000) and 1,500 of 10,000. Unreferenced-first deleted none.

## Gaps, stated plainly

- **Which rows survive at the cap changes.** The count, cap, schema, and rollback do not change, but the documented order ("removes the oldest entries") does. A superseded vector can be deleted before a live one that is newer. If its text is restored later, that costs one re-embedding, and under plain oldest-first the same row would usually have gone anyway, because it is old.
- **The fence is the oldest published chunk across all sources and models.** After incremental syncs it can be far in the past, so fewer rows qualify, and the eviction falls back to oldest-first. Nothing extra is deleted.
- **The fence compares clocks.** Chunk and cache `updated_at` both come from `Date.now()` in the writing process. A writer whose clock runs behind can make a row look older than it is. The only effect is on order. The count is unchanged.
- **Eviction is slower when there are many chunks.** It takes about 32 ms per 100-row batch with 10,000 chunks, against about 1 ms oldest-first. It runs only above the cap, inside the existing worker write transaction.
- **Stale identities, byte budgets, and age-based retention are not addressed.** Rows of a provider the user switched away from keep plain oldest-first order. The row cap is still the only bound.
- **Real-provider proof was not run.** The CLI run uses a local stub provider. Embedding quality and real provider behavior are not exercised. No built Gateway process was run; the CLI uses the same manager and publication worker.
- **Full suite not run.** The changed lanes (extensions, extension tests, docs) and the owning directory are the suites this diff can break. CI covers the rest.

prs.title: refactor(sessions): simplify maintenance ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Maintenance/deletion repeats work already owned by the same native operation: UUID-addressed preparation slots plus a release RPC, repeated lease reads, receipt identity echoes, and caller-side checks of typed worker result tags. These layers obscure the actual safety boundaries: current rows and protection, operation-bound commit settlement, archive-before-delete, and native cleanup.

## User Impact

No intended feature, storage-format or migration change. Normal maintenance/deletion keeps current protection, archive-before-delete, live ownership and accepted-write settlement. An unusually overlapping discretionary maintenance pass may fail/retry, and a canceled/lost-reply pass can leave one bounded preparation until the next prepare, metadata cleanup or native close. No operator action is required on healthy paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep one bounded worker-owned maintenance preparation, consumed by metadata cleanup or replaced by the next preparation/ordinary close. Reuse the validated lease row for its receipt and perform lease drainage/checks in one synchronous transaction. Correlate private planning, reclamation, and scoped archive requests with their actual result types; retain decoding at unknown transport/committed-facts boundaries. Remove the archive recorder's second schema ensure and the second clone of an already-detached commit-time deleted entry.

Published original head614a03abe11a89db8e6aa371b7e37f06a8ee11bf removed122 net production lines. The signed ten-file CI repair and complete own-orphan cleanup at52d5637c0113a14cf6dffbafb04a8bf672282e1f has an actual delta against pinned main df0358cdd5f7e8525a9c610dd05745806eaf0e50 of **134 net production lines removed** across25 production files (+137/-271); all29 files +180/-459. Fresh complete-caller review is scoped-clean P0-P2 with no accepted/actionable findings; a subsequent mechanical extraction names the identical execution-release callback without changing order or semantics. Focused proof is complete with the unresolved local failures disclosed below; new-head hosted CI completed successfully. Main's PostgreSQL lease-read fix (#175069) and consolidated reclamation tests are preserved. Schemas, persisted formats, retention, permissions, public config/protocol/SDK contracts, and standalone session-memory machinery are unchanged. This smaller maintenance/deletion area split follows campaign rule11; overlapping donors are counted once.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

The provenance below distinguishes original additions from later extractions. Inspected descriptions provide synthetic/internal boundary evidence, not a cited human wrong-operation/echo/slot-identity incident.

| Removed guard/mechanism | Original provenance | Accepted case and outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Duplicate preparation ID and two-slot capacity checks | `7555e3f88132`, [#158251](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158251) | Automatic maintenance coalesces per store, but a retiring predecessor can overlap a successor. Unusual overlapping discretionary passes may fail/retry instead of retaining independent snapshots. |
| Cleanup-only preparation release RPC and its separate admission source | Same #158251 introduction | A canceled/lost-reply pass may leave one bounded readonly preparation until the next prepare, metadata cleanup, or ordinary native close. Actual write/close settlement remains required. |
| Orphaned preparation-release interface and six empty caller stubs | Orphaned by this PR's removal of the last real release-RPC producer | Remove only an artificial empty async yield. Source and owned-execution cleanup still run in order, retain both failures, and join real native settlement. Synthetic microtask/reentry timing is best effort; no actual cleanup is lost. |
| Second lease SELECT and its missing-receipt guard | `7ab507770f3`, [#140897](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140897) | No await separates exact lease validation and receipt construction; consume that validated row. Native-exit receipt identity and later effect checks remain. |
| Per-row lease-existence re-reads between drain transactions | `8a5b4af66074`, [#111678](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111678): original new-file addition; cooperative-interleaving audit/test proof, not a cited human reread incident | One synchronous transaction owns row selection, stale cleanup, live refusal and deletion fences, so the former gaps between transactions no longer need a second existence query. A blocking live lease may roll back earlier stale bookkeeping; the next drain retries it. The original deletion/authorization and cross-process live-lease protections remain. |
| Pending receipt's seven command-identity echoes | `1f8e5985e10b`, [#165151](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165151) | The operation-bound kernel constructs these fields from the same input. A future kernel/binding programming error loses a second echo comparison, not authorization. Unknown-facts tag decoding stays. |
| Rediscovery of the actor's already-typed pending receipt | Same #165151 introduction; activated by #170712 | Trust the typed operation result; retain missing-receipt errors, actual DB/session/hash ownership, transaction AND commit grants, current authority, and unknown-outcome no-replay. |
| Entry planning operation check | `26dffe7468cd`, [#160858](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160858) | The private typed entry request receives its corresponding producer result; no duplicate caller check for an internally wrong tag. |
| History planning operation check | Same #160858 introduction | Same paired producer contract; actual historical generation/source decisions remain. |
| Check planning operation check | Same #160858 introduction | Same paired producer contract; actual deletion/protection checks remain. |
| Scoped archive materialize result tag | `7ab507770f3`, #140897 | One paired FIFO request is in flight; an internally buggy worker is not rechecked at this application caller. |
| Scoped archive publish result tag | Same #140897 introduction | Same paired FIFO contract; actual publication, file/native cleanup and error retirement remain. |
| Scoped archive final-read result tag | `31172cf54466`, [#149223](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149223) | Trust the paired read result type; preserve complete exact-run answer retrieval and current access checks. |
| Scoped archive page-read result tag | `4c7c64734452`, [#157247](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157247) | Trust the paired page result type; preserve bounded preview/page behavior and security revalidation. |
| Lifecycle historical-generation reclamation tag | `789513231d7d`, [#126035](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/126035) | Typed plan/result correlation replaces only the duplicated wrong-kind assertion. |
| Lifecycle entry reclamation tag | Same #126035 introduction | Same correlation; current empty-state alternate and commit authority remain. |
| Lifecycle artifacts reclamation tag | `a1566b2dbfd`, #163269 | The typed plan/result correlation also makes this caller assertion unreachable; preserve the worker wire boundary and actual artifact/deletion authority. |
| History-eviction reclamation tag | Same #126035 introduction | Same correlation; archive-before-delete and source/generation checks remain. |
| Archive publish-prepare result tag | `1ed98e67c92c`, [#155988](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155988) | Trust the actual typed dispatcher; physical owner translation/current settlement remain. |
| Archive publish-record result tag | Same #155988 introduction | Same dispatcher contract; no archive durability or retry change. |
| Maintenance plan result tag | `c9584688c461`, [#148630](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/148630) | The result relation keeps both plan and stale outcomes; wrong internal tags are not rechecked at every caller. |
| Maintenance finalize result tag | Same #148630 introduction | Committed subsets, retained-execution alternate, FIFO and publication ordering remain. |
| Maintenance age result tag | `2ff5d6fbb21d`, [#172985](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172985) | The relation retains maintenance-plan-stale for age AND plan;64-entry fairness/continuation and real protection checks remain. |
| Recorder's repeated archive-schema ensure | `fc4d5d744fad`, [#123495](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/123495), not later extraction#147946 | Recording follows nonempty schema-establishing preparation or existing pending rows and only UPDATEs. Unsupported record-without-prepare/offline table removal gets the ordinary missing-table failure. |
| Second deleted-entry clone | `0a8e3604ba24`, [#98236](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98236), not later worker move | Return the already-detached commit-time decode, not a plan/cache/public-input alias. Recipient mutation isolation remains; no supported behavior is relaxed. |

**Human incidents remain KEEP:** [#138555](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/138555) reported a truncated child answer after cleanup; exact-run complete-answer/archive retrieval is preserved. [#110152](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/110152) reported Windows EPERM/fsync and long database delays; archive durability and off-thread responsiveness stay. Native cleanup recovery, failed-close custody/retry, and bounded contention handling also remain unchanged.

Keep the measured planning-outside-writer/refresh-at-admission path from [#171154](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171154). This PR claims no new performance measurement. No dormant foundation or standalone session-memory backend, factory, registry, expiry, federation or tests are removed.

## Evidence

**Repaired exact-head hosted CI passed:** run39073995568 completed SUCCESS on52d5637c0113a14cf6dffbafb04a8bf672282e1f, including openclaw/ci-gate. Complete head check census:148 completed,90success/54conditional skips/1neutral CodeQL/3canceled non-product automation checks, zero failures/pending/foreign-head checks. Canceled dispatch and PR-context jobs have newer same-head successes; auto-response has a same-head successful run and a canceled later automation invocation, not an omitted product suite. Neutral CodeQL is not claimed as a successful alert comparison. Both current-head hosted reviews report no actionable findings and no before-merge action; their noted absent shipped CLI/Gateway E2E remains disclosed and outside this campaign's local proof budget. No CI rerun was requested. The original failure attribution and local timing gaps below remain historical evidence, not green local-suite claims.

Original exact-head CI39060215095 failed. Two lint diagnostics in the unreachable artifact result-kind assertion and three maintenance preparation/native-join assertions are ours, not inherited. The published repair removes the impossible assertion, excludes explicit verification SELECTs from operation-only SQL observation, and gives the existing maintenance-plan preparation its existing native failure-retirement policy, with the preparation hook inside that boundary. Kept path-replacement/row-preservation/zero-host-SQL assertions are not relaxed. The first four-file repair passed targeted types and independent review but exposed a new local max-lines error; the smaller complete owner cut removes its six orphaned empty release callbacks and preserves actual ordered cleanup. Fresh complete ten-file/caller review is scoped-clean P0-P2 (confidence0.96); the subsequent mechanical callback extraction preserves its behavior and removes two code lines.

Current repair proof has passed18-root targeted types, ten-file lint/format, all nine selected maintenance cases (including the three original CI failures), and the unchanged real late-protection keeper. Affected consumers add ten passing cases: three Gateway corrections, two rewrite alias-retarget variants, legacy post-await authority, raw-event append, two single-reset cases and batched reset. All runtime wrappers completed final generation verification: **20 passing cases and four unresolved local timeouts**, not an aggregate passing invocation. Gateway accepted-correction shutdown expired its unchanged120000ms timer at120142ms; cold restoration expired the same unchanged limit in turn/locked-owner/locked-SDK modes at121201/124538/136540ms. These remain unresolved local evidence, not proven product regressions or baseline attribution. Actual owners were inspected, without establishing a concrete cause. No timeout/retry/skip/assertion change or failed-case rerun was made. Runtime and static import cycles both pass with zero cycles; wrapper inventory1PASS (18filtered), source closure3PASS and mandatory lint suppressions14PASS completed their wrappers (120.28/81.65/103.56s). Whitespace passes. The remaining-proof script joined exit1, deliberately preserving its runtime failures after passing all final guards. New exact-head hosted CI completed successfully.

All seven PostgreSQL-infra failures on that original head match scheduled main39058564617@ec36f9b9617a8d668a660d97e262a861453d9246/job117471751210 individually: archive restore240000ms, following backup-create no-local-state error at414, Doctor v30/foreign=false120000ms, Matrix225450000ms, Matrix405 expected0 to be2, database port60000ms and update-preflight120000ms. The five failing test files and backup-create owner are byte-identical at PR base/head and baseline. PostgreSQL integrations passed; Git-backup passed and is not included in this attribution. This historical attribution does not waive our defects or new-head CI.

Targeted types and type-aware lint for all22 source/test roots passed, as did formatting and whitespace. The complete composed area received a fresh independent P0-P2 review with full owner/producer/keeper context and final source verification: scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings. This is not reuse of the older component reviews. Retired release-RPC references are absent across src/test/docs/scripts/packages/extensions/config. Changed-file classification was inspected through check-changed --dry-run; its printed broad commands were not executed locally.

The first unit lease file passed2 cases and the infra lease-owner file passed17. The original fourteen-file invocation was deliberately interrupted after73 minutes of proof/58 minutes of runtime execution, including39 minutes in runtime-config. Its wrapper joined exit143 and all tracked descendants exited. It is NOT a completed passing invocation or successful final generation-verification result. Remaining broad runtime coverage moves to exact-head hosted CI under the busy-host proof policy; it was not rerun locally for green.

Six unresolved local cases expired their unchanged timers:

| Case | Limit / observed milliseconds |
| --- | --- |
| Archive-read unique-generation continuation |120000 /121222 |
| Archive-read short final answer beyond runtime string limit |30000 /30227 |
| Archive-session reuse across deletion generations/database close |120000 /126831 |
| Archive-session idle reuse, worker not exited |120000 /124515 |
| Archive-session idle reuse, worker exited |120000 /124503 |
| Archive-session joins scoped done before close |120000 /141606 |

The actual diagnostics are elapsed timers, not completed assertion failures. They remain unresolved/inconclusive local evidence, not passing suites or proven baseline failures. No timeout, retry, skip or assertion was changed. Other archive/read/reclamation cases passed, including complete multiline imported-event deletion/final lookup, both compressed archive reads, off-main publication, sequential deletion reuse, failed-publisher/result-recording committed archive recovery, FIFO-independent queued retirement and scoped publication before close. Partial case results are not presented as an aggregate green suite. The previously unrun three real lease-drain cases passed with successful final worker-generation verification; prior runtime/static cycles, wrapper inventory and source closure passed. The mandatory suppression guard exposed a separate existing main fixture defect, reproduced on fresh main and fixed independently by df0358 without changing the allowlist. prs.title: fix(memory-core): bound managed dreaming under pressure
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: managed memory dreaming cron could keep adding workspace and Dream Diary work while the gateway was already under RSS/heap pressure, and the pressure wait path did not observe the enclosing cron timeout/cancellation.
- Solution: preserve the existing full scheduled sweep, but add abort-aware bounded memory-pressure backoff before each cron workspace attempt and before detached Dream Diary scheduling.
- Exact behavior now: each cron-triggered managed dreaming run still iterates every configured workspace in the same cron invocation. Before starting each workspace, memory-core checks process RSS and heap usage. Before scheduling the detached deep Dream Diary narrative, it checks the same pressure again because promotion/report work may have raised memory usage. If RSS is at least 1536 MiB or heap used is at least 1024 MiB, it waits and retries with exponential backoff: 30s, 60s, 120s, 240s, then capped at 300s between retries. It keeps retrying at the capped delay until pressure clears or the enclosing cron run aborts/times out.
- Cron cancellation behavior now: the cron run abort signal is forwarded through before_agent_reply hook contexts for getReply, CLI cron, and embedded Pi cron paths. If that signal fires while memory-core is sleeping in pressure backoff, the sleep resolves immediately, the dreaming hook stops, and the timed-out cron run does not later resume memory mutations after pressure clears.
- Dream Diary behavior now: Dream Diary generation is not dropped just because pressure is high after promotion. Detached narrative scheduling waits with the same bounded backoff and proceeds after pressure clears; if the cron timeout/cancellation arrives first, the cron run stops cleanly.
- What did NOT change: direct non-cron dreaming requests are not delayed by this scheduler guard; the dreaming frequency/config switches are unchanged; memory storage formats are unchanged; cron still owns one scheduled managed dreaming job; memory-core does not intentionally defer remaining workspaces to a later cron tick.

## Motivation

- Observed gateway performance logs showed managed memory dreaming processing 10 workspaces in one background tick, taking 69621 ms, while nearby diagnostics reported high RSS and saturated event-loop/CPU conditions.
- The desired fix is to avoid adding more work while the process is under pressure, without dropping the existing full-sweep semantics for multi-workspace users or dropping Dream Diary output under pressure.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #84847
- Closes #84849
- Related #
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior addressed: Managed memory-core dreaming cron keeps the existing all-workspace sweep, waits under gateway RSS/heap pressure before each workspace and before detached Dream Diary scheduling, and exits pressure backoff promptly when the enclosing cron abort signal fires.
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw worktree with focused static/type proof and autoreview; before evidence comes from redacted runtime diagnostics captured from the affected gateway.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `pnpm format:fix extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming.ts extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.before-agent-reply.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner.ts src/agents/cli-runner.before-agent-reply-cron.test.ts src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run.ts src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run.before-agent-reply-cron.test.ts src/plugins/hook-types.ts`; `git diff --check`; `pnpm run lint:extensions:bundled`; `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/plugins/hook-types.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.before-agent-reply.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner.ts src/agents/cli-runner.before-agent-reply-cron.test.ts src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run.ts src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run.before-agent-reply-cron.test.ts`; `pnpm tsgo:extensions`; `pnpm tsgo:core`; `AUTOREVIEW_AUTO_TESTS=0 .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local`.
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output):

```shell
$ git diff --check
# no output

$ pnpm run lint:extensions:bundled
# passed

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/plugins/hook-types.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.before-agent-reply.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner.ts src/agents/cli-runner.before-agent-reply-cron.test.ts src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run.ts src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run.before-agent-reply-cron.test.ts
# passed

$ pnpm tsgo:extensions
# passed

$ pnpm tsgo:core
# passed

$ AUTOREVIEW_AUTO_TESTS=0 .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local
autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported
overall: patch is correct (0.81)
```

- Observed result after fix: The changed tests cover abort-aware pressure backoff, propagation of abort signals through before_agent_reply hook contexts, continued full-workspace cron iteration after pressure clears, capped pressure retry behavior, and Dream Diary scheduling after pressure clears instead of being dropped.
- What was not tested: Local Vitest execution is currently blocked in this worktree: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 timeout 180s node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ...` timed out after printing only the Vitest banner. Remote focused Vitest proof was also blocked here: Blacksmith Testbox is unavailable because the `blacksmith` CLI is not installed, and direct AWS Crabbox is unavailable because AWS credentials/IMDS are not present. A live multi-workspace gateway run with private agent/session data was not rerun.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged):

```shell
memory-core: dreaming promotion complete (workspaces=10, candidates=10, applied=1, failed=0)
observed managed background task duration: 69621ms
memory pressure warning: rssBytes=1827979264 heapUsedBytes=684072312 thresholdBytes=1610612736
liveness warning: eventLoopUtilization=0.991 cpuCoreRatio=1.107 active=0 waiting=0 queued=0
```

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Managed cron dreaming collected every configured workspace and processed them in one cron delivery without pausing between workspaces when process memory was already above warning thresholds. The new pressure backoff initially had no cancellation/deadline awareness, so a timed-out cron run could keep sleeping and later mutate memory after pressure cleared.
- Missing detection / guardrail: Existing tests covered short-term dreaming promotion but did not exercise multi-workspace managed cron sweeps, pressure backoff cancellation, detached Dream Diary pressure handling, or hook-context abort propagation.
- Contributing context (if known): The managed cron system event can be claimed through before-agent-reply hooks in getReply, CLI cron, and embedded Pi cron paths, so all three hook contexts need the same abort signal.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [ ] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.before-agent-reply.test.ts`, `src/agents/cli-runner.before-agent-reply-cron.test.ts`, `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run.before-agent-reply-cron.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: managed cron dreaming keeps the full configured workspace sweep, waits under RSS/heap pressure before workspace and detached narrative work, doubles retry delay from 30 seconds to a 5 minute cap, continues in the same cron invocation after pressure clears, and stops without later memory mutation when the cron abort signal fires.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: The behavior is owned inside the memory-core dreaming cron seam and before-agent-reply hook contexts, so it can be exercised without private gateway sessions or provider credentials.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): Existing dreaming tests covered promotion behavior but not the pressure, cancellation, and detached narrative cases.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Scheduled memory dreaming still uses `dreaming.frequency` as the cadence for a full configured-workspace sweep. When gateway RSS or heap usage is above the warning threshold before a workspace starts, or before the detached Dream Diary narrative is scheduled, scheduled dreaming waits before continuing. The wait starts at 30 seconds, doubles, and caps at 5 minutes between retries. No remaining workspaces are intentionally deferred to a later cron tick by memory-core; the run continues when pressure clears unless the enclosing cron run aborts/times out.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
cron tick -> workspace A -> workspace B -> workspace C -> detached diary work, without pressure-aware waits or abort-aware pressure sleep

After:
cron tick -> pressure check before workspace A -> workspace A -> pressure check before detached diary A -> pressure wait if needed -> diary A -> pressure check before workspace B -> ... full sweep continues until clear/completed or cron aborts
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux worktree
- Runtime/container: Node via repo wrappers for static/type checks
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): memory-core plugin cron seam and before-agent-reply hook contexts
- Relevant config (redacted): memory-core dreaming enabled with multiple agent workspaces

### Steps

1. Run the focused formatting, lint, and TS checks listed above.
2. Review the memory-core pressure tests and hook-context tests added for the cron abort path.
3. Confirm full-sweep semantics are preserved, pressure waits happen before workspace and Dream Diary scheduling, backoff caps at 5 minutes, and abort signals are available to memory-core from all cron before-agent-reply paths.

### Expected

- Cron-triggered managed dreaming preserves the full configured workspace sweep, waits under RSS/heap pressure before adding workspace or detached narrative work, and stops promptly when cron cancellation fires during pressure backoff.

### Actual

- After the patch, static/type proof and autoreview are clean. Focused Vitest could not be executed in this environment because the local Vitest runner hung before test execution and remote providers were unavailable.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [x] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: code-path review for memory-core pressure waits and before-agent-reply abort propagation, focused formatting/lint/type checks, and autoreview closeout.
- Edge cases checked: queued cron work receives abort signals through all relevant hook paths, pressure backoff exits on abort, detached Dream Diary scheduling waits under pressure rather than being dropped, and full-sweep behavior remains in the same cron invocation.
- What you did **not** verify: focused Vitest execution and private live multi-workspace gateway run, for the blockers listed in Real behavior proof.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for maintainers.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Config/env changes? (`Yes/No`) No
- Migration needed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: If memory pressure remains high for a long time, a scheduled dreaming cron run may take longer because it waits before starting the next workspace or detached Dream Diary work.
  - Mitigation: The backoff is capped at 5 minutes per retry, logs each wait with RSS/heap context, preserves the existing full-sweep behavior instead of skipping workspaces, preserves Dream Diary generation instead of dropping it, and now observes cron abort/cancellation.

prs.title: fix: Teams Graph and media work with RFC2544 proxy DNS
prs.body:
Closes #107163

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams plugin users in host-proxied deployments could have Graph requests and media downloads blocked when DNS resolves allowed external hosts to RFC2544 fake-IP addresses before egress interception.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Teams plugin now passes a host-scoped SSRF policy with `allowRfc2544BenchmarkRange` for known Microsoft Graph hosts, and media downloads add the same RFC2544 opt-in only when the configured media host suffixes produce an actual hostname allowlist. The change stays in the Teams plugin boundary and does not allow arbitrary private-network targets.

## User Impact

Teams Graph-backed operations and attachment/media handling can work in RFC2544 fake-IP proxy environments while keeping the existing hostname restrictions for Graph and media URLs.

## Evidence

Behavior addressed: Microsoft Teams Graph and media guarded fetches rejected RFC2544 fake-IP DNS results before host-proxied egress could intercept the request.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw worktree with the Microsoft Teams extension Vitest config. Remote Blacksmith Testbox was attempted but blocked because the installed Crabbox binary reported version `0.12.0`, while this repo requires Crabbox `>=0.22.0` for the Blacksmith Testbox provider.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/msteams/src/graph.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/attachments/shared.test.ts` and `git diff --check`.

Evidence after fix:
```shell
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.extension-msteams.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9 /home/galini/GitHub/worktrees/bug-055-msteams-rfc2544-policy


 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  78 passed (78)
   Start at  05:21:03
   Duration  11.99s (transform 7.89s, setup 887ms, import 12.32s, tests 342ms, environment 0ms)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 17.34s
```

Observed result after fix: The focused Teams tests pass, including assertions that relative Graph requests and absolute Graph pagination URLs carry a Graph-host-scoped RFC2544 policy, non-Graph absolute URLs do not receive that policy, media suffix allowlists add the RFC2544 opt-in, and wildcard media allowlists still return no SSRF policy.

What was not tested: No live Microsoft Teams tenant or host-proxied container was available, and no raw failed gateway run was present in the bug bundle. Remote Testbox proof was blocked by the local Crabbox version mismatch described above.

Before evidence:
```shell
Current-main source proof before the patch:
extensions/msteams/src/graph.ts requestGraph called fetchWithSsrFGuard without a policy.
extensions/msteams/src/graph.ts fetchGraphAbsoluteUrl called fetchWithSsrFGuard without a policy.
extensions/msteams/src/attachments/shared.ts resolveMediaSsrfPolicy returned only buildHostnameAllowlistPolicyFromSuffixAllowlist(allowHosts).
```

prs.title: fix: keep keyless web search on secrets fast path
prs.body:
Closes #107154

## What Problem This Solves

Deployments using host-proxied, keyless web search fell off the secrets runtime fast path during startup even though OpenClaw does not hold the search credential in-container.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fast-path guard now recognizes a generic keyless host-proxy shape: `tools.web.search.provider` must name a provider, and the matching `plugins.entries.<provider>.config.webSearch.omitAuth` value must be exactly `true`. The selected provider must remain enabled by plugin policy. Unrelated allowed plugins and load paths are supported, matching the host's real plugin loadout.

Credential-bearing search values, a denied or omitted selected provider, mismatched provider entries, legacy `x_search`, active web-fetch provider configuration, and additional plugin web-provider surfaces still select the full resolver path.

## User Impact

Operators using a keyless web-search plugin through a host proxy can keep the startup secrets fast path without moving the provider credential into the OpenClaw container. Existing credentialed and mismatched configurations continue through full secret resolution.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
Keyless host-proxied web search must keep gateway startup on the secrets fast path with the host's unrelated plugin allow/load entries, while a credential-bearing control must still load the full resolver.

Real environment tested:
Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL2, Node source checkout at exact PR commit `ff85c33c553de8c87e9f5d3098764672cc76cd45`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, and the real `openclaw gateway run` startup path. The proof used minimal locally loaded WorkIQ, tools-code-mode, and WebIQ plugin fixtures plus the bundled diagnostics plugin to reproduce the Lobster-shaped plugin policy without contacting a private host service.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

1. Ran the complete focused Linux test file:
   `CI=1 NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/secrets/runtime.fast-path.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
2. Started the gateway with keyless WebIQ configuration (`omitAuth: true`), the four-plugin allow list, and non-empty plugin load paths. A narrow Node loader hook recorded only imports whose resolved URL contained `runtime-prepare`.
3. Repeated the same gateway startup with `plugins.entries.webiq.config.webSearch.apiKey` set to a resolved environment `SecretRef` as the credential-bearing control.
4. Allowed each gateway to reach ready state, then sent `SIGTERM` through GNU `timeout` and verified clean shutdown.

Evidence after fix:

The actual gateway startup path reached ready state with the Lobster-shaped keyless plugin loadout without loading the heavy secret resolver. Adding a credential-bearing SecretRef to the same provider caused the full resolver modules to load, and startup still completed successfully. prs.title: fix(msteams): normalize inbound mentions and forwards
prs.body:
Closes #102376

Authored by @galiniliev and refreshed onto current `main` with the original contributor branch retained.

## What Problem This Solves

Microsoft Teams can deliver mentions, inline quote markers, `quotedReply` entities, and forwarded bodies in parallel activity fields. Without normalization, agent text can lose mention identity, retain transport markers, or present forwarded text as sender-authored. Quote authorization must bind authenticated entity identity to the same quoted body rather than an unrelated attachment or channel-thread parent.

## Summary

- normalizes non-bot Teams mentions to readable `@Display Name` text while removing bot mentions
- matches mention entities to their corresponding `<at>` text instead of relying on entity array order
- removes all inline `<quoted />` markers from agent text
- labels Teams forwarded-message body segments
- prefers authenticated `quotedReply` entity identity over attachment display metadata
- parses quote ID, sender, and body from the same Reply block
- requires matching entity and attachment message IDs before accepting quote context
- carries an unambiguous quote fact through debounced message bursts
- uses Graph parent identity only as fallback for legacy HTML quotes

Quoted previews remain supplemental quote context and continue through the existing sender allowlist and context-visibility checks.

## Review Fixes

- prevents an allowed channel-thread parent from authorizing a blocked `quotedReply.senderId`
- rejects an attachment quote body when its message ID differs from the authenticated entity
- prevents one Reply block's ID from authorizing another Reply block's body
- matches reordered bot and user mention entities to the corresponding text tags
- removes every inline quote marker rather than only the first marker

## Evidence

Exact head: `56419fce2f9f345340aa142b0c5852278249ad80`

Blacksmith Testbox: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37427555613

```text

passed; 1,710 lockfile entries passed supply-chain policy checks

Vitest: inbound, inbound-facts, and message-handler authz
3 files passed
60 tests passed

oxfmt --check (7 changed files)
passed

oxlint --deny-warnings (7 changed files, 231 rules)
0 warnings, 0 errors

git diff --check
passed
```

OpenClaw native CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37427571503

```text
openclaw/ci-gate
passed
```

Coverage includes reordered mention normalization, all-marker removal, forwarded-body labeling, matching and mismatched entity/attachment quote IDs, same-block quote binding, debounce quote preservation and ambiguity suppression, allowed quote inclusion, blocked entity-sender exclusion, and a handler-level two-block regression proving an allowed first Reply block cannot authorize a blocked second block before final agent context.

prs.title: fix(agents): warn when model rollback preparation fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Preparing the rollback guard for an agent-selected session model can fail, but the initial catch silently disables rollback. Operators receive no default-level explanation for that non-outcome.

## User Impact

Record a warning from the existing guard owner with the canonical error and a next step: check session storage and model settings. Inference remains best effort and rollback stays disarmed when preparation failed. Missing sessions or absent/non-agent markers stay quiet. Incognito refusals, caller cancellation and source revocation still propagate before the warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

Seven production lines added in one owner; this is a silent-failure bug fix, not cleanup deletion credit. Reuse the canonical subsystem logger and policy-free shared error formatter, with no new callback, helper, fallback or result shape. Logs are written raw; existing console/transport egress redactors remain responsible for outbound diagnostics. The final reconciliation callback and execution caller remain unchanged so normal terminal reconciliation refusals are not promoted indiscriminately.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Failed rollback preparation still permits inference without an armed rollback; the existing behavior is now visible, not repaired by rereading, retrying or fabricating a marker. A later permanent model failure may need an operator to change model settings.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep unused harness plugins out of agent-runtime load plans
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #175861

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where users with an agent-harness plugin installed (e.g. `codex`) but unused — no agent selects or configures that runtime — would see the Gateway spend roughly a core of CPU and heavy filesystem I/O on every ordinary agent turn, because the harness plugin's npm project (including `node_modules`) was loaded and re-captured into a fresh plugin capture on every turn.
- **Related:** #175861; #166310 already scoped the `isolated-completion` purpose the same way; capture reuse by source fingerprint remains tracked separately in #157989 / #160959.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** an installed harness plugin joins an agent-runtime metadata scope (and therefore registry acquisition and capture) only when a selection or the configured harness policy resolves to that harness runtime.
- **Out of scope:** capture caching by source fingerprint (#157989); no changes to runtime registration, activation policy, or the plugin loader itself.
- **Highest-risk area:** metadata scope narrowing must keep the owners of runtimes that are actually selected or configured (picker runtimes, shorthand model owners, selections resolved through harness policy).
- **How is that risk mitigated?** Harness owners still enter through the existing planner paths — per-selection resolution via `resolveSelectedAgentHarnessRuntime` → `addAgentHarnessOwners`, configured runtimes via `collectConfiguredAgentHarnessRuntimes`, and shorthand model owners via `addShorthandModelOwners`; the existing picker-harness and shorthand-model regression tests keep passing, and a new routed-runtime positive control proves a selected harness still loads.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** with an unused harness plugin installed and enabled, an ordinary agent turn on the default runtime no longer loads, evaluates, or captures that plugin; routing a model to that harness runtime still loads it.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/agents/harness/runtime-plugin-load-plan.ts` (the unconditional `startup.agentHarnesses` loop removed from `resolveAgentRuntimeMetadataPluginIds`); regression tests in `src/agents/harness/runtime-plugin.test.ts` and `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.unused-harness.plugin-scope.test.ts`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** isolated worktree running the real plugin loader path — real written plugin packages, real discovery, metadata snapshot resolution, and registry acquisition — not mocks of the planner or loader.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  skills/fix-pr/scripts/validate.sh src/agents/harness/runtime-plugin-load-plan.ts src/agents/harness/runtime-plugin.test.ts src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.unused-harness.plugin-scope.test.ts
  # oxfmt + oxlint + same-directory tests (37 passed) + tsgo:core — all green

  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/harness/runtime-plugin-load-plan.executor.test.ts \
    src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.remote-publication.test.ts \
    src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.reply-fallback.test.ts \
    src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.startup-registry.test.ts \
    src/agents/runtime-plugins.test.ts \
    src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.unused-harness.plugin-scope.test.ts \
    src/commands/doctor-session-state-providers.test.ts
  # 65 tests passed across the unit-fast, infra, agents-core, and commands shards
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:** the new registry-acquisition test installs an enabled, allowed `codex` harness fixture plus an `openai` provider fixture and runs the real acquisition path (`prepareOwnedPluginLoadContext` + `prepareWorkspacePluginRegistries`):
  ```text
  unused harness, default-runtime selection:
    metadataSnapshot.pluginIds = ["openai"]      (was ["codex", "openai"] on unpatched main)
    loaded registry plugin ids   = ["openai"]    (harness neither evaluated nor captured)
  routed-runtime control (agentRuntime id "codex"):
    metadataSnapshot.pluginIds = ["codex", "openai"]
    loaded registry plugin ids   = ["codex", "openai"]  (harness still prepared when selected)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** an installed but unused harness plugin stays out of the agent-runtime metadata scope and out of the loaded registry; a harness runtime that a selection or config actually resolves to still loads its owner plugin.
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** on unmodified `origin/main` both new regression tests fail — the metadata scope returns `["codex", "openai"]` because the unconditional `startup.agentHarnesses` loop admits every installed harness plugin into every cold metadata scope (matching the issue's dist source pointers, lines 43-61 of `runtime-plugin-load-plan-*.mjs`).
- **What was not tested:** a live Windows Gateway with the real npm-installed `codex` plugin; the reporter's CPU/file-open measurements were not re-measured locally. Capture-content reuse (#157989 / #160959) is untouched.
- **Proof tier:** L2
- **Proof limitations:** none beyond the untested live-Gateway scenario listed above
- **Review state:** Awaiting CI + maintainer review (CI lanes pending)

prs.title: test(database): refresh PostgreSQL conformance shard budgets
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL conformance's shard weights still included timeouts from a red pre-transform-reuse run. A new test target could move several expensive recovery flows into the same shard and push 120-second cases over budget.

## User Impact

The three PG shards now use passing post-fix timings for all 91 current targets. This is test-only: migration, backup, rollback, foreign-write refusal, and credential assertions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor's real-agent cases accumulated distinct registrations for the same synthetic agent, so later backups discovered earlier fixtures. Clear those registrations before each case and build the independent current-schema reference once in the setup hook. Archive and updater tests reuse the existing real native-worker fixture; task-scoped connection selection still follows each operation.

The remaining integration flows retain measured headroom instead of running near their deadlines. Matrix already reuses workers and its preflight/repair assertions, full round trip, and recovery actions are part of the behavior being proven; reverse-port's four actions likewise protect distinct recovery boundaries. Budgets use at least twice the nearest-rank empirical p95 of two green CI samples, rounded upward. No tests are skipped or assertions weakened.

## Evidence

Timings: [dispatch 39068774273](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39068774273) and [scheduled 39071119824](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39071119824), all three PG shards green. No other post-fix green scheduled run was available when measured. The resident-session target landed on main during this work; its nine passing cases in green run 39075024684 supply the additional 3.801-second weight. Each job log was fetched once successfully; the scheduled downloads required the direct job-log endpoint after the run-log transport failed.

All 1,754 passing case rows from the first two runs match their job-summary counts. Weights are the maximum across those runs of each target's three-worker makespan, using observed per-file case spans, longest-first allocation, a 1-second floor, and millisecond rounding. The newly added target uses the same method on its nine passing cases from run 39075024684. There are no timeout samples and no new generator.

For the complete 91-target inventory, applying the new measurements to the old cohorts gives **1144.616 / 1625.474 / 1532.849 s**; refreshed cohorts give **1433.907 / 1434.824 / 1434.208 s** (30 / 31 / 30 targets). The old configured totals would be 2064.614 / 2064.630 / 2064.887 s, including two missing-target 30-second fallbacks.

| Case | Before CI / budget (s) | PR CI / budget (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Doctor v27, no foreign write | 72.3 / 120 | 72.4 / 220 |
| Doctor v27, foreign write | 85.1 / 120 | 69.1 / 220 |
| Doctor v30 rollback | 103.4 / 120 | 73.0 / 220 |
| Updater baseline | 91.6 / 120 | 91.3 / 200 |
| Updater agent/credentials | 93.9 / 120 | 79.5 / 200 |
| Archive recovery | 150.8 / 240 | 128.7 / 320 |
| Matrix round trip | 309.6 / 450 | 250.3 / 650 |
| Matrix resume | 189.0 / 300 | 140.3 / 400 |
| Reverse port, namespace present | 76.8 / 120 | 56.4 / 180 |
| Reverse port, namespace missing | 82.0 / 120 | 61.1 / 180 |

The 193.428-second one-shot CLI case is below 41% of its composed budget (more than 480 seconds) and is unchanged.

Final-head [CI run 39076561986](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39076561986) passed on `1100b6742af1acac5c9a21293c403653de4fc4b8`: all three PostgreSQL shards actually ran and passed (890 tests total). All ten formerly near-budget cases are now below 46% of their budgets. [PG 1/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39076561986/job/117525127726), [PG 2/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39076561986/job/117525127760), [PG 3/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39076561986/job/117525127762). The original head also passed all three PG shards in run 39075024684.

Local Homebrew PG17 proof used internal-disk HOME/TMPDIR and all CI extensions. All 43 changed-file cases are covered: 42 passed in the combined run (491.9 seconds including wrapper), and its sole Unix-socket/TCP-proxy mismatch passed unchanged on loopback TCP (11.6-second case; 67.6-second wrapper). The pre-change Doctor/updater baseline passed 16 cases in 197.1 seconds. Doctor real-agent cases fell from 17.7 / 20.5 / 26.1 seconds locally to 15.2 / 13.9 / 14.5 seconds after reference reuse and registry cleanup; updater baseline/recovery took 20.0/15.3 seconds.

Core-test typechecking, scoped lint/format, changed-file line-cap, timeout-race, and exact 91-target shard coverage checks passed. Independent autoreview through P2 is clean on the final patch; both hosted reviews of the original patch also found no actionable issues. The local repository-wide max-lines check reported three inherited UI suppressions; those files and the baseline are unchanged from starting main, and both PR CI runs passed.

Release-note context: refresh PG conformance scheduling and reduce recovery-test fixture cost without runtime behavior changes.

Diff: 6 files, +362/-341 lines; +126/-105 ignoring whitespace (the explicit updater timeouts cause formatter indentation). No production files changed.

The final follow-up head `1100b6742af1acac5c9a21293c403653de4fc4b8` rebases onto main to include the new target and adds its measured weight. All five test-file blobs remain identical to the prior green head. Fresh independent autoreview is clean, and all three final-head PG shards passed.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes periodic node workspace and worker-bundle retention failing with `This operation was aborted` after a scheduler callback finishes.

## User Impact

Paired nodes can complete their scheduled retention and bundle-status publication instead of repeatedly abandoning maintenance.

## Why This Change Was Made

The coordinator already owns cancellation and joins its pending operations at shutdown. Start those operations outside the caller's short-lived async-work scope, preserving the existing node and placement authority checks.
