prs.title: feat(cron): select a search provider for isolated automations
prs.body:
Related: #173518

## What Problem This Solves

An isolated scheduled workflow cannot select a managed search provider without also changing search for interactive conversations and other jobs owned by the same agent.

## User Impact

This proposal lets an operator pin an isolated agent-turn automation to a provider such as Brave while ordinary conversations keep their existing search route. The job's prompt, schedule, model, and delivery do not change. The provider must already be available and configured; selecting it grants no additional tool access.

Maintainer acceptance of the public automation contract remains pending. This is not a provider fallback chain or a request to widen the public Plugin SDK.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `payload.webSearchProvider`, `--web-search-provider`, and `--clear-web-search-provider`. Omission on creation inherits normal selection. Omission in an update preserves an existing pin; an explicit null update or the clear flag removes it. Unsupported session targets and CLI inference backends, including CLI model fallback, reject the option instead of ignoring it.

The existing prepared-runtime selection/load-plan owner admits the requested plugin within the run's generation. The late-bound tool resolves the selected provider through its existing plugin-owned credential contract, independently of the inference account, against current secrets source configuration. The run-local projection does not publish a global secrets snapshot or swap global configuration. An unavailable or unusable pinned provider fails explicitly rather than selecting a different managed or native provider.

Existing search disablement, tool policy, plugin admission, sandbox restrictions, and execution authority remain in force. Authority captured before asynchronous credential resolution is checked again before provider I/O. A native Codex domain restriction that cannot be preserved by the managed route also fails closed.

`PluginCodingToolsOptions` omits `webSearchProvider` for both public coding-tool factories; internal host options retain it for cron propagation. Compiler-checked regressions derive those public signatures from the actual `agent-harness` SDK entrypoint. This is a TypeScript API-scope restriction, not a new runtime authorization barrier. The feature adds no dependency or database schema.

## Changes Since the Previous Reviewed Head

Current candidate: `2d6efc24dadc2f62f7ea10f1720006ed634ef6a6`. Runtime/package proof revision: `17cb655f619e24ada09f9b21e4649c54611d987a`.
Integrated main: `21a47ad54eca42c6f1bbdab5af7da644a886575e`.
The ordinary merge preserves published `047eebe7b35fb23fac6ab5df4a93040a2e0d71d9` ancestry; no rebase or force-push.

- Resolved real conflicts in the CLI and runtime-secrets tests while retaining incoming main's refactored test owners and all feature cases.
- Regenerated prompt snapshots through the canonical generator, then checked them; no hand-edited hashes.
- Moved the unchanged CLI-backend refusal into the existing cron candidate-execution resolver, which already owns preparation and fallback selection, instead of growing the prompt executor past its line budget.
- Preserved job-scoped selection, no fallback, prepared-generation admission, late credential authority, and the host-only SDK restriction.

## Evidence

### Source identity and reusable package gates

- All 49 files in the final base-to-candidate diff were frozen for fresh canonical review and matched the committed blobs. The final commit changes only whitespace in three generated JSON fixtures; parsed JSON values, all runtime code, tests, dependency locks, and build inputs are unchanged from `17cb655f`. None of those three fixture files is included in the retained package tarball.
- Fresh canonical independent autoreview completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings in the complete final candidate. This is scoped static review, not maintainer approval or runtime proof; the earlier authentication-unavailable result is historical.
- On `17cb655f` runtime sources, 262 focused tests in 13 files passed before the final ownership-only adaptation. The final affected recheck passed 99 tests in four files, including the CLI/fallback owner and adapted tests. These overlapping runs are not added together.
- Core types and eight affected test-type graphs passed; services/cron types were repeated after the final owner move. Formatting, generated prompt checks, and final-owner lint passed.
- Two full touched-surface lint findings are inherited: `openclaw-tools.ts` and `run-attempt-dispatch.ts` exceed the line limit on untouched pinned main too. Both were independently reproduced there. No suppression, baseline change, or unrelated refactor was added.
- The exact-commit `17cb655f` build and canonical installable-package integrity check passed. This package proof is reused by the byte equivalence above, not relabeled as a new-head package execution. A local merge-tree check against newer main `d508bbe3c96a73fe97117afe29a17e98ac92c813` was conflict-free; that is textual compatibility, not a claim that future merge CI passed.

### Packaged CLI, Gateway, and provider HTTP

Fresh package matrix: **PASS on `17cb655f619e24ada09f9b21e4649c54611d987a`.**

The published `2026.10.4` package created two original jobs and history through its CLI in disposable synthetic state. The exact-head candidate, also versioned `2026.10.4`, was directly installed into that private prefix. The CLI, Gateway, prepared runtime, tools, credential resolver, and provider HTTP code were the installed package, with no provider execute/fetch mocks. Inference was scripted locally; search requests reached loopback fixtures, not public services.

| Scenario | Observed search HTTP | Additional assertion |
|---|---|---|
| Original job after candidate installation | 1 SearXNG request | Original definition/history retained |
| Interactive turn before override | 1 SearXNG request | Session and nonempty prompt hash recorded |
| CLI set Brave and run original job | 1 Brave request | Pin read back; no SearXNG fallback |
| Interactive turn after override | 1 SearXNG request | Same session and prompt hash |
| CLI clear and run original job | 1 SearXNG request | Pin absent; inheritance restored |
| Job with an empty allowed-tool list | 0 requests | Matching attempted call explicitly rejected |
| Revoke search during tool-time SecretRef resolution | 0 requests | Owner acknowledgment before resolver release; explicit refusal |

Unique query nonces and matching function-call outputs make positive and negative assertions non-vacuous. The private Gateway applied revocation through its authenticated config owner with revision/CAS protection; runtime application and secrets-reload acknowledgment preceded release of the blocked resolver. The final original definitions, history, and stable configuration were compared again.

Independent package verification: PASS: all 15,307 installed package-owned regular files matched the tarball, excluding dependency trees and the lifecycle marker that canonical postinstall removes. Brave, SearXNG, and Codex resolved to candidate bundled roots. The global database migrated from schema 20 to 27 and the agent database from 24 to 31. Both original authored job definitions, the original history entry, and stable configuration were preserved. Existing main-owned Doctor migration added its internal inference-account restriction to legacy jobs; that scheduler-only field is not part of the public job definition. The verifier read byte-matched, read-only SQLite/WAL/SHM snapshots without checkpointing or changing the original databases. No owned test process, running cron receipt, runner lock, or occupied fixture port remained. An initial bind check observed only kernel TIME_WAIT; the unchanged strict port checks passed after drain. The exact disposable container was then removed and its absence read back.

Package SHA-256: `0fb5515dd1fbdcacb4ba32833c8579a47426a8b265c78b0ef504818d84423ee1`.

### Fixture and evidence boundaries

The source/build lane used a secretless filesystem sandbox. Its initial package-baseline attempt correctly refused a shared temporary-directory write. Package execution moved to a disposable non-root container with a read-only root filesystem, no capabilities, no production credentials/state, and no published ports. No host permission or sandbox guard was relaxed. Network access was available for package setup; this is not a claim of network-isolated execution.

The first candidate attempt exposed interference from auxiliary inference consuming the fixture's global response script. The failed receipts were retained, an independent routing contract failed before the fixture correction and passed afterward, and the original stopped baseline was restored before replay. Auxiliary inference now uses a separate synthetic response lane. Short unique call IDs retain exact correlation under the current runtime's normalization. All 11 final harness contracts passed. These are fixture corrections, not additional product changes.

Stable plugin package roots were quarantined only in the disposable fixture; packaged Doctor reconciled the stale installed records so they could not shadow candidate bundles. The original stopped data snapshot was retained, including an exact symlink-preserving copy. Doctor's original-state capture succeeded in the container; its Codex plugin recovery-coverage warning remains a limitation, not a guarantee of full plugin rollback.

This is a synthetic same-version direct-install data transition, not native-updater success, production migration/deployment, hosted Codex execution, validation of real provider credentials, public search-service compatibility, or concurrent-chat stress coverage. Native/managed Codex separation has source-level boundary coverage; the packaged interactive scenario uses SearXNG.

## Hosted Validation and Remaining Gates

The previous [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39074877796) tested synthetic merge `7c710b1dbf4024a8afa98f6c63aeffa9dc5ddceb` over main `0a0d88df543a9d36c4708f93c56d995da769050c`. Its only technical failure was generated JSON snapshot formatting; the failed CI aggregate reflected that failure.

The cause was the local proof environment, not inherited main or a behavior change: a temporary directory inside the checkout inherited the formatter's JSON-ignore rule. With task-owned temporary output outside the checkout, matching CI's directory layout, untouched main passed and `17cb655f` reproduced the failure. The canonical generator then corrected the three JSON fixtures. Its check passed on the final candidate and on the exact CI merge with the same correction. No hand-edited hashes, generator/config changes, weaker assertions, or suppression were used.

[Current-head technical CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39076740639) **passed** for `2d6efc24dadc2f62f7ea10f1720006ed634ef6a6`: 75 successful jobs and 23 intentionally skipped jobs, with no failed technical job. Checkout logs and Git object parents confirm that CI executed synthetic merge `a5658cf7ebad9535d6d6ae20538cba4040bfc334` over main `e39ce04c819707527c313686d3fd99bd1cc297e5`. The previously failing snapshot job passed. Separately scheduled checks also settled without failures. A final local merge-tree check against newer main `32820c2618f75b51383f34678b28a5332c5c8ac4` was conflict-free; that last check establishes textual compatibility, not new-base runtime qualification.

The [current-head hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173552#issuecomment-6204715304) explicitly reviews `2d6efc24dadc2f62f7ea10f1720006ed634ef6a6`, reports no actionable findings, marks the fix scope complete, accepts the original packaged proof and its byte-equivalent reuse, and confirms the snapshot blocker is resolved. The final candidate also passed fresh scoped canonical P0–P2 review. Its only listed before-merge requirements are the maintainer product decision and current-head security-sensitive approval.

Maintainer acceptance of the persisted automation contract and security-sensitive approval for the current head remain external gates. The security approval status is distinct from technical test results. No merge, approval bypass, production change, or new duplicate proposal is requested or claimed.

prs.title: fix(cron): warn when an explicit allowlist suppresses configured MCP tools
prs.body:
Related: #120385

## What Problem This Solves

A cron automation with a finite explicit `toolsAllow` can silently prevent configured MCP tools from materializing. The job runs, the MCP runtime never starts, and nothing tells the operator why their MCP tools are missing. This is the policy foot-gun behind the "Unknown tool id" class of cron failures.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cron preflight now records a warning when a non-empty explicit finite allowlist omits every configured MCP selector, naming the concrete remedies (`bundle-mcp`, `group:plugins`, an exact `<server>__<tool>` selector, or `*`).

Established semantics are deliberately preserved: intentional deny-all `[]`, omitted policy, wildcard, plugin-group, and MCP selectors all behave exactly as before and produce no warning.

**Compatibility fix:** `resolveCodexMcpToolOverridesForAgent` is now applied only when `agentRuntime === "codex"`. It was previously applied to every cron run, which let Codex-specific MCP filtering distort static server resolution for non-Codex runtimes. Non-Codex coverage is included.

Preflight diagnostics are now accumulated and merged rather than early-returned, so an allowlist warning and a `web_search` provider warning can both surface from a single run instead of the first one silently masking the second.

This PR is AI-assisted. I reviewed the implementation and validation results and understand the shipped behavior.

## User Impact

Operators get a durable, actionable warning in cron run history when their explicit allowlist is the reason configured MCP tools are absent, instead of silently missing tools. Non-Codex cron runs no longer inherit Codex-specific MCP filtering.

## Scope Note

This is the second half of a deliberate split of #121488. This PR carries the `merge-risk: compatibility` surface; the cron run-history diagnostic ships separately.

## Evidence

### Exact head and current-main integration

prs.title: fix(test): stabilize update and auth-refresh fixtures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes timing-sensitive update and model-auth-refresh test failures seen during the Bun S2 trial.

## User Impact

Test-only change. Production behavior, runtime routing, timeout constants, and the Bun pin are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `update-cli.candidate-admission.test.ts` checks propagation of a 17-second timeout but also spends that live activation budget on fixture I/O. Freeze the monotonic activation clock for this propagation case. Keep wall time real because SQLite forwards absolute deadlines to real workers. All existing timeout and installed-Node-preflight assertions remain; the separate activation suite covers actual expiry. The S2 trial failure did not reproduce in isolated macOS runs, so its original load/deadline attribution remains an inference.
- `models-auth-refresh.catalog.integration.test.ts` uses an external Node SQLite writer whose default busy timeout is zero. The S2 trial failed inside that fixture with `database is locked`. Apply the existing canonical SQLite busy timeout; retain real external writes and all renewal, replacement-account, and revocation checks.

Both changes address test assumptions (bucket 2). The socket batching failure from the same trial is handled by #175846, now on main. This PR preserves that production fix and its stronger one-write regression unchanged.

## Evidence

Before the fixes, the admission case passed 3/3 on b76e and S2 and 1/1 on Node on macOS. The catalog test passed 3/3 on both Bun builds and 1/1 on Node on Linux; its zero-wait contention failure reproduces with built-ins alone on all three runtimes. The original socket test failed 3/3 on both Bun builds and passed on Node; [daily run 39066988478](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39066988478/job/117496811655) confirmed b76e was affected before #175846.

All four full files passed on b76e, S2, and Node in the initial Linux verification: socket connection (29 tests), candidate admission (18), auth-refresh catalog (1), and auth-refresh sibling (2). That admission revision froze both clocks; subsequent macOS verification exposed SQLite worker deadline failures, so the final patch preserves real wall time and freezes only the activation clock. The final admission revision is reverified below. The first Linux admission probe was excluded because its temporary directory permissions were unsafe; verified runs used a private directory.

The final admission file passes all 18 tests on b76e (170.44s wall time) and Node (220.56s) on the loaded Mac. The final 17-second case also passes on S2 (`-t 'retains work deadline 17'`, 38.78s launcher wall time). These tests exercise the actual update CLI, isolated SQLite state, and subprocess fixtures to retain the preflight, admission, and lifecycle boundary checks. The catalog and auth-refresh sibling files also pass on both runtimes (catalog: 68.71s / 69.43s; sibling: 98.05s / 66.10s, b76e / Node).

Commands, each one file at a time:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1
```

Bun runs put the checksum-verified b76e or S2 binary first on `PATH` and select it through `OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH`. Files: `src/gateway/server/ws-connection.test.ts`, `src/cli/update-cli.candidate-admission.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/models-auth-refresh.catalog.integration.test.ts`, and `src/gateway/server-methods/models-auth-refresh.integration.test.ts`.

Format, scoped oxlint, and test typechecks for `gateway-server`, `gateway-methods`, and `cli-update` passed on Linux; final changed-file format and lint were rechecked locally. `pr-simplify` completed. Final staged Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2. After integrating current main, its unchanged 29-test socket file passed on b76e, S2, and Node. The catalog and auth-refresh sibling files passed again on b76e and Node; the catalog fixture hunk is unchanged from the Linux verification.

After rebasing onto `69eefd48c800e`, the branch preserves main's stronger one-write socket assertion and includes the terminal-PTY mock-exports baseline repair from #171916. The branch was squashed to `f50628a687b26c30f6524c37520ee3a4b758b7e5` with an accurate test-only commit subject. Candidate admission (18 tests), auth-refresh catalog (1), and socket connection (29) each passed once on Node 26.12.0 and pinned Bun `1.4.3-canary.1+b76e4b4e6`, run serially with `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/oc-s2triage`. Exact-head [CI run 39076327765](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39076327765) completed green according to the native exact-head CI watcher (zero pending; superseded checks excluded). No CI rerun or baseline exception was needed. The prior-head ClawSweeper re-review reported no findings; the coordinator approved the unchanged two-file fixture diff for landing.

Production LOC: +0/-0. Test LOC against current main: +5/-1. No skips, test-timeout increases, Node routing, or fork workarounds.

prs.title: refactor(skills): make Skill Workshop a direct, versioned self-learning loop
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skill Workshop learned through proposals that waited in an approval queue nobody reviewed, so agents rarely improved. Per-agent skill allowlists also hid learned skills from the agent that learned them. Proposal storage, a weekly AI curator, collection reviews and approval UIs added a lot of code and several competing owners.

## Why This Change Was Made

- One write owner: the `skill_workshop` tool (list, view, create, patch, write_file, remove_file, archive, restore) makes every learned-skill change.
- Every change saves the previous version (ten per skill) and records a change row, so undo is a restore. Each write rechecks the caller's authority at the file effect.
- Background review: it runs after about ten model steps, or after a turn that used a learned skill.
  - It forks the conversation. It may use read-only lookup tools, and `skill_workshop` is the only tool that changes anything.
  - It posts "💾 Learned … Say "undo" to revert" in the originating chat, plus a system event with the exact revert call.
- Learning modes are `off` and `auto`. Learned skills are always visible to their agent.
- A deterministic 30-day unused-skill archive replaces the LLM curator. Skills named by a cron job are kept.
- Writes return non-blocking authoring advisories. A `create` lists the agent's other learned skills so the agent can merge duplicates.
- Doctor retires the proposal system:
  - exports pending drafts to `workshop-skills/.archive/.retired-proposals/`;
  - recovers half-finished applies;
  - keeps proposals whose owner is unknown;
  - drops the four proposal tables;
  - rewrites `propose` to `off`;
  - removes collection-review cron jobs.
- Control UI Workshop page: skills, change feed with Undo, Learning switch, built on the shared settings and Carapace primitives. Gateway methods and the CLI: `skills.workshop.*`. The retired `skills.proposals.*` and `skills.curator.*` methods return an error that names the replacements.

## User Impact

- Agents now learn and improve skills on their own, announce each change, and undo it on request.
- Users who chose `propose` are switched to `off` and keep their drafts in the archive folder; turning on `auto` resumes learning.
- Plugins lose the proposal hooks. No schema version bump: the change log table is additive, and only Doctor drops the retired tables.

## Config compatibility

Every changed `skills.workshop` key has a Doctor migration. `openclaw update` and Docker startup run Doctor, so updated installs are migrated before the Gateway starts. A raw package install left on an old config is refused, with a message naming the key and `openclaw doctor --fix`. Defaults are unchanged: an unset mode is `auto`, and `maxSkillBytes` stays 40000 (1024–200000).

| Old config | Before Doctor | After `openclaw doctor --fix` |
|---|---|---|
| `autonomous.mode: "propose"` | invalid (allowed: `off`, `auto`) | `"off"`, with a hint to set `auto` |
| `autonomous.enabled: true` (legacy) | invalid | `mode: "off"` (previously mapped to `propose`), same hint |
| `autonomous.enabled: false` (legacy) | invalid | `mode: "off"` |
| `approvalPolicy`, `maxPending` | unrecognized keys | removed |
| `maxSkillBytes`, `autonomous.mode: "off"`/`"auto"` | valid | unchanged |

Observed with the candidate CLI on isolated configs: `config validate` reports each retired key, `doctor --fix` prints the change lines above, keeps `maxSkillBytes: 20000`, and `config validate` then passes. Downgrading leaves a valid config, since `off` and `auto` exist in earlier releases.

## Evidence

- Telegram Test Server with a real `openai/gpt-6-astra` model on the Codex runtime: `/learn`, a background review with the notice in the same chat, "undo" restoring the exact pre-review version, and Learning off suppressing reviews.
- Upgrades through the published updater: from 2026.9.4 with every proposal shape, from 2026.9.7, and from 2026.9.7 with `propose` mode and an allowlist. Drafts were exported, tables retired, the mode rewritten, and the Gateway ready.
- Control UI before/after screenshots (Workshop page, Undo, polish pass): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161057#issuecomment-6029477642
- Two live claws ran the change, and a live run on the head merged with current main confirmed create, notice and undo.
- Archive and restore authority at the final file effect: the real `skill_workshop` tool on a real filesystem, as a background review, revoked by a real abort signal or a real Learning-Off config change at 0–120% of the measured operation time (164 runs). Each run either completed or was refused with the live skill byte-identical; none left a partial skill or staging directory. The same sweep on the previous archive (guarded recursive removal) left a partly deleted live skill in 19 of 80 runs, which is why archive now takes the skill out of service by one fenced rename.

  | action / revocation | completed | refused, live intact | partial |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | archive / abort | 12 | 28 | 0 |
  | archive / Learning-Off | 19 | 21 | 0 |
  | restore / abort | 20 | 20 | 0 |
  | restore / Learning-Off | 17 | 23 | 0 |

- Operator archive and restore (`skills.workshop.archive`/`restore`) bind the Gateway request-mutation authority captured at admission as the library's final-effect guard. On an isolated candidate Gateway, a real paired operator device started an archive or restore of a 20,001-file learned skill, and while it was still staging, the real admin CLI revoked it (`openclaw devices remove`, and separately `openclaw devices revoke --role operator`). In all four revoked runs the Gateway refused with "Gateway requester authority changed", the live skill stayed byte-identical, and no version, change row or staging directory was left. The same requests without revocation completed. A handler regression test fails without the binding. Full report: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161057#issuecomment-6046044250

- Doctor recovery of state written by published 2026.9.7 (its CLI created the proposals, its Gateway applied, quarantined and rejected them; full report: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161057#issuecomment-6029283234). Each case ran `doctor --fix` twice, then the step the warning names, then Doctor again until it settled:
  - Half-finished apply with SKILL.md past its pre-apply bytes but support files not: Doctor exports the other drafts, keeps all four tables and the nine proposal files byte-identical, and leaves the live skill alone. Run 2 changes nothing. After the operator restores the recorded pre-apply files, Doctor drops the tables.
  - Half-finished apply with SKILL.md still at its pre-apply bytes: Doctor puts the support files back, removes the created file and retires everything in one run.
  - Draft whose agent was removed from config: kept whole (draft and both support files, matching sha256) across repeated runs. Re-adding the agent exports the full bundle to that agent's archive; deleting the directory instead retires the record. Both settle on the next run.
  - Clean state (applied, pending, quarantined, rejected): pending and quarantined drafts are exported with every support file, the applied skill stays live, and the tables drop. Run 2 does nothing.
  - Config: the candidate Gateway refuses `propose` with "Run openclaw doctor --fix"; Doctor rewrites it to `off`, after which the Gateway is ready (`/healthz` 200). A candidate Gateway on the retired state starts without Workshop errors.
- Typecheck, lint, architecture, protocol and dead-code checks pass, along with the Workshop, Doctor, CLI, Gateway e2e and UI suites. Full CI on `0ac6d718` is red only in tests that are red on its main merge parent `07e9a251942`: each of the 23 failing files was run on both. In 17 files the failing tests and error signatures are identical. In the other 6 (Gateway chat and session suites), the failing set shifts between runs on both sides with the same `Agent database execution admission is closed` error, and every failure seen only on this branch passed on rerun.


### Landing CI repair verification

At `caa11e2e71f73b2ac8a102db34a26f06561330ba`, two test-only fixups address the failed jobs from `765584c7`; production code is unchanged (22 added lines in two test/config files):

- Ported the already-landed [directive database-worker routing fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3cbd049ccfd8b952d9e6a8de7ba7cb0829275ca3), preserving Peter’s authorship. The six broker-admission failures were independently observed on main as well as this PR. The tests now run through the real host rather than a new placement mock.
- The plugin fixture now awaits real post-ready maintenance and existing reload settlement before further mutations. A controlled real-lease probe demonstrated that config settlement alone could return while maintenance still held the lease. The precise holder in the original CI log was not recorded; this does not claim an ordinary local reproduction of that scheduling race. No retry or weaker assertion was introduced.

**Exact repaired-candidate proof:** 174 tests across the three directive consumers and `server-plugins.startup-error.test.ts` passed with `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/directive-handling.mixed-inline.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/directive-handling.model.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-native-slash-fast-path.test.ts src/gateway/server-plugins.startup-error.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, wrapper wall time 134.80s. The earlier 44 focused Workshop/Doctor/UI tests passed on `765584c7` in 74.22s; that result remains stamped to its original head. Independent P0/P1 review of the final two-file delta completed with no actionable findings.

The new head still goes through normal required CI and review gates. Earlier red CI and overrides are not represented as a current-head pass.

<!-- roboclaw-landing-proof:caa11e2e71f73b2ac8a102db34a26f06561330ba -->


**Conflict repair:** `54dfe9761360cf46ad0ec41aa65e50f80de86e64` integrates main `2a305612` after GitHub reported an actual conflict. The sole conflicted file was generated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`; `pnpm config:docs:gen` regenerated it and `pnpm config:docs:check` passed. No production code needed manual conflict resolution. On the merged tree, 39 tests across database preflight, Workshop Doctor recovery, Workshop RPC and config-baseline suites passed (five Vitest shards, 60.05s). Earlier proof above retains its original head attribution. Normal required gates remain in force.

<!-- roboclaw-conflict-proof:54dfe976 -->


### Latest landing repair evidence

At `ee2d42aa751e90ec7135f096d81971959445e87b`:

- The remaining restart CI failure was reproduced in the supported network-isolated runner. The fixture reused the Control UI device identity for a non-inline TEST client, rotating the original credential; recovery correctly refused it. Giving the observer its own identity fixes the test without changing production authority checks, timeouts, or completion assertions. The real process-restart case now passes, including durable/projected `done`, the widget update, terminal publication, and exactly one final reply (Vitest 62.73s; test body 30.684s). Pinned Node 26.8.2, pnpm 12.5.1 and prepared Playwright 1.63.0 image were used.
- Independent P0/P1 review of that fixture patch found no actionable issue; scoped lint and formatting passed.
- Actual conflicts with main were resolved without restoring the retired proposal lifecycle. The readonly/Doctor suites passed 29 cases on `f574902d` (49.11s). Main had moved an unrelated `before_install` case into a retired file; its event and assertions were preserved byte-for-byte in their original test owner, and that case passed (2.72s).
- The later Code Mode test conflict preserves both main’s cleanup/consolidation and the Workshop usage regression. All 35 Code Mode cases passed on the final merged tree (46.95s). The restart fixture and its authority/issuer/validator source inputs did not change in that merge.

The earlier auto-merge request was explicitly retired through native recovery before changing its head. Replacement landing awaits completed required CI; prior red runs are not relabeled as green and no CI exception is asserted.

<!-- roboclaw-replacement-proof:ee2d42aa751e90ec7135f096d81971959445e87b -->


<!-- roboclaw-replacement-proof:482ad096dea9f48d5ba90683be22d19395a5e8a8 -->
### Landing repair evidence — `482ad096`

The simplified Workshop cutover is unchanged. This candidate repairs the concrete owner/fixture failures found while landing, and resolves the actual conflict with main `5ffec9b0`:

- Locked transcript writes retain the captured logical owner selector separately from the physical database path, including upstream native adapters. No authority checks were relaxed.
- Concurrent baseline requests reuse the same settled capture instead of repeating it after a delayed claim response.
- Late schema observers preserve only current matching admission receipts; local DDL, changed markers, and revoked receipts still invalidate them.
- The Doctor fixture now asserts its preliminary catalog diagnostic separately; the actual future-version refusal and zero service-stop assertions remain unchanged.

**Executed proof:** 143 combined writer/capture/admission regressions passed on the composed tree (120.60s). All 8 audit/progress tests passed, including the immutable `5dc4cf6` terminal-only reader across reopen (35.26s). The first reader attempt stalled acquiring an old Git object; the scoped acquisition was repaired before the passing replay. The generated database-worker inventory was regenerated and checked; scoped lint/format passed. Prior Doctor proof: 45 cases passed in 68.85s on the repair before this main merge.

Independent P0/P1 reviews of the three substantive repairs and the exact merged writer integration were scoped-clean. The integration review used an explicit review-only snapshot of the three composed files, verified byte-identical to this candidate; it was not represented as a hosted-head review or execution.

**Limits:** full local QA smoke replay stopped at a Crabline Telegram `getMe` HTTP 500 before the scenario; the boundary regressions above are not a claim that the full smoke flows passed. The separate node-relay failure did not reproduce in isolated execution; no speculative node patch or inherited/flaky waiver was adopted. Required CI and native replacement admission still apply to this head. Older proof sections retain their original executing revisions.


<!-- roboclaw-replacement-proof:21918d1bf2314e2f91ab4161aba779f4e36aeb84 -->
### Subsequent main conflict — `21918d1b`

Main `0ed468e6` changed the same plugin reload fixture. The resolution keeps upstream isolation of background maintenance for this manual-RPC test, removes the obsolete observer/wait for the now-disabled work, and keeps config reconciliation settlement after a successful reload. All activation-error, recovery and disable assertions remain. Production scheduling and authorization are unchanged.

Both reload cases and all four separate post-ready-maintenance scheduler cases passed on the composed tree: **6/6, 44.33s**. Scoped lint/format and native localization inventory verification passed. Independent P0/P1 review of the exact one-file resolution was scoped-clean; its review snapshot was verified against the merged source.

The writer, baseline-capture and schema-admission repair owners are unchanged from `482ad096`; their previously recorded proof retains that executing revision. The older CI run is being collected separately and is not counted as CI success for this replacement. Required new-head gates remain mandatory.


<!-- roboclaw-replacement-proof:d16f8868f9e4c9326911992de39f3935bb11c2c0 -->
### Landing candidate — `d16f8868`

- Composed main `b5c9a256` with the existing late-reader fix. A narrow publication check now refuses an older independent receipt if a newly promoted schema cell was revoked. Four negative controls failed before the repair; healthy promotion, fresh worker readmission and optional transfer semantics remain covered. No new registry, epoch, query, retry or persisted schema was added.
- Reused the canonical nonblocking-title fixture fix from [#166888](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166888), preserving @RomneyDa’s credit. Deletion completes while title generation is pending, and the late title cannot recreate the deleted row. No title runtime behavior changed.
- Corrected the side-question fixture to configure an actual sender denial. Restricted search is disabled; an allowed sender can still use cached hosted search without a managed provider. Production search policy is unchanged.

**Repair-head proof (`40f14079`; not relabeled as new-head execution):** 121 schema/admission/index-owner cases passed (56.55s), plus 22 Gateway title/session cases and 56 Codex side-question cases (92.08s). Core types, the gateway-server/state-logging test type graphs, scoped type-aware lint, formatting and the regenerated worker inventory passed. Independent P0/P1 review of the exact repair snapshot was scoped-clean; snapshot blobs were checked against the candidate.

prs.title: fix(telegram): agent gets the same image twice when a reply re-sends the replied-to image
prs.body:
Supersedes #126789 (same fix, re-derived on current main). Related: #57278, #57280.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the agent receives the same Telegram image twice when a user replies to an image with that same image, because the current message and the reply ancestor are staged at different local paths.

## User Impact

User impact: a same-source image in a reply reaches the agent once instead of twice. Distinct images are unaffected, and replies to images the bot sent keep delivering that image to the agent, as on `main`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram's `file_unique_id` is the stable source identity across file-id changes and local restaging. It is carried on the transient `TelegramMediaRef` from singleton ingress, album ingress, retained reply media and downloaded reply media, and checked at the current-media/reply-media join before a reply ancestor or an explicit external reply is hydrated. Only current media that actually reached the agent claims its source, so if the current download fails, a replied copy still reaches the agent next to the `[media unavailable: ...]` notice.

Earlier heads also skipped reply media the bot had sent. That is gone: `main` hydrates it on purpose (`hydrates allowlisted group reply ancestors`), the bot's earlier image is context the user may be asking about, and ClawSweeper flagged the skip as P1. #57278, which asks for the skip, stays a separate product decision, so this PR no longer closes it.

Re-derived on `main` (`7a3a827c85`) rather than rebased, because `main` restructured `resolveReplyMediaForChain` into a `hydrateMedia` helper and added external-reply hydration (#151911). The e2e file keeps its own media-group timer hold because #155842 moved the shared helper on `main`. Since then `main` moved the singleton attachment download into a deferred media resolver (#162787); the `fileUniqueId` handoff moved into it with the merge below (`extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.inbound-processing.ts:209`).

No config, default, protocol, SQLite or persisted-schema change: `TelegramResolvedMedia.fileUniqueId` was already part of the persisted message-cache value, and the new optional field is on the transient ref.

## Evidence

Head `e8f999cf4b2`. The branch conflicted with `main`, so this head merges `main` `27e3afbd8fc` into `0e1bce35c2d`. One conflict, in `bot-handlers.inbound-processing.ts`, where #162787 had rewritten the block that builds the singleton media ref; the resolution is main's block plus the one `fileUniqueId` line. The diff against `main` is the same 6 files as before the merge, +394/-3. Runs below are on an M4 Pro, Node 26, pnpm 12.

- `bot.media.reply-source-identity.e2e.test.ts`: 4 passed. Same-source reply -> 1 provider image. Failed current download keeps the notice and the replied copy. One album that replies to an earlier photo, carrying that photo plus a new one -> 2 images, not 3. Same-source external reply is not fetched.
- The same file against `main`'s production code (the 4 production files at `27e3afbd8fc`, tests unchanged): 3 failed, 1 passed. `expected { payloads: 2, unique: 1 } to deeply equal { payloads: 1, unique: 1 }` for the same-source reply, a third media path for the album, and `getFile` called once for the external reply. The unavailable-media case passes on `main` by design, since it guards against over-deduping.
- `bot.test.ts`: 61 passed. The file is `main`'s, untouched by this PR, including `hydrates allowlisted group reply ancestors`.
- `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test` rc=0; oxlint on the 6 changed files, 0 warnings and 0 errors; line-cap, max-lines and assertion-safety ratchets pass against `27e3afbd8fc`.
- Test cost, `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/bot.media.reply-source-identity.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: Vitest 29.8 s, the 4 cases 0.8-1.1 s each; 226 s wall including the e2e build prerequisites on a cold checkout. No CI run exists for this head yet.

CI on the previous head `0e1bce35c2d` (run 35895745567) was red on `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`, in a file this PR does not touch: the assertion-safety ratchet reported `extensions/google/realtime-voice-provider.ts: 4 < 5`, a stale baseline entry on that run's base `0b0777a1705`. `main`'s baseline now lists 4 for that file, and the ratchet passes on this head.

Earlier history: at `a36b01fe994` `bot.test.ts` failed 3 external-reply cases with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'type')` (CI job 106584279631); that read went away with the bot-media skip. The album case fails with only the album-ingress `fileUniqueId` handoff removed: the replied-to original shows up as a third media path (measured before the merge, not re-run).

Known `main` failures, not regressions, measured at `7a3a827c85` with a clean-main dist build: 4 album/media-group e2e cases (`warning-topics` 0/1/2 failed attachments, `downloads-media-file-path` custom apiRoot) fail identically without this change. Not re-measured at `27e3afbd8fc`.

Not covered: a live Telegram Test Server run. The request-bound Telegram proof is maintainer-only, rejects fork heads and excludes media, and the userbot proof needs Convex-leased QA credentials I don't have, so it needs a maintainer or a credential owner with the telegram-e2e-userbot skill: a DM photo, a reply to it carrying the same photo (the final provider request should hold 1 image), and a reply to a bot-sent photo (the image should still arrive). The open question for that run is whether Telegram gives a user's re-sent copy of the same image the same `file_unique_id`. If it does not, this PR won't dedupe that case.

## After-fix proof (production, retained data to 2026-10-16)

**1. The duplicate case has not happened in production.** The two gateways' retained Telegram message caches (2026-09-15 to 2026-10-16) hold 281 inbound messages that carry media and reply to another message. 45 of them reply to a message that itself carries media. In 0 of those 45 does the current media share a `file_unique_id` with the replied-to media. So no production turn exists where this dedupe fired, and there is no final provider image count for one. This is a fact about the incoming Telegram messages as stored, so it does not depend on which build received them.

**2. Telegram gives a re-sent copy the same `file_unique_id`, in every case we have.** That was the open question for a live run. On the gateway with 3 Telegram accounts:

- 18 photo `file_unique_id`s each appear on 2 to 4 separate messages. That is 38 messages, all from human senders and none forwarded. 5 of the 18 appear in two different chats.
- Documents and videos repeat the same way: 12 ids across 50 non-forwarded messages.

We cannot see which client action produced each copy. A re-encoded copy would be a new file with a new id. Like item 1, this is a property of Telegram's updates, not of the build.

**3. A reply to an image the bot sent still carries that image into the turn.** These two turns ran on v2026.10.1 with local patches. In that build's four source files, every line this PR adds or removes is added or removed the same way. The build's other local patches touch the same files in other places, and `bot.media.reply-source-identity.e2e.test.ts` is byte-identical.

On 2026-10-13/14, two DM replies on the 3-account gateway replied to images the bot had sent: a sticker replying to a bot photo, and a photo replying to a bot image sent as a document. In both turns the stored transcript lists two attachments: the current one, then the replied-to file (matched by its stored media id).

- **Sticker reply.** Media understanding described the sticker in text, and the turn's image layout makes the bot's photo the one inline image. The run recorded `imagesCount: 1`, and that image is the replied-to photo.
- **Photo reply.** Media understanding described the photo in text. The bot's image entered as a `document` attachment, so it was handled as a file (an "Unsupported document format" note with its local path), not as an image attachment.

**Not shown:**

- A same-source reply through the real gateway, and its final provider image count. Production never had one.
- The provider request for the photo reply. The run recorded `imagesCount: 1` and its prompt contains exactly one detectable image path, the replied-to file's. That path is the likely source of the image, but the request body is not stored.
- Actual `file_unique_id` values. They are in the gateway's cache and are left out here.
- A Telegram Test Server run.

prs.title: fix(secrets): accept config-owned env markers in models.json audit
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Custom model providers configured with env SecretRefs write bare env-name markers into agent `models.json` (for example `"apiKey": "FACTCHAT_API_KEY"`). That is the intentional serialization contract. `openclaw secrets audit` only treated a fixed list of built-in env markers as non-plaintext, so an unregistered custom marker was reported as `PLAINTEXT_FOUND` even when `openclaw.json` owned the same provider with the same env SecretRef id. Operators then saw a false security finding that regenerating models.json could not clear.

Ownership must follow the models.json writer. The writer normalizes the complete provider map, then inspects the winning apiKey. Exact canonical spelling wins over aliases regardless of credential source or insertion order. A losing alias such as `OpenAI` with `LOSING_ENV` must not suppress `PLAINTEXT_FOUND` when the canonical `openai` winner is another env id, a file or store SecretRef, a literal credential, or an absent apiKey.

## Evidence

Live `node scripts/run-node.mjs secrets audit --json` against an isolated state dir on head `2d9f413b8ad15b8cc295268d59291f52428397a5`. Never `~/.openclaw`. Config and models files lived under `PROOF_HOME` and `STATE`.

Owned custom marker. Config owns `custom-factchat-cloud-mindlogic-ai.apiKey` as env SecretRef id `FACTCHAT_API_KEY`. Production writer `ensureOpenClawModelsJson` wrote that bare marker into models.json. Audit is clean:

```console
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=STATE OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=PROOF_HOME/openclaw.json node scripts/run-node.mjs secrets audit --json
{
  "status": "clean",
  "plaintextCount": 0,
  "modelsJsonFindings": []
}
```

Writer-collision control. Config has both `OpenAI` (`LOSING_ENV`) and `openai` (`WINNING_ENV`). models.json `openai.apiKey` is `WINNING_ENV`:

```console
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs secrets audit --json
{
  "status": "clean",
  "plaintextCount": 0,
  "modelsJsonFindings": []
}
```

Same env-versus-env config with models.json marker set to `LOSING_ENV`:

```console
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs secrets audit --json
{
  "status": "findings",
  "plaintextCount": 1,
  "modelsJsonFindings": [
    {
      "code": "PLAINTEXT_FOUND",
      "jsonPath": "providers.openai.apiKey",
      "provider": "openai"
    }
  ]
}
```

Mixed-source collision on this head. Canonical `openai.apiKey` is a file SecretRef; alias `OpenAI.apiKey` is env `LOSING_ENV`. models.json `openai.apiKey` is `LOSING_ENV`:

```console
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs secrets audit --json
{
  "status": "findings",
  "plaintextCount": 1,
  "modelsJsonFindings": [
    {
      "code": "PLAINTEXT_FOUND",
      "jsonPath": "providers.openai.apiKey",
      "provider": "openai"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** secrets audit accepts a models.json bare env-name marker only when the writer-winning models.providers apiKey is that env SecretRef. Losing alias `OpenAI`/`LOSING_ENV` cannot hide plaintext when the canonical winner is another env, a file or store SecretRef, a literal, or an absent apiKey.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS Darwin 25.6.0 arm64, Node v26.8.2, OpenClaw worktree at `2d9f413b8ad15b8cc295268d59291f52428397a5`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` under `/tmp/oc-proof-state-121578` (not `~/.openclaw`).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** wrote isolated openclaw.json; generated owner models.json through production `ensureOpenClawModelsJson`; ran `node scripts/run-node.mjs secrets audit --json`; then collision config with `OpenAI`/`openai` env SecretRefs, models.json `WINNING_ENV` then `LOSING_ENV`; then mixed file-canonical `openai` plus alias `OpenAI`/`LOSING_ENV` with models.json `LOSING_ENV`; same audit command after each write.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output copied above. Owner generated `FACTCHAT_API_KEY` marker is clean. Canonical `WINNING_ENV` is clean. Losing alias `LOSING_ENV` reports `PLAINTEXT_FOUND` on `providers.openai.apiKey` for both env-versus-env and file-canonical mixed source.
- **Observed result after fix:** generated config-owned custom env marker is accepted. Writer-winning canonical env marker is accepted. Losing-alias marker stays plaintext when the canonical winner is env or file.
- **What was not tested:** live gateway model call that regenerates models.json on a Windows host with a real FACTCHAT key; exec SecretRef mixed-source collision on the production CLI.

## Summary

Follows ClawSweeper fix shape for #121543: keep the models.json env marker writer contract; select the owner from the complete provider map; inspect only the winning apiKey.

Closes #121543

prs.title: fix(feishu): stop inbound mentions from cascading into replies
prs.body:
Closes #121921

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu group replies would automatically mention every non-bot participant mentioned in the inbound message, even when the agent's reply did not request those mentions. Error and fallback replies could therefore wake multiple bots and create an unintended cascade.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inbound mention targets remain available as agent context, but they are no longer passed into the reply dispatcher or automatically attached to generated replies. Explicit outbound mentions, native Feishu `at` rendering, and bot-authored required mentions (`requiredMentionTargets`) remain unchanged.

This restores the boundary introduced by #71396 without reverting the native mention-rendering improvements from #93522.

## User Impact

Feishu users and multi-agent groups no longer receive unrequested `@` notifications from ordinary, error, fallback, card, streaming, block, or chunked replies. Agents can still explicitly mention users when the outbound content or message-tool request asks for it.

## Evidence

- Regression coverage verifies non-streaming final/error replies, static cards, streaming card closes, and independent block/chunk delivery do not inherit inbound mention targets.
- Existing coverage verifies `requiredMentionTargets` still reaches every required text chunk and static card reply.
- Focused Feishu tests pass:
  - `reply-dispatcher.test.ts`: **124/124**
  - `bot.test.ts` + `send.test.ts`: **131/131**
  - Total: **255/255**
- `oxfmt --check` passes for all 3 changed files.
- Focused `oxlint` passes for all 3 changed files.
- `git diff --check` passes.

It resolves the contribution conflicts by adopting the author’s existing accepted-catalog/receipt guards and retaining the remaining executor-preparation and producer-owned per-turn context/compaction safeguards. The reconciled candidate passed 382 selected tests, affected type/lint/format checks, the canonical build, and fresh independent P0–P2 review. Exact provenance and inherited-check limits are recorded there; hosted CI/automation still requires repository-owner action. No parallel main-target source repair is being published here.

This original PR remains open pending verified adoption and complete consolidation coverage. No merge, upstream resolution or production change is claimed. The original narrow proposal and evidence below are retained as historical context; no parallel source repair is being published here.

Related: #153354. Builds on the owner/private/owner reproduction in #153356 by @jonesthefox. Related alternative: #174900.

## What Problem This Solves

Private completions can unnecessarily replace a Codex parent thread, or fail with `claimed by active work; stop it first`, when the sender transition changes the advertised built-in OpenClaw tools without changing persistent policy.

## User Impact

The participating **core** tools retain stable registration across owner/private/owner turns, including protected parents and the host-shell path used when native Codex tools are disabled. Execution still uses the real current sender and current permissions.

This is deliberately not a general plugin-catalog fix. Sender-dependent bundled or third-party factories, including the Codex management/supervision tools, can still change their declarations. No live child-notification, deployed Gateway recovery, or arbitrary client/capability transition is claimed. There is no data migration, persistent catalog, configuration change, or permission expansion.

## Why This Change Was Made

The host derives fresh data-only declarations from the actual core producers and their existing policy/availability owners. The Codex registration path consumes that projection while dispatch keeps its current-turn executors. Plugin factories never receive a fabricated owner identity.

Schemas, descriptions, conditional availability and direct/deferred placement remain owned by the real producers. Prepared executable definitions retain precedence. Genuine configuration/schema changes still invalidate normally, and the existing active-work, admission, generation and final-effect guards remain intact.

Unlike #174900's creation-time catalog receipt, this proposal does not freeze a previous whole catalog or introduce a separate broad configuration fingerprint. Its narrower core-only scope avoids changing the lifecycle of dynamically discovered plugin/MCP declarations.

## Evidence

- The original real-builder owner/private/owner regression failed with parent rotation or the active-work error, while an unchanged-owner protected control passed.
- Independent review exposed a further supported case with native tools disabled. Before the shell repair, the protected `full`/private/non-native case failed while six existing cases passed. The final candidate repairs it without weakening the fingerprint or protection guard.
- **260 selected tests pass on the updated integration candidate**: the original CI shard has 173 passes and 3 unchanged skips; 56 focused declaration/availability/portal/delegation/attempt tests and 31 shell-description/sessions-send tests also pass.
- The final tests retain the actual `runCodexAppServerAttempt` wiring smoke, protected-parent continuity, genuine schema/configuration/description invalidation, configured/runtime denies, actual plugin-factory identity, core-name replacement rejection, host revocation and explicit private dispatch rejection.
- The updated integration candidate passes core/extension/selected-test typechecks, fixture lint, 32-file formatting and `pnpm build`. Prior unchanged-core lint, SDK surface/export and docs checks remain recorded separately; fresh broad CI has now passed on the updated head.
- The original core implementation passed supplemental independent static review. The complete updated candidate passed a fresh canonical `autoreview` P0–P2 pass (`scoped-clean`) with no actionable findings; these reviews did not execute project tests.
- The commit-ref SDK API comparison completed on the tested commit. It reports no added/removed entrypoints or removed exports. The intended changes are an optional data-only host reader and a broader accepted input type for `getPluginToolMeta`; the other affected exports are declaration-reachability changes. The API delta was inspected, rather than treating exit zero as proof of an unchanged API.

The continuity fixtures exercise production construction, admission, dispatch and lifecycle owners with synthetic native transport. Separate native-finalization tests execute the actual Codex binary against a loopback Responses fixture; they do not establish the requested Gateway owner/private/owner trace. No live provider/channel calls or deployed-Gateway recovery are claimed.

### CI integration repair

The first remote CI run failed six cases in `settled-turn-finalizer.native.test.ts`. Its checkout was the PR merge with main at `a1ba919b315f`, not the originally tested branch tree. Upstream #173945 moved context capture behind `onSettledTurn`, but this native fixture had not adopted the callback. An untouched checkout of that main parent reproduced the same **6 failures / 3 passes**. Adding only the fixture callback produced **9 passes**, without changing assertions, production capture, credentials or authority checks.

This revision integrates that exact CI baseline and the four-line fixture migration. Before the fixture change, the local merge tree was verified identical to the failing CI merge. The original six-file shard now passes locally. The old failed CI result is retained as historical evidence. **[Remote CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39000888171) on updated head `324abbddbc26261c0b9131274f585dde2432f576`**, and the aggregate CI/dependency/security status contexts are successful. This does not resolve the separate runtime-proof or maintainer-decision requests below.

### Isolated real-runtime attempt: prerequisite blocked, not behavior proof

An attempt on exact head `324abbddbc26261c0b9131274f585dde2432f576` used the canonical built Gateway, native Codex `0.162.0`, a persistent authenticated task-only operator client, and a scripted loopback Responses provider inside a network-none container. The real core `plugins({action:"list",query:"codex"})` call succeeded and its result was consumed by Codex.

The next real native `exec_command` call, under explicit `guardian` / `on-request` / user-reviewer / `workspace-write` permissions, returned exit 1 with `bwrap: No permissions to create a new namespace`. Its error was consumed in the subsequent Responses request; it produced neither background readiness nor a session ID. This identifies a native-sandbox prerequisite failure under the test container's restrictions, not which host/Docker security layer denied it and not regression evidence against this patch.

**The requested owner → private child completion → owner trace remains unexecuted.** No child was spawned, no private `plugins disable codex` attempt occurred, and no protected-parent continuity or private rejection was established. The intact baseline was not run because this prerequisite failure would not provide a discriminating before/after comparison. The saved driver currently covers startup and these prerequisites, not the complete remaining scenario.

No sandbox bypass, extra container privilege, host-policy change, real credential or production access was used. The containers, runtime processes and disposable state were cleaned up and independently checked. This is local-provider prerequisite evidence only, not remote-model/OAuth/channel proof. Further execution requires an authorized isolated environment capable of running the native sandbox without weakening its controls.

### Remaining before merge

- Maintainer direction on the additive, intentionally core-only public host contract is still needed.
- The real Gateway/native-Codex protected owner → private completion → owner proof with private-tool rejection remains author-owned work, blocked by the prerequisite above. Existing harness evidence and the partial runtime attempt do not satisfy that request. No re-review has been requested on the strength of this partial result.
- Remote review of the earlier head found no actionable code defects, which is not approval of the updated head or permission to merge.

<details>
<summary>Scope and local proof cost</summary>

The candidate is not a small diff: production +681/-293, tests/support +770/-12, documentation +46/-0 across 32 files. Some churn moves the existing assembly/control code; the new responsibilities are core provenance, a host-lifetime-bound declaration projection and conditional producer coverage. No second permission owner, persistent cache, new tool or general plugin descriptor API is introduced. The test matrix was reduced to representative cases while retaining distinct security and lifecycle boundaries.

The updated candidate's original-CI-shard replay took 76.40 seconds; focused contracts took 192.56 seconds; producer siblings took 87.53 seconds; build took 213.15 seconds. These slower fixtures exercise real admitted tool construction, native processes and retained thread ownership rather than mocking the repaired decisions. They are not runtime-latency benchmarks. Remote job timing is available in the linked passing CI run; a per-file CI timing breakdown has not been extracted.

</details>

prs.body:
Builds on Ricardo Almeida’s #175009, whose commits remain in the ancestry. Integrates main’s #175309 stable tool surfaces and invocation-time denials.

## What Problem This Solves

Caller-dependent declarations can make OpenClaw replace a Codex thread while native background work still owns it, failing with “claimed by active work.” Stable core producers avoid incidental changes; genuine plugin or MCP discovery changes still need the native thread owner to decide when to publish them.

Keep that decision in the existing owners: core producers supply literal declarations, and the native binding retains only the declarations Codex accepted while work protects the thread. New declarations become available through the existing idle replacement/history handoff. Dispatch still uses current-turn executors, permissions and invocation authority; an accepted declaration never grants execution.

The refresh preserves main’s stable sender-dependent tool definitions and denied-call behavior, including completion-handoff execution limits. It adds the declaration projection without reinstating older per-turn schema selection. The saved catalog contains bounded serializable data, with no executors, grants, separate manager or pending queue.

## User Impact

Owner replies can continue while native work is active; genuinely new declarations wait for idle publication, with current execution denials preserved. If an existing tool’s schema or description changes during protected work, the incompatible implementation remains unavailable until idle publication.

## Why This Change Was Made

The core producer supplies stable declarations and the existing native binding owns accepted-catalog publication, avoiding competing catalog state or premature busy-thread replacement.

## Maintainer decision requested

Approve the optional `hostCapabilities.readCoreToolDeclarations(tools)` contract and the existing binding’s accepted-catalog receipt, including deferred additions until native work is idle. The optional method preserves existing harness consumers; the Codex harness adopts it for registration only. The tradeoff is explicit: a genuinely new tool may wait for idle publication instead of making an otherwise valid reply replace a busy thread. Unknown older remote catalogs remain preserved with an actionable refusal rather than guessed declarations.

No approving owner decision is claimed. This remains the genuine maintainer decision before merge.

## Compatibility

No SQL schema migration is added by this PR. The existing binding record remains readable without the optional accepted snapshot. The reader accepts validated receipt versions 1, 2 and 3 without rewriting existing receipts; unknown resumes stay unknown, incompatible or corrupt receipts preserve the thread, and native-owned supervision catalogs remain native-owned. Existing configuration, permission and native-work guards still apply.

The isolated official-stable `2026.10.4` upgrade below loaded existing session/binding data through the supported offline `doctor --fix` migration, retained the physical session and model selection, and produced a real native reply. Its native thread rotated because the releases have different actual tool descriptors. This proves successful upgrade, not same-thread continuity across incompatible catalogs or restart survival of busy native work. The earlier byte-identity comparison supported reuse on the prior refreshed revision. Earlier outputs below remain explicitly prior-revision evidence. Fresh merged-tree native compatibility and actual-native stable-upgrade proofs are recorded first below; earlier revision outputs retain explicit source labels.

## Evidence

Published merge `1bc5852d47ef09a53a864be284cb88d94073aa3d` has the two declared parents and tree `e2b7d13597fa850c884d9202483e6cffd10eb1dc`, exactly matching the frozen source used by both fresh native proofs. The merge conflict is resolved; replacement-head CI is pending.

**Pinned-main conflict refresh:** Frozen candidate index tree `e2b7d13597fa850c884d9202483e6cffd10eb1dc` has publication parents `6bb14b98219bf8139c4cf86cd6096f2e11818d0c` and pinned main `bcd6ab322aeb6d7a1bd3550477c1875213889e64`. Main #175787 moved descriptor snapshot caching/schema preparation back into the finalizer owner. The resolution keeps that owner and forwards the existing optional core declarations into final availability guidance; it does not restore the removed helper or older producer selection. Both original #175009 commits remain ancestors through the first parent.

The merged candidate passes 75 focused tests across final descriptor reuse, declaration guidance/registration, active/fallback executor compatibility, accepted heartbeat constraints, catalog receipts and protected warm admission; scoped core lint, formatting, and the canonical runtime build pass. A fresh whole-candidate review found no actionable P0–P2 defects. Broad type/package/architecture and platform checks remain for the new published merge head's CI; prior-head green checks are not relabeled current.

The owner explicitly authorized the harmless peer probe without changing tool authority; JSON-quoted tool arguments ensured the source sent the complete probe. No production Gateway or user session is used.

Existing [native-owner transport proof](https://github.com/enki/openclaw-public/actions/runs/39010719179) covers host and MCP catalog changes, deferred publication, denial of unavailable executors and idle adoption. [Producer/authorization proof](https://github.com/enki/openclaw-public/actions/runs/39008361719) and [fixture proof](https://github.com/enki/openclaw-public/actions/runs/39012631251) remain prior-head evidence. Exact refreshed-head broad CI will be reported separately.

The operator Gateway has not been deployed from this public revision.

### CI integration repair

The refreshed-head native attempt suite exposed two stale private-completion assertions after main’s stable-declaration change. The regression now checks the actual invocation boundary: offered owner-gated tools return explicit authority guidance without executing, identityless transcript access throws its exact denial, and the UI capability ceiling still withholds screen access. Schema-valid harmless arguments prevent validation errors from masquerading as authorization proof. The complete published-tree attempt suite passes all 136 cases. Fresh P2 review and formatting pass. Scoped extension lint could not reach linting because its managed SDK declaration prerequisite exceeded the fixed five-minute budget; owning extension types and lint remain for exact-head PR CI, with no guard bypass or timeout increase. Production source is unchanged by this test repair.



### Bun fixture launcher CI repair

The isolated-completion adapter test used `process.execPath` for a Node wrapper fixture. Under Bun, that selected Bun itself, and the existing private launcher correctly rejected its script prefix. The fixture now uses the already-exported SDK `resolveTestNodeExecPath`; Vitest continues running under the selected runtime. Production code, private-launch isolation, credentials, scenarios, and assertions are unchanged.

Qualified baseline: the existing allowed case fails under the actual pinned Bun runtime with the exact private-launcher prefix rejection. Fixed fixture: all three allowed/forbidden/revoked cases pass under true pinned Bun and Node, including their existing account-binding and no-protocol-effects assertions (3/3 each; 25.38s and 26.06s test durations). Artifact verification, formatting, diff checks, and fresh independent P0–P2 review pass. Types and type-aware lint remain for PR CI; no broad local SDK/type graph was run for this test-only change. Runtime tests used independent copies of the exact previously built parent artifacts.

prs.title: fix(update): recover migrated Gateways after verification failure
prs.body:
Fixes #175865

## What Problem This Solves

After state migration, an unverified activation could leave the installed Gateway stopped and report `verifying: exit unknown`, `package-backup-retention: exit 1`, and `state-migrated-no-rollback`.

## User Impact

Recovery can start and verify the installed candidate after normal Doctor completion. Verified activation still succeeds when obsolete backup removal is blocked; its warning now preserves the filesystem cause and retained path. The original verification failure remains visible when recovery cannot establish that the whole update completed successfully.

## Why This Change Was Made

A normal, fully settled Doctor often emits no process-settlement step. Forward recovery incorrectly required that step or a database-rollback attempt before it would inspect the candidate schemas. The existing recovery owner now admits that inspection when candidate schema metadata is available, then uses its existing migration check, owned-service restart, and health verification. Failed writer settlement, other named data risks, foreign services, and restored databases retain their existing restrictions.

The package cleanup owner already bounds obsolete backup work and classifies ordinary filesystem errors as maintenance warnings. Its fallback discarded the deletion and rename causes. Both are now included, including `EPERM` and `EBUSY`, without adding retries or changing backup custody.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the new composed regression reproduced all three reported phases and ended `stopped-free`. Afterward, the same real retained package transaction and finalization path recover and verify the candidate. The focused new case takes 827 ms of test time; the complete invocation took 90.26 s including a 63.1 s runtime build.
- The new cleanup case injects `EPERM` during removal and `EBUSY` during fallback rename. It checks that the candidate and launcher remain active, the old backup remains retained, the persisted run succeeds, and the report includes both causes. The pre-fix run failed because those causes were missing.
- The published `v2026.10.3` driver already records `candidateSchemaVersions` in `update-command-execution.ts` and carries it through the existing migrated-worker handoff. No new driver marker or input field is required. This is source compatibility evidence, not a claimed live Windows upgrade.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <38 importer files in original discovery order> --maxWorkers=2`: **858 passed**, 37 files passed, one existing file / six tests skipped; exit 0 in 747.52 s. The three runtime groups reported 436 + 260 + 162 passing tests. Exact imports were discovered from the two changed production owners plus their `update-command-service` / `package-update-swap` barrels.
- In the complete run, the new migration case took **413 ms**, and the retained-backup case **504 ms**. The complete modified files used 22.193 s and 10.639 s of summed test time, respectively.
- Core and CLI-update test `tsgo`, type-aware Oxlint on all four TypeScript files, Oxfmt, `git diff --check`, the line-cap ratchet, MDX validation, and Madge (zero cycles) passed.
- Independent Codex review: scoped-clean at P0–P2. The simplification pass retains the existing owners and adds no new policy, configuration, schema, dependency, or retry mechanism.
- Windows native execution was not performed. Proof uses isolated HOME/state, real package swaps and recovery orchestration, with filesystem/service I/O fixtures. The issue's redacted diagnostics do not establish whether Defender, another open handle, permissions, or path length caused the original Windows error.
- Full `check:changed` was replaced with the campaign-authorized targeted checks; its SQLite inventory was skipped for time. PR CI supplies broad proof.

Production: +6/-4 (net +2). Tests: +41/-11 (net +30). Documentation: +7/-0. The test growth extends two existing scenario tables to cover the missing recovery and error-reporting contracts.

Existing slow files (summed test time):

- `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-original-service.test.ts`: 182.674 s.
- `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-database-rollback.test.ts`: 164.438 s.
- `src/cli/update-cli.windows-lifecycle.test.ts`: 153.314 s.
- `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-lease.test.ts`: 138.372 s.
- `src/cli/update-cli.service-authority.test.ts`: 123.326 s.

These unchanged scenarios repeatedly exercise real package/database copies and native-process lifecycle fixtures. The campaign's pre-existing slow-suite exception applies; no timeout, retry, skip, or baseline was changed. CI timings are not yet available.

Closes #175736

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: typing a URL in the SGLang or vLLM setup prompt appends it to the prefilled default.

## User Impact

A typed URL is saved as typed. Enter on a blank prompt uses the stored URL, else the default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The default is now a hint, not prefilled text. Only a stored URL is prefilled, as LiteLLM does.

## Evidence

Terminal capture (pty, isolated state dir), `openclaw models auth login --provider sglang`, then reading `models.providers.sglang.baseUrl`. `stable` is the published v2026.10.4, `PR` is this branch.

```
# stable, fresh state, type http://gpu-box:30000/v1
◆  SGLang base URL
│  http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1█
saved: http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1http://gpu-box:30000/v1

# PR, fresh state, type http://gpu-box:30000/v1
◆  SGLang base URL
│  http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1
saved: http://gpu-box:30000/v1
```
