prs.title: fix: keep agents responsive when recovery closes temporary SQLite readers
prs.body:
Related: #158592 (the same unpublished-runtime symptom; this patch addresses a different, reproduced trigger).

Prepared and submitted by Codex on behalf of Victor Sesma (@VictorSesma), with his explicit authorization. Originally submitted as a draft at his request; the PR is now ready for review. Validation below identifies the tested revisions.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agents becoming unavailable when an authentication change queues a model refresh from temporary SQLite readers that close before the refresh finishes, as can happen during deferred database recovery.

## User Impact

The refresh completes and the agent can handle its next request without restarting the Gateway. Credential invalidation and genuine publication failures continue to reject affected requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

The queued refresh inherited the emitter's SQLite AsyncLocalStorage scope. Closing that scope caused real catalog reads to fail with `SQLite read-only worker scope closed`, leaving the reply runtime unpublished.

Schedule auth publication outside that SQLite scope. Reads continue through the existing bounded worker pool and runtime lifecycle; the spawn broker, plugin registry, publication ordering, and synchronous credential invalidation retain their existing behavior. No retry manager, new state, configuration, or schema changes are added.

## Evidence

### Latest integrated revision (`dcc5a5f`)

Merged upstream `0a0d88df543a9d36c4708f93c56d995da769050c` into the PR branch. The resulting PR diff remains three files, 45 additions and 9 deletions: the reader-scope scheduling fix, existing auth-directory normalization moved into its processing owner, and the connected-Gateway regression.

[Hosted CI on this exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39075176358) **completed successfully on 2026-10-17 at 22:49 UTC**, including lint, test type checks, changed tests, the baseline ratchets, and all three PostgreSQL conformance shards. The historical LRU failure documented below is from an earlier revision, not a failing test in this CI run. The inspected lint/ratchet annotations do not flag any of the three changed files; advisory annotations elsewhere remain visible in GitHub.

[Codex code review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173482#issuecomment-6202612344) completed on `dcc5a5fced7cb41027e056e433dc772c1394ad28` with no findings. [Maintainer approval](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173482#issuecomment-6214284179) remains required for the current revision because the patch touches auth-publication code; the associated approval gate is separate from the CI execution result.

The live Gateway proof and local red/green regression results below retain their original tested revisions. They have not been relabeled as new local runs on this merge commit.

### Requested CI rerun (`6e83931d5`)

The author requested a fresh CI execution. This empty commit has exactly the same Git tree as `7328d09d3`; it changes no source files, tests, or CI configuration. The validation and pinned-base failure attribution below remain attached to their recorded revisions. [Checks for this rerun](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6e83931d55c9a4710415d3060f9e69ed4bd5ed1f/checks).

### CI failure attribution: identical failure on the pinned main base

Completed the pinned-base comparison requested by [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173482#issuecomment-6203074770). **Historical result on `7328d09d3`: the failing LRU assertion also fails on that revision's pinned main base without this PR.**

[Failed CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38989511189/job/117268832730): `checks-node-changed-compact-small-3`, `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-llm.prepared-owner.test.ts`, `keeps completion ownership coherent: lru`, line 923. The global CI gate also fails as a consequence. The native failure classifier reported `unknown` because the scheduled-main run had no matching job; the following direct comparison supplies the missing attribution.

In the same isolated Ubuntu VM, with Node 24.21.0, pnpm 12.11.1, unchanged dependencies, and the same three plugin test files selected by the failed CI shard:

| Checkout | Result | Failing assertion | Wall / Vitest time |
|---|---|---|---|
| PR head `7328d09d3` | 29 pass, 1 fail | line 923: expected 3 to be 2 | 217.64 / 208.97 s |
| Exact integrated main base `b0ab44081ef483fcd0a86c8afae3b4eb30e9bc24`, clean detached checkout, no PR changes | 29 pass, 1 fail | same test, line 923: expected 3 to be 2 | 202.84 / 195.82 s |

Both runs used:

```bash
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3072 \
pnpm test \
  src/plugins/prepared-model-generation.lifecycle.test.ts \
  src/plugins/runtime/runtime-llm.prepared-owner.test.ts \
  src/plugins/runtime/runtime-llm.retained-generation.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

The LRU diagnostic reports `buildsBeforeSecond: 11` and `secondBuilds: 11` in both runs: the owner-reuse assertion passes; the subsequent global `ModelRegistry.fork` count fails. Source inspection shows a possible additional catalog-projection fork: [snapshot capture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b0ab44081ef483fcd0a86c8afae3b4eb30e9bc24/src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.capture.ts#L82) wraps `createStores()` with another fork when published models are available, after [background catalog discovery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b0ab44081ef483fcd0a86c8afae3b4eb30e9bc24/src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.refresh-scope.ts#L29). The test and these owners are unchanged by this PR.

The comparison establishes that the CI assertion is pre-existing, rather than a regression from detaching the auth-publication reader scope. No source, test expectation, baseline, or CI setting was changed during this investigation. The PR checkout was restored cleanly to `7328d09d3`. That revision's failing check was retained for maintainer handling under the repository's inherited-failure policy. See the latest-revision status above for current CI and approval requirements.

### Conflict resolution against current main (`7328d09d3`)

Merged upstream `b0ab44081` to resolve the conflict introduced when #174670 refactored the connected-Gateway test helpers. Preserved the upstream test file and adapted the temporary-reader regression to `refreshAuth`, `sendAgentRpc(agentId, runId)`, and `expectCompleted`. The runtime scheduling fix and the line-cap repair are unchanged.

Validation on the merged candidate in the isolated Ubuntu VM (Node 24.21.0, pnpm 12.11.1):

- Full connected-Gateway auth-refresh file: **5/5 pass**, including the adapted recovery regression. Wall time: 201.16 s; Vitest duration: 191.41 s, including cold compilation/Gateway startup. The regression body took 6.284 s and reuses the existing suite-level server to prove the SQLite-to-Gateway dispatch boundary.
- Negative control: reverted only the scheduling line locally, then ran the adapted regression. It fails at the publication assertion with `phase: failed` and `SQLite read-only worker scope closed` (154.04 s wall time). Restored and verified the exact reviewed/passing source bytes before committing; the negative-control edit is not published.
- Official line-cap ratchet against the integrated main: **passes**, three changed source files, no new violations or growth. Targeted type-aware lint: **292 rules, zero warnings/errors**; formatting and `git diff --check` pass.

[Hosted checks for the merge commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7328d09d3dd46cc601b8c56e987cd5d9041805b7/checks) record the CI state for that revision. This run uses the existing connected-Gateway harness with real SQLite and mocked provider discovery/agent execution. The separate shipped-Gateway/live-model evidence below remains explicitly attributed to its original revision.

### Line-cap follow-up (`a85c45b`)

Moved the existing auth-event directory normalization into `invalidatePreparedModelRuntimeOwnersForAuthMutation`, its sole processing owner. `prepared-model-runtime.ts` now has **697 counted lines** instead of 701 (cap: 700). The scheduling fix and all regression coverage remain intact; no lint limit or baseline was relaxed.

- Full connected-Gateway auth-refresh test file: **5/5 pass**, including temporary-reader closure, cancellation, rejected publication, and provider failures.
- Independent `autoreview` of the incremental change: no actionable P0–P2 findings.

[Hosted checks for this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a85c45b2e1fc8f45a91cf1f499dc420c3d186ce7/checks). The shipped-Gateway red/green output below was recorded on `67eb4ad`; it is retained with its original revision rather than relabeled as a new run.

### Live Gateway proof (outside Vitest)

Added in response to [ClawSweeper's proof request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173482#issuecomment-6203074770).

On 2026-10-15, built and ran head `67eb4ad0be334581d3af129b15649fd025800bb9` through the shipped `pnpm openclaw gateway run` entry point in a disposable Ubuntu VM. The Gateway selected the pinned Bun 1.4.3 runtime (Node compatibility version 26.3.0); build tooling used Node 24.21.0 and pnpm 12.10.1. Agent execution used the native OpenClaw agent harness and **real llama.cpp inference with Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0**, over loopback, without external model credentials.

| Build | Before the trigger | After temporary readers close | Subsequent real Gateway `agent` RPC |
|---|---|---|---|
| PR head `67eb4ad` | Gateway publication ready | `published` | Exit 0, `status: ok`, model reply returned |
| Same head, only the scheduling line reverted and rebuilt | Real agent RPC succeeds | `failed`: `SQLite read-only worker scope closed` | Exit 1, `UNAVAILABLE`: runtime owner was not published |

Within each run, the reader close and publication events below come from the **same running Gateway process**. The post-recovery RPC is a separate CLI process using `gateway call agent --expect-final`; it does not fall back to local execution. No Vitest, mocked provider discovery, mocked agent command, or fabricated model response is used. The negative control was saved as disposable local commit `637a346fb07ee5cc5e05796591d4d520ad237f3d`; its diff against the PR head is exactly the one scheduling-line reversal. Configuration and preload file hashes were identical across the final red/green runs.

The deterministic input is disclosed: a disposable preload calls the existing auth-snapshot setter from a temporary SQLite reader scope, then closes the scope, using synthetic credentials and an actual persisted agent database. This isolates the publication boundary used by deferred recovery. It does **not** claim an end-to-end OOM/restart reproduction, an OAuth renewal test, or a production/Telegram deployment. The preload and negative-control edit are laboratory artifacts, not additions to this PR.

   ```bash
   export OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1
   export OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1
   pnpm openclaw setup --non-interactive --accept-risk --mode local \
     --auth-choice custom-api-key --custom-base-url http://127.0.0.1:18080/v1 \
     --custom-model-id qwen3-0.6b --custom-api-key synthetic-local \
     --custom-provider-id recovery-proof --custom-compatibility openai --custom-text-input \
     --gateway-port 18790 --gateway-bind loopback --no-install-daemon \
     --skip-channels --skip-skills --skip-health --skip-ui --skip-hooks --skip-search \
     --skip-bootstrap --workspace "$LAB/workspace" --agent-name main \
     --suppress-gateway-token-output --json
   pnpm openclaw config patch --stdin --replace-path models.providers --replace-path agents.defaults.models <<'JSON'
   {
     "models":{"providers":{"llama-cpp":{
       "baseUrl":"http://127.0.0.1:18080/v1","api":"openai-completions","apiKey":"synthetic-local",
       "request":{"allowPrivateNetwork":true},
       "models":[{"id":"qwen3-0.6b","name":"qwen3-0.6b","contextWindow":16384,
         "maxTokens":96,"input":["text"],"reasoning":false,
         "cost":{"input":0,"output":0,"cacheRead":0,"cacheWrite":0}}]
     }}},
     "agents":{"defaults":{"contextInjection":"never","heartbeat":{"every":"0m"},
       "model":{"primary":"llama-cpp/qwen3-0.6b"},
       "models":{"llama-cpp/qwen3-0.6b":{"agentRuntime":{"id":"openclaw"}}}}},
     "tools":{"profile":"minimal","deny":["*"],"codeMode":false},
     "plugins":{"allow":["llama-cpp","openai"],"slots":{"memory":"none"}},
     "cron":{"enabled":false}
   }
   JSON
   ```

The native `llama-cpp` provider is important: a generic custom provider can have no generated-catalog owner, so `loadPersistedPluginModelCatalogs` returns early for an empty plugin list and the closed-reader bug is not exercised.

4. Save the diagnostic preload below as `$LAB/recovery-preload.mjs`. Adjust its `root` and `dist` constants if using different disposable directories. Start the shipped Gateway command in that shell:

   ```bash
   NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=2048 --import=$LAB/recovery-preload.mjs" \
     pnpm openclaw gateway run --port 18790 --bind loopback --verbose
   ```

5. Wait for `gateway-publication-ready` in `$LAB/live-events.jsonl`. In another shell with the same state environment, write `{"run":"patched"}` to `$LAB/trigger.json`. Observe `invalidated`, `readers-closed`, then `published`. After `published`, call the actual Gateway RPC (there is no CLI local-execution fallback):

   ```bash
   pnpm openclaw gateway call agent --expect-final --json --timeout 240000 \
     --expect-url ws://127.0.0.1:18790 \
     --params '{"agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:live-proof","idempotencyKey":"live-proof-unique-1","thinking":"off","message":"Say hello in one short sentence. Do not use any tools. /no_think"}'
   ```

6. Negative control: stop only the disposable Gateway, replace the single scheduling line below in source, save it in a disposable local commit, and rebuild through the same CLI. The local commit keeps the source runner from rebuilding a dirty tree at every Gateway start; do not push it. Keep the configuration and preload identical. Restart, verify an ordinary agent RPC succeeds, and trigger `{"run":"negative-control"}`. Publication now fails with the real closed-reader exception and a subsequent Gateway RPC is rejected. Use new session and idempotency keys for each request.

   ```diff
   - const job = readOnlyWorkerScope.exit(() => modelRuntimeDrain.runAfter(publicationQueue, publish));
   + const job = modelRuntimeDrain.runAfter(publicationQueue, publish);
   ```

The negative control is a local experiment, not an additional PR commit. Restore the source from the pinned head afterward. This reproduces the recovery publication boundary; it does not manufacture an OOM or claim to exercise every startup-recovery branch.

</details>


<details>
<summary>Exact diagnostic preload used for the live check</summary>

This imports the existing compiled module exports without modifying them. Capturing the initial publication context preserves the Gateway's ordinary async context; the temporary reader scope is created only around the synthetic mutation. The RPC and model server run separately from this observer.

```javascript
// Diagnostic-only preload for the shipped CLI Gateway, outside Vitest.
// All publication, SQLite, discovery, admission and inference code stays real.
import fs from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url";
import { AsyncLocalStorage } from "node:async_hooks";

const root = "/home/lab/recovery-live-proof";
const dist = "/home/lab/src/openclaw-proof/dist";
const agentDir = path.join(root, "state/agents/main/agent");
const record = (event, details = {}) => fs.appendFileSync(
  path.join(root, "live-events.jsonl"),
  JSON.stringify({ at: new Date().toISOString(), pid: process.pid, event, ...details }) + "\n",
);

async function compiledExport(prefix, name) {
  for (const file of fs.readdirSync(dist).filter(f => f.startsWith(prefix) && f.endsWith(".mjs"))) {
    const source = fs.readFileSync(path.join(dist, file), "utf8");
    const match = source.match(new RegExp("export \\{[^}]*\\b" + name + " as ([\\w$]+)[^}]*\\};"));
    if (match) return (await import(pathToFileURL(path.join(dist, file)).href))[match[1]];
  }
  throw new Error(`Compiled export not found: ${name}`);
}

async function install() {
  const createScope = await compiledExport("sqlite-readonly-worker-", "createSqliteReadOnlyWorkerScope");
  const setSnapshot = await compiledExport("runtime-snapshots-", "setRuntimeAuthProfileStoreSnapshot");
  const listen = await compiledExport("prepared-model-runtime.publication-events-", "registerPreparedModelRuntimePublicationListener");
  let inGatewayContext;
  let activeRun;
  let running = false;
  listen(event => {
    if (event.phase === "published" && !inGatewayContext) {
      inGatewayContext = AsyncLocalStorage.snapshot();
      record("gateway-publication-ready", { node: process.versions.node, bun: process.versions.bun });
    }
    if (activeRun && ["invalidated", "published", "failed"].includes(event.phase)) {
      record(event.phase, { run: activeRun, ...(event.error ? { error: String(event.error), stack: event.error.stack } : {}) });
    }
  });
  const timer = setInterval(() => {
    const trigger = path.join(root, "trigger.json");
    if (!inGatewayContext || running || !fs.existsSync(trigger)) return;
    const { run } = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(trigger, "utf8"));
    fs.unlinkSync(trigger);
    activeRun = run;
    running = true;
    inGatewayContext(async () => {
      record("trigger", { run, agentDatabaseExists: fs.existsSync(path.join(agentDir, "openclaw-agent.sqlite")) });
      const readers = createScope();
      try {
        readers.run(() => setSnapshot({ version: 1, profiles: {
          "llama-cpp:recovered": { type: "api_key", provider: "llama-cpp", key: "synthetic-recovered-key" },
        } }, agentDir));
        await readers.close();
        record("readers-closed", { run });
      } finally {
        await readers.close();
      }
    }).catch(error => record("diagnostic-error", { run, error: String(error), stack: error.stack }))
      .finally(() => { running = false; });
  }, 250);
  timer.unref();
  record("preload-installed");
}

if (process.versions.bun && process.argv[1]?.endsWith("openclaw.mjs") && process.argv.includes("gateway")) {
  await install();
}
```

</details>

### Fast regression reproduction (Vitest)

This is a deterministic regression at the auth-publication boundary used by deferred database recovery. It uses a real persisted SQLite database and a connected Gateway, with synthetic credentials and mocked provider/agent execution. It does not require a Telegram account or a real model API key, and does not simulate the preceding out-of-memory crash or a full Gateway restart.

Use Node 24.21.0 and pnpm 12.10.1, the versions used for the recorded run. The commands below use a new disposable checkout and pin both the tested base and the PR commit.

1. Prepare the checkout and dependencies:

   ```bash
   git clone --depth 1 --single-branch --branch fix/auth-refresh-reader-lifetime \
     https://github.com/VictorSesma/openclaw.git openclaw-recovery-repro
   cd openclaw-recovery-repro
   git fetch --depth 1 origin \
     6e7781b5968ff4c3b8b660bd1b6b0def24503d48 \
     ee6ef3aeede951c1070082a6482f9c1e69ac4a55
   git switch --detach ee6ef3aeede951c1070082a6482f9c1e69ac4a55
   pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
   ```

2. Keep the new regression test, but restore the production file from the failing base:

   ```bash
   git restore --source=6e7781b5968ff4c3b8b660bd1b6b0def24503d48 --worktree -- \
     src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.ts
   OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3072 \
     pnpm test src/gateway/server.agent.gateway-server-agent-auth-refresh.test.ts \
     --maxWorkers=1 -t 'temporary SQLite'
   ```

   Expected: exit code 1. The test `dispatches after the auth mutation's temporary SQLite readers close` receives publication phase `failed` instead of `published`, with `SQLite read-only worker scope closed`. It fails at that assertion before sending the next agent RPC. Running the base alone would not reproduce this test failure because the new regression test is absent there.

3. Restore the fix and run the same test:

   ```bash
   git restore --source=ee6ef3aeede951c1070082a6482f9c1e69ac4a55 --worktree -- \
     src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.ts
   OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3072 \
     pnpm test src/gateway/server.agent.gateway-server-agent-auth-refresh.test.ts \
     --maxWorkers=1 -t 'temporary SQLite'
   ```

   Expected: exit code 0. Publication reaches `published`, the following Gateway `agent` RPC returns `ok` with payload status `ok`, and the agent-command mock is invoked exactly once. Remove `-t 'temporary SQLite'` to run all five tests in the file. A cold compiler preparation adds roughly two minutes on the recorded VM; the individual regression timing below excludes most of that startup cost.

The test first persists the affected agent's database and prepares its runtime. It then calls `setRuntimeAuthProfileStoreSnapshot(...)` inside `readers.run(...)`, immediately awaits `readers.close()`, and observes the asynchronously queued publication. Persisting the database is essential: an empty fixture can skip the SQLite catalog read and miss the bug. The closed-scope exception is produced by the real reader implementation.

### Earlier regression evidence

- On base `6e7781b5968ff4c3b8b660bd1b6b0def24503d48`, the new regression fails with the exact closed-scope error. It emits a real auth mutation using an actual persisted agent database, then closes the temporary readers; the error is not mocked.
- With the patch, publication succeeds and the next `agent` RPC completes. All 5 tests in the Gateway auth-refresh file pass, including cancellation and rejected-publication behavior.
- 35 related tests pass across `prepared-model-runtime.reload-auth`, `prepared-model-runtime.auth-recovery`, and `sqlite-readonly-worker-session`.
- Independent `autoreview` of the complete patch and lifecycle context: no P0-P2 findings.
- Targeted type-aware lint (292 rules, zero warnings/errors), formatting, the deprecated-API usage guard, and `git diff --check` pass.

Hosted validation on `67eb4ad` passed: [production types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38813663347/job/116694847116), [test types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38813663347/job/116694847161), [lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38813663347/job/116694847280), and [changed tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38813663347/job/116694118222). The local full typecheck had previously been stopped under the 4-GiB VM's memory pressure; no success is claimed for that interrupted run. Hosted CI supplies the completed validation on `67eb4ad`.

Local proof used Node 24.21.0 on Ubuntu in an isolated 2-vCPU, 4-GiB VM. The regression took 1.37 seconds on the failing base and 6.29 seconds after the fix, including the successful RPC. The complete Gateway file took 159.29 seconds with a cold compiler preparation; the three related files took 58.09 seconds. Real SQLite plus Gateway admission is necessary to exercise the lifecycle boundary that a fixture without a persisted database misses.

The original Vitest results above use mocked provider/agent execution; the new live Gateway proof separately exercises real local-model inference. Neither is a production deployment or live Telegram test. The scope remains the reader-lifetime publication failure, not the preceding OOM or every cause of an unpublished runtime.

prs.title: refactor(gateway): prune worker history from resident inventory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Worker-history cleanup reads and decodes a second candidate inventory even though
the store already owns every committed environment record, then rereads and
compares full rows before deleting them.

## User Impact

No retention-policy change. Cleanup keeps the seven-day cutoff, terminal-state
eligibility, oldest-first ordering, default 256 and maximum 1,000 total deletions,
placement references, orphaned reserves and live provider demand protection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Select candidates from the committed resident owner, send at most 256 IDs per
existing worker mutation, and perform predicate-guarded DELETE RETURNING. Only
actual deleted IDs enter the existing publication receipt. Remove the private
candidate-read command, cursor/page/observation types, duplicate decoder and
full-row reread/deep comparison. Readiness, FIFO, physical identity, native commit
admission, unknown-outcome recovery and accepted-work shutdown settlement remain.

This is one worker-history AREA recovered from the wider parked family, not its
old receipt/incarnation cut: nine paths, seven production files, currently
+103/-217 = 114 net production lines removed after formatting. No schema, persisted shape,
protocol/config/SDK, dependency, permission or durability change. Phase E session
memory and its factory/registry/expiry/federation/tests are untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- #143372 introduced the raw-row observation/comparison protocol for potentially
  reentrant policy; #154804 retained it during the measured resident-inventory
  cutover. Their feature descriptions and controlled tests do not establish a
  human actual-use stale-prune incident. Existing immutable resident identity and
  live demand are checked at the existing effect admission; SQL retains actual
  deletion eligibility and placement-reference checks.
- A veto or error on a later page does not undo earlier committed cleanup pages.
  A named demand veto returns the completed count; arbitrary errors still
  propagate. Earlier real receipts remain authoritative, and the next reconcile
  retries remaining rows. The original single-page rollback contract remains.
- Policy may inspect more resident terminal candidates, including referenced
  rows. Its only production callback is the existing side-effect-free prepared
  demand policy. Protected/referenced first pages do not consume the deletion
  limit or starve a later eligible row. No new cache, fence, retry owner or
  all-or-nothing cross-page promise is added.

## Evidence

Source-qualified against the original retention owner and full introducing PRs;
the resident owner has measured 5,000-row performance evidence and is retained.
The complete retired command/type/reader chain has no remaining references.
Eight owning retention cases preserve age, reference, cascade, recent/nonterminal,
single-page live-demand rollback, error identity and retry. Added coverage uses
real worker execution and receipts for protected-page progress,
600-row default/total limits, UTF-8 equal-age ordering and later-page outcomes.
Offline bulk fixtures reopen the resident store before pruning.

A new case in the existing PostgreSQL conformance owner uses the real worker
store and query, checking limit-one UTF-8 ordering, placement protection, actual
deletion receipts and persisted PostgreSQL rows. That suite is selected by the
existing database conformance runner. Its runtime result remains pending.

Independent P0-P2 review completed scoped-clean (.92) for the original eight
paths and scoped-clean (.94) for the PostgreSQL supplement and its three changed
query-path owners. Complete captures were reverified after both reviews; static
review is not actual SQL execution proof.

Final complete nine-file review after removing the unnecessary test command
observer completed all five passes scoped-clean (.92), with143intact source/
context files and full diff319c4ddd verified before/after. The helper refused an
unchanged credential.ts dataset before starting; it was explicitly excluded
from review context without bypassing the guard. No credential-internals review
is claimed, and all nine changed files remained in scope.

Pinned physically owned oxfmt 0.72.0 formatted the original eight paths in 4.55
seconds and the PostgreSQL supplement in 335 milliseconds; diff-check passed.
Fresh frozen install passed in1141.51 seconds,1575 packages reused and none
downloaded. Targeted10-root types initially found that an added test-only generic
command observer did not narrow its input. Removed that private call-shape
instrumentation and assertions rather than adding a cast, property probe or
production type widening. Real persisted-row/count/default/total-limit assertions
remain. Final targeted types passed in35.42 seconds. The focused owning retention
suite passed all8cases:677.56seconds runner,817.86seconds shard and877.63seconds
isolated wrapper, including completed-generation verification. Native SQLite
workers/receipts protect the actual deletion, cascade, paging and rollback
contracts; this boundary proof does not cover PostgreSQL execution. Nine-file
type-aware lint with the official core config and one thread passed in212.69
seconds. Mandatory suppression audit passed all14cases in91.38seconds runner,
129.78seconds shard and144.24seconds isolated wrapper. No suppression or allowlist
changed. Exact-head hosted CI run 39071869735, attempt 1, completed green at
e5b57e76a0d4ff62db26999c56b0792f163c531e: 57 successful and 27 policy-unselected
jobs, with no pending or failed job in that run. All three PostgreSQL conformance
jobs, security-fast and openclaw/ci-gate passed. The full paginated head census
contains 213 checks; its only nonpassing record is a superseded cancelled
auto-response, not an executable proof suite. No CI rerun, new push or rebase
was used to obtain this result.
No old parked-family proof is credited and no timeout, retry, skip, suppression
or kept-behavior assertion is weakened.

prs.title: fix: reuse session replicas through symlinked state paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A state directory reached through a symlink, including macOS `/var` or a symlinked `.openclaw`, misses the session replica even when admission has established that both path spellings identify the same store. Warm history and activity-summary reads then add 15 SQLite statements and two worker requests per turn.

## User Impact

Warm reads and committed row/membership/transcript publications reuse the same state through either admitted spelling. Different databases remain isolated, and committed writes invalidate stale facts. No configuration, schema, SDK, update, or lifecycle change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing admission registry owns identity. Replica selection uses its SQLite physical identity/birthtime or PostgreSQL `(namespace, storeId)` facts without opening a database, calling `realpath`/`stat`, or querying SQL. The existing row-scope resolver indexes admitted identity to its resident path when topology is prepared. Membership uses the canonical path already carried in its prepared publication.

The complete lexical-gate cutover and accepted edges are:

- `readCurrentEntryCellForPath`: history/accounting and activity-summary accept admitted aliases. Externally relinking a path requires normal readmission; reads do not probe filesystem topology.
- `readSessionActorProjectionReceiptFromCells`: receipt selection accepts those aliases. The receiving owner's existing token check decides whether the receipt is current.
- `readCurrentReceipt`: removes filename equality and the redundant receipt `path`. Two spellings share a scoped receipt; different stores and later writes still reject it through the token.
- Row publication: removes filename equality after physical identity/birthtime matching. The row-scope resolver covers row/transcript publications, bare transcript notifications, and alias queries even when topology deduplication retained one spelling. Externally relinked paths require readmission.
- Membership publication: removes the equivalent filename equality and routes using the prepared canonical path. Existing identity and revision ordering remain authoritative.

Native connection custody, destructive/external-effect authority, and compaction writer/target checks remain intact. No new owner, generation, handshake, SQL, or fallback path.

## Evidence

One shared v3 baseline/candidate pair per path spelling, ten warm turns per arm, all threads counted. Baseline `d6a7e3d211ec`; candidate `de2e4cbae634`. The final sibling rebase onto `60dfac55a80` produces `00fde2c05cb5`: all three patches are exactly equal by `git range-diff`, with touched production and PG fixture bytes unchanged.

| Warm fixture | Base SQL / requests / MAIN | Candidate SQL / requests / MAIN |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Symlink root | 72 [72–74] / 18 [18–20] / 0 | 57 [57–59] / 16 [16–18] / 0 |
| Canonical root | 57 [57–59] / 16 [16–18] / 0 | 57 [57–59] / 16 [16–18] / 0 |

Counts are median [min–max]. On every symlink warm turn, history-page falls **8 SQL / 1 request → 0** and activity-summary falls **7 / 1 → 0**. Exact-entry, actor hydration, entry-cache snapshots, row facts, and watermark reads remain zero in both pairs. Canonical warm SQL shapes and request origins match exactly. The owned harness copy changes only scratch-root `.resolve()` to `.absolute()` to preserve the fixture alias; shared harness and workload remain unchanged. No latency claim.

Raw symlink warm medians also fall 72 [72–94] / 18 [18–24] → 57 [57–61] / 16 [16–20]. Canonical raw SQL median 57 → 57.5 is background scheduling: its mean falls 60 → 58 while causal counters match exactly. Canonical first-turn SQL is 169 → 170 with 54 requests unchanged, from one activity-summary projection read. This bounded cold difference is retained in the evidence; no extra pair was run. Whole observed workload counts decrease in both comparisons: symlink 3,252 / 886 → 3,030 / 861; canonical 3,413 / 896 → 3,370 / 894.

Both canonical workloads pass all phases. Both symlink arms complete all 14 turns, RPCs, cron, restart, and shutdown but report the same pre-existing compaction error, `session writer claim changed before transcript persistence`. This is not a full symlink workload pass. The separate compaction follow-up owns that target-binding defect; this PR preserves its write-authority checks.

The shared regression **fails on the base on both SQLite and PostgreSQL** at the cross-spelling receipt assertion and passes on the candidate. It verifies correct warm history/activity data with zero history-worker reads, distinct-store misses, and freshness after an in-process append. Additional regressions cover row/membership alias publication and native transcript append/notification delivery without row reads/backfills.

Both permitted independent Codex review rounds were clean through P2. Prior-head [CI 39072747467](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39072747467) passed completely, including all three PostgreSQL shards and **43 cases across all six changed test files**. Types, selected lint, source contracts, Madge (zero cycles), and ratchets passed. T1 is **0 → 0 in this area**, **181 → 181 globally**; all dialect classes remain zero across seven production files. Knip adds no findings: its dependency/export/type findings exactly match [scheduled-main job 117508966070](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39071119824/job/117508966070) and are recorded with the main repair owner. The PostgreSQL owner explicitly approved the unchanged patch and independently confirmed that the symlink-root census matches the canonical baseline: PostgreSQL traced means **16.67 requests / 68.67 trips / 82.67 SQL**, SQLite **16.67 requests / 57.67 SQL**; both fallback operations are zero on both engines. This approval and census remain applicable after the patch-identical sibling rebase. Final rebased-head [CI 39074761474](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39074761474) passed: **53 successful jobs, 24 skipped, no failures**, including all three PostgreSQL shards and `openclaw/ci-gate`. All selected changed tests, production/test types, lint, source contracts, Madge, and ratchets are green on `00fde2c05cb5`. The PostgreSQL owner approval explicitly extends to this head.

Production **+74/−24** lines (net +50); tests **+379/−11**; docs **+6/−0**. The growth routes existing consumers through admission-owned identity while removing redundant lexical checks and receipt state. SDK diff and published-driver update cell are not applicable.

prs.title: fix(gateway): IPv6 Gateway hosts fail in SSH targets and discovery URLs
prs.body:
Closes #127454

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: IPv6 Gateway hosts produce SSH targets and discovery URLs that OpenSSH and `new URL` reject.

## User Impact

IPv6-only remote Gateways work with inferred SSH routing, `gateway probe --ssh`, and discovery output. DNS names and IPv4 are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`parseSshTarget` now reads `[IPv6]` and `[IPv6]:port` as the raw host. Discovery and status bracket IPv6 through one `formatUrlHost` helper, which replaces six inline copies.

## Evidence

Shipped CLI (`pnpm dev`) on Linux, Node 24, before then after.

Configured inference, `gateway.remote.url = ws://[::1]:18789` and a local sshd, `openclaw gateway probe --json`:
- before: warning `SSH tunnel failed: invalid SSH target: <user>@[::1]`
- after: `sshTunnel` target active, `tunnel.target = <user>@[::1]:22`, OpenSSH reached `::1`

Discovery, `openclaw gateway discover --json` with a beacon whose host is `2001:db8::10` (stub `avahi-browse` on PATH, since real avahi reports `.local` names):
- before: `"wsUrl": "ws://2001:db8::10:18789"`
- after: `"wsUrl": "ws://[2001:db8::10]:18789"`

Explicit `openclaw gateway probe --ssh 'me@[2001:db8::10]:2222'`, before: `ssh: Could not resolve hostname [2001:db8::10]`. After: the raw address reaches SSH and times out (unreachable documentation address).

New tests fail before the fix and pass after. Touched and sibling suites, `tsgo:core`, oxlint, and oxfmt pass.

Not covered: the macOS app's Swift SSH parser.

prs.title: fix(browser): Chrome extension reports "Not installed" when macOS blocks profile reads
prs.body:
Closes #172272

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes OpenClaw reporting an installed, connected Chrome extension as "Not installed / manual setup required" when macOS privacy protection blocks reading Chrome's profile files.

## User Impact

User impact: when Chrome profile files are unreadable, status reports unknown install state instead of "extension missing", and that unknown fact now survives a successful connection check, so the Mac app's Chrome setup card never flips to "Not installed" while the extension shows connected. `openclaw browser extension status` prints the discovery warnings its summary references (including the Full Disk Access remedy), and `setup` steers to the live relay check instead of Store reinstall guidance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Profile discovery conflated "cannot read Chrome's profile files" with "extension not installed". Blocked reads now surface as `discoveryBlocked` on status and, as an installation-level fact, inside the setup `installation` projection (CLI JSON, the macOS Swift bridge, and the dashboard card), because the connection reason replaces the inspect reason during verify and previously erased the uncertainty. The CLI status command now prints issue lines before the summary. Review follow-ups from @clawsweeper are addressed: the blocked fact is independent of the connection reason (`installation.discoveryBlocked`, covered by the inspect→verify transition in the new e2e), and human-readable status prints the warnings it references.

## Evidence

Real-machine repro (macOS 27.0.1, OpenClaw 2026.10.3, TCC-blocked Chrome profile, extension connected — the exact contradiction from #172272):

```text
BEFORE (released openclaw 2026.10.3):
  setup --action inspect:
    {"phase":"needs_browser_action","reason":"extension_missing","nextAction":"install_from_store","nativeHostRegistered":true,"installedProfiles":0}

AFTER (this branch, built from source, same machine, same block):
  setup --action verify  (unknown install state survives a connected verify):
    {"phase":"ready","reason":"connected","connection":{"state":"connected","extensionVersion":"2.3.0"},
     "installation":{"installedProfiles":0,"discoveredProfiles":0,"discoveryBlocked":true}}
```

`extension status` on the same machine now starts with the previously hidden warning:

```text
Google Chrome: could not list profiles (Error: EPERM: operation not permitted, scandir '.../Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome'); on macOS, grant Full Disk Access to the app running OpenClaw, then check again
```

After-fix CLI behavior in a clean hermetic environment (owned native-host registration, profile directory made unreadable → same EACCES blocked-read path):

```text
status (human-readable; warnings now printed above the summary):
  Google Chrome profile Default (Preferences): EACCES: permission denied, lstat '.../Chrome/Default/Preferences'
  ...
  Setup:          unknown (Chrome profile files unreadable for Google Chrome; check the warnings above)

setup --action inspect:
  {"phase":"waiting_for_connection","reason":"profile_inspection_blocked","nextAction":"check_connection",
   "installation":{"nativeHostRegistered":true,"installedProfiles":0,"discoveredProfiles":0,"discoveryBlocked":true}}

setup --action verify (relay not running here; no false extension_missing, fact preserved):
  {"phase":"waiting_for_connection","reason":"relay_unavailable","nextAction":"check_connection",
   "connection":{"state":"unavailable"},"installation":{"discoveryBlocked":true,...}}
```

Desktop card before/after — the dashboard row driven through the macOS native bridge reply contract (the same `chrome-extension-setup` reply shape the Mac app posts back), captured via headless Control UI e2e:

- Before (base `ff22ecbe` build): after inspect, the card renders **Not installed**; after a connected verify it renders **Not installed** alongside **Extension connected on this device** — the reviewer's exact P2. Captured card text: `...Not installedExtension connected on this device....`
- After (this PR): inspect renders **Status unavailable** + the Full Disk Access hint; after a connected verify the card keeps **Status unavailable** and the hint alongside **Extension connected on this device**.

Four screenshots below: **before** (base `ff22ecbe` build — the reviewer's exact P2) and **after** (this PR):

Before — inspect says "Not installed", and a connected verify keeps saying it:

![Before fix: blocked inspect renders Not installed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4db56ba5-974b-4d32-9acb-69b7d24dae26)

![Before fix: Not installed alongside Extension connected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b06ab479-ad38-4d4b-ad94-b845784dd75d)

After — "Status unavailable" with the Full Disk Access hint, preserved through a connected verify:

![After fix: Status unavailable with Full Disk Access hint](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a1601b6-48d3-4abc-8c00-b0e42a2eecc1)

![After fix: unknown survives connected verify](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a7ae34e5-6c12-4d9a-9638-ba3939015759)

Regression run for the transition (failing base / passing head):

- Added `ui/src/e2e/chrome-extension-status.e2e.test.ts` → "keeps unknown install state through blocked inspect and a connected verify".
- Base UI build: `FAIL ... expected 'Chrome extensionSet up Chrome on this…' to contain 'Status unavailable'`.
- This head: `✓ keeps unknown install state through blocked inspect and a connected verify 743ms` (`vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts`).

Suites on `1e2ad88e`:

- `vitest.extension-browser.config.ts`: 82 passed (incl. blocked status/inspect/verify, survives-verify, CLI warnings test).
- `vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts` Chrome setup file: passed; UI unit suites touching the card (`chrome-setup`, `native-device-settings`, `device-pages`): passed.
- `tsgo` extensions, ui, core-test ui-e2e projects: clean. `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, docs format, line-cap + assertion-safety ratchets: clean. Full `pnpm build`: clean.
- The Swift bridge change cannot be covered by CI on fork PRs (`macos-swift` skips); it is verified with a local `swift test --filter ChromeExtensionSetupTests` run, and the result will be posted as a follow-up comment on this PR.

Known-unrelated CI flake observed on the previous head: one UI shard (`chat-transcript-end-follow`, then `canvas-widget-view`) — neither file is touched by this PR.

The test-reduction campaign found repeated setup, mock envelopes, and assertion scaffolding across core and Control UI tests. This batch replays the compatible cleanup onto current main without changing production behavior.

## Changes and impact

Consolidate test fixtures, repeated assertions, and table setup. The 62 changed source paths are tests or test-only support, including the existing plugin-SDK contract test helpers. Production LOC: +0 / -0. Test/support LOC: +9471 / -14754 (net -5283). The only additional path is a shrink-only timeout-race baseline adjustment (+1/-1 metadata line). No product or visual changes, dependency updates, schema changes, or runtime configuration changes.

Base: `9b4fdb0829fdbba686799c09e463b972dde317f8`. Applied 28 of the 30 requested commits in order, with conservative conflict resolution; skipped both x7894 commits. The remaining source commits retain their original subjects.

## Replay decisions

- x7894: skipped both commits (`66eb1fd11ce9c3e634e5ea93eac18af709b7aab9`, `13c018c0fdcf27a04ca0d0829ed562b424dd633b`). Extensive earlier fixture transformations are absent from current main; this avoids transplanting stale test structure.
- x7901: leave `src/state/openclaw-state-db-schema-policy.test.ts` unchanged from main, retaining all schema drift, native close/dispose, and admission tests. Retain the compatible cleanup in its sibling files.
- x7904: leave `history.test.ts` and the Google prompt-cache test/support trio unchanged from main. Static inspection found newer main cases referencing helpers removed by the replay; dropping that coupled rewrite preserves all of those cases and avoids stale helper calls. Retain the lane and model cleanup.
- x7907: leave `ui/src/pages/plugins/consent-dialog.test.tsx` and `plugin-discovery-controller.test.ts` unchanged, retaining ClawHub/git provenance and category/featured cases.
- x7912: leave `src/secrets/runtime-provider-and-media-surfaces.test.ts` unchanged, retaining the canonical memory snapshot cases.
- x7911: leave `ui/src/app/question-prompt-secret-store.test.ts` unchanged, retaining all host-proposal, absent-draft, and environment-entry cases.

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline`: passed.
- Direct `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --write <62 changed files>`: passed.
- Plain `node_modules/.bin/oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json <62 changed files>`: exit 0 after removing one unused fixture.
- `git diff --check 9b4fdb0829fdbba686799c09e463b972dde317f8`: passed.

- Independent review runs during CI; auto-merge is pinned to the pushed head.

No changed paths match the base's CODEOWNERS rules. The secrets and SDK changes are confined to test fixtures/contracts, not runtime or public SDK exports.

The first PR evidence check failed only because it requires the exact headings used above; the body is corrected. Auto-merge was disabled for the static prompt-cache finding; the corrected head restores the affected files to main exactly.

The first corrected-head CI run found concrete issues missed by the static review. Fixed stale secret-state helper names, optional deferred callbacks, pending-promise filtering, fixture input types, browser test tuple/element types, and typed UI preference callbacks. Restore `.toBeUndefined()` checks for absent campaign properties rather than requiring an explicit undefined property. Shrink `config/test-timeout-race-baseline.txt` for the removed duplicate race.

This retains the existing request-handler and JSON contracts, mock-isolation declarations, Buffer fixture types, and visualization ordering proof instead of carrying riskier fixture rewrites.

CI evidence: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39072812375 . Failures were addressed from the recorded job logs; no local test/typecheck execution and no blind reruns. The subsequent CI run found one remaining optional producer-callback call; it is repaired by using the typed `finish` closure returned by the existing fixture owner, without a cast or optional-call skip. prs.title: refactor: simplify System Agent dependency ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

System Agent verification, setup and turns expose private dependency substitutions that no production caller selects. Tests supplied alternate auth, registry, artifact and runner callbacks, leaving production responsible for forwarding a second implementation-selection API.

## User Impact

No user-visible change, migration or operator action. Public plugin SDK, configuration, protocol and persisted shapes are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Call the existing auth, CLI fingerprint, plugin artifact and runner owners directly. Use ordinary owner-module mocks and registered harness fixtures for tests, remove empty dependency plumbing, and delete the private turn test global and its adapter. Preserve the real snapshot-reader capability, prepared plugin metadata, primary/utility selection, live authority, artifact validation, cancellation and shutdown settlement. The standalone session-memory backend and its tests are untouched.

This is the System Agent area of the private runtime dependency-selection family. Its 36 paths are disjoint from the regular-runtime area's 79 paths; the two areas remove 508 production lines together. They are split by area under the campaign's wide-change rule, with independent proof and CI attribution.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

No runtime guard is removed. Only test-selected collaborator substitutions disappear; production uses the same canonical implementations as before. Tests now select fixtures at their existing module/harness owners instead of at each invocation.

The private turn global was introduced specifically to privatize test seams in #108325. The current verified-dependency names came through the internal rename in #107237; the current all-tree caller census establishes no production override or public SDK contract. Adjacent #174381 follows the same owner-mock boundary. These are test/implementation history, not human-reported incidents; no incident guard is being removed.

## Evidence

Measured against rebased base 232dee1422b1355df0ebda11752dfb4d567b0980: production +43/-156, **113 net lines removed**; tests/support +702/-732, **30 net lines removed**. The exact assertion baseline shrinks from two to one for agent-turn.ts; the canonical mock-export checker removes its retired embedded-runner allowance. There are 36 changed paths including those baselines. No configuration, protocol, persisted shape, dependency or public SDK changes.

Targeted types and type-aware lint passed, including the corrected fixtures. The original focused run passed 253 of 259 cases in 19 files. Four deterministic failures came from importing the config namespace before the shared hoisted mock. The two fixtures now set that existing mock directly, with every behavior assertion preserved; both corrected suites pass all 35 cases (316.40 seconds test run, 393.83 seconds including wrapper cleanup).

Two original 120-second timeouts remain unclassified: first-team provisioning on successful provider activation, and credential authority after an OAuth lock wait with authority retained. The provisioning case timed out again at 123,289 ms in its single replay at the original 120-second bound (260.29-second run, 582.25 seconds including preparation/cleanup). Its activation/team-creation/auth assertions are unchanged; the shared fixture retains the captured real auth resolver and existing prepared-generation wrapper. No deterministic assertion defect or cause is established. The authority case passed its single replay in 41,468 ms (189.31-second run), with no source correction for that timeout. Passing replay is not a proven repair. Neither an inherited-failure nor timeout repair claim is made; the original failures and uncertainty remain recorded. No timeout, retry, skip or retained assertion has been relaxed.

The route/setup-turn sibling suites passed 23 cases in two files (475.53-second run), and the Codex-authority sibling passed five cases (197.28-second run). The original suppression check passed 14 cases. Both runtime and static/madge import scans found zero cycles; whitespace checks passed. Fresh independent review after the fixture correction is scoped-clean through P2. The repair-proof command finished nonzero because provisioning still timed out; this is not represented as an all-green local run. Exact-head hosted CI remains the broad gate.

GitHub reported the initial draft conflicting. The conflict-only rebase preserves main's test consolidation and helpers; both conflicts concern replacing the same removed registry/fingerprint fixture options with the reviewed module mocks. prs.title: fix(agent-core): bound runaway loops with turn/error-batch/idle-repeat guards (#120962)
prs.body: Closes #120962 [AI-assisted] ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where a worker agent could enter an unbounded retry loop inside the native runLoop: an external service returning HTTP 429 (masked inside a "successful" tool output) drove 219 assistant turns / 177 tool calls / ~15M tokens over 6h42m, stopped only by the global `stuckSessionAbortMs` timeout rather than by any active guardrail. ## Why This Change Was Made Adds three opt-in hard cutoffs to the agent-core runLoop, each activating independently when set to a positive integer in `tools.loopDetection`: - **`turnLimit`** — max assistant turns per run; ends gracefully with a terminal message instead of another provider request. - **`maxConsecutiveErrorBatches`** — max consecutive all-error tool batches; any success resets the streak. - **`maxIdleRepeatCalls`** — max consecutive identical tool calls (same name + args); catches errors hidden inside successful output. Steering-skipped calls are excluded. `enabled: true` alone does not engage hard cutoffs (preserves upgrade contract). `enabled: false` disables both layers. Resolved config propagates through sessions, compaction, and worker launch descriptors. The launcher fences guard-enabled turns on worker bundles lacking the `worker-loop-guard-v1` capability; configless and `enabled:false` turns are unaffected. ## User Impact Operators who want the guardrails set at least one guard key (e.g. `turnLimit: 200`) in a `tools.loopDetection` block. Existing configurations gain no new hard termination behavior unless a guard key is explicitly set. Public package consumers see no change unless they opt in. ## Evidence **Focused tests (all pass):** - `packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.guard.test.ts` — 23 tests: maxTurns, error-batch, idle-repeat, steering-skip exclusion (sequential + parallel), steering requeue - `src/agents/sessions/agent-session-loop-guard-transport.test.ts` — real `AgentSession` through local HTTP/SSE transport, 3 repeated calls → graceful termination, no 4th request - `src/agents/tool-loop-detection-config.test.ts` — 9 tests: per-key activation, `enabled:false` kill switch, per-agent cascade - `src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-launcher.loop-guard.test.ts` — 6 tests: launcher fence, serialization, guard-off compatibility - `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/worker-admission.test.ts` — 25 tests: loop-guard capability in worker protocol features

prs.title: fix(discord): prevent shutdown failure after hot plugin updates
prs.body:
Related: #146319

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway shutdown failing after Discord is hot-updated from a generation whose in-memory component registry predates `withRegistryLock`.

The observed failure is `Failed to reset global singleton lifecycle state`, caused by `TypeError: state.withRegistryLock is not a function`. This is reproduced on current `main`, not only on the affected 2026.9.6 installation.

## User Impact

Discord can reuse a legacy component registry without that missing field breaking component operations or lifecycle cleanup. Fresh starts and existing locks, including queued work, keep their current behavior. No configuration, persistent-state schema, plugin permissions, or SDK surface changes are introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveGlobalSingleton` intentionally returns an existing object without rerunning its factory. The new cleanup callback therefore sees the older state shape. Initialize only an absent/undefined lock immediately after resolution, preserving the singleton, its maps/stores, and any existing lock. Defined but invalid lock values remain errors rather than being silently replaced.

The production change is six lines in the Discord-owned state module. The regression tests stay on public SDK entrypoints: they use the actual singleton resolver and capture Discord's actual cleanup callback without registering test callbacks in the host lifecycle. The existing core lifecycle tests are run separately.

## Evidence

Tested against upstream `main` at `d7e26112cce8d384cbc8aa5064887350725073c4`, using its frozen pnpm lockfile, Node 26.7.0, pnpm 12.9.0, and the standard repository test runner.

- **Negative control:** removing only the production fix reproduced the exact missing-lock TypeError in the focused tests. The additional shipped-Gateway witness below reproduces the failure through the complete native shutdown lifecycle.
- **Fixed:** all 9 new cases pass. Coverage includes legacy state identity/data, fresh state, reimports, an existing active/queued lock, cleanup ordering, and error propagation.
- **Related owners:** component persistence, shared singleton lifecycle, and keyed FIFO tests pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, scoped typed lint, formatting, the extension-test/core-import guard, mock-export guard, and `git diff --check` pass.
- The full `check-changed` run passes its checks through extension production/test typechecking, then stops at the repository-wide unused-export scan. That scan also fails on the **unmodified base commit**, with 41 reported entries in untouched code and none in the changed module. No baseline, suppression, or skip flag was added; the full aggregate check is **not claimed green**.
- Independent read-only review found no P0–P2 issues. The canonical autoreview helper was also attempted but could not complete because the local reviewer CLI authentication was unavailable; this is not claimed as a successful canonical autoreview.

Commands:

```sh
pnpm test extensions/discord/src/components-registry-state.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test extensions/discord/src/components-registry-state.test.ts extensions/discord/src/components-registry.persistence.test.ts src/shared/global-singleton.test.ts src/shared/keyed-fifo-lease.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
pnpm lint:plugins:no-extension-test-core-imports
pnpm check:test-mock-exports
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/discord/src/components-registry-state.test.ts extensions/discord/src/components-registry-state.ts
```

**New test cost:** 974 ms Vitest wall time, 1.99 s including the repository runner, measured with one worker after the review-requested test removal. No sleeps, network requests, or Gateway boots in the CI regression file. The exact follow-up head `3632e9dab64606de76fdbdc71db93af31b0187a2` passed [hosted technical CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38161816579). The [current-head hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169233#issuecomment-6111656442) reports no findings or remaining author proof requests and is ready for maintainer review. This is not maintainer approval or a merge claim. The source is unchanged.

### Review follow-up: shipped Gateway lifecycle proof

[Reproducible fixture, pinned source identities, and sanitized captured output](https://gist.github.com/Ricardodpalmeida/033e07565a4d6084e7993e56e6a3de71)

The witness uses a separate **official npm OpenClaw 2026.9.6 Gateway**, with its public package payload independently checked against the registry tarball. Its native Gateway entrypoint, singleton resolver, lifecycle drain and shutdown handler are unmodified.

The actual legacy registry module is loaded first. After the Gateway logs `ready` and returns HTTP 200, the current production registry module is dynamically imported over the same pre-lock object. Only then is SIGTERM sent. The controller neither mocks nor directly invokes cleanup callbacks.

| Variant | State/data preserved on hot-load | Native shutdown | Process exit | Registry after exit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Without fix | Yes; lock remains absent | Original `state.withRegistryLock is not a function` failure | 1 | Entries remain |
| With this fix | Yes; missing lock initialized | `shutdown completed cleanly` | 0 | Same registry, entries cleared |

The fixture uses private configuration/state/workspace/log paths and no real channel/provider credentials. The existing production service was untouched. Both variants also record a post-ready maintenance task being refused while draining; this is not a claim of a warning-free run.

**Precise boundary:** this is live production registry-module hot-loading plus the complete shipped Gateway shutdown lifecycle. It is not an exercise of the plugin manager's `plugins install` / `plugins reload` route or Discord transport, and does not change plugin provenance or privileges. The cited evidence contains the executable fixture and exact before/after output, not only a unit-test summary.

Also addressed the low-value-test feedback: removed the migrated-lock task-error case, whose rejection recovery is already covered by `src/infra/json-files.test.ts`. The nine remaining regression cases, component-persistence suite, and existing JSON-file/lock suite all pass (29 tests). The six-line production fix is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(sessions): degrade duplicate keyed-user dedup when the transcript index is transiently dirty
prs.body:
# PR #154904: fix(sessions) — degrade duplicate keyed-user dedup when the transcript index is transiently dirty

Repair for #152511. After the agent replies into a captured conversation turn, reply-capture writes audit artifacts with `appendMode: "side"`, which transiently marks the transcript projection index as needing reconcile. While dirty, `readActiveTranscriptEntryAnchor` returns undefined. A duplicate keyed-user delivery in that window previously hit the in-memory dedup branch and hard-threw "Session transcript anchor was not returned".

The fix keeps a three-state decision:
- **(A) projection index transiently dirty** (`needs_rebuild=1`) — a benign ~0.5–10s window after a concurrent side append: degrade to an idempotent no-op (return the cached entry, no anchor) without throwing.
- **(B) index clean and the cached turn IS active** — return its canonical anchor.
- **(C) index clean but the cached turn has no active row** — another manager removed/rewrote it (stale cache): REJECT, never silently false-acknowledge a non-existent turn.

Implemented by `readActiveTranscriptEntryAnchorStatus()` (single opened handle; reconcile state read before the active-join; fail-closed: only an explicitly dirty index degrades).
The canonical-adoption strong anchor constraint in `session-manager-persistence.ts`
(`result.messageId !== entry.id`) is untouched; the async user wrapper shares this decision.

## What Problem This Solves

Duplicate keyed-user message delivery after a transiently dirty transcript projection hard-throws instead of degrading idempotently. This PR bounds that into a three-state decision (benign dirty window degrades; clean-active returns anchor; clean-stale rejects), reusing the production current-turn owner so a completed/displaced/runtime-context turn is never false-acked.

## Evidence

ClawSweeper Rev4 P2 findings fixed in 251ffb39945: (1) a dirty index alone no longer degrades -- the cached turn is revalidated against the authoritative `transcript_event_identities` log in the same snapshot, so a suffix-removed cached turn still throws; (2) the reconcile probe and anchor join now run inside one read transaction instead of separate autocommits (TOCTOU closed). New regression test F covers dirty-index + deleted-identity-row -> throw.

All evidence below is from a local isolated detached worktree, Node 24, authoritative runner `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <files>` (real SQLite, not mocked persistence/transport).

- New `src/agents/sessions/session-manager.anchor-dedup-3state.test.ts` (registered in
  `test/vitest/vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs`): 8/8 passing.
  - A transient dirty (`needs_rebuild=1`) duplicate -> no throw, `appended:false`, same id, anchor undefined.
  - B clean index duplicate -> returns the existing canonical anchor.
  - C two managers: m1 writes keyed K, m2 `removeTrailingEntries` removes K, m1 re-delivers K -> throws.
  - D fresh append -> `appended:true` + anchor.
  - E async user wrapper shares the dirty degrade.
  - F dirty index but cached turn deleted from the durable log -> throws.
  - G dirty index but cached turn displaced off the canonical active path by a real branch switch -> throws.
  - H duplicate delivery inside an enclosing write transaction reaches the savepoint replay.

## Rev9 P2 resolved (head b774fd18c9f)

- Nested-safe snapshot uses runSqliteDeferredTransactionSync (savepoint-aware); test H opens the outer transaction on the SAME fixture db via {agentId, path}.

## Rev10 P2 resolved (head 395efe0e2ca)

- Dropped the handwritten max-seq recursive CTE. On a dirty projection the cached turn is now revalidated through the SAME canonical visible-path owner the projection rebuild / parent-fork / tail resolver use: `isTranscriptEntryOnActivePathInTransaction(database, sessionId, entryId)` (scans the durable event tree, selects the leaf's visible branch). No SQL or algorithm is copied; imported from the sibling internal module, not the public barrel. The clean path delegates to `readActiveTranscriptEntryAnchorInTransaction`, removing the duplicated identities⨝active⨝rewrite join and keeping the main-thread SQLite T1 callsite count at the base ratchet (database-worker ratchet OK).
- All dirty probe / current-turn / anchor reads run inside the single `runSqliteDeferredTransactionSync` nested-safe (savepoint-aware) snapshot.
- Test G now drives a REAL production branch switch: m2 appends an assistant turn after K, then `appendLeafControl({ targetId: existing-assistant, appendParentId: existing-assistant })` moves the canonical leaf back off K's branch. K's identity history is retained (not deleted). Non-vacuity: the old raw max-seq chain walk is replayed in-test and asserts `hit === 1` (would have false-acked / stays red), while the new owner rejects (throws). No `DELETE identity` / direct `leaf_event_id` edit.
- Test F deletes the durable `transcript_events` row (FK cascades identities) so K truly leaves the tree; the off-path owner rejects.
- Test H opens the SAME fixture db in an outer `runOpenClawAgentWriteTransaction` and asserts `db.isTransaction === true` and that a raw `db.exec("BEGIN")` throws `/cannot start a transaction within a transaction/` -- proving the nested tx is real and the old unconditional-BEGIN read would have failed -- while the savepoint-safe replay passes with `replay.appended === false`.

Gates on head 395efe0e2ca (Node 24, real SQLite runner):
- `session-manager.anchor-dedup-3state.test.ts` 8/8.
- `tsgo:core` exit 0; `db:kysely:check` 5/5; `check:database-worker-ratchet` OK (no T1 growth vs base 259033fe97); `deadcode:exports` 0 entries; oxfmt --check and oxlint (boundary guards) 0/0 on both changed files.

Inherited failures reproduced identically on the previous head b774fd18c9f (not introduced by this PR, zero suppression): `check:env-var-count` 477>476 (also on main; this PR adds 0 new OPENCLAW_* names); one gateway test-file tsgo error (`worker-turn-launcher.claim-recovery.test.ts` `appendMessage` on a Promise<SessionManager>); `settled-turn-finalization.provider-error.test.ts` 3 failed (provider error-string text).

## Rev11–13 correctness follow-ups (final head 4246b643e61)

ClawSweeper Rev10->Rev11->Rev12 surfaced three bounded correctness P2s, all fixed; Rev14 verdict on 4246b643e61 reports **Findings: None**, patch quality platinum hermit.

- **Rev11 (5682aec80e8) — visible-path membership was too weak.** A cached user turn K whose turn another manager completes with a *same-branch* assistant reply remains an ancestor on the visible path, so the Rev10 active-path check would have wrongly degraded it (false-ack). Added `resolveTranscriptCanonicalCurrentTurnEntryIdInTransaction`, a durable mirror of the manager's in-memory `resolveCurrentTurnEntryId`: it drives the shared `walkSessionCurrentTurn` generator up from the append cursor, applies the same traversability rules (thinking/model/custom/label/session_info/compaction + runtime-context custom_message), and returns the first non-traversable entry id (the durable canonical current turn). The dirty anchor path now degrades iff the cached entry id **equals** that resolved current turn (exact equality, not ancestor membership). New regression **G2**: same-branch assistant completes K -> reject (the old active-path check stays red, the new exact match rejects).
- **Rev12 (53ba4c3f326) — customType was stripped.** The resolver consumed `readTranscriptNavigationEvents`, whose shared `TRANSCRIPT_NAVIGATION_KEYS` projection omits `customType`, so the runtime-context discriminator was always undefined and every `custom_message` row looked like a turn boundary. Added a resolver-specific reader that projects the same navigation keys **plus `customType`** (json_set), leaving the shared projection and its other cursor consumers untouched. New regression **G3**: runtime-context metadata above a cached keyed user, dirty projection -> replay degrades (walk skips the metadata row, resolves back to K) instead of throwing.
- **Rev13 (4246b643e61) — test-only type fix.** CI's test-types stripe typechecks the test files; G/G2 manager-side assistant replies now use a complete `AssistantMessage` (`createZeroUsageFixture()`). No production change.

Gates on final head 4246b643e61 (Node 24, real SQLite runner): `session-manager.anchor-dedup-3state.test.ts` **10/10** (A–H + G2 + G3); agents-sessions test tsgo stripe clean; `tsgo:core` 0; `check:database-worker-ratchet` OK; `deadcode:exports` 0; oxfmt/oxlint 0 on changed files.

The prior anchor-dedup test-types stripe failure introduced in Rev11 was fixed in Rev13. No session/anchor/db-regression failure is attributed to this PR.

**Outstanding (per ClawSweeper, not a code finding):** after-fix production trace exercising synchronous cached replay after a real side append, subsequent assistant persistence, and stale-turn rejection (`live_verification=absent`). Supplied evidence is real-SQLite regression tests + static checks.
