prs.title: fix(gateway): keep service credentials referenced only by auth profiles
prs.body:
Related: #162675

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a systemd Gateway drops inherited managed credentials referenced only by saved auth profiles during startup.

## User Impact

API-key and token references keep inherited service values needed for resolution. Values absent from trusted dotenv and selected config/auth references are still removed. Unreadable rows preserve uncertain values with a credential-safe Doctor warning; database admission, native-close and snapshot-cleanup failures remain startup errors. Dev reset skips stores it is about to delete.

Whole-database inspection adds startup I/O and temporary storage. Installed-systemd EnvironmentFile to full Gateway resolution, representative startup/storage measurements and exact-head maintainer security approval remain outstanding. No authored schema, stored-format, service-file, dependency, protocol, permission or credential-selection policy change is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing auth owner reads reference names before service-env cleanup without activating credentials or modifying source artifacts. Row decoding contains unreadable rows; lifecycle failures propagate with their causes. Ordinary pooled readers retain the prepared snapshot until native close succeeds; one-shot inspection owns its image. Failed ordinary closes remain available for scoped retry.

This maintenance also aligns an inherited queue test with main's deliberate cancellation contract from Peter Steinberger's a5787464af4 / #173452. The aggregate uses AbortSignal.any throughout the batch. The stale test still expected an older client's cancellation to be disconnected. Only that test's title and first expected observation change; original grant-revocation, rejected post-revocation effect and source-release assertions remain intact. The runtime cancellation owner is unchanged.

## Evidence

Current-head natural build/test CI run **38832906877** is now **SUCCESS** on head **28e6e7ab3c70564779daeeeb5db5a83879eea24a**; build-artifacts job **116755888713** also succeeds. Maintainer security approval remains outstanding. This newer passing run does not establish the cause of the earlier PTY exit timeout; the earlier failure and the different source-mode diagnostic remain qualified below.

Current source: 28e6e7ab3c70564779daeeeb5db5a83879eea24a. Normal merge of author 5f40981acf8af4c8f0be65d835f25d5c7c0a0935 with exact CI base 62d2fce2b38d4fbee7784379c91975604c869ddc, selected for the named queue CI failure. The complete pre-edit merge tree matches actual CI merge a98ca3ce2a2a75e65e75cb6b2822583cb10716a7. After the two-line queue test correction, every tracked production/config/package/runtime input still matches that tested merge.

- Before: the selected original queue case fails with received [true, true] versus expected [false, true] on both the exact CI merge and an independent clean exact-base checkout with private frozen dependencies. Each has one failure and 14 unselected cases; Vitest takes 47.34 / 44.00 seconds respectively. Exact-base wrapper time is 111.487 seconds. This establishes the queue failure's inheritance and stale assertion; it does not establish anything about the separate PTY failure.
- After: 39 selected regressions pass across four files: the complete 15-case queue authority file, 11 collector/read-pool controls, and all 13 startup-admission fixture cases. Aggregate wrapper times are 107.288 and 164.401 seconds. Current cancellation, grant refusal, source custody, native-close behavior, malformed metadata, source artifacts and lease checks retain their assertions.
- Eight production roots and their consumer closure pass types in 99.499 seconds; five test-consumer roots pass in 108.973 seconds. All 12 changed TS files pass type-aware lint in 45.636 seconds. Format, diff and the native staged line-cap ratchet pass. Fresh independent full 13-file P0–P2 review is scoped-clean, with exact reviewed source/index bytes.
- Input-qualified build reuse: existing natural CI run 38822808116, job 116723653011, has successful Build dist, CLI launcher help, CLI launcher status-json and built-CLI-with-Bun steps on a98ca3ce. Build phase timing is 169.5 seconds. The only source difference from that complete tree is the queue test title/expectation, so these remain build evidence for unchanged runtime inputs. No fresh local build or artifact-freshness override was used; this is prior-merge step evidence, not new-head CI success. The overall job remains failed because of the separate TUI case below.
- Actual Node 24.19.0 / pnpm 12.10.1 satisfy the branch. Manifest and lock are exact official-main inputs, frozen installation is unchanged, and both existing author and upstream parents are preserved. No timeout increase, retry-to-green, expected-failure mask, runtime revert, paid allocation or upstream merge was used.

The earlier 5f fixture correction remains: invalidate the canonical clean-close seal before the fixture injects malformed rows through raw SQLite. It keeps exit-78, source/config-byte, metadata and lease assertions. Original CI's unexpected READY outcome was not reproduced in bounded 012/base/merge replays; that original incident's root cause remains unknown. Its actual setup Node was 24.19.0, not the 24.21 value in a job environment variable.

**Retained PTY failure and limits:** run 38822808116's local chat PTY receives CHAT_ALIAS_RESPONSE and then fails the original four-second exit wait. Its cause is still unestablished; neither unchanged test files nor a successful build proves inheritance. A bounded supported source-mode local-only diagnostic used the original timeouts and no Gateway fixture, but failed earlier because the synthetic model request was never received (one failed / 27 unselected, 202.77 seconds wrapper). It does not reproduce or waive the built-launcher exit failure and is not presented as a product fix. Next proof needs a head-matched built CLI at the original chat-alias boundary, exact-base/head comparison and exit-resource observations; no forced exit, longer timeout or unrelated runtime patch is proposed.

Installed-systemd startup, latest-stable upgrade, representative whole-database scan cost and current-head maintainer security/fixture approval remain separate upstream requirements. No local Gateway, operator data, external message, vendor inference or paid resource was used for this integration.

<details>
<summary>Earlier head-specific proof, failures and costs</summary>

Current-head natural CI run **38822808116** is **failed**, separately from the focused fixture proof above. Job **116723654912** fails `queue.authority.test.ts` (`keeps original grant revocation effective after collect retires an older client cancel`: received `[true, true]`, expected `[false, true]`); job **116723653011** fails the real local TUI PTY smoke with `timed out waiting for PTY exit`. The checkout log identifies tested merge `a98ca3ce` of this head into base `62d2fce2b38d4fbee7784379c91975604c869ddc`. Neither failure is waived, classified as inherited, or covered by a passing replay here; exact-base ownership/runtime diagnosis remains pending. No CI rerun, assertion relaxation, or timeout increase was used.


Current head: `5f40981acf8af4c8f0be65d835f25d5c7c0a0935`. This follow-up changes only the existing startup-admission test fixture; all eleven previously reviewed auth/environment files remain byte-identical to `012248ae2bbe47d6033557fcfb50c886067e6e3b`.

Natural [CI run 38811844372, job 116687858014](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38811844372/job/116687858014) tests merge `67875e61091b7a290be8caa201d74a99e4e021ea` against base `5348bbcd42061eb1f044fa155ae4b93a30d0e28f`. Its Bun startup-admission file has **12 passes / 1 failure**: corrupted `gateway.supervision` unexpectedly reaches `__READY__` with exit 0 instead of refusal 78. This path does not enter this PR's systemd environment-reference scanner. The actual runner uses pinned OpenClaw Bun `1.4.3-canary.1+94f8f5ffe` and resolved Node **24.19.0**; the declared `NODE_VERSION=24.21.0` variable is not its resolved runtime.

A bounded exact-input replay did **not** reproduce that failure: the isolated case passes on exact base/merge in **79.859 / 75.373 seconds**, and the full 13-case file in original order passes in **165.135 / 122.924 seconds**, using the same pinned Bun and Node 24.19. These are retained observations, **not a demonstrated inherited failure, flaky diagnosis, CI waiver or proof of the original cause**. CI's seal/stat state was not captured.

The fixture has a separate established setup defect: it closes a healthy database through its owner, which can publish clean-close proof, then injects damage through raw `node:sqlite` without invalidating that proof. The documented maintenance contract requires invalidation before direct rewriting. The existing seal deliberately does not hash all database contents or promise detection of silent corruption preserving all compared metadata. The fixture now calls the existing `invalidateSqliteDatabaseCleanClose(databasePath)` before raw mutation, as adjacent admission tests do. This makes its intended unsealed malformed-store boundary explicit. It keeps the corrupt metadata, real startup entry, exit-78, source/config byte-preservation and lease assertions intact; no production validation, seal format, permissions or timing rules change.

- The corrected fixture overlaid onto the **exact failed CI merge** passes **all 13 cases** in **170.584 seconds wrapper / 161.75 seconds Vitest**, using the checksum/revision-verified pinned Bun parent and Node 24.19 child. These processes execute startup preflight only; they never start a Gateway or service.
- Relevant test-consumer types pass in **74.902 seconds**, typed core lint in **16.056 seconds**; format, diff and native staged one-file line-cap checks pass. No new test, mock, sleep, timeout, retry, skip or expected-failure exception is added.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the full one-file fixture and its owner/maintenance contract is scoped-clean; the committed fixture hash matches reviewed bytes. The unchanged eleven-file product review, 19 focused regressions, types/lint and **648.712-second** normal build remain input-qualified below. Node24.19.0 / pnpm12.10.1 satisfy this branch; no package or lock changes are included.

Natural new-head CI remains pending. The setup correction alone does not establish which seal/metadata state caused the original CI acceptance, and passing replay is not labeled a production fix. Installed-systemd EnvironmentFile-to-Gateway upgrade proof and representative startup/storage measurements remain uncovered; no old Gateway approval was reused and no local Gateway, paid allocation, CI rerun or upstream merge was performed.

<details>
<summary>Previous owner integration and head-specific proof</summary>



Current head: `012248ae2bbe47d6033557fcfb50c886067e6e3b`, normal merge of author `106060e0c06dc09e8801a9ee452134952317cf0f` with official main `c26f117d8aba20d351e70e5167df234aff61cbd5`.

The integration retains main's injected database opener, identity-checked reader reuse, worker schema facts and retained runtime readers. The one-shot environment-reference reader supplies its private snapshot as the final optional lifetime argument and explicitly closes before cleanup. A failed native close retains snapshot custody. The shared-state reader keeps main's extracted row/engine/TTS owner; only row-read/JSON failures are mapped to an unreadable auth store, while admission, close and cleanup errors propagate.

- **Before:** exact-main pre-bootstrap drops a real persisted auth-profile-only environment reference: startup is admitted but the key is absent and resolution returns `SECRET_REF_NOT_FOUND`. The existing process entry regression has **1 intended failure** in **105.889 seconds wrapper / 96.30 seconds Vitest**; 22 unrelated cases are unselected. The wrapper stops after that failed CLI shard, so the requested pool controls were not executed in that negative run. Candidate files are restored by exact hashes.
- **After:** **19 distinct cases pass**: collector/pool 11 in **54.335 seconds**, four selected pre-bootstrap process controls in **95.210 seconds**, three selected real read-worker controls in **36.212 seconds**, and the credential-copy cleanup control in **52.237 seconds**. The final extra selector uses a short stable phrase because the parameterized display title truncates the word `failure`. Coverage includes shared and agent-local reference names, source artifact hashes, missing stores, malformed/unreadable stores, readable/schema-refused native-close failures in both inspection modes, replaced-file identity, cold initialization, reader release before deletion, unknown-reference preservation and both ownership/credential snapshot removal failures. These processes call only the pre-bootstrap selection/preparation/recheck owners; they do not start a Gateway or systemd service.
- A retained fixture originally called the cold synchronous ownership consumer. The first candidate aggregate is **10 passes / 1 failure**, retained as a fixture migration failure. The same `state-db` assertion now awaits the real `prepareSharedAuthStoreOwnership` owner; no fabricated admission or production fallback is added.
- Eight production module roots and their consumer closure pass types in **101.075 seconds**. The final test-consumer closure passes in **20.152 seconds**; original relevant consumer compilation also passed in 102.563 seconds. Typed lint passes for all ten TS files in **34.149 seconds**, then for the corrected test in **21.073 seconds**. Format, diff, targeted MDX sanity and the native staged line-cap ratchet pass: **10 changed source files, no growth**. An initial non-staged ratchet selected the old historical merge base and exceeded Git's pipe buffer; the supported `--staged --base c26...` invocation checks the exact authored index rather than incoming main history.
- Fresh full **11-file** independent P0–P2 review, including the staged new collector and tests, is scoped-clean. Earlier review passes omitted those two untracked sensitive-name source files and are not claimed as complete proof. All committed blobs match the final review manifest.
- Required normal `pnpm build`: **passes in 648.712 seconds** (native phases total 640.2 seconds; SDK declaration generation 344.7 seconds). No timeout, guard or compiler substitution was used. Actual Node 24.19.0 / pnpm 12.10.1 satisfy the integrated branch; manifest and lock remain exact official-main inputs.

Current-head natural CI remains separate. Prior run **38037208366** tested merge `83c4721d46448b0c58e1bbba303d36ee48b8d9f8` against base `72eafadc01a01781cd4ac114f9397c02af9b367f`. [UI 5/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38037208366/job/114170270217) failed two Pin clicks blocked by Details; [UI 6/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38037208366/job/114170270214) failed to populate an IndexedDB snapshot because its mock roster lacked `kind`. Relevant browser/runner/config/package inputs are identical between that tested merge and base, and both browser mocks bypass this PR's startup/auth reader. Official fixes [#168494](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168494) and [#162316](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/162316) are ancestors of integrated main. No fresh UI replay or inherited-runtime waiver is claimed by this source attribution.

Installed-systemd EnvironmentFile to full Gateway resolution, representative whole-database startup/storage measurements and exact-head maintainer security review remain outstanding. No local Gateway, operator state, external provider, paid test allocation, schema/version change or upstream merge was used. Earlier head-specific live/process proof stays historical.

<details>
<summary>Earlier head-specific proof and costs</summary>



Previously tested source head: `310deda0c23193e8d8dfcdf6a7f17feabb4a6cb5`. Integrated official main: `a204bb6d9f4d23fcf8b780dc8ea9137a2b57b028` because the PR was conflicting.

Real private images, native close failure and subsequent successful retirement prove storage custody; no new timers, Gateway boots or test-only production seam. Current-head CI seconds are not yet available.
- Fresh full-candidate P0–P2 independent review and final fixture correction review are scoped clean; a separate read-only owner review found no P0–P2 finding. Review is static and does not supply the outstanding live or scale evidence.

## Schema-Admission Import Conflict Maintenance

Normal integration preserves incoming head `310deda0c23193e8d8dfcdf6a7f17feabb4a6cb5` and pinned official main `6996363759660d5aae6a24625ef805225d87fcb5`. The max-lines failure is the unchanged stale `doctor-memory-search.test.ts` entry; its source/baseline/guard inputs equal this round's complete-main reproduction. Fresh complete tracked **official `6996363`** reproduces the current unused-export fingerprints in **136.359 seconds**: production `isPollVoteEchoText` and `PUBLIC_SESSION_ENTRY_SCRIPT`, full-tree `isClaudeLikeLiveAgent`, scripts zero. Candidate files—including both added collector files—modes and index were restored exactly after the temporary main-only scan. These remain failed checks; no guard, ignore or baseline policy was altered and current CI is not claimed green.

**External proof and approval remain outstanding:** installed-systemd EnvironmentFile through full Gateway resolution, representative startup/temp-storage measurements and exact-head maintainer security approval. Previous 310deda runtime/native checks and earlier proofs above retain their original heads; no current full installed-Gateway, scale, vendor or security acceptance is claimed. The installed updater keeps its own published driver; the patch applies at candidate bootstrap, and this maintenance adds no new update or service policy. No workflow rerun, timeout/assertion/baseline exception or green-only push was used. Node 24.19.0 / pnpm 12.9.0 and installed lock alignment match main without author package/lock changes or another dependency install.


### Current-head UI CI investigation (2026-10-10)

[Run 38037208366](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38037208366) tested merge `83c4721d46448b0c58e1bbba303d36ee48b8d9f8`: current head `106060e0c06dc09e8801a9ee452134952317cf0f` into official main `72eafadc01a01781cd4ac114f9397c02af9b367f`. Failed UI jobs:

- [Shard 5/7, job 114170270217](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38037208366/job/114170270217): two existing `session-dashboard` Pin clicks time out at 30 seconds because SVG/span children of `.chat-gutter-stack--details` intercept pointer events, before mocked `board.widget.put`. - [Shard 6/7, job 114170270214](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38037208366/job/114170270214): `chat-history-stale-geometry` fails at line 172, polling for the expected IndexedDB snapshot record for 10 seconds, before the viewport change/reload. Other tests: 130 passed.

The tested merge differs from that main only in this PR's eleven files. UI source, protocol, Workboard fixture, browser helpers, Vitest config/runner, package and lock are identical to main. These two browser flows use synthetic Mock WebSockets and a built UI preview; they do not invoke the changed auth-profile or Gateway pre-bootstrap owners.

A bounded local replay on the **complete official main 72eafadc source**, using its unchanged tests and the same installed Node/pnpm/dependencies, produced **2 failed, 1 passed, 6 filtered skips in 149.312 seconds**. prs.title: fix(chat): retain warm startup receipts after deferred mount
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes full-history downloads on warm reload when the chat pane mounts after the Gateway is ready. Follow-up to #175816: startup can no longer outrun retained cursor and metadata hydration.

## User Impact

Warm reloads reuse the conversation and receipt hashes while retaining the earlier first paint. Missing, invalid, or unavailable caches still fall back to a full request. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The history owner previously joined snapshot hydration only before applying the response, after sending an empty `knownState` without a cursor. Move that existing bounded wait before request construction, after stream admission. The frame handoff is unchanged. The existing two-second cache timeout now bounds request issuance, so unavailable storage still fails open.

Production change: **−1 line net**, with no new owner, state, timer, or cache. Consolidated the now-impossible history-before-initial-cache test ordering while preserving cached row identity and widget-height assertions.

## Evidence

**All 12 unprofiled candidate warm reloads:** retained cursor plus all three receipt hashes, **306 framed bytes / 224 payload bytes**, **zero messages and no `chat.history`**. Failing baseline runs returned **154,318 framed bytes / 80 messages**. The baseline reproduced the race in 4/4 fast-connection and 7/8 deferred-mount runs.

Concurrent pairs on an isolated Linux sandbox use separate 16-core CPU sets, state, and ports, swap core halves each pair, and hold an exclusive measurement lock. Actual warm starts differ by at most 2 ms; per-pair outside load was recorded. Values below are median **candidate minus baseline within each pair**:

| Metric | Fast connection, 4 pairs | Deferred mount, 8 pairs |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| FCP | 0 ms | 0 ms |
| Final retained message visible | +4.55 ms | −0.05 ms |
| Sidebar final order stable | +18.4 ms | +0.4 ms |

Deferred restore blocking remains **0 ms on both sides in all eight pairs**. Final-message mean difference is +7.88 ms, range −39.4…+100.4 ms. The +100.4 ms outlier remains included; four extra pairs checked the distribution. Cold FCP medians are +4/0 ms and cold final-message medians +11.7/+2.75 ms respectively. Final row counts and ordered sidebar keys match, with no browser errors.

Two separate traced pairs confirm an actual Chrome Paint between sidebar restoration and pane mounting, with retained data still pending. Example candidate: sidebar task ends 223.977 ms, Paint 234.417–234.939 ms, pane starts 236.164 ms, retained-record delivery 336.4 ms. Traced timings are excluded from the comparison above.

The headless fixture uses 80 retained messages, 80 sidebar sessions, five pending inputs, session info, and 150 commands. Deferred mode releases hello after the sidebar frame boundary and adds 120 ms only to retained chat-record delivery; subscription is immediate. It proves avoided full-page resend and no candidate history fill, but does not model the reported larger-session pagination cascade. Synthetic data only. Chromium 155 actually paints, verified by trace Paint events and filmstrip. Identical measurement-only dependency deviations on both sides: Vite 8.3.2 versus 8.3.4, Playwright 1.63 versus 1.64, CodeMirror language 6.12.4 versus 6.13.1 and view 6.43.13 versus 6.43.14; Solid runtime/compiler match the pinned version. Owned sandbox and processes are removed.

The deferred-mount regression fails on the base with `knownState: {}` and no cursor, then passes with retained data. Focused checks: warm startup **26/26**, persistent snapshot hydration **7/7**, stream admission **7/7**, changed-file lint/format and diff checks pass. Independent autoreview is clean through P2 after correcting a sibling test's obsolete immediate-request expectation. [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39074727735) passed all required checks on `9b542203ba906c26137ccccb0803a082a6eed2ec`, including UI tests, E2E, performance, types, lint, and the final CI/security gates; no Testbox lease or local broad gate was used.

prs.title: fix(signal): inline external-native outbound attachments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Outbound Signal attachments are handed to signal-cli as a filesystem path under the gateway-owned `0700` outbound media directory. An external-native signal-cli daemon running as a different uid cannot traverse that path, so image and video sends fail at the last hop with `AttachmentInvalidException (Permission denied)` after the attachment was already validated.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native signal-cli already accepts an RFC 2397 data URI in place of a path, and the Signal plugin already has a bounded file-to-data-URI encoder for the container transport. External-native sends now reuse that encoder, so the already-authorized bytes travel over the open JSON-RPC connection. Managed-native still passes the staged path because that daemon shares the gateway uid. Container still receives the path and performs its own conversion. Directory permissions stay private, and this does not add a config switch or a new attachment channel.

## User Impact

Hardened deployments that run signal-cli as its own service user can send outbound media again. Same-uid managed-native sends and container REST sends keep their existing behavior. External-native payloads grow by about a third because the bytes are base64, and they remain bounded by the existing media size cap.

## Evidence

Head `5ef2734b8945cabaf2fd36f3f09c2dc46fd868aa`, rebased onto `upstream/main` `0e6eb6908bd5743aab9c1190998c3e89ce88974d`.

`check-test-types` on the previous head failed with a real type error:

```text
extensions/signal/src/send.test.ts(41,44): error TS2556: A spread argument must either have a tuple type or be passed to a rest parameter.
```

The hoisted attachment mock had dropped its rest parameter, so the `unknown[]` spread was illegal. Restoring `(..._args: unknown[])` matches the resolver mock on main. Local `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` then exited 0.

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-signal.config.ts \
  extensions/signal/src/send.test.ts \
  extensions/signal/src/media-access.test.ts \
  extensions/signal/src/outbound.media-limit.test.ts \
  extensions/signal/src/client-container.test.ts
```

```text
Test Files  4 passed (4)
     Tests  62 passed (62)
```

oxlint on the five changed files: 0 warnings, 0 errors.

Live JSON-RPC stub, no Signal account: `sendMessageSignal` staged a real 68-byte PNG under the private outbound media directory and posted to a local `POST /api/v1/rpc` stub. External-native carried a `data:` URI whose decoded bytes matched the file. Managed-native carried the staged path. The outbound directory mode was `700`. The JSON-RPC `id` is redacted. No phone number was used.

External-native body:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"send","params":{"message":"proof","account":"proof-account","attachments":["data:image/png;filename=chart.png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAQAAAC1HAwCAAAAC0lEQVR42mP8/x8AAwMCAO+ip1sAAAAASUVORK5CYII="],"groupId":"proof-group"},"id":"<redacted>"}
```

Managed-native body:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"send","params":{"message":"proof","account":"proof-account","attachments":["/home/synth/.hermes/cache/scratch/oc-vt-Tihmj7/openclaw-signal-rpc-proof-6vc4G2/state/media/outbound/chart---1492f4c2-3cbe-43f7-8259-7ae195778ee2.png"],"groupId":"proof-group"},"id":"<redacted>"}
```

Fixes openclaw/openclaw#123815

prs.title: fix: resume queued user work after Gateway restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: queued user work can fail to resume after a Gateway restart with a transcript idempotency conflict.

## User Impact

Accepted user input remains intact, and its restart continuation starts without conflicting with the original transcript row. No configuration, schema, or permission changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Queued work keeps its original user transcript key as the recovery source while execution can have a different run ID. Recovery mistook the original admission ID for an already reserved continuation ID and tried to append different content under the original input key.

Recognize the existing canonical user-key form when choosing a fresh continuation ID. Keep the original source correlation and the strict transcript guard. Actual continuation IDs remain stable across uncertain transport failures; prior-lifecycle admissions still rotate.

## Evidence

- The new regression uses the real user recorder, reply claim actor, shutdown marking, recovery dispatcher, and strict transcript append. On the original production source it fails with `TranscriptTurnAdmissionConflictError` for the original synthetic input key.
- Fixed source: six focused cases pass, including the new queued-input recovery, both source identity forms through an uncertain dispatch retry, prior-lifecycle rotation, and completed-RPC reuse. The original user row remains singular and its source correlation is retained.
- Runtime-value import cycles and Madge cycles: zero. Format and diff checks pass.
- Fresh independent review: scoped-clean through P2 (patch-correct confidence 0.93).
- Exact-head PR CI is green at `2e3a493d828185504fcf240dbaec31452da5b755`, including production types, test types, lint, and the CI gate ([run 39070159117](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39070159117)). The earlier bounded local compiler checks were stopped under host memory pressure without diagnostics; no local typecheck pass is claimed.

Local activation: the equivalent recovery fix is built and deployed in the operator’s existing beta runtime. All six recovery cases pass against that local backport. The managed Node 24 Gateway passes deep status and health checks; the web UI and assets respond, and the final restart window contains no ERROR/FATAL entries. Existing voice and plugin changes were preserved. This is a combined local backport, not a claim that the exact public PR binary or an external-provider recovery turn was exercised.

The focused regression uses synthetic data and simulated Gateway RPC execution with real persistence/recovery/transcript owners. The separate shipped-runtime proof below uses a real isolated Gateway and native provider. No production Gateway or private user transcript is used.


### Actual Gateway/native recovery proof

A fresh isolated shipped-runtime proof exercised explicit owner `chat.send` followup behind an active native turn. Its original user admission ID differed from the queued turn’s actual execution ID. After a canonical preserve suspension, zero-write-custody check, exact-task process handoff and helper stop/start, an actual native assistant final `QUEUED_RECOVERY_DONE` was recorded under a third, fresh recovery run ID. The canonical transcript retained exactly one original user row with unchanged content; recovery was internal-system work and added no new user row. This uses the built v18 combined backport: the recovery identity-selection block is byte-identical to this PR, while other owner context includes additional repairs. The fixture’s old-client history polling timed out; independent read-only task transcript/session readbacks qualify the final and identity assertions. No fresh active source-claim snapshot was captured, so source continuity is limited to the original claim/key and unchanged canonical row plus reviewed propagation code. Both attempts were cleaned up; no production Gateway or user session was used.

prs.title: fix(ui): model picker opens squeezed below a cramped composer on iPhone
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: on iPhone, the New Session model picker sometimes opens below the composer, squeezed into the strip above the bottom edge of the screen, when it should open above. ## User Impact User impact: the model and effort pickers open above the composer at full height whenever there is room. They no longer get stuck squeezed below after the phone keyboard closes. Shared menus near the bottom of the screen now flip above instead of shrinking to a sliver below the trigger. ## Why This Change Was Made Two overlay rules combined to cause this: - **The shared overlay never flipped.** The `.oc-overlay` base budget was `min(420px, 100% - 16px, 100dvh - 16px)`. Inside a `position-area` grid, `100%` is the height of the chosen side, so the base position always shrank to fit. It never overflowed, so `flip-block` was dead code unless less than about 22px was left. - **The composer pickers always shrank into the opposite side.** `.chat-picker-overlay` overrode that budget and the fallbacks. Its first fallback was `--chat-picker-fit flip-block`, which shrinks onto the opposite side. So whenever the full 420px panel did not fit above, the picker went below and shrank, even when there was more room above. - **The chosen fallback is remembered.** Anchor positioning keeps the last successful fallback until it overflows ([spec](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-anchor-position-1/); Safari 26.1+ per [WebKit features in Safari 26.1](https://webkit.org/blog/17541/webkit-features-for-safari-26-1/)). A shrinking fallback never overflows. On iPhone, `shell-viewport.ts` shrinks the shell to the visual viewport while the keyboard is up, so the composer sits high and neither side holds the full panel. Tapping the pill opens the picker in that state, and it picks "fit below". The picker then focuses its search field in a later frame, which closes the keyboard. The composer moves back down, but the picker keeps the remembered "below" option and shrinks to the remaining strip. That matches the reported screenshot. The fix keeps one placement policy in the shared overlay: - The base budget is now `max(200px, 100% - 16px)`. A long panel still shrinks into its placed side, but only down to 200px. Below that it overflows, so the engine tries the other side. While the panel is open, overflow also makes the engine choose again once the remembered side gets too short, for example after the keyboard closes. - A new last-resort `--oc-overlay-fill` option, tried on the placed side and then the other side, keeps the old fill-to-fit behavior when neither side holds 200px. Side menus (`left*`/`right*`) try fill beside their anchor before their existing below/above options, so their outcomes are unchanged. - The `.chat-picker-overlay` override and its `@position-try --chat-picker-fit` rule are removed, so the composer pickers use the shared policy. Trade-off: when the placed side holds at least 200px but not the full panel, the panel still shrinks on its placed side rather than moving to a roomier opposite side. I did not use `position-try-order: most-block-size` for three reasons: - In the keyboard state it would rank the area hidden behind the keyboard as "most height" and choose below. - WebKit applies it only to fallbacks, not the base position ([WebKit bug 317916](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=317916)). - A recent CSSWG resolution changes it to sort the base position too, so its behavior is still changing. The design keeps placements that already fit unchanged. It also avoids putting panels that fit their placed side into a fallback position, where Chromium's End-key `scrollIntoView` used the base-size geometry (the board widget menu test caught that in an earlier draft). Other placement changes: on desktop New Session, the picker now opens above the composer (shrunk slightly) instead of below. At 1280×600 the old below position was only about 166px tall. The chat-page composer is unchanged: it has room above, so the base position fits. ## Evidence **Root cause reproduced through the real New Session page** (mocked Gateway, Playwright WebKit and Chromium). The scratch harness focuses the editor, shrinks `visualViewport.height` to emulate the keyboard (as `mobile-shell-geometry.e2e.test.ts` does), taps the model pill, then restores the full visual viewport: | Case (WebKit and Chromium matched) | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | 430×932, no keyboard | above, 420px | above, 420px | | 430×932, keyboard 560 → closed | **below, 226px** | above, 420px | | 393×852, keyboard 500 → closed | **below, 188px** | above, 420px | | 393×640 static (above 415, below 108) | **below, 92px** | above, 399px | | 393×560 open → resize to 852 | **below, 188px** (stuck) | above, 420px | | 1280×600 desktop | below, 166px | above, 371px | Before and after (WebKit, 393×852, keyboard closed after opening; this matches the reported screenshot): WebKit, 430×932, the same flow: WebKit, 430×932 with room (unchanged), before and then after: Desktop New Session, WebKit 1280×600, before and then after: All screenshots use synthetic mock data. **Regression tests** (both fail on the merge base and pass with the fix): - `chat-model-picker.browser.test.tsx`: "returns above the composer at full height once a cramped phone layout regains room". It opens the picker with a cramped composer, then lowers the composer while the picker stays open. On the merge base it fails in both Chromium and WebKit (`expected 690 to be less than or equal to 250`, i.e. opened below). The test now imports `overlay.css` before `composer.css`, matching the app's stylesheet order; without that, the test cascade hid the composer override. - `overlay-style.browser.test.tsx`: "flips a long menu above when too little room remains below". On the merge base it fails (`expected 590 to be less than or equal to 452`, i.e. squeezed below). **Commands** (macOS, local): - `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-model-picker.browser.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1`: 16 passed, 5.2s wall (Vitest 3.2s). - `pnpm test ui/src/components/solid/overlay-style.browser.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1`: 9 passed, 5.4s wall (Vitest 4.0s). - `OPENCLAW_UI_WEBKIT=1 pnpm --dir ui test --project=webkit --maxWorkers=1 src/pages/chat/components/chat-model-picker.browser.test.tsx`: 16 passed, 3.7s wall. - The new tests themselves take about 85–220ms each. CI seconds are not available yet. - `pnpm --dir ui test --project=browser --maxWorkers=3` (full Chromium UI browser project): 1704 passed, 70s. - `OPENCLAW_UI_WEBKIT=1 pnpm --dir ui test --project=webkit --maxWorkers=3`: 533 passed, 12 failed. All 12 are inherited: - 11 fail identically on the unchanged merge base in this local WebKit: `image-lightbox` ×3, `modal-dialog` ×2, `popover`, `sidebar-community-invite`, `agent-file-preview` ×3, and `chat-effort-picker` Escape/tooltips. - 1 is a `tooltip.test.ts` hover flake. It also fails on the unchanged merge base (3 of 6 runs) when run together with `chat-model-picker.browser.test.tsx`. - UI e2e: `chat-picker-interaction-contract`, `chat-composer-picker-layout`, `mobile-shell-geometry`, `mobile-new-conversation`, `chat-model-controls`, `chat-model-picker-composition`, `lobster-pet-dismiss-menu-overflow`, `theme-typography`: 8 files, 64 passed, 51s. - `pnpm lint:ui:styles` and `oxfmt --check` on changed files: clean. - `pnpm check:changed --base `: the changed files are clean. Four checks fail only on files this PR does not touch, which exist on the merge base: the max-lines suppression ratchet, the core tsgo shard-root budget, the dead-export scan, and lint `max-lines` errors. **Browser support:** the fix uses only `position-try-fallbacks` with `@position-try` and `flip-block`/`flip-inline`, plus `max()` inside `min()`. These are part of the anchor positioning that Safari 26.0 shipped ([WebKit features in Safari 26.0](https://webkit.org/blog/17333/webkit-features-in-safari-26-0/)), and the Control UI already requires Safari 26.2. It does not rely on `position-try-order`. **Gap:** iPhone Safari real-device confirmation is still pending. Playwright WebKit with an emulated visual-viewport keyboard reproduces the reported geometry, but it does not drive the real iOS keyboard.

prs.title: fix(node): restore automatic updates for installed node services
prs.body:
Fixes #175831

## What Problem This Solves

Installed headless nodes launched `dist/index.js`, bypassing the supervisor that enables automatic node updates. On Windows, batch wrappers could fail with `spawn EINVAL`, and failure after a partial task registration change could prevent restoration.

## User Impact

New node services use the package launcher by default. `openclaw doctor --fix` repairs legacy node definitions while retaining their connection arguments, environment, runtime pins, and stopped state. Customized or externally owned definitions remain unchanged with actionable guidance. Legacy direct-entry nodes now warn when automatic updates are enabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The service argument resolver now chooses node supervisor entrypoints separately from the Gateway entrypoint, retaining stable pnpm package links. Doctor reuses native service installation, drift inspection, and rollback. Windows fallback launches use the existing batch-command quoting owner, and task registration records a successful `/Change` before a later step can fail.

## Evidence

- Regression proof: the old resolver fails the platform/launcher tests and the stored-service live process test; the old Doctor flow leaves the legacy entrypoint unchanged. The Windows regressions reproduce both batch-wrapper `EINVAL` failures and refused restoration after partial registration.
- Live local proof: a synthetic package's real stored systemd command starts distinct launcher/child processes with supervisor IPC. The real node auto-update controller starts after authenticated readiness and exercises update handoff. Doctor tests use real service files and native installation/rollback with a stubbed service manager, isolated HOME/state, and isolated service locks.
- Focused regression/consumer proof: 213 passed, 1 existing skip across 11 touched suites. This includes native-file Doctor repair/rollback (10), real launcher processes (13), Windows launch/rollback and resolver coverage (80), node/controller and Doctor contribution coverage (91), and installer consumers (19).
- Cross-consumer run: 81 files, 1,199 passed, 6 failed, 8 existing skips in 2,338.90 s. Three failures were stale Scheduled Task call-order expectations, now updated for the registration receipt and passing. The other three were nested-temp fixture ownership errors in `update-cli.git-service.test.ts` and `update-command-migrated-windows.test.ts`; all three reproduced with the unchanged starting production code. Running from the normal private temporary directory passed the wrapper case and all six migrated-Windows cases (7 passed). HOME and OpenClaw state remained isolated in every run.
- Existing slow update cases were 38.870 s (`reports managed Git restart failure: stopped`) and 30.938 s (`uses only the owned profile when switching package installs to dev (owned service)`). These exercise existing database snapshot/process work; no timeout, retry, or assertion was weakened.
- Core and touched-test TypeScript checks, touched-file oxlint/oxfmt, import-cycle check (0 cycles), and `git diff --check` pass. Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Native Windows execution was not available; batch launch and restoration are covered by faithful tests. The Windows-only native integration suite was not run on macOS. Per campaign guidance, the full `check:changed` SQLite inventory was skipped for time; PR CI supplies broad proof.
- Diff against the starting base: production +273/−8 lines; tests +564/−24; docs +6/−0. The main addition is Doctor’s previously missing node-service repair path; no new options, schemas, or dependencies.

### Linux CI follow-up

The Linux failures were fixture defects, so this follow-up leaves production launcher selection and Doctor maintenance admission unchanged. The native restore contract retains an installed package location (whose canonical launcher is `openclaw.mjs` or `dist/entry.js`); its fixture had created only `dist/index.js`. Restore tests now retain and assert the launcher, including the built-entry-only layout, and cover source/package selection with Node and Bun.

The managed-approval fixture simulates the native service and replaces Doctor contributions. Its fixed Gateway PID accidentally matched a real CI ancestor before any contribution ran. Synthetic native fixtures now supply consistent ancestry and use a non-self Gateway PID; the explicit ancestor-refusal case still uses the current PID. The node-service fixture initializes private runtime-pin state under the host OS before simulating launchd, canonicalizes its temporary root, and covers an absent service. All four new partial mocks preserve real exports.

Linux arm64 container proof (isolated HOME/state): **Node 26.11.1: 154 passed across 9 files, 325.16 s. Pinned Bun 1.4.3: 153 passed, 1 existing Node-only skip across the same 9 files, 359.54 s.** This covers the three failing suites, resolver/pnpm/Doctor contribution siblings, managed admission and settlement, and read-only configuration. The slowest case was existing approval migration under Bun (40.598 s); no timing controls changed.

The full first-party mock-export ratchet passes with no baseline edits. Focused TypeScript, oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and independent Codex review pass. The local proof container was removed after validation.

Follow-up delta: production +0/−0; tests +86/−13. No runtime safeguards, schema, timeout, retry, or baseline changes.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and validation commands</summary>

All test invocations used an isolated `HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; the final fixture replay used macOS's normal private `TMPDIR` outside the checkout.

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/program-args.test.ts src/daemon/program-args.pnpm.test.ts src/daemon/schtasks.startup-launch.test.ts src/daemon/schtasks-install-rollback.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

prs.title: fix(codex): steer busy sessions and unblock thread handoffs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Messages and peer results sent to a busy agent can wait behind the work that needs them, while an exact-thread handoff can wait indefinitely for a Codex process retained by another session. This routes busy peer input through the existing active queue, preserves its original source identity across recovery, and waits for the retired thread rather than requiring its entire process to exit.

## User Impact

A busy recipient accepts ordinary messages and explicit followup into its active input queue and returns admission only. An idle recipient starts a turn and can return a correlated completion. Self-send, paused-child resume, provenance/display, generation checks, and native writer locking retain their existing owners. Accepted input stays in receiver custody; RPC acknowledgment is not transcript-consumption proof, and confirmation waits settle within their existing request budget.

Two related delivery failures are also repaired: a captured receiver that finishes before admission can retain the ordinary follow-up path after source revalidation, and fresh native child input uses internal completion rather than requiring the child to have a messaging tool.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the recipient’s active queue for dependency input, preserve the original source identity during recovery, and release only the exact retired native thread before handoff. Known receiver settlement before admission must remain distinct from an authority refusal; native child follow-ups must retain their existing internal completion owner.

## Evidence

### Current revision: main integration and HTTP teardown fix

Current head `62078dfa6ee15ae944ab00c70f6567d363508d1e` is a true merge of prior head `f71dd46d8304da701c73a5ca852de478e27a81c1` and pinned main `bcd6ab322aeb6d7a1bd3550477c1875213889e64`, with frozen tree `aa315fad6f561cbfe71f470d3044b887ce950c31`. All 30 PR-owned files are byte-identical to the prior head; the native delivery evidence below retains its stated scope.

This consumes the merged upstream HTTP teardown fix [#175846](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175846), commit `964d3238270df34715cd3064ca1d3625facbc8db`, rather than accepting the older CI failures as a landing exception. **115 focused tests pass with the pinned Bun runtime**, including 47 HTTP/SSE tests covering the two previously failing files and the new late-abort regression, with no unhandled errors. The other passing cases cover 35 steering, 12 queue-authority, 20 policy, and one saved message-less child test. Diff checks and a fresh scoped P0–P2 review pass; that review inspected the complete PR patch without executing the project. Broad types, lint and full-suite validation remain for new-head CI.

The followup behavior still requires the maintainer decision described below. These integration checks ran in isolated task state and did not restart the operator Gateway. They do not claim that every latest upstream change is locally deployed.

### Earlier integrated-main validation

The local candidate merges PR head `e56ea81b6caf04fd12f08e981fb412d144632fee` with main `feeafd6b1e79ff4b8791ed6aa3096df4c47a6dae`. Production changes merged without conflicts; three prompt snapshots were regenerated with the canonical generator. The frozen candidate tree is `1ab9f1112ac46e20828da80d97d01a25f2141a11`.

All runtime evidence below uses synthetic messages and fresh isolated state. No operator Gateway, user conversation, or production workspace was used. The Gateway cases use its authenticated HTTP `sessions_send` route, enabled only in the task fixture; receiving turns use the real native Codex 0.163.0 process and provider.

- **Busy followup:** while the recipient was executing a bounded checkpoint command, explicit `followup` returned `accepted` / `steered`. Its actual final model reply consumed the marker. The assertion excludes the attributed peer transcript row.
- **Returned peer result:** an actual idle worker produced its result; the busy requester received one attributed result row and subsequently included the marker in its actual final reply. The requester's original prompt did not contain the result marker. Its native work continued after result admission.
- **Reset after preparation:** a test-only module-load barrier pauses the real `runAgentStep` immediately after `prepareSessionDeliveryGeneration` returns. Canonical `sessions.reset` runs before the original code resumes. Delivery rejects because the original session changed. A transparent native stdio observer records zero result-marker frames to the original native thread; a read-only check of the original transcript records zero marker rows. No production test hook or guard bypass was added.
- **Native handoff:** real old and successor app-server processes use the same isolated native home. The actual release owner observes the old client's exact `thread/closed`; the successor resumes that thread while the old process still serves a real retained idle sibling. Native persistence locking remains authoritative.
- **Stable upgrade:** official OpenClaw 2026.10.4 and its own CLI write/read a synthetic session. After stopping that Gateway, the candidate's canonical `doctor --fix --non-interactive` migration succeeds, creates pre-migration backups, and the candidate preserves the session ID, transcript count, and marker. Direct startup correctly refuses the older schema until Doctor runs. This PR introduces no additional schema.

Focused owner tests: **131 passed across three shards**. Canonical runtime build, generated prompt check, formatting of all 23 changed files, and diff checks pass. A fresh frozen P2 review reports no findings. Current-main core type checking was stopped through its cleanup owner after an extended active compile and remains for PR CI. Scoped lint reports only two existing file-length violations that this patch increases: `sessions-send-tool.ts` 706→707 and `run-attempt-dispatch.ts` 710→721 (limit 700); these are disclosed rather than suppressed.

### Additional delivery-owner repairs on `3071a5f`

These eight-file changes build on the published merge head `3071a5f47f4a4b15427ca5aa1b0ef80834d6ab41`; the earlier runtime/upgrade/handoff evidence above remains evidence for its stated revision.

- **Receiver ends before admission:** the captured embedded target can finish or be replaced while an input waits in its FIFO. Known target loss now uses the existing target-unavailable classification. The source is revalidated before ordinary follow-up fallback; a revoked caller or a live receiver's authority refusal remains an error. Explicit `steer` still refuses an unavailable target. Accepted or unconfirmed input keeps its existing non-replayable custody.
- **Native child input:** fresh `sessions_send` input to a classified native subagent uses `automatic` internal completion. The existing task/one-way completion owner still returns the result; the request does not grant a message tool. Ordinary peer and canonical ACP targets retain `message_tool_only`. Access to another parent's child remains forbidden.

Synthetic owner proof on this public base passed in separate focused runs: **35 embedded-queue tests** (including RED→GREEN FIFO receiver settlement/replacement and caller/receiver revocation controls), **20 tool-policy tests** (including owned child, forbidden unowned child, ordinary peer, and persisted canonical ACP metadata), and **one actual Codex attempt** that resumes a saved message-less child thread and captures its visible internal final. The Codex transport is controlled in that last test; it is not an external-provider proof. Owning `agents-other`/`agents-tools` type graphs and the focused new Codex test type graph pass; typed plugin lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. Fresh P2 reviews of the changed owners report no findings.

An additional **two-case isolated test on the matching local candidate** exercises its preserved message-tool availability guard: `automatic` resumes the exact saved child and captures the final with an empty message-tool catalog, while `message_tool_only` fails with the exact availability error before `turn/start`. That additional guard is absent from this public base; this does not claim that the public test exercised it. No operator conversation, protected source, or production Gateway was used for these tests.

Scoped typed core lint passes without changing or suppressing any rule. The ownership-lookup failure formatting and logging moved unchanged to the existing send helper; the producer retains its lookup classification and all authority decisions. This keeps the native-child conditional below the 700-line limit. The final layout also passes the 20 tool-policy cases again, two separately filtered existing lookup-error regressions, and the owning agents-tools type graph. The existing `run-attempt-dispatch.ts` 710→721 disclosure above is unchanged by these additional repairs. Broader current-head checks remain for PR CI.

### Maintainer decision still requested

This deliberately changes explicit `followup` for a busy recipient to admission into that recipient's active input queue, with an admission-only receipt. An idle recipient still gets a separate turn and can return a correlated completion. The earlier owner decision in #160842 preserved explicit followup as a separate-turn escape hatch; this proposal asks to replace that behavior, and does not claim approval has already been granted.

Codex 0.163.0 uses `MessageDeliveryMode::TriggerTurn` for `followup_task`: an active session drains its mailbox, while an idle session may start a turn. Matching that busy/idle distinction prevents a dependency result from waiting behind the work that needs it. The motivating reports included messages waiting tens of minutes or hours; that history supports this change, without claiming every reported hang had the same cause. Input is consumed at supported execution checkpoints, not by forcibly interrupting an arbitrary blocking tool.

Security review should assess the complete preparation-to-effect chain and the intentional busy-followup contract. The runtime evidence strengthens that assessment; it does not substitute for the maintainer's product/security decision.

### Synthetic result readbacks

The additional repairs passed the isolated tests described above and were subsequently activated in the operator’s local Gateway. Post-activation RPC health and plugin loading pass. Separate retained-turn recovery errors remain under investigation; this is not a claim that all historical queueing or recovery failures are resolved.


### Test inventory integration

CI caught that the new saved-subsession regression was absent from the full-suite database-worker inventory. The existing manifest now registers it. The actual exact-once coverage regression, scoped lint, formatting, and fresh P2 review pass. The saved-subsession source and its behavioral proof are unchanged by this manifest-only commit. Broader CI continues on the current head.

### Real native receiver-settlement fallback capture

Receiver-settlement fallback now has a real isolated Gateway/native-provider capture through authenticated HTTP `/tools/invoke` → `sessions_send` (`mode=followup`, `timeoutSeconds=0`). prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A current-only plugin metadata read keeps a second lazy loader for the current-snapshot module, even though supported publication and scoping register that reader before exposing a snapshot. Read the registered owner directly.

## User Impact

Current reads stay lightweight and return the existing published/scoped snapshot or undefined. Explicit snapshot resolution and required policy readers retain their cold-loading/error behavior. Gateway reader lifetime, real reload/installation policy, credential/manifest authority and ordinary shutdown settlement are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the unused-in-supported-flows current-module fallback and its misleading comments: eight net production lines removed (+6/-14), two files, no test changes. This is the metadata area of the prior >80-file cleanup family, split for bounded CI attribution; historical ONE savings are not counted again.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Manually assigning internal nonempty snapshot state after clearing its reader slot no longer cold-loads a reader to recover. Production publishers/scopers register during module evaluation before they can run; the actual state-writer census has one nonempty publication owner and a separate clear owner. That synthetic bypass is not a supported lifecycle. A cold process with no owner returns undefined.
- The bridge originated in499d81/#120876 to keep doctor/plugin static closures off the heavy metadata graph, with measured import work. That boundary and the explicit resolver stay. No human current-read cold-load incident is claimed. Real package-replacement reader retention and the newer native required-policy readers remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Complete determining owners, state writers, reader lifetime, required bridge, lifecycle/current/required tests and current consumers source-audited. Normalization explicitly resolves discovery on a current miss; provider artifacts retain manifest fallback; media roots, skills capture and Gateway presentation consume existing inventory or intentional absence.
- Fresh complete independent two-file review with12 determining datasets: scoped-clean P0-P2/0.91; final source verification passed. Canonical formatting passed22ms, whitespace passed. Frozen blobs8e1fd09/940c537 match the reviewed candidate.
- Receiving-head required-reader/lifecycle runtime attempt stopped before assertions when actual cold-worker compilation appeared; all eight owned PIDs drained. No equivalent cold retry or runtime pass claimed. Targeted two-root types exited2 with36 unchanged parse5/MCP declaration and implicit-any diagnostics, none naming either changed file; not a type pass. Canonical two-file core type-aware lint passed. Mandatory suppression guard14PASS/48.15s Vitest/74.64s wrapper (git enumeration12.17s). No local broad build/profile/whole-graph check under shared-host budget; no comparative performance or live Gateway claim. Exact-head CI supplies broad proof before landing.
- No added dependency edge/cycle, public SDK/config/protocol/dependency/persisted shape/permission/durability change. No test/suppression/timeout/retry/skip/baseline changes. Phase E standalone session-memory backend and its tests untouched.

Release-note context: internal current-metadata ownership cleanup only.

Initial exact-head CI39072797919 found one owned shrink-only ratchet error: the removed fallback also removed a type assertion, so config/assertion-safety-baseline.txt must decrease this owner's allowance2→1. Signed repair d4877ebef7016dcf7b07dba4265e104097f7abab changes only that entry; both production blobs remain identical to the reviewed candidate. prs.title: refactor(mattermost): pass native request errors to retry owner
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The private Mattermost DM retry operation catches every failure only to rethrow native Errors unchanged. Its actual send route constructs the concrete native client, whose transport, provider response and authority failures are already Errors.

## User Impact

Pass the request directly to the existing retry owner. Preserve error identity, provider-status precedence, permanent authority refusal, retry attempts, full-jitter schedule, delay caps, timeout and diagnostic callback. No send/public SDK contract changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Six net production lines removed in one private owner, no tests changed. This is the Mattermost area of the preserved wide cleanup family, split by area under the campaign rule rather than bundled with unrelated transport or authority work. Historical residue savings are not counted again.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- A hand-constructed private client rejecting a string or plain object no longer gets coerced before retry classification or its diagnostic callback. The sole production caller constructs the native client with no arbitrary operation/transport hook; all its actual failures retain their Error identity. Shared retry still normalizes terminal failures. Its callbacks receive raw errors, not falsely claimed pre-normalized ones.
- The wrapper came from the shared full-jitter migration #104594/d4adddbe, whose body describes schedule/classification preservation and synthetic tests, not a human report requiring non-Error recovery. Real jitter, network/429 retry, auth checks and partial-delivery safety are retained.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(gateway): reverting a deferred restart-required config edit still restarts the Gateway
prs.body:
Closes #119360

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Gateway still restarts after an operator reverts a restart-required config edit (for example `gateway.port`) to the exact running config while that restart waits for active work to drain.

## User Impact

User impact: probing a restart-class setting and putting `openclaw.json` back no longer drops Control UI and channel sessions for a full restart. A revert to any other config, a second restart-required edit, an explicit writer restart request, and plugin install changes still restart as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a restart is deferred, the reloader advances its diff baseline to the deferred candidate before the process actually restarts. The revert is then compared against that candidate, so it looks like a new `gateway.port` change and plans another restart. The reloader now remembers the config and plugin install records the process still runs while a restart is deferred. A candidate that matches them exactly takes the existing unchanged-config path, so the restart coordinator's existing acceptance retires the config-owned debt. The coordinator stays the only owner of restart debt, so there is no second copy of restart-owned paths in the reloader (the open findings on #119576).

Restart requests that carry a reason other than a changed config path, such as writer restart intent, now keep their debt across later config changes, so a config revert cannot cancel them (the concern on #119577). This is a small behavior change maintainers should see.

Install records are compared by path diff, as `pluginInstallRecordChangedPaths` already does, not with `isDeepStrictEqual`. The startup records are a plain object and the ledger reader returns null-prototype maps, so a strict compare never matches in a real Gateway. The live run below caught this. The tests now mock the reader with the production shape.

A revert does not retire the restart while a shared-auth requirement is pending (commit 077cca214c7). When the deferred candidate changed shared auth, for example a token to password switch, `runManagedRestart` has already marked the candidate's shared-auth generation as required, and only a restart clears it. Retiring the restart there would leave the Gateway rejecting the restored token with nothing scheduled to fix it. In that case the revert takes the normal restart path, as on main, where `runManagedRestart` sees an unchanged generation and clears the requirement. The guard is a `canRetireDeferredRestart` option on the reloader that the managed reloader answers from `sharedGatewaySessionGenerationState.required`.

Out of scope, and unchanged from main: a revert after a hot edit was applied during the deferral still restarts once, because the running snapshot then holds the hot-applied values. Batching distinct edits (#98436) is separate.

## Evidence

- New `deferred restart followed by a revert` tests in `src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts` drive the real managed reloader with its watcher and write listener (8 cases: revert by config write, revert by file edit, revert to a different config, writer restart intent, a second restart-required edit, a hot edit during the deferral, a new edit after a retired revert, and an auth mode change that reverts during the deferral). On the test commit 50c219cf955: 2 failed, 5 passed (both exact-revert cases still owe a restart). On the fix 84d63e3b783: 7 passed. The auth case was red on 6701e77d283 (the revert retired the restart and the restored token stayed rejected) and passes on 077cca214c7.
- Test time for `pnpm test src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, vitest `Duration` over 3 local runs each (the first run of each set is a cold transform cache): base 0e17a464f0d, 119 tests, 26.71 s / 14.42 s / 14.30 s. Head 077cca214c7, 127 tests, 27.27 s / 14.63 s / 14.56 s. About 0.2 s added warm. In CI on 077cca214c7, `checks-node-changed` took 2m49s; there is no base-commit CI run of this file to compare.
- `pnpm test` on every `src/gateway/config-reload*.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server-reload*.test.ts` file: 24 files, 476/476 pass.
- `oxfmt --check` and `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` are clean on the 3 changed files, `git diff --check` is clean, and `pnpm tsgo:core` plus `tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json` exit 0.
- The repo's `autoreview` skill (Codex, branch mode) reported no actionable findings.

### Real behavior proof (live Gateway, before and after)

The agent ran the Gateway from source (`node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --port 18960`) in a scratch HOME on Node 26.8.2 with `logging.level: "debug"` and no real credentials. A local OpenAI-compatible mock model answers any turn containing `SLOWTURN` after 40 s, which keeps work active. The script, the same on both commits:

1. Send `SLOWTURN` through `openclaw gateway call chat.send` on `agent:main:main`.
2. Copy `openclaw.json` byte for byte, then write it with `gateway.port` set to 18962. Wait for the deferral line.
3. After 2 s, copy the original back (`cmp` confirms it is byte-identical).
4. Wait for the slow turn to finish, then 15 s more.

Before (base 9fe692d3e29). The revert plans a second restart, which fires after the drain:

```
10:41:21.368 [reload] config change requires gateway restart (gateway.port) — deferring until 2 operation(s), 1 reply(ies), 1 embedded run(s), ...
10:41:24.486 [reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (gateway.port)
10:41:24.499 [reload] config change requires gateway restart (gateway.port) — deferring until ...
10:42:00.869 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting
10:42:00.870 [reload] all operations and replies completed; restarting gateway now
10:42:03.763 [gateway] ready
```

After (fix 84d63e3b783). The revert retires the debt, and no restart follows:

```
11:05:57.786 [reload] config change requires gateway restart (gateway.port) — deferring until 2 operation(s), 1 reply(ies), 1 embedded run(s), ...
11:06:00.858 [reload] config matches the running Gateway; deferred config restart not required
(no SIGUSR2, no restart line, and no second ready line through 15 s after the slow turn finished)
chat.history tail: user: SLOWTURN proof final1 / assistant: chat turn finished normally
```

The base result held on 2 of 2 runs. The fix result held on 3 of 3 runs (two with the comparison applied to the working tree, one on the final head). In every run the Gateway kept listening on 18960, nothing listened on 18962, and the slow turn finished.

What this run did not cover: a supervised restart (launchd or systemd), a deferral timeout or forced restart, and a revert of auth-changing paths. The unit tests cover the remaining negative cases, including the auth-mode revert, which keeps the restart.

Rebased 2026-10-17 onto main 437db07c97f (head e1600f9). Main's #174112 inlined `prepareRestart` into a direct `opts.onRestart(...)` call, so the runtime baseline line now sits just before that call. The commit ids and counts above are from the old head. Commits now: c372247 tests, cc2d181 fix, 0f910c1 auth test, e1600f9 auth fix. An earlier rebase onto 4b791ee33e0 (head ff16e45) had 4 failing CI tests in `server.sessions.create.dispatch.test.ts` and `server-methods/agent.test.ts`. This PR does not touch those files. Main fixed them in 88d32ca6e63, so this rebase picks that fix up. On e1600f9, the config-reload and server-reload test files pass 229/229. `server-reload-handlers.test.ts`, `server.sessions.create.dispatch.test.ts` and `server-methods/agent.test.ts` pass 540/540. The live Gateway proof above ran on the old commits.

AI disclosure: an AI agent (Claude Code) reproduced the bug with the failing tests, wrote the fix, and ran the checks above: `pnpm test` on the new tests on the test commit and on the fix, `pnpm test` on the reload test files, `oxfmt --check`, `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `git diff --check`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs`, the timing runs above, and the repo's `autoreview`. It also ran the live Gateway proof above against a local mock model, on the base commit and on the fix.

prs.title: fix(meeting): give the pulse capture source its own name
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Linux with **PulseAudio**, `openclaw teamsmeetings setup` always fails exactly one check:

```json
{ "id": "chrome-local-audio-device", "ok": false,
  "message": "OpenClaw PipeWire-Pulse sink or monitor source was not created." }
```

even though both modules load successfully.

Root cause: PulseAudio keeps **one name registry shared by sinks and sources**. `module-remap-source source_name=openclaw_meeting_audio` cannot take the sink's name, so PulseAudio creates the source as `openclaw_meeting_audio.2`; `ensureMeetingAudioBackend()` then lists sources and requires the **exact** name, never finds it, and throws. PipeWire's pulse server tolerates the sink/source name collision, which is why this only bites PulseAudio (WSLg, plain pulseaudio on Linux desktops).

Fix: the capture source gets its own name, `openclaw_meeting_audio_in`. The sink name, the human-facing device label (`device.description` = "OpenClaw Meeting Audio") and the `parec`/`pacat` command shape are unchanged; the capture device derives from the same constant, so there is still one place to change.

## Evidence

Reproduced on WSL2 (PulseAudio via WSLg) with a controlled pair:

- `module-null-sink sink_name=zz_ns_test` + `module-remap-source source_name=zz_ns_test` (same name) → `pactl list short sources` shows `zz_ns_test.2`; the exact name never appears.
- The host had left `openclaw_meeting_audio.2`, `.3` and `.4` behind from three earlier setup attempts — the same signature.

After the change:

- the source is created as exactly `openclaw_meeting_audio_in`;
- `parec --device=openclaw_meeting_audio_in --raw --format=s16le --rate=24000 --channels=1` captured 43 KB in 3 s;
- `pacat --playback --device=openclaw_meeting_audio` played cleanly (both exits were only the 3 s test timeout).

Tests: the new `uses distinct pulse device names for capture and playback` fails on the old constant (both commands pointed at `--device=openclaw_meeting_audio`) and passes with the fix; the `configured-node-host.test.ts` fixtures are updated for the new source name. `oxfmt@0.72.0` applied.

Not run locally: `vitest` — this working copy is a sparse `blob:none` clone with no `node_modules`, so CI is the gate.


## Real behaviour proof (shipped entry point, 2026-10-17)

Box: WSL2 (`6.18.54.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2`), PulseAudio via WSLg — the same machine that hit the failure.

### 1. After the change: `teamsmeetings setup` is green and the capture device is distinct

```
$ openclaw teamsmeetings setup --mode agent
{ "ok": true, "checks": [
    { "id": "chrome-profile",              "ok": true, "message": "Local Chrome uses the configured OpenClaw browser profile" },
    { "id": "guest-join",                  "ok": true, "message": "Guest name, auto-join, and tab reuse are configured" },
    { "id": "captions",                    "ok": true, "message": "Caption scraping is not used by talk-back modes" },
    { "id": "audio-bridge",                "ok": true, "message": "Command-pair audio bridge configured (pcm16-24khz)" },
    { "id": "chrome-local-audio-device",   "ok": true, "message": "Virtual meeting audio backend is ready" },
    { "id": "chrome-local-audio-commands", "ok": true, "message": "Configured Chrome audio commands are available" } ] }

$ pactl list short sources | grep openclaw
3  openclaw_meeting_audio.monitor  module-null-sink.c     s16le 2ch 48000Hz  SUSPENDED
5  openclaw_meeting_audio_in       module-remap-source.c  s16le 2ch 48000Hz  IDLE
$ pactl list short sinks | grep openclaw
2  openclaw_meeting_audio          module-null-sink.c     s16le 2ch 48000Hz  IDLE
```

Before this change the same check reported `✗ Virtual meeting audio backend not ready` on this host, with `openclaw_meeting_audio.2/.3/.4` left behind by earlier attempts.

### 2. The collision, reproduced with the exact `pactl` call the pre-fix backend makes

Same box, sink already holding the name:

```
$ pactl load-module module-remap-source master=openclaw_meeting_audio.monitor \
      source_name=openclaw_meeting_audio rate=48000 channels=2 remix=no
25
$ pactl list short sources | grep openclaw
3  openclaw_meeting_audio.monitor  module-null-sink.c     s16le 2ch 48000Hz  RUNNING
5  openclaw_meeting_audio_in       module-remap-source.c  s16le 2ch 48000Hz  SUSPENDED
6  openclaw_meeting_audio.2       module-remap-source.c  s16le 2ch 48000Hz  IDLE

exact-name matches for "openclaw_meeting_audio" among sources: 0
what PulseAudio actually created:                            openclaw_meeting_audio.2
```

That is precisely the predicate `pulseListContains(PIPEWIRE_SOURCE_NAME)` evaluates after module loading — so it fails, and the module was in fact created successfully. (Module 25 unloaded immediately afterwards.)

### 3. Re-running over an existing install keeps devices and settings (the upgrade case)

```
before: 1 remap source, guestName="Juno (OpenClaw notes)"
$ openclaw teamsmeetings setup --mode agent      # devices + settings already present
  ... 6 checks, "ok": true, "ok": true (overall)
after:  1 remap source                            # no duplicate module, nothing orphaned
```

### Scope of this proof

The `teamsmeetings setup` checks execute inside the running OpenClaw service, so the transcript in §1 comes from a build with exactly this one-line change applied to the installed bundle — I cannot show a pre-fix CLI transcript without restarting that service onto an unpatched build, so §2 gives the pre-fix side as the raw `pactl` reproduction plus the exact-name predicate instead of a fabricated failure transcript.

### On the added test

The existing raw-command-pair test asserts each command against the same two constants, so it would still pass if both constants were collapsed back into one shared name — the failure mode this PR fixes. The added test asserts the invariant directly (capture name ≠ playback name) and is the only guard on it.

### 4. Upgrade from a pre-fix install with legacy devices present

A 2026.10.4 install leaves the colliding remap sources behind (`openclaw_meeting_audio.2`, `.3`). Reproduced exactly, on the same host, with the same `pactl` call the pre-fix backend makes; then the fixed setup was run on top:

```
# legacy state left by the pre-fix build
$ pactl list short sources | grep openclaw
3  openclaw_meeting_audio.monitor  module-null-sink.c     s16le 2ch 48000Hz  RUNNING
5  openclaw_meeting_audio_in       module-remap-source.c  s16le 2ch 48000Hz  SUSPENDED
7  openclaw_meeting_audio.2       module-remap-source.c  s16le 2ch 48000Hz  IDLE
8  openclaw_meeting_audio.3       module-remap-source.c  s16le 2ch 48000Hz  IDLE
settings before: guestName="Juno (OpenClaw notes)", defaultMode=transcribe

$ openclaw teamsmeetings setup --mode agent          # the upgrade
  chrome-local-audio-device   ok: true  "Virtual meeting audio backend is ready"
  chrome-local-audio-commands ok: true  "Configured Chrome audio commands are available"
  ... all six checks ok: true, overall ok: true

$ pactl list short sources | grep openclaw           # legacy devices untouched
3  openclaw_meeting_audio.monitor  module-null-sink.c     s16le 2ch 48000Hz  SUSPENDED
5  openclaw_meeting_audio_in       module-remap-source.c  s16le 2ch 48000Hz  SUSPENDED
7  openclaw_meeting_audio.2       module-remap-source.c  s16le 2ch 48000Hz  SUSPENDED
8  openclaw_meeting_audio.3       module-remap-source.c  s16le 2ch 48000Hz  SUSPENDED
settings after:  guestName="Juno (OpenClaw notes)", defaultMode=transcribe
```

(The simulated legacy devices were unloaded after the run; the real `openclaw_meeting_audio_in` source was already present from the patched build.) Installing 2026.10.4 to run the pre-fix binary would have swapped the live gateway on this host, so the legacy device state is the one thing simulated rather than installed.

**On the changing capture device name.** The default generated command pair now points at `openclaw_meeting_audio_in`; the human-facing label (`device.description` = "OpenClaw Meeting Audio"), the sink name and the `parec`/`pacat` shape are unchanged. Anyone who set explicit `chrome.audio.commands` keeps them — explicit commands win over the defaults — so only installs using the generated defaults are affected, and those are exactly the installs that were broken.
