prs.title: fix(acp): treat missing cwd as stale bound session
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: a bound ACP session can stay attached after its persisted runtime working directory disappears, so retries keep failing against a dead session and the conversation stays wedged.
- Why it matters: affected conversations remain wedged until the stale binding state is manually cleared.
- What changed: during ACP dispatch, treat a generic `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED` as stale when the bound session's persisted `runtimeOptions.cwd` can no longer be resolved on disk (`ENOENT`/`ENOTDIR`), then unbind the dead conversation. The signal is folded into the existing `isStaleSessionInitError` classifier and the existing `maybeUnbindStaleBoundConversations` dispatch helper — no new module, no parallel helper.
- Scope: dispatch-only. Two files: `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts` and its test.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- ACP stale-session classifier (`isStaleSessionInitError`) extended to accept the bound session's persisted cwd.
- Auto-reply ACP dispatch stale-binding cleanup (`maybeUnbindStaleBoundConversations`) passes the persisted cwd at the `runTurn` catch.
- Regression tests: generic `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED` + missing persisted cwd unbinds; generic init failure + existing cwd does not.

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #60720
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause

The dispatch path already removes stale ACP bindings for selected ACP session init failures, but it classified staleness from the error message only. The live missing-cwd case surfaces as a generic spawn `ENOENT` wrapped as `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED`, whose message does not match the stale-message set. The reliable signal is the bound session's persisted `runtimeOptions.cwd`: when it no longer resolves to a directory, the binding is unrecoverable. Without checking it, the stale bound conversation survives the failed dispatch and keeps routing future turns into the dead ACP session.

## Implementation Notes

- Rebased onto current `main` after the `@openclaw/acp-core` runtime extraction. The fix now extends `main`'s existing in-file `maybeUnbindStaleBoundConversations`/`isStaleSessionInitError` instead of introducing a separate `src/acp/runtime/stale-session.ts` helper (which no longer fits the post-extraction layout). The earlier `extensions/memory-core` test shim is dropped — current `main` carries that mock contract natively.
- Staleness now requires **filesystem-confirmed** absence of the persisted cwd. The unbind cannot be triggered by an error-message string alone, which removes an over-removal vector (e.g. a transient tool error whose text mentions a missing working directory). `ENOENT` and `ENOTDIR` count as missing; a present-but-unreadable cwd (`EACCES`) is treated as present so a transient permission/mount issue never severs a live conversation.

## Maintainer Decision (session-state semantics)

This removes persisted bound-conversation state when a generic `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED` is paired with a filesystem-confirmed missing cwd — the recovery is correct for a permanently gone cwd, but it is session-state behavior worth explicit maintainer acceptance (per ClawSweeper's `merge-risk: session-state`). Two residual, deliberately out-of-scope behaviors to weigh:

- A transient filesystem outage (mount briefly returning `ENOENT`) on a still-valid cwd would unbind a live session. Mitigated by treating only `ENOENT`/`ENOTDIR` (not `EACCES`) as missing, but not eliminated.
- `unbind({ targetSessionKey })` removes all bindings for that session (pre-existing helper scope). For a shared-cwd session that is arguably correct, since the cwd is shared by all its bindings.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: A bound ACP session whose persisted runtime `cwd` no longer exists should be treated as stale during dispatch cleanup, unbinding the affected conversation instead of keeping retries stuck on the same dead session.
- Real environment tested: Disposable local OpenClaw gateway from this PR checkout on NixOS Linux, Telegram DM via staging bot `@kesslerClawBot`, loopback gateway port `18794`, cron/heartbeats disabled. Gateway was stopped after the proof run.

prs.title: fix(gateway): finish config save responses before restart
prs.body:
Fixes #120408.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a restart-required `config.patch` or `config.apply` can lose its success response when restart emission overtakes the save acknowledgement.

## User Impact

Managed configuration saves acknowledge restart admission and finish their response before restart emission. Authorization revocation remains immediate, while an already accepted writer can finish its response before its socket closes.

No public configuration, protocol, plugin SDK, database schema, or serialized-state format changes; no migration or operator action is required. `config.set` remains persistence-only, and reload-off direct scheduling is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dispatcher owns response completion; its existing private config-write receipt carries that completion promise to the restart coordinator. Pending responses survive watcher echoes and newer writes. Shutdown releases waiting work without emitting a stale restart. This retains the restart-ordering remainder excluded from #129321.

Rebased onto `75b463e1c83f0b26034290e4ccae5ccd1e30c71a`, preserving current upstream auth and model-publication fixtures. Restart regression tests now advance monotonic deadlines while retaining real wall time shared with SQLite workers. Polling settings and shared test fixtures were moved into focused existing owners to satisfy current file-size gates.

## Evidence

Validated head: `29fc81928dfd67c24e89cb4fb621762b1c1a6b04`.

- **849 final-source tests passed** across reload handlers, config reloading, shared-auth rotation, and model publication. The forced-restart scenarios cover direct writes, watcher echoes, newer responses finishing first, and shutdown.
- Real Gateway loopback WebSocket tests passed for both `config.patch` and `config.apply`: restart admission, success response, auth close, and restart-emitter completion occur in the expected order. The injected emitter does not relaunch an OS process.
- **All selected `check-changed` gates passed**, including production and full test typechecks, formatting, file-size ratchets, contract guards, dead-export scans, storage/schema checks, and import-cycle checks. Type-aware lint: zero warnings/errors across 17 changed files.
- Independent P0-P2 autoreview found no actionable issues. A separate extraction review verified the moved bodies and preserved assertions. Registry contracts and the other config/dispatcher suites also passed during the refresh.

The earlier stored-data review flag does not apply: response settlement is process-local and attached through a private WeakMap. The earlier restricted-test-path concern was checked against current CODEOWNERS, which does not assign the touched paths. No owner approval is claimed; GitHub's required `openclaw/ci-gate` remains authoritative for this head.

Production delta: +91/-31 (net +60, including mechanical moves/imports); tests/support: +404/-102 (net +302). Functional production growth connects the existing lifecycle owners and retains response obligations through supersession and shutdown.
### CI follow-up: archive reclamation admission fixture

CI job [checks-node-compact-large-27](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35522519709/job/106109154820) failed the unchanged cold-drain revocation case in src/config/sessions/session-history-archive-pruning.admission.test.ts:531. The entire file passed six consecutive local runs (108 test executions; 18 tests per run). Source inspection found that the fixture infers its drain boundary from a separate setImmediate, while the maintenance owner intentionally permits early completion on checkpoint contention or no progress. The actual CI cause is unconfirmed: follow up by capturing completion, checkpointIncomplete, vacuumPasses, and childChecks if it recurs. No production change, assertion weakening, or timeout increase was made. The failed-job rerun request was rejected by GitHub with HTTP 403 ("Must have admin rights to Repository"). A repository maintainer must rerun job 106109154820; no rerun was started.

prs.title: feat(googlechat): add sessionThread option to bind OpenClaw sessions to Google Chat threads
prs.body: AI-assisted: yes (Claude Opus 4.7). ## Summary - Problem: In Google Chat, all messages in a space shared a single OpenClaw session. Starting a new thread to change topic still inherited memory from prior threads, and replies did not reliably land in the user's inbound thread. - Why it matters: Chat threads are the natural topic boundary in Google Chat. Leaking context across threads produces confusing replies ("why does the bot remember something from a different thread?"), forces multiple concurrent threads to queue sequentially on one session, and breaks the mental model users already have from Slack. Requested in #13373. - What changed: Added an opt-in `sessionThread` channel option. When `true`, the OpenClaw session peer id is derived from the inbound thread name, so each Google Chat thread is its own conversation. Replies are now threaded via `thread.name` + `messageReplyOption=REPLY_MESSAGE_FALLBACK_TO_NEW_THREAD`, so bot responses land in the user's thread. - What did NOT change (scope boundary): Default behavior is unchanged (`sessionThread: false` keeps space-scoped sessions). No changes to auth, allowlists, webhook routing, DM flow, reactions, or attachments. No slash commands / `/focus`-style bindings added (see "future work" below). ## Change Type (select all) - [x] Bug fix - [x] Feature - [ ] Refactor required for the fix - [x] Docs - [ ] Security hardening - [ ] Chore/infra ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [ ] Gateway / orchestration - [ ] Skills / tool execution - [ ] Auth / tokens - [ ] Memory / storage - [x] Integrations - [ ] API / contracts - [ ] UI / DX - [ ] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue/PR - Closes #13373 (per-thread session mode feature request) - Closes #41788 (Google Chat replies creating new threads instead of staying in the existing one) - Related #44347 — resolves the first of the two requests in that issue - [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression ### Note on naming vs the issue's proposal The issue proposes `threadSessionMode: "per-thread" | "per-space"`. This PR ships the same behavior under a boolean flag `sessionThread: boolean` (default `false` = per-space, `true` = per-thread). Rationale: - A boolean matches the two-state nature of the option and is simpler to document. - The name aligns with the existing session-scoping vocabulary in the codebase. - Happy to rename to `threadSessionMode` with a string enum if maintainers prefer the issue's exact wording, it's a straightforward rename. ## Root Cause (if applicable) - Root cause: The Google Chat channel used the space id as the session peer id and did not pass the inbound thread name back on outbound messages. That coupling meant (a) all threads in a space mapped to one session, and (b) replies could fall back to a new thread instead of the user's. - Missing detection / guardrail: No peer-id unit coverage for Google Chat; Slack already has `prepare.thread-session-key.test.ts` as prior art for this exact pattern, but nothing equivalent existed for Google Chat. - Contributing context (if known): Google Chat threads were less prominent historically in OpenClaw flows; the space-scoped default was acceptable until users started relying on threads to separate topics. ## Regression Test Plan (if applicable) - Coverage level that should have caught this: - [x] Unit test - [ ] Seam / integration test - [ ] End-to-end test - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient - Target test or file: `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.session-thread.test.ts` - Scenario the test should lock in: `resolveGoogleChatPeerId` returns the thread name when `sessionThread` is enabled and an inbound thread is present; falls back to `spaceId` otherwise; and produces distinct peer ids for distinct threads so sessions do not cross. - Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: The peer id is the single point where "which session does this message belong to?" is decided for Google Chat. Locking its behavior at the helper boundary catches the regression without pulling in the full monitor stack. - Existing test that already covers this (if any): None for Google Chat. Slack's `prepare.thread-session-key.test.ts` covers the analogous primitive. ## User-visible / Behavior Changes - New opt-in config: `channels.googlechat.sessionThread` (default `false`). - `false` (default): space-scoped sessions, prior behavior unchanged. - `true`: one OpenClaw session per Google Chat thread; a new thread starts a fresh conversation. - Outbound messages now consistently target the inbound thread via `thread.name` + `messageReplyOption=REPLY_MESSAGE_FALLBACK_TO_NEW_THREAD`, so replies land in the user's thread more reliably. This applies regardless of `sessionThread`. ## Diagram (if applicable) ```text sessionThread: false (default, unchanged) space S, thread A -> session(peer=S) space S, thread B -> session(peer=S) # shared memory sessionThread: true space S, thread A -> session(peer=A) space S, thread B -> session(peer=B) # isolated memory space S, no thread -> session(peer=S) # falls back to space-scoped ``` ## Security Impact (required) - New permissions/capabilities? No - Secrets/tokens handling changed? No - New/changed network calls? No (same Chat API endpoints; only request payload now sets `thread.name` and `messageReplyOption`) - Command/tool execution surface changed? No - Data access scope changed? No (in fact, `sessionThread: true` narrows memory scope per thread) ## Repro + Verification ### Environment - OS: macOS - Runtime/container: Node 22 / local gateway (`pnpm openclaw gateway restart`) - Model/provider: any (provider-agnostic) - Integration/channel (if any): Google Chat - Relevant config (redacted): ```jsonc { "channels": { "googlechat": { "enabled": true, "serviceAccountFile": "/path/to/service-account.json", "sessionThread": true } } } ``` ### Steps 1. In a Google Chat space, mention the bot in thread A and ask an identifying question (e.g. "remember the color red"). 2. Start a new thread B in the same space and ask "what color did I mention?". 3. Reply again inside thread A and ask the same question. ### Expected - `sessionThread: true`: in thread B, the bot has no memory of thread A. In thread A, the bot still remembers "red". Replies land in the thread the user messaged in. - `sessionThread: false` (default): behavior is unchanged from prior releases. ### Actual - Matches expected for both modes. ## Evidence - [x] Failing test/log before + passing after ``` pnpm test extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.session-thread.test.ts ✓ resolveGoogleChatPeerId returns spaceId when sessionThread is disabled ✓ resolveGoogleChatPeerId returns spaceId when sessionThread is undefined (default) ✓ resolveGoogleChatPeerId returns thread name when sessionThread is enabled and inbound has a thread ✓ resolveGoogleChatPeerId falls back to spaceId when sessionThread is enabled but inbound has no thread ✓ resolveGoogleChatPeerId produces distinct peer ids for distinct threads so sessions don't cross Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 5 passed (5) ``` - [ ] Trace/log snippets - [x] Screenshot/recording - When disabled(previous behavior): - When enabled: - [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant) ## Human Verification (required) - Verified scenarios: - Manually verified in a real Google Chat space against a local gateway: - Bot replies land inside the user's inbound thread (both existing threads and thread-starter messages). - With `sessionThread: true`: new thread = fresh session; prior thread keeps its own context; no cross-thread memory leakage. - With `sessionThread: false`: unchanged, space-scoped memory. - Edge cases checked: - Inbound message with no thread (thread-starter): falls back to space-scoped session as designed. - Two concurrent threads in the same space maintain separate sessions. - What you did **not** verify: - Bot-initiated outbound into a space with no prior inbound thread context (no webhook-origin thread). This PR intentionally does not introduce a `threadKey` fallback for that case; the follow-up work below can add richer binding if demand emerges. - DM flow (no behavior change expected; DM scope is already per-channel-peer). ## Review Conversations - [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR. - [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment. ## Compatibility / Migration - Backward compatible? Yes - Config/env changes? Yes, additive only: new optional `channels.googlechat.sessionThread` boolean (default `false`). - Migration needed? No. Existing configs continue to behave as before. - If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A. To opt in, set `channels.googlechat.sessionThread: true`. ## Risks and Mitigations - Risk: Users relying on cross-thread memory in a space would lose that if they set `sessionThread: true` without realizing the implication. - Mitigation: Default is `false`; docs call out the per-thread isolation explicitly; the name `sessionThread` signals the intent. - Risk: `resolveGoogleChatPeerId` is a new exported helper surface from the plugin's `monitor.ts`. - Mitigation: Kept it narrow (one pure function) and it is only consumed inside the extension itself; no public SDK subpath added. ## Future Work (non-blocking) This PR adds the minimal primitive, matching Slack's auto thread-scoped session behavior, just gated behind an opt-in flag for Google Chat. A follow-up could align with the Telegram/Discord `session.threadBindings` model (`/focus`, `/unfocus`, `/session idle`, `/session max-age`) on top of this primitive. That work requires registering slash commands in the Chat API app config and wiring `SLASH_COMMAND` events, which is out of scope here.

prs.title: perf(sessions): reduce PostgreSQL turn preparation reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL sessions reread four sets of facts during every warmed turn even when the session worker already owns their committed state.

## User Impact

Eligible PostgreSQL turn preparation uses one SQL read instead of five, with the same worker request and no main-thread database access. Session selection, pending-input custody, transcript versions, and retry behavior are preserved. No configuration or schema changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the PostgreSQL-only exclusion from the existing resident-state path. Scoped write receipts already work on both engines, and actor postimages are pinned to their commit receipt. Reuse still requires the retained token to match the current token for the session key and dependency session IDs, plus the exact expected entry/window and a warm transcript. This introduces no query, cache, generation, or alternate owner.

Canonical idempotency lookup remains necessary because the actor's 512-event window cannot prove absence. Custody and write authorization remain with their owners; cold, evicted, reset, moved, and incomplete state retains canonical preparation.

The four removed warm rereads have the same accepted edge case under Gateway single-writer ownership:

- Window/key selection: a writer bypassing Gateway ownership or exclusive offline custody would not publish invalidation.
- Exact entry/lifecycle facts: unsupported external writes could leave retained facts stale until admission or invalidation.
- Transcript version/cold-state facts: unsupported external writes are outside the receipt contract; normal writes invalidate or publish their postimage.
- Pending-input facts: unsupported external writes are outside the receipt contract; live custody still gates consumption.

## Evidence

The shared PostgreSQL regression fails on the unchanged implementation with `expected 5 to be 1`. All nine cases pass on both PostgreSQL and SQLite using the same suite for committed facts and custody rejection, rollback, in-process entry/transcript writes, reset/key movement, eviction/restart fallback, committed transcript versions, and idempotent retries before and after the retained 512-event window.

| Measurement | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PostgreSQL warm prepare SQL | 5 | 1 (focused regression; full census pending) |
| PostgreSQL prepare worker requests | 1 | 1 (dispatch unchanged; census pending) |
| SQLite warmed causal SQL, median [range] | 57 [57–59] | 57 [57–59] |
| SQLite warmed causal requests, median [range] | 16 [16–18] | 16 [16–18] |
| SQLite warmed raw SQL, median [range] | 57.5 [57–61] | 57.5 [57–80] |
| SQLite warmed raw requests, median [range] | 16 [16–20] | 16 [16–24] |
| Warm MAIN SQL | 0 | 0 |
| T1 call sites in changed owner | 0 | 0 |

One independent Codex review is clean through P2. Changed-file type-aware lint, format, and diff checks pass. Canonical Knip adds zero findings: the same 11 production and 18 full-tree findings reproduce on the base and candidate, with identical runtime/configuration; these inherited findings are routed for cleanup. The full SQLite v3 pair passes, including restart. Normalized causal SQL and request-stack fingerprints match exactly. Exact-entry reads, actor hydration, entry-cache snapshot loads, row-fact reads, and watermark reads remain zero per warm turn. The raw-window tail differs because background lease/config maintenance overlapped candidate turns; turn-attributed SQL and requests are identical. The PostgreSQL owner approved the exact head; the full PostgreSQL census remains pending. CI production/test types, selected lint, source contracts, architecture and database ratchets pass. PostgreSQL shards 1 and 3 pass, including the new resident-state suite. Shard 2 and the aggregate gate fail as described below. No latency claim is made on the shared host. Production is net −2 lines; the conformance runner gains one target; shared test coverage is net +112 lines. No SDK or update/Doctor/migration/lifecycle changes: those specialized cells do not apply.

### PostgreSQL CI disposition and approved landing exception

[Candidate CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39071675403) has two 120-second timeouts: Doctor migration v27 with foreign writes enabled, and update preflight retaining agent/local-credential recovery. The subsequent Doctor v30/false maintenance-owner failure is a cascade. The PostgreSQL owner classifies the timeouts as capacity/near-budget fragility owned by the PostgreSQL conformance suite and approves landing this exact head through the admin exception.

On [scheduled main run 39071119824](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39071119824), the three cases passed in 85.1 s / 103.4 s / 93.9 s against the 120 s budget. Focused local runs passed 3/3 on both the exact base `d6a7e3d211ec40935cb702c00611a320e32c307c` and candidate `aa0e113bc5558acd37100dd74ec48a2b086d4fc7`. This PR touches no Doctor or updater code.

The new test file's default 30 s weight reshuffled the PG2 cohort from 19 to 28 infra files. The PostgreSQL owner is refreshing `config/postgres-conformance-timings.json`. The test file stays in place and timeouts remain unchanged. No CI rerun was requested, and the failed CI run is not claimed green or fixed.

prs.title: fix: recover Responses streams stalled on bookkeeping events
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Responses requests remaining busy indefinitely when the transport keeps sending bookkeeping events, empty reasoning deltas, or repeated snapshots without advancing model output.

## User Impact

Nonproductive requests reach the existing timeout/recovery path. Nonempty hidden reasoning remains progress even when chat shows no new text. Streams without request-activity notifications keep their existing yielded-output fallback. No migration or new configuration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Responses currently reports every wire event as progress. The reducer now distinguishes physical activity from model progress, using existing output trackers. The watchdog also preserves that producer classification when an active caller consumes assistant events; empty emitted events cannot overwrite it. Canonical identity validation retains its original ordering, including active tool-call index rejection. Transcript and assistant event contents are unchanged.

Related: #165983 (separate progress deadline), #140335 (parked-consumer liveness), #152705 (SSE comments as physical activity).

## Evidence

On the previous PR revision, both the native wrapper chain and an actively consuming real HTTP/SDK client reproduce the empty-reasoning and repeated-snapshot failures. Each has passing bookkeeping and hidden-reasoning controls. With the repair, 98 focused cases pass, including existing identity rejection coverage, structural streams without notifications, and actual transport recovery. Production types, owning test types, scoped lint, formatting, and fresh independent review through P2 pass.

The retained real-time behavior trace (production source identical to this revision) uses a real isolated loopback HTTP server, Node fetch, OpenAI SDK Responses client, shared reducer, composed run-signal relay, canonical watchdog, and real timers. Only the wire frames are scripted. A real SDK warmup request separates lazy initialization from the measured progress deadline. Idle/progress budgets are 1000/2000ms; frames arrive every 200ms. After each scenario, a second watched request completes. The recorded output is:

```jsonl
{"proof":"real Responses HTTP transport","activity":"bookkeeping","consumer":"active","injectedFrames":10,"outcome":"expired: no model progress","recovery":"second request completed","elapsedMs":2106}
{"proof":"real Responses HTTP transport","activity":"empty reasoning","consumer":"active","injectedFrames":10,"outcome":"expired: no model progress","recovery":"second request completed","elapsedMs":2046}
{"proof":"real Responses HTTP transport","activity":"repeated snapshot","consumer":"active","injectedFrames":11,"outcome":"expired: no model progress","recovery":"second request completed","elapsedMs":2247}
{"proof":"real Responses HTTP transport","activity":"hidden reasoning","consumer":"active","injectedFrames":16,"outcome":"completed without timeout","recovery":"second request completed","elapsedMs":3311}
```

This proves the transport boundary and subsequent-request recovery; it does not claim an external provider was contacted, full Gateway automatic failover was exercised, or that these events caused a particular live incident. This consumer-path revision has not been activated in the operator Gateway. All fixtures and exported output are synthetic; no real messages, logs, credentials, endpoints, or incident identifiers are included.

### Controlled-clock regression

The committed regression retains the real HTTP/fetch/OpenAI SDK/Responses reducer and watchdog, with claimed ports and body-receipt barriers. Only the watchdog clock is advanced: no real timer intervals, sleeps, or polling. The first completed snapshot establishes progress; unchanged repeats must not extend that deadline. prs.title: fix: failed turns lose their "ended before a reply" notice when another session is mid-turn
prs.body:
Related: #150372

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users whose turn fails before any reply would see the turn
marked failed but get no explanation in the conversation, when the failure is
handled while another session's agent turn is still running.

The affected surface is durable conversation history: the "This turn ended
before a reply: ..." notice that normally explains a failed turn. On an affected
run the session status still becomes `failed`, but the transcript has no notice,
so the conversation simply stops with no visible reason. The Gateway logs
`terminal session persistence failed ... SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError`.

Observed on 2026.9.4 on a subagent session whose run failed after provider
context-overflow recovery was exhausted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway's definitive lifecycle write now runs detached from any inherited
owned-transcript write context, which is what every comparable detached Gateway
and registry path already does (`update-run-notice.runtime.ts`,
`session-event-wake.ts`, `subagent-registry-run-wait.ts`,
`sessions-send-tool.ts`, and the explicit `else` branch in
`session-prompt-state.ts`).

Cause: agent events dispatch synchronously through `notifyListeners`, so the
Gateway handler executes in the emitter's async context and inherits that
attempt's writer context. Inside `withCurrentTranscript`,
`withOwnedSessionTranscriptWriterFence` spreads the inherited fence last, so it
replaces the `sessionId` and `expectedLifecycleRevision` that
`persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent` had just read from its committed status
write, and adds an `expectedWriterRunId` the Gateway never supplied. That last
part is what makes the failure loud: without a writer id a fence mismatch
returns `err(refusal)`, but with one `withCurrentTranscript` throws. The status
write is awaited first and had already committed, which is why the session shows
`failed` with no notice.

Non-goal: this does not change the ownership guard itself. It changes only which
context the Gateway's own write is validated against. `chat-send-dispatch-errors.ts`
still calls `persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent` directly, outside this owner
seam; that path is guarded by `if (!hasActiveRun)` and is left alone here.

## User Impact

A failed turn keeps its durable explanation even when the failure is processed
while another session's turn is running. Operators reading a session after the
fact see why it stopped instead of a silent gap, and the spurious
`SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError` no longer appears for writes whose
owner never actually changed.

## Validation

`src/gateway/session-lifecycle-terminal-write-detach.test.ts` (new, 9 tests),
verified against `main` at `cea9c9cb7695e8817ca72d7fcc2884d031e5ff30`.

With the source change reverted, the 6 inheritance tests fail with the exact
production error, `SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError: session writer
claim changed before transcript persistence`; the 3 ownership-protection tests
pass both before and after, so they are not vacuous.

Coverage: ordinary failed run; same-session compaction followed by failure under
an unchanged owner; duplicate suppression when the run already has a durable
assistant error; repeated terminal events; a delayed retained callback that
reinstalls a settled context; the non-definitive `persist()` fallback; and three
cases that must stay rejected (cross-session report, replaced session, expired
run authority).

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/gateway/session-lifecycle-terminal-write-detach.test.ts \
  src/gateway/session-lifecycle-run-failure.test.ts \
  src/gateway/session-lifecycle-persistence-owner.test.ts
  -> 43 passed  (6 fail without the source change)

pnpm tsgo:core                      -> exit 0
oxlint --type-aware (changed files) -> exit 0
oxfmt --check       (changed files) -> exit 0
```

The 21 pre-existing tests in `session-lifecycle-run-failure.test.ts` are
unmodified and still pass. CLI-history behaviour is unchanged: the detach happens
before `writeContext.run`, which still re-establishes the CLI history writer, and
the five existing CLI-history-through-terminal-persistence tests still pass.

The incident that prompted this was observed on the 2026.9.4 release build; the
affected file is byte-identical there and on `main`, and all figures above are
from `main`.

prs.title: fix(memory): prevent duplicate Gemini batch jobs after timeouts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gemini native embedding-batch creation is non-idempotent. If a create response is lost or times out after the provider accepted it, an immediate retry can create a second paid remote job. The provider assigns the batch name only in the response and does not expose a caller-supplied idempotency key.

- https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/batch-api#best-practices
- https://ai.google.dev/api/batch-api#method:-models.asyncbatchembedcontent

## What Changed

This version treats batch submission as a crash-recoverable ownership protocol:

- Memory Core persists an exclusive reservation in the published memory database before Gemini's non-idempotent create call.
- Acknowledged provider batch names are attached to that reservation as soon as they are returned.
- Each request set has a deterministic SHA-256 fingerprint; manifests retain content-independent custom IDs and chunk hashes, not source text, credentials, or vectors.
- Restarted managers adopt an acknowledged job only when its exact request fingerprint matches.
- Completed output is reconciled by stable chunk hash and published idempotently to the shared embedding cache, including when source enumeration has drifted since submission.
- Ambiguous create outcomes remain quarantined. Definitive non-ambiguous 4xx rejections (except 408) release the reservation.
- The reservation is cleared only after local cache/index publication commits.
- Closing a manager aborts local polling without cancelling or duplicating an accepted remote job.
- Gemini's native-batch failure mode remains fail-closed instead of fanning a large migration into synchronous paid requests.
- Status output exposes the submission, provider job, timestamps, and recovery state.
- Deliberate quarantine clearing requires both `--force` and `--clear-batch-quarantine`.

The ownership record lives in the published database while a shadow rebuild remains isolated. Independent managers serialize reservation changes through SQLite immediate transactions.

## User Impact

Interrupted Gemini memory migrations can resume acknowledged work without resubmitting already accepted requests. Operators get an explicit quarantine for genuinely ambiguous remote ownership instead of hidden duplicate spend or an uncontrolled synchronous fallback.

## Evidence

Exact candidate head: `ca2a3d6a9bcb7215a9dfba22f8407b06ab116206`

Candidate base at construction: `044cf2e6e027591e6361dbd2784a8b9c68959e18` (`upstream/main` at the time)

- Focused Google provider/lifecycle tests: **67/67 passed**.
- Memory integration tests: **235/235 passed**.
- Plugin contract suite: **1,117/1,117 passed**.
- Total: **1,419 tests passed**.
- Core and extension production/test TypeScript checks passed.
- Changed-file structural, dependency, formatting, documentation, SDK, and extension-boundary gates passed.
- Documentation validation passed: 1,294 MDX files, 13,239 internal links with 0 broken, and 1,224 config examples.
- Full production build passed, including 91 external plugins, 152 public SDK subpaths, CLI bootstrap, and Control UI performance gates.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- A secrets/logging audit found no credentials, request text, vectors, or authorization values added to logs.

The implementation has also been exercised against a real authenticated Gemini migration outside CI: completed jobs were reconciled, cache entries advanced, and a subsequent quota rejection occurred before a new provider job ID was assigned. Completed fingerprints were not replayed. No provider identifiers or credentials are included here.

## Scope

This PR intentionally adds no quota-size, parallelism, or retry-policy configuration. It does not alter production deployment files. Provider transport remains in the Google extension; Memory Core owns durable publication and recovery state.

## Required Before Ready/Merge

- Upstream CI must pass on this exact head.
- An independent exact-head review must complete; the author-side GCP environment does not currently have an independent Codex reviewer identity, so this is not being bypassed.
- Maintainers must approve the fail-closed ambiguity/quarantine contract and its operator-recovery tradeoff.

This PR is kept as a draft until those gates are satisfied.

prs.title: fix(prompt): unbounded channel context arrays and objects flood the model prompt
prs.body:
Related: #119213 — the review feedback there flagged this exact spot (the unbounded `sanitizeContextJsonValue` in `channel-prompt-context.ts`); this PR addresses that feedback directly.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users whose channels or plugins attach structured context to inbound messages — group directories, member lists, reply chains, or other channel-supplied payloads — would have the entire array or object serialized into the model prompt with no size limit: thousands of entries and hundreds of kilobytes in a single context block. The prompt grows far beyond what the operator expects, token spend inflates, and useful context gets crowded out of the window.

The affected surface is the user-role context blocks built on the inbound reply path (`Conversation info:`, `Reply chain of current user message:`, and one block per structured-context entry), plus the equivalent user-message boundary block in the embedded agent runner.

## Why This Change Was Made

The prompt-context sanitizer already capped every string at 2,000 chars, but it mapped arrays and objects through with no bound on entry or key counts, so one channel payload could carry unlimited repeated entries into the prompt. Two budgets now apply, each measured against the largest first-party payloads:

- **Per-block, inside the JSON sanitizer** (`channel-prompt-context.ts`): arrays cap at 20 entries and objects at 50 keys (50 leaves headroom over the largest first-party payload, the Conversation info block at ~25 keys) — these bound fan-out. On top of them, one **cumulative serialized-character budget of 50,000 chars per block** is shared across the whole recursion through a mutable counter: the per-container caps alone cannot bound the total (50 keys × 20 entries × 2,000 chars passes every per-level cap yet serializes ~2 MB). 50k is ~2.6× the largest measured first-party block (a 10-link reply chain at ~19k serialized chars, each body already at the 2,000-char string cap). Nesting is capped at **depth 8** (4× the deepest measured first-party payload, which nests 2 levels). Key text is channel-controlled too, so keys are now capped and neutralized like string values and charged to the budget. When the budget runs out, the walk stops adding siblings and appends an explicit `…[truncated: context budget exhausted]` marker; the depth cut emits `…[truncated: max depth reached]` — the serialized block stays valid, parseable JSON in every case.
- **Per-message, in the inbound context assembly** (`buildInboundUserContextPrefix` in `inbound-meta.ts`): one **cumulative budget of 150,000 chars** covers labels plus every emitted block — Conversation info, reply chain/target, forwarded, location, chat-window and one block per structured-context entry (whose count is unbounded), chat history, goal, and current-message blocks. The largest measured first-party assembly (group Conversation info + 10-link reply chain + forwarded/thread-starter blocks + 20-entry chat history) totals ~43k chars, so 150k leaves ~3.5× headroom. When it is spent, later blocks are dropped behind a single `…[truncated: inbound context budget exhausted]` marker line, stamped with the same `⟦openclaw:ctx⟧` provenance marker as every other injected header so strippers recognize it.

Non-goals: no change to the per-string cap, the history bound, or the chat-window formatter.

## Response to round-3 review

Both findings were correct; both fixes live in `channel-prompt-context.ts` and no new constant or export was added.

**String channel-context path bounded.** The canonical `ChannelPromptContext` string array reaches the prompt through `appendChannelPromptContext` (called from `prompt-prelude.ts`), a body join that never passes through the inbound context assembly — the assembly budget covers the runtime-only context prefix, not the command body these strings are appended to, so the bound belongs at the append point rather than in the assembly. The string form is one model-visible context block exactly like the fenced JSON blocks, so it now shares the same per-block cumulative budget (`MAX_CONTEXT_JSON_BLOCK_CHARS`, 50k — the measured justification carries over unchanged: one block is one block, whichever form it takes). Entries are kept whole while the budget lasts; the first entry that would overflow is head-truncated with `…[truncated]` (same convention as `truncateContextJsonString`) and the drop is flagged with the same `…[truncated: context budget exhausted]` marker as the JSON path, so both forms now cross one bounded, uniformly-marked boundary. The envelope-level regression builds a full `buildReplyPromptEnvelope` with 5,000 × 2,000-char channel strings: `prefixedCommandBody` was ~10 MB and is now < 51k chars ending in the marker.

**Escaped keys charged by their JSON size.** Raw key length undercounted exactly as described: a key of N raw chars emits ~2N once quotes and backslashes are escaped. The object walk now reserves each property's serialized size — the `JSON.stringify` length of the escaped key plus the serialized value — before appending it; a property that would cross the remaining budget is dropped behind the budget marker instead of overshooting, so the emitted block can no longer approach twice the budget while the counter reads under it. The covering test mixes backslashes, quotes and a control char in every key: raw key text totals 40,140 chars (the old counter stayed under 50k and accepted the block) while the emitted keys total 70,290; the emitted JSON now stops at 49,657 chars, carries the marker, and parses cleanly.

## Response to the P1 review

The review was correct: per-level count caps bound fan-out, not total size — a 50-key object of 20-element arrays of 2,000-char strings passed every limit and emitted ~2 MB, and nesting depth and key text were unrestricted. The rework follows the suggested shape: the inbound context assembly now owns one cumulative serialized-character budget (150k) spanning labels and all structured entries, while the JSON sanitizer enforces a per-block cumulative budget (50k, shared across the recursion) and a depth cap (8), always preserving valid JSON with an explicit `…[truncated: …]` marker. The saturated nested payload from the review (2,014,851 chars raw) now serializes to 40,099 chars with the marker and parses cleanly; the per-container caps (20/50) stay because they bound fan-out within the budget. All budget values are measured against the largest first-party payloads (see Evidence), not picked arbitrarily.

## Response to round-4 review

The nested-budget finding was correct, and the repair is split into two reviewable commits at the same sanitizer owner boundary.

- `062cd6316d9` (`fix(prompt): avoid double-charging nested context`) sanitizes candidates against a scratch copy of the remaining budget at both recursive retain edges (object property and array element), then charges the parent exactly once for the serialized value it actually keeps. This preserves the exact ClawSweeper object → array repro (`{ payload: Array(20).fill("x".repeat(2_000)) }`, 40,073 JSON chars) and the sibling array → objects shape (40,269 chars) byte-for-byte, without a marker.
- Review of that commit found one remaining acceptance gap: the array parent retained a sanitized candidate even when its serialized size exceeded the remaining parent budget. `e090a2a82e2` (`fix(prompt): enforce nested array budget`) mirrors the object acceptance check: measure the sanitized candidate, omit it when it does not fit, set budget exhaustion, and commit its cost only when accepted.

The exact 50,080-character nested-array repro demonstrates RED → GREEN:

```text
RED on 062cd631:
input JSON:       50,080
emitted JSON:     50,080
formatted block:  50,101
budget marker:    false

GREEN on e090a2a:
input JSON:       50,080
emitted JSON:     48,118
formatted block:  48,139
budget marker:    true
retained content: first 20-string array intact; first 4 strings of the second array + exhaustion marker
```

Fresh exact-head focused verification is **18/18**. Direct `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and `git show --check` pass. A deterministic sibling sweep covered 867 array→object, object→array, and array→array shapes below 50,000 chars with zero content loss; 13 oversized shapes all carried the marker, none reached 60,000 chars, and the largest emitted JSON was 49,645 chars. Object and array cycles still parse and carry the depth marker; the ~2 MB saturated payload remains bounded and marked.

Proof limits are explicit: the grouped area run reached 30 passing tests, then three suites failed during collection because this checkout's shared Typebox install is missing `typebox/build/type/script/token/internal/match.mjs`; no assertion failed and dependencies were not reconciled. No fresh full suite, build, or typecheck is claimed for `e090a2a`. The parent `062cd631` had fresh `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` passes; the final commit has the 18/18 focused run plus the static gates and semantic probes above.
## Response to round-5 review — real behavior proof, and both findings fixed

This round supplies the runtime proof that was missing and fixes the two open findings. The branch is also rebased onto current `main` (was `CONFLICTING`, now merges cleanly).

### [P1] Preserve the current reply target before exhausting the budget — fixed

`currentMessageContext` is emitted last but also suppresses the reply-chain fallback, so a saturated structured payload could drop the only quoted text the model needs. Its cost is now **reserved up front**, the same way the exhaustion marker already reserves its own, and released when the block is emitted.

### [P2] Keep capped object keys distinct — fixed

Capping channel-controlled keys could map two distinct keys onto one string, and `Object.fromEntries` then dropped the earlier value silently. Colliding capped keys now get the smallest `~N` discriminator that is unique.

### Real behavior proof: after-fix run through the production path

Executed against the real `buildInboundUserContextPrefix` and `formatContextJsonBlock` entry points (no mocks, no stubs), on Node 24.15.0.

**BEFORE the fix (reservation and key disambiguation removed, same harness):**

```text
[channel-context-budget proof] head=6dfdb54057
[reply-target] raw_channel_chars=12000000 rendered_chars=148191 bounded=true budget_marker=true
[reply-target] current_message_block_present=false quoted_target_preserved=false
[reply-target] tail="xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx…[truncated]\"}}\n```\n\n…[truncated: inbound context budget exhausted] ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧"
[key-identity] distinct_input_keys=2 surviving_values=1 values=["second"] no_silent_overwrite=false
[key-identity] rendered_keys=["…[truncated]"]
```

The reply target is gone and one of two distinct values was silently overwritten.

**AFTER the fix:**

```text
[channel-context-budget proof] head=6dfdb54057
[reply-target] raw_channel_chars=12000000 rendered_chars=148275 bounded=true budget_marker=true
[reply-target] current_message_block_present=true quoted_target_preserved=true
[reply-target] tail="cated]\"}}\n```\n\n…[truncated: inbound context budget exhausted] ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧\n\nCurrent message:\n[Replying to: \"the quoted sentence the model must answer\"]\n#5150:"
[key-identity] distinct_input_keys=2 surviving_values=2 values=["first","second"] no_silent_overwrite=true
[key-identity] rendered_keys=["…[truncated]","truncated]~2"]
```

12,000,000 channel-supplied chars are bounded to 148,275 rendered chars, the budget marker still fires, **and** the reply target survives at the tail. Both distinct keys survive.

### Red/green on the acceptance-criteria command

The listed criterion was `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/channel-prompt-context.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/prompt-prelude.test.ts`.

**RED** — new regressions against the unpatched code:

```text
 ❯ |unit-fast| src/auto-reply/reply/channel-prompt-context.test.ts (24 tests | 1 failed)
   × keeps distinct oversized keys distinct after capping
 AssertionError: expected [ 'second' ] to have a length of 2 but got 1

 ❯ |auto-reply| src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.test.ts (82 tests | 1 failed)
   × keeps the current reply target when structured context fills the budget
 AssertionError: expected 'Conversation info: ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧\n``…' to contain 'Current message:'
```

**GREEN** — same command on the patched tree:

```text
 ✓ |unit-fast| src/auto-reply/reply/channel-prompt-context.test.ts (24 tests) 212ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| src/auto-reply/reply/prompt-prelude.test.ts (12 tests) 29ms
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  36 passed (36)
 ✓ |auto-reply| src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.test.ts (82 tests) 185ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  82 passed (82)
[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 32.33s
```

118 tests pass, 0 fail.

### Conflict resolution note

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): bound deferred ingress handoffs
prs.body:
## Summary

- Keep the shared ingress watchdog bounded before and after explicit deferred handoff.
- Preserve the original claim-time deadline for every caller that does not configure a distinct deferred window.
- Let opted-in owners reset the watchdog at handoff so healthy scheduler waits receive their own bounded adoption window.
- Give WhatsApp a deliberately long seven-day operational bound instead of the generic five-minute bound.
- Fail closed with `handler-timeout` when a deferred scheduler never adopts or abandons, aborting late work and releasing the conversation lane.
- Close the shared state database before Windows test cleanup so SQLite-backed owner tests remove their temporary directories reliably.
- Keep core reply-queue lifecycle helpers out of the Plugin SDK test surface; exercise the WhatsApp owner proof through the supported `turnAdoptionLifecycle` contract.

Related to #120265 and #116547. This fixes the WhatsApp owner path without introducing an unbounded scheduler-owned deferral mode.

## What problem this solves

The generic ingress watchdog is appropriate while a claimed message is dispatching, but WhatsApp may legitimately defer adoption while its debounce and reply scheduler waits behind an active turn. Applying the same five-minute clock across both phases can dead-letter healthy queued work.

Clearing the watchdog after handoff is also unsafe: WhatsApp's scheduler has terminal callbacks but no independent liveness timeout, so a never-settling scheduler promise could refresh the durable claim and block the conversation lane forever.

This revision uses two bounded policies:

1. the generic watchdog starts at claim time and remains unchanged for callers that do not opt in;
2. an explicit `deferredAdoptionStallTimeoutMs` resets the watchdog only when deferral actually occurs;
3. WhatsApp opts into a seven-day operational safety bound for that second phase;
4. a missing terminal callback aborts and dead-letters the claim, rejects late adoption as guillotined, and lets the next same-lane message proceed.

The seven-day value is an operational recovery policy, not a scheduler-derived semantic maximum. A renewable scheduler heartbeat remains the stronger future refinement if arbitrarily long healthy waits must be supported.

## Safety and public contract

- No unbounded scheduler-owned deferral mode remains.
- Callers without an explicit post-handoff timeout keep the original claim-time deadline.
- The post-handoff clock resets only for an owner that explicitly configures it.
- Adoption and abandonment cancel the post-handoff watchdog.
- Timeout preserves claim-token fencing, abort, `handler-timeout`, and failed-tombstone behavior.
- Late adoption after timeout fails loudly instead of replaying work.
- The Plugin SDK channel documentation explains omission, explicit deferral reset, timeout behavior, the WhatsApp seven-day policy, and the renewable-lease alternative.
- Internal reply-queue admission helpers remain core-owned and are guarded by a negative SDK source-contract regression.
- Production configuration, services, queues, credentials, and WhatsApp traffic were not touched.

## Review verdict and scope

- Best-fix verdict: the distinct opt-in deferred watchdog is the narrowest compatible seam. A core-wide reset would change every channel, while clearing the watchdog would make lost scheduler ownership unbounded.
- Production TypeScript: **+38 / -11**.
- Tests: **+362 / -8**.
- Documentation: **+21 / -0**.
- Generated Plugin SDK contract: **+91 / -91**.

## Evidence

- Exact tested and reviewed head: `54b018b8ae641d29934291feb50c2cf948e3fa3d`.
- Latest frozen `main`: `5295f2578e1be11671987df79a2110f36e663daa`, normal-merged as `74b2cacc12c`; the sole genuine conflict was the generated Plugin SDK JSONL baseline, resolved by canonical regeneration. Earlier refreshes likewise preserved `main`'s generated-contract changes.
- Focused behavior proof: **61/61 tests passed** across four files and two Vitest shards covering WhatsApp durable receive, the mock-socket inbox owner path, the core deferred watchdog, and the core drain contract.
- SDK-boundary repair proof: the new negative source-contract regression failed before the fix with exactly the two leaked queue helpers, then passed after their removal; the complete affected WhatsApp file passed **17/17**, the complete SDK contract file passed **18/18**, and the focused core lifecycle-owner slice passed **3/3**.
- Windows cleanup regression: the first run's only failures were ten `EBUSY` removals of open SQLite temp files; the repository's test-only database closer was added before cleanup, after which all focused tests passed.
- Core production types passed: `pnpm tsgo:core`.
- Extension production types passed: `pnpm tsgo:extensions`.
- Core test-source types passed: `pnpm tsgo:core:test`.
- Extension test-source types passed: `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`.
- Plugin SDK API generation/check passed with the canonical JSONL contract.
- Plugin SDK surface check passed: 336 total entrypoints, 7,738 total exports, 151 public entrypoints, 4,847 public exports, and zero forbidden package subpaths.
- Exact changed-file type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Mandatory trusted exact-final-branch autoreview completed with **0 accepted/actionable findings** and **0.99 correctness confidence** (254,237-byte one-pass bundle).
- TruffleHog's exact committed branch scan passed clean against frozen `main`, including the review runner's independent 7.5-second scan.

## Owner-path proof available today

The current automated proof reaches the real OpenClaw ownership seams but uses an ephemeral durable queue and mock Baileys socket. It does not use credentials or send live traffic.

```json
{"scenario":"lost-scheduler-adoption","transport":"mock-baileys-socket","durableQueue":"ephemeral","timers":"real","configuredProductionBoundMs":604800000,"harnessBoundMs":50,"path":["messages.upsert","durable-delivery","whatsapp-debounce","turnAdoptionLifecycle.onDeferred","handler-timeout","same-lane-successor"],"sameLaneSuccessorDispatched":true,"lateAdoptionRejected":true,"credentials":false,"liveSend":false}
```

The sibling healthy-path regression uses the same owner path, keeps the second same-lane event pending, adopts through the supported `turnAdoptionLifecycle.onAdopted` contract, and then observes successor dispatch. Core-owner tests separately prove queue admission behavior, reset-at-handoff timing, timeout dead-lettering, late-adoption fencing, and adoption/abandonment timer cancellation.

## Outstanding acceptance — do not merge yet

1. Maintainers must explicitly accept the seven-day WhatsApp delivery-versus-recovery tradeoff. This PR documents the proposed operational policy but does not assume that product decision.
2. The mandatory real Baileys/WhatsApp lost-adoption trace is still missing. The mock-socket path above must not be represented as live external-account proof, and no synthetic external traffic should be created to satisfy it.

## AI assistance

AI-assisted investigation, implementation, tests, merge maintenance, and PR preparation. Review findings were independently reproduced by tracing the shared watchdog and the real WhatsApp debounce/reply ownership path before the bounded revision was implemented.

prs.title: fix(google): report embedding batch lifecycle statistics
prs.body:
Related: #120889

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an observability gap where operators running Gemini native embedding batches could not see the provider-reported request totals, success/failure/pending counts, lifecycle timestamps, elapsed time, or whether downloaded results fully reconciled with submitted requests.

The Gemini embedding API exposes `createTime`, `updateTime`, `endTime`, `batchStats`, state, and output metadata, but the adapter previously discarded those fields.

- https://ai.google.dev/api/embeddings#method:-models.asyncbatchembedcontent
- https://ai.google.dev/api/embeddings#embedcontentbatch

## Why This Change Was Made

The Google adapter now normalizes both current top-level Batch fields and the legacy Operation-metadata shape, with top-level terminal fields taking precedence over stale metadata. It emits structured subsystem events when a job is created, reaches a terminal state, and reconciles output.

Successful events report provider counts/timestamps plus separate provider and locally observed durations. Terminal failures report only structured provider codes. Output transport, HTTP, parse, record, missing-response, and unusable-metadata paths emit sanitized failure classes and reconciliation counts.

Durable events never include request text, provider error text, authentication, file URLs, response bodies, request IDs, or embedding vectors. Existing thrown error behavior and debug callbacks are unchanged.

This PR intentionally adds no configuration or quota claims. Public numeric batch knobs were deliberately retired upstream, and a real concurrency ceiling requires one shared admission semaphore across both file scheduling and group submission. That design remains separate follow-up work.

## User Impact

Operators can diagnose Gemini batch progress and failures from durable, structured evidence without enabling payload-level debug logging or exposing user content. The counts distinguish returned embeddings, provider record errors, genuinely missing responses after clean EOF, and unreconciled responses after transport/parse failure.

## Evidence

- Exact refreshed head: `2f67cd46baaaf29072427f27c5588cabd481fd3d`.
- The branch was refreshed by a normal merge from validated upstream `main` at `e97c3450a2724a6189762fa0d6c76284b9b83071`; no rebase or force-push was used.
- 27/27 focused Gemini batch tests pass, including the disposable loopback HTTP lifecycle.
- Regression coverage includes current and legacy API shapes, canonical top-level output precedence over stale legacy aliases, fail-closed rejection when conflicting legacy output aliases lack a canonical field, provider statistics/timestamps, terminal failure/cancel/expire states, output HTTP/parse/record errors, full-stream reconciliation after a record error, missing output metadata, fallback and provider timing semantics, and log-content secrecy.
- All four TypeScript surfaces pass: core production, core tests, extensions production, and extensions tests.
- Plugin SDK API baseline, export synchronization, and public-surface checks pass; no SDK regeneration was required.
- Targeted formatting, direct type-aware extension lint on both changed files, and `git diff --check` pass.
- The repository lint wrapper was attempted twice and timed out during broad plugin-boundary artifact preparation after 124 seconds and 304.1 seconds without a diagnostic. It is not counted as green; the underlying repository `oxlint` binary completed the equivalent type-aware two-file lint cleanly in 70.1 seconds.
- Mandatory isolated autoreview passed on the final branch against the frozen validated base: TruffleHog v3.95.9 reported the exact patch clean in 3.6 seconds, and Codex `gpt-5.6-sol` with high reasoning reviewed one complete 27,812-byte bundle and returned no accepted/actionable findings (`patch is correct`, confidence 0.98).
- Exact-head CI [run 31476497307](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31476497307) is terminal with 29 successful and 15 skipped jobs; its only underlying failure is [`build-artifacts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31476497307/job/93731653297), followed by the aggregate gate. The Control UI build exceeded its startup-JS gzip ceiling by exactly two bytes (326,658 B versus 326,656 B). Recovery and registry bookkeeping repeat copies and checks around values already owned by the current operation. This recovers the remaining recovery/registry area from the parked cleanup without changing its durable-work or effect-authority owners.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry detached acquired rows and owned target/claim objects forward; consume synchronous planned drafts and fresh terminal events once; remove adjacent duplicate checks and local-only array freezing; use the actual wait adapter's narrowed fields; and reuse the existing six-field kill-intent comparator. This 17-path area removes 47 net production lines (+33/-80). Tests add 28 net lines (+45/-17), principally failure-safe cleanup of named diagnostic targets, with one assertion added to the existing real marking-failure/retry flow. The rule-11 size floor is waived for area recovery.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- The diagnostic reset came from [abort/restart recovery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146792). Lifecycle rotation no longer silently discards an unresolved warning. A removed store's warning may remain until same-target success or process restart; diagnostics never authorize dispatch or writes. The existing docs already describe success-driven clearing.
- Acquired recovery rows and private target/claim inputs are handed off without another clone. The target path was carried through [incognito consumer preparation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168005); historical research found no human caller-mutation incident supporting these allocation-only copies. In-process callers must not mutate handed-off inputs. Exact session/claim/native-source predicates and release remain.

[Immutable registry publication](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163195) introduced synthetic snapshot controls; the codec still detaches/normalizes before worker I/O. The typed synchronous plan contract replaces an impossible Promise detector. [Queued-write settlement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151303), unknown receipts, FIFO, and native transaction/commit authority are unchanged.
- The same publication change introduced the incidental completion metadata comparisons and postpublication execution snapshot. Same-owner metadata can now be overwritten by a fresh capture, and metadata progress no longer revokes already-published bookkeeping. The original publication machinery supplied synthetic interleavings, not a verified human reentrant-resolver incident. prs.title: fix(build): prevent concurrent Control UI artifact failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes production Control UI builds failing when concurrent E2E workers or UI build commands regenerate the same Settings plugin artifacts.

## User Impact

Concurrent UI builds now serialize their shared artifact writes on both Node and Bun. Browser behavior is unchanged; there are no new options, migrations, dependencies, or runtime skips.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Vite plugin's `buildStart` calls `prepareControlUiSettings`, which spawns `build-plugin-control-ui.mts --prepare-settings`. Even builds with separate UI output directories overwrite the same plugin manifests and rebuild `dist/extensions/node_modules/openclaw/plugin-sdk`. The Settings path was outside the checkout artifact lock already used by runtime-postbuild and bundled runtime staging. Two actual concurrent Settings commands reproduced the reported fs-safe `path-mismatch` failure on both runtimes.

Use that existing lock for Settings preparation and full UI publication, and transfer ownership to the Vite child. Nested preparation shares the active async call's owner; independent callers still contend. The Settings helper uses native module loading so Vite cannot create a second owner instance or rewrite the child TypeScript loader into an HTTP URL. The native Vite launcher preserves the existing UI cache decision and validator behavior. The build-all dispatcher transfers its existing lock to the UI step, and dedicated CLI children retain inherited ownership until process exit, including native bundler callbacks after module import completes.

Classification for `service-worker-update.e2e.test.ts` and the phone recovery cases: **bucket 1, shared build tooling defect exposed by concurrent execution**, affecting both runtimes. Their build-error paths on the current base already throw: `buildProductionControlUiE2e` includes build stderr, service-worker setup awaits it without a catch, and phone setup rethrows after cleanup. There is no build-failure-to-skip branch to remove at this revision; legitimate browser/platform skips remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Focused two-writer reproduction, three rounds per runtime: **before 0/3 successful pairs; after 3/3 successful pairs**, for both Node v26.12.0 and pinned Bun `1.4.3-canary.1+65d94e715`. Each failing baseline pair had one fs-safe identity failure. All six post-fix children per runtime exited 0.
- Real Settings CLI regression holds the checkout lock, verifies both writers wait, then verifies the resulting browser asset, manifest and SDK alias. It also runs the installed Vite CLI with a bundled config under inherited ownership and executes the real build-all dispatcher with a focused UI step.
- Nested-owner regression, existing independent-waiter/cancellation tests, and focused uncertain-child cleanup tests pass.
- Existing UI publication, cache, validation and signal tests pass.

| Focused file | Node | Bun |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test/scripts/build-plugin-control-ui.test.ts` | 2/2 | 2/2 |
| `test/scripts/dist-artifact-lock.test.ts` | 7/7 | 7/7 |
| `test/scripts/ui.test.ts` | 18/18 | 18/18 |

Commands for each listed file:

```sh
TMPDIR=/private/tmp/oc-buildrace OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1
PATH=/private/tmp/oc-bun-fork/bin:$PATH TMPDIR=/private/tmp/oc-buildrace OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH=/private/tmp/oc-bun-fork/bin/bun OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1
```

prs.title: fix(android): make sidebar session parentage explicit
prs.body:
Related: #150054 — Android-specific context: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/150054#issuecomment-5848447065

## What Problem This Solves

Android needs explicit root and child session choices without changing the existing sidebar header action. The previous revision mislabeled a session as independent while the Gateway could persist implicit main-session parentage, and replacing the header action changed inherited settings.

## User Impact

- The original header **+** is restored and keeps its existing inherited-session creation path.
- A separate **New independent session** action creates a root without implicit main-session parentage.
- **New child** beside the selected eligible session creates a distinct child and preserves that parent.
- Existing sessions are not reparented or migrated. Connection, busy-state, write-access and selected-parent guards remain.

## Why This Change Was Made

Addresses both actionable findings in the review of `b4dd5ac951d513df93156362b60179024865f889`. The Gateway `sessions.create` schema now accepts optional `independent: true`; that intent cannot be combined with a parent or used to adopt an existing session. Omitted intent retains the existing behavior. Android sends the explicit intent only for the separate independent action.

This is an Android proposal, not a change to web Control UI `/new`. Unlike the earlier revision, this repair **does include Gateway/schema changes**. The new root action requires a Gateway supporting that field; older Gateways reject it rather than guarantee independence. The app now explains that the Gateway must be updated, without retrying or navigating away. Maintainer acceptance of the API and product surface remains pending.

## Evidence

Repair commit: `806788de0ac6158be42f7516c6f94ae870996767`. Prior upstream integration at `b4dd5ac951d513df93156362b60179024865f889` is retained.

- **20 focused Gateway tests passed**, including root persistence and conflicting-intent/existing-key regressions; the test snapshot was checked against every changed file.
- **4 focused Android tests passed** across `ChatControllerSidebarCreationTest` and `SidebarSessionCreationTest`.
- **1 public socket-RPC test passed** using the repository's isolated Gateway harness: advertised `sessions.create`, returned distinct root/child keys, persisted root with no parent, child with the selected parent, inherited child thinking/Fast Mode, unchanged pre-existing parent, and subsequent `sessions.describe` reads. Test time 3.204 s; Vitest duration 37.10 s; container exit 0. Process-main-thread configuration: `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PROJECT_SHARDS=0`.
- Independent incremental review found no actionable P0–P2 findings in the ten-file repair. This is not whole-PR clearance. Normal pre-commit hooks passed in a secretless container. Hooks changed only wrapping and optional trailing commas in two TypeScript files; quoted literals and remaining content were verified unchanged, so unaffected tests/review were reused.
- Native-i18n inventory repair `2ac85996eb77c9e7c4343cb3c15bdab7ebe32ebd` remains included.

### Compatibility and generated-protocol follow-up

Follow-up commit: `b58ea35fe9d061bbfc7c4047a4880b3b59d5a57f`.

- Unsupported `independent` schema errors now produce **Update your Gateway to create independent sessions.** No retry or navigation occurs; existing child/default behavior is unchanged.
- Regenerated the Swift protocol model through the canonical generator to include the optional `independent` field, addressing the stale-output failure in `checks-fast-bundled-protocol`.
- Four focused `ChatControllerSidebarCreationTest` tests passed, including the older-Gateway regression: 3.957 seconds test execution, 134.892 seconds contained recipe wall time. Exact Android patch bytes matched the test receipt. New-head CI timing is not yet available.
- Protocol registry and Swift freshness checks passed; Kotlin regeneration produced no changes. The full `protocol:check` command was not run. The generated Swift file matched its recorded generator output hash.
- Fresh independent incremental review found no actionable P0–P2 findings in these three files. Normal hooks passed without changing the reviewed tree. This is not whole-PR clearance.

### Contributor-reported connected-device evidence

[Connected-device report by saariuslystoned](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159159#issuecomment-5901361888) covers published head `806788de` and merge-base `0c8e56cf`, using synthetic sessions and a throwaway Gateway. The contributor reports root/child/grandchild creation, preserved existing lineage across upgrade, inherited header behavior, and the old-Gateway rejection; the comment includes a comparative image. This is third-party reported evidence, not independently reproduced by this author, and predates the error-message follow-up. Web Control UI, busy-session guards, and write-access guards were not covered. The reported header/search ordering difference is not changed by this follow-up.

### Before / after

Inspected synthetic Compose renders, also delivered to the originating chat. **Before** is the preceding PR UI with the header + missing; **after** is the repaired candidate. These are not device captures. Incidental navigation ordering differs between fixture snapshots and is not the claimed fix.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: separate independent action replaced the inherited header plus](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/2a4345bdedeb8eb8a3dc76d502d32e5c3831b034/20260929-before.png) | ![After: inherited header plus restored alongside independent and child actions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/2a4345bdedeb8eb8a3dc76d502d32e5c3831b034/20260929-after.png) |

### Scope and remaining limits

The socket proof exercises real Gateway RPC handling and synthetic persistence, not a live Android-to-Gateway end-to-end session. External dispatch/title/lifecycle mocks remain in the repository harness. It proves preservation of a pre-existing synthetic parent, not a complete deployed-version upgrade matrix. Android dependency-seed provenance remains unverified. No APK was installed during this repair.

The full cross-platform build/check/test suite was not rerun; validation was scoped as listed above. The separate RPC log export was denied by the execution tool; the retained completion receipt and independently observed container exit are the basis for the reported result, not an exported raw log.

**Not a merge-clearance claim:** current-head CI, reviewer reassessment, and maintainer product/API acceptance remain separate gates. No upstream merge is requested or performed by this update.

## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL update-preflight tests could start a successor while a timed-out test still held the shared maintenance lease, producing a secondary lock failure.

## User Impact

This changes test fixture cleanup only. The original timeout remains a failure; the next case waits for the original body and its release to settle.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing fixture lifetime helper for case work and suite-owned inputs. Record case drains and teardown under the suite owner so unverified cleanup retains the shared directory. Remove the independently scheduled temporary-directory cleanup.

Production LOC delta: 0. Test LOC delta: +27 net; most changed lines are callback indentation. No timeout or assertion changes.

## Evidence

- Independent source review and scoped autoreview: no accepted P0–P2 findings. Pinned oxfmt 0.72.0 and `git diff --check` passed.
- [Exact-head CI attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39070727640) passed at `3aeaa40193f409550b1b9a1c207d710b307c26e2`: all 49 jobs terminal, no failures, all three PostgreSQL shards and the aggregate gate passed.
- [PostgreSQL shard 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39070727640/job/117507882684) passed all five preflight tests in their original order. Tested merge `f0c2aa0d25104eefa6a5c1f6ac6c994e75a133a7` contains the exact PR test-file blob and unchanged fixture helper.
- Real PostgreSQL fault proof used the same ordered final pair on unmodified base `d559000492dd59cb028fc76d55704a12cfeaace4` and this head, lowering only the test deadline to 15 seconds. Base: primary timeout, then a live maintenance-lease collision in the successor. Repair: both intentional timeouts remain failures, each original body drains, and the successor starts without that collision. Owned processes and PostgreSQL clients settled after each command. These diagnostic commands exited 1; they are failure-path proof, not passing tests.
- Local normal proof did not pass: two tests passed and inventory, baseline sealing, and retained-agent capture exceeded the unchanged 120-second deadline. One unmodified-base discriminator reproduced the same initial inventory timeout. Hosted CI supplies the successful whole-file proof; the local latency cause remains unattributed, and this PR makes no performance claim.
- The shared helper is unchanged and was not rerun separately; the real owning-module fault proof covers the repaired lifecycle.

prs.title: fix(gateway): defer plugin runtime generation reserve until retained work admits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a plugin reload is refused before replacement actually starts (for example while retained work is still draining), `reloadGatewayPlugins()` had already called `pluginRuntimeGeneration.reserve()`. That fenced the still-serving generation even though no replacement was committed, so operations through the captured plugin runtime could fail while the registry object was unchanged.

## Solution

Defer `pluginRuntimeGeneration.reserve()` until after the first retained-work admission drain succeeds (post `reserveResourceHandoff`, after `drainRetainedWork`). Prepare-time failures and pre-admission refusals no longer touch the serving generation. Existing rollback and cleanup after a committed replacement are unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-plugins.lifecycle.test.ts -t 'a retained-work reload refusal leaves the serving runtime generation authoritative'`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-plugin-runtime-generation.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

Fixes #157670
