prs.title: improve(openai): vary provisional voice launch acknowledgments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Voice delegation repeated a fixed English launch receipt even for callers speaking another language. This uses a short natural acknowledgment in the caller's language, with varied wording on repeated requests. The receipt confirms hearing the request; it does not establish admission or task completion. A fresh later result is still delivered through the existing completion owner.

## User Impact

Callers hear a short varied acknowledgment in their language, followed separately by a confirmed result or failure. Launch phrasing does not promise admission.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing delegation controller supplies a bounded launch-only instruction and retains the existing completion and failure owners.

### Refinement from live evidence

The launch acknowledgment now confirms hearing the request only. Real voice testing exposed that “on it” and even “checking that” could imply work had started before admission. The refined note explicitly excludes checking/doing claims, remains limited to this launch acknowledgment, and preserves natural wording, the caller’s language, variation, and the under-eight-word limit. Later confirmed results remain unchanged.

Live synthetic proof used the real subscription WebRTC transport, canonical production instruction builder, locally synthesized English/Polish input, and isolated callbacks. Repeated English acknowledgments were “Okay, I hear you.” and “Right, got it.” Polish acknowledgments were “Jasne, rozumiem.” and, for injected rejection, “Jasne, słyszę prośbę.” The rejected request’s spoken result was “Nie udało się tego wykonać. Spróbować jeszcze raz?” Three successful callbacks spoke the synthetic file’s correct first word. The synthetic terminal readback is included below; source recordings remain local and are not required to interpret these observed results.

Validation: final 26 owner tests, scoped extension lint, formatting, and fresh P0–P2 independent review pass. Previous unchanged bridge sibling proof is reused; no API or type shape changed.

Limits/decision: the rejection is injected at the consultation callback, not a real Gateway scheduler denial. One call demonstrates observed phrasing, not guaranteed compliance. Maintainer approval of provisional conversational receipts remains required; no approval is inferred from this evidence.

## Evidence

Code CI for head `15ff9e2b9e4ca5f29c31c09a8525153845547ed8` passed, including production/test types and lint ([CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39063056563)). PostgreSQL session postimages captured without published physical admission facts could be treated as current because absent admission and write tokens compared equal. This follows up #175718.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Record a null admission when PostgreSQL capture lacks physical facts, and reject that marker through the existing admission predicate. The marker survives worker serialization, so the decision does not depend on process-local bookkeeping. Admitted PostgreSQL sources retain their existing identity and commit-token checks. No SQL, schema, generation, handshake, or new owner is introduced.

No checks are removed. Accepted edge case: an optional postimage captured before admission remains unusable; a later demand recomputes it from the admitted owner.

Explicit PostgreSQL semantic review approved head 058b8624c062: the marker survives transport, both currency predicates reject it, admitted sources retain their checks, and the replica consumer checks currency before using prepared facts.

## Evidence

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: new web-chat messages remain queued behind a busy Codex-backed turn when steering admission loses the active turn’s reply requirement.

## User Impact

Users can steer an active Codex conversation when the new message has the same reply requirement as the running turn. No configuration changes or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex published its delivery facts without the host-owned terminal reply requirement. Admission treated the missing value as `required`, so web chat’s `result-required` input was rejected with `reply_expectation_mismatch`. Publish the attempt’s accepted requirement on its backend handle; the existing mismatch guard and undefined legacy behavior remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- A missing-producer baseline through real shared admission reproduces two causal failures: matching `result-required` input is rejected, and `required` input is wrongly accepted into an `optional` backend.
- All 12 owning hook cases pass, including matching and mismatched shared-admission inputs for `required`, `optional`, `result-required`, and undefined legacy behavior. Each accepted input reaches the actual attached Codex backend, issues one native `turn/steer` RPC request, settles after a native user-message echo, and captures the synthetic final. The controlled transport invokes the real physical-write currentness callback; this owner regression is separate from the external-provider capture below. Focused types, typed lint, formatting, and diff checks pass; a fresh P0–P2 review found no actionable defects.
- An isolated real Gateway/native-provider run authenticated as the owner through the UI chat protocol, reached a busy execution checkpoint, accepted a second same-capability input, and completed the original run successfully. The actual assistant final contained a unique synthetic marker absent from the initial prompt. The task-owned Gateway was stopped and copied authentication was removed. This proves the real consumer path in addition to the synthetic native-RPC regressions.
- Deployed the isolated fix locally after the native-provider check. The new managed Gateway owns its listener; deep RPC status and health pass, Codex and the existing plugins are available, and the startup log audit contains no errors. Existing recovery warnings remain separate from this fix. Voice and plugin integration changes were preserved.

prs.title: fix(tts): preserve unread preferences during updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An unreadable or malformed TTS preference file is silently treated as empty. Preference-changing commands can then replace that existing file with defaults plus one changed setting.

## User Impact

Read-only TTS operations warn with repair guidance and continue using configured defaults. Preference updates refuse before writing when the existing file cannot be read, preserving it for repair. Slash-command setters return a terminal repair reply instead of letting that refusal escape without a response. A genuinely missing file remains a quiet first-run default and can still be created by a setting command.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep one file-read owner with an internal update context, rather than a competing reader or a blanket throw on normal reply paths. The existing mutation owner requests refusal before its unchanged private atomic write. Public setter signatures, valid-file updates, preference JSON shapes, config keys, permissions and durability remain unchanged.

This is a real silent-failure/data-preservation fix, not cleanup-floor credit: **36 net production lines added**,55 net test lines added,5 documentation lines added. The lightweight config module uses a generic warning without logging preference contents or adding a heavy logger import. The existing command adapter shares one error-to-reply boundary across its six setter sites and logs through its existing subsystem logger plus the canonical error formatter.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Optional reads still use configured defaults after a non-missing read/parse failure, now visibly. They do not block unrelated text replies. Mutations do not accept that fallback because it would overwrite unread settings.
- Valid JSON shape coercion is unchanged; this fix handles read failures and malformed JSON, not a new schema or migration. No new retry, race fence or warning cache.
- Existing quiet read behavior predates the shared-reader consolidation in #157982 and the lightweight extraction776c8e. No human incident or original-regression attribution is claimed; the concrete defect is the present read-default→mutate→atomic-write path.

## Evidence

- Fresh independent complete six-file review with determining read/write/command/private-file/errno/authorization/temp-directory owners: scoped-clean P0-P2,0.97; final source verification passed. Root and frozen review candidate match on all six files. Hosted P2 finding4304553893 was accepted: the initial setter refusal could escape slash-command dispatch without a reply. This repair handles the failure at the actual command boundary; original-head CI does not qualify the repaired head.
- Three real-filesystem regression cases in the existing config fixture cover quiet missing vs visible malformed optional reads; actual setTtsMaxLength refusal with byte-identical malformed contents; and missing/valid-file successful updates preserving settings. Only console output is spied on.
- A distinct command-boundary regression invokes actual handleTtsCommands('/tts limit 2000') with the real settings writer through the fixture's one-call setter implementation, asserting a terminal repair reply and byte-identical malformed contents. Shared temporary-directory cleanup and a static narrow writer import keep lifecycle/compilation at collection; no production test seam or new module mock.
- Baseline and fixed runtime tests have not been executed locally. The same TTS/settings dependency graph reached actual cold-worker compilation during the immediately preceding focused run; that task-owned attempt was stopped before assertions and all descendants drained. No equivalent cold retry, runtime pass, measured test cost, or reproduced red/green claim. Exact-head CI must execute the changed owner suite before landing; record its cost when available.
- Canonical original four-file formatting passed256ms; the two command repair files passed14ms; whitespace passed. Focused docs MDX check passed1file/589ms; docs-list completed. The documentation skill kept recovery guidance beside the existing per-user preferences reference, with no navigation, headings, links, generated locales or governance changes.
- Repaired five-root core-test types (actual owning allowJs config plus ambient declarations) exited2 with36 unchanged parse5/MCP declaration and implicit-any diagnostics; no diagnostic names the changed files. This is not a qualified type pass. Original canonical core three-file type-aware lint and14-test suppression guard passed; repaired command two-file type-aware lint passed. Current pre-push suppression guard14PASS/106.28s Vitest/133.88s wrapper (git enumeration42.08s). No broad local build/check-changed/whole-graph types/E2E. The new errno/error-format imports use existing canonical owners and no public SDK surface is changed.

Release-note context: TTS preference commands no longer overwrite an existing file after a read/JSON parse failure; optional reads report fallback with repair guidance. No live channel/provider or operator-state proof claimed.

## User Impact

No intended change on supported Node, latest stable Bun1.4.3 or the pinned OpenClaw Bun fork. Browser-safe conditional builtin loading, public getEnvApiKey/findEnvKeys signatures, provider aliases and precedence, blank trimming, Vertex ADC discovery and AWS ambient authentication remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Delete the private proc environment cache and fallback reader; use the runtime-owned process environment directly. No replacement helper, retry, import, test seam, configuration or dependency change. This one-file owner slice of an unfinished >80-file proposal removes **35 net production lines** (+1/-36), with no test changes. No SDK/protocol/schema/durability/retention/permission change. Phase E session-memory code and tests are untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Unsupported older/custom Bun builds that still expose an entirely empty environment now use the existing missing-key result instead of best-effort recovery from proc. Human issue [bun#27802](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/27802) describes macOS Seatbelt on Bun1.3.10, despite the old Linux comment. Upstream [#28785](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/28785), merged asd63aa714, loads OS environment before directory traversal. Personally inspected both supported implementations: stock bun-v1.4.3 and exact forkb76e4b4e6725dfc84eadc67059753a389e4b1c54 transpiler.rs639–675, plus the fork's env_loader.rs558–582. The support policy already rejects older runtimes; this change does not repin or expand it.

## Evidence

- Fresh complete one-file independent review: scoped-clean P0-P2 (0.99), final source verification. Current Bun policy and exact fork pin supplied; unchanged tests personally inspected and run.
- Fresh receiving-head focused owner/browser suites: five tests passed,33.09 seconds Vitest /58.79 seconds wrapper. Covers absent browser process, blank-key precedence/trimming, AWS profile authentication, negative ADC retry and actual esbuild browser bundling without static node:fs require.
- Bounded environment/unit/browser three-root typecheck passed without diagnostics; no broad type/build claim.
- One-file formatting passed (43ms/one thread), TypeScript-focused boundary lint and whitespace passed. Production import edges are unchanged, so no new cycle is possible. Raw Node --check could not parse this workspace TS mode; Vitest, targeted types and focused lint validate the actual TypeScript source instead.
- Mandatory suppression check: all14 tests passed,60.08 seconds Vitest /96.63 seconds wrapper. No suppressions or baselines changed.
- Earlier unchanged baseline: five tests passed on the prior clean checkout; this is scoped source-identical evidence, not a fresh receiving-base or Bun sandbox replay. No real process environment was dumped, no credentials were read, and no paid/live provider was called.
- Supported Bun binary/sandbox/device proof is not claimed. Exact-head PR CI supplies broad repository and consumer qualification.

Release-note context: simplify provider environment lookup by retiring obsolete Bun proc recovery, retaining supported-runtime and browser behavior.

prs.title: fix(gateway): handle history disconnects and batch Bun broadcasts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes uncaught errors when a session-history stream disconnects and excess writes when Gateway WebSocket broadcasts run on Bun.

## User Impact

Closing a history stream stays local to that connection. Broadcast bursts retain their one-write batching and response order on Node and Bun. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

An HTTP request can emit its abort error after its response closes. The response handler removed the request's error listener too early; the request now owns removal of its listeners at its own close, while SSE subscription and heartbeat cleanup still happen immediately.

The WebSocket adapter collects already-encoded frame bytes and flushes each broadcast burst through one public `socket.write` call. It preserves ws framing and compression, settles each send callback from the combined write, and includes queued bytes in backpressure checks. This replaces the private Writable-hook patch and removes its lint suppression. The test observes the public write API and retains exact response order.

The daily Bun rollout in #175699 exposed both existing paths. No runtime policy, public API, authorization, deadline, retry, dependency, or schema change.

## Evidence

- Main hourly 39066988478 (head `4aa0e219fef1`): jobs 117496811602 and 117496811648 report unhandled HTTP `aborted` exceptions; job 117496811655 reports the missing `_writev` spy. Each log was fetched once.
- Before repair, the physical-source history suite passes its four assertions but produces three unhandled errors on both local Node and pinned Bun. The new close-order regression independently fails with `Error: aborted` before repair; the existing cleanup assertions remain unchanged.
- The real Gateway batching test fails with eight native writes instead of one before repair, while preserving frame order. The repair retains that exact one-write assertion.
- Public-write revision: all eight requested Gateway files pass on Node 26.12.0 and pinned CI Bun `1.4.3-canary.1+b76e4b4e6`, 100 cases per runtime, with `--maxWorkers=1`.
- The updated shared socket fixture is proven across all 22 direct and indirect consumer files: 274 Node cases, including the WebSocket files and the synthetic Cloudflare/visitor-access E2E. The E2E runtime build also passes.
- Both Gateway type graphs, targeted lint, formatting, and the 14-case suppression ratchet pass. No suppression or allowlist change remains.
- Initial local runs caught a captured-send fixture mismatch and lint issues; those are fixed. A later compile collided with the E2E package rebuild before any test ran; the blocked check passed after the build completed. Fresh P2 autoreview of the complete PR and connection-owner context is scoped-clean with no actionable findings.

No CI dispatch or rerun. PR CI supplies broad and Linux proof; the lead owns landing after the new head's checks.

prs.title: perf(gateway): trim redundant session tool event payloads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Tool-heavy sessions send unused session metadata, duplicated exec output, and raw dispatcher result mirrors in live tool events, increasing WebSocket traffic for every observer. The raw mirror can include full text and image base64 even though the displayed result is already bounded.

## User Impact

Live tool cards and activity previews keep their existing output, ordering, and completion behavior while receiving smaller payloads. Stored tool results and internal result callbacks are unchanged. Native clients retain their existing delivery rules; no protocol version or configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`session.tool` consumers use the tool event and explicit session address; roster metadata already arrives through `session.message` and `sessions.changed`. The mirror now sends that event directly. The existing exec-result projection also omits `details.aggregated` when text content is present, preserving the existing cap for results without text content. Separate command-progress output is prepared before this projection so its whitespace and truncation remain unchanged.

The consumer audit covers Activity, foreground chat, sidebar/subagent activity, pull-request refresh, Apple hover cards, Android, and the TUI. A blanket 2,000-character cap was rejected because foreground chat and structured results need more than Activity's preview. The history detail projection also omits metadata needed by live permission/model/status consumers, so it is not substituted wholesale. At the existing Gateway wire projection, terminal `dispatch_action` results omit only `details.tool` and `details.result`; every other detail and the original internal envelope survives. MCP App contents still come from `mcp.app.view`.

## Evidence

Four concurrent A/B pairs on the same Linux host, under an exclusive measurement lock, used separate synthetic state and loopback ports. Each side had 16 CPUs; successive pairs swapped the CPU halves. Preparation ran separately. Both sides ran the source-mode Gateway with the same dependency overlay and ten synthetic sessions. Each active window executed exec, read, edit, an HTTP MCP structured result, and a real headless Chromium screenshot returned through MCP, twice each. Source was pinned to base `3a5456567068` and head `25bab8194a2d`; start skew was 0/2/1/0 ms. Active-window CPU busy time from `mpstat` averaged 5.35%/7.38% on the two halves in pair 1, 6.67%/5.24% in pair 2, 5.53%/5.58% in pair 3, and 5.91%/6.01% in pair 4 (total load including the benchmark, recorded for context); byte results are paired differences, not comparisons across different load windows.

| Pair | Before bytes | After bytes | Paired difference | Before / after active time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 1,029,306 | 491,880 | −537,426 | 9,047 / 8,983 ms |
| 2, CPU halves swapped | 1,029,300 | 491,890 | −537,410 | 9,007 / 9,061 ms |
| 3 | 1,029,312 | 491,892 | −537,420 | 8,941 / 8,969 ms |
| 4, CPU halves swapped | 1,029,298 | 491,888 | −537,410 | 8,952 / 9,027 ms |

Mean `session.tool` size fell **17,155.07 → 8,198.13 bytes per frame (−52.21%)**. Each side delivered the same 60 per-socket frames: 30 to an exact subscriber and 30 to a legacy roster client; the scoped web roster-only client received zero. The initiating tool-capable client received its 30 tool `agent` frames without a duplicate `session.tool` copy. Gateway `gateway.ws.event` counter totals matched received `session.tool` bytes and counts exactly in every run. Model-facing output length arrays and retained live content/argument field sizes matched in all four pairs.

At a fixed **1,000 synthetic turns/hour**, with the same mix and two observers, the counter-derived traffic is **102.93 → 49.19 MB/hour**. Extrapolating each measured active window instead gives a mean **412.34 → 196.54 MB/hour**; this burst-rate extrapolation is not measured production-hour traffic. Elapsed differences of −64/+54/+28/+75 ms (mean +23.25 ms) are neutral; this change claims a serialized event-byte reduction, not a throughput improvement. These are application-frame bytes counted before any WebSocket transport compression.

Representative exact-subscriber result frames explain the reduction:

- Exec: **21,354 → 8,671 bytes**. The original probe contained 8,046 bytes of text content, 8,033 bytes of duplicated aggregate, and about 4.5 KiB of session metadata.
- MCP dispatcher: **106,672 → 10,196 bytes**. Its raw nested result alone was 96,157 bytes, including unbounded text and a second structured result. The direct MCP result's 26,190-byte structured content remains unchanged.
- Screenshot dispatcher: **10,475 → 1,505 bytes**. The nested base64 field was 8,006 bytes for a 6,003-byte PNG; top-level image omission metadata remains. The capture used real headless Chromium through MCP, not the browser plugin's routing.
- Edit result: **21,715 bytes unchanged**; the rendered diff/content remains available.

The session-row/exec-only intermediate change saved 11.24% in its own two swapped pairs; removing the measured raw dispatcher mirror accounts for the larger final reduction.

### Regression proof

All three regressions fail on the original corresponding producer code: the session mirror includes the redundant row, exec live results include duplicate aggregated text, and dispatcher wire results retain the raw mirror. A non-dispatch control retains identically named fields.

Focused proof covers five files (240 tests): `tool-search.mcp-error.test.ts`, `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts`, `server-chat.agent-events.test.ts`, `server-broadcast.board.test.ts`, and `worker-environments/live-events.test.ts`. The initial four-file run passed 234 tests in 87.08 seconds; the final Gateway/MCP run passed 90 tests in 54.38 seconds, including imports/transforms. Changed-file formatting and core lint, plus `git diff --check`, pass. Broad typecheck/build/suites run in [exact-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39070973110); no Testbox/Crabbox lease was used.

Fresh independent autoreview is clean through P2 for the complete production diff, and GitHub's code review reports no findings on the final head. Production change is net **+17 lines** (44 additions, 27 deletions): the dispatcher's raw result is a required internal/Code Mode contract, so its client-only projection must preserve the original envelope. No new module, cache, configuration, subscription mode, or truncation policy. CI required shrinking the existing assertion allowance from 7 to 6 after removal of a cast; regenerated with the owner parser for that one file.

Native compatibility is source-audited, not a native-device runtime claim. The synthetic workload uses actual tool execution with bounded isolated state and synthetic model/MCP responses. Measurement equality checks compare output lengths and retained field sizes, while focused regressions assert result contents; production traffic, native devices, and browser-plugin routing were not exercised. Direct MCP structured content remains a separate payload source.

prs.title: fix(update): avoid oversized runtime retention replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes updates failing during runtime retention when a large installation's verification metadata exceeds the worker's 64 MiB output limit, even after its files have been materialized.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175626

## User Impact

Large runtimes can complete retention without sending their full verification inventory back to the updater. This repairs the updater driver; an older installed driver still uses its previous retention behavior for the first upgrade.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the complete admission plan inside the worker through materialization, then return only the original file paths, relocations, counts, and timings consumed by the parent. Import identity, cancellation, cleanup, and the existing capture limit are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Exact-head [CI focused job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39066615729/job/117495868098): the four required producer, retention, import-process, and materialization suites passed 57 tests, with one case-sensitive-volume skip. Four related backup tests also passed.
- The producer regression measured the old reply at 69,810,554 bytes and the projected reply at 25,440,405 bytes against the unchanged 67,108,864-byte cap. Materialization received the original full plan, and the reply preserved all 160,002 original file paths in order, relocations, and metrics.
- Full `pnpm build` passed on the exact head in 2m58s with Node 26.7.0 and pnpm 12.11.1. This used the supported isolated local fallback after the single remote allocation queued and was stopped; source remained clean. Pinned oxfmt 0.72.0 and `git diff --check` passed.
- Baseline-red execution was not run. Live update recovery and overall duration remain unverified by this PR.

CI attempt 1 has two failing PostgreSQL lanes; its original failures and logs remain recorded. An unchanged-source comparison ran the complete preflight (5 tests) and Git backup (2 tests) files on both the exact CI base `c14f1da` and tested merge `95c9c179`, through the native database harness. All four runs passed with exit 0 and completed cleanup. This used macOS Node 26.7.0 and the same pinned PostgreSQL 17 image under amd64 emulation, so it does not reproduce the CI workload or establish equivalent timing. The preceding timed-out test retaining its maintenance lease explains the secondary lock collision; the original capture and setup timeout causes remain unclassified. The single authorized failed-surface retry completed on the unchanged head and the same tested merge. PostgreSQL lane 2 passed. Lane 1 has only the 60-second port-command privilege/refusal/staging timeout; its complete failure signature matches scheduled-main runs [39058564617](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39058564617) and [39062485709](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39062485709), and the relevant test/owner inputs are unchanged in the tested PR merge. The exact slow operation remains unknown. CI and its aggregate remain failed; landing uses the native inherited-only exception for that single case, with independent source and failure attribution. The original unmatched failures did not recur, which is not claimed as a fix. Passing focused tests and build remain separate evidence.

ClawSweeper's optional rank-up run through a metadata-heavy subprocess is deferred: this patch measures the capacity boundary and exercises real worker/import lifecycle contracts separately, without creating 160,002 physical fixture files. Large-inventory end-to-end recovery remains unverified until deployment verification.

Production: +18/-16 lines; tests: +106. The small production increase defines the worker's consumed result instead of transporting unused verification metadata.

prs.title: perf(gateway): omit session rows from hidden agent progress
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Observing a channel-routed run repeats a full session row on every non-tool agent progress event, even though bundled clients consume roster metadata from `sessions.changed` and `session.message`.

## User Impact

Live text, reasoning, item progress and lifecycle delivery keep their existing subscription, pacing and continuity semantics, with smaller agent payloads for exactly subscribed channel sessions. Native broad delivery and tool payloads are unchanged. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove session-row enrichment from the shared hidden-progress send path. Keep hidden tool enrichment with the tool producer, and carry `sessionId` from the admitted run/event so SDK identity survives without looking up the row. No new cache, timer, coalescer or subscription mode is introduced.

Production delta is +1 line: removing generic row enrichment saves 6 lines, retaining the existing tool envelope takes 4, and preserving the SDK's session identity takes 3. Tests shrink by 21 lines while retaining queued ownership, recipient replacement and streaming assertions.

## Producer and Consumer Audit

Embedded-agent reply delivery emits assistant/item progress; stream rendering emits thinking; tool start/progress/completion handlers emit tools and items; lifecycle handlers emit start/end. These converge on `src/infra/agent-events.ts` and the existing Gateway event handler. Ordinary spawned runs are not inherently hidden: the changed path is used by channel-routed runs that explicitly suppress broad Control UI delivery.

Capable web roster-only sockets already receive neither `agent` nor `session.tool` without exact subscriptions. The chat pane consumes text/reasoning/tool data; its live text uses the existing chat projection. Activity Current Work holds up to 100 full subscriptions but parses only tool and answer-candidate records (`ui/src/pages/activity/live-activity.ts`, `tool-activity.ts`). Sidebar narration holds at most six narration subscriptions. Session rows belong to `sessions.changed`/`session.message`, not these progress consumers. Apple, Android and TUI consumers likewise use progress identity/data; the SDK's optional `sessionId` is retained. Native broad delivery is unchanged.

The existing 75 ms producer pacing, per-recipient coalescing, chat-only assistant capability, append baselines and slow-write handling already cover the proposed coalescing work. This PR removes repeated row construction instead of adding another timer or subscription policy. Activity-only subscriptions and tool-output limits are separate work.

## Paired Measurement

Four concurrent A/B pairs compared baseline `3a5456567068` with candidate `9214fe285f7e` under an exclusive measurement lock. Each side used 16 cores; A/B alternated CPU halves 96–111 and 112–127. The measured starts were within 1 ms of each other (1–2 ms after the common barrier). Separate built Gateways, synthetic state, homes and loopback ports; Node 26.8.2. Builds/fixture generation used cores 64–95, with small sequential writes. Dirty pages stayed below 424 MiB during preparation and below 6 MiB at completed pair boundaries.

Each fixture contains 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 cron jobs and 12 real project worktrees. Transcripts are limited to 8 MiB; each agent database is about 53 MiB. Each side has ten socket clients: one foreground, six Activity-style full subscribers, one narration subscriber, one capable roster-only client and one legacy roster-only client. One normal RPC turn and three synthetic channel reply-dispatch turns each perform one real `read`, then receive 300 text deltas at 10 ms intervals and 75 reasoning deltas. This exercises the production channel/agent/broadcast path, with a mock SSE provider.

| Pair | A/B core halves | Agent bytes A → B (KiB/cohort) | Paired byte change | Main-thread CPU B−A (ms/cohort) | Foreground TTFT B−A (ms) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 96–111 / 112–127 | 2,456.5 → 2,233.3 | −9.09% | −16.57 | +16.85 |
| 2 | 112–127 / 96–111 | 2,461.9 → 2,228.9 | −9.46% | +23.84 | +4.96 |
| 3 | 96–111 / 112–127 | 2,377.3 → 2,227.9 | −6.28% | −15.68 | −20.48 |
| 4 | 112–127 / 96–111 | 2,380.0 → 2,228.1 | −6.38% | −11.98 | −36.65 |

Mean paired reduction: **193,897 agent bytes per four-turn cohort (7.83%)**, or 48,474 bytes/turn. Agent rates averaged 20.69 → 19.10 MB/min (decimal), a paired reduction of 1.59 MB/min. Event counts are neutral: 1,435.75 → 1,436/cohort and 12,005 → 12,016/min. Each run waited for 2.5 seconds without subscriber events after completion: pair 1 drained for about 4.82 seconds, pairs 2–4 for 2.51 seconds. Rates include that drain; cohort totals are the primary byte comparison.

Main-thread CPU is neutral: 1,278.94 → 1,273.84 ms/cohort (319.73 → 318.46 ms/turn; −0.40%), or 178.06 → 177.59 ms/second. This measures the entire Gateway main thread, including turn admission, tools, persistence and drain, not only serialization. Foreground TTFT averaged 958.64 → 949.81 ms; model-first-delta to subscriber averaged 5.64 → 3.21 ms. Inter-delta p50 was 75.21 → 75.20 ms and p95 76.20 → 76.32 ms. Per-pair p99 was noisy: A/B 75.96/87.97, 76.40/76.27, 76.43/76.59 and 79.80/85.83 ms (mean +4.52 ms; with 40–41 intervals, each p99 is also that run's maximum). There is no demonstrated CPU or streaming-speed improvement; median/p95 pacing is unchanged, with the small-sample p99 caveat retained.

`mpstat -P 96-127` was recorded for every pair. Mean utilization on the two halves during measurement was 2.72/2.59%, 3.41/3.32%, 3.44/3.35% and 3.35/3.33%, including benchmark work. This is context, not a run-validity filter.

### Delivery and Kind Counts

Mean agent deliveries per cohort, with bytes counted once per receiving socket:

| Recipient class | Agent events A → B | Agent bytes A → B | session.tool events / bytes (both) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Foreground exact | 54 → 54 | 85,359 → 85,232 | 0 / 0 |
| Six Activity exact clients | 1,248 → 1,248 | 2,193,723 → 2,024,016 | 12 / 94,596 |
| Narration exact | 40 → 40 | 108,437 → 84,432 | 2 / 15,766 |
| Capable roster only | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Legacy roster only | 93.75 → 94 | 89,463 → 89,406 | 2 / 15,766 |

Delivered agent kinds per cohort: thinking 1,066 plus 26 persisted-thinking events; lifecycle start/model/finishing/end 30/90/30/30; tool start/result 22/22; item/tool start/end 30/30; usage 18; assistant 41–42. Deduplicated observed kinds are respectively 164+4, 4/12/4/4, 4/4, 4/4, 2 and 41–42. These are observed deliveries after pacing, not an instrumented census of every internal producer event. The provider emitted exactly 1,200 assistant and 300 reasoning deltas per cohort. No separate status-tick or swarm-specific progress kind was observed. Non-tool nested-row field bytes fell from 129,344/cohort to zero; existing tool row fields remain.

The Activity clients account for about 89% of baseline agent bytes. Narrowing their subscription remains the larger separate opportunity; this patch removes redundant metadata without changing subscription ownership.

### Measurement Limits

This is a synthetic parallel channel/normal-turn workload, not an agent-created `sessions_spawn` swarm, live external channel or production traffic replay. Clients emulate capability sets; latency is measured at a Node subscriber, not browser paint or a native app. Initial provider requests synchronize before tool calls, while answer continuations start as their tools complete. Bytes are uncompressed JSON, excluding WebSocket/TCP framing. There is no injected slow consumer in this measurement; existing wire tests cover slow writes and baseline recovery.

Every accepted run reconstructed the exact final foreground text, preserved streamed prefixes, delivered all three channel finals, and reported no outer sequence gaps or missing chat baselines. Discarded setup/diagnostic runs exposed two harness issues: a missing synthetic-channel lifecycle callback and an assertion that incorrectly required the last incremental frame to contain the final tail. Both were corrected in the task-only harness; production code did not change. Only the four completed, swapped pairs above inform the result.

## Evidence

- The revised regression fails on the original code: non-tool events still contain `session` and query the row. Candidate: 84/84 agent-event tests pass (29.37 s Vitest wall; 34.02 s wrapper, including worker preparation).
- Wire and reasoning sibling coverage: 34/34 pass (13.41 s Vitest wall; 16.80 s wrapper), including append reconstruction, late subscribers, slow writes and chat-only recipients.
- Changed-file oxfmt, repository oxlint and `git diff --check` pass. Broad typecheck/build/suite proof belongs to PR CI. No Testbox or Crabbox lease was used.
- Independent Codex autoreview: no accepted/actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Four concurrent split-core pairs pass the production-path text, channel-final, sequence and baseline checks above. Candidate build and baseline build were prepared only for measurement; PR CI owns broad validation.
- [PR CI run 39070558201](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39070558201) passed on exact head `9214fe285f7ef2e9454a2ecd41f18d98f86f2159`, including changed-code tests, typechecks, UI checks and all three PostgreSQL conformance shards. Dependency review and security-sensitive review passed; the independent GitHub code review also reported no findings. No CI rerun was needed.

prs.title: refactor: keep internal core helpers with their owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Private single-consumer helpers split agent tool finalization, terminal outcomes, secret warning projection and node-host operations away from their existing owners. Some exist only to transfer the same facts into a one-use adapter.

## User Impact

No supported behavior or public contract changes. Tool descriptors, executor bindings, warning refresh, node lifecycle, read presentation, group policy and prompt text remain with their existing owners.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep descriptor snapshot preparation in the existing tool finalizer, removing the one-use normalization/bind/settle adapter while preserving detached immutable descriptors, complete cache keys, bounds, sharing, prewarming and lifecycle clearing. Keep read presentation, terminal error recording and write no-progress interpretation local to their actual owners. Fold dotenv audit and provider-auth warning projection into the existing secret operations. Keep the node-host journal configuration, launcher, desktop launch and update-pause operations in their actual execution owners. Remove the unused internal tagged policy result and exercise group formatting through the real conversation-context entry point.

This is an area slice of the wider single-consumer internal-surface family under the campaign's rule 11. At signed head c4c0798c3739cd7218d811b2dcc7a2262f542a4c against dc4b96e6d4580c272f2a324a1b5ff9209e939b38, production changes are +470/-610 across 30 paths: **140 net production lines removed**. The full cut touches 41 paths. Moved implementations count as additions, not deleted behavior.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None. No guard or supported behavior is removed. Preserve authorization at effects, write settlement, ordinary concurrency, lifecycle cleanup, bounded caches, provider warning replacement, launch containment, subprocess cancellation and exact group-policy behavior. No configuration, protocol, dependency, persisted schema, durability, retention or permission changes. The standalone Phase E session-memory backend, factory, registry, expiry, federation and all its tests are untouched.

## Evidence

The recovered four-slice branch received a fresh independent P0-P2 scoped-clean review (0.96). The descriptor-finalizer append received a fresh independent P0-P2 scoped-clean review (0.99). The complete existing finalizer test remains unchanged; migrated tests retain production-boundary assertions rather than replacement test-only exports. Current main's shallow secret-copy behavior, bounded supervisor error logging and removed node-host platform injection remain intact. Normal signed commit hooks, canonical formatting and whitespace checks pass.

The author simplification pass retains the existing operations as the only owners: no replacement service, DTO, compatibility branch or test-only production export is introduced. All moved implementation lines count as additions; only superseded private seams disappear. Existing descriptor sharing, immutable publication, complete cache inputs and lifecycle clearing remain rather than being treated as redundant functionality.

Focused isolated one-worker proof completed successfully on the prior reviewed head 53833193eb174cb9d83e1ddd85164f4673f3faa4: **4 files / 63 tests passed**, comprising suppression 14, provider-auth warnings 3, terminal outcomes 31 and finalizer 15. The three shards completed in 967.40 seconds; the isolated wrapper exited 0 with no signal after 977.5 seconds, including compiler-generation verification and cleanup. This terminal result was recovered after the connection interruption; it was not rerun for green. Targeted types, other owner siblings and broad proof remain pending. No full local build, broad typecheck, E2E or live operator-state test is claimed; exact-head hosted PR CI owns broad proof. No assertion, timeout, retry, skip or allowance was weakened.

GitHub reported a real modify/delete conflict after main b79af97db6c made OpenAI wire descriptors request-owned. Conflict-only replay onto dc4b96e6d4580c272f2a324a1b5ff9209e939b38 preserves that change in the folded finalizer: only schema normalization is prewarmed; the deleted shared wire-descriptor prewarming is not restored. The first replayed commit is patch-identical; range comparison limits the second commit's delta to main's prewarming change at its new owner. Fresh independent P0-P2 resolution review is scoped-clean (0.99), canonical formatting and focused syntax/boundary lint pass, and both replayed commits have verified signatures.

On the replayed head, the isolated one-worker suppression suite passed all 14 tests (122.27 seconds Vitest). The affected finalizer suite failed before collecting any cases because this dedicated checkout lacks the package-local `mdast-util-from-markdown` dependency imported by markdown-core; its worker preparation/import path took 904.96 seconds. This is an uncovered current-head finalizer proof, not a passing replay or an attributed product regression. No dependency install, timeout, retry, assertion or allowance was changed. Exact-head hosted PR CI must provide the affected finalizer and broad proof.

Run 39064091859 on 6eaff1d948b9be5c3c28bba1878e2af52e19a9f3 completed with seven PR-caused failing proof jobs (plus the aggregate gate): check-prompt-snapshots, checks-node-compact-small-2, checks-node-changed-compact-small-10, check-test-types, and check-test-types-core-1/-3/-5. All identify the same two missed fixture imports of the now-private group formatter. Build artifacts, production types, lint, architecture/ratchet checks and the other selected test shards passed. The signed two-file repair migrates those fixture calls to the existing conversation-context owner; their explicit group/channel context selects the identical private formatter. No prompt string, option, assertion or snapshot changes. Fresh independent P0-P2 repair review is scoped-clean (0.99), with final source verification complete.

With that exact repair, isolated one-worker composition proof passes 1 file / 2 tests (959.60 seconds Vitest), and suppression proof passes 14 tests (88.65 seconds). The snapshot suite did not enter its 13 cases because this dedicated checkout lacked Codex's package-local smol-toml dependency; the combined command exited 1 after 2,047.0 seconds including verification. The pinned Codex manifest is unchanged from the installed checkout. An absent-only link to its existing package dependencies corrected the setup without installing or changing dependencies. The snapshot-only local replay was stopped during worker compilation once exact-head hosted CI completed successfully; it is not counted as a local pass.

Exact-head hosted CI [39067150884](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39067150884) completed successfully on c4c0798c3739cd7218d811b2dcc7a2262f542a4c. The exact-head watcher reports GREEN, excluding superseded old-head contexts. No CI rerun or inherited-failure exception was used. The local setup failures and incomplete replay above remain separate from that passing hosted proof.

prs.title: fix(codex): render dynamic tool images in chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex dynamic tools can return image content successfully, but the durable transcript projection flattened those images to text. Control UI then hid or rolled up the surviving tool result, and chat-history budgeting replaced a typical screenshot-sized message with a message-too-large placeholder. The result was a successful computer screenshot that never rendered in chat.

## What Changed

- Preserve validated dynamic-tool image outputs as top-level transcript image blocks.
- Replace invalid inline image payloads with safe explanatory text.
- Keep image-bearing tool results outside completed-work and activity rollups.
- Render tool-result images even when tool details are collapsed or tool calls are hidden.
- Give image-bearing history messages a bounded 1 MiB per-message allowance while preserving the 128 KiB ordinary-message cap and existing total-history cap.

## Evidence

- Seven focused Codex projector, chat grouping/rendering, and history-budget suites: 387 tests passed.
- Changed-file Oxlint: passed.
- Changed-file Oxfmt check: passed.
- Full pnpm build, including Control UI compressed assets and performance checks: passed.
- Live pinned CUA Driver 0.19.0 gateway replay: the stored screenshot survives chat.history as toolResult + image with a 418,067-character data URL and no omitted-message placeholder.
- Live Control UI verification: the Linux XFCE screenshot visibly renders inline with the Computer screenshot tool result.

## Impact

Computer screenshots and other dynamic-tool images survive transcript persistence, history transport, grouping, and rendering, so they appear inline in Control UI chat without requiring users to expand tool details.

prs.title: fix(message): status replies do not open ClawHub cards
prs.body:
Supersedes #151791 with a current-main refresh. This version keeps existing nonblank query-only ClawHub recommendation requests valid instead of requiring a new `intent` field.

## What Problem This Solves

Routine status replies can accidentally open ClawHub recommendation cards when a model combines ordinary send content with a `clawhub` payload.

## User Impact

Explicit nonblank query-only recommendation requests keep working. The current patch rejects mixed ordinary-send payloads before catalog discovery or conversation persistence. Optional card copy belongs in `clawhub.intro`.

Compatibility note: the mixed-send contract still requires an explicit maintainer decision. Callers that intentionally combined top-level `message` with `clawhub` would need to move that text to `clawhub.intro` if strict rejection is accepted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime validates the recommendation branch before any catalog lookup, sanitizes nested intro text through the existing visible-text guard, and keeps prompt/schema/docs guidance aligned. Recommendation lookup still returns only official cards with Gateway-derived installation state and never installs a capability automatically.

## Evidence

- Exact published head: `980a08a346bfb0e417a60131c5e3675575b46209`
- Publication chain: `95a421137ff39a012cf0111225c1396b4a458832 -> a33ae5870f353e48300b00811e780b9f54b76ad1 -> 980a08a346bfb0e417a60131c5e3675575b46209`
- Detached Mac isolated validation passed at the substantive head: `20/20` focused ClawHub integration tests, exit `0`, using `openclaw-validation-deps:f6339e90e37` and a network-disabled harness.
- The follow-up head changes formatting only. The corrected test file was produced by pinned `oxfmt 0.72.0`, matched locally by SHA-256 `fe393482d836d9894e99900b707c458dbc7023819844f2bd35e727729d6a4926`, and passes `git diff --check` plus the staged-content scan.
- The broader Mac agents-tools shard remains separately classified as unavailable because the projected image lacks `@solidjs/vite-plugin`; it did not exercise this focused test file.
- Focused coverage includes query-only compatibility, mixed status rejection before discovery/persistence, blank-query rejection, intro sanitization, installed-state replay, official-card limits, and absence of automatic installation.
- Fresh hosted CI is running at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39070610107. The required `openclaw/ci-gate` result remains a gate.
- Fresh exact-head ClawSweeper review requested at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175358#issuecomment-6241288962.
- Required Control UI behavior canary/screenshot evidence remains pending; no production deployment or restart is part of this PR.

prs.title: test(core,ui,scripts): remove low-value tests (batch d235)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Replay batch d235 onto current main to reduce repetitive test fixture, request, and assertion scaffolding. This is test maintenance only: no production behavior, configuration, dependency, or release changes.

All 30 requested commits were replayed in order. Some file-level portions were dropped where they depended on an unlisted precursor or overlapped newer main tests. Existing security, recovery, lifecycle, and protocol assertions take precedence over reduction targets.

## Scope and impact

84 changed test/support files: +11,577 / -17,919 lines, net -6,342. Production: +0 / -0. The mock-export ratchet additionally removes two obsolete allowlist rows (+0 / -2); 85 changed files overall. The test-support split is included in these totals. Static test declaration counts are source counts, not expanded runtime case counts; table consolidation can reduce declarations without reducing cases.

| Shard | Test/support LOC before → after (net) | Static declarations before → after | In-shard coverage totals |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| x7838 | 263 → 255 (-8) | 2 → 2 | Not run (CI-only) |
| x7844 | 3293 → 2649 (-644) | 35 → 32 | Not run (CI-only) |
| x7841 | 2963 → 2336 (-627) | 25 → 24 | Not run (CI-only) |
| x7845 | 2708 → 2141 (-567) | 70 → 66 | Not run (CI-only) |
| x7846 | 3304 → 2599 (-705) | 46 → 31 | Not run (CI-only) |
| x7848 | 3335 → 2864 (-471) | 90 → 83 | Not run (CI-only) |
| x7842 | 2368 → 1930 (-438) | 41 → 38 | Not run (CI-only) |
| x7850 | 3018 → 2680 (-338) | 55 → 54 | Not run (CI-only) |
| x7849 | 3052 → 2460 (-592) | 101 → 93 | Not run (CI-only) |
| x7856 | 3036 → 2277 (-759) | 57 → 57 | Not run (CI-only) |
| x7853 | 3279 → 2679 (-600) | 54 → 52 | Not run (CI-only) |
| x7854 | 3277 → 2684 (-593) | 86 → 78 | Not run (CI-only) |

The supplied shard reports contain no coverage totals: they explicitly state tests and coverage were not run under CI-only mode. Their earlier LOC/case snapshots precede the complete replayed commit series; the table above is recomputed from the actual pinned-base diff. No new coverage-percentage or runtime-speed claim is made.

## Replay decisions

- x7838: retained the independent process-fixture cleanup. Dropped changes to preflight-frozen-target-contracts, preinstall-package-manager-warning, prepare-extension-package-boundary-artifacts.native, prepare-git-hooks, prepare-vitest-runtime, and prepublish-plugin-registry-shell: the supplied series omits the precursor introducing their helper fixtures.
- x7844: kept main's two successful memory/wiki lookup cases and adapted them to the compact table.
- x7848: kept main's no-package-type CommonJS resolution and import/probe tests; dropped later conflicting check-package-dist-imports rewrites. Kept the positive embedded-agent sessionTarget case while compacting surrounding accessor tests.
- x7842: dropped inference-proxy rewrites during replay; after CI/review, also restored model-catalog.test.ts to the pinned base, preserving WebSocket/stdio remote transport, discovery-timeout, native-auth and catalog ownership coverage.
- x7850: retained current session-catalog import-ceiling and deduplication coverage; dropped conflicting later rewrites of that file. Corrected preserved callers to await the current promise-returning import helper and pass an explicit paging spy.
- x7853: retained current workspace recovery rollback/manifest coverage, dropping the two later conflicting rewrites of workspace-reconcile-recovery.
- x7854: retained main's hosted setup and memory-import cases; dropped the later conflicting operations-setup-flows rewrite.

No complete commit was skipped. The only baseline change is deletion of the two exact stale mock-export rows reported by CI; no exemptions were added or broadened. No changed path matches an explicit CODEOWNERS rule at the pinned base.

## CI and review corrections

The initial head's [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39064441624) exposed fixture/type failures in batch-touched files. No inherited-failure or admin exception is requested.

- Restored five files to the pinned base: model-catalog.test.ts, terminal-tool.test.ts, services.scheduler-context.test.ts, plugins-credentials.e2e.test.ts, and browser-tab-preview.test.ts. Their consolidation had dropped distinct transport coverage, rebuilt identity-bound contexts, exposed unbound methods, or broken fixture/browser contracts.
- Initialized personal-background browser mock responses before navigation rather than calling a not-yet-installed mock; retained the light/dark assertions.
- Corrected the page helper to await and return void, typed the request mock against its actual Gateway contract, used the database engine connection contract in Doctor helpers, and asserted the SQLite revision's numeric type before comparisons.
- Restored per-mock isolation explanations, removed unnecessary helper generics, retained an explicit Error for the self-archive abort, and derived skill install refs from the fixture's effective owner and slug.
- Independent full-diff review completed four passes with three findings. All accepted: numeric revision typing, remote-transport coverage, and skill install-reference consistency. None rejected. The corrective commit passed its additional focused review with no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- The second head passed the prior fixture/type failures but its mock-exports ratchet identified one compacted native-turn mock. Added its required isolation explanation; no mock behavior changed.
- After adding that explanation, the next ratchet run identified exactly two stale allowlist rows: the explained bounded-turn mock and the second occurrence of the consolidated process-fixture mock. Removed those two rows after source verification, keeping the first process-fixture occurrence.
- A late Doctor auth-consumer run exposed raw auth-profile writes outside the owner transaction (`auth_profile_store` was not initialized). Restored the original `runAuthProfileWriteTransaction` fixture boundary, retaining the compact fixtures and all three migration cases.
- The initial PR-context heading failure was corrected to the repository's exact template headings; the replacement context check passed.
- The Doctor transaction repair passed its focused independent review with no actionable findings.
- The subsequent head passed the batch's changed-file checks but PostgreSQL conformance (1/3) timed out in the unchanged `port-command.postgres.test.ts` refusal test. The same test and 60-second timeout are present in completed main CI run [39066988478](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39066988478/job/117496810269). Current main already carries `f15a2b8f938`, which moves that contract intact to the reusable-worker fixture without increasing its timeout. Rebased onto `6ebd9d9dd9ffd9d627effa6c3988e8a75a69e5fb` to include that repair. All 35 commits replayed without conflicts; `git range-diff` confirms every batch/repair patch is unchanged. No admin exception or CI rerun was used.

## Evidence

- Base pinned before replay: `da6e8aa17eba90412624afe0c890d09958ca2186`.

prs.title: fix: recover Workboard after SQLite worker failures
prs.body:
Fixes #169981

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Workboard staying unavailable until Gateway restart after its shared SQLite worker fails.

## User Impact

Workboard reads and writes recover on the next call once the underlying storage problem is resolved. Logbook and Team Reports use the same recovery owner. Operations already in flight retain their failure or unknown-write outcome and are never replayed automatically. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reopening a handle alone can reuse the same failed actor when another client retains it. The broker now joins its existing actor retirement before opening again, and retained engine stores reacquire a usable handle. Workboard's duplicate logical connection protocol is removed so the broker owns the kernel's lifetime.

Main already removed the once-per-second external-change check in #167965. This completes recovery without restoring polling.

## Evidence

### Broker conflict resolution and current validation

Current head: `871df1563850984b09efa60785a19952aee24ff8`, after merging main `b70cab277ca2c5480117c3a2ecae09a54027ada0` without rebasing. Only `src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.ts` conflicted. The resolution keeps failed-actor retirement before a client acquires main's new scheduled-maintenance hold, and preserves both hold-release paths. Main's pending-dispatch admission wait and shutdown write drainage remain intact. Failed or uncertain writes are not replayed.

Local validation on this merge: all four broker files passed (41 tests, 125.81s), and all eight selected Workboard/Logbook/Team Reports storage and lifecycle files passed (119 tests, 200.66s); 369.82s total command wall time. Workboard's retained-sibling recovery case passed in 4.240s. The production-only negative control replaced only the eight production files with this main revision and retained the regression: the next lookup failed with `database is locked`, as expected (242.06s including cold runtime preparation).

`pnpm tsgo:core` (47.26s), `pnpm tsgo:core:test --ci-graphs-json '["core-test-infra"]'` (74.87s), targeted broker oxlint (27.10s), oxfmt (0.51s), and `git diff --check` passed. The prescribed independent review of the conflict resolution is clean through P2. The original real-Gateway evidence below remains prior-head proof; this merge was validated locally.

Exact-head [CI run 38313101657](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38313101657) completed successfully: 49 jobs passed, 23 skipped, zero failed. All selected Node suites, UI, PostgreSQL conformance, production/test typechecks, lint, source contracts, and the aggregate CI gate passed. No inherited-failure exception was needed for this run.

- Original live-proof candidate: 48f3e676add98834bdae39a7056d7be5451d1174, after merging main 9b00610bd3cb30459d971fe22acb4a58a8c97280. The merge preserves main’s explicit Workboard transaction and commit admission checks.
- All 52 SQLite-worker/database-engine owner and direct-caller test files, including the affected PostgreSQL and SQLite transaction suites, pass: 431 tests passed, one skipped; 160.88-second runner (161-second stage).
- All 59 Workboard, Logbook, and Team Reports test files ran: 693 tests passed, 11 skipped, two unchanged failures reproduced on main; 304.70-second runner. The real-worker recovery regression and lifecycle tests pass; the recovery test body takes 1.494 seconds.
- Production-only negative control fails the next Workboard lookup with the retained database-is-locked error (28-second stage). The regression holds two real Workboard facades on the same actor.
- Real isolated Gateway on fresh AWS Crabbox: baseline fails three repeated statistics calls until restart; the live-proof candidate succeeds on the first post-fault call and subsequent read/write calls in the same Gateway process.
- Original branch autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Deslop removes 58 net production lines.
- All four typecheck lanes pass on the original live-proof head: core 76s, infrastructure-test shard 65s, extensions 90s, extension tests 130s. Targeted core/extension lint passes with no warnings or errors (205s/32s); formatting and diff whitespace checks pass.
- The compiled Gateway runtime build passes on the original live-proof head: the supported qaRuntime profile completes in 67 seconds. The batch exits nonzero solely because of the two inherited test failures described below.
- The supported full runtime build passed on the previous candidate 2a316a9bae3d81b315f71cb10154baeabde93a80: pnpm build:runtime (720.30 seconds, including runtime bundles, all 96 plugin distributions, bootstrap guards, UI, and metadata).

<details>
<summary>Commands, leases, live excerpts, and inherited failures</summary>

Baseline owner source: 8eae8c826dd97a0d25569cbe4e93545a26d85aea. The negative control preserves the regression and replaces only the eight production files with main's versions.

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/workboard/src/sqlite-store.recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/workboard/src/sqlite-store.recovery.test.ts extensions/workboard/src/sqlite-store.lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
    pnpm tsgo:core
    pnpm tsgo:core:test --ci-graphs-json '["core-test-infra"]'
    pnpm tsgo:extensions
    pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime
    pnpm build:runtime

The full owner inventory contains every SQLite-worker test, every database-engine directory test, and all direct test importers, plus all three plugin source suites and index tests. The run records the 52-file core inventory and executes both complete inventories through scripts/run-vitest.mjs.

Baseline/restart: AWS lease cbx_41237cfd86d0, r7a.xlarge, [run evidence](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_56656ea5c43cac89f6909ecee94e3c5c). PID 3617 returns the same synthetic database-is-locked error three times; restart PID 4292 reads the persisted card (total: 1). Baseline/restart stages: 87/114 seconds.

Original live-proof candidate: fresh AWS lease cbx_af08237f5708, r7a.xlarge, [run evidence](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_77997d301ff5c6133d604052faee8f1e). The lease verified about 30 GiB RAM and ran without credential hydration.

    CRABBOX_ENV_ALLOW=CI crabbox run --provider aws --id cbx_af08237f5708 --no-hydrate --no-sync --timing-json --script aws-integration-proof.sh
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .workboard-slot-live-proof.ts fixed

    before-fault: pid=8399, port=35353, agents=[main, worker-a, worker-b]
     after-fault: attempt=1 ok=true; attempt=2 ok=true; attempt=3 ok=true
    recovered-write: ok=true, pid=8399
    WORKBOARD_SLOT_LIVE_PROOF_PASS

The synthetic driver starts the real Gateway, creates three agent sessions, and calls Workboard through GatewayClient WebSocket RPCs. It induces terminal slot failure with the existing Worker error event seam. The 90-second run uses isolated state and an ephemeral port and shuts down cleanly. Actual disk exhaustion, lock contention, model turns, and the original macOS incident environment were not exercised.

Two inherited failures remain in unchanged native-backend tests:

- Logbook store-read-budgets: schema admission on reopen.
- Team Reports store-read-budget: admitted persistent schema on reopen.

Both close every native connection, then expect admission facts to survive. Main commit 19eddcf75194e (#169956) intentionally retires those facts on the final native close. With all eight changed production files reverted to main b8ab5dee86cf9fa2ea6682275bed4edd39a4269e, the same two assertions fail and 12 other tests pass (84.16-second runner; 112.99-second outer wall):

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/logbook/src/store-read-budgets.test.ts extensions/team-reports/src/store-read-budget.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

The fixtures and assertions are unchanged by this PR. Scheduled main run 38285052539 had other failures but supplied no matching signatures for these two tests; attribution here uses the direct baseline reproduction.

The previous candidate’s remote batch was stopped after all required unit/live/type/lint stages completed, before repeating broader global declaration generation. A preliminary all-infra selection was also stopped during unrelated E2E build preparation. Those broader runs are not reported as passes; the completed scope is the full owning modules/direct callers above plus the supported runtime build.

Production +139/-197 (net -58); tests +86/-154 (net -68); docs +8/-0. Total: 14 files, +233/-351.

</details>


### Previous landing-attempt evidence

Reviewed landing head: `c4526d00cd39fe9c55d11b72aab6b0b2bb155cbc`. [CI run 38303665062, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38303665062) completed on GitHub merge `9fadb4795da0e819a877f730d58961cfa0402798` against main `24dec4d6c370c9ac1b8f1f534efc20e8b37dd27a`. All selected jobs passed except `checks-node-changed-compact-small-5` and its aggregate gate.

The failed job contains exactly two inherited failures in unchanged `src/config/sessions/session-pending-input-operations.test.ts`: “keeps host-created synchronous completion usable through the SDK compatibility window” and “reports a withdrawn input only after confirmed cancellation: consumed”. Both report `Runtime config is not prepared. Await captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader()() first.` The same cases and error appear in [scheduled main job 114956274893](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38292584060/job/114956274893), and the coordinator reproduced them on clean main `930bb545e38b`. The latest scheduled main run, 38298274614, was inspected; its different shard layout yields no matching job, so the automated table says unknown. Direct case comparison supplies the attribution. Native inherited-failure landing is authorized; CI remains failed, not green.

The earlier Logbook/Team Reports schema-admission failures were fixed on main by `5168930e11e23` and are not failures in this exact-head CI run. UI, typechecks, lint, PostgreSQL conformance, and security-fast passed. No PR code or head changed during landing.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): preserve frozen capabilities for same-owner steering
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Compatible owner messages can be queued behind a busy or recovered turn because incoming browser discovery facts or an active completion’s policy provenance are compared as replacement execution authority.

## User Impact

The same authenticated owner can steer compatible busy turns while retaining their existing tools and personal destinations. No configuration or migration is required. Optional-reply completion turns retain their existing reply-expectation guard.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the prepared owner’s normalization before the early adoption comparison as well as overlay projection. A capability superset cannot expand the active turn’s frozen capabilities or add a personal destination. For human owner input joining an existing trusted completion, projection retains that completion’s verified handoff and provenance; the incoming message and its provenance remain unchanged.

All other incoming permission, scope, model, tool-binding and live authority checks remain authoritative. Reduced capabilities, reduced privileges, different-profile changes, peer-origin messages and revoked handoffs remain rejected. The separate terminal-reply expectation publication fix is not included here.

Related: #170216. This complements #165122’s execution-route compatibility work.

## Evidence

The earlier client-envelope regression and actual-native positive/revocation proofs remain applicable to the unchanged normalization semantics. The added canonical handoff regression exercises real admission, prepared authority, registered direct target, inbound overlay and injection, including reduced scopes, revoked source/cohort, different profile, peer provenance, post-projection revocation and optional-reply controls.

On the preceding implementation revision, 33 focused tests pass (nine canonical direct-handoff cases and 24 early-adoption cases). Core types, both owning test type graphs, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. Fresh P0–P2 review found no actionable issues. An isolated actual-Gateway/native-provider test using only synthetic conversation content also passed: a model-created child produced a new busy direct completion, authenticated owner steering reached that captured target, the verified handoff remained retained, and the original direct provider run finished with the injected marker. The marker was absent from the initial prompt/transcript; the final was a provider result, not a Gateway fallback or provenance mirror. The task Gateway stopped and its temporary authentication copy was removed. This combined runtime proof also included the separate reply-expectation publication fix; that fix is not part of this PR. Earlier actual-native capability and canonical-device-revocation proof covers the discovery normalization path. No live incident content or production configuration is used in the fixtures. Exact live fingerprint preimages were unavailable, so the tests establish these concrete failure classes rather than claiming every observed queue had the same cause.


The combined runtime was subsequently activated in the operator’s local Gateway; RPC health and plugin loading pass. Separate retained-turn recovery errors remain under investigation. The isolated same-direct-run native-provider proof above establishes the steering behavior; deployment alone does not establish that every historical hang is resolved.


### Architecture CI repair

The new full-input type import introduced a static dependency cycle through queued execution state. The normalization contract now depends only on the existing lightweight client-discovery fields, while a generic preserves the caller’s full input type and all other fields. No runtime normalization or authority check changes. The actual architecture check now reports zero cycles; all 33 focused cases, scoped type-aware lint, formatting and fresh P0–P2 review pass on the corrected source. The cold local core type check exceeded its 600-second budget without diagnostics; the owning test graph was stopped under host memory pressure. Exact-head CI for `76eed159575c95001bf5a9582116fe986d6bcdee` now passes, including production types, test types, lint, runtime checks, and `openclaw/ci-gate` ([CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39069762409)). This supplies the previously pending type-check evidence; earlier local type results above apply to the preceding revision.

### Inspectable synthetic native results

This is an allowlisted projection of actual isolated RPC/provider and final-effect readbacks. The run labels preserve the observed equality of the steering target and provider-final owner. The capability-positive and direct-handoff runtimes also include the separate reply-expectation publication fix. prs.title: fix(database): avoid redundant recovery capture isolation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL archive recovery, port verification, and upgrade rollback repeatedly isolate SQLite images that are already owned by the recovery operation. The main hourly still timed out after #175774; that earlier improvement did not resolve the cluster.

## User Impact

PostgreSQL backup and recovery capture does less work while retaining the same source isolation, integrity checks, sanitization, exact rollback data, and publish-last behavior. No schema, format, timeout, or permission changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture copied the live anchor to identify its engine, then copied it again into the archive. It now derives provider identity from the verified archive image. The newly created private PostgreSQL export also uses the existing in-process snapshot acquisition path inside its owning worker, avoiding another child process without exposing any live source descriptor.

Port migration and staging now read their exclusively owned private SQLite images directly inside the native worker. Reverse staging uses the existing in-process acquisition mode, and verifies its own staged target without another child snapshot. Published-source inspection and verification retain process isolation. Physical-store helpers are imported from their owner instead of the backup orchestration graph.

The same repair removes two orphan exports and moves asynchronous file-identity helpers beside their existing synchronous counterparts. `sqlite-snapshot.ts` falls from 701 to 648 counted lines without deleting checks or coverage.

## Evidence

- Native Node 24.21/PostgreSQL 17 archive profile: 147.662s total, including 77.909s capture, 32.910s restore and 17.097s Gateway startup. Seven-store seed/copy work took 1.475s. A warm baseline was 102.058s; these are busy-host observations, not a controlled percentage claim.
- The new work-count regression fails on the base: one redundant live-anchor acquisition, expected zero. The repaired backup regression passes, including the private export acquisition check.
- All three archive-restore cases pass unchanged: 98.699s full five-family plus retained Matrix-root rehydration and Gateway startup; 54.854s mixed-engine/config-alias recovery; 30.612s legacy-export preservation and failed-provider cleanup. Native wrapper 221.35s, `--maxWorkers=1`.
- Snapshot lifecycle/publication tests: 73 passed, 2 existing platform skips, 76.66s wrapper. Read-worker and compile-cache tests: 35 passed, 53.65s wrapper. These use the same native entry point as `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`.
- Infra and state/logging test type graphs, targeted type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks pass. Independent P2 autoreview: no actionable findings.
- The two requested dead exports are absent from the full export scan. The scan remains red on 18 untouched findings in other owners; no suppression or baseline change was added.
- All 11 Doctor migration cases and the backup regression pass across the valid runs. Agent v27 rollback: 36.396s/35.980s; v30 rollback: 42.548s. Three cases initially lacked the disposable database's `unaccent` extension; installing the prerequisite and rerunning those cases resolved the setup failures without source/test changes.
- Matrix/port/updater-preflight: 14/14 pass, 522.35s native wrapper with `--maxWorkers=1`. Full retained-root port/restore 162.386s; partial-publication resume 109.281s; partial-publication rollback 46.118s; real privilege/wrong-owner/RLS/refusal boundaries 35.970s. One earlier command named a nonexistent preflight file and executed no tests; the corrected command passed.
- Changed regression cost: `src/infra/database-engine/backup.test.ts` ran through the native PostgreSQL conformance wrapper with `--maxWorkers=1`; its retained user/Git/exact-update round trip, including the added assertions, took 28.771s. No test timeout, retry, skip, or assertion was loosened.

The existing three-shard PostgreSQL rebalance landed separately as 58ef51f9ecf6. PR CI remains the broad proof for this production change.

### Port and Matrix follow-up

The first PR CI passed archive restoration and Doctor rollback, but timed out in the standalone refusal case and full Matrix flow. The next Matrix case then selected the suite-wide home and failed with a missing-config preflight error. Port preflight, migration checking and fixture ordering are unchanged from main at 7d81a7d13af9. A timed-out test body can later restore its environment over the next fixture; the ordered Matrix replay passes the original Doctor-first guidance assertion without changing it.

The profile measured 21 migration/staging source acquisitions at 17.894 seconds total; 28 reference-catalog builds together cost 2.076 seconds. This change removes the redundant acquisitions instead of changing catalog validation. The full Matrix case was 130.350 seconds in the instrumented baseline and 129.830 seconds after the change on this host, so no end-to-end percentage improvement is claimed.

The existing canonical round-trip regression now also counts private-image isolation. It fails before this follow-up with ten redundant calls and passes afterward with zero. Its repaired case took 42.277 seconds in the six-file native run. The single-file negative control took 57.77 seconds including Vitest preparation (32.103 seconds in the case). Commands use the native PostgreSQL conformance entry point and `--maxWorkers=1`, equivalent to the repository's focused `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` path with the PostgreSQL environment prepared.

The six-file native replay passed 56 tests and timed out only the standalone refusal fixture. All three Matrix cases passed in file order: full flow 129.830s, partial-publication resume 68.109s, rollback 28.824s. Command custody, source/config drift, exact rollback, lost-COMMIT reconciliation, mixed-family operations, all recovery fault injections and worker refusals passed. Vitest duration: 1181.10s.

The refusal fixture fix then landed on main as f15a2b8f9380 (#175655). Its exact file contents were checked against the local extraction. The final focused two-file run passed 6/6 tests, including the unchanged privilege/owner/RLS/catalog/resume case in 20.078s (156.13s Vitest, 174.71s wrapper including cold preparation). Together these completed runs cover 57 unique cases across seven files; the 56 unaffected passes were not rerun.

Targeted infrastructure test types, type-aware lint, formatting, diff checks and the database-worker ratchet pass. Independent P2 autoreview is scoped-clean. Every existing assertion and timeout remains.

The standalone refusal fixture move from Peter-authored #175655 is now on main (f15a2b8f9380). The identical local extraction passed and was removed from this branch to avoid duplicating the landed fix. Environment-sensitive preflights retain their fresh-worker file. The remaining change here is the production private-image optimization and its work-count regression. Recent open-PR file lists and main history contain no duplicate of that owner change.
