prs.title: refactor(gateway): simplify terminal persistence handoff
prs.body:
Related: #131561

## What Problem This Solves

The eager lifecycle writer and lazy chat consumer exchange one already-started
terminal write through a second serialized receipt protocol. That protocol
duplicates runtime event identity with claim/generation/run/sequence keys,
expiry timers, settled/expired flags and destructive lookup.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Terminal status still persists eagerly, uses
the original physical session target and preserves authorization, FIFO ordering
and ordinary shutdown settlement. No operator action or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the original runtime event through both callers and use it as the weak key
for the existing persistence promise. Observation and consumption reuse the same
fulfillment or rejection; a separately reconstructed event cannot borrow it.
Carry a differing client run ID as a private fact into the writer's existing
explicit worker-event projection, rather than cloning the event in each caller.

Eager durability, captured physical target/write context, live claim and source
checks at commit, per-session/global-alias FIFO, deferred non-definitive errors,
root work admission and ordinary shutdown drain remain with their current owners.
There is no new persistence path, timer, fence or public contract.

This is one terminal-persistence AREA split from the wider parked family:
14 paths, five production files, +18/-119 = 101 net production lines removed
after formatting. No schema, persisted shape, protocol/config/SDK, dependency,
permission, retention or durability change. Phase E standalone session-memory
backend/factory/registry/expiry/federation and coverage remain intact. Its
provider-review fixture has only the constructor and orphan scheduler migration;
both cases, assertions, actual write gate, worker-operation spy and drain remain.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Equivalent reconstructed events no longer exchange terminal receipts. The
  runtime emitter and its real consumers already pass the original event.
  #132309 added the serialized lookup and expiry with controlled regressions;
  no separate human incident establishes a need for that exchange protocol.
  An unobserved definitive event refuses with the existing stale-lifecycle error,
  including when it has no sequence. No fallback writer is added.
- An original event retained after settlement may still retrieve its existing
  outcome rather than expiring after an arbitrary minute. This is not a new
  write or renewed authority. Weak keys do not retain abandoned events, and
  shutdown joins accepted work before clearing the table.
- The owner no longer copies an internally owned event before persistence.
  These internal consumers do not mutate it; the current worker adapter still
  explicitly projects private metadata instead of transporting host callbacks.

Human report #131561 describes a successful Telegram turn left running for
roughly 15 minutes. Its eager-durability repair is deliberately retained, along
with the original physical target and effect checks. Synthetic handoff controls
are not used to justify deleting that real repair.

## Evidence

Fresh independent P0–P2 review completed all six passes, scoped-clean
(confidence .85), covering every changed file and 193 intact unchanged context
files. The complete diff and 208-file capture were verified before and after.
One unchanged secrets-runtime fixture dependency was excluded under the review
helper's sensitive-path guard, explicitly declared as a scope limitation; no
guard was bypassed and no secrets-runtime review is claimed.

The owner cases retain source/claim refusal, FIFO/global aliases, deferred
errors and drain, and cover distinct equal-ID events and same fulfilled/rejected
promise reuse. A real-database chat/owner/worker-writer case checks exact promise
identity and the persisted remapped run ID. The existing source-authority Stop
case uses its production canonical writer directly instead of a test-only
unobserved terminal handoff; its source, SQL and effect assertions remain.

The physically owned frozen install passed in 250.95 seconds, reusing 1,575
packages with no dependency edits. Fourteen-file formatting passed in 16.07
seconds. The formatter changed only import order and generic wrapping in the
source-authority test; the original six-pass semantic review remains valid.
A complete 208-file formatting-bridge capture was independently hash-verified.

The eight-file focused invocation completed normally with 190 passes, three
failures and one pre-existing Linux-only skip (194 cases; 2883.65 seconds runner,
3033.23 seconds wrapper, maxWorkers=1). All three failures are in the database-close
file: the incognito outbox case reached its unchanged 120-second deadline; the
next plugin-work case recursed in the unchanged metadata fixture's kernel spy;
the Doctor lease case reported an already-listening fixture port. The final
agent-close refusal case passed. None is attributed to load, inherited behavior,
or a causal fix. The reported timeout location is actor acquisition, so the last
startup log alone does not identify the blocked await.

The one serial exact-base whole-file replay completed normally with four failures
and the same Linux-only skip (1187.04 seconds runner, 1352.31 seconds wrapper).
The original outbox case timed out at 121274ms and the following case again hit
the recursive metadata fixture. The Doctor case failed differently, on superseded
config publication; the final close-refusal case hit an occupied fixture port
instead of passing as it did on the candidate. Thus the first two failures have
matching baseline evidence; the candidate's Doctor-port failure remains unresolved,
and no cascade cause or hosted-CI failure exception is claimed. All fourteen
candidate files were restored and the complete 208-file capture reverified.

The one original-consumer negative control reached the intended promise-identity
assertion (line 230, 42706ms), with one selected failure and four filtered cases.
The driver reported inconclusive because its exact-stack-token parser expected
the line number while the canonical runner redacted that line/column token.
The retained failure excerpt independently identifies the exact source path,
highlighted assertion and Promise identity mismatch. This is manually verified
negative evidence, not a passing driver result. The reviewed consumer was restored
in finally and the complete 208-file capture verified afterward (1131.06 seconds
wrapper, 1102.12 seconds failed shard). No test rerun or parser bypass was used.

Targeted types initially found an excess-property error in the new missing-sequence
fixture. Destructuring the sequence out fixes the fixture without widening the
production contract, a cast or an assertion change. Targeted types then passed
in 21.04 seconds. A fresh three-file, 28-context-file independent review supplement
completed scoped-clean at P0–P2 (confidence .94), with intact captures verified.

Fourteen-file type-aware lint with the official core config passed in 297.63
seconds, using one lint thread. The repaired fixture passed the pinned formatter
check. A new full 14-file/208-file capture differs from the earlier capture only
in that reviewed fixture and has been hash-verified.

The repaired owner suite passed all 13 cases (590.49 seconds runner, 732.64
seconds shard, 753.76 seconds wrapper). Completed compiler outputs were verified
before the command exited successfully. This focused pass does not resolve
the separate database-close failures above.

The mandatory suppression audit completed with 13 passes and one inventory
failure (120.88 seconds runner, 171.67 seconds shard, 188.90 seconds wrapper):
97 expected entries versus 98 actual. The extra directive is in the unchanged
src/infra/database-engine/admission-role.test-support.ts fixture. Both the fixture
and audit are unchanged from this branch's base; current main has already removed
that directive using the normal MessagePort transfer-list argument. This cut
adds no suppression and changes no allowlist. The investigated local failure is
retained as a failure, not a passing audit or a future hosted-CI waiver.

Production runtime imports only lose dependencies; no new runtime edge or cycle
is introduced. Exact-head hosted CI supplies broad architecture proof. No earlier
parked proof is credited. No timeout, retry, skip, suppression or assertion for
kept behavior is weakened.

## Exact-head CI attribution

Run 39066706939 on cbdae207e21a666e09b631a412231fde7035a9f6 completed failed.
All three failing cases exactly match the newest completed scheduled main run
39062485709 (7d81a7d13af9df93a0f92c459fa4e2cb64801a08), job117483328996:

| Failed job | Case and observed failure | Main evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PostgreSQL conformance (1/3),117496087830 | port-command.postgres.test.ts refusal boundaries:60,000ms timeout at88 | Same case, deadline and88 stack in main117483328996 |
| PostgreSQL conformance (3/3),117496087919 | matrix-roots.postgres.test.ts retained account-root portability:450,000ms timeout at225 | Same case, deadline and225 stack in main117483328996 |
| PostgreSQL conformance (3/3),117496087919 | matrix-roots.postgres.test.ts partial publication recovery:expected2, received0 at405 | Same assertion and405/170 stack in main117483328996 |
| openclaw/ci-gate,117500316792 | Downstream aggregate of those two executable jobs | Complete exact-head check census; all other selected executable jobs passed |

Neither failing test is modified here. Matching main signatures establish inherited
failures, not a root-cause repair or an attribution to machine load. CI stays red;
landing uses the native inherited-only admin exception after exact merge-source,
review, security and gate verification. No CI rerun, branch update or test weakening.

prs.title: fix(cli): preserve explicitly allowed message tools in MCP
prs.body:
Related: #167085. Reported by @jaimeehenry.

Current validation head: `10d6086debe18d520682aaefc81dd032b4440879`.

## What Problem This Solves

CLI MCP tool preparation drops an explicitly allowed `message` tool when a global or provider-specific tool profile is restrictive, leaving an isolated agent turn with `read` but no requested messaging capability.

## User Impact

An explicit `message` request in a run cap survives restrictive profiles on CLI runtimes, matching embedded behavior. Other allow/deny policies, final caps, channel/account restrictions and live invocation authority still apply. Delivery mode, configuration, SDK contracts, protocol and stored state do not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The MCP owner previously removed the cap before constructing its Gateway catalogue. The final cap could narrow the remaining tools but could not restore `message` already removed by a profile. Reuse the Gateway's existing requested-tool allowance for only the explicitly requested messaging capability. The embedded rule moves to its existing shared tool-policy owner; both callers use it. The whole cap is not converted into `alsoAllow`, and `message_tool_only` is not forced.

Conflict maintenance normally merges official main `a08628b21a322481886d18f320b5575993dbba5f`. The single overlapping allowance hunk retains this PR's shared message-profile rule and main's stable Heartbeat offer. Main's separate offered/callable/exported tool surfaces, post-await authority checks, prepared-read disposal, memory audience and grant filtering are retained. No new SDK/configuration/schema/protocol/dependency contract is introduced.

## Evidence

Current reviewed maintenance head: `10d6086debe18d520682aaefc81dd032b4440879` (2026-10-18).

- Before maintenance, GitHub reported `CONFLICTING`; both Git's three-way merge analysis and the ordinary merge reproduced the same single `agent-tools.ts` conflict. The resolution keeps the message allowance and current-main Heartbeat offer together. Original product before/after evidence remains explicitly prior-head evidence below.
- **102 distinct cases pass across six existing files**, native Node wrapper **477.081 s** (five native shards). The actual MCP catalogue passes **22 cases / 119.08 s**, embedded assembly **45 cases / 63.35 s**, prefix stability **5 cases / 73.02 s**, CLI completion/search preparation **29 cases / 129.00 s**, and turn authority **1 case / 4.29 s**. Durations include native per-shard preparation. Catalogue and preparation tests exercise real in-process owners; the existing computer case uses controlled transport. No test/assertion/timeout or runtime seam was added or weakened.
- Targeted production types: **158.645 s**; native `agents-root`, `agents-other` and `gateway-root` test-consumer graphs: **467.603 s**; type-aware core lint: **60.224 s**. Formatting, five-file line-cap growth against the exact prepared main, assertion safety and whitespace checks pass. An initial line-cap invocation selected the older merge base while the merge was uncommitted and reported four upstream UI files; all four match prepared main byte-for-byte. The supported exact-base mode passes; the failed invocation is retained, without changing guards or baselines. Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the candidate is scoped clean; all five final blobs match the reviewed input.
- Node **24.19.0** / branch-pinned pnpm **12.11.1**. Manifest and lock match the already verified private install. This repair changes no new lazy-loading or artifact boundary; focused production-owner execution and targeted types are rerun, rather than repeating an unrelated full build. Current-head natural CI run `39066901315` is **failed**; see the investigation below, separate from the prior successful run `38786409707` on `0eee64e5`.

This proof does not start a real Gateway, run a real Claude/Codex CLI, use a real paired device or deliver an external message. The original report's effective profile remains unknown. Upstream approval and merge remain maintainer-owned.

### CI investigation (current source head unchanged)

- CI run `39066901315` / job `117496658293` (`checks-node-changed`) tested merge `db27383606c89a72ce8b158830d070aec4a8b619`, with parents main `7f4c63524a63ffc3466b19cfa131e327e36d731f` and this PR's `10d6086d`. The existing X publication composition E2E timed out after **120,000 ms**, waiting for the allowed child transcript write. The derived CI gate also failed. Native `test:ci-failed` classifies this as **unknown: no matching job on main**.
- On that exact clean CI merge, the same unchanged composition passes under **Node 24.19.0**: one test covering its six cases, **25.073 s** test body / **838.773 s** wrapper including normal native E2E build/preparation. It also passes under the checksum-verified repository-pinned Bun **`1.4.3-canary.1+b76e4b4e6`**: **19.086 s** test body / **102.457 s** wrapper, reusing the successful source-matched native build. Duplicate reporter summaries are counted once. No production/test source, assertion, timeout or policy changed.
- Scoped source attribution: both calls to the changed coding-tool assembly omit `runtimeToolAllowlist`, so the old and new message-profile allowance both produce `[]` for this case; the composition uses direct chat/session owners and does not enter the MCP loopback catalogue. This is causal source evidence, **not** a full runtime replay of the clean main base or a qualifying inherited-failure exception.
- The same pending-child timeout was previously recorded in [#173989](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173989), whose unchanged replays also passed. [#172823](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172823) improved error observation without claiming the original nondeterministic trigger fixed. These histories and the present passes do not establish a repair. CI runner load/order and local environment are not claimed identical.
- The CI failure remains unresolved/unknown. If it recurs, capture the accepted child's terminal dedupe/broadcast outcome before the transcript gate; do not extend the timeout or infer success from the creation ACK. No CI rerun, no-op source push, status override or merge was requested. Current-revision maintainer security approval is still required.

### Prior-head evidence (0eee64e5, 2026-10-16)

- That maintenance baseline with the existing catalogue table reproduced **4 intended missing-message failures / 3 passing denial controls / 12 cases not selected by the filter** in **182.81 s** wrapper wall (174.60 s Vitest). The failure is the real catalogue `['read']` instead of `['message', 'read']`, not an import or admission failure. All three candidate source files are restored exactly afterward.
- That candidate: **88 distinct cases pass across four files**, native wrapper **553.90 s**. The actual catalogue file passes **19 cases / 83.64 s**, the embedded assembly sibling **45 cases / 105.41 s**, and the two CLI preparation siblings **24 cases / 246.88 s**. These include main's controlled computer-capability lifecycle, explicit/global/provider/message-group requests, explicit/Gateway denies, exact final caps, requester/root restrictions, completion policy and native search preparation. Existing files and synthetic fixtures are reused; no new process boot, timer, polling or worker override.
- Targeted production types pass **132.492 s**, the four-file test-consumer closure **139.614 s**, and type-aware core lint **53.952 s**. Formatting, whitespace and the five-file growth ratchet pass. Fresh full-candidate independent P0–P2 review is scoped clean; all five committed blobs match the reviewed copy.
- Actual Node24.19.0 and the unchanged current-main pnpm12.10.1 manifest/lock are used in the private checkout. The normal merge preserves both contributor and official-main history, followed by an ordinary fork push. Current-head natural CI and qualifying maintainer review remain separate.

The current proof uses actual in-process catalogue/policy owners in hermetic test state. It does not start a real Gateway, execute a real Claude/Codex CLI, contact a paired device or deliver an external message. The computer lifecycle sibling uses its existing controlled transport. The reporter's effective profile remains unknown, so this fixes the independently reproduced restrictive-profile catalogue defect rather than claiming every reported configuration is explained.

## Prior-head evidence (b1fc97d7)


- Product baseline `0043bb028914e6f92632623a99b482a8cd93b3b5`: the unchanged production policy/exact catalogue resolvers return only `read` for explicit `message,read`, the messaging group, and a provider-specific coding profile. With the three original product files restored and the frozen final test table retained, **4 product assertions fail / 14 controls pass** in **102.00 seconds**. No mocked catalogue resolver or supplied expected tool inventory is involved.
- Candidate: all **18 catalogue cases pass**. Global and Gateway `message` denies retain only `read`; a read-only cap retains only `read`; existing exact-group semantics remain unchanged. This checks actual catalogue output, not a private helper or call shape.
- The existing embedded assembly sibling passes 48 cases, including runtime messaging groups, requester restrictions and child-session controls. The existing CLI preparation siblings pass 21 cases covering completion policy, requester/group restrictions, persisted roots and preparation behavior. **87 distinct cases pass** across four files; repeated catalogue successes are not counted twice.
- Independent full-patch P0–P2 review and a fresh test-only provider-identity review are scoped-clean (static evidence). The added table uses the existing fixture and real resolvers, with no new test-only production seam, process boot, sleep, polling or worker pin.
- All production/test type and static maintenance gates completed, with the inherited test-export failure qualified below. The final provider-specific test addition also receives its affected type/lint checks; results are recorded before publication.

The maintainer's differently identified fake-CLI probe on main returned `[message, read]`; it did not establish the real Claude CLI's offered tools. This patch establishes the separate, concrete restrictive-profile catalogue failure. The reporter's effective profile is unknown, so this PR does not claim to explain every reported configuration, perform real Claude inference, deliver a Telegram message or exercise an operator Gateway.

<details>
<summary>Validation costs and inherited guard failure</summary>

Node 24.19.0 / pnpm 12.5.1. New catalogue tests run through `pnpm test src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. The actual policy, factory selection, native worker scope and final-cap composition require the owning resolver; a cheap helper assertion would miss the original defect. No production or test timeout changed.

- Initial baseline table: 3 failures / 13 passes, 128.79 s. Initial after catalogue plus embedded sibling: 64 passes, 183.70 s. Adding the Gateway-deny control: all 17 catalogue cases pass, 59.92 s.
- Final baseline product-only overlay, including provider identity: 4 failures / 14 passes, 102.00 s. Final 18-case after wrapper wall: 106.01 s.
- `pnpm test src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.completion-tools.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.web-search.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 21 passes, 102.28 s.
- Canonical five-file check plan: 34 completed stages in 3,084.55 s, **33 pass / one inherited full-tree export scan fails**. Production types, all 27 core test consumer graphs (1,838.97 s), lint/format, docs/config, schema and other required static guards pass. Production and script export scans each report 0 entries; runtime value import cycles are 0.
- Entire tracked tree restored to the exact official baseline, same installed environment: the same native three-scan command reproduces the identical five unused test-helper exports in 144.94 s. They are `LocalRemoteShellSpawnResult` in `src/agents/sandbox/remote-fs-bridge.test-helpers.ts`, and `TURN_MODEL_PERSISTED_CHANNEL_REF`, `TURN_MODEL_PERSISTED_PEER_REF`, `TURN_MODEL_SESSION_REF`, `TurnModelSelectionPath` in `src/test-utils/turn-model-selection-differential.ts`. The candidate is then restored byte-for-byte. This is a retained failed guard, not a green result or an approved exception; no ignore, baseline or scanner rule was changed.

prs.title: refactor(plugins): use concrete runtime owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin loading repeatedly constructs the same narrow logger, Discord voice listeners duplicate their only manager's contract, and plugin preparation exposes an internal multi-capture client that is always created for one capture.

## User Impact

No user-visible feature, SDK, config, CLI, protocol or persisted-data change. Explicit logger overrides, Gateway info suppression, lazy voice initialization and worker lifetime/cleanup behavior remain.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing load-context owner's narrow logger value instead of allocating identical projections. Point Discord listeners at the concrete manager with a type-only import and import the listener owner directly inside the existing voice-enabled startup branch, removing the reverse runtime reexport. Inline the private one-shot preparation client; each artifact still owns a separate worker, callback port, source mapper, admission facts and cleanup lifetime.

Worker recovery, current authority, native admission, read-only handling, pending-work drainage and physical settlement remain unchanged. Mocks follow the actual module owners. Two stale non-owner fixtures now test the newer main contract directly: owner-only definitions stay offered for prompt-cache stability, but their actual executors refuse unauthorized calls. Sender identity, owner-positive, profile and conversation-policy assertions remain. The baseline changes delete three obsolete mock-export tuples and add no allowance.

This is an owner-area slice of the wider private-seam family, split under the campaign's area-split rule. It is not a final residue declaration. Net production LOC: **50 removed**; test/support LOC: **14 added**; baseline: **3 removed**; whole diff: **39 removed**, 25 paths. This subset is not credited again in the retained unsplit branches.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Unsupported mutation of a shared default logger's method properties can affect later default consumers. The zero-argument factory introduced by `58f4099a4fb0aede5afe2595f79d1daebbeeaf4d` always forwarded to one process-owned plugins logger; no serving caller mutates it. Explicit custom loggers and the Gateway's intentional suppression copy remain independent. We do not add copying/freezing machinery for unsupported mutation.
- No security, durability, concurrency or shutdown guard is removed. The private preparation factory never escaped and its sole caller immediately invoked `prepare` once; removing unused multi-capture bookkeeping preserves separate artifact lifetimes.

## Evidence

Targeted semantic types covering all 22 existing changed TypeScript roots and four owning test roots pass (233.466 seconds). An initial check failed because the older task-owned install lacked four dependencies already declared by current main; a frozen, prefer-offline, ignore-scripts install repaired those links without changing manifests or the lockfile. All three commits are signed. Production preimages were unchanged when replayed onto fresh main; the newer voice harness retains all main changes plus only the two listener-module additions.

Combined independent review is scoped-clean through P2 (correctness 0.98), specifically confirming per-capture ownership and drainage, supported logger behavior and lazy voice loading.

The focused ready-listener run reached canonical Vitest but executed no cases before a worker-cache miss selected broad worker compilation. Only the verified task-owned compiler and wrapper were stopped and joined (174.153 seconds; canonical exit 130); runtime proof remains incomplete, not passing or a product failure. Targeted lint initially selected declaration preparation because the custom typecheck config was not the matching lint config; that attempt was stopped normally before lint analysis. Its retained task-only artifact lock was reconciled through the owner's advertised recovery after all registered children stopped. The corrected 13-source core lint passes (333.467 seconds). Formatting passes for all 22 existing changed TypeScript files; whitespace checks pass. Both architecture gates pass: zero runtime value cycles (282.663 seconds), zero static cycles (429.427 seconds). One initial static command used a nonexistent script name and failed before analysis; the corrected package-owned command produced the passing result.

Initial exact-head CI run 39058060803 failed in three leaf jobs: baseline-ratchets 117470390896 exposed two incomplete mock factories, node-changed-1 117470391935 exposed stale Discord hidden-tool assertions, and extensions-bundle 117470391980 exposed the same stale QA assertion. None is claimed as inherited-only landing evidence. Both mocks now retain their real namespace and override only their intended values; exactly their two obsolete tuples are pruned. Main's #175309 intentionally retained owner-only definitions while gating execution, but did not migrate these two consumer suites. The fixtures now execute each offered non-owner tool and require both gated:true and the owner-authority refusal, without exercising an external effect.

The named failing-gate repair rebased conflict-free onto main `10cbb85fdd98845512b94b5c8e1abd23062d343c` to consume that actual policy. This was not an update for green or a CI rerun. All five resulting commits are signed. Current architecture gates pass with zero runtime cycles (222.098 seconds) and zero static cycles (461.897 seconds). The current mandatory suppression suite passes (136.481 seconds). prs.title: fix(usage): keep cost reports from restoring out-of-range cold sessions
prs.body:
Related: #157643

## What Problem This Solves

Bounded `usage.cost` reports can restore unrelated old cold transcripts, while a metadata-only cutoff can miss recently imported usage. Select by transcript event time, include unknown/in-range/all-history sources, and cache only verified out-of-range exclusions for unchanged cold sources. Preserve explicitly selected rollup repairs, including newer repairs queued during a busy retry.

## Scope

The existing 24-file fix is synchronized with upstream main `21a47ad54eca42c6f1bbdab5af7da644a886575e`, including the upstream SQLite lint repair #175796. It retains current actor/session ownership, physical-database admission, Kysely/session-window queries, batched pruning, worker budgeting and precise-read priority. No dependency, workflow, configuration or new host-effect surface is added.

## Validation

The prior synchronized revision passed 90 unique focused cases. On synchronized head `ff9b2f53fe35ae94a43de82d621fda3ec3d36638`, the cold-cache and coalesced-report files passed: **5/5 cases**, covering the sole overlapping upstream zstd simplification. Focused typed lint of that codec and the formerly failing SQLite worker passes with 0 warnings/errors. Current-head hosted CI is required; an older failed run is not a new-head verdict.

Earlier CI run [39060491772](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39060491772) failed in core lint and PostgreSQL infra. The lint cause is fixed by #175796. The two non-timeout PostgreSQL failures passed locally with the official runner on both that run's exact main parent and executed merge (2/2 per tree); this did not reproduce the full 64-file shard or its five timeouts, and does not establish their cause.

## Real Behavior Proof (historical revision `4cb72702`)

**Behavior addressed:** Keep unrelated archives cold in bounded reports without dropping recent imported usage or selected repair work.

**Real setup tested:** An isolated source Gateway using real SQLite transcript APIs, cold-storage maintenance, usage workers, authenticated WebSocket requests and archive restoration. No production Gateway or mocked database/archive I/O.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Through normal APIs, create 30 current-day tokens, 17 current-day tokens in a session whose metadata is 120 days old, and an unrelated 260-token old session. Archive the latter two; request the current day's `usage.cost` twice, then all history.

**Evidence after fix:** Both bounded requests returned 47 tokens, including the imported 17; the unrelated archive stayed cold with 0 hot transcript rows and 0 rollups. All-history returned 307 and restored that archive (2 hot rows).

**Observed result after fix:** One source-Gateway case passed; source remained clean, isolation checks passed, and listeners/resources were closed. The clean automated review on `4cb72702` reported no findings or before-merge requests. Both that review and Gateway execution are historical evidence, not fresh executions on this synchronized head.

prs.title: fix(storage): scan large JSON members without regex backtracking
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Daily Bun CI stalled in `src/transcripts/library.query-budget.test.ts` while reading a summary with a transcript field just over 4 MiB. The shard continued printing results from its other worker, then hit the no-output watchdog after the final ACP test. The transcript file had completed only 11 of its 13 cases.

The JSON member tokenizer introduced in #169414 uses a repeated regex group to scan quoted strings. On the pinned Bun runtime, a standalone 4 MiB input spins in that regex; Node completes it in about 16 ms. Replace tokenization with a linear scan of the already validated JSON. Keep the first duplicate member, raw numeric spelling, escaped strings, and whitespace-free compound representations used by SQLite-compatible projections.

Updates and Doctor retain the same schema and projection values while processing large retained summary JSON through the linear scan. Existing transcript byte limits and all assertions remain intact.

## Evidence

- Main reproduction: hourly 39066988478, job 117496811668, head `4aa0e219fef1`; local reproduction on `f15a2b8f9380` with pinned Bun `1.4.3-canary.1+b76e4b4e6`.
- The exact shard replay left the transcript worker spinning after its first 11 case results. The isolated complete file reproduced the same stall. A standalone parser probe narrowed it to the 4 MiB quoted string; after the fix it completed in about 6 ms.
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/transcripts/library.query-budget.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db-schema-v21-columns.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **18 passed**. The complete transcript file finished in **10.12 s**, including both formerly unreachable cases.
- Core tsgo, targeted oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent P2 autoreview: scoped clean.

The Linux Testbox runner queued and was stopped without executing tests. PR CI supplies the hosted Linux proof; no CI rerun was requested.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Models shows a rejected model choice or a previous connection's default after a failed save or configuration refresh.

## User Impact

The pickers return to saved defaults after a rejected save, while **Retry** retains the requested change. Unsent edits survive a temporary disconnect, and a failed configuration read leaves defaults unavailable instead of presenting an old value as current.

## Why This Change Was Made

This refines #174045's draft retention: the page distinguishes a settled write from a deferred one and retires only the matching settled draft. The configuration write owner still owns the retry payload. Retained configuration is displayed only while the same client is disconnected; live defaults require its current snapshot.

The three reported unused exports are now private. Their implementations remain in use, and the patch-serialization and log-parser assertions now exercise their public operation boundaries.

## Evidence

- Current-main negative control: all four reported failures reproduced across the three browser files (17 passed / 4 failed, 102.21s).
- After: the same three native browser files pass all 21 cases in 68.91s, including rejected-save recovery, Retry payload, agent switching, reconnect, external changes, and a failed replacement config read. No E2E assertions were changed.
- `pnpm test ui/src/pages/model-providers ui/src/pages/usage/helpers.node.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 202 tests pass across 16 files, 26.06s wall. Every existing assertion is retained; the rejected-save unit case now expects the saved selection while offline and undispatched cases retain their drafts.
- UI production and page-test type graphs, typed lint, boundary lint, formatting, the full source-contract lane, and `pnpm check:architecture` pass. P2 autoreview found no actionable defects.
- The global unused-export scan still reports 23 unrelated exports in unchanged source/import regions. All three exports named by this regression are absent from that report; no allowlist or suppression was added.

The screenshots use synthetic Gateway data. They show the same rejected save before and after the repair, on desktop and mobile: the displayed model returns from GPT-4.1 mini to the saved GPT-4.1, while the failure and Retry remain available. Temporary capture instrumentation was removed.

prs.body:
Closes #167876
Related: #165386

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway-owned Talk consultations failing after the setup request finishes, even though the voice call is still active.

## User Impact

Browser and Android gateway-relay calls keep the initiating caller's authority for later agent requests. Already accepted work retains its own authority when audio disconnects or is replaced. Explicit task cancellation and actual device/profile/role/Gateway revocation remain effective. No Android protocol, configuration, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The setup RPC and the call have different lifetimes. Capture the existing authenticated continuation at setup, transfer its ownership to the call, and retain the source independently for accepted consultations. Release failed setup and closed admission through the existing owners.

The runtime/helper extraction keeps changed files within their structural limits and preserves current upstream terminal-write draining from #167455 and async close settlement. No generic authorization checks are weakened. This differs from #165386's target-currentness checks around queued provider sends.

## Evidence

- Against upstream `7f47fad0433fa8508c38c8bb224585b82f0e8d76`, the new browser/relay cases fail before the fix: 6 failed, 38 passed. Failures include late `Gateway caller authority is no longer active` and missing operator source.
- With the repair, 76 tests pass across native-consult-target, agent-consult control, browser close, and relay close suites (118.99 seconds wrapper wall time, one worker). The cases cover request completion, accepted detached work, setup failures, source revocation and existing ownership/close behavior.
- Tests exercise the real Gateway dispatch and authority owners with synthetic provider/embedded execution. This is not an authenticated phone/native-process end-to-end claim.
- Production-core and scoped Gateway test types, Oxfmt, Oxlint, line-cap/max-lines, assertion-safety, mock-export, database-worker and test-timeout ratchets passed. The changed integration file alone passes 44 tests: 62.95 seconds command wall time / 61.03 seconds Vitest, dominated by the existing Gateway/SQLite fixture startup; no added sleeps or process boots.
- Full `pnpm build` completed with exit 0 in 295.66 seconds, including runtime bundles and declarations. Its UI performance report flagged startup gzip at 373500 bytes versus the 373454-byte limit (46 bytes over). No UI source or budget was changed; this is disclosed rather than claimed as a completely clean size check, and baseline attribution has not been established.

prs.title: fix(cron): scheduled reports leave sessions marked read
prs.body:
Closes #142002. Reported by @lakemike; @DarkJuanFra supplied the fresh scheduled-session reproduction.

## What Problem This Solves

A scheduled agent report can be saved to a persistent conversation after its last read acknowledgment while the Control UI still shows that conversation as read.

## User Impact

Visible scheduled reports restore the conversation's unread indicator, including with delivery mode `none`. Assistant-written blocker reports count without implying scheduler execution failure; empty results, text-only silent replies and heartbeat acknowledgments preserve read state. Detached runs with no source delivery preserve their source conversation’s read state; source delivery keeps its existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Record the completed output's visibility on the original live run claim before its existing terminal event is emitted. The existing lifecycle owner remains the activity writer; execution timing, transcript identity, delivery and access checks stay with their owners. Shared reply/payload classifiers preserve silent and structured-output semantics. Gateway test doubles now use the real Cron function contract and preserve the facade's exports, so the regression reaches actual execution. The canonical mock-export prune removes one obsolete closed-factory entry from the ratchet; it adds no exception.

No local Gateway operation or CI rerun was used.

It does not change production error classification or replace a visible assistant report with a synthesized provider error. It is **not Gateway runtime-error proof**.

- Two existing real Cron outcome-owner controls, distinguishing ordinary output from structured errors while keeping delivery-target failure separate, pass: **2 passed / 7 unselected**, **95.987 seconds wrapper / 87.42 seconds Vitest**. ## What Problem This Solves

On 2026-04-27 I asked my OpenClaw agent over Telegram to fix two failing evals in one of my repositories. It handed the work to a coding agent running in the background, and six seconds after the exec tool reported the session as running it told me the work had started and promised to report back. It never did, twice. The exchange, condensed (times UTC):

```text
13:13  me     Can you use the good-oss-citizen tile to get the two failing evals to 100%?

13:14  agent  I set up a fresh worktree and I'm handing the implementation to a
              coding agent now.

13:15:14 exec Command still running (session crisp-breeze, pid 3469063).
              Use process (list/poll/log/write/kill/clear/remove) for follow-up.

13:15:20 agent Started. Worktree, branch, and session are set up.
              I'll report back when it has a commit and gate results, or if it blocks.

13:23  (the coding agent finishes with a local commit; the agent is woken with the
        completion event but that turn is told user delivery is disabled, so I am
        not notified)

13:26  me     Is it still going

13:26  agent  No, the coding agent finished and exited cleanly. There is already a
              local commit. I'm not calling it done yet because I still need to verify.

13:26  (no tool call and no message follow; the agent is idle until my next question)

13:27  me     I'm confused, are you still doing something

13:27  agent  Sorry, yes, that was confusing. The coding agent is no longer running.
              I'm doing the final verification myself now.

13:27  (it amends the commit and starts the gates as another background command)

13:27:55 exec Command still running (session mild-rook, pid 3477273).
              Use process (list/poll/log/write/kill/clear/remove) for follow-up.

13:27:55 agent Yes, but only final verification now. Gates are running now.
              I'll report DONE/BLOCKED when those gates finish.

13:28  (the gates finish; the agent is woken again and again told that user
        delivery is disabled; it writes a "successfully completed" message inside
        that turn, and I am not notified)

13:33  me     Are the gates still running.

13:33  agent  No. Gates finished successfully.

13:33  me     Why didn't you notify me then?

13:33  agent  Because the completion event explicitly said "user delivery is disabled"
              and told me to handle it internally. I should have stayed quiet there.
              But after that, I also failed to proactively send a normal concise DONE
              update once I confirmed the gates had finished. That's on me. I made
              you ask twice.
```

### What the transcript shows

- A running result means a process was spawned and was alive when the result was written. "Started." was true.
- What the agent could not know from that result: whether the command was making progress, was waiting for input, or had since exited or failed.
- The harm was not a false start. It was a promise to report back that could not be kept, twice.
- When a background command finishes, the agent is woken with a completion event by default (`tools.exec.notifyOnExit`, [background process docs](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/background-process#disable-automatic-completion-turns)), but that turn may not be allowed to message the user. That is decided when the turn runs, from the heartbeat delivery route and visibility settings ([heartbeat docs, "Delivery behavior"](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/heartbeat#delivery-behavior)). On 2026-04-27 the agent was woken both times and told both times that delivery was disabled.
- At the moment the running result is written, the exec tool knows whether a completion event will be queued, but not whether that later turn will be allowed to message the user.

That leaves two ways to stop an agent from promising a report it cannot deliver:

1. Tell the agent, in the running result itself, what "running" does and does not mean, and that the completion turn may not be allowed to reach the user, so a promise of updates has to be backed by the agent polling the session to the end and reporting itself.
2. Resolve at exec time whether the completion turn will be allowed to deliver, and put that answer into the result.

This PR takes the first. It is one sentence group in one producer, it is true in every configuration, and it needs no knowledge of delivery routing inside the exec tool. The second would couple the exec tool to heartbeat delivery resolution and still could not promise delivery, because the route can change before the command exits.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared running result from `createExecTool` currently reads:

> `Command still running (session ..., pid ...). Use process (...) for follow-up.`

#161780 (merged 2026-10-02) split the follow-up route into three notification modes. This PR adds the same first sentences to all three, then folds the delivery caveat into each mode's own wake wording:

> `Command still running (session ..., pid ...). Running means the process was started and was alive when this result was written; it says nothing about progress, waiting for input, or a later exit or failure. Do not report progress from this result alone. <mode-specific follow-up>`

With completion waking on every exit (`notifyOnExitEmptySuccess=true`, the default for chat channels), the follow-up reads:

> `Completion will wake this conversation automatically. The completion turn may not be allowed to message the user, so if only waiting remains, report that the job is running without promising to report back and end this turn; do not keep polling. Use process (...) for follow-up.`

With silent empty successes (`notifyOnExitEmptySuccess=false`):

> `Use process (...) for follow-up. Completion wakes this conversation on output or failure; empty successful jobs are silent (tools.exec.notifyOnExitEmptySuccess=false). Arrange continuation or collect the result before ending the turn if empty success matters. The completion turn may not be allowed to message the user, so do not promise the user updates unless you poll this session until it finishes and report the outcome yourself.`

With `tools.exec.notifyOnExit=false`:

> `Use process (...) for follow-up. Automatic completion wake is disabled (tools.exec.notifyOnExit=false). If the task needs this result, use poll with a timeout to collect it before ending the turn, unless another continuation is already arranged. Without a completion wake, do not promise the user updates unless you poll this session until it finishes and report the outcome yourself.`

Each clause is checked against the code. "The completion turn may not be allowed to message the user" holds whenever a wake is queued: `buildExecEventPrompt` in `src/infra/heartbeat-events-filter.ts` still tells the completion turn "user delivery is disabled for this run" when `canRelayToUser` is false, and `heartbeat-runner-execution.ts` computes that at wake time from heartbeat visibility (`showAlerts`) and the delivery route. In the every-exit mode #161780 tells the agent to end the turn and stop polling, so that mode drops the promise outright ("without promising to report back") instead of offering polling as the way to back one. The other two modes already ask the agent to collect the result when it matters, so the promise rule there keeps the poll-to-the-end condition. The "what running proves" sentences name no tool and sit before the follow-up, so the trailing follow-up sentence stays adapter-owned:

- base exec uses `process`
- sandbox exec uses `sandbox_process`
- Gateway exec uses `gateway_process` when exposed
- Gateway exec without process follow-up tells the model to rerun in the foreground
- remote-node exec says background follow-up is unavailable and to wait for completion

### Overlap with #158884 and #161780

#158884 (merged 2026-09-26) appends a no-wake warning to the follow-up route when `notifyOnExit=false`. The previous head of this PR chose its own wake clause by `notifyOnExit` and left that warning alone.

#161780 (merged 2026-10-02) then made the follow-up conditional on `notifyOnExitEmptySuccess` as well. Stacked on the previous head, the every-exit mode would have said "you may be woken with a completion event ... do not promise the user updates unless you poll this session until it finishes" and, a sentence later, "Completion will wake this conversation automatically ... end this turn; do not keep polling". Those pull in opposite directions.

This head removes the separate wake clause. The delivery caveat and the promise rule now live inside each of #161780's three branches and agree with that branch's instruction, so they also reach the structured `details.followUp`. The "what running proves" sentences stay in the visible text only, before the follow-up. #161780's own sentences are unchanged except for the inserted caveat in the every-exit branch, where "report that the job is running" gains "without promising to report back".

On current `main`, `qa-lab`'s mock provider regex still matches only the pre-#161780 running text, which no mode emits any more. This PR's regex matches the caution followed by any single-line follow-up that contains the `Use process (...)` route, so it covers all three modes.

### How I expect this to help, and what it cannot do

This is an instruction in a tool result. A model can ignore it, and I could not make a model reproduce the original failure in a replay, so I cannot show a before/after in behavior, only in what the model is told. What I can say:

- On 2026-04-27 the agent read "Command still running" over Telegram and answered "Started. I'll report back". On current `main` that is the every-exit mode, which now tells the agent to report that the job is running and end the turn. The new text adds, at that exact point, that it must not promise to report back. In the other modes an agent that follows it has two honest moves: keep polling in the same turn and report when done, which is delivered because it is a reply to the user; or say "launched, ask me or I'll check", which makes no promise it cannot keep. Either avoids the wait I had.
- The misleading input is gone. Today's text reads as confirmation; the new text states the constraint where the decision is made.
- On the same day, 4 of the 64 background commands with a recorded exit in that session ended with a non-zero code, so a "started" relayed from a running result is wrong often enough to matter.

What it does not do: it does not make the agent keep a promise, and it does not change why the completion turns were silenced. That is the delivery-routing topic linked above and is out of scope here.

## User Impact

There is no API, field, or control-flow change. The "what running proves" sentences appear only in the visible text of the `status: running` exec result. The delivery caveat and promise rule are part of the mode-specific follow-up, so they appear in that text and in the structured `details.followUp` string, next to the wake wording they qualify. Subsequent process results are unchanged.

## Real Behavior Proof

I reran the behavior proof against exact head `0eac408a0ac213770c0147d82bbb09aa5fb34468`, rebased onto upstream `main` at `1a331439952556d653b14973fe294e158d1106bd`.

The harness is a `tsx` script that imports `createExecTool`, `createProcessTool`, and `waitForExecScope` from the checked-out `src/` and runs them unmodified. It spawns a real OS child with `background: true`, immediately reads its log, and then polls its terminal outcome. It uses no exec or process mocks.

The child waits 500 ms before printing `WORK_STARTED` and exiting with code 7.

The recording below is one asciinema 3.2.1 session from the earlier head `d85e6cac`, before #158884 landed: it runs the same harness twice, first in a checkout of upstream `main` at that head's base commit `8adb6ebf5f`, then in the PR checkout. `git log` shows the head before each run. On the base commit the running result has no caution while the immediate log is already empty and the child later exits 7; on the PR head the same result carries the caution before the unchanged follow-up sentence. The host I used for this revision has no asciinema or agg, so the recording was not redone; the transcripts further down are from the current head and show the wording that replaced the recorded one. Final frame of the rendered recording:

![Before/after terminal recording: on main the running result reads Command still running, Use process for follow-up; on the PR head the same result adds the new text. Both runs show an empty immediate log, then WORK_STARTED and exit code 7](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/martinfrancois/openclaw/assets/pr-120414-proof/proof-before-after-v3-final-frame.png)

- [proof-before-after-v3.gif](https://github.com/martinfrancois/openclaw/blob/assets/pr-120414-proof/proof-before-after-v3.gif?raw=true): the full rendered recording (agg 1.9.0).
- [proof-before-after-v3.cast](https://github.com/martinfrancois/openclaw/blob/assets/pr-120414-proof/proof-before-after-v3.cast): the asciinema recording itself.
- [proof.mts](https://github.com/martinfrancois/openclaw/blob/assets/pr-120414-proof/proof.mts) and [proof-driver.sh](https://github.com/martinfrancois/openclaw/blob/assets/pr-120414-proof/proof-driver.sh): the harness, with a [README](https://github.com/martinfrancois/openclaw/blob/assets/pr-120414-proof/README.md).

Redacted stdout transcripts of the same harness on the current head, one per notification mode. The harness now reads `notifyOnExit` and `notifyOnExitEmptySuccess` from the environment; everything else is unchanged.

Every-exit mode (the default for chat channels):

```text
head: 0eac408a0ac213770c0147d82bbb09aa5fb34468
node: v24.20.0
notifyOnExit: true notifyOnExitEmptySuccess: true
exec: Command still running (session <session-id>, pid <pid>). Running means the process was started and was alive when this result was written; it says nothing about progress, waiting for input, or a later exit or failure. Do not report progress from this result alone. Completion will wake this conversation automatically. The completion turn may not be allowed to message the user, so if only waiting remains, report that the job is running without promising to report back and end this turn; do not keep polling. Use process (list/poll/log/write/send-keys/submit/paste/kill/clear/remove) for follow-up.
immediate-log: (no output yet)
immediate-status: running
terminal-output:
WORK_STARTED

Process exited with code 7.
terminal-status: completed
terminal-exit-code: 7
```

Silent empty success:

```text
head: 0eac408a0ac213770c0147d82bbb09aa5fb34468
node: v24.20.0
notifyOnExit: true notifyOnExitEmptySuccess: false
exec: Command still running (session <session-id>, pid <pid>). Running means the process was started and was alive when this result was written; it says nothing about progress, waiting for input, or a later exit or failure. Do not report progress from this result alone. Use process (list/poll/log/write/send-keys/submit/paste/kill/clear/remove) for follow-up. Completion wakes this conversation on output or failure; empty successful jobs are silent (tools.exec.notifyOnExitEmptySuccess=false). Arrange continuation or collect the result before ending the turn if empty success matters. The completion turn may not be allowed to message the user, so do not promise the user updates unless you poll this session until it finishes and report the outcome yourself.
immediate-log: (no output yet)
immediate-status: running
terminal-output:
WORK_STARTED

Process exited with code 7.
terminal-status: completed
terminal-exit-code: 7
```

Wake disabled, with #158884's sentence also repeated by the `log` result:

```text
head: 0eac408a0ac213770c0147d82bbb09aa5fb34468
node: v24.20.0
notifyOnExit: false notifyOnExitEmptySuccess: false
exec: Command still running (session <session-id>, pid <pid>). Running means the process was started and was alive when this result was written; it says nothing about progress, waiting for input, or a later exit or failure. Do not report progress from this result alone. Use process (list/poll/log/write/send-keys/submit/paste/kill/clear/remove) for follow-up. Automatic completion wake is disabled (tools.exec.notifyOnExit=false). If the task needs this result, use poll with a timeout to collect it before ending the turn, unless another continuation is already arranged. Without a completion wake, do not promise the user updates unless you poll this session until it finishes and report the outcome yourself.
immediate-log: (no output yet)

Automatic completion wake is disabled (tools.exec.notifyOnExit=false). If the task needs this result, use poll with a timeout to collect it before ending the turn, unless another continuation is already arranged.
immediate-status: running
terminal-output:
WORK_STARTED

Process exited with code 7.
terminal-status: completed
terminal-exit-code: 7
```

This demonstrates the boundary on the current PR head: session liveness is visible before any evidence that the command reached its work, it says nothing about eventual success, and the delivery caveat matches the configured notification mode.

On this same head:

- `bash-tools.exec-background-followup.test.ts` drives a real `createExecTool` background process on the explicit-background and elapsed-yield-window paths, each in all three notification modes. It asserts the visible text carries the running caution right before the structured follow-up, that the delivery caveat appears exactly when a wake is queued, that the every-exit mode drops the promise and the other two keep the poll-to-the-end rule, and that only the disabled mode carries #158884's sentence. With `bash-tools.exec-run.ts` reset to `main`, 6 of its 10 cases fail.
- `dynamic-tool-build.background-followup.test.ts` (sibling file; `dynamic-tool-build.test.ts` is over the repo line cap and the ratchet rejects growth) asserts the complete model-visible sandbox output. The existing `node_exec` case in `dynamic-tool-build.test.ts` asserts the complete remote-node output.
- `qa-lab`'s mock OpenAI provider parses the running text to drive its progress scenarios. `server.progress.test.ts` uses the every-exit text as `RUNNING_OUTPUT` and `server.tool-routing.test.ts` uses the silent-empty-success text, so both shapes (route last, route first) are parsed. With the regex reset to `main`, 11 of the 50 cases in those two files fail.
- Focused run on this head: 178 tests across the five touched test files pass.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passes on this head (format, lint, typecheck of core and extensions plus their tests, dead-export scan, ratchets).
- Exact-head GitHub CI is pending on this head.

## Codex App-Server Contract Review

I inspected the direct sibling Codex source required by `AGENTS.md`, pinned to the version the rebased plugin declares: `@openai/codex` `0.154.0`, tag `rust-v0.154.0`, commit [`6b9826e3aa83b1a5947db50f4332cb9c65f1b340`](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/6b9826e3aa83b1a5947db50f4332cb9c65f1b340).

- Codex app-server v2 accepts dynamic-tool text as an `InputText { text }` content item: [`app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs#L1653-L1669`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/6b9826e3aa83b1a5947db50f4332cb9c65f1b340/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs#L1653-L1669).
- The app server decodes those items and submits them unchanged as `Op::DynamicToolResponse`: [`app-server/src/dynamic_tools.rs#L18-L58`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/6b9826e3aa83b1a5947db50f4332cb9c65f1b340/codex-rs/app-server/src/dynamic_tools.rs#L18-L58).
- Codex core maps every content item into the model's function-tool output without rewriting its text: [`core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs#L153-L163`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/6b9826e3aa83b1a5947db50f4332cb9c65f1b340/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs#L153-L163).
- Codex's integration test confirms that the exact `InputText` reaches the follow-up `function_call_output`: [`app-server/tests/suite/v2/dynamic_tools.rs#L341-L577`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/6b9826e3aa83b1a5947db50f4332cb9c65f1b340/codex-rs/app-server/tests/suite/v2/dynamic_tools.rs#L341-L577).

On the OpenClaw side, the patch preserves the exact trailing `Use process (...)` literal. The sandbox adapter rewrites only that suffix to `sandbox_process` in [`dynamic-tool-build.ts`](https://github.com/martinfrancois/openclaw/blob/d85e6cac256bc945032ef5357789e2908ca58949/extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.ts#L802-L817). The node alias and the Gateway projection replace the same suffix with their available or unavailable next step in [`shell-dynamic-tools.ts`](https://github.com/martinfrancois/openclaw/blob/d85e6cac256bc945032ef5357789e2908ca58949/extensions/codex/src/app-server/shell-dynamic-tools.ts#L51-L92), the Gateway one through the shared projection in [`exec-tool-target-pinning.ts`](https://github.com/martinfrancois/openclaw/blob/d85e6cac256bc945032ef5357789e2908ca58949/src/agents/exec-tool-target-pinning.ts#L106-L115).

## Evidence

- `git diff --check` and `oxfmt --check` pass on the tree.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passes on this head.
- The core real-process test owns the exec result.
- The Codex sibling test and the existing `node_exec` case own the complete adapter output.
- The `qa-lab` mock provider is the one consumer that parses the running text; its regex and fixture are updated in the same commit.
- Production changes: three string constants, the three follow-up branches, and one template line in `bash-tools.exec-run.ts`; one regex in `qa-lab`'s `mock-openai-tool-routing.ts`; one note in `docs/tools/exec.md`.
- `CHANGELOG.md` remains untouched.
- The previous head `da456ec3` passed exact-head CI ([run 36861733565](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36861733565)). This head is rebased onto `1a331439` to take in #161780; the rebase conflicted in `bash-tools.exec-run.ts` and its test, resolved as described above.
- Earlier heads of this PR carried a shorter caution ("Running means only that the session is alive, not that the command's work started or succeeded; do not report progress based on this result alone."). It was replaced because it read as denying that a process had started, which is not what the running result means, and because it said nothing about the promise that caused the harm in the transcript.

## AI Disclosure

This pull request is AI-assisted. Claude prepared the original change and tests. Hermes prepared an earlier exact-head behavior proof and dependency inspection. Codex prepared an earlier rebase, review fix, and cross-surface test refresh. Claude prepared the earlier rebase onto `main`, the `qa-lab` consumer update, the sibling test file, the Codex 0.154.0 source inspection, the recorded before/after proof, the transcript excerpt from my own OpenClaw session logs, the reconciliations with #158884 and #161780, the three-mode test, the docs note, the rerun transcripts, and this description. The author remains responsible for the submitted change.

prs.title: improve(doctor): avoid duplicate integrity scans during upgrades
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Historical SQLite upgrades scan the same unchanged agent data twice: QUICK certifies the raw recovery image, then live-source admission repeats QUICK before the first migration. In the original 6.07 GB trace these are checks #23 and #186; #186 is pre-migration, not post-migration.

## User Impact

Candidate Doctor reuses the first source QUICK proof during an automatic upgrade when capture established byte equality and the live source remains unchanged under the same exclusive maintenance owner. Explicit `--full-integrity-check`, runtime FULL admission, transformed recovery-image verification, post-migration scoped FULL, and mutation foreign-key checks retain their coverage. The already-installed updater still executes its own version's behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The capture owner records a one-use QUICK receipt before private-image transformation. Admission consumes it only for the same unchanged source and table coverage. Empty WALs contain no changed pages; the raw-copy branch now compares main bytes as well as sidecars. Nonempty WALs, recovery journals, pending writes, changed files, and another maintenance scope do not qualify. QUICK never creates or satisfies a FULL receipt.

Removed check and accepted edge case: skip the duplicate pre-mutation live admission bundle only for a byte-equal, unchanged source already checked in this exclusive operation. A new operation or any unscoped mutation checks again. Out-of-custody writers remain unsupported. The transformed backup is a different image and is checked independently.

This builds on merged #175808, which separately narrowed later callback scopes and reuses unchanged scoped-table checks. It does not transfer private-image table-cache entries to the live database. No schema, PostgreSQL behavior, worker protocol, retry, or generation is added.

## Evidence

Regressions cover same-source QUICK reuse without FULL admission, explicit FULL still scanning, untouched-table physical corruption refusal before capture, committed/uncommitted unscoped writes invalidating reuse, touched-table corruption refusal after mutation, and empty-WAL main-byte mismatch refusal. The new reuse and copy assertions failed on the original main base; actual Doctor migration cases cover v24/v26 with default and explicit FULL. Two Codex autoreview rounds are clean through P2. The rebase preserves both reviewed commits, with only the neighboring scopefix import added to patch context.

The matched **6,070,161,408-byte** synthetic stable agent24/state20 fixture passed public Doctor on exact scopefix base `bdb482a8dfef` and candidate `7e8c8dea073`. Both reached agent31/state27 with recovery captures retained and bounded row-count/sample-hash preservation assertions passing.

| Upgrade measurement | Scopefix base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Native integrity/FK statements, all observed threads | 259 | 233 |
| Whole-database QUICK | 16 | 15 |
| Whole-database FULL | 0 | 0 |
| Scoped FULL | 226 | 202 |
| Foreign-key checks | 17 | 16 |
| Integrity-worker requests | 1 | 0 |
| Doctor seconds, observed | 292.653 | 209.967 |

The ordered trace is identical after removing base checks **186–211**: the duplicate pre-mutation live-agent admission bundle (QUICK + 24 scoped FULL + FK). All later checks remain. This is **26 fewer statements (10.0%)** on top of scopefix. The requests count is integrity-worker IPC only, not all Doctor IPC or SQL. Timings come from one busy-host pair and are observations, not controlled latency evidence.

An initial refreshed pair used fixture files at 0644 instead of the original quickpath recipe's 0600. Doctor repaired permissions, changed the file fingerprint, and correctly declined reuse: both arms ran 259 checks with one worker request. Only the synthetic pristine fixture permissions were then normalized to the original recipe (files 0600/directories 0700), without changing database bytes, before the matched pair above. That first pair is retained as conservative fallback evidence.

Exact-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39067823588) passed **57 jobs**, with 26 intentionally skipped. The selected tests include all three changed files; production/test types, type-aware lint, source contracts, Madge, T1 and dialect ratchets pass. T1 is 181→181 (compatibility 10→10); dialect counts do not rise. PostgreSQL jobs were not selected for this SQLite-only diff. Canonical `pnpm deadcode:exports` reports exactly the same 14 production and 13 full-tree findings on actual base `bdb482a8dfef` and candidate `7e8c8dea073`; the script scan is clean. Both commands exit 1 because of those inherited findings, with zero candidate-only findings and identical finding-file blobs; recorded for the main repair owner.

The exact-candidate [published-driver update cell](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39067881500) passed: **9 jobs succeeded, 15 intentionally skipped**, including the real published-driver update and package-acceptance verification. No retry was needed.

Earlier focused proof passed 40 SQLite/Doctor/copy cases, 19 import-closure cases, and 15 provisioning cases. One additional unmodified macOS sparse-provisioning case hit its 120-second limit on the shared host; it remains unclassified and is not claimed passing or inherited. The original CI repair fixes the type-import cycle and wrapper inventory; the final rebase required no implementation changes.

This is offline upgrade work: no warmed-turn SQL saving or controlled latency improvement is claimed. Area T1 remains 0; global T1 remains 181. No SDK or schema-version change. Change size: 302 additions / 16 deletions across nine files (production +117/−15, tests +173, documentation +11/−1, wrapper inventory +1). The bounded production growth carries source proof between existing owners instead of repeating a whole-database scan.

The original quickpath scoped census found 292 calls over 153 labeled image/table pairs, with 139 repeats. Those repeats were not all redundant because mutations intervene. Scopefix removes 66 checks from four later admissions; this PR isolates the additional duplicate pre-migration bundle on top of that merged result. The PostgreSQL bisect refuted quickpath as the infra-timeout cause; this is a normal performance PR.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep screen awake during voice activity
prs.body:
Closes #120245

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running Browser Talk or holding the composer voice-dictation control on a mobile browser can have the interaction interrupted when the device's normal screen timeout expires.

This was reproduced on a Huawei P30 Pro using Brave Browser on Android.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the browser Screen Wake Lock API while microphone-driven Talk or dictation is active, release the lock when the activity stops, and reacquire it when the page becomes visible again. The feature is progressive: unsupported browsers and rejected wake-lock requests continue with the existing microphone behavior, with no new configuration, dependency, or backend protocol.

## User Impact

Mobile users can continue a Browser Talk session or voice dictation without periodically touching the screen solely to prevent display timeout. The screen is allowed to sleep normally again as soon as the microphone activity ends.

## Evidence

- Reproduced before the change on a Huawei P30 Pro in Brave Browser on Android: allowing the normal display timeout to expire disrupted the active Browser Talk interaction.
- Verified the reversible Control UI backport on the same device: the display remained awake while Browser Talk was active and returned to normal timeout behavior after the session ended.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/screen-wake-lock.test.ts` — 3 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/realtime-talk-lifecycle.test.ts` — 21 tests passed.
- Focused wake-lock, Talk, and dictation test suite during initial implementation — 43 tests passed.
- Formatting across all seven changed files — passed.
- Production Control UI build, precompressed-asset verification, and performance checks — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- The Browser Talk Playwright fixture and assertions cover wake-lock acquisition and release. Local Chromium execution is unavailable on this host, so that E2E scenario was not run locally.
- The standalone composer-dictation test invocation is blocked before test collection by the repository browser-test harness resolving `node:` imports (`ERR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN_MODULE`); no dictation assertion failed.

No visual layout changes are introduced, so before/after screenshots would be identical. The relevant before/after evidence is the device screen-timeout behavior described above.

## AI Assistance

AI assistance was used to inspect the codebase, implement the change, add tests, run validation, and draft this PR. Matt  reproduced the original issue and manually verified the live behaviour on the stated Android device and browser. The submitted diff and evidence were reviewed before publication.
