prs.title: fix(agents): prevent needless cache rebuilds from workspace and turn context
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can change an early instruction block when workspace Markdown files are edited or when an otherwise unchanged conversation moves between ordinary input, internal handoffs and completion turns. That can invalidate a large reusable prompt prefix. The reporting user experienced rapid Claude allowance depletion that made the PA feel practically unusable.

This is a cache-efficiency bug, with two distinct causes addressed here. Three observed resumed Claude calls recorded `system_changed` and about **943,000 total cache-created input tokens** despite identical retained workspace content. An offline regression also reproduced three system variants across four turns with unchanged intended authority/tools/workspace. Historical full system bodies were not retained, so the exact avoidable share cannot be reconstructed. **Cache-token counts do not measure subscription allowance consumed or prove this alone exhausted it.**

## Changes

### Automatic correction: current turn facts leave reusable system instructions

Producers identify their exact generated routing, delivery, account-format and inbound-metadata contribution. On the existing eligible per-turn context path, preparation carries those current facts through that carrier—private turn context on native Claude—while enduring conditional rules stay authoritative system instructions.

For example, the current account/thread is turn context; authorization, privacy, progress/final delivery and reaction rules remain system policy. Exact producer-recorded offsets/components establish ownership. Missing or mismatched provenance preserves the original caller instructions; there is no heading matching or arbitrary text stripping. Required facts survive optional-context failure.

This correction applies automatically on the eligible path, independently of the workspace setting. It does not freeze the whole system prompt. Genuine owner, permissions, tools, plugin and caller instruction changes remain current and may legitimately invalidate a cache prefix. Ineligible paths retain existing behavior.

### Opt-in workspace freshness cadence

```json5
{
  agents: {
    defaults: { workspaceContextRefresh: "compaction" },
  },
}
```

- `"compaction"`: load current workspace files for a new session, retain their snapshot across ordinary turns/process restarts, and refresh at compaction before continuation.
- `"every-turn"`: immediate file refresh; remains the default. Per-agent overrides are supported.

An agent's own edits and tool results are normally already in the conversation, so reloading the file into an earlier block can be redundant. External edits may not be: operators selecting compaction mode intentionally defer their visibility. Snapshots cover workspace-file input, not dynamic permissions/tools/skills. Saved raw files rerender under current privacy filters and injection budgets; scope changes cannot reuse another scope's private native context.

The implementation reuses existing session metadata and lifecycle ownership, without a new database schema or sidecar. The opt-in supports managed local Claude and embedded execution with built-in compaction; unsupported harnesses/remote snapshot paths/opaque compaction owners reject it explicitly. **Codex support for this snapshot mode is not claimed.** An optional public CLI workspace lifecycle callback is part of the proposed contract and needs maintainer approval.

## General mechanism versus Claude integration

Changing an early prefix can affect any exact-prefix cache; [OpenAI documents the same requirement](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching). This is not established as a Claude Code cache defect.

OpenClaw's managed Claude transport receives rebuilt `appendSystemPrompt` with `systemPromptSnapshot:false`, exposing host prefix changes on resume. Codex's parent-local persona/skills/memory instructions also expose early-prefix changes, although its AGENTS snapshot differs. Embedded exposure depends on the final carrier: eligible native OpenAI Responses and direct Anthropic on this newer base already preserve prompt-series prefixes and append updates. Builder changes alone do not prove a changed outgoing prefix on every route. **GPT cache loss, comparative allowance impact and universal provider coverage have not been measured.**

## Evidence

Current PR head: `585915a9020e96a69e2110540f23977197db5111`.

| Scope | Executed result and limitation |
| --- | --- |
| Latest upstream behavior plan | Normal exit1: **38 passed, 6 failed, 219 skipped across nine files**; a separate unchanged projection suite passed **8/8**. The failures were a new native-initialization timeout, two fixture expectations, and three existing native stdio startup/cleanup controls. The fixture expectations and a subsequently reviewed test-import path were corrected but **not rerun**. Native timeout/cleanup failures remain unresolved. |
| Latest upstream static/source checks | Production type checking, scoped lint and format/diff checks passed. Independent review verified the import correction and source semantics. Changed-test type checking is **incomplete**: an unrelated pre-existing NUL-damaged working file prevented scope discovery; the conservative broad fallback was stopped/joined. That file was preserved and excluded from the commit. No current-head upstream runtime-build pass is claimed. |
| Exact older installed-version port | Official declarations, scoped typed lint, unified runtime build, source/output/import preservation and seven copied-installer cases passed. Independent source and exact-payload review approved the final candidate. These results concern `2026.10.2`/`b8952d4` plus existing local patches, **not an executed runtime build of this newer PR head**. |
| Genuine release compatibility attempt | The genuine npm `2026.10.4` package wrote isolated settings/history/binding state; normal Doctor migration24→28 passed. Feature-disabled reading timed out on the original attempt and one unchanged authorized retry. Activation, restart and compaction phases did not execute. This is migration proof only, not upgrade continuity. |

### Executed compiled native-boundary proof on the older port

Actual ordinary reply producer/queue and public command producer/prepared-generation/attempt compose through actual admission, plugin loading and the unchanged Anthropic transport, with a synthetic stdio peer. Final run: **exit0, eleven behavior groups**.

```text
ordinary -> internal handoff -> completion -> ordinary
host appendSystemPrompt: identical across four turns
native tool/settings argv: identical except session-id/resume selectors
current private facts, account formats and original input: pass
persisted binding and host resume/history: pass
saved workspace, compact refresh, stale-context refusal: pass
native exec denial, genuine overrides and policy/provenance: pass
specific closed/stale/foreign ownership controls: pass
native initializations=6; successful terminal results=5
provider/network/channel attempts=0 in this final corrected fixture
remaining children=0; backend/runtime/registry cleanup joined
```

Proof inputs/payload were unchanged before/after. Final result SHA256: `7fa6f83023807cfafa0be750607d736ae3751472e23d2c79848f5773aab2e74b`. Exact reviewed payload manifest SHA256: `a1af6a27393d83a57fe76b411a81fec40ce00b7a84192923e6c45f54c733360c`. Failed setup attempts remain retained; the earlier isolated default-CLI/login failure is not described as zero provider activity.

This proves host system bytes, launch policy, host resume selection/history and transport lifecycle with a synthetic peer. It does **not** prove Claude consumes that native history, full native built-in prompt stability, live provider cache reuse, actual reply delivery or subscription savings. Raw `reuse-with-drift` labels can remain despite stable rendered system bytes.

## Local deployment

The exact older-version port is deployed after cooperative drain, fresh backups and independent final payload approval. Twelve existing runtime files plus one pure source-owned chunk changed. All **24,935 original events across569 history sessions**, including13,162 main events, original session windows, main/native bindings, native transcript prefix, settings and schemas are preserved. All55 runtime/preservation fingerprints and609 dependency hashes match. Gateway health passed; WhatsApp is running/connected/healthy, with no plugin errors. Existing main-only compaction mode is unchanged. No live model or WhatsApp test message was generated for deployment. Rollback must retain the compatible raw-snapshot reader and must not restore old history.

## Before merge

The PR remains a draft. The [current review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174235#issuecomment-6216686310) has **no code findings**, but requires:

- Completed current-head native-boundary evidence and a shipped Gateway/native automatic-compaction trace showing fresh workspace context in its first continuation. Synthetic/local-port evidence does not replace those gaps.
- Genuine settings/history upgrade, activation, restart and compaction continuity proof.
- A maintainer decision on compaction-delayed freshness and the public callback. The reviewer recommends separating the automatic turn-fact repair from the snapshot feature; that decision remains open.

prs.title: fix(chat): keep session filters when changing model settings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Changing a Chat model or thinking setting triggers a second session roster read and replaces the user's foreground list query.

## User Impact

Confirmed settings still reconcile before the send barrier releases, without an extra read or losing the current list limit/filter.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session capability already awaits canonical mutation reconciliation. Remove the second page callback and its orphan option/wrapper rather than adding another reconciliation policy. Per-session ordering, confirmed receipts, live authority and optimistic ownership remain with their existing owners.

Net production LOC: 10 removed.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None: the redundant second reconciliation is removed; canonical mutation reconciliation remains mandatory.

## Evidence

The real mounted-pane model/thinking regression failed before the fix (expected one roster read, received two). Both pass after the fix and preserve foreground limit 7. Existing send success/failure cases now seed a real held agent-scoped row and hold the canonical reconciliation rather than relying on the removed second read; original ordering and final-model assertions remain.

The original stream/settings focused run passed 156/156 across ten files. On fresh main, both touched test files passed 6/6, their targeted UI test graph typechecked, and all four changed files passed lint and formatting. Fresh independent Codex review of the source change was scoped-clean at P0–P2. No visual markup change.

The mandatory suppression scan passed 13/14 and found the existing `src/infra/database-engine/admission-role.test-support.ts|unicorn/require-post-message-target-origin|1` entry missing from its allowlist. This branch changes neither that file nor the allowlist test and adds no suppression; no allowlist expansion or passing replay is claimed. Exact-head PR CI supplies broad proof.

CI fixture repair: the fake patch now holds its own canonical reconciliation rather than a retired page refresh. The browser case queues an unrelated refresh while canonical reconciliation is held, then verifies send and delivery before releasing that second deferred response. Original ordering and delivery assertions remain; no timeout, retry, skip, or production behavior was added. The failed unit case passed locally (53.41s Vitest / 102.92s wrapper). The failed browser case passed on an isolated Linux Testbox (1.313s scenario, 14.90s Vitest / 16.96s wrapper); the resource is stopped. Targeted four-file official UI test types, exact lint/format, and diff check passed. The suppression result above remains 13/14 on this base; upstream commit df0358cdd5f repairs that unchanged file.

Fresh independent repair review raised one finding that the later response was no longer deferred. Declined after source verification: both `deferNext` calls remain before the patch; the first release takes only the first matching response, and the second release still occurs after final delivery. The mock consumes one deferred selector per request, so a send barrier incorrectly waiting on that second response would still block and fail this case.

## Exact-head CI attribution

Run 39061918273 on `ebcafe04d5a70bc934d88238c98704f6fe475d91` completed with the repaired UI and mocked-E2E cases passing. All 95 exact-head check-run records were enumerated; none remains pending. Two nonaggregate jobs failed:

| Failed job | Failure | Inherited evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `check-lint-core-2` (117482761494) | `src/infra/sqlite-readonly-location.worker.ts:381`, `typescript(await-thenable)` | Identical error in unrelated PR #175792, run 39062213925, job 117483563965. That exact peer head changes only `packages/ai/src/env-api-keys.ts`; this PR changes neither the SQLite worker nor the linter. |
| `checks-ui-e2e-real-gateway (2/2)` (117481769470) | QA cross-channel automation non-owner assertion at line 350: expected false, received true | Identical case and assertion on scheduled main run 39058564617, job 117471751050. The assertion happens in Telegram before later browser management. |

`openclaw/ci-gate` (117484187253) is the downstream aggregate. `security-fast` (117481768794) passed. The successful replacement PR metadata check (117481485969) supersedes the cancelled metadata run (117481446691); no test coverage was cancelled or inferred. The Models/CLI API-key case passed this head. The inherited-failure landing exception is requested for these two attributed jobs, not a claim that CI is green. CI tested merge `6fcb5f4c5bacf2d765098b5006b7d88c94060943` into main `c3ddb202e63f5dbee790c217411dac5571361cd7`.

prs.title: perf(config): defer form schema generation during config reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The first `config.get` after a Gateway restart builds the entire form JSON schema just to obtain redaction hints. Reconnecting Control UIs that previously loaded config trigger this work on the Gateway main thread.

## User Impact

Config reads, writes, and command transcript redaction can use the existing sensitivity metadata without constructing form schemas. Explicit `config.schema` and `config.schema.lookup` requests retain their full schema and presentation hints. SecretRefs, disabled channel owners, sensitive URLs, and explicit non-sensitive fields keep their redaction contracts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime schema was already cached by prepared config identity and active plugin registry generation; this was cold work rather than a build per client. Both lazy results now share that existing metadata cache and its explicit invalidation. The change removes the caller-supplied redaction callback and reuses one extension hint merger. All Gateway runtime consumers needing only redaction hints use the lighter path.

Production delta: **+39 lines** (82 added, 43 removed). The additional code separates the two required contracts—sensitivity hints and the public form schema—while preserving full schema responses. No new config option, database shape, or compatibility path. Codex protocol validators were inspected: each schema already compiles once per module instance, so they are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Focused runtime-schema and config-get tests: 38 passed (41.35 s wall time; runtime-schema test bodies ~3.3 s, config-get bodies ~1 s).
- Focused config-write/recovery/profile and command-permission tests: 73 passed, one existing skip (34.84 s wall time). Includes the updated config-get redaction cases.
- Full schema contract test file: 26 passed (7.57 s wall time).
- Export-name guard passed; eager-import and PR-wrapper closure files: 22 passed (35.25 s wall time).
- Changed-file formatting, scoped core lint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Regression control: temporarily restoring the original full-schema call in the config.get owner makes the new cold-read regression fail at the expected “schema builder was called” assertion. The reviewed implementation is restored.
- Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean at P0–P2.
- GitHub's code review completed on `6fb8314341fb71f4cffbf18b5abe3b98d4a74916` with no findings. Advisory ClawSweeper review did not complete: its input scanner refused the reviewed source. No scanner policy was changed or bypassed; the independent review above completed successfully.
- No Testbox/Crabbox lease. Broad type/build/test gates are delegated to PR CI under the current validation policy.
- Initial PR CI rejected two changed mock factories for missing isolation explanations. Both intentionally exclude runtime config/plugin discovery; the repair documents those contracts without changing the mocks or production code. The two files passed all 20 tests in 10.13 s, their targeted mock-export scan and scoped formatting/lint passed, and an independent review of the repair was clean. The next CI run exposed one obsolete grandfathered mock entry; the native baseline generator removed that exact entry (8,954 → 8,953), with no new exemptions. Independent review of that deletion was also clean.

## Paired measurements

Four concurrent Linux A/B pairs, each side restricted to 16 cores under an exclusive measurement lock, with the core halves swapped between pairs. Each side used eight clients, identical synthetic config, and separate state and ports. The fixture loaded 18 startup plugins and exposed 169 plugin schema entries. Outside CPU load was recorded with `mpstat` for context.

| Pair | Cold config.get before → after | Paired difference | Targeted schema self samples before → after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 329.89 → 73.69 ms | −256.20 ms | 218 → 6 |
| 2 | 335.90 → 64.90 ms | −271.00 ms | 219 → 5 |
| 3 | 322.65 → 65.45 ms | −257.21 ms | 207 → 5 |
| 4 | 330.37 → 72.00 ms | −258.38 ms | 235 → 5 |

Mean cold `config.get`: **329.70 → 69.01 ms (4.78×)**; mean paired difference **−260.70 ms**. Targeted schema self samples: **219.75 → 5.25**; the broader schema subtree: **313 → 48**. Main-thread CPU over the profile window: **1272.81 → 1040.68 ms**, mean paired difference **−232.13 ms**.

The work is deferred: a subsequent first explicit `config.schema` takes **28.71 → 312.00 ms**, because the baseline already built it during `config.get`; a second schema request takes **24.44 → 27.39 ms**. Full schema responses were 3,413,441 bytes on both revisions; canonical hashes matched in all three pairs that captured hashes. Each side produced 242 valid, redacted, byte-stable config replies per pair.

Initial warm polling measured mean **1.71 → 2.29 ms**, p50 **1.52 → 1.65 ms**, and p95 **3.16 → 3.04 ms**. Two pairs had candidate p99 spikes near 35 ms. These polls followed the cold response, so their timing shifted by ~260 ms between revisions; both profiles contain startup GC pauses.

Two additional swapped control pairs fixed warm requests to identical absolute timestamps and retained per-request times. Warm means were **1.510 → 1.535 ms** (paired differences −0.037 and +0.086 ms), p50 **1.392 → 1.543 ms**, p95 **2.721 → 2.233 ms**, and p99 **3.498 → 2.659 ms**. Neither reproduced the 35 ms candidate tail. This supports effectively neutral warm performance, with a small median increase; no warm speedup is claimed. The controls repeated the cold improvement (**335.66 → 70.58 ms**) and identical full-schema hashes. Each side validated another 201 config replies per control pair.

Limitations: this fixture stresses config/plugin metadata, not a large session database or live model/channel traffic. The primary 30-second profiles began 305–368 ms after ready; the synchronized controls began 330–374 ms after ready. All measured config reads were captured. There were no Codex validator compilation samples, so no Codex performance improvement is claimed. One initial harness run with a baseline package-file layout error was excluded before these four valid pairs.

## Final CI and inherited-failure qualification

Exact reviewed head: `6fb8314341fb71f4cffbf18b5abe3b98d4a74916`. [CI run 39067600216, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39067600216) completed. Its only root failures are the three PostgreSQL conformance shards; the aggregate CI gate consequently failed. All other selected CI jobs passed, including builds, production/test types, lint, changed/sibling tests, UI tests, and `security-fast`. Independent reviews are clean. No CI rerun was used.

The CI table classified these by job name only. Inspection of both sets of retained logs confirmed the exact failing cases and errors against [scheduled main run 39066988478](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39066988478), head `4aa0e219fef1bb622632052a21c10c4d09b83cce`:

| PR job → main job | Exact inherited failure |
| --- | --- |
| [PostgreSQL 1/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39067600216/job/117498989428) → [main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39066988478/job/117496810269) | `port-command.postgres.test.ts`: “probes real privileges, refuses occupied/wrong-owner/RLS sources, and resumes verified staging”; timeout at 60,000 ms. |
| [PostgreSQL 2/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39067600216/job/117498989421) → [main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39066988478/job/117496810251) | `doctor-migration.postgres.test.ts`: “keeps the real agent v30→current rollback exact (foreign write: false)”; timeout at 120,000 ms. |
| [PostgreSQL 3/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39067600216/job/117498989357) → [main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39066988478/job/117496810299) | `matrix-roots.postgres.test.ts`: “ports every retained token/account root with the state family and restores fresh namespaces”; timeout at 450,000 ms. “resume recovers a partially published multi-root port and blocks ordinary startup meanwhile”; `expected +0 to be 2`. |

The actual CI checkout was merge `db2f8c4134f357271f19965f357502d0a515da7d`, with ordered parents `51aa1b76d5d3dde7b4972e09f28f6495b081a7d6` (main) and the reviewed PR head. Its tree matches a reconstructed merge. The entire database-engine tree, Doctor port entry point, update database restore owner, and config IO owner are byte-identical between that main parent and the tested merge. These failing database paths do not call the changed runtime JSON-schema/hints entry points. Landing is under the authorized inherited-only CI exception; this does not claim green CI.

## What Problem This Solves

Fresh cron-session preparation drops an explicitly linked authentication profile, allowing Doctor migration to choose a different shared account instead of honoring the original selection.

## User Impact

Linked account selections remain strict across fresh cron sessions. If the original account is missing or unavailable to unattended execution, migration leaves the job unchanged and reports the explicit account-selection action instead of silently adopting a competing account. This does not grant unattended access to a personal account.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve `user-link` authentication overrides alongside existing explicit user overrides in the session-sanitation owner. Automatic selection, account authorization, route selection, refresh, and Doctor migration policy are unchanged. The existing real-runner fixture now covers the linked-account path through Doctor and provider-request authorization rather than only inspecting the prepared session.

## Evidence

- Audited the account-continuity and regression fixes in #172590, #172792, #173411, #173509, and #173572, plus prepared-session pins in #172374 and later relevant owner changes.
- All 5 added composed cases fail without the one-line fix. With it, all 11 real-runner cases pass: selected shared link wins over a competing default; personal/missing links do not adopt another account; replacement/sign-out produces zero provider requests. Existing API/OAuth identity, reversed defaults/order, configured-key, unadopted-account, personal-first planner, and temporary-cooldown cases still pass. Only provider HTTP is stubbed; Doctor, persistence, auth planning, and the runner are real.
- 31 companion tests pass: 17 Gateway creation/adoption/ownership tests, 7 durable-authorization tests including same-account refresh and incompatible-route rejection, and 7 cron/event auth-boundary tests. The prior 7 account-migration and 21 session tests remain valid unchanged-input proof.
- Core, Doctor, and cron-test typechecks; touched-file lint/format; whitespace checks; full touched-file/test audit; simplification; and fresh independent API-only review passed with no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Exact-head CI run 39013952088 completed successfully: 62 jobs on `782cc3b97c55990d1aade8cf3e8472fc38fe252f`. The earlier run 39006770847 also passed on the original patch head `c09531f` but is not used as proof for this test commit.
- ClawSweeper re-reviewed `782cc3b` with no correctness findings and accepted the real authority-boundary proof. Its separate request for an installed latest-stable upgrade run remains unperformed; this change introduces no schema or serialized-format change.
- Bounded v2026.10.4 source compatibility check: the shipped session type already accepts `user-link`, and the complete auth-provenance and session-selection modules are byte-unchanged in this candidate. The fix retains an existing stored profile/provenance at the fresh-session sanitizer; it changes no schema, serialized format, storage writer, or credential authority. This is source-contract evidence, not an installed stable-to-candidate execution test.
- The broader Doctor integration test fails identically on the base and candidate: the `memory-wiki` migration declaration is rejected in plugin preflight before cron migration. That unrelated failure is not repaired or called passing here. No installed-release upgrade test was run; the migration evidence uses persisted legacy fixtures. No live jobs, configuration, credentials, or runtime state were changed.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On the 2026.9 maintenance line, Microsoft Edge text-to-speech fails with `Unexpected server response: 403`. The bundled `node-edge-tts@1.2.10` still opens the retired Bing synthesis endpoint, so every spoken reply and `/tts audio` request fails.

Upstream fixed this in #172381 by moving to `node-edge-tts@1.2.11`, which targets `api.msedgeservices.com`. This PR carries that same fix onto `extended-stable/2026.9.33`, because the 2026.9 line is the current extended-stable (LTS-equivalent) line and the regression is user-facing.

## What This Change Does

- bumps `node-edge-tts` from 1.2.10 to 1.2.11 in `package.json` and `extensions/microsoft/package.json`
- regenerates `pnpm-lock.yaml` and adds the reviewed exact-version exemption in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`
- adds an offline regression asserting the `api.msedgeservices.com` synthesis host and path
- documents the outbound allowlist (`api.msedgeservices.com` for synthesis, `speech.platform.bing.com` for voice discovery)

No configuration keys, plugin SDK surface, migrations or runtime requirements are added.

## Evidence

Environment: OpenCode container, branch `backport/2026.9.33-edge-tts-172381` at `670157f00d0065ed79010acf06bc10e444f3f0c8`, base `extended-stable/2026.9.33` (`5873f8174e`). The live test used an empty isolated `HOME`, so it did not read personal configuration, credentials, or a newer OpenClaw state database.

### Real Microsoft behavior proof on the September candidate

Command:

```console
HOME=/workspace/openclaw/.live-home-proof node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-live.mts --no-quiet -- extensions/microsoft/microsoft.live.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

Redacted output (public format identifiers only; no IPs, keys, phone numbers, or private endpoints):

```text
RUN  v5.0.1 /workspace/openclaw

Microsoft synthesis: {
  bytes: 24336,
  format: 'audio-24khz-48kbitrate-mono-mp3',
  extension: '.mp3'
}
✓ microsoft plugin live > synthesizes nonempty MP3 audio 1099ms
✓ microsoft plugin live > lists Edge speech voices 1472ms

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       2 passed (2)
Duration    56.04s
```

This exercises the production provider path through `buildMicrosoftSpeechProvider().synthesize()` and confirms that the September candidate returns nonempty MP3 audio from the real Microsoft transport.

### Additional validation

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`: passed; `node-edge-tts` 1.2.11 installed
- `extensions/microsoft/tts.test.ts`: 6/6 passed, including the new endpoint guard
- `extensions/microsoft/speech-provider.optional-capture.test.ts`: 3/3 passed

The broad local extension wrapper could not verify managed-process cleanup in this container before starting Vitest. The focused live runner above completed successfully and produced the requested real behavior proof.

No push to upstream and no merge were performed.

prs.title: fix(agents): incrementally append tagged stream snapshots
prs.body:
Closes #175441

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Gateway CPU is blocked for seconds on long replies from tagged-provider streams (`enforceFinalTag`), because the whole reply is re-rendered twice per streamed delta (5.7 s at 32 KB, 22.7 s at 64 KB per #175441).

## User Impact

User impact: long streamed replies from tagged providers no longer stall the Gateway as they grow, so other sessions and clients stay responsive while a reply streams. Streamed output is unchanged; the fast path falls back to the existing extraction whenever it cannot prove an append is equivalent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an incremental fast path for tagged block-reply streaming when `enforceFinalTag` is enabled, so each delta no longer re-extracts the full accumulated text.

- The fast path appends directly only when the existing stream state is known to be verbatim and the incoming delta contains no markup that could invalidate that assumption.
- A trailing reasoning-close guard keeps a later delta from bypassing canonical reconciliation after a `</think>`-style boundary.
- Whenever those invariants do not hold, the canonical extraction/reconciliation path runs as before, so there is still one owner of the resulting stream state.
- Added differential tests cover reasoning-close boundaries, supported close-tag variants, mid-stream chunking/draining, and equivalence with canonical extraction.

Accepted tradeoff: the append-unstable final-answer sanitizer is mutually exclusive with the `enforceFinalTag`/`blockVerbatim` fast path, so the fast path never has to account for it.

## Evidence

- Focused `update-stream-items` test: 48/48 passed.
- Differential fuzzing against canonical extraction: 68,702 steps, 0 mismatches; the fast path was exercised 3,316 times.
- Full embedded-agent-subscribe suite: 35 files / 524 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`: 29 shards passed.
- `oxfmt --check`: passed.
- oxlint: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Autoreview reviewed the diff and the tests/evidence (it did not execute the code) and produced no accepted or actionable findings. Its one P2 finding concerned the append-unstable final-answer sanitizer; it was investigated and disproved because that sanitizer is mutually exclusive with the `enforceFinalTag`/`blockVerbatim` fast path.
- Not run here: repo-wide CI; this branch is 1 commit ahead and 248 behind `main`, and I did not rebase it.

prs.title: fix(cli): interactive setup works on PostgreSQL
prs.body:
Related: #175069

## What Problem This Solves

Interactive setup accessed state before selecting the configured PostgreSQL engine. Real CLI PTYs against PostgreSQL 17 reproduced `onboard` and `setup --wizard` failing with “Existing SQLite state data cannot switch engines” after creating 101 shared-state and 57 agent SQLite tables. The legacy `crestodian` skip route returned exit 0 but left 101 shared-state SQLite tables.

## User Impact

All three entries now select the configured engine before their first state access. PostgreSQL application database files remain anchors, alongside the existing intentional local journals. SQLite behavior is preserved. Setup keeps consent-gated malformed-config recovery, structured JSON failures, immutable-config guidance, and interruption status.

`onboard --reset` refuses PostgreSQL routing and unreadable source configuration before changing anything. Reset retains database state, so automatically switching retained PostgreSQL anchors to SQLite is unsafe. Rerun setup without `--reset`, or explicitly port supported stores to SQLite before resetting. Standalone `openclaw reset --scope config` remains the file-only recovery path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Setup keeps one immutable CLI one-shot process role. Guided foreground quick start and the classic wizard's temporary Gateway on containers without user systemd launch a separate Gateway CLI process. The child owns Gateway admission throughout its lifetime. Existing managed service installation and Gateway lifecycle semantics are unchanged; the old embedded starts and their separate auth override are removed.

The child preserves the caller working directory, so relative configured paths resolve exactly as they did during setup. Canonical executable and loader selection remain with the CLI invocation owner.

The child uses the existing parent-bound lifetime and targeted shutdown contracts. Setup preserves interruption status 130/143. Readiness observes early child exit, cancels the losing probe, and completes before TUI startup even with `--skip-health`. Failed readiness closes and joins the child before local TUI fallback. Credentials remain in configured environment/SecretRefs.

For malformed source, consented Doctor file-only repair runs before engine selection. Declining or unsuccessful recovery opens no database. Bare root retains its previous conservative launch owner and manual Doctor guidance. JSON setup retains structured errors, and read-only/Nix configuration reports the config owner's immutable-file error before recovery or storage access.

SQLite reset defers final engine selection until cleanup has removed the old configuration, then uses the canonical selector before setup state access. PostgreSQL reset is refused before cleanup instead of carrying a stale engine, silently porting data, or retaining arbitrary old secret settings. The process role never changes.

Interactive remote setup still accesses local migration/provider metadata and database-backed plugin lifecycle leases. It therefore needs a resolvable local database credential even when configuring a remote Gateway. Skipping engine selection would recreate SQLite fallback or refuse a PostgreSQL anchor later. This existing ownership limitation is documented; a truly file-only remote path is outside this change.

## Evidence

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, runtime build, scoped typecheck/lint/format, docs links, line-cap and mock-export checks passed. Independent autoreview is clean, including the latest reset follow-up.
- 299 existing regressions passed, including 62 real TUI PTY cases. Additional Gateway ownership, readiness, signal, finalization, and trusted-proxy regressions passed.
- Eight real CLI PTY scenarios passed locally and again in CI on final head `d50657ec500`: the three requested commands on SQLite and PostgreSQL, malformed-config recovery, and bare-root refusal. They assert persisted config/state, PostgreSQL anchor-only application stores, subsequent authenticated Gateway startup, clean shutdown, immutable parent role, and Ctrl+C exit 130. Final local run: 160 seconds of test time / 245 seconds including preparation. Final-head CI scenario times: 4.7–49.2 seconds each.
- The PTYs defer external AI setup deliberately: they prove setup persistence, storage, and authenticated Gateway handoff without external model calls. The legacy `crestodian` skip route intentionally saves consent without workspace provisioning. The TUI fixture declares its unsupported optional program-status protocol; strict rendering assertions are unchanged.
- Final routing/config guards: 187 passed. Six real subprocess cases cover malformed SQLite/PostgreSQL config with JSON output and immutable-config guidance. They fail before the corresponding corrections and pass afterward without opening storage or changing config.
- Final reset proof: 74 onboarding/reset tests passed. All three retained-PostgreSQL-anchor cases first failed at the real onboarding writer after cleanup removed config; they now refuse before cleanup and preserve the original configuration. Unreadable-source cases also preserve it. SQLite reset continues to work. File run: 40.8 seconds including cold preparation. No Trash operation was run.

CI exposed two test-cost issues. The long PostgreSQL refusal/resume case now uses the existing real-native-worker reuse fixture in its own file; its ownership, RLS, drift, preservation, and resume assertions remain intact. Environment-sensitive preflight cases keep fresh workers. The focused six-test run passed; the case took 3.0 seconds locally, and subsequent infrastructure CI passed.

The former integration job spent 1,099 seconds in command integrations and 269 seconds in command diagnostics before timing out during still-passing plugin tests. Current `main` independently replaced those two fixed groups with the shared timing-weighted three-shard scheduler. This branch adopts that owner unchanged and contributes the measured 416.622-second cost of the serial interactive PTY file. The partition test proves complete coverage without overlap. No additional workflow, concurrency, or timeout changes remain in this PR.

That run also timed out the lost-COMMIT test and then failed the following config-pinning assertion. Both passed on the exact clean CI base locally, so the Linux failure is not claimed as reproduced or proven inherited. The lost-COMMIT test now verifies the PostgreSQL anchor and canonical committed rows through its existing independent client, removing a redundant reverse migration. Dedicated recovery tests retain reverse-port coverage. The two focused cases passed in 9.1 and 4.0 seconds; four runner-partition tests passed in 2.6 seconds. Independent review is clean.

The final real-child regression first failed in both plugin-generation variants because the child reported the package working directory. It now reports the distinct caller workspace while retaining the freshly installed plugin inventory. All 11 foreground lifecycle/child-inventory tests pass (42.5 seconds including cold preparation); scoped typecheck, lint, and fresh independent review pass.

Final-head [CI run 39066684710](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39066684710) completed: **70 passed, 3 failed, 25 skipped**. All three PostgreSQL shards actually ran. All eight real interactive CLI cases passed on this head. The two failing PG shards contain six inherited recovery failures; the third failed check is the derived CI gate. prs.title: fix(compaction): add bounded resumable recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Required preflight compaction can fail before an agent run begins. When recoverable and terminal failures collapse into free-form text, callers can either terminate a reply that could continue safely or accidentally soften a cancellation, authentication, binding, or malformed-request failure that must remain terminal.

Related: #100778 and the closed, unmerged #116404.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Introduces a closed `CompactionFailure` identity and carries it through embedded compaction, queued execution, harness, context-engine, and plugin boundaries.
- Preserves terminal-identity precedence across primary and recovery attempts and keeps ambiguous legacy failure data fail-closed.
- Preserves the original typed/provider error across the compaction safeguard cancellation boundary, so a provider 429 remains retryable instead of collapsing to generic `guard_blocked`.
- Validates the complete closed failure envelope before it may authorize continuation, select another compaction owner, or cross a public delegate boundary; malformed status values, legacy raw fields, and extra fields fail closed.
- Preserves a validated alternate-owner fallback unchanged and stops the generic model-candidate loop before any configured backup model can run.
- Retains released-plugin compatibility only when no `disposition` property is present.
- Uses a dedicated 1,024-token degraded-recovery safety margin in addition to `reserveTokensFloor`, independent from the soft threshold that triggers preflight, so the normal 4,000-token path has a reachable but bounded recovery window.
- Limits mandatory preflight recovery to one bounded attempt.
- Emits a degraded-compaction notice when a transient failure is safely bypassed instead of reporting the attempt as a normal no-op.
- Documents the public compaction failure contract without increasing the capped public export surface.

## User Impact

A transient preflight compaction failure can recover without permanently terminating the reply, while cancellation, authentication, binding, malformed-request, and other terminal failures remain blocking. Recovery is deliberately bounded so it cannot loop or continue into unsafe token pressure.

## Evidence

### Current final-refresh head `3fddb6277f64ff1d089df97096b11e6503de8071`

- Normally merged the final frozen `upstream/main` at `3d2f134d16f6c227094ab7f0b73c294472e8f0a5`. The only conflict was the generated Plugin SDK JSONL baseline; the combined tree preserved current-main generation semantics and regenerated the canonical artifact (**204 replacements** versus the frozen base).
- Final overlap/baseline validation produced **189 passes**. Three additional harness-selection assertions fail only because current main still compares POSIX `/tmp/...` literals with normalized Windows `C:\tmp\...` paths; the same assertions and expectations are present on the frozen base, so they are not represented as branch regressions.
- Core production, scripts, and extension TypeScript surfaces passed. The test-type surface remains blocked only by three inherited non-PR current-main diagnostics: `src/gateway/managed-image-actions.e2e.test.ts` `TS2345`, plus `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.ts` `TS2339` and `TS2493`; it is not represented as green.
- Plugin SDK generation/API baseline, export synchronization, and surface checks passed.
- Targeted formatting passed across all 28 applicable task files; type-aware lint passed for 25 core and 2 extension task files; max-lines and `git diff --check` passed.
- Mandatory exact-branch autoreview ran against `3d2f134d16f6c227094ab7f0b73c294472e8f0a5`: the 312,597-byte safe bundle completed in one pass with zero findings. Final result: **clean, 0.98 confidence, no accepted/actionable findings**.
- TruffleHog was clean in autoreview (**10.5s**) and in the final local exact-branch preflight (**8.6s**) using pinned v3.95.9.
- Exact-head hosted CI [run 31419187116](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31419187116) completed with **53 successful**, **13 skipped**, and **4 failed test shards**; the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` failed only because those shards failed. The exact failures were `small-11` cron (job `93555895123`), `small-9` agent-runner progress (`93555895256`), `small-2` changed-target routing (`93555895132`), and `large-6` UI cursor policy (`93555895143`). All failed files are outside this PR delta, and the same four signatures reproduced on unrelated PR #115786. Live main subsequently repaired the cron assertions in `21e7f200aa84dd3cf76681040212ec5a2be37eea`; the other three failed test blobs are byte-identical to live main. These are recorded as inherited current-main failures, not branch-local regressions, and CI is explicitly **not** represented as green.

This evidence does **not** resolve the remaining maintainer product decision: maintainers must explicitly accept or reject `CompactResult.failure` as a permanent additive plugin-facing contract. The PR is not being represented as proof-complete or merge-ready until that decision is made.
### Comprehensive repaired-head proof on `c01c7d2a59211d2f8cb16942cebc1cc73947855e`

- The two August 8 review findings are fixed at their policy boundaries:
  - typed native-binding fallback requires the strict closed-envelope validator before it can select the context engine;
  - the public context-engine delegate forwards only strictly validated failure envelopes.
- Sibling policy/export paths were audited and hardened: malformed typed data cannot authorize the CLI's unsupported-harness fallback, and queued context-engine results cannot re-export it. Released untyped harness metadata remains compatible only when `disposition` is genuinely absent.
- Regression run: **308 tests passed** across the strict failure contract, configured model-fallback runner, and embedded/queued compaction hook lanes. The configured-chain regression returns the original `disposition: "fallback"` result and proves the backup model is never called.
- Core production and test TypeScript, `pnpm deadcode:full`, Plugin SDK API generation/check, formatting, lint, diff checks, mandatory autoreview, and TruffleHog passed.
- Full `pnpm build` passed, including all nine runtime bundle stages, the CLI bootstrap guard, 151 public Plugin SDK subpaths, native plugin control-plane loading, and Control UI performance limits.
- Sixteen repository preflight guards passed. The changed-file route could not start because the local Crabbox binary failed its own `--version` / `--help` sanity check; exact-dependency local checks were used instead. GitHub CI remains authoritative for the unrelated broad lockfile lane.

### Codex protocol evidence

Current official Codex source was audited at `266c6920d9b82fe4d68959529565256b12a9be99`:

- `thread/compact/start` loads the thread before submitting `Op::Compact` (`codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs:1913-1924`), and the response is sent only after that handler returns (`codex-rs/app-server/src/message_processor.rs:1491-1495`).
- Submission enqueues work; a separate session loop executes `Op::Compact` (`codex-rs/core/src/session/mod.rs:843-859,880-889`; `codex-rs/core/src/session/handlers.rs:818-820`). Progress can therefore precede the RPC acknowledgement, which the existing OpenClaw watcher handles.
- Manual compaction emits the canonical `turn/started`, `contextCompaction` item start/completion, and terminal turn lifecycle (`codex-rs/core/src/compact.rs:138-150,242-244,381-382`; `codex-rs/core/src/tasks/mod.rs:379-407,795-812`).
- A well-formed but unloaded thread returns JSON-RPC `-32600` with `thread not found: <id>`; Codex's integration test asserts both the code and message (`thread_processor.rs:865-879`; `app-server/tests/suite/v2/compaction.rs:347-374`). OpenClaw preserves that binding metadata and maps only this released message contract to `stale_thread_binding`.

The PR's remaining Codex producer change is limited to the sanitized fallback identity.

### Redacted Gateway canaries

Three disposable Gateway scenarios passed on the preceding source-identical merge head `62b9896cdaa6680fd85cdbc9d289395714975ead`, using loopback-only providers/plugins and no paid or external request:

```json
{"testedCommit":"62b9896cdaa6680fd85cdbc9d289395714975ead","passed":true,"retryable":{"status":429,"compactionHttpAttempts":3,"replyContinued":true,"degradedEvidence":true},"terminal":{"status":401,"compactionHttpAttempts":3,"replyBlocked":true,"terminalEvidence":true},"malformed":{"failure":{"disposition":"fallback","reason":"stale_thread_binding","extraField":"present"},"compactInvocations":1,"harnessRunAttempts":1,"providerRequests":0,"safeNoticeShown":true,"fallbackBlocked":true},"externalNetwork":false,"productionModified":false}
```

- Retryable 429: one bounded degraded preflight was recorded and exactly one second model reply (`CANARY_REPLY_OK`) continued.
- Terminal 401: the preflight failed, no second model reply request occurred, and the safe recovery notice was visible.
- Malformed typed fallback: a real installed test harness returned `disposition: fallback` plus a legacy extra field and spoofed thread-not-found prose. The exact built Gateway invoked compaction but did not execute a second harness attempt, made zero provider requests, and showed only the safe “auto-compaction could not recover this turn” notice.

All temporary Gateway state, plugin files, and transcripts were deleted afterward; no host service or production state was modified.

The malformed-envelope scenario was then rebuilt and rerun on the current exact head after the `ba5895a976a` main merge:

```json
{"testedCommit":"b66aa28ffd11e7a91081be02ccb72d932ed1ea69","passed":true,"exactHeadBuilt":true,"seedSucceeded":true,"malformedCompactionRan":true,"malformedFallbackBlocked":true,"noSecondHarnessAttempt":true,"providerRequests":0,"failedClosed":true,"externalNetwork":false,"productionModified":false}
```

prs.title: fix(matrix): warn when open DMs lack an allowlist wildcard
prs.body:
Fixes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89254.

Matrix already denies inbound DMs when `dm.policy: "open"` has no effective `dm.allowFrom: ["*"]`. The shared configuration diagnostic accidentally skips Matrix because its DM configuration is nested. Make that diagnostic mode-aware, cover default, account-scoped, and inherited-wildcard configurations, and document the existing requirement.

Runtime authorization, pairing semantics, and explicit allowlists remain unchanged. Release-note context: this makes the established fail-closed Matrix DM policy actionable rather than changing its behavior.

prs.title: fix(ui): model picker closes when tapping a provider on iPhone
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on iPhone, the Control UI chat model picker closes when you tap a provider (for example "OpenAI") to expand its models.

## User Impact

User impact: on iOS Safari, tapping a provider in the model picker expands it, so you can reach and pick models on a phone. The fix lives in the shared overlay layer, so other Control UI menus with tappable buttons no longer close on iOS either.

## Why This Change Was Made

On a touch tap, the browser sends `pointerup` before the compatibility `mousedown` that moves focus, so the overlay registry no longer treats the gesture as in progress. iOS also doesn't focus a tapped button. It focuses the nearest focusable ancestor instead, which is the `tabindex=-1` main region. The registry's focus-outside dismissal saw focus leave the picker and closed it before the tap's `click` reached the provider toggle.

The registry now remembers the last pointer release. When the next focus change lands on an element that contains that release target, and the target is inside an open overlay, the overlay stays open. The remembered release covers only that one focus change, and the next `pointerdown` or `keydown` clears it. Real outside taps and keyboard focus moves still dismiss as before.

## Evidence

- **Diagnosis:** frames from a screen recording on an iPhone showed the picker opening and then closing on each provider tap. A traced Playwright repro confirmed the close comes from the registry's `focusin` handler after focus lands on `main.content`, and that catalog refreshes aren't involved.
- **New unit test** (`overlay-lifecycle.browser.test.ts`): focus falling back to an ancestor after an in-overlay release keeps the overlay open, and a later outside focus change still dismisses. It fails without the fix and passes with it.
- **New touch e2e test** (`chat-model-picker-touch.e2e.test.ts`, 390×844, `hasTouch`): tapping the OpenAI provider with iOS-style button focus expands it and keeps the picker open. It fails without the fix (`aria-expanded` stays `false`) and passes with it.
- **Existing suites:**
  - Overlay lifecycle/shadow/anchor, select-picker and chat model picker browser tests: 101 passed.
  - Touch, picker interaction contract and model controls e2e tests: 18 passed.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and `pnpm tsgo:ui` are clean on the changed files.
- **Autoreview** (Codex, P0–P1): scoped-clean.

**Gaps:**
- Playwright can't drive real iOS Safari, and its Linux WebKit build doesn't send click events for touchscreen taps. The e2e test reproduces iOS by making tapped buttons not take focus.
- There are no screenshots because nothing looks different. The fix changes whether the menu stays open, not how it renders.

**Not in this PR:** tapping plain, non-interactive text inside the picker can still close it through a separate path. The composer's click-to-focus handler moves focus to the message box. That will be a separate fix.

prs.title: docs(google-vertex): add Google Vertex AI provider setup guide
prs.body: Related PRs: #118745, #87800, #83971 Related issues: #56253, #85864, #79595, #79837, #11413, #49191, #50053, #52476, #48910, #77643, #55572, #53566, #9729 ## What Problem This Solves OpenClaw has no documentation for the `google-vertex` provider. Users who want to run Gemini models through Google Cloud Vertex AI have no setup path to follow: the provider has no onboarding wizard entry, and the only mention was a couple of lines on the Google (Gemini) page. Anyone on Google Cloud hit trial-and-error to get authentication, environment variables, model selection, and the gateway working together. ## Why This Change Was Made Vertex AI is a distinct provider in the bundled Google plugin that authenticates via Application Default Credentials, but it is setup-only (no wizard), so it needs a clear manual path. This adds a dedicated provider guide documenting the real, working flow on current `main`: authenticate with ADC (gcloud user credentials or a service-account key), set the model in `openclaw.json` and environment variables in `~/.openclaw/.env`, verify, provision the gateway, and use the agent. Every step was validated against live behavior rather than assumptions. This PR documents the Vertex AI ADC behavior shipped in #118745, and ships the documentation portion of the earlier, broader #87800. ## User Impact Users can now follow a single, accurate page to get Gemini models running through Vertex AI end to end. The guide covers both auth sources (gcloud ADC with auto-detected credentials, and service-account keys), where each environment variable must live (notably that `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` must go in `~/.openclaw/.env`, not `openclaw.json`), the bundled model catalog, verification via `openclaw models status`, and troubleshooting. The Google (Gemini) page now cross-links to it, and it appears in the providers sidebar as "Google (Vertex AI)". ## Evidence Verified end to end on a GCE VM against `main`: - **gcloud ADC path:** `gcloud config set project` + `gcloud auth application-default login` + project/location in `~/.openclaw/.env` → `openclaw models status` shows `google-vertex ... source=gcloud adc` → `openclaw tui` responds via Vertex AI. - **Service-account path:** key created via `gcloud iam service-accounts keys create`, `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` set in `~/.openclaw/.env` → resolves and responds. - **Detection is real:** `gcloud auth application-default revoke` flips `models status` to `[indeterminate]` ("auth readiness could not be confirmed"). - **Docs checks:** `pnpm check:docs` passes (format, markdownlint, MDX, i18n-glossary, link audit — 0 issues). --- **Rendered provider page: `/providers/google-vertex`** --- **Bundled model catalog: `openclaw models list --provider google-vertex`** --- **gcloud ADC configured: `openclaw models status` resolves (`source=gcloud adc`)** --- **Service-account key configured: `openclaw models status` resolves the same way** --- **Gateway provisioned without changing Vertex AI config: `openclaw onboard --auth-choice skip`** --- **Agent responds end to end via Vertex AI** ## Metadata-server ADC: tested, not currently supported end to end ClawSweeper flagged that the guide omits metadata-server / Workload Identity ADC. I tested this end to end on a GCE VM, and it does **not** currently work through the full agent request path, so the guide intentionally stays file-based. **Repro (GCE VM):** - Attached service account with Editor + the `cloud-platform` scope; `aiplatform.googleapis.com` enabled. - No credential file (`gcloud auth application-default revoke`; `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` unset). - `~/.openclaw/.env` sets only `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION`. - `model.primary = google-vertex/gemini-3.5-flash`; gateway restarted (confirmed healthy and listening on 18789). **Result:** `openclaw models status` shows `[indeterminate]` (expected), and sending a message in the TUI fails before any request reaches Vertex: ``` No API key found for provider "google-vertex". ... | missing-provider-auth ``` **Root cause:** the credential is resolved synchronously by `resolveGoogleVertexConfigApiKey` -> `hasGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserAdcSync` (`extensions/google/vertex-adc.ts`), which requires a credentials file. With metadata-only identity there is no file, so it returns undefined and the request is rejected with `missing-provider-auth` before the transport runs. The `google-auth-library` metadata fallback in the transport is real but is never reached on this path. The no-file metadata regression test drives the transport directly with a mocked `GoogleAuth`, so it passes without going through the auth gate and does not cover the end-to-end agent path. **Conclusion:** this guide documents the file-based paths (gcloud user ADC, service-account key), which work today. Making attached-SA / Workload Identity usable without a file requires a runtime change to the auth gate (ambient env-marker evidence, as originally prototyped in #87800). We can track this as follow-up after the documentation in this PR is in place rather than documenting a path that currently returns `missing-provider-auth`. ## Vertex AI Express API key: intentionally out of scope Review cycles have asked both to document and to remove `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` on this page. It is deliberately not covered, because the transport cannot perform an express-mode request. `buildGoogleVertexRequestUrl` (`extensions/google/transport-stream.ts:434-446`) always emits a project- and location-scoped path and throws when either value is unset, while Vertex AI in express mode requires the global `aiplatform.googleapis.com` endpoint with no `projects` or `locations` segment. `model.baseUrl` overrides only the origin, so no config reaches that shape. The route also has no test coverage for `google-vertex` (every Vertex transport test uses the ADC marker `gcp-vertex-credentials`) and was never verified live. Per the P1 note in the review, adding endpoint-specific operator instructions without that proof would be wrong, so the guide stays scoped to ADC, as its summary, intro, and auth bullet already state.

prs.title: refactor(openai): simplify realtime retirement flow
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Realtime retirement splits local retirement and remote disposal into manual synchronous/Promise branches. Use one async operation and retain the existing completion/failure handlers outside it.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Real cleanup, retry, capacity and settlement protections remain; synchronous hangup initiation is not promised.

## Why This Change Was Made

This removes 16 net production lines (+15/-31) and one immediate-timing assertion, with no test case removed. This is the OpenAI area slice of the previously assembled wide cleanup family, split under the campaign's area-sizing rule.

Synchronous admission removal, shared closing ownership, local bridge retirement, original remote cleanup capability, capacity reservation, retry budget/delays, late-answer join, old-broker custody, and awaited settlement remain intact. No public SDK, config, protocol, dependency, or persisted data shape changes.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Void local retirement yields a microtask before remote hangup; void/no-op disposal settles bookkeeping asynchronously. The callers join the closing Promise, while admission removal and local bridge close stay synchronous. The removed assertion pinned same-stack hangup initiation only; awaited once-only cleanup remains covered. Original retry machinery came from #137636 and #137574, whose first 503 was explicitly injected, not a human production incident requiring the manual representation. Real remote-resource and capacity protections remain.
- No new machinery handles hypothetical throws from trusted logger/Map/Set bookkeeping callbacks. Completion stays outside the operation catch, so callback failures are not reclassified as failed remote disposal.

## Evidence

- Independent complete two-file review: scoped-clean P0-P2, 0.96; final source verification passed.
- Focused syntax lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. No import edges added; no new runtime cycle can be introduced by this local control-flow cut.
- Focused runtime baseline stopped before assertions when actual cold-worker compilation began, honoring the shared-host budget. No runtime pass or product failure claimed; no equivalent cold retry.
- Targeted package-boundary types did not pass: built SDK declarations are absent (49 missing-module diagnostics), plus four diagnostics in unchanged dependencies (delegation controller, offer HTTP, session). No broad SDK build, declaration substitute, suppression, retry, skip, or timeout change was used. This is not type-aware lint proof.
- Mandatory suppression guard: 14 passed, 64.36s Vitest/100.05s wrapper. Exact-head hosted CI supplies broad runtime/type proof before landing.

Release-note context: internal cleanup only; no user-facing feature removal. Live provider/device proof is not claimed.

prs.title: perf(ui): paint restored sidebar before mounting conversation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Warm cached reloads can postpone first contentful paint until both the sidebar and conversation pane render. The MessageChannel split in #175772 still lets Chrome run both tasks inside one animation frame.

## User Impact

The restored sidebar paints sooner, while final conversation content stays within one frame of its previous timing. Retained receipts and compact warm startup responses are preserved. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing cache owner still publishes synchronously, then releases routing through requestAnimationFrame followed by a timer. Resolving inside rAF would still mount the pane before paint. A 100 ms timer fallback handles suspended frames; connection and disposal continue to release routing immediately.

This replaces the channel and port cleanup, with no new owner, module, or export. Production delta: **−1 line**; test delta: +11 lines.

## Evidence

Four unprofiled concurrent A/B pairs, with identical synthetic fixtures and swapped 16-core halves under an exclusive lock. Differences are **candidate minus baseline**, in milliseconds:

| Pair | FCP | Restore-frame blocking | Final retained message |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | −68 | −8.4 | +11.0 |
| 2 | 0 | 0 | +1.7 |
| 3 | −68 | −9.4 | −11.4 |
| 4 | −52 | −5.8 | +6.7 |
| **Median paired difference** | **−60** | **−7.1** | **+4.2** |

Candidate initial restore had no ≥50 ms long-animation frame in all four runs; baseline had one in three runs. This means no observed long frame, not zero restore work. Median paired sidebar timing improved 42.55 ms. Total blocking before hello was neutral (+0.25 ms): the pane work moves after paint. Cold FCP (−2 ms) and final-message timing (+0.1 ms) were neutral.

All final row counts and ordered sidebar keys matched. All three retained receipts survived; warm startup stayed **306 framed bytes / 224 payload bytes, zero messages**, and cached content appeared before hello. Warm navigation offsets were 0–1 ms.

Two separate traced pairs proved actual Chrome Paint events between the sidebar IDB task and MountedPane on the candidate, versus none on baseline. Trace timings are excluded from the table. These inspected synthetic filmstrip frames show the baseline still loading at 243.3 ms and the candidate's populated sidebar already painted at 227.9 ms:

![Before: loading skeleton at 243.3 ms](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/21757238-611e-415c-92cb-76eb049531ea)

![After: populated sidebar at 227.9 ms, before conversation rendering finishes](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a7ed0682-ff55-4b97-abf2-eab6b80e6028)

The settled before/after screenshots are byte-identical.

Focused owner tests **31/31** (4.46 s command wall time), route warm boot **9/9** (1.52 s), sidebar integration **25/25** (1.58 s), changed-file formatting, scoped lint, and diff checks pass. New tests reject both the original MessageChannel path and resolving directly inside rAF; they cover suppressed frames and immediate connection/disposal release. Independent review is clean through P2. CI caught an existing sidebar integration fixture awaiting the new handoff with its fake clock stopped. The timeout reproduced locally; advancing pending timers after IDB restoration fixes it while retaining every shared-read and invalidation assertion. All 44 checks on the final head passed, including the CI gate: [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39066912919).

<details>
<summary>Measurement scope and limits</summary>

Production renderer on an isolated Linux sandbox, Chromium 155, visible headless rendering verified by trace Paint events and compositor filmstrips. Fixture: 80 messages, 80 retained sessions (10 displayed), five pending inputs, session metadata, and 150 commands. Separate state directories and loopback ports; CPU halves 96–111 / 112–127 swap each pair. Outside load was recorded with mpstat for context. Preparation used CPUs 64–95 with sequential writes; dirty pages remained below the 2 GB limit, including cleanup. The owned sandbox has been removed.

Baseline `5c7123f25123a586fffbe3863b8909072b094283`; final head `1c0f3f907bfa126d423aba07b889e34a50d53507`. Measured production source was verified against the candidate source map. Both sides used the same dependencies, including exact Solid rc.14. Shared measurement dependencies differ from the lock in Vite (8.3.2 vs 8.3.4), Playwright (1.63 vs 1.64), and two CodeMirror patch versions. These are synthetic renderer comparisons, not a new production-session measurement. Suspended-frame fallback is unit-tested, not timed in a background browser tab.

</details>

prs.title: perf(doctor): scope and reuse maintenance table checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a historical upgrade, later current-schema Doctor admissions inherited the migration owner's cumulative table set. A credential source read checked 18 unrelated historical tables; credential cleanup checked those same tables despite modifying only two. Passing scoped checks also repeated without intervening writes.

## User Impact

Candidate-side update behavior: automatic Doctor still runs whole-database QUICK, scoped FULL for migration/repair tables, and FK checks. Explicit FULL, corruption refusal, private-image certification and rollback validation retain their coverage. The installed updater still executes its own version's behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current-schema callback admissions now declare their own mutation tables. Read-only admission has an empty scope; schema convergence and direct schema-maintenance owners retain their migration coverage. Within the same exclusive QUICK maintenance owner, passing table checks reuse the existing physical write receipt. Transaction-local reuse additionally follows the existing native mutation witness and schema listener. Any write conservatively expires committed proof; row writes, DDL and rollback expire transaction proof. No new mutation counters, probes, generations or cross-thread handshakes.

## Removed work and accepted edge cases

- Later callback admission no longer inherits historical table checks: unrelated index inconsistency remains outside the documented QUICK contract; explicit FULL still detects it.
- Repeated scoped FULL on an unchanged image/table reuses the owner's passing receipt: out-of-band writers during exclusive offline custody remain unsupported. Every observed native mutation invalidates conservatively, including unrelated writes.
- Transaction proof stays connection-local and never becomes committed proof on rollback.

## Evidence

The new auth and receipt regressions fail on the unchanged base and pass on this branch. Auth read has zero scoped checks; auth cleanup checks exactly two tables; unchanged same-table checks run once; a sibling write, transaction write, DDL or rollback forces rechecking; explicit FULL remains unchanged. Existing structural-corruption and touched-index refusal regressions pass.

Public Doctor upgraded the same synthetic stable agent24/state20 fixture to agent31/state27, preserving retained-row samples and recovery assertions. This uses the large quickpath recipe with a smaller population; the base reproduces its 292 scoped checks.

| Doctor mode / measurement | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Default whole QUICK | 16 | 16 |
| Default scoped FULL | 292 | 226 |
| Default FK | 17 | 17 |
| Default total integrity/FK statements | 325 | 259 |
| Default integrity-worker requests | 1 | 1 |
| Default observed seconds | 136.255 | 144.171 |
| Explicit whole FULL | 12 | 12 |
| Explicit scoped FULL | 42 | 42 |
| Explicit FK | 12 | 12 |
| Explicit observed seconds | 134.170 | 151.907 |

All 66 removed checks come from later agent admissions: auth read 18→0, auth cleanup 18→2, entry rewrite 18→4, title repair 18→0. The base has 153 labeled image/table pairs and 139 repeats; those repeats are not all redundant because mutations intervene. Receipt reuse is covered by regressions but saves no additional calls in this fixture. QUICK, private-image certification, migration pre/post checks, and FK counts remain unchanged. Times are observations from a busy host, not latency claims. The default candidate harness's final HEAD-stability assertion saw the already-running implementation being committed; all behavior assertions passed, and all 15 frozen implementation-file hashes match the committed head. Explicit FULL passed without that caveat.

The five requested PostgreSQL infra files passed on both base and candidate: **5 files / 28 tests / 0 skips**, Node 24.22.0, PostgreSQL 17.11, internal-disk HOME/TMPDIR, two workers. The original setup attempt lacked `unaccent`; it was corrected before the valid comparison.

| PG file, wall seconds including setup | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| archive-restore | 219.101 | 247.920 |
| doctor-migration, including v30 rollback | 200.978 | 201.516 |
| matrix-roots | 313.241 | 385.038 |
| port-command | 39.769 | 44.186 |
| update-preflight, five-family restore | 131.981 | 135.076 |
| Whole command | 539.966 | 527.681 |

These overlapping per-file times reflect shared-host load and automatic scheduling; they do not establish a latency improvement or regression. All frozen candidate source hashes match the committed head. Task PostgreSQL and fixture scratch are cleaned up.

This is offline Doctor work, with no warmed-turn savings claim. Area T1 remains 0; the CI ratchet reports global 181→181 (compatibility tier 10→10). Dialect counts are unchanged. No SDK, schema version, engine-routing or PostgreSQL behavior change.

Two independent Codex autoreviews are clean through P2 (implementation, then the one-line wrapper manifest addition). Type-aware lint, source/export contracts, Madge (zero cycles), and database ratchets pass. Canonical Knip production findings match actual main `140dda0308c` exactly; all candidate all-exports findings also occur on that main, with zero candidate-only findings. These inherited findings are routed to the main repair owner. The [implementation CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39065162698) passed Node behavior tests and production types but caught an overloaded-call type error in the new test spy. Final commit `e4341ce6d1b` removes unnecessary argument forwarding; the exact failed state/logging type graph, all four auth cases, and targeted type-aware lint now pass. This is test-only; production and measurement inputs are unchanged. The original run was superseded by the test-fix push: 90 jobs passed, the corrected type job failed, and its three still-running PostgreSQL jobs were cancelled rather than failed. Both requested local PostgreSQL arms passed as reported above. [Replacement CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39066050921) now passes every static/type/lint gate on final `e4341ce6d1b`, including the corrected test graph, source/export contracts, Madge, T1 and dialect ratchets. Final CI completed with 93 successful and 24 skipped jobs; PostgreSQL shards 1/3 and 2/3 failed on the previously identified archive-restore, port-command, update-preflight, and Doctor rollback timeouts (with follow-on missing-state/ownership errors). Shard 3 passed. These four failure classes are a subset of the coordinator-confirmed inherited PostgreSQL infra cascade; the same five files pass 28/28 locally on both revisions. The aggregate failure reflects those shards. Landing uses the inherited-failure exception, not a claim of fully green CI. The [published-driver update check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39065163017) passed all nine selected jobs, including package integrity, installation, and the published-driver scenario. It tests the exact unchanged production bytes; the later commit only repairs the test spy. LOC: 285 additions / 8 deletions across 16 files, including 138 test lines and 9 documentation lines; the bounded production growth declares callback scopes and reuses existing mutation receipts. The PG bisect refuted quickpath as the timeout cause, so this is a normal PR; it is independent of #175776.
