prs.title: feat(deepseek): search the web with the standalone Search API
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

DeepSeek users cannot use its new standalone Search API through OpenClaw’s managed `web_search`.

## User Impact

Users can select `deepseek` for web search with any model after installing the existing official DeepSeek plugin. Credentials come from plugin search config, `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, or the configured model-provider key, with standard SecretRef preparation. Existing auth-profile-only keys are not reused.

This PR is **ready for landing under maintainer direction**; authenticated DeepSeek source-provider and compiled-package verification now pass. The plugin keeps its current installable distribution; this does not bundle it into the host, change search defaults for installations without the plugin, or add DeepSeek Fetch. An installed, enabled plugin can participate in normal credential auto-detection at order 80.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing vendor-owned plugin using the public web-search contract and lazy runtime. Call `POST https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/search` directly with query/count and `need_content: false`; return model-oriented summaries with snippet fallback. No model call, new dependency, new core tool, SDK expansion, or additional state owner.

Preflight the 128-Unicode-character query limit and unsupported structured filters before making a paid request. Reuse shared guarded HTTP, cancellation, timeout, error redaction, and cache helpers. Cache identity includes query, count, and a hashed credential scope. Malformed/non-HTTP(S)/oversized source URLs are omitted, valid paid results are retained, and omissions mark the result truncated so provider prose cannot enter raw compatibility output.

Simplification: search-only is the smallest coherent stage; Fetch and richer provider-specific tool surfaces are deferred. The necessary growth is the thin adapter/manifest plus independent request, lifecycle, and production-composition proof; no new framework or compatibility machinery. Against the base: production/config +281/−4 lines; tests +743/−1 lines; documentation +82/−4 lines.

## Evidence

- **71 focused tests pass:** 31 DeepSeek provider/contract tests, 14 real production-tool integrations, 5 existing DeepSeek model-plugin tests, and 21 normalized-output/error siblings.
- Production integrations exercise real manifest/artifact discovery, config validation, readiness and explicit/automatic selection, SecretRef preparation, tool execution, and normalized schema-valid output. Only external HTTP responses are fixtures; provider routing, credential preparation, and normalization are not mocked.
- **Settings/onboarding completeness repair:** mirror DeepSeek search metadata in the existing official external-provider install catalog, so it is offered before the plugin is installed. The shared provider list feeding Search settings and onboarding contains exactly one DeepSeek entry after installation. A fresh-install setup regression fails without the catalog descriptor and passes after it, proving selection, credential configuration, and handoff to the standard package installer (installer I/O is a fixture; no package is installed on the live Gateway).
- Follow-up focused proof: **28/28 pass** across 12 search-setup cases, 2 install-catalog cases, and the 14 production-tool integration cases, in 48.34 seconds wrapper wall. Original provider/live proof remains valid because the adapter is unchanged. Targeted lint/format and independent P0–P2 review are clean. The full repair build passes (3 minutes 1 second), and a compiled install-catalog smoke confirms DeepSeek onboarding scope, package/credential paths, and environment discovery. Real Chromium → isolated compiled Gateway → installed candidate → authenticated DeepSeek Search settings E2E now passes, including persisted provider/enabled settings, live sources, reload, and served-asset identity. [Inspected before/after setup screenshots and uncached benchmarks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175729#issuecomment-6238658524) are published on this PR. The opt-in browser regression passes 1/1; the default path skips without loading the live fixture graph. No Gateway RPC or provider HTTP responses are mocked in this browser proof.
- Coverage includes query operators and Unicode limits; credential precedence; missing/unresolved credentials; disabled plugins; count and cache/TTL/account isolation; malformed/empty responses; 401/402/429/5xx and redaction; cancellation; bounded untrusted prose; and invalid-source URL handling.
- Independent Auto Review (Codex, P0–P2): malformed-URL raw-output finding reproduced with 3 failing integration cases, repaired, then final review completed scoped-clean. A later test-only change narrows the captured request body to a string for lint.
- Built-plugin smoke: compiled public artifact → lazy execution module → guarded HTTP fixture → safe result mapping passes, including invalid-source omission.
- Plugin production typecheck, targeted extension/core lint, formatting, plugin inventory, docs config examples, docs links, and `git diff --check` pass.
- `pnpm build`: completes successfully on the final production change (2 minutes 58 seconds). The full build emits non-fatal Control UI size-budget warnings; this change edits no UI source, and baseline attribution was not separately established.

<details>
<summary>Commands and test cost</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/deepseek/web-search-provider.test.ts extensions/deepseek/index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/web-search.deepseek.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/web-search.provider-errors.test.ts src/agents/tools/web-search-output.security.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/deepseek/tsconfig.json --noEmit
```

Latest provider/model file run: 36 tests, 12.08 seconds wall. Production integration file: 14 tests, 10.33 seconds wall (about 2.5 seconds test execution); sibling files: 21 tests, 27.67 seconds wall. Wrapper compilation accounts for much of wall time. CI seconds are pending.

</details>

**Authenticated live verification (2026-10-17, head `8e236614c49650f9d35d808e568748d8750348a2`):** the opt-in source-provider live suite passes **1/1** with no HTTP mocks (743 ms test execution; 30.61 seconds Vitest wall including preparation/setup). The compiled public artifact and lazy runtime also pass real API checks: a site-filtered search returns 3 usable `docs.openclaw.ai` sources with nonempty summaries in 966 ms; repeating it returns matching results with `cached: true` in under 1 ms; a Unicode query returns 2 results in 684 ms. These timings are individual smoke observations, not a performance benchmark. No code changes were needed after the environment’s secret-host authorization was corrected and a fresh execution run picked it up.

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node DEEPSEEK_SEARCH_LIVE_TEST=1 \
  pnpm test:live extensions/deepseek/web-search.live.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

**Remaining live gaps:** broad relevance/quality benchmarks, rate-limit saturation/recovery, and billed-charge verification were not performed. The credential remained in the protected store and was neither printed nor committed. The PR is ready for review; authenticated source and compiled-package search are now verified.

**Stable-to-head upgrade proof — PASS (2026-10-17):** official npm `openclaw@2026.10.4` (build `383c124cc32ffee3f8e56f549b88da94d269a4af`) produced real persisted configuration/state under an isolated named profile. Its archive SHA512 matches registry integrity, and a standalone module-resolution guard prevented borrowing checkout dependencies. After copying the stable-produced state, candidate Doctor completed successfully; separate candidate CLI processes validated and read back preserved explicit Gemini selection, disabled search, count/cache/timeout, synthetic Google credentials and header SecretRef, MiniMax credential SecretRef/settings, and sibling fetch settings. Complete authored subtrees were compared; Doctor-owned agent/plugin/migration/wizard/skill additions were enumerated. The approved application and exact `@openclaw/ai@2026.10.4` cooldown exceptions were confined to isolated acquisition/installation; shared policy is unchanged.

Nine production-owner consumer checks pass: disabled search remains unavailable; explicit Gemini wins despite available DeepSeek credentials; automatic selection prefers MiniMax order 15, then Gemini order 20, before DeepSeek order 80; DeepSeek is eligible with either config or environment-only synthetic credentials; disabled, uncredentialed, or catalog-unavailable DeepSeek is not selected. These use real compiled discovery/preparation/selection owners, not mocked decisions. Executing candidate build is `af2cd07b25d90a7318a4746714e79fc945f3e38c`; current head `baf7345c357ab31808acec35717da46ebec0641b` changes only the browser E2E and its two inventories, with production inputs unchanged.

**Upgrade proof boundaries:** this qualifies stable-produced state → candidate Doctor/cold-process CLI readback and real owner selection, not a public updater run or live Gateway restart. Positive DeepSeek discovery in this upgrade lane uses the canonical source-checkout contract. A separate optional local-link install was rejected by the scanner for the generated SDK symlink escaping its install root; no guard was weakened. The independent browser E2E above instead installs the ordinary packed candidate tarball successfully and performs authenticated search. Protected credentials were not accessed by the upgrade lane; all fixtures were synthetic.

**ClawSweeper setup-fallback repair:** shared search setup now recognizes the provider-declared configured credential fallback when deciding whether a key already exists, while leaving fallback values and SecretRefs at their model-provider owner. Dedicated-key extraction/storage is unchanged. Six regressions failed before the repair (interactive/quickstart disabled search; reference mode shadowed the existing fallback) and now pass across inline/SecretRef credentials and all three setup modes. The existing setup suite and real DeepSeek production integration pass **32/32** in **42.92 seconds wrapper wall** (18 setup cases, 14 provider-composition cases). Core typecheck (`-p tsconfig.core.json`), targeted lint/format, whitespace, and independent Codex P0–P2 Auto Review pass. An initial unscoped root typecheck hit UI JSX configuration errors; it is not reported green. The initial attempt to host setup regressions in the agent-tools lane hit a missing shared-state broker fixture before the intended boundary; regressions were moved to the existing setup owner suite, where the original defect was reproduced. No new runtime cache, migration, or credential copy was added. Previous upgrade/browser/live evidence remains revision-bound above; this later repair touches only shared CLI setup and its tests.

**Landing CI repair:** regenerated the config-doc baseline with its canonical generator. The plugin budget increases **4711 → 4713**, exactly for the optional `plugins.entries.deepseek.config.webSearch` object and its sensitive `apiKey` leaf already described above; core/channel counts are unchanged. This intentional vendor-owned credential field supports a search-specific key/SecretRef without adding core settings. Corrected HTTP fixture types and serialized-body assertions, reused the generic wizard fixture, and completed/sorted the real-Gateway inventory assertions. Four focused test files pass (125 seconds wrapper wall), both canonical extension/core-other test typecheck lanes pass, targeted lint/format and independent P0–P2 review pass. The final adjusted count case also passes.

**Inherited first-CI lint failure:** run `39064813746` tested merge `aa581ef5dd3478ae3478f0944b0350ff6306d5ab` on main parent `4cedba23b86608a5993200d9ff1ec5c2949c498b`; its SQLite worker/registry/operation contract/handlers match that parent, not this PR. Main’s snapshot cutover removed the last async operation but retained an `await`. Canonical fix `53ca17dc04e4f41a24e8f769eba8535bd3efe7ab` (#175796) is already on main. No unrelated SQLite repair is included here; fresh merge-ref CI must establish the current outcome.

**Base conflict resolution:** GitHub reported a real merge conflict after the CI repairs. Integrated main `cbca502786b` and resolved the sole conflicting generated config hash by rerunning `pnpm config:docs:gen`; no manual hash editing or production conflict rewrite. Config baseline verification passes. Re-ran the four affected setup/provider/UI-inventory workflow test files successfully (125.31 seconds wrapper wall), both canonical test-type lanes and core production typecheck pass. The current published head includes the upstream SQLite lint repair through main. Previous authenticated browser, API, and stable-upgrade proof remains explicitly revision-bound above; no claim is made that old CI covers this head.

prs.title: perf(gateway): avoid display work in session sharing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Adding a session member can fail when unrelated worker-placement display reads fail, and sharing pickers wait for full session facts even though they already have an indexed source of creator identities.

## User Impact

Session sharing remains available while unrelated display rows refresh. Ownership, membership, guest access, and live authorization checks remain unchanged. No configuration, schema, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the projection's existing metadata-only preparation for member listing and recipient selection. Unknown metadata and membership still reconcile, and each operation rechecks the manager after awaits and at commit. The creator index already exists from #152497; this completes the caller cutover without adding another index or cache.

Row acquisition already preserves entry identity when metadata is unchanged. Publication now consumes that identity instead of repeating a deep comparison. Production delta: 5 additions / 6 deletions (net −1 line); no new production state, API, or module.

## Evidence

The extended real-handler regression fails before the fix with `placement display unavailable` when adding a member, after both list variants succeeded. It checks persisted membership after the fix.

Focused local proof: **30 tests passed** across `sessions-sharing.identities.test.ts`, `sessions-sharing.test.ts`, `session-row-projection-record.test.ts`, and `session-row-projection.invalidation.test.ts` (`--maxWorkers=1`; 76.32 s wall time including compilation). Shared/draft/guest visibility, caller revocation during preparation, and commit-time authority cases pass. Changed-file formatting, core lint, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent Codex autoreview was scoped-clean through P2. No Testbox lease was used.

[PR CI run 39066034921](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39066034921) completed successfully on `f84ac0d4124091e6681fb632973d3ab56eb2eeec`; all 76 checks passed. No CI reruns or inherited-failure exception were needed.

## Before / After Measurement

Baseline `5c7123f25123` versus candidate `f84ac0d4124091e6681fb632973d3ab56eb2eeec`, with separate source-performance bundles and synthetic state. Four concurrent pairs ran under an exclusive measurement lock, assigning 16 cores per side (96–111 / 112–127) and swapping halves every pair. Preparation used cores 64–95. Gateway spawn skew was at most 1 ms.

Each side had 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained-run inputs, 200 approvals, 100 cron jobs, 12 projects, and 24 synthetic identities. The two databases totaled 31.12 MiB per fixture. Transcript payload generation was disabled: this tests metadata and sharing, not production-sized transcript I/O. Twelve clients connected concurrently and then issued the two sharing RPCs on identical fixed schedules (250 ms per client, evenly staggered), with at most one outstanding request each. All **11,371 RPCs succeeded**. Each run skipped only 1–2 scheduled slots instead of issuing catch-up bursts.

Profiles cover approximately ready +5 ms through ready +30,000 ms. In-flight RPCs finish before profile serialization. CPU figures below are main-thread milliseconds; latency figures are milliseconds. Decisions use within-pair candidate minus baseline differences.

| Pair | Main CPU A → B | CPU B−A | `members.list` p99 A → B | `members.listEvidence` p99 A → B | Sharing self samples A → B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4236.4 → 4268.6 | +32.2 | 49.04 → 44.39 | 37.82 → 48.70 | 22 → 21 |
| 2 | 4280.3 → 4165.8 | −114.5 | 40.80 → 47.70 | 28.39 → 40.26 | 14 → 17 |
| 3 | 4208.6 → 4229.2 | +20.6 | 44.71 → 52.27 | 43.97 → 38.48 | 14 → 19 |
| 4 | 4255.2 → 4130.4 | −124.8 | 39.90 → 41.29 | 46.69 → 36.21 | 15 → 16 |

Median paired differences: main CPU **−46.95 ms (~−1.1%)**, listing p99 **+4.15 ms**, evidence p99 **+2.69 ms**, sharing self samples **+2**, and `objEquiv` self samples **0**. RPC medians stayed at **0.73–0.77 ms**. `prepareSessionRowSelection` had **zero samples on both sides in every pair**: the earlier creator-index change already removed that original hotspot. Observed CPU busy percentages on the two measured halves were 5.45/4.17, 4.02/4.00, 4.50/4.42, and 6.85/7.71; recorded as context, not an exclusion criterion.

**Neutral performance result; no speedup claim.** CPU and steady latency show no material regression; startup p99 changes reverse sign across pairs and methods. The largest stalls are existing boot catalog publication and plugin prewarm work. This lands for the proven display-failure fix and the smaller implementation.

Two earlier response-relative polling pairs are retained as exploratory evidence: median paired p99 rose by 20.31/19.09 ms. Inspection found profile-stop serialization overlapping final requests and larger synchronized client bursts on the candidate (up to 12 requests versus roughly 5 per burst), with correspondingly higher worker queueing. The four fixed-schedule pairs above remove those measurement confounders; they do not discard any startup stalls. An initial pilot with an incorrectly extended capture window was excluded. The results do not establish performance for every possible reconnect/load pattern.

prs.title: fix(ui): align Usage intervals and context accounting
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Usage's selected-session header, chart, and loaded conversation calculated their intervals separately. With a cursor spanning selected nonadjacent days, the header and conversation counts included an excluded day. The context summary also counted embedded files, skills, and tool descriptions again inside the full system prompt.

## User Impact

Usage headers, charts, message/tool counts, and conversation rows now agree on the selected interval, and context estimates count embedded prompt sections once. Undated rows remain visible, full-session tool options stay available, and Reset restores full-session totals/logs. Existing query behavior, controls and layout are preserved; no user action or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing time-series projection for both header and chart, with the same selected-day and cursor inputs. Prepare the calendar predicate once and share one parsed-log interval projection between the summary and conversation. Partition known prompt sections before estimating system tokens, retaining unknown native-file sizes as unknown. Prepare session logs and query terms once for their existing consumers rather than parsing them repeatedly.

The regression fixture previously showed 1.2K tokens/$9.30 above a 300-token/$0.30 chart; both now show 300/$0.30. The context fixture's double-counted total changes from 450 to 325. Query chips, suggestions, filtering, and layout remain unchanged.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- The removed header aggregator and selected-cost summary no longer independently zero-fill malformed internal point values. The existing time-series producer already supplies complete numeric points and applies missing-cost defaults; the chart already consumed those numeric fields directly. This path was ported in [#168788](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168788), whose evidence concerns renderer migration, not a human malformed-point incident. A producer-contract violation is no longer masked as zero in just one consumer.
- No lifecycle, security, retry, or stale-response guard was removed. Context token figures remain estimates; native-unverified file content remains unknown rather than invented.
- Retain the existing full-session fallback without a filtered indicator when a cursor/calendar intersection has no sampled points. The Gateway downsamples to at most 200 buckets and timestamps each at its last record, so no point is not proof of zero interval usage. The proposed zero-valued fallback was declined on that producer contract; empty-interval behavior from #168788 is preserved.

## Evidence

Net production LOC: **8 added** (185 added / 177 deleted; bug-fix exception to the cleanup floor). The small growth supplies one shared calendar owner and fixes the adjacent selected-day log discrepancy; it is not claimed as cleanup savings. Test/support additions are not counted as cleanup.

Three mounted regression cases failed before the initial fixes. The selected-day log follow-up also failed before its repair (expected 2 messages, received 3). All 49 focused cases pass on the revised candidate: 40 mounted detail/view/query cases (157.66 seconds wrapper wall time under shared-host load; Vitest 101.55 seconds) and 9 parser/helper cases (70.11 seconds wrapper wall; Vitest 11.49 seconds). A mounted work-count test verifies one query parse per draft change and none for chart changes. Fresh full-candidate review found only the already-reproduced bug in the old index snapshot, confirmed the working-tree repair, and identified no additional P0–P2 defects. Terminal verification completed; that exact repair is now staged, with no remaining unstaged delta. Synthetic before/after component captures show the accounting correction and unchanged query layout; this is component proof, not a live Gateway claim.

Targeted production and canonical touched-test typechecks, targeted type-aware lint, formatting and diff-check pass. Lint found one local shadowed name, fixed with a mechanical variable rename; both typechecks passed again. The required local suppression suite ran all 14 cases: 13 pass; its unchanged baseline failure is `src/infra/database-engine/admission-role.test-support.ts|unicorn/require-post-message-target-origin|1`. The named source and checker are byte-identical to base `61d3a21374c`, and this diff adds no suppression. No allowlist widening or timeout increase. An initial lint preparation timed out generating unrelated extension declarations; the supported core lint config covers these explicit UI files without that extension-only preparation. Hosted CI on the exact pushed head remains the broad gate.

Current exact-head CI at `660e0adb01e` is red only on `check-lint-core-2` and its downstream aggregate: `await-thenable` in the unchanged SQLite worker after newer main #175774 removed the registry's async operation. Targeted lint on fresh main `7d81a7d13af` reproduces the identical diagnostic. All selected UI/type/architecture/i18n/performance/security jobs pass; all 88 checks are completed. Landing uses the standing inherited-only exception with a per-job evidence table, not a claim of green CI. No CI rerun or green-only repush.

## Synthetic before / after

Before: header/chart interval disagreement and double-counted context.

![Usage accounting before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61fd6291-d200-40c5-ae5d-3613afaecfc2)

After: header and chart share their selected interval; embedded context sections are counted once.

![Usage accounting after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f13bb147-5247-49d3-9e96-8fb9e8ba2032)

The query controls retain their layout and behavior while sharing prepared terms.

![Usage query before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5a23e80a-8cf3-48f5-ab40-7c3a09548e1c)

![Usage query after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3ea9a7c-659a-41eb-b006-a64ced5bb479)

prs.title: ci: default daily tests to Bun and retain dual release validation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Daily CI still uses the earlier partial Bun qualification policy even though five paired main trials support making Bun the normal test runtime.

## User Impact

Pull requests, automatic main validation, and plugin prerelease extension batches use the pinned Bun fork. Full Release Validation keeps both Node and Bun. Manual dispatches can force Node with `test_runtime_policy=node`; named Node contracts and the documented direct-entrypoint lanes retain their existing runtime.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime owner now supports `node`, `bun-all`, and `dual-all`. This removes the superseded compatible-file allowlists, plain dual policy, and their tests while preserving exact Node exceptions and native Bun source/hash qualification.

| Manifest selection | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pull request | `bun-compatible` | `bun-all` |
| Main push/schedule and main-shaped dispatch | `node` | `bun-all` |
| Full Release Validation | `dual` | `dual-all` |
| Explicit manual Node override | unavailable | `node` |

Timing learning and pruning separate Node, the complete daily Bun envelope, and the combined release envelope. Dual validation contributes only its full Node and combined dual costs; its partial Bun pass never becomes a complete daily-Bun measurement. A Bun envelope includes its native-Bun and required Node companions. Missing policy-specific scheduling costs retain historical estimates until measurements arrive; measured runtime-placement observations never cross policies. Old partial `bun:` estimates are not reused as full-Bun measurements.

The aggregate UI configuration has a different name from its root project owners, which could omit five named Node-only retention tests from `bun-all`. UI routing now uses its actual package inventory. Timing regression coverage ensures partial dual-run Bun costs cannot replace complete daily-Bun measurements. Other test edits replace expectations for retired policies with the current runtime contract. No new runtime skips or fork workarounds were added.

The runtime switch adds no job definitions or per-runtime registrations: CI remains 42 jobs and plugin prerelease 9, with identical runner declarations, strategies, and concurrency. Both runtime passes reuse each selected row. Timing estimates may repack work within the existing caps. The manifest regression compares normalized PR/main/full-release output with captured pre-change digests and changes only policy fields and the sequential release deadline. The live registration bucket reports 10,000 capacity and 10,000 remaining.

Related rollout: #173807. Five paired main trials established the default:

| Trial | Run | Aggregate Bun/Node wall ratio |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| 1 | [38870726251](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38870726251) | 0.752 |
| 2 | [38902779924](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38902779924) | 0.733 |
| 3 | [38989076752](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38989076752) | 0.727 |
| 4 | [39034539771](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39034539771) | 0.735 |
| 5 | [39042099307](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39042099307) | 0.735 |

The last trial had no incomplete shards.

## Evidence

Focused files were run separately on both runtimes:

```sh
TMPDIR=/private/tmp/oc-flip2 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1
PATH=/private/tmp/oc-bun-fork/bin:$PATH OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH=/private/tmp/oc-bun-fork/bin/bun TMPDIR=/private/tmp/oc-flip2 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1
```

Local Bun proof uses the requested `1.4.3-canary.1+65d94e715`; PR CI uses the repository pin.

| File under `test/` | Passing cases on each runtime |
| --- | ---: |
| `scripts/ci-native-bun-qualification.test.ts` | 5 |
| `scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.test.ts` | 72 |
| `scripts/ci-shard-timings-refresh.test.ts` | 11 |
| `scripts/ci-test-runtime-trial.test.ts` | 15 |

prs.title: fix: show recommended Wonder and distinct Muse model names
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes recommended Muse Wonder disappearing from the model picker without Meta API credentials, and native-only Wonder variants showing raw or incorrect sibling names.

## User Impact

Muse subscribers can find recommended standard Wonder and distinguish Wonder, Full, and Contributor offerings. Existing API credentials, authored API bindings, explicit runtime choices, and required cloud-worker policy keep precedence. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recommendation already existed. Catalog readiness incorrectly treated an API metadata twin as preventing selection of the uniquely discovered native runtime. The existing catalog decision owner now distinguishes metadata from credentials, without guessing between multiple native runtimes.

Muse Code also returned raw labels and mislabeled Full Contributor with its sibling's ID. The Muse adapter corrects only those observed display defects. Native `model/list` still owns account membership and executable IDs; OpenRouter's different Wonder slug remains separate. No picker workaround, recommendation edit, new mapping layer, or state owner is introduced.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the configured-view regression returned four available Meta offerings instead of eight, and the native reader reproduced the raw/incorrect labels. After repair, all eight are available; only standard Wonder and Spark 1.3 receive the captured Meta recommendations.
- **31 focused tests pass** across catalog, Gateway composition, Muse process/reader, and browser regressions. They protect direct/profile credential precedence, required workers, ambiguous native owners, unknown future IDs, exact account membership, and exact native/OpenRouter selection IDs.
- Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, full CLI/plugin build, and independent P0–P2 autoreview passed. [Exact-head hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39065081707) passed, including the required `openclaw/ci-gate`, for `06c2cb3cfcb86ccb687160b0aefcecce8aa656b8`.
- Live native account discovery was captured and sanitized. The browser proof uses isolated source-response fixtures through real enrichment and `models.list` projection—not a redeployed operator Gateway. Authenticated Meta Model API inventory was unavailable (credential-free discovery returned 401); an optional native inference smoke did not complete within 60 seconds. Successful live inference is not claimed.

### Before and after

Before — affected live picker:

![Before: Wonder missing and native variant labels incorrect](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/528ff09d-cf69-4514-89bf-9bb59e1cd7f1)

After — isolated browser regression, standard Wonder recommended:

![After: recommended standard Muse Wonder](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d52cf03f-c0ee-4f9c-a9b0-2a570e1faa16)

After — distinct native offerings:

![After: distinct Wonder Full and Contributor labels](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01d75065-30a9-4944-bd4d-2d50a13e2f81)

<details>
<summary>Simplification and change size</summary>

Ran `$pr-simplify` before publication. Kept the fix in the two existing owners: catalog readiness and the Muse adapter. Removed unused diagnostic captures from the proposed source fixtures, stripped unconsumed hosted/OpenRouter metadata, and removed a redundant assertion. Original diagnostics remain local evidence rather than product files. This cuts 991 fixture lines and one duplicate assertion from the earlier proposal; it does not remove an existing product path.

Whole-change delta against the merge base: production **+37/-8 lines**, executable test/helper code **+466/-2**, JSON fixtures **+232/-0**, and documentation **+54/-2**. Remaining growth is focused regression proof, shared source fixtures, and documentation; no production scaffolding or alternate renderer is added. Tests retain distinct owner-level, Gateway-composition, and rendered selection failures rather than repeating one helper's output.

</details>

prs.title: fix(gateway): cancel disconnected hook admission
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Authenticated hook requests that disconnect while admission is still queued stay eligible to start. A client retry, including a watcher that times out before admission, can then run the same work twice.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pending bounded admission now follows the HTTP request lifetime. When the last connected caller disconnects before lane placement or runner entry, that admission is canceled and its replay identity is retired so the retry can start once. Acceptance detaches cancellation, so work already handed to the runner continues. Background fan-out keeps its documented replay contract and is not canceled by disconnect. Authentication still runs before admission.

## User Impact

A disconnected hook client no longer starts an agent run it already abandoned. Retries of that request execute once. Runs that already passed admission keep going. Gmail fan-out batches still finish in the background and replay instead of duplicating.

## Evidence

Rebased onto current `upstream/main`. Head `80acac776684bba94a01b3dc3935cc80dee506e9`.

Previous CI on `ca9f24ca5d0`:

- `check-lint-core-1` failed on `src/gateway/server-http.hooks-request-lifetime.test.ts:162:36` and `:203:36`: `This is the default value for this type parameter, so it can be omitted. (typescript(no-unnecessary-type-arguments))`.
- `checks-node-changed-compact-large-24` failed in `src/gateway/server-http.control-ui.test.ts` (`expected "prepareIdentityFile" to not be called at all, but actually been called 2 times`). That test is not in this diff and is not on current main. This branch does not change Control UI identity.

The lifetime suite now waits on request-close and dispatch-arrival signals instead of `setTimeout` or `vi.waitFor`.

- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/gateway/server-http.hooks-request-lifetime.test.ts` (0 errors)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-http.hooks-request-lifetime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (5 passed)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server/hooks.agent-trust.test.ts src/gateway/server/hooks-request-handler.fanout.test.ts src/gateway/server-http.hooks-delivery.test.ts src/gateway/server/hooks.early-failure.test.ts src/gateway/server/hooks.wake-admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (89 passed)

Live proof was captured at `3b2b5ed1541c8f325a68458ee3d59b1173b5d95f`. `80acac77668` only annotates the test gate as `Deferred`; production hook admission is unchanged. A real Gateway HTTP server accepted `POST /hooks/agent`, the client destroyed the socket after auth and body parsing while the request was queued behind a same-session run, and the agent runner did not start for the abandoned request. The same idempotency key then ran once. The isolated runner was instrumented only to hold the queue and count starts. Token redacted.

```
HEAD 3b2b5ed1541c8f325a68458ee3d59b1173b5d95f
gateway listening 127.0.0.1:38995
dispatch entered message=blocker
runner start message=blocker count=1
blocker is holding the shared session queue
dispatch entered message=retry-me
abandoned request passed auth and body parsing and is queued
client destroy message=retry-me
abandoned admission {"ok":false,"statusCode":503,"error":"hook request disconnected before agent run started","runId":"54249773-d308-486c-ac4e-63cdc46979ed"}
abandoned http status=0 body=socket hang up
blocker http status=200 body={"ok":true,"runId":"06f509b7-bc3e-4b26-abf1-5e5581d5512b"}
after disconnect and blocker release runner=["blocker"]
dispatch entered message=retry-me
runner start message=retry-me count=2
retry http status=200 body={"ok":true,"runId":"51255037-608e-4a40-b1ff-4335740b56da"}
retry executions=1 prior=0
proof: disconnected queued hook did not run; retry ran once
```

prs.title: fix(ai): send max_tokens on Model Studio compatible-mode endpoints
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Model Studio compatible-mode requests (`qwen`, `qwencloud`, `modelstudio`, `dashscope`, `qwen-token-plan`, and `bailian-token-plan`) send the output cap as `max_completion_tokens`. Alibaba's OpenAI-compatibility reference documents `max_tokens` for that surface and does not list `max_completion_tokens`, so the configured cap can be ignored or the request can be rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveOpenAICompletionsCompatDefaults` already treats this family as Model Studio for other flags, but `usesMaxTokens` omitted it and fell through to the OpenAI field. The fix adds that family only when the base URL is an Alibaba compatible-mode host (`*.dashscope*.aliyuncs.com` or `*.maas.aliyuncs.com` with a `/compatible-mode/` path).

Coding Plan hosts stay on `max_completion_tokens`. That surface shares the `modelstudio-native` endpoint class, and the cited reference does not cover it. Explicit `model.compat.maxTokensField` still wins. OpenAI and the other vendors that already select `max_tokens` or `max_completion_tokens` are unchanged. Unrelated `/compatible-mode/` proxy URLs are unchanged.

## User Impact

Compatible-mode Model Studio calls now send the configured output budget as `max_tokens`. A budget stored as `params.max_completion_tokens` is still honored; only the wire field changes. Coding Plan, OpenAI, and other providers keep their current field. No config migration is required.

## Evidence

On head `ecdd7b81ce7a9740b097340d0b336fb64134040c` (rebased onto current `upstream/main`):

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/ai/src/transports/openai-completions-params.test.ts packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.compat.test.ts packages/ai/src/transports/openai-completions-transport.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
Test Files  3 passed (3)
Tests  81 passed (81)
```

Live transport proof did not call Model Studio, OpenAI, or Coding Plan. A local HTTP server on `127.0.0.1` received the raw POST body from `streamOpenAICompletionsRequest` in managed mode. Host classification came from `resolveProviderRequestCapabilities` (plugin metadata). The fetch hook refused every hostname except the three proof hosts and forwarded only the request body to that local server. No provider key was read or sent.

1. Model Studio compatible-mode (`qwen`, `https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1`, classified `modelstudio-native` / `modelstudio`) sent `max_tokens` and not `max_completion_tokens`.
2. OpenAI (`openai`, `https://api.openai.com/v1`, classified `openai-public` / `openai-family`) sent `max_completion_tokens`.
3. Coding Plan (`qwen`, `https://coding.dashscope.aliyuncs.com/v1`, classified `modelstudio-native` / `modelstudio`) sent `max_completion_tokens`.

The redacted bodies are in the PR comment on this head. Vendor acceptance of the field was not observed. The field choice follows https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/compatibility-of-openai-with-dashscope

prs.title: fix(ui): keep settings drafts and data through reconnects
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: unsaved Settings edits disappear when the Gateway connection blips.

Several Settings pages treated an ordinary reconnect of the same client as an identity change and reset their state: Model Providers dropped default-model drafts, key editors, entered keys and login flows; Plugins closed credential editors and cleared details; Devices discarded unsaved execution-approval policy edits; Skills reset library editor content; Profile reset the display-name draft and account-linking flow; GitHub identity, Session Storage, Channels (Nostr drafts) and Cloud Worker pool/policy drafts reset too, and Channels claimed nothing was connected. Model default drafts and profile-order intent were also cleared after a failed or never-dispatched save. Config autosave paused after any disconnect until an explicit Save, even when nothing was in flight.

## User Impact

User impact: you can keep editing Settings through a spotty connection; your drafts and the last loaded data stay put, saves are disabled only while disconnected, and autosave resumes on its own after a clean reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

Request-generation fencing is unchanged (old-epoch results are still discarded); only drafts and presented data now outlive a same-identity transport edge. A different client, Gateway or account still resets everything, and typed secrets stay in memory only. Model default drafts and profile-order intent clear only on acknowledged success. The config write coordinator resumes autosave after reconnect only when no submission was in flight and the base revision is unchanged; uncertain submissions and changed bases keep the existing pause and explicit recovery.

Part of the offline-first series.

## Evidence

- Per-page regression tests: drafts and data survive a same-client disconnect/reconnect and reset on identity change (Model Providers, Plugins credential editor, Devices, Skills, Profile and model accounts, GitHub identity, Session Storage, Channels, Cloud Workers); config autosave resume and pause branches.
- Remote Testbox run found a type error, two lint violations and two test expectation issues; all fixed in this branch.
- Access revocation: a late response from a request started before `operator.admin`/read access was revoked can no longer republish restricted data (Cloud Workers environments/images/editor, Models, Plugins, Channels plugin presentation, config writes, Profile, GitHub identity before identity readiness).
- Scope note: Memory search moved into the memory-core plugin on main while this PR was open; its retention was dropped here because the plugin settings-view host owns that lifetime (it remounts on reconnect). Follow-up: let plugin settings views survive a same-identity reconnect.

## Landing validation

The current head merges main through `45c6db39b27`. The Skills conflict keeps main's shared `createPageRequest` owner while retaining drafts and loaded results and canceling pending reads on reconnect or access loss. Six focused files passed all 51 tests; formatting and whitespace checks passed; independent Codex autoreview was scoped-clean. The offline guide no longer promises memory-search retention, which remains the plugin-host follow-up described above.

prs.title: fix(agents): prefer write/edit tools over heredocs to prevent literal-newline corruption
prs.body:
Fixes #114128

## What Problem This Solves

Agents writing multi-line Python via unquoted heredocs (`<<EOF`) or `bash -c` corrupt `\n` into literal backslash-n. This compiles-fails silently and can rot for weeks before discovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exec description now prefers dedicated file-writing tools over shell heredocs or `bash -c` for multi-line content, and names only the tools that survived filtering (`write`, `edit`, and/or `apply_patch`). A write-only session is told to prefer `write`, not the unavailable siblings. Tool permissions are not widened.

## User Impact

When a dedicated file-writing tool is available, agents are steered to that tool instead of a shell heredoc, so multiline files keep real newline bytes. Sessions that do not have those tools are not told to call them.

## Evidence

Live proof on `401c566eb96410ae5989f69a160784e7405a1222`, using the production tool finalizer plus the real exec and write tools (`--pool=forks`).

Exec-only session omits the guidance. With only `write` available, the description names `write` and the selected file tool is `write`. The real exec tool ran the historical unquoted heredoc and left literal backslash-n bytes (`5c6e`). The real write tool wrote the same intended Python and the file bytes contain newline bytes (`0a`) and match the requested content.

```
HEAD 401c566eb96410ae5989f69a160784e7405a1222
EXEC_ONLY_HAS_FILE_WRITES false
EXEC_ONLY_DESCRIPTION Run shell and wait for completion. Omit host to use the session's configured host. TTY CLI/UI/coding agent: pty=true. Quote arguments containing shell metacharacters, including URL query strings with `?` or `&`.
WRITE_ONLY_DESCRIPTION Run shell and wait for completion. Omit host to use the session's configured host. TTY CLI/UI/coding agent: pty=true. File writes: prefer dedicated file-writing tools (write) over shell heredocs or bash -c for multi-line content. Quote arguments containing shell metacharacters, including URL query strings with `?` or `&`.
SELECTED_FILE_TOOLS write
HEREDOC_EXEC_RESULT [{"type":"text","text":"(no output)"}]
HEREDOC_FILE_REPR "def greet():\\n    return \"ok\"\\n\n"
HEREDOC_FILE_HEX 64656620677265657428293a5c6e2020202072657475726e20226f6b225c6e0a
WRITE_TOOL_RESULT [{"type":"text","text":"Successfully wrote 29 bytes to /home/synth/.hermes/cache/scratch/oc-vt-w5SDu1/oc-117274-proof-E6H7A1/write.py"}]
WRITE_FILE_REPR "def greet():\n    return \"ok\"\n"
WRITE_FILE_HEX 64656620677265657428293a0a2020202072657475726e20226f6b220a
WRITE_CONTAINS_NEWLINE_BYTE true
WRITE_MATCHES_INTENDED true
```

`src/agents/bash-tools.descriptions.test.ts`: 5 passed, including write-only, edit-only, and partial sets. `src/agents/agent-tools.deferred-followup-guidance.test.ts`: 12 passed.

Previous CI on `7bdf478a` failed `checks-node-changed-compact-large-12` (`AssertionError: expected 'blocked' to match object { state: 'reclaimed' }` in `src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-dispatch-reclaim.test.ts`) and `checks-node-changed-compact-large-7` (`ENOENT` for `dist/index.js` in `src/cli/update-cli.windows-lifecycle.test.ts`). Neither file is in this diff.

AI-assisted: yes (OpenClaw subagent).

Acceptance of the standalone EOL warning and unhealthy diagnostic classification remains a maintainer decision. This maintenance does not change that choice. No public flags, configuration, database schema, stored data, migration, dependency, protocol, permission or service policy changes are included.

## Why This Change Was Made

## Maintainer status — local candidate, not published

**This PR remains open at contributor head `a86cfd4e370614dfbbaffc05b23a26dd9710af0c`.** The integration described here is an uncommitted, unpublished maintainer candidate (staged tree `4862cde3fbe12995820c4fc4b088fe9988ce170b`), not the current PR branch. Original work and contributor ancestry from @zyw02 are preserved.

### Proposed repair and user impact

Related: #119929. Remove → Save clears a stored avatar; clearing the custom emoji input clears that stored value. The proposed API clear contract is explicit `null`; empty, whitespace, and omitted API fields preserve existing values.

On a configuration-write failure after the identity file changes, the candidate saves the previous bytes (or a prior-absence marker) and returns an actionable pending-recovery error. It never restores or deletes the current identity file, which may contain a newer external edit. Operators must compare the recovery artifact, current file, and configuration before retrying and remove the artifact after reconciliation. **This is not automatic rollback or a multi-file transaction.** The earlier conditional-rollback claims below are historical contributor notes, not an accepted correctness claim.

Current ownership checks, authenticated avatar rendering, generated protocol declarations, and legacy Swift initializer call shapes are retained. Text-only default avatars do not expose a misleading Remove action after reload.

prs.title: fix(gateway): report active unmanaged restart startup accurately
prs.body:
Closes #119958

## Summary

Fixes the unmanaged SIGUSR1 restart path that reports a 60-second health timeout even when the same gateway process has accepted the restart and is still progressing through startup.

## Root cause

The CLI sends SIGUSR1 and then polls only listener health. An in-process restart can retain its PID while the listener is intentionally absent, so PID and port state cannot distinguish active startup from a dead restart.

## Fix

The gateway loop owns a short-lived renewable startup-progress lease while awaiting each startup. The unmanaged listener waiter accepts a typed `still-starting` result only when that lease is fresh, belongs to the signaled gateway process, and began after this restart request. The normal 60-second listener window is not extended. Missing, stale, expired, or non-progressing lease evidence still fails the restart.

## User impact

A bounded still-starting result tells operators to run `openclaw gateway status --deep` instead of treating a healthy slow boot as failed and applying destructive recovery.

## Validation

Run the focused lifecycle, listener-health, run-loop, and lease regressions; then `git diff --check` and `pnpm check:changed`.

## Credit

Thanks @islandpreneur007 for the source reproduction in #119958.

prs.title: refactor(update): stop polling completed report refusals
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Update failure reporting retains two outer loops that repeat completed receipt-state refusals. SQLite exceptions already stop those loops; the native worker owns proven pre-admission BUSY retry and reconciliation after lost replies.

## User Impact

Use one state-write attempt and the existing pending/retryable outcome. Keep consent/redaction, current effect authority, canonical receipt confirmation, saved-report custody, at-most-once external submission and ordinary shutdown settlement. No public status, schema, config, dependency, protocol, durability, retention or permission change. Phase E session-memory code/tests are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace both private retry helpers with one tryUpdateReportStateWrite and migrate exactly six callers. The browser-authority test now actually persists its receipt before retiring authority. The refusal/unknown-finalization table retains one issue creation, returned URL, pending next request and saved artifact instead of manufacturing success from a second automatic finalization.

Four-file report-area slice of an unfinished >80-file proposal, split for CI attribution: production **28 net lines removed** (+13/-41), tests **5 net removed** (+11/-16). Main's already-landed sweep cleanup is unchanged and receives no duplicate credit.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- A completed domain refusal is no longer polled twice or five times over875ms hoping another actor changes phase/reservation/CAS state. Introducing #139704 supplied generic resilience, not a cited human refusal-contention incident; worker migration #167572 moved actual lock/reply uncertainty handling to the native owner and made exceptions terminal. The current store returns false for domain refusals, not transient thrown SQLite errors. A genuinely later state change may require explicit status/reconnect/retry; the existing visible pending/retryable result and saved report remain. prs.title: fix(sessions): keep custom session icon across /reset
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves Channel `/reset` dropped a custom session icon even after #126575. Operator-owned appearance (icon, color, category, boardFace, visibility) was not part of the preserved reset selection, so the Control UI row came back bare after the channel acknowledged the reset. ## Why This Change Was Made Gateway resets and channel `/new` and `/reset` share `preserveResetSessionPresentation()` in `src/config/sessions/reset-preserved-presentation.ts`. That helper keeps operator-owned appearance (`icon`, `color`, `category`, `boardFace`, `boardPresentation`, `visibility`) along with `pinnedAt` and the organization fields it already carried. `resolveResetPreservedSelection` still filters model, auth, and communication choices, and the session store still drops `visibility` when the session id changes. A session with no icon still has none after reset. Channel rollover in `src/auto-reply/reply/session-rollover-state.ts` calls that helper instead of copying a shorter field list. The fast-path bootstrap tests and the two `resolveResetPreservedSelection` appearance-copy cases are removed. The channel lifecycle cases in `src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts` stay. Keeping `visibility` is deliberate. A durable channel reset does not change the session id, and the sqlite entry store drops `visibility` only when the session id changes. Omitting it from the written entry clears the field. `resolveSessionVisibility` treats a missing value as `shared`, so a draft would become visible to other readers. The authority-chain run below checks that the retained draft is still enforced. ## Evidence Both runs below use the repo's own QA lane, `pnpm openclaw qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai`, which boots a real Gateway child on a throwaway state dir with the `qa-channel` plugin and the `mock-openai` provider. The scenario chats once in a DM so the channel session exists, sets `icon`, `color` and `category` through the same `sessions.patch` RPC the Control UI uses, sends `/reset` as an inbound channel message, then reads the row back through `sessions.list`. The model is the only stand-in; the channel plugin boundary, the auto-reply command path, the session store and the Gateway RPCs are the real ones. The scenario file is at the end of this section. Before: same worktree, with `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts`, `src/config/sessions/reset-preserved-selection.ts` and `src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts` checked out from `upstream/main` at `832ce3c68b7`. Output is the `qa-suite-report.md` the run wrote. ```text $ pnpm openclaw qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario channel-reset-keeps-session-appearance --output-dir EVIDENCE/before-run ### Channel reset keeps session appearance - Status: fail - Details: appearance lost across /reset; before={"key":"agent:qa:main","sessionId":"94795739-7ac6-4e74-81ab-52ccb9d16bf1","icon":"🦞","color":"blue","category":"qa-appearance","updatedAt":1788544605661,"totalTokens":64} after={"key":"agent:qa:main","sessionId":"94795739-7ac6-4e74-81ab-52ccb9d16bf1","updatedAt":1788544605933,"totalTokens":0} resetReply="✅ Session reset." - Steps: - [ ] keeps icon, color and category across channel /reset (fail) ``` After: this head, the three files restored. ```text $ pnpm openclaw qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario channel-reset-keeps-session-appearance --output-dir EVIDENCE/after-run ### Channel reset keeps session appearance - Status: pass - Steps: - [x] keeps icon, color and category across channel /reset - Details: {"verdict":"PASS","patchAck":{"key":"agent:qa:main","sessionId":"ec427fd2-2297-43a7-bd17-e51c8d131169","icon":"🦞","color":"blue","category":"qa-appearance","updatedAt":1788544430355,"totalTokens":64},"before":{"key":"agent:qa:main","sessionId":"ec427fd2-2297-43a7-bd17-e51c8d131169","icon":"🦞","color":"blue","category":"qa-appearance","updatedAt":1788544430355,"totalTokens":64},"resetReply":"✅ Session reset.","after":{"key":"agent:qa:main","sessionId":"ec427fd2-2297-43a7-bd17-e51c8d131169","icon":"🦞","color":"blue","category":"qa-appearance","updatedAt":1788544430618,"totalTokens":0}} ``` The reset ran in both cases: the channel answered `✅ Session reset.`, `updatedAt` moved forward and `totalTokens` went from 64 to 0 (a durable reset keeps the session id on purpose, see the comment above the `sessionId` assignment in `initSessionState`). On main the `sessions.list` row loses `icon`, `color` and `category`. On this head it keeps all three. ### Authority-chain proof This run is the retained-draft check. It uses a real Gateway, trusted-proxy identities, and the live session-read and broadcast paths. Only the model is mocked. The scenario was not committed. Two non-admin clients connect with role `reader`, `sessions.others: view`, and scopes `operator.read`, `operator.write`, and `operator.sessions.read` (not `operator.admin`). Profiles are distinct. The creator opens `agent:main:telegram:dm:draft-reset-proof` as `draft`, sends one turn so the row has tokens, then `sessions.patch` sets icon 🦞, color `blue`, and category `qa-appearance`. The reset is production `initSessionState` with Provider and Surface `telegram`, body `/reset`, and `commandAuthorized: true`, writing the gateway's live store. A Control UI `chat.send` of `/reset` does not take that path for these clients: internal `/reset` requires `operator.admin`. prs.title: test(gateway): cron live suites hang on a same-root forced run and ignore stored accounts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the live Gateway cron suites fail even when cron itself works. `gateway-cron-placement.live.test.ts` hangs until "The forced cron run did not publish its completion record", and the cron suites depend on whatever provider keys happen to be in the environment instead of a stored inference account.

## User Impact

User impact: no product change. Maintainers get cron live suites that pass on a healthy build and prove the current ordering contract instead of an interleaving the product no longer allows.

## Why This Change Was Made

Since #165310, cron session preparation waits behind active work on the same root; `mode: "force"` skips schedule eligibility, not that FIFO. The placement test paused a reply hook on a root and then awaited a forced cron run on the same root before releasing the hook, so neither side could progress. The old `HOOK_ROTATED` step, where cron rotates the root while the hook is paused and the hook's effect is rejected, is unreachable under FIFO. The step now:

1. queues the forced run;
2. asserts it stays pending and the root is unchanged;
3. releases the hook;
4. waits for that exact run id and verifies the root rotated and the old transcript is unchanged.

The cron suites also store the live provider key through `models.authSetApiKey` and pin the model to that profile, matching how users configure inference.

A reply supplied by a `before_agent_reply` hook is not written to the session transcript, so the test makes no transcript claim for it.

## Evidence

- Offline diagnosis (real Gateway, loopback model): it reproduced the hang. The lane snapshot showed one active root task with the cron task queued behind it (`waitedMs=198437 activeAhead=1 taskKind=cron`). With the corrected ordering the queued run completed under its exact id.
- Live, OpenAI, with this branch plus #175656: `gateway-cron-placement.live.test.ts` passes in 94s across first-root admission, stale-generation rejection, fresh-root admission, and both hook settlements. `gateway-cron-tools-allow.live.test.ts` passes both the OpenClaw and Codex harness cases. Its OpenClaw case also needs #175656: without it, storing the key for the fresh probe agent fails with the database-identity error.
- Unit: `src/gateway/live-agent-probes.test.ts` passes (8).
- Autoreview: scoped-clean at P2.

prs.title: fix(doctor): show progress while checks and repairs run (#154636)
prs.body:
Closes #154636

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor --fix` awaits checks and repairs without identifying the pending work. Expensive database and configuration preparation also occurs before the contribution loop.

## User Impact

Doctor identifies preparation stages, contributions, and structured checks before awaiting them, then prints elapsed milliseconds. Void contributions report `finished` or `failed` as lifecycle facts; their existing health notes describe unresolved issues. Structured checks retain finding- and validation-based outcomes. JSON omits human progress, and other repair callers retain their silent default.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Root cause:** reporting belongs at the existing Doctor execution owners. The bounded updater digest, or a counter populated by only some legacy warning writers, cannot supply an authoritative health verdict for a void contribution.

**Changes:** report at those owners, cover pre-contribution preparation, remove the partial warning counter, and preserve ordered awaits, cancellation, cleanup, post-commit failures, and repair results. Migration and installation preparation stay in the existing startup sibling so the coordinator respects its unchanged line cap.

Integrated main at `3b3492490602` with a merge commit that preserves existing ancestry. The original-capture hook retains `fullIntegrityCheck` forwarding from main together with all maintenance authority fields; this PR does not change the quick/full integrity policy.

This addresses standalone Doctor, not the update-parent SQLite progress forwarding in #167055.

The author simplify pass adds no production module, manager, persistent state, CLI option, or timer. Against the base, production is +300/-165 lines, tests are +305/-38, and docs are +6. These totals include intact code moved under lifecycle finalization and preparation moved to its existing owner.

## Evidence

### Real Behavior Proof

Ran the real `pnpm --silent openclaw --profile pr154636 doctor --fix --non-interactive` entrypoint with an isolated synthetic home/state and external service-repair policy. The JSON control used `doctor --json`.

| Real CLI observation | Before: main `51128567f542` | Candidate `8fdb7fb3cf48` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Human command exit | 0 | 0 |
| Lifecycle starts | 0 | 95 |
| Matching terminal outcomes | 0 | 95 |
| First progress line | none | `Doctor: startup prerequisites started` |
| JSON command exit and parse | 0; valid JSON | 0; valid JSON |
| Progress lines in JSON mode | 0 | 0 |

These are 95 balanced lifecycle pairs in a CLI run, not 95 distinct checks or test cases. Every terminal label matches a started label. The proven production bytes are identical to commit `8fdb7fb3cf48cbf5603c75713ccf4426fbe87c80`; their diff against integrated main `3b3492490602` has SHA-256 `8b6f0c531f54d32ca71131263daf212b3314186ab95381d535b25ae07161107b`.

### Published Updater Compatibility

The existing `published-driver-update` Docker lane passed with its acceptance assertions and budgets unchanged. It used the actual npm `2026.10.4` driver to update to the canonical exact-head candidate package.

- Package build and tarball integrity passed. Tarball SHA-256: `c9dd78748e7db71313ec730a5a706e8ba74359284792731d36a94e7707db50bc`.
- The real update exited 0 in 221.129 seconds and its durable run reached `finished`.
- Installed metadata and the connected Gateway build ID matched `2026.10.4-8fdb7fb3cf48-2026-10-17T19-44-38.729Z`; `/readyz` returned HTTP 200.
- The unchanged lane completed its service replacement and session/retention acceptance checks. Service teardown and fixture cleanup exited 0 with terminated process trees; no container from the fixture image remained.

The identity probe lacked `operator.read`, so its read-only diagnostics are incomplete. Connected build identity, HTTP readiness, and the lane acceptance checks were observed separately.

### Test

- 158 distinct focused cases passed across ten existing Doctor owner/sibling suites.
- All 158 cases passed again after the main integration: 125 unit-lane cases and 33 Gateway-lane cases. These are reruns of the same cases, not additional distinct tests.
- The startup ordering regression failed before the repair with zero progress calls while the real native preflight was held. The actual legacy Gateway-note regression also failed against the partial-counter implementation. Both pass after the repair.
- Core and all 29 core-test type graphs, targeted lint, and changed-file format passed again after the main integration.
- The Doctor line-cap ratchet, format, docs MDX, diff checks, SQLite worker call-count ratchet, and runtime import-cycle check passed after the final owner move.
- Fresh independent Codex P0-P3 review after the main integration, including full lifecycle owners and original-capture integrity contracts: no findings, scoped-clean.

The full changed-check run against integrated main exited 1 on three unchanged global checks outside this patch: UI max-lines suppressions, gateway/infra test-root budgets, and unused exports outside Doctor. The Doctor line-cap, lint, format, core typecheck, and all test type graphs pass. Those unrelated files and baselines are untouched; no baseline execution is claimed.

The package build exited 0 with TypeScript/Vite toolchain warnings.

### Risk

Human output gains a start and terminal line per executed lifecycle. JSON silence, generic callers, real preflight ordering, legacy warnings and unhealthy state, healthy siblings, repair failures, cancellation, and published-driver service recovery are covered. There is no speedup claim.

### Changelog

User-facing fix notes are recorded here; `CHANGELOG.md` is release-owned.

AI-assisted: yes. Testing includes the real CLI, exact-head package integrity, a published-driver upgrade, focused regressions, scoped static checks, and independent review.

prs.title: fix: refresh SQLite schema snapshots and stabilize Bun tests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes stale SQLite schema facts that can hide newly installed skills, and corrects four fixtures behind failures in the Bun dual-runtime test campaign.

## User Impact

Skill discovery sees a sibling writer's committed schema after a transaction has only evaluated constants or connection-local PRAGMAs. Real-table reads retain their historical view. Unchanged schemas keep their existing cached admission; historical agent metadata stays scoped to its schema snapshot.

## Root Causes and Changes

| Campaign test | Classification and root cause | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/gateway/sessions-resolve-projection.test.ts` | Bucket 2: the JSON.parse spy counted a lazily parsed source map containing its static prompt marker. | Generate the marker at runtime; still reject decoding unrelated saved prompts. |
| `src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.test.ts` | Bucket 2: synchronous authority revocation was mistaken for completion of asynchronous persisted locator cleanup. | Await readiness and the existing drain boundary, retaining immediate authority assertions. |
| `ui/src/app/control-ui-presentation.test.ts` | Bucket 2: inherited light-mode DOM state made setting light mode a legitimate cache hit. | Establish the test's initial theme and mode before asserting invalidation. |
| `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/skill-library-worker-wire.e2e.test.ts` | Bucket 1: the schema owner treated any managed native step as binding MAIN, including constants and connection PRAGMAs that do not establish a SQLite snapshot. | Qualify the native catalog when a sibling schema revision changes; retain explicit schema snapshot handling. The E2E stays unchanged. |
| `src/gateway/gateway-ssh-upload-signal.test.ts` | Bucket 2 fixture simplification: an unnecessary runtime launch sat between consuming the archive and emitting SIGABRT. The historical timeout did not reproduce standalone or in the original shard replay. | Signal the transport shell directly; retain exact signal, visible chat error, successful retry, and complete-byte assertions. The historic timeout's cause remains unproven. |

The schema regression covers a real-table read, `SELECT 1`, `PRAGMA busy_timeout`, and `PRAGMA query_only`, with one catalog qualification followed by cached reuse. The initial PR revision repeated validation for unchanged schemas; the repair restricts qualification to changed published revisions and preserves the native step callback for explicit schema snapshots. Once an ordinary transaction qualifies its historical catalog, its metadata is cached only under that admission ID, never as current metadata. Review also exposed a cold batched transaction that could forget its pre-read revision; capture it before the batch can pin the snapshot. The added control-batch regression failed before the repair on Bun; an independent focused repro failed on both runtimes and now passes both. A later pinned schema read after sibling DDL also exposed a transition that marked discarded facts as bound. Require actual schema facts before retaining that binding; the new regression failed before the repair, and all 12 raw/managed/pinned read sequences now agree with native SQLite on both runtimes.

Simplification retains the existing schema and metadata owners without a new cache or compatibility path. Whole-PR delta against `2e1468478d68dd6495185ab92a2befb1d110f062`: production **+22/-24 (net -2)**; tests **+56/-17 (net +39)**. No configuration, migration, runtime pin, skip, or timeout changes.

## Evidence

Linux x64 used Node `v24.19.0` and pinned Bun `c45839085e`, short TMPDIR, CI mode, and one worker. Projection, relay, and presentation passed 3/3 per runtime plus a final candidate run. The unchanged skill-library E2E passed 3/3 on each runtime. SSH passed **20/20 consecutive Bun runs**, 3/3 Node runs, and a final candidate run on both. Native schema and observer suites passed both runtimes.

Initial CI run `39055065848` found three PR-caused jobs: `checks-node-changed-compact-small-1`, `checks-node-changed-compact-small-6`, and `checks-node-changed-compact-large-10`. Their failures exposed repeated state admission and missing historical metadata cache reuse. The targeted repairs preserve the query-count contracts and add one bounded qualification assertion for an unqualified historical transaction.

Post-repair focused local proof (Testbox queued, request stopped; no local full suite). The earlier Linux 3/3-per-runtime proof above precedes these admission-cache refinements. The final local skill-library E2E also passed on both Bun and Node after the pinned-transition repair:

| File | Bun | Node |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/infra/sqlite-schema-facts.native.test.ts` | 48 passed, 3 existing API skips | 51 passed |
| `src/state/openclaw-state-db-checkonce.test.ts` | 10 passed | 10 passed |
| `src/state/openclaw-agent-db.checkonce.test.ts` | 11 passed | 11 passed |
| `src/state/openclaw-state-db-existing-write.test.ts` | 15 passed | 15 passed |
| `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/skill-library-worker-wire.e2e.test.ts` | 1 passed | 1 passed |

Focused command template:

```sh
PATH=/private/tmp/oc-bun-fork/bin:$PATH TMPDIR=/private/tmp/oc-bunci5 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1
TMPDIR=/private/tmp/oc-bunci5 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1
```

Linux used the same runtime selection with `PATH=/tmp/oc-bunci5/current/bin:$PATH`, `OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH=/tmp/oc-bunci5/current/bin/bun`, `TMPDIR=/tmp/oc-bunci5/tmp`, and `CI=1`. UI used `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config ui/vitest.config.ts src/app/control-ui-presentation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.

Initial changed-file format/lint, core typecheck, and gateway-root/agents-tools/ui-app/infra test typechecks passed. Latest repair format, lint, state-logging test typecheck, and fresh Codex autoreview through P2 passed. The final staged review is scoped-clean through P2.

No fork bug established and no new runtime-only skips. Known campaign failures outside this lane remain untouched: provider-crabbox-runtime-preflight, pairing-allowlist.lifecycle, server.chat-abort-dispatch-rejection, server.session-row-deltas.integration, and server.sessions.create-worktree-spawn. The coordinator subsequently reviewed this diff and decided to land it.

Prior head `d2897c7317ba18679111eb461c0de17279e69afb` passed [CI run 39056646519](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39056646519), including both PostgreSQL conformance jobs. The subsequent pinned-snapshot fix has fresh native-suite, cache-suite, format/lint/typecheck proof and a scoped-clean Codex review. Its final E2E passed on both runtimes.

Pre-rebase head: `43ac450d41431d48486cf43c2c16572924433d2a`; [exact-head CI run 39058559033](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39058559033) initially failed only `PostgreSQL conformance (infra)`. Its unchanged `port-command.postgres.test.ts` refusal-boundary test hit 60 seconds; the other 359 tests passed. The same test took 43.45 seconds on the prior green head, and neighboring tests were approximately twice as slow in the failed run. A focused replay on this exact head against a disposable PostgreSQL 17 service passed in 23.619 seconds (one selected test, five filtered tests). This supports a load-sensitive timeout; it does not establish a product fix. No timeout or unrelated test was changed. Only the failed job was rerun once. Attempt 2 failed on the same 60-second timeout (job `117476913769`), again with the other 359 tests passing. The exact-head CI remains red. The cause is unresolved: the local pass and neighboring slowdown support a load-sensitive explanation, but do not prove causality or establish that this is an inherited failure. No second rerun was requested; the unrelated test remains unchanged for coordinator triage.

Focused replay command: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/oc-bunci5 CI=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:55435/postgres -- src/infra/database-engine/port-command.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'probes real privileges'`. The disposable service used the pinned CI image and was removed afterward. Testbox was queued and stopped; the replay ran locally as one focused file.


## Landing refresh

Rebased without conflicts onto `3b3492490602f5080d3fbe7d2df9618cdb82ea9a`; exact head is `685323aff7d4a05c7696cfb8954e9cf2fd29e864`. It contains the inherited terminal-PTY ratchet repair `255c4d47a33`. The introduced diff is unchanged and the first commit subject still describes it.

Node replay after the rebase: all six touched files passed, 146 tests, with `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/oc-bunci5` and one worker. The four PostgreSQL files named in the original baseline evidence also passed locally against the pinned CI PostgreSQL 17 image: 23 tests, including the port refusal boundary in 37.794 seconds. The disposable service included CI's `unaccent`, `pg_trgm`, and `vector` extensions. An initial replay was stopped after the missing extensions exposed a fixture setup error; the corrected service passed. The additional updater-preflight file also passed all five tests, including its CI-timeout case in 49.951 seconds. Total real PostgreSQL proof: five files, 28 tests. No product code, skips, assertions, or timeouts changed.

[Exact-head CI run 39062409422](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39062409422), attempt 1, completed with two inherited failed jobs plus the aggregate gate:

- `check-lint-core-2` (job `117484113158`): `src/infra/sqlite-readonly-location.worker.ts:381:31`, `typescript(await-thenable)`. This worker, its operation registry, and registry implementation are byte-identical to tested main parent `3b3492490602`. The same diagnostic appears in [main run 39062485709, job 117483329751](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39062485709/job/117483329751). The job-name comparison labels this new because main's matching job number covers a different stripe; main's actual failing infra stripe is `check-lint-core-4`. Focused local lint reproduces the exact diagnostic. Main commit `f15018960a17d` removed the asynchronous registry operation while leaving this await.
- `PostgreSQL conformance (infra)` (job `117483218317`): seven failed cases across archive-restore, doctor-migration, matrix-roots, port-command, and update-preflight. All seven test names and error messages exactly match [main run 39058564617, job 117471751210](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39058564617/job/117471751210). The newer scheduled main run also fails those cases. All five test files are unchanged between the tested main parent and PR merge. The failure table is job-name-only, so attribution uses the inspected test/error comparison, not a matching-signature-table claim.
- `openclaw/ci-gate` (job `117488951289`) aggregates those two failures. `security-fast`, PostgreSQL integrations, and all other selected jobs passed. No CI rerun was requested.

The native inherited-failure exception is authorized by the coordinator's landing instruction. This preserves the failed CI result; local passes do not claim a repair of the baseline failures.

prs.title: fix(oc-path): resolve and edit empty string keys
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw path` cannot read or edit a JSON/JSONL/YAML field whose key is an empty string, and wildcard searches silently omit it, even though `""` is a valid quoted path segment.

## User Impact

Empty string keys can now be found, resolved, and edited, including when they contain a nested object. Other fields remain unchanged, and an empty key still cannot address an array element.

## Why This Change Was Made

The JSON and YAML resolvers checked for an empty segment after removing quotes. Check the raw segment instead so the explicit key `""` is distinct from a missing path segment. JSONL already uses the JSON value resolver, so it receives the same fix without another traversal implementation.

## Evidence

- At base `3d58fa98356cb9a745064938360b8a8f32619155`, the six new object-key cases fail because `find` omits the empty key; the three array rejection cases pass. With the fix, all nine pass.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/oc-path --maxWorkers=1`: 356 passed, five existing platform skips, 33 files; 18.64 seconds in Vitest, 21.61 seconds for the wrapper.
- The changed `find.test.ts` alone passes all 64 tests: 22.07 seconds in Vitest, 31.76 seconds for the wrapper, with most time in setup/transform/worker startup. CI timing is pending.
- Scoped production and test typechecks, type-aware lint for the three changed files, formatting, and whitespace checks pass.

### Shipped CLI at `a5f08668f18a4207cb7ad1d89365a6eed3bb1c93`

On Windows with Node 24.19.0, `pnpm dev path` rebuilt this clean commit and passed all 12 commands across JSONC, YAML, and JSONL. The build stamp matched the commit with clean inputs. Fixtures used isolated HOME/config/state with only oc-path enabled.

For `{"":{"value":"old"},"keep":"unchanged"}` and its YAML equivalent:

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `path find 'oc://sample.jsonc/*' --file sample.jsonc --json` | Both `oc://sample.jsonc/""` and `oc://sample.jsonc/keep` are returned |
| `path resolve 'oc://sample.jsonc/""/value' --file sample.jsonc --json` | `resolved: true`, value `old` |
| `path set 'oc://sample.jsonc/""/value' new --file sample.jsonc --json --dry-run` | Returns the exact expected replacement bytes; original file unchanged |
| Same `set` without `--dry-run` | Writes exactly `{"":{"value":"new"},"keep":"unchanged"}` plus the original trailing newline |

The same four operations pass for YAML and JSONL (with `/L1` before the JSONL key). Each actual file was compared byte for byte with the expected output; preview calls preserved the original bytes. Before the fix, a shipped CLI with identical resolver source omitted the key and returned `unresolved` for reads and both forms of `set`.
