prs.title: feat(media-understanding): shared structured extraction for image-capable providers
prs.body:
Closes #119772

> AI-assisted PR. Written with Claude Code; I have reviewed the change and understand what it does. See **Evidence** for validation.

**Rescoped on 6 September.** The previous head of this branch bundled two fixes. The provider-resolution half landed on `main` as #139231 (`18733285112b`), rewritten by @steipete at the shared catalog owner — I am not carrying a second version of it here. What remains is the other half, now filed as the feature it is rather than a bug fix, at +220/−11 production lines instead of +336/−27.

## What Problem This Solves

Logbook's `visionModel` is effectively single-provider. On current `main`:

- `extensions/codex/media-understanding-provider.ts` is the only `extractStructured` implementation in the repository.
- Registry hydration binds `describeImage` and `describeImages` from the shared image runtime for every image-capable provider (`src/media-understanding/provider-registry.ts:44-45`) but never `extractStructured`.
- So `extractStructuredWithModel` throws `Provider does not support structured extraction: <id>` (`src/media-understanding/runtime.ts:372`) for any non-Codex provider — after #139231 made that provider resolvable, it resolves and *then* throws.

The `extractStructured` contract shipped in May with Codex as its only implementer; the docs already say other providers "do not currently expose" it. This PR gives them one.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Owner:** the registry hydration and the shared image runtime that already own the `describeImage`/`describeImages` defaults.

**Canonical fix.** Hydration binds `extractStructured: provider.extractStructured ?? extractStructuredWithImageModel` next to those defaults; providers with their own hook (Codex) keep it. `src/media-understanding/structured-extraction.ts` runs one completion through `completeImagesWithModel` with the extraction instructions — including a no-secrets rule — as the prompt, supplemental text inputs as `userText` in the user message, and the reply parsed and schema-validated the same way the Codex extractor does it. It never routes through a provider's bespoke `describeImages`. Replies are parsed strictly first; a fenced or prose-wrapped reply falls back to the first balanced JSON object or array via normalization-core's `extractBalancedJsonPrefix`, so a model that ignores "no Markdown fences" does not fail the whole batch — Codex's own extractor does a raw `JSON.parse`, so the shared path is now the more tolerant of the two. A reply with no JSON in it is still a controlled error.

**The delivery gate, and what it deliberately is not.** The output is persisted, so the instructions must reach the model as an instruction, not as user text beside a screenshot. `promptDelivery: "system-required"` makes the runtime refuse — before any stream is registered or request sent — exactly the routes on which the runtime *itself* decides to demote the prompt into user content: `shouldPlaceImagePromptInUserContent` (the GitHub Copilot, OpenRouter, and Alibaba Model Studio endpoint classes) and both MiniMax VLM branches. Those get a named batch error.

The previous head instead carried an allowlist of transport names. That was wrong in both directions — it refused Ollama on its `api` string even though Ollama's plugin stream sends `Context.systemPrompt` as a `role: "system"` message (`extensions/ollama/src/stream.runtime.ts:740`), and it admitted plugin streams on a declared name it could not verify. The gate now records only the one decision the runtime owns. The trust boundary for a plugin stream that demoted `systemPrompt` is the plugin install — such a plugin would break every agent turn on that provider — and I have left that as a question for maintainers rather than a promise in code.

**`agentDir` default.** The shared extractor defaults an empty `agentDir` to the configured default agent dir (`structured-extraction.ts`). The dispatcher is unchanged and still passes `""` through, so a bespoke extractor such as Codex — which uses a non-empty `agentDir` as its thread `cwd` and loads project-local configuration from it (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/bounded-turn.ts:125`) — sees no change at all. On the shared path that value is the key for prepared-model owners, and `""` matches none of them on a long-lived gateway; Logbook never passes one. An earlier revision of this head put the default in the dispatcher, which would have changed Codex's working directory for existing installs — the review caught it, and it is fixed here.

**Removed versus the previous head**, so reviewers who saw it know what went where: the by-id resolver (superseded by #139231); the transport allowlist and `KnownApi` inspection (above); `imagePayloadTransform` and the opencode rewrite (opencode-only and separable — opencode is now hydrated with the shared hook without its reasoning-strip transform, which I am naming as a follow-up rather than carrying an SDK-adjacent field for one plugin). `runtime.ts`, `runtime.test.ts`, and all three opencode files are byte-identical to `main`.

## Maintainer decision requested

**Hydration now supplies `extractStructured` to every image-capable provider that lacks one — including providers whose `describeImage`/`describeImages` are bespoke.** That is a change to the provider-plugin capability contract, and I would rather state it than have it found.

What it does and does not do: the shared extractor never calls a provider's describe hooks — it runs its own completion through `completeImagesWithModel`, the same stream path `describeImage` takes when a provider does not override it. So a provider with bespoke description hooks that previously returned a visible `Provider does not support structured extraction` error now either extracts, or returns a visible provider error recorded on the batch. The delivery gate applies either way. On current `main`, the only bundled provider with bespoke hooks and no extractor of its own is opencode (its reasoning-strip transform is the named follow-up); Codex keeps its own.

I looked for a narrower rule and there isn't a correct one expressible from hook shape: deepinfra assigns the shared functions by reference, openai wraps the shared function in a lazy-import closure, and anthropic/google/ollama leave the hooks undefined — presence or identity checks each exclude a provider that is plainly on the shared path. The alternatives are therefore **(a)** this behavior, documented as above, or **(b)** an explicit opt-in on the provider contract, which is SDK surface and a maintainer call. I am asking for (a) and will implement (b) if that is the decision.

## User Impact

- Logbook works with any image-capable provider for which the shared runtime delivers the prompt as a system instruction. `visionModel` becomes a real choice.
- The Copilot, OpenRouter, and Model Studio endpoint classes and the MiniMax VLM endpoint are refused with an error naming the route, recorded on the batch, instead of running with a weaker boundary. `docs/plugins/logbook.md` and the `visionModel` help text state this rule and nothing broader.
- No behavior change for providers with their own `extractStructured`, for audio/video-only providers, or for plain `describeImage`/`describeImages` — only `promptDelivery: "system-required"` consults the gate.

## Evidence

**Regression tests fail on pre-fix code**, captured by removing the relevant line and re-running:

- Hydration line removed → `provider-registry.test.ts`: `expected undefined to be [AsyncFunction invoke]` on "hydrates structured extraction from the shared runtime".
- `promptInUserContent` refusal removed → `image.test.ts`: the Copilot case reaches `complete()` (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'stopReason')`), the MiniMax case resolves `"portal ok"` instead of rejecting — i.e. the request went out.
- `agentDir` default removed → `structured-extraction.test.ts`: `''` received where the configured default agent dir was expected.
- Fence fallback removed → `structured-extraction.test.ts`: a ` ```json ` -wrapped reply fails with `Structured extraction returned invalid JSON: anthropic`.

**Boundary tests.** `image.test.ts` asserts the exact `Context` handed to `complete` — system prompt equals the instruction, user message holds the caller text and image only — and that refused routes make no stream registration, no `complete`, and no `fetch`. `structured-extraction.test.ts` covers prompt assembly, text-input placement, JSON parsing, and schema validation. `provider-registry.test.ts` covers hydration identity and bespoke-hook preservation.

**Ran locally on this head:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` over `image`, `provider-registry`, `runtime`, `structured-extraction`, `image-tool.provider-loading`, and both opencode suites — all green; `oxfmt`, `oxlint` on changed files; `git diff --check`; `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` (no new SDK exports); `check:assertion-safety`; `check:coercion-helpers`; `config:docs:check` after regenerating `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` for the help-text change, as that check's own message instructs; an independent `$autoreview` pass at P2, which produced one finding — the fenced-JSON hard failure above — fixed in this head.

**Left to CI on purpose:** `pnpm build`, the `tsgo` typecheck lanes, and the full suite. My development machine cannot run those lanes, so this PR's CI on the exact head is the authority for them.

### Real-behavior proof (this head)

Isolated dev gateway on an x86-64 Linux box (Node v24.19.0), own `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, own port, never the operator's gateway. Logbook capture is macOS-only, so two synthetic JPEGs (a mock editor window; no real screen content) were seeded as frames — extraction, provider resolution, and the batch pipeline are all real; only the screenshot source is not.

Head `ce8458199cf95c85703fa1c884943e3541a552e1`; base `dd3faf5f`. Built dist self-reports `OpenClaw 2026.9.2 (ce84581)`. Vision model: `qwen2.5vl:7b` on local Ollama — a plugin stream with no bespoke `extractStructured`, which the previous head's allowlist would have refused on its `api` string.

#### 1. Accepted route completes (Ollama)

`visionModel: ollama/qwen2.5vl:7b`

```
$ openclaw gateway call logbook.analyze.now
{ "started": true }
$ openclaw gateway call logbook.status
lastBatch: { "id": 1, "day": "2026-09-06", "status": "done", "endMs": 1788750180139 }
todayCards: 2
```

`logbook.timeline` returns two cards built from the seeded frames:

```
{ "title": "Drafting release notes",
  "detail": "Added a short paragraph about how the extraction prompt travels in the system channel",
  "category": "coding", "keyframeId": 1 }
{ "title": "Re-read runtime dispatcher", "category": "coding", "keyframeId": 2 }
```

`batches` row: `{id:1, status:"done", error:null, frame_count:2, model:"ollama/qwen2.5vl:7b"}`. Gateway log: `[plugins] loading ollama from <dist>/extensions/ollama/index.js`.

**The prompt reaches the model in the system channel.** A logging pass-through proxy in front of Ollama recorded the extraction request:

```
POST /api/chat  bytes=87752
  model='qwen2.5vl:7b' stream=True
  messages[0].role='system' text="You are OpenClaw's bounded structured-extraction worker.
    Return only the requested extraction. Do not include secrets such as passwords, API keys,
    tokens, or credentials, even when they are visible in the input. ..."
  messages[1].role='user' images=2 text=''
  -> upstream 200
```

That is `STRUCTURED_EXTRACTION_INSTRUCTIONS` verbatim as `role: "system"`, images in the user message — the property `promptDelivery: "system-required"` exists to protect.

#### 2. Refusal happens before extraction I/O

`visionModel: minimax/MiniMax-VL-01`, with that provider's `baseUrl` pointed at a local listener that logs every TCP connection.

```
$ openclaw gateway call logbook.analyze.now      # 23:20:56
$ openclaw gateway call logbook.status
lastBatch: { "id": 1, "status": "error",
  "error": "Provider does not accept system instructions for image requests: minimax/MiniMax-VL-01 (the prompt is delivered as user content)" }
```

Listener log, complete file:

```
23:20:39 LISTENER-START port=19001
23:20:41 CONNECT from ('127.0.0.1', …)   first-bytes b'GET /listener-self-test HTTP/1.1…'
```

The single entry is a `curl` self-test proving the listener records. **Zero connections after the trigger** — the route was refused before any request was built.

Same refusal on the OpenRouter class against the real `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` with a dummy key, terminal in 5s (a key that reached OpenRouter would return 401 instead):

```
lastBatch: { "id": 3, "status": "error",
  "error": "Provider does not accept system instructions for image requests: openrouter/qwen/qwen2.5-vl-7b-instruct (the prompt is delivered as user content)" }
```

#### 3. Existing route (Codex) is untouched

```
$ git diff HEAD~1 -- src/media-understanding/runtime.ts extensions/codex/media-understanding-provider.ts
$ echo $?
0
```

Empty. Neither file is in the commit's changed set, and the dispatcher still passes `agentDir: params.agentDir ?? ""` unchanged (`src/media-understanding/runtime.ts:387`), so the bespoke Codex extractor keeps receiving `""` as its thread cwd. No OpenAI/Codex credentials were available for a live Codex run; the diff is the proof offered.

#### 4. Before/after on the same batch

Base `dd3faf5f` built separately in its own checkout, same state dir and frames:

```
BEFORE (dd3faf5f)  lastBatch: { "id": 4, "status": "error",
                     "error": "Provider does not support structured extraction: ollama" }
AFTER  (ce845819)  lastBatch: { "id": 4, "status": "done", "endMs": 1788751260139 }
```

Identical frames, identical batch id, only the checkout differs.

**Complete diagnostics** — the full proxy and listener logs, every gateway batch/refusal/plugin-load line, RPC captures, and redacted configs — are in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/119773#issuecomment-5565102396).

#### Limits of this proof, stated

- **The `github-copilot` class could not be exercised.** That provider validates its token against GitHub before any inference (`extensions/github-copilot/runtime-auth.ts:83-96`) and derives its API base URL from that response, so without valid Copilot credentials the batch fails at `Copilot authentication failed: HTTP 401` before the gate runs. With valid credentials the classification is the same as OpenRouter's and the gate applies; I have no Copilot account to show it live. The OpenRouter and Model Studio branches are classified from `baseUrl` (`resolveProviderRequestCapabilities`), so they cannot be aimed at a local listener — hence OpenRouter was proven against its real host and MiniMax carried the zero-I/O proof.
- **Pre-existing Logbook behavior found on the way, not this PR's:** card synthesis (`reviseCards`) runs on the agent default model, not `visionModel`. With no `agents.defaults.model` configured, extraction succeeds and the observations are written, but the batch is then marked `error` by the synthesis step. Worth its own issue; I can file it.

**Production LOC:** +220/−11 across four files (`image.ts` +55/−8, `provider-registry.ts` +9/−2, `image-runtime.ts` +8/−1, `structured-extraction.ts` +148). Tests +347/−3. Docs and manifest +36/−19. The growth is the capability; about 35 lines of `structured-extraction.ts` mirror Codex's parse/validate and could be shared through the SDK later, which would need a surface-budget decision I am not making here.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #114169. A healthy awaited WhatsApp inbound handler can remain busy without changing its pending-work count, leaving `lastRunActivityAt` stale and allowing the channel health monitor to restart it after 25 minutes.

## Approach

Keep the gateway's fixed stuck-run threshold unchanged. The WhatsApp status lifecycle now refreshes activity every minute only while known pending work is busy and the socket remains connected. It clears that timer on idle, connection close, and terminal shutdown, so transport failures are still detected.

## Evidence

Focused fake-timer coverage proves activity remains fresh beyond the gateway threshold and stops refreshing after idle or teardown. Existing gateway-policy tests retain the stale-busy restart contract.

## Release note context

Fixes a WhatsApp channel lifecycle regression where a legitimate long-running inbound turn could be restarted mid-turn.

prs.title: fix: drain inbound debounce buffer and followup queues before SIGUSR1 reload
prs.body:
Related: #51620

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users whose inbound message was accepted shortly before a SIGUSR1 or config reload could have buffered message content silently dropped before it reached the reply pipeline.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway now closes ordinary work admission synchronously, flushes accepted inbound debounce work inside one core-private restart continuation, drains channel, active-turn, and followup work in order, then rechecks work created by followup delivery. Pre-created debounce callbacks reserve tracked required-continuation ownership, including parentless accepted work. Already-reserved required continuations may finish during the signal-pending gap while ordinary roots remain fenced, and removed-but-unsettled timer flushes remain visible until settlement. Buffered callbacks can also be explicitly rebound to the private restart admission context, while the global sweep is bounded by both the remaining restart deadline and a 100-pass/30-second ceiling so continued ingress cannot stall reload indefinitely.

Every non-forced phase now shares one absolute restart-drain deadline. Initial active-task and embedded-run waits receive only the budget remaining after inbound debounce and channel queue draining, so earlier phases cannot reset the configured maximum.

Forced restarts retain the existing skip-drain behavior. This does not persist messages sent while the gateway is offline.

## User Impact

Messages accepted immediately before an in-process reload can complete through the normal command/reply path instead of being rejected by the restart fence or disappearing from in-memory buffers. A sustained stream of new transport events also cannot hold the gateway forever in the debounce-flush phase, and the configured restart deferral maximum is honored across the full drain sequence.

## Evidence

Exact-head validation for `bb8f1b842e85c6745e7f8a1bfb8303d73ca6f7f6`:

- **Focused behavior tests:** 4 files, 167 tests passed.
  - `src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts`: 65 passed.
  - `src/process/command-queue.test.ts`: 42 passed.
  - `src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts`: 16 passed.
  - `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts`: 44 passed.
- **New P1 regressions:** a buffer created inside an admitted inbound root survives that root's release; timer-started required work can finish through the restart-signal-pending fence while ordinary roots remain blocked; a timer-started callback remains visible and keeps the restart sweep pending until its real command enqueue settles; parentless accepted continuations retain required ownership; continuous ingress stops at the pass cap; the exact final-pass boundary reports drained correctly; a slow callback returns at the supplied deadline; and a deterministic 100 ms restart budget reduced to 40 ms by earlier debounce/channel work is passed as 40 ms to both initial active-work waits and the final close drain.
- **Formatting/lint:** `oxfmt --check` and type-aware `oxlint` passed on all touched files.
- **Type safety:** core production, core test, and plugin SDK declaration `tsgo` checks passed.
- **Tree identity:** GitHub tree `37822eb909f4bd797d9bc6eb7d8488286f39637a` is the exact locally tested tree; both newly uploaded blob SHAs matched the local Git objects.
- **CI:** GitHub Actions is running on the exact head above.

A live Signal/Telegram account is not paired in this environment. I have requested the repository's Mantis Telegram proof flow below so maintainers can attach redacted channel-to-gateway reload evidence to this exact head.

## Implementation and Safety Notes

- `createInboundDebouncer()` retains its public `enqueue` / `flushKey` / `cancelKey` return shape.
- `ChannelRunQueue` retains its public `enqueue` / `deactivate` shape.
- No public `enqueueInternal`, `allowDuringGatewayDrain`, or command-queue admission bypass is exposed.
- The debounce registry is weak, avoiding channel teardown requirements.
- Overflow-summary backlog is included in followup pending counts.
- Bounded restarts use one absolute deadline; unbounded restarts continue passing `undefined` and wait indefinitely.
- The branch remains a focused 13-file change.

## Synchronization

- **PR head:** `bb8f1b842e85c6745e7f8a1bfb8303d73ca6f7f6`

## What Problem This Solves

The public representation cache duplicates facts already owned by its entry map
and the admission gate's configuration-qualified key. Remove the parallel cache
current/active flags and redundant configuration pointer without removing the
response-currentness contract.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. Invalidation, eviction and ordinary close still
make held representations unavailable. Final HTML/card/media publication and
physical-source checks remain unchanged, as do rate limits, FIFO capacity,
singleflight, completion-time LRU promotion and the 16 MiB/128-entry limits.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use exact installed entry identity for the existing isCurrent predicate and
cancel operation. The sole production begin/complete caller is the request gate;
its config-qualified key already partitions pending and cached work. Every
completion is synchronous and called once by that owner, so remove the duplicate
completion fallback and redundant post-eviction flag check as well.

This is a narrowed AREA recovery from the wider parked cleanup: four files,
two production paths, 19 net production lines removed. Phase E standalone session
memory and its factory/registry/expiry/federation/tests are untouched. No schema,

prs.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier
prs.body:
Closes #22438

## Motivation

Bootstrap files consume LLM tokens on every session. For users with large workspaces, loading all files into every session — including sub-agents and cron jobs — wastes context window budget on files the agent never references. This PR introduces tiered loading so users can control how much context each session type receives, **reducing unnecessary token usage** while preserving persona consistency where needed.

## What

Introduces a three-tier bootstrap file loading system (`minimal` | `standard` | `full`) with a new `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` configuration option. Both the `minimal` and `standard` tiers exclude hook-loaded extras (e.g. `packages/*/AGENTS.md` from the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook); `full` keeps everything.

## Why

The current binary split (main=all, subagent/cron=minimal) doesn't support use cases where subagents need persona context or where main sessions should be lightweight. This adds a clean, backward-compatible middle ground that lets users optimize their token budget per session type.

## How

- **`resolveBootstrapTier(sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — resolves the effective tier from session type + optional config override.
- **`filterBootstrapFilesForSession(files, sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — extended with optional tier parameter (backward compatible — no tierOverride = existing session-type heuristic).
- **Hook-source guard** — both `minimal` and `standard` filters check `file.source !== "hook"` before allowlist matching, so a hook-loaded extra whose basename happens to be in the allowlist cannot slip in. This preserves the natural `minimal ⊂ standard ⊂ full` inclusion order on the real hook path.
- **Config** — `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` in the zod schema, TypeScript types, labels, and help text.

The `source: "root" | "hook"` provenance field on `WorkspaceBootstrapFile` is the discriminator: root-level bootstrap files keep flowing through `minimal` and `standard`; per-package extras registered via the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook are only reachable through `full`.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: tiered bootstrap loading — `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` (`minimal` | `standard` | `full`) controls which workspace files are injected into each session's context window. Closes #22438. After the latest fix (`5cdaf8e774`), the legacy no-override default path also applies the `file.source !== "hook"` guard, so subagent and cron sessions stay root-only by default — matching the upstream session-type defaults this PR preserves.

Real environment tested: macOS 26.2 on Apple Silicon, Node 24.13.0, pnpm 11.2.2, against the fork branch tip at commit `5cdaf8e774`. Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. `git checkout 5cdaf8e774` (this PR's head)
2. `pnpm install --prefer-offline --frozen-lockfile`
3. Author the reproduction harness at the repo root, importing `./src/agents/workspace.js` and calling the exported functions directly with a `WorkspaceBootstrapFile[]` shaped like a real workspace (root files + two hook-sourced `packages/*/AGENTS.md` entries).
4. `node ./node_modules/.bin/tsx repro-tiered-bootstrap.mts`

prs.title: fix(web-fetch): remove unpublished spill files after cancellation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cancelling a large built-in `web_fetch` response can leave a private spill file even though the caller never receives its path. A failed transport release or sandbox projection checkpoint can produce the same unpublished output.

## User Impact

Rejected fetches remove their own unpublished output. Successfully returned and cached spill files stay available with the existing output format and lifetime.

## Why This Change Was Made

The private file or prepared sandbox staging owner supplies a scoped cleanup operation as soon as it owns an artifact. The fetch retains that operation until transport release and final cancellation/currentness checks succeed. Sandbox cleanup uses the prepared host root rather than treating a container path as a host path or granting the guest write access.

## Evidence

Current candidate `42e0cc294b3e` was validated with Node 24.19.0 and pinned pnpm 12.10.1 on macOS arm64.

- **22 distinct scoped cases passed** across the native tools, sandbox and local-workspace owners. One GNU-host composition case is Linux-only and was skipped locally. The later exact-case type-fix check is included in those 22, not counted twice.
- The affected files passed formatting, typed lint and strict scoped production/test TypeScript checks. The qualified registered Gateway build passed.
- A direct real HTTP/filesystem control consumed two 2,000,000-byte responses: cancellation left zero unpublished spills, while success retained the complete 2,000,313-byte owner-only file.
- The official CLI and a separate isolated Gateway exercised the original user path: authenticated chat, the real model-visible tool/catalog dispatch, native guarded HTTP/filesystem output, and an actual abort naming the admitted run. After producer settlement, the rejected turn had **0 unpublished spills** before harness cleanup. A successful control resumed the model, persisted its final marker, and retained its complete owner-only output (6000313 bytes).

The Gateway proof joined native client database/worker owners, observed product clean shutdown and natural CLI exit 0, joined all retained processes, and checked unchanged source identity after cleanup. Its external model/HTTP endpoints were deterministic loopback fixtures; production tool admission, host authority, cancellation, storage, sessions and persistence were real.

Earlier failed invocations remain failed. The first whole tools invocation contained a macOS-incompatible GNU fixture; only its 16 unchanged passing output-contract observations are reused. A later type error was fixed and the affected checks passed. The first Gateway fixture incorrectly required a direct tool schema rather than handling the default catalog; it produced no fetch oracle and remains archived as failed/inconclusive, including its teardown gap. The next execution reached and cancelled the real run with clean process/worker joins, but the path was already published; it remains inconclusive. The final control uses the same two-million-character bound with a real six-megabyte BMP UTF-8 response under the supported response limit, without filesystem mocks or injected product delays.

- Public proof excerpt: Validation `web-spill-real-gateway-chat-abort` (pass, exit_code=0, 30239ms):

## Risks And Limitations

One Linux/GNU host-composition case is skipped on macOS and remains for Linux CI. External model/web services, cached spill retention, real sandbox guest execution, and session actor replacement are not claimed by this Gateway control. Initial marker creation relies on the existing fs-safe atomic-create contract. Cleanup retains root/leaf identity guards and the original rejection; it grants no new guest mutation permission. Existing settled-finalizer CI failures remain separately unattributed; no unrelated source was changed. Hosted CI still needs to evaluate the updated head.

prs.title: refactor(state): retire unused terminal-latch generations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The terminal database-open latch still carries optional file generations, synchronous hashing and asynchronous expiry machinery after its only generation-bearing production producer was retired. Production callers already record only a pathname and error.

## User Impact

Normal terminal refusals, explicit Doctor clearing and real native integrity recovery retain their behavior. Persisted quarantine generation checks remain unchanged. No database schema, persisted format, durability, retention, permission, config, protocol, dependency or public SDK change is proposed. Phase E session-memory code and tests are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use a path-to-Error map and a two-argument void record operation. Delete the orphan asynchronous generation facade and synthetic generation-expiry cases; adapt existing real owner tests to the simpler record signature. Keep native disposal ordering, validation invalidation, worker admission after awaits, FIFO and write-capable shutdown settlement. Main's explicit-FULL index-corruption repair coverage and tooling inventory remain unchanged.

This is a coherent four-owner area slice from an unfinished >80-file cleanup proposal, split for precise CI attribution. Twelve files: **79 net production lines removed** (+14/-93) and **109 net test lines removed** (+11/-120). No replacement helper, test seam or import edge is added.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Process-local generation-bearing records no longer expire through an unrelated file metadata change or asynchronous hash probe. That producer was removed in #174726 (`aba15693`), an ancestor of the base. Every remaining production record already omits the optional generation, so the removed path now exists only for synthetic tests. Recorded ordinary refusals continue to require explicit clear/restart; actual integrity failures still use the independent full native verifier before clearing. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw infer web fetch --url <url>` fails on a default install with `web.fetch is disabled or no provider is available.`, even though `web_fetch` is documented as enabled by default with no configuration.

## User Impact

User impact: `infer web fetch` works out of the box, using the same direct fetch and Readability extraction the agent's `web_fetch` tool uses. `--provider <id>` still pins a specific fetch provider such as Firecrawl. When fetching is turned off, the error now names `tools.web.fetch.enabled`; an unavailable provider is named, with a pointer to `openclaw infer web providers`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI only resolved provider-backed fetch definitions, so with no fetch provider configured it had nothing to run. Without `--provider` it now executes `createWebFetchTool`, the owner of the default path, rather than re-implementing fetch, SSRF guarding, or extraction in the CLI.

## Evidence

- Live, before: on a fresh isolated state, `infer web fetch --url https://example.com/ --json` failed with the error above, while `--provider firecrawl` worked.
- Live, after (source entry, isolated state): `ok: true`, `provider: "direct"`, HTTP 200, Readability extraction, wrapped title "Example Domain".
- Unit: new tests cover the default path, `--format` mapping, disabled config with and without `--provider`, and explicit-provider pinning (they fail before the fix). The web-related tests in `src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts` pass (8). Full-file local runs under heavy host load hit different unrelated timeouts on each run; CI is the broad proof.
- Autoreview: scoped-clean at P2.

## CI repair

- CI run 39052690140 failed only the mock-export ratchet (plus its aggregate gate): the new closed web-fetch mock lacked its required isolation rationale. Commit d71481c4e98 documents that the CLI fixture intentionally excludes the network, cache, and secret-owner runtime. No production behavior, assertions, timeouts, or baselines changed.
- The mock-export ratchet passes against the branch baseline; formatting and diff checks pass. Comparing this older checkout directly with newer main reports 27 already-removed baseline entries, not new mock sites; no baseline was edited.
- Isolated local run: all 8 selected fetch/search cases passed. Two provider-inventory cases also selected by the filter produced an initial timeout and a subsequent mismatch; both passed on their focused rerun without code changes (40.3s and 65ms; total runner wall 305.37s including module preparation). This is not claimed as a repair of the transient local timeout.
- CI after the mock-isolation repair passed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39054054862 (head d71481c4e98ce35571c90177617af08e05f0c045).

## Review follow-up

- Updated `infer list`/`infer inspect` metadata to describe direct URL fetching as well as provider selection, and page content with fetch metadata. Verified the exported metadata directly and checked formatting. Latest head: `5d809582cfeaf1acac83304b147cbf665e0576ad`; [exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39058951801).
- The CLI tests intentionally protect routing, format forwarding, disabled configuration, and envelope attribution. They are not claimed as extraction proof. The coordinator's isolated before/after CLI live proof above exercises the production owner; existing owner-level HTTP fixtures in `src/agents/tools/web-fetch-visibility.tool-extraction.test.ts` and `src/agents/tools/web-fetch.json-fidelity.test.ts` exercise real tool extraction and wrapping. Those existing fixtures were inspected, not rerun for this text-only follow-up. Retaining the routing tests avoids duplicating the fetch owner's integration coverage in the CLI suite.

prs.title: fix(update): show progress while migrated updates finalize
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Migrated updates can appear stalled because the retained updater withholds the finalizer's progress until the child exits.

## User Impact

Finalization diagnostics now reach stderr while the update is running. Terminal stdout remains deferred until executor and package cleanup settle. Doctor also keeps running when its output stream reports ordinary backpressure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing process observer for live stderr and retain raw UTF-8 buffers until unseen cancellation output is selected. This preserves partial character bytes, bounded capture, Windows encoding behavior, and exact-once diagnostics without changing timeouts or terminal publication ownership.

Release-note context: show progress during migrated update finalization and avoid cancelling Doctor on output backpressure.

## Evidence

- Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh autoreview and independent source review found no actionable production findings; the final mechanical test corrections were independently reviewed.
- Added coverage for a real finalizer held behind a release gate, deferred stdout, cancellation tails beyond the capture cap, incomplete UTF-8 bytes, Windows capture boundaries, and Doctor backpressure. Existing legacy, package-retention, and Windows terminal tests remain in scope.

Each shard finished with exit 0. The unchanged generic `src/process/exec.test.ts` suite was not selected; no six-suite pass is claimed.
- Production and all test type lanes passed. The runtime build (`pnpm build qaRuntime`) passed in job 117478871116, including tsdown compilation, CLI bootstrap import checks, plugin assets, runtime postbuild, and stamps. Full release packaging and `published-driver-update` were skipped by CI.

The worker and operation-registry blobs are identical between tested main `45c6db39b27d38c4fec1175194168def4c2cb2a9` and CI merge `2e3f08e2b35a86058076f3e63033494bf2f4909f`.

Its five test files and implicated backup/process owners are unchanged between tested main and the PR merge. PostgreSQL integrations passed. prs.title: fix(android): keep answered question cards in chat history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Android users answering a question would keep seeing the completed card after newer messages, at the latest end of the chat. Continuing the conversation did not move the answered card back into history.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep pending and submitting questions at the live edge, but place completed questions into the transcript by creation time. Insert them before transcript projection groups tool events, so an older tool row cannot drag a completed question out of order. Preserve completed cards when corresponding messages are not loaded.

This changes presentation only: no question-resolution, approval, persistence, or Gateway protocol changes.

## User Impact

Answered questions remain in their original conversational context instead of following the composer. Questions that still need an answer remain reachable and selectable.

## Evidence

### Upstream integration — September 29

Merged upstream `c82063902aa1aee76da2ee1b965bab8643be4b20` into this branch; preserved question history and current upstream tool grouping. Published merge: `3cdd1d479510c5ec5cf61b30957da08d2013f7cc`.

prs.title: fix(agents): warn once when a requester settle wake keeps hitting owner changes
prs.body:
Related: #154252, #154129, #157871, #163195

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a requester settle wake that keeps failing because stored rows disagree about who owns a completion looks, in the Gateway log, exactly like a storage outage. After five failures the Gateway logs `requester settle wake commit still failing; retries continue` with no cause, so an operator cannot tell a persisted owner divergence from a locked or read-only database.

## User Impact

User impact: the existing sustained-failure warning now carries the error that caused it, for example `error={"name":"SubagentRegistryWriteError","message":"...subagent completion owner changed before settlement: run-154252"}`. Retry cadence, the retained wake and the stored row do not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retry episode already reports once at five failures. `deferWakeCommit` now receives the failing error and adds it to that one warning through the existing `buildSafeLifecycleErrorMeta`. Earlier revisions of this PR added a separate owner-changed classifier, counter, module and second warning (+988/-12); this revision replaces that with the error on the existing warning (+29/-2 against main).

## Evidence

Shipped Gateway, built from this branch (`85f443a`, the same production diff as the head after merging main), isolated `HOME` and state directory: `node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port 19642 --bind loopback --auth token --allow-unconfigured`. Seeded state: a requester session for `agent:main:main`, row A (`run-154252`, wake `pending` for the cohort `[run-154252, run-154252-b]`) before boot, and sibling B written to SQLite only after registry restore, so every settle of A is rejected for an owner change. prs.title: fix(media): retry against the original file when Wikimedia rejects a thumbnail width
prs.body:
Closes #119684

## What Problem This Solves

Users asking an agent for a Wikimedia image received **nothing at all — not even the text portion of the reply** — when the agent picked a thumbnail width Wikimedia hasn't pre-rendered for that file. Wikimedia's thumbnail servers only serve a whitelist of widths per file and reject anything else with `HTTP 400 "Use thumbnail sizes listed on ..."`; the media-fetch failure took down the whole reply.

## The Fix

When a media fetch fails with **HTTP 400** and the URL is a rewritable `upload.wikimedia.org` thumbnail URL, retry once against the original (non-thumbnail) file, which Wikimedia always serves:
`.../wikipedia/<project>/thumb/<a>/<b>/<file>/<width>px-<file>` → `.../wikipedia/<project>/<a>/<b>/<file>`.

Key properties (directly addressing the earlier review):

- **Reachable on the real path (was the P1).** The trigger keys off **status + URL shape, not the response body.** The managed-media store path (`saveRemoteMediaForStore`) drains non-OK response bodies (`store.remote.runtime.ts`), so a body-text predicate (`"thumbnail sizes"`) never matched in production — the first revision's fallback was dead exactly where it mattered.
- **Covers both fetch entry points.** The fallback is shared (`withWikimediaOriginalFallback`) across `saveRemoteMedia` (managed-media store write) **and `readRemoteMediaBuffer`** — the path Telegram reply delivery actually uses (`loadWebMedia → readRemoteMediaBuffer`), the exact route the bug report described.
- **Exact host match.** `hostname === "upload.wikimedia.org"` (the previous `endsWith("wikimedia.org")` also accepted `evilwikimedia.org`). The original URL is derived purely from the same file's path, so it can never point at another origin.
- **Rewrites only genuine renditions.** The last path segment must be a `<width>px-<sourcefile>` rendition (contains a `\d+px-` width token and the source filename); an incomplete thumbnail-shaped URL whose tail is not a real rendition is left alone, not rewritten.
- **Safe failure.** If the original file also fails, the **original** error is surfaced — error reporting is unchanged for genuine failures.
- **No new lint suppression.** The logic lives in `src/media/wikimedia.ts` (fallback + URL rewrite) and `src/media/remote-filename.ts` (filename decoders split out of the grandfathered-oversized `fetch.ts` to satisfy the `max-lines` ratchet without a suppression).

## Tests

Unit (`src/media/wikimedia.test.ts`): thumb→original rewrite, non-Wikimedia and `evilwikimedia.org` host rejection, original-error propagation.

Integration (`src/media/fetch.test.ts`), for **both** `saveRemoteMedia` and `readRemoteMediaBuffer`:
- `retries against the original file even when the 400 response body was drained` — mocks a body-less `Response(null, { status: 400 })`, the exact shape the store wrapper produces, proving the fallback fires on the production path.
- `does not rewrite non-upload.wikimedia.org hosts (guards the endsWith overmatch)`.
- `surfaces the original thumbnail error when the original file also fails`.

## Evidence

Real deployment: an agent asked for a dog photo, picked `.../thumb/e/e7/007_American_Pit_Bull_Terrier.jpg/800px-...jpg`, got the 400, and the reply never reached the user.

The drained-body reachability tests are the in-repo proof that the fallback now fires on the production (store + Telegram-reply) paths; a live redacted delivery screenshot would require a running deployment.

## Real Behavior Proof (real transport client over a real socket)

Drove the **real `readRemoteMediaBuffer`** — the path outbound web media / Telegram reply delivery uses (`loadWebMedia → readRemoteMediaBuffer`) — with **no `fetchImpl`, no mocked `globalThis.fetch`, and no runtime-deps override**. Because a pinned dispatcher is attached and nothing is stubbed, `fetch-guard.ts` takes the runtime path (`shouldUseRuntimeFetch === true`) and a **real `undici` client opens a real TCP connection**. The Wikimedia host is DNS-pinned to loopback (`lookupFn → 127.0.0.1`) and the SSRF policy is opened for the private network (`ssrfPolicy: { allowPrivateNetwork: true }`), so the real client connects to a **real local HTTP origin server** standing in for `upload.wikimedia.org`. That server returns a genuine HTTP **400** (with the real `"Use thumbnail sizes listed on ..."` body) for the out-of-whitelist thumbnail width, then a genuine **200 + image bytes** for the original file. The only thing "mocked" is which machine answers — the transport, the request, the status codes, and the bytes are all real.

### Before — fallback removed from the buffer path (the bug)

```
REAL TCP requests received: [ "/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/007_American_Pit_Bull_Terrier.jpg/800px-...jpg" ]
readRemoteMediaBuffer THREW: MediaFetchError code=http_error status=400
  "...HTTP 400 Bad Request; body: Use thumbnail sizes listed on ..."
```

The buffer read aborts — the reply/attachment would be lost.

### After — with the fix

```
REAL TCP requests received by the origin server:
  #1 (thumbnail 400) -> /wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/007_American_Pit_Bull_Terrier.jpg/800px-...jpg
  #2 (original 200)  -> /wikipedia/commons/8/88/007_American_Pit_Bull_Terrier.jpg
readRemoteMediaBuffer resolved: contentType=image/jpeg, bytes=3
PASS: real undici client recovered the original file over a real socket
```

The recovery is driven entirely by the real guard/dispatcher/undici pipeline reacting to a real 400 — no stub can influence which URL is fetched or how the SSRF/redirect logic runs. The store-write path (`saveRemoteMedia`) shares the same fallback and is additionally covered by the drained-body integration tests (the managed store delivers non-OK responses with an empty body, which the status-based predicate handles).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: iOS Safari shows an "AutoFill Contact" button and address suggestions above the keyboard whenever the chat or New Session composer is focused.

## User Impact

User impact: typing into the composer on iPhone no longer offers to fill in contact or address details. The iOS form bar (previous/next arrows and the checkmark) still appears, because web content cannot hide it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Neither composer textarea set `autocomplete`, so Safari treated it as a field it might fill with saved contact data. Both now set `autocomplete="off"`, matching nearly every other text input in the Control UI. `aria-autocomplete="list"` stays as it is; it describes the slash, mention, and emoji menus to assistive technology, and Safari's AutoFill ignores it.

## Evidence

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/pages/chat/chat-composer-autofill.test.ts src/pages/new-session/composer.test.tsx` (from `ui/`): 2 files, 50 tests passed.
- The chat composer regression fails without the source change (`expected null to be 'off'`) and passes with it.
- `pnpm check:changed`: the UI and core-test typechecks, formatting, i18n, and controller guards pass. The line-cap ratchet passes after the chat regression moved to a focused sibling file. The max-lines suppression ratchet still fails on `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts` and the core tsgo boundary on its advisory shard-root budget. This PR does not touch either; both come from current `main`.
- Autoreview (branch mode against `origin/main`): scoped-clean.

**Gap:** this needs an after-screenshot from an iPhone in Safari. That is the only place the AutoFill bar appears, and desktop or emulated browsers cannot reproduce it. The PR stays in draft until that screenshot is added.

prs.title: feat(msteams): expose opt-in private-channel rosters
prs.body:
Related: #175208

## What Problem This Solves

Privacy-sensitive Teams workflows cannot currently observe the complete user roster of a private channel through the native message tool.

## User Impact

Adds opt-in `channel-info` with `includeMembers: true` for private channels only. Metadata-only calls, existing `member-info`, target authorization and account selection are unchanged.

**Draft pending maintainer product/security agreement on the output and permission contract.** This does not grant Microsoft Graph permissions or establish tenant access. Operators must already have the documented channel-member permission; this is not a bypass of the default membership restriction. The result is an observation, not an atomic audience snapshot, delivery authorization, or bot/app-installation evidence.

## Why This Change Was Made

Uses the channel-scoped Graph members endpoint, never the parent-team roster. Successful output includes the user members, explicit completeness, requested team/channel scope, and the start of observation. Unsupported channel types, malformed pages or users, off-resource continuation URLs, denied reads and the 100-page limit fail closed. Existing pagination callers keep their behavior.

The optional schema contribution remains cross-channel-visible so the existing metadata-only action is not accidentally hidden. No manifest, permission, installation or runtime configuration changes are included.

## Evidence

- **Baseline at `14bab05f`: 163 tests passed across seven focused real repository suites** (113 Teams + 50 core discovery), via the official test-project wrapper. Combined wrapper wall time: 71 seconds. This is retained pre-trim evidence, not a fresh all-suite run of the latest head. CI timing is unavailable; broad jobs remain draft-skipped, not passing build evidence.
- **Latest deletion-only trim `09a321c3`: 42/42 focused tests passed** (37 action cases + 5 unchanged real-host authority cases), via the same repository wrapper; wall time 74.792 seconds. Only two redundant mocked roster/denial cases were deleted (43 lines). Metadata-only omission/false coverage remains. Changed-file official-config narrow types, lint, format and whitespace checks passed; independent canonical P0–P2 review found no actionable trim regression. No full build or live tenant run is claimed.
- New source-level integration proof constructs the real admitted host message tool and plugin registry, then follows the native action → Teams runtime → Graph request/guarded transport owners. Only HTTP and DNS I/O is intercepted with synthetic fixtures; no runtime, Graph-request, or authority owner is mocked. It proves denied conversations make no token/Graph request, a denied sibling account cannot reuse a warmed permitted account, real registry retirement after page one prevents page-two dispatch, a synthetic Graph 403 surfaces rather than returning a complete roster, and allowed private pagination reaches the exact endpoint with the selected account/token scope.
- Focused reproduction: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/msteams/src/channel-roster-authority.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Five cases pass. The isolated child run took 53 seconds including worker preparation, with approximately 12 seconds in test bodies during concurrent checks. This exceeds the 5-second target because the requested host/tool/lifecycle boundary is real; replacing that boundary with mocks would remove the authority proof.
- All three changed test files pass a narrowed configuration extending the official extension-test TypeScript configuration (same compiler safety settings/ambient types), the real targeted lint owner, formatter and whitespace checks. A broad extension test typecheck reached its 60-second execution bound; it is not claimed passing. Production-scoped types/lint were verified on the unchanged original implementation.
- Canonical independent P0–P2 review of the follow-up reports scoped-clean after supplying the unchanged registry, admitted host and test-state implementations; the earlier limited-context review is not the final proof. Parent separately inspected the source and executed the tests.
- Reproduced corrupt-roster acceptance and channel-ID mismatch before the original correction; native cross-channel discovery also failed before its visibility repair. The latest change is test-only, not a new production defect fix; no additional pre-fix regression run is claimed.

## Simplification

Removed the redundant mocked includeMembers-presence test; the real core discovery case remains its owner. Folded unexpected-member retention into the existing multi-page result case instead of a second copy. The earlier `14bab05f` follow-up removed 51 lines from the older test structure while adding five production-path cases for the distinct authority-lifetime boundary. The latest trim removes the two further mocked roster-propagation/denied-target cases (43 lines), as requested; the real-host suite already owns both contracts. Production code and permissions are unchanged. The original simplification removed a duplicate helper-test suite and exported assertion wrapper; shared pagination remains the sole traversal owner.

## Separate rollout constraint

Source review of official Teams 2026.10.4 found that introducing the first exact `teams.<team>.channels` map also blocks ordinary groupchats without a team ID. This is existing documented route scoping, not a regression introduced here. No live configuration was changed. A supported exact off-conversation read-target path that preserves existing groupchat handling is still needed; neither wildcard/open policy nor an installed-plugin patch is proposed. Maintainer guidance is requested separately, without changing this PR's authorization behavior.

**Still required before acceptance:** maintainer agreement on the private-roster output and permission contract, plus tenant-qualified behavior evidence through an approved official path. Synthetic 403/pagination evidence is not a real tenant grant/RSC test or a shipped-package reproduction. No app installation, private-channel delivery, deployment, TLS or atomic-snapshot claim is made. No live tenant data, private identifiers, credentials or operator configuration are included. prs.title: chore(tooling): type check with tsrs instead of tsgo
prs.body:
Draft for evaluation only: tsrs reports false-positive errors on five type graphs (see blockers), so CI type lanes are expected to fail.

## What Problem This Solves

Type checking each large OpenClaw graph with tsgo takes 9–17s wall, 64–127s CPU and 9–16 GB of memory on our dev host. This draft measures what switching the repo type checker to tsrs would buy, and what it currently breaks.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Developers and CI type-check lanes (`pnpm tsgo`, every `tsgo:*` script, `run-tsgo-core-test-shards`) would run tsrs on Linux and Apple Silicon, about 4–11x faster in wall time with roughly half the peak memory. Windows and Intel macOS keep running tsgo because tsrs ships no binary for them.

## Why This Change Was Made

`scripts/run-tsgo.mts` is the single owner of type-check execution, so the switch is one resolver change there: it now asks `resolveRepoToolBinPath` for `tsrs` (resolved through the package's own `lib/getExePath.js`, like tsgo) unless the host has no tsrs binary. tsrs takes the same flags the runner already passes (`-p`, `-b`, `--incremental`, `--tsBuildInfoFile`, `--declaration false`, `--singleThreaded`, `--checkers`, `--pretty false`) and prints tsc-format diagnostics, so the CI static-evidence parser and exit-code contract (0 clean, 2 diagnostics) are unchanged.

tsrs is pinned exactly to `0.16.0-ts7.1.0-dev.20260929` (`Version 7.1.0-dev.20260930.4 (tsrs 0.16.0-ts7.1.0-dev.20260929, microsoft/TypeScript@b85298b6a81f)`). It was published 2026-10-16, inside the 7-day `minimumReleaseAge`, so `pnpm-workspace.yaml` gets a time-boxed exclusion for it and its platform packages (remove after 2026-10-23T16:59Z). That dependency-policy exception needs maintainer sign-off.

Kept on tsgo (`typescript@7.1.0-dev.20260928.1`), because these are not the repo type-check lanes:

- declaration emit (tsdown dts, `native-declaration-emitter`, plugin-SDK boundary dts);
- `check-plugin-sdk-exports`, which smoke-checks a consumer against those tsgo-emitted declarations;
- `check-tsgo-core-boundary` file inventories;
- `tsgo:profile`, which relies on Go-only `--pprofDir` (tsrs accepts and ignores the flag).

`@typescript/native-preview` is no longer a direct dependency on main; it only appears as an optional peer of `rolldown-plugin-dts`, so there was nothing there to remove. Script names, `[tsgo]` log prefixes, `ci-static:tsgo` evidence and `.artifacts/tsgo-cache` are unchanged to keep the diff reviewable; renaming them belongs in a follow-up if this lands.

Test fixtures that run `run-tsgo` against a real compiler now also copy tsrs into the fixture install (`materializeTypeChecker`), and `overrideNativeFixtureExecutable` intercepts both native packages.

## Known blockers for un-drafting

1. **False-positive TS5115 in tsrs 0.16.** tsrs reports errors that tsgo does not on five graphs. They are stable across all four runs of each graph. No source files were edited and nothing was suppressed.
   - zod v4 types, `Instantiations of the following types appear infinitely circular: 'IsOptionalIn', '$ZodTypeInternals', '$InferZodRecordInput'`:
     - `extensions/codex/src/app-server/mcp-app-session-preparation.ts:206`: extensions, extensions-test
     - `extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-transcript.ts:26`: extensions, extensions-test, test-root-other
     - `extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-mcp-app.ts:39` (`z.record(z.string(), z.json())`): extensions-test
   - postcss-selector-parser types, `... infinitely circular: 'Container', 'Diff'`:
     - `scripts/audit-control-ui-dead-css.mts:430`: scripts, test-root-scripts
     - `scripts/lib/control-ui-icon-grid-fit.mts:211`: test-root-scripts
     - `scripts/lib/control-ui-icon-grid-fit.mts:92`: TS7006 `Parameter 'part' implicitly has an 'any' type`, a knock-on of the same failed instantiation (scripts)
   - The reported site depends on the graph, so this looks like checker-order-dependent circularity detection in tsrs.
2. **Platform coverage.** tsrs publishes binaries only for darwin-arm64 and linux x64/arm64 (gnu and musl). Windows and Intel macOS fall back to tsgo, so diagnostics can differ across platforms until tsrs ships those targets. The fallback is unit-tested, but I have not run it on a Windows or Intel Mac host.
3. **0.x compiler** with a release-age exception (above).

## Evidence

Host: shared 128-core / 187 GiB Linux box (team-metal), base `origin/main` f20ce151e4a, Kysely types generated first (`node scripts/generate-kysely-types.mts`). prs.title: refactor(status): keep report assembly with command owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Status commands build large private transfer objects solely to pass their existing facts into one report renderer. Those extra modules and exports split one command operation across redundant internal interfaces.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior or migration is intended. Status output, section order, diagnostics, lazy imports, read-only probes, database engine facts, and startup/recovery guidance stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the status report data assembly in its existing report owner and keep status-all assembly/rendering in its existing command owner. Remove the three superseded private report-data/report-lines modules, redundant result projections, and their exact obsolete mock-inventory entries. Migrate existing assertions from private transfer objects to the rendered report or the actual status-all command. Preserve the maintained database engine resolver added on main rather than replacing it with inferred configuration facts.

This is a status area slice of the whole-tree single-consumer family, split under the campaign's wide-family rule. At f06d2ddcc4e28b520c55e31e8687bbc68cdc3acc against bbb775bd011b435f51a0d0ee2df2b51285f16761, the production delta is +411/-509, **98 net lines removed**, across seven production paths. The complete change touches 14 paths. Moved implementations count as additions, not deleted behavior.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None. No guard or supported behavior is removed. Partial-report recovery, diagnosis ordering, Gateway budgets, provider usage isolation, SQLite diagnostics, backup freshness, authorization and read-only behavior remain. No schema, protocol, public SDK, configuration key, dependency, or protected standalone session-memory backend change.

## Evidence

Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the assembled replay is scoped-clean (0.94). Source inspection confirms the existing asynchronous fact resolution, lazy text-runtime boundary, section ordering, failure reporting and main's admitted database-engine resolver remain. Canonical formatting and diff checks pass through the normal signed commit path. Existing assertions now enter the real report/command boundaries without a replacement test-only export.

The isolated one-worker focused selection passed **5 files / 30 tests**, covering status-all diagnostics/rendering, status report data/rendering, cold-import isolation, and the unchanged database-engine owner. Vitest duration: 923.27 seconds, dominated by transformation/import preparation under shared host load; the complete wrapper exited successfully in 1,088.9 seconds after generation verification and cleanup. No full local suite, product build, broad typecheck, E2E, or live operator-state access is claimed. Exact-head hosted CI will be the broad gate. No timeout, retry, skip, assertion or allowance is weakened.

The first exact-head hosted run 39038032989 on f06d2ddcc4e28b520c55e31e8687bbc68cdc3acc completed with two failing leaves and the consequential aggregate. check-lint-core-1 /117412271574 reported one PR-caused no-import-type-side-effects error: status-all had changed the RuntimeEnv import from a top-level type import to an inline type specifier. Signed repair e23b90afc676e648ef49a17447286ca397a273f5 restores the original form, without any other source change. Fresh independent P0-P2 review is scoped-clean (0.99); syntax lint, matching formatter, diff checks, normal commit hooks and signature verification pass. Current-head hosted CI remains required.

checks-node-changed-compact-large-8-2 /117412041050 timed out the unchanged server.sessions.preview-resolve.test.ts case “lists and previews the selected aggregate global owner over WebSocket.” This is an inherited fixture deadlock: the test awaited demand-driven transcript enrichment without first requesting details. Main's b7f945c105b2414df10a2036c34bd2358c70ea57 (#175564) fixes this exact case by making the initial sessions.list detail request before awaiting backfilled.promise. The test blob is identical between this PR base and head; none of this PR's status command/report files is called by that Gateway fixture. The lead inspected the exact repair. New CI merge context will include main's repair; no test, timeout or unrelated production path is changed here, and no inherited-red landing exception is claimed in advance.

The isolated one-worker pre-push suppression selection on e23b90afc676e648ef49a17447286ca397a273f5 completed four passing cases and one failure (39.58 seconds Vitest, 66.1 seconds wrapper). Its old inline allowlist expects preserve-caught-error count 1 in backup-restore.ts but observes 2, and omits the existing native-bridge require-post-message-target-origin directive. Both source blobs and the suppression test are byte-identical between this branch's base and head; this PR adds no suppression directive. Git enumeration passes (16.811 seconds). This is an investigated, unmodified-baseline local failure, not a passing suite or a current-head CI exception. The assertions/allowlist remain unchanged; fresh hosted merge-context CI must cover the guard.

Completed exact repaired-head hosted CI run 39039368242 is successful, and its exact-head watcher completed GREEN with zero pending proof checks. The original lint error is repaired and the inherited preview fixture timeout does not fail the new merge-context run. No CI rerun, synthetic code push or inherited-red landing exception is used. The separate investigated local suppression failure remains a failure in the native review record; hosted success is not claimed as its repair.

prs.title: improve(llm-task): constrain Codex output with task schemas
prs.body:
Closes #137432

## What Problem This Solves

Schema-backed `llm-task` automations can fail local validation because isolated
Codex generation never receives the schema as a native constraint.

## User Impact

Codex can constrain task results during generation; local JSON validation
remains authoritative. An explicit native-schema rejection permits one fresh
prompt-constrained retry on the same route within the original timeout, which
can add inference usage and latency.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward optional advisory `outputSchema` through the existing isolated-completion
contract. The host retains the 1 KiB context bound and passes the schema by
reference under the plugin value contract; callers must not mutate it after
handoff. Calls without schemas and owners that ignore the optional field keep
their existing generation behavior. Codex retains tool isolation.

Maintainer acceptance is still needed for the public SDK field and bounded
retry semantics.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto `2aee2fa5be6`, preserving upstream's retirement of startup-selection
  retries. A merge simulation against `38f456226f6` succeeds without conflicts.
- [ClawSweeper's current-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/137450#issuecomment-5529756123)
  found no actionable defects and confirmed the reference-ownership repair.
- 211 focused tests across nine files passed in 102.25s, covering task dispatch,
  native schemas, rejection fallback, input validation and passive finalization.
  Production/test types, changed-file typed lint and formatting pass.
- Production build completes; unchanged Control UI code exceeds its startup-JS
  budget. The broad local changed gate stops on unused exports also reproduced
  on the untouched pinned base, with no head-only findings.
- Historical macOS Codex 0.159.2 live app-server proof returned `LIVE_SCHEMA_OK`
  and `LIVE_FALLBACK_OK`. This is prior-head evidence.

[Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38138616186)
on `064ebf5b955f` passed build, lint and type lanes but failed two jobs:

- Native steering has a shared transcript queue deadlock tracked in
  [issue #169105](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/169105).
  [Existing repair #168830](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168830)
  gives source preparation a nested settled read queue; its head CI gate
  succeeds, but it remains unmerged. We independently reproduced the exact
  CI merge `3ea967210951` on Linux. An equivalent local repair passes the
  original 137-test Linux shard on Node24.19, both macOS steering tests and
  26 source/read tests. That proof covers the deadlock repair, not every
  change in #168830. This PR awaits the upstream repair and affected CI.
- The scan coverage guard omits upstream's `worker-heap-flag.mjs`.
  [Upstream's one-line fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/cd6509510b12d996c60e9dcaeb700539554d436e)
  passes the full guard locally against the failing CI base.

CI is not green.

prs.title: fix(ios): allow sending messages during active replies
prs.body:
Closes #150695 ## What Problem This Solves The native iOS app disables Send while a response is running, so users cannot submit a follow-up or `/steer` until it finishes. ## User Impact Text messages remain sendable during a response. Tap preserves the Gateway default; hold offers the opposite action when the default is Queue or Steer. The current response stays in place, and the existing delivery footer shows the explicitly chosen action. Attachments and local reset/compact commands still wait. ## Why This Change Was Made Reuse the existing durable outbox and native context menu. Capture the choice per message so reconnects preserve it without changing session settings. Other or unreported Gateway defaults retain both explicit choices. **Design review needed:** this includes the additive native client-state outbox v10 migration. Existing rows keep the Gateway default; older clients are prevented from replaying an explicit choice as an ordinary send. The Gateway schema is unchanged. Maintainer acceptance of the native schema/upgrade design is pending and required before merge. ## Evidence - Released-source app upgrade: `v2026.9.8` (`fc23bc864e4`, public app version `2026.9.80`) to reviewed head `6f96a96d74d1` passes. The installed candidate performs v10 itself; existing queued text/image, cache, routes, settings expectations and nine checked preferences survive. Both messages replay through the real native transport with the exact image bytes and Gateway-default mode; retry/reopen passes on a copy of the upgraded app state. Details below. - At behavior head `6f96a96d74d1`, 215 native Swift tests in 9 suites passed, covering busy sends, active stream ownership, replay and upgrade safety. The broader view-model selection also passed (537 tests; overlapping counts), as did 20 typography tests. - At `7f2ad38f95a1`, 134 focused native tests pass (116 Swift Testing + 18 XCTest), including preservation of explicit intent when a transport cannot support it. The full iOS simulator app, extensions, Watch companion and UI runner build passes. SwiftFormat, Apple source lint, native source inventory verification and the native schema guard pass. No dependency or generated locale changes. - Actual native simulator flow: five `chat.send` requests with modes default/default/default/steer/followup; live default refresh changes the one-item menu; no session-setting writes; response frame remains stable; history confirmation removes temporary badges. - Independent review of the behavior patch and the contributor-check repair found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The repair review used `gpt-6-sol` with `xhigh` reasoning. The repair removes unused transport adapters, migrates test fixtures and updates the extracted native source inventory; UI, storage and production transport behavior are unchanged, so the upgrade and UI evidence at `6f96a96d74d1` remains applicable. - Scoped app/doc checks were exercised. Two local macOS runner environment-equality failures in `macos-native-test-launch.test.ts` also reproduce on clean upstream base `123d5a1331a` (fresh cleanup-parent nonce); they are not reported as passing. Full core build/check/test was not run for this native-only change. Selected [hosted CI lanes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38097133994) and [shared OpenClawKit dead-code checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38097133812) pass on `7f2ad38f95a1`.
Published-source upgrade and data compatibility proof The source-built Debug app comes from the published `v2026.9.8` tag. The pending text and PNG are captured by that version's actual native store APIs in the task app's data directory. Both are visible in the released app before upgrade. The paired app is upgraded in place; onboarding and preferences are retained. The installed candidate's source stamp matches the reviewed head, and its committed v10 marker is observed read-only before the verification harness opens the store. Redacted native execution output: ```text released source: fc23bc864e4553c2d215e479eeec47b67a0bf943 reviewed candidate: 6f96a96d74d168008bcc481e9ca2becae06cf15d released busy-send regression: XCTAssertTrue failed — An active response must allow the next text message (expected pre-fix failure) released offline UI: cached reply + queued text + queued image visible; PASS candidate offline UI: same content visible; PASS (13.31s execution) app-owned v10 migration: absent before upgrade, present before observer; PASS queued messages: 2 retained; explicit queueMode remains nil presentation/delivery: main / agent:main:main retained routing and permission/tool settings expectations: unchanged existing app preferences: 9 checked, unchanged; no onboarding reset image: 68 bytes retained; SHA256 9650eb2ef8b938a5e48e539632fc0cd31216d1f910d85f3855ccb9570c7d97e8 reconnect: 2 real native chat.send requests; exact texts and image bytes wire queue mode: Gateway default / Gateway default; session-setting writes: 0 upgraded-state copy: FIFO claim, fail, reopen, retry, reopen; both messages PASS ``` This exercises source-built native iOS apps, SQLite and real client transport with a synthetic Gateway. It does not run Apple's distributed App Store binary or a provider. Cached replies may be replaced normally by live canonical history after reconnect. No production state or product-source changes were made for this proof.
The UI flow uses a controlled loopback Gateway and synthetic chat/model data. It verifies the real native app, transport and SQLite boundary; it does not execute a provider or establish unchanged backend queue/steer semantics. Real native iPhone simulator screenshots with synthetic chat/model data.
