prs.title: perf(sessions): reuse resident facts for durable turn preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Durable turn preparation rereads the runtime-window key, qualified entry, transcript version/cold presence, and pending input even when the serialized execution worker already owns those committed facts.

## User Impact and Design

Reuse those facts inside the existing worker-resident actor and its write-receipt lifecycle. Eligible warm SQLite preparation falls from **5 to 1 SQL statement**, reducing the measured warmed turn from **61 to 57 statements (6.6%)**. Requests remain 16 and warmed MAIN statements remain zero.

Missing, evicted, moved, cold, unsupported, or incomplete resident state uses the existing canonical readers. The memory-only MAIN helper is unchanged; no full history is sent to MAIN. PostgreSQL keeps the unchanged canonical preparation path. There is no SQL-shape, schema, retention, SDK, or public-contract change, and no second owner, registry, generation, or handshake.

The canonical idempotency lookup remains because the bounded 512-event window cannot prove absence of an older identity. Source validation, pending-input custody, and live write authority remain at the existing effect boundaries.

Removed ordinary reads and accepted edges:

- Runtime-window key reread: reuse the actor-owned exact window; eviction, key movement, or receipt invalidation falls back to canonical selection.
- Qualified-entry reread: reuse the exact committed actor entry; reset/rebinding invalidates eligibility rather than reading again on every warm turn.
- Transcript version/cold-presence reread: trust committed actor facts; cold archives or unavailable facts retain canonical readers, and unsupported external writes remain subject to exclusive offline custody.
- Exact pending-input reread: use the complete resident pending map; rollback preserves its preimage, while custody still controls promotion. No history-window absence inference is introduced.

## Measurement

Unmodified harness v3, **M,C,M,C,M,C**, ten warmed turns per arm (30 per revision), five-second settling, 300-second connected idle, and full restart. Base `ec36f9b9617a8d668a660d97e262a861453d9246`; candidate `bea03535036b66ff8e8b6eb5f560c2f8db44ee5b`. Same Node 24.22.0 / SQLite 3.54.0 runtime and harness hashes. All six runs and final attribution validation pass. Counts are load-independent; no latency claim.

Values are **SQL / requests / MAIN**, each median [min–max]. Warm pooled rows include all 30 turns; arm-median rows summarize the three run medians.

| Measurement | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Warm causal, pooled | 61 [61–63] / 16 [16–18] / 0 [0–0] | 57 [57–59] / 16 [16–18] / 0 [0–0] |
| Warm causal, arm medians | 61 [61–61] / 16 [16–16] / 0 [0–0] | 57 [57–57] / 16 [16–16] / 0 [0–0] |
| Warm raw, pooled | 62 [61–99] / 16 [16–30] / 0 [0–0] | 57 [57–61] / 16 [16–20] / 0 [0–0] |
| Warm raw, arm medians | 61.5 [61.5–62] / 16 [16–16] / 0 [0–0] | 57 [57–58] / 16 [16–16] / 0 [0–0] |
| First turn, causal | 173 [173–173] / 54 [54–54] / 0 [0–0] | 169 [169–169] / 54 [54–54] / 0 [0–0] |
| First turn, raw | 343 [341–462] / 110 [106–111] / 0 [0–0] | 319 [316–337] / 107 [104–110] / 0 [0–0] |
| Restart first turn, causal | 136 [136–140] / 43 [43–43] / 0 [0–0] | 132 [132–132] / 43 [43–43] / 0 [0–0] |
| Restart first turn, raw | 222 [222–226] / 67 [67–67] / 0 [0–0] | 184 [184–220] / 66 [64–69] / 0 [0–0] |
| Boot + connect + first turn, raw | 923 [879–925] / 228 [216–229] / 59 [59–59] | 916 [913–920] / 227 [227–229] / 59 [59–59] |
| Restart boot + connect + first turn, raw | 602 [602–606] / 191 [191–191] / 56 [56–56] | 564 [564–600] / 190 [190–193] / 56 [56–56] |
| Whole workload, causal | 1370 [1370–1374] / 376 [376–376] / 0 [0–0] | 1314 [1314–1314] / 376 [376–376] / 0 [0–0] |
| Whole workload, raw | 3462 [3454–3472] / 896 [894–897] / 129 [129–129] | 3375 [3370–3402] / 896 [895–897] / 129 [129–129] |

Every eligible warm `session.turn.prepare` is **5 [5–5] / 1 [1–1] / 0 → 1 [1–1] / 1 [1–1] / 0**: exactly four statements removed with no request displacement. Causal whole-workload requests are 376 in every run. Raw background timing redistributes a few requests (2,687 total across baseline runs versus 2,688 candidate); medians remain 896, raw statements fall in all three pairs, and no changed-owner operation adds work. First-turn, restart-first-turn, and warmed medians do not regress.

Shared warm read-family SQL per turn (medians, ranges, and means are identical within each side):

| Family | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact-entry facts | 0 [0–0]; mean 0 | 0 [0–0]; mean 0 |
| Actor hydration | 0 [0–0]; mean 0 | 0 [0–0]; mean 0 |
| Entry-cache snapshots | 0 [0–0]; mean 0 | 0 [0–0]; mean 0 |
| Row facts | 1 [1–1]; mean 1 | 0 [0–0]; mean 0 |
| Watermark reads | 1 [1–1]; mean 1 | 0 [0–0]; mean 0 |

## T1 Inventory

| Scope | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Worker preparation path T1 | 0 | 0 |
| Shared pending-input kernel T1 | 7 | 7 |
| Shared pending-input kernel T3 | 1 | 1 |
| Repository T1 | 181 | 181 |
| Repository T1-compat | 10 | 10 |

The preparation path remains worker-only. The shared pending-input helper also serves existing synchronous SDK/native completion/read/consume callers outside this cutover; their seven T1 call expressions remain unchanged. Static inventory counts are distinct from measured MAIN statements. The whole-workload rows include unchanged MAIN work outside the turn phases.

## Proof and Review

All nine focused native regressions pass: committed pending/lifecycle writes; native entry/transcript writes followed by preparation; actor transcript commits; rollback; session reset/key movement; eviction/restart fallback; unauthorized custody; and idempotent retries beyond 512 events. The resident preparation fixture asserts the one remaining canonical identity SELECT.

Changed-file type-aware oxlint, formatting, and diff checks pass. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39058778984) passes selected tests, production/test types, lint, export-name collisions/source contracts, storage boundaries, Madge, and database-worker/dialect ratchets. The candidate Knip export scan has **zero new findings**: eight production and eight full-tree export findings exactly match the [exact-base main scan](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39058564617/job/117471751841); the script export scan is clean. These inherited findings are outside the changed files. SDK API diff and published-driver update cell are inapplicable.

The sole behavioral CI failure is inherited: `port-command.postgres.test.ts`, “probes real privileges, refuses occupied/wrong-owner/RLS sources, and resumes verified staging,” times out at 60 seconds on both this head ([candidate job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39058778984/job/117472557589), 60021 ms) and exact-base main ([main job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39058564617/job/117471751210), 60026 ms). This records inheritance, not a diagnosed timeout cause; no retry was used to chase green. Landing uses the authorized inherited-failure exception.

Independent Codex autoreview is scoped-clean at P0–P2 (one round). Completed automated PR reviews identify no actionable defect; the previously pending Gateway measurement evidence is supplied above.

Production: **+52/−21 (net +31)**; tests/support: +232; docs: +7; seven files. The added production code carries existing owner facts into preparation and removes the redundant warm reads.

prs.title: refactor(test): remove dead Startup inventory fixture branches
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165743

## What Problem This Solves

Windows Startup inventory tests still contain unreachable fixture branches left behind when their case tables were reduced.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. All 16 existing cases and their reachable assertions remain; production code is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace four single-row tables with direct cases, remove their unused alternatives, and remove a repeated directory-error condition. Keep real cmd/VBS parsing, profile precedence, exact process ownership, Doctor reporting, abort settlement, shared deadlines, and malformed or inaccessible discovery coverage.

This maintainer-requested test audit removes 29 net test lines without removing a case or changing production guards.

## Evidence

- Baseline and candidate: all 16 cases pass with `FORCE_COLOR=0 NO_COLOR=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/inspect.startup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Targeted type-aware lint: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/daemon/inspect.startup.test.ts` passes.
- Formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent P2 review: no actionable findings; reachable setup and assertions preserved.
- Local proof uses the existing simulated Windows boundaries, not a live Windows service installation. Broad proof is delegated to PR CI.

prs.title: test(control-ui): reproduce Team boot queries and warm snapshots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Team-scale cold-load fixture answered different `sessions.list` queries with the same oversized rows, omitted the paginated cron workload, and did not reliably retain the Online view across reloads. These differences hid work observed during a signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link.

Use one parameter-driven session inventory for all bench requests, with canonical ordering, requested filters/pagination, owner-first rows/counts, and bounded row projections. Add 120 valid cron jobs (three compact pages of 50/50/20) and seven activating plugins. Before every measured reload, restore the original persisted sidebar and trimmed v8 chat snapshot. Replay follows app unload and preserves the HTTP cache; the Online browser regression waits for its committed snapshot.

This supersedes #175190 with the retained fixture fixes. It drops the bespoke fidelity reporter and its tests; L119's existing `--cpu-profile` and `--cpu-profile-compare` remain the sole profiler/comparison path. No application code, Gateway schema, configuration option, or durable server record changes.

## Evidence

The supplied r149 board reference has five distinct session-list queries, three compact cron pages, and seven plugin activations. The revised gate compares those known counts (±1) and verifies that actual sidebar/chat snapshot restoration appears in the existing CPU profile. No cross-revision function-share threshold or speedup claim.

Validation on AWS Crabbox `cbx_1a3227209604`, fixed `c7a.4xlarge`, exact head below ([run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_c61e41f3b7372418f6eb9b124cc09cd5)):

| Focused file (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`) | Result | Wall time |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `src/gateway/session-list-retention-scale.test.ts` | 1 passed | 47.06 s |
| `ui/src/test-helpers/control-ui-e2e.mock-gateway.test.ts` | 10 passed | 3.78 s |
| `ui/src/test-helpers/control-ui-team-scale-fixture.test.ts` | 5 passed | 2.92 s |
| `ui/src/lib/sessions/sidebar-list-churn.test.ts` | 1 passed | 3.35 s |
| `ui/src/e2e/team-scale-cold-load.e2e.test.ts` | 1 passed | 55.34 s including build |

Both targeted lint groups and all three targeted typechecks passed. Independent P0–P2 review is clean. Exact-head GitHub CI is green: [run 39050827804](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39050827804). Focused regressions cover all five query shapes, independent pagination/filtering, bounded enrichment, canonical ordering, valid cron definitions and paging, seven activation reports, and Online/snapshot persistence through reload.

### Fidelity gate

Seven profiled board reloads on the fixed AWS instance all match the complete r149 reference counts:

| Method | Live reference | Each of 7 board reloads |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `sessions.list` | 5 | 5 |
| `cron.list` | 3 | 3 |
| `plugins.controlUi.report` | 7 | 7, all `activated` |

Every measured reload starts from the same 80-message v8 chat snapshot (projection v3) and persisted 120-person sidebar. The probe records an IndexedDB snapshot hit and cached-transcript paint in all seven runs. Existing `--cpu-profile` output samples `restoreSnapshotSession` in 7/7 runs, `restoreSidebarSnapshot` in 1/7, `applyChatCacheSnapshot` in 4/7, and `readStoredChatSnapshotRecord` in 2/7. These are actual restore/read paths; short sampled functions need not appear in every run. The Online reload also preserves the selected view and all 120 people (4 session lists, 3 cron pages, 7 activated plugins). No function-share threshold or timing/speedup claim.

</details>

### Full UI suite and broader checks

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts` completed once on this head: **820 files passed, 3 failed, 1 skipped; 3,571 cases passed, 1 failed, 5 skipped**, wall time **5,456.47 s**. Two suites could not start because the lease lacked WebKit. After installing the matching browser, focused replays passed: `tooltip-first-activation.e2e.test.ts` 2/2 (23.86 s), `workboard-native-bundle.e2e.test.ts` 2/2 (30.25 s). No full-suite replay was used to chase green.

The remaining QA-lab case (`control-ui-automation-management.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`, configured owners/admin management) fails with `Private mutation boundary is writable by another POSIX principal.` The identical test file (same Git blob on both revisions) reproduces the same error on pinned main `bebee58450d179e806e4e1e85074444c391de2bf`, using its own frozen dependency install and matching build. No filesystem protection was relaxed.

`node scripts/check-changed.mjs` completed in 2,059.43 s. Changed-file formatting/lint, UI types, scripts types, controller/API guards, and script unused-export scan passed. Four broader gates fail identically on that pinned main baseline:

| Gate | Matching baseline evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Max-lines suppression ratchet | Same three untouched files: `chat-message.test.tsx`, `config-page-state.ts`, `sessions-page-state.ts` |
| Core graph boundary | Same pre-existing root counts: gateway-root 728 and infra 736, over 720 |
| UI chat test typecheck | Same three undefined snapshot-store constants in `session-snapshot-store.test.ts` |
| Production/full-tree unused exports | Same eight production exports and three test-support exports; scripts scan clean |

The snapshot-store unit file also reproduces its undefined-constant failure on pinned main (31 passed, 1 failed). These failures are outside this diff; exact-head GitHub CI is green. Local proof retains each failed command, exit code, baseline comparison, and the complete CPU/bench summaries.

## Size and ownership

Head: `9159fd1e18512b4781d4abcc3c593375fb162f04`. The campaign non-test diff filter reports 586 additions and 236 deletions: **+350 tooling lines**. Application runtime delta: **0**. Growth belongs to the query/inventory and warm-state fixture owners; frozen query responses and the custom report are removed.

The campaign lead owns landing. Do not merge automatically.

prs.title: refactor(ai): prepare continuation requests before claiming cache slots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

HTTP continuation preparation installs a cache claim before synchronously restoring and resolving a request, then catches failures solely to remove that claim and rethrow. Preparing first makes failure naturally non-admitting and removes the compensating catch.

## User Impact

Normal requests, overlapping calls, visible preparation errors and full-history recovery retain their behavior. Runtime/session/credential identity, tool/history/reasoning eligibility, cache bounds, cleanup, current dispatch authority and accepted-work settlement remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepare the restored, full and wire requests before publishing the claimed slot. The returned handle is still installed before any actual awaited dispatch. Remove only the synthetic synchronous-reentry exclusivity test; retain main's consolidated fixtures and the real SDK serialization-recovery regression instead of adding duplicate proof.

This is a coherent owner slice from an unfinished >80-file proposal, separated for precise attribution. **5 net production lines removed** (+44/-49, mostly return-body dedenting), plus **23 net test lines removed**. No new helper, owner, import edge, public SDK export, config, schema, protocol or dependency change. Phase E session-memory code and tests are untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- A custom getter/toJSON or injected restore callback that synchronously reenters claim/cleanup during preparation may replace or lose an optional metadata baseline. The extra exclusivity/replacement assertion in #137630/0771b291 is synthetic, not a cited human actual-use incident. A later normal request sends full history. The original ordinary preparation-failure recovery remains fixed; no dispatched result, transcript or accepted paid-work state is removed.

## Evidence

- Fresh complete two-file independent review with full owner/client/lifecycle/SDK context: scoped-clean P0–P2 (0.98), final source verification. Root and sparse review mirror blobs match exactly.
- Full owner and retention suites: 42 tests passed, 95.89 seconds Vitest / 128.12 seconds wrapper. Preserve ordinary overlap, runtime/credential isolation, tool IDs/history/reasoning, size/count/idle bounds and actual completed-caller collection.
- Existing real SDK recovery table: both SSE and cached-WebSocket routes passed, 122.12 seconds Vitest / 181.10 seconds wrapper. Checks visible serialization error without an extra physical send, next full history, then resumed continuation at exactly three physical requests. Fourteen unrelated cases were name-filtered; no test skip/retry/timeout was added. No paid provider was called.
- Two-file formatting (72 ms), fail-fast boundary lint, native syntax and whitespace passed. Imports are unchanged, so no new cycle can be introduced; no broad local build/cycle suite was run.
- Targeted owner/client typecheck attempted: exit 2, 36 unchanged missing parse5/split-MCP declaration and related implicit-any diagnostics; none names changed production. This is a local dependency qualification gap, not a type pass. Shared installs were not modified.
- Mandatory suppression check: 14 tests passed, 155.08 seconds Vitest / 207.42 seconds wrapper; no suppression or baseline edit.
- Earlier packet baseline/head results remain prior scoped evidence, not relabeled as current CI, live, billing, performance, Bun or OS proof. Exact-head PR CI supplies broad qualified type/build/consumer coverage.

Release-note context: simplify Responses continuation preparation without changing ordinary recovery or dispatch semantics.

All164 check runs accounted:66 successful,95 skipped, one neutral CodeQL and two failures; no cancelled or unfinished check remains. ## What Problem This Solves

Automatic ChatGPT Responses transport fallback retains up to eight complete credential/header authorities per session merely to decide whether to retry a failed WebSocket endpoint. Actual authenticated socket reuse already has a separate full-authority owner.

Auto sessions remember their last failed WebSocket URL and continue using current credentials for SSE. Explicit WebSocket modes, endpoint changes, session cleanup and restart can still probe WebSocket. Actual authenticated connection reuse, concurrent ownership, cancellation and request dispatch retain their existing checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the fallback authority history and its three helpers with a runtime-local session-to-URL map. Keep the real socket authority comparison and public runtime-host foundation. Narrow the existing real HTTP/WebSocket test to runtime isolation and current SSE credentials; retain its cleanup, bounded payloads and all other transport tests.

- A WebSocket endpoint that starts working solely after token/custom-header rotation is not automatically reprobed for that session. Introducing #158901 covers this with a synthetic loopback capability switch, not a cited human deployment incident. Freshly authenticated SSE still runs and can fail visibly; explicit WebSocket, cleanup or restart can retry.
- Alternating between failed endpoints remembers only the most recent URL, so returning to an older failed endpoint can make another upgrade attempt. The removed eight-authority eviction history was a synthetic policy test, not a user-data/security requirement. Existing fallback/error handling applies.

The memo is written before SSE succeeds. The existing first-mapped-event fallback policy is unchanged; a WebSocket request may already have been dispatched at that point. ## What Problem This Solves

Chat panes still relied on a pane-wide redraw callback after their domain owners moved to Solid projections.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the generic pane revision signal and page/controller redraw callbacks. Pane inputs, attachments, approval errors, configuration, and visibility now publish through their owners. `updateComplete` observes pending DOM work; `awaitDomCommit()` supports focus and geometry tasks without forcing an unchanged pane to render. Hidden panes keep their content, flush queued stream publication, and settle DOM tasks on reveal or disposal.

Queued edits publish custody independently of rendering, so parked panes remain protected from eviction. Durable recovery explicitly resumes the existing persistence owner. Equivalent frame subscriptions use the existing source list, retaining every owner and its revision semantics. Ordinary typing stays composer-local; attachment changes and entering or leaving a control command update the relevant pane presentation.

This is an atomic 69-file cutover: 32 production TypeScript files, 36 directly coupled test/support files, and the reactive README. Removing the shared callback contract requires real native fixture facades to change with its callers. Genuine transcript/detail-panel DOM lifecycles remain.

## Evidence

Compared with base `b326dc0201221366ed905f632f210ca78e6d1b13` on the same Mac:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| UI and UI-chat test type graphs | Pass on final source |
| Scoped lint, formatting, whitespace, assertion-safety ratchet | Pass |
| Full bridge and frame-cadence files | 17 tests pass, including hidden completion, attachment updates, and ordinary typing |
| Original CI unit regressions | All 17 exact failing cases pass after owner/fixture repairs; assertions preserved |
| Delayed recovery readiness | Real-pane empty-history regression fails before the owner sync, then all 20 connection tests pass |
| Inventory-only desktop discovery | Visible, settled pane regression fails before existing-owner reconciliation and passes after; all 20 lifecycle tests pass |
| Private-draft reload | Exact E2E passes on final build; the assertion awaits the identical restored text with the existing timeout |
| Independent isolated review through P2 | Complete final repair review; no actionable findings |
| Production Knip | Same base/head finding: unused `@modelcontextprotocol/client` |
| Base/final UI builds | Pass |
| Strict startup performance | Both exceed existing 339,379-byte ceiling; 340,000 → 340,012 bytes, identical 1,031,995 raw bytes, 7 JS requests and 1 CSS request unchanged |
| Chat boot performance | 1,489,702 → 1,489,928 bytes (+226); 25 requests unchanged, 72 bytes below unchanged 1,490,000-byte ceiling |
| Synthetic dashboard and reset dialog | Final before/after inspected; no page errors |
| Replacement full UI/E2E/Gateway CI | [39059794890](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39059794890): all selected jobs passed except one inherited automation case and the aggregate gate; exact name/assertion also fail on completed scheduled main [39058564617](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39058564617) |

Initial full CI [39053307519](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39053307519) exposed missing owner dependencies for comments, approval errors, applied MCP configuration, and hidden progress, plus fixtures connecting before initial setup. Those are repaired. None of its 17 failing unit names matched the latest completed scheduled main run. The initial auto request was explicitly retired before replacing its head.

Replacement run [39055159978](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39055159978) exposed one private-draft reload assertion that read immediately at textarea mount. An instrumented local replay proved the unchanged saved text was adopted asynchronously; the test now waits for that same exact value. A separate empty-history regression proved that late recovery readiness also needs an explicit persistence wakeup, now invoked at the existing recovery-ready connection edge before outboxes resume.

The following full run [39056640132](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39056640132) passed every unit, E2E, and real-Gateway shard but exposed a 39-byte chat boot overage in the actual merged source. Current `main` was merged normally, then ten equivalent frame subscriptions were consolidated into the existing source list. The final same-host base/head comparison includes that main context; no budget changed. The separate project-catalog read remains intact because it also synchronizes its connection.

Run [39058193020](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39058193020) passed performance, all UI unit and browser E2E shards, and real-Gateway 1/2. Real-Gateway 2/2 failed only `configured owners and admin chat manage a Telegram-created job while a non-owner cannot`: the mock provider observed automation tool availability for its non-owner sender before the browser portion. The final replacement run repeated exactly this single failure. Completed scheduled main [39058564617](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39058564617) fails the identical full test name and assertion at line 350: `provider.toolAvailability.get(nonOwnerMarker)` expects `false`, receives `true`. The earlier scheduled run passed; the current matching failure is independently established. Landing uses the documented inherited-failure exception for this case and its aggregate only; no assertion is weakened.

The final review also reproduced an inventory-only discovery stall in an idle visible pane: clearing the cache did not resume the resource read. The handler now invokes the existing observation-reconciliation owner, which revalidates assignment and resumes discovery with its existing lifecycle guards. The regression uses the real `nodeId` payload after deferred startup frames settle; an independent isolated P2 review accepted the repair.

The base/head builds use the repository’s `COMPARISON_BUILD_ENV` from `scripts/check-control-ui-performance-base.mts` to hold build metadata constant, with unchanged production budgets.

The final CI proof includes `chat-composer-input-measurement.e2e` (zero transcript `scrollHeight` reads across ten native keys), `chat-transcript-message-index` (bounded stream-only work across history sizes), `chat-transcript-invalidation` (settled-run idle and row identity cases), and the chat retention suites. The final UI unit, browser E2E, performance, retention, and real-Gateway 1/2 jobs passed. Real-Gateway 2/2 has only the inherited automation assertion described above. No performance budget changed. The final byte figures above supersede the earlier candidate measurements.

Production LOC: **12,652 → 12,584 (-68)**. Test/support LOC: **19,690 → 19,959 (+269)**. Across touched production files: `.subscribe(` **14 → 14**, `createEffect(` **2 → 2**, `createRenderEffect(` **1 → 1**, `untrack(` **2 → 2**, `createSignal(` **2 → 2**. `requestUpdate` identifiers **25 → 0** and pane `this.invalidate()` calls **36 → 0**; no redraw aliases remain in `ui/src`.

The test growth protects optional first inputs, hidden/reveal completion, draft/queue custody, native context transport, attachment publication, and stream frame absorption. Redraw spies and no-op fixture callbacks are removed. Native input writes use the existing guarded setters; redundant memo and promise setup are removed.

prs.title: fix: guide repair of archived native command sessions
prs.body:
Related: #168540

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Discord slash commands failing without actionable guidance when their internal command-source session has been archived.

## Why This Change Was Made

Commands remain fail-closed: no automatic restoration or replay. Exact bundled Discord/default Slack source sessions are protected from manual and maintenance archival. Plain Doctor diagnoses existing archives; explicit standalone `openclaw doctor --fix` restores matching sources under the existing exclusive maintenance owner. Updater Doctor does not run this repair. The operator then retries the command.

## User Impact

Discord names the archive problem and points to explicit repair or the existing guarded Control UI Restore flow. Repair retains source identity, activity, history and managed worktree; ordinary and plugin-owned archives remain archived. Each repair follows the physical store that was scanned, including when one agent has both custom and default stores.

## Author Simplification (17 October)

Applied upstream `$pr-simplify` pinned at `665536c406c825b44a0feba58795df774e6ae78f`, auditing all 15 changed files and their existing owners. Only the Doctor archive test file changes versus `9d2eb9ef3`: **124 additions / 194 deletions, net −70 test lines**. The selective-repair matrix now uses real standalone Doctor custody; repeated synthetic custody setup and duplicate assertions were consolidated. Missing-owner/foreign-database rejection, three physical-store identity cases, updater exclusion, ordinary/plugin preservation, transcript/worktree retention and stale-revision behavior remain covered.

The diagnostic assertion now depends on the actual contribution hook rather than a direct call that pre-populated the mock. Disconnecting that hook makes the test fail at zero note calls; after restoring the hook, **8/8 cases pass** (the prior ninth case was merged into the real-custody matrix). Matching test types, targeted lint, formatting and diff checks passed. Two read-only native independent reviews accepted the patch, including clean-context Astra/high acceptance. Standalone autoreview returned HTTP401 and produced no report; it is not counted as review. New-head hosted CI/review are pending reconciliation, separate from prior-head results above.

The full proposal remains **995 net lines across 15 files**: production +254, tests +707, docs +32, test routing +2. The remaining production growth uses existing Doctor, archive, maintenance and transport owners. A smaller coherent guidance-plus-existing-Control-UI-Restore stage would omit the accepted explicit Doctor repair and future protection outcome; this remains a product/staging alternative, not a silently implemented scope reduction or a claim that the XL size target was met. Maintainer archive-policy acceptance is still required.

## Evidence

Current head: `ace7baa16bf4ed1e9415a83f21ae80b3308896d6` (test-only simplification). Accepted production proof was executed at `9d2eb9ef3cf143e19d7e72fd5a6b13244ffc953b`; all production/build/config/docs inputs are byte-identical, so that behavioral evidence is reused, not relabeled as a new-head execution. Earlier runtime/released-state/Discord proof below was captured at `b29fa615d7ee9eb00869764c02b3ee47b6f60c2f`; the focused multi-store correction is validated separately. Base `b76de819f009d18114fb42db91bd51eb5fd7cb56`.

- The earlier PR commits were patch-equivalent after rebase (`git range-diff`, independently reviewed). Rebase integrates upstream #172495 (`c66b65121`), which fixes native SDK compiler sizing on constrained CI runners. Prior head failed after the SDK declaration preparation's 300-second deadline, not on a lint diagnostic; local prior-head preparation emitted 13,675 declaration files successfully.
- Prior-head validation: 96 focused tests passed: archive lifecycle (15), classification/maintenance (34), Doctor (6), Discord interaction boundary/dispatcher (20), upstream compiler-resource tests (21). Production core/extension types, targeted lint, formatting and diff checks passed.
- The hosted P1 at `bf5985f06` is corrected: only the exact archived-source rejection receives archive guidance; unrelated errors rethrow untouched to the existing transport dispatcher. Failure-first regression and all 20 interaction/dispatcher cases pass; independent review accepted the correction and rebase.
- Prior-head `cliStartup` and full `ciArtifacts` core/CLI/UI builds passed. The prior-head Linux ARM64 Docker build-stage image passed all six actual standalone CLI stages: initialize, seed, plain diagnostic, unchanged baseline, explicit repair and persisted repaired readback. Subprocess cleanup passed, container was removed and VM stopped. This is not a production release image or production activation.
- Released-state compatibility passed at the prior head: genuine official OpenClaw 2026.9.9 synthetic agent-schema-24/shared-state-19 backups migrated to 27/24 through one actual standalone Doctor CLI invocation. The native source was restored while the ordinary target stayed archived; both physical IDs, activity and all 16 transcript events were retained. Full parsed configuration matched exactly after only the existing, explicitly checked Doctor changes: 15 unavailable-skill disable flags and version/run bookkeeping. Two pre-existing missing-title repairs were separately verified against the exact original first-user texts. Raw config bytes are not claimed unchanged.
- Real-browser Control UI checks with a mocked Gateway previously passed: Archived exposes the source, Restore sends its exact key/session-ID guard, and the ordinary archive remains. Separate real RPC regression passes. This is not a live browser-to-storage proof.
- Real human Discord behavior was observed at the prior head: `/help` first returned the intended ephemeral archived-session guidance; after explicit standalone Doctor repair, a human manual `/help` returned normal Help (Session, Options, Status, Skills). The original guidance run was interrupted by the test-owner session failure, so repair/retry used a fresh copy of the same archived synthetic fixture—not uninterrupted original-state continuity. The repaired snapshot verifies retained IDs/activity/history and ordinary/plugin-owned archives. The canary container was removed and isolated VM stopped cleanly. Earlier timeout/harness-failed attempts are not counted as successful feature proof.
- The revision-10 review identified a two-store repair defect: an agent-only lookup could select the default store for a finding from a configured custom store. Each finding now carries its scanned physical target through repair. Three new real-store regression cases (default source absent, different ID, same ID) fail before the fix and pass after; all 9 Doctor archive tests pass (6.6 seconds test time, 23.2 seconds wall including compiler preparation). Core and focused test types, targeted lint, formatting and diff checks passed. Independent native review accepted this correction; the separate review CLI failed authentication and is not counted as review coverage. The exact-head CI workflow completed successfully; separate per-file CI timing has not been extracted.
- [Pre-simplification CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38785393336) completed successfully at `9d2eb9ef3cf143e19d7e72fd5a6b13244ffc953b`; the CI gate is successful, with no failed or pending checks at reconciliation. Older canceled auto-response/context jobs have successful replacement jobs; skipped and neutral checks are not execution proof. The [completed exact-head revision-11 review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168596#issuecomment-6100953959) explicitly clears the physical-store finding and reports no actionable code findings.
- Latest-stable **2026.10.4 → pre-simplification candidate compatibility passed**: official macOS 10.4 Doctor promoted genuine released synthetic data to 24/20; a frozen checkpoint then passed the `9d2eb9ef3` Linux ARM64 candidate standalone Doctor (27/24) and normal session/history readers. Both IDs, activity, all 16 transcript events, all four cold-metadata rows and all 23 workspace files were retained; only the native source was restored. Full parsed configuration matches the exact expected existing Doctor maintenance, and ten corruption controls were rejected. See the inspectable packet below for provenance, isolation, failures and limits. Maintainer archive-policy acceptance remains required; no merge-readiness claim.

<details>
<summary>Inspectable actual CLI evidence (synthetic, redacted)</summary>

Linux ARM64, prior-head `b29fa615d7ee9eb00869764c02b3ee47b6f60c2f` build-stage image; non-root, read-only root, no host mounts or published ports, network disabled, synthetic persisted SQLite state, no model/production credentials.

Actual Doctor repair output:

```text
Found 2 archived native-command source session(s); restored 2, skipped
0. Failed slash commands are not replayed.
```

Actual final readback:

```text
FIXTURE global teardown complete
SNAPSHOT_PASS repaired
```

The before/after snapshots assert matching IDs/activity for both native sources and retained JSON transcript history for the Discord source; a removed managed worktree and draft are restored. Ordinary and plugin-owned archive timestamps/identities remain unchanged. The separate diagnostic-only invocation matches the original persisted baseline. Controller: `success: true`, six steps `passed: true`, subprocess cleanup `quarantined: false`, `stopVerified: true`.

Actual released-state Doctor output:

```text
Found 1 archived native-command source session(s); restored 1, skipped
0. Failed slash commands are not replayed.
Repaired 2 of 2 missing session title(s) without changing activity.
```

Exported independent readback and lifecycle result:

```json
{
  "head": "b29fa615d7ee9eb00869764c02b3ee47b6f60c2f",
  "schemas": {"before": {"agent": 24, "state": 19}, "after": {"agent": 27, "state": 24}},
  "sourceRestored": true,
  "ordinaryTargetStillArchived": true,
  "idsActivitySettingsAnd16EventsPreserved": true,
  "fullParsedConfigMatchesExactExpected": true,
  "cleanup": {"quarantined": false},
  "quiescent": true,
  "success": true,
  "stopVerified": true
}
```

The config assertion permits only the exact unavailable-skill flags shown by Doctor, writer version, and a canonical wizard timestamp inside the actual CLI lifetime; every other parsed value (including secret fields) must match. It does not blanket-ignore metadata. Seven projection-only corruption controls were rejected: wrong title, ordinary archive clearing, changed activity/transcript, unexpected model/secret changes and an out-of-window wizard timestamp.

Setup limits: active synthetic workspace/agent/config/cron-store paths were relocated into the Linux container; historical transcript content was not rewritten. This is released synthetic persisted-data compatibility, not an untouched real-user snapshot, published update-driver test, live model turn or live Discord proof. Original fixture hashes were retained/verified; no production state or model credentials were used.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Human Discord retry evidence and interruption boundary</summary>

Prior-head `b29fa615d7ee9eb00869764c02b3ee47b6f60c2f`, isolated Linux ARM64 build-stage image and dedicated test bot; no production state/model credentials or host mounts/ports.

```text
18:52 CEST, human /help:
This command’s internal session is archived. Ask your OpenClaw operator
 to run openclaw doctor --fix, then retry.

Fresh same-fixture recovery after the owner-session interruption:
SNAPSHOT_PASS baseline
[actual standalone openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive]
SNAPSHOT_PASS repaired
Discord health: lifecycle=ready, running=true, connected=true, lastError=null

19:51 CEST, human manual /help:
Help — Session / Options / Status / Skills
(ephemeral reply; normal help, no archive warning)
```

Both human responses were visually inspected from supplied screenshots. The fresh recovery fixture preserves source IDs, activity and JSON transcript history, restores the managed-worktree draft, and leaves ordinary/plugin-owned archives unchanged. This combines real human Discord observations with actual offline repair assertions; it does not claim original temporary-state continuity across the interruption, production deployment, or a live model turn. The deliberately unavailable synthetic model provider produced an unrelated scheduled-heartbeat error during the window; that is not counted as model proof or a `/help` failure. Lifecycle receipt: `success=true`, `lifecycleSuccess=true`, `stopVerified=true`, no remaining owned processes/sockets and no isolation violation.

</details>

<details>
<summary>2026.10.4 → tested 9d2 head: actual CLI and preservation packet (17 October; production inputs unchanged)</summary>

**Candidate:** `9d2eb9ef3cf143e19d7e72fd5a6b13244ffc953b` (no source change for this proof). **Official installed baseline:** `OpenClaw 2026.10.4 (383c124)`, build commit `383c124cc32ffee3f8e56f549b88da94d269a4af`; no package installation or package-age exception. The exact-head candidate Linux build uses the previously verified build-stage image plus the only two changed tracked files since `b29fa615d`, rebuilt with networking disabled; its actual `dist/build-info.json` reports the tested candidate commit `9d2eb9ef3`. This is a CLI/runtime rebuild, not a new full UI/package build; Doctor's UI-assets freshness warning is retained and is not counted as UI proof.

Provenance is deliberately bounded: genuine 2026.9.9 synthetic state was promoted by actual official **macOS 2026.10.4** `doctor --fix --non-interactive`, frozen at agent/shared schemas **24/20**, and consumed from a separate copy by the actual **Linux ARM64 candidate** standalone Doctor. This is not freshly authored 10.4 sessions, arbitrary real-user data, the public update driver, or a successful macOS candidate CLI run. Only three active config destinations and five existing shared-state path columns were relocated; historical content was not rewritten.

Actual candidate CLI output:

```text
Found 1 archived native-command source session(s); restored 1, skipped
0. Failed slash commands are not replayed.
Doctor complete.
```

Independent persisted snapshots, normal production accessor readback, verifier and lifecycle receipts:

```json
{
  "candidateHead": "9d2eb9ef3cf143e19d7e72fd5a6b13244ffc953b",
  "baseline": "official 2026.10.4-written frozen synthetic checkpoint",
  "schemas": {"before": {"agent": 24, "state": 20}, "after": {"agent": 27, "state": 24}},
  "actualDoctorExit": 0,
  "normalSessionAndTranscriptReadersExit": 0,
  "nativeSourceRestored": true,
  "ordinaryTargetStillArchived": true,
  "bothPhysicalIdsAndActivityPreserved": true,
  "transcriptEventsRetained": 16,
  "coldMetadataRowsRetained": 4,
  "workspaceFileHashesRetained": 23,
  "completeConfigMatchesExactExpected": true,
  "corruptionControlsRejected": 10,
  "subprocessesQuiescent": true,
  "containerRemoved": true,
  "vmStopped": true,
  "isolationViolations": 0
}
```

The full reader hydrates the separately stored skills snapshots and system-prompt reports; it matches exact preserved hot **and** cold values, not merely a compact metadata row. Every transcript-event hash matches through the normal history reader. The complete parsed configuration comparison permits only the same 15 explicitly named unavailable-skill disable flags and precise writer/wizard bookkeeping established in the earlier packet; the wizard timestamp must fall inside the actual CLI lifetime. Existing titles were already filled by official 10.4 and remain unchanged. Corruption controls reject identity, title, archive, activity, transcript, cold metadata, workspace, model, secret and timestamp mutations. This released checkpoint has no managed-worktree binding; workspace preservation here is not relabeled as the separate prior managed-worktree restoration proof.

Isolation: synthetic credentials only; macOS denies all IP networking and all writes outside task paths, with task-path Unix IPC only. Linux is non-root, read-only-root, network-none, no host mounts or published ports, no capabilities, no-new-privileges, init/reaping and bounded resources. Original 52-file/link and frozen-checkpoint manifests remain unchanged. Four pre-existing VM-disk hashes and two links are verified preserved; task container removal, VM stop and absence of owned processes/sockets are checked independently.

Failed attempts are retained, not counted as passes: macOS candidate Doctor made the intended data changes but exited 1 because Seatbelt denied its setuid process-census executable during cleanup. The first Linux attempt completed Doctor but rejected a harness comparison of a hydrated full entry against hot metadata only; the corrected full-reader comparison passed on a fresh checkpoint copy. Neither consumed fixture was replayed. Official macOS Doctor's own recovery capture was unavailable because of the SSD ancestor permission check; this proof uses its independently hashed frozen checkpoint, not a claim that built-in recovery capture succeeded. Production was not changed.

</details>

## Maintainer decision and compatibility boundary

Maintainer acceptance is required before merge: should exact bundled Discord/default Slack sources become unarchivable and exempt from maintenance, with standalone Doctor reopening matching existing archives? This PR does not assume approval. The narrower alternative is archive-specific guidance plus the existing guarded Control UI Restore operation.

No PR-owned schema migration, background repair, automatic replay or production activation is added. Reverting the change restores prior behavior. The archive/maintenance/Doctor policy is one cohesive change; broad automatic source/reset-target restoration from earlier versions of this PR is removed. Known proof and product gates above remain explicit.

AI-assisted implementation, validation and review.

prs.title: fix(agents): detect reworded sessions_send floods via semantic loop-hash normalization
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #119600.

The tool-loop detector hashes full `sessions_send` params, including the free-text body. A model that rewords every attempt therefore produces a new argument hash, preventing a repeat streak from forming even when it repeatedly targets the same peer session with stable outcomes. In the reported incident this allowed a semantic send flood to continue while the detector remained silent.

This is the send-side counterpart of #117637 (exec argument churn) and complements #89090, which stabilized send *outcome* hashes; this PR stabilizes the internal-session send *argument* hash.

## Change

`src/agents/tool-loop-detection.ts`:

- Normalize free-text `message`/`text` fields for `sessions_send` before hashing.
- Preserve `sessionKey`, so different peer sessions remain distinct.
- Keep `conversations_send`, `conversations_turn`, and `message` fully text-sensitive because they deliver directly to external conversations/channels where distinct text is legitimate.

## Tests

Regression coverage in `src/agents/tool-loop-detection.test.ts` verifies:

- reworded `sessions_send` bodies to one session hash identically;
- sends to different sessions stay distinct;
- 20 stable same-target outcomes cause the next reworded `sessions_send` admission to return critical `generic_repeat`;
- mixed-target fan-out remains allowed;
- `conversations_send`, `conversations_turn`, and `message` remain text-sensitive.

## Evidence

### Exact-head runtime proof

A redacted runnable harness and its clean-worktree output are attached here:

- `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/119604#issuecomment-5231243497`
- reviewed head: `6e727cb08b0c4408f239607b935e49e40caa43ce`

The harness imports the reviewed head's source module and exercises `hashToolCall`, `recordToolCall`, `recordToolCallOutcome`, and `detectToolCallLoop`. It refuses to run unless tracked files are clean and `HEAD` matches the supplied SHA.

Observed boundary:

```text
{
  "reviewedHead": "6e727cb08b0c4408f239607b935e49e40caa43ce",
  "sourceModule": "src/agents/tool-loop-detection.ts",
  "assertions": {
    "rewordedSessionsSendSameTargetHashesEqual": true,
    "rewordedSessionsSendTextAliasSameTargetHashesEqual": true,
    "sessionsSendDifferentTargetsRemainDistinct": true,
    "nextSessionsSendAfterTwentyStableOutcomes": {
      "stuck": true,
      "level": "critical",
      "detector": "generic_repeat",
      "count": 20
    },
    "rewordedConversationsSendRemainsTextSensitive": true,
    "rewordedConversationsTurnRemainsTextSensitive": true,
    "nextDistinctConversationSendAfterTwentyOutcomes": {
      "stuck": false
    },
    "rewordedMessageToolSendsRemainTextSensitive": true
  }
}
```

This demonstrates:

- same-target reworded `sessions_send`: critical `generic_repeat` after 20 stable outcomes;
- different internal targets: distinct hashes;
- distinct external conversation/channel text: remains allowed and text-sensitive.

### Integrated admission/outcome proof

A second redacted exact-head harness closes the production-lifecycle boundary identified by ClawSweeper:

- proof comment: `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/119604#issuecomment-5233962446`
- selector-canonicalization follow-up proof (covers `prepareBeforeToolCallParams` selector resolution and the rotation block): `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/119604#issuecomment-5381049977`
- reviewed head: `be424e866abae3a1eba1ab5de0cb87cd7ad84cc6`
- real `agent-core` tool-call loop and schema validation;
- actual `sessions_send.prepareArguments` alias canonicalization;
- real wrapped before-tool admission and outcome recording;
- actual `conversations_send` production execution with an injected contract-valid no-network gateway.

Observed integrated boundary:

```text
same-target sessions_send:
  model attempts: 21
  synthetic executor invocations: 20
  admission/history records: 21
  executed outcome records: 20
  prepared argument hash count: 1
  stable normalized result hash count with unique run IDs: 1
  prospective attempt 21: blocked (generic_repeat, count 20)

target-separated sessions_send:
  target-A synthetic executions: 20
  identical target-B call after target-A threshold: allowed
  next target-A call: blocked
  prepared argument hash count: 2

external conversations_send:
  model attempts: 21
  injected fake-gateway invocations: 21
  admission/history records: 21
  executed outcome records: 21
  prepared argument hash count: 21
  critical generic-repeat events: 0
  network delivery performed: false
```

The detector evaluates completed prior outcomes before execution; therefore the event reports `count: 20` while blocking the prospective 21st same-target attempt. The production `sessions_send` delivery body is replaced by a contract-shaped synthetic executor, and the external tool uses its production dependency-injection seam. No real inter-agent or external-channel messages are emitted by this proof.

### Local validation

```text
Focused Vitest: 178/178 passed across agents-core and agents-support
oxfmt (changed files): passed
type-aware oxlint (changed files): 0 warnings, 0 errors
tsgo:core: passed
tsgo:core:test: passed
```

The earlier full legacy `tsc --noEmit` command now exceeds even an 8 GB Node heap on the expanded repository; the maintained `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` project checks pass.

### Shipped beta.7 corroboration

A behaviorally equivalent normalization for the canonical runtime `message` shape was ported to the installed `2026.7.2-beta.7` loop-detector bundle and exercised through its shipped detector exports. It produced the same critical `generic_repeat` boundary for reworded same-session sends while 20 distinct-text external conversation deliveries remained allowed. The beta.7 port did not separately normalize the pre-canonicalization `text` alias, so it is corroborating operator evidence rather than a byte-for-byte copy of the PR helper. The exact-head harness above is the inspectable proof for both `message` and defensive `text` handling.

## Scope Note

Loop history is per run, so this closes the within-run evasion class. Cross-run loops driven by heartbeats, recall cycles, or separate autonomous runs additionally need session-level budgeting/policy containment and remain out of scope.

prs.title: fix(auth): saving an API key for a new agent fails with a database identity error
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: saving an API key for a newly configured agent (Gateway `models.authSetApiKey`, as used by onboarding, the Control UI, and live suites) fails with `UNAVAILABLE: SQLite database path identity changed: …/agents/<id>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite` when that agent's database does not exist yet.

## User Impact

User impact: storing credentials for a fresh agent succeeds instead of failing the first time. Integrity checks for existing agent databases are unchanged: a known database file that gets replaced is still rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Candidate auth-store discovery records each candidate database's identity. For a fresh agent that identity is "absent at this path". The same Gateway then creates the database, either in the operation itself or through concurrent startup work, and the later identity assertion rejects the file that now exists. The capture/check pair came from #166183.

An absence snapshot protects no file. So the first check after the file appears adopts its identity once, and every later check (including candidates discovered as existing files) stays strict. The Gateway owns these databases, so a foreign writer creating the file in that window is not a supported concurrent case. That trade is noted in the code.

A first attempt only accepted files created by the same operation's execution owner. Under host load it still failed intermittently when startup work created the database first. The second commit replaces that with the simpler rule and removes the owner-witness plumbing, leaving a net diff of 2 files.

## Evidence

- Offline repro (fresh agent, loopback provider, no inference): before, `models.authSetApiKey` failed with the identity error. After, 8/8 consecutive runs succeed, moving `path:` → `file:` with zero inference requests.
- Live: `src/gateway/gateway-cron-tools-allow.live.test.ts` used to fail its OpenClaw-harness case with this identity error on main and on the first attempt. It now passes both cases (OpenClaw 173s, Codex 188s). `gateway-cron-placement.live.test.ts` still fails with an unrelated "forced cron run did not publish its completion record", the same as before this change.
- Unit: `candidate-stores.test.ts` covers creation before and during first use, replacement after adoption, and replacement of a file discovered as existing (37 tests with the creation-witness suite).
- Autoreview: scoped-clean at P1.

## What Problem This Solves

Windows upgrades restart the gateway twice: `gateway install --force` already activates the replacement service, and the installer immediately invokes another restart.

## User Impact

Upgrades activate the gateway once, then check its status before running Doctor. A failed status check produces a verification warning and the correct diagnostic command without reporting a successful refresh.

## Why This Change Was Made

Service installation owns replacement and activation. Removing the extra restart aligns PowerShell with both Unix installers and avoids interrupting the replacement during startup. Existing missing-command, missing-service, and install-failure handling is unchanged.

Release note: Windows installer upgrades no longer restart the newly activated gateway a second time.

prs.title: fix: status --json --all reports memory vectors as available after the vector probe fails
prs.body:
Closes #153488

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw status --json --all` keeps reporting a memory plugin's last-known vector state (for example `vector.available: true`) when the vector probe it just ran rejects, with no error in the report.

## User Impact

User impact: when the memory vector probe fails, `status --json --all` now shows the affected vector availability as `false` with the probe error in `memory.vector.loadError`, instead of reporting an unverified vector store as healthy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The status collector now records which probe rejected and applies that to the snapshot it returns. A failed store probe sets `storeAvailable`, `semanticAvailable`, and `available` to `false`, because semantic vectors are served from that store. A failed semantic probe sets only `semanticAvailable` and `available` to `false` and leaves `storeAvailable` as reported, since that probe does not inspect the store. The error text goes through the shared redacting `formatErrorMessage`. A failure of the initial status read is still tolerated as before, and the manager is still closed in `finally`.

The memory section is only collected by the local `status --json --all` fallback, used when the Gateway is not reachable. The bundled memory-core plugin already catches sqlite-vec load errors and load timeouts inside its probe and reports `storeAvailable: false` with `loadError`. Its probe only rejects on manager-admission failures such as a closed manager, and those also fail the status read that follows. The case that still reached the empty `catch {}` is a memory plugin selected through `plugins.slots.memory` with the legacy memory-manager runtime whose `probeVectorStoreAvailability()` or `probeVectorAvailability()` rejects (for example an unreachable remote vector store) while its `status()` still returns cached healthy fields. Native provider plugins already report their errors through `health`.

Keeping store availability untouched when only the semantic probe fails comes from the earlier attempt, #119993 by @xialonglee, which was closed unmerged. This PR keeps only the status-collector part of that attempt, without its text renderer or Telegram changes.

## Evidence

Later commits on main don't touch these files.

Regression tests in `src/commands/status.scan.shared.test.ts` (custom memory slot whose manager reports healthy vectors, then its probe rejects).

Before (current production code, new tests applied):

```
 FAIL ... > reports a rejected vector store probe instead of the pre-probe vector state
-     "available": false,
+     "available": true,
-     "loadError": "vector store unreachable",
-     "semanticAvailable": false,
-     "storeAvailable": false,
+     "semanticAvailable": true,
+     "storeAvailable": true,
 FAIL ... > reports a rejected semantic vector probe without marking the store unavailable
-     "available": false,
+     "available": true,
-     "loadError": "embedding index offline",
-     "semanticAvailable": false,
+     "semanticAvailable": true,
```

After:

```
 ✓ ... > reports a rejected vector store probe instead of the pre-probe vector state 2ms
 ✓ ... > reports a rejected semantic vector probe without marking the store unavailable 2ms
```

The rest of `status.scan.shared.test.ts` and the sibling suites `status.scan.test.ts`, `status.memory-presence.worker.test.ts`, and `status.scan.fast-json-cold-imports.test.ts` pass.

Real CLI proof: `pnpm openclaw status --json --all` with an isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, the Gateway pointed at an unused port (so the local fallback runs), and a synthetic local plugin selected in `plugins.slots.memory`. The plugin registers a legacy memory runtime whose `status()` returns healthy vector fields and whose vector probes reject with `connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:6333 (proof vector store)`.

Before:

```json
"vector": {
  "enabled": true,
  "storeAvailable": true,
  "semanticAvailable": true,
  "available": true
}
```

After:

```json
"vector": {
  "enabled": true,
  "storeAvailable": false,
  "semanticAvailable": false,
  "available": false,
  "loadError": "connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:6333 (proof vector store)"
}
```

Not proven live: a failure from the bundled memory-core plugin, because as described above its probe does not reject while its status read still succeeds.

Checks: `check-changed` passes typecheck, format, and the changed-file guards, and oxlint passes on the changed files. Its other failures are unrelated: the max-lines suppression ratchet and the Knip unused-export scan also fail without this change, and the core tsgo test-shard root budgets are for shards this PR adds no tests to.

Test cost: the two new tests take about 2 ms each. `pnpm test src/commands/status.scan.shared.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took about 30 s wall time, almost all of it shared compile and transform setup.

prs.title: fix(update): a short update deadline silently cuts update check time on large state
prs.body:
Related: #163172

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an update fails its pre-activation checks with "exceeded budget" or "Update validation deadline exceeded" when the update deadline (`--timeout`) is shorter than the automatic per-check allowance for the measured state, and nothing in the output names the deadline as the cause.

## User Impact

User impact: when the update deadline is shorter than the size-scaled allowance for each update check, the update report, `openclaw update status`, and `--json` steps include one warning with both values and a next step:

```
Warning: The update deadline limits each update check to 1800 s, below the automatic 2860 s allowance for this state. If a check runs out of time, retry with a longer --timeout.
```

Timeout behavior is unchanged. Updates without a deadline, or with one at or above the automatic allowance, show nothing new. The installed updater produces this warning, so it appears once the installed version includes this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

This implements the "keep `--timeout` as a limit and warn" option from #163172. That option is consistent with #171077, which made `--timeout` one overall update budget. It does not make `--timeout` a per-check floor, the issue's first option: an existing test requires a shorter explicit deadline to win, and a floor could not outlast the overall deadline anyway. A maintainer should confirm this contract, since the issue is labeled for a product decision.

Each update check normally gets 300 s plus 40 s per 32 MiB of copied SQLite and plugin state, and a `--timeout` replaces that allowance. The canary now resolves this budget before it records the `candidate-state-snapshot` step, which already carries the measured state size, and adds the warning to that step's existing `warnings`. Those warnings already reach the report and run history.

The warning is worded neutrally because the operator may not have passed `--timeout`. An update started inside the Gateway's process tree hands off to a background updater with `--timeout` set to the parent's default step deadline (`update-command-execution.ts` `handoffUpdateFromGateway`, then `startManagedServiceUpdateHandoff`). The recommended next step, a longer `--timeout`, works in both cases.

`update-candidate-canary.ts` is at its 700-line cap, so the existing budget calculation moves unchanged into a small sibling module together with the warning. `docs/cli/update.md` gets one paragraph.

## Evidence

Base: 1108a99d3. The branch was rebased from e032d1e31 and then onto current main after #175596 restructured the canary budget table test; the regression cases now sit in that table (including its 32 MiB snapshot case, which gets the 30 s vs 340 s warning). The canary, report, and budget production code did not change upstream, so the before-fix evidence collected on e032d1e31 still applies.

- Regression: the existing state-size budget table in `src/infra/update-candidate-canary.test.ts` now renders the real update report from each canary result.
  - The 2 GiB + 1800 s case must contain the warning. Its 2860 s value is computed by hand in the test.
  - The no-timeout cases and a new 2 GiB + 3600 s case must not contain it.
  - The source-selection test passes 3 s, so it now also expects the warning after the snapshot warnings.
- Before, with base production code and this test file: `Tests 3 failed | 4 passed`. The table case fails as `expected '⚠️ OpenClaw update failed: doctor-fai…' to contain 'Warning: The update deadline limits e…'`. Its report only said `Failed: candidate-doctor — Exit code: 1; Update validation deadline exceeded`. The other two failures are the node and bun source-selection cases.
- After: `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 81 passed (81)` (after #175596 pruned cases upstream).
- These sibling and caller suites pass:
  - canary cleanup, exit (real child processes), lint, and integration (real built candidate);
  - `update-command-execution-validation`;
  - `update-command-candidate-exit`;
  - `update-failure-report-prepare`.
- Test cost: `pnpm test src/infra/update-candidate-canary.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took 38.5 s wall (Vitest 15.9 s) on a shared host. Each changed case takes 5–6 ms.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main -- <changed files>` (merge base 1108a99d3): format, docs, the line-cap ratchet, core typecheck, core oxlint, and the other guards pass. These also fail on the base, outside this change:
  - the max-lines suppression ratchet (`ui/src/pages/**`);
  - the core test shard root budget (infra 736 and gateway-root 727 test roots, above the advisory 720; this change adds no test files);
  - core test typecheck: three `TS2304` errors in `ui/src/pages/chat/session-snapshot-store.test.ts`;
  - Knip unused exports in files this change does not touch (for example `src/logging/diagnostic-*`, `src/infra/diagnostic-rpc-types.ts`, `scripts/generate-dependency-release-evidence.mts`).
- Real behavior, through the packaged CLI: I packed this branch with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` and installed it globally with `npm install -g` in the repo's `bare` E2E image (`node:24-bookworm-slim`), using fresh isolated state from `openclaw-test-state`. I then ran `openclaw update --tag <local candidate .tgz> --yes --no-restart` twice. Each target was a same-schema candidate built from the same pack by `update-first-hop-package-fixtures.mjs future-tarball`. The container has no service manager, so `--no-restart` was used; candidate validation still ran in the `validating` phase.
  - Control, no `--timeout`, 2026.10.4 to 2026.10.5-first-hop.0: `✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.10.5-first-hop.0 (from 2026.10.4); 15 warnings need attention.`, `Phases: requested (87ms) → staging (7ms) → validating (49.37s) → activating (65.19s)`. The update output, `openclaw update status`, and `openclaw update status --json` contain no "update deadline" warning, and the run has no `warning:candidate-state-snapshot` step.
  - `--timeout 240`, first-hop.0 to first-hop.1: `✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.10.5-first-hop.1 (from 2026.10.5-first-hop.0); 14 warnings need attention.` The report and `openclaw update status` both include:
    ```
    Warning: The update deadline limits each update check to 240 s, below the automatic 303 s allowance for this state. If a check runs out of time, retry with a longer --timeout.
    ```
    `openclaw update status --json` records it in `lastRun.steps`:
    ```json
    {"step":"warning:candidate-state-snapshot","status":"completed","detail":"The update deadline limits each update check to 240 s, below the automatic 303 s allowance for this state. If a check runs out of time, retry with a longer --timeout."}
    ```
  - Gap: the container state was small, about 2 MiB of SQLite, so the automatic allowance is 303 s and validation finished well inside 240 s. A large-state host where a check actually runs out of time was not reproduced through the CLI. That failure path is covered by the unit table (2 GiB at 1800 s) and by the canary-level runs below.
- Canary-level run against the built candidate, rendering the report from the result. This used real Doctor, plugin, config, and Gateway child processes with isolated state and `HOME`.
  - Before (e032d1e31 canary), 5 s deadline: `Failed: candidate-doctor — timeout; candidate-migration-rehearsal: doctor exceeded budget after 5 s (...)`, and nothing names the deadline.
  - After, 5 s: the same timeout, plus the deadline warning (5 s against 300 s).
  - After, no deadline: no warning.
- Docs checks pass: `format-docs --check`, `docs:check-mdx`, and `docs:check-links` (0 broken links).
- Autoreview (local, max P2): no actionable findings.

## What Problem This Solves

Private UI presentation helpers duplicate their single caller's fields and actions in parameter bags, even though that caller already owns the page operation.

## User Impact

No user-visible change or migration is intended. Rendering, controls, lazy routes, native hosts, and Gateway/security authority stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep plugin settings editing in its existing page owner. Keep Desktop presentation in its existing Solid entry, retaining the one reactive view prop. Keep Debug's presentation local to the page, reading its live owner facts directly instead of constructing a 21-field transfer object. Existing public Debug tests now enter through the real page and Gateway fixture boundary; all 80 original assertions remain. Keep Activity and Lobsterdex presentation private to their page owners, and Browser/Terminal content private to their native host registration owners. Existing component boundaries and reactive JSX bindings remain; Lobsterdex retains its value-prop boundary so storage parsing is not repeated by every view read.

This is an area split of the wider single-consumer family, under the campaign's rule 11. The lint-repaired candidate removes **121 net production lines** across 14 production paths (+1,157/-1,278) against base 51ebf30c8e054fb00dba3b6bb425253e8b14c5c1. Plugin credential matching, per-edit flush acknowledgment, Gateway/agent scopes, request ordering, lifecycle cleanup, and Desktop's imperative island stay with their current owners. No public SDK/protocol/config/schema/dependency contract or protected Phase E backend changes. prs.title: fix(ui): stop redundant session reads during swarm updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes redundant `sessions.describe` traffic while the Control UI renders active swarms. The reported incident recorded 1,581 describes over 20 minutes across roughly 20 web clients. A complete-UI reproduction produced one extra parent describe for every child event, even though the event already delivered the needed parent facts.

## User Impact

Swarm progress, completion, and new child membership update without re-describing the parent. Authorization, explicit fresh operation reads, and recovery for incomplete rows remain intact. No protocol or native-client changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The swarm owner assumed all event rows omitted member details. Current recipient-authorized nested `session` and `ancestorSessions` rows include them; only the outer envelope retains summary-only swarm counts. It also compared child-list callbacks with its previous parent callback's copy: list listeners run first, although the shared parent observation already holds the current frame. That stale comparison forced a describe for every child status change.

Use the current parent observation when checking child consistency and re-read changed parent summaries only when member details are absent. The shared descriptor implementation and API comment are unchanged from the branch base: connection/request-shape isolation, in-flight joins, the 128-entry completed-read limit, event invalidation, and explicit fresh reads retain their existing behavior. There is no TTL or new snapshot/lifecycle invalidation.

The simplification removes redundant reads and the stale callback copy used for child consistency; no new cache or owner was introduced. Production delta against the merge base: 16 added / 7 removed lines, all in the hydrator. Tests: 173 added lines protecting request volume, rendered state, and reuse across unchanged observations. Documentation: 9 added lines.

## Evidence

The existing production Control UI browser harness, with synthetic Gateway frames and four children, exercised the actual transport, session store, swarm owner, and rendered widget:

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Initial connection describes | 2 | 2 |
| 12 alternating child message/change events with full ancestor rows | 12 additional | 0 additional |
| New fifth child, with full ancestor row | 1 additional | 0 additional |

Child names and statuses were checked after every event. Completion text and the four-to-five-child transition matched before and after. This is synthetic browser/runtime proof, not a new live production traffic measurement. The unchanged Gateway parity test separately passed: authorized nested event rows equal full list rows, including owner versus viewer member filtering.

The added descriptor regression installs 12 successive roster observations with unchanged session identity/`updatedAt` and advancing `snapshotAt`, with 31 seconds of fake time between reads. It checks that the observed clock advances, then calls `describe` after each observation: one total RPC. Descriptor production code, including current-main unchanged-ancestor-reference reuse and explicit fresh reads, is unchanged by this PR.

Passed after conflict resolution: 51 focused session-describe/swarm tests; browser regression; `pnpm tsgo:ui`; type-aware oxlint and oxfmt on touched files; assertion-safety; line-cap ratchet; `git diff --check`; pr-simplify; isolated Codex review at P1 (scoped-clean). The unchanged Gateway row-event parity test passed during the original investigation. No Gateway production files changed, so core typecheck is not required.

CI initially found overly broad fixture annotations in the new browser test: `GatewaySessionRow` permits nullable/missing fields that the mock Gateway requires. The fixture now declares its concrete `kind`, `label`, and `updatedAt` fields. The exact failing UI E2E chat type graph and the browser regression pass locally; runtime behavior is unchanged, and the focused repair passed isolated P1 review.

Conflict resolution onto `665536c406c8` preserves main's direct parent observation, its provider-status/collector distinction, and its descriptor event handling. Re-ran the browser regression, all 51 focused tests, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, the exact UI E2E chat type graph, targeted lint/format, and fresh isolated P1 review. Browser result: 12 child events and one new-member event each add zero describes, with matching rendered state.

Test timing after rebase: focused pair 1.62 seconds (3.62 seconds including runner); browser case 1.444 seconds, file 2.233 seconds, 13.89 seconds including build/process. Current-head PR CI pending.

An additional optional `check:max-lines-ratchet` run reports three pre-existing suppressions missing from its baseline in `chat-message.test.tsx`, `config-page-state.ts`, and `sessions-page-state.ts`. Those files are identical to `origin/main`; the required line-cap ratchet passed.

<details>
<summary>All Control UI describe callers and triggers</summary>

Normal calls converge on `ui/src/lib/sessions/session-describe.ts:91`; its explicit fresh initiating-client path at line 72 remains separate for reconnect settlement.

| Call site | Trigger and needed facts |
| --- | --- |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-board.ts:503` | Swarm/subagent parent hydration, changed summary, child consistency, observation invalidation. Dominant incident path: `SwarmRosterHydrator.applyChildren` compared a stale parent and forced a read. Needs group counts/member status and child keys; complete nested event rows now suffice. |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-session-observation.ts:54` | Parent mount/invalidation and selected runner-availability recovery; full identity, placement, runner facts. |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-active-resources.ts:226` | Visible desktop/browser discovery and invalidation; session identity, archive state, placement, exec node. |
| `ui/src/components/session-lineage.ts:521` | Missing selected descriptor or runner-availability invalidation; otherwise reuses observed row. Needs identity and navigation ancestry. |
| `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-child-session-data.ts:109` | Unknown ancestor recovery in the bounded 16-level ancestry walk; known rows are reused. |
| `ui/src/components/session-details.ts:82` | Compact-row expansion/session-menu open and invalidation while open; full execution/communication settings omitted by list projections. No direct hovercard describe. |
| `ui/src/components/desktop/desktop-session-owner.ts:316` | Standalone Desktop open/refresh and matching session events without a supplied target; placement/exec-node resolution. Embedded supplied targets bypass this. Secondary event caller, unchanged here. |
| `ui/src/components/board/board-document.tsx:151` | Board binding/open or connection/target change without a prepared session; canonical identity. |
| `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-personal-navigation.ts:169` | Missing saved pin, once per connection; identity/display/navigation metadata. |
| `ui/src/lib/sessions/session-placement-startup.ts:106` | Startup/recovery/retry/cancellation settlement; explicitly fresh placement and session identity before effects. Passed through `app/session-placement-startup.runtime.ts:180` and `pages/new-session/draft-session-placement.ts:129`. |
| `ui/src/components/session-organizer-archive.runtime.ts:74` | User archive with descendant hint; explicitly fresh root identity/archive/topology. |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-command-executor.ts:532` | User model/thinking/verbose/fast/usage commands; execution settings and usage. |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-goals.ts:335` | User goal recovery after roster reconciliation; explicitly fresh goal and exact session incarnation. |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-state-refresh.ts:342` | Catalog/metadata invalidation or on-demand model catalog; explicitly fresh thinking/context/model facts. |
| `ui/src/lib/mcp-app-catalog.ts:108` | MCP app preparation for an unprepared destination; existence check before creation. |

The browser identifies as `openclaw-control-ui` / `webchat`; RPC attribution uses the negotiated client ID, not the operator role. Swift/Android describe callers use separate native identities and are untouched. The caller census does not attribute live incident counts individually; dominance is established by the reproduced web swarm path.

</details>
