prs.title: fix(update): update status help and docs show a stale --timeout default
prs.body:
Related: #174060

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update status --help` says `--timeout` defaults to 3 seconds and the status docs table says 300, when neither is the real default.

## User Impact

User impact: the help and the docs table now both say that, without `--timeout`, update checks share the 30-second overall status limit, and that a longer value extends that limit. A shorter value only caps each check. Command behavior does not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

`update status` stopped using a 3-second check default in #145219, which changed the docs table to 300 but left the help string. #174060 then added the 30-second overall limit and described it in the page's opening paragraph, but left the table at 300. The sentence under the table, "Explicit timeouts replace the default", also suggested that a short `--timeout` replaces the 30-second limit, which it does not.

This change corrects those statements and nothing else. The `--timeout` options on `update`, `update wizard`, `update repair`, and `update recover` describe other budgets and are still accurate.

<details>
<summary>Current behavior (src/cli/update-cli/status.ts)</summary>

- `checkTimeoutMs = parseUpdateTimeoutMs(opts.timeout)` is `undefined` without the flag.
- `timeoutMs = Math.max(30_000, checkTimeoutMs ?? 0)` is the overall status limit.
- The installation check and the Git target read use `Math.min(checkTimeoutMs ?? Infinity, remainingMs())`. Without the flag they are bounded only by the shared limit; with it, each is capped at the given value.
- The Gateway channel-warning read uses `Math.min(checkTimeoutMs ?? 5_000, remainingMs())`, so it keeps a 5-second default unless `--timeout` is set.
- The help string dates from the original `update status` command, when checks defaulted to 3.5 seconds.

</details>

## Evidence

Base: `093dc48a1`.

`pnpm openclaw update status --help` (isolated `HOME`, no state written):

```text
# before
  --timeout <seconds>  Timeout for update checks in seconds (default: 3)

# after
  --timeout <seconds>  Timeout for update checks in seconds (default: shared 30s
                       limit; longer values extend it)
```

- Existing test `src/cli/update-cli/status.deadline.test.ts` already covers the behavior that the new text describes: with `--timeout 1`, the update check gets 1000 ms and history still returns; without the flag, status returns partial JSON at 30 seconds. It passes on this branch (3 tests, 19.8 s wall including startup). No test asserts this help string, so there is no test change.
- Docs checks: `pnpm format:docs:check`, `pnpm docs:check-mdx`, `pnpm docs:check-links` (0 broken), `pnpm docs:check-i18n-glossary`, `pnpm docs:check-config-examples`, and markdownlint (`pnpm lint:docs` config) all pass. `git diff --check` is clean.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 093dc48a1 -- <changed files>`: core typecheck, core test typecheck, oxlint on `src/cli/update-cli.ts`, and format pass. Three lanes fail for reasons that come from the base and do not involve these files: the max-lines suppression ratchet (`ui/src/pages/**`), the core test shard root budget (`gateway-root` 727 and `infra` 733 roots against an advisory 720; this change adds no files), and the dead-export scan (`src/logging/diagnostic-*` and others).

prs.title: fix: failed auto-compaction reply recommends /compact, which hits the same failure
prs.body:
Closes #148766

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a session overflows and auto-compaction also fails, the reply tells the user to "try again, use /compact, or use /new", then repeats "Try starting a fresh session…". Retrying and /compact rerun the compaction that just failed, and the reply never names the command that does recover the session.

## User Impact

User impact: after a failed auto-compaction, users are pointed at `/new` (fresh session) or a larger-context model. Operators who want to keep the session get a session-specific trim command. Ordinary keys are shown once and paste into cmd.exe, PowerShell, or a POSIX shell. Keys that need quoting, such as Matrix keys with `!` and `$`, get two labeled forms: one for macOS, Linux, or PowerShell and one for Windows Command Prompt. A warning before the command says trimming permanently deletes older history with no backup and suggests `openclaw backup create` first. The reply no longer recommends retrying or /compact. Session handling is unchanged, and no action is required.

New reply for a typical session:

```text
⚠️ Auto-compaction could not recover this turn. I kept this conversation mapped to the current session. Use /new to start a fresh session.

Try a model with a larger context window.

To keep this session instead, an operator can trim its transcript. Trimming permanently deletes older history and keeps no backup, so run `openclaw backup create` first if that history matters, then `openclaw sessions compact agent:main:main --agent main --max-lines 200`.
```

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildContextOverflowRecoveryText` hard-coded the retry, /compact, and /new advice and never received the session key. Both production callers (the execution error handler and fallback settlement) now pass `turn.sessionKey`. The builder renders the documented `openclaw sessions compact <key> --max-lines` fallback through the existing `quoteCliArg` and `formatCliCommand` owners. `formatCliCommand` adds `--profile`/`--container` when the Gateway runs under one. The heartbeat-bleed hint still replaces the generic model hint.

Quoting:
- Ordinary keys like `agent:main:main` stay bare and work in every shell. This addresses the last open review finding on #149415.
- When a key needs quoting, the reply labels two forms.
  - For macOS, Linux, or PowerShell, it uses single quotes, which keep `!` and `$` literal.
  - For Windows Command Prompt, it uses double quotes. cmd.exe would keep single quotes as part of the key, and inside double quotes it leaves `!` and `$` literal while delayed expansion is off, which is the default.
- `sessions compact` has no key-free selector (it takes only `<key>`), so a shell-specific form is the smallest supported route.

/new stays because an explicit reset writes a `context: "clear"` boundary (`session-hooks.ts`). The issue comment's other root cause, `/new` rejected by the preflight compaction gate (#121617), was closed by #172912, which is already in this base. The Feishu/WeCom reset-remapping theory in the issue is still unverified and is out of scope here. The preflight-compaction failure copy in `agent-runner-failure-reply.ts` is a separate path, includes timeout failures that can be transient, and is left unchanged.

Builds on #149415 by @aldiz1711 (closed by its author with an invitation to continue). That PR's deletion/backup warning and session-specific command carry over. The single-quote-only rendering that review flagged for cmd.exe is replaced.

## Evidence

Base: rebased onto `879e99cb1` (current `main`). That base includes 25acc454d, which repairs the `ui/src/pages/chat/session-snapshot-store.test.ts` failure behind the earlier red lint/test-types CI lanes. The before/after proof below was recorded on `e032d1e31`, and `main` has not changed these files since then.

**Shipped entry point: Gateway `chat.send`, the WebChat/Control UI path, before and after.**

Setup:
- Real built Gateway and CLI (`pnpm openclaw gateway run`, `node openclaw.mjs gateway call`).
- Isolated state directory and loopback ports.
- One custom `openai-completions` provider pointing at a small loopback server. The server answers every completion with HTTP 400 `context_length_exceeded`.
- One `chat.send` per session key. Replaying the same `idempotencyKey` returns the settled run result, whose error message is the reply text delivered to the chat client.

Gateway log for each turn (same on base and branch):

```text
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 1/3); attempting auto-compaction for fakeoverflow/tiny
[agent/embedded] auto-compaction failed for fakeoverflow/tiny: Nothing to compact (session too small)
[agent/embedded] [context-overflow-recovery] exhausted provider overflow recovery for fakeoverflow/tiny; livenessState=blocked suggestedAction=reset_or_new kind=context_overflow
Auto-compaction failed (400 This model's maximum context length is 8192 tokens. However, your messages resulted in 250000 tokens. Please reduce the length of the messages.). Preserving existing session mapping for agent:main:main.
```

Base build (`e032d1e31`), `sessionKey: "agent:main:main"`:

```text
$ openclaw gateway call chat.send --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:main","message":"hello from the proof","idempotencyKey":"proof-before-1"}'
{ "runId": "proof-before-1", "status": "started" }
$ (same call again, same idempotencyKey: settled result)
"message": "⚠️ Auto-compaction could not recover this turn. I kept this conversation mapped to the current session. Please try again, use /compact, or use /new to start a fresh session.\n\nTry starting a fresh session or using a model with a larger context window."
```

Branch build, `sessionKey: "agent:main:main"`:

```text
"message": "⚠️ Auto-compaction could not recover this turn. I kept this conversation mapped to the current session. Use /new to start a fresh session.\n\nTry a model with a larger context window.\n\nTo keep this session instead, an operator can trim its transcript. Trimming permanently deletes older history and keeps no backup, so run `openclaw backup create` first if that history matters, then `openclaw sessions compact agent:main:main --agent main --max-lines 200`."
```

Branch build, `sessionKey: "agent:main:matrix:channel:!ops:example.org:thread:$RootEvent:Example.Org"`:

```text
"message": "⚠️ Auto-compaction could not recover this turn. … then `openclaw sessions compact 'agent:main:matrix:channel:!ops:example.org:thread:$RootEvent:Example.Org' --agent main --max-lines 200` (macOS, Linux, or PowerShell) or `openclaw sessions compact \"agent:main:matrix:channel:!ops:example.org:thread:$RootEvent:Example.Org\" --agent main --max-lines 200` (Windows Command Prompt)."
```

**The displayed Matrix commands, run against that Gateway and its disposable session:**

```text
### POSIX/PowerShell form, pasted into zsh as rendered
$ openclaw sessions compact 'agent:main:matrix:channel:!ops:example.org:thread:$RootEvent:Example.Org' --agent main --max-lines 200
No compaction needed for session agent:main:matrix:channel:!ops:example.org:thread:$RootEvent:Example.Org.
exit=0

### Command Prompt form: cmd.exe strips the double quotes and leaves ! and $ literal; same argv, spawned without a shell
argv: ["sessions","compact","agent:main:matrix:channel:!ops:example.org:thread:$RootEvent:Example.Org","--agent","main","--max-lines","1"]
Compacted session agent:main:matrix:channel:!ops:example.org:thread:$RootEvent:Example.Org (kept 1 lines).
exit=0

### Single-quoted form as cmd.exe would forward it (quote characters kept): the case this PR now avoids
Compaction failed: Session 'agent:main:matrix:channel:!ops:example.org:thread:$RootEvent:Example.Org' not found. Run openclaw sessions list --json to choose a valid key.
exit=1
```

**Tests:**
- Failing before (new assertions, production code at base):
  - `agent-runner-context-recovery.test.ts`: 5 failed / 1 passed. The trim-command case fails on the old `...Please try again, use /compact, or use /new...` copy. It asserts that the reply has no `/compact` and that the no-backup warning, `openclaw backup create` and the session-specific command appear in that order. It no longer pins the whole paragraph; that was narrowed after review, and the base still fails 5 / 1 at `331be5dc9`.
  - `agent-runner-execution-context-failures.test.ts`: 3 failed / 1 passed.
  - The labeled-forms Matrix case fails on the previous single-quote-only head.
- Passing after:
  - `agent-runner-context-recovery.test.ts`: 6 passed.
  - `agent-runner-execution-context-failures.test.ts`: 4 passed. This suite runs both production callers through `executeAgentTurn`.
  - `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` (full file): 234 passed.
- Checks:
  - `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base e032d1e31 -- <changed files>`: format, lint, core typecheck, and core test typecheck pass. The only red lanes (max-lines suppression ratchet in `ui/src/pages/**` and the core test shard root budget) are already red on the base and unrelated to these files.
  - `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`: 0 cycles.
  - Autoreview: no P0–P2 findings.
  - Rerun after narrowing the test (`check-changed --base 879e99cb1`, madge, autoreview): format, full typecheck and the import-cycle check pass, and autoreview is clean. The remaining red lanes cover none of these files: `max-lines` in untouched files, unused exports in `src/logging/diagnostic-*` and two test-support files, and the core test shard root budget.
- Test cost, `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall time on a heavily loaded host:
  - `agent-runner-context-recovery.test.ts`: 22s, mostly transform.
  - `agent-runner-execution-context-failures.test.ts`: 16s.
  - `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts`: 102–245s for the existing 234-test file; only two assertions changed.
  - No new test files.

**Gaps:**
- In this run, auto-compaction fails with "nothing to compact" (one-message session) rather than because the compaction request itself overflows, as in the issue. Both outcomes reach the same "Auto-compaction failed … Preserving existing session mapping" branch and the same reply builder.
- No Windows host and no PowerShell here. The Command Prompt form is shown by spawning the exact argv cmd.exe forwards. The single-quoted form follows the same literal rules in PowerShell as in POSIX shells.

prs.title: perf(ui): yield warm routing after sidebar restore
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A warm short-link reload can mount the sidebar and the conversation pane inside the same IndexedDB completion task. The browser cannot paint or accept input until that task finishes. Closed select pickers also read computed direction during mounting, adding unnecessary style work.

## User Impact

Publish the admitted cached roster immediately, then release waiting chat routing through a posted browser task. The sidebar can paint before the pane mounts. Connection and disposal still release routing immediately; the posted callback cannot republish stale state. Projection ownership, retained receipts, and storage formats stay intact.

Pickers now read direction and bind their anchor when opening; submenu keyboard navigation still reads the current direction. There is no new cache, configuration, or dependency.

## Evidence

Four concurrent A/B pairs compared base `ec36f9b9617a8d668a660d97e262a861453d9246` with this complete change. Each pair held the exclusive measurement lock, used separate browser state/ports on two 16-core CPU halves, and swapped halves on the next pair. Warm navigation starts differed by at most 1 ms. Outside CPU load was recorded for context. The fixture has 80 retained messages, 80 sessions, five pending inputs, session metadata, and 150 commands.

Decisions use B minus A within each pair, in milliseconds:

| Metric | Pair 1 | Pair 2 | Pair 3 | Pair 4 | Median paired difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Warm FCP | -16 | -52 | 0 | -4 | **-10** |
| Restore-frame blocking | -17.5 | -26.3 | -8.9 | -15.5 | **-16.5** |
| Final retained message visible | -38.9 | -30.5 | -3.6 | -17.6 | **-24.1** |
| Final sidebar rows stable | -15.2 | -53.2 | -4.0 | +0.7 | **-9.6** |

Cold FCP was neutral/improved in every pair (median -2 ms); the final retained message was also earlier in every cold pair. Final rows match. Warm `chat.startup` retains all three receipts, sends zero messages, and stays **306 wire bytes / 224 payload bytes** in every pair. Cold response size stays 154,318 bytes. These synthetic byte counts are not production payload estimates.

A separate source-mapped trace confirms the boundary: the sidebar IDB task falls from **60.9 to 14.2 ms**, and `MountedPane` moves into the following MessagePort task. That traced comparison isolates scheduling on top of the picker change. Profiling is diagnostic only: browsers can coalesce the tasks into one frame, so this creates a paint opportunity rather than guaranteeing a paint. The approximate historical 52 ms frame / 1–2 ms blocking target is not consistently reached. In the final campaign one candidate restore produced no frame above the 50 ms LoAF threshold; that means no observed long frame, not zero work.

The picker regression proves closed ordinary/submenu style reads fall **2/3 → 0**. Its isolated four-pair startup result was mixed/near-neutral; the table above measures the complete PR.

Two swapped pairs per historical single reversal of #175575, #175571, and #175565 did not identify a reproducible large restore-blocking culprit. A compatible-cache r153/r154 comparison also changed direction between pairs. This PR fixes the observed task boundary without claiming historical commit attribution.

## Proof

- Focused Chromium picker files: 40/40 passed. WebKit picker behavior: 21/21 passed.
- Cached-roster owner: 30/30 passed; route warm boot: 9/9 passed.
- Regressions fail on old code: eager picker reads, and all three early route-settlement cases (normal delivery, connection, disposal).
- Changed-file formatting, scoped lint, and diff checks passed. Two independent reviews found no actionable issues.
- [Full PR CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39060191492) on `12b9d1c6997330a11ec741bcfd181cebd5546e1f`: 40 completed checks passed, including `openclaw/ci-gate`, with none pending or failing at merge. No Testbox lease or local full build/suite was used.
- Benchmark builds used the same isolated Linux dependency graph for both sides: exact Solid runtime/compiler; Vite 8.3.2 versus repository 8.3.4 and Playwright 1.63 versus 1.64, plus some CodeMirror patch differences. This limits absolute production comparisons, not the paired source comparison.

Production delta: +22 lines; tests: +75. The added lines implement the browser-task handoff and preserve accepted-open/RTL behavior. No duplicate owner or compatibility path remains.

Before and after final-state screenshots are byte-identical and synthetic-only; timing evidence is above.

![Before: base warm reload with final sidebar and transcript](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0524bca-3854-471f-884e-e079e7b4768b)

![After: split warm restore with the same final sidebar and transcript](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b7809a53-3660-4652-8c84-6a7577cc88e6)

prs.title: refactor(storage): trust supported runtime Zstd availability
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The shared Zstd codec repeats unsupported-runtime availability handling in its callers even though every supported runtime provides the required synchronous methods.

## User Impact

No intended change on supported Node/Bun installations. Existing identity and Zstd data remain readable, with the same compression settings and integrity bounds. ## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI wire-tool preparation keeps bounded variants of three small wrapper objects per published schema, freezes those wrappers, and prewarms them at descriptor settlement. Expensive schema publication and normalization already have separate owners; the request builders need only wrap their prepared parameters.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change is intended. Tool request shapes and immutable parameter publication remain unchanged; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Build request-owned Responses and Completions wire wrappers directly. Keep the function signature and wire shape, strict-flag omission, canonical immutable schema publications, normalization caches, descriptor snapshots, and per-attempt authority untouched. Settlement still prewarms schemas but no longer constructs discarded wire wrappers. Replace wrapper identity/freeze assertions with wire-shape/schema-reuse coverage; keep request-local cache-marker assertions and all behavioral schema tests.

Production delta: +4/-34, **30 net lines removed** across two production files. Tests: +7/-3, four net lines added. Whole change: four files, +11/-37. No public API, Plugin SDK, configuration, protocol, persisted-data, schema, or durability changes.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Repeated conversion allocates tiny wire wrappers instead of sharing a cached identity. [#170610](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/170610), introducing commit `bca779eac0c`, explicitly reports no demonstrated overall CPU or latency reduction. This removes only wrapper caching, not its expensive schema/descriptor publication work; no performance improvement is claimed.
- Request wrappers are no longer frozen just because their parameters were published. The introducing PR records nested in-place mutation as a compatibility follow-up, not a security boundary or cited human incident. Published parameter trees remain detached and immutable, and request-specific cache markers remain local.
- Settlement does not prebuild wrapper variants that request builders can construct directly. Future requests may allocate their wrappers then; retained strict/loose schema warming still avoids the substantive normalization work.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

- Actual unavailable-store reads exercise both native admission and reclamation. A local worker timeout is injected at the read boundary and passed through the real cron error and retry classifiers.

## User Impact

CLI plugin metadata inspection can read a busy live database without waiting for its files to stop changing. Offline, unverifiable-owner, inherited-snapshot, and schema-maintenance reads retain artifact-preserving behavior. Snapshot errors still fail with their existing diagnostics; unreadable inventory is never treated as empty.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared snapshot worker now checks the exact database's recorded Gateway or embedded-writer owner using the existing process-identity verifier. A verified live owner selects the existing online-backup implementation, which pins one read transaction and permits normal SHM read marks. Other sources retain private copying. Physical identity, admission, and cleanup checks remain in place.

Removed the separate metadata snapshot operation and its extra dispatch; metadata now uses the shared snapshot lifecycle. Native backup runs in a one-shot child, retaining the existing protection against persistent-IPC backup stalls. No schema, stored-data, or user-config changes.

## Evidence

- Regression: concurrent checkpointing of a 32 MiB WAL database exhausts all 10 raw-copy attempts. Live-owner acquisition then succeeds, passes `integrity_check`, preserves equal transaction generations, and keeps the retained snapshot below 34 MiB.
- Absent and unverifiable owners remain byte-neutral; a replaced source identity is rejected. Config metadata and the write snapshot used by plugin updates both validate while a recorded live owner checkpoints the database, without main-thread SQL.
- Isolated, fully ready Gateway on the committed tree: `pnpm openclaw config validate --json` returned `valid:true`, `warnings:[]`; `pnpm openclaw plugins update --all --dry-run` exited 0 with no tracked installs. Gateway stayed alive through both commands and logged clean shutdown in 131 ms. This was an inventory/preflight smoke, not a package installation. The earlier dirty-tree source launch hit the artifact-publication fence before SQLite; committing the reviewed inputs resolved that launcher-only refusal.
- Focused tests passed: metadata ownership regression, config snapshots, plugin metadata, worker diagnostics, and retained-child compile-cache cleanup. Core and focused test type checks, touched-file oxlint/oxfmt, import-cycle check, line-cap and SQLite worker ratchets passed. Independent Codex review: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Repaired packaging proof: 82 tests passed across the service-relay, wrapper-closure, and state-worker build suites.
- All 77 selected sibling/focused files passed across the recorded runs. The final 55-file sweep passed 623 tests with five pre-existing skips in 782.66 s; the earlier 11-file unit lane passed 86 tests, all 8 tooling files passed after the packaging fix, and the final focused run passed 101 tests. The final sweep retained original file order in its invocation and used one worker. The unchanged `test/scripts/vitest-worker-artifacts.test.ts` took 185.869 s (30 tests); its slowest case, “builds changed source despite valid stale dist and fails visibly on build errors,” took 38.456 s because it builds full worker graphs and reconstructs the fixture checkout. No timeouts or retries were raised.
- Full `check:changed` SQLite inventory was omitted under the local gate budget. The max-lines checker reports inherited suppressions in untouched `chat-message.test.tsx`, `config-page-state.ts`, and `sessions-page-state.ts`; these files match the starting HEAD.

Production: +92/-188 (net -96). Tests: +250/-8 (net +242). Documentation: +8/-0. Wrapper inventory: -1 obsolete entry.

<details>
<summary>Focused and live proof commands</summary>

All runtime commands used isolated `HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` beneath the worktree’s `.artifacts/l1676/`; no existing Gateway was used or stopped.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts test/scripts/tsdown-config.test.ts test/scripts/pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts test/scripts/state-read-worker-build.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-readonly-location.metadata.test.ts src/config/io.load-async.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# 101 tests passed across the 6 selected files.

# Waited for /readyz: HTTP 200.

# Exit 0: valid=true, warnings=[].
pnpm openclaw plugins update --all --dry-run
# Exit 0: No tracked plugins or hook packs to update.
# The task-owned Gateway remained running, then joined its SIGTERM shutdown.
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): steer compatible inputs into admitted direct runs
prs.body:
Related: #163058, #163064

## What Problem This Solves

Compatible ordinary input can be queued instead of steering an admitted direct embedded run that has no ReplyOperation. Restore that path without allowing a different model, explicit credential profile or execution restrictions to borrow the old run's authority.

## User Impact

Eligible corrections reach the existing run. Incompatible input stays on the protected follow-up path rather than silently using the active run's model, account or execution permissions. No configuration key, deployment step or persisted format is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture the original direct target and source identity before asynchronous preparation. Project current caller facts through that captured owner, but retain incoming model/profile/session/workspace/exec/elevated facts as comparison inputs. The canonical full fingerprint checks both live owner/caller authority and incoming execution compatibility; the captured target route must not overwrite an explicit incoming selection. This preserves the compatibility intent of #158699 / 13747e05516a95003941b99e0d70bb9cced74419.

Loss of authority still refuses input. Only a definite execution mismatch before an injection attempt exists returns it to follow-up custody; accepted or indeterminate input is not replayed. No backend is retargeted and no second authority controller is added. Typing refresh requires a real ReplyOperation. Embedded dispatch retains its execution level, and absent profile selection does not fabricate automatic-selection provenance.

This revision is synchronized onto upstream 03da25412dc17ecb7562f19dd8dcac86d3d2f40f, preserving its current authority-input and inbound owners. Incoming and direct-owner authority both retain forceRestartSafeTools / forceCodeModeTools. Steering capture and terminal-receipt checks share the existing steering module; the line limit is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Behavior addressed

The earlier candidate's fresh review identified a P1: its caller-only projection erased incompatible execution selections. On the earlier source base, four real canonical-owner regressions failed before repair for model/profile/elevated/exec changes while the unchanged control passed; they passed after repair. An initial trace-mismatched control was rejected as invalid and is not counted as product-failure proof.

### CI/review follow-up to the reviewed source

The review of `9a444799be6ee3b190a5e3286ee3b8580b3b0647` accepted the supplied real behavior output and resolved the earlier execution-compatibility/security findings. It found a separate P1 introduced by the steering extraction: the terminal-receipt follow-up branch used a reason variable no longer in caller scope, throwing after enqueueing but before admission recording and drain scheduling.

This follow-up returns that same reason from the existing helper and destructures it in the caller. A real `getReplyFromConfig` / `runReplyAgent` regression reproduces the exact ReferenceError on the public caller/helper bytes, then verifies successful follow-up admission, one retained queue item, actual call-through drain scheduling, the terminal-pending diagnostic and no native injection after repair. The two related caller/binding/fencing files pass 28/28 on the repaired source. No assertions, admission predicates or authority comparisons were weakened.

The execution overlay now declares its portable field shape without importing the deferred queue's full run type into the registry contract. The canonical Madge check reports zero cycles. The test fixture selects `modelId` from the actual harness-attempt interface rather than the higher-level embedded-run input. These are type-only corrections; execution selection and restrictions are unchanged. All four follow-up paths pass formatting and scoped lint.

The reviewed source's 174 checks were terminal: 79 success, 73 skipped, 1 neutral, 18 failure and 3 Auto-response concurrency cancellations. Actual checkout logs and diagnostics bind the failures to its merge commit: 16 root jobs reported the missing reason, one root job reported the type dependency cycle, and one job was an aggregate gate; one type root also reported the fixture-interface errors repaired here. This is not an inherited-main claim or a rerun-to-green claim.

Prepared follow-up commit: `dbd8a9707e49ac71dd2e98a18c3fffdd819b99bd`, parent `9a444799be6ee3b190a5e3286ee3b8580b3b0647`. Four paths differ from the reviewed source. The real native/provider/transcript pair below remains bound to the source published as that parent; it is not relabeled as a fresh execution of this follow-up. This repair changes diagnostic-reason plumbing and erased type contracts/fixture typing, not the matched pair's authority comparison or native-effect path. The changed terminal fallback has its separate red-to-green caller proof above. No completed compiler pass, new-head broad CI result, maintainer approval or merge is claimed for this follow-up.

### Current-main synchronization

The same 12-file fix is now based on `03da25412dc17ecb7562f19dd8dcac86d3d2f40f`. The dispatch-test conflict preserves upstream prepared-auth/no-auth and retry coverage alongside this PR's four credential-source cases. Current main's owner and lifecycle changes are retained; there is no separate compaction or UI patch in this PR.

Synchronized commit: `bdc4f54240222e51aa470de47be10f97c38194de`. Current-source qualification: dispatch **24/24**, caller/binding/fencing **28/28**, execution authority **11/11** (**63/63** total). All 12 paths pass formatting. Script type-aware lint and focused boundary guards pass with unchanged rules. Core type-aware lint reports one max-lines error: dispatch is 713 counted lines against the 700-line limit. A diagnostic-specific replay of the exact main-file bytes reports the same rule at 710 lines; this is not a full baseline replay or a passing core lint result. No rule was disabled and no unrelated refactor was added. Broad compilation subsequently passed in the exact-head CI run below.

[Exact-head CI run 39058540101](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39058540101) completed successfully (attempt 1). All 147 recorded check runs are terminal: 92 success, 54 skipped and 1 neutral, with no failed check run. Separate security-sensitive-review / aggregate commit statuses still require a maintainer to approve this exact revision; no maintainer approval or merge is claimed. The real native/provider/transcript pair below remains historical evidence bound to `9a444799`. It is not relabeled as a new execution on this base. Current caller/dispatch composition has the focused regression qualification above.


### Evidence after fix

- On the source published as `9a444799`: 11/11 canonical-owner checks, including both newly retained tool-mode restrictions. Those owner/runtime bytes remain unchanged through the final steering-only extraction. Final caller/binding/fencing suites: 27/27, including both different-tool-mode owner cases; final dispatch suite: 17/17. The two new tool-mode controls have no separately executed pre-repair baseline.
- All 12 changed paths passed formatting and scoped lint without disabling rules. A strict focused native CLI typecheck with all 12 changed roots, canonical test-shard declarations and transitive imports did not complete within its bounded run. It ended with exit 137 and no diagnostics; the exact termination cause is unverified. It is inconclusive, not a compiler pass or identified source error. - Fresh matched real pair on this private source: 2/2 accepted, eight runtime inputs bound to the actual compiled borrower/generation, zero production-path/network tripwire violations, test resources and listeners released. The real native owner remains the decision maker. Compatible input steers without a ReplyOperation. Changed execution settings remain follow-ups; independently, original-owner role removal at held preparation refuses input before native acceptance, model consumption and canonical user-row commit.

prs.title: fix(heartbeat): isolated heartbeats resume the same native thread on every run
prs.body:
Closes #175365

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes isolated heartbeats repeatedly resuming the same Codex thread, accumulating earlier heartbeat turns and increasing context until native compaction.

## User Impact

Each heartbeat with `isolatedSession: true` starts a fresh native session. Ordinary conversation continuity, stable heartbeat session keys, usage attribution, and transcript lineage remain intact. No configuration or schema migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The isolated heartbeat rollover preserves predecessor lineage for usage and transcripts. Without retiring native ownership first, the next generation adopts the predecessor's thread. This uses the existing harness reset operation before replacing the isolated session, just as ordinary session rollovers do.

Original fix by @LiuwqGit; thanks to @zionhann for the report and production evidence. The contributor's commit is retained.

## Evidence

Built Gateway + real bundled Codex 0.162.0 app-server, with only the OpenAI Responses HTTP endpoint replaced by a loopback provider:

| Three scheduled isolated heartbeats | Distinct native threads | Model-request input bytes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline `d93ad5fc0e31` | 1 | 13,405 → 26,142 → 38,879 |
| Current candidate `fe8b6317c233` | 3 | 14,301 → 14,301 → 14,301 |

After merging current main's heartbeat construction cleanup, the focused tests, Gateway heartbeat proof, and live provider check were repeated on `fe8b6317c233`. The request size remains constant across all three runs.

The ordinary non-heartbeat control retained its native thread on both sides: control turns 2–3 reused one thread after initial setup. Actual app-server `thread/start`, `thread/resume`, and `turn/start` requests were recorded.

A separate live check on final head `fe8b6317c233` used the real OpenAI `gpt-5-mini` endpoint through the Codex harness, with low reasoning: returned `LIVE_GATE_OK`, 5,695 input tokens and 140 output tokens. Credentials were task-scoped and deleted afterward.

Focused validation on the merged head: 15 tests passed across the native-retirement regression, isolated-key stability, isolated-session mirror, and exact-session busy suites. Changed-file Oxfmt and Oxlint passed before the main merge. The simplified regression fails on the baseline because the native reset is absent, while its first-run and ordinary-heartbeat cases pass.

The mock-export ratchet also passes with the explicit delivery-isolation annotation restored; its scanner reports the violation without the annotation and none with it.

The simplification removes the test's duplicate in-memory binding/adoption implementation and channel-routing scaffolding. Native behavior is covered by the real Gateway proof instead. Against the merge base: production +17 lines, tests +85 lines; versus the contributor revision: production −3 and tests −212. Existing heartbeat documentation already promises fresh isolated sessions and is unchanged.

Merge risk: this affects native-harness cleanup at isolated-heartbeat rollover. Reverting restores the previous behavior for future runs; already-created native threads remain distinct. There is no schema or public API change.

prs.title: feat(agents): show input progress for every streaming tool call
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a model streams a long argument for any tool other than write, edit or apply_patch, no progress is reported while the input is generated, which can take minutes. An embedding client that watches the run sees nothing until the tool starts. If it enforces idle or turn deadlines, it ends up killing generations that are slow but healthy.

## User Impact

Clients now receive the existing counts-only `tool` / `input_delta` event for every tool call while its input streams. The event carries the tool name, the call id and `inputChars`, the streamed argument length so far. File-mutation tools still add their `diff` line counts as before. Events never include argument content. Clients that read only `diff` keep working, because they already skip `input_delta` events that have no `diff`.

## Why This Change Was Made

#121528 added a bounded, throttled counter for live edit progress. This PR widens it instead of adding a second path:

- Every tool call reports `inputChars` under the same 250ms throttle and 64-call bound. Reading the length costs O(1) and nothing is parsed.
- Only file-mutation tools parse, and only under the 1 MiB cap. Past the cap their line counts freeze while the length keeps reporting. Before this change, an oversized edit stopped reporting entirely.
- The gateway progress snapshot keeps `inputChars`, so reconnect replay shows the same event.

Relation to #167789 (CLI backend progress for Write/Edit, now on main): main split the counter into `updateLiveEditDiffProgressFromInput`, which takes `partialJsonLength` separately from a lazy `readPartialJson`. This PR applies the all-tool change inside that shared function: the length alone drives `inputChars`, and only file-mutation tools under the parse cap call `readPartialJson`. So CLI backend runs also get progress for every tool, still without assembling cumulative arguments for other tools. Main's CLI tests now expect `inputChars` on each event.

One limitation is unchanged by this PR. Claude 5-family models on `anthropic-messages` use the streaming-refusal contract, which holds all deltas until the terminal event. They therefore get no live `input_delta` events, for edits or any other tool.

## Evidence

- Base: `72ccf6ff92931fff2d49473fe1571f39e8311ad2` (upstream main, merged in `efcb0ca662`)
- Candidate: `2bb1f3562e0`

### Real Gateway run (shipped entry point)

`pnpm build` at `465aba3` (later commits change only the in-process test), then `openclaw gateway run` as a separate process with token auth, in a throwaway `HOME`. A standalone loopback Anthropic-format provider streams a ~40KB `read` argument in 16 `input_json_delta` chunks, 500 ms apart. Observer A is a `tool-events` client: it sends one `chat.send` and logs every `tool` event. After three progress events, observer B connects as a fresh client while the input is still streaming and reads `chat.history`. `argumentText` is whether the event JSON contains a marker string that appears only inside the streamed argument.

```text
$ openclaw --version: OpenClaw 2026.10.3 (465aba3)
$ openclaw gateway run --port 18789   (model mock-anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5)
2026-10-14T03:34:50.843-04:00 [gateway] starting HTTP server...
2026-10-14T03:34:53.136-04:00 [gateway] http server listening
[observer A] + 2713ms chat.send -> status=started runId=live-1791963300798
[observer A] + 4425ms tool phase=input_delta name=read id=call_large_read inputChars=2520 diff=absent argumentText=false
[observer A] + 4905ms tool phase=input_delta name=read id=call_large_read inputChars=5040 diff=absent argumentText=false
[observer A] + 5406ms tool phase=input_delta name=read id=call_large_read inputChars=7560 diff=absent argumentText=false
[observer B] + 5500ms reconnected; observer A last saw inputChars=7560
[observer B] + 5500ms chat.history inFlightRun replay: tool phase=input_delta name=read inputChars=7560 diff=absent
```

prs.title: fix: refresh workspace bases with missing partial-clone contents
prs.body:
Fixes #175710

## What Problem This Solves

Refreshing a guest workspace can fail after Git reports a successful fetch of the selected base. A partial clone may already know the commits while still missing their file contents. Offline integration also needs older file versions from merge bases, so fetching only the selected tip is insufficient for diverged branches.

## User Impact

`github_publish` with `action: "refresh_base"` now prepares missing contents through the selected repository's authenticated host transport before offline integration. Fetch failures preserve saved work for retry. Guest edits, ignored data, conflict recovery, and private sandbox Git history keep their existing contracts; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Refresh explicitly requests content preparation from its existing Git transport owner. It discovers missing objects without lazy fetching, fetches them in an authenticated batch, and verifies availability before continuing. It also prepares the common ancestor versions Git needs when combining multiple merge bases. This keeps preparation limited to relevant tree versions. Other publication callers retain ordinary ancestry-only fetching.

Retained integrations reuse their already-present commit, and complete trees need no additional content fetch. Current-authority and cancellation checks guard the preparation steps. Snapshot and packing operations retain their offline configuration boundary.

## Evidence

Remote formatting, lint, and affected production/test types passed. The related proof covers 138 passing cases across ten files, with one existing opt-in Podman case skipped; unchanged importing-test and consumer proof was reused after the correction.

The changed action file was rechecked with `pnpm test src/gateway/github-publication-actions.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **31 passed, 109.77 seconds wall time** (106.26 seconds reported by Vitest). The expanded refresh scenario took 23.936 seconds and exercises the registered tool/Gateway entry, real Git, projection journal, conflict recovery, and review-base transfer. The file's remaining time covers its existing action/authority/publication variants; hosted CI passed, with the expanded scenario taking 9.028 seconds in its 64.06-second two-file shard.

The fixture includes missing selected-tip blobs, two merge bases with a missing older ancestor blob, an unavailable configured promisor, rejected content fetching, cancellation after discovery, preserved guest data, no ordinary commit refetch on retained integrations, and no extra content fetch for complete trees. An independent real-Git counterexample demonstrated offline merge failure after tip-only hydration and success after fetching the missing ancestor.

A separate public-GitHub control fetched an absent blob by OID using the production `--refetch --stdin` command, verified its exact Git hash and 12,061 bytes, and created no refs or `FETCH_HEAD`. The registered-action suite uses synthetic GitHub responses and sandbox execution; no private-account authentication or deployment claim is made. Independent re-review is clean. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39058797747) passed; ClawSweeper reports no findings, Gold overall and Platinum patch quality.

prs.title: fix(cli): keep read commands off the writable shared state DB
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Several CLI inspection paths could re-enter task and TaskFlow runtime restore through writable state owners. On a host with a running Gateway, commands such as task listing/audit, maintenance preview, TaskFlow inspection, and default plugin inventory could therefore create or migrate the shared state database, or record configuration observation, despite being read-only operations.

This change makes those inspection restores fail closed when the existing state DB is older than the current schema, rather than opening it writable. It preserves the writable migration path for explicit mutations.

## Why This Change Was Made

#124110 now owns the generic non-creating, non-migrating state/doctor loaders. This PR has been reshaped after it and drops the overlapping work.

The remaining scope is limited to the unique guarantees:

- task and TaskFlow runtime inspection restores use a current-schema read-only state DB path;
- explicit task and flow mutations still restore writable state and may migrate it;
- plugin/task inspection config reads use an internal non-observing config seam;
- channels status has regression coverage for its non-observing fallback config reads;
- task maintenance preview does not promote a failed read-only restore into a writable migration.

No schema version, public config option, or CLI flag is added.

Refs: #119583, #120222

#120222 is retained as resilience context only. This PR does not change Gateway startup ordering or claim to resolve that open product decision.

## User Impact

Read-only CLI inspection no longer creates or migrates `state/openclaw.sqlite`. If a task or TaskFlow inspection encounters an older state schema, it explains how to repair it (`openclaw doctor --fix` or starting the Gateway) without changing the DB.

Explicit mutation commands, including task notification/cancellation and flow cancellation, retain their existing writable migration behavior.

## Evidence

- Rebased and narrowed on current `openclaw/main` after #124110.
- Focused tests: 98/98 passing across 7 files, including old-schema assertions that inspection leaves `user_version` unchanged and mutations can then migrate.
- Targeted formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- `CI=true pnpm build` completed.
- Local autoreview completed clean.

prs.title: fix(acp): generated sessions fail without an agent owner
prs.body:
Closes #137247

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where IDE users in explicit multi-agent setups could create an ACP session but have its first prompt rejected because the generated session had no agent owner. An explicit shared session key worked around ownership but lost per-editor-thread isolation.

## User Impact

Users can select an OpenClaw agent with `openclaw acp --agent <id>` while retaining a unique session for each editor thread. Local sessions preserve recorded fixed-store ownership; other local sessions use the existing system/sole-agent selection policy. Remote connections selected by `--url`, `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL`, or `gateway.mode: "remote"` defer ownership to the remote Gateway: explicit agents are forwarded, and an omitted agent leaves the generated key bare for Gateway resolution. An explicit remote fleet that cannot resolve an owner still requires `--agent` or an existing agent-owned session key/label.

The new bridge-specific `--agent` interface remains subject to maintainer acceptance as requested in the linked issue. This repair does not add another public option or change `acp.defaultAgent`, Gateway ownership policy, schemas, or persisted-session migration behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Generated local session keys include their selected owner, except implicit fixed-store sessions retain a bare key for Gateway ownership; explicit session-key and session-label routing keep precedence. The bridge now consumes the shared Gateway bootstrap's resolved URL override provenance, so environment-selected remote targets cannot accidentally use the client's local agent roster. Documentation describes both local defaults and the remote implicit-owner exception.

The repair incorporates main `7bc4491e537` to resolve the actual merge conflict, preserving main's asynchronous state-database shutdown and the PR's agent-ID validation. The original PR branch/history is retained.

## Evidence

This update preserves the existing production ACP repair and history. It fixes two CI test regressions: startup cases now remain inside their shared lifecycle cleanup, and the generated local-session expectation includes its selected owner.

Current candidate `d7bfd3bbae22` was checked with Node 24.19.0 and pinned pnpm 12.9.0 on macOS arm64:

- Startup suite: **22/22 passed**; session setup suite: **27/27 passed**, each through its unique native test owner.
- Both affected tests passed formatting, type-aware lint and strict scoped TypeScript checks. The qualified native Gateway build also passed.
- The official CLI, real ACP stdio, separate isolated Gateway, production session persistence and a loopback HTTP/SSE model completed **five prompt scenarios across two executions**: two isolated local editor threads, restart/load of the first thread, and remote CLI URL routing with implicit and explicit agent selection. All completed prompts returned `end_turn` and the expected response marker; persisted owner was `ops` throughout. The local thread keys were distinct; implicit remote routing retained a bare generated key for Gateway resolution.

The first execution completed all three local scenarios but then failed remote initialization because the fixture omitted explicit remote credentials; that whole validation remains failed. After supplying the task token explicitly, only the two unfinished remote scenarios were run and the native validation passed (exit 0, 27.072 seconds). No passed local suites or prompt scenarios were repeated. Both executions joined owned processes with the Gateway's native clean-shutdown receipt and CLI exit 0; the remote pass checked unchanged source identity after cleanup.

<details>
<summary>Current remote proof excerpt and limits</summary>

```text
Validation acp-remote-url-owned-session-gateway-proof-20261018: pass; exit_code=0; 27072ms
remote-cli-url-implicit-owner: newSession=ok; key=acp-bridge:<uuid>; persistedOwner=ops; end_turn; modelRequests=1
remote-cli-url-explicit-owner: newSession=ok; key=agent:ops:acp-bridge:<uuid>; persistedOwner=ops; end_turn; modelRequests=1
All retained processes joined; forced cleanup=false; Gateway wrapper exit=0; native clean shutdown=true
Source identity unchanged after cleanup
```

This is current-source proof on one host using a deterministic external model fixture. It does not claim a stable-release upgrade, an external Gateway host, or a real model tenant. Historical environment-selected-remote and fixed-store full Gateway scenarios were not rerun on this candidate; the current focused source suites cover those routing exceptions. Earlier CI and proof observations belong to their earlier heads, and hosted CI for this update is still pending. Acceptance of the public `--agent` selector remains a maintainer decision.

</details>

Providers that serve Muse Wonder under the unversioned `muse-wonder` id (OpenRouter, Kilocode, Venice) don't match the curated recommended-models list, which only contains `muse-wonder-1`.

## User Impact

Muse Wonder now shows as recommended on OpenRouter, Kilocode and Venice as well as Meta. Pricing, metadata, defaults, configuration and automation are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only `scripts/lib/recommended-models.json` changes: `muse-wonder` is added immediately after `muse-wonder-1`. Meta serves `muse-wonder-1.0`, which normalizes to `muse-wonder-1`; the unversioned id normalizes to `muse-wonder` and so needs its own entry. It's the same model rather than a successor, so `muse-wonder-1` stays for Meta coverage. Sources: [Meta pricing and rate limits](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits), [OpenRouter listing](https://openrouter.ai/meta/muse-wonder), [OpenClaw catalog v2](https://catalog.openclaw.ai/models/v2/catalog.json).

**Skipped:** all other catalog changes, including other additions, removals, reordering, metadata or pricing edits, defaults, configuration and automation.

## Evidence

- Based on main `ec36f9b9617`. The daily model-catalog advisory validated the proposal `[{"op":"add","id":"muse-wonder","after":"muse-wonder-1"}]` against pinned main `176df466214`; the list is unchanged between the two.

prs.title: perf(ui): reuse swarm descriptors across unchanged child updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI repeatedly describes a swarm parent when child updates repeat an unchanged ancestor or a provider finishes before its collector result settles.

## User Impact

Swarm activity sends fewer redundant Gateway reads while retaining collector-owned progress, member details, and current child presentation. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The connection-scoped describe owner now retains reads across ancestor references, which certify content already delivered by a full snapshot. Full snapshots, missing ancestor coverage, reconnects, explicit refreshes, and subscription outages retain their invalidation behavior.

Swarm hydration stops comparing child provider status with collector status: those deliberately differ until collector completion. Parent summary and membership changes still refresh details. The shared row-provenance owner already preserves omitted member details, so the duplicate hydrator merge is removed. Production delta: 6 additions, 24 deletions (net -18 lines).

## Evidence

Headless Chromium, synthetic mock Gateway, one visible parent pane with its Details/Subagents panel, 16 children, identical virtual-clock playback before and after:

| Trigger (16 events each) | Before describes | After describes |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Child updates with unchanged full ancestor | 0 | 0 |
| Child messages | 0 | 0 |
| Unchanged ancestor references | 16 | 1 |
| Provider terminal while collector remains running | 16 | 0 |
| Actual collector progress changes | 16 | 16 |
| Total | 48 | 17 |

This removes 64.6% of describes in this workload: 3.00 to 1.06 reads per child across the five phases. The 43-second virtual-clock schedule corresponds to 67.0 to 23.7 describes per simulated minute; these are fixture cadence figures, not production throughput. Provider-only completion falls from one describe per child to zero; necessary collector progress reads remain one per child. All runtime describes originate from the parent roster's readParent path. Runtime talk.config, talk.catalog, and sessions.processes.list calls are zero in both captures. Source audit confirms talk reads follow composer identity/focus/picker changes; process reads poll only while their panel is presented. These secondary paths are unchanged. Both browser captures have no page errors and preserve the final 16-completed presentation.

Regression tests first failed on the original code (17 describes instead of 1), then passed with the fix. Focused validation: 69 tests across session-describe.test.ts, swarm-roster.test.ts, and session-row-observation.test.ts; 2.98 seconds wrapper wall time. Changed-file oxfmt and oxlint pass; git diff --check passes. Broad validation ran in PR CI [39058573961](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39058573961) on head `3bdc615f7b7a2a7a7251e050cc2054a5de259b50`: Control UI unit/E2E/performance, changed Node lanes, lint, type checks, docs, architecture/boundary guards, and security checks passed. Required CI gates are green; no reruns or inherited-failure exception were needed. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was allocated under the current validation policy.

Independent Codex autoreview completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings.

The browser figures measure requests under a virtual clock. No appearance change is intended.

## Paired Server Measurement

Replayed that captured descriptor schedule against real, isolated Gateways with the same server build (`f58d46d2a4fee066cc00cefb918d1565dcde945f`) and separate, identical synthetic parent/16-child state. Eight clients per side, four concurrent 43-second A/B pairs under an exclusive measurement lock. Before and after used CPUs 96–111 / 112–127, swapping halves each pair; sequential fixture preparation used CPUs 64–95. Each pair completed all 384 before / 136 after requests. Main-thread CPU came from the benchmark's private thread CPU sampler.

| Pair | Before main-thread CPU | After main-thread CPU | Paired difference (after − before) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 357.606 ms | 252.653 ms | −104.953 ms |
| 2 (swapped) | 359.759 ms | 260.065 ms | −99.694 ms |
| 3 | 349.546 ms | 275.190 ms | −74.356 ms |
| 4 (swapped) | 363.930 ms | 265.731 ms | −98.199 ms |

Mean paired difference: **−94.301 ms**, mean per-pair reduction **26.3%**. Mean CPU totals were 357.710 → 263.410 ms per window. Whole-process CPU also decreased in all four pairs (mean paired difference −134.750 ms).

Both sides shared each start barrier and reported 16 available CPUs with the intended affinity. CPU sample windows were 43.022–43.023 seconds; maximum schedule delay was 87 ms. `mpstat` average busy across the measured cores was 1.359%, 0.651%, 0.532%, and 1.160% by pair, including benchmark and outside load; recorded for context, not used to reject samples. Recorded dirty pages stayed at 25.7–164.2 MiB during the pairs.

This measures server cost of the reduced descriptor traffic, not a full live swarm, provider execution, or production-sized session inventory. It does not establish a total production Gateway CPU reduction. Per-request latency did not improve: pair means were 1.83–1.97 ms before and 2.07–2.27 ms after, with different request density against identical server code. The demonstrated benefits are fewer requests and lower aggregate CPU, while collector updates remain intact.

prs.title: fix(agents): return the full sessions_send reply past the terminal snapshot bound
prs.body:
Related: #175597. This fixes the reply an inline (waiting) `sessions_send` returns. Delayed delivery, where the reply arrives later as an inter-session input, still carries the bounded snapshot and is left for a follow-up.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a waiting `sessions_send` returned the target's final reply cut at 4,096 characters, ending in "…", with no flag that it had been cut. A requester agent that delegated a long brief silently lost its tail and had to ask again.

The reply comes from the run's terminal reply snapshot. That snapshot is deliberately bounded lifecycle evidence (#173548), and both the `agent.wait` path and the in-process followup completion pass it through as `replyText`.

## User Impact

User impact: `sessions_send` now returns the accepted run's complete reply.

- **Reply under 4,096 characters:** unchanged, with no extra request.
- **Reply that may have reached the bound:** any reply ending in the truncation marker `…`. The tool reads the accepted run's own stored reply. If that reply extends the bounded prefix, it is returned in full; if it equals the bounded text (a reply that really ends with `…`), it is returned unchanged and unflagged.
- **Full reply unavailable:** if the stored reply cannot be read (for example after retention), the result keeps the bounded text but now says so: `replyTruncated: true` plus a note to read the rest with `sessions_history`. Nothing is cut silently.

The terminal snapshot bound itself is unchanged, and so is every other consumer of it.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **`src/agents/agent-run-terminal-reply.ts`:** a new `mayBeTruncatedAgentRunTerminalReply` sits next to the bound and its marker. It checks only for the marker: truncation trims the whole retained prefix, so a cut reply can be far below 4,096 characters (4,000 characters, 100 spaces and `TAIL` become 4,000 characters plus `…`).
- **`src/agents/run-wait.ts`:**
  - `readLatestAssistantReply` takes an optional `runId` and then considers only assistant rows whose `__openclaw.runId` matches. It reuses the existing `chat.message.get` fallback for rows that `chat.history` caps.
  - The new `readCompleteAgentRunReply` uses it for any reply ending in `…`. The stored reply decides: if it equals the bounded text, the reply is complete; if it extends the prefix, it is returned in full; otherwise, or if it cannot be read, the result keeps the bounded text with `replyTruncated`.
- **`src/agents/tools/sessions-send-reply-flow.ts`:** `finishSessionsSendReply` is the single point where a waiting send returns its result, whichever source produced it, so the recovery happens there, keyed to the accepted run ID and target session.
- **`src/agents/tools/sessions-send-helpers.ts`:** `sendReplyResult` reports `replyTruncated` and the note.

No config key was added, and the Gateway protocol is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway agent turn, Windows 11.**

- **Gateway:** the built Gateway (`main` `9513b30` vs this branch), with agents `main` and `helper`, and a local OpenAI-compatible mock model.
- **Turn:** one `main` turn through `/v1/chat/completions` (model `openclaw/main`) calls `sessions_send` through `dispatch_action` to `agent:helper:main` and waits.
- **Reply:** `helper` answers with a 60-item brief, 5,708 characters, ending in `END-OF-BRIEF-7f3a`.
- **Measured:** the `sessions_send` tool result that the agent loop handed back to `main`.

![sessions_send full reply](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/175597/sessions-send-full-reply-live-proof.png)

| Build | helper reply | tool result chars | ends with `END-OF-BRIEF-7f3a` | told it was cut | end of the reply `main` received |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` `9513b30` | 5,708 | 4,595 | **no** | **no** | `… Item 44: see https:…` |
| this branch | 5,708 | 6,241 | **yes** | n/a (complete) | `… Item 60: see https://example.com/research/60 … END-OF-BRIEF-7f3a` |

`main` reproduces the report: the reply is cut mid-URL, and nothing tells the requester.

**Regression tests:**

| Test | `main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| `sessions-send-policy.test.ts`: returns the accepted run's full reply when the terminal snapshot hit its bound (unique marker past character 4,096) | fails | passes |
| `run-wait.test.ts`: a bounded reply returns the accepted run's stored reply and ignores a later row from another run | (new API) | passes |
| `run-wait.test.ts`: marks the bounded reply as truncated when the full reply cannot be read | (new API) | passes |
| `run-wait.test.ts`: recovers a truncated reply that trailing whitespace shortened below the bound (4,000 chars + 100 spaces + `TAIL`) | fails with the previous length-based check | passes |
| `run-wait.test.ts`: keeps a complete reply that ends with an ellipsis unflagged | (new API) | passes |
| `run-wait.test.ts`: does not read history for replies without the truncation marker | (new API) | passes |

**Gates:**

- `run-wait*.test.ts`, every `sessions-send*.test.ts` and `agent-run-terminal-reply.test.ts` pass.
- oxfmt, oxlint and `pnpm tsgo:core` pass. All 29 core test-graph type-check shards for the changed paths pass.
- The shard runner still exits 1 on its advisory root-budget check. On this base, `gateway-root` has 727 test roots and `infra` 733, against a limit of 720. This change adds no test files and does not change those counts.
- `pnpm check:changed` could not run locally. Its Crabbox route downloads from github.com, which this network resolves to a private address, so CI covers it.

prs.title: fix(update): target-native-unsupported refusals don't say which candidate check failed
prs.body:
Related: #157105

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `target-native-unsupported` refusals save the same sentence for every executor-check failure, so support bundles can't name the failing condition.

## User Impact

User impact: when an update refuses with `target-native-unsupported`, the saved report (`stderrTail` and `failureFacts`) now names the failed executor-check condition, for example `missing Gateway entrypoint`, `code=1, termination=exit` or `missing retainedOwnerBinding`. Which candidates are accepted or refused does not change. The installed updater runs this check, so the detail appears once the installed version includes this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

In #157105 a maintainer asked for `failureFacts` and `stderrTail` to identify the failing check. A second reporter supplied them. They contain only the generic sentence, and the probe passes on that host when run by hand, so the report can't be diagnosed. The cause is `isUpdatedInstallGatewayExecutorSupported`. It folded about twelve conditions into one boolean and returned `false` silently when the staged root had no `dist/` entrypoint.

The probe now names the first failed condition through an `onUnsupported` callback, the same pattern it already uses for `onDefinitionBackupCapability`. All three refusal messages append `(executor check: <condition>)`:

- the candidate refusal before Gateway stop
- the activation refusal
- the original-definition refusal

The condition text uses only process status (exit code, termination, signal, killed, cleanup) and our own capability field names. It never includes the child's stdout, stderr or any path.

In the activation refusal, a missing install root skips the probe and reads `missing install root`. That branch is a type guard: a missing root already fails entrypoint resolution earlier in the same function (`updated install entrypoint not found`), so it is not reachable today. The candidate refusal defaults to `unreported` in the same way, although the probe always names a condition when it refuses.

<details>
<summary>Condition vocabulary</summary>

- `missing Gateway entrypoint`
- `code=<n>, termination=<exit|timeout|no-output-timeout|signal>[, signal=<SIG>][, killed=true]`
- `cleanup=<value>`
- `output limit exceeded`
- `<stdout|stderr> stream error`
- `output is not a JSON object`
- `unsupported updateExecutor`
- `missing <targetRootBinding|originalDefinitionBinding|originalRuntimePinBinding|retainedOwnerBinding>`

</details>

This PR does not change the public GitHub update report. That report still shows only the check and code and redacts `failureFacts.message`. The detail is in the local support bundle that maintainers already request.

## Evidence

Base `e032d1e31`; later commits on main don't touch these files. Tests run in `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-custody.test.ts` against the real update executor, its lease database and real child processes:

- **New:** `candidate refusal names the failed executor check` covers a candidate with no entrypoint, one that exits 1, and one that omits `targetRootBinding`. Each asserts the exact `UpdatePreMutationError` message and the error's normalized `failureFacts` entry.
- **Tightened:** the existing retained-owner case now asserts `(executor check: missing retainedOwnerBinding)` on the activation path.

Before the fix (production code at the base):

```text
× candidate refusal names the failed executor check: without entrypoint
× candidate refusal names the failed executor check: exiting 1
× candidate refusal names the failed executor check: without target binding
× requires retained capability before private native input (true / undefined)
× requires retained capability before private native input (true / true)
+ "message": "Target runtime cannot fence update-owned native commands; refusing before Gateway stop or package activation."
Received: "Target runtime cannot fence update-owned native commands."
Tests  5 failed | 2 passed | 13 skipped (20)
```

After the fix:

```text
✓ candidate refusal names the failed executor check: without entrypoint 14ms
✓ candidate refusal names the failed executor check: exiting 1 37ms
✓ candidate refusal names the failed executor check: without target binding 34ms
✓ requires retained capability before private native input (true / undefined) 226ms
✓ requires retained capability before private native input (true / true) 183ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  20 passed (20)
```

- **Sibling suites pass, 149 tests in all:** `update-command-service-command.test.ts`, `.timing.test.ts`, `.process.test.ts`, `update-command-admission.test.ts`, `update-command-execution.test.ts`, `update-command-original-service.test.ts` and `update-command-execution-validation.test.ts`. The existing custody cases are unchanged and still pass, including `without-backup`, `legacy`, `false` and the cooperative/forced cleanup cases.
- **`check-changed`** on the changed files: format, core and core-test typecheck, lint and the other selected guards pass. Three lanes are red on the base and untouched by this change: the max-lines ratchet (`ui/src/pages/**`), the core test-root budget (`gateway-root`, `infra`; this PR adds no test files) and the Knip unused-export scan (other modules).
- **Autoreview:** no actionable findings.
- **Test cost:** the three new cases add about 85 ms. The custody file runs 31–55 s of Vitest duration locally, about 80% of it transform, and was already over the 30 s target before this change.
- **Live gap:** only the `code=1` condition was driven through the real CLI (below). The other conditions are covered by the tests above.

### Live managed-service proof (systemd)

I ran this on Docker Desktop with the official `node:24-bookworm` image, Debian systemd 252 as PID 1, and an unprivileged user with linger enabled. All state stayed inside the container. In each container:

1. `npm install -g` the installed build.
2. `openclaw config set gateway.mode local`, then `openclaw gateway install --port 18789`. The Gateway became an enabled, active systemd user service.
3. `openclaw update --tag /pack/openclaw-2026.10.4-probe-exit1.tgz --yes`, launched from a user-manager transient unit (`systemd-run --user --pipe --wait`).

The candidate is this branch's pack from `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` with one edit. Its `gateway install --update-executor check` handler waits for stdin EOF and then exits 1 without output. Its content-inventory entry and `buildId` were updated so the updater doesn't treat it as the installed build.

| Installed updater | CLI refusal and saved `stderrTail` / `failureFacts[0].message` |
| --- | --- |
| Shipped `openclaw@2026.10.4` (`383c124`) | `Target runtime cannot fence update-owned native commands; refusing before Gateway stop or package activation.` |
| This branch (`f446473`) | `Target runtime cannot fence update-owned native commands (executor check: code=1, termination=exit); refusing before Gateway stop or package activation.` |

In both runs the update refused during `validating`. The Gateway unit stayed enabled and active on the installed build, the recovery record says `"service": "healthy"` with the installed `buildId`, and nothing was activated.

<details>
<summary>CLI output and saved failure report (both runs)</summary>

Repeated `pacman inspection failed` warnings and triage-hint lines are omitted. The two runs print different recovery-guidance lines because current main's `update-recovery-guidance.ts` is newer than 2026.10.4; this PR doesn't touch that file. With the shipped 2026.10.4, a run launched straight through `docker exec` stopped earlier with `service-ancestry-unverified`, so both runs shown here use `systemd-run --user`.

Shipped 2026.10.4 updater:

```text
Phase: validating
  ✓ updater-runtime-retention (34.71s)
Gateway: verified serving after update failure.
⚠️ OpenClaw update failed: target-native-unsupported.
Admission: candidate (2026.10.4).
Phases: requested (31.92s) → staging (20ms) → validating (54.32s)
Failed: package-update — Exit code: 1; Target runtime cannot fence update-owned native commands; refusing before Gateway stop or package activation.
```

prs.title: fix(telegram): failed "Something went wrong" reply leaves no trace when Telegram rejects it
prs.body:
Closes #153491

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when Telegram message processing fails and the bot's last-resort "Something went wrong while processing your request" reply is also rejected by Telegram (bot blocked, chat gone, network failure), the second failure is silently discarded, so nothing records that the user got no reply at all.

## User Impact

User impact: operators now see a default-level `telegram sendMessage failed: <reason>` error in the Telegram channel log whenever the last-resort reply could not be delivered, without turning on verbose logging. The reply text, thread routing, the returned retryable failure and spooled-replay suppression are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The processor's fallback `sendMessage` sat in an empty `catch {}`. It now runs through `withTelegramApiErrorLogging`, the Telegram plugin's existing reporter for failed Bot API calls, which writes to the channel `runtime.error` and rethrows. The processor still swallows the rethrow, so the original dispatch error remains the returned result. This is the same shape as the sibling apology send in `bot-handlers.inbound-pipeline.ts`.

No new log format, config, or retry is added. #174402 removed routine success traces from channel callsites and kept failure and non-outcome notices; this routes a user-facing non-delivery through the existing failure owner rather than adding a new callsite log.

## Evidence

Base: `e032d1e31`. The empty catch is still present on current main.

Regression, at the processor boundary: `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message.test.ts`, "reports a rejected fallback send without replacing the dispatch failure". It drives the real `createTelegramMessageProcessor` with a real grammY `Api` client whose transport returns Telegram's 403 error body (`Forbidden: bot was blocked by the user`). It replaces the old "swallows fallback delivery failures" case, which used a mocked `sendMessage`.

- Before (base source): `1 failed | 16 passed`. `runtime.error` received only `telegram message processing failed: Error: dispatch exploded`.
- After: `17 passed`. The result is still `{ kind: "failed-retryable", error: dispatchError }`, the request body is still `{ chat_id: 123, text: "Something went wrong while processing your request. Please try again." }`, and `runtime.error` also gets `telegram sendMessage failed: Call to 'sendMessage' failed! (403: Forbidden: bot was blocked by the user)`.
- Cost: `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/bot-message.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took 19.9 s wall on the quietest run (45 to 83 s with parallel jobs loading the host). Almost all of it is transform and import; the new case runs in 5 to 6 ms. CI seconds are not measured yet.
- Sibling suites `extensions/telegram/src/api-logging.test.ts` (11) and `extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts` (61) pass.

Real-transport harness (temporary, not committed): the real processor and a real grammY `Bot` with `apiRoot` set to a loopback HTTP fake Bot API that answers `sendMessage` with 403. It used the Gateway's channel runtime construction (`runtimeForLogger(createSubsystemLogger("channels").child("telegram"))`) and wrote the real file logger to an isolated temp dir. Dispatch was forced to throw to reach the processor catch.

```text
fake Bot API requests (both runs):
  POST /bot<TOKEN>/sendMessage {"chat_id":4242,"text":"Something went wrong while processing your request. Please try again."}

before (base bot-message.ts), log records:
  ERROR {"subsystem":"channels/telegram"} telegram message processing failed: Error: session store read failed

after, log records:
  ERROR {"subsystem":"channels/telegram"} telegram message processing failed: Error: session store read failed
  ERROR {"subsystem":"channels/telegram"} telegram sendMessage failed: Call to 'sendMessage' failed! (403: Forbidden: bot was blocked by the user)
```

`node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: format, line-cap, assertion-safety, mock-export, plugin-boundary, import-cycle and the other changed-file guards pass, as do extension typecheck, extension test typecheck and oxlint on both files. Two failures are inherited from the base and touch no file here: the max-lines suppression ratchet (three `ui/src/pages/**` files) and the Knip unused-export scan (`src/logging`, `src/infra` and others).

Live gap: not run against the real Telegram Bot API with a userbot. The processor-level catch is only reached when pre-dispatch work throws (for example a session-store or sticker-cache failure), which can't be triggered on demand in a live chat. The harness above covers the grammY client, HTTP transport, Bot API error parsing and the Gateway channel logger, but not api.telegram.org itself.

Prior attempts: @xialonglee's #119993 and #120126 first proposed reporting this failed send at the default error level in this same catch, and this PR keeps that outcome. It routes the failure through the existing Telegram API failure reporter instead of a new log line, and credits @xialonglee as co-author. #153722 proposed a verbose-only log. All three were closed by their authors.
