prs.title: fix(gateway): respawn state-owner heartbeat worker and self-restart on custody loss
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Observed on a Windows/schtasks-supervised dev gateway after sleep/wake: the state-owner heartbeat worker dies silently while custody is fully intact. The old behavior treated the dead renewal loop as a custody failure — admission self-fenced with `utimes heartbeat renewal did not complete within 60 seconds` and the renewal worker was never respawned. The Gateway kept listening but every state call stayed fenced: a zombie whose clients hang in reconnect loops until someone manually restarts it. This port hardens exactly that path, re-implemented against the current state-owner design (it replaces local-only ops behavior this box already runs; it does not carry over any local fork rework).

## Why This Approach

- A worker crash or clean exit says nothing about custody, so those events are now recorded (`workerFault` / `workerExited`, spawn-generation guarded) instead of fencing by themselves. The existing synchronous inode/content proof decides.
- When that proof passes, the renewal worker **respawns** with fresh copies of the current lock bytes — including projection locks added after start, which is why lock handoff now goes through `heartbeat.addLock()` so parent-side bookkeeping survives respawns.
- When the proof genuinely fails, losing custody schedules a supervisor restart (`scheduleGatewayRestart({ reason: "state-owner custody lost", skipDeferral: true })`) through a small dynamic-import bridge, so the run-loop process recovers instead of limping; holders without a run-loop SIGUSR2 listener keep the fence as their terminal contract. Dynamic import keeps the unified bundle's lazy boundaries intact.
- Fence reasons keep the most specific cause: worker custody verdict → worker crash → timing symptom, so a dead worker no longer masquerades as a renewal timeout.

## Evidence (2026-10-16)

- Focused tests on the two touched suites (`src/infra/gateway-state-owner.heartbeat.test.ts`, `src/infra/gateway-state-owner.test.ts`): **44 passed / 3 skipped**, including two new ones: respawn after silent worker exit (custody continues; a second worker with a fresh beat is observed), and custody-loss supervisor restart (`scheduleGatewayRestart` called with the exact reason/skipDeferral).
- Backwards-clock re-baselining within the failure window is covered by the existing parent-custody `-5_000` case, which passes.
- Two failures in the same local run (`keeps the selected heartbeat generation alive through native retirement` — esbuild top-level-await/cjs transform error in the test's inline fixture on this Windows machine — and `checks dead PID persisted ownership…` — offline-maintenance state leak) reproduce **identically on an untouched control branch** and are unrelated to this change.
- Live observation: this box has been running the equivalent local commit (`1b3f55c`) as its gateway build since today; upstream port waits for review.

Builds on the restart/state-owner foundation of #170919.

prs.title: perf(gateway): reduce Control UI bootstrap blocking
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening the Control UI immediately after Gateway readiness parses plugin browser bundles on the main thread and materializes the complete configuration JSON Schema just to redact a small bootstrap preference projection.

## User Impact

Bootstrap keeps the same preference redaction, plugin asset authorization, immutable revisions, reload behavior, and static dependency preload hints. Import discovery runs through the existing esbuild native service; browser JavaScript is neither executed nor rewritten on disk.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use esbuild's import metadata instead of creating full Acorn ASTs on the Gateway main thread. Keep the existing catalog owner and snapshot lifetime. For bootstrap's core-only config projection, reuse core sensitivity hints without constructing the full core/plugin JSON Schema.

RPC validators already compile lazily once; plugin config validators already cache by schema contents. `processSchema` in the reported profile is Zod JSON Schema conversion, not TypeBox compilation.

Production delta: **+2 lines**; tests: **+3 lines**. The retained preload contract accounts for the small growth: a concurrent cold-browser comparison with 20 ms response delays showed roughly 45 ms slower activation without transitive hints. The final change preserves those hints and removes the main-thread AST. No dependencies, config options, or database changes.

## Evidence

- Regression reproduced before the change: bootstrap called `OpenClawSchema.toJSONSchema()` once. Afterward it calls it zero times while preserving MCP credential redaction and restricted-viewer omission.
- Focused bootstrap and asset tests passed. Final asset rerun: **21 tests passed**, 34.78 s Vitest wall time (mostly worker artifact preparation); includes static imports, re-exports, cycles, dynamic/missing/external exclusions, and optional parse failure. Bootstrap test: 37 ms. Changed-file format, lint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Codex autoreview of the final change: scoped clean through P2; no actionable findings.
- Four concurrent, core-swapped Chromium pairs rejected removing preload hints; the final implementation preserves the existing dependency graph expectations.
- Four concurrent Linux split-core Gateway boot pairs passed: cold bootstrap **580.93 → 255.80 ms**, paired mean **−325.13 ms (56%)**; first-30-second main-thread CPU **2598.50 → 2135.56 ms**, paired mean **−462.94 ms (17.8%)**. Readiness was neutral: paired mean **−8.54 ms**.
- Exact-head [CI run 39057327019](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39057327019) and aggregate CI gate passed on `027336ba77154b93cbef1abbeebcc5373992bc9b`; code/security checks passed. No CI rerun or inherited-failure exception was needed. No Testbox/Crabbox lease used, per the current validation rule.

## Paired Boot Measurement

Baseline `df0358cdd5f7e8525a9c610dd05745806eaf0e50`; candidate `027336ba77154b93cbef1abbeebcc5373992bc9b`. Four simultaneous A/B pairs held the exclusive measurement lock. Each process had 16 cores; assignments alternated between 96–111 and 112–127. Both sides used the same start timestamp, separate state and loopback ports, and identical dependencies. Decisions use B−A within each pair.

The synthetic inventory contains 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 disabled cron jobs and 12 projects. Transcript volume is reduced to 4 MiB; each fixture has approximately 39 MiB agent DB plus 11 MiB state DB. MCP Relay and Workboard are the active bundled browser UIs. ClawRouter and X remain inactive without their provider/channel configuration. This is an inventory-shaped boot measurement, not a full production plugin/configuration or large-transcript reproduction.

Each Gateway received ten concurrent bootstrap requests and ten fresh WebSocket connections immediately after ready, repeated at ready+15 s (20 bootstrap requests and 40 connect/catalog RPCs per process). CPU profiles began before ready; the table counts main-thread SELF samples only in the next 30 s, at a nominal 1 ms interval.

| Pair | Readiness B−A (ms) | Main-thread CPU B−A (ms) | Cold bootstrap B−A (ms) | Acorn samples A→B | processSchema samples A→B | TypeBox samples A→B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | -5.63 | -377.22 | -332.25 | 181→0 | 20→0 | 40→46 |
| 2 | +29.27 | -408.73 | -326.54 | 159→0 | 18→0 | 38→46 |
| 3 | +42.75 | -495.64 | -334.43 | 181→0 | 18→0 | 38→41 |
| 4 | -100.56 | -570.16 | -307.29 | 185→0 | 21→0 | 45→47 |

Warm bootstrap averaged 9.95 → 10.68 ms (paired +0.73 ms). Both sides advertised the same preload-hint count for every response. Recorded per-pair mean non-idle CPU across the measurement cores was 7.40%, 6.82%, 7.54%, and 9.99%; this includes the benchmark and concurrent outside load, and is context rather than an exclusion criterion. All owned Gateway processes exited cleanly.

Attribution: Acorn samples came from `staticBrowserImports`; every `processSchema` sample came through `prepareControlUiBootstrapPreferences` and full Zod JSON Schema conversion. Remaining TypeBox samples came mainly from `listManagedPlugins → resolvePluginConfigEnablement` during inventory prewarming, plus first-use RPC validation. Neither side had samples in these three categories during the second 15-second half. Those existing validators already compile once per cached schema; this PR adds no competing cache or changes to their validation boundary. Tool argument validators also already cache by schema and reference-root identity; agent tool execution was not exercised here.

The existing plugin-record catalog reuses discovery within a process, including reconnects, but is not persisted across restarts. This change uses the existing native esbuild service for the cold parse instead of adding a persistent parser cache. The main-thread CPU reduction does not claim total-system CPU savings: native parsing still consumes CPU outside the Gateway thread.

Measurement preparation used sequential synthetic fixture generation and isolated source-performance builds. Both sides shared the same external dependency graph, with task-owned missing dependencies; this was not an exact frozen-lockfile installation. PR CI provides the exact package/build/typecheck/test gates. One initial pair was excluded because the fixture incorrectly expected two inactive plugin UIs; both sides failed the identical assertion and shut down cleanly before measurement completion.

prs.title: perf(chat): defer warm snapshot receipts until after paint
prs.body:
## Decision: do not land

Measurement rejects this proposal. Moving retained receipt admission after paint preserves the startup byte savings, but the final candidate has unchanged warm FCP, a median **21.25 ms more restore/render blocking**, and **53.30 ms later startup**. This PR is being closed unmerged because of the measured regression, not merely because it is neutral on FCP.

## Problem and proposed change

Warm snapshot restore currently imports and validates optional retained pending-input, session-info, and command-catalog receipts before returning the cached transcript. Invalid receipts also discard otherwise usable cached messages.

The proposal carries raw receipts with the existing snapshot, validates lazily after a paint opportunity when the live request needs them, and preserves the existing IndexedDB format. Invalid or unavailable receipts request complete metadata. A task yield preserves separation between sidebar IDB completion and cached transcript application; hidden tabs request full metadata instead of waiting indefinitely for animation frames. Request ownership is rechecked after awaited work.

Related receipt behavior: #175585 and #175674.

## Paired measurement

Baseline: `df0358cdd5f7`. Candidate: `70dfdc8467b0` (measured build differs only by a lint-only Promise-executor brace change and comments).

Headless production Control UI bundles, synthetic fixture with 80 messages, five pending inputs, session information, and 150 commands. Four concurrent A/B pairs held one exclusive measurement lock. Each side had 16 CPUs; halves 96–111 and 112–127 swapped every pair. Separate browser profiles, state and loopback ports; warm navigation starts within 1 ms. Outside CPU load was recorded for context. Wire simulation used 35 ms latency, 4 ms frame gap, and a 100 ms subscription delay.

All values below are milliseconds. The long-frame metric is the maximum-duration frame between snapshot completion and the startup request; blocking is from that same frame.

| Pair | Warm FCP A → B | Restore/render long frame A → B | Blocking A → B | Startup request A → B |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 212 → 212 | 95.1 → 157.4 | 44.1 → 76.5 | 445.5 → 507.8 |
| 2 | 200 → 200 | 113.4 → 101.4 | 49.1 → 50.5 | 443.6 → 495.1 |
| 3 | 208 → 208 | 99.4 → 140.7 | 36.5 → 69.3 | 434.2 → 489.3 |
| 4 | 192 → 192 | 112.4 → 127.4 | 43.8 → 53.9 | 436.3 → 454.6 |

Median paired B−A differences: warm FCP **0 ms**, long frame **+28.15 ms**, blocking **+21.25 ms**, startup **+53.30 ms**. Cold FCP differences were 0, −20, +8, +44 ms (paired median +4 ms).

Every A/B warm startup response was **306 framed bytes**, with zero messages and all three retained revisions; request size was 302 bytes. Payload-only response size was 224 bytes. Every cold response was 152,198 framed bytes. Candidate validator fetch began after FCP in every pair.

A separate useful-content diagnostic found first cached transcript at 315.6 → 316.7 ms, with the same five visible cached rows and no removals. The change did not improve useful-content timing.

## What the profile explains

The validator itself costs about 2 ms, and snapshot structured clone about 0.2–0.3 ms. Removing the dynamic import changes task ordering. In a separate paired CPU/trace diagnostic, baseline hello ran before transcript rendering; the candidate's cache timer rendered first and delayed hello. Hello then cost 30.7 ms versus 19.0 ms with the transcript already mounted. Timestamp preparation, reactive recomputation, and layout work increased. Sampled profiles do not establish the exact number of reactive invalidations.

This identifies why the proposal regresses. It does **not** prove the cause of the historical r153→r154 blocking increase. Sidebar IDB completion also releases route and render work, so attributing an entire IDB callback to clone or receipt validation is misleading. Further work belongs with the Control UI boot/render sequencing owner; no additional independent fix was established here.

## Proof and limitations

- Three focused files passed: snapshot store, warm startup, and pane snapshot hydration; **74 tests, 4.78 seconds**. Regression cases cover restore without receipt validation, invalid receipts preserving messages, background visibility, serialization/privacy, and retired request ownership. The original store fails the new restore-validation and invalid-receipt regressions.
- Changed-file formatting and type-aware lint passed. Independent Codex review was clean through P2 on the final whole-PR diff. The review's background-tab finding was fixed and covered by tests.

prs.title: fix(imessage): prevent reflected replies from triggering duplicate turns
prs.body:
Closes #135704

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an inbound iMessage reflection could trigger a duplicate agent turn when the reflected row carried the outbound message GUID only in `reply_to_guid`.

## User Impact

Verified self-chat reflections marked `is_from_me=false` no longer start a duplicate turn when their parent GUID and normalized body match a recorded send within four seconds. Authored inline replies marked `is_from_me=true`, normal direct messages, groups, different-body replies, and replies outside that window retain their existing behavior.

**Maintainer decision remains open:** an incoming human self-chat reply that repeats the same parent GUID and body inside four seconds is indistinguishable from a reflection using these fields and is also suppressed. A reliable native transport discriminator would be preferable; this update does not claim to eliminate that ambiguity.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reflected row has its own row ID/GUID; the outbound GUID appears only in `reply_to_guid`. The existing persistent echo entry owns the scoped GUID/body pair, so the narrow parent lookup uses that same record, requires explicit incoming direction and verified self-chat, and refuses ID-only memory fallback. Exact provider chat-id targets are included alongside the existing prepared conversation scopes. Confirmed reflections keep the `self-chat echo` classification so they do not exhaust the loop limiter.

The update retains current main's cache entries, normalization, mention/authorization policy, and database fixtures. The existing general matcher moves unchanged into the local echo-scope module to satisfy the source-size ratchet. Regression tests cover persisted GUID/body/age matching, legitimate inbound controls, and the monitor loop budget. No schema, configuration, public SDK, or native iMessage transport change.

## Evidence

Final local diff: four affected native extension database-worker test files passed **99/99** with one worker on Node 24.19.0. Native formatting, nine-file type-aware lint, the iMessage production package typecheck, a strict check of the five modified test/support roots, and both previously parser-blocked line-cap/mock-export ratchets passed. The line-cap check required moving the existing matcher unchanged into its cache-scope module; its signature/body and all three call sites retain their behavior. Current hosted CI has not run for this unpushed update.

A current-source driver used the production inbound resolver and real worker-backed SQLite in isolated state. Both persisted reflection shapes dropped within four seconds (13 ms for handle scope, 5 ms for exact provider chat-id scope); different-parent, different-body, and normal-DM controls all dispatched. These are the same boundary evidence, not separate independent runtime experiments.

- Public proof excerpt: Validation `imessage-real-sqlite-proof-after-extraction-20261018` (pass, exit_code=0, 23189ms):

  ```text
  inbound-processing.ts sha256=82dd0a50fc10d8a360a272ae59e3df875bb6003fd154afa34b31ac45d310eecb
      log: imessage: skipping echo message id=200
  [PASS] reflected self-chat reply (echo under the handle scope) is dropped, not dispatched :: kind=drop reason=self-chat echo seed->decide=13ms (window 4000ms)
      log: imessage: skipping echo message id=207
  [PASS] reflected reply persisted under the provider chat-id target is dropped too :: kind=drop reason=self-chat echo seed->decide=5ms (window 4000ms)
  [PASS] an inline reply to a different parent message still dispatches :: kind=dispatch reason=undefined
  [PASS] an inline reply with different text still dispatches :: kind=dispatch reason=undefined
  [PASS] a matching inline reply in a normal (non-self) direct message still dispatches :: kind=dispatch reason=undefined
  RUNTIME PROOF PASSED
  isolated-state=<redacted task-owned synthetic state>
  ```

An actual isolated production Gateway run then exercised the full iMessage monitor/state/turn/delivery chain, using a synthetic imsg JSON-RPC subprocess and loopback OpenAI Responses provider:

```text
PASS reflected incoming self-chat row: monitor dropped it; 0 added model calls; injection 653 ms after accepted send
PASS same body / different parent: real model turn + transport reply; injection 694 ms
PASS same parent / different body: real model turn + transport reply; injection 25 ms
2 total model calls; 4 transport sends
Native Gateway shutdown clean; pnpm exit0; all retained process identities joined
Read-only SQLite after shutdown: 2 exact send GUID/body/conversation records verified
```

The plugin ran from this verified source checkout. The external imsg wire and model endpoint are fixtures; this does not prove Messages.app, iCloud, native imsg, hardware, a signed-in tenant or a real model service. No restart/downtime replay or attachment claim is made. An earlier run observed the same behaviors but failed the fixture's cleanup check; only the corrected fully joined run is reported as passing. Historical read-only `imsg 0.14.1` observations are prior-source evidence and do not establish current native transport behavior.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skill/hook requirements have all-of `env` with no any-of equivalent: a skill accepting either of two credential env vars cannot declare it, so eligibility is either too strict (all-of) or credential-blind (bins-only). This PR adds a generic `requires.anyEnv` contract (eval, manifest, runtime eligibility + credential injection, doctor/CLI/UI rendering, snapshot carry) with optional injection for alternate keys.

Note: #147346 (sag readiness) is already CLOSED completed by canonical #147685 (binary-only). This PR no longer claims it — sag stays binary-only here (P1 fix below). Generic sponsorship decision remains with the maintainer.

## Changes

- Generic `requires.anyEnv` plumbing: `src/shared/requirements.ts` (any-of eval), `frontmatter.ts`, `config-eval.ts`, `doctor-skills-core.ts`, CLI/hook formatters, UI `skills-shared`, `workspace-skill-prompt.ts` snapshot + `SkillSnapshot`/`OpenClawSkillMetadata` types, `env-overrides.ts` propagation on both direct + snapshot paths.
- `skills/sag/SKILL.md`: readiness restored to binary-only `{ bins: ["sag"] }` (matches `upstream/main`), preserving file-key setups (`--api-key-file`, `*_API_KEY_FILE` per SKILL.md:34). `primaryEnv` + `SAG_API_KEY` docs kept for optional injection only — no env gate. P1 regression withdrawn.
- Docs: `creating-skills.md` + `skills.md` generic contract.

## Evidence

P1 fix proof from this head (`02cfc06e1`), branch source:
```
sag requires now: { "bins": ["sag"] }
eligible binary-only zero-env: true
missing: {"bins":[],"anyBins":[],"env":[],"anyEnv":[],"config":[],"os":[]}
```
`isEnvSatisfied` (`requirements.ts:31`) checks env only, never key files — so the removed gate was the failure path; binary-only restores canonical behavior. Verified `upstream/main` sag is also bins-only (fetch `43d413bd`).

Gates on this push:
- `requirements` + `frontmatter` + `env-overrides`: 39/39 pass
- `oxlint`: 0 errors; `git diff --check`: clean
- Author: `Navras98 <andrea.sforna@gmail.com>` (amended before push)

## Honest gaps (not claimed)

- Maintainer decision on generic sponsorship is OPEN — happy to split, defer, or close on guidance.
- Snapshot carry is proven at unit level, not via a fresh-session resume run.
- UI screenshots exist locally (before/after) but are not embedded — no image-upload path from CLI.
- Full CI: runs on push, not claimed green here.

Related #147346 (closed by #147685); supersedes #147381 (closed unmerged).

## Generic proof (non-sag) from this head (`02cfc06e1`), real CLI entrypoints

Workspace skill `proof-anyenv` (generic, not sag) with
`metadata.openclaw.requires.anyEnv: [PROOF_KEY_A, PROOF_KEY_B]`, isolated
`OPENCLAW_HOME`, branch source, run from source:

**Neither key set** — `skills check` lists it under missing with the alternates group:
```
proof-anyenv (anyEnv: PROOF_KEY_A, PROOF_KEY_B)
```
(Eligible 44, Missing 22.)

**Only the alternate `PROOF_KEY_B` set** — it moves to "Ready and visible to model";
`skills info proof-anyenv --json` returns `"eligible": true` with
`"anyEnv": ["PROOF_KEY_A","PROOF_KEY_B"]` and `"missing": {"anyEnv": [], ...}`.
(Eligible 44→45, Missing 22→21.)

Injection + snapshot-carry: `env-overrides.test.ts` covers the direct path, the
snapshot path (`applySkillEnvOverridesFromSnapshot`), and the always-blocked guard;
335/335 touched-area tests pass locally (see comments).

UI: `computeSkillMissing` renders `env:any of (A, B)`; covered by
`skills-shared.test.ts` + page `view.test.ts`. Before/after screenshots of the real
Skills page were captured in headless Chromium (missing-requirements box absent
before, `env:any of (PROOF_KEY_A, PROOF_KEY_B)` shown after) — held locally, can be
drag-dropped into the thread on request.


## CI shard-failure attribution (finished run 34825094814, head `02cfc06e1`)

- `checks-node-compact-small-12` — `test/scripts/docker-build-helper.test.ts` expects `clawhub:@openclaw/kitchen-sink` in the Docker plugin sweep; area this PR never touches (no docker files in scope). Upstream-broken candidate.

## Proof 2026-09-14 (head `02cfc06e1`, fork-only, log redacted `/tmp/proof-147455.log`)

Real proof from this head, worktree pinned detached `02cfc06e1` (fork `Navras98/openclaw`), no push to upstream:

**sag accepts `SAG_API_KEY` alternate** (`sag 0.3.0` binary):
- `strings /usr/local/bin/sag | grep -o`: `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY_FILE`, `SAG_API_KEY`, `SAG_API_KEY_FILE` all present.
- No keys => `Error: missing ElevenLabs API key (set --api-key, --api-key-file, or ELEVENLABS_API_KEY)`.
- `SAG_API_KEY=[REDACTED]` dummy only => `Error: list voices failed: 401 Unauthorized` (missing-key gate GONE => alternate accepted; dummy value never printed, log contains no secret).

**`requires.anyEnv` resolves** (`src/shared/requirements.ts`, this head):
```

```

**sag readiness binary-only** (`skills/sag/SKILL.md`, this head):
```
sag requires now: { "bins": ["sag"] }
eligible binary-only zero-env: true
missing: {"bins":[],"anyBins":[],"env":[],"anyEnv":[],"config":[],"os":[]}
```

**Local tests green** (canonical `scripts/test-projects.mts`):
- `requirements` + `frontmatter`: 20/20 pass (unit-fast)
- `env-overrides` anyEnv (direct + snapshot + always-blocked guard): 3/3 pass
- `skills-cli.formatting` + `hooks-cli.toggle`: 143/143 pass
- `doctor-skills`: 10/10 pass
- Total touched: **176 passed, 0 failed**
- `oxlint`: 0 warnings, 0 errors · `git diff --check`: clean

Merge-risk/compatibility: sag stays `{ bins: ["sag"] }` (canonical, no env gate); generic `anyEnv` is opt-in per-skill, defaults to empty (no behavior change for existing skills). No upstream push — fork branch only.


## Runtime proof: fresh + cold-resumed delivery, old snapshots, guard (head `f942a4d`, fork-only, redacted)

Real entrypoint `applySkillEnvOverridesFromSnapshot` in **separate fresh OS processes** (no shared memory), snapshots reloaded from disk JSON after the same JSON round-trip the session store performs (`stripRuntimeOnlySessionSkillsFields` drops only `resolvedSkills`; `skills[].anyEnv` survives persistence — `store-entry-shape.ts:190`). Config values were synthetic dummies, never printed; output below is booleans only.

- **FRESH** — new-format snapshot (`skillKey/primaryEnv/requiredEnv/anyEnv`, as `buildSkillSnapshot` emits), only the alternate `PROOF_KEY_B` configured:
`{"expectKey":"PROOF_KEY_B","hadBefore":false,"delivered":true,"alwaysBlockedHeld":true,"reverted":true}`
- **COLD RESUME** — same persisted JSON reloaded by a *different* fresh process (simulates restart: disk → parse → apply), only alternate configured:
`{"expectKey":"PROOF_KEY_B","hadBefore":false,"delivered":true,"alwaysBlockedHeld":true,"reverted":true}`
- **OLD SNAPSHOT (pre-change format, no `anyEnv` field)** — `requiredEnv: ["LEGACY_KEY"]` still delivered, no crash:
`{"expectKey":"LEGACY_KEY","hadBefore":false,"delivered":true,"alwaysBlockedHeld":true,"reverted":true}`
- **GUARD** — with `anyEnv` declared, always-blocked host key (`OPENSSL_CONF`) configured alongside the alternate: alternate delivered, host key refused (`Blocked skill env overrides for proof-anyenv: OPENSSL_CONF` in log):
`{"expectKey":"PROOF_KEY_B","hadBefore":false,"delivered":true,"alwaysBlockedHeld":true,"reverted":true}`

So: alternate-key delivery works fresh and after cold resume through the real snapshot path; pre-change snapshots load unchanged; the sanitizer allow-list still refuses host-dangerous keys.

## Generic Skills UI screenshots (real rendering, headless Chromium 153)

Real Skills page (`renderSkills` from `ui/src/pages/skills/view.ts` + app `styles.css`, served by vite from this head) with a generic non-sag skill `proof-anyenv` missing `anyEnv: [PROOF_KEY_A, PROOF_KEY_B]`, detail dialog open. Same harness, only `computeSkillMissing` differs:

Before (base `61fe467c`): the dialog shows **no** Missing-requirements box — the alternate-credential need is invisible.

![before: no missing-requirements box](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Navras98/openclaw/proof/147455-assets/proof-assets/skills-before.png)

After (this PR): `Missing requirements — env:any of (PROOF_KEY_A, PROOF_KEY_B)`.

![after: env any-of group shown](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Navras98/openclaw/proof/147455-assets/proof-assets/skills-after.png)

## Why generic (maintainer decision on deferral)

- **Concrete any-of credential reality, in-repo:** the `sag` binary itself accepts `SAG_API_KEY` **or** `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` (plus `*_FILE` variants — verified via `strings`/runtime in this thread). All-of `env` cannot express that without marking single-key users ineligible; bins-only cannot name the credential at all. File-key setups stay bins-only (P1 lesson kept); `anyEnv` is opt-in metadata for key-based setups, never a gate.
- **Symmetry with `anyBins`:** the codebase already solved the identical any-of problem for binaries (`anyBins`, rendered as `bin:any of (...)` in CLI/hooks/UI). `anyEnv` is the missing half — same evaluator shape, same render pattern, same snapshot carry.
- **Additive and safe to land:** optional field, defaults to empty (zero behavior change for existing skills); old snapshots load (proven above); the P2 propagation bug this PR fixed (eligible-but-keyless) already demonstrated the trap is real — deferring leaves it for the next alternate-credential skill. Happy to add a first in-repo consumer annotation if the maintainer prefers.

prs.title: refactor(ui): consolidate page reads and canonical display facts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI pages independently implement replaceable reads and reconstruct already-canonical Gateway records, leaving several competing owners for the same work.

## User Impact

Rendering and supported workflows are unchanged. Skills Library and Workshop now also keep a retired scope's failed read from publishing an error or clearing the current scope's loading state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Relocate Usage's request executor into one small page-request owner and adopt it in Plugins, Providers, Worktrees, New Session remote search, Meetings, Memory Import, and Skills. Retain ordinary scope cancellation and caller-owned mutation/security admission. The executor releases before completion callbacks so existing refresh policies can start a successor; publication failures still propagate.

Consume typed update and question records from their Gateway producers instead of maintaining parallel structural decoders. Keep display normalization, URL/media/secret-store checks, omitted-versus-null update semantics, hydration and resolution authority. Reuse the existing text-diff traversal in Workshop and avoid re-normalizing already-normalized theme/settings facts.

Net production reduction: 502 lines against the branch base (tests and proof artifacts excluded). No schema, config, protocol, dependency, or changelog change.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Update display DTO filtering/cloning/capping: #121686 and #148830 document extraction/additive-field concerns, not a human report of malformed canonical output. UI and Gateway co-ship; malformed producer facts are now a producer defect rather than a silently filtered display copy. Safe URL sinks and update effect admission remain.
- Question record/list/event structural reconstruction: #109922 introduced the feature with synthetic/live feature proof, not a human malformed-Gateway incident. Trust the canonical manager/protocol shapes; malformed producer output may fail visibly. Display trimming/header bounds and the URL safeguards from #132158 and media safeguards from #161747 remain, as do secret-store and resolve-answer admission.
- Theme definition re-normalization: #168027 adds branding and #154935 adds plugin artwork; neither identifies a human malformed-canonical-output incident. The Gateway theme owner already validates and normalizes definitions. An invalid typed definition is now a producer defect instead of being silently discarded by a second UI parser.
- Settings whole-map own-write normalization: #110728 and #113712 introduce the layout features, not a human invalid-own-write incident. New entries and persisted loads still normalize and bound maps. Internal writers must honor that contract; save no longer repeats it for every existing entry.
- Worktree read publication: the existing Gateway binding retires both reads synchronously on scope replacement. Rechecking the same scope at publication duplicates that lifecycle; all mutation and confirmation authority checks remain.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix: honor quick integrity checks during historical upgrades
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Routine upgrades from historical SQLite schemas silently selected whole-database FULL integrity checks despite the default QUICK policy. On a 6.07 GB stable agent24/state20 fixture, public Doctor executed 12 whole FULL checks and no explicit QUICK check.

## User Impact

Ordinary update and Doctor upgrades now use whole-database `quick_check`, FULL checks of affected tables, and foreign-key validation. `--full-integrity-check` retains whole-database FULL validation. Explicit backup/database verification, Doctor recovery, rollback-image certification, restore validation, and corruption refusal keep their existing contracts. QUICK receipts cannot satisfy a later FULL request.

This is **candidate-side behavior**: the installed updater runs first, so this change cannot accelerate work already performed by an older installed updater. No schema, SDK surface, or PostgreSQL behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Historical migration backup eligibility and integrity coverage shared one decision, so a required full-file recovery backup implicitly forced FULL verification. The existing integrity owner now receives a separate cumulative migration-table scope; backup eligibility is unchanged. The requested mode reaches original captures, legacy Doctor/media repairs (including pre-v17 media prerequisites), same-version repairs, ACP inspection, credential relocation, and disposable update rehearsals. Doctor's existing maintenance scope carries that policy through synchronous and asynchronous repair opens and lease cleanup. The integrity worker receives both the mode and table scope. Temporary QUICK repair handles do not publish FULL runtime admission.

The superseded backup-driven FULL selection is removed. History inspection traced this to #174742 (`dae099a9414`): QUICK eligibility depended on declared migration/backup scope, while undeclared and same-version repairs selected FULL. That was a generic repair policy, not a distinct rollback-certification requirement. This change extends the QUICK default to ordinary historical repairs; explicit recovery and restore certification remain distinct. Accepted edges for the removed implicit checks:

- Historical/default repair admission: logical index inconsistency in untouched tables may remain undetected until explicit FULL verification. In a pre-v13 source, a corrupt workspace-alias secondary index can leave an attestation-only migrated path NULL; its alias/path and attestation data remain stored, and the existing workspace writer heals the NULL path.
- Automatic/manual original captures: default capture verification accepts the same untouched-index edge; restore certification remains FULL.
- Disposable rehearsal images: untouched indexes need not be exhaustively verified; rewritten shared tables remain scoped FULL.
- Maintenance repair opens and cleanup: inherit the requested coverage; unspecified or out-of-scope callers retain their FULL default.

Structural corruption, affected-table defects, foreign-key violations, and real credential/ownership conflicts still refuse the operation. No foreign-key check was removed.

## Evidence

Final candidate: `417c5180c88f61ce01ce80110c30ec59a8b953bc`.

The synthetic fixture uses actual stable v2026.10.4 agent24/state20 DDL, 665,600 transcript rows and 1,024 sessions, totaling **6,070,161,408 bytes**. Each public Doctor arm runs on a fresh private copy. Completed arms preserve original capture, reach agent31/state27, and preserve relevant row counts plus ordered 100-row hashes. This is bounded preservation proof, not full-corpus byte equality. Times below are observations on a busy host, not controlled speedup claims.

| Arm | Source | Doctor seconds | Whole FULL | QUICK | Scoped FULL | FK |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Base, default | `57314db33e30` | 319.591 | 12 | 0 | 2 | 13 |
| Candidate, default | `cb17486ac75e` | 294.849 | 0 | 16 | 292 | 17 |
| Candidate, explicit FULL | `f4def059a682` | 310.499 | 12 | 0 | 42 | 12 |

The default 6.07 GB result is transparently reused from `cb17486`: the `f4def059` correction changes only FULL/unspecified lease-cleanup policy. Its public Doctor QUICK smoke produces identical check counts (0/16/292/17), and its FULL smoke and 6.07 GB FULL control both produce 12/0/42/12. The final pre-v17 correction cannot run on an agent24 source: both changed call sites require source version <=16. The completed 6.07 GB arms therefore remain applicable, with separate real-v16 regression proof for the final correction. Earlier arms that exposed policy omissions are excluded from this comparison. Explicit FULL measurement source: `f4def059a6820da5498ec04d64b540d809224621`.

Default native integrity/FK invocations increase **27 → 325**, as whole scans become individual affected-table checks. This PR does not claim fewer total SQL statements. Completed live-agent integrity-worker requests remain **1 → 1**; that is the traced integrity-worker boundary, not total Doctor requests. The four extra FK checks are repeated live-agent admissions during shared-auth read, shared-auth cleanup, delivery rewrite, and title repair. The trace does not establish unchanged images after identical mutations, so none were removed as duplicates.

Gateway main-thread SQLite in affected owners remains **T1 0 → 0**; global T1 remains **181 → 181**. No warmed-turn SQL/request change is claimed; this is an upgrade-only behavior fix.

Focused regressions fail on base or on the demonstrated omission before correction. They cover historical default versus explicit FULL using real SQLite index corruption, cumulative table scopes, original capture/rehearsal policy, credential and delivery repair, synchronous/asynchronous maintenance inheritance, lease cleanup, and rejection of QUICK-to-FULL receipt promotion. The cleanup regression fails three of four cases before its fix and passes all four afterward. The real pre-v17 regression reproduces both default whole-FULL and explicit-FULL-to-QUICK omissions before correction; both modes and the malformed-transcript rollback case pass afterward.

Final-head CI [`39054935606`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39054935606) completed **SUCCESS: 138 successful jobs, 22 skipped, zero failures**, including all test matrices, PostgreSQL conformance, types, lint, source/export contracts, Madge, and worker/T1/dialect checks. The required CI gate is green. The exact-head published-driver update cell [`39054941238`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39054941238) completed **SUCCESS: 9 successful jobs, 15 skipped**, including its update product exercise. All 16 changed tests appear in the final CI preflight and directly edited-test selection policy; all 97 Node matrix jobs succeeded. Two consolidated-log transport failures prevent a per-file execution-log map, which is not claimed.

The pre-v17 correction exposed two TS2339 diagnostics because its internal parameter type omitted `integrityCheck`; commit `417c5180c88` fixes that annotation without changing runtime behavior or public database options. The directly affected Doctor typecheck, single-file type-aware lint, formatting, and diff check pass. The pre-v17 policy/rollback regression passes all 3 cases and remains applicable to the type-only correction.

Canonical Knip export scans ran on the exact CI merge `754001c841e2` and its actual main parent `484f36aa09a6`: both exit 1 with the same **13 inherited findings** (8 production, 5 full-tree, zero scripts), byte-identical logs, and zero new findings. This supersedes the earlier 35-finding result because upstream removed exports and changed scan configuration. The new main findings have been routed to their maintenance owner. No green-Knip claim is made.

Two independent Codex autoreview rounds are complete, with no accepted unresolved finding. The second round's only finding was an index-only version of the old same-version FULL override; the reviewed working-tree successor fixed it. Subsequent measured policy violations were corrected with failing regressions, respecting the two-round cap. The simplification pass reuses existing policy/maintenance owners; no new cache, handshakes, schema or fallback path.

One investigated local tooling failure remains disclosed: the Darwin-only PR worktree provisioner case exceeded its 120 s timeout (164.523 s) on this busy host. Linux skips it, and ordinary macOS PR CI does not select it. No timeout was raised and no full-suite replay is claimed.

The seven SQLite-native STRICT ADD COLUMN checks cost **14.961 s** on this baseline and **102.474 s** in the prior 43.615 GB measurement. SQLite performs existing-row validation for every STRICT ADD COLUMN, including nullable TEXT/INTEGER/ANY, so no harmless column-definition change avoids them while retaining the canonical schema. No such change is made, and no five-minute large-fixture claim is made.

LOC: **73 files, +1115/-165**; production/tooling **+504/-88**. Most growth is explicit historical table scope and boundary regressions. The full check-by-check evidence below identifies mode, scope, database/image, and elapsed seconds.

prs.title: fix: activate context engines with distinct plugin and engine IDs
prs.body:
Related: #126972

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes context-engine plugins selecting or loading the wrong owner when their plugin and engine IDs differ, including mixed-case runtime IDs. Ownership must remain consistent through install, activation, update, Doctor and removal.

## User Impact

A plugin's declared engine can be selected without rewriting explicit custom selections or `none`. Deny, disable and independent trust requirements remain enforced; ambiguous approved owners fail before runtime import. Existing plugin settings and installation metadata remain under their original owner.

Older hosts do not implement this declared-owner activation contract. Downgrade requires compatible config/install state and, when necessary, a matching verified backup. Automatic failed-update rollback is not claimed. Human maintainer review of configuration compatibility is still required before merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

`plugins.slots.contextEngine` remains an exact **engine ID**, not a plugin ID. Optional manifest `contextEngineIds` resolves its eligible plugin owner; existing installation records retain ownership metadata for lifecycle cleanup, without a new table, dependency or sidecar store. Runtime owners remain exact while allow/deny/config-entry policy remains canonical.

[Josh's documented contract acceptance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146018#issuecomment-5705710381) covers selector semantics, manifest metadata, persistence and recovery. This repair preserves contributor history and main's loader, custody and consent owners. It also fixes Doctor's canonical-key/exact-owner join, preserving authored settings paths and matching deferred migration receipts to their actual owner.

## Evidence

Final source **a47cd40760e3bb8bf0e03a8ffc7d3b6bbbd82061**, integrated with pinned main **02f671cd22a7b4be9aca038ce5bc1d4a58b3809c**. Build and runtime/upgrade proof are bound to **92d38ce3ada57a9403a72b17bb8c150b136cdce9**; the sole later change is two test-helper references in one test file. All production and other files are byte-identical. No production state or services changed.

- Built production at `92d38ce`: full build exit 0; `dist/index.js` SHA-256 `947a4571202710cf225172dd2fbe301aa88d903f15de62d8a9f2b046ceb97771`. Final-source focused regressions: **293 tests / 16 files passed**. This is explicit production-equivalent proof reuse, not a claim of rebuilding the test-only commit.
- Broad changed-file lane completed at `92d38ce`: production types, changed-file lint/format and other guards passed; it exited 1 for one test-harness naming defect (now corrected), three UI max-lines suppressions and six unique dead exports. All suppression/export findings were reproduced on exact unmodified pinned main using the same dependency snapshot; the base has twelve unique export findings. The first base scan lacked its UI module link and was discarded, then rerun correctly. No scan was skipped or baseline weakened. Final-source validation passed all 29 selected test-type graphs and targeted test lint; 293 focused tests across 16 files passed.
- Four built-Gateway cases passed with direct helper exit 0: distinct engine with mixed-case owner executes assembly/commit; independently approved owner collision rejects before either import; denied legacy owner is not imported; selecting `none` preserves independently approved unrelated capabilities. Scripted loopback Responses provider, not an external LLM.
- **Published stable 2026.9.9 → candidate upgrade passed:** real CLI plugin installation and execution, a baseline conversation, verified backup, stopped owned foreground Gateway, external package switch, full Doctor, retained settings/install record/payload/plugin-created data/history, then public CLI selection and an actual turn using the distinct mixed-case engine. Baseline owner is `upgrade-proof-plugin`; engine is `MiXeD-upgrade-proof`. Baseline explicitly uses `legacy` with a no-degradation guard.
- Plugin-created data SHA-256 was `e448c2850f74b06e795d5a15eda6db1470cee55478b1c5511cb92212776bb525` before replacement, after Doctor and after the candidate turn. issues.title: SSE Responses consumer drops `response.reasoning_text.*` events that the SDK consumer handles
issues.body:
While comparing the two Responses API stream consumers in `nanobot/providers/openai_responses/parsing.py`, I noticed a transport asymmetry:

- `consume_sdk_stream` handles `response.reasoning_text.delta` / `response.reasoning_text.done` (accumulates raw reasoning text, forwards deltas to `on_reasoning_delta`).
- `consume_sse_with_reasoning` handles only the `response.reasoning_summary_*` events. Raw `response.reasoning_text.*` events fall through silently.

Both the xAI Grok provider (`xai_grok_provider.py`) and the OpenAI Codex provider (`openai_codex_provider.py`) consume the Responses API over raw SSE via `consume_sse_with_reasoning` and wire `on_reasoning_delta`. When an endpoint streams raw reasoning-text deltas instead of (or in addition to) reasoning summaries — e.g. DeepSeek-style reasoning output, which the existing test suite already models for the SDK path (`test_deepseek_reasoning_text_streamed`) — the SSE transport drops them: no `on_reasoning_delta` callbacks fire and `LLMResponse.reasoning_content` falls back to whatever the terminal summary salvage can recover.

Minimal reproduction with the repo's scripted-SSE test harness:

```python
response = _SseResponse([
    {"type": "response.reasoning_text.delta", "delta": "step 1 "},
    {"type": "response.reasoning_text.delta", "delta": "step 2"},
    {"type": "response.reasoning_text.done", "text": "step 1 step 2"},
    {"type": "response.completed", "response": {"status": "completed", "output": []}},
])
_, _, _, _, reasoning = await consume_sse_with_reasoning(response)
assert reasoning == "step 1 step 2"  # today: None — events are ignored
```

The same event stream through `consume_sdk_stream` returns `"step 1 step 2"`.

Proposed fix: mirror the SDK consumer's two handlers in `consume_sse_with_reasoning` (accumulate deltas, use `.done` text only as a no-stream fallback so it never double-counts). I have the patch with regression tests ready and will open the PR right away.

issues.title: Matrix: "listen" group policy — observe the room, reply only on mention
issues.body:
## Problem

Under Matrix's `mention` policy, messages that fail the policy check are dropped outright in `_on_message` (`nanobot/channels/matrix/runtime.py`) — the bot never ingests them. So in a busy group, when someone finally @mentions the bot, it has no knowledge of the conversation that happened since its last reply. Under `open` it replies to everything. There is no way to get "aware but quiet": read the room, respond only when addressed.

## Request

Add a third group policy value, **`"listen"`** (usable as the channel-wide `groupPolicy` and, with #6286 / PR #6287, per-room via `groupPolicyOverrides`):

- Every message from an allowed sender in a listen room is ingested.
- The bot replies only when mentioned (same `m.mentions` / `allowRoomMentions` semantics as `"mention"`).
- When a mention-triggered turn fires, the recently heard room chatter is attached as context for that turn, so the reply reflects the intervening conversation.

## Proposed v1 (channel-contained, no agent-core changes)

- A bounded per-room transcript buffer (oldest-dropped, hard caps on entries and characters) is filled at ingest time for unmentioned messages.
- On a mention-triggered turn the buffer is attached via the **existing trusted channel seam** `_runtime_context_blocks` (`nanobot/runtime_context.py`, `RUNTIME_CONTEXT_INPUT_META`) — blocks are appended to the turn's user content and persisted with a display-time-removal marker, and the buffer is cleared once consumed.
- No LLM cost for unheard messages; bounded memory; delimiters and caps per the `RuntimeContextBlock` docstring's "bound and delimit content obtained from untrusted sources" requirement.

## Future option (separate discussion if there's interest)

Fully persisting unheard room chatter into the session transcript *without* an agent turn would need an append-only admission path in the loop — today every non-user inbound becomes a `TurnKind.SYSTEM` turn, which runs the LLM. That interacts with auto-compaction/token burn, so it needs maintainer design review; v1 above needs none.

issues.title: Matrix: add groupPolicyOverrides (per-room group policy, parity with Napcat)
issues.body:
## Problem

`groupPolicy` is channel-wide on Matrix (one of `open`, `mention`, `allowlist` applies to **every** group room). Only DMs (≤2 members) bypass it (`_should_process_message`, `nanobot/channels/matrix/runtime.py`, v0.3.5).

A deployment with many rooms usually wants different behavior per room:

| Room type | Desired policy | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Topic/project rooms | `open` — respond to every message | Bot is the copilot there |
| Shared / busy room | `mention` — respond only when @mentioned or replied to | Unprompted replies are noise, and the room will also host another bot |

This cannot be expressed today: `open` everywhere is noisy in the shared room, `mention` everywhere silences the topic rooms.

## Existing precedent in the codebase

The Napcat channel already ships this exact mechanism — the ask is a small parity port to Matrix:

- `nanobot/channels/napcat/manifest.py`: `"groupPolicyOverrides": field("json", default={})`
- `nanobot/channels/napcat/runtime.py`:
  ```python
  group_policy_overrides: dict[str, GroupPolicy] = Field(default_factory=dict)
  policy = self.config.group_policy_overrides.get(str(group_id), self.config.group_policy)
  ```

Related Telegram-side RFCs with the same gap: #3309, #5972.

## Proposed config

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "matrix": {
      "groupPolicy": "open",
      "groupPolicyOverrides": {
        "!aaaa...:example.org": "mention"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

- **Keys:** Matrix room IDs. **Values:** the same vocabulary as Matrix's `groupPolicy` — `"open" | "mention" | "allowlist"` (Napcat additionally accepts a probability float; not required here).
- **Precedence:** per-room override → channel `groupPolicy`. Rooms not listed behave exactly as today, so existing configs are unaffected.
- An `"allowlist"` override would reuse the existing channel-wide `groupAllowFrom` list for that room (minimal change; per-room allow lists could come later).
- `allowRoomMentions` semantics unchanged.

## Implementation

Single lookup change at the existing policy-resolution point in `nanobot/channels/matrix/runtime.py`, `_should_process_message()` (~L1136–1149 in v0.3.5):

```diff
-        policy = self.config.group_policy
+        policy = self.config.group_policy_overrides.get(room.room_id, self.config.group_policy)
```

plus the matching `field("json", default={})` declaration in `channels/matrix/manifest.py`, mirroring Napcat.

Happy to attempt the PR if this is wanted.

issues.title: web_search (DuckDuckGo): no retry/backoff — back-to-back searches fail with "No results found"

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### Bug Description

With the default search provider (DuckDuckGo, no API key), consecutive web_search calls in the same turn fail with an error that reads like an empty result set:
  Error: DuckDuckGo search failed (No results found.)

The same distinct queries, spaced a few seconds apart, all return results. The underlying cause is that _search_duckduckgo has no retry/backoff (while _search_brave already retries once on HTTP 429), and neither the tool nor ddgs paces calls, so back-to-back searches hit the upstream rate/anti-bot rejection. The error message is also misleading: it reports "No results found" where the upstream response is actually a rejection, not an empty result set.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Keep the default provider (tools.web.search.provider = "duckduckgo", empty api_key), no proxy.
2. In one turn, issue several distinct web_search calls with no pause between them (a normal multi-query research turn does this).
3. Observe that a subset of the calls fail with the "No results found" error; repeating the same queries with a pause succeeds.

Isolated library repro (no nanobot involved), same host:
  from ddgs import DDGS
  qs = ["capa galaxy a12 preco", "fone bluetooth barato", "notebook i5 usado", "cadeira gamer preco",
        "tenis corrida promocao", "panela eletrica preco", "mochila escolar", "lampada led preco"]
  d = DDGS(timeout=15)
  # no pause -> 0/8 results, all DDGSException: No results found
  # 3 s pause between queries -> 8/8 results

### Expected Behavior

- A rate/anti-bot rejection should be distinguishable from a genuinely empty result set in the error text, so the agent does not report "nothing found" to the user.
- The tool should absorb a transient rejection with a short retry/backoff before giving up, the way the Brave provider already does.
- Ideally, pacing/backoff should be tunable under tools.web.search for users of the anonymous providers.

### Relevant Logs

```shell
Two calls issued in the same second, then the failure (Telegram turn, 17/10/2026):
2026-10-17 21:32:33 | INFO  | - | Tool call: web_search({"query": "REDACTED_QUERY", "count": 8})
2026-10-17 21:32:33 | INFO  | - | Tool call: web_search({"query": "REDACTED_QUERY", "count": 8})
2026-10-17 21:32:44 | INFO  | - | Tool call: web_search({"count": 6, "query": "REDACTED_QUERY"})
2026-10-17 21:32:50 | WARNING | - | DuckDuckGo search failed: No results found.
2026-10-17 21:32:54 | INFO  | - | Tool call: web_search({"count": 6, "query": "REDACTED_QUERY"})
2026-10-17 21:33:40 | WARNING | - | DuckDuckGo search failed: No results found.
2026-10-17 21:33:51 | WARNING | - | DuckDuckGo search failed: No results found.

Additional measurements
- 8 distinct queries with no pause: 0/8 returned results (all DDGSException: No results found).
- The same 8 queries with a 3 s pause: 8/8 succeeded.
- The host recovers after idling, and a second host on a different IP served results while the first was failing — transient and rate/IP dependent, not a permanent block.
- exclusive=True only keeps DuckDuckGo out of the parallel batch; it does not pace calls, so consecutive searches still go out immediately.
- The per-turn guard in utils/runtime.py (_MAX_REPEAT_EXTERNAL_LOOKUPS = 2) only blocks repeating the same query or URL, so it does not help with distinct queries.
- ddgs 9.16.0 itself has no retry/backoff (checked its sources).
- Checked todays `main`: _search_duckduckgo is unchanged there.
```

issues.title: Allow agents to observe group messages without always replying

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
### Problem / Motivation

In group chats, there is an important distinction between:

1. receiving/observing a message,
2. deciding whether the message is relevant to the agent,
3. processing it with the main agent,
4. deciding whether a response should actually be sent.

Today, group message handling is mainly based on whether a bot should be triggered by a message at all, for example through mention-based or open group handling.

For multi-agent group chats this is limiting.

Example:

A Telegram group contains several specialized agents:

- a calendar / personal assistant
- a project management agent
- an information/archive agent

A user writes:

> I will be on vacation next Thursday.

This information may be useful context for multiple agents, but only one of them may have something useful to say.

Ideally:

- the calendar agent may handle the message and respond
- the project management agent may observe it as useful context but remain silent
- the archive agent may ignore it entirely

Without such a distinction, users either have to explicitly mention every relevant bot or allow multiple bots to respond to messages where they have nothing useful to contribute.

This becomes especially noisy in groups with multiple agents.

### Proposed Solution

Introduce an optional contribution policy for incoming group messages that separates message observation from response delivery.

Conceptually, an incoming message could pass through the following stages:

```text
Incoming group message
        |
        v
Contribution decision
        |
        +--> IGNORE
        |
        +--> OBSERVE / CONTEXT_ONLY
        |
        +--> HANDLE
                 |
                 v
             Main agent
                 |
                 v
          Delivery decision
                 |
          +------+------+
          |             |
       SUPPRESS       DELIVER
```
The exact API/configuration is open for discussion, but an opt-in policy could conceptually look like:
```json
{
  "channels": {
    "telegram": {
      "groupPolicy": "open",
      "contributionPolicy": "relevant"
    }
  }
```
The important behavior would be:
- IGNORE: do not invoke the main agent
- OBSERVE / CONTEXT_ONLY: retain the message as conversation context without generating a response
- HANDLE: invoke the normal agent
- after agent execution, optionally allow the resulting response to be suppressed instead of requiring every successful agent run to produce a user-visible message
The contribution and delivery decisions could use a lightweight configurable evaluator rather than the agent's main model.
Explicit mentions should probably bypass the contribution gate and continue to trigger the addressed agent directly.
Existing group behavior should remain unchanged unless the new policy is explicitly enabled.

### Alternatives Considered

### Mention-only group handling

This avoids unwanted responses, but the bot does not get useful context from messages where it was not explicitly mentioned.

It also requires the user to know in advance which agent may need a piece of information.

### Open group handling

This gives agents access to the whole conversation, but can cause every agent to react to every message.

In a multi-agent group this quickly becomes noisy and can also cause unnecessary LLM calls.

### Prompt the main agent to return something like `NO_REPLY`

This could suppress some responses, but the expensive main agent has already been invoked.

It also makes "no user-visible response" a special text convention instead of an explicit runtime behavior.

### Only add a post-run delivery evaluator

This would solve unwanted responses, but would not avoid unnecessary main-agent invocations for clearly irrelevant messages.

A pre-run contribution decision and a post-run delivery decision solve different problems and could therefore be useful independently.

### Related Component

Channel (WeChat, Feishu, Telegram, etc.)

### Additional Context

A similar separation already exists conceptually in the heartbeat flow:

- work is performed internally
- the resulting response is evaluated
- only relevant results are delivered to the user

The proposed group-chat behavior could reuse or generalize this idea, while additionally introducing a lightweight pre-run contribution decision to avoid unnecessary main-agent executions.

This would be particularly useful for groups containing multiple specialized bots, where all agents can share conversational context but should only speak when they have something relevant to contribute.

The evaluator implementation should not necessarily depend on a specific model or provider. A configurable model preset, deterministic policy, or another lightweight decision mechanism could be supported by the underlying abstraction.

prs.title: fix(mcp): propagate resource and prompt failures as structured tool errors
prs.body:
## Summary

Fix MCP resource reads and prompt calls being reported as successful tool executions when they fail.

## Root Cause

`MCPResourceWrapper` and `MCPPromptWrapper` returned caught failures as plain strings. The harness recognizes failures through `ToolResult.is_error`, so these responses triggered success hooks and `status="ok"` events and skipped the existing recovery hint.

`MCPToolWrapper` already uses structured error results for these failure paths.

## Changes

- Wrap nine terminal failure returns in ToolResult.error(...), preserving their existing messages.
- Strengthen timeout, exception, retry exhaustion, and recovery assertions.
- Add regression coverage for SDK cancellation, external cancellation, and resource/prompt execution through the tool registry and executor.
- Verify that successful content beginning with "Error:" still follows the success lifecycle.

## Result

Failed resource reads and prompt calls trigger error hooks and `status="error"` events. Their original failure details receive the existing recovery hint.

Successful responses, retry and reconnect behavior, and external cancellation propagation remain unchanged.

## Test

- Red/green verification: 14 regression cases failed before the fix and passed afterward.
- Related MCP, registry, execution, runner error, and logging suites: 240 passed.
- Real MCP SDK 1.28.1 client/server verification over in-memory transport: six scenarios passed, covering protocol errors, timeouts, and successful responses.
- Ruff on changed files: passed.
- BasedPyright on nanobot/agent/tools/mcp.py: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- Import boundary checks and git diff --check: passed.

prs.title: feat(api): stream tool progress SSE events
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #3698.

- Emits structured `event: nanobot.tool.progress` SSE events from `/v1/chat/completions` when streaming is enabled.
- Keeps normal OpenAI-compatible `data:` chunks for assistant text unchanged.
- Maps nanobot tool event phases to client-friendly statuses: `running`, `completed`, and `error`.

## Problem / Root Cause

The API streaming path only forwarded assistant token deltas via `on_stream`. AgentLoop already emits structured tool progress through `on_progress(..., tool_events=...)`, but `handle_chat_completions` did not register an `on_progress` callback, so API clients could not observe tool start/finish events during streamed requests.

## Scope

- Files/modules changed: `nanobot/api/server.py`, `tests/test_api_stream.py`
- Explicit non-goals: no changes to channel streaming, WebSocket envelopes, AgentLoop tool event shape, or non-streaming API responses
- User-visible behavior changes: streaming API clients may now receive named SSE tool progress events alongside existing chat completion chunks
- Compatibility notes: ordinary OpenAI-compatible chunks and `[DONE]` remain in the same format

## Design

The API stream queue now carries already-formatted SSE bytes. Token deltas are still formatted with `_sse_chunk`, while tool events use a small named-event helper. This keeps the API-specific projection local to `server.py` and reuses the existing AgentLoop `on_progress` contract instead of adding another tool-event path.

## Safety / Risk

- Default behavior impact: only applies to `stream=true` API requests that produce tool events
- Config/API/channel/session/storage/network impact: API output adds optional named SSE events; no config, channel, session, storage, or network behavior changes
- Rollback plan: revert this PR to stop emitting named tool progress SSE events
- Residual risk: clients that assume every SSE `data:` line is an OpenAI chat chunk may need to ignore named events, which is standard SSE behavior

## Validation

- `uv run --extra dev ruff check nanobot --select F401,F841`
- `uv run --extra dev ruff check nanobot/api/server.py tests/test_api_stream.py --select F401,F841,E501,F821`
- `git diff --check`

prs.title: feat(matrix): add "listen" group policy (observe room, reply on mention)
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds a third Matrix group policy value — **`"listen"`** — for rooms where the bot should read the whole conversation but reply only when mentioned (#6288).

Under `mention`, messages that fail the policy check are dropped outright (`_on_message`), so the bot has no knowledge of the conversation when it's finally mentioned. Under `open` it replies to everything. `listen` closes that gap:

- Every message from an **allowed sender** in a listen room is ingested into a bounded per-room buffer.
- The bot replies **only when mentioned** — same `m.mentions` / `allowRoomMentions` semantics as `mention`.
- On a mention-triggered turn, the buffered chatter rides along as **trusted runtime context** so the answer reflects the intervening conversation.

## How context is attached

Uses the existing trusted channel seam `RUNTIME_CONTEXT_INPUT_META` (`nanobot/runtime_context.py`) — this is the first channel producer of `_runtime_context_blocks`, whose docstring describes exactly this: *"trusted, channel-produced context blocks"* read from inbound metadata. Blocks are appended to the turn's user content and persisted with a display-time-removal marker, so the LLM retains the context in subsequent turns while users never see the injected block as chat output.

Bounds per the `RuntimeContextBlock` docstring's requirement ("callers must bound and delimit content obtained from untrusted sources"): 30 messages / 6,000 chars per room, 500 chars per line, header-delimited block, buffer cleared once consumed. No LLM calls for unheard messages; no agent-core changes.

## Behavior details

- Deny-listed senders are never buffered.
- Direct rooms (≤2 members) bypass the policy entirely, as today.
- Media messages buffer a caption or `[attachment]` note — downloads/transcription are not triggered for unheard messages.
- Composes with per-room `groupPolicyOverrides` from #6287 once that lands (a trivial rebase in `_should_process_message`).

## Fixes #6288

## Tests

Seven new tests in `nanobot/channels/matrix/tests/test_matrix_channel.py`:

1. `"listen"` accepted via attribute and camelCase config; unknown policy values still rejected.
2. Buffer bounds: oldest-dropped at 30 entries, 6,000-char budget, 500-char line truncation.
3. Unmentioned messages buffered with no reply/typing; the next mention triggers one turn carrying a bounded `matrix_room_transcript` block containing the buffered line; buffer cleared (subsequent mention carries no block).
4. Denied senders neither replied to nor buffered.
5. Direct rooms unaffected (no buffering, normal DM path).
6. `open` policy rooms never buffer (regression guard).
7. Media captions buffered as notes.

Verified locally: 127 matrix-channel tests pass, 152 channel-contract tests pass, `ruff check nanobot tests` clean, import-boundary check passes, `basedpyright` clean (0 errors) on touched files. WebUI locale copy added for all 10 languages (en, es, fr, id, ja, ko, pt-BR, vi, zh-CN, zh-TW).

> Note: this branch is based on current `main` without #6287. If #6287 merges first, expect small conflicts in `_should_process_message` (adjacent lines) and the docs table — happy to rebase.

prs.title: feat(matrix): per-room group policy overrides (groupPolicyOverrides)
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds `groupPolicyOverrides` to the Matrix channel — a per-room policy map that overrides the channel-wide `groupPolicy`, mirroring the mechanism the Napcat channel already ships (#6286).

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "matrix": {
      "groupPolicy": "open",
      "groupPolicyOverrides": {
        "!abc123:matrix.org": "mention"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Behavior

| Room | Global `groupPolicy` | `groupPolicyOverrides` entry | Resulting policy |
|---|---|---|---|
| `!abc123:matrix.org` | `open` | `"mention"` | `mention` |
| `!def456:matrix.org` | `open` | — | `open` (fallback) |
| Any DM (≤2 members) | any | any | Unaffected — DMs bypass group policy as before |

Resolution is a single lookup in `_should_process_message`:

```python
policy = self.config.group_policy_overrides.get(room.room_id, self.config.group_policy)
```

- Values share the `groupPolicy` vocabulary (`"open"`, `"mention"`, `"allowlist"`); an `"allowlist"` override checks the existing channel-wide `groupAllowFrom` (no per-room allow-list surface added).
- Rooms not listed behave exactly as before — existing configs need no changes, zero migration.
- `allowRoomMentions` and `groupAllowFrom` semantics unchanged.

## Why room IDs (not aliases) as keys

Keys are Matrix room IDs (`!local:server`) exactly as reported in sync — the same identifier `_should_process_message` already compares for the `allowlist` policy. This is homeserver-agnostic: Synapse, Conduit/Conduwuity/Continuwuity, and Dendrite all emit spec-compliant room IDs, and a room keeps its ID regardless of which server implementation serves it, so a config keyed by room ID works identically across backends. Alias keys (`#name:server`) would need lookup calls at startup and stop matching when aliases move; room IDs are stable and opaque.

## Related

- **Fixes #6286**
- Same pattern as the Napcat channel: `groupPolicyOverrides` manifest field + runtime lookup (`nanobot/channels/napcat/manifest.py`, `nanobot/channels/napcat/runtime.py`)
- Telegram counterparts: #3309, #5972

## Tests

Five new behavioral tests in `nanobot/channels/matrix/tests/test_matrix_channel.py`:

1. An override of `"mention"` beats a global `"open"` and the room falls silent without `m.mentions`, while a non-overridden room still follows the global policy.
2. `m.mentions` user mentions are still accepted in an overridden-mention room.
3. An override of `"open"` opens a room under a global `"mention"` policy.
4. An `"allowlist"` override is checked against `groupAllowFrom` (allowlisted room handled, non-allowlisted overridden room blocked).
5. Direct rooms (≤2 members) bypass overrides, as with the global policy.

Contract checks covered by the existing suite: `test_every_runtime_channel_field_has_a_webui_contract` and `test_channel_locales_cover_authoritative_setup_contracts` — locale copy added for all 10 languages (en, es, fr, id, ja, ko, pt-BR, vi, zh-CN, zh-TW), matching how Napcat localizes its override field.

Verified locally: 125 matrix-channel tests pass, 152 channel-contract tests pass, `ruff check nanobot tests` clean, `basedpyright` clean (0 errors) on the touched files.

prs.title: fix(tools): accept a top-level path in apply_patch
prs.body:
## What this changes

`apply_patch` accepts an optional top-level `path`, inherited by every edit that omits its own. A per-edit `path` still wins when both are present, and a patch with no path anywhere is still rejected.

## Why

A patch that touches one file has to repeat the same path in every edit, and one omitted path rejects the entire call before anything runs. The shape that is natural to write —

```json
{"path": "notes.py", "edits": [{"action": "replace", "old_text": "...", "new_text": "..."}]}
```

— is refused, and the refusal reports an absence rather than the accepted alternative:

```
unexpected parameter path; missing required edits[0].path
```

In one agent deployment driving nanobot through a tool-calling model, `unexpected parameter path` appears in 257 tool results and `missing required edits[` in 371 — the same rejection, over and over, for a one-file patch written the obvious way. The usual recovery was to re-send the identical patch with the path copied into each edit. A shape a caller reaches for that reliably, and that one character of difference makes invalid, is worth accepting.

## Compatibility

- Callers that already name a `path` in every edit are unaffected: a per-edit `path` is still authoritative, and `path` remains accepted per edit.
- A patch with no path anywhere still fails with a message beginning `path required for edit` (now naming both accepted shapes), so the assertion in `tests/tools/test_apply_patch_tool.py` continues to pass. The one string that does change is the non-string case: it previously reused `path required for edit` and now reports the offending value, as in `path must be a string: 123`.
- An explicit `"path": null` — which tool-calling models emit for unfilled optional fields — is accepted and treated as absent rather than failing validation while a usable top-level path is supplied.
- The edit object now rejects unknown keys (`additional_properties: false`, matching the root schema). This is deliberate and worth a release note: with a top-level default in place, a misspelled key such as `"file"` would silently inherit that default and write to the wrong file, so the misspelling has to be refused at validation. The cost is that calls which previously smuggled a stray key now fail — measured at 47 of the 2,181 calls in the same store, 38 of them `expected_replacements`, a key this tool has never implemented and was ignoring silently. Those callers were already getting something other than what they asked for.
- `_resolve_apply_patch_paths` in `nanobot/utils/file_edit_events.py` learns the same inheritance rule; without it the WebUI file-edit activity and diff tracking silently produced no events for the newly accepted shape.
- The tool's schema changes: a new root `path` property, `nullable` on both path fields, `required` narrowed to `action` on the edit item, unknown keys refused there, and the description of the per-edit `path` now mentions the top-level fallback. No other tool changes.

## Tests

`tests/tools/test_apply_patch_tool.py`, six cases:

- a top-level path is inherited by every edit (two edits, one file);
- a top-level path creates a new file for `add`;
- a per-edit path overrides the top-level path, and the default file is not touched;
- the default survives an edit that names a different file: the pathless edit still lands in the default, which an implementation that lets the loop overwrite it would not;
- a patch with no path anywhere is rejected and writes nothing;
- a misspelled per-edit path key is reported instead of inheriting the default.

Plus one schema case asserting that both shapes and explicit nulls at either level validate, so a future change to `required` or `nullable` cannot quietly take the acceptance away again, and one case in `tests/utils/test_file_edit_events.py` for the tracker path.

Results on this branch: `pytest tests/tools/test_apply_patch_tool.py tests/utils/test_file_edit_events.py` → 67 passed; `ruff check` clean on all four files (the project config ignores E501, so the long literals in the new tests are within policy). Reverting only `nanobot/agent/tools/apply_patch.py` to the base commit fails 5 of those cases; reverting only `nanobot/utils/file_edit_events.py` fails 1. Both fixes are therefore load-bearing rather than descriptive.

## Scope

Two source files and their two test files. No formatting churn, no unrelated refactor.

prs.title: refactor(settings): let the config store own read-modify-write transactions
prs.body:
Settings writes used to hold a file lock around callbacks that unpacked the config path, loaded it again, and saved it themselves. The existing `WebUISettingsConfig` now owns the complete read-modify-write transaction. Unchanged snapshots preserve the config file's bytes and mtime, including an absent file.

Bound settings operations use raw persisted config and build responses from the committed snapshot. The gateway's model, provider, runtime, MCP, skill, and optional-feature mutations use that owner. Runtime reloads and live-state publication follow a successful commit. Model-preset rename and staged skill deletion compensate a failed save before releasing the locks. MCP credential and runtime-directory cleanup completes after a successful save while the same locks remain held, so a concurrent enable retains its directory. Existing public Python settings functions retain their signatures through a small facade adapter.

Optional-feature requests share a process-local installation lock. Dependency checks and the complete installer run stay serialized outside the config transaction, so unrelated settings writes can proceed.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Before
    B1["Gateway handler"] --> B2["Generic read / mutate callback"]
    B2 --> B3["Pass config path into feature"]
    B3 --> B4["Load, mutate, save inside feature"]
    B4 --> B5["Load again for response"]
    B6["Store"] -. "Outer serialization only" .-> B3
  end
  subgraph After
    A1["Gateway handler"] --> A2["Bound settings operation"]
    A3["Public Python facade"] --> A4["Compatibility adapter"]
    A4 --> A2
    A2 --> A5["Store owns locks and raw snapshot"]
    A5 --> A6["Mutate and compare"]
    A6 --> A7["Atomically save only changes"]
    A7 --> A11["MCP commit cleanup under the same locks"]
    A7 --> A8["Build response from committed snapshot"]
    A11 --> A8
    A7 -. "Save fails" .-> A9["Compensate before unlock"]
    A8 --> A10["Publish live state / refresh runtime"]
  end
```

PR 4 of the four refactors preceding #6261. Stacked on #6269. Related to [NAN-264](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-264/). Literal `${VAR}` references and the persisted agent workspace survive settings edits even when the running gateway uses a different launch workspace.

Validation passed on Linux with Python 3.12.

- Full Python regression passed, 9803 passed and 49 skipped. Serial CLI tests passed, 163 passed and 1 skipped. Ruff, BasedPyright, and eleven import-boundary rules passed.
- Independent review passed. All 24 public settings function signatures are unchanged. Existing facade, OAuth, concurrency, and rollback contracts passed.
- Public Python checks verified exact no-op bytes and mtime, absent-file behavior, two independent process writers, raw environment references, and persisted workspace retention.
- Real lock-contention probes verified rename and skill-deletion compensation. The same concurrent MCP remove/enable probe passed on the PR3 base, failed before the cleanup fix, and passed after it.
- The actual async settings router passed concurrent enable and install-only requests with an injected installer runner. A queued request for the same feature installs once. An unrelated config edit completes while installation is paused and survives the feature commit.
- A real isolated gateway and built WebUI passed HTTP and WebSocket settings mutations, invalid-update rejection, plugin approval and replacement revocation, browser refresh persistence, and token renewal. Launch workspace overrides stayed out of the config.

[Remote CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39020676631) passed on the current PR head. Python 3.11 required one rerun after an unchanged test helper raced with process reaping. Native macOS execution is unavailable locally.
