## Latest approval and recovery acceptance (2026-10-17)

**Not activated or release-ready. Do not merge or publish yet.**

The approval environment now requires independent review (no self-review or environment admin bypass, main-only). Existing main branch rules are unchanged. The signing enable variable remains absent; no signing workflow, tag, release, PyPI upload or catalogue write was performed.

This pass rejects malformed bundles before trust-service refresh and verifies that a failed second approval check never requests gateway shutdown. Stable and Preview still require the same fixed official manual-workflow identity, with no unsigned/checksum-only fallback.

Native acceptance now covers consecutive upgrades and a fresh healthy update after each restored service, retaining the same account and conversation history. Private feed generations advance and observed versions are never overwritten. Backup-write failure persists through the first job's automatic retry, but not a separately confirmed next job. The Windows native job budget is 60 minutes (individual subprocesses remain bounded); completed per-case reports survive a later failure. The previous cancelled Windows run was not a completed acceptance pass.

Current head: `0c6e0981073c6138c3627b24d25ea13f39e6149a`. [Current CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39005971036) is complete: **9/9 SUCCESS**. Its first full-suite attempt passed 10,346 tests but failed one existing process-tree liveness assertion (child not confirmed stopped within three seconds). The affected shell/exec-session code and helper are unchanged from the preceding green head; five local focused repeats and 59 related tests passed, which is not Linux reproduction or a root-cause fix. No assertion or timeout is weakened. The first failure remains recorded with no confirmed root cause. Only that failed job was rerun; the native jobs' first-attempt bytes/reports remain authoritative and were not rebuilt.

Main advanced during acceptance to `508cedff3` (durable scheduled delivery). The integration retains its outbox owner and adds that store to the existing lease/backup inventory. Scheduled writes and replay participate in runtime admission; parked gateways cannot initialize the lazy database. No data is moved and no second migration is introduced.

An actual retained updater then exposed a compatibility defect: the new restart coordinator computed the latest data inventory, which exceeded the old immutable reservation. Automatic recovery restored the old service, but that is not a successful upgrade. The fix issues only the reviewed old grant, keeps the new lazy store under a separate ordinary lifetime lease, and defers its writes until activation. Missing authority for any other existing store still fails closed. A real parked-gateway regression reproduced the failure before the fix and passes for both scopes afterward; protocol 1 and old reservations are not rewritten.

Latest local evidence: 130 intersecting regressions and 108 update-job/stop/restart checks passed after the main merge. The compatibility fix passed 35 data/backup/profile/restart tests, an additional 10 data-lease checks, touched lint, focused strict types and all 13 import-boundary rules (groups overlap).

The new macOS arm64 native candidate passed all nine scenarios/15 hops, preserving pending scheduled-delivery records as well as configuration, canonical/display history, continued writes and second starts. Both actual retained baselines (the recent pre-outbox updater and an earlier pre-SQLite updater) passed four scenarios/seven hops each, including post-restoration updates. The actual installer serves 377 WebUI assets and bundled native TUI without frontend build tools and stops its ready gateway cleanly. Candidate `423ff3aa2b0e1c4a88d72270cddc6ce3b71ea7d7` is a private version-only child of the current head; native-wheel SHA-256 `2b1d47abeb9327f5c5cd9ef9913a38d9bf79dcab3e9a145e2eaec10a03fddc3c`.

Reports bind CI merge `3df7943b89ba4f251161c0adaa4db2f0841a3473`; its verified parents are main `508cedff3` and this PR head. These overlapping groups are not summed.

Prior-head evidence: `83d5dfcb7` completed [CI 39002575097](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39002575097), **9/9 SUCCESS**. Those packages predate the new outbox integration and are not evidence for the current target bytes. An earlier CI run exposed a 15-second cold PowerShell ACL/cleanup probe timeout. Its bounded budget is now 60 seconds with every security assertion retained; production browser behavior is unchanged. The incremental approval-patch security review found no confirmed blocking issue in its six changed source files and required callers. This is not an exhaustive audit of the entire PR. Private lifecycle fixtures substitute signature admission; they do **not** prove official signed public continuity.

Remaining release gates: the real official signed old→candidate→next/public-download acceptance; independently reviewed runtime dependency inventory/enforcement and trusted original-owner bootstrap; final same-batch native platform coverage and maintainer/license handoff. Approval authenticates the nanobot artifact, not all owner-selected dependencies, reproducible builds or benign source. It cannot promise protection after full repository/host compromise or 100% availability.

---

## Summary

Integrate managed installation, prebuilt release candidates, exact-version updates, failure recovery and one shared WebUI flow.

This continues chengyongru's work in #5817; its commits and attribution remain intact. #5817 is closed as a duplicate of this PR. Candidate preparation from #6154 is already incorporated. #6146 is the design record. Review this PR as the integration target; do not merge the incorporated branches again as independent updaters.

Ordinary users install prebuilt WebUI and native TUI packages without Bun or Node. Maintainers decide when to request a candidate. There is no scheduled daily packaging or automatic publication.

## User flow and installation ownership

The sidebar and Settings → About share confirmation, progress and saved-job recovery. The gateway selects an exact target, stages and verifies files, obtains stop/install/restart consent, waits for reviewed runtimes to be idle, installs offline and verifies the restarted gateway. Refresh, reconnect and duplicate requests read the same job. Installed package metadata alone cannot prove success.

| Installation | Supported route |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh official installer | Dedicated environment, selection receipt and persistent gateway; inline update and bounded automatic service recovery for eligible layouts. Interrupted first installs retain their owner for retry. |
| Verified POSIX uv 0.11.16 registry tool | Inline update preserves the uv receipt, extras, constraints and additional packages. Saved-job/original-launcher recovery remains available; this does not convert the install to a managed environment. |
| Other uv, pipx, ordinary pip venv | Owner-specific in-app guidance: correct machine/environment, stop and backup steps, applicable copyable command, original-launcher restart and authenticated running-version verification. Unknown extras, fixed sources, unsupported layouts and GitHub-only Preview targets do not receive guessed registry commands. |
| Source, Docker, services, Desktop | Use the original owner/deployment route. Source `update`, `--check` and opt-in `--dev` keep their existing restrictions; source is not Preview. Preserve container volumes. Native Desktop keeps the distributor's updater. |

Only affected background gateways restart, not the computer. Stopped profiles stay stopped. Active tasks and other writers block shutdown. Remote mutations require the existing explicit package-install permission. Displaying or copying guidance never executes it.

## Stable and Preview

**Receive preview updates** is visible, off by default and installation-scoped. Saving it does not authorize installation.

- Offer only a newer compatible Stable or Preview target. Installing a final does not unsubscribe from Preview.
- Turning Preview off does not downgrade. Keep a newer installed Preview until an eligible final appears.
- Reject stale preference revisions and reviewed plans after a channel change. Active/admitted jobs must finish or recover first.
- Preserve withdrawal history, offline errors and incompatible-release explanations. A verified newer final can remain available when the Preview index is unavailable.
- Use complete PyPI artifacts for Stable discovery and a protected catalogue with immutable manifests for Preview. Revalidate exact targets, approved HTTPS hosts, pinned DNS, checksums, sizes and catalogue history.

Stable patches can ship between monthly feature releases. Preview can be prepared as frequently as maintainers request. Candidate preparation and approval to publish its exact artifacts are separate actions. No timer, automatic channel enrollment or public feed is enabled here.

## Ownership and dependencies

- `update_service` owns update policy and saved-job operations. WebUI and CLI are consumers, not alternate executors.
- Agent/session owners expose generic admission, shutdown and pending-work contracts. They do not import update policy.
- Installation/data leases are shared primitives. The updater and ordinary runtimes use the same ownership checks.
- Frozen worker/recovery code can run outside a broken application environment. Do not collapse this independent boundary into the live UI or gateway.
- The protected restart adapter composes the existing CLI launcher; it does not construct a second AgentLoop. Executable import rules restrict this integration to the required startup/process contracts.
- Packaging scripts are preparation tools, not another runtime updater. Feed/plan persistence imports the atomic-file primitive directly rather than the broad model/token helper module.

Previous simplification removed the unmounted prototype updater, duplicate state/lock ownership and pass-through methods without removing supported flows. The current integration preserves main's settings-domain controllers rather than restoring the old flattened controller.

## Failure recovery and compatibility

Eligible managed installs preserve the original program and dependencies before mutation. An independent frozen supervisor can retry the admitted target once. If that fails before activation, it can restore the original program and restart reviewed gateways **only if protected user data is unchanged**. Journaled renames support interrupted restoration. The UI reports **Previous version restored**, not update success.

Recovery never replaces current configuration or chats with an old backup. Activated or data-changing candidates cannot be downgraded automatically. Missing base Python, corrupt backups, persistent storage/ownership failure or loss of both recovery processes can still need an operator. There is no boot-time recovery service or zero-failure guarantee.

Fresh official installation intentionally changes to managed/persistent defaults. Existing installation ownership and protocol 1 remain supported. Optional wire additions and old saved-job behavior remain compatible.

Latest-base integration includes main's SQLite session owner (#5943). Runtime drain precedes backup; the scoped session directory includes the database and sidecars. Do not treat older JSONL-based packaged acceptance as proof for this new base. This update implementation does not add another session migration or storage root.

## Earlier installation-matrix verification (2026-10-16)

Evidence head: `dbba58a058a5d588ae1c7d775bfc3263896c92e9`. [That-head CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38910467525): **all nine checks passed**, including Windows installer checks. This is historical evidence; the latest results are recorded at the top. No merge or release is authorized.

- Real installed-process acceptance on macOS arm64 completed **21 consecutive upgrade/recovery steps**. It covered the official managed installer; uv 0.11.16 inline updates; ordinary pip; pipx 1.8.0 and 1.17.12 (pip backend), including custom constraints/index options; pipx 1.17.12 with its uv backend; and editable source updates with real Git fast-forward and WebUI/TUI builds.
- The same managed account moved from Stable to Preview, skipped Preview versions, reached a final, restored after a bad candidate, then successfully accepted another update. Turning Preview off did not downgrade or restart. A corrupt download was rejected before shutdown. Repeated confirmation did not restart the completed job.
- Each step checked the running gateway, retained configuration and history, canonical SQLite records separately from display transcripts, continued writes, another ordinary start and final listener cleanup. Private synthetic versions and controlled transport are labelled fixtures, not historical or public-download evidence.
- This found a real pipx defect: a generic upgrade can discard the original requirement constraints and pip options. Guidance and both bootstrap scripts now refuse that unsafe route for customized records, without changing the installation owner or exposing private options. Ordinary installs still update; custom-owner reinstall trials retained the original settings across two upgrades. The exact manual handoff documents its base-installation scope.
- The existing eight-scenario packaged recovery probe also passed again on macOS. The harness now reuses seed/snapshot/data checks for consecutive updates and uses the production channel revision and preparation route. No second updater was added.
- **172 focused update/import-boundary tests passed**. **83 real offline installer/hand-off tests passed**, including the four new pipx policy cases. Test groups are not summed. Touched Ruff, shell syntax, diff checks and focused production strict types passed.
- The new Linux x64 and Windows x64 native packages each passed **8/8 installed upgrade/recovery journeys**. Their reports bind CI merge `0d06065e470154847ce222b0646315654a760a76`; its parents are main `559107172` and this head `dbba58a05`. Healthy-wheel SHA-256: Linux `915187e88dd803cdc9033b9a1fd8e04714f668194b2deeb820cca4ed1567e2cd`; Windows `b3b832568e0f10b6c28e0f0498c14251b8467b7e0db79fa1da6cbca52fec9f8a`. Final five-platform artifact acceptance, historical public bootstrap coverage and public downloads remain release gates.

prs.title: fix(tools): number read_file lines by newline like edit_file
prs.body:
## Problem

`read_file` numbers lines with `str.splitlines()`, which also breaks on form feed, vertical tab, lone CR, NEL, U+2028, U+2029 and the ASCII separators `\x1c`-`\x1e`. `edit_file` reports and checks `line_hint` by counting `"\n"`. So the two tools disagree on any file that contains one of those characters. Form feeds are a common page break in C and Python sources (GNU style), and U+2028 appears raw in JS/JSON string literals.

For `"alpha\n\f\n    beta\n    gamma\n"`, `read_file` prints `4|     beta` and "5 lines total", while `edit_file` places `beta` on line 3. The `edit_file` schema tells the model to copy `line_hint` from `read_file`, so `edit_file(old_text="beta", line_hint=4)` fails with "line_hint 4 does not match the old_text location. old_text appears at line 3."

Two more places inside `edit_file` number lines the `splitlines()` way: trim-fallback matches (so an exact match and a trim match of the same block report different lines) and the "Best match ... at line N" hint shown when `old_text` is not found, which the model then uses as its next `line_hint`.

## Fix

- `read_file` splits on `"\n"` (after the existing CRLF normalization; a trailing newline does not add an empty line, so "N lines total" is unchanged for normal files). A file with lone-CR line endings now reads as one line, which is where `edit_file` already placed its text.
- Trim-fallback matches and the best-match hint compute their line number by counting `"\n"` before the match, the same expression the exact and quote-normalized matchers already use.

Not changed: the `grep` tool still numbers lines with `splitlines()`. It reads files without the CRLF normalization, so it needs a separate change.

## Tests

- New `test_edit_file_line_hint_matches_read_file_numbering` (exact and trim-fallback cases): `read_file` shows `3|     beta` and "4 lines total", and `line_hint=3` applies. On main both cases fail with `assert '3|     beta' in '1| alpha\n2| \n3| \n4|     beta ...'`.
- New `test_edit_file_best_match_line_matches_read_file_numbering`: the not-found hint says "at line 3". On main it says "line 4".
- `tests/tools/`: 1172 passed, 6 skipped.
- `ruff check` is clean. `basedpyright` reports 0 errors in `filesystem.py`.

prs.title: fix(matrix): keep HTML formatting in m.new_content for edits
prs.body:
## Problem

A streamed Matrix reply is sent once and then updated through `m.replace` edits of that first event (the throttled intermediate edits and the final one). `_build_matrix_text_content` puts `format` and `formatted_body` on each edit's top-level fallback, but builds `m.new_content` from `body` and `msgtype` only.

Clients that apply edits read `m.new_content`. From the spec, [Applying `m.new_content`](https://spec.matrix.org/latest/client-server-api/#applying-mnew_content): "When applying a replacement, the `content` of the original event is treated as being overwritten entirely by `m.new_content`, with the exception of `m.relates_to`, which is left *unchanged*." Its example ends with "Note that `formatted_body` is now absent, because it was absent in the replacement event." So in Element and other edit-aware clients the finished reply shows raw Markdown (`**bold**`, headings, backticks, tables), although the first draft was rendered as HTML.

## Fix

When the text renders to HTML, put `format` and `formatted_body` inside `m.new_content` as well. This applies to the intermediate edits and the final one. Plain-text edits are unchanged.

## Tests

- New `test_build_matrix_text_content_with_event_id_preserves_html_formatting`. On main it fails because `m.new_content` lacks `format` and `formatted_body`; it passes with the fix.
- `nanobot/channels/matrix/tests`: 123 passed.
- `ruff check` is clean. `basedpyright` reports 0 errors in `runtime.py`.

Not tested against a live homeserver.

prs.title: fix(cli-apps): record install provenance, fail closed on registry drift
prs.body:
## Problem

The CLI Apps catalog (`nanobot apps`) installs packages from remote registries whose metadata is **unsigned** — anyone controlling (or compromising) a registry entry can change what gets executed on a user's machine. `installed.json` only recorded the resolved version, so `nanobot apps update` had no way to detect that the install command had changed upstream since install time. A swapped `install_cmd` / `npm_package` / `entry_point` would be executed silently on the next update.

Refs #4885

## Change

- **Record provenance at install time**: `registry_url`, `catalog_updated_at`, `install_cmd`, `npm_package` are persisted into the install entry (kept internal, stripped from the app payload).
- **Drift gate on update** (`_registry_drift`): compare a fresh catalog entry against the recorded install metadata:
  - Blocking drift in `install_strategy` / `install_cmd` / `npm_package` / `entry_point` **fails closed** with a `CliAppError` instructing the user to uninstall and install again to accept the new source.
  - `version` drift is reported but never blocks.
  - Entries installed before this change carry no provenance and keep updating unchanged (backwards compatible).
- **Command visibility**: surface the exact argv (`subprocess.list2cmdline`) in `last_action` for both install and update, so logs and UX show what was actually executed.

## Tests

4 new tests in `tests/cli_apps/test_service.py`:

- `test_install_records_registry_provenance`
- `test_update_blocks_changed_install_command`
- `test_update_reports_version_drift_without_blocking`
- `test_update_allows_legacy_entries_without_recorded_provenance`

`tests/cli_apps` suite: 45 passed.

prs.title: fix(deepseek): align model capabilities with the official API
prs.body:
## Why

DeepSeek serves both legacy Flash names through the current multimodal `deepseek-flash`, but nanobot silently removes images for `deepseek-v4-flash`. Model discovery also discards official capability metadata and suggests generic reasoning levels. Keep immutable compatibility facts in the existing provider model registry and normalize advisory discovery metadata at the settings boundary.

## What changed

- Resolve Flash aliases through shared model metadata and preserve image input on Chat Completions and Responses; Pro remains text-only. Keep wire model IDs and existing official/proxy API routing unchanged.
- Validate catalog output limits, modalities and supported/default thinking levels, with known-model fallback. Preserve the explicit `none` control even when the live catalog lists only enabled thinking levels; distinguish it from provider-default and keep custom strings usable.
- Extend the settings DTO with optional fields, reuse the existing picker without frontend provider branches, and document naming, budgets and deferred search support.

## Scope

Tracks [NAN-271](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-271). This PR was initially published as **Draft** at `b0eb7608517`; bounded real-key verification subsequently passed on `2ecebac8a96fd96ea94c47898e9984a2baac5844` before requesting Ready for review.

Does not enable standalone DeepSeek Search/Fetch, Pro hosted search, Anthropic Messages or Files; does not migrate cross-provider reasoning configuration. Does not rewrite users' model IDs or change existing preset budgets, API routing, credentials or services. Catalog output limits remain advisory; existing new-preset context initialization is unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

Runtime image policy uses the immutable provider record, not online discovery or a new network/cache service. Valid online metadata takes precedence over static fallback, with a known explicit off control separate from enabled thinking strengths. Raw `api_capabilities` is not forwarded: its Messages behavior has no adapter consumer here.

The suspected Responses reasoning-history incompatibility did not reproduce: a real Chat-history reconstruction containing `output_text` reasoning parts returned HTTP 200 and the expected synthetic token. The shared OpenAI converter therefore remains unchanged; this single successful case is not a guarantee about every future endpoint or payload.

## Blast Radius

DeepSeek message sanitization and additive model catalog fields. Unknown/custom models retain manual values and do not inherit DeepSeek model facts. The existing picker tolerates hosts without the new fields; older clients can ignore the optional additions. Other providers' request conversion and third-party naming/routing are unchanged.

## Verification

- Relevant provider/settings suite: **1624 passed** (`PYTHONPATH=tests .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/providers tests/webui/test_settings_routes.py tests/webui/test_settings_models.py tests/webui/test_settings_api.py -q --disable-warnings`). Legacy-alias regression demonstrated before the fix; updated the existing text-only image test to use nonvisual Pro instead of the now-visual Flash alias.
- Model-settings frontend suite: **75 passed** (`PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:$PATH /home/cyr/.bun/bin/bun run test src/tests/settings-models.test.tsx --reporter verbose`, in `webui/`).
- Full repository Ruff and BasedPyright: passed, 0 type errors/warnings. Python import boundaries: passed. `bun run check:imports`, `bun run test:imports`: passed (37 tests, one Windows-only case skipped on Linux). `bun run lint` and `bun run build`: passed; build retains the bundle-size warning.
- Isolated gateway + Chromium, synthetic local catalog: `max`, `none`, Default and a custom effort each saved and survived reload; no browser runtime/console errors. Catalog fields reached the existing picker. Owned gateway, fixture server, browser and ports were cleaned up. This browser check is not a real model call.
- **Real DeepSeek official API**, locally configured credential loaded only in-process: **14/14 HTTP 200 requests and 26 checks passed on the final head**, plus one earlier successful `/models` discovery request (15 total, within a 16-request budget). The initial discovery exposed that live `supported_levels` omits `none`; a failing regression and the final normalization correction cover that observation.
  - Authenticated `/v1/models`: real max output, modalities, enabled levels/default retained; explicit off control preserved.
  - Chat Completions and Responses basic calls with `none`: expected marker returned, no thinking content.
  - Canonical Flash and both legacy aliases × both APIs: in-memory blue PNG retained on the wire and correctly identified (6 calls).
  - Both APIs: low-effort streaming function call, reasoning deltas, synthetic tool result and final answer; Responses continued from raw provider state (4 calls).

## Why

Implement [NAN-249](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-249): renaming one topic should not interrupt the conversation with a modal. Keep the existing action-menu entry and edit the topic directly in its sidebar row.

## What changed

- Add a shared inline editor for standalone topics and grouped panes, with prefill/autofocus, Enter/checkmark to save, Escape/× to cancel, the existing trimmed nonblank/160-character validation, and composition-safe keyboard handling.
- Wait for the existing sidebar mutation's acknowledgement before restoring the title. Failed saves retain the draft and show a localized inline error; explicit retry reuses the draft without silently requeuing failed renames.
- Preserve focus and navigation isolation, including the mobile navigation sheet, and update the gallery, user documentation, and regression tests.
- Remove the obsolete topic-dialog defaults and their two translation keys from all ten locales. Rename the still-used shared modal to `RenameDialog`, require caller-supplied group/project copy, and replace the stale topic-dialog gallery example and unused focus-test fixture.

## Scope

Only topic/pane rename interaction changes. Project and conversation-group rename behavior remains unchanged; their shared dialog is renamed and no longer carries unused topic defaults. No backend, wire protocol, capability, persistence-schema, dependency, or configuration changes.

## Tradeoffs

Keep the existing serializer/coalescing policy for optimistic pin/archive/workbench changes and add a narrow acknowledged rename operation to that same writer. Parallel full-state writes could clobber concurrent changes; a generalized persistence-queue rewrite is unnecessary for this interaction.

## Blast Radius

Standalone topic rows, grouped pane rows, and the desktop/mobile sidebar share the editor. The main persistence risk is preserving optimistic edits made before/during a rename; hook regressions exercise serialization, canonical titles, rejection, reconnect, and explicit retry. Current client/host traffic uses the unchanged `sidebar.update` contract.

## Verification

- Initial feature snapshot: `bun run test` — **PASS**, 161 files / 2,825 tests. The follow-up cleanup does not change the inline editor or persistence implementation.
- After cleanup: focused Vitest run — **PASS**, 7 files / 193 tests covering the sidebar list, inline rename, action focus, persistence, app layout, gallery inventory and localization.
- `bun run lint` — **PASS**.
- `bun run build` — **PASS** (existing large-chunk warning).
- `bun run check:imports` — **PASS**.
- `bun run test:imports` — **PASS**, 37 passed / 1 Windows-only case skipped on Linux.
- Real Chromium 149 against the built UI and an isolated real gateway — **PASS**: autofocus/prefill; Enter + trimming + refresh persistence; Escape/blank validation; actual server filesystem write failure retaining the draft and prior stored title, followed by same-name retry; grouped-pane inline rename and unchanged group dialog; mobile IME/Escape isolation; 390px touch Save + reload; no browser runtime errors.

After cleanup, fresh Chromium verification against the rebuilt isolated preview also passed: inline draft editing/cancellation without navigation, the renamed dialog's lazy chunk loads successfully, localized group dialog input/blank validation/cancellation, and no page runtime errors. All follow-up drafts were canceled without modifying existing sample data.

Browser verification used fixture-only isolated data and no real model credentials. Local evidence and the authenticated preview link are kept private rather than publishing access credentials in this PR.

prs.body:
## Why

Several tests could pass without exercising their named behavior: copied production orchestration, background assertions swallowed by error handling, disconnected negative spies, and fixtures rejected before reaching the intended I/O or rendering path. Replace those false-green checks with observable behavior and remove only scenarios dominated by identified stronger retained coverage.

This completes the **63 recorded findings across nine audit domains, plus both Docker smoke concerns**, rather than leaving another implementation batch. The original audit structurally triaged 683 test/infrastructure files at `c7ab7aa6`, with deeper owner/counterpart inspection for candidates; this is not exhaustive semantic certification of every surviving test.

## What changed

- **Agent/session:** actual registry context injection and subagent callbacks; requested/acknowledged responsiveness and physical-worker-slot ownership; real second-request shell-guard payloads; accepted durable transcript preservation across checkpoints; Dream progress privacy; failure followed by healthy real recovery. Retain supported `(nothing)` checkpoint semantics, identity composition, and exact stronger consolidation counterparts.
- **Providers/tools:** real SDK requests with rotating Azure bearer tokens/scopes and explicit-key precedence; deterministic Copilot singleflight; rendered substantive Codex diagnostics and real transport-error privacy; emitted events/raw SQLite usage privacy; genuinely UTF-8-sensitive surrogate checks; actual second-write rollback and successful filtered children. Exec early-yield now uses child readiness/release rather than a ceiling longer than the entire yield budget.
- **Dispatch/channels/CLI:** real ChannelManager routing/coalescing/pending final delivery and compaction events before adapter filtering; observable WebSocket wrapper arguments/results plus semantic namespace ownership; real history surrogate roundtrip. Fix reaction/UTF-16/MIME fixtures, ephemeral listener readiness/cleanup, worker/typing handshakes, SDK domain selection, best-effort failures and timer-driven Linear checks. Isolate media, recovery transcripts and startup persistence seams.
- **API/settings/build:** actual two-file multipart upload and durable transcript-cache output; real cross-setting restart mutations/reversions; independent shared runtime wire-key fixture checked against executed catalogues; actual wheel/sdist bytes for channel UI/resources; actual Rollup write hook compressing finalized disk bytes rather than calling its helper directly.
- **Clients/rendering:** connected Service Worker observers on discriminating requests, effective Tailwind channel CSS, valid canonical replay fixtures, actual TUI lifecycle decoding and automatic animation ticking, independent forbidden classes, and parsed-HTML preboot locale execution in document order.
- **Browser acceptance:** real Chromium with production CSS/components verifies both oversized-dialog placements (beginning/end keyboard reachability, focus restoration and scroll unlock) and twice-reopened completed history (positive content plus subtree animation observation). Keep component declaration smoke tests honestly named; add the browser tests to the existing Ubuntu WebUI CI job.
- **Docker:** preserve nonzero status even with plausible success text; unique owned image/container names and early EXIT cleanup. Real-shell tests at a fake external Docker boundary verify failures and concurrent resource ownership without requiring a local daemon.

Consolidations preserve full SSE/segment/fallback framing, actual large-code renderer coverage, exact long tool-text/image persistence, both early-persist branches, read-only model switching, ordinary config inspection, retry/error/platform matrices, and the stronger real-child/recursive-merge/Matrix-wire counterparts. Security, durability, wire compatibility and supported platform regressions are not blanket-pruned.

## Scope

**91 files, +1,906 / -1,406** against `c7ab7aa6`. No production implementation or protocol behavior changes. The original tests-only scope is expanded only for the missing real-browser proof: pinned Playwright **dev** dependency (both lockfiles), fixture/config/typecheck/lint/docs, and the existing CI job. Runtime dependency entries remain unchanged. Independent final review covers all 47 root-test paths and all 44 remaining paths, including new/deleted files; no actionable findings remain.

## Blast Radius

Tests and verification infrastructure. The primary risks are losing a distinct regression during consolidation and test-owned I/O escaping isolation. Explicit retained-counterpart tracing, exact-snapshot independent reviews, offline guards, child/listener/task cleanup, deliberate-fault controls and complete suites address those risks. Browser fixtures use real components/CSS without a gateway; they are not a live deployment or full PWA lifecycle test.

## Verification

- Python 3.12/Linux, all channel dependencies installed: `pytest -q -n 4` — **9,927 passed, 52 skipped**. Final startup-isolation change also has its affected-file recheck and exact-final full repeat.
- WebUI: `bun run test:coverage --maxWorkers=4 --minWorkers=1` — **162 files / 2,828 passed**. Every source-file line/statement/function counter matches the unchanged baseline: **50,563/54,167 (93.34%)** lines/statements; **2,783/3,064 (90.82%)** functions. Aggregate branches **18,741/21,332 → 18,740/21,331 (87.85% both)**; four files have branch-counter differences, not claimed identical branch identities.
- Browser: matching Playwright Chromium 156.0.8078.4/revision 1248, `bun run test:browser` — **3 passed**, including the browser TypeScript check.
- TUI: `bun test` — **265 passed / 29 files**; `bun run check` passed.
- Full WebUI lint/build (production TypeScript), Ruff on all **53** extant changed Python files, Bash syntax, import-boundary/checker tests, frozen Bun lock consistency and `git diff --check` passed.
- Deliberate faults reject missing checkpoint/registry updates, premature worker-slot release, transcript rewrite, progress leakage, recovery early exit, stale/detached bearer auth, broken singleflight, dropped/corrupt dispatcher output, bad wrapper delegation, namespace duplication, lossy history/text sanitation, missing rollback/cache/upload behavior, escaped channel errors, wrong SDK domains/MIME, inert gzip/catalogue/preboot behavior, disabled TUI ticking, descendant entrance animation and clipped dialog controls. Behavior-preserving formatting/instrumentation/coalescing/message-copy controls pass. These are selected regression probes, not an exhaustive mutation score.

prs.title: fix(update): close revalidation and recovery gaps
prs.body:
## Why

Stacked follow-up to #6168, targeting `codex/live-update-ui`. This addresses the three confirmed review findings: [catalogue history at handoff](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6168#discussion_r4302673476), [stale first supervisor launch](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6168#discussion_r4302673485), and [interrupted preparation recovery](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6168#discussion_r4302673488).

## What changed

- Reuse the installation's `releases` cache for final handoff revalidation, so a catalogue rollback cannot erase an already observed withdrawal before shutdown.
- Validate confirmation identity before the first supervision journal is published, and keep recovery/restoration bound to that confirmation while allowing an admitted completion to outlive its launch window.
- Offer **Review update** for preparation jobs restored after reconnect. Clear the saved job only after successful gateway settlement, then show a fresh review requiring another installation confirmation; keep refused or lost responses recoverable.

## Scope

The three update-flow fixes and their regression tests, plus documentation cleanup. The update guide now focuses on user actions and recovery; a separate `docs/update-protocol.md` owns developer API and lifecycle rules. The quick start and CLI reference link to the owning guide, the release checklist removes repeated explanations, and Markdown paragraphs use one source line each.

No dependencies, capabilities, persistence formats, release artifacts/workflows, or installation permissions change. Normal preparation confirmed in the current tab continues without an extra recovery prompt; handoff settlement remains gated by its existing optional capability.

## Blast Radius

Final pre-shutdown release checks, automatic-recovery supervisors, and restored WebUI update dialogs. Stale supervisor launches now stop before taking a newer confirmation's recovery budget. Preparation settlement still relies on the gateway's real ownership checks, refuses live owners, and does not prepare or install another update automatically.

## Verification

Documentation follow-up checks: Markdown AST inspection across nine related pages found no manual paragraph wraps and validated 231 local links. All 18 release-guide headings and nine command blocks were preserved. `tests/test_documentation_build.py` passed **3 tests** with one Windows-only skip; the actual documentation build hook copied all **60 documents** byte-for-byte in a disposable tree, including the new protocol guide. CLI flags were checked with isolated `nanobot update --help`; no update or publication was run.

The behavioral checks below ran at `66f6da20b6a492be931756102544cb495b7f7516`. The follow-up changes only Markdown; runtime code, tests, configuration and dependencies are unchanged, so those results are carried forward rather than presented as reruns.

- Python 3.12: `pytest -q tests/test_update_jobs.py tests/test_update_stop.py tests/test_release_feed.py tests/test_release_trust.py tests/webui/test_update_plans.py tests/test_update_plan.py tests/test_update_channels.py` — **237 passed**, two metadata deprecation warnings. A host-only launcher used symlinks for disposable fixture venvs because this standalone Python cannot execute copied binaries; updater code and frozen helpers were unchanged.
- `cd webui && bun run test` — **2,841 passed** across 163 files. `bun run build`, `bun run lint`, and `bun run check:imports` passed; `bun run test:imports` passed 37 tests with one Windows-specific skip.
- Touched-Python Ruff, focused basedpyright, Python import boundaries, and `git diff --check` passed.
- All three new regression scenarios failed on the original implementation before passing with the fixes. The supervisor regression uses real frozen supervisor/worker processes and offline pip in disposable fixture installations, with synthetic preflight/restart bodies.
- Chromium plus an isolated gateway: both saved preparation phases survived refresh, settled to `preparation_failed`, and opened a new review without sending prepare/execute/retry. A real preparation lease produced 409 and preserved read-only recovery. Saved jobs were synthetic and only the fresh-plan response was substituted; this is not a crash-to-upgrade E2E. Browser, lease child, and isolated gateway were cleaned up.
- Linux-only local verification; no Windows/macOS or public-release installation claim. The existing Test Suite workflow only triggers for PRs targeting `main`, so this stacked PR does not automatically receive that CI matrix.

prs.title: fix(tools): accept integral JSON numbers for integer parameters
prs.body:
## Problem

A model can return `{"query":"hello","count":3.0}` for a tool whose `count` parameter has an integer schema. [JSON Schema treats numbers with no fractional part as integers](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/numeric#integer), but Python decodes `3.0` as a float. Nanobot rejects the call with `count should be integer` before the tool can run.

The same mismatch affects nullable integer fields and unions such as `["integer", "string"]`.

## Fix

Use one integer predicate for validation and union matching. When an integral float matches an integer parameter, convert it to a Python `int` before execution so tools can safely use it for counts, ranges, or indexes. Fractional values, booleans, and non-finite numbers remain invalid integers.

## Tests

Added three schema cases and a registry execution regression. All four fail on the base revision; the registry now executes the call with `count=3`.

- Full tool-validation suite: **144 passed**.
- Existing fraction, boolean, range, and union checks pass.
- Ruff, BasedPyright on the changed implementation, import-boundary checks, and `git diff --check`: passed.

prs.title: fix(media): keep Unicode upload names within the filesystem byte limit
prs.body:
## Problem

Document uploads can fail with `OSError: [Errno 36] File name too long` when the original name contains CJK characters or emoji. `media_destination` limits the stem to 80 characters, but filesystem component limits are measured in bytes on Linux.

For example, an 80-character CJK stem plus `.pdf` uses 244 UTF-8 bytes. The 12-character upload ID and underscore increase the saved name to 257 bytes. The same helper chooses names for data-URL attachments and binary WebUI uploads.

## Fix

Keep the existing character limit, then fit the stem into the byte budget left by the ID, separator, and MIME-derived extension. Drop an incomplete final UTF-8 sequence when truncation is needed. Names that already fit retain their current layout.

## Tests

Added real file-write regressions for CJK and emoji document names. Both fail on the base revision with `ENAMETOOLONG` and pass with this change. The tests also check the extension, saved content, and valid Unicode name.

- Media decoding and binary attachment-store suites: **38 passed**.
- Ruff on both changed files: passed.
- BasedPyright on `media_decode.py`: passed.
- Import-boundary checks: passed.

prs.title: fix(webui): preserve list semantics around links
prs.body:
## Why

Fix [NAN-269](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-269): a normal Markdown list item containing a web link could be flattened into a single compact preview. The replacement consumed nested items, inline formatting, additional link destinations, ordered markers, and task status; desktop truncation then hid part of the resulting label.

## What changed

- Classify compact previews at the Markdown AST boundary, where the parent list type and the entire item structure are available. Only a non-task unordered item consisting of one plain-text title, one line break, and one HTTP(S) URL-only link is eligible. Custom link labels, tooltips, prose, additional blocks, and additional links stay ordinary Markdown.
- Pass validated preview metadata to the list renderer instead of recursively flattening React descendants. Keep the existing compact row, title cleanup, and favicon fallback unchanged.
- Add real-component regressions for the complete reported message, distinct link targets, nested/ordered/task lists, structural boundaries, unsafe protocols, all static/streaming/preserved-layout combinations, streaming completion, and a preview gaining more streamed content.

## Scope

Only the Markdown renderer and its tests change. No dependency, styling, transport, gateway, authentication, production configuration, or unrelated PR changes. Compact previews still work without a Sources heading, including URL-only angle autolinks and hard line breaks/CRLF. Formatted titles and ambiguous structures deliberately retain their original Markdown semantics.

## Blast Radius

This affects compact-preview eligibility in shared WebUI Markdown rendering. The important regression risks are suppressing legitimate previews or replacing content that carries additional semantics; both positive preview tests and negative structural cases exercise the actual parser and renderer.

## Current snapshot and verification

Rebased onto latest fetched `main` **`756f6a6fe5012fb59e690850d2a41517e116c786`** at the user's request. Current head: **`7cff9781b461cc650ba480e774ed0697f7cee7ac`**, one task commit above that main, published with an explicit `--force-with-lease` for the previous head. One renderer conflict was resolved by keeping main's `!documentPath` boundary: document previews never opt into chat compact previews or load favicons. A document-mode regression was added; no other PR or daily gateway configuration was changed.

- Fresh focused run: `bun run test src/tests/markdown-text-renderer.test.tsx src/tests/file-preview-panel.test.tsx src/tests/preview-pane.test.tsx --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=1` — **3 files / 138 passed**, including **121 renderer tests**.
- Fresh full `bun run test:coverage --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=1` — **160 files / 2,812 tests passed**, exit 0, on this exact head.
- ESLint, production build/TypeScript, frontend import boundaries, import-checker tests (**37 pass / 1 Windows-only skip**), Python import boundaries, and `git diff --check` — passed. Existing large-chunk and test-environment warnings remain in raw logs.
- Real Chromium on this head's production bundle and an authenticated isolated Gateway: desktop **1440×1050**, narrow **390×1050**, original/controls, refresh/replay, distinct targets, nested/ordered/task lists, compact rows, and intentionally induced favicon-to-globe fallback — passed. Real composer SSE was observed in flight, completed, and replayed after reload, preserving **2 top-level + 3 nested items**, **4 code tokens**, and the bold **#6269** PR label only.
- The new main's real Markdown file-preview path also passed: title-plus-URL stays ordinary, external embeds remain links, fragments do not navigate to chat, **zero external HTTP requests** were observed, and Source/Preview toggles work. No browser runtime exceptions or unexpected console errors; auth 401 and induced icon 404s are expected.
- The original regression-first 18 failures and old-head results remain historical evidence, not fresh executions. Local Python unit tests were not run because the available runtime venv lacks test dependencies; the current backend's provider/stream path was exercised through the real Gateway. CI skips are not counted as test passes.
- [GitHub CI for the current head](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39049950177): **success**. Detect changes, WebUI and Docker passed; Python/Windows/TUI jobs were skipped by changed-path scope, not counted as test passes.

**Visual report and replacement instance:** [NAN-269 verification and isolated acceptance](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/document/nan-269-pr-6276-验证与隔离验收-bbd29886fd11) (Linear workspace access required). The latest section identifies this head; older sections/screenshots are explicitly historical. A new screenshot shows this head's chat and document preview together. Current raw screenshots/results, per-command receipts, range-diff, and reproducible scripts are retained outside tracked source at `/home/cyr/.nanobot/workspace/tmp/nan-269-rebase-20261018/`.

The old acceptance instance was stopped and its data retained. A replacement, persistent, authenticated interactive instance is running at **`http://127.0.0.1:18769/`** from this exact head. It has independent OS HOME/nanobot home/configuration/workspace/sessions and uses a loopback deterministic SSE fixture model, with no production keys or sessions. Original repro, boundary controls, real streaming, and a guarded Markdown file-preview fixture are available. The newly generated password is read locally from the private path in the report; never publish its contents. The report includes safe SSH tunneling and scoped status/stop instructions.

The PR is **not merged**. Human visual acceptance remains pending. The replacement instance remains running after handoff.

prs.title: feat(providers): add IO Intelligence (io.net) provider
prs.body:
> **Official io.net contribution.** This pull request is submitted on behalf of io.net, the team behind [IO Intelligence](https://io.net). We would like nanobot (HKUDS) users to be able to run inference on IO Intelligence out of the box. Happy to adjust anything to match the project's conventions, and we will keep the integration up to date.

## Summary

Adds IO Intelligence (by io.net) as a built-in provider, following the same registry pattern as SiliconFlow / Novita AI (OpenAI-compatible gateways whose model ids keep their `org/name` prefix).

IO Intelligence serves an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API at `https://api.intelligence.io.solutions/api/v1` (Bearer auth; `GET /models` is public). Model ids are `org/name` style, e.g. `meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct`. Users configure `apiKey` (env var `IONET_API_KEY`) and everything else derives from the registry entry.

## Changes

- `nanobot/providers/registry.py` — `ProviderSpec(name="ionet", ...)`: `backend="openai_compat"`, `is_gateway=True`, `env_key="IONET_API_KEY"`, `display_name="IO Intelligence"`, `detect_by_base_keyword="intelligence.io.solutions"`, `default_api_base="https://api.intelligence.io.solutions/api/v1"`, `strip_model_prefixes=("ionet",)` (an explicit `ionet/org/model` id is sent as `org/model`; opencode precedent). Placed in the gateway cluster after Novita AI.
- `nanobot/config/schema.py` — `ionet: ProviderConfig` field (the registry's documented step 2).
- `docs/providers.md` — "IO Intelligence Gateway" section in the same format as the Eden AI Gateway section (config example + notes), including the multi-gateway routing note.
- `docs/configuration.md` — `ionet` row in the provider directory table.
- `tests/providers/test_ionet_provider.py` — mirrors `test_edenai_provider.py`: config field exists, registry contract, forced-provider default base URL, gateway routes unprefixed models when configured (novita-parity), model-id preservation and top-level `reasoning_effort` passthrough through `_build_kwargs`.
- `tests/webui/test_settings_api.py` — `test_settings_payload_exposes_ionet_provider` (precedent parity with the Eden AI / OrcaRouter rows).
- `webui/src/lib/provider-brand.ts` + `webui/src/components/settings/shared/ModelControls.tsx` — WebUI brand entry, deferred model list, and provider icon, matching the OrcaRouter precedent (the WebUI loads the catalog after the API key is saved).
- `webui/src/tests/settings-models.test.tsx` — "defers the IO Intelligence catalog until the user searches" (OrcaRouter-parity coverage for the deferred list).

## Testing

- `pytest tests/providers/test_ionet_provider.py tests/webui/test_settings_api.py tests/config` — 209 passed (7 ionet provider tests, including the prefix-strip and unprefixed-routing cases).
- Full python suite — 6102 passed / 9 skipped / 0 failures; serial CLI subset 157 passed. Two timing-sensitive gateway tests flake only under full-CPU parallel runs and reproduce identically on the base commit (environmental).
- `ruff check nanobot tests conftest.py` (full CI scope) — clean; `basedpyright` (strict, full project) — 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes.
- WebUI (bun, as CI runs it): `bun install --frozen-lockfile` clean, `bun run lint` (eslint --max-warnings 0) clean, `bun run test` — 96 files / 1554 tests passed; `tsc --noEmit` zero new errors vs the base commit (verified in a scratch worktree).
- Routing: 14 probe scenarios — ionet-only config routes everything; with other providers configured, colliding families (`deepseek-ai/*`, `qwen/*`, `google/*`, `mistralai/*`, …) route away (hence the docs pinning note); forced `provider: "ionet"` always wins; `ionet/org/model` is sent as `org/model` (prefix stripped).
- Live endpoint (unauthenticated): `GET /api/v1/models` → 200, 35 models, both example ids present, and the response parses through nanobot's catalog parser 35/35; `POST /api/v1/chat/completions` → 401 (base URL + Bearer model correct). `nanobot status` with an io.net config renders "IO Intelligence: ✓".
- `ruff format --check` not applied: the existing tree predates `ruff format` (it flags unrelated pre-existing lines); formatting churn is kept out of this PR. The new code follows the surrounding style.
- Live chat generation not tested (no API key available to the contributor); io.net-side acceptance of `reasoning_effort` on reasoning models remains the one key-gated unknown.

## Notes

- Chat Completions only: the spec sets no `responses_models`, so the OpenAI Responses path is never selected for io.net models (verified against the provider-level Responses restriction and the config-level `api_type` gate).
- `keywords=("ionet",)` keeps model-name matching conservative — io.net ids (`meta-llama/...`, `deepseek-ai/...`) are ambiguous across gateways, so users select the provider explicitly (same behaviour as SiliconFlow/Novita). With io.net as the only configured provider, plain model IDs route to it.
- `detect_by_base_keyword` is kept for registry-schema parity with the other gateway entries; it is only consulted in the local-endpoint fallback loop and has no runtime effect for a cloud gateway like this one.

prs.title: refactor(agent): deduplicate model request preparation
prs.body:
## Why

Normal model requests and no-tools recovery requests duplicated context preparation and provider-context assembly. Share this preparation without combining their different streaming, response-observation, cancellation, and usage-accounting behavior.

## What changed

- Replace `_build_request_kwargs` with `_prepare_model_request`, which prepares the governed messages and assembles generation settings and provider context for both paths. Malformed-call recovery continues to use the prepared messages.
- Attach streaming callbacks conditionally, then dispatch normal requests through a single provider call site.
- Add a regression covering two malformed tool-call responses followed by successful no-tools recovery, including tool suppression, callback selection, transcript content, and usage from all three requests.

## Scope

Only `nanobot/agent/runner.py` and `tests/agent/test_runner_core.py` change. No changes to `AgentLoop`, scheduling, provider retries, public APIs, configuration, persistence formats, or dependencies.

Production code decreases by 15 lines; the regression adds 58 test lines. The runner retains 28 methods and gains no classes. This is request-preparation deduplication, not a full lifecycle redesign or a performance/token-use improvement.

## Tradeoffs

Usage accounting and request completion remain at their existing call sites. No-tools finalization observes responses and handles exceptions in a different order from normal tool-capable requests; forcing those stages into one helper would require modes or callbacks and risk changing behavior.

## Blast Radius

Both main-agent and subagent execution use the shared runner. The affected contracts are governed request payloads, generation/preset propagation, streaming callbacks, and recovery usage totals. The refactor retains `tools=None` for no-tools requests and preserves the existing cancellation, reasoning-close, compaction, and accounting order.

## Verification

[Full pre-PR CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39048081173) passed all nine jobs on commit `d8830d4463fe74a73bf9d3efe77920299faaafec`: Python 3.11, Python 3.14 with coverage, Windows Python 3.14, Windows process compatibility, WebUI, Linux/Windows TUI, Docker, and change detection.

Local Linux/Python 3.12 verification with all extras and channel dependencies:

- Full Python/channel suite plus serial CLI tests: **9,936 passed, 52 skipped**, no failures; combined coverage **86.18%**. Skips include platform-specific checks and two unchanged Feishu collection guards.
- `python -m pytest -n 4 --dist loadfile --ignore=tests/cli/test_commands.py --cov=nanobot --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered -q -o faulthandler_timeout=60`
- `python -m pytest tests/cli/test_commands.py --cov=nanobot --cov-append --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered -q`
- `ruff check nanobot tests conftest.py scripts/check_import_boundaries.py`
- `basedpyright` — 0 errors or warnings.
- `python -B -m scripts.check_import_boundaries` — 10 rules, 160 files passed.
- `uv pip check` and diff whitespace checks passed.

Additional public SDK HTTP/SSE smoke verification used `Nanobot.from_config`, `stream`, and `run` with the actual configured provider and a local scripted model endpoint. A real file-tool run completed in two requests; empty-response recovery completed in three requests with no tools in the final wire payload. Both scenarios verified output, usage, and nonempty preset/generation settings. All owned resources were cleaned up; this was protocol verification, not a paid/live-model evaluation.

prs.title: fix(webui): align mention overlay spacing with the native caret
prs.body:
## Why

When the composer decorates an app or session mention, its textarea keeps the native caret while an overlay draws the visible text. The textarea uses `text-autospace: no-autospace`, but the overlay inherits `normal` from the body. In browsers that support CJK autospace, mixed-script text then drifts away from the caret.

Fixes [NAN-270](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-270). The issue's Resources contain the original screenshot, the failing spacing control, and a screenshot from the fixed production build.

## What changed

- Apply `text-autospace: no-autospace` through the composer text classes shared by the textarea and mention overlay.
- Add a mixed-script mention regression test that checks identical display text and the spacing rule on both layers.

## Scope

This covers CLI, MCP, and session mention overlays in thread, hero, and compact composers. Message-body autospace remains enabled. Mention identities, selection handling, IME events, logo geometry, host protocol, and persisted browser state are unchanged.

## Blast Radius

Only composer typography changes. The regression risk is mismatched editing and overlay geometry, especially around CJK/Latin boundaries and wrapped lines; the checks below exercise those paths without changing the native caret.

## Verification

- Regression test demonstrated failing before the fix and passing after it.
- Full WebUI coverage run: `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --coverage --maxWorkers=4 --minWorkers=2` — 160 files and 2,781 tests passed; coverage thresholds passed (93.24% statements/lines, 87.74% branches, 90.77% functions).
- ESLint across WebUI and channel-owned frontend/tests with `--max-warnings 0` passed. `bun run check:imports` passed for 364 files; `bun run test:imports` passed 37 tests, with one Windows-only skip.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` and `vite build` passed.
- Built production App against a real isolated gateway in Chromium 149: restored the old overlay inheritance as a failing control, then verified corrected geometry, native mouse/arrow positioning, CLI mentions with/without logos, MCP/session mentions, mixed-script/digit boundaries, narrow wrapping and scrolling, thread/hero/compact layouts, clipboard cut/copy/undo, and draft restoration.
- CDP-driven IME composition, cancellation, and commit passed. This is not hardware IME or cross-browser certification.
- A separate retained acceptance instance serves the same tested bundle; HTTP health, bundle hash, actual conversation rendering, and browser geometry were rechecked. Its textarea/overlay maximum horizontal character-position difference was 0.016 px, with no browser runtime errors.

No Python or terminal code changed; the Python/TUI suites were not run. GitHub CI is separate from these completed local checks.

prs.title: feat(webui): preview Markdown files with a source toggle
prs.body:
## Summary

Markdown files currently open as source in the file preview pane. This change adds a read-only Preview / Source control. Preview is the default.

- Reuse the shared Markdown renderer, segmented control, theme tokens and source viewer.
- Keep source text, line numbers, truncation notices and the existing file API. The control does not read or write the file again.
- Show embedded images as links. Do not load remote images or favicons when a document opens. Local links use the current session's file access checks and resolve from the document's folder.
- Keep HTML and MDX components inert. Section-only links remain text. Other file types keep their existing behavior.
- Add all ten translations, a component gallery example and user documentation.
- Reuse the existing file tab when a relative return link resolves to the same file. Use the gateway's resolved path, not the filename, to identify it.

## Validation

- 317 focused WebUI tests passed after syncing main, covering file previews, tab reuse, Markdown rendering, file icons, activity, the thread shell and the component gallery. Earlier checks also passed for localization and cached reads. The complete document return-flow regression failed before the fix and passes after it.
- WebUI lint and production build passed.
- GitHub CI passed on `ff9eff473`: WebUI and Docker checks passed; Python jobs were skipped by the changed-path filter.
- Real-backend E2E passed with the compiled WebUI and an isolated Python gateway: open a Markdown file from chat, follow sibling/parent links, return to the same tab, switch Preview / Source, close, refresh and reopen. The source view matches the file content exactly. Files with spaces open; missing and out-of-workspace files remain rejected.
- Light/dark desktop and 390-pixel browser checks passed. The narrow preview has no horizontal layout overflow. No browser errors or warnings were recorded. Earlier component checks also cover truncation, loading and image states.
- All seven checked source/test-file hashes remained unchanged. Tests used isolated files and a repository-document copy; no user files, live sessions or active gateway were changed.

No backend, prompt, tool, model-request, persisted-data or dependency changes. Existing file preview payloads remain supported.

Related: #5487 also includes Markdown preview in a broader change with file path resolution and subagent lifecycle work. This PR is limited to read-only Markdown display and its controls.

prs.title: fix(webui): keep CLI Apps reads off the event loop
prs.body:
## Why

A cache-only CLI Apps list can spend seconds scanning a slow or mounted PATH. Its async API helper did all configuration, cache and executable discovery work synchronously, so it also stalled unrelated WebUI HTTP requests. Move the whole local read behind one worker-thread boundary, without changing the synchronous manager used by tools and skills.

## What changed

- Offload manager/config creation, cached full or installed-only payload construction, freshness checks and empty-catalog fallback together; keep background refresh task/throttle state on the event loop.
- Offload disk reads and atomic writes in the existing asynchronous registry refresh while retaining asynchronous HTTP and cache fallback behavior.
- Add real-helper regressions for full and nonempty installed-only reads, cancellation without late refresh, async cache IO/fallback, and authenticated socket HTTP progress while a real executable probe is held.

## Scope

Tracks [NAN-268](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-268), a child of NAN-33. No UI/schema/protocol, package metadata, install/update/uninstall/run, PATH, dependency or TTL/snapshot changes. Installed-only still skips refresh and omits `catalog_refresh_pending`; existing full-list content/source/status and empty-cache behavior remain covered.

## Tradeoffs

This fixes event-loop responsiveness, not the time needed to finish the list. Cancellation stops waiting but cannot stop an already-running filesystem probe, and enough slow readers can still occupy the shared default executor. A local read now publishes refresh intent only after payload/fallback succeeds: cancellation or a failing fallback no longer starts a late background refresh. No persistent cache, dedicated pool, global lock or single-flight policy is introduced.

## Blast Radius

Affects the WebUI CLI Apps HTTP/message list helper and disk IO during its background registry refresh. The manager remains synchronous for its other consumers, and management/execution actions continue performing their own live checks. Existing auth, error, sorting/merging and action tests are included in the full Python suite. The wire format and independently upgraded client/host contract do not change.

## Verification

Local Linux / Python 3.12.10 on the independent worktree, with all extras/dev and channel dependencies:

- Baseline RED: four new helper/refresh tests and both real HTTP list variants failed against the original implementation; finite independent watchdogs prevented hangs. Candidate focused suite: **194 passed**.
- `ruff check nanobot tests conftest.py scripts/check_import_boundaries.py`, `basedpyright`, `python -m scripts.check_import_boundaries` and `uv pip check`: passed.
- `python -m pytest -n 4 --dist loadfile --ignore=tests/cli/test_commands.py --cov=nanobot --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered -q -o faulthandler_timeout=60 --durations=25`: **9,777 passed, 51 skipped**, 226.49 s.
- `python -m pytest tests/cli/test_commands.py --cov=nanobot --cov-append --cov-report=term:skip-covered -q --durations=10`: **163 passed, 1 skipped**; combined coverage **86.18%** (required 75%).
- Separate documented gateway CLI process with isolated home/config/workspace/cache and a test-only held executable probe: unauthenticated list 401; authenticated full, nonempty installed-only and 2/4 concurrent full lists all returned 200 after release. `/api/workspaces` and `/api/settings` completed **before** release in every case (observed 1.944–50.522 ms). Owned gateway shut down; temporary runtime removed and both ports released.
- Read-only implementation/simplify review found no blocking issues. No browser/frontend build claimed: UI and wire behavior are unchanged; the public proof is authenticated HTTP.

### Fixed-104-row comparison

Same Python/dependencies/real manager, frozen 104-app caches and original 80-entry PATH; no profiler, network refresh, fake probe delay or reduced probe count. Each installed-state workload has one warmup per variant and five interleaved AB/BA pairs. Primary zero-installed maximum-loop-lag median: **11,329.47 ms → 0.846 ms**; list-wall median: **11,334.38 ms → 10,126.62 ms**. List completion still takes roughly 10–12 seconds; this is responsiveness evidence, not a list-speed or tail-latency guarantee.

| Fixture / variant | List wall ms (min / median / max) | Per-run max loop lag ms (min / median / max) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 0 installed / baseline | 9775.50 / 11334.38 / 12225.69 | 9770.64 / 11329.47 / 12220.77 |
| 0 installed / candidate | 9246.05 / 10126.62 / 10632.67 | 0.442 / 0.846 / 0.855 |
| 1 installed / baseline | 9965.43 / 11671.06 / 12248.75 | 9960.51 / 11666.14 / 12243.83 |
| 1 installed / candidate | 10891.58 / 11541.86 / 12018.13 | 0.757 / 1.030 / 13.144 |

Fresh-interpreter first reads are reported separately (not filesystem-cold). Finite 2/4-reader group loop lag: baseline **22,155.46 / 39,250.12 ms**, candidate **0.836 / 1.355 ms**; each group has only one sample, so no throughput-scaling or unbounded-starvation claim. All full reads returned 104 apps with 187 native `which` calls; all 42 reads succeeded, and the entire JSON payloads matched across variants with **no fields ignored**. Twelve child processes exited/reaped and isolated temporary data was removed. Shared-host scheduling/filesystem-cache variance is not controlled. [Full method, first-read/concurrency tables, provenance and verification record](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/document/nan-268-验证与固定负载对比-pr-6275-5d9c9b7e1290).

### Current-head CI

[Run 39046013881, attempt 2](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39046013881/attempts/2) is pinned to `5e3698b5e6acf6770478d5aae5a187e92d3bf255` and succeeded. All applicable current-head checks passed: Linux 3.11, Linux 3.14 + coverage, Windows 3.14, Windows process compatibility and Docker; unrelated frontend jobs were skipped by path detection. The successful Linux/Docker/Windows-process results carry forward from attempt 1 on the same unchanged head; only the failed full Windows job was rerun.

The first Windows 3.14 full-suite attempt had one failure (9,649 passed / 119 skipped): the unchanged Slack late-result test timed out during its two-second `SessionState.aclose` cleanup. Its routing assertions precede cleanup; the stack does not traverse the changed CLI Apps read/refresh paths. Original failure logs are retained. Exactly one evidence-based complete Windows rerun succeeded with **9,650 passed / 119 skipped** plus serial CLI **163 passed / 1 skipped**. No source, timeout, test-selection or workflow change/waiver was used to remove the failure; the initial cleanup timing failure remains disclosed rather than claimed fixed.

prs.title: refactor(config): separate config reads from network policy activation
prs.body:
Reading another config, inspecting settings, or attempting a config write used to replace the running process's SSRF whitelist. `load_config` now only reads and validates configuration. Runtime initialization and accepted refresh paths explicitly activate their candidate policy.

`AgentLoop.from_config` covers the gateway, classic CLI, and Python SDK startup. Runtime refresh carries the candidate CIDRs on the existing immutable provider snapshot, including whitelist-only changes. Rejected configuration candidates and unconfigured-provider fallbacks retain the active policy. MCP, image, and channel refreshes and standalone guarded-network actions activate policy at their execution boundary. Targeted whitelist environment resolution rejects missing variables without requiring unrelated provider credentials.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Before
    B1["Settings / catalog / config read B"] --> B2["load_config B"]
    B2 --> B3["Replace active process whitelist A"]
    B2 --> B4["Return config B"]
  end
  subgraph After
    A1["Settings / catalog / config read B"] --> A2["Read and validate config B"]
    A2 --> A3["Return snapshot, keep active policy A"]
    A4["Runtime initialization or explicit refresh"] --> A5["Validate runtime candidate"]
    A5 --> A6["Accepted candidate activates policy B"]
    A5 --> A7["Rejected configuration keeps active policy A"]
  end
```

prs.title: refactor(tools): bind media read roots at construction
prs.body:
Media reads used to select the process-global config and create its media directory while resolving paths or wrapping shell commands. Runtime construction now captures an exact `media_root` and shares it through `ToolContext`, main tools, subagents, and Dream. Existing image-tool registration and reload derive their read root from their explicit config snapshot.

Filesystem writes retain their existing project boundary. Message attachments and image references use the same read capability. Sandbox backends receive the root explicitly and retain read-only media rules. Standalone tool constructors capture their default once; path resolution and sandbox rendering no longer select config paths or create media storage.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Before
    B1["File / attachment / shell reads"] --> B2["Look up global config during each operation"]
    B2 --> B3["Derive and create media directory"]
    B4["Sandbox backend"] --> B3
  end
  subgraph After
    A1["Runtime or image-tool construction"] --> A2["Pure media root derivation"]
    A2 --> A3["Exact Path in ToolContext"]
    A3 --> A4["File / attachment / image / shell reads"]
    A3 --> A5["Read-only sandbox media rule"]
    A6["Filesystem writes"] --> A7["Existing project write permissions"]
  end
```

PR 2 of the four refactors preceding #6261. Stacked on #6267. Related to [NAN-264](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-264/). Media storage layout, channel writers, authentication, and CLI flags are unchanged. The new import-boundary rule rejects config imports from the path resolver and sandbox modules.

- Ruff, BasedPyright, and eleven import-boundary rules passed. The rule also rejected both actual forbidden imports from the pre-change source.

Unrelated-home reads, escaped symlinks, and filesystem writes to media were rejected. Image-tool reload retained its explicit config root.

```mermaid
flowchart LR

    B1["Skills / files / MCP / CLI / WebUI"] --> B2["Free plugin operations"]

```

CLI flags, disk layout, and WebUI wire contracts remain unchanged. This closes plugin ownership; standalone construction still selects default paths at its existing entrypoints.

File-change activity keeps the operation label (Created / Edited / Deleted) visible while neighboring tool activity uses a shared icon column. Use one file-type icon per row to make this timeline consistent and quieter.

WebUI file-change presentation only. Paths, diff statistics, file previews, context actions, and diff expansion remain intact. No tool execution, protocol, persisted state, dependency, or localization changes.

prs.title: fix(providers): preserve disabled reasoning for GPT-6 Sol and Luna
prs.body:
## Summary

Fix explicit `reasoningEffort: "none"` being dropped from OpenAI requests for GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna.

These requests retained `temperature` while omitting the explicit reasoning setting required to permit it.

## Root Cause

The Chat Completions request builder filtered out every `none` reasoning effort. The Responses request builder preserved `none` only for DeepSeek and MiMo.

Meanwhile, the temperature capability check treated explicit `none` as disabling reasoning for GPT-6. This produced inconsistent requests: temperature was included, but the field disabling reasoning was missing.

GPT-6 Sol and Luna support `none` and default to reasoning when effort is omitted, as documented in the [OpenAI model guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model#update-api-and-model-parameters).

## Changes

- Preserve explicit `none` for `gpt-6-sol` and `gpt-6-luna` through the OpenAI provider in both Chat Completions and Responses requests.
- Extend the existing temperature regression test to verify reasoning fields, cover Luna, and exercise streaming and non-streaming calls.
- Retain coverage for omitted effort and `high`.

Production changes are limited to two request-building conditions in `openai_compat_provider.py`.

## Result

Explicitly disabling reasoning now sends `reasoning_effort: "none"` for Chat Completions or `reasoning: {"effort": "none"}` for Responses, alongside the configured temperature.

Omitted effort continues to preserve provider defaults. The change is scoped to the OpenAI provider's Sol and Luna models; it does not extend `none` support to Astra or GPT-6.1 Sol.

## Test

- Before the fix: all 8 explicit-none regression cases failed; 20 control cases passed.
- After the fix: 330 tests passed across provider compatibility, custom thinking controls, Responses backend, and model API presets.
- Additional real OpenAI SDK serialization checks: 24 passed across both models, both APIs, streaming/non-streaming calls, and omitted/none/high effort.
- Ruff passed for both changed files.
- BasedPyright passed for the modified provider module.
- `git diff --check` passed.

prs.title: fix(webui): report unreadable sidebar state explicitly instead of serving silent defaults
prs.body:
Focused follow-up to #6237, scoped as requested in [the review](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6237#issuecomment-6218193390): backend-only hardening on current main, with the client side left to the freshly merged #6009.

## What remains broken on main

#6009 fixed the client lifecycle (a failed read no longer wipes state), but the GET handler still collapses every failure — corrupt, oversized, unreadable — into 200 + defaults. A failed read is indistinguishable from a fresh install, so the corrupt/unreadable cases flagged in the [#6008 analysis](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/issues/6008#issuecomment-5986203909) are still silent.

## Read layer

`load_webui_sidebar_state()`:
- keeps the established empty-store contract: missing file → 200 + defaults, unchanged;
- returns `(defaults, reason)` with a machine-readable reason (`"corrupt"` / `"oversized"` / `"unreadable"`) when the file exists but cannot be served;
- the GET handler maps that reason to **409**, so a failed read is distinguishable from a fresh install;
- **serializes with writers on the state write lock**, so a quarantine decision can never race a concurrent save and move a freshly written file aside (race reproduced during internal review; covered by a lock-serialization test).

## Recovery and write authorization, together

- a corrupt file (invalid UTF-8 included) is quarantined on read as `sidebar-state.json.corrupt-<ts>`, keeping the original bytes inspectable;
- the write path quarantines an unparseable file **before** replacing it. Honesty note: a file that cannot even be opened (e.g. a permission error) is *not* quarantined — the replace proceeds, since nothing was readable to preserve;
- with #6009's client lifecycle a 409 blocks persistence until the retry loop succeeds, so recovery and write authorization are defined together;
- self-healing differs by reason: `corrupt` recovers automatically (quarantined on first read, next retry loads a clean store); `oversized` and `unreadable` **do not self-heal** — the client stays blocked until the file is removed or fixed manually (documented in docs/webui.md); oversized files are left in place on reads (no quarantine, since they are readable) and can still be replaced by a legitimate write, which loses no readable data.

`read_webui_sidebar_state()` is unchanged in behavior for existing callers — while here, its except tuple gains `UnicodeDecodeError` so the gateway heartbeat falls back to defaults instead of crashing on a non-UTF-8 state file.

## Compatibility (per .agent/review-guide.md)

- **Missing file: 200 + defaults, byte-for-byte unchanged** — the empty-store contract is preserved (the existing fresh-config-dir route test is untouched and passes).
- **Current client / current host**: new route-level test (corrupt → 409 + quarantine) and unit tests, including lock serialization.
- **Oldest client / current host**: a 409 is just a fetch failure; old clients fall back to defaults as before, and a quarantined file can no longer be destroyed by their writes (strictly better).
- **Current client / oldest host**: hosts without this change always return 200, so the client takes the loaded path, unchanged.
- No protocol/capability changes.

## Docs

`docs/webui.md` sidebar section documents the loading/blocked behavior, the quarantine filename, oversized-file semantics, and the recovery flow.

## Tests

- 7 new unit tests (four read outcomes incl. non-UTF-8 bytes, quarantine assertions, write-path quarantine + clean-store recovery, read/write lock serialization) and 1 new route-level test (corrupt → 409 + quarantine); full affected files: **134 passed**.
- Known unrelated: `src/tests/remote-instances.test.tsx` has one failing test on clean `main`; not touched here.

Fixes #6008
