prs.title: feat(api): serve stored images to API-server clients
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds authenticated `GET /api/media?path=...` to the API server so API-key clients can render stored image attachments. The dashboard already offers this response through its separate session-token authentication. API-server clients should not need a dashboard session token to retrieve an image referenced in their conversation.

The response is `{"data_url": "data:image/...;base64,..."}`. Paths must resolve inside the active Hermes home's `images`, `screenshots`, or `cache` directories. The route checks the resolved path, permits supported image extensions, and rejects files larger than 25 MiB. File resolution, reading, and encoding run off the event loop.

Clients can discover the route through `features.media_api` and `endpoints.media_read` in `/v1/capabilities` and retain their fallback on older gateways. This change does not add upload, profile inventory, dictation, or outbound streaming support.

## Related Issue

No issue found for this specific API-key stored-image retrieval gap. Related work:

- #41336 added the dashboard media route. Its authentication remains unchanged.
- #103239 handles outbound `MEDIA:` processing in streamed model responses. This PR handles explicit reads of existing stored images, not stream rewriting.
- #10595 proposes broader bidirectional file transmission through a file registry. This PR is limited to the existing dashboard-compatible image-read contract.
- #45235 expands dashboard media roots and changes Desktop session classification. This PR does neither.
- #136269 addresses the skills catalog failure.
- #68190 and #117405 address profile inventory.
- #43411 adds transcription.

This PR complements those changes and does not supersede them.

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/platforms/api_server_media.py` implements image retrieval and owns the unchanged core route rows moved out of the oversized adapter file.
- `gateway/platforms/api_server.py` registers the media route and advertises its capability. The existing adapter route-table method remains unchanged as a caller interface.
- `tests/gateway/test_api_media.py` covers image retrieval, authentication, allowed paths, symlink escape, unsupported types, missing paths/files, size limits, and capability discovery.
- `website/docs/user-guide/features/api-server.md` documents the endpoint and capability fields.

## How to Test

1. Use a prepared test interpreter and run the canonical runner:

   ```bash
   scripts/run_tests.sh \
     tests/gateway/test_api_media.py \
     tests/gateway/test_api_server.py \
     tests/gateway/test_api_server_multiplex_secret_scope.py \
     tests/gateway/test_api_server_profile_prefix_misdelivery.py \
     tests/gateway/test_api_server_media_data_urls.py \
     -j 2 --file-retries 0 -q
   ```

2. Run `python scripts/check` and `git diff --check`.
3. With a stored image in the active Hermes home's `cache` directory, request it from the API server using `Authorization: Bearer $API_SERVER_KEY`. Verify the returned data URL decodes to the original bytes. Repeat without the key and with a path outside the allowed directories.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)

The focused suite passed in an isolated clone. The full repository suite was not run. The symlink test skips on this Windows filesystem because symlink creation is unavailable.

The API-server documentation is updated. Config keys, development workflows, and model-tool descriptions/schemas are unchanged. Path handling uses `pathlib`; cross-platform symlink coverage is included.

```text
Canonical focused runner: 134 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped
```

prs.title: fix(local-models): recover interrupted model downloads
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

An interrupted model download can exhaust its retry budget even when each request saves more data. The failed job then loses **Resume**. An engine download can also lose recovery details when its error passes through the package installer and worker.

This change renews the budget when saved progress increases. Four failures without new progress stop automatic recovery and leave **Resume** available. Saved model plans survive a backend restart. The source of the reported connection reset is unknown.

## Related Issue

Reported split GGUF download failure. No separate issue.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Changes Made

prs.title: fix(state): a canonical rewind refuses a target that is not a live user row
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A canonical `session.mutate` rewind trusted the client's `target_message_id`. Desktop renders rows that in-place compaction archived with their row ids (it loads `include_compacted=true`), so editing, restoring or regenerating above a compaction boundary sent an archived row; the rewind then deactivated every active row with a larger id, which is the compaction summary and every later turn, and left the live transcript empty.

`_rewind` now requires the target to be an active user row of the physical session, the same rule `_branch_boundary` applies to a branch's `through_message_id`, and refuses with `RuntimeStoreError('invalid_params', field='target_message_id', detail=...)` otherwise. The transcript is untouched and no receipt is stored. A missing or non-user target, which used to raise a bare `ValueError` past `dispatch` (the WebSocket client got `-32603 internal error`), gets the same typed refusal.

The check sits in the canonical handler, not in the shared `rewind_in_transaction`: its other callers (gateway `/retry`, `rewind_user_turn`) already address active rows, and their error text is unchanged.

Not covered: Desktop still offers Edit/Restore on archived bubbles and shows this refusal as a generic error (its "compressed away" notice keys on the legacy 4018 + `segment_ordinal` shape). Hiding those actions, or mapping `field: target_message_id` to that notice, is a small Desktop follow-up; this PR only stops the transcript loss.

## Related Issue

Fixes #140635

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_state_mutations.py`: `_rewind` refuses a target that is not an active user row of the physical session.
- `tests/hermes_state/test_runtime_rewind_mutations.py`: an archived target is refused with the live transcript and generation unchanged, and the live turn after the compaction still rewinds; a missing and an assistant target are refused.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/hermes_state/test_runtime_rewind_mutations.py`: 5 pass. With `hermes_state_mutations.py` reverted, the 3 new cases fail (the archived target empties the transcript; the other two raise `ValueError`).
2. Real authority, SQLite and `AuthorityConnection.dispatch` (the harness from `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_chat_retry_lost_refresh.py`), Q1–A2 compacted in place, then Q3/A3, then `session.mutate rewind` at the archived Q2 row:

| | main 868b9f244f | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| reply | `{'rewound_count': 4, 'new_head_id': None}` | `4001 invalid_params`, `field: target_message_id` |
| active after | `[]` | `['[CONTEXT SUMMARY] …', 'ok, continuing', 'Q3', 'A3']` |
| missing row 99999 | `ValueError` raised past `dispatch` | `4001 invalid_params`, `field: target_message_id` |

3. Neighbouring rewind/undo/retry/mutation/branch/compaction tests, one folder at a time. `tests/hermes_state`: 291 passed, 5 skipped. `tests/gateway`: 589 passed, 18 skipped; 126 failed, 18 errors, and `test_telegram_rich_messages.py` does not collect (no `telegram`). `tests/hermes_cli`: 445 passed, 14 skipped; 18 failed, and `test_profile_rename_service.py` does not collect (no `pwd` on Windows). `tests/tui_gateway`: 194 passed, 5 failed. `tests/acp_adapter`: 29 passed, 1 skipped. prs.title: plugin-catalog: bump hyatlas to 4.9.0
prs.body:
Bumps the `hyatlas` catalog entry from 4.7.3 (39bdccc) to 4.9.0 (386515b).

The pin is 386515b, the merge of the 4.9.0 docs refresh (tuancookiez-hub/HyAtlas-Memory#17), one commit after the `v4.9.0` tag (d6ae5f7). That commit also updated the plugin's tool descriptions in `plugins/hyatlas/schemas.py`, so it is the plugin code that should ship.

Only `plugin-catalog/hyatlas.yaml` changes:
- `sha`, `version` and every pinned URL (image, screenshots, docs) move to 386515b.
- The known-issue line now points to server v4.9.1 (https://github.com/tuancookiez-hub/HyAtlas-Memory/releases/tag/v4.9.1), a server-only fix release; the plugin pin is unchanged. Server 4.9.1 is what makes reconcile cover aliased user IDs, as the disclosure says.
- `description` is now a `>-` folded block with one sentence per line, the style most catalog entries use. That part is layout only, so later bumps diff by line.
- The disclosure changes as follows:
  - **Keys.** Extraction uses an LLM the user chooses: `hermes memory setup` asks for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, model and key, and stores the key in Hermes's `.env` as `HYATLAS_LLM_KEY`. The entry now says this up front. A plain key file (`HYATLAS_LLM_KEY_FILE`) also works, and the entry warns not to point it at another program's credentials. Since 4.8.0 the sample Windows launcher no longer reads Hermes `auth.json`.
  - **`share_llm_key`** (new, off by default; `HYATLAS_SHARE_LLM_KEY=1` also turns it on) is an optional shortcut for Nous Portal users. It asks Hermes for its own Nous key through Hermes's resolver (`resolve_runtime_provider`, which may renew the token with the Portal). Only when the server's endpoint is on that key's host does it POST the key, over plain HTTP, to the configured HyAtlas server (default 127.0.0.1:19528) at `/api/v1/llm/key`; the entry says to use it only with a server on the same machine. It checks every 60 s and re-sends every 15 min. The server keeps the key in memory only and never writes it to disk. While the endpoint and model are set but no key has arrived, `/api/v1/status` reports `llm: "awaiting_key"`.
  - **Episode summaries (pro and ultra).** After a 30-minute pause in an owner's writes (`HYATLAS_EPISODE_GAP`), up to 40 of that stretch's facts are sent to write one summary.
  - **Now page.** It now also reads the owner's newest facts.
  - **`HYATLAS_RECONCILE=on`** (off by default) adds a second LLM call per write. That call sends the new facts with similar stored ones, including those under user IDs grouped by `HYATLAS_USER_ALIASES`, so the model can update or replace them. It is meant for a local model.
  - **Corrections to existing text.** The extraction call has also been sending up to 5 related stored facts, 3 entity pages and 5 open intentions with each turn, and the entry now says so. "Stored memories stay local" now reads "kept locally", and the disclosure points to the LLM calls through which they leave the machine.

The other 4.8.0–4.9.0 features stay on the machine: task experiences, schema evidence, sentence-level indexing of long facts, date-aware search, entity boost and graph-assisted recall.

The maintainer's auto_start sentence is unchanged.

Checks: `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` on the entry passes. The banner, screenshot and docs URLs resolve at the new SHA. Repo CI on 386515b is green.

Release notes: https://github.com/tuancookiez-hub/HyAtlas-Memory/releases/tag/v4.9.0 (see also v4.8.0 and v4.8.1, and `CHANGELOG.md` at the pin).

prs.title: fix(cron): retain execution outcomes for at least 30 days
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

<!-- Describe the change clearly. What problem does it solve? Why is this approach the right one? -->

Guarantee a minimum 30-day audit window for completed, failed, and unknown cron attempts. Previously, the 1,000-terminal-row cap could evict recent outcomes during high-volume activity. Pruning now deletes a terminal attempt only when it is outside the latest 1,000 terminal attempts **and** its finish instant is strictly older than 30 days. Active attempts remain untouched. Existing records are preserved; already-lost history cannot be restored.

The change adds no configuration, dependencies, schema migration, or delivery-history changes. This PR has not been deployed to a running gateway.

## Related Issue

<!-- Link the issue this PR addresses. If no issue exists, consider creating one first. -->

No issue filed; implements an explicitly requested minimum audit-retention window. Related: #121899 proposes an eight-day completed/failed window and a separate unknown window; #97818 and #93858 address configurable count limits. Those proposals do not provide this unconditional, all-terminal-state 30-day minimum, including above the count cap.

prs.title: fix(tools): coerce non-str content in scan_for_threats to a stable string form
prs.body:
## Summary

`scan_for_threats()` in `tools/threat_patterns.py` assumed its `content` argument was always a `str` and sliced it unconditionally with `content[:MAX_SCAN_CHARS]`. Tool calls that pass non-string content — e.g. memory operations carrying a `dict` — crashed the tool executor instead of failing the advisory scan: a `KeyError` on `dict[:MAX_SCAN_CHARS]` was seen in real gateway logs.

Threat scanners are advisory by design: they must never take down the tool executor. This change coerces non-`str` content to a stable string form (`json.dumps(content, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)`, falling back to `repr(content)` if serialization itself raises) before the existing cap, so the scan degrades gracefully and the serialized payload is still scanned. `str` content is untouched.

## Notes

- Recovered from a lost autostash of a live deployment, so the change is deliberately minimal: one `import json` plus the defensive coercion block, nothing else.
- Verified: `python -m py_compile tools/threat_patterns.py`, plus a smoke test — dict content now returns `[]` (previously raised), and string scanning is unchanged (`'ignore all previous instructions ...'` still flags `prompt_injection`).

prs.title: fix(async_delegation): add recovery mechanism for WebUI async results
prs.body:
## Summary

Background subagent results from `delegate_task(background=true)` are silently lost in WebUI (and potentially TUI gateway) sessions when:

- The browser tab disconnects before the subagent finishes
- The session was busy (streaming response) when the completion arrived
- The completion event was consumed but the delivery path dropped it

This PR adds defense-in-depth recovery mechanisms to `tools/async_delegation.py` and `tui_gateway/server.py`.

## Changes

### `tools/async_delegation.py`
- Add `consumed` flag to delegation records (set `False` on completion)
- Add `list_async_completions(session_key)` — returns unconsumed completed delegations for a session, enabling recovery sweep queries
- Add `mark_async_delegation_consumed(delegation_id)` — marks a record so it won't be re-injected

### `tui_gateway/server.py`
- Add recovery sweep at `_notification_poller_loop` startup — checks for any completions that arrived while no poller was running (tab closed, session reconnect, etc.)
- Add consumed marking after successful injection in the regular poller loop
- Add `delegations.list` RPC method for WebUI polling/querying

### `tests/tools/test_async_delegation.py`
- 5 new tests covering `list_async_completions` and `mark_async_delegation_consumed`

## Motivation

This is the **agent-side companion** to nesquena/hermes-webui#4799. The WebUI PR handles the actual delivery path (keying async delegation events by `delegation_id`, cross-path dedupe, next-turn drain routing); this PR provides the underlying recovery infrastructure that the WebUI PR's best-effort `mark_async_delegation_consumed()` call depends on.

**Status update (2026-06-27):**
- **Rebased onto current main** (448 commits, zero conflicts — clean rebase)
- **CI fully green** — all test shards, lint, build, e2e, contributor-check pass
- **The companion WebUI PR (#4799) is ready** — rebased on master, CI green, narrowed to the dedupe/routing/recovery-coordination delta. It is labeled `hold` + `upstream-change` pending this PR's merge.
- **#4912 / v0.51.652** landed on WebUI master (minimal `format_wakeup_prompt` async_delegation delivery fix). #4799 is now the narrowed delta beyond that fix.

The root cause chain:
1. `delegate_task` forces `background=true` for top-level agents (`_model_background_value` returns True)
2. The completion event is pushed to `process_registry.completion_queue`
3. The WebUI's `bg_task_complete` drain consumed ALL events but only handled `completion` type, not `async_delegation` — **fixed by #4912 on WebUI master**
4. No recovery mechanism existed for missed events — **fixed by this PR**

The WebUI PR (#4799) fixes delivery-path dedupe/routing. This PR adds #4 — a recovery mechanism that works even if the primary delivery path fails.

## Related Issues
- Closes #10760 (partial — the synchronous fallback for api_server adapter remains, but sessions now recover missed results)
- Companion: nesquena/hermes-webui#4799
- Related: nesquena/hermes-webui#4691 (original bug report)

## Testing
```bash
python -m pytest tests/tools/test_async_delegation.py -v -o 'addopts='
python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_async_delivery_capability.py -v -o 'addopts='
python -m pytest tests/test_tui_gateway_server.py -v -o 'addopts='
```
All 317 tests pass. CI fully green on rebase.

prs.title: feat(skills): routing-layer guard — steer background-review growth from fat SKILL.md into references/
prs.body:
## Problem

The auto-evolution loop (post-turn background review + the skill nudge) places what it learns per `_LESSON_LAYER_BLOCK`: *"Always-on rules … live in SKILL.md itself, whole."* For skills that accumulate frequent user corrections this grows the body without bound. Real-world case from a daily-driver domain skill (a family beekeeping assistant with several corrections per day): **SKILL.md reached ~73k chars / 137KB in about two months**, degrading every turn that loads it.

Existing mitigations don't address placement:

- `MAX_SKILL_CONTENT_CHARS` (100k) only stops the explosion at the top.
- pin / user-ownership (#27643's "already on main" answer) stops the learning loop for a skill entirely.
- `skills.write_approval` gates *when* writes land, not *where*.

## Change

1. **Size-aware placement** in `_LESSON_LAYER_BLOCK`: past `skills.routing_cap_chars` (default 20,000 chars) a SKILL.md **is** the routing layer — new rules go to the most topical existing `references/` file (creating `references/<topic>.md` only when nothing fits), and SKILL.md gains at most a one-line pointer entry.

2. **Mechanical enforcement** — `_routing_layer_size_guard` in `tools/skill_manager_tool.py`, wired into `edit` / `patch` / `write_file(SKILL.md)`:
   - Compares the **full before/after document** (a patch whose fragment strings are tiny but whose net growth is large is still caught; verified by a `replace_all` ×700 ×+1-char probe).
   - `allowed_max = max(cap, len(current)) + 400` — pointer-line entries stay allowed, shrinks are always allowed, sub-cap writes are untouched.
   - The refusal message teaches the correct placement (`write_file(file_path='references/<topic>.md')` + one-line pointer), mirroring how the read-before-write guard already steers the reviewer.
   - `create` is deliberately NOT wired: a new skill keeps the plain `MAX_SKILL_CONTENT_CHARS` ceiling.

3. **Config**: `skills.routing_cap_chars` (default 20000, `<=0` disables; read failures fall back to the documented default).

Every write path that funnels through those handlers is covered: single operations, batch `operations`, pending-approval replay, the dashboard editor, and journey mutations. Whole-directory sync/install paths (`skills_sync`, hub, optional-skills) are intentionally out of scope.

## Tests

- New `tests/tools/test_skill_routing_layer_guard.py` (19 tests): guard off, sub-cap growth, fat-skill refusal (message includes the references/ guidance), pointer allowance, shrink-allowed (edit + patch), boundary `cap+400` allowed / `+401` refused, cross-threshold growth refused, `write_file` to `references/` unaffected, direct `write_file(SKILL.md)` refused, batch path, config parsing.
- Two existing tests that probe the linter's oversized-body budget with 24k-char bodies now disable the guard via config (`routing_cap_chars: 0`) — they test the linter contract, not the guard; their assertions are unchanged.

## Relation to prior art

| Mechanism | What it controls | Gap this PR fills |
|---|---|---|
| `MAX_SKILL_CONTENT_CHARS` | explosion at 100k | nothing steers placement below that |
| pin / user-ownership | whether the loop may touch a skill at all | kills the learning, not the placement |
| `skills.write_approval` | when writes land (staged for review) | reviewers still merge body growth |
| **this PR** | **where writes land** | |

Closes the placement half of #27643 that the opt-out discussion left open.

prs.title: OpenRouter errors name the upstream provider and its reason, not just "Provider returned error" (port oh-my-pi#14435)
prs.body:
When OpenRouter relays an upstream refusal, the error Hermes shows now names the upstream and its reason instead of just "Provider returned error".

**Ported from** can1357/oh-my-pi#14435 (OpenRouter errors drop the upstream detail in `error.metadata.raw`).

## Changes
- `agent/api_error_summary.py::_openrouter_upstream_detail`: builds `"<provider_name>: <reason>"` from OpenRouter's `error.metadata`. `raw` is the upstream's own body; when it is JSON its `error.message` is used, otherwise the plain text.
- `_summarize_api_error` adds that detail on both paths that read the `Provider returned error` envelope: the SDK `.body` dict (top-level or nested `error`) and the httpx `response.text` fallback. Both paths stay redacted.
- One parametrized invariant test, plain-text and JSON `raw`.

## Validation
| | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Live `hermes chat -Q` against a loopback stub returning OpenRouter's real 403 envelope (fresh gateway per leg) | `Provider said: HTTP 403: Provider returned error` | `Provider said: HTTP 403: Provider returned error: Azure: Access denied by security policy: request flagged by upstream WAF` |
| `tests/agent/test_summarize_api_error.py` new cases | 2 failed | pass |
| `test_summarize_api_error`, `test_nonretryable_error_html_summary`, `test_failed_turn_chat_copy`, `test_error_classifier` | | 222 passed |

**Root cause:** `error_classifier` already reads `metadata.raw` to classify (merged class work from #94199/#72691), but the user-facing summary only showed `error.message`, which for this envelope is always the literal "Provider returned error".

## Ours vs theirs
omp had dead code reading a property that does not exist on its error type, and fixed it to append `metadata.raw` to the stream error message. Hermes had no dead read: the classifier parses the envelope correctly, and only the display summary skipped it. We also include `provider_name`, which omp leaves out. It is the half the user needs to know which upstream to route around (`provider.ignore`/`order`).

Adjacent open PRs on other axes: #135638 (keeps the embedded message on HTTP-200 invalid-response exhaustion), #132642/#132643 (classify the guardrail 403). This PR changes display only and does not change any classification.

prs.title: fix(update): hold a stable-channel install whose release predates the gateway runtime (GW-19)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A stable-channel install whose `state.db` already holds gateway-runtime history could never update when the channel's release predates that runtime. `hermes update` (CLI, Desktop hand-off, `/update`) picked the release, `update_downgrade_guard.downgrade_refusal` refused it as a downgrade, and every attempt exited 1 with "Refusing to move this install to d923a5eb487a… Downgrading is unsupported". The user never asked to go back (#140729).

The fix follows the maintainer's direction on #134889. When the **channel** picks a release older than the runtime the stores already use, the update keeps the install where it is, says so, and exits 0:

```
→ This install is ahead of the stable release d923a5eb487a: that release predates the gateway runtime your sessions use, so there is nothing to update to yet.
  Hermes stays on 6df56c5446d7 until a newer stable release ships. To follow every commit instead: `hermes update --set-channel main`.
```

An explicit `--branch` to a pre-runtime ref is still refused with the full recovery guide. A store with no runtime history still moves to the release as before.

**Design choice:** the hold reuses `downgrade_refusal` itself as its predicate, so the hold and the refusal can never disagree about which targets are unsafe. It runs only for a channel-selected release (`release_sha and not target_is_head`): that is the only target the user did not name. It pins the target and `expected_sha` to HEAD, so the run finishes through the existing up-to-date path, the same no-op shape the forward-only default already uses for a checkout that contains the release. No new state, no change to the guard. `--branch` never reaches the hold.

Where this still reproduces on current `main`: since #140203 (v0.22.2 recorded as an ancestor of `main`), an *unconfigured* install on `main` already holds via forward-only. It still breaks:
- for an install whose channel is **recorded** as stable (Desktop's Settings channel selector, `hermes update --set-channel stable`): forward-only never applies, so it was refused every time;
- for the reported topology (a `main` line that does not contain the release), which any future release cut from a pre-runtime branch recreates.

Both are covered below.

## Related Issue

Refs #134889 (GW-19)
Refs #140762
Refs #140729

(`Refs`, not `Fixes`: the CLI and the Desktop hand-off now hold, but Desktop's update card still offers v0.22.2 as an update until the check side lands. See "Not in this PR".)

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py` (salvaged unchanged from #140741, @arcabotai): `_hold_channel_release_behind_runtime`, called before `_refuse_before_commit_point` for a channel-selected release.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_channel_release_hold.py`: the salvaged tests (preview channel holds; same release still applies with no runtime history; `--branch` still refused), plus tests on the shapes #140729 and Desktop actually reach:
  - unconfigured install, default channel stable, `main` line beside the release: `hermes update --yes`, and the argv `scripts/desktop-update/posix.sh` runs (`--yes --keep-stash --channel stable`);
  - channel recorded as stable on a checkout that contains the release.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_update_channel_release_hold.py`: 6 passed. With `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py` reverted to the base, 4 fail with `SystemExit: 1` at the downgrade refusal (`update_cmd.py:1277`), and the 2 guard-preserving tests pass.
2. Related suites (every test file that references `_cmd_update_impl`, `downgrade_refusal`, `update_downgrade_guard`, `select_apply_target` or `_refuse_before_commit_point`, plus `test_source_channel_integration.py`): 24 files, 512 passed, 0 failed, 19 skipped. Old-updater compat and completion routing: 5 files, 679 passed.
3. Live retest (real `hermes update` CLI process; real git; the real v0.22.2 commit `d923a5eb487a` as the stable tag on a local origin reached through `url.insteadOf` from the official URL; a `HERMES_HOME` whose `state.db` holds real runtime ledger rows; completion child replaced by a recorder; `--no-gateway-restart`):

| Case | base `e6cf2a9b` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| A: reported topology, default stable, `hermes update --yes` | exit 1, downgrade refusal | exit 0, held |
| B: same, Desktop hand-off argv `--yes --keep-stash --channel stable` | exit 1, downgrade refusal | exit 0, held |
| D: channel recorded as stable, checkout contains the release | exit 1, downgrade refusal | exit 0, held |
| C: `--branch release/0.22.1` (real ref downgrade) | exit 1, refused | exit 1, refused |
| E: control, unconfigured, checkout contains the release | exit 0, forward-only | exit 0, forward-only |

## Not in this PR

- **Desktop's update card and `hermes update --check`** still offer v0.22.2 ("Selected release available… Run `hermes update`") to an install this update now holds. With this PR, clicking Update hands off to `posix.sh`, which runs `hermes update --channel stable`. That now exits 0, and the result file reads `ok:true` (logged "finished OK", no error dialog), but the card keeps offering the same release. #140215 (@ethernet8023, the earliest PR on this topic) fixes exactly that side: `source_check` and `--check` ask the same `downgrade_refusal` question and report the release as held, with copy ("Hermes stays on this build until a newer stable release ships") that matches this hold. The two PRs touch different code and don't conflict. Its own premise was "`hermes update` refuses (unchanged)", and this PR changes that refusal to a hold. That makes the copy more accurate, not less. Merge it alongside this one to close #140729.
- **#140742** (@liuhao1024, "name a divergent-line release a rollback"): not taken. It labels the divergent release a *rollback* in `source_check`, so Desktop would offer "Roll back to v0.22.2" to a store with runtime history. That is the exact move the contract keeps refused (or now held), so the surface would advertise an action that never happens. For a store without runtime history the release really is a move back, but #140215 already keys the offer on the guard's own answer, and that matches the contract.
- **How a curl install on stable landed on `main`:** the reported commit `046094df28b7` was `main`'s tip from 2026-10-15 16:25Z to 18:43Z, and `scripts/install.sh` at that commit still cloned `main` (`BRANCH="main"`). #139311 (merged 2026-10-15 19:09Z, in this base) makes new installs land on the latest stable release. Its own live table shows the old installer landing on `main @ 046094df28`. No separate bug.
- **The reporter's install itself** runs `046094df28b7`'s updater, which predates this PR, so a stable update there keeps refusing until they move once to `main`: `hermes update --branch main` is a forward update the guard allows (or `hermes update --set-channel main` to keep following `main`).
- Cosmetic, pre-existing: the `--branch` refusal truncates the ref name to 12 characters ("to origin/relea"). Not changed here.

## Credits

- @arcabotai, #140741: the hold (salvaged unchanged as its own commit; Git author preserved).
- @ethernet8023, #140215: earliest PR on this topic; the check/Desktop side, complementary and not duplicated here.
- @liuhao1024, #140742: evaluated; not taken (above).

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass (related suites only: 24 files / 512 passed, 0 failed, 19 skipped; compat 5 files / 679 passed)
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (12 checks, ok; `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all` clean)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Linux (kernel 6.8, Python 3.14)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation — N/A (docstring on the new helper)
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact — the hold adds no process or path handling; same git calls the guard already makes
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A

## Native Windows Desktop retest

Run on a Windows 11 install with `channel: stable` recorded (`hermes update --set-channel stable`) and a `state.db` holding 54 `session_admissions` rows, using Desktop's Settings > About > Update now (`scripts/desktop-update/windows.ps1 -Channel stable`) and the CLI:

| | base `e6cf2a9b` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `hermes update --yes` | exit 1, "Refusing to move this install to d923a5eb487a … Downgrading is unsupported." | exit 0, hold notice, HEAD unchanged |
| Desktop Update now | `hermes update exit code: 1`, updater shows "Failed to update", relaunched Desktop shows "Hermes couldn't finish updating"; desktop.log `detached update FAILED (exit 1)` | hold notice, `hermes update exit code: 0`, updater reaches its done state, Desktop relaunches; desktop.log `detached update finished OK`; receipt `outcome: success`, apply stage `skipped`; no error dialog |

The Windows hand-off treats exit 0 the same way as `posix.sh`: `windows.ps1` records failure only for a non-zero exit without a committed receipt, and `update-handoff-report.ts` shows a dialog only when the result is not ok.

As expected, About still offers v0.22.2 afterwards ("Installing it moves Hermes back to that release"), and so does `hermes update --check`. That is #140215's side.

## Still needs a live retest

- Desktop on macOS/Linux (`posix.sh`). Its argv was exercised live (case B) and it maps exit 0 to `ok:true`, but a built Desktop was only driven on Windows.
- The completion stage (PM venv sync, fleet restart) was replaced by a recorder in the Linux live run. The Windows Desktop run went through the real completion stage.

prs.title: feat(gateway): add guarded automatic handoff rollover
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds an **opt-in, context-pressure-driven handoff and fresh-session rollover for gateway messaging lanes**. The old tool-capable agent runs a configured handoff skill, writes its complete packet, and produces the restart message. The gateway preserves that actual message unchanged and owns the guarded identity transition and compulsory first-turn recentering.

This is not a timer reset, a forged `/new`, or a compact summary substituted for a full handoff. Configuration defaults remain unchanged. Local-session admissions, proxy execution, mixture-of-agents turns and Codex app-server execution are outside this path.

## Related Issue

No issue is closed by this PR. Related work considered: #29293 (bounded handoff after repeated compression), #47877 (context/runtime governors), and closed, unmerged #102415. This slice specifically covers pre-compaction safe points, a configured full handoff procedure and exact restart message, atomic gateway ownership, bootstrap-first FIFO handling, and authority-preserving continuation.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature (opt-in)
- [x] Documentation update
- [x] Behavior-contract tests

## Changes Made

- `agent/session_rollover.py` and the existing turn safe points use the actual resolved runtime window, earliest compaction/hygiene threshold, provider usage anchor plus appended growth, and a measured reserve. An oversized result invalidates the attempt before native emergency recovery; ordinary compaction settings are not replaced.
- `gateway/run_rollover.py` runs the old agent's configured skill, binds the packet/hash and exact final restart message, settles callback-dependent work and resources, and commits under the native lane lease. Independent running infrastructure is not killed.
- `gateway/session_rollover.py` and `hermes_state_rollover.py` persist an exact-attempt receipt and atomically end the predecessor with `session_reset` while creating one fresh child with native parent/reset lineage. SQLite work stays off-loop and outside the global route lock; stale writers cannot overwrite a newer reset or receipt.
- The successor starts with no old transcript replay and must recenter before retained input can act. Native FIFO order and separate reply delivery are preserved; continuation is admitted only after newer queued input has been accounted for.
- `continue-authorized`, `await-user`, `monitor`, `reconcile` and `idle` directives carry existing authority, not new permissions. Await-user asks its unresolved question and waits. Native user controls, privacy policy and prompt pins remain in force.
- Cancellation settles the bound transition to a visible reconciliation block before propagating. A committed, not-yet-started bootstrap can recover the same successor; uncertain work is not automatically replayed.
- Strict resource cleanup retains failed backend ownership for retry. The disabled configuration example and lifecycle documentation describe setup, measured reserve selection, supported scope and recovery limitations.

## How to Test

Use the checkout's PM-built development/test environment and `scripts/run_tests.sh`, with an isolated `HERMES_HOME` and `HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR`.

Core regression files:

```sh
scripts/run_tests.sh -j 3 \
  tests/agent/test_session_rollover.py \
  tests/agent/test_rollover_cleanup.py \
  tests/gateway/test_session_rollover_store.py \
  tests/gateway/test_guarded_rollover.py \
  tests/gateway/test_plaintext_approval_routing.py \
  tests/tools/test_terminal_tool_lifecycle.py \
  tests/tools/test_computer_use_backend_lifecycle.py \
  tests/tools/test_computer_use_cua_0_9.py -q
python scripts/check --base 27edc417d75db34be8bb6e285e33edda88451b43
```

Final combined integration gate: **264 tests passed across 24 files**. This includes neighboring session/hygiene/lease/security, native FIFO/queue/steer/stop/reset, final-delivery/ledger, browser cleanup, memory-sync and overflow behavior. **All 12 native blocking checks passed**, with zero blocking or advisory code-health findings. The full repository suite was not run.

An isolated rehearsal used the real `GatewayRunner`, native base adapter with a capture-only transport, a real model and native file/skill tools confined to synthetic files. It exercised:

- Context-triggered full handoff without a human handoff/reset/paste; empty successor history, fresh-reset flag before consumption, persisted parent lineage and exact restart-message preservation.
- Two arrivals during cutover, actual FIFO model processing and delivery of both replies, then one authorized action.
- Await-user question delivery, one-time monitoring, and cancellation during packet authoring.
- A real test-process exit after commit/before bootstrap, followed by fresh-process recovery of the same successor and one action; repeated startup added no turn.
- Native `/stop` during admission and retained-input processing: no action writes and no model work while blocked; a separately requested synthetic `/new` with native approve-once cleared the block without replay.

The rehearsal resolved a 272,000-token window and 231,200-token effective trigger despite a configured 0.5 ratio. Full-handoff calibration measured 12,027 tokens of peak growth, a 5,554-token request jump and 4,467 completion tokens (143.94 seconds), giving a **fixture-specific** 22,048-token reserve. These are evidence, not hardcoded defaults or recommended universal settings.

## Safety and Limits

- Disabled unless exact native session keys and complete policy are configured. No live gateway or profile was activated by this change.
- The receipt protects rollover ownership, not general inbound durability. Busy queues remain process-local; hard-crash input loss and ambiguous action outcomes require reconciliation.
- Disabling stops new attempts but does not erase a committed or uncertain transition's safety gate.
- After compulsory bootstrap, native busy-input policy still applies. An actual interrupted/cancelled tool-capable turn blocks rather than replaying uncertain work; native redirects and explicit control commands retain their behavior.
- No external handoff skill, operator-specific policy, private operational plans, model credentials or rehearsal data are included in this PR.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contributing guide and applicable area rules.
- [x] Searched related PRs; no unrelated commits or integrations included.
- [x] Added behavior-contract regressions and exercised the complete isolated path.
- [x] Updated lifecycle documentation and `cli-config.yaml.example`.
- [x] Ran native blocking checks and targeted/neighboring tests through the prescribed runner.
- [ ] Full repository test suite.
- [x] Tested on Linux in an isolated runner; no OS-specific implementation added.

Draft for external review. No merge or deployment is requested by this PR publication.

prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`_should_stream` force-disabled streaming for every provider whose `auth_type` is `external_process`. That default is right for most ACP-style agent CLIs (request/response, no incremental output), but it also blocked a subprocess-backed provider whose transport genuinely yields incremental `content`/`reasoning_content` chunks — the UI showed one assembled response instead of word-by-word text and a live thinking panel, with no way to opt back in.

This adds the same kind of opt-in capability flag the profile already uses elsewhere (`supports_health_check`, `supports_model_listing`, `supports_vision`, `supports_prompt_cache_key`): `ProviderProfile.supports_streaming`, default `False`. `_should_stream` now consults it through a new `_external_process_provider_streams` helper that follows the same registry order as `_is_external_process_provider` (CLI registry first, then the profile registry), so:

- every existing external-process provider keeps its non-streaming behavior (default off);
- the `acp://` / `acp+tcp://` scheme stays non-streaming even for an opted-in profile;
- every other transport streams unconditionally and ignores the flag.

prs.title: fix(gateway): retain image attachments in canonical Bot deliveries (AGC-1702)
prs.body:
Canonical `bot_relay.deliver` rejects image attachments even after the native gateway has staged them successfully. This carries the existing authenticated attachment representation through Bot admission, the durable automation queue, and restore/retry, so Bot images follow the same media path as direct native prompts.

If both retained and staged image bytes disappear, Bot recovery records a durable identity refusal while ordinary direct retries retain their existing storage refusal. The same lost-media test fails on the prior candidate and passes with this correction.

The change binds receipt replay and derived retries to the admitted image digests and MIME types, refuses changed or malformed references, and retains FIFO, Bot author/target ownership, text-only delivery, and cleanup custody. prs.title: fix(gateway): a prune is not a permanent tombstone, and retirement is keyed by profile (LC-25, LC-26)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes two ways a session id stays retired where it shouldn't, both in the retirement records #106742 added (`hermes_state_mutation_retirement.py`). They share one design.

- **A prune is not a delete (LC-25).** A housekeeping prune (`sessions.auto_prune`, `hermes sessions prune`, the dashboard) of an API session whose id the caller chose (`POST /api/sessions`, `X-Hermes-Session-Id`) wrote the permanent tombstone a user delete writes. The id was then refused for good: `POST /api/sessions` answered 409 `session_deleted` and chats answered 409 `not_found`, even after the 7-day horizon.
- **Retirement is keyed by (profile, id) (LC-26).** With `gateway.multiplex_profiles`, a delete or prune in a secondary profile fenced its routes in the launch home's `state.db`, the routing index every served profile shares. It did so with the launch profile's own deletion marker. The launch profile, which never had the session, then refused the id for good.

**Design choice.** Each profile's store keeps its own marker (`retired_session.v1.<id>`), and that marker stays that profile's deletion fence. It is permanent only for an explicit delete or a door-derived id (header-less chat `api-<16 hex>`, a deleted chat's or chain's next generation, hosted-room member, Bot Chat, A2A). A prune's marker ages out at the 7-day retry horizon, as it did before #140232.

The shared routing index gets its own per-(profile, id) fence, `retired_route.v1.<namespace>:<id>`, keyed by that profile's `agent:<ns>:` routing slot. Only routing saves and the `sessions.json` import read it. The fence copies the owner marker's lifetime, and `prune_retired_tombstones` reclaims expired ones. Every check reads only the record of the profile the request targets:

- the launch profile's create, bind and generation walk read its own marker;
- a routing save reads the marker or fence of the profile that owns the route.

**Why.** Under the one-gateway contract each profile is its own session authority. Its retirement must not leak into another profile through the one database they share for routing. This adds no second writer: all fences are written in the gateway's own transactions. Retries keep their identity: exact-retry receipts and their horizon are unchanged.

A chain root that a Responses/Runs continuation walked past keeps a permanent fence (`keep_passed_fences`, from #140732). The walk runs before the binding transaction, so housekeeping can reclaim the root's sweep marker in between. The bind therefore checks the walk again in its own write. It binds the successor and pins the passed fences only if every generation the walk passed still holds a marker. Otherwise it refuses with `chain_moved`, a retryable 503 with `Retry-After: 1`. The retry looks the chain up again and stays on the root, which is free by then.

- A successor is bound only together with permanent fences for every generation it passed. A root that ages out before any successor is bound keeps the chain itself. So a later continuation can't move back from a successor to an aged-out root.
- I chose refusal over re-resolving inside the bind. The request's target id, route and payload were built for the successor. Switching the target inside the write would admit a payload built for another session. The race needs a tombstone sweep to land in a window of milliseconds, and the retry is automatic in the OpenAI SDKs.

**Mirror (LC-26 follow-up).** `sessions.json` mirrors the routing index. A whole-index save now leaves out of the mirror exactly the keys the `gateway_routing` write skipped as retired (`replace_gateway_routing_entries` returns them), so both copies use one predicate. A start whose legacy import skipped retired mirror entries rewrites the mirror while the fence still holds. Without these two steps, a mirror written from a pre-prune snapshot would restore the pruned route on the first start after its shared fence aged out. Its session row is gone, and the stale pass keeps routes without a row. The fences still age out, so the id stays reusable: a session recreated with that id after the horizon routes and survives a restart. I didn't make the shared fence permanent again, because that would undo the reuse LC-25/LC-26 restore.

**Shared fences expire on their own.** Each profile's housekeeping (auto-prune, `hermes sessions prune`) sweeps only its own store, and the launch profile's auto-prune is off by default. A sweep fence in the shared index therefore can't rely on a launch sweep to go away. The routing-save check takes the save's time, and a sweep (`expires`) fence older than the 7-day horizon no longer fences. Without that, a secondary could reuse a pruned id after the horizon, but its recreated session's route stayed out of `gateway_routing` and `sessions.json` indefinitely. `fence_shared_routes` also reclaims expired sweep fences in the write that adds new ones, so the owner's own prunes keep the index bounded. A delete's fence and a pre-upgrade unscoped marker never expire.

**Upgrade compatibility.** Rows written before this change can't be classified:

- An earlier release wrote the same unstamped `{"retired_at"}` marker for a user delete, for a swept caller-named API id (since #140232) and for a secondary's shared fence. These rows keep their most restrictive meaning. They stay permanent, an old shared-index marker still fences every route to its id, and the launch profile keeps refusing that id.
- Only retirements after the upgrade age out or are scoped by profile. The exposure is the few days since #140232 / #140191 merged. Resurrecting an id the user actually deleted would be worse.
- New own markers are stamped `own`, so the code can tell them from those older rows.

## Related Issue

Fixes #140731
Fixes #140744
Refs #134889 (LC-25, LC-26)
Refs #140762

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `1c971ea` (salvaged unchanged from #140732, @dokterdok):
  - `hermes_state_mutation_retirement.py`: derived API ids are matched by id (`api-<16 hex>`, `bot_room`), not by `source='api_server'`, so a swept caller-named id ages out. Adds `keep_passed_fences`.
  - `gateway/session_api.py`: `bind_api_steps(walked_from=…)` makes the fences a continuation passed permanent.
  - Responses/Runs doors: `prepare_context` and `_admit_api_payload`, plus `_resolve_chained_history`, `_RunLaunch`, `_admit_run_to_authority`, `_handle_runs` and `_run_agent`, pass `walked_from`.
  - `api_server_memory_sessions.py`: a memory manager parked longer than the horizon is not handed to a reused id.
- `b3e9907`: tests pinning that a caller-named API id ages out, a door-derived one stays, and an old-shape permanent marker stays.
- `644209d` (rebuilt from #140745, co-authored):
  - `hermes_state_mutation_retirement.py`: `ROUTE_FENCE_PREFIX`, `route_namespace`, `route_retired_sql`/`route_retired`, `fence_shared_routes` and `expiring_retirements`. Own markers are stamped `own`, and expired route fences are reclaimed.
  - `hermes_state_gateway.py`: routing saves check through `route_retired_sql`, and `retire_gateway_routes(namespace=, expiring=)`.
  - `gateway/session_persistence.py`: `fence_retired_routes` passes the namespace, and the `sessions.json` import uses `route_retired`.
  - `gateway/session_mutations.py::retire_live_sessions` passes the secondary's namespace and its sweep-expiring ids.
- `c17095b` (LC-25 follow-up):
  - `keep_passed_fences` now returns whether the walk still holds.
  - `bind_api_steps` refuses `chain_moved` when it doesn't.
  - `api_server_authority_runs._STORE_ERROR_STATUS` maps `chain_moved` to a retryable 503.
- `15fbbf1` (LC-26 follow-up):
  - `replace_gateway_routing_entries` returns the retired keys it skipped, and `_persist_routing_data` leaves them out of `sessions.json`.
  - `_import_legacy_sessions_json` counts skipped retired entries, and `_ensure_loaded_locked` then rewrites the mirror.
- `3f49adb` (LC-26 follow-up):
  - `route_retired_sql(entry, namespace, now)`: a sweep fence older than the horizon no longer fences. Its callers in `hermes_state_gateway.py` pass the save's time.
  - `fence_shared_routes` reclaims expired sweep fences in its own write, through `_reclaim_expired`, which `prune_retired_tombstones` now also uses.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_secondary_route_fence_scope.py tests/gateway/test_derived_generation_after_sweep.py tests/hermes_state/test_retired_fence_outlives_horizon.py tests/gateway/test_api_server_memory_sessions.py tests/gateway/test_delete_secondary_profile_multiplex.py`
2. Live multiplexed gateway (`hermes gateway run`, default + `alpha`, throwaway HOMEs, loopback stub models). Seed an ended `cli` session `user-42` in alpha, run `hermes -p alpha sessions prune --source cli --yes` against the live gateway, then on the launch profile send `POST /api/sessions {"id":"user-42"}` and a chat with `X-Hermes-Session-Id: user-42`.
   - On `main` (e6cf2a9b): 409 `session_deleted`, then 409 `not_found`.
   - With this PR: 201, then 200.
   - Alpha still refuses its own id within the horizon with 409 `session_deleted`, and its chat with 409 `not_found`.

   - Interleavings (deterministic: the root's sweep marker is reclaimed right after the chain lookup returns):
     - `test_a_fence_reclaimed_between_chain_lookup_and_bind_never_splits_the_chain[/v1/responses|/v1/runs]`
     - `test_keep_passed_fences_reports_a_walk_it_could_not_pin`
   - Mirror after expiry (multiplexed, real `state.db` files):
     - `test_a_delayed_snapshot_cannot_restore_a_pruned_route_once_its_fence_ages_out` (also covers same-id recreation)
     - `test_a_start_within_the_horizon_strips_a_pruned_route_from_an_older_mirror`
   - Expiry without a launch sweep (fences aged 8 days; only alpha sweeps):
     - `test_a_pruned_id_routes_again_after_the_owner_alone_sweeps_past_the_horizon`
     - `test_the_owners_next_prune_reclaims_its_expired_shared_fences` (a delete's fence stays)

Related-suite run (95 files that grep the touched symbols): 1430 passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed. The failure, `tests/pm/test_takeover_preparation.py::test_fresh_takeover_prepares_generation_and_runs_selected_python`, fails the same way at the base sha. 0 `ERROR` lines.

## Checklist

### Code

- [ ] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu (Linux 6.8)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A

- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

## Credits

- #140732 by @dokterdok: its commit is included unchanged as `1c971ea` (author kept). It already says `Fixes #140731`, which this PR also earns.
- #140745 by @dokterdok: rebuilt, credited with `Co-authored-by`. It kept one shared fence per id (`retired_route.v1.<id>` listing the profiles that deleted it) and made it permanent for prunes too, so a secondary's pruned id was fenced in the shared index forever. Here the fence is keyed by (profile, id) and copies the owner marker's lifetime. A launch delete no longer blocks a secondary's route to its own session of the same name. Its rule for launch-keyed routes to an id the launch store doesn't hold is kept, as a conditional `main` fence.

## Still needs a live retest

- The 7-day ageing on a live gateway. Locally it is covered by `prune_retired_tombstones(older_than=0)` in real `state.db` files. A live check needs wall-clock time past the horizon.

## Known limits (out of this PR's scope)

- `DELETE /p/<profile>/api/sessions/{id}` (`APIServerAdapter._handle_delete_session` → `db.delete_session`) never reaches `retire_live_sessions`, so it writes no shared-index fence for a secondary (#138826 still open on that path). It also never refused the launch profile, so LC-26 never applied there.
- An owner's own delete (`retire_routes`, `SessionStore.retire_runtime_sessions`) still drops every route and in-memory entry naming the id, whatever profile owns the route. The save check no longer blocks the next save of that route, so the route comes back on the next save.
- The mirror is filtered only when the `state.db` save succeeds; a save that falls back to `sessions.json` alone can't evaluate fences. A pre-prune mirror is also cleaned only by a gateway start inside the horizon. Such a mirror comes from an earlier release, a crash before the next save, or a DB-less fallback save. If the gateway then stays down for the whole 7 days, the route can come back.

prs.title: fix(gateway): name an elevated gateway from its control pipe instead of OpenProcess (W9)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

On the #140706 reporter's host (Windows 10 19045), a non-elevated Desktop or CLI could never reach an elevated gateway. The client half of the control-pipe identity check (`_peer_subject(handle, server=True)` in `gateway/runtime_bootstrap_windows.py`, new with #106742) identified the server with `OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION)` on `GetNamedPipeServerProcessId`. There that call is denied from a filtered (Medium) token against the High-integrity gateway, so every attach failed with `cannot verify bootstrap peer process`, discovery reported the generic `authorization`, and the gateway logged nothing. #139661 fixed only the server half.

**The base does not behave the same everywhere.** On a Windows 11 test machine the same `OpenProcess` call succeeded, the token user matched, and the base **silently attached** a non-elevated client to the elevated gateway (`hermes gateway ensure --json` → `ready`). So the base either fails with a misleading `authorization` error or crosses the UAC boundary without saying so, depending on the host. This PR makes both cases the same named refusal (see "Native Windows retest").

Following the maintainer triage, the client now checks the server from the pipe itself, through its own handle:

- the pipe object's **owner and DACL** (`GetSecurityInfo`; the client's `GENERIC_READ` includes `READ_CONTROL`),
- the **server's logon session** (`GetNamedPipeServerSessionId`),
- next to `GetNamedPipeServerProcessId` and the existing `OpenProcess` read when that works.

A new pure function, `judge_pipe_server()`, makes the decision. When the pipe proves the server is elevated and the client isn't (only the two cases in the trust argument below), it refuses with the named reason added in #140490 (`classify_refused_owner()` / `refused_owner_remedy()`, so the wording stays the same: "The running gateway (PID N) was started as administrator … start Hermes without elevation"). The refusal is a `PermissionError` subclass (`RefusedOwner`) that carries the reason code. `discover_gateway_endpoint()` reports it as-is, which is what `hermes gateway ensure` and the Desktop boot read, so naming the boundary no longer depends on a provable `gateway.pid`/`gateway.lock` record.

A named profile served by the default profile's multiplexer has no pipe of its own, so its discovery asks the multiplexer's pipe (`_served_by_multiplexer()`). That lookup used to treat every `PermissionError` as "not served", so the refusal was lost: the secondary reported its own lock state and `ensure` waited out its deadline. It now returns the same named verdict direct discovery returns, so `ensure` for that profile answers at once and starts nothing. Every other lookup failure is still treated as "not served". A profile with `gateway.standalone: true` is never served by the multiplexer, so the existing boot policy (`host_serves_named_profile()`, the predicate behind `implied_host_root()` and `multiplexer_serves_home()`) keeps the multiplexer's refusal away from it: it falls through to its own lock and start path, as on the base.

This is a client-side diagnosis, not enforcement of an elevation boundary. It fires in two cases: an Administrators-owned pipe seen by a non-elevated client, and a server the client can't open whose pipe has this user's private shape. A readable same-user server whose pipe owner is the user (for example under the "Object creator" owner policy for administrators) still attaches, as on the base. A serving-side check, where the gateway itself refuses a client at a different elevation, is a follow-up.

### Design choice: refuse, don't attach

The elevated gateway's identity can be proven from the pipe, so attaching would have been possible. I chose a named refusal:

- An elevated gateway runs every tool with the user's full administrator token. If a non-elevated client handed it work, that would be a silent UAC crossing, and the client would become a second way to run elevated work.
- One-gateway contract: clients only read and submit, and a missing capability gets a gateway handler or a **named refusal**. The fix stays on the gateway path. The client gets no fallback and holds no state.
- The installer's scheduled task (`RunLevel` LeastPrivilege) and the Desktop manifest (`asInvoker`) both expect a non-elevated gateway, so the remedy (restart the gateway non-elevated) points back to the supported setup.
- **Behaviour change to note:** on hosts where the base attached (the Windows 11 run below), a user who today runs an elevated gateway with a normal Desktop will now get the refusal and has to restart the gateway non-elevated. That follows the triage direction ("when the server is elevated and the client isn't, refuse with the named reason"); attaching there was the unsupported UAC crossing, not a working feature.

### Trust argument (what is proven before anything is sent)

`judge_pipe_server(own_sid, process_sid, pipe, pid, own_elevated, own_session, server_session)`:

1. **Server process readable** (same as before): its token user must be this user, otherwise `named-pipe peer belongs to another user`. New: if the pipe's owner is `BUILTIN\Administrators`, which means an elevated process created it, and this client isn't elevated, the client refuses as `gateway_elevated`. Same level on both sides (neither elevated, or both) attaches as before. If an elevated server's pipe is owned by the user rather than `BUILTIN\Administrators` (the "Object creator" owner policy), the client can't tell it's elevated from a readable process and attaches, as on the base.
2. **Server process unreadable** (an elevated server seen from a filtered token): **never attached.** The pipe has to show it's this user's gateway pipe:
   - The **owner** is this user's SID or `BUILTIN\Administrators`. Another non-administrator account can't set either one as owner of an object it creates. Doing so takes being this user, being an elevated administrator, or holding SeRestore/SeTakeOwnership, and any of those already controls this account.
   - The **DACL** is exactly one allow ACE for this user's SID. That's the gateway's own private pipe shape (`_create_pipe`: `D:P(A;;GA;;;<user>)`). A squatter pipe that's open to Everyone, has extra or deny ACEs, has a NULL DACL, or grants another user doesn't match.

   Only when both match is the pipe treated as this user's gateway behind a boundary. `classify_refused_owner()` then names it: `gateway_elevated` (same session, client not elevated), or `gateway_other_session` when the pipe reports a different session. Every other case stays the generic refusal. An elevated client that can't open the server also stays generic and doesn't attach.
3. The serving side (`server=False`) is unchanged and never consults the pipe owner.

What a squatter can achieve: an elevated administrator could create a matching pipe under this user's pipe name and get a misleading "gateway started as administrator" message. That actor already controls the account, and the client still sends nothing. No unproven pipe ever gets a request.

The chat/client-facing refusal is the #140490 remedy text and doesn't name these checks. The proven facts (pipe owner, process readable or not, both sessions) go to the client's log at INFO.

## Related Issue

Refs #134889 (W9)
Refs #140762
Refs #140706

(`Refs`, not `Fixes`: the fix was run natively on Windows 11, but the reporter's failing base behaviour (Windows 10, `OpenProcess` denied) did not reproduce there, so the exact reported path hasn't been retested. See "Native Windows retest".)

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/runtime_bootstrap_windows.py`
  - `_pipe_security(handle)`: the pipe's owner SID and DACL as `(ace_type, sid)` pairs, from the client's handle (`GetSecurityInfo` + `GetAce`). `_pipe_server_session(handle)`: `GetNamedPipeServerSessionId`. `_sid_text()` is factored out of `_token_sid()`.
  - `judge_pipe_server()`: the pure decision above. `_server_subject()` gathers the Win32 facts for it. `_peer_subject(server=True)` now goes through it.
  - `RefusedOwner(PermissionError)`: `reason_code`, `pid`, and `str()` = the existing remedy.
- `hermes_cli/gateway_runtime.py`: `discover_gateway_endpoint()` reports a `RefusedOwner` as `inaccessible` with its reason code and remedy. Any other `PermissionError` still goes through `_refused()` as before. `_served_by_multiplexer()` returns the same verdict (shared `_refused_owner_verdict()`) when the multiplexer's pipe raises a `RefusedOwner`, unless `host_serves_named_profile()` rules the home out (a standalone secondary). Any other failure there still means "not served".
- Tests:
  - `tests/gateway/test_runtime_bootstrap_server_identity.py` (new, runs on every OS): drives the real `_peer_subject(server=True)` entry with the Win32 layer injected (`ctypes.WinDLL` for the ULONG-out queries, `_process_sid`, `_pipe_security`, `process_is_elevated`). It doesn't touch `sys.platform`. Covers the named refusal (process unopenable or readable), the same-user-owner boundary, other session, discovery without any owner record, eight squatter/unprovable pipe shapes, an elevated client, another user's readable server, same-level attach, and that the serving side never uses the pipe owner. For a multiplexed secondary profile (no pipe of its own, the multiplexer's pipe raises the refusal), `discover_gateway_endpoint()` and `ensure_gateway_runtime()` return the same named verdict at once, `ensure` attempts no service start or spawn, and a generic refusal from the multiplexer still leaves the secondary's own state in charge. A `gateway.standalone: true` secondary under the same elevated multiplexer discovers its own `absent` and `ensure` starts its own gateway.
  - `tests/gateway/test_runtime_bootstrap.py` (`platforms("windows")`): reads a live gateway pipe's owner, DACL and session through a client handle and attaches with the same token.
  - `tests/e2e/core/windows_update/test_elevated_gateway_attach.py` (`platforms("windows")`, `integration`): the live W9 check on the #140701 runner. The elevated runner hosts the real `NativeControlServer`. A child under `_tokens.StandardUserProcess` (Administrators deny-only, Medium, checked with `probe_token_elevation`) runs `query_runtime_control` and `discover_gateway_endpoint`. Asserts the named `gateway_elevated` refusal with the exact remedy from both, and that the gateway handler never ran.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_runtime_bootstrap_server_identity.py`. On the base, 5 tests fail on assertions (plain `PermissionError('cannot verify bootstrap peer process')`, and discovery `authorization`). With the multiplexer change reverted, the two multiplexed-secondary tests fail on assertions (discovery `absent`, ensure `starting`/`deadline`). Without the standalone check, the standalone-secondary test fails on an assertion (discovery `inaccessible` instead of `absent`). With the fix, 23 pass.
2. On Windows: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/e2e/core/windows_update/test_elevated_gateway_attach.py -- -m "platforms and integration"` from an elevated session (the Windows install/update E2E workflow runs it with the rest of `tests/e2e/core/windows_update/`).
3. Manually: start `hermes gateway run` from an administrator prompt, then run `hermes gateway ensure --json` from a normal prompt (or start the Desktop). Expect `inaccessible` / `gateway_elevated` with the remedy, not `authorization`.

## Checklist

### Code

- [ ] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate (#140587, #140707, see Credits)
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass (related suites only, below)
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [ ] I've tested on my platform: Linux (Ubuntu, kernel 6.8, Python 3.14.7), plus a manual native run on Windows 11 (above). The Windows pytest files haven't run yet

Related suites, Linux:
- Every test file that references the touched symbols (`runtime_bootstrap_windows`, `discover_gateway_endpoint`, `ensure_gateway_runtime`, `_served_by_multiplexer`, `RefusedOwner`, `judge_pipe_server`, `_pipe_security`, `host_serves_named_profile`; 34 files): **320 passed, 0 failed, 18 skipped** (the Windows-only tests skip on Linux). Exit 0, 0 ERROR lines.
- Wider sweep (136 files that import `gateway_runtime` etc.): 2853 passed, 3 failed, 1 collection ERROR. These are `test_config_secret_scope.py::…[fallback_providers_dict]`, two in `test_update_lock.py`, and `test_fal_sdk.py` (`fal_client` not installed). All four fail the same way on the pinned base `e6cf2a9b1e8f`, so they aren't caused by this PR.
- `python scripts/check --base e6cf2a9b…`: 12 checks ok. `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all`: clean.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Docstrings updated. Other docs N/A
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A

## Credits

- **@SmelterLabs, #140587** (draft, head `e5c283d18343`; the earliest open PR for this). It found the client-side `OpenProcess` denial and the pipe-owner approach (`GetSecurityInfo` on the client's handle, owner `BUILTIN\Administrators` for an elevated creator), and wrote the real-pipe owner test that this PR's Windows test is based on. Its commit isn't cherry-picked because it **accepts** an Administrators-owned pipe and attaches the non-elevated client. That's the UAC crossing the maintainer direction refuses, and it doesn't check the DACL, so any elevated process's pipe under this name would be trusted. The owner read was rebuilt here with the DACL and session added, so the commit carries `Co-authored-by: Casey <caseyrussell1976@gmail.com>`.
- **@srymak1r7, #140707** (head `83adf500a9a9`) and the #140706 report. The report pinned down the root cause and asked for a named diagnosis. #140707 adds a second elevation wording to `_process_sid`'s error. That wording also fires on the serving side, where the unopenable peer is the *client*. Rather than add a second phrasing, this PR uses #140490's named refusal, so no code from #140707 is taken. Its diagnosis is what this PR delivers.

Windows 11 Pro, managed install, user `hermes` (administrator behind UAC). Gateway started with `hermes gateway run` from an administrator PowerShell (`whoami` High, S-1-16-12288); clients from a normal prompt and a normally launched Desktop (Medium, S-1-16-8192).

| elevated gateway, non-elevated `hermes gateway ensure --json` | `ready`, exit 0, **attached** (Medium `OpenProcess(0x1000)` on the gateway pid succeeds on this host) | exit 4 in 2 s: `inaccessible` / `gateway_elevated`, "The running gateway (PID 6116) was started as administrator, so this non-elevated app cannot reach it. Stop it from an administrator prompt (hermes gateway stop), then start Hermes without elevation"; nothing spawned |
| elevated gateway, non-elevated Desktop | not run | boot card "Gateway inaccessible (gateway_elevated)" with the same remedy; no attach, no second gateway |

- The reporter's failing path: a host where Medium `OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION)` on the elevated gateway is denied (the reporter's Windows 10 19045). That is the unreadable-server branch of `judge_pipe_server()`, so far covered only by injected tests.

prs.title: feat(skills_guard): scan Windows script files and add PowerShell/LOLBin threat patterns
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`tools/skills_guard.py` currently never looks at Windows script files: `.ps1`, `.psm1`, `.psd1`, `.bat`, `.cmd` and `.vbs` are not in `SCANNABLE_EXTENSIONS`, and `THREAT_PATTERNS` has no entry for the common Windows download-and-execute idioms. A community skill can therefore ship a clean `SKILL.md` next to a `scripts/setup.ps1` containing `iwr https://… | iex` and scan **SAFE**, while the equivalent `curl … | sh` in a `.sh` file is blocked.

This PR closes that gap:

- adds the six Windows script extensions to `SCANNABLE_EXTENSIONS` and wires their comment syntax into `_COMMENT_PREFIX` so the existing inert-reference demotion (comments/docs) keeps working for them;
- adds a `Windows / PowerShell / batch / VBScript` block of 16 threat patterns, mirroring the severity/category conventions of the existing shell patterns:
  - **critical**: `iwr|irm|Invoke-WebRequest|DownloadString … | iex` (download-and-execute), `FromBase64String … Invoke-Expression`, `-EncodedCommand <base64>`, `mshta` with a URL/`vbscript:`/`javascript:` payload, `rundll32 javascript:`, `Set-MpPreference -Disable*` / `Add-MpPreference -Exclusion*` (Defender tamper), `$env:<API key/token>` inside a web request to a non-loopback host;
  - **high**: `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass|Unrestricted`, `$env:USERPROFILE\.ssh|.aws|.gnupg` reads, `certutil -urlcache|-decode`, `Start-Process -Verb RunAs`, `CreateObject("WScript.Shell"|"MSXML2.*HTTP"|"Shell.Application")` in VBScript;
  - **medium**: `-WindowStyle Hidden`, `bitsadmin /transfer`, `HKCU\…\Run` / `schtasks /create` / `Register-ScheduledTask` (autostart), caret obfuscation like `p^o^w^e^r^s^h^e^l^l`;
- bumps `SCANNER_VERSION` to `skills-guard-v6` so cached verdicts are recomputed.

The patterns are deliberately narrow: `certutil -hashfile`, `Invoke-WebRequest -OutFile`, `Get-MpPreference`, `Get-ScheduledTask`, `[Convert]::ToBase64String`, loopback requests carrying `$env:*_API_KEY` and plain `$env:USERPROFILE\Documents` paths do not fire (covered by the negative tests).

## Related Issue

None found — searched open and merged PRs/issues for `skills_guard`, `PowerShell`, `.ps1`, `LOLBin`.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🔒 Security fix
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

- `tools/skills_guard.py`: `SCANNABLE_EXTENSIONS` (+6), `_COMMENT_PREFIX` (+6), new pattern block before `# ── Privilege escalation ──` (16 pattern ids: `ps_download_execute`, `ps_base64_execute`, `ps_encoded_command`, `ps_execution_policy_bypass`, `ps_hidden_window`, `ps_env_exfil`, `ps_credential_dir`, `certutil_lolbin`, `bitsadmin_lolbin`, `mshta_execute`, `rundll32_javascript`, `windows_autostart`, `defender_tamper`, `ps_runas_elevation`, `vbs_shell_object`, `cmd_caret_obfuscation`), `SCANNER_VERSION` → `skills-guard-v6`.
- `tests/tools/test_skills_guard_powershell.py` (new): extension coverage, the `.ps1`-dropper-next-to-clean-`SKILL.md` regression case, one positive case per pattern (29 lines), `.bat`/`.vbs` coverage, community-source block on a critical finding, 11 benign PowerShell negatives, and comment demotion for `#` comments in `.ps1`.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/tools/test_skills_guard_powershell.py tests/tools/test_skills_guard.py tests/tools/test_skills_guard_agent_config.py -q` — 251 passed (new file plus the existing guard suites).
2. Regression check on the hub catalogue: ran `hermes skills audit` before and after the change against 23 installed hub skills — every verdict unchanged (no new false positives on existing skills). Over ~1.5k scanned files the new patterns produced two hits, both genuine documentation of `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass` and `irm … | iex` install one-liners.
3. Regression fixture: a skill with a clean `SKILL.md` and `scripts/setup.ps1` containing `iwr https://… | iex` now scans `dangerous` from a community source (`test_ps1_dropper_next_to_clean_skill_md_is_dangerous`); before this change `.ps1` was not scanned at all, so the same fixture scanned `safe`.
