prs.title: fix(desktop): read the final reply aloud after tool calls
prs.body:
With **Read replies aloud** on, the final reply after a run of tool calls often went silent. The completion ping played, but the TTS backend got no request and nothing was logged. Replies in a turn of their own played normally.

## Cause

Auto-speak claims each reply across windows with `speak:<turnKey>`, and the main-process arbiter holds speech claims for 10 minutes (`SPEECH_CLAIM_TTL_MS`). The turn key is `<session>:<user turn index>`, so every bubble a turn with tool calls speaks (short progress updates first, then the final reply) shares one key.

1. A progress update finishes, is marked spoken, and claims `speak:sess:0`. The claim is granted and the clip plays.
2. The final reply lands while that clip is still playing, so it is held. That part works as designed.
3. When that clip ends, the final reply is marked spoken, then asks for `speak:sess:0`. The claim is refused, and the hook returns without logging. Since the reply is already consumed, no later event retries it.

The turn key came from #121560, which stopped hydration's id rewrite from reading one reply twice. That fix holds, but its key was one level too coarse.

## Fix

- `spokenSegmentKey(turnKey, text)` in `lib/spoken-reply.ts` appends an FNV-1a fingerprint of the spoken text. Every window computes the same key, separate bubbles in one turn get separate keys, and an id rewrite keeps the text, so the double-speak guard still holds.
- `useAutoSpeakReplies` uses the segment key for the cross-window claim **and** for `playSpeechText`'s same-turn join, which had the same per-turn collision.
- A refused claim now writes `console.debug('[auto-speak] claim already taken', key)` instead of returning silently.

## Not changed

Holding the reply until the playback-idle edge is unchanged. `$voicePlayback` is a nanostores atom set with a fresh object on every transition, and every way playback ends writes `idle` (or hands the state to a newer playback). The idle edge was not being missed; the claim after it was refused.

## Tests

- `use-auto-speak-replies.test.tsx`: a turn with tool calls where a progress update plays, the final reply waits behind it, and the clip ends normally. It runs against a claim arbiter that keeps the first claim of each key. **Red on `main`** (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called 2 times, but got 1 times`), green with the fix.
- `spoken-reply.test.ts`: the segment key survives an id rewrite, separates segments within a turn, and separates two turns that say the same thing.
- `npx vitest run src/app/chat/composer/hooks/ src/lib/spoken-reply.test.ts src/lib/voice-playback.same-turn.test.ts`: 34 files, 241 tests pass. `tsc -p .`, eslint, prettier, and `scripts/check --only health` are clean.

Reported on Discord (Windows 11, local OpenAI-compatible TTS bridge) with a backend access log correlated against `state.db`: final replies got zero TTS requests while mid-session replies were fetched about 1 s after completing. Not reproduced live; covered by the regression test above.

Supersedes #139981. Thanks @xxxigm for pinning the drop to the hold path. That PR re-arms on a timer, but this reply is refused after the idle edge and already consumed, so a retry has nothing left to speak.

prs.title: Archive stale dirty worktrees before removing them, sweep every repo, ask on dirty exit
prs.body:
Idle worktrees that hold uncommitted changes or unpushed commits are now archived to a git ref and then removed, instead of being kept forever. Every repo Hermes has made a worktree in gets swept. A dirty `hermes -w` exit asks Keep / Archive / Discard, and `hermes worktree restore` brings an archived tree back.

**Root cause:** the pruner never removed a dirty or unpushed tree at any age, and its 6h sweep only knew the Hermes checkout and cron workdirs. Lane leftovers piled up: 658 trees / ~1 TB on one machine, 553 of them plain `git worktree add` lanes.

## What changes
- **Snapshot-then-delete** (`hermes_cli/worktree_sweep.py`, `hermes_cli/worktree_archive.py`):
  - Applies to a tree past its existing tier (`hermes-*`/`subagent-*` 24h idle, named trees 72h) that is dirty or unpushed.
  - The archive is a commit at `refs/hermes/archive/<tree>` (with a timestamp suffix on collision).
  - It holds HEAD, staged changes, unstaged changes and non-ignored untracked files, raw bytes. Filters are off, autocrlf is off, and attributes are read from the empty tree.
  - It is built with a temporary `GIT_INDEX_FILE`. The real index and working tree are only read.
  - Metadata (path, branch, HEAD, reason, skipped files) is JSON in the commit message.
  - Untracked files over `archive_max_file_mb` (50) are skipped and listed.
  - The tree is removed only after the ref exists. A failed archive keeps the tree, and so does an untracked embedded repo or any submodule: a gitlink in the index or a repository under the tree's `modules/` dir (`keep-submodule-work`; an archive records only the gitlink). The submodule rule is re-checked right before `git worktree remove`. If the tree is entered, edited, or its staged entries (`ls-files --stage`) change after the capture, the archive stays and the tree is kept, reported as "archived, kept".
  - Branches: one published on a remote is kept. Otherwise the archive anchors its commits and the local branch is deleted.
- **Never touched, at any age or budget:**
  - a live `hermes` lock owner
  - any live process whose cwd, or on Linux an open fd, is inside the tree (`/proc` scan; psutil cwd elsewhere)
  - file / `HEAD` / reflog activity younger than the tier
  - Kanban `t_<hex>` trees
- **No count cap.** The optional `worktrees.max_total_gb` (default 0, off) evicts the oldest *idle* past-tier trees first, archiving before removal.
- **Cross-repo registry** (`hermes_cli/worktree_registry.py`):
  - Every repo is recorded in `<HERMES_HOME>/worktree_repos.json`, per profile, with atomic writes under a file lock and missing repos dropped.
  - Recording happens on `hermes -w` / `/worktree new` (`_setup_worktree`), subagent isolation, and the Desktop git pane's `worktree_add`.
  - `cron.scheduler._worktree_maintenance_repos` unions the registry with its existing sources.
  - The cron sweep is throttled **per profile home** and runs in a copy of the caller's context, so a multiplexed tick sweeps each profile's repos under that profile's config.
- **Subagent worktrees:** a child that leaves commits or edits gets its tree archived and removed at finish. The branch is kept for the parent to merge, and the payload carries `archive` plus a restore hint.
- **Dirty-exit question** (`hermes_cli/worktree_exit.py`):
  - Classic CLI: asked in `_tui_shutdown` before `_run_cleanup` arms the exit watchdog.
  - TUI: asked by the launcher after Ink exits. It waits up to 5s for its own `tui_gateway` child to leave the tree.
  - Options: Keep (default; also Esc), Archive & remove (prints the restore command), Remove and discard (explicit choice only).
  - It never asks without a TTY, on a signal-driven shutdown, or while a live process is still in the tree. `-q`/`-z`/cron/gateway never reach it.
- **CLI:**
  - `hermes worktree restore <name> [--path DIR]` re-creates the tree with its branch (detached if the branch moved), staged index and untracked files.
  - `hermes worktree list` shows archives.
  - `hermes worktree prune --dry-run` prints the sweep's full decision table without changing anything.
  - Archive refs older than `archive_retention_days` (30) are deleted by the sweep.
- **Config:** `worktrees.{archive_dirty, archive_max_file_mb, archive_retention_days, max_total_gb}` added in `config_defaults.py`, `cli-config.yaml.example` and the docs. `archive_dirty: false` with no budget runs the classic pruner unchanged.
- **i18n:** 12 new `cli.worktree.*` keys (d70ebda swaps `archive_not_removed` for `archived_kept`, `sweep_archived_removed`, `sweep_archived_kept`) plus the updated tip `t244` in all 17 locales.
- **Shape:** new behaviour lives in 4 new siblings. `config_defaults.py` growth is offset by moving its env-entry factories to `config_defaults_env.py`. `python scripts/check --only health` reports 0 blocking.

## Invariants → tests (red on origin/main → green)
| Inv | Test | origin/main | head |
|---|---|---|---|
| I1 + I4 | `test_worktree_snapshot_prune.py::test_removed_dirty_tree_restores_byte_for_byte_and_archiving_never_touches_the_tree`: HEAD, staged, unstaged, CRLF bytes and untracked binary survive remove → restore; ignored `node_modules` and the >cap file are not archived; real index + files byte-identical after archiving | FAIL (no archive module) | PASS |
| I1–I4 | `::test_sweep_archives_idle_work_and_never_touches_live_kanban_or_young_trees` through `_prune_stale_worktrees`: idle dirty + unpushed archived then removed; live cwd (real `sleep` child), live lock, kanban, young and an un-archivable tree (embedded repo) untouched | FAIL (dirty kept, no refs) | PASS |
| I6 | `::test_archive_dirty_false_keeps_the_classic_never_delete_dirty_pruner` | PASS (parity guard) | PASS |
| I7 | `::test_cron_sweep_visits_only_the_active_profiles_registered_repos`: profile A sees its repo, profile B does not, a deleted registered repo drops out | FAIL | PASS |
| I5 | `::test_exit_question_never_prompts_without_a_tty` | FAIL (no module) | PASS |
| subagent | `tests/tools/test_subagent_worktree.py::test_finalize_archives_{dirty_worktree,worktree_with_commits}` | FAIL | PASS |

Review fixes (d6e341a), proven red on 058ea2d and green on head:
| Finding | Test | 058ea2d | head |
|---|---|---|---|
| eol rules from `info/attributes` / `core.attributesFile` changed archived bytes | I1 test extended (`*.md eol=crlf` LF file, `*.cfg eol=lf` CRLF file) | FAIL (digest differs) | PASS |
| `subagent-*` got the 72h tier | board test: `subagent-done` idle 30h must be archived | FAIL (kept) | PASS |
| a deletion in a subdir looked idle | board test: `lane-deleted` (newest work = unlink in `sub/`) must survive | FAIL (archived) | PASS |
| liveness checked once per batch / not after the snapshot | `::test_a_tree_resumed_mid_sweep_is_never_removed` | FAIL (lane-a deleted) | PASS |
| `prune --older-than` ignored by the sweep | `::test_prune_older_than_bounds_what_the_sweep_removes` | FAIL (both removed) | PASS |
| Desktop `existingBranch` skipped the registry | `test_web_server_git.py::test_worktree_add_existing_remote_branch_tracks_not_detaches` (+ registry assert) | FAIL | PASS |
| `text=True` without `encoding` in `worktree_sweep.py` (CI) | `test_subprocess_text_encoding.py[worktree_sweep.py]` | FAIL | PASS |

Second review fixes (d70ebda, @unsupportedpastels), proven red on d6e341a and green on head:
| Finding | Test | d6e341a | head |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1: dirty submodule edits deleted by archive-then-remove (archive holds only the gitlink) | `::test_dirty_submodule_work_is_never_archived_away` (real `git submodule add` from a local bare repo, `protocol.file.allow=always`): plan says `keep-submodule-work`, real `_prune_stale_worktrees` keeps the tree, dirty file byte-identical, `snapshot_worktree` raises; clean-submodule control still archived + removed | FAIL (`lane-subdirty` planned `archive-remove`; `sub/file.txt` gone) | PASS |
| Independent review (72ef744): deinitialized submodule's retained `modules/` repo with an unpushed private commit, and a submodule file edited right after the snapshot | same test, cases `lane-deinit` / `lane-late`, real sweep entry point | FAIL on d70ebda (module repo deleted; edited file gone) | PASS (tree, module repo, private ref and edited bytes survive; no archive) |
| Index-only edit (`git apply --cached`) after capture deleted | `::test_a_tree_resumed_mid_sweep_is_never_removed` extended: wrapped snapshot runs a real `git apply --cached -` + `git status` right after capture | FAIL (`lane-staged` removed) | PASS |
| Retained-after-snapshot tree reported as "archived + removed" | same test asserts `hermes worktree prune` actions read `archived, kept (changed during the sweep) → <ref>` | FAIL | PASS |

On d70ebda: tests/hermes_cli/test_worktree*.py, tests/tools/test_subagent_worktree*.py, test_subprocess_text_encoding.py, test_web_server_git.py, tests/cron/test_worktree_maintenance_isolation.py, tests/agent/test_i18n.py → **949 passed, 0 failed**; ruff, Windows-footgun, no-tmp, `scripts/check --only health` (0 blocking), `git diff --check` clean.

Suites run with `scripts/run_tests.sh`: tests/hermes_cli worktree + kanban-worktree + gateway-launch + tui-resume, tests/tools/test_subagent_worktree.py + test_delegate.py, tests/cron/, tests/security/test_gitspawn_config_injection.py, tests/agent/test_i18n.py, tests/pm/test_install_states_gc.py, tests/hermes_cli/test_config.py + test_web_git.py. Result: **1984 passed, 0 failed** before the rebase. On the rebased head, the 14 worktree/i18n/config files: **385 passed**. On d6e341a: tests/hermes_cli/test_worktree*.py, test_web_git*.py, test_web_server_git.py, test_subprocess_text_encoding.py, tests/tools/test_subagent_worktree.py, the worktree tests in tests/cron, tests/agent/test_i18n.py → **979 passed, 0 failed**. test_worktree.py, test_worktree_selfheal.py, test_gitspawn_config_injection.py, test_delegate.py, lsp/test_workspace_release.py → **148 passed**.

## Changed existing assertions
Under Teknium's 2026-10-17 approval of snapshot-then-delete, each "dirty/unpushed is never removed" assertion was rewritten to "never removed without a restorable archive":
- `tests/tools/test_subagent_worktree.py::test_finalize_keeps_worktree_with_commits` → `test_finalize_archives_worktree_with_commits`. It used to assert the tree was kept. It now asserts `pruned`, the tree is gone, and `archive^1 == branch tip` (branch kept).
- `tests/tools/test_subagent_worktree.py::test_finalize_keeps_dirty_worktree` → `test_finalize_archives_dirty_worktree`. It used to assert the tree was kept. It now asserts the tree is gone and `git show <archive>:wip.txt == "uncommitted\n"`.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_worktree_gc.py::test_list_json_shape`: the key set gains `"archives"` (additive, not weakened).

The `TestWorktreeLockReaping` / `TestPruneParallelEquivalence` "dirty survives" assertions are unchanged. They still pass because their trees' files are fresh (activity-gated as *young*), which is the intended behaviour for a tree touched moments ago.

## Live validation (real processes, scratch `HOME` + `HERMES_HOME`, real model via Nous endpoint)
| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| `hermes chat --cli -w` in tmux, model writes `notes.md` (staged) + `scratch.txt`, `/exit` → **Keep** | question shown; tree kept, warning printed, 0 archives |
| same → **Archive & remove** | `✓ Worktree archived to refs/hermes/archive/hermes-54d26619 and removed`, restore hint printed; `hermes worktree restore hermes-54d26619` → `A notes.md`, `?? scratch.txt`, branch back |
| same → **Remove and discard** | tree + branch gone, 0 archives |
| d6e341a: same → **Archive & remove**, now applied synchronously before the exit watchdog | `Archiving <path> … (this can take a while for a large tree)`, then `✓ Worktree archived to refs/hermes/archive/hermes-bc64b99f and removed` + restore hint; `.worktrees/` empty; archive holds `notes.md` + `scratch.txt` ($0.014) |
| `hermes --tui -w` (prebuilt Ink), model dirties tree, `/quit` → **Archive**, then restore | question shown after the TUI backend left the tree; archived + removed; restore brings back both untracked files and the branch |
| `hermes chat -w -q "..." < /dev/null` with a dirty tree | **no prompt**, tree kept |
| 30-tree synthetic sweep (`_prune_stale_worktrees` + `hermes worktree prune --dry-run`) | see table below |

Billed for live runs (scratch `state.db`): **$0.169** ($0.155 + $0.014 for the d6e341a leg).

30-tree sweep (every class) decisions:
| Class | Trees | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| clean merged (hermes-*, named) | 7 | remove |
| dirty idle (incl. dead-pid lock, node_modules, 60 MB file) | 7 | archive-remove |
| unpushed idle | 3 | archive-remove (branch deleted, archive anchors it) |
| pushed branch + stray file | 2 | archive-remove (branch kept) |
| live cwd (real `sleep` inside) | 3 | skip-live-process |
| live `hermes pid=` lock (running pid) | 2 | skip-live-lock |
| kanban `t_<hex>` | 3 | skip-kanban |
| young / deep file edited now | 3 | skip-young |

Result: 11 survivors (exactly the skips), 12 archive refs, `.git/objects` 456K (the 60 MB file was skipped and listed). After the sweep the live `sleep`s still had their cwd inside their trees. `restore lane-bigfile --path …` printed `Not captured (over the size cap): model.bin (60 MB)`.

## Real-repo dry run (read-only, scratch HERMES_HOME, `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`; nothing executed)
| Decision | Trees | GB (du) |
|---|---|---|
| remove (clean + merged/pushed, the classic pruner's own reap verdicts) | 305 | 168.7 |
| remove-keep-branch (head == origin) | 8 | 5.1 |
| **archive-remove** (130 uncommitted, 124 unpushed; 246 named, 8 `hermes-*`) | **254** | **149.6** |
| skip-live-process (`hermes-b294df2b`, `hermes-d935e342`, `r6-confirm`, `tui-turn`, `uf-f3-buildart`) | 5 | 4.7 |
| skip-young (younger than tier by stat or by file/ref activity) | 87 | not measured |
| unknown-hung (`uf-f8b`: `git status` blocked in kernel D-state on this host) | 1 | — |
| **Total** | **660** | |

Submodule bucket (72ef744): a read-only scan of all 678 current trees found **0** with a `160000` gitlink and **0** with a non-empty `<gitdir>/modules/`, so **0** of these trees move to `keep-submodule-work`; the classification above is otherwise unchanged.

**Estimated reclaimable: ~323 GB** (remove + archive-remove, measured trees). No tree was touched. Only `plan_sweep` was called, never `execute_plan`. Kanban count is 0 because this repo has no `t_<hex>` trees.

## Not covered
- **Recursive submodule archiving** is not implemented. A tree with any submodule (a gitlink in its index, or a submodule repository under its `modules/` dir, including after `git submodule deinit`) is **kept, never archived or removed** (`keep-submodule-work`). A clean merged tree is removed only when `modules/` is absent and its gitlink was never initialized. Nested submodules need no separate check: the outer gitlink already keeps the tree.
- **Submodule checks on exit-time Archive / subagent finish** were exercised through the shared `snapshot_worktree` refusal in the test, not through a live CLI exit or live `delegate_task`.
- **Staged-change gate**: an index change landing after the pre-removal comparison but before `git worktree remove` finishes is still a race window (milliseconds); not exercised.
- **Desktop surface for the exit question.** Only the classic CLI (`hermes -w`) and the TUI launcher
  (`hermes --tui -w`) ask Keep / Archive / Discard. Desktop/dashboard worktrees are recorded in the
  registry and swept, but closing a Desktop session never asks. Out of scope by design.
- **Windows / macOS live-process detection.** On Linux the gate reads `/proc/*/cwd` and `/proc/*/fd`.
  Elsewhere it is best-effort psutil `cwd()` only (no open-file check), and it was not run on those OSes.
- **`max_total_gb` budget** is covered by code and docs, but no live run set a budget. The 30-tree
  sweep ran with the default `0` (off).
- **Archive retention** (`archive_retention_days`) was not exercised live with a backdated archive.
  The deletion path is the same `update-ref -d` call the tests use.
- **Restore when the branch moved** (detached fallback) and **restore of a tree whose original
  path is occupied** are reachable through code paths only; neither was run live.
- **git < 2.40**: archive bytes no longer depend on `--attr-source` (every blob is re-hashed with
  `hash-object --no-filters` and restored by writing blob bytes), so old git stores exact bytes too,
  but only git 2.53 was run.
- **Ctrl-C during an exit-time Archive**: an interrupt before the archive ref exists keeps the tree;
  an interrupt during `git worktree remove` (after the ref exists) can leave a partial tree next to
  a complete archive. Not exercised.
- **Real-repo dry run**: a few trees can be reported `unknown-hung`. That happens when their
  `git status`/`du` blocked in kernel D-state during the run (the host had load ~1860 from
  concurrent `du` scans of the same filesystem). Those trees were not classified.
- **Gateway / cron live sweep on a real gateway** was not run. The cron path is covered by
  `test_cron_sweep_visits_only_the_active_profiles_registered_repos` (registry + profile scope)
  and the existing `test_maintenance_prunes_via_real_pruner`.
- **Subagent finish path live** (a real `delegate_task` with `delegation.worktree_isolation: true`)
  was not run end-to-end. It is covered by the real-git tests in `tests/tools/test_subagent_worktree.py`.

## Infographic
![Worktree lifecycle](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aaec148/QgBRVVvApJ3_R5M-3gJZx_t8ewmZLO.png)

prs.title: fix(web): bump uvicorn pin to 0.54.0 so a padded `Connection: close` is honoured
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Bumps the `[web]` extra's uvicorn pin from `0.41.0` to `0.54.0` and adds a regression test for it.

uvicorn <= 0.52.0 decided "the client asked to close" by testing the request's raw header list for the exact tuple `(b"connection", b"close")`:

```python
# uvicorn/protocols/http/flow_control.py
CLOSE_HEADER = (b"connection", b"close")

# uvicorn/protocols/http/httptools_impl.py — RequestResponseCycle.send()
if CLOSE_HEADER in self.scope["headers"] and CLOSE_HEADER not in headers:
    headers = headers + [CLOSE_HEADER]
```

Chrome on Windows sends that value padded (`Connection: close␣␣␣␣␣`, captured on the wire). The exact match misses it, so uvicorn neither answered with `connection: close` nor closed the socket — and it then stopped serving later requests on that connection (they were ACKed by the kernel but never reached the app; no FIN until the keep-alive timeout). Chrome, having seen no close, reused the socket and waited forever: the dashboard's login page never finished loading on a LAN/remote bind.

uvicorn 0.53.0 replaced that logic with the parser's own `should_keep_alive()` (which handles case, surrounding whitespace and comma lists) and no longer has the problem, so the fix on the Hermes side is the pin.

## Related Issue

Fixes #140860

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `pyproject.toml` — `[web]` extra: `uvicorn==0.41.0` → `uvicorn==0.54.0`, with a comment recording why the floor matters (an accidental re-pin below 0.53.0 reintroduces #140860).
- `tests/dashboard/test_uvicorn_keepalive_pin.py` — new test asserting the `[web]` extra cannot resolve a uvicorn below 0.53.0 (parses `pyproject.toml` with `packaging.Requirement`, so both `==x.y.z` and range pins are handled).

## How to Test

Reproduce the bug on the pinned version (any host, any ASGI app, or the real dashboard):

```bash
python -m uvicorn app:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9119
```

Then on a single TCP connection:
1. send `GET /a HTTP/1.1` + `Host: x` + `Connection: close     ` (value padded with 5 spaces) and read the response
2. send `GET /b HTTP/1.1` + `Host: x` + `Connection: keep-alive` on the same connection

On 0.41.0 the second request is never answered. On 0.54.0 the first response carries `connection: close` and the socket is closed immediately (and `Connection: keep-alive` reuse keeps working).

Verified end to end here:
- uvicorn 0.54.0 installed in the dashboard's venv, `hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9119` restarted: the padded request gets `connection: close` + an immediate FIN, keep-alive reuse works, `auth_required`/`auth_providers` unchanged, and Windows Chrome (the client that reproduced it) now loads the dashboard.
- The new test was run against three pins: `==0.41.0` → fails, `==0.54.0` → passes, `>=0.31.0,<1` → fails.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — **not run in full**: this host has no dev extras installed, so I executed the added test standalone (three pins, results above) instead of the whole suite.
- [ ] `python scripts/check` passes — **not run**: same reason (dev tooling not installed on the host that found this).
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 15.8 (Hermes host) with a Windows 11 24H2 / Chrome 155 client, the combination that reproduced the hang

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the compatibility guide — this is exactly a Windows-client/macOS-host interaction; no code path changes, only the dependency pin
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

`tcpdump` of the failing request (client 192.168.0.8 → dashboard 9119), with the five
trailing spaces of the `Connection` value drawn as `·`:

```
GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: 192.168.0.7:9119
Connection: close·····
```

The follow-up request Chrome sends on that same socket (still expecting to reuse it)
never receives a response. Full details and the local workaround used before this pin
existed are in #140860.

prs.title: fix(kanban): release a dead attempt's claim when its owner receipt cannot be resolved
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A `running` card whose worker is killed can become **permanently unreclaimable by every reclaim path** when its current run carries an `owner_admitted` receipt that never resolved (the owner was killed by a restart, so the admission is `terminal`/`interrupted` and/or its pid is gone) **and** that run never wrote a `worker_bound` event.

`owner_reclaim_paused()` then held the card in `release_stale_claims()`, `enforce_max_runtime()`, `detect_stale_running()`, `reconcile_orphaned_running()` and `_reclaim_dead_workers()`, while `bound_interpreter_gone()` — the only override for that pause — requires a `worker_bound` event those runs never wrote. The card keeps its profile's `kanban.max_in_progress_per_profile` slot indefinitely, silently: every card behind it is deferred with `has 1 of 1 allowed worker(s) running`, and `hermes kanban diagnostics` had no rule that can see a `running` card at all (`stranded_in_ready` watches READY cards), so the alarms named the deferred victims and never the cause.

Measured on one board: 16 hours on a single card (claimed 07:48, worker pid killed by a restart at 08:59, claim expired 08:03, no heartbeat), 15 cards queued behind it, **2 runs in exactly that shape** (`owner_admitted` 76 vs `worker_bound` 74), and 4 cards that had needed a human `hermes kanban reclaim` over two weeks.

The pause is right: an attempt whose effects may still be in flight must never be repeated. That is a different question from *whether anything can still be executing it*, and it was the only question being asked. This PR asks the second one, and answers it from evidence the board already keeps.

## Related Issue

Fixes #140858

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/kanban_owner_recovery.py`
  - `owner_attempt_provably_over()`: True when the receipt is unresolved but the attempt is provably over — host-local **expired** claim, no heartbeat inside `DEFAULT_CLAIM_HEARTBEAT_MAX_STALE_SECONDS`, the receipt's own process gone or recycled (same identity rule the pause already applies to `birth`), and every worker pid recorded for the current run (`tasks.worker_pid`, its `spawned` / `worker_bound` events) dead or recycled. Missing evidence is never proof: a live pid, an unreadable fingerprint, no recorded pid at all, or another host's lock all return False.
  - `owner_reclaim_blocked()`: `owner_reclaim_paused() and not (bound_interpreter_gone() or owner_attempt_provably_over())` — the one predicate every reclaim path now asks.
  - `bound_interpreter_gone()` is now host-local only. A `worker_bound` pid is this host's pid; a numeric coincidence on another host must not read as a death and release a live claim. Its only existing caller already checked the lock's host, so no behaviour changes there — this closes the hazard the newly-widened call sites would otherwise open.
- `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py` (`release_stale_claims`), `hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py` (`enforce_max_runtime`, `detect_stale_running`, `reconcile_orphaned_running`, `_reclaim_dead_workers`): the pause is no longer read as an unconditional veto. Both ratcheted files stay line-neutral.
- `hermes_cli/kanban_diagnostics.py`: new `stale_running` rule — a `running` card whose claim expired past `kanban.diagnostics.stale_running_grace_seconds` (default 1h) with no live recorded worker and no fresh heartbeat. Severity escalates with age (2x → `error`, 6x → `critical`); silent for a live claim, a fresh heartbeat, a live recorded worker, a foreign lock, or a card that is not `running`. Actions: reclaim + CLI hint.
- `website/docs/user-guide/features/kanban-worker-lanes.md`: documents both halves under failure modes.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_owner_receipt_reclaim.py` (new, 20 tests).

## How to Test

1. Reproduce on the base build with the snippet in #140858 (scratch board seeded with the incident's own events):

```text
owner_reclaim_paused: True
bound_interpreter_gone: False
release_stale_claims: 0
detect_crashed_workers: []
reconcile_orphaned_running: []
detect_stale_running: []
status: running
```

With this branch the same script prints `release_stale_claims: 1` and `status: ready`, with the run closed as `reclaimed`.

2. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_owner_receipt_reclaim.py` → **20 passed, 0 failed**.
3. Regression sweep: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_*.py -j 6` → **`=== Summary: 77 files, 540 tests passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped ===`**.
4. `python scripts/check (--base <base>)` → code health clean; both ratcheted files kept line-neutral.

## What the new tests pin

- The incident shape (unresolved receipt, no `worker_bound`, dead pids, expired claim, no heartbeat) is reclaimed by `release_stale_claims()` and by `detect_crashed_workers()`, the run closes as `reclaimed`, and the profile's slot frees so the next dispatch tick spends it.
- The pause still holds everything that may be alive: a live worker pid with a real fingerprint, a live bound interpreter, a heartbeat inside the max-stale window, an unexpired claim, another host's lock, a live owner pid with no `birth` to compare, and a run that recorded no worker pid at all.
- The diagnostic fires for the jam, escalates at 2x/6x grace, and stays silent for the healthy shapes.

## Notes for reviewers

- Deliberately **not** changed: the pause itself, and `reconcile_orphaned_running()`'s NULL-lock requirement (a different, rarer bookkeeping shape — its guard is the worker-liveness check it already does, and this PR leaves it alone rather than widening the same reasoning into an unrelated path).
- No new config keys beyond the diagnostics knob (already folded in by `config_from_kanban_config`); `cli-config.yaml.example` does not document the `kanban.diagnostics` block, so it is untouched.

prs.title: catalog: Hermes Telegram Bridge 1.8.0 — modular single package
prs.body:
## Single-package community submission

Owner submission for **Hermes Telegram Bridge 1.8.0**, MIT, public repository and release. Exact immutable source: `4874276f519f68fdbacb9767f70c5ed760b5c6fb`; subdir `desktop-plugins/session-complete-telegram`. This supersedes the earlier two-install design: one package registers Desktop, fixed native CLI and handlers on the existing Telegram Application. The obsolete companion PR #135957 is withdrawn; it is not a required package. No new SDK/core changes are requested.

## Public surfaces and retained safety

One `ctx.register_cli_command` and one `ctx.register_telegram_handler` factory. Neither is a tool/hook/middleware registration; those capability arrays are empty by design. A dedicated Telegram Bridge settings page exposes a common service switch and five effective modules backed by seven native booleans. Existing `replies_enabled` and `approvals_enabled` consent still defaults false independently; service/native selection and parent-notification switches also gate the actions. Installing or re-enabling code neither grants consent nor revives retired cards. The package/helper/renderer version is 1.8.0 with the v4 action handshake; mixed older/newer components deny versioned actions. No self-updater, runtime core override, private store patch, second poller, arbitrary renderer command or automatic consent/config/state migration. Exact private owner/original card/live local route/session/request/queue, strict raw AND effective consent, full safe review, fresh leases and final read-only claim validity remain required. Only once/deny with `all:false`; no permanent/session grants, callback shell execution or ambiguous replay. Unsupported/unsafe reviews remain command-free Desktop guidance. Native queue settlement remains authoritative; local freshness is not atomic fingerprint CAS. Delivery is not command completion.

## Required disclosures

The plugin reads the user's existing default-home Telegram setup (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL), sends cards to api.telegram.org, and reads same-home local profile session titles, persisted final responses and pending requests. Previews are redacted/capped at1200characters, but redaction is not absolute. Cards are copyable/forwardable. The renderer never receives the bot token; no credentials are copied, refreshed, rotated or written, including other vendor stores. No telemetry is sent to the author. Local plaintext SQLite stores hold expiring inbox content and retained dedupe/tombstone identifiers; owner-only OS access is required and not automatically audited. Messages are primarily Korean; no physical macOS/another user's GUI/every newer core compatibility guarantee.

**SDK initialization limit, also in README/SECURITY/setup docs and known_issues:** if the host cannot attach even the reject-only guard, the bridge refuses readiness and grants no bridge approval authority, but the native host can continue ordinary Telegram input, including old-card text. Users should use Desktop during initialization/receiver failure and recover Gateway normally. This package is not a whole-platform input firewall. The owner explicitly accepted this existing-public-SDK scope rather than requesting SDK development. Retain the real failure characterization; old NO-GO/RED evidence is not rewritten.

## Actual v1.8.0 evidence and explicit limits

- Exact released source `4874276f519f68fdbacb9767f70c5ed760b5c6fb`, independent Heavy source GO C0/H0/M0/L0 under the retained public-SDK scope. The release tag is unchanged.
- Python214/Node149, actual native React DOM6; exact-source Windows/Ubuntu GitHub CI runs 38383537489 and 38384937442 completed successfully. These are source-package CI, not this upstream catalog PR's approval.
- This catalog update extracted all34 committed package files and verified each Git blob. The current official catalog entry parser and `validate_plugin_dir` admission API passed with zero warnings: isolated register/capability probe, safe scanner, valid dependency declarations, no core override and supported Desktop surface. No dependencies were installed and no production configuration/state was modified by this check. Upstream's own normal dependency/security gates still apply.
- The author v1.8.0 native install/Doctor/read-only settings and receiver heartbeat were separately verified with config/auth preserved. Actual installed GUI interaction and a human Telegram reply/approval click roundtrip remain unverified; heartbeat is not message delivery.
- Anonymous fresh installation, full-history audit and PM dependency-resolution evidence from the previous v1.7.0 submission remain historical, not new v1.8.0 execution. The previous strict lazy-disabled `--install-deps` preparation refusal remains a retained failure; this update does not claim to rerun or cure it, and it does not weaken scanner/CAS/lease policy.
- Real historical rollback, native PTB dispatcher, managed/raw/effective-policy, Unicode/frame/claim and authorization regressions remain in the package suites. New module revocation/re-enable tests cover independent store cleanup, late-card epoch rejection and final dispatch/notification boundaries.

Immutable source docs were written pre-release; `readme:false` avoids presenting that frozen preparation status as current listing status. `docs_url` points to current public setup guidance; it does not control what installs. Source/release is public, but admission/search/production activation are not claimed. Please approve fork workflow execution and review the pinned source. This PR changes only one catalog file.

prs.title: fix(kanban): per-board counts survive a worker env pin
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`hermes kanban boards list` run inside a dispatcher-spawned worker (any session with `HERMES_KANBAN_DB` plus the `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` fence) printed the pinned board's task counts on **every** row, and `count_running_tasks_other_boards()` always returned 0: each enumerated slug resolved through `kanban_db_path()`, where the env pin — and, post-#131913, the worker fence — beats the explicit `board=` argument. The bundled dashboard's board list feeds off the same shape.

This PR keeps the fence for routing and writes exactly as-is and gives the three **read-side enumerators** a dedicated resolver, `kanban_db_connect.unpinned_db_path()`, which returns each board's own `kanban.db` regardless of pins:

- `hermes_cli/kanban_boards.py::_board_task_counts` — the `boards list` rows
- `plugins/kanban/dashboard/plugin_api.py::_board_counts` — the dashboard board list
- `hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py::count_running_tasks_other_boards` — host-wide running totals (its own docstring already documented the pin collapsing it to 0)

The enumerator's question is "what does each board hold?", which the pin answers with one board's numbers — a board with open cards can even render as `(empty)`. Enumeration now reads each board's own file and hands it to `connect(db_path=...)`, which already bypasses pin resolution. Notifier/watcher machine flows inside `pin_first_board_resolution()` are untouched, and single-board operations still resolve through the pin, so worker fencing is unchanged.

## Related Issue

Fixes #108401

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/kanban_db_connect.py`: add `unpinned_db_path(board=None)` — each board's own `kanban.db` ignoring env pins/fences, for read-side enumeration only
- `hermes_cli/kanban_boards.py`: `_board_task_counts` resolves and connects via the unpinned path
- `plugins/kanban/dashboard/plugin_api.py`: `_board_counts` ditto
- `hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py`: `count_running_tasks_other_boards` resolves both the excluded board and every enumerated board via the unpinned path (the exclusion previously compared pin-resolved paths), and its docstring no longer documents the yield-0 behaviour
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_board_path_priority.py`: fenced-worker regression coverage — two seeded boards with distinct contents keep per-board counts and a correct cross-board total under the pin

## How to Test

1. `python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_board_path_priority.py -q` → Observed result: 18 passed (4 new fence tests; the pre-fix code fails them by printing the pinned board's counts on every row)
2. `python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_boards.py tests/plugins/test_kanban_dashboard_plugin.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_host_cap.py -q` → Observed result: 77 passed
3. Manual probe of the issue's shape: with `HERMES_KANBAN_DB` and `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` set, `_board_task_counts("default")` / `_board_task_counts("proj-b")` return each board's own `{"done": 2}` / `{"running": 1}` instead of two copies of the pinned board's counts, and `count_running_tasks_other_boards("default")` returns 1 instead of 0.

prs.title: fix(dashboard): remove avoidable waits before chat startup
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Start the built-in dashboard chat without waiting for unrelated plugin bundles, a roughly 300 ms Suspense retry, or the sidebar RPC WebSocket to connect ahead of the terminal.

```diff
 /chat
   fetch plugin manifests
-  wait for unrelated plugin bundles
+  release the chat gate once a chat override is ruled out
   import ChatPage on demand
-  wait for the Suspense retry
+  mount the resolved component
-  connect sidebar RPC → events → PTY
+  connect events → PTY → sidebar RPC
```

## Related Issue

Fixes #140828

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix / performance improvement

## Changes Made

- Apply the existing manifest decision to fresh responses as well as cached ones.
- Resolve ChatPage inside the persistent host before rendering it. Import errors still propagate during rendering; late resolution after unmount is ignored.
- Delay only the sidebar's first RPC connection for each channel until the PTY opens or exhausts its initial retries. Its subsequent retries remain independent.
- Reset old sidebar status/info when the channel or profile changes and ignore an open callback after PTY cleanup.
- Reuse the same sidebar element in the two responsive layouts and remove duplicate reconnect-timer cleanup.
- Update existing sidebar test renders for the required readiness prop. No new tests or fixtures.

TUI startup order is unchanged. An isolated catalog-order experiment was excluded because it did not produce a consistent gain in the complete browser path.

## Evidence

Real browser measurements on a v0.22.2 deployment with equivalent frontend backports:

| Measurement | Before the corresponding change | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Manifest response → ChatPage request | 406 / 730 ms | 2 / 2 / 2 ms |
| ChatPage request → first WS-ticket request | about 300 ms | 19 / 20 / 22 ms |
| PTY handshake completion, connection-order comparison | 842 / 940 ms | 703 / 688 ms |
| Navigation → first PTY ready frame, connection-order comparison | 1.833 / 1.943 s | 1.668 / 1.657 s |

Final verification after closing temporary test terminals measured 1.609 / 1.467 s. Changed-asset downloads and accumulated test processes also produced slower samples, up to 2.55 s during this follow-up. These are small observed samples, not a performance guarantee.

The main-based branch was built and checked separately. These timings come from the stable backport; the current main backend was not deployed.

Live checks confirmed saved-history recovery, reload with the sidebar connected, plugin rendering, persistent normal-tab navigation, and no ChatPage/PTY load when opening `/sessions` directly. All 37 pre-existing session rows and 1,438 message rows were preserved exactly. Config files and account/provider identity were preserved; ordinary OAuth token refresh continued.

## How to Test

1. Open a fresh authenticated chat with non-chat-override plugins and inspect the manifest, module and WebSocket timings.
2. Navigate away and back, reload, and reopen a saved conversation.
3. Open `/sessions` directly and confirm it creates no ChatPage/PTY connection.
4. Check the existing PTY retry-exhaustion path: the sidebar must remain able to connect.

Validation:
- Official web build and typecheck passed on main and stable backport.
- Final targeted main run: 53 existing ChatSidebar/ChatPage/accessibility cases passed. Earlier plugin/registry/chat-activation checks also passed.
- Full web ESLint: zero errors; 28 existing warnings.
- `scripts/check --base HEAD`: 12 checks passed on both worktrees, with zero blocking/advisory findings. The final web files are unchanged from that checked version.
- Independent review and `git diff --check` passed.

The full Python suite was not run for this frontend-only patch.

## Merge Danger

Reversible frontend changes limited to chat startup. Plugin overrides still control mounting; the event subscriber stays ahead of the terminal and initial PTY failure releases the sidebar. No configuration keys, migrations, authentication protocol changes or session-data writes are introduced.

prs.title: Failed provider calls name the provider request id on the failure line and log (port goose#12587)
prs.body:
Failed provider calls now name the provider's request id on the failure line and in the log, so a support ticket to OpenAI, Anthropic or AWS can cite the exact request.

Port of [aaif-goose/goose#12587](https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/pull/12587) ("surface provider x-request-id on responses and errors").

## Changes
- `agent/api_error_summary.py::provider_request_id` walks the exception chain: SDK `.request_id` (openai sets it from `x-request-id`), then the httpx response headers (`request-id` for Anthropic, `x-request-id`), then botocore `ResponseMetadata.RequestId` (Bedrock). Capped at 128 chars.
- `agent/turn_recovery.py` appends ` (provider request id: <id>)` to the terminal failure status lines (non-retryable, billing, rate-limited, retries exhausted) and to the per-attempt / exhausted log lines.
- The id stays **out** of `_summarize_api_error` on purpose: that summary is persisted, shown in `final_response`, and hashed by cron incident signing (`cron/incidents.py::_error_signature`). A per-request id there would mint a new incident on every failure of one outage. Goose folds the id into the error message itself; we keep it beside it.

## Validation

**Live repro** (real `hermes chat -q`, real OpenAI endpoint, invalid key, scratch `HOME`/`HERMES_HOME`):

| tree | failure line |
|---|---|
| `origin/main` | `❌ custom rejected the request and retrying won't help: HTTP 401: Incorrect API key provided: sk-inval…robe. …` |
| this branch | `… https://platform.openai.com/account/api-keys. (provider request id: req_054d6d135f1e4b84a72043528bd765a0)` |

`agent.log` on the branch: `API call failed (attempt 1/3, not retryable) … summary=HTTP 401: … (provider request id: req_054d…)`. Header names verified live: api.openai.com → `x-request-id`, api.anthropic.com → `request-id`.

- New test `test_provider_request_id_reaches_failure_line_but_not_summary` (both header spellings, exception-chain walk, no-id case, id absent from the summary). Red on `origin/main`.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` over the turn-recovery / summarize-api-error files + `tests/cron/`: 1540 passed, 0 failed.
- Not covered live: Anthropic native and Bedrock wires (header/metadata shapes read from vendor responses and the SDK source, exercised by the unit test only).

prs.title: CLI and TUI report idle/working/blocked/done/error to the terminal over OSC 7501 (salvage #138152, port goose#12928)
prs.body:
Interactive Hermes (classic CLI **and** `hermes --tui`) now reports its state over OSC 7501, so terminals that track the Program Status Protocol show which tab is working, waiting on an approval/question/credential, finished, or failed, without parsing output.

Salvage of #138152 by @KoNit-K (commit cherry-picked, authorship intact; fork CI never dispatched there), plus hardening. Fixes #138147. Upstream parallel: [aaif-goose/goose#12928](https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/pull/12928). Spec: [Program Status Protocol (OSC 7501)](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/build/program-status).

## Changes
**From #138152 (@KoNit-K):** `hermes_cli/terminal_notify.py::program_status_sequence` encoder (`app=hermes`, ST-terminated, base64 `msg` capped at 2048 bytes); classic CLI reports `idle` at the prompt, `working` on submit, `blocked:kind=permission|question|auth` on approval / clarify / sudo / secret / vault / connect prompts (`working` again once answered), `done` / `error` at turn end, `idle` on cancel. Only on an interactive stdout.

**Hardening (this PR):**
- **Ink TUI parity.** `ui-tui/src/app/useProgramStatus.ts` derives the state from stores every path already updates (busy, the prompt overlays, a turn outcome recorded in `turnController`), so no answer path has to remember to report. A 150 ms settle absorbs the busy flicker between submit and `message.start` that otherwise flashed `working → idle → working` on every turn (seen in the first live run).
- **Spec-safe `msg`.** The spec drops a whole report whose decoded text holds C0, DEL **or C1** controls; C1 (U+0080–U+009F) passed the old strip. Controls now collapse to one space (same on both surfaces).
- **Config:** `display.program_status` (default `true`) beside `bell_on_complete` / `bell_on_prompt` instead of `terminal.program_status`: it is a display preference and the TUI config sync already reads `display.*`. Documented in `configuration.md`.
- **One owner on the classic CLI.** The first cut had per-prompt `blocked`/`working` calls, which missed transitions: the save-login password step stayed `working`, and connection phase changes never updated the tab. `CLIChatTurnMixin._sync_program_status` now reports what the screen shows (blocking prompt, else running turn, else last outcome). It runs from `_paint_now`, which every modal open/close/phase change already calls, plus the turn boundaries. `cli_modal_mixin.py` and `callbacks.py` are unchanged vs main.
- Edge states (review findings): a connection card is `blocked` only while it waits on the user, not while the backend works. A setup failure or early return in `chat()` drops back to idle. A missing turn result claims no outcome. A backend-reported interrupt (voice barge-in) reads `idle`. The TUI outcome clears on session reset. The TUI writes nothing until the first successful config read, and a failed read keeps the last known opt-out.

## Validation

**Live PTY repro**: real interactive `hermes chat` (and `hermes chat --tui --dev`) in a scratch HOME, real gateway, loopback scripted LLM. Turn 1 = `rm -rf <scratch dir>` under `approvals.mode: manual`, approved; turn 2 = plain reply. Every OSC 7501 report on the PTY decoded:

| leg | reports (consecutive duplicates collapsed) |
|---|---|
| `origin/main` CLI | none (0) |
| `origin/main` TUI | none (0) |
| branch CLI | `idle → working → blocked:permission ("rm -rf …") → working → done ("all gone") → working → done ("hello there")` |
| branch TUI | `idle → working → blocked:permission → working → done → working → done` |
| branch CLI, `display.program_status: false` | none (0) |

- `scripts/run_tests.sh` over every test touching the CLI turn/modal/secret paths + `tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_*` + config: 1309 passed, 0 failed. ui-tui: `vitest run` 1827 passed; `tsc --noEmit` clean; eslint clean on touched files.
- New: `ui-tui/src/__tests__/programStatus.test.ts` (encoder parity + C1 strip; prompt > busy > outcome; connection phase; backend interrupt). Python: `test_program_status_follows_the_screen_through_one_owner`, `test_display_program_status_false_from_config_writes_nothing` (both red at the first-cut head). Live legs re-run after the restructure: same sequence; TUI opt-out leg 0 reports too.
- Not covered live: a terminal that actually renders 7501 (verified at the byte level on the PTY instead).

## Infographic

![osc7501-program-status](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aaed0ba/o4FaA9ZwyxC3EqNDE9-MF_VXgjuRcv.png)

prs.title: feat(web): add DuckDuckGo Instant Answer API search provider (HER-52)
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds a new bundled web-search provider plugin — **DuckDuckGo Instant Answer API** — for free, no-key, no-rate-limit, no-extra-deps web search.

- **Endpoint**: `https://api.duckduckgo.com/?q=…&format=json` (no API key, no documented rate limit)
- **Implementation**: stdlib-only (`urllib.request` + `json`) — no new dependencies, distinct from the existing `ddgs` provider (which HTML-scrapes via the optional `ddgs` package)
- **Provider name**: `ddg-instant` (added to `web.search_backend` / `web.backend` options)
- **Result shape**: legacy contract `{success, data: {web: [{title, url, description, position}, …]}}`

## Why

HER-52 / Gold #11 (free-apis-corpus). Free web search for subagents — replaces some OpenAI browse calls at zero cost.

## Coverage caveat (documented in the plugin docstring)

DDG Instant Answer is a **knowledge-base endpoint**, not a full search index. It returns results for factual/entity queries (`linux`, `python`, `tokyo`) and is sparse for how-to/tutorial queries (`python async tutorial`). For sparse responses the plugin returns an instructive `search_fail` message pointing the caller at a full-text backend (`ddgs`, `brave`, `tavily`, `exa`) instead of silently returning `[]`.

## Files added

- `plugins/web/ddg_instant/__init__.py` — plugin entrypoint with `register(ctx)`
- `plugins/web/ddg_instant/plugin.yaml` — plugin manifest (`kind: backend`, `provides_web_providers: [ddg-instant]`)
- `plugins/web/ddg_instant/provider.py` — `DDGInstantWebSearchProvider` (urllib + json, no httpx import in this file)
- `tests/tools/test_web_providers_ddg_instant.py` — 12-test unittest (stdlib-only, runs with `python3 -m unittest tests.tools.test_web_providers_ddg_instant`)

## Files modified

- `tests/tools/conftest.py` — added `DDGInstantWebSearchProvider` to `register_all_web_providers` so it appears in tests that populate the registry

## Tests

```
$ python3 -m unittest tests.tools.test_web_providers_ddg_instant -v
… 12 tests … 
Ran 12 tests in 0.120s
OK
```

Includes a live network smoke test against `api.duckduckgo.com` that confirms the real shape:
- 1 abstract (`Wikipedia | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linux`)
- N RelatedTopics flattened from the nested `Topics` array

## Out of scope (per AGENTS.md standing rule)

- No edits to `/opt/hermes/` core config or root manifests
- No new runtime dependencies
- Shipped as a self-contained plugin directory + 1 conftest wiring line

prs.title: feat(cli): add explicit single-query cache scope
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds an explicit `hermes chat --cache-scope NAME` option for fresh single-query calls. Applications that start a new Hermes process for each request can give otherwise-stable instruction/tool prefixes a consistent cache-routing scope without resuming a conversation.

```bash
hermes chat -Q --provider openai-codex --cache-scope article-drafts --query-file prompt.txt
```

The opt-in scope is hashed together with the canonical profile home and working directory. It feeds the existing content-addressed cache key; on the Codex backend it also supplies the `session_id` affinity header. Instructions and tool schemas still participate in the key. The physical session ID, transcript persistence, gateway session key, and memory-provider session mapping are not replaced.

No flag means the existing per-conversation behavior. Interactive/TUI and resumed sessions reject the flag. This is a routing capability, not a guarantee of cache hits or a measured latency improvement.

## Related Issue

Related to #136359: implements the CLI slice. ACP support and the proposed `HERMES_CACHE_SCOPE` environment variable are intentionally out of scope; non-secret behavior uses the CLI option in accordance with the current contribution rules.

Duplicate search: no PR directly referencing #136359 was found before submission. #135783 is related but proposes an xAI-specific profile-wide setting; this PR adds a per-invocation, profile/workspace-namespaced CLI option and Codex affinity wiring. #129704 only publishes existing cache-key helper names. Neither supplies this CLI feature.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/cli_cache_scope.py`: label validation, fresh-query guards, profile/workspace hashing, and binding to the parent CLI agent.
- `hermes_cli/_parser.py`, `hermes_cli/main.py`, `cli.py`, `hermes_cli/cli_agent_setup_mixin.py`: argument propagation through the real CLI initialization path, without a persistent config key.
- `agent/prompt_cache_scope.py`, `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py`, `agent/transports/codex.py`: reuse the existing key derivation and optionally route the Codex header through the explicit scope.
- Two new test files and `website/docs/user-guide/cli.md`: isolation contracts and usage/limitations.

## How to Test

1. Run the focused regression files with the canonical runner:

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_cache_scope.py \
  tests/agent/test_cli_prompt_cache_scope.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_argparse_flag_propagation.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_chat_query_file.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_init.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_single_query_plugin_cli_ref.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_single_query_exit_contract.py \
```

prs.title: fix(telegram): ignore edited messages to prevent admission_conflict crash
prs.body:
## Problem Description
Fixes #140845.
Replaces and rebases stale PR #81183 on latest `main`.

When a user edits an already-sent message on Telegram, `python-telegram-bot` (PTB) emits an `update.edited_message` with the original `message_id`. Because `_effective_update_message()` returned `update.effective_message` without checking whether it was an edit, `_handle_text_message()` dispatched the edit as a new turn.

With the unified session authority ledger (#134889), Hermes generates the admission request key from `message_id`:
```python
request_id = str(payload['native_text_v1']['event']['message_id'] or uuid.uuid4().hex)
```
When `hermes_state_runtime.py` checks `session_admissions` for `request_id`, it finds the completed record from the original message. Because the payload digest has changed, SQLite raises an unhandled `RuntimeStoreError('admission_conflict')`:
```text
Sorry, I encountered an error (RuntimeStoreError).
admission_conflict
Try again or use /reset to start a fresh session.
```

In contrast, Discord explicitly suppresses re-dispatching edits (`# of the unedited message and never re-dispatches on edit` in `plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py`).

## Solution
1. In `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py`:
   Update `_effective_update_message` to return `None` when `update.edited_message` or `update.edited_channel_post` is present.
   This prevents edits from re-dispatching as conversational turns while keeping the `message_edited` platform hook observer (`group=99`) fully functional.
2. In `tests/gateway/test_telegram_channel_posts.py`:
   Added `test_effective_update_message_ignores_edits` regression coverage verifying that `edited_message` and `edited_channel_post` updates return `None`, while normal `message` and `channel_post` updates are accepted.

## Test Plan
- [x] Verified unit test `test_effective_update_message_ignores_edits` passes locally
- [x] Verified against live Telegram bot instance: editing past messages no longer triggers `admission_conflict`
- [x] Normal text messages and channel posts continue to work without regression

prs.title: fix(vision): image_input_mode native keeps its pixels at the send layer
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

With `agent.image_input_mode: native`, inbound routing (`decide_image_input_mode`) attaches `image_url` parts on the config setting alone, on every surface (CLI, gateway, TUI, Desktop, delegation). The send-layer guard in `agent/vision_message_prep.py` then asked only the capability lookup. For a model the catalog does not know, that lookup returns None, so the guard treated the model as text-only and:

- replaced each user image with an auxiliary description in `_prepare_messages_for_non_vision_model`; with no auxiliary vision backend that description is "Image analysis failed.", so the image was silently dropped;
- sent a native `vision_analyze` result through `_tool_result_content_for_active_model` as its text summary, which tells the model the image is attached natively and to answer with built-in vision, while the pixels are gone.

`_model_supports_vision` now returns True when `agent.image_input_mode` is explicitly `native` (normalized with the existing `_coerce_mode`), before the capability lookup, and reuses the same loaded config for the lookup otherwise. Both send-layer paths go through this one gate. This matches `website/docs/user-guide/features/vision.md`, which says `native` means "Always attach pixels, even when the catalog says the model is text-only." A provider rejection and the existing shrink/strip retries stay the recovery path.

Repro on main (real routing, unknown custom model, no auxiliary vision backend):

```
routing mode: native
wire content: "[The user attached an image. Here's what it contains:\nImage analysis failed.]\n\nwhat is this?"
aux describer calls: 1
vision_analyze native fast path: True
tool message content the model gets: "Image attached natively for the main model (1.2 KB). Answer using built-in vision."
```

With the fix both keep the `image_url` part and the describer is called 0 times.

### Compared with #83676

- #83676 (@astraltrekkin, Noa) fixes the user-image half of the same bug, but it is stranded: it edits methods in `run_agent.py` that have since moved to `agent/vision_message_prep.py`, so it no longer applies to main.
- It patches the two `_prepare_*` functions only and leaves the tool-result lane (`_tool_result_content_for_active_model`) alone, so a native `vision_analyze` result would still lose its pixels.
- This PR applies the same rule at the one gate both lanes share.
- #83676's 4 `TestNativeImageInputModePreservation` tests pass on this branch unchanged; its 2 native-mode tests fail on main.
- Noa is credited with `Co-authored-by` on the commit.

prs.title: fix(agent): read /models pricing aliases only from scalar values
prs.body:
## Problem

An OpenAI-compatible gateway's `/v1/models` payload can carry keys whose values are lists or dicts (magpie publishes `"modalities": {"input": ["text", "image"]}`). `_extract_pricing` guarded each pricing alias with a **set membership** test:

```python
if alias in normalized and normalized[alias] not in {None, ""}:
```

`value not in {None, ""}` hashes the value, so a list/dict under any key the pricing walk reads raises `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'`. `_extract_pricing` is called for **every** entry from `_parse_models_payload`, and that parse runs inside `fetch_endpoint_model_metadata`'s per-candidate `try`. One such key therefore aborted the whole catalog parse, the empty mapping was read as a probe failure, and the user-visible result was exactly what #137991 reports: context length falls back to 256K, compression fires ~3x too often on a 1M-window model, and the picker discovers zero models from the provider. The only trace was a debug-level log line, so nothing pointed at the cause.

## Fix

Guard on the value's **type** instead of set membership, keeping the original `None` / empty-string exclusion:

```python
if isinstance(value := normalized.get(alias), (int, float, str)) and value != "":
```

A quoted `0` (free model) is still a rate — the guard narrows what counts as one, it does not disable the alias walk. The change is line-neutral: `agent/model_metadata.py` sits at its `FILE_LINES` cap, so the added line pays for itself (`git diff` is 2 insertions / 2 deletions in the module).

## Tests

New file `tests/agent/test_model_metadata_endpoint_parse.py` (the existing `tests/agent/test_model_metadata.py` is at its own cap):

- `test_parse_models_payload_survives_list_valued_entry_keys` — the reporter's payload shape end-to-end through `_parse_models_payload`: the model survives with `context_length == 1_000_000` and its per-token pricing intact.
- `test_extract_pricing_ignores_non_scalar_values` — a list and a dict under pricing aliases are skipped instead of raising, while a scalar under the same key is still read.
- `test_extract_pricing_keeps_zero_rates` — control: the old behaviour for a quoted `0` is preserved.

Sabotage evidence (tests written first, source reverted with `git stash push -- agent/model_metadata.py`):

```
FAILED test_parse_models_payload_survives_list_valued_entry_keys
FAILED test_extract_pricing_ignores_non_scalar_values
  E   TypeError: cannot use 'list' as a set element (unhashable type: 'list')
=== Summary: 1 files, 1 tests passed, 2 failed ===
```

With the fix, the same three tests plus the neighbouring metadata/pricing suites:

```
tests/agent/test_model_metadata_endpoint_parse.py + 7 related files
  (model_metadata, model_metadata_cache, model_metadata_http, model_metadata_local_ctx,
   probe_cache_followups, usage_pricing, local_probe_disk_cache)
=== Summary: 8 files, 244 tests passed, 0 failed ===
python scripts/check --base upstream/main
=== code health: 2 files vs ccc6956350: 0 blocking, 0 advisory ===
scripts/check: 12 checks, ok
```

## Not done

- **Per-entry containment** in `_parse_models_payload` (one unparsable entry must cost that model, not the catalog). It is the right follow-up for the "silently swallowed" half of the report, but it cannot be added without blowing the file's `FILE_LINES` cap; the reviewed remedy — moving a function out to a topical sibling module — is a larger refactor than this bug fix should carry.
- No change to `_normalize_token_rates` / `usage_pricing`: with non-scalar values filtered out here, they never see one from this path.

## Relation to existing PRs

- #137990 (open, 8 lines, no tests, not cross-linked to this issue) makes the same guard change. This PR covers the same root cause **and** adds the regression tests, the zero-rate control, and the reproduction of the reported end-to-end symptom; either fixes #137991.
- #96275 (open since 2026-08-27, conflicting, from #96138) also touches `_extract_pricing` as part of a broader "preserve gateway-advertised context windows" change. This PR is deliberately the minimal slice of that behaviour that the crash in #137991 needs.

Closes #137991

prs.title: fix(skills_sync): do not seed a category DESCRIPTION.md into a category the profile does not hold
prs.body:
On a profile opted out of bundled skills (`.no-bundled-skills`), only the
essential skills are considered, and the sole essential (`hermes-agent`) lives
under the `autonomous-ai-agents` category. When that skill is not materialised
locally — it is already in `.bundled_manifest` with no copy on disk, or it is
deferred to an external dir — the skill loop writes nothing for it, yet
`_seed_category_descriptions` still created the category dir unconditionally to
hold the bundled `DESCRIPTION.md`.

That leaves a stray top-level REAL directory in the lane's skills root —
`skills/autonomous-ai-agents/` containing nothing but `DESCRIPTION.md` — which
a lane drift/sync check reads as an extra real dir. Deleting it is not a fix:
the next sync (any lane session touching the profile) puts it straight back.

## Change

Gate the seed on the category dir already existing. The function runs *after*
the skill loop, so the parent dir exists iff the profile actually received a
member of that category:

```python
        if (only_dirs is not None and dest_desc.parent not in only_dirs) or dest_desc.exists():
            continue
        # Only seed into a category the profile actually holds. ...
        if not dest_desc.parent.is_dir():
            continue
        try:
            dest_desc.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
```

No member ⇒ no description ⇒ no stray dir. A category that *does* hold a
materialised skill still gets its `DESCRIPTION.md` re-seeded.

## Verification

- `py_compile` clean; `tests/tools/test_skills_sync.py` and
  `tests/tools/test_skills_runtime_cache.py`: 54 passed before and 54 passed
  after the change.
- On opted-out lanes (essential in the manifest with no copy on disk,
  `ABSENT → REALDIR['DESCRIPTION.md']` before), the patched writer leaves the
  category dir absent.
- Regression: a lane whose category dir *does* hold a materialised
  `hermes-agent` but whose `DESCRIPTION.md` was removed gets it re-seeded
  byte-identically to the bundled file.

Reproduced and diagnosed on macOS 26.5 (Hermes host install); no platform-
specific behaviour involved.

prs.title: chore(plugin-catalog): update Magi to v1.7.8
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Update the existing **Magi** community plugin catalog listing from **1.7.3** (`f849295b63a8af55b7130467167b3b6dcc19be8a`) to **1.7.8**, pinned to the corrected, published commit **[`3f1a38c1804b12080a329a41fc2cc257f1af151a`](https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/magi/commit/3f1a38c1804b12080a329a41fc2cc257f1af151a)**. The catalog pin (not the release tag) is the exact source revision under review.

Magi provides Hermes Desktop interfaces for pending-memory review and stored `MEMORY.md` / `USER.md` management, including explicitly approved AI compaction. This remains a **catalog metadata/SHA-only** PR: no Hermes core or plugin source files are changed in this PR.

## Maintainer review addressed

In [review #5557895958](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/140369#pullrequestreview-5557895958), the maintainer identified a catalog rule 9 violation at the previous Magi pin: `_apply_compaction_batch` temporarily rebound the private `MemoryStore._mutate` to perform an in-lock fingerprint check, coupling Magi to `skip_drift`.

**Fixed in [Magi `9327744`](https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/magi/commit/93277443fff21d4b97355d833cd544b5e2d25947):** the Desktop apply route retains its initial fingerprint/budget/input validation and exact `matched_entry` removal pins, then calls **`store.apply_batch(target, operations)` directly**. It does not call, wrap, rebind, or depend on the signature of private `_mutate`. The existing Memory/User routes, pending-write review, compaction preview, UI and plugin registrations remain unchanged.

The [1.7.8 changelog and locked POLIS V6 contract](https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/magi/commit/030df6ebd87b0c001b35a638fe51c2710ac15c7e) record the fix; the [subsequent compatibility note](https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/magi/blob/3f1a38c1804b12080a329a41fc2cc257f1af151a/docs/hermes-memory-compatibility.md) documents observed concurrency boundaries and pre-existing issues. The Magi version remains **1.7.8**.

## Changes made in this PR

Only `plugin-catalog/magi.yaml` is modified:

- Set `sha: 3f1a38c1804b12080a329a41fc2cc257f1af151a`, including the public-API fix and subsequent documentation.
- Point both Pending writes and Stored memory screenshots at the **same immutable pin**.
- Keep `version: "1.7.8"`, `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.5"`, `name`, `repo`, `maintainer`, community/desktop classification, README and declared capabilities unchanged.

Follow-up catalog commit: [`580b4791206750e73a8714bbe68620af24e4b30d`](https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/hermes-agent/commit/580b4791206750e73a8714bbe68620af24e4b30d).

## Validation and test evidence

- **This catalog update:** `python scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py --json plugin-catalog/magi.yaml` → **PASS**, `ok: true`, zero warnings/errors; checked the Magi 1.7.8 manifest, both screenshot paths and exact published SHA; `git diff --check` clean.
- **Corrected Magi 1.7.8, first regression campaign:** complete suite **91/91 PASS**; **4,800/4,800** native stress scenarios and **200/200** multiprocess races PASS; POLIS workspace `test.complete` and `coverage` gates PASS; global line coverage **96.45%** (includes tests; the four main production files measured **91.49%**, so this is **not** a 95% production-only claim). Hermes plugin validator **15/15** checks PASS, with pre-existing private-import warnings and **no core-method override**.
- **Independent second campaign:** **2,000/2,000** deterministic interleavings (including simultaneous compactions); **540/540** high-contention multiprocess races with 8/16/24 writers, preserving **8,640** confirmed adds; **600/600** reorder/ABA/batch-order probes; **480/480** additional checks against the precise Hermes CI-pinned revision, plus **19/19** selected upstream Hermes tests; **180** instrumented persistence-fault cases and **120** further pre-rename SIGKILL runs passed. One earlier uninstrumented fault-injection pilot was inconclusive and is not asserted to be a fixed upstream or Magi bug.

The full Hermes core test/lint suite was **not** rerun for a catalog-only pin update. Checks that require upstream GitHub Actions authorization are **not claimed as passed**.

## Concurrency guarantees and residual limits

Hermes' public batch mechanism serializes cooperating writers, validates exact `matched_entry` removals under its lock and avoids partial batch writes. A removed/changed pinned entry causes a conflict; a concurrent **addition** can be preserved while compaction succeeds. Magi's **full source fingerprint is checked before** calling `apply_batch`, **not atomically under the batch lock**. Therefore source reordering and ABA (removal/reintroduction of identical pinned text) can pass: we **do not claim an atomic full-snapshot guarantee**. A public expected-snapshot precondition, and a monotonic revision or entry identity to detect identical-content ABA, would require upstream API support.

A separately reproduced, **pre-existing** Hermes entry-delimiter (`\n§\n`) serialization round-trip issue has a shared responsibility: general lossless storage needs an upstream change, while Magi could add local input rejection. It is **not** a new regression from replacing `_mutate` with `apply_batch`. See the [technical note](https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/magi/blob/3f1a38c1804b12080a329a41fc2cc257f1af151a/docs/hermes-memory-compatibility.md).

## Security and privacy disclosures (catalog rule 13)

- **Hermes surfaces:** native plugin registration, memory APIs and Desktop plugin SDK; no new catalog tools, hooks or middleware.
- **Local reads:** pending-memory records and `MEMORY.md` / `USER.md` for the active profile; optional `home_override` selects another home.
- **Writes:** user-initiated review decisions, add/edit/delete and AI compaction through Hermes memory APIs, with confirmations and the safeguards described above.
- **AI:** selected memory is sent via Hermes `ctx.llm` to the configured model/provider; provider credentials remain under Hermes control.
- **Other activity:** no Magi-initiated third-party HTTP calls, subprocesses, telemetry or long-lived background jobs; an open Desktop page polls the local backend.
- **Existing compatibility warning:** Hermes' validator notes pre-existing imports of private memory modules, but found no core-method rebinding/overrides.

## Screenshots

**Pending writes**

![Magi Pending writes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MarcosAlves90/magi/3f1a38c1804b12080a329a41fc2cc257f1af151a/docs/screenshots/pending-writes.png)

**Stored memory**

![Magi Stored memory](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MarcosAlves90/magi/3f1a38c1804b12080a329a41fc2cc257f1af151a/docs/screenshots/stored-memory.png)

prs.title: fix(gateway): answer messaging /kanban and /curator quote parse failures by name
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

On messaging platforms, `/kanban show it's` or `/curator it's` (any apostrophe or unclosed quote in the argument) crashed the handler with an uncaught `ValueError: No closing quotation`, and the user got a generic internal error instead of any command output. Both messaging handlers parsed the raw argument with `shlex.split` and no guard.

The bound-session classification path for the same bug class was already fixed on `main` (`226d854e8d`, Refs #134889 CMD-1 — `/skills`, `/kanban`, then `/memory` in `f2fe6f5ef3`); these two handlers are its messaging-side siblings. This PR gives them the same contract `/resume` already had (`gateway.resume.parse_error` since #18505): catch the `ValueError` and answer with a named parse-error reply that carries the cause and shows how to quote the argument.

For `/kanban` the refusal is also the semantically correct outcome: the underlying CLI (`hermes_cli/kanban.py::run_slash`) parses with shlex too and cannot run an unclosed quote either — exactly what `226d854e8d` established for the session side.

## Related Issue

Fixes #140803

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/slash_commands.py` — `_handle_kanban_command`: wrap the `shlex.split` verb scan in try/except, return `gateway.kanban.parse_error` on `ValueError` instead of letting it escape.
- `gateway/slash_commands.py` — `_handle_curator_command`: same guard around its `shlex.split`, returning `gateway.curator.parse_error`.
- `locales/*.yaml` (all 17 bundled languages) — new `gateway.kanban.parse_error` and `gateway.curator.parse_error` strings ("Could not parse … : {error}. Quotes must be paired — wrap text containing an apostrophe in double quotes, for example …"), placed alphabetically (`curator` between `compress` and `debug`).
- `tests/gateway/test_slash_quote_parse_errors.py` (new) — three regression tests: unclosed quote on each handler answers by name (the shlex cause rides the reply), and a paired quote still parses through to the CLI unchanged.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/gateway/test_slash_quote_parse_errors.py -v` — Observed result: 3 passed.
2. Red/green proof: with the two try/except guards reverted (main's code), the two unclosed-quote tests fail with `ValueError: No closing quotation` escaping the handler; with this PR they pass. The paired-quote test passes both ways, confirming it pins the parse layer, not the guard.
3. `pytest tests/gateway/test_session_memory_review.py` — Observed result: 17 passed, 1 skipped (the session-side CMD-1 fix's own suite, no regression).
4. `python -c "import yaml; ..."` — all 17 locale files parse and expose both new keys under `gateway:` (run as part of development; observed pass).
5. `ruff check gateway/slash_commands.py tests/gateway/test_slash_quote_parse_errors.py` — all checks passed.

Note: `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_notify.py` shows 14 failed / 13 passed in this environment, but the identical set fails on a clean checkout of `main` with no changes (the failures are the home-I/O test guard tripping on environment paths, not this diff).
