prs.title: fix(gateway): name the parse error when a messaging /kanban or /curator argument is unclosed
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`/kanban` and `/curator` on a messaging platform answer a named parse error when the argument contains an unclosed quote or a stray apostrophe, instead of dying with an uncaught `ValueError`.

Both handlers parsed the user's raw argument with `shlex.split` outside a `try`:

- `_handle_kanban_command` — `tokens = iter(shlex.split(text) if text else [])`
- `_handle_curator_command` — `tokens = shlex.split(event.get_command_args() or "") or ["status"]`

`/kanban show it's` raises `ValueError: No closing quotation` before anything runs, and neither the dispatch chain nor the handler catches it, so it escaped to the message loop's catch-all and the user got a generic internal error with no command output.

The bound-session side already classifies this input — `226d854e8d` for `/skills` and `/kanban`, `f2fe6f5ef3` for `/memory` — and `_handle_resume_command` (`gateway/slash_commands_session.py:1020`) answers `gateway.resume.parse_error` from its own `shlex.split`. These two handlers now do the same: the `ValueError` becomes a reply that names the problem and asks for quotes, so the messaging path matches the classification the session path settled on.

## Related Issue

Fixes #140803

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/slash_commands.py` — `_handle_kanban_command` and `_handle_curator_command` guard their `shlex.split` and return `gateway.kanban.parse_error` / `gateway.curator.parse_error` with the underlying error interpolated.
- `locales/*.yaml` — the two keys in every catalog (`en`, plus the 16 others that the parity test pins), so no locale falls back to English or breaks `test_catalog_keys_match_english`.
- `tests/gateway/test_slash_command_parse_errors.py` — one regression test per handler: the reply names the command and the error, and the underlying CLI is never reached.

## How to Test

1. Unit regression (fails on `main`, passes here):

```bash
uv run --group dev python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_slash_command_parse_errors.py -q
# 2 passed
```

Without the two guards the same file fails with the uncaught error:

```text
ValueError: No closing quotation
FAILED test_kanban_with_unclosed_quote_replies_with_a_parse_error
FAILED test_curator_with_unclosed_quote_replies_with_a_parse_error
2 failed
```

2. i18n parity and a neighbouring slash-command suite:

```bash
uv run --group dev python -m pytest tests/agent/test_i18n.py tests/gateway/test_restart_notification.py tests/gateway/test_slash_command_parse_errors.py -q
# 68 passed
```

3. Blocking checks:

```bash
uv run python scripts/check
# scripts/check: 12 checks, ok
```

4. On a live gateway, send `/kanban show it's` and `/curator it's` on any messaging platform: each answers `⚠ Could not parse ... arguments: No closing quotation ...` instead of the generic internal error.

issues.title: [Feature]能不能支持反向代理，可以支持使用nginx把服务挂载到比如/pico路径下面
issues.body:
## 🎯 The Goal / Use Case
希望在同一域名下通过 Nginx 反向代理，将 PicoClaw Web Console 挂载到 /pico/，而不是占用网站根路径。例如访问 https://example.com/pico/，且页面、登录、API、静态资源、聊天 WebSocket 和附件请求都保持在该前缀下。
当前前端与后端部分地址使用根路径（如 /api/...、/launcher-login、/pico/ws），仅在 Nginx 中配置路径转发无法完整支持这一场景。

## 💡 Proposed Solution
为 Web Launcher 增加可选启动参数 -base-path，例如 -base-path /pico。默认值为空，保持现有根路径部署行为。
配置后，应用使用该前缀生成浏览器可见的路由、资源、请求和重定向地址；Nginx 负责剥离外部前缀，再转发给现有后端路由。同一份前端构建产物应能兼容根路径和子路径部署。

## 🛠 Potential Implementation (Optional)

- 校验并规范化 -base-path，仅接受 URL 路径前缀。

- 在服务端返回的首页中提供运行时基础路径。

- 前端路由、API 请求、静态资源、登录跳转及 WebSocket 地址统一使用基础路径。

- 后端生成的重定向和 Pico WebSocket 地址包含外部前缀。

- 增加根路径兼容性和子路径部署的回归测试。

## 🚦 Impact & Roadmap Alignment
- [ ] This is a Core Feature
- [ ] This is a Nice-to-Have / Enhancement
- [ ] This aligns with the current Roadmap

## 🔄 Alternatives Considered
使用独立子域名：无需子路径支持，但不适合需要共享同一域名的部署环境。
仅在 Nginx 中添加根路径转发规则：可能占用 /api/、/assets/ 等路径，与同域其他应用冲突，也不能保证所有请求都位于 /pico/ 下。
构建时固定 /pico/：实现较简单，但不同部署路径需要分别构建前端，不如运行时配置灵活。

## 💬 Additional Context
示例部署地址：https://example.com/pico/。其中外部 /pico/pico/ws 对应后端内部 /pico/ws：前一个 /pico 是部署前缀，后一个 /pico 是现有接口路径。

prs.title: feat(agent): add wall-clock turn time budget
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds an optional **wall-clock budget per turn** (`agents.defaults.turn_time_budget_seconds`, `0` = disabled by default).

When a turn exceeds the budget, the agent is asked to **stop scheduling new tools and deliver a concise summary of the work done so far**, instead of looping until `max_tool_iterations` (or until the provider request times out).

## Motivation

A single turn can currently run for tens of minutes when the model keeps scheduling tool calls. In practice this manifests as:
- turns that hit the provider timeout and deliver **nothing** (empty final message), or
- turns that burn the full iteration cap with no useful output.

The existing `max_tool_iterations` is a *count* valve, not a *time* valve: a handful of slow tool calls can blow well past any reasonable wall-clock limit long before the iteration cap is reached.

## Design

- New config: `agents.defaults.turn_time_budget_seconds` (`AgentDefaults.TurnTimeBudgetSeconds`, env `PICOCLAW_AGENTS_DEFAULTS_TURN_TIME_BUDGET_SECONDS`). `0` disables it (default → no behavior change).
- `AgentInstance.TurnTimeBudget` carries the duration into the turn loop.
- At the top of each iteration in `runTurn`, if `time.Since(startedAt) >= budget`, a **graceful interrupt** is requested with a hint telling the model to stop scheduling tools and summarize. This reuses the existing graceful-interrupt path, so the same iteration's `CallLLM` drops tools and returns a partial summary.
- Requested **at most once per turn** (`markBudgetStopRequested`), so it does not fire repeatedly.
- Emits `agent.interrupt.received` with `Kind: graceful` for observability.

## Files

- `pkg/config/config.go` — new field + docs.
- `pkg/agent/instance.go` — parse config into `TurnTimeBudget`.
- `pkg/agent/turn_coord.go` — budget check at iteration start.
- `pkg/agent/turn_state.go` — `budgetStopRequested` flag + `markBudgetStopRequested()`.
- `pkg/agent/turn_budget_test.go` — unit + integration tests.

## Tests

- `TestTurnState_MarkBudgetStopRequested` — dedupe (fires once).
- `TestRunTurn_TurnTimeBudgetTriggersGracefulStop` — a provider that always returns a tool call is stopped by the budget and the turn completes with a partial summary (instead of running to `MaxIterations`).

Verified locally:
- `go build ./pkg/agent/... ./pkg/config/... ./cmd/...` — OK
- `go vet ./pkg/agent/... ./pkg/config/...` — clean

prs.title: typing: follow the runner's turn state, show its status text, and clear when the turn ends
prs.body:
## What

The typing indicator now follows the runner's own turn state instead of guessing liveness from a heartbeat file, and it can carry a short status line the runner publishes.

- **Mailbox model.** `ContainerRecord` gains `turn: 'working' | 'idle' | null` (null = not reported). `container_state` gains a `turn` column. The runner adds the column on start behind a `PRAGMA table_info` guard; the host read tolerates a table that still lacks it.
- **Runner report.** The runner's SQLite mailbox gains `markContainerTurn(turn)`, which writes `turn` and stamps `updated_at` and leaves the tool-in-flight fields alone. The poll loop marks `working` when a turn starts, re-marks every 5s while it runs (so `updated_at` keeps moving through long generations), and marks `idle` when the turn ends and on clean loop exit. Every write is best-effort: a failure logs and never breaks the loop.
- **Delivery poll → presence.** The host reads `getContainerState()` and `getState('live_status')` on the same poll it already runs and hands one presence report (turn, its stamp, optional status text) to the typing module (`notePresence`). No new session, no new poll. The host mailbox contract gains an optional `getState(key)` read of the runner's generic `session_state` rows.
- **Typing module.** Tick rule, in order: inside the post-delivery pause skip; within the 15s grace since the last inbound refresh; a reported turn exists refresh while `working` and its stamp is within `TURN_STALE_MS` (three 5s re-marks) else end; no turn ever reported keep the heartbeat-file fallback. Ending a refresh clears the interval and fires the adapter's new optional `clearTyping` once.
- **Status text.** A runner may publish a short activity line under the `live_status` state key. While the turn is `working` and fresh, every refresh tick sends `setTyping` exactly as plain typing does and the text only changes the payload (`setTyping(..., text, 'agent')`), so the cadence is unchanged and channels that cannot show text keep their indicator alive as before. With no text, plain typing as before. Text is shown only once the runner is provably in this turn, so a line left over from an earlier turn is not shown during a cold-start grace window.
- **Clear verb.** `clearTyping` is added to the channel adapter contract, dispatched to the exact adapter instance by the registry, and implemented in the Chat SDK bridge: a Slack-shaped adapter (one exposing `setAssistantStatus` and `decodeThreadId`) is cleared with `setAssistantStatus(channel, threadTs, '')`; anything else is a no-op. The bridge's `setTyping` now passes the status line to `startTyping(threadId, status)`, normalized to one trimmed line and capped at 200 characters (neither the adapter nor the platform documents a limit).

## Why

Driving typing from a heartbeat file breaks in two ways:

1. **No shared filesystem.** Where the process that delivers messages does not share a filesystem with the runner (any remote or containerized runtime), the heartbeat file is never visible. The indicator then either dies at the end of the grace window or, if the deployment answers "fresh" by default, never stops.
2. **Indicators that outlive the turn.** On Slack, `setTyping` maps to `assistant.threads.setStatus`, which persists until a post in the thread, an explicit clear, or a two-minute timeout. A turn that ends without posting leaves the agent "typing" for two minutes after it finished, because the module never sent an explicit clear.

The runner is the one component that knows exactly when a turn starts and ends, and it already keeps a per-session record in the outbound mailbox that the host reads on every delivery poll. Typing should follow that. The same read path carries the runner's status line: the indicator is the natural place to show "what the agent is doing right now", and a channel-side reconstruction of turn boundaries from deliveries is unnecessary once the runner reports them directly.

## Compatibility

- **Older runners.** A runner that predates this change never writes `turn`, so its records parse with `turn: null` and the delivery poll reports "not reported". Those sessions keep the exact heartbeat-file behaviour they have today.
- **Older session DBs.** The `turn` column is added with a guarded `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` on the runner side; the host read uses `SELECT *` with per-field picks, so a `container_state` table that still lacks the column reads as `turn: null` rather than erroring. A `session_state` table that does not exist yet reads as no status.
- **Older persisted records.** `parseContainerRecord` treats a missing or null `turn` as null, so records written before the field existed still parse.
- **No status published.** Runners that never write `live_status`, and channels that cannot show text, get plain typing exactly as before.

## Tests

- **Model:** a reported turn parses; a record without the field reads as null; a turn outside the contract is rejected.
- **SQLite, both sides:** the host reads a `container_state` row written before the `turn` column existed; `markContainerTurn` moves only `turn` and `updated_at` and survives a tool starting mid-turn; `getState` reads a runner-written row with its stamp normalized and returns undefined for a missing key or a DB without `session_state`.
- **Runner poll loop:** a two-message turn stays `working` until the loop returns to waiting; a quiet turn that delivers nothing still ends `idle`.
- **Delivery poll:** the turn report is read on the poll and forwarded to the typing module; a `live_status` row rides along as the status (trimmed); a blank line reads as no status; a missing record forwards as null.
- **Typing module scenarios:** quiet turn (idle report, no delivery → refresh stops, exactly one clear); multi-message turn (two deliveries pause and resume, one clear at idle); dead runner (`working` stops advancing → clear after `TURN_STALE_MS`); old runner (no turn ever reported → heartbeat-file behaviour, existing tests keep passing).
- **Status text:** text present → sent with `statusKind: 'agent'` and no plain calls interleaved; unchanged text is re-sent on every tick; changed text shows on the next tick; after a post-delivery pause the next tick sends it again; no text → plain typing every tick; idle → one clear while text is showing; a stale line is not shown before the runner reports `working`.
- **Channels:** the registry dispatches `clearTyping` to the exact instance; the bridge passes a normalized status line to `startTyping` (whitespace collapsed, blank → none, over-long capped) and clears a Slack-shaped adapter with `setAssistantStatus(..., '')`, no-op when it cannot clear or the thread has no `threadTs`.

prs.body:
## Summary Lets an agent create another agent from a template, from this machine or the public library, instead of writing the persona by hand. - **Before**: `create_agent({ name, instructions })` only made a blank agent; templates were reachable only from a terminal (`ncl groups create --template`) or setup. - **Now**: `create_agent({ name, template: "sales/sdr" })`, plus `ncl templates list` (this machine, no network) and `ncl templates list --registry` (the public library's `index.json`) so the agent can offer one. - **Fetch**: a template not on this machine is shallow-cloned from `nanocoai/nanoclaw-templates` into `templates/` after the permission check and before any DB write. A local copy always wins. - **Approval**: same `agents.create` rule as today (`cli_scope: global` creates directly, anything else waits for an admin). The hold stores the template, the grant is bound to it, and the card says whether approving downloads it. - **Provider**: the child runs on its creator's provider, like a plain create. - **Slack**: the `slack-agent-flow` wrapper keeps the template through its own hold, names it in the success text, seeds the bot's avatar from the template's description and reports the ref to the provisioning service. - **Library content is data**: the clone runs with `core.symlinks=false` and Git LFS skipped; every copy goes through the hardened plugin copier with a real-path check, and a fetched template must parse before it becomes the local copy. - **Delivery stays responsive**: `ncl templates list --registry` runs inside the host's delivery loop, so the index (or its failure) is memoized for five minutes. - **Moved**: the library code setup used (`cloneRegistry`, `listTemplatesFromDir`, `copyTemplate`) moves from `setup/templates.ts` to `src/templates/library.ts`, so setup and agents share one copy. The precheck accepts only plain `/`-separated segments, so it cannot leave the templates directory; nothing is read or fetched before that check and the permission decision. - The library URL is fixed; nothing the agent typed is sent anywhere. - No new permission: a template create is still `agents.create`. prs.title: fix(discord): Approve clicks recorded as reject (custom_id value suffix not stripped)
prs.body:
## Problem

On Discord, every **Approve** click on an approval card is recorded as a **reject**. The card footer shows `0\n0 by <user>` instead of `✅ Approved by <user>`.

## Cause

`@chat-adapter/discord` encodes a button's `custom_id` as `<actionId>\n<value>` (`encodeDiscordCustomId`). The approval card's Approve button (`id: ncq:<approvalId>:0`, `value: '0'`) therefore arrives as `ncq:<approvalId>:0\n0`.

The raw `GATEWAY_INTERACTION_CREATE` handler in `handleForwardedEvent` takes everything after `ncq:<id>:` as the option index, gets `'0\n0'`, which fails the `/^\d+$/` check in `resolveSelectedOption`, and is passed on unchanged. `handleRegisteredApproval` treats any value other than `'approve'` as a rejection.

## Fix

Strip the adapter's `\n<value>` suffix before resolving the index (one line). Legacy custom_ids without the suffix (e.g. `ncq:q-1:approve`) are unaffected.

## Tests

- New regression test in `chat-sdk-bridge.test.ts` posts a Gateway click with `custom_id: 'ncq:q-index:0\n0'` and asserts `onAction(..., 'approve', ...)`.
- It fails without the fix and passes with it; the full file passes (38/38), `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- Verified on a live install: Approve on an `install_packages` card now approves and rebuilds the container.

## Summary

prs.title: feat(telegram): bot-to-bot admission gate (doorman) behind TELEGRAM_BOT_INBOUND
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 draft payload. Branch: feat/telegram-bot-admission, cut from the upstream/main tip. -->

## Summary

Stops other Telegram bots from waking a NanoClaw agent into unbounded reply loops once Bot-to-Bot Communication Mode is enabled.

- **Problem**: with BotFather B2B on, every other bot's group message reaches the gateway and engages like a human mention. The Chat SDK skips only self-messages, so two bots sharing a group wake each other endlessly, and unregistered bot senders flood the unknown-sender path (#3235).
- **Fix**: a bridge-level admission policy for `channelType: 'telegram'` (built on the `registerBridgeInboundPolicy` seam), gated by `TELEGRAM_BOT_INBOUND`. It admits bot-authored inbound only from an allowlisted channel (`chatId` means anywhere in that chat, `chatId:topic` means one forum topic) and only when the message is addressed: the text opens with `/command@<botname>` or `@<botname>`, or it replies to the bot's own message content (forum-topic anchor replies excluded). Mid-text quotes, in prose or code spans, do not address. A per-peer throttle allows one admitted turn per peer per 30 s, and every decision logs one line.
- **Out of scope**: the unknown-sender gate itself (#3446 covers it), per-wiring topic engagement, and an `/add-b2b-peer` setup skill (follow-up).

## Related work

- #3235: bot senders generate unbounded approval cards, and this policy complements the gate-layer fix. Traffic dropped at the bridge never reaches the sender gate. PR #3446 fixes the gate layer itself; the two compose and are merge-order independent (this PR's only bridge hunks are two optional `ReplyContext` fields). Its auto-drop denies at the gate; this policy prevents earlier with a positive allowlist.
- #3600 / #3601: adapter and router reply-to-bot mention semantics. This policy does not consume `isMention` for bot-authored messages; it derives addressing itself and stamps `isMention` on admits, so it is unaffected either way. A note for #3601: its proposed `isReplyToBot` (a username match) counts forum-topic anchor service messages as "reply to bot". The anchor exclusion this PR adds to `ReplyContext` (`replyToForumTopicAnchor`) is that finding, expressed as a field.
- No open issue asks for an admission policy directly; #3235 is the closest pain. This change is safe to review directly as defense-in-depth.

## Change kind

<!-- Check exactly one. -->
- [x] `kind/hardening`
- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`

Hardening rationale: CONTRIBUTING routes new capabilities to skills; this PR uses the hardening kind instead. It adds a missing admission boundary (loop containment against bot-authored traffic on a stock install), is dormant by default, and exposes no capability surface. If maintainers read it as a capability, the payload converts to a channels-branch skill delivery; only the two `ReplyContext` fields are core.

## Validation

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/telegram-bot-admission.test.ts` returns 27/27 on a fresh `upstream/main` worktree (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`), and `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` passes. The 27 tests cover every drop reason, both addressing legs, anchor exclusion, bare-chatId entries, per-peer throttle isolation, and real-bridge integration (an admitted reply reaches the host mention-stamped; the firehose never does; humans flow untouched).
- Live fire in a production two-bot deployment: 5 drops, 1 admit (a raw `/ping@bot`), and an agent reply after 9 s. The chain ended human-addressed. The peer agent found the anchor-overload bug during this test; we fixed and re-verified it.

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change, release note below
- [ ] Breaking change, release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Telegram: new opt-in bot-to-bot admission gate (TELEGRAM_BOT_INBOUND="chatId" or "chatId:topic"). Bot-authored messages are dropped unless they address the bot (start-anchored command or mention, or a reply to its messages) in an allowlisted channel. Per-peer 30 s throttle; every decision is logged. Inert unless set; human traffic is unaffected.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- Adds an admission boundary for untrusted bot-authored input. Only allowlisted channels pass. This policy derives addressing itself and does not trust the adapter's substring `isMention` for bots. Admitted messages are stamped and forwarded to the existing router gates unchanged.
- Gated channels are default-deny. Drops are silent in chat and each writes one audit line (reason, sender id, chat, topic) to the host log; admits log at INFO. No new credentials, egress, or runtime changes.
- Human-message handling is untouched on every path. Rollback is removing the env var and restarting; nothing registers without it.

## Skill delivery

- [x] Not a skill
- [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

This is the trunk hardening piece. The companion Telegram-adapter registration ships as a small patch on the `channels` branch, delivered through the channel-skill flow once the trunk change lands.

## AI assistance

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change
- [x] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

<!-- The attestation box above is deliberately unchecked. It is the operator's to tick after reviewing the diff (compare/files tab). Required by CONTRIBUTING regardless of the disclosure box. -->

<details>
<summary>Appendix: install DX, scaling, two-target split</summary>

**Install (post-merge)**

1. In BotFather, enable B2B for the bot pair and add both bots to the group.
2. Update NanoClaw. The policy ships inert.
3. Add `TELEGRAM_BOT_INBOUND="-1001234567"` (whole group) or `"-1001234567:42"` (topic only) to `.env`, then restart the host. To roll back, remove the line and restart.
4. Register the peer: `ncl members add --user telegram:<peerBotId> --group <agentGroupId>`.
5. The peer addresses the agent at message start (`/cmd@bot`) or by replying to the agent's messages. Every admission decision is auditable in the host log.

**Scaling**

Comma-separate env entries for more channels or topics, and run `ncl members add` for more peers. The throttle is per peer, so one chatty bot cannot starve the others.

**Two-target split**

Trunk ships channel-adapter infrastructure; the Telegram adapter lives on the `channels` branch. This PR (trunk) adds `src/channels/telegram-bot-admission.ts` with tests that compile standalone, plus the two optional `ReplyContext` fields. The `channels` branch gets a 66-line patch that exports and extends the adapter's `extractReplyContext` and registers the policy at module load (a no-op without the env var). Upstream `chat-sdk-bridge.ts` has moved past some forks; this PR's hunks touch only the `ReplyContext` interface and apply cleanly on the current tip.

</details>

prs.title: fix(agent-runner): set busy_timeout before journal_mode on outbound open
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops the first `outbound.db` open in a container process failing with `database is locked`.

- **Problem**: bun:sqlite starts with `busy_timeout` 0, and `getOutboundDb()` set it only after `PRAGMA journal_mode = DELETE`, the first schema read. If the runner, the MCP server or another `ncl` call held the write lock, the open threw `SQLITE_BUSY` at once and the cached connection kept `busy_timeout` 0. Each `ncl` call is a fresh process, so each one takes this path.
- **Fix**: set `busy_timeout` before `journal_mode`, as the inbound opens already do. `getOutboundDb()` takes an optional path so the test can use a temp file.
- **Out of scope**: an open that still fails after 5 s stays cached half set up. Host opens use better-sqlite3, which already defaults to a 5 s timeout.

Same fix as #3708 by @davekim917, closed unmerged; this version adds a test against the real function.

prs.title: fix: include /opt/homebrew/bin in launchd plist PATH
prs.body:
## Summary

The launchd plist generated in `setup/service.ts` hard-codes

```
PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:${homeDir}/.local/bin
```

On Apple Silicon Macs, Homebrew installs to `/opt/homebrew/bin` — both `brew install node` and Apple Container's `container` binary end up there by default. With the current PATH, an Apple-Silicon user who picks Apple Container as their container runtime sees the service crash immediately with "FATAL: Container runtime failed to start", because `ensureContainerRuntimeRunning()` can't find the `container` binary on launchd's PATH. `KeepAlive` loops the failure forever.

`npm run dev` works fine because the interactive shell gets `/opt/homebrew/bin` via `brew shellenv`. The bug only surfaces once launchd takes over.

## Change

Prepend `/opt/homebrew/bin` to the PATH in the generated plist. This is a no-op on Intel Macs (the directory usually doesn't exist) and fixes every Apple Silicon brew install.

Also updated `setup/service.test.ts` which maintains its own copy of the expected plist string.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run setup/service.test.ts` — all 10 tests pass
- [x] End-to-end: after applying, `container` resolves correctly from launchd on an Apple Silicon Mac with Homebrew Node + Homebrew Apple Container. Before: PID `-` with non-zero exit every 2s.

Closes #1935

prs.title: fix(discord): connect the Gateway through Node's env proxy
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Lets the Discord Gateway connect on hosts that reach the internet only through an HTTPS proxy.

- **Problem**: with `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` / `--use-env-proxy`, `fetch` goes through the proxy, so Discord REST works. The Gateway doesn't: `@discordjs/ws` dials it with the `ws` package, which opens TLS itself and ignores the env proxy, so the connection gets reset. Discord looks connected but never receives messages.
- **Fix**: when a proxy is set (`HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY`, either case) and Node's env proxy is on, `discord.ts` loads `@discordjs/ws` with `ws.WebSocket` briefly pointed at the native `WebSocket` (which does honor the env proxy), then puts it back straight away. `@discordjs/ws` reads `require('ws').WebSocket` once at load, so only the Gateway gets the native constructor.
- **Scoped to Discord**: the swap is synchronous and restored in a `finally`, so other `ws` users see the real package. That includes Slack Socket Mode, which passes an options object the native `WebSocket` would drop.
- **Why not an option**: neither `@discordjs/ws` 1.2.3 nor `@chat-adapter/discord` 4.29.0 lets callers pass a WebSocket implementation. The adapter builds its own `Client` without passing through `ws` options.
- **Load order**: `@chat-adapter/discord` moves from a static import to a dynamic `import()` inside the (already async-capable) factory, so the swap runs before discord.js loads. The type still comes from a type-only import.
- **Node version**: the check reuses `nodeHonorsEnvProxy` from `setup/service.ts`, now living in `src/env-proxy.ts` (re-exported from `setup/service.ts`) so `src/` can import it. On a Node that ignores the flag (23.x, 22 before 22.21, 24 before 24.5) nothing is swapped.
- **Observable and safe**: it logs `Discord Gateway routed through the env proxy` when the swap ran, warns and skips it if `@discordjs/ws` was already loaded (the swap would do nothing), and falls back to starting Discord without the swap, with a warning, if module resolution throws.
- **Unchanged without a proxy**: no proxy or no env-proxy flag means nothing is patched and the adapter builds exactly as before.

## Related work

No issue. Pairs with #3901 (the host launcher side of running behind an HTTPS proxy). That PR gets the service's REST traffic through the proxy; this one covers the Discord Gateway WebSocket, which it can't reach.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/discord.test.ts src/channels/discord-registration.test.ts` -> 16 passed
  - `isEnvProxyActive`: off with no proxy, off with a proxy but no env-proxy flag, on via `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`, `--use-env-proxy`, and `NODE_OPTIONS`
  - `withNativeWebSocket`: the native constructor is visible only while the gateway loads, and gets restored even when loading throws
  - `isEnvProxyActive`: off on a Node version that ignores the flag (23.11.1, 22.20.0)
  - `resolveGatewayModules`: resolves the same `ws` copy `@discordjs/ws` loads, in the installed layout, and reports whether the gateway was already loaded
- Run behind a proxy (local only): a CONNECT proxy on 127.0.0.1, `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`, Node 25.8.2, a stand-in gateway at `ws://gateway.test:19001` that the proxy maps to a local `ws` server. With the swap, the proxy saw `CONNECT gateway.test:19001` and the gateway accepted the shard. Without it, `@discordjs/ws` dialled the host directly and failed to resolve it. This host cannot reach Discord, so this was not run against the real Gateway or a real corporate proxy.
- Manual smoke (tsx): loaded `@discordjs/ws` through the helper with a stand-in native class, then called `WebSocketShard.connect()` -> the shard built the stand-in (`native:wss://…?v=10&encoding=json`), and `ws.WebSocket` was restored to the real class afterwards
- `pnpm run typecheck` -> no errors in the changed files; 28 errors in untouched files on the base branch (local-web, canvas-actions, slack-onboarding, slack-room-membership)
- `pnpm exec eslint src/channels/discord.ts src/channels/discord.test.ts` -> 0 errors (2 existing `no-explicit-any` warnings)
- `pnpm run format:check` -> clean
- `pnpm test` -> the only failures are in untouched files on the base branch: registration tests for channels the barrel doesn't import on this branch (gchat, github, matrix, …), local-web suites, and `slack-raw-text`
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Discord now connects behind an HTTPS proxy when Node's env proxy (NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY / --use-env-proxy) is on.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

No new credentials or inputs. Behind a proxy, Gateway traffic, including the bot-token IDENTIFY handshake, now goes through the proxy the operator already set. It stays inside TLS (the proxy sees the destination host and a CONNECT tunnel, not the token), the same exposure REST traffic already has. Nothing changes when no proxy is set.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Lets a provider limit a gateway credential to one exact path, so Cursor's key can be injected on its key exchange without overwriting the token Cursor then sends to the same host.
- **Problem**: `GatewayCredentialTarget` scopes by host only. Cursor swaps its key at `api2.cursor.sh/auth/exchange_user_api_key`, then calls RPCs on the same host with the token it got back. Under OneCLI a host-wide entry overwrote that token: `GetUserPrivacyMode` returned 401 in an exe.dev e2e.
- **Fix**: an optional exact `path` on the target. OneCLI maps it to `pathPattern` and Iron to rule `paths`; each accepts an existing entry only when its path matches. Core accepts plain path characters only and refuses a path unless the gateway's store declares `connectionPaths`. The credential-connection seam goes to 2 so a provider can refuse an older core; OpenCode's check now accepts 1 or later.
- **Out of scope**: path-aware conflict checks between two path-scoped Iron credentials on one host. That case fails closed today, and no provider needs it.

## Related work

No issue. Unblocks the `/add-cursor` PR.

- e2e on exe.dev with OneCLI 1.42.0: Cursor setup through this seam created both entries with their path. The key exchange returned 200 with the key injected, and the RPC that had returned 401 returned 200 with no injection. A rerun reused both entries.

- ReleaseSmall build passed.

All four request bodies passed the request schema/context-budget checks used then.

issues.title: [Feature] Persist Computer Use app approvals across sessions
issues.body:
**Problem Statement**

Computer Use asks for per-app approval ("Allow LobsterAI to use <app>?") at the start of every new chat session, even for apps that were approved minutes earlier in a previous session.

The approval is kept only in an in-memory `Set` inside the Computer Use MCP bridge (`mcp-bridge/bin/computer-use-mcp-server.mjs`, `approvedApps`). The bridge process is spawned per session, so that set is recreated and the dialog reappears. The dialog text itself says the grant is "for this session", which confirms the scope is intentionally session-bound — but there is no way to make it durable.

Impact: a routine desktop task (open app → click → type → verify) costs one extra modal confirmation per session per app. With two or three apps the interruptions multiply, and a short follow-up question in a new chat re-triggers everything from scratch.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Start a new chat session (the Computer Use MCP bridge starts at the same timestamp).
2. Ask the agent to click or type in an application → approval dialog appears.
3. Approve → further actions on that app in the same session run without prompts.
4. Open a new session, repeat the same task → the dialog appears again for the same app.

**Proposed Solution**

1. Add a "Remember this app" / "Always allow" checkbox to the existing approval dialog.
2. Persist approved apps (app label + bundle id / executable path) in the app's user config, and load them into `approvedApps` when the bridge starts.
3. Provide a management list in Settings → Capabilities → Computer Use where the user can review and revoke remembered apps.
4. Keep the current hard denials (terminals, password managers, system auth dialogs, Task Manager, and LobsterAI itself) non-overridable regardless of the allowlist.

**Alternatives Considered**

- Keep approvals session-scoped and document the behavior so users know to do related work in one conversation. This is the current state; it does not remove the friction.
- Auto-approve every application by default. Rejected: that removes the only gate between the agent and an arbitrary local application.

**Additional Context**

Environment: Windows 11, LobsterAI desktop (Electron), Computer Use MCP bridge `mcp-bridge/bin/computer-use-mcp-server.mjs`, runtime `computer-use/win-x64/1.0.7`.

Observed behavior: the bridge process start time matches the chat session start time exactly, confirming its per-session lifetime. After approving once, all later actions on the same app within that session proceed without prompts, and the prompt returns only in a new session.

prs.title: refactor(cowork): remove the OpenAI compatibility proxy
prs.body:
> Stacked on netease-youdao/LobsterAI#2897. Review that one first; once it merges, I'll change this PR's base to `release/2026.10.19`.

## Summary

Removes the Claude Agent SDK-era **OpenAI compatibility proxy** (`coworkOpenAICompatProxy.ts` and `coworkFormatTransform.ts`, about 3500 lines). It translated Anthropic `/v1/messages` to OpenAI Chat Completions or Responses. The agent runtime is OpenClaw now, so only two live users were left, and both get a smaller replacement. Design doc: `specs/refactors/remove-cowork-compat-proxy/2026-10-17-remove-cowork-compat-proxy-design.md`.

Commits, in order:

1. **Delete dead code:** `getEnhancedEnv`, the model probe, `get-api-config` / `save-api-config` IPC and `api-config.json`, the Claude SDK telemetry and count-tokens routes, and the unused passthrough route.
2. **`copilotLoopbackProxy.ts`:** the Copilot passthrough that OpenClaw's `lobsterai-copilot` provider uses, moved out unchanged. It keeps the same path, port key, `LOBSTER_PROXY_TOKEN` auth and 401/403 refresh-and-retry, so `openclaw.json` does not change and no gateway restart follows the upgrade.
3. **`oneShotModelClient.ts`:** sessionless streamed text calls. It resolves the model through the same `buildProviderSelection()` that renders `openclaw.json`, so its transport and endpoint always match the agent runtime. It supports Anthropic, Chat Completions, Responses and Gemini, and the loopback token routes server models and Copilot like OpenClaw does.
4. **Callers moved off the proxy:**
   - Desktop companion quick answers use the one-shot client.
   - `check-api-config` uses the raw config. An OpenAI-format model is no longer reported as "no model" when the proxy fails to start, and the response no longer carries API keys to the renderer.
5. **Delete the proxy and what only it used:** `resolveCurrentApiConfig`, the server token refresher and `setCoworkProxySessionId`.
6. **IM cleanup:**
   - Removed the dead `IMChatHandler`, the scheduled-task LLM detector, the `processMessage` path of `IMCoworkHandler`, and helpers and i18n keys only those used.
   - Removed the unused `skillsEnabled` and `systemPrompt` IM settings.
   - Per-message IM logs moved to debug.

Net change: about 7000 lines removed.

## Electron-specific behavior

- **Startup:** the compat proxy no longer starts. The Copilot loopback proxy starts in its place, before the first config sync, on the same remembered port.
- **Quick answers:**
  - They now call the upstream directly, or go through the token proxy or the Copilot passthrough, like OpenClaw does.
  - Responses-mode and custom Gemini providers now work.
  - ChatGPT OAuth and other OAuth providers whose credential isn't in the rendered config now show an explicit "not supported" message. They didn't work through the proxy either.
- **`check-api-config` IPC:** returns `{ hasConfig, error }`.
- **IM plugin approvals:** the 60 s auto-deny for channel plugin approvals is kept unchanged.

## Testing

- `npm test` passes. One known-flaky watcher test fails occasionally and passes on rerun.
- CI eslint on touched files, `npm run compile:electron` and `npm run build` pass, and the legacy IM `node:test` suites pass.
- New unit tests cover the Copilot proxy (auth, host check, retry, streaming), the one-shot client (four transports, token placeholders, unsupported routes), the new SSE readers and quick answer integration.
- Not yet checked in `npm run electron:dev`:
  - Copilot chat across a token refresh, with no gateway restart and an unchanged `openclaw.json`
  - quick answers on Anthropic, Chat Completions, Responses, Gemini, server and Copilot models
  - an IM channel round trip with reminder relay

prs.title: feat(providers): support OpenAI Responses and Gemini formats for custom providers
prs.body:
## Summary

Custom model providers can now use the **OpenAI Responses** and native **Gemini (generateContent)** API formats, on top of OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic. Both reuse OpenClaw's native transports instead of adding LobsterAI-side protocol code.

- **Settings UI:** the API format radio buttons become one dropdown. Custom providers list OpenAI Chat Completions, Anthropic, OpenAI Responses and Gemini; built-in providers keep Chat Completions and Anthropic only.
- **Storage:** Responses is a sub-mode, `ProviderConfig.openaiApiMode`, stored next to `apiFormat: 'openai'`. Older builds therefore fall back to Chat Completions. Gemini is stored as `apiFormat: 'gemini'` on custom providers only.
- **OpenClaw config sync:** Responses mode maps to the `openai-responses` transport (a pasted `/responses` suffix is stripped). Custom Gemini maps to `google-generative-ai`, with a versioned base URL that keeps relay path prefixes and adds `/v1beta` when no version is given.
- **Other callers follow the same choice:** the connection test (native `generateContent` probe for Gemini) and provider export/import, plus the compat proxy, legacy chat path and native Gemini clients for titles and quick answers.

### Why built-in providers don't get Responses yet

Several OpenClaw provider plugins are tuned for Chat Completions:

- The DeepSeek V4 and Xiaomi MiMo thinking wrappers inject Chat Completions fields regardless of transport. This is still true upstream in v2026.10.4.
- Moonshot's Kimi K3 runtime profile requires Chat Completions.
- Volcengine Ark rejects unknown Responses fields.

So the option is limited to custom providers for now.

## Electron-specific behavior

- **OpenClaw config:** changes only for custom providers set to Responses or Gemini. The gateway picks the new transport up through the normal config sync.
- **Provider export:** writes `openaiApiMode` only when it is Responses, so default exports stay importable by older builds with the strict schema.
- **Renderer config normalization:** keeps `apiFormat: 'gemini'` on custom providers. It used to coerce unknown formats to Anthropic.

## Testing

- `npm test`, CI eslint on touched files, `npm run compile:electron` and `npm run build` pass.
- Not yet checked in `npm run electron:dev`: the new dropdown, a Responses or Gemini custom provider (connection test and chat), and that built-in providers show only two options. No screenshots yet.

prs.title: feat(openclaw): keep user overrides in openclaw.user.json across config syncs
prs.body:
## Summary
LobsterAI regenerates `openclaw.json` on every config sync, so users who hand-edit it (e.g. to enable enhancement plugins or tweak OpenClaw options) lose their changes on restart. Instead of a "protection" switch that freezes the file — which would stop model, IM, MCP, skill and agent changes from reaching the gateway and can break startup when ports or plugin paths change — this adds a persistent user override layer: `openclaw.user.json` next to `openclaw.json` is merged on top of every rendered config.

Merge order: LobsterAI-generated config → user overrides → enterprise config (enterprise still wins).

## Related Issue
User feedback: manual `openclaw.json` edits are reset after restart; request for a protection toggle.

## Changes Made
- **Override layer** (`src/main/libs/openclawUserConfigOverlay.ts`): JSON5 file (comments, trailing commas), JSON Merge Patch semantics (objects merge, arrays replace, `null` removes). `plugins.allow` / `plugins.load.paths` are unioned so users can't drop bundled plugins; `plugins.allow` stays sorted so repeated syncs are stable.
- **Protected paths** are ignored and reported: `gateway.auth/mode/port`, `meta`, `agents.defaults.sessionStore`, `plugins.installs`, `plugins.slots.memory`, LobsterAI-internal plugin entries, and `$include` anywhere.
- **Removal works**: the renderer copies existing `gateway`, `plugins.entries` and unknown top-level keys back from the file, so a deleted override would otherwise linger. The paths each sync applied are recorded (kv) and reverted from the base before the next render, only where the value is still what was applied. `createOpenClawConfigTarget` gains an optional merge base / extra owned sections; `baseRaw` stays the real file so the rebase propagates removals.
- **Fail-safe**: a syntax error keeps the last valid overrides. If OpenClaw rejects the config (`config.apply` → `Rejected`, or startup "Invalid config"), overrides are suspended and the config is retried without them (the gateway is restarted once on startup failure); if it still fails, overrides are restored and not blamed again. Quick Repair also suspends overrides until the user applies them again.
- **Settings card** in Agent Engine → 运行维护: enable toggle, state (missing / active / parse error / suspended / disabled), overridden and ignored paths, OpenClaw's rejection detail, Open File / Show in Folder / Apply. zh + en strings.
- **IPC**: `openclaw:userConfig:*` (constants in `src/shared/openclawUserConfig/constants.ts`), handlers in `src/main/ipcHandlers/openclawUserConfig/handlers.ts`, exposed as `window.electron.openclaw.userConfig`.
- `json5` added as a runtime dependency (was dev-only transitively). It's imported as `json5/lib/parse` because the package's ESM entry has only a default export, which broke the Vite-bundled main process with a named import.

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Code refactoring
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Other (please describe):

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests
- [x] Manual testing performed

- `npm test`: 689 files / 7439 tests pass. New: `openclawUserConfigOverlay.test.ts` (19), two `OpenClawConfigSync` runtime tests through the real renderer (apply → steady state reports `changed: false` → removal → steady again; minimal no-model path), one `openclawConfigTarget` test.
- ESLint (CI command) clean on all touched files; `tsc --noEmit` for renderer and `electron-tsconfig.json` pass; `compile:electron` passes.
- End-to-end in `electron:dev` on an isolated profile (`LOBSTERAI_DEV_USER_DATA_DIR`), driven via CDP, both logged out and logged in (lobsterai-server provider): template creation, apply, survives restart, coexists with a managed setting change in the same `agents` section, removal across `agents` / `plugins.entries` / `gateway`, protected paths ignored, syntax error keeps last valid overrides, invalid key rejected while running (engine stays up), invalid key at cold start (gateway auto-restarts without overrides), toggle off/on, Quick Repair suspend + reapply, file deletion.

## Screenshots (if applicable)
Not attached. The card was checked in the dev app (dark theme) in active, ignored-paths, parse-error and suspended states.

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

## Electron-Specific Changes
- [x] Changes to main process (src/main/)
- [x] Changes to preload script (src/main/preload.ts)
- [x] Changes to IPC communication
- [ ] Changes to window management
- [ ] None

**OpenClaw config / restart behavior:** with no `openclaw.user.json` (the default), the rendered config is unchanged. With overrides, they become part of the target `OpenClawConfigSync` renders, so the existing change detection, `config.apply` delivery and restart decisions apply to them. New automatic restart: only after a gateway startup failure caused by the overrides (one attempt without them).

## Additional Notes
- This branch was cut from `release/2026.10.19`, so against `main` the diff also shows the two commits of #2892 (kit catalog recovery) that are not on `main` yet. The override feature itself is commit `ad8a3009`.
- Suspension is all-or-nothing: one invalid key withholds the whole file until it changes or the user clicks Apply Again; the card lists the paths and OpenClaw's error.
- Local dev note: a runtime built before the 2026-10-16 preset context-window patches rejects LobsterAI's own config after login (`contextWindowDefault` unrecognized). That's unrelated to this PR; `npm run openclaw:runtime:host` fixes it.

prs.title: feat(desktop): add custom companion skins, screenshot tools and Cowork follow-ups
prs.body:
## Summary
The desktop companion currently offers bundled skins and immediately attaches a selected screenshot. Cowork also leaves users to compose every follow-up from scratch. This adds three complementary, portable enhancements:

- **Custom companion skins:** upload PNG/JPEG/WebP, preview scale and position, save multiple named skins, rename/delete them, and restore the default LobsterAI appearance. Images are normalized to 512×512 PNGs in the local profile; built-in skins and branding remain available.
- **Cowork follow-up suggestions:** after a completed reply, show one contextual suggestion in an empty composer. Tab inserts it as an editable draft and Escape dismisses it; it never sends automatically. A separate, bounded completion uses the existing model configuration, with account/turn/model-scoped caching and stale-response protection.
- **Screenshot tools:** adjust the region, annotate rectangles/ellipses/arrows/pen/mosaic/text, and undo. Copy, save, ask LobsterAI, extract text, or translate. OCR/translation use independent existing Cowork tasks and preserve the unsent composer draft; failed tasks keep a retry action.

## Electron behavior
- Keep the existing sandboxed screenshot renderer, per-display capture, and sender/main-frame checks. Full-screen PNG frames stay in memory; only an approved crop is saved. Annotated PNG headers and dimensions are checked before decoding.
- Store custom skin PNGs under the current profile with content-hash filenames; only the main settings window can mutate them. Add preload methods for skin management, isolated screenshot task handoff, and suggestions.
- Suggestions make at most a short 160-token completion per cached turn, with a 10-second timeout, using the existing default-model routing. No agent turn is interrupted.
- No server API, database migration, bundled runtime change, or private cloud image-generation dependency is introduced. Add `jsdom` as a dev dependency for actual React interaction tests.

## Validation
- Targeted Vitest: **241 passed, 1 skipped**, across 14 files. The skipped test checks macOS screen-recording permission behavior and is not applicable on this Windows host.
- Renderer TypeScript (`tsc --noEmit`), `npm run compile:electron`, and `npm run build`: passed.
- Changed TypeScript/TSX files: ESLint with zero warnings. `git diff --cached --check`: passed.
- Coverage includes region adjustment, explicit screenshot actions, annotation undo/export, cancellation and account changes, independent task handoff/retries, local skin persistence/permissions, and Tab accepting a suggestion without submitting or overwriting typed text.

## Manual validation still needed
Native Electron visual acceptance and screenshots were not completed: the available Browser connection exposes only MCP Apps, with no local-page browser connection. In particular, real multi-monitor/DPI behavior, OS clipboard/save dialogs, image uploads, and live-model OCR/translation/suggestions still need manual desktop validation. Automated tests and build results above do not claim that acceptance.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): bound disk usage of repair backups and runtime caches
prs.body:
## Summary

A long-running install reached ~17G under `~/Library/Application Support/LobsterAI`. Most of it came from OpenClaw data that only grows and is never cleaned up. End users hit the same sources, so this PR bounds each one from the LobsterAI side, without an OpenClaw patch.

| Source | Observed | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `openclaw/repair-backups` | 8.2G (2 runs) | Snapshots skip regenerable caches. At most 2 runs are kept, none older than 14 days; the current run is always kept. Pruning runs after each repair and in the background cleanup, and caches are stripped from retained older runs. |
| `state/.compile-cache` | 1.0G | Subdirectories left by other Node/Electron versions are removed. |
| Agent browser caches | 1.6G + 0.9G (`~/Library/Caches`) | The HTTP cache is capped via `--disk-cache-size` in `browser.extraArgs`. Once a day, if no Chrome holds the profile and its caches exceed 512 MiB, `Cache`, `Code Cache`, `GPUCache` and `Service Worker` are cleared. Cookies, Local Storage, IndexedDB and Login Data are never touched. |
| `agents/*/sessions/sessions.json.*.tmp` | 249M | Orphaned files older than 7 days are removed, matching OpenClaw's own temp file name pattern. |
| `*.jsonl.deleted.*` / `*.reset.*` archives | 50M | `session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention` is set to `30d`, so OpenClaw expires both the files and their `session_transcript_archives` rows. |
| `agents/*/session-sqlite-import-archive` | ~1G | Removed 14 days after the last clean session→SQLite migration. Archives are kept while the newest migration run is in flight, failed or unreadable, since `doctor --session-sqlite recover` may need them. LobsterAI itself only runs `import`. |

### Cleanup timing and pacing

All cleanups live in `openclawStartupDiskCleanup.ts`. A first pass after an upgrade can delete several hundred thousand files; on the reporter's machine the old snapshots' compile caches alone held ~266k. To keep that off low-end machines' disks:

- **Deferred:** a pass starts 60s after the gateway reports `running`. Gateway restarts inside the window share one pending pass, and timers are `unref`'d.
- **Paced:** `openclawDiskCleanupThrottle.ts` runs deletions in 20ms work slices with 80ms rests (about 20% duty cycle). Steps run one at a time, cheapest per byte first: session temps, import archives, browser caches, repair backups, compile cache.
- **Bounded:** each pass stops after 5 minutes of wall time. A stopped pass retries after 30 minutes and on the next app start.
- **Battery:** the pass is skipped on battery power (`powerMonitor.isOnBatteryPower()`), and a running pass stops at its next rest once the laptop switches to battery.
- **Resumable:** every step is idempotent. Repair backup runs and import archives are renamed aside (`.lobsterai-stale-*`) before deletion, so a partly removed one is finished later and is never mistaken for an in-progress repair or a recently modified archive. The post-repair prune is paced the same way.

Measured on an M1 with 100k small files: unpaced deletion ran at ~9.7k files/s using a full core; paced deletion runs at ~1.1k files/s using ~0.2 of a core, with main-process event-loop lag ≤ 8ms. One pass can therefore delete roughly 330k files there; slower disks take more passes.

Every step is best-effort, logs its own failures, and never follows symlinks or Windows junctions. A repair backup run modified in the last hour is never touched.

## Behavior changes to note

- **OpenClaw config:** `openclaw.json` gains `--disk-cache-size` in `browser.extraArgs` and `session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention: "30d"`. The first config sync after an upgrade may restart the gateway once.
- **History:** LobsterAI's visible chat history is in `lobsterai.sqlite` and is unaffected. `chat.history` reads only the current transcript generation, never the `.deleted`/`.reset` archives.
- **Repair helper:** the snapshot exclusions take effect once the bundled `openclaw-gateway-repair.mjs` is rebuilt, which happens in the normal runtime build.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run src/main/libs/openclaw src/main/openclawSessionPolicy src/main/libs/removeTreeNoFollow`: 1226 passed
- [x] `npx eslint --ext ts,tsx --report-unused-disable-directives --max-warnings 0` on touched files
- [x] `npm run compile:electron`
- [ ] Manual check with `npm run electron:dev` on an existing profile: about 60s after the gateway is running (on AC power), the cleanup log lines appear, the agent browser keeps its logins, and one-click repair succeeds with a slimmer snapshot

prs.title: feat: native gpui desktop client (apps/desktop) and moltis-client crate
prs.body:
## Summary

A native Rust/gpui desktop client that **connects to a running moltis daemon** instead of embedding it. Quitting the app leaves the daemon running. It connects to the local daemon, to remote daemons over HTTPS, or through SSH tunnels.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    UI[apps/desktop gpui] --> Client[crates/client moltis-client]
    Ctl[moltis-ctl] --> Client
    Client -- "WSS /ws/chat v4 + scoped mk_ key" --> Daemon[(moltis daemon)]
    Client -- "ssh -L" --> Daemon
    Proto[crates/protocol typed payloads] --- Client
    Proto --- Daemon
```

- **`moltis-protocol`** now owns the client-facing wire types:
  - Persisted message types and `ExternalAgentKind` moved here and are re-exported from `moltis-sessions`.
  - Typed `chat` events and typed `sessions.list` / `chat.*` / `models.list` / approval payloads.
  - As a result, `moltis-config` no longer depends on `moltis-sessions`, which drops sqlx and tokio from its dependency tree.
- **New `moltis-client` crate:**
  - v4 handshake, responses routed by request id, and an event broadcast.
  - Keepalive pings and a `ManagedClient` that reconnects with backoff and stops on auth failures.
  - Typed RPC helpers.
  - Password login exchanged for a scoped API key.
  - TLS trust by local CA, pinned fingerprint (trust on first use), or the platform verifier.
  - Failure classification, so the UI can tell an unreachable daemon from a TLS or auth failure.
  - Optional local-config discovery, mDNS discovery, and SSH tunnels.
- **`moltis-ctl`** is ported onto `moltis-client`. Its old handshake waited for a top-level `hello-ok` frame that the gateway never sends, so every invocation timed out.
- **`apps/desktop`** is a separate Cargo workspace:
  - Sessions sidebar and a streaming transcript.
  - Native markdown with syntect code highlighting.
  - Tool cards, reasoning and model picker; stop and approvals, including system notifications.
  - Server list with Nearby (mDNS), direct HTTPS and SSH tunnels.
  - API keys stored in the keychain.
  - Starts the local daemon as a user service when it isn't running.
  - Settings, providers, cron and logs open in the web UI.
- Packaging script for `Moltis Desktop.app`, `just desktop-*` recipes, a Desktop App CI workflow, and docs (`docs/src/desktop-app.md`).

Security hardening is included in the branch:
- No credentials over plain HTTP to non-loopback hosts.
- Approve from a notification only for short printable-ASCII commands.
- Changed certificates are flagged as changed, not as a first-use prompt.
- Markdown nesting is capped.
- mDNS entries are labelled unverified and saved only after the user trusts the certificate.

No GraphQL was needed.

## Validation

### Completed
- [x] `cargo test -p moltis-client --all-features` (54 tests, including a TLS mock server)
- [x] `cargo test -p moltis-protocol -p moltis-sessions -p moltis-config` and `cargo test -p moltis-chat --lib chat_final_broadcast_parses`
- [x] `cargo test -p moltis-httpd --test native_client` (client against a real in-process gateway)
- [x] `cd apps/desktop && cargo test` (63 tests), plus clippy with `--features capture` and with `--no-default-features`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `./scripts/check-file-size.sh`
- [x] Manual end to end against a real daemon in a temp config dir:
  - TLS through the local CA, then the handshake and model list.
  - A streamed reply rendered with markdown and code highlighting.
  - The daemon kept running after the app quit, and history reloaded on relaunch.
  - Checked with screenshots from the `capture` feature.
- [x] `./scripts/package-desktop-macos.sh` builds and launches the bundle; `just desktop-open-macos` bundles a portable release daemon, and with no service installed the app started it and connected in 4s.
- [x] `OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR=/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3 ./scripts/local-validate.sh 1306`: fmt, file-size, biome, tsc, zizmor, lockfile, `just lint` and the full build pass. The targeted-test step then tried `-p moltis-desktop` from the root workspace; fixed in `86f5fe40` (the script now skips `apps/desktop`, which `desktop.yml` tests).
- [x] `cargo nextest run -p moltis-chat -p moltis-client -p moltis-config -p moltis-ctl -p moltis-httpd -p moltis-metrics -p moltis-protocol -p moltis-sessions`: 1057 passed.

### Remaining
- [ ] mDNS discovery verified live. In the dev sandbox even `dns-sd` saw no advertisements.

## Manual QA

1. `moltis service install` (or run `moltis`), then `just desktop-run`. The app should connect to "This computer".
2. If the daemon has a password: sign in. The key appears in the web UI under Settings → Security as "Moltis Desktop (host)".
3. Send a message and watch it stream. Try ⌘. to stop and ⌘N for a new chat; switch sessions and switch models.
4. Quit the app, then `curl -k https://localhost:<port>/health` still answers. Relaunch and the history is there.
5. Servers (⌘⇧S) → add `https://other-host:port`: the fingerprint prompt appears; trust it and you are connected.
6. Add an SSH tunnel (`user@host`, daemon port) and connect.
7. `moltis service uninstall`, then `just desktop-open-macos`: the app installs the bundled daemon as a service by itself and connects within a few seconds (measured: 4s).

prs.title: feat(gateway): open the browser on first run and make the URL hard to miss
prs.body: ## Summary First-run users often didn't realize they had to open a browser to finish setup. This PR makes the next step obvious: - **Auto-open the browser on first run.** When moltis runs in a local desktop session (TTY, not SSH/CI/container/systemd, a display on Linux), it opens `/onboarding#setup=`. The setup code travels in the URL fragment (never sent to the server), is pre-filled in the auth step, and is stripped from the address bar via `history.replaceState`. Configurable via `[server] open_browser = "first-run" | "always" | "never"` and `--open-browser` / `--no-open-browser`. - **Plain HTTP on loopback.** New `[tls] loopback_http` (written as `true` in fresh configs): loopback binds serve `http://localhost`, which browsers treat as a secure context, so passkeys work without certificate warnings. `MoltisConfig::tls_active()` / `TlsConfig::active_for_bind()` replace raw `tls.enabled` checks. - **Trustable local CA.** The CA is now persisted with X.509 name constraints (localhost, `.local`, loopback, private/CGNAT/link-local ranges plus exact SANs), `pathlen=0`, 10-year validity; server certs are re-issued from it on renewal. When TLS is active and the CA is untrusted, an interactive `[Y/n]` prompt installs it (macOS keychain, Linux `update-ca-certificates`, Windows user Root store, NSS DBs for Chromium/Firefox). `moltis trust-ca` uses the same code. The decision is recorded per CA fingerprint. - **Clearer logs.** A boxed "next step" message after listening, an `ssh -L` forward hint over SSH, and periodic reminders until onboarding completes. - **Pinned status line.** On an interactive stdout, a bottom line shows `▶ Finish setup at … · setup code X`, then `● Moltis running at …`. Logs scroll above it. - **Security hardening.** Private keys are written via `create_new` + mode `0600` + rename (no permission TOCTOU), the certs dir is `0700`, and the setup code is no longer written to the log stream (only the startup banner and the pinned line, which isn't logged). ```mermaid flowchart TD A[moltis starts] --> B{loopback bind and loopback_http?} B -- yes --> C[serve http://localhost] B -- no --> D{TLS CA trusted?} D -- no, TTY --> E[prompt: install CA] D -- yes --> F[serve https] E --> F C --> G[listen] F --> G G --> H{local desktop and open_browser policy} H -- yes --> I[open /onboarding#setup=CODE] H -- no --> J[next-step box + ssh -L hint] I --> K[pinned status line / reminders until onboarded] J --> K ``` ## Screenshots **Onboarding page opened from the launch link.** The setup code comes from `#setup=…`, and the fragment is removed from the address bar once read. **Local terminal with `--no-open-browser`.** The next-step box is logged without the setup code, and the pinned bottom line shows the URL and code. **Over SSH.** The box shows the `ssh -L` port-forward command to run on your computer. Addresses are example values. ## Validation ### Completed - [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` - [x] `cargo clippy -p moltis-config -p moltis-tls -p moltis-httpd -p moltis -p moltis-onboarding -p moltis-web --all-targets -- -D warnings` - [x] `cargo test -p moltis-config` (391 pass) - [x] `cargo test -p moltis-tls` (35 pass, includes rustls chain verification after renewal) - [x] `cargo test -p moltis-httpd launch` (10 pass) - [x] `cargo test -p moltis status_line` (2 pass) - [x] `cd crates/web/ui && npx playwright test e2e/specs/onboarding-auth.spec.js` (2 pass) - [x] `biome check --write crates/web/ui/src/`, `npm run build`, `npx tsc --noEmit` - [x] `./scripts/check-file-size.sh` ### Remaining - [ ] `./scripts/local-validate.sh ` - [ ] `just lint` (full OS-aware clippy) ## Manual QA 1. Fresh install: `rm -rf ~/.moltis-qa && MOLTIS_CONFIG_DIR=~/.moltis-qa MOLTIS_DATA_DIR=~/.moltis-qa moltis`. Expect the browser to open at `http://localhost:/onboarding`, the setup code pre-filled, and `#setup=` gone from the address bar. 2. Check the bottom line of the terminal shows `▶ Finish setup at …`, and changes to `● Moltis running at …` after onboarding. 3. Run with `--no-open-browser`: the browser doesn't open and the next-step box is logged. 4. Over SSH: the browser doesn't open and the box shows an `ssh -L :localhost: user@host` hint. 5. Set `[tls] loopback_http = false` with an untrusted CA: you get the `[Y/n]` trust prompt, and after accepting, `https://localhost:` loads without warnings in Safari, Chrome and Firefox. 6. `moltis trust-ca` prints a ✓/✗ line per store. 7. `ls -l ~/.moltis-qa/certs` shows keys as `-rw-------` and the dir as `drwx------`.
