prs.title: fix(agents): recognize llama-server and DashScope URL audio rejections in audio-fallback classifier
prs.body:
## Description

Follow-up to #7015 (fixed by #7024). The modality-aware audio stripping works, but its reactive learning entry point (`_is_audio_fallback_error`) only recognizes DashScope's "incorrect modal" rejection. Two rejection shapes still fall through and kill the entire agent turn *after* `send_file_to_user` has already delivered the audio file to the user:

1. **DashScope URL-shape rejection** — the first failure mode documented in #7015: local audio serialized as raw base64 is rejected with HTTP 400 `"The provided URL does not appear to be valid"`. This wording never reaches the audio classifier, so no strip-and-retry happens, no `rejects_audio` capability is learned, and **every subsequent turn re-crashes** while the audio block remains in session history (reproduced: the user had to switch the active model to recover the conversation).
2. **llama.cpp `llama-server`** (self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint with a vision-only mmproj, e.g. Qwen-VL-family GGUFs) rejects `input_audio` with HTTP 500 `"audio input is not supported - hint: ..."`. Same outcome: turn dies, nothing learned.

Both shapes were reproduced in production on QwenPaw 2.2.0 (Windows 11, Python 3.12.13):

- provider `aliyun-tokenplan` / model `qwen3.8-max` → shape 1
- custom provider → local `llama-server` (b10715) serving a Qwen-VL GGUF with vision mmproj → shape 2

The fix reuses the existing strip → retry → learn machinery: both shapes now classify as audio-fallback errors, so the turn recovers and `rejects_audio` is learned for the model key (subsequent requests strip audio proactively while images keep working).

**Related Issue:** Relates to #7015

**Security Considerations:** None. The change only widens error-message classification for the existing audio strip-and-retry path; no new inputs are accepted and no credential/config handling is touched. The URL-shape match is gated on a 400-class status and, at the call site, on `_last_wire_request_had_audio()`, so malformed image/video URLs cannot be misclassified as audio rejections (addressing the concern raised in #7015 about matching the URL error broadly).

prs.title: perf(agent): byte-stable prompt envelope + Claude prompt caching
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Byte-stable system prompt.** The live clock and query-matched memory moved out of the system prompt into a once-per-turn `<turn-context>` block. It is prepended to a *request copy* of the latest user message, so persisted history is unchanged. `ToolRegistry` is now a `BTreeMap`, so tool definitions are always name-sorted.
- **Claude prompt caching.** Up to 4 `cache_control` breakpoints go on the serialized request: the system prompt (or the last tool if there is none) plus the trailing messages. Cache read/write tokens are debug-logged.
- **Bug fix: loop-guard notices replaced Claude's system prompt.** `convert_messages` kept the *last* `System` message as `system`. Now only the first one is; later notices are sent as user-turn text after any tool results.
- **Response-cache key includes the turn context**, so a stale answer isn't reused now that time and memory left the system prompt.

## Related Issue

Part of #661. This is phase 1; the issue stays open for session-start freezing and deferred prompt/toolset mutations.

Closes # <!-- intentionally not closing #661 -->

## Pre-submit Checklist

- [x] I branched from `upstream/main`
- [x] This PR contains only commits related to this change
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` passes
- [x] `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` passes (default and `--features panel`)
- [x] `cargo nextest run --lib` passes
- [x] I added or updated tests for my changes
- [x] New constants/limits are shared (not duplicated across files)
- [x] No new dependencies unless necessary (we target ~6 MB binary)

## Security Considerations

- The `<turn-context>` block holds memory values (user-controlled, as before). The default system prompt now tells the model that the runtime adds this block and that it is background facts, not instructions.
- No new endpoints, secrets or unbounded collections. Cache markers only change the outbound request copy.

## Test Plan

- `test_request_prefix_is_byte_stable_across_tool_loop_and_turns` runs two turns, each with a tool call, through a capturing provider. It asserts:
  - the system message and tool list are byte-identical on all 4 calls
  - tools arrive name-sorted
  - each tool-loop call extends the previous request exactly
  - the turn context sits on the newest user message only, with history left clean
- Claude: marker placement (system, tool fallback, tool_result / tool_use blocks, empty-text skip, max 4), system-notice placement after tool results, and cache-usage deserialization.
- Context builder: clock and memory excluded from the system prompt, turn-context shape, image-message text part, history not mutated.
- Registry: all three `definitions*` paths return name-sorted tools.

  - `cargo nextest run --lib`: 3611 passed (default), 3814 passed (`panel`)
  - `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test --doc`: 132 passed

**Follow-ups (not in this PR):** Anthropic excludes cache reads from `input_tokens`, so the token budget and cost tracker will under-count once caches hit. This is worth its own issue.

issues.body:
### Affected component

tooling/ci

### Severity

S3 - minor issue

### Current behavior

On current `master` (`bf38521fc4`), `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes on the CI-pinned Rust 1.98.0 but fails on Rust 1.99.0.

This is not a present CI failure. Every toolchain pin in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `ci-sbom.yml` is `toolchain: 1.98.0`. It becomes one when the pin moves to 1.99, and it already affects anyone running stable 1.99 locally.

Running clippy without `-D warnings` (so no crate stops the build) on both toolchains and diffing the results: 1.98.0 reports **0** findings, 1.99.0 reports **18**. They come from three lints new to 1.99:

- **`clippy::needless_borrows_for_generic_args`** (4, default `clippy::all`): passing `&f` where `f` already implements the required `Fn` trait.
  - `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs:1121`
  - `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs:1125`
  - `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/turn/stream_guard.rs:149`
  - `crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs:4911`
- **`deprecated`** (1): `AtomicU64::fetch_update` is deprecated, renamed to `try_update`.

- **`clippy::assert_is_empty`** (13, enabled through `#![warn(clippy::pedantic)]` in `src/lib.rs`), all in test code:

### Expected behavior

The workspace is clippy-clean on Rust 1.99.0, so the CI pin can move to 1.99 without lint fallout.

It compiles on 1.98.0, so the change stays compatible with the current pin. It fails on 1.93.0 with `E0658 atomic_try_update`, as expected for a pre-1.95 toolchain.
- `assert_is_empty`: `assert!(x.is_empty())` becomes the form clippy suggests, or the lint is allowed at the test-module level if maintainers prefer the current style in tests.

Consequence: noisy local lint runs today; CI lint failures once the pin moves to 1.99. No runtime behavior is affected.

issues.body:
### Task

Move the `aarch64-apple-darwin` leg of the `plugin-smoke` job from `macos-14` to `macos-15` in `.github/workflows/release-stable-manual.yml` and `.github/workflows/cross-platform-build-manual.yml`. Add an architecture test that fails if any workflow names a `macos-14` runner. Land it before 2026-10-19 14:00 UTC, or before the next Release Stable dispatch whose smoke leg would run inside a brownout window, whichever comes first.

### Context

#11347 adds a `plugin-smoke` job that runs each packaged release archive on a native runner of its own platform. Its `aarch64-apple-darwin` leg runs on `macos-14`, at `release-stable-manual.yml:778` and `cross-platform-build-manual.yml:482` (line numbers at #11347's head `f39ffd4791`).

GitHub retires the macOS 14 image on November 2, 2026 ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-01-github-actions-macos-14-runner-image-retirement/)). Until then, jobs on `macos-14`, `macos-14-large` and `macos-14-xlarge` fail during scheduled brownouts. Five windows remain: October 19, 23, 26, 29 and 30, each from 14:00 UTC to midnight UTC.

In Release Stable this leg is not advisory. `publish` and `docker` both need `plugin-smoke`. A run whose smoke leg lands in a brownout fails before anything is published, and after November 2 every release run fails until the label changes. In Cross-Platform Build the same leg fails the qualification rehearsal.

#11522 moved every other `macos-14` job on master to `macos-15` on 2026-10-06, for this reason. Master has no `macos-14` left; #11347 brings back two. The `build` job already builds `aarch64-apple-darwin` on `macos-15`, so after the change the smoke runs on the same image as the build.

A Release Stable run on October 17 or 18 is outside every window, so this does not need to hold v0.8.6. On October 19, count from when the smoke leg starts, which is after the whole build matrix finishes, not from the dispatch.

Changing `release-stable-manual.yml` also changes the whole-file digest pinned in `tests/architecture/release_workflow.rs` (around line 602), so this PR has to update that literal. #11830 tracks removing the digest.

Raised in the #11347 review.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both `plugin-smoke` matrices run `aarch64-apple-darwin` on `macos-15`. Nothing else in those jobs changes.
- [ ] A new architecture test fails when any file under `.github/workflows/` names a `macos-14` runner, including `macos-14-large` and `macos-14-xlarge`. The PR shows it failing with `macos-14` restored and passing after.
- [ ] The Stable workflow digest in `tests/architecture/release_workflow.rs` is updated, and the release workflow architecture tests pass.
- [ ] Merged before 2026-10-19 14:00 UTC, or before the next Release Stable dispatch whose smoke leg would start inside a window.

### Likely files or areas

- `.github/workflows/release-stable-manual.yml` (`plugin-smoke` matrix)
- `.github/workflows/cross-platform-build-manual.yml` (`plugin-smoke` matrix)
- `tests/architecture/release_workflow.rs` (the digest literal, and the new test beside the existing release workflow tests)

### Contributor fit

maintainer-scoped task, not yet ready for pickup labels

### Mentor, reviewer, or contact

@JordanTheJet. Review by `.github/**` CODEOWNERS (@Audacity88, @tidux, @JordanTheJet).

### Risk notes

Low. Two matrix rows change runner label, and one static test is added. Land it as its own PR right after #11347 merges, so #11347 keeps the approvals on its reviewed head. The `macos-15` image differs from `macos-14` in Xcode and system libraries, but the release build already runs on `macos-15`, so the smoke now matches it.

### Task

Remove the SHA-256 assertion over `release-stable-manual.yml` from `immutable_stable_release_recipe_has_real_command_and_failure_baselines` in `tests/architecture/release_workflow.rs`. Keep the semantic assertions. Add a named assertion only where the digest protects something that matters and no other assertion covers.

### Context

The test is at `tests/architecture/release_workflow.rs:581` on #11347's head `f39ffd4791`. It reads the Stable workflow, removes the arm64 build-memory block, and cuts out the one reviewed `Build release` step. It then compares a SHA-256 of everything else with a literal (lines 602 to 605). A change to any other byte in the file fails the test, and the failure shows only two hashes.

Most changes to that file are routine. Of the last 15 commits on master that touched `release-stable-manual.yml`, seven would have failed this test:

- five action-version bumps: #10598, #10500, #9920 and #9752 from Dependabot, plus #9856
- the `macos-14` to `macos-15` runner move, #11522
- the 1.98.0 toolchain bump, #9527

Each author would have had to find this test and recompute the hash, with nothing to say what the hash guards. The Dependabot PRs would have stayed red until a maintainer pushed to them.

The semantic checks already pin what matters:

- `assert_arm64_build_memory` checks the arm64 memory handling.
- `assert_release_caller` checks the `Build release` step's inputs.
- The matrix loop checks each target's linker and `use_cross` settings.
- The recipe runs check the command and failure traces for all ten targets.
- A separate test checks that the shared body inverts the input adapters back to the immutable body.
- Other tests in the same file assert the `needs` of `publish` (including `plugin-smoke` and `crates-preflight`) and of `docker` (including `plugin-smoke`).

`OLD_RELEASE_RECIPE_SHA256`, in the same test, pins a constant inside the test file, not the workflow. It can stay.

Raised in the #11347 review.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The whole-file digest assertion is removed.
- [ ] The PR lists what the digest covered, and each part either has a named assertion or is stated as intentionally unpinned.
- [ ] Changing a `uses:` pin outside the `Build release` step, as Dependabot does, no longer fails the test. Shown on the PR.
- [ ] Mutation checks still fail a test: removing `plugin-smoke` from `publish`'s `needs`, removing it from `docker`'s `needs`, and removing the arm64 memory step.

### Likely files or areas

- `tests/architecture/release_workflow.rs`

### Contributor fit

maintainer-scoped task, not yet ready for pickup labels

### Mentor, reviewer, or contact

@JordanTheJet. Review by `tests/**` CODEOWNERS (@JordanTheJet, @Audacity88).

### Risk notes

The digest is a blunt guard against unreviewed edits to a publishing workflow. Without it, that guard is the named assertions plus CODEOWNERS review of `.github/**`. The risk is a semantic gap, and the mutation checks above cover the main ones. Until this lands, every PR that touches the Stable workflow has to update the literal, including the `macos-15` runner fix.

issues.body:
### Task

Find out whether the plugin host works inside the signed and notarized macOS desktop app. If it does not, add the hardened-runtime entitlement that Cranelift needs and sign the bundled `zeroclaw` sidecar with it. Until this is confirmed, nothing should tell desktop users that plugins work.

### Context

**The desktop app now carries the plugin host.** Release Stable's `build-desktop` job builds the app's bundled `zeroclaw` with `scripts/desktop/prepare-kernel.sh --target universal-apple-darwin --features embedded-web`. That script resolves the `dist` selection for each target. With #11221 and #11347, `dist` includes `plugins-wasm-cranelift` on both macOS targets. So the sidecar in the dmg carries the plugin host and the Cranelift compiler.

**Nothing in the signing setup allows JIT.** The repo has no entitlements file. Neither `apps/tauri/tauri.conf.json` nor the `apps/tauri/tauri.bundled.conf.json` overlay has a `bundle.macOS` section, so Tauri signs the bundle with its defaults. Notarization requires the hardened runtime. Under the hardened runtime, a process cannot make anonymous memory executable unless it is signed with `com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit` (for `MAP_JIT` mappings) or `com.apple.security.cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory`. Cranelift compiles each plugin to machine code in memory and then runs it.

**This is reasoning, not a reproduction.** Nobody has run `zeroclaw plugin install` inside a notarized dmg yet. Two things need checking: which entitlement Wasmtime's code memory needs on macOS, and whether Tauri signs `externalBin` sidecars with the app's entitlements.

**The plugin smoke does not cover it.** #11347's `plugin-smoke` job runs the CLI archives on native runners. It does not test the desktop bundle. The macOS CLI archives are not signed with the hardened runtime either, so their smoke pass says nothing about the notarized app. The Linux and Windows desktop bundles build their sidecar the same way and are not smoke-tested either, but they have no equivalent signing restriction.

**Why it matters.** On builds with the plugin host, `zeroclaw status`, `/api/plugins` and the dashboard report the plugin host as available. If the reasoning holds, a macOS desktop user is shown plugins as available, and loading one fails.

Raised in the #11347 review.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On a signed and notarized dmg from a release or release candidate, the bundled `zeroclaw` installs and loads a registry package. The `redact-text` tool needs no account, so it is a good test. The result is recorded here with the macOS version and chip.
- [ ] If that fails: an entitlements file with the narrowest entitlement that works is added and wired through the Tauri config so the sidecar is signed with it. Then the check above passes and notarization still succeeds.
- [ ] Until the first item passes, no release note or doc says the desktop app runs plugins.
- [ ] Optional: a desktop release check that runs `plugin install` against the signed sidecar, so this cannot regress silently.

### Likely files or areas

- `apps/tauri/tauri.conf.json`, `apps/tauri/tauri.bundled.conf.json`
- a new entitlements file under `apps/tauri/`
- `scripts/desktop/prepare-kernel.sh`
- `.github/workflows/release-stable-manual.yml` (`build-desktop`)

### Contributor fit

maintainer-scoped task, not yet ready for pickup labels

### Mentor, reviewer, or contact

@JordanTheJet. Review by `apps/tauri/**` CODEOWNERS (@JordanTheJet, @Audacity88), and `.github/**` CODEOWNERS for any workflow change.

### Risk notes

- `allow-unsigned-executable-memory` is broader than `allow-jit`. Use `allow-jit` if Wasmtime works with it.
- An entitlement loosens the hardened runtime for the whole binary it signs. Give it to the sidecar only, unless the app shell needs it too.
- A signing change can break notarization. Check the notarization result on the first release run after the change.

issues.body:
### Task

Make the `dist` image build in `.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml` fit in memory on arm64 before the v0.8.6 release, or decide to release without the `dist` image and rebuild it from the tag afterwards. The arm64 build of the `Dockerfile` is killed in the final fat-LTO link of `zeroclaw` (`signal: 9, SIGKILL`, buildx `ResourceExhausted`). #11347 adds swap and `--jobs 2` for the Stable ARM64 GNU archive build only. Neither reaches this image build.

### Context

**What runs at release.** Release Stable's `docker-matrix` job calls `docker-publish.yml` with `release_ref` set to the new tag. It needs `publish` and `docker`, so it starts after the GitHub Release is out. `docker-publish.yml` builds each variant in `dev/ci/docker-tags.toml` as one job on `ubuntu-latest`. The `dist` variant builds `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` in one Buildx build. The Dockerfile's builder stage runs on the amd64 host and cross-compiles arm64, so both fat-LTO links run on the same runner and can overlap. The job has no swap step, no build cache and a 60-minute timeout. The file is identical on master, #11221 and #11347.

**What changed in v0.8.6.** #11221 and #11347 add `plugins-wasm-cranelift` and 13 `tool-*` features to the `dist` selection, so the final link has more to do. The release profile is unchanged: `opt-level = "z"`, fat LTO, one codegen unit.

**Evidence.** `docker-image-pr.yml` builds the same Dockerfile on the same runner class. It builds one platform per job and uses a build cache, so it is an easier job than the release one.

- With the v0.8.6 `dist` features, every completed arm64 run was killed in the `zeroclaw` link:
  - [39040526108](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39040526108), #11347 at `f39ffd4791`, 42 minutes in
  - [39032381913](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39032381913), #11347 at `1395d0d251`
  - [39028646647](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39028646647), #11221 at `04746465a0`
  - [39003316285](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39003316285), #11221 at `a4c62dc5e1`
  - [38149015787](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38149015787), #11221 at `ab6eee8711`
- Master's own `dist` features (no Cranelift) were already at the limit. The same leg failed in [38845347616](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38845347616) and [39014710610](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39014710610), and passed in 29 minutes in [38973259412](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38973259412). The last two are both #11741: it passed on a 2026-10-16 master base and failed on a 2026-10-17 base.

**What happens if it fails during the release.**

- The GitHub Release and the archives are already published. So are the `v0.8.6`, `latest`, `v0.8.6-debian` and `debian` images, which repackage the smoke-tested archives and include arm64.
- No later job needs `docker-matrix`. Crates, Scoop, AUR and the announcements need only `publish`.
- A failed multi-platform build pushes nothing for that variant. Neither architecture gets `dist-v0.8.6`, and the floating `dist` tag stays on v0.8.5. The other variants still publish.
- The Release Stable run ends red.

**A second risk in the same job.** The `all-features` variant (`Containerfile`, amd64 only) took 41 to 64 minutes on recent PR runs with a warm cache, including 62 minutes on #11347's head in 39040526108. `docker-publish.yml` gives it 60 minutes and no cache.

**Today's manual dispatch is not a safe dry run.** `docker-publish.yml`'s `workflow_dispatch` has no inputs and always pushes and signs. Dispatched on master before the version bump, it would push unreleased code under the `*-v0.8.5` pinned tags and move every floating tag.

**Fix routes.**

1. **Bound the memory in `docker-publish.yml`, the way #11347 does for the archive build.** A one-file change is drafted and can open as a PR once #11347 merges, because it uses #11347's `scripts/ci/dist_runner_memory.sh`:
   - On variants that build `linux/arm64`, run `dist_runner_memory.sh prepare` before the build and `cleanup` after it. The cleanup reports any kernel OOM kills. Also set Buildx `max-parallelism = 1`, so the amd64 and arm64 links never overlap.
   - Set `timeout-minutes: 120` on every variant.
   - Add `workflow_dispatch` inputs `release_ref`, `stems` (comma-separated variant names) and `push`. `push` defaults to false, so a manual run is a dry run unless asked. `workflow_call` gets `push` with default true, so Release Stable still publishes.
   - It applies cleanly to master `3f2f028b0f`, to #11347's head, and on top of #11741's version of the file.
   - The jobs run the script from the checked-out `release_ref`. A later rebuild of `v0.8.6` with this workflow therefore needs #11347 in the tag.
2. **Thin LTO for the image.** #11741 adds `ZEROCLAW_RELEASE_LTO` and `ZEROCLAW_RELEASE_CODEGEN_UNITS` build args to the `Dockerfile`, and `docker-publish.yml` forwards per-variant `lto` and `codegen_units` values from `dev/ci/docker-tags.toml`. #11741 sets thin LTO only for its new `dist-broad` variant. Setting `lto = "thin"` on `dist` would avoid the fat-LTO link. Two trade-offs: the setting covers both architectures of the multi-platform build unless the build is split by platform, and the image binary would no longer use the release archive's profile.
3. **A larger runner.** `docker-image-pr.yml` already sends the Alpine arm64 build to the 32 GB `blacksmith-8vcpu-ubuntu-2404` runner, and the same `runs-on` expression would work for the variants that build arm64. This one needs a maintainer decision: no job that pushes images or signs with OIDC runs on Blacksmith today.

Raised on #11221 and #11347 in review. Related: #11741.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Before the v0.8.6 Release Stable dispatch, a non-publishing run of the workflow Release Stable calls builds `dist` for both architectures and `all-features` within the job limit, and the run is linked here. Or a maintainer records here the decision to release without the `dist` image.
- [ ] `dist-v0.8.6` is on GHCR for amd64 and arm64, from the release run or from a rebuild of the `v0.8.6` tag that publishes only `dist`. `docker buildx imagetools inspect` shows both platforms and `cosign verify` passes.
- [ ] Until it is published, the v0.8.6 release notes say the `dist` image is missing.
- [ ] A manual dispatch of `docker-publish.yml` pushes and signs only when asked to.

### Likely files or areas

- `.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml`
- `scripts/ci/dist_runner_memory.sh` (added by #11347)
- `Dockerfile`, `dev/ci/docker-tags.toml` and its generator `xtask/src/generate/docker_tags.rs` (route 2)
- `.github/workflows/release-stable-manual.yml` (`docker-matrix`)
- `docs/book/src/maintainers/release-runbook.md` (the failure steps below)

### Contributor fit

maintainer-scoped task, not yet ready for pickup labels

### Mentor, reviewer, or contact

@JordanTheJet. Review by `.github/**` CODEOWNERS (@Audacity88, @tidux, @JordanTheJet).

### Risk notes

- This workflow pushes images and signs them with OIDC. Review the push and signing conditions closely: one mistake publishes from a dry run, the other publishes unsigned images.
- Route 1 depends on #11347 for the script. If #11347 slips, copy the script in or wait.
- Route 2 changes the image binary's build profile. The archives are unaffected.
- Route 3 moves a publishing and signing job to a third-party runner.
- If the leg fails during the release:
  - Re-run the failed jobs only for a transient error (registry, network, signing transparency log).
  - For `ResourceExhausted`, an OOM kill or a timeout, do not re-run as is. Land a fix first.
  - Then, with route 1, rebuild only `dist` from the tag: `gh workflow run docker-publish.yml --ref master -f release_ref=v0.8.6 -f stems=dist -f push=true`. This needs #11347 in the tag. Otherwise use route 3 for the rebuild.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
Phase 3: The Gateway. Separate the web surface from the agent core so the gateway is optional and can restart independently.

Source of truth: [#7432 - v0.9.0 gateway](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432#v090-gateway), including existing issues/PRs, missing work, sequencing, and acceptance evidence.

Deliverables: agree the full core IPC contract first; finish the supported local IPC server; ship standalone zeroclaw-gw; migrate vendor webhook behavior into channel plugins; and have Tauri package and manage both processes.

Completion requires a core artifact without web assets or HTTP server code, a working IPC-connected gateway, core/channel operation when the gateway is absent, and demonstrated two-process desktop lifecycle. Existing OIDC, principal-isolation, and ZeroRelay work must integrate with this boundary. WATI is already retired. Feature acceptance and normal review/CI/release holds still apply.

issues.body:
## Purpose

This tracker is the source of truth for completing the remaining **Phase 2 runtime work in v0.8.6** and **Phase 3 gateway separation in v0.9.0** from [RFC #5574](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/5574).

It owns the deliverable map, remaining gaps, sequencing, and release-completion evidence. The [v0.8.6 milestone](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/milestone/31) and [v0.9.0 milestone](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/milestone/11) provide release assignment views. Existing implementation trackers, especially #8850, retain their detailed work lists; link them here instead of opening duplicate program trackers.

This revises the earlier fixes-only description of v0.8.6 to include the remaining Phase 2 work alongside compatible fixes. v0.9.0 is centered on separating the web surface from the agent core. Existing authentication, principal-isolation, security, and ZeroRelay work must integrate with that boundary.

## Evidence and scope

Audit date: 2026-09-18. Source baseline: [core master ecc0c30c6b](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/tree/ecc0c30c6b58c61914b665d51887870e008f34b0), live issue/PR states, and the official plugin repository.

“Landed” below means the named implementation was merged and/or is present in the inspected source. It does not certify the complete release acceptance scenario. No release-artifact or live-service acceptance test was run for this planning audit. All delivery checkboxes remain open until their acceptance evidence is attached.

Delivery-issue pass: 2026-09-20, checked against [core master a7dad4ae5c](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/tree/a7dad4ae5c0fa1b24996f6d94e07251edf11880b) and the live open-issue inventory. The uncovered work now has 12 focused sub-issues: seven assigned to v0.8.6 and five to v0.9.0. Each has acceptance criteria and links to the relevant existing work. `status:accepted` records the agreed delivery scope; it does not ratify an unresolved design or approve an implementation. Native blocking relationships record the explicit dependencies between these new issues.

The maintained [FND-001](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/master/docs/book/src/foundations/fnd-001-intentional-architecture.md), [ADR-006](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/master/docs/book/src/architecture/decisions/ADR-006-runtime-channel-plugins.md), [ADR-007](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/master/docs/book/src/architecture/decisions/ADR-007-gateway-extraction.md), and [ADR-009](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/master/docs/book/src/architecture/decisions/ADR-009-wit-wasmtime-plugin-execution.md) qualify the older RFC excerpts:

- The accepted plugin execution backend is direct Wasmtime with WIT components. Extism was superseded by ADR-009.
- WATI was retired by #9571 and removed from FND-001's migration target. It is not a remaining channel deliverable.
- A `zeroclaw-gateway` crate and local daemon RPC already exist. A standalone `zeroclaw-gw` process and its complete supported IPC boundary do not.
- The current IPC endpoint is `<data_dir>/daemon.sock` on Unix and a data-directory-derived named pipe on Windows. The future `zeroclaw-kernel`, `ipc` feature, and `kernel.sock` names in the old text need an explicit mapping to the current implementation; they are not existing components.
- This plan does not require deleting all of `zeroclaw-runtime` before the gateway can be separated.

## v0.8.6 runtime

Theme: formalize a clean agent runtime and let users install optional capabilities without rebuilding ZeroClaw.

| Deliverable | Existing work and verified state | Remaining work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **D1: Clean runtime composition boundary** | #5559 landed the workspace split; #7430 landed `DaemonRegistry`. Current `daemon/registry.rs` registers subsystem starters. The old #5618 issue is closed as not planned, so its state alone is not delivery evidence. | Define and finish the public runtime/registry composition contract, or record the reviewed equivalent of the RFC sketch. Move concrete provider/tool/channel construction to the owning composition layer. Runtime still depends on `zeroclaw-tools` and constructs concrete tools. Prove independent runtime use and a thin executable entry point. **Delivery: #10993**, with existing channel dependency work in #6864. |
| **D2: WASM execution bridge** | #8368 landed the Wasmtime component host; #10146 activates logical channel instances; #9582 governs tool HTTP egress; #10750 governs channel HTTP egress. ADR-009 owns the accepted backend design. | Complete the supported release-artifact backend/permission/configuration path and its end-to-end proof. #8863 supplies the still-open WebSocket capability needed by Discord and declares #8923 as its prerequisite. The existence of a host adapter does not prove every channel's networking or lifecycle is supported. **Delivery: #10994** (supported artifact) and **#10999** (Discord acceptance). |
| **D3: Registry client and package lifecycle** | #8264 landed registry search and install-by-name. Current `src/plugin_registry.rs` reads the official JSON registry, resolves versions, downloads archives, and checks provided hashes. `PluginHost` applies the configured manifest signature policy. CLI list/search/install/remove/info/migrate exist. #7333 was closed unmerged; #8264 is the landed implementation. | `plugin update` is absent from the current command enum. Define update/rollback and trust/compatibility behavior. Existing open work: #9584 grant ceremony, #10746 install load-verification, #10752 info/list load verdicts (depends on #10746), #10162 incomplete install/config seeding, and #9624 host/registry WIT compatibility. **New delivery issues: #10995** (update/rollback) and **#10996** (channel-instance configuration/grants). |
| **D4: Plugin installation during onboarding** | #9009 owns the broader operator onboarding program. Current Quickstart configures agents and channels. | Add an explicit onboarding-to-registry install/configure/activate flow that works from a downloaded binary without Cargo. **Delivery: #10997**; no implementation PR for the complete flow was found in the audit. Reconcile the original `zeroclaw onboard` command wording with the maintained CLI/Quickstart interface. |
| **D5: Core tools only in the default runtime** | #8850 is the existing optional-channel/tool migration tracker. Historical #5617 was closed with a “requirements have shifted” comment; its associated #5566 PR was closed unmerged. | Reconfirm the core tool set and move optional capability construction out of the default runtime. Current `all_tools_with_runtime` still builds cron, scheduling, Pushover, calculator, weather, canvas, and other tools beyond the RFC list. **Delivery: #10998**, including the focused composition slice and binary-size proof under #8850. |

### Runtime implementation PRs

PR states below were checked on 2026-09-18. Each link identifies the slice it supplies; the phase acceptance criteria still require the complete user-facing outcome.

| Deliverable | PRs to follow | Coverage and missing PRs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **D1: Runtime composition** | Merged: [PR #5559: workspace split](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/5559); [PR #7430: daemon registry](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/7430). Open supporting extraction: [PR #10557: extract cron into its own crate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10557). | Cron extraction reduces the holding crate, but does not complete the generic runtime composition contract. **No open PR completing the full D1 boundary was found.** |
| **D2: WASM execution and channel support** | Merged: [PR #8368: Wasmtime component host](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8368); [PR #10146: activate channel instances](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10146); [PR #9582: govern tool HTTP egress](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9582); [PR #10750: govern channel HTTP egress](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10750). Open drafts for the Discord transport path: [PR #9142: named TLS profiles](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9142); [PR #8923: TCP and STARTTLS](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8923); [PR #8863: channel WebSocket capability](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8863). | The execution foundations are present. The transport drafts, release backend/configuration choices, compatible Discord package publication, and end-to-end artifact proof remain. |
| **D3: Registry and package lifecycle** | Merged: [PR #8264: registry search and install by name](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8264). Open: [PR #9584: install/list egress-grant ceremony](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9584); [PR #10746: load-verify installation](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10746); [PR #10752: report info/list load verdicts](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10752). Merged supporting fix: [PR #11107: escape apostrophes in egress remedy commands](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11107), preserving the complete grant list as one shell argument. | These cover install usability and verification. **No open PR implementing the missing plugin-update/rollback command was found.** Channel-only grant seeding is explicitly outside #9584's scope. |
| **D4: Install plugins during onboarding** | **No dedicated open implementation PR found.** Existing coordination: #9009 and #8850. | Link the eventual install/configure/activate onboarding PR here; general onboarding changes alone do not meet D4. |
| **D5: Minimal core tools** | **No open PR delivering the complete core-only runtime tool set was found.** Existing coordination: #8850; historical #5617. | A focused tool-composition/packaging PR and binary-size evidence are still required. |

**Declared prerequisite order:**

- [PR #10746: install verification](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10746) precedes [PR #10752: load verdicts](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10752).
- [PR #9142: named TLS profiles](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9142) precedes [PR #8923: TCP/STARTTLS](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8923), which precedes [PR #8863: WebSocket capability](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8863).
- #9142 still cites [PR #8857: scoped secrets and encrypted state](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8857), which is **closed unmerged**. Its [closure record](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8857#issuecomment-5681552958) identifies merged [PR #9128: scoped tool secret service](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9128) and [PR #9129: channel config services](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9129) as the scoped-secrets replacement; the encrypted-state portion was deferred. Its other declared foundation, [PR #9137: shared egress policy](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9137), is merged. Reconcile that stale prerequisite before treating the transport chain as ready.

These dependency links come from the current PR descriptions and the verified predecessor dispositions. They do not certify that each branch has already incorporated the latest predecessor revision.

### Runtime gaps to close

- [ ] **R1: Runtime API and ownership.** #10993; supporting channel dependency cleanup remains in #6864. Finish D1 with explicit injection boundaries, dependency checks, and an independently usable runtime; incorporate the landed `DaemonRegistry` instead of treating it as missing.
- [ ] **R2: Supported plugin distribution.** #10994. Select and verify the execution backend for each shipped target and record the loading, grants, signature, and compatibility decisions. The current Cargo default feature set omits the plugin host. #8135 is still an unaccepted RFC with older Extism assumptions; citing it does not approve a default-on policy change.
- [ ] **R3: Registry update and install completeness.** #10995 (update/rollback) and #10996 (channel-instance configuration/grants), alongside existing #10162 (install recovery) and #9624 (compatibility). Finish the relevant #8850 install/verification work and define the missing update/rollback command. Include channel-instance grant/config seeding; #9584 explicitly excludes channel-only grant seeding.
- [ ] **R4: Install-from-onboarding experience.** #10997, coordinated with #9009/#8850. Provide a focused implementation under the existing onboarding/plugin programs and prove the complete user flow without a Rust toolchain.
- [ ] **R5: Minimal core and size evidence.** #10998. Agree the retained core tools, implement the optional-tool boundary, and record binary size for named release targets/profiles in release notes. Reuse #8850; historical issue closure is not proof of this criterion.
- [ ] **R6: Discord acceptance.** #10999. The official plugin repository contains [Discord source](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw-plugins/tree/main/plugins/discord), but its README requires host WebSocket capability. #8863 is open, that host feature is absent from the inspected master, and the [official registry index](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw-plugins/blob/main/registry.json) has no Discord entry. Publish and verify the compatible package and demonstrate install, configuration, inbound delivery, and replies from the supported release binary. Reconcile the original `channel-discord` example with the actual package name `discord`.

- **2026-10-16 v0.8.6 scope decision (@JordanTheJet):** R1 and R6 are deferred from v0.8.6 to the next release; neither is complete. R1 (#10993): #11092 landed the composition contract, and #11174 and #11187 continue and may still land in v0.8.6 if their reviews clear, but they do not complete R1. The runtime still depends on `zeroclaw-tools` and constructs concrete tools, so the dependency-boundary criterion has not started. #10557 (cron extraction) is deferred separately. R6 (#10999): the Discord plugin source is merged in zeroclaw-plugins, but no compatible package is published in the registry; a compatible-WIT registry promotion and an install, configuration, inbound and reply run from a release binary remain. v0.8.6 keeps R2, R3, R4 and R5 in scope.

The RFC core-tool baseline is `shell`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `file_edit`, `git_operations`, `glob_search`, `content_search`, `memory_recall`, `memory_store`, `memory_forget`, and `web_fetch`. Any revised set needs a recorded rationale before D5 is marked complete.

**Runtime acceptance:** an independently usable runtime with the agreed dependency boundary; a real Rust/WIT tool plugin executing under the shipped host; Discord plugin installation and operation without recompilation; onboarding that installs plugins without Cargo; and published size measurements for the supported runtime artifact. A component unit test or a source directory alone does not establish these product outcomes.

## v0.9.0 gateway

Theme: make the web surface a separate, optional process that can be omitted or restarted without interrupting healthy agent execution.

| Deliverable | Existing work and verified state | Remaining work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **D1: Agreed kernel IPC contract** | [RPC socket documentation](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/master/docs/book/src/architecture/rpc-socket.md), `zeroclaw-api/src/jsonrpc.rs`, and the runtime RPC code define an existing NDJSON/JSON-RPC transport. The gateway also generates a partial OpenAPI 3.1 document in `openapi.rs`. #9133 recorded ADR-007; #8691 remains its decision-record home. | Agree the complete core-to-gateway contract for messages/streams, sessions, installed plugins, status, memory, and cron, including identity, permissions, version negotiation, cancellation, errors, reconnect, and lifecycle. Explicitly resolve how the requested OpenAPI 3.1 specification relates to existing non-HTTP JSON-RPC and the no-HTTP-server-in-core success criterion. **Design delivery: #11000**, with the review and decision linked through #8691/ADR-007 before dependent implementation. |
| **D2: Supported local IPC server** | `rpc/local.rs` already implements Unix sockets and Windows named pipes. Existing session/turn methods and protocol initialization are useful foundations. #8289/#7141 and open #10259 supply related principal/authentication work. | Complete the D1 method and lifecycle coverage for an external gateway; record the core owner/feature/endpoint mapping; prove isolation, authentication, version mismatch, cancellation, and reconnection on supported platforms. Existing local transport is partial delivery, not a reason to write a second server. **Delivery: #11001**, after #11000's contract review. |
| **D3: Standalone zeroclaw-gw** | `zeroclaw-gateway` already exists. ADR-007 describes the intended process boundary. Its current manifest still directly depends on `zeroclaw-runtime` and `zeroclaw-channels`; the daemon starts it through an in-process registry callback. PR #11041 supplies the dashboard/OpenAPI Nix package and NixOS module wiring as a packaging slice; it does not provide the standalone gateway process or IPC boundary. | Build and ship the standalone executable as an IPC client, move web assets and the HTTP server into its release artifact, replace process-local runtime access, and prove operation/restart/removal independently of the core. **Delivery: #11002**; no existing PR completing this extraction was found in the audit. |
| **D4: Channel-owned webhook behavior** | #8862 and #8949 are merged; generic plugin ingress and typed challenge replies are in current source. #8850 owns plugin migration. #8586 owns a narrower webhook-dispatch cleanup and explicitly does not implement the plugin migration. | Finish WhatsApp Cloud, Linq, Nextcloud Talk, and Gmail migrations with vendor-owned parsing/authentication, challenge replies, media, and delivery parity. Carry plugin route registration and dispatch across IPC: today's gateway receives an in-process `Arc<PluginWebhookRegistry>`. WATI is excluded because it was removed. **Cross-process delivery: #11003**; #8850 retains vendor migration ownership. |
| **D5: Tauri starts both processes** | #8708 and #9032 are merged, providing earlier sidecar packaging and dashboard embedding work. Current desktop code supervises the existing daemon/gateway product. | Package and supervise the separate core and `zeroclaw-gw` executables: startup ordering, readiness, authentication, compatible versions, gateway restart, coordinated shutdown, and upgrades. **Delivery: #11004**, after #11002; no implementation PR for the final two-process arrangement was found in the audit. |

### Gateway implementation PRs

| Deliverable | PRs to follow | Coverage and missing PRs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **D1: IPC contract** | Merged design record: [PR #9133: record gateway process and channel-plugin targets](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9133). | **No open PR completing the full gateway IPC contract was found.** The remaining design belongs with #8691 and ADR-007. |
| **D2: Local IPC parity and authority** | Open: [PR #10259: authenticated RPC principals](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10259). Open draft: [PR #10274: gateway route-layer principal consumption](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10274). | These are supporting authentication slices. **No single PR completing gateway IPC method/lifecycle parity was found.** The existing socket/pipe server is already present. |
| **D3: Standalone gateway** | **No standalone `zeroclaw-gw` extraction PR found.** Supporting viewer-lifetime work: [PR #10538: preserve a turn after WebSocket disconnect](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10538) and [PR #9002: gateway session lifecycle and reconnect](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9002), both open. | The two viewer-lifetime PRs overlap and need scope reconciliation. Neither implements the separate executable, removes direct runtime dependencies, or proves gateway-process fault isolation. |
| **D4: Channel webhooks across IPC** | Merged: [PR #8862: generic plugin webhook ingress](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8862); [PR #8949: typed plugin challenge replies](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8949). | **No verified open PR completing the required vendor migrations and cross-process webhook registration/dispatch was found.** Continue through #8850; #8586 remains a narrower dispatch-cleanup issue. |
| **D5: Two-process desktop** | Merged predecessors: [PR #8708: desktop sidecar packaging](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/8708); [PR #9032: embed dashboard in the release sidecar](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9032). | **No open PR implementing final core-plus-gateway packaging and supervision was found.** Link that implementation after D1-D3 establish the supported process boundary. |

### Gateway gaps to close

- [ ] **G1: D1 design record.** #11000. Review the full IPC contract and its relationship to existing JSON-RPC before the process extraction is implemented. Link the decision through #8691 and ADR-007.
- [ ] **G2: IPC parity and authority.** #11001, blocked by #11000. Complete D2 for every supported gateway operation; keep domain state and authorization in the core and make the gateway a client.
- [ ] **G3: Binary and dependency separation.** #11002, blocked by #11000/#11001. Deliver D3, including release packaging and evidence that the core artifact contains no web assets or HTTP server implementation. Resolve any IPC transport conflict with that criterion in G1.
- [ ] **G4: Vendor webhook migration.** #11003 owns IPC registration/dispatch; #8850 retains the four vendor migrations. Finish D4 under #8850 with per-channel parity evidence and the cross-process registration/dispatch contract.
- [ ] **G5: Desktop integration.** #11004, blocked by #11002. Finish D5 and attach installer/startup/restart/upgrade evidence for the supported desktop platforms.

**Gateway acceptance:** `zeroclaw-gw` starts and serves the dashboard through the agreed local IPC contract; the core release artifact has no web assets or HTTP server code; stopping, restarting, or removing the gateway leaves healthy agent execution and supported channel plugins working; vendor webhook behavior lives in the channel plugins; and Tauri starts and manages both binaries.

#7759, #9002, and #10538 address viewer-disconnect/turn-lifetime behavior and are supporting work. They do not establish separate-process fault isolation. OIDC/principal work (#8289, #8290, #10259, #10274) and ZeroRelay (#8358) must be reconciled with G1/G2 rather than treated as proof of gateway extraction.

## Delivery order and routing

1. Close the runtime gaps through #10993–#10999 and the existing plugin/onboarding programs. #10998 depends on #10993; #10997 depends on #10996; #10999 depends on #10994/#10996 and the existing host WebSocket PR chain. The gateway IPC design (#11000) can proceed alongside this work.
2. Agree G1 in #11000, complete local IPC coverage in #11001, and deliver the standalone gateway in #11002. #11003 carries plugin webhooks over the reviewed IPC boundary. D4's channel migrations remain under #8850 and can proceed where their host and ingress contracts are ready.
3. Finish desktop integration in #11004 after #11002 supplies the separate executable and supported IPC boundary.
4. Attach release-artifact and end-to-end evidence before closing either phase.

Feature scope must be accepted before new milestone scheduling. Native reviews and checks remain the merge authority; normal compatible changes can merge once those requirements pass. Breaking changes keep `breaking-change` and the recorded `do-not-merge` release hold until the appropriate window and current validation permit it. This tracker does not ratify an open RFC or approve an implementation.

The target phase is recorded above. Linked work may currently be assigned to an earlier fix release, a later compatibility window, or no milestone; reconcile those assignments with scope and compatibility before claiming a complete release queue. In particular, #9584 and #10162 currently sit in v0.9.0 even though they contribute to the Phase 2 closeout, while #10746/#10752/#8863 are unassigned. This audit does not silently convert their PR review states into approval.

milestone.description:
Phase 3: The Gateway. Separate the web surface from the agent core so the gateway is optional and can restart independently.

Source of truth: [#7432 - v0.9.0 gateway](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432#v090-gateway), including existing issues/PRs, missing work, sequencing, and acceptance evidence.

issues.body:
### Affected component

tooling/ci

### Severity

S3 - minor issue

### Current behavior

`codex_cli::tests::codex_cli_resolves_relative_working_directory_under_workspace` (`crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/codex_cli.rs`, added in #7967) sets the process-wide `PATH` to an empty temporary directory so that `codex` deterministically fails to resolve, and restores it on drop. Its `SAFETY` comment says it "is intended to run with `--test-threads=1`", but nothing enforces that. Under the default parallel `cargo test`, every other test in the `zeroclaw-tools` lib binary that resolves an executable through `PATH` during that window fails.

At `4719fca3e5` (upstream master `cdefa0d0a6` plus #11822, which does not touch `zeroclaw-tools`), `cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib` failed in 3 of 4 runs, each time in different tests:

```
run 1: FAILED. 2100 passed; 4 failed
  browser::tests::computer_use_dispatch_does_not_forward_path_and_writes_local_target
  browser::tests::computer_use_dispatch_passes_through_empty_string_path
  browser::tests::computer_use_dispatch_fails_closed_on_malformed_screenshot_response
  browser::tests::computer_use_dispatch_writes_validated_png_locally_without_forwarding_path
run 2: ok. 2104 passed; 0 failed
run 3: FAILED. 2103 passed; 1 failed
  coding_agent_budget_tests::coding_agent_wrappers_charge_one_action_each
  (panicked at coding_agent_budget_tests.rs:65: `which::which("true").expect("installed true executable")`)
run 4: FAILED. 2102 passed; 2 failed
  content_search::tests::content_search_count_mode
  content_search::tests::content_search_context_lines
```

Skipping only this test removes the failures (6 of 6 runs passed):

```
$ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib -- --skip codex_cli_resolves_relative_working_directory_under_workspace
test result: ok. 2103 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 1 filtered out
```

`--test-threads=1` also passes (2092 passed at `329e66f763`).

CI is not affected: it runs `cargo nextest`, which runs each test in its own process, so the `PATH` change does not leak. The failure shows up for contributors running plain `cargo test`, which `AGENTS.md` lists as the standard validation command.

### Expected behavior

`cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib` passes reliably with the default test threads, and no test mutates process-global environment that other tests in the same binary depend on.

Options (`#[serial]` alone is not enough: `zeroclaw-tools` already depends on `serial_test`, but it only orders tests that also carry `#[serial]`, and the affected tests are unrelated and widespread):

- Give the coding-CLI command resolution a test seam (an explicit search path or a resolver) so the test can force "not found" without touching `PATH`.
- Assert only the property under test ("relative `working_directory` resolves inside the workspace, not 'outside the workspace'") and accept either a not-found error or a launch result, so `PATH` need not change.
- Move the test into its own integration-test binary or subprocess so the mutation cannot leak.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Linux, from the repo root: `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib`, repeated 3 or 4 times.
2. Some runs fail in tests that resolve executables through `PATH` (for example `which::which("true")` in `coding_agent_budget_tests`, plus `content_search` and browser tests), and the failing set changes between runs.
3. Repeat with `-- --skip codex_cli_resolves_relative_working_directory_under_workspace`; every run passes.

### Impact

Contributors running the documented `cargo test` see random, unrelated failures in `zeroclaw-tools`, which costs triage time and erodes trust in local validation (seen while validating #11822). There is no CI or runtime impact.

### Logs / stack traces

```
thread 'coding_agent_budget_tests::coding_agent_wrappers_charge_one_action_each' panicked at crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/coding_agent_budget_tests.rs:65:43
thread 'content_search::tests::content_search_count_mode' panicked at crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/content_search.rs:1199:9
thread 'browser::tests::computer_use_dispatch_fails_closed_on_malformed_screenshot_response' panicked at crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/browser.rs:4658:13
```

### ZeroClaw version

master `cdefa0d0a6` (v0.8.5-571), observed at `4719fca3e5` (#11822 head)

### Rust version

1.98.0

### Operating system

Linux

### Regression?

Unknown

issues.body:
### Affected component

security/sandbox

### Severity

S2 - degraded behavior

### Current behavior

Under the `ShellDialect::WindowsCmd` dialect, `split_unquoted_segments` (`crates/zeroclaw-config/src/policy.rs`) does not model `cmd.exe` parenthesized blocks. A grouped command stays glued to `(`, so the classifiers see `(del` instead of `del`, and the closing `)` sticks to the last word.

Observed at `4719fca3e5` (upstream master `cdefa0d0a6` plus #11822, which leaves `cmd.exe` splitting unchanged on purpose), evaluated with the `WindowsCmd` dialect:

| Command (`cmd.exe` dialect) | Result | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `del /q build` | risk: `High` | `High` |
| `(del /q build)` | risk: `Low` | `High` |
| `(type C:\Windows\win.ini)` | path scan: `Some("C:\Windows\win.ini)")` | `Some("C:\Windows\win.ini")` |
| `split_unquoted_segments("(type C:\Windows\win.ini)")` | `["(type C:\Windows\win.ini)"]` | `["type C:\Windows\win.ini"]` |
| `(git status)` (default strict policy) | rejected | rejected (correct) |

Risk used a `*` allowlist with `block_high_risk_commands = false`. The path scan used `forbidden_paths` containing the default `C:\Windows`.

Forbidden paths inside a block are still refused (just reported with a trailing `)`), and the strict allowlist rejects the `(git` executable. The functional gap is risk classification: wrapping a high-risk command in parentheses lowers its rating from High to Low.

### Expected behavior

`cmd.exe` parenthesized blocks are segment boundaries for the `WindowsCmd` dialect, so commands inside them are path-scanned and risk-classified as their own segments. This is the `cmd.exe` counterpart of #11822, which did this for POSIX `(...)`, `$(...)`, `<(...)`, `>(...)`, and backticks and deliberately left `cmd.exe` alone.

`cmd.exe` rules differ from POSIX and need their own handling:

- `(` opens a block at command position and after `if ...`, `else`, and `for ... do`.
- `)` closes a block only while one is open. At depth 0 it is an ordinary character (`echo a)` prints `a)`).
- `^(` and `^)` are caret-escaped literals. The strict allowlist already rejects `^` through `contains_unmodeled_shell_word_expansion`, but the risk and path scans still see it.
- No backtick or `$(` substitution exists.

The strict allowlist currently rejects `(git status)` only because the executable becomes `(git`. If splitting changes that, keep the rejection explicit, as #11822 does for POSIX with an unquoted-paren guard.

### Steps to reproduce

1. With `allowed_commands = ["*"]` and `block_high_risk_commands = false`, call `command_risk_level_for_shell("(del /q build)", ShellDialect::WindowsCmd)`; it returns `Low`, while `del /q build` returns `High`.
2. With `forbidden_paths` containing `C:\Windows`, call `forbidden_path_argument_for_shell("(type C:\\Windows\\win.ini)", ShellDialect::WindowsCmd)`; it returns `Some("C:\\Windows\\win.ini)")`.

### Impact

Native Windows hosts running the shell tool under `cmd.exe`. A model-authored command can lower its own risk rating by wrapping it in parentheses, which under Supervised autonomy with a permissive allowlist skips the approval a High rating would require. The trailing `)` in path reports is cosmetic. The execution sandbox remains the real boundary. Found while working on #11822.

### Logs / stack traces

_No response_

### ZeroClaw version

master `cdefa0d0a6` (v0.8.5-571), observed at `4719fca3e5` (#11822 head)

### Rust version

1.98.0

### Operating system

Linux host evaluating the `WindowsCmd` dialect; affects native Windows `cmd.exe` execution

### Regression?

No, first-time setup

- [x] I reproduced this on the latest master branch or latest release.
- [x] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

issues.body:
### Affected component

security/sandbox

### Severity

S2 - degraded behavior

### Current behavior

The POSIX shell command scanner (`split_unquoted_segments` in `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/policy.rs`) skips heredoc bodies entirely. That is correct for a quoted delimiter (`<<'EOF'`), where the body is literal. With an unquoted delimiter (`<<EOF`), the shell performs command substitution in the body, so `$(...)` and backticks there run as commands. The scanner never sees them:

- The workspace path scan (`forbidden_path_argument*`) misses forbidden paths inside a body substitution.
- `command_risk_level` misses high-risk commands inside a body substitution.

Observed at `4719fca3e5` (upstream master `cdefa0d0a6` plus #11822, which does not change heredoc handling), with `forbidden_paths = ["/dev", "/etc"]`, and `allowed_commands = ["*"]`, `block_high_risk_commands = false` for the risk rows:

| Command (POSIX dialect) | Result | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `cat <<EOF` / `$(cat /etc/passwd)` / `EOF` | path scan: `None` | `Some("/etc/passwd")` |
| `cat <<EOF` / `` `cat /etc/passwd` `` / `EOF` | path scan: `None` | `Some("/etc/passwd")` |
| `cat <<EOF` / `$(rm -rf ./build)` / `EOF` | risk: `Low` | `High` |
| `cat <<'EOF'` / `$(cat /etc/passwd)` / `EOF` | path scan: `None` | `None` (correct: quoted delimiter, body is literal) |

Bash confirms the difference:

```
$ bash -c 'cat <<EOF
$(echo SUBST-RAN)
EOF'
SUBST-RAN
$ bash -c "cat <<'EOF'
\$(echo SUBST-RAN)
EOF"
$(echo SUBST-RAN)
```

The strict allowlist is not affected: its raw-text guards (`contains_unquoted_shell_variable_expansion`, the backtick check) run on the whole command, including heredoc bodies, and reject `$(` and backticks before segment splitting matters. The gap is in the path scan and risk classification, which apply in every mode, and matters most with a `*` allowlist and high-risk blocking off, where risk decides whether Supervised autonomy asks for approval.

### Expected behavior

For an unquoted heredoc delimiter, command substitutions (`$(...)`, `` `...` ``) in the body are scanned and risk-classified as their own segments, the same way #11822 handles substitutions elsewhere. Plain body text stays data and is not scanned as commands (`forbidden_path_argument_ignores_tilde_non_path_and_heredoc_body` pins that and should keep passing). Quoted-delimiter bodies (`<<'EOF'`, `<<"EOF"`, `<<\EOF`) stay fully literal.

A possible approach: `split_unquoted_segments` already strips quotes from the delimiter word. Record whether the delimiter was quoted, and for unquoted delimiters run the body through the same substitution-frame handling #11822 added, emitting only the substitution contents as segments.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a `SecurityPolicy` with `forbidden_paths = ["/dev", "/etc"]` (the defaults include both).
2. Call `forbidden_path_argument_for_shell("cat <<EOF\n$(cat /etc/passwd)\nEOF", ShellDialect::Posix)`; it returns `None`.
3. With `allowed_commands = ["*"]` and `block_high_risk_commands = false`, call `command_risk_level_for_shell("cat <<EOF\n$(rm -rf ./build)\nEOF", ShellDialect::Posix)`; it returns `Low`.

### Impact

A defense-in-depth gap in the static command scan, not in the execution sandbox, which remains the real boundary. A model-authored command can wrap a high-risk command or a forbidden-path read in an unquoted heredoc body, and neither the path scan nor the risk classifier sees it. Under a permissive `*` allowlist with Supervised autonomy, that skips the approval prompt the same command would otherwise get. Found while working on #11822; left out of that PR to keep its scope to substitution boundaries.

### Logs / stack traces

_No response_

### ZeroClaw version

master `cdefa0d0a6` (v0.8.5-571), observed at `4719fca3e5` (#11822 head)

### Rust version

1.98.0

### Operating system

Linux

No, first-time setup

### Task

Make the 23 `late_tool_search_*` tests in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/r5_namespace_tests.rs` opt-in outside the CI step that prepares their fixture receipt.

### Context

These tests read a fixture receipt from `ZEROCLAW_LATE_TOOL_SEARCH_FIXTURE_RECEIPT` and `expect` it to be set (`r5_namespace_tests.rs`, around line 358). Only the runtime plugin job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` prepares that receipt, and the other CI jobs filter the tests out by name. A plain local `cargo test` or `cargo nextest run` that includes the runtime crate's lib tests with the plugin features therefore reports 23 panics ("explicit fixture receipt required") that say nothing about the code under test. Both reviewers of #11221 hit this when running the suite unfiltered.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Without the receipt variable, the 23 tests are skipped or ignored with a message that names the variable and the CI step that sets it, rather than panicking.
- [ ] The runtime plugin job still runs all 23 and still fails if any of them is missing or does not pass (its existing listing and pass checks in `ci.yml` keep working).
- [ ] The name filters in the other CI jobs are no longer needed, or a comment says why they stay.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add the missing explicit plugin update operation for #7432 R3 / Phase 2 D3.

### Problem statement

The current plugin CLI supports list, search, install, remove, info, and migrate, but has no update command. Re-running installation is not a defined update/rollback contract.

### Proposed solution

Specify and implement `zeroclaw plugin update` using the existing registry, version selection, trust policy, and load-admission path. Stage and verify a replacement before committing it, and preserve the working installation when an update fails. Define active-instance restart behavior and partial success when updating multiple plugins.

### Non-goals / out of scope

Another registry or installer; solving first-install recovery already owned by #10162; changing signature requirements or silently expanding grants.

### Alternatives considered

Reuse the existing implementation and extend its missing boundary; a parallel subsystem would create another source of truth.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Document command syntax, version-selection rules, no-update behavior, per-plugin results, exit status, and rollback guarantees.
- [ ] Resolve and verify packages through the canonical hash/signature/compatibility/admission path; incorporate #9624 and #10746 where applicable.
- [ ] Failed download, verification, admission, or replacement leaves the prior payload and configuration usable; interrupted updates have a documented recovery path.
- [ ] Preserve instance identities, configuration, secrets references, and grants; any additional permission requires the existing explicit consent mechanism.
- [ ] Tests exercise a successful update, rejection of an incompatible/untrusted package, interrupted replacement, and mixed results for multiple plugins.
- [ ] Link implementation and operator documentation to #7432 R3.

### Architecture impact

CLI, registry client, plugin installation state, and runtime activation. Coordinate with #10162, #10770, and #9624; #10746 provides installation load verification.

### Risk and rollback

Replacement can lose a working plugin or broaden privileges. Use staged verification and recoverable commit semantics, with a documented return to the prior package/version.

### Expected routing

Should attach to an existing roadmap/tracker issue

### Next decision surface

#7432 R3, v0.8.6. Review update/rollback and active-instance semantics before implementation.

### Breaking change?

No

### Data hygiene checks

- [x] I removed personal/sensitive data from examples, payloads, and logs.
- [x] I used neutral, project-focused wording and placeholders.

### Affected component

plugins

### Severity

S3 - minor issue

### Current behavior

When a channel plugin delivers a message from a sender outside the instance's peer group, the host drops it before any agent turn (correct) and writes one record:

```text
2026-10-17T07:47:30.378Z WARN Ignoring channel-plugin inbound from an unauthorized sender {"action": "reject", "category": "channel", "outcome": "failure"} {"channel_alias": "acceptance", "error_key": "plugin_channel_sender_denied", "ingress": "poll", "plugin": "discord"} {"channel": "plugin.acceptance", "channel_alias": "acceptance", "channel_type": "plugin"}
```

The record has no sender identity (`sender_is_authorized`, `crates/zeroclaw-plugins/src/wasm_channel.rs:814-837`). The built-in Discord channel logs the author in the same situation (`crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/discord/mod.rs:3205`):

```text
WARN ignoring message from unauthorized user {"author_id": "<user-id>"}
```

In my run the peer group held a different account ID from the one actually posting. The host rejected both test messages and the log could not say which ID to add; I had to read the channel over the REST API to find it.

### Expected behavior

The `plugin_channel_sender_denied` record carries the sender as the plugin reported it (bounded and escaped like other guest-supplied attributes), and ideally the config path that admits it (`external_peers` of the peer group whose `channel` is `plugin.<alias>`). The denial itself stays as it is.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
# A bound plugin channel instance plugin.<alias>, then:
zeroclaw config set peer_groups.<group>.channel plugin.<alias>
zeroclaw config set peer_groups.<group>.external_peers '["<id-a>"]'
zeroclaw daemon
# Post in the bound channel from an account whose ID is <id-b>
# Observe: no reply, and the record above with no sender
```

### Impact

Operators setting up a plugin channel's peer group for the first time. The usual mistake (wrong or outdated ID) is silent apart from a record that cannot tell them the right one.

### ZeroClaw version

v0.8.6 release-candidate build (61a2c95); code references are to current master

Ubuntu 24.04 (WSL2)

issues.body:
### Affected component

config/onboarding

### Severity

S2 - degraded behavior

### Current behavior

With a daemon running, `zeroclaw config set` of a plugin instance's settings (`plugins.entries.<key>.config.<name>`) or its egress grant (`plugins.entries.<key>.egress_hosts`) rewrites `config.toml` and reports success, but the running daemon never sees the change. Nothing says so.

Seen with the Discord channel plugin: after removing `*.discord.gg` from the instance's grant and restarting (gateway refused, as expected), I put the grant back on the running daemon:

```text
$ zeroclaw config set --no-interactive plugins.entries.<key>.egress_hosts ["*.discord.gg","discord.com"]
plugins.entries.<key>.egress_hosts updated.
```

The plugin kept being refused once a minute for the next five minutes:

```text
08:40:45.998Z WARN discord: gateway connect failed {... "raw": "{\"error\":\"destination-denied\",\"host\":\"gateway.discord.gg\",\"resume\":false}"}
08:40:45.998Z ERROR discord: gateway connection refused by the host; retrying every minute {... "raw": "{\"reason\":\"egress_denied\"}"}
... (same pair at 08:41:47, 08:42:52, 08:43:54, 08:44:56)
```

`POST /admin/reload` (same PID) applied it, and the gateway was READY about 3 s later.

Why:

- `config set` sends only agent paths to the daemon (`src/main.rs:11721`). Every other path is written with `set_prop_persistent` and `save_dirty` (`src/main.rs:11763-11764`). The daemon does not watch the file; it re-reads it only on reload or restart (`src/main.rs:9391-9394`).
- The plugin host is built to apply such edits live. Egress is resolved from the daemon's live config on every request (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/mod.rs:933-952`), and plugin config and secrets on every call (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/mod.rs:1001-1045`). The orchestrator passes the live handle to plugin channels (`crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs:17164-17170`). The plugin guide promises that a config plus credential rotation "is visible together on the next operation without daemon reload or channel reconstruction" (`docs/book/src/plugins/writing-a-channel-plugin.md:350-357`), and the Discord package's README says an edit "applies without a restart".
- The daemon already has a `config/set` RPC that publishes a new live revision (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/dispatch.rs:9263`). The CLI uses it only for `agents.*`.

`plugin install --channel-alias`, `plugin bind` and `plugin info` do say it ("A running daemon picks up plugin.<alias> after a restart or reload.", `src/main.rs:4734-4738`). `config set` prints only `updated.`

### Expected behavior

When a daemon owns the config, `config set` of `plugins.entries.*` goes through the daemon's `config/set`, as agent paths do, so the next egress check or `config.get` / `secrets.get` call sees the new value. If the CLI keeps writing those paths offline, it should at least say that a running daemon picks the change up after `POST /admin/reload` or a restart.

Note for whoever picks this up: routing through the daemon makes a grant or a public setting apply live, but not every credential. 10 of the 12 channel packages in the registry read their credential once in `configure()` and keep it (for example `load_config()` in zeroclaw-plugins `plugins/telegram/src/lib.rs`), so for them a rotated token still needs the instance rebuilt, which a reload does. Discord and Matrix read it at each use.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
zeroclaw plugin install discord --channel-alias main --egress declared
# set bot_token, channel_ids, the agent's channels and the peer group as the Discord docs describe
zeroclaw config set --no-interactive plugins.entries.<key>.egress_hosts '["discord.com"]'
zeroclaw daemon
# gateway connect refused once a minute (expected: *.discord.gg is not granted)

# in another terminal, with the daemon still running:
zeroclaw config set --no-interactive plugins.entries.<key>.egress_hosts '["*.discord.gg","discord.com"]'
# prints "updated."; the daemon keeps refusing the gateway every minute
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:<gateway-port>/admin/reload
# the gateway reaches READY within a few seconds
```

### Impact

Any operator who edits a plugin instance from the CLI while the daemon runs: grants, channel filters, tokens. The command reports success and the daemon keeps the old value until something reloads it, so it looks like the plugin ignored the change.

### ZeroClaw version

v0.8.6 release-candidate build (61a2c95); code references are to current master

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04 (WSL2)

### Regression?

No, first-time setup

### Related

#11329 (its acceptance template's "Grant restored" row says "without a restart" and names no way to apply the grant)

### Affected component

config/onboarding

### Severity

S3 - minor issue

### Current behavior

For a new provider, Quickstart prompts the fields in the order `model`, `auth_mode`, `api_key`, `uri` (`MODEL_PROVIDER_ESSENTIALS`, `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/quickstart/mod.rs:953`). Before the `model` prompt it fetches a live catalog and, when one comes back, turns the field into a picker (`src/main.rs:2293-2313`):

- The catalog call is `zeroclaw_runtime::quickstart::model_catalog(&chosen.kind)` (`src/main.rs:2300`), which passes no config (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/quickstart/mod.rs:2342-2350`). With no configured profile there is no `uri` to honour (`crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/catalog.rs:314`), so the provider is built against the family's default endpoint (`:352`).
- The picker is a `FuzzySelect` over the catalog entries (`src/main.rs:3318-3328`). It has no way to type a model that is not in the list. Free-text entry is used only when the catalog is empty or not live.

The `uri` the operator is about to enter is asked last, after the model is already chosen from someone else's list.

Seen on macOS with the `llamacpp` provider: another local server was answering on the llama.cpp default `127.0.0.1:8080`, so the picker listed that server's models. The intended server was at `http://127.0.0.1:18431/v1`, entered later at the `uri` prompt, and its model could not be selected or typed.

### Expected behavior

- Ask for `uri` (and credentials) before the model, and query the catalog at the endpoint the operator gave, or at the default only when `uri` is left empty.
- Let the picker accept a typed model ID (an "enter a model ID" entry or a free-text fallback), since catalogs can be incomplete or come from a different server.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
# Any server that answers /v1/models on 127.0.0.1:8080 (the llama.cpp default)
# Your real llama.cpp-compatible server on another port, e.g. 127.0.0.1:18431
zeroclaw quickstart
# Provider type: llama.cpp server (local) -> alias: default
# model: the picker lists the models of the server on :8080; no free-text entry
# api_key: (empty)
# uri: http://127.0.0.1:18431/v1
```

Workaround: pick any entry, finish Quickstart, then:

```bash
zeroclaw config set --no-interactive providers.models.llamacpp.default.model <model-id>
```

### Impact

Local and self-hosted provider families (llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM and other OpenAI-compatible servers) when the server is not at the family default. If nothing answers on the default port the picker is skipped and free text works, so the failure shows up only when something else is listening there.

### ZeroClaw version

v0.8.6 release-candidate build (61a2c95); code references are to current master

### Operating system

macOS 26.5 (arm64)

### Regression?

Unknown
