v4.39.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206

  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init.   • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

v4.38.2

v4.38.1

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

prs.title: ci(docker): bound arm64 build memory and add a dry-run dispatch to docker-publish
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Legs that build `linux/arm64` now add the same bounded 8 GiB swap that the release workflow gives its Linux ARM64 build (`scripts/ci/dist_runner_memory.sh prepare`, then `cleanup` with `if: always()`). The arm64 build of the `dist` image runs out of memory in its final link. The same Dockerfile leg in `docker-image-pr.yml` was killed with `ResourceExhausted` on #11347's approved head ([run 39040526108](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39040526108)) and on earlier runs with the v0.8.6 `dist` feature set.
  - Those legs also set up Buildx with `max-parallelism = 1`. One job builds amd64 and arm64, and this keeps the two release links from running at the same time. Legs without arm64 keep the default Buildx setup.
  - The `publish` job timeout goes from 60 to 120 minutes. A two-platform leg now builds one platform after the other. The `all-features` Containerfile leg alone takes 41 to 64 minutes in `docker-image-pr.yml`, so 60 is already too tight.
  - Manual dispatch gains three inputs: `release_ref`, `stems` and `push`. `push` defaults to false for a dispatch and to true for `workflow_call`. A dispatch can now dry-run the release legs without publishing anything. It can also rebuild one variant of a release, for example only `dist` for a tag.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to the Dockerfiles, Rust profiles, LTO or codegen settings (#11741 proposes per-variant LTO), runner classes, the tag matrix in `dev/ci/docker-tags.toml`, or the release workflow. The maintainer CI docs (`docs/book/src/maintainers/ci-and-actions.md`) are not updated here.
- **Blast radius:** Release Stable's `docker-matrix` job, which calls this workflow at the release tag, and the tag-push trigger. Both still push, sign and scan, because `push` defaults to true for `workflow_call` and the tag-push path checks `github.event_name == 'push'`. Manual dispatches change behavior: they no longer push unless `push` is set.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11828. Depends on #11347 (adds `scripts/ci/dist_runner_memory.sh`). Related #11741.

### What this does, simply

When a stable release is published, the release workflow calls `docker-publish.yml` to build four container image variants from source. The `dist` variant is built for both amd64 and arm64 on one hosted runner. With the v0.8.6 feature set, the arm64 build needs more memory than the runner has, and the build is killed near the end. That would leave v0.8.6 without a `dist` image.

This change gives those builds the same extra swap the release workflow already uses for its own ARM64 build. It also makes BuildKit run one step at a time, so the amd64 and arm64 links never overlap. It doubles the time limit to cover the slower serial build.

It also makes a manual run safe to use as a rehearsal. Today any manual run of this workflow pushes and signs every image. After this change a manual run builds without publishing unless someone ticks `push`. It can also be limited to named variants.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. A maintainer with write access runs the dry run below. The branch must be in this repository, because the build job only runs in `zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw`.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** None of the product surfaces. GitHub Actions `workflow_dispatch` of `docker-publish.yml` only.
- **Setup / preconditions:** #11347 merged (it has); this branch is based on master after it.
- **Steps to run:** `gh workflow run docker-publish.yml --ref <branch> -f stems=dist,all-features`. Leave `push` unset; it stays false.
- **Expected on this branch (after):**
  - Only the `dist` and `all-features` legs run.
  - The `dist` leg prepares swap, builds both platforms and releases the swap.
  - Both legs finish within 120 minutes.
  - "Sign container image", `publish-relay`, `scan`, `scan-relay` and both SARIF uploads are skipped.
  - Nothing is pushed to GHCR.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Do not dispatch `master`'s version to compare: there, every dispatch pushes and signs all four variants and the relay. On `master`, the comparable evidence is the `docker-image-pr.yml` arm64 Dockerfile leg, which is killed on `ubuntu-latest` (run 39040526108).

### How I tested

This has **not run in GitHub Actions yet**. The checks below were run locally on Linux x86_64 against the patch file. The planned Actions check is the dry run above.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** None cover it. No PR workflow runs `docker-publish.yml`. The architecture tests `tests/architecture/container_release.rs` and `xtask/src/generate/docker_tags.rs` assert strings in this file; I checked those strings by hand (below) but did not run the test suites.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The memory change only proves itself in Actions. That is the dry run above. Pushing and signing are exercised only by a real release or a dispatch with `push` set.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```text
  # git apply --check, temporary index per tree
  master  8ed287bd4b  docker-publish.yml blob 01cdf944e7
  #11347  7d2bef733d  docker-publish.yml blob 01cdf944e7
  apply --check OK on 8ed287bd4b
  apply --check OK on 7d2bef733d
  # applied on the #11347 tree
   .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml | 83 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++---
   1 file changed, 77 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)
  scripts/ci/dist_runner_memory.sh present

  # YAML parse (PyYAML 6.0.1)
  triggers: ['push', 'workflow_call', 'workflow_dispatch']

  # stems filter: the workflow step's yq (v4.44.3) + jq, run against dev/ci/docker-tags.toml
  stems=''                       -> minimal, default-features, dist, all-features

  docker/setup-buildx-action@37fe631 (v4.3.0): buildkitd-config-inline present
  docker/build-push-action@1dc7386 (v6.18.0): push, default 'false'
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - Release Stable's `docker-matrix` job passes only `release_ref`, so `push` takes its `workflow_call` default of true.
  - `dist_runner_memory.sh` already runs on hosted runners. Its prepare and cleanup steps passed on the `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` legs of Cross-Platform Build [run 39001999557](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39001999557).
  - `stems` reaches the shell only through `env` and `jq --arg`. It is never interpolated into the script.
  - Not verified: that 8 GiB of swap is enough for the arm64 link inside BuildKit, and the runner's disk headroom with the swap file in place. The dry run answers both.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No user-visible interface changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Patch applied to `7d2bef733d` (#11347's merge head, tree `1d64325b`, the same tree as master `bf38521f` this branch is based on); checks above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. Job permissions are unchanged. The swap file is created under `RUNNER_TEMP` with `sudo` on the hosted runner, by the script the release workflow already uses.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. A dry run still logs in to GHCR with the job's `GITHUB_TOKEN`, as before. It does not push.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

**Please read the push gating closely.** Pushing and cosign signing now happen only when `inputs.push || github.event_name == 'push'` is true. The expression appears on both build steps (`push:`) and both signing steps (`if:`). The scan jobs use the same condition, so they never scan a tag a dry run did not push.

- The release path keeps publishing because `workflow_call` defaults `push` to true.
- The tag-push path keeps publishing through the `push` event check.
- A dispatch with `push` ticked publishes from the dispatched ref, which is what every dispatch does today. Without `release_ref`, the tags come from that ref's `docker-tags.toml`.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for the release and tag-push paths. A manual dispatch no longer publishes by default.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. Product config, env and CLI are unchanged. The workflow gains three optional dispatch inputs.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: Maintainers who dispatch this workflow to publish must now set `push: true`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`. One workflow file; no state to migrate.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. A dispatch with `push: false` is the dry run.
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - In a release run, "Publish Docker Variant Matrix" legs show "Sign container image" as skipped, or `scan` as skipped. Either means `push` resolved to false.
  - "Prepare bounded build memory" fails with "Need 8 GiB for swap plus 8 GiB of build headroom".
  - The arm64 leg still ends with `signal: 9, SIGKILL` or `ResourceExhausted`.
  - The cleanup step prints "Swapfile retained" or "Refusing cleanup".
  - A leg hits the 120-minute timeout.

prs.title: ci(release): run the macOS plugin smoke on macos-15
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The `plugin-smoke` job in `release-stable-manual.yml` and `cross-platform-build-manual.yml` ran its `aarch64-apple-darwin` leg on `macos-14`. GitHub retires that image on November 2, 2026, and until then fails jobs on it during scheduled brownouts: October 19, 23, 26, 29 and 30, each from 14:00 UTC to midnight UTC. In Release Stable, `publish` and `docker` both need `plugin-smoke`. A run whose smoke leg lands in a brownout fails the release, and after November 2 every run would. Both legs now run on `macos-15`, the image #11522 moved master's other macOS jobs to. Both workflows already build `aarch64-apple-darwin` on `macos-15`, so the smoke now runs on the same image as the build.
  - A new architecture test, `workflows_never_name_the_retired_macos_14_runner`, fails if any file under `.github/workflows/` names `macos-14`. Since it matches a substring, it also catches `macos-14-large` and `macos-14-xlarge`. #11522 removed every `macos-14` label, but nothing stopped a new job from naming it again. This test does.
  - `immutable_stable_release_recipe_has_real_command_and_failure_baselines` pins a SHA-256 of the Stable workflow outside the shared build step. The runner line is inside that region, so the literal is updated. Nothing else in that test changes.
- **Scope boundary:** Only the runner label of the two `aarch64-apple-darwin` smoke legs changes. No other step, job, matrix row or target changes. The digest test keeps its current shape; replacing it is a separate change.
- **Blast radius:** The `aarch64-apple-darwin` smoke leg in Release Stable and in the manual Cross-Platform Build. The `x86_64-apple-darwin` leg already runs on `macos-15-intel`. The architecture suite gains one test.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11831. Related #11347, Related #11522.

### What this does, simply

Before a release ships, the release workflow runs a plugin smoke test against each platform's packaged binary, on a machine of that platform. The Apple Silicon Mac leg asked GitHub for a macOS 14 machine. GitHub is retiring those machines on November 2. On several days before then, it deliberately fails any job that asks for one. The release waits for the smoke test, so a release started on one of those days would fail, and after November 2 every release would.

This asks for macOS 15 instead, which is what the release build and the rest of CI already use. It also adds a test that fails if any workflow asks for macOS 14 again. Nothing about what the smoke test checks changes.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The change is two runner labels and one static test. The architecture test and actionlint cover the files, and PR CI does not run the plugin smoke legs. A manual Cross-Platform Build dispatch with the `dist` distribution would run the leg on `macos-15`; I have not run one.

### How I tested

I tested this on a local merge of master `3f2f028b0f` with #11347's head `f39ffd4791` (Linux x86_64). That merge has tree `1d64325b`, the same tree as current master `bf38521f` after #11347 merged, so this branch is byte-identical to what I tested.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The workspace test run includes the `architecture` test target, which holds the new test and the digest test.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** PR CI does not dispatch Release Stable or Cross-Platform Build, so the `macos-15` leg itself runs for the first time on the next dispatch.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```text
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check
  (exit 0)

  $ cargo test --locked --test architecture release_workflow
  test release_workflow::immutable_stable_release_recipe_has_real_command_and_failure_baselines ... ok
  test release_workflow::plugin_execution_smoke_gates_the_release ... ok
  test release_workflow::workflows_never_name_the_retired_macos_14_runner ... ok
  test result: ok. 26 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 53 filtered out

  $ cargo test --locked --test architecture
  test result: ok. 79 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

  $ cargo clippy --locked --test architecture -- -D warnings
      Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)

  $ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh tests/architecture/release_workflow.rs
  Comment hygiene gate passed.
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - **`macos-14` restored in the manual workflow only:** the new test fails with `macos-14 is a retired runner image; use macos-15: ["cross-platform-build-manual.yml:482"]`. All other tests pass.
  - **`macos-14` restored in both workflows** (the workflows exactly as before this change): the new test names `release-stable-manual.yml:778` and `cross-platform-build-manual.yml:482`. The digest test reports the previous literal `a48e3f77…`. That shows the runner line is the only change inside the pinned region.
  - **`macos-14-xlarge` in the manual workflow:** the new test fails on line 482.
  - After each check I restored the files, confirmed them by SHA-256, and re-ran the tests green.
  - **actionlint 1.7.11 on both workflows:** `release-stable-manual.yml` is clean. `cross-platform-build-manual.yml` reports one existing warning, the same before and after this change: `matrix.use_cross` at line 1060, in the `stable-gnu-build` job, whose matrix has no cross targets. The expression falls back to `'false'` there.
  - I did not run either workflow on GitHub.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** local merge of `3f2f028b0f` + `f39ffd4791`, with this patch on top
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The full workspace test run was skipped. The change touches two workflow files and one architecture test file, and the whole `architecture` target passes.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: `git revert <sha>`. A revert puts the smoke leg back on `macos-14`, which fails during brownouts and after November 2.

prs.title: feat(release): ship the WASM plugin host in supported release artifacts
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (the #11310 signer and #11311 smoke harness have merged).
- **What changed and why:**
  - Integrate the current public tool-selection changes from #11221 and the landed Wasmtime 48.0.6 / Rustls 0.23.46 security update from #11755. Distribution builds retain compatible tool implementations; existing and newly generated configurations retain full tool availability by default. An explicit `[tools] optional = []` selects the minimal tool set.
  - Root `Cargo.toml`: `plugins-wasm-cranelift` joins `dist_extra_features`, so the standard distribution artifacts carry the WASM plugin host with the compiler that loads `.wasm` components, the only form the plugin registry publishes. `dist_target_exclusions` removes it for `armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf` and `arm-unknown-linux-gnueabihf` (Cranelift has no native ARM32 backend, and no native ARM32 runner can prove wasmtime's Pulley fallback) and for `aarch64-linux-android` (experimental, not a required asset). The Pulley feature comment now describes what the feature does.
  - Generated surfaces regenerated with `cargo generate installers` (source container builds, AUR package, Nix flake, `setup.bat`, container tag registry); the base-image digest refresh the generator also performs is left out on purpose.
  - `release-stable-manual.yml`: `plugin-smoke-packages` builds the fixture plugin packages once on Linux; `plugin-smoke` downloads each of the seven 64-bit desktop and server archives on a runner of its own platform and runs `scripts/ci/plugin_artifact_smoke.sh` against the packaged binary; the legs set up no toolchain and compile nothing. `publish` and `docker` need it. Both jobs run with `permissions: contents: read` and a checkout that persists no credentials. `BINARY_SIZE_HARD_LIMIT` rises from 64 MiB to 80 MiB.
  - `cross-platform-build-manual.yml`: the same two jobs against the binaries it builds, so one dispatch both measures sizes and proves plugin execution for a distribution change.
  - Tests and docs: an xtask test ties "this target carries a plugin backend" to "the release has a smoke leg for it" in both directions; the architecture suite pins the wiring (needs, artifact names, least privilege, the whole smoke invocation, no `continue-on-error`, no condition on the smoke step); generator tests match feature names as whole tokens; the dist parity test reads the build job's matrix. Every page that said prebuilt binaries lack the host now says which artifacts carry it, which do not, and where the proof is recorded; the protocol page gains a per-artifact table and the limits that hold for all of them; the operator page gains the release-binary walkthrough and rollback; the Nix module and README explain `MemoryDenyWriteExecute` against plugin loads.
- **Scope boundary:** The artifact changes preserve plugin enablement/discovery/signature defaults, the WIT contract and desktop packaging recipes. The normal public #11221 integration also carries its tool-selection and CLI/config changes, including the full default and explicit minimal selection described above. The normal master integration carries the reviewed security and supporting fixes. Existing external actions remain pinned; the Stable build step now uses the local shared release recipe. No release asset is added, renamed, or removed. The `v*` tag trigger of docker-publish.yml is unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** the seven 64-bit desktop and server CLI archives; the GHCR `latest`, versioned and `debian` images, repackaged from two of them; source builds from the generated distribution list (the GHCR `dist` variant, the AUR package, the Nix flake package, `setup.bat`); desktop bundle sidecars built from the generated `dist` feature list (plus `embedded-web` on macOS); the stable release and manual cross-platform workflows; the plugin documentation; consumers of `/api/plugins`, the dashboard Plugins page, and `zeroclaw status` output, which change what they report; the cron database, where any plugin-host binary that opens or creates it adds an empty `plugin_outbox` table; and, with `skills.install_suggestions.enabled = true` (default off) and a registry index cached by `plugin search` or `plugin install <name>`, a release binary now answers a matching turn with a `zeroclaw plugin install` suggestion instead of calling the model, whatever `plugins.enabled` says. The ARM32 and Android archives remain without the host. `cargo install` and `install.sh` source builds keep their existing feature defaults.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10994; the issue closes after the v0.8.6 run posts downloaded-artifact evidence on #10994, #7432 and #10999. Depends on #11221: this branch carries its minimal-tools selection, upgrade-persistence and registry-assembly lineage, and the release artifacts are built with those runtime semantics. #11311 and #11310 have merged.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can load WebAssembly plugins, but until now the prebuilt release binaries were built without that plugin host: `zeroclaw plugin ...` was not even a command, and outside the amd64 `all-features` container image a plugin needed a source build. This PR puts the plugin host, with the compiler that loads ordinary `.wasm` plugins, into the release binaries for the seven 64-bit desktop and server targets. For an operator who does not use plugins, what is off stays off: the plugin system is disabled by default, a plugin is instantiated only by the operator's own `plugin install`, `plugin info` or `plugin list --verify` commands, and it is offered to the model only after the operator enables the plugin system and turns discovery on. What such an operator does see change on a release binary: `zeroclaw plugin` exists as a command, `zeroclaw status` lists a `Plugin` channel row, `/api/plugins` reports `wasm_plugins_available: true`, and the dashboard's Plugins page says the plugin system is disabled instead of unavailable in this build.

What was missing was proof. A binary can carry the host and still fail to run a plugin, so the release now checks itself: one job builds a small test plugin, and one job per archive downloads the archive that is about to be published, installs the plugin through the normal commands, and makes an agent call it. On a dispatched release, the GitHub Release and the container images are created only if every one of those checks passes. The manual cross-platform build runs the same checks, so a change to what ships can be rehearsed before a release.

Limits: the two 32-bit ARM archives and the experimental Android archive still have no plugin host. Normal-profile run [39001999557, attempt 1](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39001999557/attempts/1), on `61a2c951`, measured all ten main binaries below 80 MiB. The largest was x86_64 musl at 76,241,040 B, leaving 7,645,040 B of headroom. The historical same-source x86_64 GNU comparison at `88f69013` measured a separate host+Cranelift delta of 9,086,320 B (8.67 MiB). Desktop sidecars now also compile the host through `dist`; the CLI archive smoke does not qualify desktop bundles. Plugins are experimental and must match the release WIT contract.

Decisions taken here and flagged for maintainers (from the plan on #10994):

| # | Decision | What this PR does | Needs sign-off |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Size cap | 64 MiB to 80 MiB (83,886,080 B). Normal-profile run [39001999557 attempt 1](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39001999557/attempts/1), source `61a2c951`, measured all ten targets; the maximum is x86_64 musl at 76,241,040 B (72.71 MiB), leaving 7,645,040 B (7.29 MiB). The historical matched `88f69013` B/C comparison separately measures +9,086,320 B for x86_64 GNU host+Cranelift. | Yes. The cap is measured; the refreshed source still needs its own qualification. |
| D2 | Backend per target | Cranelift on the seven 64-bit desktop and server targets; none on ARM32 and Android. | Yes |
| D3 | Package formats | `.wasm` only; no artifact ships a deserialize-only backend. | Follows from D2 |
| D4 | Smoke plugin | The in-tree `tool-fixture` packages (eight variants) for the blocking gate. `redact-text@0.3.0` from the registry was verified by hand on a release-profile build while planning. | No |
| D5 | Gate strength | `publish` and `docker` both need `plugin-smoke`; the images repackage two smoke-gated archives. | Yes, for `docker` |
| D6 | Nix hardening | `MemoryDenyWriteExecute` stays on; comments and README say plugin loads fail under it and how an instance overrides it on its own unit. | No |
| D7 | Authority | FND-001 section 4.4.2 plus `status:accepted` on #10994 are the cited basis for artifact inclusion with plugin defaults unchanged. Standard desktop sidecars also carry the host through `prepare-kernel.sh` and generated `dist` features. ARM32 and Android remain exclusions; desktop bundle execution is not covered by the CLI smoke. No protected foundation text is changed. | Yes. Core and owner acceptance remain separate. |

### Source and qualification scope

The public branch is based on `master` and depends on #11221. Head `f39ffd4791e08f2d9a08339128bfc61eeb52cc2b` keeps the original topic and normal merge history: master `cdefa0d0a6bf95bb9c7fe90e174b948af3a76166` merged in, then #11221's head `04746465a06b2b6d5e1d3fa9fc622ee87ca4da0d`, then one commit with the review's CI, docs and cap-comment fixes (`1395d0d2`), then `f39ffd47`, which gives Stable's two macOS build legs the manual workflow's 180-minute limit after the qualification run measured 86 and 99 minutes. Required CI on this head is pending; normal and stable-gnu-ubuntu22 qualification passed on `1395d0d2` (runs 39032435906 and 39032438005), and the timeout change touches no build step. #11221 preserves full tool availability for existing and fresh configurations by default; operators explicitly select the minimal set with `[tools] optional = []`. Plugin enablement and discovery remain off by default.

The two completed artifact runs below qualify their exact source and profile. They do not qualify the pending refresh, desktop bundles, companion runtime, or the full Stable matrix. Current required CI, human and Core review, parent landing, and release acceptance remain separate requirements.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional: an A/B run of the smoke against a release-profile build takes about twenty minutes of compile time on a laptop plus a minute for the checks.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`
- **Setup / preconditions:** Rust 1.98.0 with the `wasm32-wasip2` target, Python 3.8 or newer, bash. Nothing under `~/.zeroclaw` is used; the smoke runs in a throwaway configuration directory.
- **Steps to run:**
  ```sh
  FEATURES="$(cargo run -q -p xtask --bin generate -- features --selection dist --target "$(rustc -vV | sed -n 's/^host: //p')")"
  echo "$FEATURES"
  cargo build --release --locked --no-default-features --features "$FEATURES" --bin zeroclaw
  bash scripts/ci/build_plugin_smoke_packages.sh /tmp/plugin-smoke-packages
  bash scripts/ci/plugin_artifact_smoke.sh --binary target/release/zeroclaw --expect host --packages /tmp/plugin-smoke-packages
  ```
- **Expected on this branch (after):** `$FEATURES` contains `plugins-wasm-cranelift`; the smoke prints eighteen `PASS` rows and a report headed `... passed`, exit 0.
- **Baseline comparison:** build the distribution without the plugin-host feature. The smoke must refuse it because the binary has no `plugin` command. Use the same public harness and record the exact source, feature list and binary digest for each side.

### How I tested

**Completed GNU qualification, exact historical source:**

[GNU qualification run 38865614019, attempt 1](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38865614019/attempts/1), on `d79fb11f53eb6ec64c279f582dde64f3ade83c23`, passed all 11 selected jobs and strict same-source/run/attempt completeness. Four GNU archives and 12 binary-input/ABI pairs verified. The two native legs each passed 13 provider tests and 18 artifact controls: **26 provider and 36 artifact named PASS results** in total.

With two Cargo jobs and guarded 8 GiB temporary swap, the ARM64 build completed in **36m 4.774s**; preparation and always-cleanup both passed. Its main binary measured **55,588,688 B**, below the **80 MiB (83,886,080 B)** cap.

This run qualifies GNU only. The later normal-profile run below covers additional build and smoke legs on its own source. The full Stable matrix and desktop bundle execution remain unqualified. The GNU ARM64 native leg ran on Ubuntu 24.04, so it does not establish native Ubuntu 22.04 ARM64 runtime support.


**Completed normal-profile qualification:**

[Run 39001999557, attempt 1](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39001999557/attempts/1), on `61a2c951`, completed successfully: 21 successful jobs and five expected GNU-profile skips. Both validators selected `dist / normal / false`. All ten main-binary cap steps and all seven native plugin smoke jobs succeeded. These are job/step outcomes; no additional per-control counts are inferred from them.

| Target | Main binary bytes | Plugin host |
|---|---:|---|
| aarch64-apple-darwin | 42,561,168 | Cranelift |
| aarch64-linux-android | 45,264,216 | none |
| aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu | 55,584,592 | Cranelift |
| aarch64-unknown-linux-musl | 51,438,816 | Cranelift |
| arm-unknown-linux-gnueabihf | 53,087,588 | none |

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `Yes`. The 64-bit desktop and server release binaries now contain a code-loading runtime (wasmtime with Cranelift). Compiled-in effects that do not depend on config: the `plugin` CLI, the gateway plugin webhook routes, `/api/plugins`, a status row, and the empty `plugin_outbox` table added when the cron database is opened or created. Instantiating a component calls no export but does run any start function its core modules carry (for example a reactor's `_initialize`). `plugin install` (unless `--no-verify`), `plugin info` and `plugin list --verify` instantiate the component whether or not the plugin system is enabled, in a store with no preopened files, no network or egress authority, and the per-call fuel, memory and time limits. Exports run only after the operator opts in. With `plugins.enabled` and `plugins.auto_discover` set, every build of the tool registry compiles, instantiates and queries each admitted tool component for its metadata under the package's declared permissions and egress policy, and the tool is offered to the model; each `execute` then needs approval unless pre-approved (`auto_approve` by name or `*`, `level = "full"`, or an Always grant). A skill package needs `enabled` and `auto_discover`. A channel package needs `enabled`, a `[channels.plugin.<alias>]` declaration, and an enabled agent that lists `plugin.<alias>`. The smoke proves the closed defaults per archive: install leaves the plugin system off, discovery without enabling offers nothing, enabling without discovery offers nothing, a discovered tool waits for approval, and payload digests, the WIT world and the signature policy are enforced at install.
- New external network calls? `Yes`. `plugin search` and `plugin install <name>` fetch the registry index, operator-initiated. A plugin granted `http_client` or socket permissions can make policed egress from a release binary once enabled, including during the metadata probe; egress is deny-by-default through the per-instance allowlist. The release smoke itself talks only to a local stub provider.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Application interfaces remain unchanged. The incorporated Rustls security patch includes upstream TLS/secret-handling fixes. No new secret collection or export is introduced. The new jobs receive no secrets, hold `contents: read`, and check out with `persist-credentials: false`. The added diagnostic reads only whitelisted public identity/resource/package fields and writes two private runner-temp files. It adds a bounded upload to the existing GitHub artifact service, with no new permission or destination; no environment, argv, process, kernel, network or credential dump is collected.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `Yes`, in reach rather than mechanism: once a plugin is enabled, its tool name, description, parameter schema and results are model-visible text supplied by the plugin. Source builds have this today; this PR makes it reachable from release binaries once the operator enables the plugin system and discovery: the name, description and schema reach the model at registration without any approval, and results only after an approved call. A plugin skill package injects package-supplied skill text once the plugin system is enabled and discovery is on, and a channel plugin feeds inbound text to the model.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: covered in the answers above. wasmtime advisories become release-relevant; `cargo deny` and the daily audit already gate them.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `Yes`: the 64-bit desktop and server release binaries gain the `zeroclaw plugin` subcommand and the gateway's plugin webhook route. `/api/plugins`, present in every gateway build, now answers `wasm_plugins_available: true` and lists installed packages; the dashboard's Plugins page shows the plugin system as disabled rather than unavailable; `zeroclaw status` gains a `Plugin` channel row; any plugin-host binary that opens or creates the cron database adds an empty `plugin_outbox` table. - **Observable failure symptoms:** a `Check binary size` failure on a build leg (`Binary exceeds 80MB safeguard`); a `Plugin Smoke <target>` leg failing, with its step summary naming the failed check, which skips `publish` and `docker`; `zeroclaw --help` listing no `plugin` command on a 64-bit desktop or server archive, which is the smoke's first check.

## Known risks

- Windows and both musl native smoke jobs succeeded in normal-profile run `39001999557` on `61a2c951`. This is exact-source evidence, not proof for the refreshed source or the full Stable release.
- Musl archives build through `cross`; the normal-profile run built and smoked both host-bearing targets. Source container images and container runtime remain separate.
- `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners execute the aarch64 archives; the glibc one links glibc 2.35 (built on 22.04) and runs on 24.04. The manual rehearsal cross-builds on `ubuntu-latest`; once that label moves past 24.04 the binary may need a newer glibc than the runner has.
- The 80 MiB cap is measured: all ten main binaries in normal-profile run `39001999557` are listed above. The largest, x86_64 musl, exceeds the former 64 MiB cap by 9,132,176 B and leaves 7,645,040 B below 80 MiB. The historical same-source x86_64 GNU host+Cranelift delta is separately 9,086,320 B. Desktop bundle sizes and refreshed-source measurements remain open. The 15/5 MB advisories are unchanged and need separate disposition under #11580.
- A release started by a tag push also triggers Docker Publish on its own `v*` trigger, which does not wait for the smoke; the dispatch path is the gated one.

## Follow-ups, not in this PR

- ARM32 with the Cranelift feature and wasmtime's automatic Pulley target: a compile check in CI, then an emulated smoke.
- A `plugin sign` command (proposed in RFC #8135, which is deferred and not accepted).

prs.title: fix(daemon): contain the Windows daemon's process tree in a kill-on-close job
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - On Windows, a bare `zeroclaw daemon` or `zeroclaw gateway start` now places itself in an unnamed job object with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` and keeps the only handle for its lifetime. Every process it spawns inherits membership, so when the daemon ends by any route (Task Manager, `taskkill /F`, a crash, Ctrl+C) the kernel terminates the whole tree and the gateway port is free at once. Today those children (the `agent-browser` session and its Chrome, MCP servers, shell commands) survive a forced kill and keep the inherited listening socket open, which is the stuck port in the issue.
  - The job allows breakaway, and the post-upgrade self-respawn in `restart.rs` now spawns with `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB`, so the new binary still outlives the daemon that launched it. If an enclosing job forbids breakaway (the flag then fails with access denied), the respawn retries without it and stays where it is today.
  - The Win32 helper lives in `zeroclaw-config`'s platform module, next to the pipe and token helpers, not in the runtime holding crate. The runtime change is a behavior fix to an existing function, not new functionality.
  - A host that refuses the job (nesting disallowed, or an old Windows) gets one warning and today's behavior; the daemon never refuses to start over it. The Task Scheduler runner already confines itself the same way, so a supervised daemon now nests its own job inside the runner's.
- **Scope boundary:** No change on Unix (children survive a killed parent there too, but the port does not stay bound). Does not restrict which handles children inherit; the job terminates the orphans that hold them, which covers every inherited handle. Does not touch `agent-browser`'s unbounded waits or the interactive Ctrl+C lifecycle.
- **Blast radius:** Windows daemon and gateway process lifetime; the post-upgrade respawn on Windows; the required `windows-task-owner-recovery` CI job gains two exact-name tests and its scope rule learns the new file. Anything the daemon spawned on Windows now ends with the daemon, which is the intent, including on a clean Ctrl+C.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #8800. Related #9946.

### What this does, simply

When ZeroClaw runs on Windows it starts helper programs: a browser for the browser tool, MCP servers, shell commands for tools and cron jobs. Windows does not tie a helper's life to its parent, so when the daemon is killed from Task Manager those helpers keep running, and because they were born holding copies of the daemon's network handles, the gateway port stays "in use" by a process that no longer exists. A new daemon then fails to start until every orphan is found and killed by hand.

This change makes the daemon the owner of everything it spawns, using the Windows feature built for exactly that (a job object): the kernel kills the whole tree the moment the daemon ends, however it ends. The one child that is meant to outlive the daemon, the copy of itself it launches after an in-app upgrade, opts out of the job. Nothing changes for the service runner, which already did this for itself, or on Linux and macOS.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (`zeroclaw daemon`); no channel.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Windows. A config directory with this `config.toml`, which needs no model provider. The declarative cron job gives the daemon a long-lived child without an agent turn:

  ```toml
  schema_version = 3

  [gateway]
  host = "127.0.0.1"
  port = 18800
  require_pairing = false

  [risk_profiles.default]
  level = "full"
  allowed_commands = ["ping"]
  require_approval_for_medium_risk = false
  block_high_risk_commands = true

  [agents.ops]
  risk_profile = "default"
  cron_jobs = ["linger"]

  [cron.linger]
  name = "linger"
  job_type = "shell"
  command = "ping -n 3600 127.0.0.1"
  schedule = { kind = "every", every_ms = 15000 }
  ```
- **Steps to run:**
  1. `zeroclaw --config-dir <dir> daemon`, note its PID, wait about 20 s for the cron job.
  2. In another console: `tasklist | findstr PING.EXE` shows one `ping`; `netstat -ano | findstr :18800` shows `LISTENING` owned by the daemon PID.
  3. `taskkill /F /PID <daemon pid>`; wait 2 s; repeat the two commands from step 2.
  4. Start the daemon again.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** after step 3 the `ping` is gone and `netstat` prints nothing for the port; step 4 is listening within a second.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** after step 3 the `ping` is still running and `netstat` still shows `LISTENING` for the port under the dead PID; step 4 fails to bind until the `ping` is killed by hand.

### How I tested

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, Rust 1.98.0 MSVC, inside a shell that itself runs in a job object (so every test below exercised nested jobs).

```
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(clean)

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib --locked -- platform::job_object
running 4 tests
test platform::job_object::tests::a_process_outside_the_job_is_not_a_member ... ok
test platform::job_object::tests::a_member_dies_when_the_job_closes ... ok
test platform::job_object::tests::a_confined_parent_takes_its_tree_down_when_killed ... ok
test platform::job_object::tests::a_breakaway_child_survives_its_parent ... ok
test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1750 filtered out; finished in 1.02s

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --locked -- restart::
test restart::tests::unresolved_launch_keeps_respawn_fallback_but_not_remediation_path ... ok
test restart::tests::resolved_launch_is_available_for_remediation ... ok
test restart::tests::a_detached_child_spawns_whether_or_not_this_process_is_in_a_job ... ok
test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5599 filtered out; finished in 0.02s

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw --no-deps --bin zeroclaw --locked -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2m 43s
```

`cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config --no-deps --lib --tests --locked` and the same for `zeroclaw-runtime` report findings only in files this PR does not touch (`platform/native.rs`, `platform/docker.rs`, `secrets/windows_key_file.rs`, `service/mod.rs`, `rpc/auth.rs`, `agent/turn/vision_route.rs`), the known Windows-only lints; none in `job_object.rs`, `restart.rs` or `main.rs`.

Manual A/B with the config above, both binaries built from this checkout (`master` at 4e82ce46 into a separate target dir). The daemon was launched through WMI so that it started outside the shell's job, which makes `IsProcessInJob(daemon, NULL)` meaningful; a client connection was held open across the kill, as a dashboard would.

`master`:

```
[00:13:39.583] daemon pid 45468 started via WMI; listening after 30 ms
[00:13:40.782] --- before the kill ---
  daemon pid=45468 alive; in a job: False
  ping -n 3600 processes: 1 (pids 45168)
  netstat rows for :18800: 3
    TCP    127.0.0.1:18800        0.0.0.0:0              LISTENING       45468
    TCP    127.0.0.1:18800        127.0.0.1:61951        ESTABLISHED     45468
    TCP    127.0.0.1:61951        127.0.0.1:18800        ESTABLISHED     18920
[00:13:40.873] Stop-Process -Force 45468 (TerminateProcess, like taskkill /F)
[00:13:42.895] --- 2 s after the kill ---
  daemon pid=45468 not running
  ping -n 3600 processes: 1 (pids 45168)
  netstat rows for :18800: 1
    TCP    127.0.0.1:18800        0.0.0.0:0              LISTENING       45468
[00:13:58.052] restart failed: daemon did not appear under cmd pid 30548
```

Terminating the orphaned `ping` by hand freed the port immediately, as the issue reports.

This branch:

```
[00:14:15.647] daemon pid 47760 started via WMI; listening after 27 ms
[00:14:16.831] --- before the kill ---
  daemon pid=47760 alive; in a job: True
  ping -n 3600 processes: 1 (pids 39588)
  netstat rows for :18800: 3
    TCP    127.0.0.1:18800        0.0.0.0:0              LISTENING       47760
    TCP    127.0.0.1:18800        127.0.0.1:62004        ESTABLISHED     47760
    TCP    127.0.0.1:62004        127.0.0.1:18800        ESTABLISHED     19036
[00:14:16.915] Stop-Process -Force 47760 (TerminateProcess, like taskkill /F)
[00:14:18.924] --- 2 s after the kill ---
  daemon pid=47760 not running
  ping -n 3600 processes: 0
  netstat rows for :18800: 0
[00:14:19.483] restarted daemon pid 41252; listening again after 152 ms
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `windows-task-owner-recovery` (required) runs `a_confined_parent_takes_its_tree_down_when_killed` and `a_breakaway_child_survives_its_parent` on a Windows runner; `windows-check` compiles the root crate on Windows; `Lint` covers the Unix side of `restart.rs` and `main.rs`; the CI script tests cover the scope-rule change.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The real daemon's job membership and the respawn's breakaway are covered by the helper-process tests, not by a daemon-level test; the manual A/B above is the evidence for the daemon itself. `windows-tests.yml` (advisory) needs the `ci:windows` label to run the rest of the Windows suite.
- **Commands run and tail output:** above.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The A/B above: job membership, orphan survival vs. termination, the stuck `LISTENING` row on a dead PID vs. a free port, restart failure vs. restart in 152 ms. Not verified: an actual in-app upgrade respawn (the breakaway path is covered by `a_breakaway_child_survives_its_parent` and the detached-spawn test), and a host whose job policy refuses nesting (the warning path).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no user-visible interface state changed; one new warning log line).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** this branch's head vs. `master` 4e82ce46; `cli`; transcripts above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** transcripts above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** `taskkill`-equivalent kill of the daemon; children terminated and port freed on this branch, orphan and stuck port on `master`.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `scripts/ci/windows_test_scope.test.sh` and `windows_recovery_change_filter.test.sh` need Python, which this machine lacks; CI runs them. Workspace-wide `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and full `cargo test` fail locally on the pre-existing Windows-only lints noted above, so clippy was run per touched crate.

prs.title: fix(config): publish the secret key with renameat2 on Android
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - On Android, SELinux denies `link(2)` to apps, even inside their own data directory. `write_key_file_atomic_publish` publishes `.secret_key` with `hard_link(temp, final)`, so creating the key fails with `EACCES`. Every secret encryption then fails, and `quickstart` cannot persist an agent (#11525).
  - On `target_os = "android"` the key is now published with `renameat2(temp, final, RENAME_NOREPLACE)`. It keeps the guarantees the triage on #11525 asked for:
    - The temp file is still created `0600` with `create_new`, written and synced before publication, so the final path only ever appears with the complete key.
    - An existing key is never replaced. A concurrent creator gets `AlreadyExists`, and `load_or_create_key` already resolves that by reading the winner's key.
    - A kernel without `RENAME_NOREPLACE` returns `ENOSYS`/`EINVAL` and the publication fails. It never falls back to a rename that could replace the key.
  - The syscall is called directly through `libc::syscall(SYS_renameat2, …)`, because bionic has no `renameat2` wrapper at every supported API level. This wrapper is the one from the Android work in #10205 by @JordanTheJet, extracted on its own as the triage suggested. The commit credits them with a `Co-authored-by` trailer.
- **Scope boundary:** other Unix targets keep `hard_link`, and Windows keeps its handle-based rename. No change to key format, file location, permissions, reading, or to the rest of `[secrets]`. Nothing from the Android app in #10205 besides this wrapper.
- **Blast radius:** only builds for `target_os = "android"` (the `aarch64-linux-android` release archive, Termux, embedded Android hosts). The new helper is compiled on Linux only for its test.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11525. Related #10205.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can encrypt the API keys in `config.toml`. To do that it creates a small key file the first time. It creates that file in two steps: it writes it under a temporary name, then makes it appear under its real name in one step that refuses to overwrite an existing key. On Linux and macOS that last step is a hard link. Android forbids hard links to apps, so on Android the key was never created, and anything that saves an API key (like `quickstart`) failed.

On Android the last step is now a rename that also refuses to overwrite (`RENAME_NOREPLACE`). The result is the same as on Linux: the key appears complete or not at all, and an existing key is never replaced. Nothing changes on other platforms.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, if you have an Android device or emulator. The CI runners cannot run Android binaries.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (`zeroclaw quickstart`, or any config write that encrypts a secret).
- **Setup / preconditions:** an Android device or emulator, with the `aarch64-linux-android` build run from Termux or from an app's private directory, and a fresh config directory.
- **Steps to run:** run `zeroclaw quickstart` and enter a provider API key, or set any secret field on a config with `[secrets] encrypt = true`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the agent is created, `<config_dir>/.secret_key` exists with mode `600`, and the API key is stored as `enc2:…` in `config.toml`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `Failed to encrypt providers.models.api_key`, and quickstart makes no change on disk (as reported in #11525).

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Linux test jobs run the existing key-publication tests (the `hard_link` path, unchanged) and the new `rename_no_replace_publishes_once_and_never_replaces`, which runs the same `renameat2` syscall that Android uses.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI neither builds nor runs `target_os = "android"` on pull requests, so I cross-compiled with NDK r27c (API 24) and ran the Android binary in Termux (below).
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# (no output)
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets -- -D warnings
#     Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config
# test result: ok. 1794 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-config --target aarch64-linux-android --all-targets
# warning: function `first_available` is never used        (platform/native.rs:56)
# warning: function `shell_is_available` is never used     (platform/native.rs:79)
#     Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - **Android binary, A/B.** I built `zeroclaw` for `x86_64-linux-android`, from this branch and from `master` with the commit reverted, and ran both in the `termux/termux-docker:x86_64` image (bionic, Termux paths). Docker does not enforce Android's SELinux policy, so a seccomp profile makes `link`/`linkat` fail with `EACCES`, which is what SELinux returns (`{"defaultAction":"SCMP_ACT_ALLOW","syscalls":[{"names":["link","linkat"],"action":"SCMP_ACT_ERRNO","errnoRet":13}]}`). Inside the container, `ln` then fails with `Permission denied`. Command: `ZEROCLAW_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/cfg zeroclaw config set memory.embedding-api-key`, on a fresh config.

    `master`:
    ```text
    Error: Failed to encrypt memory.embedding_api_key
    Caused by:
        0: Failed to atomically publish key file
        1: Permission denied (os error 13)
    ```
    This branch:
    ```text
    memory.embedding_api_key updated.
    -rw------- 1 system system   64 .secret_key
    embedding_api_key = "enc2:…"
    ```
  - **Existing key reused.** On the same config, a second secret (`gateway.webhook-secret`) is written with the existing key: the `.secret_key` hash is unchanged, both values are `enc2:`, and no temp file is left behind.
  - **Unit test.** The new test shows that the first rename publishes, the second gets `AlreadyExists`, the published content is the first one, and the losing temp file stays where it is, so the existing guard can remove it. The two Android clippy warnings are already on `master` without this change, in `platform/native.rs`. I did not run it on a real Android device or emulator, so the real SELinux policy is not exercised; the seccomp profile reproduces its `EACCES`. The `aarch64-linux-android` binary also builds.
  - **Build note.** `master` does not build the `zeroclaw` binary for Android right now, because of `DESKTOP_READINESS_FRAME_MAX_BYTES` and the dead code in `platform/native.rs`. That is what #11611 fixes. I applied #11611 locally only to build these binaries; it is not part of this PR.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A, no interface change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `a7f22958a`, `cli` (`zeroclaw config set`), the commands above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** see above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full workspace suite, because the change is limited to `zeroclaw-config` and its tests pass in full.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: how the master key file is published on Android changes. The risk would be replacing or exposing a key. `RENAME_NOREPLACE` never replaces, the temp file is `0600` from creation and complete before the rename, and an unsupported kernel fails closed. On every other platform the code path is unchanged.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`. On Android that brings back the `EACCES` failure, and nothing else changes.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `Failed to atomically publish key file`, with the OS error, on Android.

prs.title: feat(cli): add zeroclaw plugin update with verified replacement
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Stacked on #11261, which is stacked on #11236. #11581 has landed on `master` as `ea4a54bb5b`: this branch merged its head first (`0ba2b77343`) and now carries the landed commit through `277aeabb0e`'s merge of `master`. `2f3409e9ba`, `bd2d4e5eea`, `f94508dc69` and `2ec36c26dc` merge #11261's head, now `369fb21334`, which carries #11236's `7a3ad81ed5`. Until they merge, this PR's diff also contains their commits. Please review the eight commits after `0ba2b77343`, up to `bab70cc225`, the follow-ups from `75116ac28a` to `a1d212eca1`, and `f3d0a59844`. `6354484051`, `2f3409e9ba`, `bd2d4e5eea` and `f94508dc69` only merge the base, `2ec36c26dc` with the adaptation described below; `277aeabb0e` and `2b3c93631d` merge `master`, with the resolutions described below.
- **What changed and why:**
  - **The command.** Adds `zeroclaw plugin update`, the missing lifecycle operation from #10995 (#7432 R3, Phase 2 D3). It implements the contract posted on the issue for review: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10995#issuecomment-5894198515.
    - Syntax: `plugin update <name>[@<version>]...`, `plugin update --all`, and `plugin update <name> --from <dir>`, with `--registry <url>` as for install. Update never installs a package that is not installed.
    - Version selection is install's rule: the last entry the registry lists for a bare name, the exact entry for `name@version`, compared only for equality. An equal version is "up to date" and nothing is downloaded. A different version, even an older one, is installed, so pinning the previous version is the way back. When both are semantic versions and the selected one is older by SemVer precedence, the result line says so (`Replaced 'x' 2.0.0 with 1.2.5, an older version than the one installed.`) instead of reporting an update. A `--from` package always replaces, so a rebuilt plugin can be reinstalled at the same version.
    - Verification is the existing path, reused: the registry download, with its digest when the registry entry lists one, then `PluginHost::admit_update` from the stacked host PR, then the install-time load check with the operator's `plugins.limits`. There is no `--no-verify` for update.
  - **Authority gate.** The runtime grants every permission a manifest requests. So an update is refused, before its component is compiled, when its manifest adds a permission, a capability, or a new `provides` id, or names a different publisher key than the installed version (or none where the installed version named one).
    - The refusal prints the exact command that accepts the difference, with one `--allow-token <item>` per added item, such as `--allow-token permission:<name>`; `--allow` still takes the same items as a comma-separated list. It is pinned to the reviewed version and quoted for the host shell by the egress ceremony's `ShellDialect`, because versions, `provides` ids and keys are publisher-controlled text. Every output line that carries manifest text escapes control, format, line separator and paragraph separator characters (Unicode Cc, Cf, Zl, Zp), line breaks and invisible characters included, so manifest text cannot rewrite, rearrange or disguise the prompt, including an approval block a batch printed earlier, or print a line of its own.
    - `--allow` and `--allow-token` apply to one plugin, and a registry update that uses either must be pinned as `name@version`.
    - The publisher key is a verified identity only under `signature_mode = "strict"`; the docs say so.
  - **Preserved state.** Config rows, secrets, `egress_hosts`, `egress_allow_private`, TLS profiles, durable state, and instance keys are never modified.
    - Missing rows are created without a grant and saved before the package changes, so nothing after the replacement can fail.
    - Egress keeps the never-extend rule: update seeds nothing, even into a row it creates, and prints the same declared-versus-granted difference install prints for an existing row.
    - When preserved config fails the new version's schema, the update still completes and names the instance and the schema location. A missing required property is named, since the name is the schema's own. A configured value, or a configured key the schema does not declare, is never printed, because either could hold a secret.
    - A package whose config row still uses the pre-1.0 package-name key is refused with the same guidance `plugin install` prints (its rename steps, or a deployment-wide egress refusal in their place), one line each under the result; the docs say so.
  - **Results and recovery.** Each plugin gets one result: updated, reinstalled, up to date, skipped (with `--all`, not listed in the registry), needs approval, or not updated with the version kept.
    - A failure does not stop the others, and the command exits 1 when any plugin was not updated.
    - A command that updated anything ends with one restart-the-daemon note, and a batch ends with a summary line.
    - A package an interrupted update displaced is put back by the next `plugin update <name>`, before the registry is consulted, so recovery works offline. Names that are not installed are answered before the registry too, with the install command for the source the update named. `plugin list` and `plugin update --all` point at the recovery with two complete commands (a plugins directory this process cannot lock, such as a read-only one, simply gets no such note in `plugin list`), one from the registry and one from a package directory, rendered for the selected configuration as the approval, install and not-installed commands are, and `--all` never restores a displaced package unasked. An update interrupted mid-swap points back at its own source, so a `--from` run is retried from the same directory; authority the update adds is asked for again.
    - A restored copy the host does not admit is reported with where it now is, and with `plugin list --verbose`, which prints discovery's reason.
  - **Pointers keep the source.** `plugin install` on an installed package now fails with the update command for the same source: `--from <dir>` after a local install, `name@version` after a pinned one. Likewise, `plugin update <name> --from <dir>` for a name that is not installed points at installing that directory. Neither ever offers the registry for a local build, and exit statuses are unchanged.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No new registry, installer, config key, or on-disk format.
  - No version ordering for selection. Semantic versions are compared only to report an older one.
  - No daemon signalling: channel instances keep their component until restart, and tool sets built afterwards load the new version.
  - Channel-instance config and grant seeding stays with #10996. Install's own `<already-installed>` semantics stay with #10162; this PR only adds the pointer.
  - Registry-side compatibility metadata (#9624) does not exist yet; the load check is the compatibility gate.
  - Known limits, documented where operators read them:
    - no `fsync` around the renames, as for install
    - a tool set built at the instant of the swap can be inconsistent once
  - A process killed between publishing the replacement and marking the replaced version for deletion leaves that version claimed in its hidden transaction. Recovery deletes it while the plugin is installed; after a later `plugin remove`, `plugin list` shows it as displaced until a named `plugin update` restores it, and `--all` never does. `plugin remove` leaving such a claim alone is a follow-up.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw plugin install`/`list`/`update`, the root plugin CLI, and five runtime Fluent catalogues.
  - `seed_plugin_config_entries` is split. Its row-finding first half becomes `ensure_plugin_config_entries`, shared with update, and install's behavior and output are unchanged.
  - A batch fetches the registry index once and compares versions before downloading, through `download_registry_entry` from #11581, which this branch merges. This PR no longer defines that function itself.
  - In `zeroclaw-plugins`, `validate_config_instance` names a missing required property in its `InvalidConfig` message, so every surface that reports that error, such as a daemon load failure, names it too. The existing test that config errors expose no secret values or undeclared keys still passes unchanged.
  - `ci.yml` adds the new component test to the root CLI plugin step, and the plugin backend change filter now selects the plugin CLI component tests. The advisory Windows workflow runs the update tests in `src/main.rs` in its plugin CLI group and the `plugin_update_cli` and `plugin_info_cli` component tests in a step of their own, and the selector contract pins both.
  - The host PR builds update and its recovery on #11236's package lock and leased transactions, so updates, installs, removals and recoveries are serialized across processes, and a claim a running update holds is never touched. #11236 now carries #11232 merged in, and the stack is restacked onto it, so it holds one revision of each. #11236, #11261 and #11581 have landed, so this PR merges on its own. #11232 has landed.
  - `semver` becomes a direct dependency of the binary, behind `plugins-wasm`. It was already in the lock file through wasmtime.
  - The `zeroclaw-config` writer change in `b118a50358` and `0960216b8f` reaches every caller of `save_dirty`, not only `plugin update`: the gateway config API, the dashboard, zerocode RPC, `config set`, and channel identity persistence. A natural-key write that the existing document cannot take, with a value present, now fails the save, where it used to log a warning and drop the write while the save reported success. An explicit empty `[]` becomes an array of tables on the first keyed write.
  - Through #11236, install, update and recovery refuse a package move where the platform or filesystem has no rename that refuses an existing destination.
  - #11309, which landed as `ecafa8f25a`, gave `stage_plugin_config_entries` Quickstart's `tool_egress` decision and moved its degraded-section check and grant-state read into `plugins_section_degraded` and `tool_row_grant_state`. `ensure_plugin_config_entries`, which update shares with install, now calls both, so Quickstart, install and update read a row's grant state one way.
  - `parse_plugin_spec` in `zeroclaw-plugins` splits `name@version` at the first `@`, for install as for update, so a version holding an `@` parses back whole. A spec whose name part held an `@` never named an installable package, since a package name cannot contain one.
  - #11302, which landed as `2286ef36c5`, and this PR refactored `seed_plugin_config_entries` in different directions (`stage_plugin_config_entries` there, `ensure_plugin_config_entries` here). `2b3c93631d` merges it: `stage_plugin_config_entries` now creates its rows through `ensure_plugin_config_entries`, and update takes its rows and declaration from #11302's helpers (`instance_rows`, `tool_binding_entries`, `declared_hosts_for_row`), as install does. Update creates only the default tool binding's row, without a grant, and a channel instance's row stays `plugin bind`'s to create.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10995. #11236, #11261, #11581 and #11715 have landed; nothing it depends on is open. Related #7432, #10162, #10996, #9624, #11232, #11302.
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `ci`, `docs`, `dependencies`, `core`, `runtime`, `tests`, `scripts`, `distinguished contributor`, `release-gate`, `domain:security`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`, `cli`, `ci:windows`, `topic:plugins`, `release:v0.8.6`.

### Since the last reviews

tidux requested changes at `796c418343`, which JordanTheJet and Audacity88 had approved. The approvals do not cover this head. Each item:

- **Superseded #11236.** Restacked onto #11236 `c5fbbe2313` and #11261 `420969ea90`. These commits applied without conflicts. The branch is still behind `master`, and it will be rebased onto `master` once the PRs below it merge.
- **`download_registry_entry` in two PRs** (raised on #11309). #11581, which bounds registry requests, now owns that function and lands first. This branch merges it (`0ba2b77343`), and the update commit no longer defines its own copy. The call sites are unchanged.
- **An older version reported as "Updated".** Reported with its own line, as above (`fdb12439ce`). It never blocks, so #10995's no-ordering rule stands.
- **"Verified" claims a digest check.** The docs and this description now say the archive digest is checked when the registry entry lists one (`bab70cc225`). Refusing a digest-less registry update is left for a separate change, because install has the same gap.
- **Prompt injection.** Answered Yes below, with the mitigation: an update can change skill content under an existing `skill` capability without asking.
- **`plugin update --help` in English.** `cli-plugin-update-about`, and `cli-plugin-about` for `zeroclaw plugin`, are in all five catalogues and in the parity test (`12aceb5a6b`).
- **Merge order with #11302.** Recorded under Blast radius.
- **`printable`.** It escapes every Cc, Cf, Zl and Zp character, from a fixed table of the format ranges, and the displaced-package note goes through it (`ed68ce6ad2`).
- **Local builds under `--all`.** Not changed. Skipping a package whose installed version the registry does not list would also skip every package whose registry has dropped an old version.
- **CLI text.** The es and fr approval lines are reworded as suggested, and `--all` no longer prints "No plugins installed." after only displaced-package notes (`bab70cc225`). The restart line is unchanged.

### What this does, simply

Until now the only way to move a plugin to a new version was to remove it and install the new one, with nothing checking the new version first or keeping the old one working if something went wrong. `zeroclaw plugin update` does it in one step.

It fetches the new version and runs every check a fresh install runs, including that the component actually loads on this host. Only then does it swap the package in. If anything fails before the swap, the old version is untouched; if the swap itself fails, the old version is put back. If the process dies mid-swap, the next update puts the old version back, even without network access.

A plugin's settings, secrets, network grants and stored data are keyed by its name, not its version, so they carry over. If a new version asks for more than the old one had (a new permission, a new capability, or a different publisher key), update stops and prints the exact command that accepts that difference. So an update can never quietly give a plugin more power. Update also never widens a plugin's network allowlist; it prints the command instead.

### Persistence and complete-token follow-up

The signed follow-up 75116ac28a0523f5e8be1304c38e070d36b3a55e repairs two update failures. New instance rows are prepared on an owned Config clone, persisted through the existing writer, and promoted to the live batch state only after a successful save. A failed save cannot leave phantom rows for a repeated target to use; earlier successful targets and unrelated pending metadata remain intact. This adds no on-disk or cross-process transaction guarantee.

Repeatable `--allow-token TOKEN` preserves complete authority values containing commas. Existing `--allow` comma lists remain supported. Printed update commands use one quoted full-token argument per item; both forms use the same pinned-version, single-target, known-kind and exact authority matching checks.

The follow-up includes real parser/shell/config-save controls and real-binary component tests for duplicate-target save failure and both approval forms. Source and independent review plus patch/whitespace checks passed; fresh official compiler, format, lint and runtime CI for this head are pending. No local Rust tests were run.

Before chain acceptance, reconcile the actual qualified #11261/#11236 parents and retain the landed #11581 registry foundation, including its mid-body stall test. The plain-rename, host-authority, single-generation discovery and other existing plugin holds remain separate. Older approvals and CI do not validate this new follow-up.

The current signed head 277aeabb0eb12673bf8b274168f50035a2f14ad2 is a normal merge of public master ea4a54bb5bd77dd56fb76e919754bc5d63a099c3 with the repair head 75116ac28a0523f5e8be1304c38e070d36b3a55e. The sole hand resolution removes registry conflict markers and retains the landed mid-body timeout regression. The reviewed save/parser/emitter helpers and new CLI tests are preserved; both parents’ feature dependencies and test selection are retained. Fresh official CI qualifies this combined tree. Separate unmerged #11261/#11236 parent reconciliation and broader plugin holds remain.

Current-head verification: [official Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38136649290). Results remain pending until all required checks complete.

### Persistence regression fixture follow-up

The fixture follow-up `3c5fd269e9c12f5f1d5d2d8ca740272341d8cc25` seeds the two update-save regressions through `Config::save` and reloads the actual persisted document through strict canonical migration. The operator comment is now in an untouched observability table instead of decorating the schema-version item that incremental save replaces. All 25 original assertions remain, including unchanged disk on failure, staged metadata isolation, retry, earlier-target preservation and both persisted row keys. Production update behavior is unchanged by this test follow-up.

That earlier workflow is historical; the current qualified head and run are recorded below. No local Rust execution is claimed. The failing two-test run at prior `1d6622b` is baseline evidence only.

Signed head `b118a503588c3de740f0b46bd9753d75f6b64190` also repairs the shared persistence defect exposed by the tests: a valid explicit empty natural-key array becomes the canonical table-array representation when its first row is written. Leading, inner and trailing operator comments are carried once onto that row. Three config-owner regressions exercise canonical loaded plugin rows, MCP inner fields, failure/retry and metadata, and no-clobber behavior for other input shapes. The correction is confined to empty arrays; populated inline arrays and other unsupported writer shapes retain their previous warning/refusal behavior. The current descendant is qualified below. Existing update-chain, concurrency, source and release acceptance holds remain.
