### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw lets one agent hand a task to another. In the "bounded" mode the second agent is supposed to stay inside three limits set by the first: it works in its own workspace, it may only use tools the first agent had, and it may only run commands the first agent could run. Those limits held while the second agent's turn was running. They were lost by anything that kept going afterwards: a scheduled job it created, a procedure (SOP) run that was waiting for approval, a message relayed to a peer, a sub-agent it started, or a further hop of delegation. In those cases the work ran later with the full authority of whichever agent owned it.

This PR carries the limits along with that work. A job or run created under a limit is capped by it, a procedure run that would wait for an approval nobody in the turn can follow is cancelled instead, and a command has to satisfy the rules of every agent above it. It adds no capability; it only removes authority that leaked.

What stays the same: agents that are not under a limit behave as before, and jobs already stored are not retroactively capped. The limits listed under "Known boundary", "Second declared gap" and "Third and fourth declared gaps" are not closed here. Only the first has a follow-up issue (#11667); the others are described under *Declared gaps* above and have no issue yet. What operators will notice: a job or run restricted by `allowed_tools` can no longer leave a SOP waiting for approval, and can no longer write SOP definitions through `sop_workshop`.

### How you can test (when useful)

and `&[]` instead of `&deferred_mcp_tool_names` at either `seal_to_registry` call in `loop_.rs` (the fourth declared gap) stays green in the full `zeroclaw-runtime --lib` run and in the twelve ceiling test binaries, at each site, on `9d7d3ce6b` (not repeated after the merge with `master@4e82ce46e`; those lines did not move).
- **Two load-sensitive local failures, both pre-existing on `master`:** `rpc::local::tests::reload_replacement_generation_waits_for_durable_session_prompt_local` also fails on a clean `origin/master@0c28d7ce8` checkout, and `web_search_tool::tests::test_keenable_oversized_chunked_response_is_rejected_before_decoding` passes alone. On an earlier merge tree, `rpc::dispatch::tests::configure_refuses_an_incarnation_replaced_under_the_lock` (`master`'s test) failed once with two test threads and passed in 3 of 3 isolated runs and with one thread. **Under the default thread count** a full local `zeroclaw-runtime --lib` run fails 1 to 4 `rpc::dispatch::tests` with timeouts (`Elapsed`); the ones I re-ran pass in isolation, the whole run passes with `--test-threads=1` (5923 on `a126de966`), and they pass in CI. I did not try them on a clean `master`; load on my machine is the likely cause, not something I demonstrated.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** For the peer relay: traced the escape end to end (the two construction sites, `process_message`'s registry assembly, `ScopedAssembly::caller_allowed`) and confirmed it does not reopen the name-based findings, since `sop_approve` and `delegate` are excluded at the ceiling's own derivation. For the cron race: read `update_job_inner`'s call graph: it is the only writer reachable from the scheduler tools that changes a job's `command` or `allowed_tools` after creation. The declarative sync (`sync_declarative_jobs` in `cron/store.rs`, anchor `allowed_tools = ?12, source = 'declarative'`) also rewrites both columns from the operator's configuration without a guard; I did not trace whether a tool can edit that configuration. For the SOP park: read `SopEngine::gate_state` to confirm a cancelled run can never resolve as `Resumed`. For `fe804dd56`: an independent, context-free adversarial pass over the diff, the delegation contract and the review protocol found the boundary above and a `schedule` resume without `approved`, both addressed or declared in this head. For `235b709f6`: a second independent pass over the whole diff found, among other things, two wrong comments (corrected), an unrelated change to the gateway's error handling (reverted to `master`'s), and the principal-session gap above (declared). For the delta after `b2795136a`: I enumerated the places that create a sealed ceiling (`loop_.rs` twice, `delegate.rs` once) and the writers of the delegate parent-tool set (the factory's initial set, eager MCP registration, `always` pre-activation, the activation hook, and the `caller_allowed` retain); both inventories come from searches calibrated against a known site, and none of those writers adds `tool_search`. For the delta after `1a328ea53`: a second context-free review of the whole diff against `master`, by reading only (it ran no code). Its test findings are closed or declared in this head: the pre-activation policy and delegate wiring, and the clearing of the deferred listing for a caller set without `tool_search`, now have tests; the two `&[]` call sites and the SOP step's raw ceiling are declared above. I counted the destructures of `ScopedAssembled` (six, all with `..`) with a search calibrated against `loop_.rs:1718` over `crates/`, `src/`, `apps/` and `xtask/`.
  **What I did NOT verify to completion:** the peer relay and the SOP step under the command chain, end to end (the Known boundary above); `sop_list` and `sop_status` (also `SAFE_FOR_BOUNDED_REUSE`) were assumed read-only from their names and descriptions; the park-cancellation in the peer relay is covered by the shared registry-factory test and by reading the call sites that pass the sealed handle (`loop_.rs` twice), not by running that route; a SOP step turn excludes `sop_execute` and `sop_advance` by name (`SOP_CONTROL_TOOLS`, `sop/active_scope.rs:11`), so it never holds them; there is no concurrency test for `SopEngine::cancel_run` itself (the argument is a reading of the code under one `MutexGuard`); whether `advance_headless_deterministic_step` can itself invoke a command, and whether `sop_execute`/`sop_advance` can resolve a checkpoint into `spawn_headless_run_driver` by a path other than the parking one, remain untraced. Also untraced: the principal-session gap above end to end; and whether a relayed peer's turn escapes the caller's action tracker and cost context. An `independent` hop below a bounded target carries neither the ceiling nor the command chain by design: the command-chain half is pinned by `policy_for_target_attaches_the_command_chain_only_for_a_bounded_target`, the ceiling half is read from the registry construction, which passes `None`. The delta after `1a328ea53` had one context-free review that read the code but ran none. That a pre-activated tool stays callable without `tool_search` is read from the dispatcher, which looks the name up in the activated set when no static tool matches (`agent/tool_execution.rs:226`, anchor `activated_tools.get_resolved`), and from `docs/book/src/security/authentication.md:376-379` ("remain callable without the helper"); the new tests assert that the tool is activated and named in the ceiling, not that a model call reaches it. The deferred-MCP loss was reproduced with a stub-level assembly test (`ScopedToolRegistry::assemble` against a mock MCP server), not by running a full delegation or peer relay with `mcp.deferred_loading`. The claim that the bounded delegate has no such gap is read from the code and pinned by one test, not run end to end. I did not trace the live SOP step reassembly path separately for the automated reviewer's remark that later SOP hops could recover names removed from an intermediate turn. `cargo fluent check` was not run (CI does not run it). The merge and `a126de966` had a read-only, context-free review on 2026-10-17 (verdict: publish after fixes; its findings were this out-of-date text and a missing negative test, now `aa2b45b56`); `aa2b45b56` itself was not seen by it, and whether `master@cdefa0d0a` builds with this branch is untested.
- **Declared limits of the regressions:** the deferred-shell integration tests stop at the store; they do not run the scheduler or execute a command. The cross-agent SOP step started by a relayed peer has no dedicated composed regression: one was written, hit an intermittent unrelated test-infrastructure race (`"Unknown tool: delegate"`), and was deleted rather than merged flaky; the fix is covered indirectly by `bounded_delegate_sop_step_ceiling`, which exercises the same `SopStepReassembly` mechanism through `spawn_subagent`. The cron-race tests use a raw second `rusqlite::Connection` and a test-only hook (`install_after_read_hook_for_tests`) to make the race deterministic.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**: this only removes capability from bounded targets and their relayed peers.
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes**
- **Risk and mitigation:** the refusal strings are model-visible. Most are static authored text; `send_message_to_peer: refused — a delegated caller ceiling was declared but never published, so the recipient's turn cannot be bounded` fires only on an internal wiring failure, the same fail-closed contract as `spawn_subagent`'s. The two SOP refusals interpolate values the caller supplied in the same tool call (`sop_execute`'s `name`, `sop_advance`'s `run_id`), each validated against a real SOP definition or run before being echoed, the same class as the existing `require_within_ceiling` echo of stored tool names. Their failure branch also echoes the backend `StoreError`, and the live SOP driver's error echoes an engine-generated run id and the same `StoreError`: backend-internal values, so no new injection surface, with the leak risk (a storage path or driver message in a tool result) of the class already accepted for `require_within_ceiling`. `fe804dd56` adds two strings in `caller_ceiling.rs`: the `refuse_deferred_shell` refusal (static text plus the tool's own name and the literal `shell`) and the stored-command refusal `{tool}: refused — {reason}`, where `reason` is the command policy's message and can echo the stored command text (`Command not allowed by security policy: <command>`). That command was supplied when the job was written and is echoed into a tool result, again the same class. `sop_workshop`'s refusal is static text plus the action's wire name, which comes from a fixed enum (`sop_workshop.rs:208`, anchor `bounded-ceiling-sop-workshop-action`; text in `locales/en/cli.ftl`). The 15 refusals this PR adds render from `bounded-ceiling-*` Fluent keys with their previous English wording, pinned by a test, so that change introduces no new model-visible text.
- **Declared gaps:** see the Known boundary, the Second declared gap and the Third and fourth declared gaps under *Declared gaps*: the command chain does not reach a peer relay or a cross-agent SOP step, a principal-narrowed `Agent` session's scheduler tools carry no sealed ceiling, a SOP step's ceiling is the caller's raw list, and the seal's inputs at its two call sites are not pinned by a test. They are limits of what this PR closes; the code before this branch had neither bound.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No**, deliberately.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- **Exact upgrade steps for existing users:** no migration is required for existing stored jobs or running deployments; nothing persisted changes shape (see Rollback). It **does** change public Rust signatures:
  1. `zeroclaw_runtime::tools::all_tools_with_runtime`, `all_tools_with_runtime_and_acp_sessions` and `all_tools_with_runtime_and_execution_capability` (`tools/mod.rs`) each gain a final `caller_ceiling: Option<CallerCeiling>` (`CallerCeiling` is a `pub(crate)` alias of `Arc<OnceLock<Vec<String>>>`): source-breaking for a positional caller; `None` keeps the previous behavior. The cross-crate callers in this tree (`zeroclaw-gateway/src/lib.rs`, twice, and `zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs`) pass `None`. The `process_message*` entry points keep `master`'s public signatures.
  2. `zeroclaw_runtime::cron::update_job_for_agent` and `resume_job_for_agent` each gain a final `guard: JobGuard<'_>` (`cron::unguarded` for a caller with no bound to enforce). Only `zeroclaw-runtime` calls them today, but both are `pub`.
  3. `zeroclaw_config::policy::SecurityPolicy` gains a `pub` field `caller_command_bounds` (source-breaking for an out-of-tree struct literal that does not use `..Default`), a new `pub` type `CallerCommandBound` is added, and `EscalationViolation` gains a variant, `CallerCommandBoundDroppedByChild` (source-breaking for an exhaustive match). `CallerCommandPolicyShell` is removed.
  4. `zeroclaw_runtime::tools::REBOUND_BY_DOWNCAST_TOOL_NAMES` is a new `pub const` (`tools/mod.rs:620`), and `BOUNDED_DENIED_TOOL_NAMES` gains the four `a2a_*` names. `SopExecuteTool::with_caller_ceiling` and `SopAdvanceTool::with_caller_ceiling` are new `pub` builder methods (`SopWorkshopTool` gains `pub(crate)` ones). The classification lists (`FILESYSTEM_TOOL_NAMES` and the other `*_TOOL_NAMES` constants), `DelegateChannelHandles`, `image_info_tool` and `BoundedSopApproveDenied` are new `pub` items of `zeroclaw_runtime::tools`; all of these are additive.
  5. `zeroclaw_runtime::tools::scoped::ScopedAssembled` gains a `pub` field `deferred_mcp_tool_names: Vec<String>`: source-breaking for an out-of-tree struct literal or an exhaustive destructure (the six destructures in this tree use `..`: `loop_.rs:1718` and `:3704`, `agent.rs:3017`, `turn/mod.rs:3801`, `delegate.rs:1556` and `zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs:16157`).
  6. `zeroclaw_api::tool::Tool` gains a defaulted method `as_any(&self) -> Option<&dyn Any>` (it returns `None`, so no implementor has to change; the MCP tool wrapper in `zeroclaw-tools` forwards it, and the bounded rebuild uses it to downcast the tools it must rebind), and `zeroclaw_tools::mcp_client::McpRegistry` gains `pub fn server_name_for`.
  The other registry-constructor changes (`send_message_to_peer_tool` and the other registry builders) are `pub(crate)`, so they carry no external burden.

  Behavior changes for bounded delegation:
  - shell-job creation, resume and force-run need `shell` in the ceiling; patches are capped; scheduled jobs store the intersection; `sop_approve` and `delegate` cannot be smuggled into a stored job by omitting `allowed_tools`; a bounded target's action budget is intersected with the caller's; a relayed peer's turn, and a cross-agent SOP step that peer starts, are bound by the intersection;
  - a concurrent write from another turn of the owning agent can no longer land between a bounded `cron_update`/`schedule` resume's check and its write;
  - a bounded caller's `sop_execute`/`sop_advance`, and the live SOP driver after a queued step, cancel a run that would park (approval, checkpoint, unmet dependency) instead of leaving it resumable with full authority; a bounded rebind of `sop_execute` records no initiating agent;
  - a bounded delegation made inside a headless SOP step seals a ceiling that excludes what the step's scope denies;
  - `backup`/`data_management` follow `master`'s shared data directory under the target's policy;
  - every command a bounded target runs, or stores to run later, must also clear the command policy of each caller above it, at every bounded hop and for a `spawn_subagent` child; a command the caller's policy refuses is refused even if the target's profile allows it;
  - a bounded registration cannot store, launch or re-arm an agent job whose `allowed_tools` keeps `shell`, and `schedule` resume reads the request's `approved` like the create routes. A job already stored with `shell` stays stored, but a bounded turn cannot launch or re-arm it;
  - a command denied by both the target's and a caller's policy reports the target's message;
  - any `agent::run` given a per-run `allowed_tools` (a stored cron agent job with its own list, for example) now builds its scheduler tools with a ceiling sealed to the tools that run actually holds (the list intersected with its assembled registry), so a job it stores or launches is capped by it and an agent job that keeps `shell` is refused (`agent/loop_.rs:1735`, anchor `crate::tools::caller_ceiling::seal_to_registry(`, and `cron/scheduler.rs:1180`, anchor `job.allowed_tools.clone()`). Read from the code.
  - `sop_workshop` keeps only `list` and `inspect` under a caller ceiling, and `sop_execute`/`sop_advance` cancel a run that would park in every registry built with one: a bounded target, a restricted `agent::run` (so a `spawn_subagent` child and a cron-fired job) and a peer relay; a SOP step turn never holds these two tools, because the step scope excludes them by name. Under a ceiling `sop_execute` also records no initiating agent. This includes a job whose `allowed_tools` an operator wrote: such a job can no longer leave a SOP waiting for approval or write SOP definitions, so a job that has to do either must not be restricted by `allowed_tools`. An RPC principal session restricted by tool names builds its registry with no ceiling and is not covered (see the Second declared gap).

  - a turn given a per-run `allowed_tools` seals its ceiling to the tools it actually holds (plus the deferred MCP tools it may activate, and, when its set does not name `tool_search`, the ones a `mode = "always"` group already activated), not to the names it was handed: a name its own policy removed no longer counts as held, for example `shell` for a peer whose profile has none;
  - a bounded delegate's rebuilt tools read the config the delegation was admitted against, so a feature switched on or off in that config is seen by the target;
  - a nested bounded hop is handed only the MCP tools its own bundles grant;
  - the 15 refusals added by this PR render from Fluent keys; in a locale without a translation they stay English.

  Jobs already stored under the old, wider ceiling are **not** retro-capped, and a SOP run already left parked before this is deployed is not retroactively cancelled.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the commits on this branch, or revert the PR merge commit. No migration or state cleanup: nothing persisted changed shape.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. The bound is active whenever a ceiling is in force.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a legitimate scheduled job stops being created, re-armed or launched; a legitimate `sop_approve`/`delegate` capability stops surviving into a stored job; a legitimate peer relay stops receiving a tool the peer's own profile grants; a legitimate concurrent job update starts losing to a rival write; a SOP run started by a bounded caller is cancelled instead of resumable; a bounded target's command is refused that its own profile allows. Grep tool results for:
  - `refused — this stores or re-arms a shell job` (`cron_add`, `cron_update`, `schedule`, `cron_run`)
  - `refused — this job's stored allowed_tools reach beyond` and `refused — this job stores no allowed_tools`
  - `refused — this agent job would keep 'shell'`: a bounded registration tried to defer an agent with `shell`; the job has to list its tools without it
  - `<tool>: refused — ... Command not allowed by security policy` from `cron_update` or `schedule` resume: a caller's policy refuses the job's stored command; check the caller's `allowed_commands` before treating it as a regression
  - `refused — this tool was registered under bounded delegation but the caller's tool ceiling was never sealed`, and `send_message_to_peer: refused — a delegated caller ceiling was declared but never published`: fail-closed paths that indicate a sealing bug, not a policy decision
  - `refused — SOP` / `refused — run ... left outside this turn ... has been cancelled` (`sop_execute`, `sop_advance`): the parked-run cancellation path
  - ``sop_workshop `<action>` is not available under a caller tool ceiling``: the `sop_workshop` write refusal (`propose`, `capture_run`, `apply`, `reject`, `quarantine`); `list` and `inspect` are unaffected
  - `could NOT be cancelled ... may still be active - treat it as unresolved, not closed`: the cancellation failed to persist, the run is still parked and resumable; investigate the persistence backend
  - log line `bounded live SOP driver: cancelled a run that would have parked outside the turn`; its unpersisted counterpart `bounded live SOP driver: parked run could not be cancelled` comes with a turn error containing `reached a park that a bounded caller's tool ceiling cannot follow past this turn`
  - a cron job update or resume that fails with no obvious cause: check for a concurrent write from another turn of the same agent; it now surfaces as lock contention or a guard refusal instead of silently winning or losing
  - From `1a328ea53` the refusal strings above come from the `bounded-ceiling-*` keys in `locales/en/cli.ftl`; in a locale without a translation they stay the English text quoted here.

Phase 2: The Runtime. Complete the remaining runtime-composition and installable-plugin outcomes from RFC #5574 alongside compatible rolling fixes.

Source of truth: [#7432 - v0.8.6 runtime](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432#v086-runtime), including existing issues/PRs, missing work, sequencing, and acceptance evidence.

Deliverables: a clean runtime composition API; the accepted Wasmtime/WIT execution bridge in supported artifacts; registry lifecycle including updates; plugin installation during onboarding without Cargo; and the agreed minimal core-tool set with measured binary size.

Completion requires release-binary proof of tool execution, Discord plugin install/use, and onboarding without a Rust toolchain. This replaces the previous fixes-only scope. Feature acceptance, normal review/CI, and explicit release holds for breaking changes still apply.

prs.title: docs(plugins): document the Discord plugin and its acceptance run
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Issue 10999 asks for the official Discord plugin to be documented under its real package name and proven end to end from a published binary. This adds the operator page and the maintainer runbook for that. It is a draft until the pieces it documents have merged (listed below).
  - `channels/discord.md` gains "Running Discord as a plugin (experimental)": what the host needs, install and bind (`zeroclaw plugin install discord --channel-alias main --egress declared`, or `plugin bind` for an installed package), why the grant is `discord.com` plus `*.discord.gg`, the instance key for the alias `main`, the token through the masked `config set` prompt, turning plugins on, routing `plugin.main` to an agent, a peer group that admits numeric user IDs, what to check once it runs, and a comparison with the built-in channel. A callout warns against giving one bot token to both.
  - `plugins/distributing-plugins.md` gains "Package names and Cargo features": the registry package is `discord`; `channel-discord` is the Cargo feature that compiles the built-in channel; FND-001 and FND-004 say `channel-discord` and `channel-discord.wasm` for what is now the `discord` package. It also tells publishers to keep a package's name, because every instance key derives from it.
  - New `maintainers/plugin-release-acceptance.md`: the acceptance runbook. It covers recording the environment, installing by name, binding, and exercising the plugin. A 14-row evidence template (inbound, outbound, built-in channel idle, negative control, reconnect, shutdown, denied destination and recovery, denied sender, missing platform permission, invalid token, trust policy) is followed by redaction, posting, and cleanup. The page is registered in `SUMMARY.md` and the maintainers index.
- **Scope boundary:** Docs only, English source only; translations follow the normal sync. No edits to FND-001 or FND-004, which are ratified; the distribution guide records the mapping instead. No edits to pages that say release binaries ship without the plugin host, which the #10994 work owns, or to the binding docs #11302 adds.
- **Blast radius:** four existing pages gain a section or a line; one new page.
- **Current prerequisites and merge hold** (the PR remains draft):
  - #11302 is merged; its binding commands, readiness report and linked `binding-a-channel-instance` heading are now in this receiving source.
  - #11303 and #11348 are merged; the documented polling, shutdown and guest-health lifecycle is in public master.
  - #11304's WebSocket-denial record remains a prerequisite. Its current `95dcb66` CI is green, but current review and landing remain separate. #11228's selected host baseline likewise still needs its protected Runtime-owner review and landing.
  - The original [Discord port #161](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw-plugins/pull/161) is merged as `a5fb8292511a11446fe591689dead3285a65fad5`. Its landed tree exactly matches [successful current validation](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw-plugins/actions/runs/38808378778): ten jobs pass, including 65 individually named Discord tests, both Clippy lanes and the Wasm build. Iftekhar’s authorship and the original PR/topic are preserved. It remains `registry = false` against `wit/next`; source landing does not establish package publication or final released-pair acceptance.
  - A compatible published host archive and a separately reviewed released-WIT/Discord registry promotion are required before install by name. Published v0.8.5 lacks the port's required WebSocket contract; current registry/release assets contain no Discord package.
  - The existing functional test of the original Discord port #161 worked and has screenshots, as confirmed during release review. Reuse that working test and visual evidence. The 14-row published-pair template remains blank in this documentation PR; that is not evidence that no Discord test occurred. Map the existing receipts to their tested host/package revisions and fill only genuine remaining published-pair gaps before making a release acceptance claim.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10999. Related #7432 (R6).

### Current source reconciliation

Signed `26b216a43451d1860191a6aff4300a685c210c51` normally merges public master `996355b83c403e8e9b8080dff5f9b75cea188459` into the original docs topic. The merge was clean, with no manual source changes: four whole author pages, the original SUMMARY insertion, all master entries and all 14 blank acceptance rows are preserved. The binding anchor comes from already-merged #11302. No #11228 or #11304 feature parent was added.

Root and independent static review checked all 15 added links and their headings against this receiving source. These are source checks, not a built-book or live-command result. #11310 subsequently landed as `266ce2e`; its public signer changes are reconciled as current-master context for the actual tested CI merge. [Automatic Quality Gate 38499975529](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38499975529) completed with its required gate successful on this head. The current native readback confirms that result; it does not turn static link checks into built-book or live-command evidence; older `25d38658` CI and author-local checks supply no successor execution credit. No local Rust, docs helper or live Discord command was run for this publication.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can talk to Discord in two ways: the Discord support built into the program, or a Discord plugin installed separately that runs in a sandbox and can reach only the servers you allow. This PR explains how to set up the plugin, how it differs from the built-in support, and how maintainers prove the published plugin installs and runs on a released copy of ZeroClaw before telling people it works.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Optional: read the new section in `channels/discord.md` and the new runbook. The commands can only be run once the dependencies above merge.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Documentation source review for this PR. The user-confirmed working #161 test and screenshots are credited above; this documentation change adds no new operator CLI or live Discord execution. Exact final released-pair acceptance remains separate.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Read the five changed pages. Live testing needs the exact compatible published host/package pair, dedicated test bot and explicit grants described in the runbook.
- **Steps to review:** Check the binding link and the package/config/egress guidance, then confirm that the evidence template keeps all 14 outcomes and redaction requirements.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The Discord operator guide and maintainer acceptance runbook are linked from the book; the binding anchor resolves in receiving source.
- **Prior behavior (before):** These operator and acceptance instructions were absent; the earlier topic also lacked the merged binding anchor.


### Follow-up: invalid-token acceptance control

The invalid-token row now requires a syntactically valid invalid or revoked
token entered through the masked prompt. It distinguishes Discord's
authentication refusal from malformed-token rejection during local
configuration. The evidence cells remain blank; this change records no new
live acceptance result.

Validation for `25d38658`:

- Full-file `docs_quality_gate.sh` on the changed runbook: zero lint errors.
- `docs_links_gate.sh` against parent `7b4e389d`: all six collector controls
  passed; no added links.
- Only the runbook's invalid-token row changed. The PR remains draft with
  the same declared merge and publication prerequisites.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Docs Style` (markdown lint, prose em-dash check, added-link and all-internal-link gates).

prs.title: fix(anthropic): support stored OAuth profiles
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. This branch integrates upstream revision `cdefa0d0a6bf95bb9c7fe90e174b948af3a76166`; both the OAuth configuration tests and the incoming effort-routing tests are retained.

**What changed and why:**

- Adds optional Anthropic `auth_mode = "oauth"` so an alias can use its same-named stored setup-token profile. Missing or unsupported profiles fail closed at request time; streaming preserves sanitized underlying store-read/parse causes.
- Preserves static `api_key` behavior when OAuth is not selected, including inline setup tokens, and preserves the selected alias through provider construction and gateway/CLI consumers. The master integration also preserves opt-in single-tool policy through Anthropic chat and streaming, including hidden-thinking fallback and accepted whitespace-padded official endpoints.
- Keeps Quickstart's existing synthetic API-key/setup-token selector and inline mapping. The schema-field filter preserves that single legacy selector; it does not onboard stored-profile OAuth aliases. Whether this filter requires a recorded runtime holding-crate exception is a Core Team decision; no exception is claimed.
- Runs gateway and foundation-only CLI provider construction off Tokio workers, including existing Qwen/MiniMax token refresh operations.
- Keeps a credential-refresh failure distinct from missing configuration, so a failed gateway seed does not block unrelated configured agents behind Quickstart.

**Scope boundary:** no profile migration, new active-profile selection behavior, browser OAuth, refresh lifecycle or retry-policy redesign, custom OAuth endpoint, provider protocol change, or general configuration/readiness refactor. The existing setup-token command still sets its active profile; runtime OAuth selection ignores that selector and uses the configured alias.

**Blast radius:** Anthropic configuration, credential lookup and request headers, typed provider factories and fallback admission, gateway bootstrap/WebSocket construction, foundation-only CLI, Quickstart field generation, the schema-driven Web config editor, and provider documentation. Alias-aware gateway bootstrap and the foundation-only `zeroclaw agent` CLI can invoke existing Qwen/MiniMax refresh calls; the CLI now honors the selected alias's endpoint and options instead of configless defaults.

**Linked issue(s):** Related #9464: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/9464

### What this does, simply

An Anthropic alias can use a setup token already saved under the same profile name. Setting `auth_mode = "oauth"` enables that lookup; replacing the saved token affects the next request. Existing supported static aliases and Quickstart setup-token onboarding keep their previous behavior. A gateway seed's credential-refresh failure remains a real error for that provider, but no longer makes unrelated configured agents appear to need onboarding.

## Testing

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: synthetic profile and HTTP fixtures exercise selection, rejection and refresh failures without an operator token or live vendor call.

### How I tested

Current candidate: `21c781f78ee100338b60afe0706c728b5d0b8fcd`, tree `9727021c67b51a0dcac7037d88cc12ae9735c0e9`, integrating master `cdefa0d0a6bf`. The only manual conflict resolution retained both independent end-of-module test additions in `schema.rs`; no production logic needed manual editing. All required checks in [exact-head Quality Gate run 39035581632](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39035581632) passed, including MSRV and Parallel Runtime Test. This is not a claim that the outstanding Core Team placement decision is resolved.

**Current integration validation:** the merged tree passed config OAuth (3), legacy-alias round trip (1), effort routing (1), Anthropic (230) and factory (53) filters, scoped config/providers Clippy with warnings denied, formatting, range diff check, scanner fixtures (58/0) and the full comment-hygiene gate. These checks were independently repeated on `21c781f7`, together with the incoming effort-policy and capability-filter regressions (1 each). Exact-head workspace CI additionally executed gateway boot (6), WebSocket alias (1) and runtime Quickstart (75) regressions successfully; the repeated Parallel Runtime Test and workspace lint passed too. The three foundation-only CLI tests were run separately with `--no-default-features`, since default workspace CI does not select them. No live vendor call or deployment was made.

```

**Previous integration evidence (`5bcf92b7` and its merge parent; not fresh reruns on `21c781f7`):** provider/config/gateway/Quickstart/foundation CLI tests, scoped Clippy, formatting, diff and both hygiene gates passed on `5bcf92b7`. - Formatting, `git diff --check 6c23e02b6d2ecce0dbc3dff6a16ce7522e5abb9c...HEAD`, scanner fixtures (`58 passed, 0 failed`) and the full comment gate (`Comment hygiene gate passed.`) succeeded.
- Documentation gates ran against `6c23e02b6d2e`. Quality reported `No blocking markdown issues on changed lines.` The duplicate `See also` heading at line 762 also exists in the named base. Link tests passed (`Ran 6 tests in 3.021s`, `OK`); optional HTTP-link validation was skipped because `lychee` is absent.
- An initial concurrent Anthropic run on the intermediate merge reported `226 passed; 2 failed`: `anthropic_thinking_fallback_honors_provider_timeout` and `anthropic_factory_forwards_timeout_to_native_provider` exceeded their elapsed-time assertions. Both unchanged tests passed in the serial 230-test run above. No timing limit was relaxed and no passing same-environment master comparison establishes the cause. Gateway/runtime links also emitted the previously observed Darwin `__eh_frame` warning; no production-performance effect is claimed.

**Historical commands and tail output (448bf7bf / f05baa7e, not fresh reruns):**

- `cargo +1.98.1 fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check`: exit 0.
- `cargo +1.98.1 test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib credential_refresh_error_preserves_chain_without_duplicate_message`:

  ```

  The assertion was observed failing before the transparent-wrapper correction: the HTTP 503 context appeared twice. It now preserves original and cloned error-chain formatting and typed downcasting.
- `cargo +1.98.1 clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings`:

  ```

- `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.test.sh`: `58 passed, 0 failed`; `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh`: `Comment hygiene gate passed.`
- `cargo +1.98.1 test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib anthropic_oauth`:

  test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1784 filtered out; finished in 0.04s
  ```

- `cargo +1.98.1 test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib gateway_boot`:

  ```text
  test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 651 filtered out; finished in 1.03s
  ```

- `cargo +1.98.1 test --locked --no-default-features --bin zeroclaw foundation_agent_provider`:

  ```text
  test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 50 filtered out; finished in 0.39s
  ```

  The gateway tests cover synthetic refresh 200/401/503 and production-handler SSE assertions; the foundation CLI tests cover synthetic refresh 200/503.
- `cargo +1.98.1 check --locked --bin zeroclaw` checked the default CLI and integrated `zip 9.0.3` dependency:

  ```text
  Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 47s
  ```

- On `f05baa7e1edb`, `BASE_SHA=b3c615644b5201b4eec651e00d0062af95701c9c bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh`:

  ```text
  Existing markdown issues outside changed lines (non-blocking):
    - docs/book/src/providers/configuration.md:750 MD024/no-duplicate-heading Multiple headings with the same content [Context: "See also"]
  No blocking markdown issues on changed lines.
  ```

- `BASE_SHA=b3c615644b5201b4eec651e00d0062af95701c9c bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh`:

  ```text
  Ran 6 tests in 0.565s
  OK
  Collected 1 added link(s) from 2 docs file(s).
  Added HTTP(S) links detected, but lychee is not installed; skipping optional HTTP(S) validation.
  ```

  English source changes do not include generated translation churn.

**CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Quality Gate run 39035581632](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39035581632) passed on `21c781f7`: workspace tests/lint, MSRV, Parallel Runtime Test, Linux build, selected macOS/Windows/plugin checks, Security and Web Permission Tests. The completed workspace-test log contains PASS receipts for all six gateway boot cases, the WebSocket alias case and all 75 runtime Quickstart cases. Eight conditional/advisory jobs were skipped, not counted as passes. One superseded report-only risk check was canceled by its concurrency policy; [replacement run 39035610727](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39035610727) succeeded. No required check was canceled or failed.

**Known CI coverage gap:** no required-check gap remains on `21c781f7`; all selected required jobs completed successfully. The foundation-only CLI execution gap was closed locally with three passing tests. The historical `5bcf92b7` MSRV timeout and denied rerun remain historical failures, not current-head results; the new MSRV job passed. Historical local Darwin parallel-runtime failures also remain failures, not passes: the unchanged finite-yield peer fixture passed alone, but no passing same-environment master baseline established their cause. No timeout increase, lint suppression or unrelated repair was added.

**Historical local diagnostics:** earlier dependency-inclusive Clippy failed three unchanged channel `drop_non_drop` sites in the no-Telegram configuration. Earlier foundation-only Clippy reported a `needless_return` statement also present on its then-named base. Those broader commands were not rerun in this integration and are not claimed as passes; no lint suppression or unrelated repair was added. Darwin gateway/runtime test links emit the previously observed large-`__eh_frame` warning; this is not a production-performance measurement.

**Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** No live vendor call, operator credential change or deployment. Automated loopback fixtures cover refresh HTTP 200/401/503 under multi-thread Tokio, exact alias/model preservation, original failure propagation, and an unrelated configured agent's successful production Web streaming path. Static tracing checks adjacent consumers and unchanged inherited construction paths.

**Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot. Adding the schema field exposes an optional Auth Mode selector in the Web config editor's Connection tab, even though this PR does not change rendering code. Actual-interface captures show its unset, `api_key`, and `oauth` choices and the unsaved OAuth selection at 1280×720 in English.

**Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** screenshots captured on `448bf7bf5ea38de6e58695cbf1feb9b27a4a0aec`, with identical code in the earlier publication `f05baa7e1edb210ae059d152027007e71c16f155`; production Web config editor served by the worktree Vite development server against its real local gateway and a disposable schema-version-3 fixture. The build used `cargo +1.98.1 build --locked --bin zeroclaw` and completed in `2m 42s`, with the previously observed Darwin linker warning described above. The new merge does not change the Web renderer, Auth Mode descriptor, or Quickstart selector; these captures are reused interface evidence, not screenshots of the entire current code tree. They prove the editor field and unsaved-state interaction, not credential persistence or vendor authentication. The gateway boot regression separately applies boot state, calls the production webhook handler, dispatches an unrelated configured agent to a loopback provider, and collects the final SSE body.

**Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Auth Mode choices](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3415bac0-b74e-4a1f-9f3d-e054c017b18a) and [unsaved OAuth selection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0b1c79b-059b-45d7-b1ea-fcf32d5d0299). The gateway regression additionally observes HTTP 200, `fixture answer`, `event: done`, no `event: error`, and exactly one refresh call for each HTTP 200/401/503 case. It also checks that the affected failed seed returns a typed refresh error rather than a successful answer or `needs_quickstart`.

![Auth Mode choices in the synthetic Web config editor](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3415bac0-b74e-4a1f-9f3d-e054c017b18a)

![Unsaved OAuth selection in the synthetic Web config editor](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0b1c79b-059b-45d7-b1ea-fcf32d5d0299)

**Action or changed state and observed result:** opening the Auth Mode selector displayed all three choices; selecting `oauth` produced one unsaved change. The draft was discarded, and a backend read confirmed `auth_mode` remained unset. No configuration save, real credential, vendor request or deployment was used. In the automated boot regression, a failing seed refresh preserves configured gateway readiness and an unrelated configured agent finishes; invalid aliases or absent models remain unconfigured. The foundation CLI retains its selected alias and the no-entry bare `openai` fallback.

**If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** no local full container `./dev/ci.sh all`, all-features/platform sweep, live vendor call or deployment. Fresh required CI supplies workspace test/lint and selected platform coverage on the actual merge, including repeated parallel-runtime execution and MSRV. Foundation-only CLI behavior was tested separately on that head. Historical local Darwin attempts are not relabeled as successful broad validation.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? Yes: alias-aware gateway bootstrap and the foundation-only `zeroclaw agent` CLI can invoke the existing Qwen/MiniMax refresh operation when their selected alias supplies a refresh token. No endpoint implementation or protocol is added; the CLI now honors the alias's endpoint and options instead of configless defaults. Both construction paths are isolated from async workers.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- Store lookup uses the existing ZeroClaw state-directory auth store, not a broader file-access scope. Its existing legacy-encryption migration can rewrite that store during a request-time load; no migration or refresh policy is added by this PR. The state directory follows the configured location, defaulting to `~/.zeroclaw` (or relative `.zeroclaw` if no home directory is available).
- Risk and mitigation: Anthropic OAuth uses only the exactly matching supported stored setup-token profile and official API root. Invalid ownership, aliases, inline keys, profile kinds and custom endpoints fail closed. Stored-profile OAuth tokens do not enter configuration or diagnostics; existing static inline credentials retain their prior behavior. Boot refresh warnings deliberately omit raw vendor bodies, while request consumers retain the original typed cause. Tests use synthetic tokens and loopback servers.

## Compatibility

- Backward compatible? No for the fail-closed ownership changes and exhaustive Rust config literals below. Existing supported static aliases retain authentication behavior.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: optional Anthropic `auth_mode = "oauth"`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: supported static aliases need no change. To opt in, store a same-named profile using `zeroclaw auth setup-token --model-provider anthropic --profile <alias>`, select OAuth mode, and leave `api_key` and `kind` unset. OAuth requires a 1–63-character ASCII alias using only lowercase letters, digits and single internal underscores, starting and ending with a letter or digit; for example, `team_sub` is valid and `team:sub` is not. This PR does not tighten ordinary validation for non-OAuth aliases. The broader legacy-alias transition described in #9464 is tracked separately for v0.9.0.
- Renaming an OAuth configuration alias does not move its stored profile. Prepare the profile under the new alias name before using it; otherwise the renamed alias fails its request instead of borrowing the old or active profile.
- Explicit cross-provider profile IDs now fail closed for every `AuthService::get_profile` caller. Select a profile belonging to the requested provider.
- A non-Anthropic slot with `kind = "anthropic"` no longer inherits OAuth mode or `server_fallback_models` from a same-named Anthropic slot. Configure its own static credentials. Anthropic `server_fallback_models` are honored only on native `anthropic` aliases; use one if you need server-side fallback. Generic client-side `fallback_models` remain available on the slot. Fallback readiness now canonicalizes supported `kind` synonyms consistently with dispatch, such as `grok` to `xai`.
- Gateway bootstrap no longer invents an `openrouter.default` seed when no model is configured. A configured seed is a bare alias provider without the resilience wrapper; production chat still constructs its selected agent's provider independently. Existing Qwen/MiniMax refresh calls can now delay gateway bootstrap and the foundation-only `zeroclaw agent` CLI within their existing timeouts, but do not block Tokio workers. The CLI now honors the selected alias's endpoint and options. A gateway refresh failure retains configured readiness, not provider-health success; the affected CLI/request still returns the original failure, and missing/invalid configuration still stays unconfigured.
- Rust exhaustive `AnthropicModelProviderConfig` literals need `auth_mode: None` or `..Default::default()`. The optional serialized field remains omitted unless selected. The additive `AnthropicAuthMode` type and `AnthropicBuilder::auth_profile` method expose the explicit mode; `AnthropicModelProviderConfig::has_official_oauth_endpoint` exposes exact public-root admission. The provider auth module exports cloneable `ProviderCredentialRefreshError` for construction-time refresh failures. Error-chain formatting remains transparent; streamed profile-load errors now retain sanitized nested causes.
- OAuth accepts only stored token profiles resolving to the Authorization setup-token kind. A stored token tagged `auth_kind = "api-key"` and generic OAuth token sets remain unsupported. Metadata-less `sk-ant-oat01-` tokens now infer Authorization in `detect_auth_kind`, including `auth paste-token` without `--auth-kind`; existing API-key metadata is not rewritten. Re-store a genuine setup token with `auth setup-token` before OAuth opt-in if old metadata prevents use.
- Missing-credential diagnostics now mention explicit stored-profile OAuth, including for legacy aliases. OAuth warmup resolves the profile and reports a non-fatal warning on failure. The debug `credential_len` log attribute is removed; diagnostic consumers must not depend on it.

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback command/path:** remove `auth_mode` from opted-in aliases and restore their prior static `api_key` configuration; reverting the feature commits restores the earlier implementation.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `auth_mode = "oauth"` is the opt-in; no feature flag.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** unsupported/missing same-named profile, invalid alias, inline-key or `kind` conflict, unsupported endpoint, or `seed_credential_refresh_failed` warnings. A warning preserves configured readiness but does not certify credential health; correct the affected provider's credentials.
- **Ownership/bootstrap recovery:** correct foreign profile selectors, configure cross-family static slots independently, and select a model when onboarding is required. Reverting the feature commits restores earlier lookup/seed behavior; disabling OAuth alone does not revert those changes.
- **API/profile recovery:** adapt exhaustive Rust literals as above. Re-store a genuine setup token when old API-key metadata prevents OAuth; retain static mode for intended API-key authentication. Reverting code does not rewrite stored profile metadata.

## Supersede Attribution

Not applicable — this PR does not supersede another PR.

Source of truth: [#7432 - v0.9.0 gateway](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432#v090-gateway), including existing issues/PRs, missing work, sequencing, and acceptance evidence.

Deliverables: agree the full core IPC contract first; finish the supported local IPC server; ship standalone zeroclaw-gw; migrate vendor webhook behavior into channel plugins; and have Tauri package and manage both processes.

Completion requires a core artifact without web assets or HTTP server code, a working IPC-connected gateway, core/channel operation when the gateway is absent, and demonstrated two-process desktop lifecycle. Existing OIDC, principal-isolation, and ZeroRelay work must integrate with this boundary. WATI is already retired. Feature acceptance and normal review/CI/release holds still apply.

prs.title: feat(runtime): surface cost warn_at_percent warnings in ZeroCode
prs.body: ## Summary - **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions) - **What changed and why:** - `CostTracker::check_budget` returns `BudgetCheck::Warning` once recorded spend reaches `cost.warn_at_percent` of the daily or monthly limit, but `enforce_tool_loop_budget` only handled `Exceeded`. The warning was dropped, so the first sign of a limit was a failed turn. - The main tool loop now calls `announce_budget_warning` before the hard-limit gate. It sends a new `TurnEvent::BudgetWarning { current_usd, limit_usd, period }` at most once per turn. It never blocks the turn: an exceeded limit is still `enforce_tool_loop_budget`'s stop, and a full or closed event channel just drops the notice. - The RPC surface forwards the event as a `budget_warning` `session/update` (`SessionUpdateEvent::BudgetWarning`, `period` is `"day"` or `"month"`). - ZeroCode parses it and shows a system notice: "Cost warning: $8.25 of the $10.00 daily limit spent (82%). Turns stop at the limit." The daemon repeats the event on every turn while spend stays over the line. The client shows it once per period and limit per session, so it reappears only when the limit changes or the other period crosses its own threshold. - **Scope boundary:** no notice for a turn that stops at the hard limit (that is still the failed-turn message, and #11589 covers the override prompt). ACP (`acp_server.rs`) and the web gateway (`ws.rs`) ignore the new event; their `_ =>` arms already drop unknown variants. Only the English locale gets the new strings; the other locales fall back to English. `cost.enforcement.mode` stays unread. - **Blast radius:** a new `#[non_exhaustive]` `TurnEvent` variant. Every existing match has a wildcard arm (workspace `check --all-targets` passes). One extra `check_budget(0.0)` per provider call, which is the same ledger read `enforce_tool_loop_budget` already does. - **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10950. Related #11585, #11589. ### What this does, simply ZeroClaw can be told to warn you when you have spent, say, 80% of your daily AI budget. The code that works out "you are at 80%" already existed, but nothing passed the result on, so you never saw a warning. You only found out when a turn failed at 100%. This PR passes the warning through to ZeroCode, which shows it once as a line in the chat. Nothing is blocked and no setting changes. ## Testing (required) ### How you can test (when useful) - **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes - **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` (ZeroCode) - **Setup / preconditions:** an isolated config with `[cost] enabled = true`, a small `daily_limit_usd` (for example `0.50`) and the default `warn_at_percent = 80`, on a priced model. - **Steps to run:** chat until recorded spend passes 80% of the limit, then send one more message. - **Expected on this branch (after):** a "Cost warning: $… of the $0.50 daily limit spent (…%)" system line appears once, before the reply. Later turns don't repeat it. - **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** no warning. The first visible sign is "Budget exceeded: … Cannot make further API calls until the budget resets." when the limit is hit. ### How I tested - **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust test and clippy jobs cover all three crates touched. - **Conflict refresh validation:** Head `42170990c043461acf72e8ebe5977160095c9cf0` integrates master `cdefa0d0a6bf95bb9c7fe90e174b948af3a76166`, preserving its seeded request usage alongside the once-per-turn warning latch. Formatting and scoped comment hygiene passed. The resolved file and the eight-file PR diff pass whitespace checks; the full merge check only flags unchanged vendored Markdown inherited from master. Comparison with Git's automatic merge confirms only the one approved conflict block differs. [Fresh Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39035246444) passed Format, `Check (default features, all targets)` and Lint on this exact head, including Clippy and the Rustdoc warnings gate; other CI jobs are still running. No local Cargo or new terminal interaction was run for this mechanical refresh. Prior-head test results below remain historical. - **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none for the logic. The live crossing in ZeroCode is being dogfooded (below). - **Commands run and tail output** (run on a Mac mini through our cargo wrapper, at 5f66713d5a9d): - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- budget_warning spend_past_the_warning spend_below_the_threshold` → `test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed` - `cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode -- budget_warning` → `test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed` - Each test fails with its fix removed: with `announce_budget_warning` made a no-op and the dispatch arm returning `None`, 2 of the 3 runtime tests fail; with the client dedupe disabled, `budget_warning_shows_one_notice_per_period_and_limit` fails. - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → `Finished`, no warnings - `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` → `Finished` - Wider runs: `zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- agent::turn rpc::dispatch agent::cost` gives 938 passed, 1 failed; `zerocode --bin zerocode` gives 1447 passed, 1 failed. The two failures (`new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants`, `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`) also fail on master on this machine. - `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the changed files is clean. - **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Tested with $40 budget. Warning appeared at $33.73. - **Visual interface evidence:** - **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 5f66713d5a9d, ZeroCode chat state (`chat::tests::budget_warning_*`). - **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** above - **Action or changed state and observed result:** see the tests above. - **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** a full `cargo test --workspace` was skipped; CI runs it. ## Security & Privacy Impact (required) - New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No - New external network calls? No - Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No - PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No - Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The notice is client-side chat state and never enters model history. - If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A ## Compatibility (required) - Backward compatible? Yes. Older clients ignore an unknown `session/update` type. Older daemons never send it. - Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. `warn_at_percent` now does what its docs say. - Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No ## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs) - **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert 5f66713d5a9d` - **Feature flags or config toggles:** `cost.warn_at_percent = 100` makes a warning coincide with the limit, which in effect turns it off. - **Observable failure symptoms:** repeated cost-warning lines in ZeroCode, or none at all. Grep the runtime trace for `cost warning threshold reached`.

prs.title: fix(agent): bound repeated tool failures and preserve completed work
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Resolve existing root pacing policy for configured Agent turns instead of forcing loop detection off.
  - Give repeated identical successful results one advisory. Contain repeated identical completed failures with a correction, one final retry, and a recoverable stop that retains completed results.
  - Use the executed tool's canonical identity so short/full aliases cannot bypass the retry budget. Keep approvals, exclusions and cancellation outside executed-failure evidence.
- **Scope boundary:** No blanket duplicate suppression, successful-polling hard stop, permanent blacklist, model setting, context/iteration-limit change, new config key or public API shape change. Standalone builders without full/live config and legacy channel detection keep their behavior.
- **Blast radius:** Both configured Agent APIs and their ACP consumers. Shared tool resolution and history closeout require coverage across sequential/parallel batches, aliases, hooks and cancellation.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11484.
- **Runtime placement:** The bounded recovery scope is covered by the approved exception merged in #11436.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw runs the model's requested tools and sends their results back so it can decide what to do next. A model can keep requesting the same action even after it gets the same error. Configured Agent turns previously forced the repetitive-tool safeguards off, so that cycle could continue until the general iteration limit.

After three identical completed failures by default, the next model request now receives a correction. The model can change approach or make one final identical retry. If that retry fails identically and nothing else in the round makes progress, ZeroClaw ends the turn with an explanation and keeps every completed result. Extra identical requests in that recovery batch get paired skipped results instead of more executions. A new user turn can retry normally.

An unchanged successful result is not proof of a stuck turn. Successful polling gets at most one reminder and can continue; changing results and successful recovery can continue too. This is a runtime retry policy, not a claim that a network error is permanent or that every model loop can be recognized.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The larger diff is one connected repair. Actual-dispatch provenance, recovery admission and transcript-preserving closeout must agree. Simply enabling the old arguments/names-only detector would stop productive polling and can discard the final completed round. The focused test module supplies deterministic Agent-boundary coverage; the runtime reuses the existing policy, executor and shared turn engine rather than adding another orchestration layer.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Whether a particular model repeats a call is nondeterministic; the focused tests deliberately repeat after correction through the production Agent APIs.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The [Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39020947601) passed at `6e7508873e3f0108efdd44173b67a689c643efaa`, including workspace tests, Lint, Format, Landlock, PostgreSQL memory and channel suites. That head merges current master (`bec5a3f04c0b744038ed6114da3ada7df4f6279d`) and updates two recovery/steering tests: mid-turn steering now yields the tool loop after a round (#11725), so each test queues its steering message at the round it exercises. The guarded behavior is unchanged: queued steering cannot restart an exhausted turn, and reentry keeps the advisory and the spent recovery budget.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** A live Woof/MLX-LM turn and complete ZeroCode UI replay were not captured. The deterministic tests reach both Agent APIs, including the streamed entry point used by ACP.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

The result below was obtained at `6e7508873e3f0108efdd44173b67a689c643efaa`. Formatting, Clippy with `-D warnings` and comment hygiene were rerun at the same head. Catalogue checks confirmed unique IDs and retention of all four recovery messages and the incoming HTTP-timeout message.

```text
cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -E 'test(agent::safety_net) | test(agent::tool_execution) | test(steering) | test(tree_budget_final_completion) | test(single_tool)'
Summary: 118 tests run: 118 passed, 5682 skipped

cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
Finished

cargo fmt --all -- --check
Passed

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.
```

The macOS debug test harness emits a linker warning because its `__eh_frame` section exceeds the 16 MiB compact-unwind offset limit. Section inspection confirms that cause. Linking and all selected tests completed successfully; this is not production-build performance evidence.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Inspected canonical policy ownership, the two Agent callers, private loop compatibility, actual completion provenance, alias resolution, paired skipped results, hook abandonment and append-before-stop ordering. Successful polling, final-attempt recovery, changed arguments, useful work in the same batch, ignored aliases, live-policy refresh and queued steering are exercised by automated Agent tests.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A for presentation. This PR changes runtime enforcement, not a renderer or layout; responses and `TurnEvent::Chunk` supply the relevant automated boundary evidence.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** This PR's candidate source, streamed and non-streamed Agent APIs; `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/safety_net_loop_recovery.rs` plus existing safety-net and executor tests.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** `repeated_failures_close_both_agent_apis_after_correction_and_preserve_pairs` checks the full correction in the next outgoing system prompt, four actual executions, preserved result IDs and the localized terminal response. Streaming cases also check matching call/result IDs and the terminal chunk.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** A scripted provider disregards the correction and repeats the failure. The turn completes recoverably after its final retry rather than requesting another summary/model round. Sequential/parallel recovery batches execute only one matching retry and pair the extra calls with skipped results.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local workspace-wide tests and Clippy are delegated to fresh required CI instead of duplicating that breadth. No interactive model/UI smoke was run.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No. The guard limits existing repeated dispatches.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. Existing executor egress scrubbing is retained.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Fixtures use synthetic tool names and arguments.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Runtime-owned localized correction and stop messages are model-visible. They interpolate no tool arguments, remote error bodies or credentials; evidence retains hashes only. Existing tool output remains subject to the same security and approval policy.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for public API/config shape, standalone defaults and legacy detector behavior. Configured Agent turns intentionally begin honoring the existing enabled pacing policy.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new fields or commands. Existing `pacing.loop_detection_enabled`, `loop_detection_max_repeats` and `loop_ignore_tools` govern the Agent guard. The legacy elapsed-output setting does not delay this failure recovery.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps for existing users: No migration. Configured turns use the existing policy; opt out with `pacing.loop_detection_enabled = false` when needed. Canonical ignore entries cover short aliases of the executed tool.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's commits, or disable `pacing.loop_detection_enabled` in the supported config editor and begin a new turn after configuration reload.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Existing `pacing.loop_detection_enabled`; existing repeat threshold and canonical `loop_ignore_tools` entries remain available.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A useful retry is stopped unexpectedly, recovery skips lack paired result IDs, or the user sees a recovery-exhaustion message despite changed completed work. The Agent-boundary tests cover these contracts. A finite retry budget can stop before a later transient network recovery; retrying in a new turn is the recovery path.

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Propose adding `src/agent/turn/mod.rs` to the existing #9447 runtime holding-crate exception, solely for drop-safe physical-attempt accounting through response interpretation.
  - Keep the original #11625 approval explicitly limited to its original scope; the added path requires a new recorded Core Team decision.
- **Scope boundary:** Only `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` changes, in one existing table row. No runtime code, new subsystem, cancellation source, asynchronous drop work, independent accounting ledger, configuration, authentication, or provider protocol change. The existing destination and review condition are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** Contributor placement authority for one additional path if approved. This governance-sensitive proposal does not certify #9447's implementation or waive its review, CI, or merge gates.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9447; follow-up to merged #11625. This proposal targets `master` independently; the approved amendment must be recorded and land before the covered addition in #9447 merges.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9447
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11625

### What this does, simply

A delegate can time out after one provider attempt has already incurred usage while a fallback attempt is still waiting. The existing usage collector knows about the completed attempt, but dropping the surrounding operation can discard that information before runtime cost settlement.

The proposed #9447 correction keeps the existing accounting owner alive through response interpretation and settles remaining known, billable usage exactly once if the future is dropped. Its normal settlement boundary is in `src/agent/turn/mod.rs`, which the original exception's path list omitted. Immediate extraction would turn this accounting repair into a broader agent-loop migration.

This PR requests only that additional path for the existing accounting obligation. Provider parsing and candidate selection stay outside runtime, and the planned agent-loop extraction destination is unchanged. Pending approval grants no additional permission.

### Requested Core Team decision

Before merging, replace the pending addition's approval text in the row with the approving Core Team member and a public decision link. The original approval is not presented as approval of the addition.

prs.title: fix(desktop): reopen the window after close and let tray Quit exit
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - **Closing the dashboard hides it.** Nothing handled `CloseRequested` before, so the X destroyed the dashboard window while the tray kept the app running. A new `window` module hides the `main` window on close instead. The splash still closes normally, because `open_dashboard` closes it to hand off to the dashboard.
  - **One way back for every route.** Tray left-click, **Show Dashboard**, **Agent Chat** and the single-instance callback (relaunching the app) each called `get_webview_window("main")`. The lookup returned `None`, so each silently did nothing. They now share `window::show_main_window`, which reveals the dashboard, or the splash during startup. Revealing also restores a minimized window, which `set_focus` alone doesn't do on Windows.
  - **Rebuild when no window exists.** If the splash was closed before the dashboard opened, the helper rebuilds the splash from its `tauri.conf.json` entry. The rebuilt splash runs the normal handoff once the gateway is healthy. The rebuild runs on its own thread, because building a webview inside a tray, menu or single-instance handler deadlocks on Windows. A mutex keeps two rebuilds from racing on the same label.
  - **A reopened splash still shows startup failures.** A rebuilt splash is a new page, so it missed a failure (missing `zeroclaw` binary, or the daemon failing to start) that was reported before it existed. The failure is now kept in shared state (`AppState::startup_failure`) when it's reported. The splash fetches it with a new `get_startup_failure` command once its status listener is registered, so it shows the error either way.
  - **Quit exits.** `.run()` declined every `ExitRequested`, including the one from tray **Quit**'s `app.exit(0)`. It now declines only requests without an exit code, which is what closing the last window sends.
  - **Tray click fires once.** Tray left-click now acts on the button release only. One click used to fire for both the press and the release.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - **Daemon unchanged.** The daemon the app starts stays detached and keeps running after Quit. Whether Quit should stop it is the open question in #11281.
  - **Not covered:**
    - The macOS dock-icon click (`RunEvent::Reopen`).
    - **Agent Chat** navigation. It sets `location.hash = '/agent'`, which the dashboard's `BrowserRouter` ignores; this is an existing bug, and the item still only brings the window back.
    - The splash handoff and pairing.
- **Blast radius:**
  - Only `zeroclaw-desktop` (`apps/tauri`) changes; nothing else depends on this crate.
  - Draft #11281 changes the same `ExitRequested` arm. This PR uses the same function name and behavior (`keep_running_on_exit_request(code) -> code.is_none()`), so #11281 can drop its copy when it rebases.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11087. Related #11281, #7527 (an older macOS report of the same end state).

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw Desktop runs in the system tray. On Windows, closing its window with the X left the app running, but nothing could bring the window back:
- clicking the tray icon did nothing;
- the tray menu did nothing;
- starting the app again did nothing.

**Quit ZeroClaw** didn't work either, so Task Manager was the only way out. With this change, closing the window hides it to the tray, and the tray icon, the tray menu and starting the app again all bring it back as it was. Quit closes the app and removes the tray icon. If you close the small startup window before the dashboard appears, the same routes reopen it, and it still shows any startup error, such as ZeroClaw not being installed. A ZeroClaw daemon the app started still keeps running after Quit, as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. The bug is on every desktop OS, but it's most visible on Windows.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** the desktop app's tray and window lifecycle. The `web` dashboard it hosts is unchanged.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A gateway on `127.0.0.1:42617` (`zeroclaw daemon`), then `cargo run -p zeroclaw-desktop`.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Wait for the dashboard window.
  2. Close it with the title-bar X.
  3. Left-click the tray icon.
  4. Close it again, then choose **Show Dashboard** in the tray menu.
  5. Close it again, then start the app a second time.
  6. Choose **Quit ZeroClaw** in the tray menu.
- **Expected on this branch (after):**
  - Steps 3, 4 and 5 each bring the same dashboard back without reloading it.
  - Step 6 ends the process and removes the tray icon.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):**
  - After step 2 the window is gone and steps 3 to 6 do nothing.
  - The process keeps running until it is killed.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Desktop App Check runs `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets -- -D warnings` on macOS, Linux and Windows. That covers compiling on all three platforms, including the macOS and Linux builds I couldn't run.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:**
  - CI runs no desktop crate tests; #11270 proposes adding them. The four new unit tests only ran locally.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - **Setup.** I ran the debug build from `master` and from this branch on Windows 11, against a stub gateway. The stub answered `/health` with `{"status":"ok","require_pairing":false}` and served a static page at `/`. No ZeroClaw kernel was installed.
  - **How the steps were driven.** Each action was sent through Win32 messages that take the same code paths as a real click:
    - closing a window: `WM_CLOSE` to it, as the title-bar X does;
    - a tray click: a left-button down and up through tray-icon's callback message to its `tray_icon_app` window;
    - a tray menu item: `WM_COMMAND` with the muda item id.

  - **Results.** The window lifecycle steps ran at `6d71b5aa`. At `9e62adb7` I re-ran a normal launch, close, tray click and Quit, plus the startup-failure steps in the second table.

  | Step | `master` | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | Launch | Splash hands off; dashboard 1215x837 visible | Same; splash destroyed, not hidden |
  | Close dashboard | Window destroyed; process keeps running | Same window handle, now hidden; process keeps running |

  | Quit ZeroClaw | Nothing; process keeps running | Process exits with code 0. Tauri's exit cleanup clears tray icons; icon removal not checked visually |
  | Gateway down: close the splash, then tray click | Nothing; process left with no window | Splash rebuilt |
  | Gateway down: close the splash, then start a second instance | Not tried | Splash rebuilt; no deadlock |
  | Gateway down: three tray clicks plus Show Dashboard in a burst | Not tried | Exactly one splash window |
  | Gateway back up | Not tried | Rebuilt splash hands off to the dashboard |

  | Start the gateway | Not tried | Splash hands off to the dashboard despite the recorded failure |

    - Real mouse clicks; the synthetic messages drive the same tray-icon and muda handlers.
    - macOS and Linux behavior.
    - Release or installer builds.
    - A real gateway or daemon.
