prs.title: feat(rpc): dispatch plugin webhooks over the core RPC
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (`a0f70b7925`). **Depends on #11319** (core ingress, which itself now builds on #11339) and **#11165** (`zeroclaw-rpc-proto`). The branch merges #11319 at `98e1666b31` plus #11319's log-path redaction `fc5f3e95b9` (merged on its own, so master does not come in with it), and #11165 at its current head `ec00bf0a12`; their commits show in the diff until they land, so review this PR's own commits, `7962184961` (the methods), `b5d9ebd577` (channel scoping), `fcf4f6121c` (the review's two non-blocking warnings), `4e9a208600` (channel rename and delete carry `allowed_channels` grants) and `d6ef5dc0af` (the removed-binding interval test). **Needs the holding-crate exception from #11317 approved first.**
- **#11165:** its current head merges master and resolves #10621 itself, so this branch now takes #11165's own resolution. The only conflict was the rewrapped catalog line in `schema.rs`, which takes #11165's wrapping; the proto crate, the OpenRPC document and the runtime RPC types match #11165 plus this PR's additions.
- **Channel scoping (maintainer decision on this PR):** `channels:execute` and `channels:read` reach only the channel instances a profile names, and config can close the path for a channel or an agent whatever the grants. Field names and defaults:
  - `[permission_profiles.<name>] allowed_channels = ["plugin.<alias>", ...]`: a channel selector like `allowed_agents`. Entries are `<type>.<alias>` names of configured instances, validated at load; `"*"` grants every instance; empty (the default) grants none. `admin`, including the same-uid shared operator, reaches all.
  - `[channels.plugin.<alias>] accept_injected_webhooks = true` (default): `false` refuses webhooks delivered through `plugin-webhook/dispatch` to that instance.
  - `[agents.<alias>] accept_injected_webhooks = true` (default): `false` refuses such a delivery to any channel the agent handles.
  - Checked at dispatch, not only when routes are listed: `PluginWebhookIngress::dispatch_admitted` runs the check on the owner the request would be queued to, before anything is queued or reserved, so a republished route cannot redirect an admitted request. A refusal is `FORBIDDEN` with an audit record. `plugin-webhook/routes` lists only granted channels.
  - The docs say what `channels = ["execute"]` and `["read"]` unlock (authentication guide and RPC socket guide), and that a route path can be a vendor's shared secret.
  - From the review's non-blocking warnings (`fcf4f6121c`): the refusal for an ungranted channel names no channel, while its audit record still does, and a route whose channel instance the live config no longer binds is refused (fail closed) until the next reload retires it. `d6ef5dc0af` proves that interval: a route admitted while its instance is bound is refused `FORBIDDEN` once a live config write removes the instance, while the route is still published, and its worker receives nothing (asked for in Audacity88's review of #11322).
  - Renaming or deleting a channel instance carries its `allowed_channels` grants along (`4e9a208600`): a rename rewrites them to the new name, a delete drops them, and the changed profiles are saved, so a grant never blocks the change.
- **What changed and why:** A gateway in another process needs to hand channel-plugin webhook requests to the core that owns the route table. Three daemon RPC methods over the core ingress:
  - `plugin-webhook/dispatch` (`channels:execute`): method, raw query, headers, and the body as standard base64 under a caller-chosen `request_id`; answers a typed outcome (`ack`, `reply` with `body`, `not_found`, `queue_full`, `unavailable`, `unauthorized`, `bad_request`, `invalid_response`, `timeout`, `cancelled`). Validated by the same shared constructor the HTTP adapter uses.
  - `plugin-webhook/cancel` (`channels:execute`): cancels an in-flight dispatch on the same connection; the dispatch response stays authoritative.
  - `plugin-webhook/routes` (`channels:read`): current route owners, for diagnostics.
  - Local IPC only: an exhaustive transport match refuses all three on WSS with FORBIDDEN and an audit record.
  - Dispatch runs in a task spawned from the dispatcher like `session/prompt`, so the serial read loop stays live for cancel and other requests. Each connection tracks in-flight dispatches for cancel and duplicate-id checks and holds at most 1024 until their responses are queued; the next gets `queue_full`. Connection close and daemon reload cancel in-flight work and send nothing; shutdown joins the tasks and never waits on a full writer queue.
  - The daemon registry hands the generation's ingress to the RPC context, and the daemon always builds one ingress.
- **Scope boundary:** No gateway change (the forwarder is the next PR). No new principal or credential. Runtime edits stay within the #11317 row: `src/rpc/{dispatch,context}.rs`, `src/daemon/{registry,mod}.rs`, and the denial message keys in `locales/en/cli.ftl`. The new config field also updates `PluginChannelConfig` literals inside the test modules of `src/plugin_runtime.rs` and `src/tools/mod.rs` (mechanical, test-only). The grant selector and config fields live in `zeroclaw-api` and `zeroclaw-config`.
- **Blast radius:** runtime RPC dispatcher (new arms, per-connection state, shutdown join), daemon registry, `RpcContext` (all 14 literals), the OpenRPC document (regenerated), `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` (8 wire types, 3 `Method` variants), `zeroclaw-api` (route listing, the `allowed_channels` selector), `zeroclaw-infra` (route listing, `dispatch_admitted`), `zeroclaw-config` (three fields).
- **Follow-ups from the review, not in this PR:** one local-only gate shared with `file/upload/*`, with a per-method "local only" classification `xtask` can emit (#11566), and `schemars` bounds on the dispatch wire fields so the OpenRPC document states them (#11567).
- **Merge-order note:** #11186 adds `TransportKind::Inproc`. The transport match here is deliberately exhaustive, so whichever of this PR and #11186 lands second must add the `Inproc` arm (refused, with its test; #11322 carries both). #11289 replaces the free-text `AuthDenied::forbidden(message)` with `RpcDenialReason`: whichever of this PR and #11289 lands second needs variants for this PR's four refusals (for example `local_ipc_only`, `channel_not_granted`, `channel_refuses_injected_webhooks`, `agent_refuses_injected_webhooks`) and the updated audit assertions, which now read `reason` as a stable identifier.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11003. Related #7432. Related #11000. Related #11001. Depends on #11165.
- **Labels:** `ci`, `docs`, `dependencies`, `core`, `daemon`, `gateway`, `runtime`, `tests`, `scripts`, `size:XL`, `cli` (applied by the labelers)

### What this does, simply

The daemon already answers RPC calls from local clients such as zerocode. This PR teaches it three more calls so a separate web gateway can say "here is a webhook request for this plugin URL, what should I answer?" and get back the same result the in-process gateway gets today. Only local connections may use them, and only callers allowed to operate the specific channels they ask for. An operator can also switch the path off for one channel, or for one agent, in config, whatever access a caller has.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** local RPC socket.
- **Steps to run:** start a daemon with a configured channel plugin that claims a webhook path, then over `socat READLINE UNIX-CONNECT:<data_dir>/daemon.sock` send `initialize`, then `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"plugin-webhook/routes","params":{},"id":2}` and a `plugin-webhook/dispatch` for that path.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** routes lists the owner; dispatch answers `{"outcome":"ack"}` or the plugin's reply.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `METHOD_NOT_FOUND`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Test` (runtime `rpc::` and `daemon::` suites, proto tests), `Parallel Runtime Test` (runtime/channels interference), `Installer Drift` (OpenRPC `--check`), plugin legs for the ingress and gateway parity.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Windows named pipes are not exercised by a required job.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (head `b5d9ebd577`: this PR with #11319 `98e1666b31` and #11165 `ec00bf0a12` merged, on master `a0f70b7925`; macOS arm64, rustc 1.98.0)

```text
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::
test result: FAILED. 784 passed; 1 failed   (configure_refuses_an_incarnation_replaced_under_the_lock, see below)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::dispatch::tests::plugin_webhook   (x3)
test result: ok. 26 passed   (includes plugin_webhook_dispatch_reaches_only_granted_channels and plugin_webhook_dispatch_honors_channel_and_agent_refusal)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib daemon::
test result: FAILED. 101 passed; 1 failed; 1 ignored   (a_live_config_write_reaches_the_daemon_pricing_refresher_without_a_reload, see below)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra --lib ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib
ok. 295 passed, ok. 335 passed ; ok. 1760 passed   (channel selector, allowed_channels validation, accept_injected_webhooks defaults, dispatch_admitted)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto --features schema-export
ok. 29 passed ; ok. 32 passed
$ cargo run --locked -p xtask --bin generate -- openrpc --check ; cargo test --locked -p xtask openrpc
openrpc: docs/book/src/architecture/zeroclaw-rpc.openrpc.json is in sync ; ok
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features plugins-wasm --lib ; --test golden_frames plugin_webhook
ok. 653 passed ; ok. 5 passed (fixtures unchanged)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib plugin_runtime:: ; cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test plugin_channel_runtime_e2e ; --test architecture
ok. 17 passed ; ok. 5 passed ; ok. 57 passed
$ cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets ; cargo check --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --tests ; RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
Finished ; Finished ; Finished, no warnings
$ cargo clippy (api, infra, config, gateway, rpc-proto; with and without zeroclaw-gateway/plugins-wasm; root bin and e2e) --no-deps -- -D warnings
Finished, no warnings
$ TMPDIR=/private/tmp ./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh ; ZEROCLAW_PARALLEL_TEST_SCOPE=channels ./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh
runtime run 1/3: 5466 passed; 1 failed (peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget; the gate stops there) ; channels x3: ok. 1967 passed
$ comment hygiene, change filter, docs quality and docs links gates
all pass
```

The three failing runtime tests fail identically on untouched master `a0f70b7925` in this environment (two runs each), and this PR does not touch them. `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` stops only on the pre-existing macOS `unused import std::sync::mpsc` in `service/mod.rs`; no lint in any changed runtime file.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Mutations caught by the new tests: releasing the permit before the send, shutdown not joining dispatch tasks, releasing the id after the send, allowing WSS, removing the send's race against connection cancel, and skipping the denial audit record.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Refresh for the #11322 review (head `d6ef5dc0af`):** the same suite again: `rpc::dispatch::tests::plugin_webhook` 27 passed (with the new test), and the only failures are the same three pre-existing runtime tests and the macOS `std::sync::mpsc` clippy warning described above. The new test fails if a missing binding is admitted.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --no-default-features --features agent-runtime` fails on six pre-existing dead-code helpers in `src/main.rs` whose only caller is gateway-gated; unrelated, reproduces on master.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes: `Resource::Channels` gains its first RPC consumers, scoped to named channel instances through `allowed_channels`. `admin`, including the same-uid shared operator, reaches every route; any other profile reaches only the instances it names. `accept_injected_webhooks = false` on a channel instance or an agent refuses the path whatever the grants. Plugins still verify vendor signatures.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No (headers pass through to the guest as they do over HTTP)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No new path: dispatched messages enter the same plugin channel listener as HTTP webhooks.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: local IPC only (WSS refused with an audit record); grants checked at admission; the core enforces the shared request bounds, so a local caller bypassing the gateway's rate limit still cannot exceed them; 1024 in-flight dispatches per connection; no diagnostic detail in results.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes (additive methods). Builds with plugins but without the gateway now build the ingress, so webhook-capable plugin channels validate and publish their route claims instead of activating poll-only. A worker that drops its reply after the caller cancelled now reports `cancelled` instead of `unavailable`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes, additive: `[permission_profiles.<name>] allowed_channels` (default empty, so a profile with `channels` grants but no selector reaches no channel; nothing consumed `channels` before this PR), and `accept_injected_webhooks` on `[channels.plugin.<alias>]` and `[agents.<alias>]` (default `true`).
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; the methods disappear (`METHOD_NOT_FOUND`) and nothing persisted changes.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** remove `channels:execute` or the channel from a profile's `allowed_channels` to deny dispatch; `accept_injected_webhooks = false` on a channel instance or agent closes the path whatever the grants; `plugins.enabled = false` publishes no routes.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `RPC authorization denied` records for `plugin-webhook/*`, with reasons naming the channel or agent that refused; `queue_full` answers at the per-connection cap; WARN `plugin_webhook_dispatch_notification` for notification-form dispatches.

prs.title: fix(prompt): drop wall-clock date from channel and agent::run system prompts
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Channels no longer refresh `## Current Date` into the system prompt on every message; generated date sections are stripped instead.
  - `agent::run` / `build_system_prompt*` no longer inject `## Current Date`.
  - Why: a date that changes at midnight busts the provider prompt cache for every live session (same reasoning as #10858 for the Agent path). Per-turn context already carries the clock.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change `[turn-context]` preamble fields, agent::run `[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS TZ]` user-message prefixes, or personality-file / deferred-tool prompt-cache work (#11696 / #11703).
- **Blast radius:** Channel orchestrator system prompts and the shared `agent::run` system-prompt builder. Messaging channels and long interactive `zeroclaw agent` sessions.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11704. Related #10858.

### What this does, simply

Long channel chats and interactive `zeroclaw agent` sessions were paying for a full uncached request after local midnight because the system prompt still contained today's date. The model already gets the current time on every turn (channel `[turn-context]` line; agent message timestamp prefix). This PR stops putting the calendar date in the system prompt so the cached prefix can stay stable across midnight, matching what #10858 already did for the ZeroCode/gateway Agent path.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — covered by focused unit tests that assert the system prompt no longer injects today's date and strips generated date sections.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** N/A
- **Setup / preconditions:** N/A
- **Steps to run:** N/A
- **Expected on this branch (after):** N/A
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** N/A

### How I tested

```sh
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib build_channel_system_prompt_strips -- --nocapture
# test orchestrator::tests::build_channel_system_prompt_strips_generated_current_date_section ... ok
# test orchestrator::tests::build_channel_system_prompt_strips_legacy_datetime_keeps_project_note ... ok
# test result: ok. 2 passed

cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib prompt_contains_all_sections -- --nocapture
# test orchestrator::tests::prompt_contains_all_sections ... ok
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Required CI on `86bcb8e3ca1129bbdfdceec998d02a16ffcfbf7c`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38971621453) passed. The Test job ran the date-removal, multibyte-text, dated-project-note, date-line-matcher, per-turn-context, and channel prompt-stability tests; runtime and channels are covered by the workspace suite.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib` was not completed locally (OOM / SIGKILL while linking the runtime test crate). Channel tests call `build_system_prompt` and assert no `## Current Date`, which covers the runtime builder change.
- **Commands run and tail output:** see above (2 + 1 tests ok).
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Did not run a live Telegram/agent session across midnight.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — no user-visible UI change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** The local commands above were run on `5e74a88a7` on `fix/11704-prompt-date-cache`. Current-head automated evidence is the [Test job on `86bcb8e3ca1129bbdfdceec998d02a16ffcfbf7c`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38971621453/job/117211101671), including the existing test that drives channel turns through a recording model provider.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full `zeroclaw-runtime` lib tests — OOM compiling the test crate on this runner.

prs.title: fix(tunnel): supervise and verify the tailscale gateway serve process
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The gateway's `tailscale serve|funnel --https=443` child was spawned in `TailscaleTunnel::start()` and never waited for. When it exited (port 443 still held by another foreground session, or a lost serve-config etag race with the `--tcp` forwarders started right after it), it stayed `<defunct>` for the life of the daemon. `health_check` still reported it alive because `tokio::process::Child::id()` stays `Some` until the child is polled to completion, and `start()` had already advertised a URL that nothing served.
  - The gateway serve process is now owned by the same watcher the TCP forwarders already use (`TcpForwarder` generalised to `ServeProcess`). An exit is reaped and logged with its stderr, stop or drop kills and reaps it, and `health_check` reflects the real state.
  - `start()` returns the URL only once `tailscale serve status --json` shows a new foreground session proxying `443` to `http://127.0.0.1:<local_port>`. Otherwise it fails with the process's stderr, and the gateway's existing `Err` path falls back to local-only.
  - `listener already exists for port N` (observed on Tailscale 1.104.1) is now retryable alongside the existing etag-conflict case, bounded to five attempts (about 2.5s of linear backoff). A previous generation's session being torn down across a reload is waited out; a holder that stays is reported, not spun on.
  - Serve stdout (an unread banner) is discarded instead of piped, so it can never fill a pipe and block the process.
- **Scope boundary:** No other tunnel provider, no change to the `Tunnel` trait or the gateway crate, no automatic respawn of an exited serve process, and no public exposure change (WSS/enrollment stay tailnet-only). Serve processes orphaned by a daemon that dies without running destructors (crash, SIGKILL) are **not** addressed here: they keep holding the port, and with this PR the next start reports that clearly instead of going defunct. A parent-death signal needs a dedicated spawner thread (Linux `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` is per forking thread, and tokio's `block_in_place` can retire such a thread), so it is left for a separate change.
- **Blast radius:** Tailscale tunnel users only. Behaviour change: if 443 cannot be published, `start()` now fails, so the gateway takes its existing "Tunnel failed to start, falling back to local-only" path and does not go on to publish WSS/enrollment via `publish_tcp_services`. Before, those were published next to a dead 443 proxy. Gateway startup may also wait up to about 2.5s (retries) or 5s (apply timeout) per serve process when tailscaled is slow or the port is held.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11530, Related #11531

### What this does, simply

With the Tailscale tunnel, ZeroClaw starts a `tailscale serve` process to put the gateway on the tailnet at `https://<node>`. If that process failed right away, for example because the port was still in use, ZeroClaw never noticed. The dead process lingered as a "defunct" entry in `ps`, health checks said all was well, and the startup output printed a URL that didn't work. This PR has ZeroClaw watch that process the same way it already watches the WSS/enrollment forwarders. It confirms that Tailscale is actually serving the gateway before printing the URL, waits briefly for a port that is still being released, cleans up the process if it exits, and logs why. It does not restart a process that dies later, and it does not yet clean up serve processes left behind by a daemon that crashed.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes`
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (`zeroclaw daemon` with `[tunnel] tunnel_provider = "tailscale"`)
- **Setup / preconditions:** Linux node logged into a tailnet (`tailscale up`), serve permitted for the operator (`tailscale set --operator=$USER`), `[tunnel] tunnel_provider = "tailscale"`.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. In another terminal, hold the gateway port: `tailscale serve --https=443 8080` (leave it running).
  2. Start `zeroclaw daemon`.
  3. `ps -eo pid,stat,cmd | grep 'tailscale serve'`
  4. Stop the holder from step 1 and restart the daemon.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Step 2 prints `Tunnel failed to start: tailscale serve --https=443 <port> did not publish the gateway: exited (exit status: 1) after 5 attempt(s): ... listener already exists for port 443` and falls back to local-only. Step 3 shows no `<defunct>` entry. After step 4, `Tunnel active: https://<node>` and `tailscale serve status` shows the gateway proxy.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Step 2 prints `Tunnel active: https://<node>` even though nothing serves it, and step 3 shows `tailscale serve --https=443 <port> <defunct>` for as long as the daemon runs.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The CI `Clippy` job (`scripts/ci/run_clippy.sh --scope workspace`, Rust 1.98.0, `--features ci-all`, `-D warnings`) and the test jobs cover the changed Rust file. I ran the same clippy script locally on this head as well (below).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No CI job runs a real `tailscaled`. tailscaled's behaviour is pinned by the manual check below, and the tests use `sh` stand-ins for the process plus status JSON captured from a live 1.104.1 node.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```sh
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
# clean (no diff)

$ RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.98.0 RUNNER_TEMP=$PWD/target/ci-tmp \
    bash scripts/ci/run_clippy.sh --scope workspace --summary-title "Lint diagnostics" --log-name cargo-clippy.log
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 3m 20s
# exit 0; 0 warning/error lines in cargo-clippy.log

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tunnel::
test tunnel::tailscale::tests::gateway_serve_exit_is_reaped_not_left_defunct ... ok
test tunnel::tailscale::tests::dropping_the_tunnel_kills_and_reaps_its_gateway_serve ... ok
test tunnel::tailscale::tests::gateway_sessions_match_only_an_https_proxy_to_the_local_port ... ok
test tunnel::tailscale::tests::held_port_is_retryable_but_other_failures_are_not ... ok
test tunnel::tailscale::tests::start_forwarder_waits_out_a_port_that_is_being_released ... ok
test tunnel::tailscale::tests::start_forwarder_reports_a_port_that_stays_held ... ok
test result: ok. 126 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5586 filtered out; finished in 0.33s
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Against a live Tailscale 1.104.1 tailscaled, on a scratch port (19999) so the running daemon's sessions were untouched: (1) a second foreground `tailscale serve --tcp` on a port held by another foreground session exits 1 immediately with `sending serve config: updating config: listener already exists for port 19999`, which is the string matched here; (2) after the holder is SIGKILLed, an immediate respawn gets the port (a new session appeared within 1s and held it until its timeout), which is why bounded retry is enough for a releasing holder; (3) a live `serve --https=443 42617` session is stored as `TCP["443"].HTTPS = true` plus `Web["<magicdns>:443"].Handlers["/"].Proxy = "http://127.0.0.1:42617"`, the shape the applied-check matches. **Not verified:** a full daemon start/reload cycle on this branch against real tailscaled (I didn't interrupt the running daemon), `funnel` mode against a live node, and non-Linux hosts.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`. No rendered interface changed; the only user-visible change is the existing tunnel start/fallback lines and log events.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** this branch's head; `cargo test` / `run_clippy.sh` on Linux x86_64, rustc 1.98.0 (clippy) and 1.99.0 (tests).
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full `cargo test` for the workspace was not run locally; CI covers it, and the change is confined to `tunnel/tailscale.rs`, whose 126 module tests ran. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` on local rustc 1.99.0 fails on lints new in 1.99 (`needless_borrows_for_generic_args` in `zeroclaw-providers`, deprecated `fetch_update` in `zeroclaw-tools` and `zeroclaw-runtime` rpc). Those are pre-existing and outside this diff, so I used CI's pinned 1.98.0 script instead, which is clean.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `No`. It adds local `tailscale serve status --json` calls to the local tailscaled during gateway startup, the same probe the forwarders already use.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`. Fixtures use the captured serve-status shape with placeholder node names and addresses.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes`. No config, CLI or trait change. The one behaviour change, where an unpublishable 443 now fails `start()`, is described under Blast radius.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk PRs: `git revert <sha>` is the plan unless otherwise noted.

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>` (single commit, single file).
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Setting `[tunnel] tunnel_provider = "none"` avoids the path entirely.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `Tunnel failed to start: tailscale ... did not publish the gateway` on startup; WARN events `tailscale did not publish the gateway` and `tailscale serve exited after publication` (attrs: `service`, `status`, `stderr`, `command`).

prs.title: fix(channels/email): save inbound documents to the channel workspace
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The email page says inbound attachments are stored under the workspace and their paths handed to the agent. Nothing was ever written: documents reached the agent only as bytes for one turn, and a `text/*` attachment was dropped whenever the email had a body (`extract_attachments` skips text parts, and `extract_text` only uses one when there is no body).
  - `collect_configured_channels` now gives `EmailChannel` its `Config::channel_workspace_dir("email.<alias>")`, as it already does for Telegram and Matrix.
  - In `dispatch_email`, after the allowlist and de-duplication checks, every attachment that is neither image nor audio is written to `<workspace>/email_files/<message-key>_<n>_<name>`. Its typed `marker` is set to `MarkerKind::Document` with the saved path and the content gets a `[Document: <name>] <path>` line, the same contract Matrix uses (`format_media_marker`), so the media pipeline defers to it. With a workspace, text attachments are saved too, even when there is a body.
  - Hardening: the name is the basename only, with control characters replaced, leading dots stripped and the whole saved name bounded to 255 bytes without splitting a character (extension kept); the message key is the id reduced to `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` (40 chars max) plus 16 hex digits of its SHA-256, so ids that sanitize alike stay apart. Files are created with `create_new`; a clashing name gets a `-1`, `-2`, ... suffix instead of replacing the earlier file. `email_files/` is canonicalized and refused if it resolves outside the canonical workspace (e.g. a symlink). Any failure is logged (`Action::Save`, scrubbed error) and the email is delivered as before.
  - Docs: the "Attachment handling" section now describes what the code does. I used `email_files/` instead of the documented `attachments/<conversation>/`: it matches `telegram_files/` and `matrix_files/`, and email has no stable conversation key (threading comes from sender-controlled headers). The old path came in with the docs overhaul (#5788) and was never implemented.
- **Scope boundary:** inbound only. No retention or cleanup of `email_files/` (Telegram and Matrix keep files indefinitely too). Images and audio are not saved and keep going through the media pipeline. No config or schema change. The one-shot send builder (`build_channel_by_id`) is unchanged because it never receives mail. Outbound attachments and #9993's "bytes only" rule are untouched: nothing here reads a file named by a message.
- **Blast radius:** inbound email turns on configured email channels. The agent now sees `[Document: …]` lines and, for text attachments on emails with a body, attachments it did not see before. Disk usage grows with inbound documents, bounded per email by the existing `max_attachment_bytes`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11745

### What this does, simply

When someone emails the agent a PDF or a spreadsheet, the agent used to get the file's bytes for that one reply and nothing else: no copy on disk, no path, and a `.txt` or `.csv` attachment was thrown away if the email also had text in it. The docs said the opposite. Now the email channel saves those documents in the agent's workspace, next to where Telegram and Matrix already save theirs, and tells the agent where each one is, so it can open it again later with its file tools. Only mail from allowed senders is saved, file names are cleaned so they cannot escape the folder, and pictures and voice notes are handled exactly as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The new tests drive `dispatch_email`, the function the IMAP loop calls for every fetched message, with a real MIME message and a real temp workspace, and assert the files on disk, the content lines and the typed markers.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the required `Test` job runs `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`. `channel-email` is in `zeroclaw-channels`' `default-channels`, so the email tests below run there. `Lint` builds them with `--features ci-all`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no test asserts the one-line orchestrator wiring (`collect_configured_channels` returns `Arc<dyn Channel>`, which exposes no workspace accessor). It mirrors the Telegram and Matrix lines next to it.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(clean)

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets -- -D warnings \
    -A clippy::needless_borrows_for_generic_args -A deprecated
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- email
test result: ok. 95 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1888 filtered out

$ BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base upstream/master HEAD) scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
Summary: 0 error(s)

$ scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
No added links detected in changed docs lines.
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - `dispatch_email_saves_documents_to_workspace_with_marker_lines`: a multipart email with a body, a PDF named `../report.pdf`, a CSV and a PNG. The PDF and CSV land byte-identical under `email_files/` as `doc-1exampleinvalid-<hash>_0_report.pdf` and `_1_rows.csv`, the content carries both `[Document: …] <path>` lines, exactly those two attachments are marked, and the PNG stays unmarked for the pipeline.
  - `dispatch_email_without_workspace_keeps_documents_in_memory`: no workspace means today's behavior (no lines, no markers, CSV left to `extract_text`).
  - `dispatch_email_saves_nothing_for_a_blocked_sender`: with a workspace and a sender outside the allowlist, nothing is delivered and `email_files/` is never created.
  - `dispatch_email_refuses_email_files_outside_workspace` (unix): `email_files` is a symlink to another directory; nothing is written there and the email is delivered without markers.
  - `dispatch_email_keeps_attachments_of_similar_message_ids_apart`: `doc.1@…` and `doc1@…` each carry `report.pdf` with different bytes; each message's marker path reads back its own bytes.
  - `write_new_file_never_replaces_an_existing_file`: a second write with the same name lands at `id_0-1_a.pdf` and the first file is unchanged.
  - `write_new_file_bounds_long_unicode_names_in_bytes`: a 200-character CJK name with a 500-character message id saves as a name of at most 255 bytes that keeps `.pdf`.
  - `safe_file_stem_keeps_similar_message_ids_apart`, `safe_file_name_strips_paths_and_leading_dots_and_bounds_length`.
  - **Not verified:** delivery from a live IMAP mailbox on this head.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** clippy reports two `needless_borrows_for_generic_args` errors in `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs` (untouched by this PR) on my local stable 1.99 toolchain; CI pins 1.98.0. I allowed that lint and `deprecated` for the local run only. The pre-push hook (`cargo test --workspace`) was skipped with `--no-verify` because of local disk limits; required CI runs the same suite.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: the channel now writes sender-supplied bytes under the agent workspace. Only allowlisted senders' mail is written, into one fixed directory whose canonical path must stay inside the canonical workspace, with names reduced to a bounded basename that cannot contain separators or start with a dot. The new model-visible text is the sanitized file name inside a `[Document: …]` line; the attachment content was already model-visible.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the squash commit. Files already saved under `email_files/` are inert and can be deleted.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `failed to save email attachment` or `failed to prepare email_files directory` warnings (`event.action = save`, outcome failure) from `zeroclaw_channels::email_channel`; the email is still delivered.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): make Config save and cancel predictable
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Honor the resolved Save action in scalar and choice editors as well as multiline editors. Preserve Enter-to-save for scalar/choice and Enter-to-newline for multiline input.
  - Show resolved Save/Cancel controls and pending-edit state. Ask Stay/Discard before navigation replaces a changed draft; allow navigation that parks it.
  - Preserve personality content after Save and retain failed-write drafts for retry. Explain automatic import/save before launching the external personality or Skills editor, including when applying a personality template.
  - Route connection paste and remapped editor actions to the visible local editor. Persist connection candidates before replacing the in-memory saved value.
- **Scope boundary:** No persisted schema, RPC method, default shortcut, modifier migration, global navigation redesign, secret-handling change or Delete/Reset confirmation change.
- **Blast radius:** ZeroCode Config key, paste and mouse dispatch; personality/Skills editing; local connection draft writes. Existing persistence owners remain unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11486. Builds on #11460 (merged).
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `risk:medium`, `size:XL`, `zerocode`, `docs`.

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode Config lets you change daemon settings, personality files, Skills and the client's connection settings. Before this change, each editor had different save and cancel conventions. Moving away could lose typed work, and saving a personality file could clear the content of the still-open editor.

This PR makes the existing Save and Cancel actions visible and consistent. Enter still saves a single value, but still adds a newline when you are editing several lines. A changed draft shows that edits are pending. If navigation would throw it away, Config asks whether to stay or discard it. Switching to a pane that keeps the draft does not ask.

Saving a personality file leaves its content open. A failed save keeps your work so you can retry. External editors still import and save changed content after a successful exit, but Config explains that behavior before launch and lets you cancel there. When applying a personality template, it compares the edited result with the current file, or an empty baseline if the file does not exist. Config continues using the same files and daemon persistence calls.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

Four files, 1191 additions and 246 deletions against current `master`. The change stays inside the existing Config editor, ZeroCode connection pane, locale file and Config docs.

The interaction policy must cover keyboard, paste and mouse entry into the existing scalar, choice, multiline and composite editors. A footer-only change would still allow silent draft loss and the personality repeat-Save defect. The change keeps one Config owner, adds an original field snapshot where none existed, and derives pending state from existing draft baselines. It does not introduce a second configuration model or replace the editor. Much of the added code exercises real handler dispatch and existing persistence boundaries; future Config navigation should preserve this same departure policy.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for the visible controls and modal layout.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Config.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use an existing non-sensitive agent and a matching-version daemon. Build ZeroCode from this head with `cargo build --locked -p zerocode --bin zerocode`, then launch `target/debug/zerocode --config-dir <your-existing-config-directory>` using your existing connection setup. An explicitly configured Cargo target changes the binary's location.
- **Steps to run:** Open Config, edit an ordinary scalar or choice and change its value without saving. Click an earlier breadcrumb or another daemon section. Cancel the dialog to keep editing, then use Save. Open an existing personality file, edit it inline, save twice, and confirm its text remains present. Return to the file list and invoke its existing external-editor action, then cancel the prelaunch dialog. Repeat that prelaunch check for an existing Skill if available.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The footer names the resolved Save/Cancel keys and pending state. Destructive navigation offers Stay/Discard without saving. Save retains personality content and failed writes remain editable. The external-editor dialog explains import/save after successful exit.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Scalar/choice editors use only Enter to save; draft loss on navigation is not deliberate; personality list refresh can clear the retained editor; no external-editor prelaunch explanation appears. Breadcrumb navigation itself came from #11460 and is already on `master`.

### How I tested

```text
# on 60f89750470d (master 4e82ce46e9c6 merged in)
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode
test result: 1536 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored
  failing: connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint
  (fails identically on plain master 4e82ce46e9c6; unrelated to this change)

cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
passed

rustfmt --edition 2024 --check (changed files)
passed

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.

git diff --check origin/master HEAD
passed
```

The suite exercises production Config handlers with scripted RPC responses. New cases check scalar/choice/array Save payloads under a remapped key, no writes on Cancel/Discard, filtered-choice cancellation, personality content after repeated Save, failed external personality import followed by inline retry, and keyboard/mouse departures. App-level connection cases verify paste reaches the visible editor, Save/Cancel remapped to Tab outrank section navigation, and a parked daemon draft stays untouched. Local connection tests use temporary real config files to check failure retention, successful retry and cancellation without a write. Existing Skills and breadcrumb-navigation tests also pass; Skills retention and payload compatibility were additionally source-reviewed rather than claimed as a new dedicated failure matrix.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Quality Gate passed on `efc9cfdb566c`; the run for `60f89750470d` (Greptile fixes) is in progress. Workspace Test and Lint provide broader compilation, test and lint coverage; Format and Zerocode RPC Boundary cover formatting and Config RPC isolation. Applicable cross-platform and MSRV checks also passed.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI and scripted handlers do not supply a human-operated TUI layout check.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source and dispatch review plus the automated tests above. I also ran the Config flows by hand on experiment build [20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d): a changed scalar draft followed by navigation, and the external-editor prelaunch dialog.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Two frames in [this comment](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11511#issuecomment-6232646371): the Stay/Discard dialog over a changed scalar draft, and the external-editor prelaunch explanation.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Automated evidence is for `60f89750470df86bc251e179530f7d2b13c0b7a5`; ZeroCode Config, English. The frames were captured on experiment build [20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d) (dogfood base `0341618f9d69`), which carries this PR's Config draft changes. It is not this exact head.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Scripted Save sends the expected persistence payload, Cancel/Discard send no write, personality Save preserves content across refresh, and failed connection Save keeps its draft until retry succeeds.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full local workspace tests and broad Clippy are delegated to current-head CI; the focused binary suite directly checks the edited dispatch paths without repeating that broader coverage.

### Visual evidence

Frames: see [this comment](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11511#issuecomment-6232646371).

Use this revision in a real 120-column by 40-row English terminal. The first frame should retain the editor's Save/Cancel/pending footer around the discard dialog. The second should show the explanation that a successful external-editor exit imports and saves changed content, with its launch and cancel actions. Expected visible result: readable explanation and controls without overlap or clipping. Observed result: readable dialog and controls, with no overlap or clipping. These frames check presentation; the handler and file tests establish save/cancel transitions.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- Risk and mitigation: The local connection candidate uses the existing config writer. External editors and daemon writes retain their existing access and persistence boundaries.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Existing defaults are retained and scalar/choice Enter remains a Save alias.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No schema, environment or CLI option changes. Config TUI interaction changes as described above.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: None. Existing keybindings continue to resolve through the current action registry.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the squash commit. It contains only this change; the navigation work from #11460 is already on `master` separately.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None; no new persisted controls.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Save does not persist the selected value, Cancel unexpectedly writes, navigation discards a changed draft without asking, or a saved personality editor becomes empty. Check the Config footer's localized save failure and pending status, then reopen the value to verify persistence.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A. No PR is superseded.

prs.title: fix(channels/whatsapp-web): tell the sender why a voice note was not transcribed
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A WhatsApp Web voice note that produced no transcript left the message content empty, so the handler returned at `ignoring empty or non-text message`. Nothing reached the agent and nothing went back. To the sender, that looks the same as a bot that is down, so they resend and wait again.
  - `try_transcribe_voice_note` now returns `Result<String, VoiceDropReason>` instead of `Option<String>`. The five reasons are: no transcription configured, longer than `max_duration_secs`, download failed, provider error, and empty transcript. On the empty-content drop, the handler sends one short sentence with that reason to the chat the note came from. The note itself is still not passed to the agent.
  - This mirrors #10620 for Telegram: the same `⚠️ Audio message skipped: …` wording, Fluent keys in all five locales (`channel-whatsapp-web-voice-drop-*`), provider and download diagnostics kept in the log, and a 10-second ceiling on the send, so a stalled send cannot hold up the messages behind it. A failed or timed-out notice is logged and swallowed.
  - The notice goes only where a normal reply would. It is sent at the existing empty-content drop, which is reached only after the allowlist, `allowed_groups`, chat policy, `mention_only` and passive-group-context gates. On top of that, the new `voice_drop_notice` helper stays silent when mention patterns apply to the chat type: a note with no transcript cannot match them, so the bot cannot tell whether it was addressed.
  - Two reasons Telegram does not have: WhatsApp Web has no retry path, so a download or provider failure is final here, and it gets its own sentence. "Not configured" also gets a sentence, because a deployment without STT should tell users to send text instead of staying silent.
- **Scope boundary:** no config, CLI or env surface; no new dependencies. No change to transcription providers, to what reaches the agent, to the voice-chat state (`voice_chats.remove` still runs for an untranscribed note, as on `master`), or to non-PTT audio when `transcribe_non_ptt_audio = false` (that stays an operator opt-out and stays silent). The Cloud API channel and other channels are untouched.
- **Blast radius:** the WhatsApp Web inbound voice path only. For an admitted sender whose voice note is not transcribed, the channel now sends one extra text message to that chat.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11764. Related: #10620 (the Telegram counterpart).

Interplay with #11056 (docs for the WhatsApp voice-note round trip): that PR says a failed note "is dropped before it reaches the agent, and the reason is logged". That stays true, but once this lands the sender is also told why. Whichever of the two merges second needs a one-line follow-up to that sentence.

### What this does, simply

When someone sends the bot a WhatsApp voice note, the bot turns it into text and answers that. When this fails (speech-to-text isn't set up, the note is too long, it can't be downloaded, the transcription service fails, or nothing could be recognized), the bot used to say nothing at all, so the person had no idea whether they had been heard. Now the bot replies with one short sentence that says why, for example "⚠️ Audio message skipped: it is longer than the 120s limit. Send a shorter recording or split it into parts." The bot only does this where it would have answered anyway: not to strangers, not in groups it ignores, and not to group messages that weren't aimed at it.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Optional, if a spare WhatsApp account is available.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `whatsapp_web`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** a Web-mode `[channels.whatsapp.<alias>]` channel paired to a test number (for example `+15550001234`), bound to an agent, with `[transcription]` enabled and `max_duration_secs = 5`.
- **Steps to run:** from an allowed number, send the bot a 10-second voice note in a private chat. Then send one from a number that is not allowed. Then remove `[transcription]` and send a short voice note from the allowed number.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the allowed sender gets `⚠️ Audio message skipped: it is longer than the 5s limit. Send a shorter recording or split it into parts.`, and later `⚠️ Audio message skipped: audio messages cannot be transcribed here. Please send your message as text.` The stranger gets nothing.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** no reply in any of the three cases; the drop shows up only in the log.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Lint job, which runs `scripts/ci/run_clippy.sh` with `--all-targets --features ci-all` (`ci-all` includes `whatsapp-web`), so it compiles and lints this code and its tests.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI compiles the new tests but does not run them. The Test job runs `cargo nextest run --workspace` with default features, `whatsapp-web` is not a default feature, and the per-channel `Test (channel ...)` matrix has no WhatsApp Web leg. I ran them locally with the feature on (commands below).
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(no output)

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets --features whatsapp-web -- -D warnings -A clippy::needless_borrows_for_generic_args -A deprecated
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2m 22s

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib --features whatsapp-web whatsapp_web
test whatsapp_web::tests::voice_drop_notice_respects_mention_patterns ... ok
test whatsapp_web::tests::voice_drop_notices_name_the_reason_without_internals ... ok
test whatsapp_web::tests::untranscribed_voice_note_reports_why ... ok
test result: ok. 180 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 2089 filtered out

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib --features whatsapp-web
test result: ok. 2267 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib i18n
test result: ok. 45 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5699 filtered out
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - New tests: `untranscribed_voice_note_reports_why` uses a real offline `whatsapp_rust::Client` and checks that `try_transcribe_voice_note` returns `NotConfigured` without transcription and `TooLong { limit_secs: 5 }` for a 30-second note, both before any download. `voice_drop_notice_respects_mention_patterns` checks that a notice is produced with no patterns, is withheld when DM or group patterns apply to the chat, is not withheld by patterns for the other chat type, and that no reason means no notice. `voice_drop_notices_name_the_reason_without_internals` checks that every reason has a distinct sentence starting with `⚠️`, that the numeric limit is included, and that there is no "error", "http" or "api" text.
  - Mutation check: removing the mention-pattern gate from `voice_drop_notice` makes `voice_drop_notice_respects_mention_patterns` fail.
  - **Not verified:** a live run on a paired number with this exact branch. The download-failed and provider-error paths need a connected client or a real provider, so only their mapping in the diff covers them. The actual `send_message` of the notice is also not covered by a test.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. The only user-visible change is a plain chat text message, shown verbatim above.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** this branch's head, unit tests on the `whatsapp_web` voice-drop helpers.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** see the test output above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** I pushed with `--no-verify` after the fmt, clippy and `zeroclaw-channels` lib tests above passed. The pre-push hook runs `cargo test --workspace`, which does not enable `whatsapp-web`, so it would not run these tests.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? Yes
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No (examples use `+15550001234`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The notice is fixed outbound text and nothing new reaches the model.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: the extra call is one WhatsApp text message through the existing client, sent only after every admission gate a normal reply passes, so a stranger or an unaddressed group learns nothing. The send is capped at 10 seconds, and a failure is logged and does not change the drop.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Admitted senders of an untranscribed voice note now get a one-line notice instead of silence.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Revert the squash-merge commit for this PR.

prs.title: fix(runtime): let the agent read the rest of a truncated workspace file
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - When a workspace bootstrap file exceeds its per-file cap, the channel/agent-loop prompt contained two conflicting instructions. The header said "They are ALREADY injected below—do NOT suggest reading them with file_read", and the marker after the cut said "use `read AGENTS.md` for full file". `read` is not a tool; the tool is `file_read`. The #11710 reporter's agent followed the header for weeks and never applied the rules in the cut-off third of a 29K AGENTS.md.
  - Added one shared marker, `system_prompt::bootstrap_truncation_marker`. It says the rest of the file is not loaded and to read it with `file_read` before relying on later sections. Both prompt paths now use it: `system_prompt.rs` (channel / agent loop / turn) and `personality.rs` (Agent / gateway). Before, each path had a hand-copied format string.
  - `load_openclaw_bootstrap_files` now renders the files before writing the header. When any file was cut, it uses a header variant that keeps "already injected, do not re-read" but makes an exception for files marked truncated.
- **Scope boundary:** The cap mismatch reported in the same issue is not changed: gateway/Agent turns use a fixed 20,000 while channel/agent-loop turns use 6,000 with `compact_context`, and `doctor` reports only the latter. Unifying those changes how much of a file gateway turns see, so it needs a maintainer decision; it is tracked in #11771. The Agent/gateway header (`prompt.rs`) has no prohibition, so only its marker changes.
- **Blast radius:** Model-visible system prompt text, only when a bootstrap file exceeds its cap. With no truncated file, the prompt is byte-identical to `master` (pinned by `untruncated_bootstrap_header_is_unchanged`), so the normal case's prompt-cache prefix is unaffected. The operator-facing WARN and `doctor` output are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11710 (prompt contradiction). The doctor/cap part is tracked in #11771. #11710 has no triage labels yet.

### What this does, simply

Workspace files like AGENTS.md are pasted into the agent's instructions, but only up to a size limit. Past the limit, the file was cut with a note saying "read the full file". The paragraph introducing these files also said "don't read them, they're already here". The agent obeyed the second instruction, so rules near the end of a long AGENTS.md were silently never seen. Now, when a file is cut, both texts agree: the rest isn't loaded, so read it with the `file_read` tool. When nothing is cut, the instructions are exactly as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The change is prompt text pinned by unit tests that build the real system prompt. Confirming that a model now reads the rest of the file depends on the model and isn't deterministic.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `cargo test` covers `zeroclaw-runtime` (`agent::system_prompt`, `agent::personality`, `agent::prompt`) and the `zeroclaw-channels` orchestrator prompt tests that build bootstrap content. `Format` and `Lint` run on Linux.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Run locally on Windows with Rust 1.98.0, the CI-pinned toolchain.

```text
$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib agent::
test result: ok. 1374 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 4200 filtered out

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib orchestrator::tests
test result: ok. 625 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1333 filtered out

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib prompt
test result: ok. 74 passed; 0 failed

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib doctor
test result: ok. 78 passed; 0 failed

$ cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-runtime   # applied
$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets   # no warnings in system_prompt.rs or personality.rs
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - New `truncated_bootstrap_header_allows_reading_the_rest`: a 7,000-char AGENTS.md under a 6,000 cap yields the exception header and no "do NOT suggest reading" header.
  - New `untruncated_bootstrap_header_is_unchanged`: the original header bytes, followed by the file, when nothing is cut.
  - Updated `bootstrap_truncation_marker_and_prompt_bytes_unchanged` pins the exact new marker and the 6,000-char cut.
  - Extended `render_truncated_file_shows_notice` pins `file_read` in the gateway-path marker and the absence of "use `read".
  - The whitespace after the marker (`]\n\n`) matches the previous output on both paths.
  - Not verified with a live model.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. Model-facing prompt text only; no user-visible interface state changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Branch head; unit tests only.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `cargo clippy ... -D warnings` fails locally on pre-existing Windows-only lints in files this PR does not touch (`zeroclaw-config` platform/secrets modules, `zeroclaw-runtime` `service/mod.rs`, `rpc/auth.rs`, `turn/vision_route.rs`). CI lints on Linux.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. `file_read` keeps its existing workspace policy; the prompt only stops discouraging its use for a file the agent already has.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Model-visible system prompt wording changes, but only for operator-authored workspace files that exceed the cap. The new text points the model at the operator's own file through the existing `file_read` tool and policy. No untrusted content is added.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: `git revert <sha>`.

prs.title: fix(skills): keep the open-skills sync from prompting for git credentials
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The open-skills `git clone` and `git pull --ff-only` now run with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` (new `open_skills_git_command()` helper in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/skills/mod.rs`).
  - Why: `Command::output()` already closes stdin, but git asks for credentials on the controlling terminal. The default remote `https://github.com/besoeasy/open-skills` now answers 404, which git over HTTPS treats as an auth challenge, so a daemon started from a terminal with `open_skills_enabled = true` printed `Username for 'https://github.com':` and sat there (#11796). With the variable set, git fails at once, the existing failure branch logs a warning, and the local copy keeps being used.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change the open-skills repository URL, the sync interval, or whether open-skills is enabled; does not touch the skills-registry clone/pull or `skills install` from a git URL (user-invoked paths). A credential helper, if configured, is still consulted; only the terminal prompt is turned off.
- **Blast radius:** Only the two open-skills git invocations used while loading skills (daemon, channel turns, `agent`).
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11796

### What this does, simply

When open-skills is enabled, ZeroClaw keeps a local clone of a community skills repo and refreshes it about once a week. That repo has been deleted, and when git can't reach a repo over HTTPS it asks for a username on the terminal. Inside the daemon nobody answers, so startup hung at that prompt. This PR tells git it may never prompt there: the refresh fails quickly, a warning is logged, and ZeroClaw carries on with the skills it already has. Whether the default URL should change is left to maintainers.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — covered by a focused unit test plus the terminal repro below; reproducing in a real daemon needs a TTY and the dead upstream repo.

### How I tested

Regression test `skills::skill_manifest_tests::open_skills_git_never_prompts_for_credentials` asserts the open-skills git command carries `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`.

Without the fix (env line removed from the helper):

```text

panicked at crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/skills/mod.rs:4838:9:
the open-skills sync must not let git ask for credentials on the terminal
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed
```

With the fix:

```sh
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib open_skills_
# test skills::skill_manifest_tests::open_skills_git_never_prompts_for_credentials ... ok
# test skills::skill_manifest_tests::open_skills_swallow_site_skips_invalid_toml_without_panicking ... ok
# test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed

cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib skills::
# test result: ok. 274 passed; 0 failed

cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-runtime --check   # clean
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --no-deps -- -D warnings
# local rustc 1.99.1 reports 2 errors in untouched files (rpc/upload.rs fetch_update deprecation, agent/turn/stream_guard.rs needless borrow); none in skills/mod.rs
```

Terminal repro of the hang (a small Rust program issuing the same `Command::new("git") … clone --depth 1 https://github.com/besoeasy/open-skills … .output()`, run under `script` to give it a TTY, no credential helper):

```text
before: Username for 'https://github.com':      (killed by timeout after 15s)
after:  exit status: 128 after 280ms: fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': terminal prompts disabled
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required gate / Test / Clippy / Format run the runtime crate that holds the change and the new test.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No test drives a real TTY prompt; the unit test checks the command configuration, and the repro above shows that configuration is what stops the prompt.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The TTY repro above. Did not run a full `zeroclaw daemon` on Termux.
- **Tested revision:** `5f86d749f` on `fix/11796-open-skills-git-prompt`.

prs.title: fix(channels/whatsapp-web): stop surfacing QR codes from a stopped listener
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - whatsapp-rust 0.7 rotates pairing QR codes on a detached task that neither `Client::disconnect` nor `BotHandle::shutdown` ends, and the client's event bus keeps calling the channel's handler. A WhatsApp Web channel stopped while unpaired therefore kept printing QR codes and emitting `LoginEvent::Qr` for up to ~160 s, for a connection that no longer exists.
  - The QR branch of the event handler now checks the listener's existing `persistence_cancel` fence, the token a drop guard cancels when `listen` stops however it stops (already used to fence the detached callbacks' pairing writes). Once it is cancelled, leftover codes are neither printed nor emitted.
  - The QR rendering moved, unchanged, from the inline closure into `WhatsAppWebChannel::surface_pairing_qr`, so the fence check can be unit-tested.
- **Scope boundary:** no change to the stop path itself (`shutdown`, timeouts, reconnect), to pair-code events, to inbound messages, or to what a running channel shows. It does not cancel the SDK's rotation task; the SDK has no public way to do that, so the task still runs out on its own, silently.
- **Blast radius:** WhatsApp Web pairing output only: the terminal QR banner and `login` QR events on `/api/events`, and only for a client whose listener has already stopped.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11758

### What this does, simply

To link a WhatsApp number, ZeroClaw shows a QR code that changes every 20 seconds or so. If the channel is stopped before anyone scans it (the config is reloaded, the channel is removed, or the daemon shuts down), the WhatsApp library keeps producing new codes in the background for a couple of minutes, and ZeroClaw kept showing them. Those codes can never work, and after a reload they appeared next to the real codes of the new connection, with nothing to tell them apart. Now a stopped channel stays quiet: only the running channel's codes are shown.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Optional, if a spare WhatsApp account is available (nothing is scanned, so no account is actually linked).
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `whatsapp_web`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** a Web-mode `[channels.whatsapp.<alias>]` channel with a fresh, unpaired session path, built with `--features whatsapp-web`.
- **Steps to run:** start the daemon, wait for the first QR code, do not scan it, then remove the channel from the config (or reload the daemon).
- **Expected on this branch (after):** no further QR codes for that channel after it stops.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** new QR codes keep appearing for up to ~160 s after the stop, and `/api/events` keeps receiving `login` QR events for the stopped alias.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Lint job, which runs clippy with `--features ci-all` (which includes `whatsapp-web`), so it compiles this code and its tests.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the tests are linted in CI but not run there: the required Test job runs `cargo nextest` with default features, and `whatsapp-web` is not one of them. I ran them locally with the feature on (commands below). The end-to-end path (the SDK's detached rotation task dispatching after shutdown) needs a WhatsApp server and is not covered by a unit test.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(no output)

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --features whatsapp-web --lib --tests -- -D warnings -A clippy::needless_borrows_for_generic_args -A deprecated
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2m 09s

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib --features whatsapp-web
test result: ok. 2266 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - New tests: `pairing_qr_is_surfaced_while_the_listener_runs` and `pairing_qr_from_a_stopped_listener_is_not_surfaced`.
  - Mutation check: disabling the fence check (`if false && fence.is_cancelled()`) makes `pairing_qr_from_a_stopped_listener_is_not_surfaced` fail; restoring it makes it pass.
  - Read whatsapp-rust 0.7.0: the rotation task in `pair.rs` exits only on its stop channel (pair-success), login or exhaustion; `disconnect` does not touch `pairing_cancellation_tx`; `CoreEventBus::dispatch` keeps calling registered handlers.
  - The stale codes were first seen on a v0.8.5-based build whose stop path disconnects the client; the same guard silenced them there.
  - **Not verified:** a live run of this exact branch against WhatsApp.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. The QR banner text and rendering are unchanged; the change only decides whether a stopped listener shows it.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** this branch's head, unit tests only.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full workspace test run (pre-push hook) was skipped with `--no-verify`; this change touches one file in `zeroclaw-channels`, whose full lib suite with `whatsapp-web` passed above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No (pairing QR payloads still ride only the broadcast-only ephemeral path; this only emits fewer of them)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
